text.enUS: Barbecued Buzzard Wings. Rigglefuzz swears by barbecued buzzard wings, a rich sauce on tangy meat. Everything for a batch is on hand except the wings themselves. Fetch enough of them and Rigglefuzz may part with the recipe. Rigglefuzz is proud of barbecued buzzard wings. The sauce is rich, the meat tangy, and the aroma carries to hungry folk a long way off. Every ingredient for a batch is already in hand, all but the wings. Bring four buzzard wings, and Rigglefuzz might share the recipe.

Barithras Moonshade. Barithras Moonshade is a night elf resident of Auberdine in Darkshore. Positioned within the coastal settlement, he seeks the help of adventurers willing to explore the shadowy wilderness and gather rare subterranean flora. Standing watch within the village of Auberdine, Barithras Moonshade contributes to the night elves' efforts to study and manage the unsettled land of Darkshore. He directs travelers to venture into nearby subterranean caverns to harvest specific fungi, such as death cap mushrooms, for study and use.

Barkeep Daniels. Barkeep Daniels tends the counter at the Lakeshire Inn, serving weary town guards, local fishermen, and visiting travelers. With the Blackrock clan raiding across the Redridge Mountains and cutting off supply routes, keeping the tavern fully stocked has become an uphill battle. Behind the counter of the Lakeshire Inn stands Barkeep Daniels, pouring drinks and greeting whoever wanders in from the bridge. Lakeshire has spent months under constant pressure from gnolls and the Blackrock orcs, and the town's defenders rely on the tavern to unwind after grim patrols. Unfortunately for Daniels, the severed roads and relentless attacks have disrupted trade throughout the region. Finding himself dangerously low on liquor during a time when the town needs good cheer most, he is eager for any passing adventurer willing to fetch shipments from safer settlements.

Baron Aquanis. Baron Aquanis is a powerful water elemental of the flooded Moonshrine Ruins in Blackfathom Deeps, where the Twilight's Hammer has made its lair. He rises from the deep water when someone disturbs the ruins' Fathom Stone. The shamans of the Earthen Ring have long thought him a corrupted elemental power, and they suspect the cult is behind it. Submerged beneath the flooded halls of the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Stone lies right under the noses of the Twilight's Hammer cultists who now occupy the ruins. Inside it is a fathom core, a device that, properly read, tells the history of all elemental activity around it. Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring sends Horde adventurers to recover the core, and disturbing the stone draws Baron Aquanis up from the depths.

Baron Aquanis. Upon vanquishing the water elemental Baron Aquanis within Blackfathom Deeps, adventurers recover a Strange Water Globe containing tainted, putrid fluid. Brought to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring, the artifact provides crucial evidence of the elemental corruption spreading beneath Ashenvale. Je'neu believes it will prove what corrupted the baron, and he wouldn't be surprised if it were the Twilight's Hammer cultists lurking in the submerged ruins. Baron Aquanis was no ordinary water spirit, but a powerful elemental corrupted by foul sorcery within the flooded grottos of Blackfathom Deeps. When destroyed, the elemental leaves behind a Strange Water Globe—an impervious orb holding a sloshing, putrid fluid that seemingly sustained and warped the creature's natural essence. The object defies physical damage, harboring energies that are deeply distressing to those attuned to the balance of the elements.

Baron Longshore's Head. This severed head is proof of the death of Baron Longshore, captain of the Southsea Freebooter vessel Heedless. Gazlowe posted a public bounty for the pirate's identifiable remains to protect Ratchet's commercial shipping along the Merchant Coast. Operating out of camps along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, Baron Longshore directed raids against regional merchant vessels on behalf of the Southsea Freebooters. His flagship, the Heedless, posed a direct threat to the goblin trade lanes linking Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Gazlowe, Chief Engineer of Ratchet, placed a bounty on Longshore requiring identifiable proof of demise. Delivering the pirate's head satisfies the contract and secures a monetary reward from the port authority.

Baron Revilgaz. Baron Revilgaz is the cunning goblin leader of Booty Bay and the Blackwater Raiders, ruling the pirate haven on behalf of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Perched high on the balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern, he balances fragile trade neutrality with ruthlessly pragmatic opportunism. He hires passing mercenaries to secure his investments, undermine rivals like the Bloodsail Buccaneers, and retrieve ancient relics of the jungle. From his vantage atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Baron Revilgaz watches the bustling docks of Blackwater Cove through a custom enchanted spyglass. Flanked by his trusted advisor, the tauren Fleet Master Seahorn, Revilgaz exercises firm control over the town's cutpurses, merchants, and privateers. Originally a human settlement overwhelmed by trolls before the First War, the port was claimed and fortified by goblins, eventually evolving into the pirate-leaning commercial nexus of the Blackwater Raiders. Revilgaz ensures the port remains officially open to both Alliance and Horde travelers, strictly enforcing neutrality within harbor limits so that trade continues uninterrupted.

Baron Silverlaine. Baron Silverlaine was the rightful human lord of the fortress once known as Silverlaine Keep, perched high above Pyrewood Village. When Archmage Arugal unleashed the savage worgen upon the region, the baron was mercilessly slaughtered. Now, his tormented spirit lingers in the ruined dining hall, bound in undeath to defend the very lair that became his tomb. Before the shadow of the wolf-beasts blanketed the southern hills of Silverpine, Baron Silverlaine ruled over a proud noble estate. His fortress provided safety and oversight to the surrounding lands. That peace shattered when Archmage Arugal, seeking a weapon against the rampaging Scourge, unleashed summoned worgen into the region. The feral monstrosities could not be controlled; they stormed the stronghold, overran its guards, and butchered the baron.

Baron's Demise. The contract you recovered bears the name of Baron Vardus, a nobleman from the old kingdom of Alterac. Magistrate Henry Maleb in Southshore wants him found and brought to justice, and asks for the baron's head. After Assassin's Contract, Magistrate Henry Maleb tells you that Baron Vardus put his name to the contract. Vardus is a nobleman from the old kingdom of Alterac, a man of cold heart and brutal ways, so Maleb is not surprised to find him behind it. Southshore will not let the baron send his thugs against the town without answering for it. Maleb wants him found among the Syndicate's haunts, perhaps in Strahnbrad's ruins or in the valley north of them, and asks for the baron's head.

Baros Alexston. In Stormwind City Hall, Baros Alexston keeps watch over the capital he helped rebuild. Once a close friend of Edwin VanCleef in the Stonemasons Guild, he stayed loyal to the crown when the guild fractured. Baros grew up on the Alexston Farmstead in Westfall's rolling grasslands. Thieves overran and burned the family homestead while he was young. Before they fled, his father hurriedly hid their cherished heirlooms across the grounds. Baros later journeyed to the capital and joined the Stonemasons Guild. For years, he labored beside Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef as they raised Stormwind anew from the ashes of the First War.

Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder. The Barrel of Barleybrew Scalder is a cask of stout ale crafted by the Barleybrew family to prove their brewing prowess against their chief competitors. It is entrusted to covert couriers tasked with infiltrating the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos to stage a sly taste-test sabotage. Brewing is serious business among the dwarves of Dun Morogh, and few rivalries burn hotter than the feud between the Thunderbrews and the Barleybrews. While the Thunderbrews enjoy vast renown and pride of place from their busy distillery in Kharanos, Marleth Barleybrew refuses to sit in their shadow. Rather than relying solely on open taverns, Marleth brews the fiery 'Scalder' to prove his recipes are second to none—hoping that unsuspecting patrons who taste it will realize the Thunderbrews do not hold a monopoly on fine dwarven drink.

Barrel of Shimmer Stout. A freshly brewed cask of Rejold Barleybrew's experimental dwarven ale, crafted in the cold reaches of Dun Morogh. Known for giving drinkers a potent jolt that supposedly brightens their vision, it is intended as a gift for guards keeping watch on the high mountain passes. Crafted by Rejold Barleybrew after gathering rare ingredients across Dun Morogh, Shimmer Stout represents the latest triumph of the storied Barleybrew family. Dwarven brewers take their craft with deadly seriousness, constantly competing to produce hearty concoctions capable of staving off the freezing mountain chill. Rejold's latest recipe is designed not only to warm the gut, but to sharpen the senses of those stationed out in the freezing winds.

Barrel of Thunder Ale. The Barrel of Thunder Ale is a prized keg of Kharanos's signature brew, smuggled straight out of the Thunderbrew Distillery's cellar. Swapped out for a cask of Marleth's Barleybrew Scalder, it serves as undeniable proof of foul play in an escalating brewing rivalry. In Dun Morogh, competition between rival master brewers runs deep, and few disputes are fiercer than the feud between the Thunderbrews of Kharanos and the Barleybrews of Brewnall Village. Marleth Barleybrew sought to slip a barrel of his own Barleybrew Scalder into his rivals' cellar, so that the Thunderbrews' patrons would taste his brew over theirs. This heavy barrel of Thunder Ale was seized in the exchange, dragged out under the noses of the local guards as physical evidence that the switch succeeded.

Barrow Key. The Barrow Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. It is kept locked inside a barrow cache to guard the ancient treasures sealed within the den's hoard. Within the subterranean barrows of the Talon Den, night elf druids established elaborate wards to protect their relics from interlopers. The Barrow Key is one piece of this multi-layered lock, concealed inside a specialized cache hidden among the subterranean passages. Accessing it requires the Gatekeeper's Key, ensuring that only those with knowledge of the druids' defensive network can ever hope to claim it.

Bartleby. Bartleby drinks and picks fights at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. His stubborn hold on his ale makes him a test for aspiring warriors who must face him in a tavern brawl. Bartleby spends his days at the Pig and Whistle Tavern in Stormwind's Old Town. The tavern draws a rougher crowd than the taprooms of Cathedral Square. He clings to his favorite mug, drinks cheap ale, nurses grievances, and picks fights with anyone who disturbs him.

Bartleby the Drunk. In the Pig and Whistle Tavern, Bartleby the Drunk faces a test set by Harry Burlguard. An aspiring Alliance warrior must take Bartleby's prized mug before Harry will teach deeper combat skills. Harry Burlguard asks for proof of a novice's backbone before teaching deeper combat skills in the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Across the room, Bartleby nurses his drinks at the far end of the counter. Harry wants you to take the man's mug, knowing Bartleby would rather fight than surrender his ale. The challenge puts a warrior's resolve to the test.

Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, a stubborn brawler keeps Bartleby's Mug close. A warrior must win it in a tavern brawl, then watch Bartleby drain his drink before he surrenders it. Bartleby keeps his mug close, and a young warrior in Stormwind must wrest it from him. The stubborn brawler gives it up only after a fight leaves him beaten. Even then, Bartleby drains every last drop before handing over the mug as proof of victory.

Bartleby's Mug. In Stormwind, Bartleby's Mug marks a young warrior's trial of grit. After besting Bartleby in the Pig and Whistle Tavern, you claim his drinking mug for your trainer, Harry Burlguard. Harry Burlguard tests young warriors with a brawl in Old Town. He asks you to take down Bartleby, a stubborn drunk at the bar of the Pig and Whistle Tavern. Once subdued, Bartleby reluctantly gives up his prized drinking mug, but first takes one final swig to drain the dregs.

Bashal'Aran. The demonic satyrs and vicious grells that infest the ancient night elven city of Bashal'Aran will not approach one shrine, bathed in an unearthly blue aura. Thundris Windweaver, the elder of Auberdine, sends adventurers to investigate the source of this untouched sanctuary. Bashal'Aran once stood as a glorious settlement of the ancient Kaldorei Empire, but its broken marble and overgrown arches now teem with demonic taint. Twisted satyrs and corrupt grells feed greedily upon the lingering magical energies of the ruins, their malice swelling with every passing day. Yet despite their predatory dominion, Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine spotted a curiosity: atop a western bluff in the ruins, an ethereal blue aura burns over a shrine that no demon will approach.

Bashal'Aran. Asterion, a sorrowful highborne ghost haunting the ancient ruins of Bashal'Aran, seeks a way to undo the binding magic that tethers his spectral form. Believing the mischievous local grells have touched the seal holding him, he tasks travelers with gathering their earrings to trace its lingering magical resonance. Amid the shattered marble of Bashal'Aran lingers Asterion, an ancient night elf spirit who has endured centuries of confinement. Trapped between life and true death, his existence has dwindled into an agonizing wait under the canopy of Darkshore. Bound directly to the ruined settlement by arcane craft, Asterion lacks the means to dispel his shackles alone, his mind worn thin by uncounted years of solitude and despair.

Bashal'Aran. Asterion, a night elf spirit trapped amidst the ruined pillars of Bashal'Aran, seeks the relic holding him bound to this world. Having sensed the corruption of his prison among the local grells, he directs travelers to hunt the satyrs who command them and recover the Ancient Moonstone Seal. For well over a thousand years, the spirit Asterion has remained tethered to the fallen ruins of Bashal'Aran. The surrounding marble pillars serve as an unyielding cage that neither his fading spiritual strength nor his ancient magic can crack. Bound by a cursed relic, he has spent centuries staring out at Darkshore's mist-shrouded canopy, wondering whether even the erosion of the stone around him would grant him release.

Bashal'Aran. Bashal'Aran is an ancient Highborne ruin situated in northern Darkshore, just east of Auberdine. Once a flourishing sister city to Ameth'Aran before the Great Sundering, the site now crawls with demonic satyrs and grells feeding on lingering arcane magic, while a solitary elven ghost remains trapped by a centuries-old curse. Before the Great Sundering broke ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Queen Azshara settled favored Highborne subjects in the twin towns of Bashal'Aran and Ameth'Aran. Governed by the powerful mage Athrikus Narassin, the cities boasted splendid markets and temples dedicated to Elune. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the cataclysm laid both settlements to waste. For reasons lost to time, Athrikus used his arcane mastery to bind his own second-in-command, the mage Asterion, into a moonstone seal within Bashal'Aran. Even after his physical body perished, Asterion's ghost remained shackled to the ruined shrine.

Bashana Runetotem. Bashana Runetotem is an herbalist and druidic researcher residing on the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. The daughter of Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, she aids the Cenarion Circle by overseeing agricultural investigations and guiding Horde adventurers against corrupting forces. Standing atop the breezy heights of the Elder Rise, Bashana Runetotem carries on the druidic legacy of her father, Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem. While her father guides the burgeoning tauren druids and advises Cairne Bloodhoof, Bashana focuses on practical research into botanical anomalies and regional threats. She equips travelers with tools like evergreen pouches to cultivate mysterious flora, notably the enigmatic morrowgrain, while also coordinating Horde efforts to cleanse foul corruption spreading from places like Blackfathom Deeps.

Bath'rah the Windwatcher. Bath'rah the Windwatcher is a solitary jungle troll shaman and weaponcrafter dwelling amidst the ruins near Chillwind Point. Far from his tropical homelands, he studies the tempestuous elements of the northern mountains, seeking champions powerful enough to help him craft formidable weapons of wind. While most jungle trolls keep to the warm forests and coasts of the south, Bath'rah has embraced the solitary life of a mountain hermit among the cold ruins of the Alterac Mountains. A seasoned shaman and craftsman, he devotes his days to listening to the howling winds and communing with nature spirits. His obsession is not merely philosophical; he seeks to bind the fury of violent elemental storms into tangible armaments for those who possess the strength to wield them.

Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is a rare, delicate herb found among the ruins of Bathran's Haunt in northwestern Ashenvale. Celebrated in night elf lore for its potent restorative qualities, the plant is believed to mend afflictions of the spirit as well as the flesh. Grown in the shadows of the ancient ruins north of Maestra's Post, Bathran's Hair has long been valued by night elf healers. Unlike common medicinal flora that soothe simple physical wounds, this herb possesses restorative properties said to cure deep ailments of the spirit. When a young night elf in Astranaar falls victim to an insidious, unyielding sickness, the herbalist Orendil Broadleaf seeks strands of this rare plant to brew a vital remedy.

Bathran's Hair. Bathran's Hair is an Alliance quest offered by Orendil Broadleaf at Maestra's Post in western Ashenvale. Desperate to treat a mysteriously afflicted night elf child whose illness transcends the physical body, Orendil sends adventurers north to scour the ancient ruins of Bathran's Haunt for a restorative plant renowned for mending ailments of the spirit. At Maestra's Post, just south of the Darkshore border, the night elf herbalist Orendil Broadleaf faces a troubling medical crisis. A young child in Astranaar has fallen grievously ill, exhibiting symptoms that resist ordinary physical remedies. Convinced that the sickness plagues the child's spirit rather than merely the flesh, Orendil seeks Bathran's Hair, an uncommon restorative herb historically gathered amidst the ancient elven ruins to the north.

Bathran's Haunt. Bathran's Haunt is an ancient kaldorei ruin nestled in northwestern Ashenvale, east of the Zoram Strand. Recently, Forsaken herbalists and their guardians have overtaken the site to harvest local flora for their alchemical research, steadily withering the surrounding woodland. North of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran, crumbling night elf pillars stand swallowed by thick Ashenvale foliage. What was once a tranquil kaldorei relic has fallen under the shadow of the Forsaken. Skulking among the broken marble, undead herbalists and their enforcers have set up a crude open-air laboratory. Their presence alone blights the ancient soil: grass rots into a sickly brown, vibrant blossoms wilt, and an unnatural decay creeps through the grove as they methodically harvest rare woodland reagents for their experiments.

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. Battle of Hillsbrad is the opening strike in the Forsaken campaign to eradicate the human settlement of Hillsbrad. Handed down by High Executor Darthalia under orders from Varimathras, this mission targets the farmers and infrastructure of the northern Hillsbrad Fields to sever the town's food supply. Tarren Mill stands as the southern spearhead of the Forsaken empire, facing an entrenched human populace clinging to the Hillsbrad Foothills. High Executor Darthalia operates under strict directives straight from Varimathras in the Undercity. Her strategy is total attrition: before marching directly on the heavily defended town of Hillsbrad, she orders the systematic disruption of its agriculture. Striking the northern fields deprives the human militia of critical provisions while sowing chaos across their homesteads.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. Battle of Hillsbrad is a Forsaken military mission directed by High Executor Darthalia from Tarren Mill. Following the initial strikes on the northern human farms, Horde operatives are sent south to slaughter the fleeing Hillsbrad Peasants seeking refuge in the orchards. The campaign against the human presence in Hillsbrad Foothills moves with cold deliberation. After Horde forces strike the northern farms, panic sweeps through the settlement. Rather than taking up arms, many laborers flee southward into the orchards and pastures of Hillsbrad Fields, hoping to hide from the advancing undead. High Executor Darthalia views their terror not with mercy, but as a strategic opening to break Hillsbrad's remaining labor force and morale completely.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. This operation represents a critical phase in the Forsaken campaign to conquer the Hillsbrad Foothills. High Executor Darthalia orders the destruction of the local smithy in Hillsbrad Fields to cut off the weapons arming the stubborn human populace. The Forsaken push across the Hillsbrad Foothills faced fiercer resistance than High Executor Darthalia anticipated. The rural humans refused to simply scatter or yield to the Deathstalkers and soldiers sent from Tarren Mill. Investigation revealed that the local peasantry were not fighting with simple pitchforks and scythes; they were actively being outfitted for war right in the fields.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. This critical phase of the Forsaken campaign against Southshore's surrounding holdings targets the civic leadership of Hillsbrad town. Directed by High Executor Darthalia from Tarren Mill, Horde forces strike at Magistrate Burnside, his council, and their administrative records to completely shatter human governance in the foothills. Even after suffering severe casualties across their fields and patrols, the human defenders of Hillsbrad cling to their remaining civil authority. High Executor Darthalia recognizes that ordinary peasants and militia rally behind their civic leaders. To ensure the town completely collapses, Forsaken operatives are dispatched directly into the Town Hall to execute Magistrate Burnside and five of his councilmen, severing the chain of command.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. This campaign order from High Executor Darthalia directs Horde agents to strike deep into Azurelode Mine, a vital iron excavation south of Hillsbrad Fields. By eliminating Foreman Bonds and his crew, the Forsaken aim to sever iron shipments to Alliance armories and seize the tunnels for themselves. Having seized the Hillsbrad Town Registry during earlier raids, High Executor Darthalia identified Azurelode Mine as a linchpin of human military endurance in the region. The mine operates just south of the contested fields, continuously extracting rich veins of iron ore to supply Alliance weaponsmiths and armories. Leaving it untouched would allow Southshore's forces to rearm and bolster their garrisons, rendering Tarren Mill's prior victories moot.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. This critical phase of the Forsaken campaign in Hillsbrad targets the dwarven stronghold of Dun Garok. High Executor Darthalia dispatches Horde champions to dismantle the dwarven garrison assisting the local humans and execute their commanding officer, Captain Ironhill. Having pressured the human farmers and town militia across the foothills, High Executor Darthalia turns Tarren Mill's fury against Ironforge's military contingent. Dwarven troops have taken up arms in support of Southshore, reinforcing the human presence in Lordaeron. To Darthalia, this solidarity is an obstacle that must be shattered, proving to the Alliance that aiding the human remnants will bring only devastation.

name.ptBR: A batalha de Eira dos Montes

text.enUS: Battle of Hillsbrad. This mission marks the conclusion of the Forsaken campaign against the human township of Hillsbrad. Having shattered the local Alliance forces, you are sent by High Executor Darthalia to present an official commendation to Varimathras in the Undercity. The campaign in the Hillsbrad Foothills represents a brutal struggle for southern Lordaeron. Across a protracted series of strikes coordinated from Tarren Mill, Horde champions dismantled the human township's farmers, militia, blacksmiths, and civic leaders. With the Alliance presence crippled and the territory secured for the Forsaken, High Executor Darthalia drafts an official commendation to ensure the champion's exploits reach the highest ranks of command.

Battleboar Flank. Battleboar Flanks are hearty cuts of meat harvested from the vicious battleboars trained by Bristleback quilboar in Mulgore. Collected by young hunters around Camp Narache, they serve both as proof of culled threats and as nourishing sustenance for the tauren tribe. The Bristleback quilboar lurking in Brambleblade Ravine have trained vicious battleboars to encroach on tauren hunting grounds. While these aggressive beasts pose a direct hazard to the young tauren coming of age at Camp Narache, nothing taken from nature is wasted. Grull Hawkwind directs novice hunters to harvest the flanks of these felled beasts alongside their snouts. The cuts of flank provide rich, sustaining meat that is cooked down into hearty stew for the tribe's youth, turning a quilboar weapon of war into vital tribal nourishment.

Battleboar Snout. Battleboar Snouts are harvested from the aggressive boars trained by the Bristleback quilboar in Mulgore. Collected by young tauren hunters, they serve both as proof of thinning an invasive threat and as hearty ingredients for tribal cooking in Camp Narache. In the shadow of Red Cloud Mesa, the Bristleback quilboar train malicious battleboars within Brambleblade Ravine to probe tauren hunting grounds. When young braves are sent out by Grull Hawkwind to push back against this encroachment, the snout serves as undeniable proof of a beast brought down. Rather than wasting any part of the kill, the tauren use these snouts alongside cuts of flank to prepare rich, sustaining stews to feed their young.

Battleworn Axe. Battleworn Axes are crude, notch-scarred weapons carried by the Blackrock orcs invading the Redridge Mountains. Marshal Marris accepts these recovered blades in Lakeshire as physical proof of dead invaders threatening the local populace. These heavy, nicked axes serve as standard gear for the Blackrock reavers pushing south from the Burning Steppes into Redridge. For Marshal Marris and the beleaguered town watch of Lakeshire, collecting them serves two purposes: ensuring another marauding orc has fallen, and gathering physical evidence of how heavily armed the encroaching warband truly is.

Bay of Storms. The Bay of Storms is an expansive, tempestuous gulf carving into the rugged eastern cliffs of Azshara. Its churning waters harbor ancient ruins, submerged caverns, and perilous marine beasts that make seafaring along this coast hazardous. Opening out toward the Great Sea, the Bay of Storms defines much of Azshara's dramatic coastal geography. Far from a tranquil harbor, its turbulent waters and rocky outcrops are home to dangerous wildlife and ancient aquatic threats. Within and along its waters lie landmarks like the sunken Temple of Arkkoran, the coral reefs of Hetaera's Clutch, and Scalebeard's Cave, leaving the bay largely avoided by casual sailors and claimed instead by coastal monsters.

Bazil Thredd. Bazil Thredd is Edwin VanCleef's lieutenant and most trusted assistant, locked in the Stormwind Stockade since the Stonemasons' riots. Now the prison has risen in revolt, and Thredd leads the rioting Defias inmates from its eastern cell block. When the Stonemasons Guild was refused payment by the nobility of Stormwind for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef rejected government appeasements and sparked open revolt. Bazil Thredd stood at VanCleef's side as his chief lieutenant and most trusted assistant. During the violent clashes that followed, Thredd was captured by the city guard. While VanCleef and the surviving masons fled into Westfall to form the Defias Brotherhood, Thredd was cast into the depths of the Stormwind Stockade.

Bazil Thredd. In Stormwind, Bazil Thredd holds insight into the Defias Brotherhood's lingering plots. After an unsent letter is recovered from the Deadmines, City Architect Baros Alexston directs you to the Defias leader's right-hand man, now locked beneath the streets in the high-security Stockade. Baros Alexston shares a bitter history with Edwin VanCleef. Both led the Stonemasons Guild, charged with rebuilding Stormwind from the ashes of the First and Second Wars. When the kingdom's magnificent white walls and towers were finished, the nobility refused to pay the masons their promised wages. Some senior members received bureaucratic posts to quiet them, but VanCleef refused to abandon the rank-and-file laborers. He led a violent riot out of the city and founded the Defias Brotherhood.

Bazzalan. Bazzalan is a sinister satyr rogue lurking within the volcanic depths of Ragefire Chasm. Alongside Jergosh the Invoker, he commands the dark activities of the Searing Blade cult directly beneath the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. While Thrall works to establish the Orcs' new home across Durotar, ancient evils have found a roost beneath his feet. Bazzalan, a cunning satyr rogue, has allied with the Searing Blade cult inside the winding lava caverns of Ragefire Chasm. Swift and lethal with twin blades, he serves as one of the cult's primary field commanders.

Beached Sea Creature. Along the fog-draped strand of Mist's Edge lies the massive carcass of a sea thresher, far larger than any native to Darkshore's shallows. While local murlocs pick through the carrion, naturalists in Auberdine seek bone samples to understand why such colossal deep-sea beasts are beaching themselves along the coast. The Mist's Edge coastline is no stranger to shipwrecks and tide-washed debris, but the sudden appearance of enormous thresher remains is troubling. The creature dwarfs typical local wildlife, pointing to depths far beyond the calm waters of the Veiled Sea. Although coastal murlocs eagerly swarm and feast on the corpse, they lack the strength or coordination to bring down a leviathan of this scale. The predator succumbed to something else entirely before washing ashore.

Beached Sea Creature. Along the misty coast of Darkshore lies the massive carcass of a sea mammal, abandoned mid-excavation. Scattered tools and an idle wheelbarrow reveal an expedition cut short, leaving the specimen to opportunistic murlocs and the curious eyes of passing travelers. The carcass resting upon the sands of Darkshore is that of an enormous marine mammal, partially gutted and heavily weathered by sea spray. Strewn about its decaying frame are a rusted wheelbarrow and discarded excavation tools, clearly showing that someone attempted an organized study of the beast before being driven off or abandoning the site in haste.

Beached Sea Creature. Along the windswept coast of Darkshore, the half-devoured remains of a massive sea mammal have washed ashore, guarded by opportunistic murlocs. Priestess Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine seeks bone samples from these stranded giants to discern why normally docile ocean beasts are violently dying upon the sands. North along the lonely beaches of Darkshore lies the rotting, half-eaten carcass of a gargantuan sea mammal. Waves crash against its exposed ribs while an unusually vicious tribe of murlocs picks the scavenged bones clean. The sight is both tragic and unnerving, signaling that the ocean's balance is tipping just as severely as the blighted forests inland.

Beached Sea Creature. Along the rocky inlets of the Twilight Shore, the colossal carcass of a giant thresher lies stranded in the surf. Far larger than any known local specimens, its sudden death and stranding are part of a worrying trend of deep-sea anomalies troubling the night elves of Darkshore. The Twilight Shore in southern Darkshore is often strewn with driftwood and sea debris, but this inlet holds something far more striking: the remains of an enormous thresher. Although scavengers and the tides have begun picking it apart, its massive skeleton dwarfs any ordinary predator found in these coastal shallows. It is clearly an outsider to these waters, driven onto the rocks either by unnatural sickness, disorientation, or some deeper disturbance out in the Veiled Sea.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along the misty, surf-battered shores of Darkshore lies the carcass of a massive beached sea turtle, surrounded by scavenging murlocs. Though picked over, viable biological samples can still be recovered from the remains. Naturalists in Auberdine collect such specimens to ship back to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus for formal study. The long coastline of Darkshore frequently catches the casualties of the Great Sea, including massive ancient sea turtles that drift ashore after death or beach themselves in confusion. Once grounded, the carcasses quickly attract scavengers. Hostile Greymist murlocs have established crude camps around this turtle's skeletal frame, carving away flesh and shell. Despite their foraging, viable bone, shell, or tissue samples often remain intact within the wreckage.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along the surf of Darkshore lies the carcass of a massive sea turtle, fitted with a broken carriage and swarming with opportunistic Greymist murlocs. Unlike other dead leviathans on the coast, this creature was harnessed as a beast of burden by the serpent-like naga before dying on the sand. The mist-shrouded shores of Darkshore are troubled by an alarming number of stranded sea giants, but this particular sea turtle tells a far more sinister story. Strapped across the creature's colossal carapace sits a dilapidated carriage, abandoned and decaying in the tide. Rather than dying of sickness or natural exhaustion like other beached creatures, this giant was pressed into service and driven onto the coast by intelligent handlers.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along the northern shores of Darkshore lies the massive skeletal carcass of a beached sea turtle, curiously untouched by the local Greymist murlocs. A sample of its remains is gathered and delivered to Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine on behalf of the Temple of the Moon. Naturalists and priestesses seek to uncover why these great oceanic creatures are washing ashore and why even scavengers seem reluctant to approach. The northern coastline of Darkshore is thick with Greymist murlocs, creatures known to aggressively scavenge anything of nutritive value that washes up from the Veiled Sea. Yet this enormous turtle skeleton lies largely undisturbed. Whether the murlocs simply overlooked the bounty or actively avoided the remains for an unseen reason remains a troubling puzzle for those studying the beach's ecology.

Beached Sea Turtle. This beached sea turtle carcass along the Darkshore coastline carries a broken carriage and a box inscribed with strange runes. Unlike other naturally stranded marine life, this creature appears to have been slain while serving as a beast of burden. The Darkshore coast is littered with the bones of ancient sea creatures, but this turtle skeleton tells a distinctly artificial tale. Strapped across its massive shell are the splintered remnants of a buckled carriage. The creature did not die of sickness or disorientation like others washed ashore; it was driven onto the rocks while hauling cargo. In the wreckage of the carriage rests a container decorated with unfamiliar, serpent-like carvings, left behind amidst the scavengers who claimed the rotting shell.

Beached Sea Turtle. Along the wind-battered coast of Darkshore, the bleached bones of giant sea turtles wash ashore with unsettling frequency. Investigating these tragic strandings provides Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde in Auberdine with specimens to study why Kalimdor's marine life is dying out. The mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore is strewn with the remains of great leviathans and majestic sea turtles. Many of these ancient reptiles have drifted onto the shoals or hauled themselves onto the sand to perish. Greymist murlocs frequently swarm the massive carcasses, picking the flesh down to the shell and bone while establishing crude camps around the carrion.

Bear's Head. Bear's Head is a secluded mountainous stretch along the southeastern cliffs of Azshara. Named for the resident Timbermaw furbolgs whose settlements dot the rugged high ground, it serves as an outpost linked to their larger homes farther north while lying directly beneath the cliffside sanctum of Archmage Xylem. Tucked away in southeastern Azshara, Bear's Head takes its name from the encampments of uncorrupted Timbermaw furbolgs established upon its heights. These rustic settlements act as outlying camps tied to the major furbolg dens of Ursolan and Timbermaw Hold to the north. Perched atop the looming cliffs directly above the area sits Xylem's Tower, an eccentric sanctuary where Archmage Xylem and his small retinue of apprentices conduct arcane studies in quiet isolation from the rest of the troubled coastline.

Beat Bartleby. In Stormwind, Bartleby guards the mug a young warrior must claim. The instructors send recruits to face him in a bare-knuckle fight and earn the vessel for their training. Stormwind's warrior instructors expect recruits to face combat without excuses or grand ceremony. As part of their formal training, young warriors must retrieve a particular mug from Bartleby, a notorious drunkard who lounges in the city. He scoffs at polite requests and swears no one will take his prized drinkware without prying it from his cold, dead fingers. For a fledgling warrior, words soon give way to a fistfight.

Becoming a Parent. Agnar Beastamer in the Hinterlands has found the egg much further along than expected, and wants a word with you about it. Agnar Beastamer was not prepared for how ready the egg turned out to be. Speak with Agnar in the Hinterlands, where you have been bringing food for the hatchling.

text.enUS: Beer Basted Boar Ribs. Ragnar Thunderbrew of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos needs fresh crag boar ribs and a mug of Rhapsody Malt to feed his hungry tavern patrons. With his regular meat supplier away fighting in the King's Army, Ragnar relies on passing travelers to keep his famed ribs on the menu. The Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos is famous for hearty dwarven ale and hearty tavern fare. Chief among its offerings are the legendary Beer Basted Boar Ribs. However, tavern keeper Ragnar Thunderbrew finds himself in a bind: the local hunter who usually kept the pantry stocked with fresh meat recently enlisted in the King's Army to reinforce the Alliance front, leaving Ragnar with plenty of eager customers and completely empty larders.

Beezil's Wreck. Beezil's Wreck marks the crash site of an unfortunate goblin zeppelin deep within the quagmires of Dustwallow Marsh. Resting east of Tabetha's Farm, the shattered vessel's cargo holds scattered supplies and volatile engineering components that attract scavengers. Hidden away in the humid muck east of Tabetha's Farm lies the splintered skeleton of a goblin zeppelin known as Beezil's Wreck. The craft was hauling cargo southward across Kalimdor before suffering a disastrous plunge into the swamp. While the wreckage still smolders amid tangled reeds, its eccentric captain, Beezil, has seemingly vanished from the marsh, leaving behind scattered crates and ticking machinery to slowly rot in the brine.

Beggar's Haunt. Beggar's Haunt is an abandoned Stormwind scout tower perched on a hillside in northeastern Duskwood, near the mountain road to Deadwind Pass. While originally built to keep watch over the kingdom's eastern borders, it has become an outpost for Forsaken infiltrators deep within Alliance territory. Perched above the foggy hills east of Manor Mistmantle, Beggar's Haunt was once an active observation post manned by the Stormwind Guard to secure the eastern approaches to the realm. As the region fell into the gloom of modern Duskwood and kingdom patrols withdrew to Darkshire, the stone tower was abandoned to the elements. Today, its commanding vantage point serves a far more sinister purpose: agents of the Forsaken, including members of the Royal Apothecary Society and Deathstalkers, use the ruined stronghold to conduct research and monitor the region under the Alliance's nose.

Beginnings. Beginnings is a rite of passage for fledgling Alliance warlocks starting in Dun Morogh. Under the begrudging tutelage of Alamar Grimm, novices are dispatched to harvest magical feather charms from nearby Frostmane troll novices to prove their competence before mastering the art of summoning an imp. Within the safe haven of Anvilmar, dark magic is not openly celebrated, but it is tolerated out of necessity. Alamar Grimm, an established warlock, conducts his occult research in relative discretion. When new practitioners show raw promise, Grimm is asked by unnamed parties who have taken an interest in the recruit to step away from his studies and assess the recruits personally.

Beldin Steelgrill. Beldin Steelgrill is a renowned dwarven engineer and the master technician operating Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Widely regarded as one of the finest siege engine mechanics in Khaz Modan, he oversees the maintenance of the Ironforge military's heavy armor and treaded warmachines. Keeping those massive contraptions running requires an endless supply of high-grade specialized tools. Situated just down the road from Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot serves as the primary proving ground and service station for dwarven steam tanks and siege engines. Beldin Steelgrill stands as its chief technician, celebrated far and wide for his unmatched expertise in repairing and tuning armored war wagons. Taming heavy metal and rumbling boilers is unforgiving work, and Beldin burns through gear rapidly. His constant demand for heavy wrenches, cutters, and precision instruments frequently pushes local ironworkers to their limits just to keep his workbench supplied.

Berard's Journal. Berard's Journal is a collection of research notes penned by Apothecary Berard before he fell victim to Archmage Arugal's curse. Left behind in Pyrewood Village, the book documents Berard's study of an ancient plague that once wiped out the aquatic life of Lake Lordamere, making it highly valuable to the Royal Apothecary Society. Before Archmage Arugal unleashed his shadow magic across Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Berard was considered one of the Royal Apothecary Society's most promising minds. Stationed in Pyrewood Village, he focused his work on an ancient, virulent blight that had eradicated all aquatic life within Lake Lordamere centuries prior. When Arugal's curse gripped the settlement, Berard's mind was shattered, turning him into another mindless thrall. His detailed field notes remained behind on a bookshelf in his quarters at the Pyrewood Village Inn.

Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a Horde quest directed by Shadow Priest Allister from the Sepulcher. Agents of the Forsaken have caught wind of a hidden conclave of Scourge massing inside a secluded cave tucked into the southern Silverpine hills, aiming to strike them down before an offensive can begin. Word reached Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher that mindless servants of the Lich King were massing deep within southern Silverpine Forest. Left unchecked, these Scourge forces posed an immediate threat to Forsaken operations throughout the region. Rather than waiting for the assault to land, Allister directs scouts to take the initiative and eliminate the gathering horde inside their secluded lair before they can mobilize.

Beren's Peril. Beren's Peril is a secluded mountain cavern tucked in the rocky hills southwest of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an entrenched redoubt for rogue Scourge loyalists serving the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, plotting against the nearby Forsaken. Tucked away high in the crags southwest of Ambermill, Beren's Peril consists of a shadowed cave and winding mountain path hidden from the main roadway. Following the devastation of the Third War, rogue Scourge undead under the command of the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw fortified this enclave. Rather than bowing to the Dark Lady or retreating north, Ravenclaw's thralls—regents, guardians, and drudgers—gathered here in secret to muster an assault against the Forsaken base at the Sepulcher. Their presence was uncovered by Forsaken scouts, turning the quiet cliffside into an active warzone for Horde operatives sent to eliminate the threat before an attack could materialize.

Bernice's Necklace. At Stonefield Farm in Elwynn Forest, Bernice keeps her late husband's necklace close. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace once belonged to her late husband, a veteran of Stormwind's military campaigns. He carried it into battle as a charm for good fortune. Bernice says tragedy came only during his final campaign, the one expedition when he forgot to bring it. Since his death, the keepsake has remained among her most cherished possessions at Stonefield Farm.

Besseleth's Fang. Besseleth's Fang is the massive venomous tooth harvested from the giant spider Besseleth in Sishir Canyon. Carried as proof of her demise, it represents the removal of a deadly threat stalking the trails of Stonetalon Mountains. Sishir Canyon has long been infested by aggressive arachnids, but none strike more terror into travelers than Besseleth. Growing to monstrous proportions, she and her brood turned the gorge into a death trap for wanderers navigating the Webwinder Path at night. The fang itself measures nearly two feet in length and drips with potent venom, making it an unmistakable signature of the broodmother's slaughter. Presenting this grisly trophy brings relief to local defenders who have suffered her venomous strikes.

Bethor Iceshard. Bethor Iceshard is a powerful Forsaken mage based in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Presiding over the arcane and shadow practitioners within the Temple of the Damned, he commands considerable authority in Sylvanas's realm. Beneath his chilly demeanor lies a past entwined with old friends torn apart by the Scourge. Standing within the Temple of the Damned, Bethor Iceshard oversees the practitioners of the arcane arts and shadow magic in the Undercity. Respected and feared for his intellect and icy resolve, Bethor wields sufficient political and magical weight to give direct instructions to provincial magistrates across Lordaeron. He directs agents of the Forsaken to secure valuable grimoires, investigate arcane anomalies, and stamp out rival powers that threaten the Undercity's dominion.

Bethor's Scroll. Bethor's Scroll contains magical incantations scribed by Bethor Iceshard to counter the dark sorcery of his former colleague, Thule Ravenclaw. Created to aid Apothecary Renferrel in brewing a protective draught, the scroll is vital for surviving the Scourge necromancy guarding Fenris Isle.

Betrayal from Within. Betrayal from Within is a task offered by Mangletooth, an imprisoned quilboar held in a cage at Camp Taurajo. Spurned and left for dead by his own kin, Mangletooth seeks bloody vengeance against the trio of Razormane warlords who emerged from Razorfen Kraul to organize assaults across the Barrens. Languishing in captivity beneath the sun at Camp Taurajo, the quilboar Mangletooth harbors no remaining loyalty toward his Razormane kin. Left behind in defeat and facing certain execution, his only surviving ambition is vengeance against the leaders who abandoned him. To achieve this, he offers Horde travelers vital intelligence on the true architects behind the ruthless raids tormenting the plains.

Betrayal from Within. Betrayal from Within is a Horde quest concluding the hunt for the leader behind aggressive Razormane raids in the central Barrens. By presenting Lok Orcbane's severed head to Thork at the Crossroads, players demonstrate that the quilboar's fiercest tactician has finally fallen. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo, the captured Razormane quilboar Mangletooth reveals that Lok Orcbane directs the vicious quilboar assaults against Horde caravans. Once the chieftain is slain deep in the southern thorn mazes, Mangletooth hands over Lok's skull, amused that the orcs will reap the benefits of internal tribal betrayal without ever guessing a captive quilboar aided them.

Big Game Hunter. Having proven skill across Stranglethorn Vale by hunting the region's deadliest predators, Hemet Nesingwary offers a final supreme challenge. The famed marksman asks for the head of King Bangalash, a great white tiger and the very reason Hemet is in the jungle at all. After completing the trials set by the expedition's huntsmen—slaying Sin'Dall, Bhag'thera, and Tethis—Hemet Nesingwary acknowledges your martial skill. According to the veteran marksman, who compares your prowess to the finest displays seen from Lordaeron's battlefields to the jungle depths, only one hunt remains to prove your abilities unmatched: felling King Bangalash, the grand white tiger that serves as the expedition leader's true target.

Billy Maclure. At Maclure Vineyards, Billy Maclure's pranks stir trouble between two neighboring farms. The young human boy dodges chores and plays at the feud between his family and the Stonefields, but fresh pastries can win his cooperation. Billy Maclure spends his days outside the barn at Maclure Vineyards, near farmer Gerard Tiller. He grows up among the grapevines in southern Elwynn Forest, often dodging chores and roaming the meadows. The Maclures and Stonefields have long been hostile toward each other. Billy treats their feud as a chance for pranks and petty theft.

Bingles Blastenheimer. Bingles Blastenheimer is an eccentric gnomish aviator stranded on the southeastern shores of the Loch in Loch Modan. Having crash-landed his experimental flying machine, he finds himself marooned amidst local troggs and beasts, desperate to salvage his precious tools and components. Like many ambitious gnomish engineers, Bingles Blastenheimer took to the skies in a customized flying craft, only to discover that coming down safely is far more difficult than lifting off. After his gyrocopter malfunctioned and crashed into the southeastern shores of the Loch, Bingles survived the impact intact, but his machine shattered into scattered parts. Stranded far from Ironforge, he remains huddled near the wreckage, guarded against hungry crocolisks and hostile troggs while pleading with passing travelers to recover the tools and Blastencapper explosives that troggs from a nearby island stole from him.

Bingles' Blastencapper. Bingles' Blastencapper is a specialized explosive device designed by the gnome pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when his gyrocopter plunged into the Loch, it was stolen by local troggs, endangering Bingles' plans to support the liberation of Gnomeregan. Bingles' Blastencapper represents the peak of pilot Bingles Blastenheimer's personal ordnance. Built to deliver decisive aerial strikes against the troggs and leper gnomes overruning Gnomeregan, the explosive was aboard his gyrocopter when mechanical failure sent him plummeting into the waters of the Loch. While Bingles survived, troggs infesting the lake's northern islands pillaged his wreckage and dragged the volatile weapon back to their camps.

Bingles' Hammer. Bingles' Hammer is an engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, an eccentric gnome aviator stranded in Loch Modan. After crashing his flying machine into the Loch, hostile troggs scavenged the hammer along with his other specialized gear. Bingles needs it recovered so he can repair his aircraft and aid the war effort to liberate Gnomeregan. When pilot Bingles Blastenheimer plunged into the waters of the Loch, his survival was only the first of his troubles. Troggs inhabiting the freshwater islands quickly raided the crash site, looting his specialized toolkit and high-potency explosives. Among the pilfered gear was his hammer, an indispensable implement for repairing the dented airframe and recalibrating the gyrocopter's mechanical assemblies. Without this essential tool and the rest of his equipment, Bingles remains thoroughly grounded, unable to fly support runs for the gnome liberation forces struggling to reclaim Gnomeregan.

Bingles' Missing Supplies. After crash-landing his gyrocopter into the waters of the Loch, the eccentric gnome engineer Bingles Blastenheimer was ambushed by local troggs who made off with his essential gear. Stranded on the lake's southeastern shore, he needs his stolen wrench, screwdriver, hammer, and customized Blastencapper explosives recovered so he can repair his craft and rejoin the fight for Gnomeregan. Bingles Blastenheimer was piloting his gyrocopter over Loch Modan when an unexpected crash sent him plummeting directly into the cold waters of the Loch. Surviving the impact was fortunate enough, but dragging himself ashore proved to be only half the ordeal. The troggs infesting the lake's central islands took immediate advantage of his predicament, swarming the dazed pilot and looting his most valuable belongings.

Bingles' Screwdriver. Bingles' Screwdriver is an essential engineering tool belonging to Bingles Blastenheimer, a gnome pilot who crashed his gyrocopter into the waters of Loch Modan. Following the crash, native troggs plundered the wreckage, scattering Bingles' tool buckets and specialized gear across the loch's northern islands. When Bingles Blastenheimer plummeted into the Loch, he lost more than his flying machine—he lost the specialized equipment needed to repair it. Among the scattered gear was his trusty screwdriver, packed away inside one of several tool buckets snatched up by opportunistic troggs inhabiting the nearby isles. For an engineer stranded in the wilderness, fine adjustment tools like this screwdriver are irreplaceable, especially when assembling delicate gyrocopter mechanisms or handling volatile armaments.

Bingles' Wrench. Bingles' Wrench is a vital piece of gnomish engineering gear belonging to the pilot Bingles Blastenheimer. Lost when Bingles crash-landed his flying machine into the Loch, it was hauled off by the local troggs alongside the rest of his toolkit. After Bingles Blastenheimer crashed his gyrocopter into the placid waters of the Loch, his survival quickly turned into an ordeal. Troggs inhabiting the small northern islands raided the crash site, looting his specialized supplies and scattering his tools into various buckets across their camps. Bingles' Wrench is one of three critical hand tools needed alongside his high-yield Blastencapper explosives. Without it, Bingles has no hope of repairing his downed gyrocopter, stalling his planned aerial offensive to aid the exiled gnomes fighting to reclaim Gnomeregan.

Bink. Bink is a gnome mage trainer who resides within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. Quick-witted and enthusiastic, she guides aspiring spellcasters through the intricacies of the arcane arts and connects them with prominent wizards across the Alliance. Located in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, Bink stands among the gathered scholars, priests, and arcanists in the Hall of Mysteries. Like many gnomes driven from Gnomeregan, she has adapted to life within the dwarven mountain stronghold, offering her keen intellect and knowledge of arcane craft to those learning the path of the mage. She is well connected to wizards across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, regularly pointing promising apprentices toward greater mentors such as High Sorcerer Andromath in Stormwind or Tabetha in Dustwallow Marsh.

Bishop DeLavey. In Stormwind Keep, Bishop DeLavey hears the court's quiet concerns. He represents the Church of the Holy Light in the Petitioner's Chamber, where matters of faith and state meet. Bishop DeLavey advises Stormwind's court from within the keep. While Archbishop Benedictus tends to the Cathedral of Light, DeLavey lives among the nobility and petitioners. He brings spiritual counsel to the court while reckoning with the kingdom's politics. His place there lets him hear whispered rumors and delicate grievances before they reach Highlord Bolvar Fordragon or the young King Anduin.

Bitter Reaches. The Bitter Reaches is a rugged, windswept wilderness in northeastern Azshara. Largely untouched by civilization, the rugged cliffs are prowled by predatory beasts and massive mountain giants. Occupying the northeastern cliffs of Azshara, the Bitter Reaches remains a stark and untamed stretch of rocky terrain overlooking the Great Sea. Flocks of feral hippogryphs and two-headed chimaeras nest amidst the heights, while acidic oozes seep through the cold ground. Along the high northern ridges, colossal mountain giants have claimed the slopes as their own, driving away lesser creatures and turning the frozen approaches into a perilous hazard for any solitary traveler.

Bitter Rivals. Bitter Rivals is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh born from the fierce competition between two proud dwarven brewing families. Marleth Barleybrew sends an adventurer to infiltrate the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos and tamper with their rival's stock. Few things in Khaz Modan stir passions as quickly as a pint of ale. The Barleybrews have long bristled under the shadow of the famed Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. While Marleth Barleybrew begrudgingly concedes that Thunderbrew craft is respectable, she cannot stomach the notion that it is the only renowned vintage in Dun Morogh. To shake up the local palate, she devises a plan to swap a cask of Thunder Ale with her own fiery concoction, Barleybrew Scalder.

Black Channel Marsh. Black Channel Marsh is a murky mire situated in the southwestern Wetlands, flanking the main road leading toward Menethil Harbor. Infested with aggressive raptors, the soggy terrain poses an immediate threat to unwary travelers and supply couriers traversing the coastal lowlands. Stretching across the swampy low ground southwest of the main thoroughfare, Black Channel Marsh is infamous among caravan drivers and couriers heading to Menethil Harbor. While the raised road offers the illusion of safety, the stagnant channels and thick reeds are home to territorial raptor packs. Hungry beasts frequently stray directly into traffic, ambushing fresh recruits and weary wayfarers who stray even a pace or two from the beaten path.
