text.enUS: Black Claw Stout. Beneath Stormwind, Zardeth of the Black Claw prepares a drink for Lord Wishock. The stout is delivered as an ordinary tavern beverage.

Black Feather Quill. The Black Feather Quill is a sacred night elf relic used by the Druids of the Talon during their rites of hibernation and awakening. Stored within a dedicated chest in the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, it is one of several vital focuses needed to safely call slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druidism relies on deeply attuned sacred items to navigate the threshold between the waking world and the Emerald Dream. The Black Feather Quill, along with the Raven Claw Talisman, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting, forms the core set of ritual items required to break the delicate hibernation of the Druids of the Talon. Without these focuses, a slumbering druid risks remaining trapped within the Dream indefinitely, unable to rejoin their waking body.

Black dragonflight. Once the stalwart Earth-Warders charged by the titans to safeguard Azeroth's deep subterranean realms, the black dragonflight fell to madness and treachery. Corrupted by the insidious whispers of the imprisoned Old Gods, their leader Neltharion became Deathwing, turning his brood into one of the most destructive and hated forces on the planet. Today, their surviving scions weave plots from the shadows and wage covert wars against mortal kingdoms. Long ago, the Titan Khaz'goroth bestowed his blessing upon Neltharion, creating the black dragonflight to watch over the earth, raise mountains, and guard Azeroth's deep caverns. For ages, they stood alongside the other flights as patient, unyielding guardians. Yet their intimate bond with the world's subterranean foundations proved their undoing. Dwelling within the deepest hollows, they lay dangerously close to the sunken prisons of the Old Gods. Over centuries, dark whispers eroded the noble Earth-Warder's mind, driving him to madness and twisting his entire brood into vicious instruments of ruin.

Blackchar Cave. Blackchar Cave is a mysterious, sealed-off cavern tucked into the southwestern crags of Searing Gorge, close to the base of Blackrock Mountain. Its entrance is choked with impassable rubble and rock. Tucked away against the scorching crags near the approaches to Blackrock Mountain, Blackchar Cave presents a solid wall of stone where a deep cavern entrance might once have been. Heavy rubble and scorched slag choke the opening, preventing anyone from exploring whatever tunnels lie deeper within the mountain roots. The desolate terrain around it is scorched by ash and magma, offering little comfort to wanderers.

Blackened Skull. A blackened skull is the darkened cranial remnant of a Darkeye Bonecaster animating in the Agamand Mills. Deathguard Dillinger in Brill demands these grisly trophies as proof of thinning the mindless Scourge forces threatening Tirisfal Glades. These blackened skulls are salvaged from the Darkeye Bonecasters haunting the Agamand Mills. These skeletal spellcasters direct necromantic malice against the living and the Forsaken alike, attempting to entrench a forward base for the Lich King's armies in northern Tirisfal. Presenting their ruined skulls to Deathguard Dillinger serves as tangible evidence that the Scourge's mystical vanguard is being crushed.

Blackfathom Deeps. Blackfathom Deeps is a flooded subterranean temple ruin buried beneath the Zoram Strand along Ashenvale's northwestern coast. Once a glorious house of worship dedicated to the moon goddess Elune, its drowned halls have been overtaken by naga, satyr, and the sinister Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, this complex was a temple dedicated to the goddess Elune, complete with its own moonwell. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the shrine sank beneath the ocean waves, presumed lost forever. Over millennia, receding shorelines and subterranean shifting left its remains partly flooded beneath the cliffs of Ashenvale.

Blackfathom Villainy. Blackfathom Villainy is an Alliance task given by Argent Guard Thaelrid deep within the ruined subterranean temple of Blackfathom Deeps. To halt the horrific sacrifices fueling an ancient horror, heroes are tasked with executing the cult leader Twilight Lord Kelris and bringing proof back to the Argent Dawn in Darnassus. The flooded cavern now known as Blackfathom Deeps was once a pristine subterranean temple dedicated to Elune. That sacred past was shattered when the corruption of an ancient Old God seeped up through the rock, spoiling the temple's Moon Well and releasing Aku'mai, a voracious servant of that primordial darkness. In the wake of this defilement, the Twilight's Hammer cult forged an unholy alliance with local naga, turning holy halls into a den of ritual murder.

Blackfathom Villainy. Blackfathom Villainy is an urgent plea delivered by a dying Argent Dawn crusader trapped inside Blackfathom Deeps. Horde adventurers are charged with putting an end to Twilight Lord Kelris, the cult leader orchestrating horrific blood sacrifices to an ancient monstrosity in the ruins below. Drawn to the subterranean temple along the Ashenvale coast, the Argent Dawn scout Thaelrid discovered horrors far worse than simple naga incursions. Wounded and stripped of strength within the caverns, the night elf realizes he cannot finish his mission alone. Rather than letting his reconnaissance die with him, he turns to any passing Horde champions willing to strike at the dark leadership presiding over the sunken halls.

Blackmoore's Legacy. Gol'dir, freed from the Syndicate, has information for Krusk in Tarren Mill. The Syndicate's leader, Aliden Perenolde, visited Gol'dir and spoke of making slaves of the orcs who stand against him, and brought a girl named Elysa who wore the pendant the Warchief desires. A day or two ago, the head of the Syndicate paid Gol'dir a visit. His name was Aliden Perenolde, and he styled himself lord of the land. He confided that he meant to enslave the orcs who resisted him, just as his father and the despised Blackmoore, his mentor, once planned. Gol'dir sends you to bring this to Krusk in Tarren Mill, and will make his own way after settling his business where he is.

Blackrock Blockade. Blackrock Blockade is an Alliance military task issued by Marshal Marris in Lakeshire. Confronting the encroaching Blackrock orcs east of Lake Everstill, the town guard aims to starve out the invaders and seize their weaponry. While the Blackrock clan has made bold incursions into the Redridge Mountains, their brazen push into Alliance territory has stretched their logistics to a breaking point. Cut off from regular supply trains, their forward war parties are forced to live off the harsh Redridge hills. Marshal Marris recognizes that even ferocious orcs cannot sustain a campaign without steady provisions and steel.

name.ruRU: Награда за головы орков Черной горы

text.enUS: Blackrock Bounty. Blackrock Bounty is a defense contract issued by Guard Howe in Lakeshire on behalf of Magistrate Solomon. With Stormwind failing to dispatch reinforcements, the town pays independent adventurers to cull the elite Blackrock Champions massing in the northern mountains. Striking down these battlefield unit commanders is aimed at disrupting the orc clan's coordinated assault on Redridge. Redridge has long fallen under the sovereign rule of the Kingdom of Stormwind, but the Blackrock clan does not honor human borders. Pouring down through the mountain passes leading from the Burning Steppes, the orcs have established heavily fortified encampments across northern Redridge. With King Varian Wrynn missing and the regency in Stormwind withholding royal soldiers, local leaders like Magistrate Solomon have been forced to put up bounties from the town's dwindling coffers to protect Lakeshire.

name.esES: La amenaza de los Roca Negra

text.enUS: Blackrock Menace. Marshal Marris of Lakeshire tasks adventurers with culling the aggressive Blackrock orcs encroaching upon Redridge. By seizing their battleworn axes, the town's defenders hope to break the siege tightening around the settlement. Lakeshire finds itself hemmed in on multiple fronts, but none pose so dire a threat as the Blackrock orcs spilling over from the fiery Burning Steppes. Having pushed south into Redridge, these veteran raiders have seized strongholds and roam the craggy passes. Their presence keeps the townspeople effectively penned inside the settlement, cutting off trade, foraging, and travel along the northern roads.

Blackrock Mountain. Blackrock Mountain is a massive, active volcano that towers between the Burning Steppes and the Searing Gorge. Borne from the cataclysmic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord, its hollowed depths house ancient dwarven masonry, warring armies, and smoldering horrors. Blackrock Mountain did not exist until the climax of the War of the Three Hammers two and a half centuries ago. Facing annihilation by the united armies of Ironforge and the Wildhammer clan, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan reached into the depths of the earth for a weapon. His reckless spell shattered the dimensional barriers and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The resulting apocalypse tore the Redridge range apart, gouging out the Searing Gorge and Burning Steppes while thrusting a colossal volcano into the sky. Thaurissan perished in the blast, and the surviving Dark Iron clan was bound into eternal servitude to the Firelord, carving their capital, Shadowforge City, deep within the mountain's roots.

Blackrock Pass. Blackrock Pass is a mountain corridor connecting the northern cliffs of Redridge Mountains to the arid wastes of the Burning Steppes. Passing beneath a heavy iron gate, it marks the sudden threshold between the tranquil human heartlands and the dangerous war grounds of the Dark Iron dwarves and the Blackrock orcs. For any weary traveler journeying north on foot, it represents a harsh and perilous frontier. Carved into the jagged spine of the mountains, Blackrock Pass serves as the overland route between Redridge Mountains and the Burning Steppes. A stout iron gate stands along the rocky boundary, demarcating the idyllic forests and lakes of the southern valleys from the volcanic ruin beyond. Crossing this line leaves behind the pastoral lands protected by Lakeshire's beleaguered militia, thrusting travelers into an open wasteland populated by fire elementals, dragonkin, and hostile orc warbands. Few make the crossing on foot unless bound for the shadow of Blackrock Mountain itself.

Blackrock Stronghold. Blackrock Stronghold is a heavily fortified encampment carved into the crags of the northern Burning Steppes, positioned right outside the entrance to Blackrock Mountain. It serves as a major field garrison for the Blackrock orcs and their allies under the Dark Horde banner. Sprawling across the scorched foothills below Blackrock Mountain, the stronghold functions as the primary ground base for the Blackrock clan in the Burning Steppes. Unlike Thrall's Horde, these orcs cling to their warlike legacy, serving Rend Blackhand and the dragonkin who lurk above in the spire.

Blackrock clan. The Blackrock clan is a martial orcish clan renowned for its strict military discipline, unmatched blacksmithing, and central role in the First and Second Wars. Today, the clan is deeply fractured: while some veterans follow Thrall in the New Horde, a vicious and renegade splinter group known as the Dark Horde occupies the upper peaks of Blackrock Mountain under Rend Blackhand. Hailing from Draenor, the Blackrock clan made its name through rigid hierarchy, heavy armor, and mastery over the forge. Under Chieftain Blackhand, they served as the brutal core of the Old Horde during the invasion of Azeroth, laying siege to Stormwind. When Orgrim Doomhammer slew Blackhand to cleanse the Horde of Gul'dan's direct puppet mastery, leadership of both the clan and the Horde remained firmly in Blackrock hands through the grueling campaigns of the Second War.

Blackthorn Ridge. Blackthorn Ridge is a jagged, bramble-choked valley tucked away in the southern reaches of the Barrens, immediately north of Razorfen Kraul. The area crawls with aggressive Razormane quilboar guarding their thorny settlements. High on the ridge above sits the camp of the orc shaman Brine, watching over an unusually pure pool of mountain water. Nestled near the towering burls of Razorfen Kraul, Blackthorn Ridge is dominated by dense thickets of massive, sharp briars. The Razormane quilboar consider these grounds ancestral territory, using the natural barricades to ambush outsiders and stage skirmishes into the southern Barrens. Despite the constant danger, travellers seek out the ridge for the hermit orc shaman Brine, who tends a camp perched above a spring noted across Kalimdor for its remarkable clarity and spiritual purity.

Blackwolf River. Blackwolf River is a waterway flowing out of Cragpool Lake down through Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Once a clean mountain stream, its waters have become thoroughly polluted by the Venture Company's aggressive logging and industrial operations. Descending from Cragpool Lake, the Blackwolf River cuts across the basin of Windshear Crag. What should be a pristine alpine tributary has instead borne the brunt of unchecked goblin enterprise. As the Venture Company clears the surrounding woodlands with heavy machinery and buzzsaws, sludge, oil, and logging waste leach steadily into the current. The despoiled river stands as a vivid example of the commercial plunder threatening Stonetalon's wilderness.

Blackwood Den. Blackwood Den is a corrupted furbolg encampment nestled in the southern reaches of Darkshore near the border of Ashenvale. Once a peaceful dwelling, the cave and surrounding camps have fallen into madness alongside the rest of the Blackwood tribe. A lone night elf scout named Volcor sits trapped within the cavern, awaiting aid from Auberdine. Situated near the southern border where Darkshore meets Ashenvale, Blackwood Den consists of a winding network of crude camps and a rocky cave. The Blackwood furbolgs who dwell here have succumbed to the pervasive corruption gripping the region, turning violently hostile toward outsiders. Deep inside the den's cave, the night elf Volcor remains pinned down and endangered by the aggressive tribe, desperately needing assistance from scouts and travelers dispatched from Auberdine.

Blackwood Lake. Blackwood Lake is a blighted body of water situated in the southern Eastern Plaguelands, teeming with hostile, corrupted elementals. The area is haunted by memories of tragedy and war, watched over by a small frontline camp of the Argent Dawn. Like so much of the Eastweald, Blackwood Lake has been poisoned by the rampant plague of undeath. Diseased and foul water elementals churn beneath the murky surface, attacking anyone who ventures near the shoreline.

Bladefist Bay. Bladefist Bay is the rugged stretch of coast lining eastern Durotar just outside the gates of Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Kargath Bladefist, the bay opens onto the Great Sea, shadowed by craggy bluffs and the nearby southern shores of Azshara. Stretching along the northeastern edge of Durotar, Bladefist Bay opens directly into the vast waters of the Great Sea. Flanked by rocky cliffs and treacherous surf, it lies just east of the Horde capital of Orgrimmar. Directly north, the ancient red cliffs and ruins of Azshara loom across the water, making the bay a vital maritime boundary for Durotar.

Bladeswift the Elder. Elder Bladeswift is an ancestral spirit honored during the Lunar Festival within the night elven capital of Darnassus. Located in the Cenarion Enclave, this ancient figure offers travelers wisdom drawn from the starry heavens above. Seeking his blessing connects adventurers directly to the revered traditions of the Cenarion Circle and the night elven people. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of revered ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom and bestow blessings upon travelers. Bladeswift the Elder stands amidst the serene boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Unlike modern residents preoccupied with the trials of the present, this spectral forebear looks upward to the cosmos, contemplating the mysteries woven into the night sky.

Blanchy. Old Blanchy is the loyal, hard-working mare belonging to Theodore and Verna Furlbrow, currently resting beside their wagon near the Jansen Stead in Westfall. Renowned for her gentle disposition and hefty appetite, she remains a steady companion to her owners amidst the turmoil gripping the countryside. Long before pulling the Furlbrows' wagon through the dust of Westfall, Blanchy worked the Furlbrows' farm in the breadbasket of Stormwind, where she earned a reputation as an exceptionally sweet-tempered, well-behaved mare. Years of heavy labor have worn her down to 'Old Blanchy,' and the arduous journey fleeing troubled homesteads has left her exhausted. Though visibly weary, her appetite remains hearty, and travelers who bring her nourishing handfuls of oats scattered across the surrounding fields are rewarded by Verna with Blanchy's own treasured blanket and feed pouch.

Blessed Arm. In Stormwind, Blessed Arm carries lightforge iron toward a weapon against Morbent Fel. After salvaging the ingots from the wreck of the Flying Osprey in the Wetlands, you bring the precious metal to master dwarven smith Grimand Elmore, who can shape it to face the necromancer. Glorin Steelbrow packs the recovered lightforge iron for Stormwind. The metal is rare, and its power against foul and unholy beings demands a smith who knows how to work it. After the shipment came from the wreck of the Flying Osprey off the Wetlands coast, Glorin knew of only one artisan in the southern kingdoms suited to the task: master weaponsmith Grimand Elmore.

Blind Cazul. Blind Cazul is a transitional step in the Horde warlock trial to bind a succubus. After being directed by the coven leaders in the Cleft of Shadow, an initiate seeks out the sightless warlock Cazul, who points toward an object of intense emotion needed for the ritual. Subjugating a demonic minion requires more than raw willpower; certain creatures of the Twisting Nether must be drawn across the veil by their innate cravings. A succubus, known as a devourer of souls, responds eagerly to mortal longing, sorrow, and unfulfilled desire. Cazul understands this well, recognizing immediately why an aspiring summoner has sought him out.

Blind Hunter. The Blind Hunter is an elusive, albino bat that roosts deep within Razorfen Kraul. Unlike the ordinary bats nesting near the cavern entrances, this rare creature prowls the sunless depths of the quilboar redoubt. Razorfen Kraul is riddled with winding briars and dark subterranean caverns. While common Kraul bats roost nearer to the surface where faint light filters in from the outside world, the Blind Hunter has adapted entirely to the furthest, darkest alcoves of the tangle. Its pale, albino hide and milky gaze are likely the result of generations spent completely isolated from natural sunlight.

Blind Mary. Blind Mary is a tormented banshee haunting an abandoned, ruined farmhouse just southeast of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once a vain and beautiful mortal woman, her violent death and transformation drove her to self-inflicted mutilation in grief over what she had become. Before the shadows fell across Duskwood, Mary was known as a striking mortal woman who took immense pride in her beauty, rarely seen without her treasured looking glass. When the undead swept over the region, Mary was slain along with many of her neighbors. Unlike those who found rest in the earth, her spirit lingered on as an ethereal banshee, condemned to wander the mortal realm in a ghastly, translucent form.

Blisters on The Land. Blisters on The Land is an Alliance quest offered by Rethiel the Greenwarden along the eastern ridges of the Wetlands. Sensing an unnatural sickness stirring the swamp, the lone bog beast warden tasks travelers with culling the diseased Fen Creepers that stalk the waterways. Putting these shambling plant horrors to rest is Rethiel's attempt to break the swamp's rising fever. From its grove amid the marshes, Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the soggy expanse of the Wetlands. The marshes have never been gentle, but recently an unnatural sickness has begun to spread through the mire. Rethiel perceives this affliction as a growing fever in the earth itself, one that causes wild nature to warp into mindless, shambling monstrosities.

Blood Feeders. Blood Feeders is a Horde hunting contract given by Xen'Zilla in the Darkspear settlement of Malaka'jin. The local trolls have found plentiful game along the slopes of Stonetalon, but the scent of their butchered meat has drawn swarms of predatory Deepmoss spiders down into their camps. The trolls who established the frontier outpost of Malaka'jin in southeastern Stonetalon Mountains came seeking good hunting. The craggy slopes proved bountiful, but the meat and game they brought back soon drew the attention of nocturnal predators. Deepmoss spiders, aggressive arachnids native to the crags and canyons to the north, began slipping into the camp under cover of dark, seeking to scavenge their caches or turn the hunters into prey.

Blood Shards of Agamaggan. Mangletooth, a captive Razormane quilboar held at Camp Taurajo, reveals the sacred origin of the blood shards scattered throughout the Barrens. Imbued with the fallen demigod Agamaggan's life essence, these red minerals grant potent ancestral magic to anyone skilled enough to channel them. In exchange for the shards, the spiteful prisoner offers to share the primal boons of his god with the Horde. According to quilboar lore, the blood of the Ancient Boar God, Agamaggan, did not merely cause giant thorn mazes to erupt across the arid plains when he fell ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. His divine blood seeped deep beneath the soil, infusing the subterranean minerals and crystallizing into blood-red stones. The quilboar revere these shards as sacred remnants of their creator, harvesting them from both mineral seams and holy grounds to serve as totems of battle and sorcery.

Blood Tithe. Blood Tithe is a quest initiated by Alvarion Windfield, an ailing Skyborne farmer seeking aid in the settlement of Valanaar. Desperate to protect his livelihood, he recruits adventurers to travel west to his lowland orchard and assist his wife, Aamelia. In the settlement of Valanaar, an injured Skyborne man named Alvarion Windfield desperately searches for capable adventurers. Wracked with visible pain, Alvarion has traveled from his homestead into town to hire fighters who can help save his livelihood. Rather than tasking travelers on the spot, he implores those willing to help to journey westward into the lowlands, where his wife Aamelia maintains their family orchard.

Blood in the Streets. Dalaran's barrier has come down, and turmoil grips the city. With its patrols dealt with, Magus Wordeen Voidglare says there is no better time to slip inside and learn the mages' secrets. You are to carry the key from the internment camp to the city's sewers on its northern edge. After Dalaran Patrols, Magus Wordeen Voidglare says that whatever lowered Dalaran's barrier has thrown the city into turmoil, so now is the time for the Horde to get inside and learn the mages' secrets. You are to take the key from the internment camp and look for the sewers on the city's northern edge, by Lordamere Lake. With luck, the mages saw no need to ward so disagreeable an entrance.

Blood of Innocents. Blood of Innocents is an errand undertaken for Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to harvest sinister alchemical components. Seeking to pacify the encroaching Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes dark ingredients gathered from regional bandits. The Horde faces persistent friction in the Stonetalon Mountains, where the rapacious Venture Company ravages the wilderness without regard for the earth or its inhabitants. Rather than dispatching armies to blunt their axes, Apothecary Lydon proposes an alchemical remedy. His plan involves concocting a paralyzing, pacifying agent designed to sap the mercenaries of their aggression, leaving them weak and docile.

Bloodfeather Belt. A Bloodfeather Belt is a crude leather strap worn by the Bloodfeather harpies infesting northern Teldrassil. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak collects these belts as proof that local nests encroaching on the Oracle Glade have been cleared. The Bloodfeather harpies have nested aggressively in the boughs around the Oracle Glade, threatening the ancient Oracle Tree and choking travel through northern Teldrassil. When a runner carrying reports to Darnassus was ambushed and slain by the flock, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak called on travelers to strike back directly at their nests. Taking the belts from fallen harpies serves as tangible proof that their numbers are being culled, securing the paths so communication with the capital can resume.

Bloodfen Burrow. Bloodfen Burrow is a cavern in southwestern Dustwallow Marsh swarming with vicious raptors. The beasts have claimed the cave and the surrounding clearing, completely overrunning the ruins of a settlement that once tried to survive the wetlands. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Dustwallow Marsh, Bloodfen Burrow serves as the primary den for the region's aggressive Bloodfen raptors. The cave mouth and surrounding hollow crawl with the pack, drawn to the sheltered crevice and the bountiful hunting ground the marsh provides. Just outside the entrance lie scattered debris and splintered remains of an unidentified settlement, serving as a grim reminder of who truly rules the swamp's interior. Travelers also whisper that Cortello, an adventurous buccaneer, left one of his hidden riddle clues somewhere within this deadly den.

Bloodfury Bloodline. Bloodfury Bloodline is a Horde task issued by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat to strike down the leader of the Bloodfury harpies. Culminating Maggran's efforts to cleanse the Charred Vale, the hunt aims to break the flock's ferocious hold over the scarred wilderness. Culling lesser harpies along the edge of the Charred Vale provides only temporary relief for Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder believes that the only lasting way to curb their aggression is to eliminate their matriarch, Bloodfury Ripper. Revering her as something akin to a queen, the flock draws its ruthless coordination and boldness directly from her leadership along the craggy western ridge.

name.itIT: Resti della Squartatrice delle Furie Rosse

text.enUS: Bloodfury Ripper's Remains. Bloodfury Ripper's Remains are the physical proof recovered from the matriarch of the Bloodfury harpies in the Charred Vale. Sought by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat, this trophy confirms the death of the brood's ferocious leader, dealing a decisive blow to the harpy presence threatening the local tauren settlement. The Bloodfury harpies nesting within the scorched ruins of the Charred Vale have long posed a savage threat to the travelers and shamans of the Stonetalon Mountains. While culling their numbers thins the immediate danger, Maggran Earthbinder of Sun Rock Retreat recognizes that true reprieve requires eliminating their leadership. Bloodfury Ripper rules her flock almost as a queen, guiding their territorial aggression. Taking her remains is essential proof of her demise, scattering the remaining harpies into disarray and granting peace of mind to the tauren striving to heal and secure their rugged lands.

Bloodhoof Village. Bloodhoof Village is a central tauren settlement resting along the banks of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Named in honor of the Bloodhoof tribe, it serves as the first major gathering hub for young hunters and braves journeying out from Camp Narache toward Thunder Bluff. Led by Baine Bloodhoof, the village coordinates local defense, trade, and traditional rites across the plains. Situated around the clear waters of Stonebull Lake, Bloodhoof Village is a bustling center of commerce, craft, and ceremony in central Mulgore. Young tauren departing their trials at Camp Narache arrive here to hone their skills before venturing onward to the great mesas of Thunder Bluff. It is also home to the patient breeders who tame wild kodo beasts for travel.

Bloodhoof the Elder. Bloodhoof the Elder is an encounter with one of the venerated ancestral spirits who manifests during the Lunar Festival. Located just outside Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, this honored spirit acknowledges the respect paid by wandering travelers and grants an ancestral token in return. During the celebration of the Lunar Festival, the spirits of great heroes and elders from ages past return to Azeroth. Shrouded in celestial radiance, Elder Bloodhoof appears just north of Bloodhoof Village near the bridge. Approaching these venerated ancestors is an act of honoring past sacrifices, and in exchange, Elder Bloodhoof offers words of encouragement and a sacred Coin of Ancestry.

Bloodied Insignia. Bloodied Insignias are tragic remnants of the fallen defenders of Lordaeron, scattered among the kingdom's blighted ruins. Bearing the old crests of the Alliance, these battered badges represent soldiers whose families fled south to Stormwind during the Third War. When Prince Arthas returned to scour Lordaeron with the Scourge, its grand military was overwhelmed and butchered. Countless soldiers perished defending the Capital City and the surrounding lands, leaving behind few physical traces beyond rusted armor and bloodstained brass. These old Alliance insignias belonged to the men and women who stood their ground against the undead onslaught. Trampled into the soil and rubble of the ruins, each medal is an artifact of the kingdom's final, desperate stand.

Bloodmage Drazial. Bloodmage Drazial is a blood elf practitioner of arcane and blood magic camped in the northern reaches of the Blasted Lands. Alongside his sister Lynnore, he studies the native beasts of the red wastes to craft potent alchemical concoctions for traveling adventurers. Perched near the northern pass where the Swamp of Sorrows gives way to the Blasted Lands, Bloodmage Drazial pursues a peculiar brand of magic. While many high elves shun the forbidden arts or despair over Quel'Thalas, Drazial and his sister Lynnore harness blood magic to harvest power from the harsh environment. The blighted fauna of the wastes—scorpoks, snickerfangs, and blasted boars—show strange, unnatural vigor, which Drazial and Lynnore believe came from the energy released when the Dark Portal opened. By harvesting specific organs and tissues from these creatures, Drazial brews volatile concoctions that grant immense bursts of physical strength, agility, and endurance.

Bloodmage Lynnore. Bloodmage Lynnore is a blood elf practitioner of forbidden blood magic camped with her brother Drazial near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands. She assists adventurers by concocting potent alchemical draughts from the organs of local beasts. Camped near the northern entrance to the Blasted Lands alongside her brother Drazial, Bloodmage Lynnore is one of the exceptionally rare elven practitioners of blood magic found in the Eastern Kingdoms. Unperturbed by the harsh and corrupting landscape of the Blasted Lands, she studies the latent arcane and vital energies coursing through native beasts. Travelers who bring her the brains and gizzards of local fauna find that she can distill these gruesome reagents into specialized elixirs granting profound enhancements to intellect and spirit.

Bloodmage Thalnos. Bloodmage Thalnos is a skeletal spellcaster who haunts the Graveyard wing of the Scarlet Monastery. Who he was in life is not recorded, but the plague of undeath claimed him, and he now lingers deep within the Crusade's holy grounds, hungering for vengeance. No record tells who Thalnos was in life. Whatever his past, the plague of undeath claimed him. Rather than being cleansed or permanently destroyed, he rose as a withered skeleton, still clinging to his fiery magic and arcane mastery, and crying out for vengeance and for more souls.

Bloodscalp Clan Heads. Following the sorting of trophies gathered in the jungle, Nimboya confirms that the missing young troll Yenniku was not among them. To discover the truth of Yenniku's fate, the Darkspear seek to compel answers from the leaders of the rival Bloodscalp tribe. After the earlier hunt proved Yenniku was not among the fallen Bloodscalp trophies, Nimboya looks to higher leadership for answers. The Bloodscalp chief, Gan'zulah, and his witch doctor, Nezzliok the Dire, are enemies of the Darkspear tribe and would never talk willingly. Nimboya means to force the truth from their dead lips, bringing their heads to the cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp to make them talk.

Bloodscalp Ears. Kebok in Booty Bay is losing guards and agents to jungle clashes with the Bloodscalp tribe. Worried about climbing expenses and answering to Baron Revilgaz, he offers coin to any adventurer willing to hunt down the trolls and return with proof of the kill. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Kebok faces a serious operational dilemma. The local trolls in Stranglethorn Vale have been killing his agents in the jungle, and he has lost many of his best guards in skirmishes with them. With the casualties mounting, so too are the costs, leaving him frantic over how to explain them to Baron Revilgaz.

Bloodstone Choker. In Stormwind, the Bloodstone Choker binds a warlock’s ritual to the void. Gakin the Darkbinder once held the bloodstone talisman, until an apprentice stole it and fled to the Defias Brotherhood. Carved from bloodstone, the choker can bridge the mortal world and the twisting shadows of the Twisting Nether. Gakin puts it to use in the crypts beneath the tavern, channeling its magic at the summoning circle to draw a hostile Voidwalker from the void. A warlock must subdue the furious creature in direct combat while wielding the talisman to prove the will to command such a guardian.

Bloodtalon Matriarch. The Bloodtalon Matriarch is the formidable leader of a swift and cunning raptor pack near Sen'jin Village. After proving too dangerous and stubborn to tame as an adult, she must be confronted so her offspring can be raised from the egg as loyal companions for the Darkspear tribe. The Bloodtalon pack is renowned along the coast of Durotar for its remarkable speed and keen cunning. Handlers in Sen'jin Village prize these traits above all else when seeking dependable mounts and companions for the Darkspear tribe. However, full-grown raptors possess stubborn and violent instincts, making adults almost impossible to domesticate once they have adapted to life in the wild.

Bloodtooth Camp. Bloodtooth Camp is an encampment of hostile, corrupted furbolgs tucked into central Ashenvale, situated just west of the Falfarren River. Led by the chieftain Ran Bloodtooth, these once-peaceful creatures have succumbed to dark madness and attack anyone who approaches. The camp is a primary target for Alliance scouts working to cleanse the surrounding woodlands. Nestled southwest of the southern Moonwell and west of the Falfarren River, Bloodtooth Camp serves as a stark reminder of Ashenvale's encroaching decay. The furbolgs living here were once connected to the sacred wilderness of Kalimdor, but a lingering spiritual corruption has consumed their tribe. Under the command of Ran Bloodtooth, they guard their crude settlement with rabid hostility, turning upon travelers and night elven protectors alike.

Bloodvenom Falls. Bloodvenom Falls is a towering, foul waterfall plunging down the corrupted cliffs of northern Felwood. Its toxic flow feeds the Bloodvenom River, spreading demon-spawned rot down the mountains and into downstream lands. Pouring over the bluffs in Felwood, Bloodvenom Falls represents one of the most vivid wounds inflicted upon the ancient forests of Kalimdor. Once a pristine mountain cascade, the waters were warped into a virulent sludge during the Third War by demonic magics and the remnants of the Burning Legion. The falls feed directly into the Bloodvenom River, which weaves through the heart of Felwood. From there, the tainted torrent rushes down the mountain slopes to become the foul Wildbend River in Darkshore, carrying blight far beyond Felwood's blighted borders.

Bloodvenom Post. Bloodvenom Post is a remote Horde settlement perched on the rocky bluffs of western Felwood overlooking Darkshore. Its tauren-style structures and tauren guards provide a foothold in a region infested with demonic taint and corrupted wildlife. Tucked away along the high cliffs above Darkshore, Bloodvenom Post is reached by following the corrupted southern bank of the Bloodvenom River away from Felwood's main thoroughfare. Built with traditional tauren tents, totems, and watch posts, this encampment provides Horde wanderers with a vital base of operations amidst a dying forest. From here, scouts track the encroaching demonic forces, study the spreading corruption of the waters, and attempt to monitor the hostile wildlife mutated by the Burning Legion's lingering power.

Bloodvenom River. The Bloodvenom River is a foul waterway cutting through central Felwood, saturated with the demonic corruption that blighted the ancient forest. Its putrid waters seep downstream across the mountains into Darkshore, transforming into the tainted Wildbend River. Running through the corrupted heart of Felwood, the Bloodvenom River serves as an open conduit of the land's spiritual and physical decay. Its banks are thick with vile oozes, mutated beasts, and foul run-off left in the wake of the Burning Legion's invasion. The corruption within the channel is potent enough to taint lands far beyond Felwood itself, flowing westward down into the coastal forests of Darkshore as the Wildbend River.

Bloody Bone Necklaces. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp has his own agenda in Stranglethorn Vale beyond assisting Nimboya. He seeks to weaken the rival Bloodscalp tribe by gathering trophies from their warriors. Though Kin'weelay arrived in the jungle outpost of Grom'gol Base Camp to help Nimboya, he maintains private purposes of his own. The Bloodscalp trolls dwelling to the north are enemies of the Darkspears. Kin'weelay believes that claiming personal trophies from fallen foes bestows spiritual power over them, asking travelers to hunt Bloodscalp warriors and take the bloody bone necklaces they wear around their necks.

Bluefen. Bluefen is a soggy marshland nestled in northern Dustwallow Marsh just east of Brackenwall Village. Crawling with aggressive wetland predators, the mire has also become a staging ground for covert Theramore Infiltrators keeping watch on local Horde movements. Situated just east of the Stonemaul ogres of Brackenwall Village, Bluefen embodies the untamed hazards of Dustwallow Marsh. The humid swampland teems with predatory beasts, including raptors, giant spiders, carrion-feeding birds, and lurking crocolisks. Beyond natural predators, travelers must contend with Theramore Infiltrators who skulk through the murky terrain to spy on the Horde and project human influence deeper into the swamp.

Bluegill Marsh. Bluegill Marsh is a sodden mire in the western Wetlands that serves as the sprawling settlement for the hostile Bluegill murloc tribe. The waterways and huts are fiercely guarded by these aquatic humanoids under the rule of the brute known as Gobbler. Travelers heading through the western fens must navigate carefully to avoid being surrounded in the shallows. Situated amidst the boggy flats of the western Wetlands, Bluegill Marsh is thick with mud, reeds, and the squawking war cries of its resident murlocs. The Bluegill tribe has erected crude primitive camps throughout the stagnant water, claiming this territory as their own. Unlike more isolated beasts of the swamp, these murlocs live and hunt in tightly knit packs. Wary wanderers and scouts from Menethil Harbor know that wading into their territory invites swift ambushes from every direction, especially with the formidable chieftain Gobbler prowling the murky shallows.

Blueleaf Tuber. Blueleaf Tubers are exceptionally rare root vegetables that grow concealed beneath the thorny terrain of Razorfen Kraul. Prized across the world as an exotic culinary delicacy, they are almost impossible to locate with the naked eye. Though native to the Barrens, Blueleaf Tubers grow only in the subterranean depths beneath Razorfen Kraul. Concealed beneath the dense root systems and quilboar briars, they remain hidden to casual foragers. Despite their harsh growing conditions, they fetch an exorbitant price among wealthy gourmands and traders worldwide who savor their unique flavor.

Blueleaf Tubers. Blueleaf Tubers is a retrieval contract commissioned by the goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Seeking to profit from a rare subterranean delicacy, Mizzyrix equips adventurers with trained snufflenose gophers to locate and dig up the tubers buried inside the thorned depths of Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted across the world as a rare and lavish culinary delicacy. Despite their high value, harvesting them is notoriously difficult because they do not grow in open fields or standard wild groves. Instead, they are found almost exclusively deep in the sunless earth beneath the southern Barrens, tangled among the labyrinthine roots of Razorfen Kraul.

Bluff Runner Windstrider. Bluff Runner Windstrider is a wandering tauren messenger roaming the mesas of Thunder Bluff. He carries urgent dispatches across the city, directing Horde adventurers toward distant frontiers like Ashenvale, Feralas, and the Plaguelands. Thunder Bluff's soaring plateaus require swift feet to keep its leaders and visitors informed, and Bluff Runner Windstrider fills that vital role. Continually jogging the rope bridges and pathways of the tauren capital, he acts as a town crier and dispatch runner. When key outposts across Kalimdor or the Eastern Kingdoms require reinforcements, Windstrider flags down passing champions to carry word and take up the call to arms.

Boat Wreckage. Beside a wrecked row boat in the water you find a well-cared-for knife in the mud. Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold wants any clue you find brought back, and a feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water. Feeling along the mud near the wrecked boat, your fingertips brush the grip of a knife that looks well cared for. Whoever was on the boat may have lost it, and the large chunk missing from the boat might have a part in the loss. You take the knife, recalling that Ginro Hearthkindle in Feathermoon Stronghold asked you to bring any clue you found back to him, yet the feeling creeps over you that something else shares the water.

Body and Heart. Body and Heart is the culminating trial in a young night elf druid's initiation into the path of the claw. Instructed by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, an initiate must travel into the darkshore wilderness, summon the moonkin guardian Lunaclaw, and prove they possess both inner resilience and martial strength before claiming the form of the bear. Night elf druid initiates are directed by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus to venture east of the coastal settlement of Auberdine. There, tucked inside a natural cavern inhabited by wild moonkin, sits an ancient Moonkin Stone. By anointing this sacred monolith with Cenarion Moondust, the initiate rouses Lunaclaw, the ancient defender of the stone, who will challenge any claimant wishing to inherit the sacred strength of the claw.

Body and Heart. Body and Heart is the culminating trial for young tauren druids seeking to master Bear Form. Dispatched by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate must travel to the border of Mulgore and the Barrens to summon and best Lunaclaw at the Moonkin Stone. To truly follow the path of the Druid of the Claw, tauren initiates must unite spiritual conviction with physical resilience. After communion with the Great Bear Spirit in Moonglade, a druid's training is put to an active test. Turak Runetotem, the elder druid trainer atop the Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff, bestows Cenarion Lunardust upon worthy aspirants, charging them to seek out a sacred stone resting near the arid frontier where Mulgore meets the Barrens.

Bodyguard for Hire. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally lead their kodo past the Kolkar centaur village, yet they stop whenever the centaur war drums are heard. Cork asks you to protect the caravan past the Kolkar village, and payment is waiting with Smeed Scrabblescrew, a bit down the road. Cork Gizelton and Rigger would normally take their kodo straight past the Kolkar centaur. Now and then the centaur war drums are heard, and the caravan stops, because dead traders make no profit. Cork asks you to guard the caravan past the Kolkar village, a short distance, and keep it in one piece. The caravan waits north of the Kolkar Village and southeast of Thunder Axe Fortress.

Bolgan's Hole. Bolgan's Hole is a subterranean cavern nestled in the southern cliffs of Gelkis Village in Desolace. It serves as the inner sanctum of the Gelkis centaur clan, housing their highest chieftains and sacred earth relics. Carved deep into the craggy bluffs overlooking the Gelkis encampment, Bolgan's Hole functions as the command center for the tribe. It is here that the ruling khan holds court, surrounded by veteran guards and the tribe's most influential shamans. The cavern offers natural fortification against rival clans, most notably the bloodthirsty Magram centaur to the east.

Bolvar Fordragon. Stormwind’s crown and armies rest with Bolvar Fordragon while King Varian is missing. As Regent and Supreme Commander of Stormwind’s armed forces, he stands beside young King Anduin in Stormwind Keep and tries to hold the kingdom together. Domestic troubles grow, while Lady Katrana Prestor’s counsel often delays his military decisions. King Varian vanished on the way to a peace summit on Theramore Isle, leaving Stormwind in political disarray. Ten-year-old Prince Anduin was crowned to preserve continuity, while Highlord Bolvar Fordragon took up the work of ruling as Regent. A venerated paladin devoted to the crown, Bolvar now faces a kingdom under strain. Stormwind’s soldiers are spread thin across Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood. Lady Katrana Prestor’s dismissive counsel adds to the burden, repeatedly blocking him from sending royal troops to towns on the frontier.

Bone Collector. At Kormek's Hut in Desolace, the goblin Bibbly F'utzbuckle is certain that kodo bones are about to transform the world. Ten of them are wanted from the Kodo Graveyard, south of the hut, and something is promised in return. Bibbly insists the hut is sitting on a goldmine. Customers make furniture, musical instruments and even blasting powder from kodo bones. Bibbly sends you south to the Kodo Graveyard to bring back ten of them, with something promised in return.

Bones of Grakkarond. The Bones of Grakkarond are the skeletal remains of a massive bronze dragon lying bleached under the sun of central Silithus. Slain during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands, this fallen wyrm serves as a grim monument held sacred by the qiraji's Anubisath sentinels. Sprawled across the windswept dunes of central Silithus lies the colossal ribcage and skull of Grakkarond, a bronze dragon who met his demise during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands. In that apocalyptic clash a millennium ago, the great dragon was struck down by Ossirian the Unscarred, an Anubisath warrior elevated by the dark powers of the city-kingdom. To the Anubisath, this battlefield trophy is a sacred testament to their might over the dragonflights, left untouched where he fell.

Book Inventory. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton is frustrated by misplaced and missing tomes. He asks young adventurers to find Daniel, his daydreaming assistant, and take stock of the library archives, but Daniel's thoughts keep wandering to local tradeskills, making a straight answer hard to get. Northshire Abbey preserves old scholarly works, spiritual writings, and historical records that survived the First War in the Kingdom of Stormwind. Brother Paxton, a meticulous monk, takes great pride in the collection. Lately, books have gone missing from the shelves, and Paxton needs a clear inventory to learn how widespread the loss is. He has little patience to chase after his daydreaming helper.

Book Return. Book Return is an Elwynn Forest quest directing adventurers to recover Brother Paxton's lost reading materials from the infested depths of Fargodeep Mine. Chief among the missing volumes is 'Fun with Elementals,' a beginner's guide that risks granting the mine's kobolds dangerous conjuration abilities if left in their clutches. While investigating the growing kobold menace within Fargodeep Mine, Marshal Dughan tasks adventurers with recovering missing volumes belonging to Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey. Among the scattered texts lost in the dim subterranean tunnels is a particularly volatile primer titled 'Fun with Elementals.' Paxton fears that the instructions within are so accessible that even the mine's crude kobold squatters could decipher them and conjure an elemental creature in the depths.

text.enUS: Book from Sven's Farm. The Book from Sven's Farm is a dirt-stained, untitled journal unearthed from the ruins of Sven Yorgen's ransacked homestead in Duskwood. Its fragmented entries reveal that an unknown onlooker witnessed the massacre of Sven's family, sparking a relentless hunt across the shadowed woods. Buried in a loose dirt mound amid the charred remains of Sven's farm in southern Duskwood, this unassuming, weather-damaged volume contains the frantic notes of an anonymous wanderer. The entries offer incomplete glimpses into the tragedy that struck the farmstead, confirming Sven Yorgen's darkest suspicion: someone lurked in the shadows while his family was slain. Because the narrative cuts off abruptly, the book raises more questions than answers, prompting investigators to carry it back to Darkshire in search of anyone who recognizes the handwriting or its enigmatic author.

Book of the Ancients. Azore Aldamort of the Ethel Rethor tower trusts you with a gem. Set in the hand of a serpent statue on Ranazjar Isle, northwest of the tower, it calls up the protector of the Book of the Ancients, which holds secrets the naga have kept for centuries. After Sceptre of Light, Azore Aldamort hands you the Gem of the Serpent. A Serpent Statue stands on Ranazjar Isle, a little island to the northwest of the Ethel Rethor tower, and the gem belongs on its hand. That will bring forth the guardian of the Book of the Ancients, a book that holds naga secrets kept for centuries. Azore hopes it will teach much about their scaled foes.

Book: Stresses of Iron. In Stormwind Keep, Margulf Blaggon’s book on metallurgy has been lent to Northshire Abbey for copying. Margulf Blaggon wrote about the practical and theoretical sides of metallurgy. Milton Sheaf cared for the volume in the Royal Library of Stormwind Keep. The library lent it to Northshire Abbey, where Brother Paxton copied it by hand for his own collection. Paxton’s work took far longer than expected, and Brother Kristoff waited anxiously in Cathedral Square for the book to return to the city.

Bookie Herod. Lieutenant Doren fears a spy among his own men after Kurzen discovered Thorsen's secret. To uncover how the secret slipped out, an investigator must infiltrate Kurzen's Compound and recover the records kept by Kurzen's logistics officer. Following the discovery of Thorsen's secret, Lieutenant Doren suspects that a traitor operates within their midst. The intelligence leak threatens their operations, and finding the traitor has become an urgent concern. Thorsen maintained a line of communication directly into Kurzen's Compound through Bookie Herod, the colonel's logistics officer. Because Herod knows how Kurzen's Compound is run from day to day, Doren believes the officer's written records hold the truth about how the operation was exposed.

Booty Bay. Booty Bay is a sprawling pirate haven built into the sheer sea cliffs of southern Stranglethorn Vale, operated by the Steamwheedle Cartel's Blackwater Raiders. Entered by land through the gaping jaws of a giant shark carcass, it serves as a fiercely enforced neutral port where Alliance and Horde mingle under the watchful eyes of heavily armed goblin bruisers. Originally known as Blackwater Cove when it was a human settlement later overrun by jungle trolls, the bay was eventually captured by the goblins of the Steamwheedle Cartel. Today, it is an international crossroads and a haven for scoundrels, outcasts, and merchants alike. Overseen by Baron Revilgaz alongside Fleet Master Seahorn from the balconies of the Salty Sailor Tavern, the port is ostensibly lawless yet strictly managed: anyone may drink, trade, or hire mercenaries here, provided they obey the cartel's peace and pay their harbor fees.

Border Crossings. Border Crossings is an espionage task assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to investigate Dalaran's covert operations in Silverpine Forest. By intercepting supply crates bound for the Dalaran encampment near Pyrewood Village, the Forsaken hope to uncover why the Kirin Tor are actively supporting the human bastion of Ambermill. While Ambermill stands as the main stronghold of surviving human resistance in eastern Silverpine Forest, the magi of Dalaran have not left them to stand alone. Wagon shipments filled with supplies and arcana have been smuggled out of the Hillsbrad Foothills, crossing through Silverpine to supply forward outposts and staging grounds. One such logistical camp sits just north of Pyrewood Village, manned by Dalaran personnel watching the road.

Bottle of Disease. A Bottle of Disease is a vial of virulent concoctions brewed by the Forsaken operating in Ashenvale. Found at an encampment near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, these vials represent an ominous attempt by the undead to introduce blighted plagues into the pristine night elven wilderness. Deep within the ancient canopy of eastern Ashenvale, the Forsaken have crept far past the front lines of the Warsong Outriders. Establishing an outpost near the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, undead alchemists brew foul contagions and seal them within glass bottles. To the night elves guarding Forest Song, these vials are clear evidence of a quiet, insidious offensive aimed at sickening the woodland soil and wildlife rather than engaging in open combat.

Bottle of Moonshine. A Bottle of Moonshine is a potent alcoholic spirit sold in the gloomy settlement of Darkshire. Barkeep Daniels of Lakeshire urgently seeks a bottle to help restock the town tavern as Blackrock orc incursions cut off regular supply shipments. Lakeshire stands besieged by the Blackrock clan, leaving its local innkeeper, Barkeep Daniels, in dire straits as regular supply caravans fail to arrive. To keep up morale among the town guards and beleaguered townsfolk, Daniels sends couriers across the southern kingdoms to gather regional specialties. Among these is a potent bottle of moonshine brewed and sold at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in neighboring Duskwood, where locals favor stiff drinks to ward off the encroaching dread of the woods.

Bottle of Zombie Juice. A Bottle of Zombie Juice is a potent, foul liquor brewed from the pungent rot blossom found in Duskwood. Procured from the tavern in Darkshire, it is supposedly requested by the reclusive hermit Abercrombie to ward off the chill of the gloomy woods. Brewed from rot blossoms gathered among the shadowed soils of Duskwood, Zombie Juice is a remarkably harsh brew. The bartender who provides it warns that the drink is potent enough to raise the dead. While ordinary folk steer clear of such vile distillations, the eccentric hermit Abercrombie claims it is the only thing capable of keeping him warm on the damp, cold nights out by his lonely shack.

Bottles and Baubles. Bottles and Baubles is a quest built around the quirky logic that because murlocs look like fish, they must think like them. Adventurers are sent to rummage through a nearby murloc camp for glittering junk and discarded trinkets that an eager angler can fashion into fishing bait. Bottles and Baubles begins with a rather unusual theory of aquatic biology: that because murlocs are fish-like beings, their minds must function just like the fish swimming in the deep. Driven by this logic, an eccentric angler posits that whatever curious oddities catch a murloc's wandering eye will surely entice a hungry fish on a hook. Scavengers are tasked with venturing into a nearby murloc camp to rummage through their hoard piles and gather shiny discarded junk to test the hypothesis.

text.enUS: Bottom of Gelkak's Key. The Bottom of Gelkak's Key is one of three fragments of a shattered mechanical winding key belonging to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel foundered off Darkshore, the piece was scavenged by the shoreline's native reef crawlers. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was sunk by threshadons off the coast of Darkshore, the gnome was thrown ashore along with his belongings. Among his most prized possessions was the winding key used to activate his mechanical first mate. The key shattered on the coastal rocks into three distinct pieces, and local scavengers immediately descended upon the debris. The bottom piece of the key was snatched up by the aggressive crustaceans wandering the surf—specifically the reef and tide crawlers that pick through the detritus along the tideline.

Bough Shadow. Bough Shadow is a secluded grove tucked away in the far northeastern corner of Ashenvale, east of Forest Song. It centers around a colossal Great Tree rooted over an ancient portal leading directly into the Emerald Dream. Bough Shadow houses one of the rare Great Trees, its roots plunging deep into the earth around a natural crossing into the Emerald Dream. Today, the tranquil yet imposing grove is heavily guarded by the Green Dragonflight. Emerald drakes such as Phantim and Dreamstalker circle above the canopy, while patrols of Emeraldon dragonspawn and oracles keep a vigilant, unyielding watch over the swirling green portal at its base, turning away any mortal who approaches unbidden.

Boulder Lode Mine. Boulder Lode Mine is an aggressive excavation cut into the hills of the northeastern Barrens. Though orcish banners and watchtowers suggest the Horde first established the site, it is now firmly seized and operated by the ruthless Venture Company. The presence of weathered orcish architecture around the mouth of Boulder Lode Mine indicates that the Horde once held or founded the claim. Today, however, the area crawls with Venture Company overseers and enforcers working under the direction of Boss Copperplug. The goblin syndicate strip-mines the canyon with little regard for the local ecosystem or their workers, driven purely by the search for valuable minerals, high-yield gems, and industrial machinery.

Boulder'gor. Boulder'gor is a rugged hill in the western Arathi Highlands, situated directly north of the ruined human kingdom of Stromgarde. It serves as an active encampment for the Boulderfist ogres and their unusual allies among the Witherbark forest trolls. Rising just north of the crumbling ramparts of Stromgarde Keep, Boulder'gor is a steep bluff claimed by the Boulderfist clan. Within its shadows sits the Boulderfist Outpost mound, making it a central bastion of ogre power across the highlands. Uniquely, the ogres here share their fires and fortifications with forest trolls of the Witherbark tribe, including shadowy spellcasters who lend their dark magic to the clan's brute force. This mutual cooperation poses an ongoing danger to any travelers passing along the central roads of Arathi.

Boulderfist Hall. Boulderfist Hall is a heavily fortified ogre mound nestled in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just north of Thandol Span. It serves as the local stronghold for the Boulderfist ogres, who exert their brute influence across the neighboring trade routes and valleys under the command of Kor'gresh Coldrage. Carved into the rugged southern bluffs of the Arathi Highlands, Boulderfist Hall is the principal redoubt of the Boulderfist clan in the region. Sheltered within its earthen ramparts and deep caverns, ogre brutes and magi maintain a fortified settlement mere steps from Witherbark Village and the strategic bridge at Thandol Span. Deep within the mound lurks their regional chieftain, Kor'gresh Coldrage, alongside enforcers like Phalanax. From this stronghold, the ogres project violent control over the surrounding roads, making any peaceful transit between Arathi and the Wetlands perilous for travelers and supply caravans alike.

Boulderfist Outpost. Boulderfist Outpost is a fortified mound nestled deep within the ogre settlement of Boulder'gor in the Arathi Highlands. Serving as an interior den and holding area, it houses aggressive Boulderfist ogres alongside a few Witherbark trolls. Carved into the earth and stone of western Arathi, Boulderfist Outpost functions as the heart of Boulder'gor. While brute enforcers dominate the settlement above, the outpost's interior concentrates the clan's core strength and provides a dark subterranean shelter. A handful of Witherbark troll witch doctors occasionally mingle among the ogres here, hinting at tenuous tribal cooperation.

Boulderslide Cavern. Boulderslide Cavern is a subterranean warren tucked at the deepest end of Boulderslide Ravine in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as the primary den and excavation site for the local Boulderslide kobolds, who obsessively tunnel in search of glowing mineral formations. The Boulderslide kobolds have burrowed deep into the crags of Stonetalon, establishing Boulderslide Cavern as their stronghold. Unlike ordinary vermin merely seeking shelter, these kobolds mine frantically for resonite, a rare glowing purple crystal embedded throughout the stone. The crystals pulse with lingering earthen magic, driving the creatures into a defensive frenzy against any intruders who approach their dig.

Boulderslide Ravine. Deep in the Boulderslide Ravine of the Stonetalon Mountains, local kobolds have begun frantically mining a rare subterranean mineral known as Resonite. Sensing a growing tension in the earth, the tauren Mor'rogal sends Horde adventurers to explore the ravine's cave system and retrieve mineral samples to uncover what lies buried beneath the rock. From his post at Sun Rock Retreat, the tauren Mor'rogal watches the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains with deep concern. The land itself feels disturbed, an unnatural agitation radiating from the southeast. There, within the crags of Boulderslide Ravine, the local kobolds have abandoned their ordinary foraging to aggressively excavate a rare, subterranean mineral known as Resonite. To determine why these superstitious vermin are mining with such desperate frenzy, Mor'rogal enlists Horde scouts to push past their defenses, plumb the lowest depths of the cavern, and bring back unrefined mineral samples.

Boulderslide Ravine. Boulderslide Ravine is a rugged, secluded canyon tucked away in the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via Webwinder Path. Largely spared from the direct clashes between the Horde and Alliance, it serves as the rocky approach to Boulderslide Cavern and remains home to wild mountain beasts. Tucked away off Webwinder Path, Boulderslide Ravine is a narrow cut of rock in the Stonetalon heights. While loggers, night elves, and the Horde battle over timber and sacred glades throughout the region, this craggy pass remains relatively undisturbed by military forces. Wild mountain rams and roaming crag beasts like Cliff Stormers make up the local fauna, navigating the treacherous ledges and sheer stone walls. Prospectors also keep an eye on the ravine, as rich mineral veins frequently crop up along the rocky slopes leading deeper toward the cavern network.
