text.enUS: Bounty on Garrick Padfoot. In Northshire, an Alliance bounty names Garrick Padfoot, a notorious local thief. Deputy Willem at Northshire Abbey calls for recruits to hunt him near the vineyards. Northshire Valley once offered a safe place to train recruits and tend its sacred vineyards. As order falters across Elwynn, thieves have reached the valley. Garrick Padfoot, a cutthroat, quickly rose to lead them. For weeks, he and his gang have plundered shipments, robbed merchants on the roads, and threatened local farmers.

Bounty on Murlocs. Murlocs are spreading through eastern Elwynn, and the Stormwind Army has put a bounty on them. With the garrison stretched thin, Guard Thomas turns to travelers to clear the shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and the southern waterways before the murlocs overrun nearby farms and roads. Murlocs have made shoreline camps around Stone Cairn Lake and along the fork of the southern streams. Lurkers and foragers now attack travelers and press toward human settlements. What began as a minor nuisance has grown into a threat across eastern Elwynn, while the western roads remain comparatively secure.

Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg. Bounty: Gnarlpine Furbolg is an Alliance quest authorized by the Sentinels to curb the aggressive furbolg population corrupting Teldrassil. Shayla Nightbreeze recruits adventurers outside Darnassus to hunt the corrupted beasts and collect their fangs as proof of deed. On the road outside Darnassus, Shayla Nightbreeze acts on direct orders from the Sentinels to place a bounty on the Gnarlpine furbolg. Once peaceful inhabitants of the ancient forests, the Gnarlpine have succumbed to a spreading corruption that stripped away their reason, turning them into vicious threats to the safety of travelers and the natural sanctity of Teldrassil.

Bracers of Binding. Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill says the Magus, busy with the stone tokens you gathered, will eventually want their counterpart: bracers of binding. You are to collect four Bracers of Earth Binding from elementals among the ruins of Dalaran. While the Magus studies the stone tokens you gathered, Bel'varil expects a further wish: samples of the matching piece, bracers of binding. Worn on an elemental's wrists, they tie it to a mage's service. Among the ruins of Dalaran, elementals wear them. Bel'varil wants four Bracers of Earth Binding brought to Tarren Mill.

Brackenwall Village. Brackenwall Village is the primary Horde outpost in Dustwallow Marsh, nestled among the bogs in the northwest corner of the zone. Founded by surviving Stonemaul ogres after dragons devastated their original settlement to the south, the village serves as a tenuous stronghold surrounded by Alliance spies, deserters, and the black dragonflight. When black dragonkin drove the Stonemaul ogres out of their ancient home at Stonemaul Village in the southern marsh, their leader, Overlord Mok'Morokk—successor to Rexxar—led the survivors north into the swamp to build Brackenwall. Formed around traditional earthen mounds, huts, and an old watchtower, the settlement gave the battered clan a defensible haven. Though aligned with the Horde, the village suffers from internal rot: Mok'Morokk sits idle, hoarding supplies and refusing to confront the draconic threat, leaving the clan's spiritual and tactical guidance to figures like the ogre mage Draz'Zilb and Horde emissaries.

Brackwell Pumpkin Patch. Defias brigands have taken over Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in southeastern Elwynn Forest. The farm once belonged to the Brackwell family, but now its cottage and fields serve as a hideout where conspirators meet and stolen mine gold is received. You find the Brackwell farm southeast of the Stonefield homestead, its fields no longer tended. The Brackwell family has vanished, driven away or worse as crime spread through the area. The Defias Brotherhood now occupies the sturdy cottage and overgrown fields. Brigands regroup here beyond the reach of Goldshire's patrols. Morgan the Collector and other prominent conspirators use the isolated farm to receive illicit gold taken from the forest's mines.

Braelyn Firehand. Braelyn Firehand is an elusive elf residing quietly among the Horde at Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. While presenting herself as an arcane practitioner seeking to clear mystical obstructions in the highlands, she pursues a deep personal grudge against the grove keepers of Stonetalon Peak. Standing out amidst the tauren lodges and rustic orcish tents of Sun Rock Retreat, Braelyn Firehand is a rare sight: a blood elf dwelling openly within a remote Horde settlement. The shaman and chieftains of the retreat tolerate her presence, seemingly oblivious to her true loyalties. Braelyn presents herself as an observer fascinated by the flow of regional magic, eager to hire passing Horde mercenaries to handle dangerous field assignments across the crags.

Braenna Flintcrag. Braenna Flintcrag is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward. She instructs devout followers of the Holy Light, guiding dwarven acolytes as they develop their spiritual disciplines and healing arts. She also passes word to visiting night elf priests when they are called home to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Residing within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Braenna Flintcrag serves the Alliance as a dedicated priest trainer. While Ironforge is renowned for its roaring forges and martial warriors, devout dwarves like Braenna tend to the spiritual welfare of Khaz Modan. She mentors novices answering the call of the Holy Light, teaching the dual disciplines of restorative mending and defensive warding required to survive in an increasingly dangerous world.

Brainwashed Noble. Deep in the caverns outside the Deadmines, Brainwashed Noble remains captive under Defias control. Magical manipulation has stripped him of his will, and he serves the Brotherhood alongside undead minions instead of walking Stormwind's grand halls.

Brambleblade Ravine. Brambleblade Ravine is a rugged canyon cutting into the northeastern edge of Red Cloud Mesa. It serves as a fortified den for the Bristleback quilboar tribe, who persistently raid the nearby tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Young tauren braves are sent here to prove their strength and protect their homeland from these fierce interlopers. Carved into the sun-scorched earth of Red Cloud Mesa, Brambleblade Ravine is choked with dense, thorny briars and quilboar encampments. The Bristleback tribe uses this natural fortress as a staging ground for raids against Camp Narache, threatening the safety of young tauren coming of age. Bristleback shamans and warriors, led by Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle, dwell deep within the ravine among trained battleboars. For the Shu'halo, striking into the heart of the canyon is a crucial rite of passage and a grim necessity to secure the plains.

Bramblescar. Bramblescar is a heavily fortified Razormane quilboar settlement situated in the southern Barrens. Thick, thorny brambles shield the encampment as its inhabitants wage a brutal war against the rival Bristleback tribe across the Gold Road. Carved into the jagged, giant briars of the southern Barrens, Bramblescar serves as a vital redoubt for the Razormane quilboar. These defensive brambles grow thick and sharp enough to deter casual wanderers, but the quilboar within are far from peaceful. Fiercely territorial and hostile to outsiders, they mount continuous skirmishes against anyone who ventures near their borders, viewing all non-quilboar as intruders upon land blessed by their ancient boar gods.

Branch of Cenarius. The Branch of Cenarius is a sacred dryad relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis in eastern Ashenvale. Recovering this heirloom was the dying wish of the dryad Anilia, who perished defending it from the woods' corruptors. Revered by the daughters of Cenarius, the Branch of Cenarius represents both the blessing of the Forest Lord and the deep connection his dryads maintain with Ashenvale. The branch was held in high regard by the dryad sisters Anilia and Illiyana until a band of corrupt satyrs ambushed them. The satyr leader, Geltharis, seized the relic and mortally wounded Anilia near the tainted ruins of eastern Ashenvale. With her dying breaths, Anilia pointed northward toward the arch where Geltharis lurks, pleading for a champion to wrest the sacred bough from his claws and restore it to dryad hands at Forest Song.

Brandur Ironhammer. Brandur Ironhammer is a dwarven paladin trainer residing in the Hall of Mysteries within Ironforge. He guides aspiring champions of the Holy Light through their early rites, testing their devotion and dispatching them across the Alliance. Stationed within the quiet alcoves of the Hall of Mysteries, Brandur Ironhammer serves the Alliance by instructing novice paladins in the ways of the Holy Light. Alongside his peer, Tiza Battleforge, Brandur keeps a watchful eye on young dwarven champions, guiding them through the trials of the Tome of Divinity. While deeply committed to his holy duties, he has acknowledged personal flaws under Tiza's frank counsel, working diligently to temper his envy and maintain the inner purity demanded of a warrior of the Light.

Brann Bronzebeard. Brann Bronzebeard is the youngest brother of King Magni and Muradin, who is believed dead, renowned throughout Azeroth as a peerless explorer, archaeologist, and founding leader of the Explorers' League. Driven by an insatiable curiosity for titan ruins and ancient history, his wanderlust has led him deep into the deadly wastes of Silithus. His field companions in southern Silithus await news of his latest expedition. While his eldest brother Magni rules Ironforge from the throne and Muradin served on battlefield frontlines, Brann took to the open wilds. He was a veteran warrior of the Second War. Yet peacetime turned his formidable constitution toward uncovering the forgotten past. As a leader of the Explorers' League, Brann charted vast swathes of the Eastern Kingdoms—from Elwynn Forest to the untamed jungles of Zul'Gurub—before turning his gaze across the Great Sea to the mysteries of ancient Kalimdor.

Branstock Khalder. Branstock Khalder is the priest trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Friendly and grounded, he introduces novice dwarven priests to the Holy Light while keeping a watchful eye on the growing trogg threat outside. Inside the bustling hall of Anvilmar, Branstock Khalder serves as a patient mentor to aspiring priests embarking on their spiritual journey. An easy-going dwarf with a deep devotion to the Light, he helps new acolytes master their early prayers and sacred runes. While his primary duty is spiritual instruction, Branstock is acutely aware of the valley's mounting perils—most notably the aggressive trogg infestation menacing the local mountaineers. Once a novice demonstrates sufficient command of the Light, he directs them through Coldridge Pass to seek further guidance from his superior, Maxan Anvol, in Kharanos.

Brass Collar. At the Brackwell pumpkin patch, Princess wears a brass collar that Ma Stonefield wants as proof the sow is gone. Princess is a huge, prize-winning sow owned by the Brackwell family. She roams their pumpkin patch east of the Maclure homestead, and her appetite leads her into the Stonefield Farm’s crops. After losing valuable vegetables to the sow, Ma Stonefield seeks someone willing to slay her. Princess wears a brass band around her neck, and the collar proves she will not raid the Stonefield fields again.

Brave Moonhorn. Brave Moonhorn is a tauren scout stationed at the top of the Great Lift on the southern border of the Barrens. From this precipice, he keeps watch over the entry to Thousand Needles and alerts travelers to the local dangers ahead. Perched above the sheer drops of Thousand Needles, Brave Moonhorn stands guard where the northern plains meet the canyonlands. His primary role is keeping watchful eyes on regional threats moving through the canyon floor below, particularly the hostile centaur clans. Anyone looking to descend into the needles often crosses paths with him first, receiving crucial warnings before they step onto the massive platforms of the Great Lift.

Break Sharptusk!. Break Sharptusk! is a decisive rite of passage issued by Brave Windfeather on Red Cloud Mesa. To secure the tauren homeland against ongoing raids, young champions are sent east into Brambleblade Ravine to slay Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle. Eliminating the Bristleback chieftain strikes a severe blow against the quilboar encroaching upon Mulgore. The grassy heights of Red Cloud Mesa have long served as a peaceful sanctuary where young tauren learn the traditions of the hunt and attunement with the Earth Mother. However, this peace is constantly contested. To the east lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked gulch claimed by the hostile Bristleback quilboar tribe. The quilboar view the tauren as invaders stealing sacred ground, launching relentless skirmishes against the tribes attempting to establish a stable life in Mulgore.

Break a Few Eggs. Break a Few Eggs is an errand assisting a harried cook who must keep up with endless meal preparations. Securing fresh, fragile ingredients without breaking them keeps the kitchen running and the cooking on schedule. Feeding a crowd is an exhausting, never-ending endeavor. Between breakfast, lunch, and dinner, there is scarcely any time to step away from the stove, let alone leave the kitchen to scrounge for raw provisions. In Break a Few Eggs, a hard-pressed cook turns to passing adventurers to secure fresh eggs before the next meal service falls behind.

Breaking the Keystone. Once the Stones of Binding were opened, much of the voice's confinement eased, yet a lock still holds it. That lock is the Keystone among a ring of stones, and the stone watcher Fozruk, one of the voice's captors, holds the key, known to the watchers as the Rod of Order. With the Stones of Binding opened, the voice's confinement has eased a great deal, but one lock remains: the Keystone, among the circle of stones around you. Its key is held by a captor, the stone watcher Fozruk, and the watchers call it the Rod of Order. Taking the rod from Fozruk and carrying it to the Keystone is how the lock will open. The voice promises that its gratitude, if you manage this, will shake the earth to its roots. The Keystone itself is charged with immense geomantic energy.

Brewer's Trade. A trade has been worked out with the Dun Garok brew-kin, who miss the Fallrook family's vineyards as much as anyone. A case of Fallrook Varietal travels to their fort in the southeast of Hillsbrad Foothills, and a sack of their Homebrew Hops comes back. Most of the best bottled years of Fallrook wine are long since drunk, but cases of the Fallrook Varietal still sit in the cellars. The Dun Garok brew-kin miss the vineyards of the Fallrook family too, and a trade has been worked out with them.

Brewmaster Drohn. Brewmaster Drohn is an orcish brewmaster living just uphill from the bustling port of Ratchet. Having learned the art of exotic fermentation through ties connected to the legendary wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout, Drohn crafts potent beverages on the arid frontier of the Barrens. Adventurers who discover discarded kegs across Kalimdor often find themselves directed straight to his porch. Overlooking the goblin docks of Ratchet sits Brewmaster Drohn, an orc who has devoted his craft to the science of brewing rather than simple combat. Brewing from his hillside home, he operates peacefully within the neutral haven established by Gazlowe's Steamwheedle cartel. While most orcs settle for coarse grog or simple spirits, Drohn's work involves rare ingredients, refined balances of flavor, and techniques rarely practiced among his kin.

Brewmeister Bilger. Brewmeister Bilger is an intoxicated dwarven brewer residing in the cellar of the inn at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He whiles away his hours tasting potent spirits and waiting on deliveries from distant lands. Bilger spends his days pacing the cool cellar beneath Southshore's inn, nursing hiccups and seeking out the strongest brews Azeroth can offer.

Brewnall Village. Brewnall Village is a small dwarven settlement nestled in Chill Breeze Valley near the entrance to Gnomeregan. Established by the Barleybrew family, this outpost serves as a proving ground for bold brewing experiments and regional defense against wild beasts. Despite being called a village, it functions largely as a rustic encampment in the snowy gnomish lowlands of Dun Morogh. Tucked away in the snowdrifts of Chill Breeze Valley, Brewnall Village lies squarely within the traditional gnomish reaches of western Dun Morogh. The settlement is home to the Barleybrew clan, stalwart dwarven brewers devoted to perfecting age-old recipes and crafting the ultimate stout. Though dubbed a village, the outpost consists mostly of tents and outdoor brewing equipment rather than permanent stone architecture. Between testing experimental batches of ale and defending against the ferocious local wolves and bears, the Barleybrews rely heavily on wandering mountaineers to gather rare ingredients and keep the valley secure.

Bride of the Embalmer. "Bride of the Embalmer" is a perilous task assigned by Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Darkshire. Having pieced together the disturbing truth behind the legendary Embalmer, town leadership sends you into the haunted cemeteries of Duskwood to find his resurrected wife's resting place. By tearing the alchemist's living heart from Eliza's cursed remains, you aim to strip him of his unholy power. For years, parents in Duskwood told their frightened children the tale of the Embalmer. According to the folktale, he was once a kindly alchemist whose mind shattered following the tragic demise of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to cheat mortality, he turned to foul sorceries and took the ultimate sacrifice: carving out his own beating heart and placing it into his wife's chest. Lord Ello Ebonlocke long dismissed this as mere village folklore, but recent revelations have proven that the Embalmer walks among them, his foul handiwork festering beneath the graveyard dirt.

Brightwater Lake. Brightwater Lake is the largest body of water in Tirisfal Glades, stretching across the mist-shrouded lowlands northeast of Brill. Once a tranquil retreat for the kingdom of Lordaeron, its waters now lie cold and dark, surrounding a central isle where an outcast necromancer conducts his forbidden research. Spanning the northern plains between the town of Brill and the Scarlet Watch Post, Brightwater Lake is a quiet and eerie landmark in the heart of Tirisfal. In the peaceful centuries under the Kingdom of Lordaeron, the lake served as a scenic country haven. Today, like the rest of the glades, its pristine character is long gone. The Plaguelands lie not far to the east, and the murky, chilled waters reflect only grey skies, withered trees, and the constant threat of roving murlocs and hostile undead.

Brightwood Grove. Brightwood Grove is a shadowed expanse of woodland located just west of Darkshire in Duskwood. Once part of the region's serene agrarian landscape, it is now infested with savage Nightbane worgen who make camp among ruined homesteads and attack any travelers wandering too close. Situated within sight of Darkshire's perimeter, Brightwood Grove represents the creeping peril threatening the town's borders. The homesteads and fences that once demarcated peaceful farmland now lie collapsed and rotting. In their place, crude camps have been erected by the Nightbane worgen, who prowl the overgrown clearings. The proximity of these wolf-beasts poses an ongoing threat to the town, forcing the Night Watch and passing adventurers to continually cull their numbers before the settlement is overrun.

Brill. Brill is the primary Forsaken settlement in the heart of Tirisfal Glades, situated just north of the Ruins of Lordaeron. Once a prosperous human town, it now serves as the administrative and military hub for newly awakened undead stepping beyond the confines of Deathknell. Before the Third War, Brill was a lively village under the sway of regional nobles such as the Barov and Agamand families. That prosperity ended when Kel'Thuzad chose the area for the Cult of the Damned's earliest experiments with the Plague of Undeath. The devastating blight swept through the population so quickly that local militia were driven out, leaving a sprawling mass graveyard in its wake. Now rebuilt by the Forsaken under the leadership of Magistrate Sevren, the town retains its weathered Lordaeron architecture beneath an atmosphere of grim purpose. Brill functions as the regional command center, coordinating defenses against Scarlet Crusade incursions, roaming Scourge remnants, and native beasts warped by necromantic decay.

Brill Town Hall. Brill Town Hall is the administrative heart of the settlement of Brill in central Tirisfal Glades. Standing as the most prominent structure in town, it serves as the civic headquarters from which the Forsaken govern their local holdings and coordinate the defense of the glades. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered and ruined, Brill Town Hall remains standing as a functioning civic center under undead rule. Inside, Magistrate Sevren directs town affairs from his podium, handing out vital commissions and directives to Forsaken adventurers. Aside from the Defiler's Den in the Arathi Highlands, it is one of the only recognized town halls in the known world actively run by the Forsaken, serving as a bleak parody and functional continuation of old Lordaeron's municipal bureaucracy.

Brine. Brine is an orc shaman residing in the arid hills of Blackthorn Ridge in the southern Barrens. As an expert on the spirits of water, she guides shaman initiates along the spiritual path to commune with the tides and earn their Water Totem. Perched upon a windswept hill in northern Blackthorn Ridge, Brine lives far from the bustling trading posts of the Barrens. Despite the dry savannas surrounding her, she has dedicated her life to understanding the fluid and fickle element of water. Shaman across the Horde are directed to seek her wisdom once they have mastered earth and fire, for water requires patience and perspective that few understand as deeply as she does.

Bring Back the Mug. After delivering a piping hot draught of Mornbrew across the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, one final errand remains: returning the empty tankard. Durnan Furcutter sends the runner back across Coldridge Valley to return Nori Pridedrift's prized mug. It is a simple courtesy, but one the brew seller deeply appreciates. Serving piping hot Mornbrew out in the biting freeze of Dun Morogh is a delicate business. Once Durnan Furcutter has finished warming his bones with the scalding brew, the empty tankard cannot simply be tossed in the snow. Dwarven hospitality runs on mutual respect, and letting good dishware go missing is a sure way to find oneself cut off from future rounds.

text.enUS: Bristleback Attack Plans. The Bristleback Attack Plans are crude maps and tactical notes drafted by the quilboar of Brambleblade Ravine. They outline a coordinated siege aimed directly at overrunning the tauren settlement of Camp Narache. Hidden deep within a dirt cave in Brambleblade Ravine, these scribbled tactical sketches reveal that the Bristleback quilboar are no longer just skirmishing on the borders of the Red Cloud Mesa. Instead, their leadership planned an organized, sustained assault to push into Camp Narache and wipe out the young tauren training there. Delivering this map to Chief Hawkwind allows the tribe to send word to Bloodhoof Village for reinforcements, blunting the impending invasion before it can begin.

Bristleback Belt. A Bristleback Belt is a piece of crudely crafted gear worn by the quilboar infesting Brambleblade Ravine. For young tauren coming of age in Camp Narache, collecting these belts serves as physical proof of valor during the Rite of Strength. The Red Cloud tribe tests every youth who aspires to earn respect in Thunder Bluff through the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. The first trial, the Rite of Strength, requires the initiate to protect the tribe from active threats. Because the hostile Bristleback quilboar repeatedly raid tribal food supplies and ambush hunting parties outside Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind demands the belts of these intruders. Returning twelve belts to the chieftain proves that an initiate can confront danger directly and strike a blow for the tribe's defense.

Bristleback Quilboar Tusk. Bristleback Quilboar Tusks are harvested from the slain Bristleback quilboar across the northern and central Barrens. Collected as proof of slaughter, they serve as gruesome tokens of vengeance for the grieving orc warrior Mankrik. Bristleback quilboar inhabit thickets and bramble dens throughout the Barrens, fiercely defending their territory against Horde expansion. Their tusks are prominent, jagged ivory used as natural weapons in close quarters. For Mankrik, a veteran warrior stationed at the Crossroads whose wife was lost during a vicious quilboar ambush, these tusks represent more than simple hunter trophies. Collecting dozens of them is a measure of pure retribution, a bloody tally meant to ensure the Bristlebacks suffer as deeply as he has.

Brock Stoneseeker. Brock Stoneseeker is a dwarven mining instructor based in the settlement of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. As the proprietor of Brock's School of Mining and Surveying, he instructs novice prospectors in the craft of extracting valuable ores and minerals from the earth. Operating out of Thelsamar, Brock Stoneseeker directs Brock's School of Mining and Surveying. In the mineral-rich hills of Loch Modan, seasoned expertise with a pickaxe and an eye for geological veins are indispensable. Brock guides aspiring miners through the foundational techniques of identifying ore nodes, extracting raw metals, and properly surveying subterranean deposits, ensuring Alliance tradesfolk can fuel Ironforge's legendary smithies.

Brock's List. Brock's List is a dispatch compiled by the mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. It contains the names of top mining pupils who have earned honorary picks from the guild halls in Ironforge. Mining is the lifeblood of dwarven civilization, and apprentice diggers must prove their skill before they are entrusted with serious work in Khaz Modan's veins. In Thelsamar, the local mining trainer compiles this parchment to reward students who excel in their lessons. The document records those who have earned honorary picks—coveted symbols of competence forged in the capital.

Broken Alliances. In Kargath, Gorn wants the Horde's honor restored after its alliance with Deathwing. The ogre Boss Tho'grun, hired to help get the Sign of the Earth, turned on the Horde and kept it for himself, and you are to take it back at Camp Boff. During the Second War the Horde stood with the dragon Deathwing. Blacklash and Hematus, a pair of his lieutenants, ended up locked away in Lethlor Ravine, far off to the east. Gorn holds that these depraved allies of old must be silenced if the Horde's honor is to be restored. To open the drakes' prison the Horde needed the Sign of the Earth, and hired ogre mercenaries under Boss Tho'grun to help find it. Tho'grun turned on them, overwhelmed them and kept it for himself.

Broken Alliances. Gorn sends you to Lethlor Ravine in the far eastern Badlands, where the black drakes Blacklash and Hematus lie bound by the Seal of the Earth. This follows the first Broken Alliances. Three runestones keep the Seal of the Earth closed. Each rests in a pillar of Lethlor Ravine: Diamond, Opal and Amethyst. The Sign of the Earth, which Gorn gives you, draws the stones out and opens the seal. Countless drakes make their home in the ravine, and Blacklash and Hematus are formidable. Gorn wants both dead, and their bindings brought back.

Broken Hall. The Broken Hall serves as the flooded outer threshold of the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Shattered when the Great Dragon Aspect Ysera and her flight dragged the grand ziggurat beneath the waters, this ruin now stands deserted as the Atal'ai zealots retreat into deeper sanctums. When the green dragons brought down their wrath upon the Atal'ai priesthood and submerged their unholy ziggurat beneath the Pool of Tears, the outermost architecture bore the brunt of the cataclysm. The floor of the Broken Hall collapsed completely, allowing murky swamp waters to flood the chamber. Because of the damage and submersion, the troll cultists abandoned this entrance hall, withdrawing further into the complex. Adventurers entering the sunken temple must wade through these sodden ruins before mounting the stairs to reach the Hall of Masks.

Broken Pillar. The Broken Pillar is a weathered cluster of ancient troll ruins jutting from the dunes south of Gadgetzan. It serves as an isolated research post for the goblin prospector and scientist Marvon Rivetseeker, who studies the enigmatic artifacts buried beneath the surrounding sands. Rising out of the sands south of Gadgetzan and east of the treacherous Abyssal Sands, the Broken Pillar marks the remnants of ancient troll architecture long swallowed by Tanaris. Despite the desolate surroundings and encroaching desert beasts, the site offers rare clues to the continent's prehistoric civilisations. Marvon Rivetseeker, a goblin researcher originally based out of Ratchet, has established a lonely camp beside the shattered stonework to examine curious relics known as Gahz'ridian scattered across the waste.

text.enUS: Broken Samophlange. The Broken Samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical device recovered from the northern Barrens. Despite its damaged state, its internal gears and shifting parts captivate engineers curious enough to uncover its true function. The samophlange remains one of the stranger contraptions found throughout the northern Barrens. Even when broken, the mechanism exhibits remarkable internal craftsmanship, filled with moving assemblies and fine gears. The Ratchet goblin Sputtervalve accidentally damaged the delicate apparatus before its full operation could be documented. Eager to deliver working results to curious colleagues in Undermine, the finder sought someone skilled enough to restore it, turning to Wenikee Boltbucket—a clever tinkerer stationed near the border outpost of Mor'shan Rampart.

Broken Tears. Warug says the Gelkis foolishly believe the centaur mother, Theradras, protects them. He sends you into the cave in their village to destroy the crystals they hoard there, the tears of Theradras, and bring him three of the broken pieces. Warug scorns the Gelkis for trusting Theradras, mother of the centaur, to protect them. To him no one protects the centaur, and the Magram, being the strongest, need no protection. He sends you to the cave in the Gelkis village, where they keep a hoard of crystals called the tears of Theradras. Smash them and bring Warug three broken pieces. He will only trust you with this if you are no enemy of the Magram.

Broken Tools. Broken Tools are the shattered remnants of dwarven prospector picks, intentionally destroyed at an anvil. They serve as physical proof to Baine Bloodhoof that the invasive dwarven excavation threatening Mulgore's land and wildlife has been disrupted. To the northwest of Bloodhoof Village, dwarven excavators have set up operations to delve into the hills of Mulgore. While the dwarves seek buried ancient history, the tauren view their aggressive excavation as a direct defilement of the Earth Mother. The noise and destruction agitate the local wildlife, particularly the roaming kodo herds. Rather than merely driving the excavators away, young Baine Bloodhoof instructs defenders to confiscate the prospectors' iron picks and shatter them upon a forge, rendering the expedition unable to gouge further into the earth.

text.enUS: Broken and Battered Samophlange. The Broken and Battered Samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical device recovered from Venture Company operations in the Barrens. After a botched tinkering attempt pushed its structural integrity to critical lows, it must be carried to goblin experts in Orgrimmar who might actually understand how it functions. A samophlange is an obscure piece of proprietary machinery designed by the Venture Company for their resource operations in the northern Barrens. When Wenikee Boltbucket attempted to inspect and modify one, she affixed extraneous gauges, levers, and dials to measure its stability. Instead of stabilizing the mechanism, her amateur meddling devastated its structural integrity, leaving it battered and teetering on the verge of ruin. Realizing more gadgets would only cause total failure, she packed off the fragile assembly to someone with real factory experience.

Bromos Grummner. Bromos Grummner is a dwarven paladin trainer stationed in Anvilmar within Coldridge Valley. He mentors fledgling dwarven holy warriors, preaching steadfast faith in the Holy Light and the vital bond between dwarves and humans in the Knights of the Silver Hand. Standing within the sturdy stone hall of Anvilmar, Bromos Grummner welcomes dwarven novices drawn to the discipline of the Holy Light. Confident and resolute, he instructs young paladins in martial rites and sacred invocations. Beyond the basic tenets of combat, Bromos emphasizes unity, reminding his pupils that the order of the Knights of the Silver Hand bridges the realms of Ironforge and the human kingdoms of the Alliance in righteous purpose.

Bronzebeard Encampment. Bronzebeard Encampment is a rugged dwarven outpost perched in southern Silithus, just east of the massive Scarab Wall. Staffed by hardy explorers and researchers from the Explorer's League, the camp serves as an operational base for investigating ancient silithid glyphs and the lingering mysteries buried beneath the desert sands. Positioned against the desolate southern bluffs of Silithus, Bronzebeard Encampment offers a rare refuge of dwarven grit in an otherwise hostile wasteland. Founded under the auspices of Ironforge's archaeological pursuits, the camp sits within sight of the towering Scarab Wall. Here, researchers like Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge braved scorching heat, scorpids, and encroaching silithid swarms to study the peculiar inscriptions and monuments left behind by forgotten civilizations.

Bronzebeard clan. The Bronzebeard clan is the ruling dwarven royal line and dominant population of Ironforge. Following their victory in the ancient War of the Three Hammers, they forged strong ties with humanity and the gnomes, standing today under King Magni Bronzebeard as a cornerstone of the Alliance. Long ago, dwarven society in Ironforge flourished under High King Modimus Anvilmar. When the king died of old age roughly 230 years ago, simmering rivalries erupted into civil war. Thane Madoran Bronzebeard commanded the traditional garrison and largest standing army within Ironforge, successfully driving both the Wildhammer and Dark Iron clans from under the mountain. When Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan mounted an assault to reconquer Khaz Modan, Madoran Bronzebeard led his clan in a decisive campaign that shattered the Dark Iron host, solidifying Bronzebeard supremacy over Ironforge.

Bronzebeard the Elder. Bronzebeard the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter with Elder Bronzebeard within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Honoring him during this ancestral celebration rewards travelers with wisdom and a token of his esteem. It reflects the deep reverence the folk of Khaz Modan hold for their forebears and long-lived heritage. During the Lunar Festival, spirits and venerable elders manifest across Azeroth to share their wisdom with travelers honoring the past. In Ironforge, Elder Bronzebeard stands as an embodiment of the stalwart resilience of the Bronzebeard clan. When approached by adventurers seeking to pay their respects, he expresses quiet satisfaction that the people of this land still acknowledge and honor the lineage of the olden races.

Brother Anton. Brother Crowley speaks of Brother Anton, a fellow warrior who learned of undead in distant Kalimdor and booked passage at once to destroy them. Anton is looking for people with bravery and resolve, and waits in Nijel's Point in Desolace. Brother Crowley says rumors of an undead infestation in Desolace, a land in far-off Kalimdor, reached Anton, who immediately booked passage to seek and destroy the menace. Anton wants help from those with bravery and resolve. If your heart is true, Crowley tells you to speak with Anton in Nijel's Point, the Alliance town in Desolace.

Brother Joshua. In Stormwind, Brother Joshua guides those who come to the Cathedral of Light to learn the ways of the Holy Light. He trains novice priests to heal wounds and strengthen their allies. Brother Joshua waits near the main altar in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, ready to teach new servants of the faith. A priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he instructs them in healing, protective wards, and the focus needed to commune with the Light. Young human priests beginning their service to the Alliance find one of their first guides in him.

Brother Kristoff. In Stormwind's Cathedral Square, Brother Kristoff preaches beneath Uther's statue. A human priest of the Church of the Holy Light, he stands outdoors near the great statue of Uther the Lightbringer and seeks practical books for sermons on spiritual strength. Brother Kristoff serves the Church of the Holy Light in Cathedral Square, beneath the statue of Uther the Lightbringer. He works among the citizens and pilgrims who pass through the plaza, rather than remaining within the Cathedral of Light. For sermons such as the Fortitude of the Spirit, he turns to worldly comparisons. In The Stresses of Iron, he finds a way to explain how the mortal soul endures pressure, comparing the Holy Light's gift of inner resolve to the tempered strength of worked metal.

Brother Neals. At Northshire Abbey, Brother Neals keeps watch over the food and drink stores. He oversees shipments and samples wine from the local vineyard. Brother Neals keeps Northshire Abbey supplied with food and drink from his rooms in the upper belfry. He follows the grape manifests from the Northshire vineyards and tastes the wine to check its quality. He also watches the shipments arriving from the fields around the valley.

Brother Paxton. At Stormwind's royal archives, Milton Sheaf sends you to Northshire Abbey for a missing dwarven treatise. The book was loaned months ago for copying, but has not returned to the city shelves. Stormwind's head librarian, Milton Sheaf, has a missing book on his hands. 'The Stresses of Iron,' a treatise on metallurgical techniques by dwarven prospector Margulf Blaggon, is gone from the capital's shelves. The book was loaned months ago to the clerics of Northshire Abbey so they could copy it. It was not misplaced in Stormwind.

Brother Sarno. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City, Brother Sarno welcomes visitors and worshipers. The human cleric also directs Alliance travelers to Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark needs help reclaiming Gnomeregan. Inside the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, Brother Sarno greets pilgrims and travelers at the entrance. A brother of the Church of the Holy Light, he welcomes those who come seeking prayer, comfort, or guidance. His kind manner puts visitors at ease amid the cathedral’s daily life.

Brother Wilhelm. Behind Goldshire's blacksmith, Brother Wilhelm trains young paladins in the Holy Light. He guides them as they leave Northshire Abbey and take their first steps into Elwynn Forest. Brother Wilhelm trains new paladins behind Goldshire's smithy. Northshire Valley shelters those who begin their path in the Light, but many seek his guidance when they enter the wider forest. He teaches them their sacred duties as they leave the abbey and take up the work of protecting the realm.

Brotherhood of Northshire. The Brotherhood of Northshire is a holy human clerical order dedicated to the Church of the Holy Light, based out of Northshire Abbey in Elwynn Forest. Originally known as the Clerics of Northshire, the order suffered catastrophic losses during the First War before being reformed under Archbishop Alonsus Faol. Today, the Brotherhood serves as both a spiritual sanctuary and the primary training ground for fledgling Alliance defenders. Centuries ago, pious missionaries traveled south from Lordaeron into the kingdom of Stormwind, establishing Northshire Abbey to minister to the people and soothe the realm through the Holy Light. Originally known as the Holy Order of Northshire Clerics, their compassion was legendary—they even tended to injured gnolls and jungle trolls during past border wars. When the Orcish Horde crossed through the Dark Portal, the clerics marched bravely to the front lines without armor or weapons to heal fallen soldiers. Because their healing sustained the Stormwind Army, the orcs ruthlessly targeted them. The order was decimated, the abbey was ransacked and burned, and the surviving clerics were forced to flee north across the sea to Southshore with Sir Anduin Lothar.

Brotherhood of Thieves. Deputy Willem sends recruits across Northshire's eastern river to face the Defias Brotherhood. Their red burlap bandanas give Stormwind its first tangible evidence of the brigands' organized presence in the valley. Northshire Valley has long been a safe haven in Elwynn Forest, guarded by Stormwind and used to train recruits and Clerics of the Holy Light. Recently, discipline along its perimeter has frayed. Vagrants and thieves have crossed the eastern river, lurking near the woods and making small camps close to the abbey. Deputy Willem maintains local order, but the guards cannot spare the manpower to watch every corner of the valley without volunteers.

Brotherhood's End. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Gregor Lescovar's killing leaves dangerous questions behind. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston and warns you to keep the killer's identity quiet. Baros Alexston, the City Architect who helped rebuild Stormwind as a stonemason, is relieved to hear that Lescovar is dead. Edwin VanCleef had marked Alexston and other prominent figures in the rebuilding effort for vengeance after the Stonemasons were cast out without pay. With Lescovar silenced and the conspiracy disrupted, Alexston believes the immediate threat to the kingdom's architects and nobility has passed.

Browman Mill. Browman Mill is a blighted lumber mill situated just north of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron's timber trade, it now swarms with undead minions under the iron grip of the Scourge. Its former proprietor, Stephen Browman, remains trapped in death within his ruined workshop. Before the Third War, Browman Mill served the surrounding towns and homesteads of Lordaeron, processing lumber harvested from the rich forests of the Eastweald. When the Scourge plague rolled across the kingdom, the mill fell alongside the rest of the province. Today, rotting timbers and shattered wheels sit idle while abominations, banshees, and skeletal warriors patrol the perimeter. Its close proximity to Light's Hope Chapel makes it a constant and menacing reminder of the undead horde pressing against the Argent Dawn's doorstep.

Bruegal Ironknuckle. Bruegal Ironknuckle is an infamous dwarven prisoner held within the Stormwind Stockade. Unlike the petty criminals and rioting rabble that fill the holding cells, he is a formidable brawler whose presence deep inside the corridors spells immediate danger to anyone trying to restore order. When the Stormwind Stockade erupted into open revolt, many of the city's most volatile cutthroats took control of the subterranean cellblocks. Among them is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a particularly dangerous dwarf inmate known for brutal brawling strength. Rather than staying confined to a single cell, he prowls the riot-torn hallways, ready to bash anyone attempting to quell the uprising.

Brutal Armor. Brutal Armor is a Horde warrior rite of passage overseen by the near-blind smith Thun'grim Firegaze in the northern Barrens. Seeking to craft armor worthy of a rising champion, Thun'grim sends seasoned warriors across distant lands to gather rare reagents and exotic smelting agents. Fulfilling his scroll begins the forging of a complete set of brutal battle gear. Perched along the craggy hills of the northern Barrens, the veteran orc smith Thun'grim Firegaze listens closely to the winds of war. Though his eyesight is failing and clouded, his reputation at the forge remains unmatched. Having heard rumors of a warrior whose strength and valor outpace ordinary soldiers, Thun'grim decides to craft an enduring set of mail that can withstand the harshest clashes of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms.

Brutal Gauntlets. Brutal Gauntlets is the culmination of an artisan's craft for seasoned Horde warriors. After gathering rare components across distant lands, the craftsman Ula'elek fashions a formidable pair of handguards designed to bring honor to both the maker and the bearer. Forging armor fit for a seasoned frontline warrior is more than simple metalworking—it is a spiritual undertaking for Horde artisans. Ula'elek, a craftsman residing in Durotar, pours his lineage and skill into shaping these brutal gauntlets. By employing hardened trophies harvested from dangerous adversaries, he constructs armor tailored to withstand ferocious blows while enhancing the wearer's offensive might.

Brutal Hauberk. Brutal Hauberk marks the culmination of an arduous rite of passage for Horde warriors in the Barrens. After gathering rare materials and proving their mettle against dangerous foes across the lands, warriors present their bounty to the reclusive smith Thun'grim Firegaze. In return, he hammers out a rugged suit of mail designed to withstand the harshest battles. Perched along the craggy hills of the northern Barrens, Thun'grim Firegaze does not forge armor for just anyone. The reclusive orc demands that aspiring warriors travel far and wide to harvest tough beast parts, rare metal, and alchemical reagents before he even lights his bellows. The finished hauberk is not merely protective gear; it is an enduring badge of endurance and grit recognized by veteran fighters throughout the Horde.

Brutal Helm. Brutal Helm marks the culmination of an arduous warrior trial overseen by Orm Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff. Having collected rare beast trophies across Kalimdor, an aspiring warrior is recognized with a formidable horned helm as a testament to their strength. Orm Stonehoof serves as a stern smith in Thunder Bluff, guiding Horde warriors through grueling rites of passage. These trials demand proof of martial capability, pushing initiates into treacherous territory to hunt ferocious creatures and claim rare trophies. Only those who have met Orm's exacting standards are granted audience for the completion of their armor.

Brutal Politics. Captain Pentigast believes whichever centaur clan wins the wars of Desolace will spill out and threaten the Alliance strongholds. To learn how to beat them, Pentigast wants an alliance with one clan: fight the Gelkis, win over the Magram, and speak with Warug. War rages across Desolace, centaur against centaur, and the Alliance believes the winner will spill out against its strongholds. That cannot be allowed. To learn how to beat the centaurs, Captain Pentigast says, the Alliance needs one of the clans as a friend.

Bugged. Bugged is a quest in Valanaar where an influx of seasonal lowland insects turns out to be an espionage plot. High Order mages discovered that local cultists are weaving listening charms onto skyhoppers to spy on the settlement, requiring an extermination effort to weed out the enchanted pests. During skyhopper season in the lowlands, swarms of native insects surge around the city of Valanaar. While usually regarded merely as a seasonal annoyance, an inspection by High Order mages revealed that several slain specimens carried sophisticated listening enchantments. A local cult has weaponized the insect swarm, transforming common lowland pests into inconspicuous surveillance tools to eavesdrop on the city.

Bulwark. The Bulwark is a fortified outpost straddling the border between Tirisfal Glades and the Western Plaguelands. Maintained jointly by the Forsaken and the neutral Argent Dawn, it serves as the Horde's front line against the Scourge and the primary launching point for expeditions into the tainted east. Positioned squarely on the eastern border of Tirisfal Glades, the Bulwark is the final barrier protecting the Forsaken heartland from the blighted horrors of the Western Plaguelands. Today, rough wooden palisades and heavily armed guards defend the pass against roaming undead. It represents an uneasy but necessary collaboration, where Forsaken forces coordinate alongside the Argent Dawn to recruit seasoned champions of the Horde, turning back the minions of the Lich King before they spill into Tirisfal.

Bundle of Crocolisk Skins. The Bundle of Crocolisk Skins is a prepared package of cured reptilian hides harvested from the dangerous marshes of the Wetlands. Destined for the leatherworkers of Menethil Harbor, it serves as valuable trade stock for crafting sturdy boots and tough harbor gear. The vast waterways of the Wetlands are teeming with crocolisks, whose tough, water-resistant hides are an essential commodity for the coastal settlement of Menethil Harbor. Hunters braving the bogs collect and cure these skins before sending them westward to local artisans like James Halloran. However, this particular bundle took an unusual detour into an adventurer's hands: the hunter Einar sought a courier purely to avoid returning to town and facing the temper of his frustrated wife, Sida.

Bundle of Hides. A Bundle of Hides consists of cured skins collected from the beasts of the Barrens, bundled together for transport across central Kalimdor. Bound for the leatherworkers of Thunder Bluff, it serves as a straightforward courier shipment that introduces travelers to the Horde's wind rider flight network. The untamed plains of the Barrens are home to vast herds of kodo, prowling lions, and roving raptors. Hunters along the trade paths skin these creatures not only for meat and survival, but to supply city artisans. Without raw pelts from the wilds, settlements like Thunder Bluff would struggle to sustain their local leathercrafters, who transform dried skins into essential gear, pouches, armor, and bindings for the Horde.

Bundle of Wood. Near Eastvale Logging Camp, Bundle of Wood waits in the trees for an urgent shipment west. Freshly chopped timber from Eastvale Logging Camp helps supply the Kingdom of Stormwind. The camp sends wood west for town buildings and other construction. Bears and wolves have pushed into the groves northwest of camp, and terrified loggers fled, leaving their freshly gathered Bundles of Wood among the trees. With delivery deadlines close, overseer Raelen needs travelers to pass the predators and recover the timber before the lumber contracts are breached.

Bungle in the Jungle. Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan has studied the silithid and likens them to bees, with the queen as the weak point. A lure must draw her out, and it calls for a scent gland and soil from Un'Goro Crater, to the west. Pestlezugg's research compares the silithid to bees. Destroy the hive's queen, and the rest should be thrown into disarray. A lure will be brewed to bring the queen out, and once she is summoned, you are the one to take her down.

Burning Blade Coven. Tucked into the northern cliffs of the Valley of Trials, the Burning Blade Coven is an infested cave network threatening the Horde's newest recruits. Corrupted cultists and summoned demons lurk within, turning an old mineral cavern into a staging ground for dark magic right on Durotar's doorstep. The dusty red mountains rimming the Valley of Trials were once simply a testing wilderness for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps in service to the Horde. In recent days, however, dark rituals have taken hold of the northern caves. Imps and lesser fiends spill from the cavern mouth, stirring chaos and threatening recruits. Led by the shadowy warlock Yarrog Baneshadow, the Burning Blade cult has entrenched itself deep inside, turning what was once a routine training ground into an active battleground against demonic corruption.

Burning Blade Medallion. The Burning Blade Medallion is a dark talisman carried by cultists lurking within the Valley of Trials. Guarded by dark magic in the depths of the Burning Blade Coven, it serves as direct proof of demonic corruption attempting to subvert the young warriors of Durotar. Discovered deep inside the winding caverns of the Burning Blade Coven, the medallion is held by Yarrog Baneshadow, an agent of the sinister Burning Blade cult. Identified through the divinations of Zureetha Fargaze, the trinket channels dark power amidst the cult's impish familiars and felstalkers. Striking down its bearer and seizing the medallion cuts short an insidious attempt to undermine the Horde's training grounds from within Durotar itself.

Burning Blade Medallion. Assigned by the warlock Zureetha Fargaze, this task sends young Horde initiates deep into the Burning Blade Coven cave in the Valley of Trials. There, players must confront a hidden cultist and recover an artifact of dark magic known as the Burning Blade Medallion. The mission reveals that demonic corruption is actively taking root right under the Horde's nose. While young orcs and trolls undergo basic trials of combat and survival in the Valley of Trials, an insidious menace lurks in the shadows. Through her divinations, the warlock Zureetha Fargaze senses that the vile familiars infesting the northern bluffs are merely the vanguard of a darker presence. Deep within a nearby cavern, the Burning Blade cult has established a hidden coven, practicing dark arts and harboring dangerous relics of demonic power.

Burning Blade clan. Once an ancient orcish clan renowned for its deadly blademasters and consumed by chaotic frenzy during the early wars, the Burning Blade now largely persists as a sinister demon-worshiping cult. Its acolytes infiltrate Durotar and the Barrens, pursuing dark agendas whispered to be guided by hidden masters. Meanwhile, a handful of honorable blademasters have forsaken its demonic corruption to serve Warchief Thrall in the New Horde. Originating in the lands of Draenor alongside clans like the Warsong, the Burning Blade were long respected for the lethal tradition of their blademasters. When they drank the blood of Mannoroth and marched through the Dark Portal into Azeroth during the First War, however, the clan fractured mentally. By the Second War, they were scarcely an organized society, behaving instead like a berserk force of nature. Nomadic and demented, they threw themselves into battle with total disregard for survival, requiring ogres to hold them in check until unleashed. Ultimately, their numbers were battered and routed near the Dark Portal by the Alliance.

Burning Blood. In Stormwind, Grimand Elmore turns to Furen Longbeard’s smithing methods. He needs burning blood and a burning rock from Duskwood to test the armorcrafting technique himself. Grimand Elmore is one of the Alliance’s accomplished armorers, and he rarely accepts that another smith might surpass his methods. Hearing of Furen Longbeard’s unusual smithing discoveries stirs his professional curiosity. Grimand agrees to test Furen’s methods by making a piece of armor. He needs strange, volatile components from the dark reaches of the south to quench and temper the metal to his exact requirements; ordinary water and common coals will not do.

Burning Blood (quest item). In Duskwood, Burning Blood is gathered from the Nightbane worgen. Grimand Elmore needs twenty vials for experiments in smithing. Nightbane worgen prowl Duskwood with a strange fury, and their blood burns with real heat. The fluid can be drawn from worgen haunting the timberlands and Roland's Doom. Though foul to gather, its heat draws the interest of armorers seeking to temper resilient plate.

Burning Legion. The Burning Legion is an infinite, apocalyptic host of demons led by the fallen titan Sargeras, dedicated to scouring all life from creation. Having already shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, the demons remain Azeroth's most relentless nemesis, orchestrating the corruption of the orcs and the horrors of the Third War. Long ago, Sargeras stood as the champion of the titans, tasked with hunting down and imprisoning the demons that plagued the cosmos. Over countless ages of battling their evil, he grew disillusioned and concluded that creation itself was fatally flawed and must be unmade in flame. To enact his crusade, he freed the demons he had imprisoned, bending them to his will through fel magic. He augmented their chaos with the intellect of the corrupted eredar—elevating Archimonde and Kil'jaeden as his chief lieutenants—and forged an unstoppable engine of cosmic annihilation.

Burning Rock. In Duskwood, Burning Rock smolders in the depths of Roland's Doom. Gutspill, leader of the Nightbane worgen, carries it, and Grimand Elmore in Stormwind needs it with fiery worgen blood to forge enchanted armor for promising warriors. Gutspill carries Burning Rock through the shafts of Roland's Doom. Grimand Elmore in Stormwind wants its heat for armor made with fiery worgen blood. He is testing smithing techniques developed by his peer Furen Longbeard, to make tough plates for veteran fighters.

Burning Shadows. Recovered from the Burning Blade cultist Gazz'uz in the depths of Skull Rock, this mysterious glowing pendant whispers urgent warnings into the bearer's mind. The voice specifically threatens Gazz'uz with the wrath of Neeru Fireblade, an orc warlock residing in Orgrimmar. Upon slaying Gazz'uz deep within Skull Rock, an ominous pendant known as the Eye of Burning Shadow is retrieved from his remains. Rather than being an inert magical trinket, the stone vibrates with psychic communication. A demanding voice speaks directly into the mind of anyone holding it, demanding reports from Gazz'uz and warning him that his clandestine operations east of Orgrimmar have been compromised.

Business in Auberdine. Borgus Steelhand seeks news of his brother Gorbold in Auberdine. The dwarven merchant asks travelers sailing west to check on Gorbold, who recently began trading in the night elven port. Their route links Stormwind Harbor with the shores of northern Kalimdor. Borgus Steelhand trusts his family's name among traders. His brother, Gorbold Steelhand, crossed the Great Sea recently to work a merchant stall in Auberdine. Gorbold hoped to profit by supplying ships that call at Darkshore. Weeks have passed without a word, and Borgus worries about how his brother fares so far from Ironforge and Stormwind.

Buzzbox 323. Buzzbox 323 is the third task in a field-research line along the coast of Darkshore, commissioned through a speaker device by the eccentric gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle. Players must gather Moonstalker fangs from local predators and deposit them into the humming contraption situated north of Auberdine. After operating Buzzbox 411 further south, the voice of the gnomish inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle crackles to life over the speaker. Interspersed with the sounds of heavy drinking and slurred directions, Wizbang directs adventurers north of Auberdine, pointing them to Buzzbox 323 near a road bridge. His research requires six Moonstalker Fangs, harvested from the fierce feline hunters roaming the shrouded forests of Darkshore.

Buzzbox 411. Buzzbox 411 is an Alliance quest found along the windswept coastline of Darkshore. Operating through an eccentric mechanical relay network, the intoxicated gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle enlists travelers to gather coastal thresher eyes to bring his second research machine back online. After assisting with the repairs of Buzzbox 827 further south, the voice of the gnome inventor Wizbang Cranktoggle crackles over the mechanical transmitter once more. Stationed somewhere safely out of sight, Wizbang directs adventurers further north along Darkshore's mist-laden beach to locate another damaged terminal: Buzzbox 411. Between transmissions punctuated by hiccups and muttered praises of crawler wine, he reveals that local aquatic predators hold the components necessary to keep his coastal apparatus functional.

Buzzbox 525. Buzzbox 525 is the final stage in a series of communicative machines scattered along the coast of Darkshore. Created by the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle, the contraption demands animal remnants to function while asking travelers for increasingly unusual repair materials. After servicing Buzzbox 323, travelers receive garbled instructions broadcast straight through the machine's rattling speakers. Wizbang Cranktoggle's speech grows increasingly slurred, filled with drunken chuckles and rambling directions leading far south along the main road of Darkshore. He directs his helpers to hunt down the local grizzled thistle bears and deliver four of their thick scalps into the compartment of Buzzbox 525, concealed carefully behind a fence in the roadside brush.

Buzzbox 827. Buzzbox 827 is the first in an experimental communication relay built by the gnome Wizbang Cranktoggle along the coastline of Darkshore. Plagued by breakdowns, these curious mechanical contraptions rely on an eccentric design that uses local wildlife parts for field repairs. Restoring the silent machine allows Wizbang to test his long-distance voice network directly from Auberdine. While visiting Auberdine, the eccentric gnomish engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle sought to bridge the long distances of the wild coast with a series of long-range acoustic relays called Buzzboxes. Designed to transmit voice over great distances, these lever-laden devices stand out starkly against the ancient ruins and somber forests of Darkshore. However, like many ambitious gnomish inventions, they suffer from chronic instability and require near-constant upkeep to keep their internal gears churning.

CLUCK!. In Westfall, a chicken may answer when you call and feed it. Follow its scratched message to the Saldean family, and a warm egg may be yours to hatch. Ordinary chickens wander the farmsteads of Azeroth, and most travelers pass them by. Mimic a chicken's gestures and clucking, and it may stop pecking to regard you with interest. In that brief moment, the bird scratches letters in the dirt. The message points to the farmer who can provide the food it wants.
