text.enUS: Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. The Cache of Zanzil's Altered Mixture is a stockpile of potent poison secured inside a locked chest at the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Named for the jungle troll witch doctor Zanzil, it serves as a critical target for the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar. North of the Sludge Fen in the Barrens, the Venture Company keeps a tower outpost. A cache of an altered mixture bearing the name of the infamous troll witch doctor Zanzil sits locked inside Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix's private strongbox at the summit of the tower. A poison has weakened everything in the tower, leaving its goblin inhabitants vulnerable to any intruder bold enough to strike.

Cactus Apple. Cactus Apples are tough, moisture-rich fruits harvested from the rugged flora of Durotar's Valley of Trials. Flourishing in the arid desert heat, they are prized by local orcs as a rare, refreshing source of sustenance. The sun-scorched earth of Durotar offers little luxury, forcing its inhabitants to make use of whatever hardy plants survive the elements. Cactus apples grow in clusters around the thick cactuses dotting the Valley of Trials. While difficult to gather without catching a few thorns, the fruit provides vital hydration in the sweltering canyon. A local orc named Galgar gathers these fruits to prepare his signature Cactus Apple Surprise, a cooling confection that brings welcome relief to recruits enduring their harsh initial training.

Caer Darrow. Caer Darrow is a fortified island situated in Darrowmere Lake in the Western Plaguelands. Formerly the aristocratic seat of the noble House Barov, the island's keep was secretly sold to Kel'Thuzad and transformed into the necromantic school of Scholomance, leaving the above-ground town plagued by wandering phantoms. Long before the Scourge, Caer Darrow was a strategic stronghold of Lordaeron that housed an ancient elven runestone. During the Second War, the Horde sacked the fortress and carved up the runestone to craft Gul'dan's Altars of Storms. When Lord Uther the Lightbringer sailed to offer relief to the survivors, his fleet was ambushed by Alterac privateers—an act of treachery that exposed Alterac's betrayal to the Alliance.

Cain Firesong. Cain Firesong is a Forsaken mage trainer located in the settlement of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. He assists fledgling practitioners of the arcane as they grow in power, guiding them before directing them onward to deeper studies in the Undercity. He can be found on the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern. While many Forsaken spellcasters delve into shadow or necromancy, Cain Firesong maintains mastery over traditional arcane disciplines. Stationed in Brill, he serves as an early mentor to Forsaken mages venturing forth from Deathknell. The local Deathguards direct visitors to the upstairs landing of the Gallows' End Tavern, joking that he arrived too late to get a room.

Cairne Bloodhoof. Cairne Bloodhoof is the venerable High Chieftain of the united tauren tribes and ruler of Thunder Bluff. A towering warrior of immense wisdom, he bound the fate of the tauren to Thrall's Horde after the orcs aided his people in escaping extinction at the hands of the centaur. For generations, the tauren lived as wandering nomads across the Barrens, continually hunted and driven toward extinction by savage centaur marauders. When Thrall and his orcs arrived on the shores of Kalimdor, Cairne recognized a rare nobility in them. Thrall offered military protection, escorting Cairne's desperate caravan across the plains to the safety of Mulgore in exchange for guidance to the Oracle at Stonetalon Peak. Settling upon the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, Cairne finally established a permanent, unified home for all tauren tribes.

Call of Air. Call of Air is a vital rite of passage for seasoned Horde shamans seeking mastery over the winds. Initiated by Searn Firewarder in Grommash Hold, this quest directs practitioners far south across Kalimdor to commune with the elusive Prate Cloudseer. Through her guidance, shamans earn the final elemental pillar of their craft: the Air Totem. Having already earned the favor of earth, fire, and water, a shaman reaching the height of early training stands ready to harness the subtle and capricious element of air. In Orgrimmar, the troll trainer Searn Firewarder recognizes when a disciple is prepared for this final foundational step. Rather than testing them within Durotar's canyons, he bids them travel south across the expanse of the Barrens and descend into the canyon labyrinth of Thousand Needles.

Call of Air. Call of Air marks a major milestone in a Horde shaman's spiritual path, directing them to seek communion with the unpredictable element of wind. Offered by Xanis Flameweaver in Thunder Bluff, this quest bids seasoned initiates journey south into Thousand Needles to learn from Prate Cloudseer. Mastering air grants a shaman the sacred totem required to channel the swiftest forces of nature. Having already attuned to the stability of earth, the ferocity of fire, and the restorative depths of water, a shaman reaches the final elemental pillar: air. Xanis Flameweaver, guiding practitioners from the heights of Thunder Bluff, acknowledges that the winds are far more fickle and difficult to control than the previous elements. The trial demands humility, focus, and an innate respect for the sky's tempestuous nature.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is the initial trial for novice Horde shaman training within the Valley of Trials. Bestowed by Canaga Earthcaller, the trial tests a shaman's endurance and patience by requiring them to hunt demonic felstalkers in order to prepare a ritual sapta. Before a shaman can call upon the elements, they must form an enduring relationship with each one in turn. In orc and troll culture, this spiritual path begins with the earth, the bedrock of life, endurance, and patience. Canaga Earthcaller serves as the guide for fledglings in the Valley of Trials, teaching that the earth demands supreme respect and steadfastness before granting its protection.

Call of Earth. This sacred rite marks an initiate's first spiritual communion with the elements in Durotar. Guided by Canaga Earthcaller, young shaman consume a potent Earth Sapta atop Spirit Rock to pierce the veil and stand directly before the Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a mystical concoction known only to a select few shaman masters. Brewed with elemental magic, the draught serves to bridge mortal perception with the spiritual plane, granting 'Sapta Sight' to the strong-willed. Because its power binds the drinker's spirit directly to an element, tradition demands that it never be consumed outside of consecrated holy ground.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is the culminating rite in the trial of earth for young shaman in Durotar. After communing with a manifestation of the earth spirit, an initiate returns to Canaga Earthcaller with rough quartz to receive their first elemental totem. To commune with the earth, a novice shaman must look beyond brute strength. Upon demonstrating patience and humility before the Minor Manifestation of Earth, the initiate is granted a modest token: a piece of rough quartz. Though unassuming in appearance, this tiny stone serves as an enduring seed of power and proof that the spirit has accepted the petitioner's pledge.

Call of Earth. This sacred rite marks a tauren shaman's spiritual attunement to the element of earth. By drinking an Earth Sapta at a holy rock east of Camp Narache, initiates peer beyond physical senses to commune directly with a Minor Manifestation of Earth. A sapta is a carefully concocted ceremonial potion crafted by shamanic elders to bind an initiate's mortal spirit directly to a primal element. Prepared with ancestral magic, only a select few among the tauren preserve the secrets of its brewing. When imbibed at a designated sacred site, the draught expands the imbiber's mind, piercing the veil between the physical realm and the spiritual plane so the elements can be witnessed in their raw form.

Call of Earth. This rite concludes a young tauren shaman's initial communion with the spirits of the land in Mulgore. After drinking the Sapta of Earth and speaking directly with a spirit manifestation, the initiate receives a fragment of raw stone to bring home. Returning to Camp Narache marks the fledgling mystic's formal bond with the first of the four elements. Upon communing with the Minor Manifestation of Earth atop the crags near Red Cloud Mesa, the spirit yields a simple Rough Quartz. Though plain in appearance, the stone represents an elemental pact and the endurance of stone itself. The spirit reminds the young shaman that patience and strength are the core virtues demanded by the earth, promising that mutual respect will grant harmony with the land.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is an elemental trial undertaken by spiritual initiates to prove their steadfastness. By retrieving requested materials, the petitioner demonstrates their grit and determination to their instructor. Successfully enduring the task confirms their readiness to proceed to the next stage of their training. The Call of Earth is a foundational trial for aspiring practitioners of the elements. Initiates are tasked with fulfilling specific demands to test their patience, resilience, and connection to the stubborn, enduring nature of the earth. Fulfilling the request demonstrates that an adventurer possesses the inner fortitude required to commune with primeval forces.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial in which an elemental initiate drinks an Earth Sapta at the Rise of Spirits to pierce the veil between worlds. Guided by an elemental spirit, the seeker learns the endurance and steadfast resolve of the earth as the foundation for rekindling their lost bond with the winds. To perceive the unseen elemental world, shamans utilize saptas—potent magical brews specifically formulated to align a mortal spirit with a particular elemental realm. When consumed by those possessing sufficient resolve, a sapta opens one's spiritual vision to elemental manifestations that are otherwise hidden from mortal sight. Because of their profound nature, these potions are closely guarded secrets known only to select practitioners.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is a sacred trial of communion where an initiate obtains a piece of Rough Quartz from an earth spirit. Brought to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, this mineral shard becomes the core of the practitioner's first Earth Totem, grounding their bond with the elemental forces. The quest begins when an earth spirit grants an initiate a shard of Rough Quartz as living proof of their communion. The spirit instructs the bearer to take this token to Windshaper Boros in Thendal Grove, explaining that even the smallest fragment carries enduring strength. The spirits demand patience, resilience, and wisdom before granting their favor and respect.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is a sacred trial overseen by Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar, testing initiates in the patience and resilience of stone. Aspirants must confront the Frostmane trolls to the south to claim their bear pendants before being granted an earthen sapta. At Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley, the mentor Teo Hammerstorm watches over initiates ready to walk the rugged path of the earth. Viewing the land as a stout and unyielding foundation, Teo guides young wanderers to heed the wisdom of the mountains. He warns that while stone serves as an enduring shield, its favor is not given lightly, requiring true grit and deep respect before any secrets of the soil will be shared.

Call of Earth. The Call of Earth is a sacred shamanic rite that binds an initiate's mortal spirit to the enduring foundations of the world. By imbibing the visionary brew known as Earth Sapta at a secluded mountain Spirit Stone, the seeker learns humility, patience, and elemental awareness amid the snow and rock. The Call of Earth is a sacred trial of spiritual attunement, requiring an initiate to drink the enchanted brew known as Earth Sapta at an isolated mountain shrine. Forged through ancient elemental magic, sapta binds the drinker's spirit to the bedrock of the world, granting mortal eyes the rare power to witness elemental spirits and subtle currents invisible to ordinary sight. Because of its potency, the draught must only be consumed in a designated holy site where the bond between spirit and stone can safely take hold.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is an elemental rite of passage for young shaman in the snowy reaches of Dun Morogh. By communing with the local earth spirits, initiates receive a rough quartz to bring to Teo Hammerstorm in Anvilmar. This simple stone proves their communion and serves as the core of their Earth Totem. The Call of Earth marks an initiate's first steps onto the spiritual path of the shaman in Dun Morogh. Deep within the frozen peaks, an aspirant must seek out the spirit of the earth and listen to its teachings. The trial demands humility: the spirit gifts only a rough quartz, a simple pebble intended to become the beating heart of an Earth Totem. It reminds the seeker that true endurance is not measured by sheer scale, but by patience, strength, and unwavering resolve.

Call of Earth. Call of Earth is an introductory summons calling an initiate to attune with the spirits of the stone. Directed to Coldridge Valley, the traveler must seek out Teo Hammerstorm within the dwarven holdfast of Anvilmar. For an initiate walking the path of the elements, the call of earth is the vital first communion. While elemental energies may already stir across the skin, learning to speak directly with stone establishes a steadfast balance. It teaches the spirit how to find immovable strength, setting firm footing beneath one's boots and within the spirit itself.

Call of Fire. This pilgrimage marks the second trial in the shamanic pursuit to commune with fire. Sent by Kranal Fiss from the Barrens, an aspiring shaman carries the unlit Torch of the Dormant Flame to a secluded mountaintop shrine perched high over the Southfury River in Durotar. While an initiate may demonstrate raw mystical strength, fire demands far more than power; it requires temperance, focus, and respect. Kranal Fiss entrusts the shaman with the Torch of the Dormant Flame. The object serves as both ritual instrument and credential, demonstrating to the shrine's keeper that the bearer has been formally judged ready to attempt the trial.

Call of Fire. This trial marks the critical preparation in a shaman's communion with fire, tasking the initiate with gathering the volatile ingredients needed to brew a Fire Sapta. Telf Joolam requires components saturated with heat and magical power: tar from Razormane geomancers and a pouch of dark reagents from Burning Blade cultists hiding in Durotar. To perceive and speak to the spirits of fire, a shaman cannot rely on mortal vision alone. Just as earth required its own draught, opening the senses to the Eternal Flame demands a specialized Fire Sapta. The potion requires reagents innately bound to heat and flame. The hermit Telf Joolam sends initiates across Durotar and into the eastern Barrens to harvest these specific elements from those who wield primal heat and corrupting sorcery.

Call of Fire. This trial marks the critical moment in a shaman's attunement to fire atop the peaks of Durotar. Guided by the hermit Telf Joolam, the initiate must drink a potent fire sapta to perceive and confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire. Slaying the spirit yields a glowing ember, used to kindle the brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame and light the ceremonial torch. Fire spirits rarely linger in plain sight for the uninitiated. To commune with them, a shaman must alter their perception using a fire sapta, an elemental draught steeped from reagents gathered across the barrens and coast. Imbibing the draught opens the senses to the unseen, revealing minor spirits and manifestations dancing across the crags of the summit.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire sends an initiate through the winds of Skywall to seek out Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei Windshaper attuned to the element of fire. By bringing the Torch of Dormant Flame to the Shrine of Flames in the Gustberry Lowlands, the traveler begins learning to heed the call of the flame even within the domain of air. Even within Skywall, the domain ruled by the air elementals, the broader currents of the Elemental Plane remain connected. The spirits of earth, water, and fire still speak to those with the sensitivity to hear them. The Windshapers count among their fellowship individuals uniquely receptive to these other forces, including Olariaan Swiftburn, a shen'dorei who fosters a deep attunement with the element of fire.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest from the Windshapers commanding the execution of Skypriest Faladiel, a former brother who betrayed his order for power. Adventurers must track the rogue skypriest to the Gustberry Lowlands and retrieve his heart to fuel a powerful elemental ritual. Call of Fire tasks adventurers with hunting down Skypriest Faladiel, a former Windshaper who abandoned his loyalties to join the Al'Aketh. Once a dedicated caller of flame, Faladiel chose power over allegiance, turning on his fellow order members and leaving their blood upon his hands. The Windshapers dispatch an agent to deliver their uncompromising judgment upon him.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a quest in which adventurers are tasked by Olariaan Swiftburn to locate and confront the ancient forest sprite Kuramaa in the Shen'dar Highlands. By invoking the sprite from its stump and defeating it with flame, travelers obtain its powerful wooden mask. The relic is then brought to the Gustberry Lowlands to ignite an eternal flame and commune with the spirits of fire. In the Shen'dar Highlands, local residents whisper tales of Kuramaa, an ancient forest sprite that resides inside a twisted tree stump at the summit of a hill near the regional Anchor Pylon. To draw the reclusive entity into the open, a challenger must strike the bark of its wooden home with a bare fist, demanding its presence and testing their mettle in combat.

Call of Fire. Call of Fire is a shamanic rite of passage overseen by the Windshapers within Skywall. Initiates must aid in invoking spirits of flame, capture the Eternal Flame, and race against time to kindle the brazier at Valanaar. Successfully completing the trial proves one's respect for the elements and earns the initiate their Fire Totem. The Call of Fire is a sacred trial of elemental attunement conducted within Skywall. Led by Olariaan of the Windshapers, initiates gather at the Brazier of Offering to invoke the spirits of flame from the Firelands. If the offerings are deemed worthy, the spirits ignite the altar with the sacred Eternal Flame, ready to be harnessed by a worthy aspirant.

Call of Water. This ritualistic step marks the culmination of the shaman's ordeal at the Brazier of Everfount along the coast of Silverpine Forest. Having shattered the corrupt spirits threatening the spring with a burst of elemental radiance, the shaman stands before an apparition of pure water to receive its communion. Upon reciting the final incantation at the Brazier of Everfount, an explosion of light scours the area of surrounding corruption. The hissed protests of tainted water drops evaporating over elemental flame fade, leaving the immediate shore silent as malevolent minor spirits disperse.

Call of Water. This quest offers a second chance for shamans completing their spiritual trials along the coast of Silverpine Forest. If a shaman's spirit-sight fades before communing with the purified manifestation of water, Tiev Mordune stands by to rekindle the communion. By providing another Water Sapta, the petitioner can witness the ritual anew and finish their communion. The path to mastering water is fraught with delicate spiritual timings. Shamans drink a potent draught known as a Water Sapta to perceive the spirits lingering around the elemental shrines. Should the draught's magic lapse before the shaman speaks with the Minor Manifestation of Water, they find themselves locked outside the spirit realm, unable to complete their trial. Fortunately, fellow shaman Tiev Mordune lingers on the fog-shrouded shores of Silverpine Forest to assist those whose visions ended too soon.

Call of Water. Call of Water is an initiation rite that directs rising Horde shaman from the heights of Thunder Bluff toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. To commune with the cleansing element of water, an initiate must seek out the recluse Islen Waterseer. This meeting marks the first step on a spiritual journey to earn the Water Totem. Having mastered the unyielding earth and the untamed flame, an aspiring shaman is eventually deemed ready to study the deeper mysteries of the elements. In Thunder Bluff, trainers like Xanis Flameweaver recognize when a student has shown enough discipline to approach the fluid, cleansing spirit of water. The journey requires leaving the windswept mesas of Mulgore behind and traveling east across the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens.

Call of Water. This leg of the Call of Water journey directs aspiring Horde shaman into the hostile southern reaches of the Barrens. Sent by Islen Waterseer, travelers must locate a hermit named Brine to further their understanding of water's purifying and restorative nature. Before granting access to the water sapta, Islen Waterseer impresses a fundamental truth upon the initiate: water signifies rebirth. Its current can carve rock, cleanse impurities, and mend flesh, yet its healing power relies entirely on its purity. Polluted water brings blight rather than life, a fragile balance every shaman must internalize before attempting to commune with the element.

Call of Water. This quest represents the final gathering trial in a shaman's journey to earn the Call of Water. Directed by the hermit Brine in the southern Barrens, initiates must venture far north into the alien, twilight groves of Ashenvale to collect pure water from the ancient fountain within the Ruins of Stardust. Having gathered samples from both the watering hole below her hut in the Barrens and the pure well of Tarren Mill, the shaman is tasked with finding a third and final essence. Brine sends the initiate across the northern border of the dry plains and into Ashenvale, a dense and ancient woodland held sacred by the night elves. The contrast between the arid Barrens and the deep canopy of Ashenvale underscores the elemental diversity a shaman must understand to truly harmonize with water.

Call of Water. This quest marks the first gathering trial assigned by Brine in the Barrens during a shaman's attunement to water. Seeking to brew a water sapta, Brine directs initiates to fetch a sample from the guarded watering hole below her hut, urging them to contemplate the sacred and contested nature of life-giving water in a desert. Before granting the water sapta needed to commune with the spirits, the hermit Brine requires shaman initiates to study water in all its forms across the world. In the arid Barrens, water is the difference between survival and starvation. Brine bids shamans to observe not just the liquid itself, but the surrounding ecology: how forests flourish in its embrace, how deserts starve in its absence, and how living beings will kill to protect even the humblest spring.

Call of Water. This pilgrimage tasks an aspiring shaman with traveling from the arid Barrens across the sea to the contested Hillsbrad Foothills. There, in the Forsaken-held hamlet of Tarren Mill, lies a small well that has miraculously remained pure despite the surrounding decay. Collecting its water teaches the initiate how purity and hope can endure within even the darkest environments. While preparing reagents for the Water Sapta, the hermit Brine directs initiates far across the sea to Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills. Amidst human resistance and the plague-tainted presence of the newly allied Forsaken, a small well in the center of town remarkably produces pure, untainted spring water. Brine views this spring as a sacred vestige—an island of cleanliness surviving within an unhallowed sea.

Call of Water. This leg of the shamanic trial tasks an initiate with bringing purified water back across the Barrens to Islen Waterseer. Prepared and blessed by the recluse Brine, this vial contains the catalyst required to distill a spiritual sapta. Once brewed, the draught will reveal the elemental spirits dwelling in the distant waters of Silverpine Forest. After trekking across the southern Barrens and fulfilling the trials set by Brine, a shaman initiate receives a Vial of Purest Water. Filled from pristine springs and consecrated by Brine's secluded rites, this vessel represents the pure potential of the element. Carrying it safely back to the eastern coast where Islen Waterseer keeps vigil is the vital link connecting Brine's rustic wisdom with the formal rites of the totem.

Call of Water. Call of Water marks the beginning of a shaman's communion with the fluid element of healing and adaptability. Having already proved their mastery over earth and fire, an initiate is directed by Swart in Razor Hill to seek out the recluse Islen Waterseer on the eastern coast of the Barrens. A shaman's training demands balance. After learning the steadfast resilience of earth and enduring the wild ferocity of fire, initiates are called toward the flowing, adaptable nature of water. In Razor Hill, the orc shaman Swart assesses his students' spiritual growth. When an initiate has proven their command of flame without being consumed by it, Swart recognizes that their spirit is tempered enough to seek out the teachings of water.

Call of Water. This crucial rite of passage directs shamans from the Barrens across the Great Sea to the blighted shores of Silverpine Forest. In order to earn commune with the water spirits, an initiate must confront a corrupted elemental and cleanse an ancient coastal shrine tainted by the Scourge's plague. After securing drops of pure water under the guidance of the hermit Brine, the shaman returns to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast. Islen then tasks the initiate with a far more perilous duty: taking that purified essence across the sea to the haunted coast of Silverpine Forest, situated just west of the Forsaken refuge of the Sepulcher.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is a spiritual quest for shamans ready to commune with the purifying nature of the water element. Having established harmony with wind, earth, and flame, the initiate reaches Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, who urges them to take the first step toward learning water's purity. The Call of Water marks a vital stage in a shaman's journey into elemental balance. With earth grounding every step, the rush of the wind at one's back, and the inner fire burning bright, the traveler is called to grasp the deeper nature of water. It is not merely an external force, but a spiritual reflection of purity and resilience.

Call of Water. Call of Water sends spiritual seekers into the Wetlands to learn the cleansing power of water and seek the water sapta. In a secluded cave beneath the southern falls, the dwarf Hervdana Saegrund greets travelers braving the wilderness. The journey to understand water begins with a simple lesson on its dual nature: water embodies rebirth, carving stone and cleansing impurities when pure, but threatening ruin when tainted. Initiates seeking communion are sent into the wild to obtain a water sapta from those who dwell beside the element.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a spiritual quest in the Wetlands guiding an initiate on the path to earning the sapta. By gathering brackish estuary water where mountain falls meet sea tides, the seeker learns the vital energies of water while navigating the hazards of the marsh. To earn the sapta and commune with the spirits, an initiate must seek water in its various forms. Hervdana guides seekers to observe how water moves, changes lives, and sustains the land. The journey begins with understanding estuary waters where ocean tide meets fresh highland runoff.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a quest tasking travelers with journeying to Stonewatch Falls in Redridge to investigate suspected corruption in the runoff from Lake Everstill. By filling an Empty Red Waterskin and returning it to Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands, shamans uncover the true source behind mutated local murlocs while securing a key reagent for their spiritual trials. Hervdana Saegrund in the Wetlands dispatches aspiring shamans south to Redridge to investigate the waterways tumbling down Stonewatch Falls. While Lake Everstill nourishes the settlement of Lakeshire with pristine water, the murlocs lurking at the base of the cascade have grown into unusually massive, twisted beasts. Suspecting venom, foul sorcery, or seepage from the old fortress above, Hervdana tasks travelers with gathering a sample in an Empty Red Waterskin.

Call of Water. Call of Water tasks an adventurer with journeying into the emerald canopy of Ashenvale to collect pure, ancient water from the lake cradling Astranaar. It marks the final gathering step before the traveler is sent back to Norric. Call of Water charges an adventurer with filling a waterskin from the uncorrupted waters of Ashenvale. The seeker must venture to Astranaar, a haven nestled amidst clean, ancient waters that lap against sunken ruins from a bygone era. This pristine sample serves as the final liquid needed by the questgiver before the traveler is sent on to Norric.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is a spiritual trial for shamans seeking the sacred water totem rites. By delivering pure water blessed by Hervdana to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, seekers prepare the elemental sapta necessary to commune with spirits at Stendel's Pond. The Call of Water represents an essential trial of spiritual attunement for aspiring shamans seeking harmony with the element of water. Undertaking this path requires gathering water blessed by Hervdana herself, proving both patience and reverence for the spirits before bringing the vessel to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan.

Call of Water. Call of Water is an elemental quest requiring a journey from Loch Modan to Westfall to restore balance to a corrupted spring. By purging the tainted entity at Stendel's Pond and performing an ancient ritual at the forgotten shrine, petitioners earn the favor of the water spirits and their Water Totem. In the shadow of Moonbrook lies Stendel's Pond, once celebrated as a clear and pure spring. Dark influences sweeping across Westfall have fouled its tranquil waters, driving the local water spirits into profound silence. An aged shrine stands along the shore, neglected and draped in dust and cobwebs, waiting for someone to awaken the dormant powers within.

Call of Water. Call of Water is a quest centered in Westfall that tasks adventurers with purifying corrupted elemental forces. By unraveling restless spirits with radiant light, players commune with a Minor Manifestation of Water to safeguard the region's dwindling vitality. In the windswept lands of Westfall, the natural balance of the waters faces contamination by corrupt spirits. The rite known as the Call of Water requires confronting this malevolence, invoking sacred words that conjure radiant light to disperse the restless, tainted essences into harmless ash and quiet mist.

Call of Water. The Call of Water is an elemental rite of passage where shamans learn to commune with water spirits and wield their restorative powers. By retrieving a Shard of Water from Westfall for Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan, initiates prove their dedication and receive their water totem. The Call of Water is a vital spiritual trial undertaken by shamans to forge a bond with the element of water. Initiates are tasked with journeying to Westfall and returning to Norric Lochthane in Loch Modan with the Shard of Water. By demonstrating their understanding of water's life-giving essence and its role in purging corruption, shamans earn their water totem and take an essential step on their elemental journey.

Call of Water. This task marks the culmination of the shaman's arduous pilgrimage to attune with the element of water. By returning a purified Shard of Water to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast, an initiate proves their harmony with restorative energies and earns their Water Totem. The quest for water requires an initiate to cross continents, traveling as far as the tainted shores of Silverpine Forest to confront corruption directly. Water represents life, adaptability, and healing, but its pliable nature leaves it uniquely vulnerable to blight and dark magic. After standing before the Minor Manifestation of Water and bearing witness to pure elemental will, the initiate is entrusted with a singular gift: the Shard of Water. Carrying this token back across the sea to the sun-scorched Barrens is a physical reminder that water connects all distant corners of the world.

Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde military initiative directed by Drum Fel from the outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Threatened by an alliance between the local Witherbark forest trolls and Boulderfist ogres, the Horde launches a preemptive campaign against the Witherbark to secure their foothold in the region. From the fortified sanctuary of Hammerfall, Drum Fel organizes a preemptive military strike against the hostile native powers of the Arathi Highlands. Surrounded by old human ruins and aggressive local factions, the Horde settlement faces an imminent threat from a cooperative pact formed between the indigenous Witherbark forest trolls and the brute Boulderfist ogres. Rather than allowing their enemies to dictate the terms of survival, Drum Fel calls on champions to take the offensive.

Call to Arms. Call to Arms is a Horde martial trial issued by Drum Fel at the Hammerfall outpost in the Arathi Highlands. Having proven their basic combat readiness, adventurers are ordered southwest toward the dwarven bridge to engage the dangerous Boulderfist ogres. Eliminating both front-line brutes and spellcasting magi tests the warrior's resolve while protecting the Horde's vulnerable foothold in Arathi. At the isolated Horde redoubt of Hammerfall, survival demands unwavering martial strength. Drum Fel, recognizing the growing capabilities of travelers aiding the outpost, refuses to let anyone rest on easy victories. Rather than facing minor skirmishers, warriors must prove their mettle against what Fel considers a genuine threat: the hulking Boulderfist ogres. These brutes have consistently harassed the Horde expedition and tested the resolve of Hammerfall’s defenders. Fel offers simple terms for the task—warriors are expected to return successful in flesh or honorably in spirit, with praise promised for sheer tenacity in battle.

Call to Arms. Following the previous Call to Arms, Drum Fel at Hammerfall declares that it is time to strike the head from the beast. He sends you after the Boulderfist lords and shaman who lair in the ruins of Stromgarde. Drum Fel says you have proven able enough to help deliver one last great blow. Those leading the attacks have made their lair in the ruins of Stromgarde, which he calls a symbol of human frailty. Hunt down the Boulderfist lords and the shaman who serve them, for they would try to drive the Horde out of these lands.

Calling in the Reserves. "Calling in the Reserves" is a Horde courier task entrusted to adventurers resting at Sun Rock Retreat. Maggran Earthbinder sends you south to the edge of the Barrens with orders to relieve an exhausted sentry watching the Great Lift. Even in an era of relative prosperity following the Third War, maintaining garrisons across central Kalimdor tests the Horde's resources. At Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains, Maggran Earthbinder oversees logistics and troop welfare. Recognizing that seasoned soldiers wear thin under endless watch duty, Maggran dispatches a letter of reassignment south to the Great Lift, where a young sentry named Grish Longrunner has been standing guard far from home.

text.enUS: Calm Before the Storm. After the queen's fall, Alchemist Pestlezugg wants the latest findings to reach people who can act on them. You carry the Un'Goro report to Gracina Spiritmight at the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Pestlezugg says that the findings of the day must reach hands that might do something with them, since Gadgetzan cannot manage alone. The latest report is to go to Gracina Spiritmight in Darnassus, whom Pestlezugg hopes can be found at the Temple of the Moon. She has friends among the Alliance bigwigs, and if they can be drawn in, there may be a way through this alive.

text.enUS: Calm Before the Storm. After the queen's fall, Alchemist Pestlezugg wants the latest findings to reach people who can act on them. You carry Pestlezugg's report on Un'Goro to Zilzibin Drumlore in Orgrimmar. Pestlezugg says that the findings of the day must reach hands that might do something with them, since Gadgetzan cannot manage alone. The latest report is to go to Zilzibin Drumlore in Orgrimmar, who Pestlezugg expects is still in the upper part of the Drag. Zilzibin has friends high in the Horde, and if they can be drawn in, there may be a way through this alive.

Calmbreeze Inn. Calmbreeze Inn refers to the primary establishments offering shelter and services across Zephras Isle, found in both Shen'dar Village and Valaanar. They serve as essential rest stops for travelers exploring the island, housing local trade trainers, innkeepers, and historical artifacts. The Calmbreeze Inns provide sanctuary amid the winding trails of Zephras Isle. In Shen'dar Village, the inn operates under Coriella Calmbreeze and doubles as a central hub where island tradesfolk gather, including mentors in herbalism, skinning, and enchanting. Across the way in Valaanar, another Calmbreeze Inn accommodates local wayfarers and shelters rare curios, including an audio crystal recording the history of the ancient rebellion in Eldre'Thalas.

Calor. Calor is a dedicated resident of Darkshire who aids the Carevin family in defending Duskwood. Operating under the direction of Jonathan Carevin, he actively coordinates efforts to hunt down the vicious worgen stalking the gloomy forests. Adventurers looking to push back the ravenous beasts haunting the woods often find their assignments through him. Stationed within the beleaguered settlement of Darkshire, Calor works closely with Jonathan Carevin, one of the town's prominent defenders. Amid the endless gloom and creeping terrors of Duskwood, Calor devotes himself to supporting the Carevin household's mission: eradicating the supernatural horrors encroaching upon the town's perimeter before the remaining townsfolk are slaughtered.

Calor's Note. Calor's Note is a scrap of faded parchment written by the woodsman Calor to recommend a tested adventurer to Master Jonathan Carevin. It serves as an introduction into a shadowy cadre operating alongside, yet distinct from, Darkshire's formal town militia. Duskwood offers very little warmth to strangers, and Calor is notoriously hard to impress. Surviving encounters with the bloodthirsty worgen stalking the woods earns his respect, prompting him to draft this brief message. Carried to Darkshire, the faded note acts as a badge of credibility, introducing an outsider directly to Jonathan Carevin.

Calvin Montague. Calvin Montague is an opportunistic Forsaken rogue loitering near the exit gate of Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. Preying on newly awakened undead as they leave the graveyard, he attempts to trick passersby into running errands on his behalf. Positioned just outside the gates leading away from Deathknell, Calvin Montague embodies the ruthless pragmatism common among Lordaeron's restless dead. Rather than handling his own correspondence or paying fair courier rates, he attempts to smooth-talk wandering adventurers into delivering letters under false pretenses. While several other prominent undead bearing the Montague family name manage banking interests within the Undercity, Calvin pursues a decidedly less reputable trade, preferring petty schemes and deception.

Camp Aparaje. Camp Aparaje was once a peaceful tauren village nestled in the eastern heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. Today, it lies overrun and occupied by the hostile Grimtotem tribe, who slaughtered the original settlers and took the outpost for themselves. Perched along the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains, Camp Aparaje was established by peaceful tauren looking to live quietly in the highlands. That tranquility was shattered when raiders from the nearby Grimtotem Post, led by Grundig Darkcloud, launched a brutal and unprovoked assault. The villagers were butchered or driven away, and survivors such as Makaba Flathoof were left mourning the destruction of their home while dreading the fate of captive kin.

Camp E'thok. Camp E'thok is a Galak centaur settlement located in northwestern Thousand Needles. The aggressive centaur tribe uses this canyon encampment as a base to stage ambushes against passing caravans traveling through the riverbed below. Tucked into the rugged northwestern reaches of Thousand Needles, Camp E'thok serves as a key settlement for the hostile Galak centaur. Like their kin across Kalimdor, the Galak are relentlessly predatory, preying upon any travelers wandering into the canyon shadows. The camp is notorious for orchestrating raids against merchant caravans, notably ambushing the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner and seizing his goods—though his prized gadget managed to slip beyond their grasp, guarded by his fierce pet panther.

Camp Kosh. Camp Kosh is an ogre encampment in the northern Badlands, inhabited by the aggressive Dustbelcher ogres. Perched near vital travel routes, its brutes prey on passing caravans and scavenge whatever equipment travelers leave behind in the harsh desert. Situated in the northern wastes of the Badlands, Camp Kosh serves as the northernmost settlement of the Dustbelcher ogres, who also occupy neighboring camps like Boff, Cagg, and Wurg. The ogres stationed here take advantage of their proximity to the roads, raiding vulnerable supply lines journeying toward Kargath or westward into the Searing Gorge. When dwarven prospectors led by Sigrun Ironhew were forced to flee the excavation at Uldaman, the brutes of Camp Kosh swiftly raided their abandoned wagons, hauling away precious food rations and armaments into the dusty encampment.

Camp Mojache. Camp Mojache is the primary Horde outpost in Feralas, established as a fortified tauren settlement along the waters feeding Wildwind Lake. It provides shelter, provisions, and flight connections to travelers contending with the untamed wilderness, aggressive wildlife, and ancient ruins of the deep forest. Situated in eastern Feralas along a swift-flowing stream that feeds Wildwind Lake, Camp Mojache is a tauren settlement built to secure a foothold in the wild southern forest. While the dense jungle holds perilous threats—from savage wildlife to Gordunni ogres and aggressive Woodpaw gnolls—the camp stands as an island of safety. Equipped with lodging, trade masters, and a wind rider roost, it serves as the vital logistical hub for Horde champions operating in the region.

Camp Taurajo. Camp Taurajo is a quiet tauren settlement nestled in the southern Barrens, sitting right along the mountain pass leading west into Mulgore. It serves as a vital frontier haven, offering tired wanderers an inn, supplies, profession mentors, and wind rider transit between the plains and central Kalimdor. Situated at the eastern mouth of the pass to Mulgore, Camp Taurajo is often the first glimpse of the wider Barrens seen by young tauren venturing out from Bloodhoof Village. Surrounded by dry scrubland and rugged mesas, the camp operates as both an outpost and a trading hub. It shelters hunters, leathercrafters, and field herbalists while maintaining wind rider connections to Thunder Bluff, the Crossroads, and Freewind Post deeper south.

Camp Wurg. Camp Wurg is an ogre encampment situated in the arid expanse of the Badlands. It serves as one of several outposts claimed by the territorial Dustbelcher ogres who dominate much of the Badlands. Tucked among the crags of the Badlands, Camp Wurg is one of four primary camps settled by the Dustbelcher ogres, alongside Camp Cagg, Camp Boff, and Camp Kosh. The ogres stationed here guard their rugged territory fiercely, scavenging what they can from the unforgiving desert wastes. While rank-and-file brutes and enforcers dwell around the crude fires and rough hides of Wurg, their chieftain, Boss Tho'grun, maintains no permanent seat here, instead roaming the Badlands trails to keep watch over all his encampments.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking teaches budding adventurers that cooking is the fundamental cornerstone of establishing a camp in the wild. By learning the craft from Cook Tomas in Goldshire, travelers acquire the ability to build campfires and pitch their own wilderness camps. For any adventurer braving the wilds of Azeroth, setting up camp begins with a reliable blaze. The quest Camping 101: Cooking instructs novice wanderers that culinary training is not merely about preparing hot meals; it is the vital foundation for survival in the wilderness. By mastering the cooking profession, travelers learn how to strike a proper campfire, turning an untamed clearing into a safe refuge.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking introduces adventurers in Dun Morogh to the essential survival skill of cooking. Beyond preparing provisions, learning this trade enables travelers to light campfires that serve as the foundation for wilderness campsites. For any traveler braving the wilds, establishing a reliable campsite begins with a flame. In Dun Morogh, novice adventurers are directed to Kharanos to learn the fundamentals of cooking under Gremlock Pilsnor. Cooking is not simply about sustaining oneself with hot meals on the road; a sturdy campfire serves as the literal and practical anchor for any outdoor camp.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers on the essentials of wilderness camping through the art of cooking. By learning to start a campfire from local trainers like Zarrin in Dolanaar, travelers establish the necessary anchor for setting up wilderness camps. It marks the first step toward mastering outdoor survival and outfitting personal campsites. Every long journey across the wilderness begins with the ability to build a warm fire. In Camping 101: Cooking, fledgling adventurers are directed to seek out culinary training as their initial lesson in bushcraft. Learning to cook is more than preparing meals from wild game; the essential skill of lighting a basic campfire serves as the physical and practical anchor for any outdoor camp. Without a fire to ward off the chill and keep the dark at bay, establishing a reliable campsite in the wilds is impossible.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that teaches adventurers the culinary arts as the vital foundation for wilderness survival. By learning to start a campfire from Zerril Softbreeze in Shen'dar Village, travelers unlock the ability to pitch their own campsites in the wild. For an adventurer traveling across untamed lands, understanding survival begins with the hearth. Camping 101: Cooking introduces wanderers to the art of culinary craft, not merely for preparing meals, but because mastering a basic fire is the essential first step to establishing a safe resting spot in the wild.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking introduces adventurers to the essential craft of survival in the wilderness. By directing travelers to Cook Torka in Razor Hill, it teaches the fundamentals of cooking and campfire creation necessary to establish personal campsites in the wild. For any wanderer setting foot beyond settlement gates, surviving the wilderness requires more than sharp steel and sturdy armor. The quest Camping 101: Cooking directs budding adventurers to Cook Torka in Razor Hill to learn the culinary arts. In the open wastes of Durotar and beyond, cooking represents far more than preparing a hot meal—it is the foundational discipline required to light a reliable campfire, which serves as the heart of any campsite.

Camping 101: Cooking. At nearby settlements, new adventurers learn to cook and kindle a Basic Campfire for life in the wild. The lesson is offered across Alliance and Horde lands. Every traveler needs to know how to build a fire beyond the safety of fortified walls. A campfire can boil water and roast meat, and it anchors a campsite in unfamiliar country.

Camping 101: Cooking. Camping 101: Cooking is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers on how basic culinary knowledge forms the foundation of establishing a campsite in the wilderness. By seeking out Pyall Silentstride in Bloodhoof Village, travelers learn to build a campfire to anchor their camp and prepare for life on the frontier. Every long journey through the untamed wilds demands basic wilderness survival, and every true camp begins with fire. For wanderers stepping across Kalimdor, the quest Camping 101: Cooking introduces the essential relationship between culinary training and frontier survival. Cooking is not merely about preparing nourishing meals from hunted game; it provides the fundamental knowledge needed to build a working campfire out in the elements. Without a fire, an adventurer has no camp to return to when night falls.

name.frFR: Introduction au camping : les premiers soins

text.enUS: Camping 101: First Aid. This task directs novice medics in Dun Morogh to expand their survival craft beyond simple bandages. By seeking out Thamner Pol in Kharanos, adventurers learn how to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit to keep campers alive in the field. Adventurers braving the frozen reaches of Dun Morogh quickly discover that linen scraps and hasty stitches are only the beginning of survival medicine. True wilderness survival often depends on having established supplies at a resting site. Those who show aptitude in basic treatment are steered toward local craft instructors in Kharanos who can teach them how to turn raw medical supplies into complete kits tailored for camp survival.

Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid is an instructional quest that sends skilled travelers to Rawrk in Razor Hill, who teaches them how to craft their own First Aid Kit for wilderness survival. It emphasizes the necessities of self-reliance on the trail, reminding adventurers to master campfire creation and respect local settlements by camping out in the wild. Survival in the untamed expanses of Durotar and beyond requires more than just raw martial strength; it demands self-sufficiency on the trail. In Razor Hill, Rawrk offers instruction to capable wanderers seeking to fashion essential wilderness gear. Through Camping 101: First Aid, practitioners who have proven their basic proficiency learn to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit, giving them the means to mend wounds and tend to injuries far from the safety of an apothecary or infirmary.

name.frFR: Introduction au camping : les premiers soins

text.enUS: Camping 101: First Aid. At the Lion's Pride Inn, Michelle Belle shows travelers how to prepare for camp. In Goldshire, you can learn to make a First Aid Kit for the road ahead. Travel across Elwynn Forest can leave you wounded, far from a town healer or inn. First Aid lets you tend your own injuries and care for yourself without relying on others. Bandages offer help with bleeding and trauma, without arcane rituals or holy supplication.

Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid introduces adventurers to wilderness survival by teaching them how to craft a field medical kit for their campsite. Instructed by Byancie in Dolanaar, it emphasizes self-reliance and practical triage far away from town clinics. Venturing deep into the wilds carries constant hazard, from beast bites to jagged terrain. For rangers and field travelers, medical supplies cannot always wait for a return to town. Learning to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit turns a simple roadside rest into a functional field station, ensuring that minor scrapes do not turn fatal under the open sky.

Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid directs adventurers with medical training to seek out Nurse Neela in Brill. By learning to construct a First Aid Kit for their campsites, travelers can provide life-saving treatment and recuperation while surviving deep in the wilderness. Venturing beyond fortified settlements carries constant physical danger, from hostile beasts to opposing factions. For traveling practitioners of First Aid, learning to assemble a dedicated First Aid Kit allows an ordinary wilderness resting stop to serve as a mobile field clinic, patching up wounds and restoring vitality far from civil infrastructure.

Camping 101: First Aid. Camping 101: First Aid directs travelers to Shen'dar Village to learn how to fashion essential medical supplies for a wilderness camp. By seeking out Naleeia Tattermend, skilled practitioners can create camp kits capable of treating injuries and saving lives far from civilization. Life on the road across Azeroth is fraught with violence, wild beasts, and environmental hazards. For any traveler, learning First Aid is as practical as it is honorable, ensuring that bloodied cuts and broken bones can be bound without relying purely on spellcraft. Establishing a dedicated First Aid Kit at a wilderness camp provides a reliable center for healing, allowing exhausted adventurers to recover and tend to their companions before moving on.

Camping 101: Fishing. Camping 101: Fishing guides outdoorsmen in the essential crafts and etiquette of wilderness survival. It teaches adventurers how to create a decorative Fish Bowl for their campsite and emphasizes the necessity of learning campfire craft from a cooking trainer before heading into the wild. Life on the road across Azeroth demands practical knowledge of the frontier. For aspiring anglers and wanderers, setting up an orderly site requires understanding basic outdoor etiquette. Townsfolk and guards frown upon travelers pitching tents and scattering gear in the center of settlements, so anyone wishing to rest must take their supplies out beyond city borders and into the open wilderness.

Camping 101: Fishing. In Elwynn Forest, novice anglers seek ways to make camp life more comfortable. Near Goldshire, fishing expert Lee Brown teaches travelers how angling can add simple comforts to a campsite. Fishing gives you food, but camp life asks for more than food and shelter. A fish bowl can bring comfort and lift the spirits of weary travelers between excursions. Sound minds and high spirits help make formidable fighters.

Camping 101: Fishing. Camping 101: Fishing directs aspiring anglers to discover how their patience with a rod and line can elevate wilderness expeditions. By seeking out Fenn Fairweather in Shen'dar Village, proficient fishermen can learn to craft a decorative Fish Bowl fixture to bolster morale and camp comfort. Life in the wilderness demands more than sharp blades and sturdy armor; keeping morale high in the field can mean the difference between triumph and exhaustion. While fishing is often treated purely as a quiet pastime or a means to harvest provisions, skilled anglers can turn their craft toward improving campsite comfort. By capturing live fish and preparing dedicated fixtures, a traveler can transform a bleak encampment into a welcoming sanctuary.

Camping 101: Herbalism. Camping 101: Herbalism is a training quest that directs skilled gatherers to seek specialized wilderness instruction in Elwynn Forest. Upon demonstrating proficiency in harvesting flora, herbalists are pointed toward Herbalist Pomeroy to learn the art of crafting campsite utilities. Completing this training unlocks the ability to create Incense Candles, botanical aids designed to bolster the focus and spirits of spellcasters resting in the field. For wandering herbalists, harvesting herbs across the wilds of Azeroth serves purposes well beyond brewing basic restorative draughts or selling bundles of flowers to city merchants. As practitioners hone their gathering craft, opportunities arise to apply their floral knowledge toward wilderness survival. Field camps require more than just a roaring fire and dry bedroll; maintaining the endurance and mental acuity of a traveling party demands specialized comforts. Experienced foragers recognize that certain plants hold aromatic properties capable of invigorating weary minds. By directing promising herbalists toward established mentors, this task bridges simple gathering with practical fieldcraft, proving that a keen eye for nature's bounty can sustain an entire expedition far from civilization.

Camping 101: Herbalism. Camping 101: Herbalism directs budding herbalists to local profession trainers across Azeroth, such as Faruza in Brill, to master the craft of Incense Candles. These aromatic creations provide vital restorative aid to spellcasters resting in wilderness camps. While herbalism is commonly seen as the groundwork for alchemy, practical field survival relies just as heavily on gathered roots and blossoms. Experienced travelers point aspiring foragers toward regional master herbalists to learn how to prepare Incense Candles. In the Tirisfal Glades, Eleanor Shackleton directs promising foragers to visit Faruza in Brill once they demonstrate fundamental skill.

Camping 101: Leatherworking. Camping 101: Leatherworking directs apprentice leatherworkers to Adele Fielder in Goldshire to learn the craft of making a travel tent. Pitching a tent in the wild offers shelter and rest against harsh weather, providing adventurers a vital survival tool outside settled towns. For an adventurer wandering far beyond town gates, shelter is as vital as armor. Leatherworkers in Elwynn Forest are directed to Adele Fielder in Goldshire to expand their craft beyond simple belts and tunics. Once a crafter demonstrates proficiency with hide and needle, Adele shares the practical art of assembling a durable camp tent designed to withstand harsh weather on long overland expeditions.

Camping 101: Leatherworking. Camping 101: Leatherworking directs fledgling leatherworkers to seek advanced instruction on crafting durable wilderness shelters. Guided to Indari Sunseam in Shen'dar Village, craftsmen learn to stitch protective tents that offer essential rest across long expeditions into the wilds. For traveling leatherworkers, the ability to work hide and pelt into durable wilderness gear is vital. Upon learning the craft, tradesfolk are directed to seek out Indari Sunseam in Shen'dar Village to learn how to fashion a proper camping tent. Such shelters keep adventurers dry during relentless downpours and cool beneath blazing suns, ensuring they stay well-rested throughout long journeys.

Camping 101: Mining. Camping 101: Mining is an instructional trade quest directing budding miners to Krunn in Razor Hill. By demonstrating proficiency in their trade, miners learn to forge a Lodestone, a specialized camp fixture that enhances the combat prowess of warriors gathered around a wilderness fire. Mining offers an honest living that provides practical materials for exploration and survival in the wild. As miners develop their trade and demonstrate proficiency with pick and ore, they can learn to craft specialized campsite equipment. In Durotar, skilled miners are pointed toward Krunn in the settlement of Razor Hill to discover how to forge a Lodestone for their travels.

Camping 101: Mining. Camping 101: Mining is an introductory quest that teaches miners how to craft a lodestone to enhance wilderness campsites. Instructed by Gelman Stonehand in Stormwind, prospectors learn to channel resonant earthcraft to bolster their companions' combat prowess around the campfire. Mining is tough, honest labor, but its rewards go far beyond smelting raw ingots and shaping armor. Dedicated miners in Stormwind can learn to harness the natural magnetism of the earth into a functional lodestone. When placed at an expedition's campsite, this stone bolsters the combat vigor of any fighter gathered around the hearth fire. Gelman Stonehand, the seasoned mining instructor in the kingdom's capital, passes down the craft to prospectors who demonstrate proficiency with a pickaxe.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory quest that instructs adventurers in the art of fashioning wilderness furnishings from harvested animal pelts. It directs skilled skinners to Balthus Stoneflayer in Ironforge to learn how to craft a comfortable Camp Chair for their campsite. Skinning fallen beasts is among the most practical disciplines an adventurer can cultivate while traversing the wilds of Azeroth. Beyond supplying raw leather for armorers and crafters, the hides gathered from predatory cats, bears, and beasts can be repurposed directly in the field. This introductory task directs skinners to transform raw materials into practical wilderness amenities rather than simply selling them off.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory wilderness quest directing skinners in Orgrimmar to Thuwd to learn how to craft a Camp Chair. By putting harvested hides to use for field comfort, adventurers can establish proper campsites out in the wilds of Kalimdor. Harvesting the pelts and hides of fallen beasts is one of the most practical survival skills an adventurer can cultivate in the wild. While raw leathers usually feed armorcraft, skilled skinners can also turn their harvested pelts into field comforts. In Orgrimmar, instructors direct capable skinners to Thuwd to learn the craft of assembling a sturdy Camp Chair from cured hides.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory instruction task for proficient skinners traveling through Elwynn Forest. It directs adventurers to Helene Peltskinner in Goldshire to learn how to fashion a Camp Chair out of harvested hides. Learning to craft personal camp furnishings allows wilderness travelers to rest and recuperate far beyond the safety of settled towns. For wilderness hunters and scouts, the art of harvesting beast hides provides more than trade goods and armor scraps. Seasoned skinners can fashion field amenities like a Camp Chair, allowing travelers to sit, rest their limbs, and maintain peak physical condition during long treks through dangerous lands. Helene Peltskinner in Goldshire instructs proficient skinners on how to turn raw beast pelts into comfortable campsite seating.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning guides skilled hide-gatherers to Bloodhoof Village to expand their practical field craft. Under the instruction of Yonn Deepcut, skinners learn to fashion beast pelts into comfortable Camp Chairs for wilderness survival. This training emphasizes the importance of rest and preparation when journeying far beyond the safety of civilization. Harvesting the hides and pelts of fallen beasts is one of the most practical survival skills on Azeroth. Beyond tanning leather for armor and gear, a resourceful skinner can turn rough animal skins into wilderness comforts. For travelers who spend long weeks traversing wild territories, learning how to work hides into resting equipment makes the difference between exhaustion and staying sharp in combat.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning instructs wilderness travelers on how to craft their own portable Camp Chair. It emphasizes the fundamentals of outdoor survival, reminding adventurers that a proper campsite requires venturing away from town and starting a campfire. Camping 101: Skinning introduces outdoorsmen and skinners to the craft of wilderness survival. By putting harvested hides and materials to practical use, travelers learn to construct a portable Camp Chair for their journeys. Rather than cluttering bustling city centers where locals object to pitched camps, adventurers are expected to take their craft out into the open wilds of Azeroth.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning is an introductory wilderness instruction given to novice gatherers in Tirisfal Glades and across Azeroth. It directs skinners who have practiced their trade to regional craftsmen to learn how to fashion a durable camp chair out of harvested hides. Survival in the wilds demands more than a sharp blade; it requires knowing how to husband your strength between trials. Adventurers like Eleanor Shackleton emphasize that harvesting beast pelts provides more than raw trade goods. By developing basic field proficiency, skinners can fashion essential camp comforts like chairs out of treated skins, allowing weary wanderers to rest and recover properly before their next perilous encounter.

Camping 101: Skinning. Camping 101: Skinning instructs adventurers in turning harvested pelts into a functional Camp Chair for field camps. Guided by Mendalass Tattermend in Shen'dar Village, skinners learn to combine their harvesting craft with wilderness survival and campfire relaxation. Harvesting hides from fallen beasts is an essential survival skill across Azeroth, but its utility extends far beyond simple armor crafting. Through Camping 101: Skinning, gatherers learn to direct their trade toward wilderness survival by crafting a portable Camp Chair. Taking time to rest upon a comfortable seat out in the wilds allows weary adventurers to regain their strength and remain in peak fighting condition before their next battle.

Canaga Earthcaller. Canaga Earthcaller is a Darkspear troll shaman stationed in the sunbaked Valley of Trials. He instructs novice Horde shamans in communing with the spirits of the land and obtaining their first elemental totems. Perched on the red bluffs of the Valley of Trials, Canaga Earthcaller serves as one of the very first spiritual guides for Darkspear trolls and orcs who walk the path of the shaman. While many trainers focus strictly on martial readiness, Canaga teaches newcomers how to quiet their minds and listen to the rumblings of Kalimdor itself, preparing the earth sapta necessary to commune with the spirits.

Canals (Stormwind City). Stormwind's Canals wind between the city's districts, where walkers and anglers share the waterside paths. You can follow the Canals between Stormwind's districts, from the Trade District's markets to Old Town's aged alleys, the cathedral gardens, and the Dwarven District. Stone bridges, archways, and waterside walks pass the Gallina Winery, tailor shops, and quiet homes. Merchants and fishermen use the waterways, while the fortified Stockade entrance lies beneath the streets, holding Stormwind's most dangerous criminals and rebels.

Canals (Undercity). The Canals form a murky, circular moat winding between the distinct quarters of the Undercity. Filled with an unnatural, noxious green slime rather than fresh water, they serve as both a sewage system and a grim symbol of the Forsaken's subterranean stronghold. Carved into the subterranean depths beneath the ruins of Lordaeron, the Canals encircle the heart of the Undercity, dividing its quarters with wide channels of sluggish green sludge. While mortal cities channel flowing river water to clean their avenues, the Forsaken have filled these stone conduits with industrial refuse, chemical runoff, and alchemical waste. The liquid emits a faint, sickly glow and foul vapors, making it impossible to traverse by ordinary magical means like water walking. Despite the lethality of the slurry, desperate anglers occasionally haul bizarre, tainted curiosities from the muck.

Candle of Beckoning. The Candle of Beckoning is an enchanted ritual taper kept by the reclusive necromancer Gunther Arcanus on Brightwater Lake. Placing and lighting the candle upon an altar on a nearby islet summons forth a restless spirit known as Lillith Nefara. Found stored in a crate beside the solitary mage Gunther Arcanus on his island in Brightwater Lake, the Candle of Beckoning serves as an instrument in a dark ritual of summoning. Gunther is a fiercely independent undead sorcerer who broke free of the Lich King's command on his own, remaining wary of the Scourge and the Forsaken alike. To prove your loyalty is not to the Lich King, Gunther directs you to take one of these candles southwest to a smaller islet. There, set upon an old, bloodstained table, the candle's flame pierces the veil between worlds to awaken and beckon the dormant shade of Lillith Nefara, a powerful Scourge agent, so she may be destroyed.

Candles of Beckoning. Candles of Beckoning is a brief task centered around salvaging specialized ritual tapers discovered in Tirisfal Glades. These eerie tallow candles are steeped in dark practices and recovered from a crate on Gunther's Retreat, Gunther Arcanus's island in Brightwater Lake. The crate on Gunther's Retreat supplies the Candle of Beckoning used in his test of allegiance. Gunther asks an adventurer to take a candle to the old, bloody altar just off the island's southern coast, light it, and confront the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara.

Cannibalistic Cousins. Mystic Yayo'jin of Revantusk Village calls the Vilebranch trolls a depraved lot who prey on other trolls and humanoids. With Zul'jin not there to destroy them, she asks you to destroy their Scalpers and Soothsayers near the temples in the north by northeast. Three tribes of trolls live in the Hinterlands, and Mystic Yayo'jin says that apart from being trolls in the same land, they have little in common. She calls the Vilebranch, aptly named, a depraved lot who prey on other trolls and humanoids. Zul'jin would have wiped them out with ease, but Zul'jin is not there, and the Revantusk are left to their own devices.

Cantation of Manifestation. The Cantation of Manifestation is a specialized arcane incantation written on a parchment scroll, used by mages to reveal unseen magical anomalies. In the Undercity, Anastasia Hartwell provides it to apprentices investigating invisible magical entities haunting Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium. The Cantation of Manifestation holds a focused spell designed to pierce magical veils and force incorporeal, invisible beings into the visible spectrum. Kept in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity near Anastasia Hartwell, the scroll is entrusted to capable mages tasked with containing rogue magical anomalies. When read aloud in an area suffering from arcane instability—such as Algernon's alchemical workshop in the Apothecarium—the words force stray rift spawns to materialize, allowing the caster to subdue and trap them within containment coffers for further study.

Canvas Scraps. Canvas Scraps are remnants of tough woven fabric carried by human invaders and centaur tribes encroaching upon Durotar. In Razor Hill, aging veteran Furl Scornbrow collects these salvaged swatches to stitch useful travel sacks for fresh Horde recruits. Canvas is not a fabric native to the rough hide-working traditions of the Orcs, but it is abundant among Durotar's enemies. The Kul Tiras marines and sailors entrenched along the eastern shoreline carry heavy canvas gear and sailcloth remnants from their naval excursions. Further inland, the roaming Kolkar centaur repurpose scraps of coarse cloth looted from supply caravans and past conflicts. Defeating these hostiles yields durable remnants that can be salvaged from their camps and gear.

Cape of Stranglethorn. The Cape of Stranglethorn forms the sun-baked southern tip of Stranglethorn Vale, stretching south from the Gurubashi Arena down to the ocean cliffs. Anchored by the sprawling pirate port of Booty Bay, the region is a battleground contested by goblins, Bloodsail Buccaneers, ancient jungle trolls, and encroaching wildlife. South of the ancient colosseum of Gurubashi Arena, the dense jungle gives way to the coastline known as the Cape of Stranglethorn. Dotted with crumbling troll settlements like the Ruins of Jubuwal and the Ruins of Aboraz, the cape has long since slipped from imperial Gurubashi control. Today, its beaches, coves, and jungle clearings host a chaotic mix of dangerous predators, murloc encampments, and rival pirate crews warring over trade routes and buried plunder.

Capital Gardens. The Capital Gardens form the western wing of the ancient elven ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Once a serene, manicured park for the Kaldorei nobility, it has withered into a blighted woodland stalked by corrupted ancients, ghosts, and remnants of the Shen'dralar. Ten millennia ago, Eldre'Thalas stood as one of the shining jewels of the Kaldorei empire. The Capital Gardens served as its outdoor district, lush with enchanted flora and grand marble terraces where Highborne sorcerers debated and relaxed. Following the Great Sundering, the enclave fell on desperate times. Deprived of the Well of Eternity, the resident Shen'dralar turned to dark magic to sustain their immortality, letting the gardens wither away. Today, gray, twisted boughs and corrupted treants fill the broken courtyards, while residual magical corruption prevents the forest from ever truly healing.

Captain Danuvin. At Sentinel Hill, Captain Danuvin helps hold Westfall's frontier together. He works with the People's Militia, directing volunteers and recruits to patrol roads and drive back Gnolls and outlaws. His orders protect the supply lines and farmlands from hostile hands. Captain Danuvin coordinates patrols from Sentinel Hill's fortified tower. Stormwind's regular garrison has withdrawn, leaving Westfall's defenses badly weakened. He depends on travelers, farmhands, and volunteer fighters to keep some order across the plains.

Captain Grayson. At Westfall Lighthouse, Captain Grayson keeps watch over the beacon that failed him. His ship smashed against the dark coastline, and now he tends the light so other sailors will not meet his fate. Captain Grayson once sailed the southern seas of the Eastern Kingdoms as a ship’s captain. One night, the lighthouse fire went dark as his vessel neared Westfall’s jagged shoals. The ship struck the rocks, and Grayson died with it. He awoke as an earthbound phantom, trapped upon the coast.

Captain Greenskin. Captain Greenskin is an elite goblin pirate overseeing the construction and crew of Edwin VanCleef's massive ironclad juggernaut. Hidden deep in the subterranean cove of the Deadmines, he commands the pirate forces hired by the Defias Brotherhood. His goal is to bring the warship to readiness to sail against Stormwind. Pacing the main deck of the gigantic juggernaut under construction in the Deadmines cove, Captain Greenskin represents the naval backbone of the Defias conspiracy. A seasoned goblin mariner, Greenskin was brought into Edwin VanCleef's inner circle to turn an underground cavern into a drydock for an engine of war.

Captain Rugelfuss. Captain Rugelfuss is a stern dwarven officer stationed at the southern gate in the Valley of Kings. Tasked with securing the border of Loch Modan, he organizes the defense against a sudden and aggressive trogg uprising. Positioned near the monumental carved arches of the Valley of Kings, Captain Rugelfuss oversees the southern gateway into Loch Modan. With Alliance forces stretched thin across the world, Ironforge relies on veteran officers like him to keep the home territories secure. Rugelfuss dismisses military pomp and formalities, preferring to focus entirely on the grim reality facing the border.

name.esES: El tesoro escondido del capitán Sanders
name.frFR: Le trésor caché du capitaine Sanders

text.enUS: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A battered parchment map sets Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure in motion along Westfall's coast. The hunt begins with a search of the shoreline for the late captain's personal footlocker, then leads toward his hidden plunder across the region. Shipwrecks and the restless spirits of drowned sailors mark Westfall's western coast. Captain Sanders, an old seafarer, met a watery grave there. He left cryptic instructions so his hard-won fortune would not be lost to the Great Sea or taken by scavengers. A determined adventurer can retrace the trail he left behind.

name.esES: El tesoro escondido del capitán Sanders
name.frFR: Le trésor caché du capitaine Sanders
name.ptBR: O tesouro escondido do Capitão Albernaz

text.enUS: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. In Westfall, Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure sends you inland after a clue found by the shore. The trail leads east from the coast toward a barrel near ruined stonework. Captain Sanders sends you inland after the first cipher is solved. The clue points away from the shore and up the rocky bluffs, toward Westfall's main roads.

name.esES: El tesoro escondido del capitán Sanders
name.frFR: Le trésor caché du capitaine Sanders
name.ptBR: O tesouro escondido do Capitão Albernaz

text.enUS: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A broken barrel on Westfall's western shore holds Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure clue. It sends you north toward an old jug beside a coastal windmill, another step along the late pirate's trail to his hidden riches. Captain Sanders scattered his directions along Westfall's western shore. Each clue leads only to the next container, never straight to the prize. You have to follow the trail from one barrel, chest, or jug to another across the bluffs to reach his plunder.

name.frFR: Le trésor caché du capitaine Sanders

text.enUS: Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure. A whiskey-soaked clue sends Captain Sanders' Hidden Treasure hunt west from Westfall's shore. The trail leads out across the Great Sea, away from the mainland's troubles, to a remote islet. Captain Sanders scattered clues along Westfall's coast for any adventurer bold enough to follow them. The last parchment came from the dregs of his favorite whiskey jug and gives the final bearing. The captain's words are clear: head west to the water's edge, then swim out into the waves.

Captain Shatterskull. Captain Shatterskull is a seasoned orc commander stationed at the Mor'shan Base Camp on the northern frontier of the Barrens. Serving as a crucial bulwark for the Horde, he coordinates efforts to repulse night elf forces contesting the border near Warsong Gulch. Positioned at Mor'shan Base Camp along the edge of Ashenvale, Captain Shatterskull serves on the front lines of the Horde's territorial clashes. Beside fellow officers like Kadrak, Shatterskull works to maintain the Horde's foothold against night elf sentinels and Silverwing forces striving to reclaim the borderlands. His post demands relentless vigilance, as the conflict over Ashenvale's timber and ancient lands constantly threatens to spill over into the Barrens.

Captain Stoutfist. Captain Stoutfist is the dwarven officer in charge of military defenses at Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. With the Dragonmaw clan pushing aggressively out of their marshland strongholds, Stoutfist coordinates defensive maneuvers and counter-offensives to ensure the vital Alliance port does not fall. Menethil Harbor serves as the principal deepwater port connecting Ironforge and Stormwind to the marshy lowlands of the Wetlands and the sea beyond. As the town's commanding officer, Captain Stoutfist bears the heavy burden of keeping its docks, civilian populace, and garrison secure against surrounding threats.
