The marshlands are notoriously hazardous, but the biggest peril to the settlement is an organized surge from renegade orcs.

Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun is a privateer affiliated with the Steamwheedle Cartel, stationed at the docks of Ratchet. Despite keeping a cordial demeanor toward traveling Alliance members, he harbors intense resentment toward the Theramore forces at Northwatch Hold who dare fire upon his vessels. Operating out of the bustling neutral port of Ratchet, Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun leads the Thalo'dan Privateers under the broad banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel. In theory, Ratchet's merchants welcome all flags so long as their coin is good, but maritime trade along the Barrens coast is fraught with danger. Just south of the port lies Northwatch Hold, an aggressive Alliance fortification whose heavy artillery threatens neutral sea lanes. Brightsun maintains an outward neutrality toward visiting travelers, but he has reached his limit with the belligerent garrison firing on his fleet.

Captain Vimes. Lieutenant Aden sends you with the orc report you found to Captain Garran Vimes, who reads orcish better than most. News of Horde spies near Theramore is to go with it. Lieutenant Aden thinks the orc report you found belongs in the hands of Captain Garran Vimes, who reads orcish better than most. Aden also wants the captain told that Horde spies are lurking close to Theramore. You will find Vimes at the barracks on Theramore Isle's northeastern side.

Captured Mountaineer. The Captured Mountaineer is an Ironforge dwarf held prisoner in the basement of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Bound and guarded by the Forsaken, he serves as an unwilling subject for the Royal Apothecary Society's grim experiments. Tucked away beneath the floorboards of the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, this Ironforge Mountaineer sits captive far from the safety of Khaz Modan. While patrons drink above, the Royal Apothecary Society puts him to work as an unwitting test subject for their concoctions. Apothecary Johaan and his peers test the lethal potency of their developing plague against living Alliance physiology, using the prisoner to gauge how well their toxins bring a swift and agonizing end to the living.

Captured Scarlet Zealot. The Captured Scarlet Zealot is a crusader prisoner held captive in the basement of Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. Watched over by Forsaken apothecaries and townsfolk, he serves as a living test subject for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing concoctions. Confined beneath Gallows' End Tavern, this member of the Scarlet Crusade embodies the unyielding fanaticism of his order. Even in chains, surrounded by the undead he views as an abomination, he offers no remorse, calling on the Light to protect him from the foul and unholy creatures around him. For the Forsaken, capturing a living zealot is not an act of mercy; it provides valuable human test material to evaluate the lethality of experimental plagues and toxins under development by Apothecary Johaan.

Carendin Halgar. Carendin Halgar is a prominent Forsaken warlock trainer residing in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. Sharp-tongued and notoriously short on patience, he oversees the training of fledgling practitioners of the dark arts. He instructs aspiring warlocks on how to subjugate powerful demonic entities from the Twisting Nether, notably teaching the rituals to bind Voidwalkers and Succubi. Within the noxious gloom of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Carendin Halgar instructs those who delve into the Twisting Nether. He demands focus and obedience, holding little tolerance for failure, hesitation, or weakness. Under his watchful gaze, warlocks are pushed beyond basic incantations into the dangerous mastery of summonings and soul manipulation, cementing the Forsaken's ruthless approach to demonic servitude.

Caretaker Folsom. Along Stormwind’s Canals near the Park, Caretaker Folsom tends the remains of a noble household. He once oversaw the Flintridge estate; now he sells what survived its bloody end. Folsom followed his father into a life of service as caretaker of the Flintridge estate. That life ended with the massacre of the household. The manor stood abandoned, and its remaining funds eventually ran out. Left to watch over what remained, Folsom now sends the family's surviving heirlooms and possessions to auction.

Carolai Anise. Carolai Anise is an eccentric Forsaken alchemist residing in the village of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. She trains novice alchemists, though her hazardous concoctions have drawn nervous murmurs from local guards. Operating out of Brill, Carolai Anise devotes her unlife to the volatile art of alchemy. While many Forsaken researchers operate under the Royal Apothecary Society's grim mandate, Carolai pursues her own strange brews right inside the settlement. Her unpredictable experiments and smoking retorts are notorious enough that the Deathguards keeping watch over Brill openly grumble that she seems bent on blowing up her own house.

Carry Your Weight. Carry Your Weight is an introductory task offered by Furl Scornbrow atop the watchtower overlooking Razor Hill. Too old to fight on the front lines, the scarred veteran asks young Horde adventurers to salvage canvas from local human and centaur hostiles so he can fashion supplies to aid their journey. Furl Scornbrow is a veteran of the Third War who marched alongside Warchief Thrall during the pioneering of Durotar and the desperate defense at Mount Hyjal. Now slowed by age and old injuries, he no longer wields his axe in battle. Instead, he maintains a steady vigil from the Razor Hill watchtower, sounding the alarm against incursions while supporting the next generation of defenders.

Cask of Merlot. A Cask of Merlot is a barrel of fine red wine produced and sold in Stormwind City. It serves as one of several regional specialty liquors needed by the Lakeshire innkeeper during the supply shortages caused by the Blackrock orc invasion. Harvested and fermented in the heart of the kingdom, this Cask of Merlot comes straight from the cellars of the Galina Winery, nestled along the canals bordering Stormwind's Trade District. Winemaker Roberto Pupellyverbos manages the vintages there, catering to the capital's more refined palates. Unlike the harsh moonshine of Duskwood or the rustic spirits brewed in Elwynn, the merlot represents the refined craft of human vintners operating under the relative safety of the city walls.

Cask of Scalder. In Stormwind, a cask of Barleybrew Scalder is on its way to an old acquaintance. The fiery ale carries a favor between dwarves. Travelers who have proved themselves across the Rethban Gauntlet carry Barleybrew Scalder to Furen Longbeard in Stormwind's Dwarven District. The dwarf is an artisan shieldsmith, and he considers dry times intolerable. A cask of the warming ale gives Yorus Barleybrew a way to call in an old favor and secure fine dwarven craftsmanship.

Cask of Shimmer Stout. The Cask of Shimmer Stout is a sealed barrel of Rejold Barleybrew's potent new ale, crafted in the cold heights of Dun Morogh. Known for its remarkable kick and head-spinning vigor, it is sent eastward across the mountains as a spirited gift for fellow dwarven mountaineers. Brewed in Brewnall Village by Rejold Barleybrew, Shimmer Stout quickly earned high marks among local patrons and mountaineers who braved the biting frosts of Dun Morogh. Impressed by his brother's concoction, Mountaineer Barleybrew commissioned a cask to be hauled through the eastern pass into Loch Modan. Dwarves hold strong drink in high regard as both a social staple and a practical defense against the biting mountain chill, and sharing a fresh vintage with far-flung comrades is a time-honored military tradition.

Castpipe's Task. Castpipe's Task is an Alliance summons directing capable adventurers to seek out Master Mechanic Castpipe in Ironforge. Castpipe is coordinating perilous salvage operations into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to extract vital mechanical and technical records. It serves as an official briefing that points mercenaries toward deep-retrieval missions inside the fallen city. Following the tragic fall and subsequent radioactive quarantine of Gnomeregan, the surviving gnomes took refuge in Ironforge's Tinkertown. While their grand home remains overrun by troggs and irradiated constructs, crucial operational records and mechanical schematics are trapped deep within the city's surviving computing arrays. Recognizing that these files could prove invaluable to reclaiming or understanding what went wrong, Master Mechanic Castpipe began actively enlisting intrepid outsiders willing to brave the toxic halls.

Catch of the Day. Cooked fish has not been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long time, and Nataka Longhorn would like that to change. Nataka rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers around, yet all the centaur activity leaves little time for the journey. You are asked to go in Nataka's place and bring back two Bloodbelly fish. No cooked fish has been smelled at Ghost Walker Post for a long while. Nataka Longhorn rates the trolls of Shadowprey Village as the finest fish-catchers, but with so much centaur activity there is little time to make the journey. So you are asked to go there, talk with the local fisherman Jinar'Zillen, and return with two Bloodbelly fish, Nataka's favorite. The road south of the post bends west and brings you to the troll village.

Cathedral Square. In Cathedral Square, faith and civic life meet beneath the Cathedral of Light. City Hall, the orphanage, and the Argent Dawn's Stormwind headquarters all stand here. Northwest of the Trade District and southeast of the Dwarven District, Cathedral Square draws the faithful from across the Kingdom of Stormwind. The Cathedral of Light rises above it, the foremost sanctuary of the Holy Light across Azeroth. Priests, paladins, and healers come to study, pray, and train. Citizens and pilgrims mingle with local schoolchildren, led by School Mistress Danna, in the square.

Cathedral of Light. The Cathedral of Light rises over Cathedral Square as Stormwind's chief sanctuary of the Church of the Holy Light. It is the spiritual heart of the city and the center of human priesthood and the Knights of the Silver Hand. Archbishop Benedictus leads the faithful from the Cathedral of Light, rebuilt after the First War's devastation. Archbishop Alonsus Faol and Bishop Benedictus guided its restoration, and its towering form remains a beacon of resilience. After the Scourge took Lordaeron during the Third War, the Church moved its seat south to Stormwind. From this great hall, Benedictus gives spiritual guidance to the Alliance.

Cats Eye Emerald. The Cats Eye Emerald is an exceptionally large, fist-sized gemstone unearthed within the Boulder Lode Mine in the northern Barrens. Coveted for its immense market value, it quickly became the subject of scheming outside the Venture Company's ranks. When laborers excavating the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine, situated northeast of the Sludge Fen, struck a massive emerald, word traveled fast across the savanna. Such rare, high-grade gemstones rarely stay secret for long in goblin-dominated territories. Wharfmaster Dizzywig in Ratchet caught wind of the discovery through the steady trade gossip passing between his docks and Booty Bay, immediately plotting to secure the prize for the open market in Undermine.

Caught!. Someone is locked inside a wooden outhouse in Searing Gorge, shouting for help from within. They were running from the Dark Iron dwarves, hid in there, and the geologists locked the door behind them. They want eight Dark Iron geologists taught a lesson, and fifteen pieces of silk cloth for... nothing in particular. The voice from the outhouse tells of fleeing the Dark Iron dwarves and ducking inside to hide. The Dark Iron geologists, with their magic, must have seen, for the door was locked on the occupant before they knew it.

Cauldron. The Cauldron is a massive open-pit excavation site dominating the center of the Searing Gorge. Operated by the Dark Iron clan, this fiery quarry is worked day and night by broken slaves under the watch of cruel overseers and roving elementals. Carved deep into the scorched earth of the Searing Gorge, the Cauldron was fortified following the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros by Emperor Thaurissan. Massive, smoke-belching Dark Iron excavation machinery rims the canyon walls, scraping rock and ore from the smoldering stone. Down within its burning crevices, living fire and magma elementals prowl alongside Dark Iron taskmasters, while subterranean heat rises continuously from the depths of the mountain.

Cave Mushrooms. Cave Mushrooms is an Alliance assignment offered by the night elf Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine. While formulating a specialized potion, Barithras tasks an adventurer with venturing into a hidden cavern behind Cliffspring Falls to harvest rare fungi and verify disturbing premonitions felt by the Grove of the Ancients. Barithras Moonshade requires specific ingredients for a potent mixture: scaber stalks and an elusive death cap. These particular fungi thrive in the damp, shadowy cavern concealed directly behind Cliffspring Falls in northeastern Darkshore. While the alchemy itself is delicate, gathering these specimens is far more hazardous than harvesting typical woodland herbs.

Cavern of Mists. The Cavern of Mists is the expansive outer antechamber leading into the depths of the Wailing Caverns. Fed by subterranean geysers that erupt through the rock, its central pool and hanging fog harbor strange, mutated wildlife roaming just outside the portal threshold. Before descending into the true heart of the Wailing Caverns, travelers must navigate the Cavern of Mists. Thick, warm vapor hangs permanently in the air, fed by natural geysers erupting from the cavern floor into a deep central pool. Though it serves as an entryway, it is far from peaceful. Swarms of raptors, serpents, oozes, and semi-aquatic threshadons wander the ledges and waters, alongside notorious beasts like the hydra Trigore the Lasher. It provides adventurers an ominous preview of the unnatural growth festering deeper below.

Caverns of Time. Tucked into the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, the Caverns of Time serve as the mystical lair of Nozdormu and the bronze dragonflight. Within its winding depths, the dragons monitor and safeguard the fragile timeways of Azeroth against any mortal intrusion or temporal tampering. Carved deep beneath the desert cliffs, the Caverns of Time are a nexus where the currents of history converge. Charged by the titans at the dawn of the world, Nozdormu the Timeless One and his bronze dragonflight act as eternal sentinels over these corridors. Inside, time behaves erratically; glimpses of past and future slip through hidden rifts, and relics plucked from distant eras lie scattered across the sands. While the great wyrm Anachronos keeps watch near the entrance, lesser bronze drakes patrol the winding descent, fiercely protective of the one true timeline.

Cazul. Cazul is an ancient, blind orc warlock dwelling in the darkened cavern of the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. Despite having lost his physical sight, he possesses profound occult insight and guides rising practitioners of the dark arts seeking to expand their demonic command. Tucked away in the cavernous depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Cazul endures as a relic of old warlock traditions. Though entirely blind, his senses are attuned to the shifting currents of the Twisting Nether and the whispers of demonic entities. Rising warlocks are often directed to him when seeking to expand their mastery and bind more dangerous servitors. His sharp awareness and occult wisdom make it clear that losing his eyes cost him nothing of his arcane power.

Cenarion Circle. The Cenarion Circle is an ancient, independent order of druids founded by Malfurion Stormrage under the guidance of the demigod Cenarius. Operating from their sacred haven in Moonglade, they strive to maintain the balance of nature, safeguard the Emerald Dream, and mend Azeroth's blighted lands. Though historically composed of night elves, they have recently welcomed the tauren into their ranks, transcending factional divides to defend the living world. The roots of the Cenarion Circle go back thousands of years to the teachings of Cenarius, the Patron of Druids, who mentored the first mortal druid, Malfurion Stormrage. Following the Great Sundering, Malfurion bound together those who wished to study nature's ways. The order made its home in the sacred vale of Moonglade, and ever since, the Circle has held sacred vigil over Azeroth's wild places.

Cenarion Enclave. The Cenarion Enclave is the verdant northwestern district of Darnassus, serving as the central gathering place and seat of power for the Cenarion Circle in the capital. While Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage lies slumbering within the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the night elven druids from the great hollows and living boughs of this grove. Occupying a high terrace above the Temple Gardens, the Cenarion Enclave is shaped from ancient oaks and ashes marked with runic bark. Convocations of the Cenarion Circle gather within structures molded directly from living wood and stone. With Malfurion Stormrage absent in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm oversees affairs here, pushing his ambitious vision for Teldrassil despite lingering political friction with High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Beyond the druids who meditate among its streams, the enclave also hosts the capital's elven hunters and the stables where skilled riders learn to tame Darnassian nightsabers.

Cenarion Hold. Cenarion Hold is the fortified stronghold of the Cenarion Circle situated in the harsh desert of Silithus. Established to keep watch over ancient dangers buried beneath the sands, it stands as one of the largest druidic settlements on Kalimdor and a rare safe haven in an unforgiving wasteland. Perched among the desolate sands of Silithus, Cenarion Hold serves as the southern command hub for the Cenarion Circle. Reached by winding past Un'Goro Crater, the fortress was raised to monitor the dormant threats sealed beneath the desert after the historic War of the Shifting Sands. In an inhospitable expanse teeming with insectoid silithid and arid storms, the stronghold provides vital shelter, trade, and logistical support for night elf and tauren druids alike who stand sentinel over the imprisoned horrors of the past.

Cenarion Lunardust. Cenarion Lunardust is a sacred powder bestowed upon young tauren druids by Turak Runetotem on the heights of Thunder Bluff. It is used to awaken the guardian beast Lunaclaw at an ancient Moonkin Stone on the border of Mulgore and the Barrens. Entrusted to initiates ready to claim their place among the Druids of the Claw, Cenarion Lunardust carries the blessings of the Cenarion Circle. When scattered across the Moonkin Stone west of Camp Taurajo, the glowing dust summons forth Lunaclaw, a sacred beast bound to test the initiate. Defeating this guardian tests both physical fortitude and spiritual resolve, allowing the young druid to absorb the strength of body and heart required to assume the form of the bear.

Cenarion Moondust. Cenarion Moondust is a sacred powder entrusted to night elf druids undergoing their trials to become Druids of the Claw. When scattered upon the ancient Moonkin Stone in the hills east of Auberdine, it draws forth Lunaclaw, the feral guardian of the cave. Bestowed by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, Cenarion Moondust serves as the catalyst for a young druid's final trial of heart and body. To commune with and prove oneself against the guardian Lunaclaw, the initiate must journey to the moonkin dens east of Auberdine in Darkshore. Applying the moondust to the ancient Moonkin Stone summons the beast to test the initiate in combat, allowing the druid to internalize the enduring strength needed to channel the form of the bear.

Cenarius. Cenarius, the Lord of the Forest, is the ancient demigod son of Elune and Malorne who taught the night elves the secrets of druidism. For thousands of years he served as the great patron of mortal druids and guardian of the wilderness before falling in battle during the Third War. Cenarius was born to Elune, the goddess of the moon, and the great white stag demigod Malorne. Because Cenarius was bound to the mortal world, Elune placed him in the care of Malorne, while Ysera the Dreamer embraced him as a foster mother and guided him through the infinite paths of the Emerald Dream. Blessed with powers over living wood and earth, Cenarius fathered the Keepers of the Grove and the dryads, forever tying his bloodline to the wild places of Kalimdor.

Cenarius' Legacy. Cenarius' Legacy is a Horde task handed out by Braelyn Firehand near Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. Frustrated by the natural wards maintained by the night elves and the children of Cenarius, the blood elf mage seeks to cull their numbers at Stonetalon Peak to restore the raw flow of magic. For the Horde, striking at the Cenarion defenders also weakens the regional Alliance presence. Braelyn Firehand resides in the hills near Sun Rock Retreat, festering with frustration at Stonetalon's natural environment. According to her, the druids of the Cenarion Circle and the demigod Cenarius's offspring actively suppress and choke the arcane currents of the land. Describing the process of channeling power here as drawing water with a perforated bucket, she hungers to strip away their natural defenses so raw magical energy can surge unimpeded once again.

Centaur. Centaur are a violent, horse-bodied humanoid race whose nomadic clans dominate the arid plains of central Kalimdor. Born from the tragic union between the demigod Zaetar and the earth princess Theradras, they spent centuries driving the tauren toward extinction before the newly arrived orcish Horde intervened. Centaur legend traces the race to the caverns of Maraudon beneath Desolace. There, Zaetar, one of the immortal sons of the demigod Cenarius, and Princess Theradras, daughter of the elemental lord Therazane, sired the first centaur. Upon their emergence, the barbaric offspring turned on their father and killed him. Grief-stricken, Theradras trapped Zaetar's spirit within the winding caverns of Maraudon, yet she shielded her vicious children, who swiftly multiplied across Kalimdor.

Centaur Bounty. After Khan Dez'hepah, Felgur Twocuts says the scared centaur clans must now be bled. Hunt centaur of any clan across Desolace and bring Felgur fifteen of their ears. Felgur Twocuts says that now the centaur clans have been scared, it is time to bleed them. Whenever you travel Desolace, hunt centaur. Felgur does not care which clan you hunt, only that you gather ears, fifteen of them. Thinning their numbers will weaken their resolve and put an end to any thoughts of expansion.

Centaur Bounty. Corporal Melkins at Nijel's Point says every centaur clan in Desolace shares one trait, cruelty, and that peace will not come while the centaur remain. Melkins asks you to hunt them across the land and bring fifteen of their ears. At Nijel's Point, Corporal Melkins describes a centaur race split among many clans, each with a leader and plans of its own, yet alike in cruelty. Peace, Melkins says, will only come if the centaurs are removed.

Centaur Bracers. Centaur Bracers are simple leather and iron armbands taken from slain Kolkar centaur throughout the Barrens. Regthar Deathgate collects them west of the Crossroads as proof of culled centaur raiders. The Kolkar tribe poses an unrelenting threat to the Horde's foothold across the arid plains of the Barrens. Stripping the bracers from fallen centaur warriors serves as undeniable proof that another hostile marauder has been removed from the trade roads. Regthar Deathgate, an orc scout stationed along the bluffs west of the Crossroads, issues a standing bounty on these trophies to blunt the tribe's aggression.

Centaur Bracers. Centaur Bracers is a military bounty offered by Regthar Deathgate west of the Crossroads. It tasks Horde champions with thinning the aggressive Kolkar centaur ranks contesting control of the central Barrens. The fledgling Horde is engaged in a broad struggle to carve out safe territory across Kalimdor, and the Barrens serve as the vital crossroads between Durotar and Mulgore. However, violent nomadic tribes of Kolkar centaur contest every watering hole and plain, attacking supply trains and scouting parties. From his bunker west of the Crossroads, the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate coordinates defensive efforts to stem their relentless advances.

Cerellean Whiteclaw. Cerellean Whiteclaw is a night elf resting near the docks and inn of Auberdine in Darkshore. Haunted by the memory of his lost love from the ancient Sundering, he struggles to lay her restless spirit to peace. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the War of the Ancients, Cerellean Whiteclaw shared his life with Anaya Dawnrunner. When the demonic invasion tore ancient Kalimdor apart, Anaya perished in the destruction of her city, Ameth'Aran. Stricken with grief, Cerellean followed Malfurion Stormrage into the long druidic slumber, yet the Emerald Dream offered him little respite from her memory. Upon awakening millennia later, he wandered Darkshore in a grief-stricken haze, only to discover that Anaya's ghost remained bound to the very stones where she fell.

Challenge Overlord Mok'Morokk. Overlord Mok'Morokk scoffs at your challenge, promises to crush you and invites you to say when you are ready to be thrashed. Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village had hoped to see Mok'Morokk driven out of the village. You step up to Overlord Mok'Morokk, who laughs at your nerve, promises to crush you and tells you to speak up when you are ready for your beating. This follows The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village expects to see Mok'Morokk chased from the village, and wonders why you would come back just to talk.

Chamber of Atonement. The Chamber of Atonement is the grim entrance hall to the Graveyard wing within the Scarlet Monastery. Here, beneath stone arches hung with iron chains, the Scarlet Crusade subjects captured undead and other perceived heretics to brutal interrogation and torture before casting their remains into the cloister beyond. Serving as the threshold to the Forlorn Cloister, the Chamber of Atonement is far from a sanctuary of peaceful prayer. Instead, the Scarlet Crusade has converted the grand entryway into a house of pain, outfitted with racks, shackles, and burning braziers. Zealous inquisitors use these instruments to extract confessions and torment captives, viewing excruciating pain as the only fitting penance for unholy beings. The chamber echoes constantly with the cries of the damned, presided over by cruel taskmasters who ensure that those who enter rarely walk out whole.

Champions' Hall. In Stormwind's Old Town, Champions' Hall is guarded and reserved for Alliance officers. Its quartermasters supply weapons, armor, and regalia to veterans who have proven themselves in battle. Champions' Hall stands behind a guarded entrance in Old Town, reserved for the Alliance's distinguished combatants. Military commanders gather around maps of Azeroth to discuss ongoing campaigns, among arms and the insignias of rank. Only Alliance soldiers who have earned the rank of Knight or higher may enter. Inside, quartermasters supply battle-hardened soldiers with elite weapons, armor, and mounts made to aid them against the Horde in contested lands.

name.zhCN: 荆棘谷的青山 - 第一章

text.enUS: Chapter I. Barnil Stonepot is trying to restore the opening portion of Hemet Nesingwary's scattered hunting manuscript, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. He needs four missing leaves gathered from across the jungle to bind the introductory section back together. Following your talk regarding The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, Barnil Stonepot sets his sights on restoring the book's opening passage. According to the dwarf, this first part sets the stage for the wider story and describes Nesingwary's hunting party, counting Barnil himself among the companions. Unfortunately, the manuscript's leaves remain lost in the wild, leaving pages one, four, six, and eight absent from the collection.

name.zhCN: 荆棘谷的青山 - 第二章

text.enUS: Chapter II. Barnil Stonepot needs assistance gathering missing leaves from the second section of Hemet Nesingwary's scattered hunting manuscript. Having gathered most of the parchment himself, he relies on travelers across Stranglethorn Vale to recover the remaining scattered accounts of panther and tiger hunts. Following the dispersal of Hemet Nesingwary's manuscript across Stranglethorn Vale, Barnil Stonepot managed to reclaim many leaves on his own. The second chapter focuses entirely on thrilling accounts of tracking panthers and tigers through the wilderness. Four specific pages—numbers 10, 11, 14, and 16—remain lost to the wind and the jungle's inhabitants, leaving this section of the expedition's chronicle unfinished.

name.zhCN: 荆棘谷的青山 - 第三章

text.enUS: Chapter III. Barnil Stonepot is trying to reconstruct the third chapter of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting manuscript in Stranglethorn Vale. The section recounts the first kill made with a dwarven rifle by Sir Erlgadin and Lady Rouack, but four specific leaves were blown across the jungle. Barnil Stonepot considers this portion of The Green Hills of Stranglethorn his personal favorite. The text recounts the early exploits of Sir Erlgadin and Lady Rouack, detailing their very first kill using a dwarven rifle. The chapter ends on a sharp cliffhanger.

name.zhCN: 荆棘谷的青山 - 第四章

text.enUS: Chapter IV. Barnil Stonepot is trying to reconstruct the thrilling finale of Hemet Nesingwary's famous manuscript. Recovering the final three sheets will restore the climactic conclusion to the wild hunting tale. Barnil Stonepot considers this section the big finale of the entire hunting volume. To assemble the fourth chapter, he needs someone to track down and return pages twenty-five, twenty-six, and twenty-seven. Once these three lost sheets are gathered from across the jungle, the manuscript's exciting conclusion can finally be reassembled.

Charlga Razorflank. Charlga Razorflank, widely known as the Crone of the Kraul, is the fierce and cunning geomancer chieftain presiding over Razorfen Kraul. Under her leadership, the Razorfen quilboar drove the tauren out of the southern Barrens through ruthless expansion. Within the tangled, massive brambles of Razorfen Kraul rules Charlga Razorflank. Revered by her people as a master geomancer whose experimental magic remains unmatched among quilboar, Charlga organized her fractious kin into a unified, lethal threat. She harnessed the primal earth and giant thorns sprouting from the demigod Agamaggan's remains, reshaping the labyrinthine Kraul into an impenetrable fortress.

Charred Horn. Charred Horns are the rugged, heat-baked horns harvested from youthful chimaeras dwelling in the crags of the Stonetalon Mountains. Tough enough to withstand harsh elemental forces, they serve as an essential tempering component in specialized armorsmithing. Harvested from fledgling and young chimaeras nesting across the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains, Charred Horns are coveted for their unnatural resistance to flame and blunt force. The dwarven armorsmith Furen Longbeard, working from his forge in Stormwind, requires a collection of these horns to craft fire-hardened mail. Combined with venomous spider fangs from the Wetlands, phlogiston from Razorfen Kraul, and the galvanized horn of a chimaera matriarch, these calcified horns provide the core structural reinforcement necessary to produce an exceptionally resilient suit of protective armor.

Charred Vale. The Charred Vale is a smoldering valley in southwestern Stonetalon Mountains, devastated by the reckless deforestation and machinery of the Venture Company. Once a thriving haven for treants and chimaeras, it is now engulfed in flames, roving elementals, and hostile harpies. Not long ago, this southwest basin was a flourishing alpine wood guarded by majestic treants and inhabited by native chimaeras and harpies. Its ruin began with the arrival of the Venture Company. The greedy goblin outfit clear-cut the forest with explosive machinery, corrupting the guardians and awakening chaotic fire elementals. Though the treants eventually forced the goblins back, the land was left broken, scarred by fire, and tainted by whatever foul devices the retreating loggers deployed.

Chef Breanna. Chef Breanna is the head cook at Lakeshire's local dining house in the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with feeding the garrison of Stormwind soldiers stationed to protect the embattled lakeside town, she relies on hearty, local ingredients to keep the defenders on their feet. Operating out of a restaurant house in northwestern Lakeshire alongside her assistants Crystal Boughman and Gretchen Vogel, Chef Breanna bears the heavy responsibility of provisioning the entire local battalion. With Lakeshire besieged by Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, maintaining the strength and morale of Stormwind's understaffed garrison is essential. Her signature dish, Redridge Goulash, relies on the wild game and beasts roaming the surrounding ridges, turning dangerous wilderness predators into fuel for the town's weary guard.

Chef Grual. Chef Grual is the resident cook at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. In a secluded town choked by mist and monsters, Grual does his best to keep the Night Watch and weary travelers fed, even if his choice of ingredients raises eyebrows. Running an eatery in Darkshire is a grim task. With supply lines from Westfall and Stormwind constantly harassed by highwaymen, wolves, and undead, fresh provisions are virtually nonexistent. Grual makes do with whatever the wilderness provides. From wolf flank to whatever scavenged meats local adventurers drag through the door, Grual cooks with pragmatism born of necessity.

Chef Jessen. Chef Jessen is Southshore's resident meat vendor and culinarian, working to keep the coastal town fed amidst constant border tensions. He is best remembered for his famous turtle bisque. Operating out of Southshore in the southern Hillsbrad Foothills, Chef Jessen provides provisions and meat to locals and visiting Alliance soldiers alike. He possesses notable culinary expertise. Years past, before plague and war disrupted northern Lordaeron, he regularly ventured north past Dalaran to the shores of Lordamere Lake. There, he harvested meat from native snapjaw turtles to concoct his prized Soothing Turtle Bisque, a hearty recipe he is willing to share with aspiring travelers who assist him in gathering ingredients.

Chen's Empty Keg. Discarded in the wilds of the Barrens lies an empty keg bearing the inscription of Chen Stormstout. Finding it begins a journey into the past deeds of the famed wandering brewmaster who once lent his fighting skills to the founding of Durotar. Scattered across the arid expanses of the Barrens, travelers occasionally stumble upon an abandoned wooden barrel. Unlike the common casks left behind by Razormane quilboar or Kolkar centaur, this barrel features careful craftsmanship and a distinct inscribed plaque: 'Chen Stormstout - May your spirit be raised and always raise your spirits.' It is an unusual relic to find baking beneath the Kalimdor sun, prompting anyone curious enough to seek out someone knowledgeable in brewing to understand how it got there.

Chen's Empty Keg. This quest continues the legendary lineage of pandaren brewing in the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet offers to recreate Chen Stormstout's renowned, potent concoction if you gather wild ingredients from the native beasts roaming the savannah. When a discarded keg marked with pandaren writing winds up in the hands of Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet, it evokes fond memories of the legendary wanderer Chen Stormstout. Chen passed the secrets of his namesake brew to Drohn's mentor, who in turn entrusted them to Drohn. Though unusual to non-brewers, the recipe calls for raw, potent elements taken straight from the fierce wildlife of the Barrens.

Chen's Empty Keg. Following the creation of the potent Stormstout, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet offers to craft another esoteric recipe learned from the elusive pandaren wanderer Chen Stormstout. This potent concoction, known as trogg ale, requires rare organs and glands harvested from the native beasts of the Barrens. After assisting Brewmaster Drohn with reproducing the legendary Chen Stormstout's initial draught, the orc brewmaster reveals that the wandering pandaren shared more than one secret. Drohn possesses the formula for an eccentric beverage known as trogg ale. Unlike mundane spirits distilled from grains, this peculiar brew relies entirely on potent organic reagents scavenged from the fiercest wildlife in central Kalimdor.

Cherry for Your Thoughts?. In Booty Bay, a mercenary named Tokal is seeking a drink in exchange for the truth behind recent attacks on human and dwarven outposts. While rumors point the finger at the Horde, Tokal insists her group was operating under a private mercenary contract. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, an individual named Tokal is keeping a low profile while watching out for law enforcement. A series of aggressive raids recently devastated human and dwarven camps, fueling rumors that the Horde had orchestrated the attacks. When approached by travelers who clearly do not work for the inquiring marshal, Tokal is quick to push back against the widespread narrative, offering a different version of events in exchange for a drink.

Chest of Containment Coffers. The Chest of Containment Coffers contains enchanted receptacles used by mages to capture unstable magical phenomena. It serves as essential equipment for practitioners sent to investigate and safely trap unseen mana anomalies. Magical experimentation and sudden planar rifts frequently spawn volatile, invisible anomalies made entirely of arcane force. Standard physical cages cannot hold entities composed purely of magic. The Chest of Containment Coffers provides mages with specialized, enchanted coffers engineered to entrap and bind these subdued creatures alive. Kept near senior instructors such as Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity and Jennea Cannon in Stormwind, the chest provides the necessary gear for initiates tasked with surveying anomalies before they can destabilize their surroundings.

text.enUS: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. Chicken Clucking for a Mint is a lighthearted seasonal Alliance quest offered in Ironforge during the Hallow's End festival. To earn a traditional Ironforge Mint on behalf of the young orphan Jesper, adventurers must put aside their battle-hardened dignity and flap their arms while clucking like a chicken for the tavern's amusement. Innkeeper Firebrew gladly rewards anyone willing to swallow their pride to bring holiday cheer to a child. During Hallow's End, spirits run high across Azeroth as folk celebrate the break between harvest and winter with costumed revelry and seasonal treats. While seasoned heroes might normally feel too old to go door-to-door begging for candy, the plight of sick or orphaned children offers an honorable excuse. In Stormwind, young Jesper longs for holiday sweets, prompting visiting Alliance champions to gather iconic regional confections from innkeepers across the Alliance capitals.

text.enUS: Chicken Clucking for a Mint. During the festive season of Hallow's End, Innkeeper Norman of the Undercity offers a piece of candy to travelers helping an ailing child. To earn the Undercity Mint, adventurers must cast aside their dignity and flap about like a chicken. The Undercity is rarely known for laughter or warmth, built as it is beneath the ruins of Lordaeron by the liberated Forsaken. Yet when Hallow's End arrives, even the grim denizens of the Trade Quarter join in seasonal revelry. Innkeeper Norman holds onto a stash of Undercity Mints, designated for those collecting treats on behalf of young Spoops, a sick orphan in need of holiday cheer.

text.enUS: Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker is an emissary of the dwarven Explorers' League stationed in Darnassus outside the Temple of the Moon. Sent from Ironforge across the sea to northern Kalimdor, he seeks to uncover ancient history and coordinates dwarven field research throughout the region. Currently, he is preoccupied with gathering field reports and tracking lost colleagues operating in Darkshore. While it is unusual to find an Ironforge dwarf nestled high in the boughs of Teldrassil, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker represents the far-reaching ambitions of the Explorers' League. Having traded the lecture halls and museum vaults of Ironforge for fieldwork in Kalimdor, he can be found standing outside the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus, conferring with local night elf scholars such as Tarelvir. Greywhisker's academic lectures back in the Eastern Kingdoms famously touched upon ancient lore and primordial entities like the Wild God Agamaggan, and he is eager to see what ancient secrets the night elves' ancestral lands might hold.

name.zhCN: 主工程师辛德维尔七世

text.enUS: Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII is a veteran dwarven engineer stationed atop the Stonewrought Dam in Loch Modan. Tasked with the upkeep and defense of this monumental feat of engineering, he oversees its delicate mechanisms while keeping watch for sabotage. Those who speak with him quickly discover that grave dangers threaten the integrity of the great dam. The Stonewrought Dam is one of the crowning achievements of dwarven stonecraft and engineering, holding back the massive waters of the Loch. Chief Engineer Hinderweir VII bears the immense responsibility of maintaining its structure and operational machinery. Perched along the crest of the dam, he monitors the waterways, sluice gates, and structural stress points against the elements and local hazards.

Chief Hawkwind. Chief Hawkwind is the tribal leader of Camp Narache, the proving grounds nestled in the Red Cloud Mesa of Mulgore. Responsible for guiding the youth of the Shu'halo, he mentors new adventurers as they embark on their traditional rites of passage. Under his watchful gaze, young braves learn humility, respect for the land, and the strength needed to protect their people. Standing at the heart of Camp Narache, Chief Hawkwind carries the solemn responsibility of preparing the next generation of tauren for the wider world. Red Cloud Mesa serves as a sheltered haven where fledgling hunters, shamans, druids, and warriors undertake the ancient Rites of the Earthmother. Hawkwind oversees these customs, ensuring that every youth learns duty and endurance before venturing beyond the safety of the mesa.

Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head. Chief Sharptusk Thornmantle's Head is taken as grim proof of victory over the leader of the Bristleback quilboar threatening Red Cloud Mesa. Recovered from the depths of Brambleblade Ravine, it is presented to Brave Windfeather to mark the end of a persistent menace against young tauren braves. The tauren carve their peaceful homeland out of Mulgore through vigilance and strength. The Bristleback quilboar entrenched within Brambleblade Ravine have waged an aggressive campaign against the tribes of Camp Narache, urged on by their ferocious chieftain, Sharptusk Thornmantle. Severing his head serves not out of senseless cruelty, but as definitive proof of his demise and a stark warning to the surviving quilboar clans encroaching upon mesa borders.

Chill Breeze Valley. Chill Breeze Valley is a rugged, snow-covered pass in western Dun Morogh linking the dwarven settlement of Kharanos with the embattled city of Gnomeregan. While its main path is a well-traveled thoroughfare for young travelers and refugees, its secluded recesses harbor dangerous beasts and bloody dens. Chill Breeze Valley forms a T-shaped trench through the mountains of western Dun Morogh. The main east-west trail sees steady foot traffic from novice dwarves and gnomes journeying between Kharanos and the outskirts of Gnomeregan. However, straying into the valley's north-south offshoot is another matter entirely. Strewn with bloodstains and mangled carcasses, these shadowy reaches harbor ferocious predators—most notably savage wendigos that lair in deep ice caves and prey on anyone reckless enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Chillwind Camp. Chillwind Camp sits at the southern pass leading into the Western Plaguelands from the Alterac Mountains. Manned by an Alliance contingent working alongside the Argent Dawn, it serves as the final safe staging ground before the blighted ruins of Lordaeron. From this precarious outpost, commanders direct strikes against the nearby Scourge strongholds and plague cauldrons. Tucked into the rocky pass descending from Chillwind Point, Chillwind Camp is the first line of defense and primary base of operations for Alliance forces pushing into the Western Plaguelands. Though physically separated from the worst of the corruption by the high mountain ridges, the dead chill of the north hangs heavily over the tents and palisades. Under Commander Ashlam Valorfist, a sparse garrison of soldiers, scouts, and Argent Dawn specialists attempts to contain the horrors lingering along the King's Road and gather the intelligence necessary to reclaim Lordaeron's fallen fields.

Chillwind Point. Chillwind Point is a rocky rise and ancient troll ruin sitting on the high frontier between the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the Western Plaguelands. It gets its name from the freezing drafts howling through the mountain pass out of the blighted north. Today, it serves as a lonely vantage point inhabited primarily by a lone troll mystic. Perched on the borderlands where Hillsbrad gives way to Alterac and the plagued north, Chillwind Point looks out over the mountain ravine leading directly into the Western Plaguelands. Long before Lordaeron claimed these passes, ancient trolls built stone structures upon these heights, the remnants of which still stand weather-beaten against the elements. Today, cold winds blow south through the ravine, carrying the chill of the fallen north into the foothill valleys below.

Chimaeric Horn. As part of the warrior rite to craft the Brutal Helm, Orm Stonehoof tasks an aspiring champion with journeying into the ruined Charred Vale. There, the warrior must hunt a maddened chimaera matriarch to claim her galvanized horn as both an act of mercy and proof of strength. Orm Stonehoof is willing to forge the legendary Brutal Helm for Horde warriors, but martial tradition demands that the wearer prove their mettle first. Orm does not simply ask for raw metal or coin; he demands proof of martial prowess and a willingness to confront the grim scars left behind by devastating conflict.

Chok'sul's Head. Chok'sul's Head serves as gruesome physical proof of the death of the Mo'grosh ogre chieftain. Brought to Magistrate Bluntnose in Thelsamar, it secures a formal bounty placed by local dwarven authorities. The ogres of Mo'grosh Stronghold pose a persistent menace to the settlements of Loch Modan, orchestrating assaults against Thelsamar, the excavation sites, and the vital Stonewrought Dam. Magistrate Bluntnose placed a bounty on the brute presumed to be coordinating these attacks: Chok'sul. Given the chaos of the northeastern hills, the magistrate demands undeniable evidence before releasing township funds. The severed head of the ogre chieftain provides the grotesque certainty the dwarven council needs to mark the contract fulfilled.

Chol'aruk the Ravener. Chol'aruk the Ravener is a feared monstrous abomination lurking in a cave on Thorn Hill within the Barrens. The local Razormane call it Chol'aruk or 'The Ravener,' and rumors claim the creature is large enough to swallow an orc whole. Bainham seeks its severed head to avenge comrades lost to similar horrors. Northwest of where Bainham waits in the Barrens sits the plateau known as Thorn Hill, long contested by the native Razormane tribes. Recently, whispered rumors have spoken of a terrifying presence entrenched inside one of its caves: a monstrous abomination the Razormane call Chol'aruk, or 'The Ravener.' Though many travelers dismiss accounts of a beast capable of swallowing an armored orc in a single gulp as campfire tall tales, those who have witnessed the carnage firsthand know the threat is all too real.

Christoph Jeffcoat. Christoph Jeffcoat is a Forsaken merchant stationed in the settlement of Tarren Mill within the Hillsbrad Foothills. He supplies local crafters and travelers with essential trade goods, cooking seasonings, and specialty recipes. In an active war zone contested by the Alliance and the Syndicate, his mundane wares keep the northern Horde war effort running. While Tarren Mill stands as the Forsaken's military stronghold in Hillsbrad Foothills, a garrison cannot fight on malice alone. Christoph Jeffcoat handles the quiet, practical side of occupation, vending reagents, tools, threads, and spices to soldiers and traveling artisans. From the soothing spices required for local culinary recipes like turtle bisque to rare schematics and alchemical vials, Jeffcoat ensures that Horde forces passing through southern Lordaeron are fully provisioned for the battles against Southshore and the regional perils.

Chronormu. Chronormu, who goes by the mortal name Chromie, is a bronze dragon disguised as an energetic female gnome. Tasked with safeguarding the flow of time on Azeroth, she often works directly with mortals rather than observing from afar. In the Western Plaguelands, she quietly intervenes in the tragic aftermath of the Third War to right disrupted temporal threads. Though she appears to mortals as an eccentric and cheerful gnome named Chromie, Chronormu is a member of the bronze dragonflight serving under the Timeless One, Nozdormu. Bronze dragons are charged by the titans with guarding history and correcting disruptions in the timeways. In the form of a female gnome, she walks beside mortals as an approachable, optimistic peer.

Church of the Holy Light. The Church of the Holy Light is the dominant religious institution of humanity, guiding mortal souls through the virtues of compassion, justice, and devotion. Originally centered in the lost northern kingdom of Lordaeron, its leadership now resides within the grand Cathedral of Light in Stormwind City following the devastation wrought by the Scourge. The Church's origins reach back over a millennium to the faith in the Holy Light that took root among the humans of Arathor, teaching them to channel sacred power to cure injuries and purge affliction. Driven by tenets of charity, righteousness, and the fundamental belief that the Light resides within all thinking beings, these teachings eventually coalesced into an organized faith. The kingdom of Lordaeron became the religious heartland of this doctrine, establishing revered sanctuaries throughout the north, including Stratholme, Andorhal, Tyr's Hand, and Light's Hope Chapel.

Circle of Aquementas. The Circle of Aquementas is a mysterious ring of upright standing stones positioned along the eastern shoreline of Tanaris, just south of Lost Rigger Cove. It serves as a ritual site where travelers can call forth the elemental spirit Aquementas. Tucked away along the windswept eastern coast of Tanaris, the Circle of Aquementas sits quietly south of the pirate stronghold at Lost Rigger Cove. Composed of weathered, upright stones arranged in a circular formation, this unusual site hums with elemental energy against the desert shore. It acts as a focus for summoning Aquementas, an elemental entity tied to an ancient artifact. While the surrounding beaches crawl with Southsea brigands and roaming sea creatures, the circle itself remains a solemn pocket of ritual power amidst the dunes.

Circle of East Binding. The Circle of East Binding is a mysterious ancient ritual site situated in the eastern reaches of the Arathi Highlands, just southwest of Hammerfall. Anchored by the Stone of East Binding, the site is violently contested and guarded by roaming water elementals known as cresting exiles. Positioned amidst the rugged highlands east of Stromgarde, the Circle of East Binding is one of several ancient sites of power scattered across the Arathi basin. At its focal point stands the Stone of East Binding, an enigmatic monument radiating potent elemental magic. Swirling water elementals known as cresting exiles roam the surrounding earth and fiercely defend the stone against any mortals who dare approach.

Circle of Inner Binding. The Circle of Inner Binding is an ancient ring of ritual stones situated in the southern hills of the Arathi Highlands, just east of Stromgarde Keep. Guarded by hostile earth elementals, it holds the Stone of Inner Binding, the most potent seal used to restrain the imprisoned elemental princess Myzrael deep beneath the earth. Perched upon a plateau south of the main road, the Circle of Inner Binding anchors the strongest of the ancient wards sealing Myzrael beneath Arathi. Towering slabs surround the central Stone of Inner Binding, which thrums with dense geo-magical power. Enormous rumbling earth elementals patrol the stones relentlessly, drawn to the site's resonance or bound as guardians. Despite these potent wards, cracks in this inner seal permit the trapped entity beneath the Highlands to reach out telepathically, whispering pleas for freedom to unsuspecting wanderers who handle shards of its stone.

Circle of West Binding. The Circle of West Binding is one of several ancient ritual sites scattered across the Arathi Highlands, situated near Thoradin's Wall. Centered around the Stone of West Binding, this arcane ring is overrun by fiery elemental entities bound to the site. Tucked against the rugged slopes near Thoradin's Wall, the Circle of West Binding forms part of a wider network of ritual sites dispersed throughout the Arathi Highlands. At its heart sits the Stone of West Binding, an ancient relic tied to elemental containment. The grounds are swarming with Burning Exiles—volatile fire elementals that relentlessly guard the perimeter, making any approach to the stone a perilous endeavor for travelers traversing the western plains.

text.enUS: Claim Rackmore's Treasure!. Rackmore's log tells of a ship bound for Feathermoon Stronghold that was set upon by creatures of the sea. To keep his treasure from his enemies, Rackmore hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle, and the silver key and golden key that open it are lost. The log says Rackmore's ship was on its way to Feathermoon Stronghold when seafaring creatures attacked it. Hoping to keep his treasure from his enemies, he hid the chest on Ranazjar Isle. Two keys open it, one silver and one gold, and both were lost. Someone who finds the keys and the chest will find a treasure.

Clam Bait. Mai'Lahii at Shadowprey Village has fished all his life and says the best bait is soft-shelled clam meat, which no fish can resist. He wants ten pieces, to be found around a wrecked ship up the coast to the north. Mai'Lahii has fished all his life, and he swears by soft-shelled clam meat as bait, since the fish cannot resist it. To the north, off the coast, lies a wrecked ship, and soft-shelled clams are scattered throughout that area. He asks for ten pieces of the meat.

Clarice Foster. Clarice Foster is a Forsaken woman residing deep beneath the bluffs of Mulgore within the Pools of Vision. Far from the plagued glades of Lordaeron, she spends her days in contemplation among the tauren seers and mystics. While most Forsaken remain in the northern lands of Lordaeron rebuilding their kingdom under the Undercity, Clarice Foster has traveled to the heart of the tauren lands in Kalimdor. Sheltered within the cavernous Pools of Vision beneath the mesa of Thunder Bluff, she dwells alongside Forsaken apothecaries and tauren shamans who study the spiritual and elemental mysteries of the earth.

Clarice's Pendant. Clarice's Pendant is a small keepsake belonging to Clarice Foster, an undead resident of the Pools of Vision in Thunder Bluff. Once a token from her former husband, Yuriv, the jewelry now serves only as a bitter reminder of abandoned family and misplaced devotion to the Light. Clarice's Pendant represents the fractured human past common to many of the Forsaken. Before the Third War consumed Lordaeron, Clarice's husband Yuriv abandoned her and their children to join the fight against the undead, proclaiming that devotion to the Holy Light took precedence over all else. Instead of saving his home, Yuriv perished, leaving his family behind to ultimately succumb to the very Scourge he set out to fight. For Clarice, the pendant is not a cherished memento, but an insulting trinket symbolizing a lifetime spent coming second to zealotry and duty.

Claw Key. The Claw Key is one of three druidic keys hidden within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Alongside the Barrow Key and Sleepers' Key, it is required to unlock the enchanted Talon Den Hoard. The night elf druids established the Talon Den high upon Stonetalon Peak as a sanctuary and repository for powerful relics. To ensure these treasures remained safe from trespassers, they hid them behind a layered security system. The hoard itself is sealed by three distinct enchanted locks: the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key, and the Claw Key. Each key is concealed inside a specialized druidic cache resembling a torch within the winding tunnels of the barrow den.

Clean Zone. The Clean Zone is a fortified, decontamination enclave nestled inside the ruined city of Gnomeregan just past the upper Hall of Gears. It serves as the sole safe haven within the irradiated facility where uncorrupted gnomish forces hold ground against surrounding troggs and leper gnomes. Here, field medics, technicians, and specialized Sparklematic machines offer respite and salvage operations amid the radioactive ruins. While most of Gnomeregan succumbed to Mekkatorque's disastrous venting of radioactive waste, the Clean Zone remains untainted. Positioned strategically between the trogg-infested Dormitory below and the contested corridors of the Hall of Gears above, it acts as a fortified forward base. Resolute gnome defenders, technicians, and field medics hold the barricades day and night, ensuring Alliance expeditions have a stable staging ground to regroup, mend wounds, and maintain machinery.

Cleansing of the Infected. Cleansing of the Infected is an Alliance task in Darkshore given by Tharnariun Treetender in Auberdine. After his attempted cure fails to halt the woodland sickness, the caretaker reluctantly orders a cull of the rabid thistle bears roaming the misty wilderness. It represents a bitter turning point where preservation gives way to containment. Tharnariun Treetender has spent long hours searching for a remedy to stem the creeping affliction corrupting Darkshore's wildlife. Despite his attempt to cleanse a captured bear, the thistle bears remain deeply diseased and violent. Having exhausted his gentler options, the night elf tender concludes that putting the beasts down is the only immediate way to prevent them from mauling other creatures and spreading their sickness further into the ancient woodlands.

Cleansing the Eye. Cleansing the Eye is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the murky Wetlands south to the human capital of Stormwind. After recovering the cursed orb known as the Eye of Paleth, travelers must seek the aid of Archbishop Benedictus to purge its lingering taint. The Eye of Paleth recovered from the marshlands does not shine with holy clarity. Instead, it is steeped in an unsettling shadow, bearing the residual sorrow and trauma of the terrible tragedy that unfolded where it was lost. The dwarf Glorin Steelbrow recognizes the power of the orb, but admits he lacks the divine craft to lift such a heavy affliction.

Cleft. The Cleft is a darkened hollow located northwest of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil corner of the boughs, it has been claimed by the corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs, who use it as a stronghold to ambush travelers moving along the main highway toward Darnassus. Situated off the highway between Dolanaar and Darnassus, the Cleft has turned into one of the most perilous dens on the world tree. Driven mad by the foul taint spreading through Teldrassil, the resident Gnarlpine furbolgs have fortified this hollow. From this redoubt, the maddened beasts terrorize the local roads, threatening to cut Dolanaar off from the capital.

Cleft of Shadow. Tucked deep within the subterranean caverns beneath Orgrimmar, the Cleft of Shadow houses the city's practitioners of stealth, sorcery, and demonology. Far from the proud warrior ethos of Thrall's upper districts, it serves as a necessary haven for rogues and warlocks operating in the shadows of the Horde. While Thrall's new Horde champions honor, shamanism, and strength of arms, practical leadership demands a place for subtler arts. Carved into the damp stone caverns below the capital, the Cleft of Shadow hosts the Shadowswift Brotherhood of rogues and the Darkfire Enclave of warlocks. Kept away from the everyday bustle of the valley districts, this dark quarter allows practitioners of poison and fel energy to ply their trades out of direct public view while remaining under the watchful eye of Orgrimmar's leadership.

Clerk Daltry. Clerk Daltry is the civic record keeper stationed in Darkshire Town Hall in Duskwood. Surrounded by ledgers and registry books, he helps investigate the village's past and track down historical records, even if his archives are somewhat neglected and out of date. While Darkshire struggles against encroaching beasts, undead horrors, and supernatural gloom, everyday civic duties fall to Clerk Daltry. Working out of the Darkshire Town Hall alongside Lord Ello Ebonlocke and the local council, Daltry maintains the town's historical ledgers, property rolls, and census data. In a region fractured by disaster, his records are among the few surviving links to the days before Grand Hamlet fell into shadow.

Cliffspring Falls. Cliffspring Falls marks the dramatic origin of Darkshore's vital Cliffspring River, tumbling down from the eastern cliffs into the coastal forest. Long celebrated as the principal source of clean drinking water for the region, its waters have recently fallen victim to a foul, spreading taint. The subterranean cavern feeding the waterfall has become infested with hostile naga and shadowy Twilight's Hammer cultists. Pouring out from caverns perched high in the rocky bluffs along Darkshore's eastern border, Cliffspring Falls feeds the Cliffspring River, which winds westward across the woods to empty into the sea. Traditionally, this cascade provided the purest drinking water for local night elf settlements. In recent times, however, the waters have turned foul and murky, spreading sickness and ecological decay throughout the river basin. Investigating naturalists have discovered that the cave network at the falls' headwaters is overrun by vile naga and dark cultists, who plot in the shadows while demonic corruption from neighboring Felwood threatens to seep through the highland bedrock.

Cliffspring River Sample. A glass vial containing murky, foul-smelling water drawn from the base of the Cliffspring River waterfall in Darkshore. Gathered on behalf of Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, the sample provides tangible proof of an encroaching corruption threatening the coastal settlement. The Cliffspring River flows down from the rugged eastern heights of Darkshore, tumbling past ancient stone bridges before washing out into the sea along Mist's Edge. Lately, the river's crystalline waters have turned foul and visibly corrupted. Fearing that the toxic wash will soon contaminate Auberdine's shoreline and water supply, the night elf Thundris Windweaver commissioned travelers to draw this water sample directly from the pool beneath the river's lower waterfall. The sample confirms the worst: unnatural rot is drifting steadily downstream toward the coast.

Cliffwatcher Longhorn. Cliffwatcher Longhorn is the stoic tauren leader stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Tasked with safeguarding the isolated Horde outpost, he coordinates defenses against encroaching Galak centaur and monitors the suspicious machinations of the Grimtotem tribe. Perched upon the soaring rock spires of Thousand Needles, Freewind Post relies on sharp eyes and steady leadership to survive. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the day-to-day security of this precarious settlement. With hostile forces gathering on the canyon floor below and along neighboring ridges, Longhorn acts as the settlement's primary coordinator for scouting reports and defensive military efforts.

Clockwerk Run. The Clockwerk Run is the main entrance corridor leading into the heart of fallen Gnomeregan. Stretching between the Train Depot and the Hall of Gears, this damaged hallway is heavily contaminated by toxic fallout and overrun with irradiated troggs. Serving as the primary gateway into Gnomeregan from the outer train depot, the Clockwerk Run was once a bustling conduit of gnomish logistics and transit. When High Tinker Mekkatorque ordered the venting of radioactive waste to stem the trogg invasion, the corridor became a lethal trap. The blast and subsequent fighting caused portions of the hallway to collapse onto itself. Today, the passage is choked with toxic fumes and prowling irradiated troggs, making it the perilous frontline that any expedition must fight through to reach the upper Hall of Gears.

Cloth Request. At the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop, Rema Schneider receives Harlan Bagley's request for fresh cloth and knitted goods. His shelves are emptying quickly. Harlan Bagley asks Rema Schneider for a fresh supply of knitted garments and cloth. Bagley notes a sudden and unsettling surge in trade: citizens and travelers are buying armor and sturdy clothing as if bracing for a brutal season. The rush leaves Rema puzzled and wary. The House of Nobles has announced no open war, so Rema wonders why city folk are quietly armoring themselves and whether the crown's leaders are hiding unrest.

text.enUS: Cloth and Leather Armor. In Goldshire, Cloth and Leather Armor sends a trusted traveler east for gear. Marshal Dughan issues an armor marker redeemable with Sara Timberlain at Eastvale Logging Camp. The trip carries recruits beyond Guard Thomas's bridge to obtain armor for the realm's defense. Guard Thomas watches Elwynn's eastern river crossing, where murlocs and gnolls threaten the border. After you carry his report to Goldshire, Marshal Dughan recognizes your service with an official Stormwind Armor Marker. Goldshire's garrison has meager stores, so Dughan gives you a marker instead of drawing equipment from them. The marker is a military voucher that records your service to the crown.

Cloven Hoof. The Cloven Hoof is a mysterious relic guarded deep within Thousand Needles by the Galak centaur tribe. Preserved inside an ancient sacred flame at Splithoof Hold, it emanates an uncharacteristic supernatural energy that tauren scholars are keen to understand. Held within an ancient brazier at the deepest recess of Splithoof Hold, the Cloven Hoof is one of the most treasured relics of the Galak centaur. The artifact is continually enveloped in a magical flame, requiring blessed water to briefly quench the blaze so it can be handled. Centaur society is notoriously brutal and splintered into violent clans, but their reverence for the brazier suggests ritual significance tied directly to their origins. Tauren observers like Rau Cliffrunner at Freewind Post believe the strange aura radiating from the hoof could reveal critical insight into the race that has plagued Kalimdor's plains for generations.

Cold Hearth Manor. Cold Hearth Manor is a blighted farmstead located just west of Brill along the main road of Tirisfal Glades. Once a bustling, hospitable estate known for bountiful crops, the outbreak of the Plague of Undeath wiped out its residents, leaving the surrounding fields choked with mindless Scourge. Today, the Forsaken have secured the main farmhouse as an outpost and waystation for travelers. Before the Third War, this homestead bore a reputation for warmth and hospitality, supporting rich harvests in the heart of Lordaeron. When the Plague swept through the kingdom, the entire family and their laborers succumbed, rising again as husks bound to the Scourge. While feral undead still stumble through the ruined fields, Forsaken forces managed to push the mindless dead out of the main farmhouse, reclaiming the structure to serve as a trading post and foothold along the road toward the eastern glades.

Coldridge Pass. Coldridge Pass is a rugged, snowbound tunnel cutting through the southern mountain ridge of Dun Morogh. It serves as the sole overland route connecting the secluded training grounds of Coldridge Valley to the rest of the kingdom, emerging near the bustling town of Kharanos. Because hostile troggs have overrun the passage, any traveler attempting the journey must either fight their way through or make a desperate dash for the other side. For young dwarven recruits and gnome novices taking their first steps beyond Coldridge Valley, Coldridge Pass is a harsh rite of passage. Chiseled straight through the rock, this tunnel forms the primary link sending newly trained adventurers eastward toward the frontier hub of Kharanos. What was once a secure mountain corridor has become a perilous choke point, infested with aggressive troggs that have pushed up from dark sub-terrains to menace any soul trying to travel between the sheltered valley and the wider reaches of Dun Morogh.

text.enUS: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery is a simple courier task entrusted to recruits by Sten Stoutarm at Anvilmar. With mountain passes often choked with snow and troggs pressing nearby, carrying fresh correspondence out to the camps along the frozen lake keeps the valley's isolated defenders connected. Life in Coldridge Valley is secluded even in the calmest of seasons. When winter couriers successfully navigate the mountain pass with mail from the rest of Dun Morogh, the missives pile up quickly at Anvilmar. Sten Stoutarm, busy managing local supply concerns and security, relies on wandering recruits to carry these bundles down the western road rather than letting vital tidings languish in the hall.
