text.enUS: Coldridge Valley Mail Delivery. This errand completes a courier run across the snowy drifts of Coldridge Valley. Passing the dispatch from mountaineer Talin Keeneye down the southeastern road ensures that Grelin Whitebeard stays connected to the dwarven capital. Even in an isolated basin like Coldridge Valley, news and formal correspondence must travel. While Anvilmar serves as the administrative heart of the valley, field scouts and sentries stationed along the trails rely on foot couriers to relay dispatches between the high passes and Ironforge.

Coleman Farthing. Coleman Farthing is a bitter Forsaken survivor residing in the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill. In life, he worked for the wealthy Agamand dynasty at their extensive flour mills in northern Tirisfal. Convinced to stay and defend the estate against the Scourge, he died alongside his fellow laborers, and now dedicates his undeath to exacting vengeance on his former masters. Before the Third War, Coleman Farthing earned an honest living as a laborer at the Agamand Mills, the largest milling and agricultural operation in Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge poured across Lordaeron, the aristocratic Agamand family refused to flee their valuable lands. Instead, they urged their household and laborers to take up arms alongside them, promising they could hold the farmsteads against the undead horde. Coleman and his fellow workers stayed, believing their masters—a decision that cost every last one of them their lives.

Collecting Kelp. In Goldshire, Maybell Maclure seeks a way to visit Tommy Joe Stonefield unseen. William Pestle needs rare crystal kelp to brew an invisibility liquor for her. The feud between the Stonefield and Maclure families keeps Maybell Maclure and Tommy Joe Stonefield from meeting openly. Maybell wants to see her beloved without provoking an armed clash between their kin, so she seeks a way to cross the valley unseen. William Pestle, an herbalist and apothecary at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, plans to brew an invisibility liquor. The rare ingredients he needs are not in the inn's cupboards.

name.frFR: À la recherche de cartes du syndicat des mineurs

text.enUS: Collecting Memories. Collecting Memories is a solemn task entrusted by the dwarven miner Wilder Thistlenettle in Stormwind City. He asks adventurers braving the ruined mines beneath Moonbrook to recover the Miners' Union Cards of his fallen coworkers. Bringing these tokens back offers grieving families in the capital closure following a catastrophic cave-in. Before Moonbrook fell completely into lawlessness and the shadow of the Defias Brotherhood, the mines of Westfall were an active source of livelihood for many working-class families. Wilder Thistlenettle survived a devastating cave-in that buried a wing of the labyrinthine tunnels, but many of his friends and coworkers were not so fortunate. Cut off from rescue, those workers perished deep underground, leaving behind mourning kin in Stormwind who never received true confirmation or closure regarding their loved ones' fates.

Collin Mauren. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies practical magic and crafts useful spells from natural reagents. He also makes arcane scrolls for his friend Gaxim Rustfizzle, a gnome engineer and explorer. In Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Collin Mauren studies magic's practical uses. He crafts arcane formulas to solve specific problems, drawing on natural anomalies and raw components gathered across Azeroth. Their properties help him make functional scrolls and reagents for friends and travelers.

Colonel Kurzen. Colonel Conrad Kurzen was once a decorated and noble officer of the Stormwind Army, sent to lead an expedition into northern Stranglethorn Vale. After descending into sudden madness and tyranny, he turned his force into a rogue jungle militia operating out of an armed compound. Today, his former subordinates at the nearby Rebel Camp actively seek his death to end his reign of terror. Before his downfall, Colonel Conrad Kurzen was regarded in Stormwind as an exceptionally capable and noble officer. Trusted by the kingdom's leadership, he was granted command of an expeditionary unit dispatched south into the dense jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. However, deep within the humid wilds, Kurzen began to exhibit erratic behavior and extreme megalomania, declaring absolute sovereignty over the surrounding wilderness and abandoning his allegiance to Stormwind.

Colonel Kurzen. Lieutenant Doren calls upon you to deliver the final strike against Colonel Kurzen and his inner guard. You are sent into the Stockpile to eliminate the rogue commander and his remaining leaders to secure the Rebel Camp's survival. Lieutenant Doren and his band of defectors have reached the climax of their struggle against their former commander. Following the suppression of Kurzen's elite specialists, Doren recognizes that the rebel forces will never truly be safe while Kurzen retains control of his jungle redoubt. He directs you into the Stockpile cave, where Kurzen directs his forces alongside his subchiefs and elites.

Comar's Heart. Comar's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Comar Villard, a faithful human wanderer searching the marshes of the Wetlands for his lost wife. Forsaken warlocks in the Undercity seek out this relic of pure devotion to feed the summoning rites of a succubus. To bind a creature as capricious and predatory as a succubus, warlocks must bait the demon with true purity and devotion. Carendin Halgar's disciples in the Undercity identify Comar Villard as one of the few men possessing such unblemished fidelity. While his wife was lost amidst the turmoil sweeping the Eastern Kingdoms, Comar stubbornly wanders the sodden roads of the Wetlands, refusing to abandon his search. It is precisely this unwavering love that marks him for slaughter, turning his still-beating heart into the ideal lure for a demonic servant.

Coming of Age. Coming of Age marks the initial rite of passage for young Skyborne taking their first steps beyond Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Guided by Ailee Farheart, novices report to village leader Rorian the Dayseeker to receive an ancestral relic and formally pledge their aid to the shen'dorei. For every young Skyborne coming into adulthood, the journey begins in Thendal Village. Guided forward by Ailee Farheart, fledglings make their way just west to the greatfather tree where the village elder awaits. Passing into maturity among the shen'dorei is not merely a social milestone, but a ceremonial commitment to serve their community amid rising local troubles.

Coming to Terms. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this quest tasks newly risen paladins with reaching out to a fellow knight struggling to accept undeath. Fleeing into the hills in terror, the newly returned warrior faces the agonizing realization of becoming what she once fought against. Awakening from death into the ranks of the Forsaken is jarring for anyone, but for former paladins of the Silver Hand, the shock is visceral. Having dedicated their mortal lives to destroying the undead in service to the Holy Light, these individuals suddenly find their souls tethered back to decomposing flesh. While some adapt under the guidance of Aramis Hammerhand, others are overwhelmed by horror and confusion, fleeing into the Tirisfal wilderness rather than confronting their grim new existence.

Command Center. In Stormwind's Old Town, the Command Center trains recruits while most of the army serves abroad. Also called the Stormwind Barracks, it houses the city's military officers and a seasoned skeleton crew focused on drilling recruits and local militia. In Old Town, Stormwind's Command Center is a garrison and training ground for the kingdom's soldiers. Its halls are quieter than usual, with much of the royal army committed to campaigns abroad. Veteran instructors, including Ander Germaine and martial artist Wu Shen, train fresh warriors to strengthen the city's defenses.

Commander Mar'alith. Commander Mar'alith is the stalwart night elf military commander directing the Cenarion Circle's vanguard at Cenarion Hold in Silithus. Clad in heavy armor and wielding a grand glaive, he coordinates the martial resistance against the silithid swarms and Twilight's Hammer cultists. Beneath his resolute leadership lies a deep personal sorrow regarding the mysterious fate of his beloved wife, Natalia. Stationed at the heart of Cenarion Hold, Commander Mar'alith bears the tremendous responsibility of safeguarding the Circle's desert bastion. While the druids unravel the ancient ecological and cosmic anomalies of Silithus, Mar'alith handles the grim, practical necessities of war. He oversees tactical strikes against the bustling silithid hives of Hive'Ashi, Hive'Zora, and Hive'Regal, ensuring that the relentless insectoid incursions do not overwhelm the expedition's central foothold.

Commander Springvale. Commander Springvale was once a devoted paladin and a commander at Shadowfang Keep. Slain alongside his men during the feral worgen slaughter orchestrated by Archmage Arugal, his vengeful spirit remains behind to haunt the castle halls. Even in death, his ghost fiercely guards the keep against all who enter. Before the ruin of Shadowfang Keep, Commander Springvale stood as an honorable paladin dedicated to the Holy Light. Leading the garrison in Silverpine Forest, he oversaw the keep's security during the fraught days following the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge.

Commons. The Commons serves as the vibrant commercial heart of Ironforge, connecting the city entrance directly to its vast caverns. Teeming with merchants, travelers, and bankers, it is the busiest thoroughfare in the dwarven capital and the central marketplace for the entire Alliance. Located just northeast of the Gates of Ironforge, the Commons is the first district that greets travelers entering the mountain kingdom. Carved directly out of the stone, this bustling market street houses the primary Alliance Auction House, the Stonefire Tavern, and the city's central bank within the Vault of Ironforge. Broad avenues connect it seamlessly to the Great Forge, the Mystic Ward, and the Military Ward, ensuring that nearly all foot traffic in the mountain passes through its bustling storefronts.

text.enUS: Components for the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe. Menara Voidrender tasks aspiring warlocks in the Barrens with procuring a set of Robes of Arcana as the base garment for a potent magical garment. This marks the initial step in crafting the Enchanted Gold Bloodrobe, establishing the foundational vessel needed to withstand dark enchantments. Before dark magic can be bound to cloth, the garment itself must be worthy of bearing such power. Menara Voidrender instructs warlocks seeking greater power to procure a set of Robes of Arcana. As Menara explains, the capacity of any magical relic relies on the skill, rarity, and effort woven into its base materials. Mundane rags would unravel under the strain of deep enchantments, making a finely stitched, receptive garment indispensable.

name.frFR: Sous les drapeaux de la Horde

text.enUS: Conscript of the Horde. Conscript of the Horde is an introductory transition quest that directs young Horde adventurers out of Durotar and into the vast wilderness of the Barrens. Initiated by the scout Takrin Pathseeker along the western road from Razor Hill, it sends recruits across the Southfury River to Kargal Battlescar's border outpost. Once an aspiring Horde soldier proves their strength around Razor Hill, the needs of the wider nation call them westward. Takrin Pathseeker keeps watch along the dirt highway leaving Durotar, evaluating travelers on behalf of his friend, veteran Kargal Battlescar. Taking Takrin's recruitment letter marks a recruit's first formal assignment beyond the orcs' new homeland of Durotar.

Consecrated Letter. The Consecrated Letter is an introductory summons carried by initiates of the Holy Light arriving in Northshire Valley. It directs the bearer to report to their class trainer at Northshire Abbey to begin their training and embrace their role as a visible symbol of faith. The Consecrated Letter marks the formal beginning of an initiate's journey in Northshire Valley. Addressed to newly arrived wielders of the Holy Light, the document calls the bearer to seek out their trainer at Northshire Abbey to formalize their instruction and accept their responsibilities within the Kingdom of Stormwind.

Consecrated Rune. A Consecrated Rune is an inscribed sacred item passed to fledgling dwarven paladins training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as an introductory summons from Bromos Grummner, directing initiates to report to Anvilmar and begin their formal duties as Knights of the Silver Hand. Novice dwarven paladins proving themselves in Coldridge Valley are handed a Consecrated Rune once they have shown basic martial competence. Inscribed with sacred words and blessed by the Holy Light, the rune originates from Bromos Grummner, the paladin trainer residing inside Anvilmar. Dwarves hold immense respect for the traditions of the Holy Light introduced to them by their human allies. Reading the rune serves as both an official summons and a symbolic rite of passage, confirming the novice's place among the Knights of the Silver Hand.

Consecrated Rune. The Consecrated Rune is an introductory summons delivered to fledgling dwarven paladins in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of Bromos Grummner, it marks an initiate's formal induction into the Knights of the Silver Hand. While novice adventurers clear out troggs and wolves around Coldridge Valley, the local leaders keep a close eye on those who display a gift for divine martial prowess. Sten Stoutarm delivers this inscribed rune to young paladins, instructing them to seek out Bromos Grummner inside the warmth of Anvilmar. It serves as both an invitation and an official notice that raw potential must now be tempered with discipline.

Console Key. The Console Key is a mechanical bypass key held by Tinkerer Sniggles at the Venture Company digsite in the Barrens. It unlocks the main control terminal housing the samophlange, allowing the device to be extracted after the apparatus has been shut down. The Venture Company maintains an extensive industrial outpost in the northern Barrens, reliant on specialized steam-driven machinery regulated by an enigmatic device known as a samophlange. To prevent unauthorized tampering, the apparatus console is locked tight. Only the chief technician on site, Tinkerer Sniggles, carries the Console Key required to pop open the terminal casing and completely cut power to the rig.

Consult Master Gadrin. Apothecary Lydon found the venom from the broodguards less potent than the sample you first brought, which points to another kind of spider. Lydon sends you to Master Gadrin in Sen'jin Village, in Durotar, who may know more. Apothecary Lydon found the venom taken from the broodguards weaker than the sample you brought first, so it must come from a different spider. Lydon wants a fresh sample of the stronger kind. To learn where it comes from, ask a troll well acquainted with the Witherbark: Master Gadrin, in Sen'jin Village, in Durotar. With luck, Gadrin can name the source of that venom.

Consumed by Hatred. Consumed by Hatred is a grim task given by Mankrik at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Tormented by the violent ambush that separated him from his wife, the grieving orc directs his agonizing uncertainty into a relentless vendetta against the Bristleback quilboar. He calls upon Horde travelers to slaughter the creatures in droves and return with a massive tally of their tusks. Standing under the harsh sun of the Crossroads, Mankrik is a warrior possessed by grief. After surviving a vicious raid by the quilboar that left him battered and his wife missing, he spends his waking hours watching the arid horizon for any sign of the pig men. His thirst for their blood remains unquenched despite the many he has personally cut down, driving him to seek help from fellow members of the Horde.

Continue Your Training. This quest directs newly risen Forsaken paladins to leave Deathknell and travel to Brill for advanced instruction. Entrusted by Aramis Hammerhand, the journey introduces the fledgling holy warrior to the wider perils of Tirisfal Glades. It also serves as a stark warning about the deep suspicion that holy practitioners face among the undead. Once a newly awakened soul has mastered the rudiments of martial combat and channelled holy power within Deathknell's cloistered graveyard, Aramis Hammerhand sends them east into the broader expanse of Tirisfal Glades. Their destination is Brill, a bustling regional outpost serving as the administrative hub for central Tirisfal. There, Shari Stilwell oversees the advancement of those who dare walk the path of the paladin in undeath.

Continue to Stormwind. You carry a requisition from Sentinel Hill to Stormwind by gryphon, where Osric Strang awaits in Old Town. Quartermaster Lewis prepares a requisition note in Sentinel Hill. The local gryphon master Thor offers you the fastest way out of the contested plains. For a modest fee, you ride one of the kingdom's trained gryphons above dusty farmlands and the river border of Elwynn Forest, then over Stormwind City's high white ramparts.

Continued Threat. Katar is pleased that your hatred of the fish men is growing alongside Katar's own, and sends you to hunt further fish men on the beach in the Swamp of Sorrows. Katar tells you to find more of the fish men along the beach, and to return once you have had enough of fighting. Marsh inkspewers, marsh flesheaters and marsh oracles are the ones wanted. Katar will take no pleasure until the sea and every one of her children is silenced, least of all the repulsive fish men.

text.enUS: Control Console Operating Manual. The Control Console Operating Manual is a technical document detailing how to operate the machinery at the Venture Company research site southwest of Sludge Fen. It contains instructions needed to safely shut down the valves and disengage the mysterious contraption known as a samophlange. The Venture Company operates a secluded drilling and research site in the northern Barrens, southwest of Sludge Fen. In typical goblin fashion, their complex machinery runs on an erratic array of gauges, pressurized valves, and interconnected mechanisms designed to harness a device called a samophlange. Without proper operating procedures, manipulating such volatile contraptions risks catastrophic backfire or complete system lockouts. This operational manual outlines the precise sequence of valve manipulation required to disengage the core apparatus safely without triggering an explosive failure.

Cookie. Cookie is an elite murloc serving as the ship's cook aboard the juggernaut hidden deep within the Deadmines. An unusual recruit among the Defias Brotherhood, he tends the crew's cauldrons beneath the watchful eye of Captain Greenskin and Edwin VanCleef. He is the only entirely optional boss encountered within the underground dry dock. Beneath the decks of the towering juggernaut in the Ironclad Cove, cooking duty falls neither to a human outrider nor a goblin engineer, but to a solitary murloc known simply as Cookie. How he came by the position is anyone's guess. Whatever doubts the rest of the crew might harbor about a murloc presiding over their rations, pirates are rarely in a position to be picky, and in the underworld of Moonbrook, a meal is a meal.

Coolant Heads Prevail. Lotwil Veriatus wants a vial of Frost Oil to strengthen the shackles meant to hold a summoned friend in check. Bro'kin, a goblin friend of Lotwil's in Alterac, can teach you to make it. Lotwil Veriatus swears nothing keeps an engine or gears from overheating like Frost Oil, and that its worth as a lubricant is without equal. It also helps magical items hold on to their enchantments. A vial would raise the magical capacity of Lotwil's shackles, making them strong enough to stop the summoned friend from killing everyone.

Corin's Crossing. Corin's Crossing is a ruined human settlement situated at a major crossroads in south-central Eastern Plaguelands. Once a thriving waystation between Stratholme, Tyr's Hand, Darrowshire, and Andorhal, the devastated town is now utterly overrun by the Scourge. Its crumbling town hall and forge harbor lingering horrors, including invisible spectral watchers. Before the Third War, Corin's Crossing served as a central junction for travel across eastern Lordaeron. Positioned between the shimmering waters of Lake Mereldar and what has now become the blighted chasm of the Infectis Scar, its thoroughfares once bore merchants, couriers, and pilgrims traveling between the great bastion of Stratholme and the southern strongholds. When the plague swept through the province, the settlement stood directly in the path of destruction, collapsing swiftly beneath the sheer weight of the undead vanguard.

Corithras Moonrage. Corithras Moonrage is a night elf scholar and quest giver stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He guides newly arrived adventurers in understanding the nature of the great World Tree and tasks them with maintaining its sacred moonwells. Through his lessons, he reveals both the spiritual importance of Teldrassil and the growing burdens carried by the kaldorei. Residing in the shaded settlement of Dolanaar, Corithras Moonrage serves as an instructor to travelers leaving the sheltered bounds of Shadowglen. As young kaldorei venture into the wider boughs of Teldrassil, Corithras ensures they understand the history of their new home. He teaches that survival in this changing era requires vigilance and reverence for the natural order.

Corrahn's Dagger. Corrahn's Dagger is the second ridge among the four mountainous fingers towering over northern Hillsbrad Foothills. This high ground serves as a hideout for rogue Syndicate operatives. Rising steeply in northern Hillsbrad Foothills, Corrahn's Dagger is the second of the four rocky projections known locally as the fingers of Hillsbrad. The ridge is overrun by cutthroats belonging to the Syndicate, who use the elevated perch to overlook the valley below.

Corroded Shrapnel. Corroded Shrapnel consists of jagged metal fragments lodged deep within the corrupted treants of the Stonetalon Mountains. Recovered from fallen protectors like Charred and Blackened Ancients, this debris provides physical evidence of the foul weaponry used by the Venture Company during their retreat. When the Venture Company was driven back from the groves of Stonetalon, the goblins unleashed brutal, reckless munitions to cover their escape. Shrapnel from these explosive weapons tore into the valley's defending treants, embedding jagged metal deep within their bark and core. Rather than healing, the ancient guardians slowly fell to corruption, their wood blackening and their fury turning upon anyone who stepped into the vale. The rusted, tainted fragments recovered from these wounded protectors are sought by Kaela Shadowspear so the gnome Gaxim Rustfizzle can analyze the exact mechanisms of the corruption.

Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers. Corrupt Manifestation's Bracers are the physical remnants recovered from a tainted water elemental on the coast of Silverpine Forest. Taken by shaman initiates undergoing the Call of Water, they serve as a vital component in an elemental cleansing rite atop the Brazier of Everfount. When the Scourge's plague swept through Lordaeron, it did not spare the natural spirits of the land. Along the misty shores of Silverpine Forest west of the Sepulcher, a once-sacred water shrine fell victim to taint, twisting its resident water manifestation into an aggressive, corrupted shade. Shaman initiates are sent to quell the creature and retrieve its bracers. Combined with purest water upon the Brazier of Everfount, these bindings are cast into the flame to undo the defilement and summon forth an unblemished elemental spirit.

Corrupted Brain Stem. Corrupted Brain Stems are biological specimens harvested from the twisted naga and satyrs inhabiting Blackfathom Deeps and the Ashenvale coastline. Gershala Nightwhisper of Auberdine seeks them to study the physical deformities wrought by reckless magical corruption. By examining these brains, night elf scholars hope to understand and potentially prevent a similar fate from befalling the blood elves. The satyrs and naga of Kalimdor stand as living testaments to the warping power of forbidden magic and demonic pacts. Long ago, reckless kaldorei highborne were irrevocably transformed into serpent-like aquatic beasts and demonic horned fiends. The brain stems harvested from these creatures exhibit heavy physical mutation, providing direct anatomical proof of how deep corruptive energies burrow into the nervous systems of once-elven beings.

Corrupted Kor Gem. A Corrupted Kor Gem is a potent magical conduit warped by the dark rites of the naga residing around Blackfathom Deeps. Spellcasters covet such stones for their capacity to store sheer arcane force, though the gem's tainted state demands purification before it can serve righteous crafts. Kor gems naturally possess the rare ability to capture and contain substantial magical energies, making them invaluable focuses for sorcerers and enchanted smithing. Along the coastline near the ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, however, the resident naga oracles and tide priestesses claim these gems for their own shadowy rituals. Through foul enchantments, the serpent-kin warp the stone, suffusing it with malevolent, sea-borne corruption. While this infusion taints the gem's nature, the core latent power remains potent, drawing those in need of exceptional magical foci to harvest them from the naga.

Cortello's Riddle. A hidden parchment found aboard the Bloodsail Buccaneer vessels along the Wild Shore presents Cortello's cryptic verse. Deciphering the poem points travelers toward a clue waiting beneath an ornate bridge. Scattered notes aboard the Bloodsail fleet anchored off the southern coast of Stranglethorn Vale carry a rhyme. Cortello's verse describes a finely worked, much-used bridge that lies east of Deadwind and south of Redridge. Anyone seeking to unravel the mystery must follow these poetic directions out of the jungle and into the marshes to find what waits underneath.

Cortello's Riddle. Following the trail begun with a waterlogged parchment found in the Swamp of Sorrows, a second cryptic verse urges travelers to a far-off land in Kalimdor. Deciphering the lines points treasure hunters toward a cave in the southwest of Dustwallow Marsh. The second verse left by Cortello directs searchers toward the far-off land of Kalimdor. The rhyme describes a perilous and gloomy territory situated east of the Barrens: the sodden, treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh.

Cortello's Riddle. A cryptic musty scroll provides the final set of verse left behind by Cortello. The rhyming instructions direct treasure hunters far north to the troubled continent of Lordaeron, where the trail reaches its conclusion along the coastal waterfalls of the Hinterlands. Following the earlier scrolls, this weathered text points away from the southern tropics toward the embattled lands of Lordaeron. The riddle bids searchers to seek out the great turmoil in the north, promising that the long chase ends by braving that unrest and pursuing the coastline.

Costly Menace. Darren Malvew of Southshore hates losing the town's beautiful horses. Undead, the Syndicate gang and assorted scoundrels have cost plenty, but Darren says nothing threatens them more than the mountain lions that keep coming down from the hills of Alterac. Darren Malvew of Southshore cannot stand losing the beautiful horses there. Quite a few have been lost to undead creeps, the Syndicate gang and the scoundrels poking about the region. By Darren's own word, though, no menace to the horses is bigger than the mountain lions up in Alterac, forever coming down from the hills.

name.esES: Garras de puma de las estepas

text.enUS: Cougar Claws. Cougar Claws are harvested from flatland cougars that roam the central plains of Mulgore. They serve as a vital material in tauren ritual craft, embodying the untamed balance and natural ferocity of the wild predators. The flatland cougar is one of the apex hunters of Mulgore's sprawling grasslands, stalking prey with instinctual grace. In tauren tradition, taking the claws of such a predator is not an act of casual slaughter or trophy hunting, but a way to harness the natural spirit of the beast. When goblin operations begin defiling the ancestral waters of the plains, Mull Thunderhorn calls upon young hunters to gather these claws alongside those of prairie stalkers. The tauren believe that the pure, uncorrupted predatory instincts of native beasts can be woven into a ritual totem capable of scouring unnatural toxins and foul sorcery from the poisoned Thunderhorn Water Well.

Councilman Millstipe. Councilman Millstipe is a member of Darkshire's governing council, residing within the town hall of Duskwood. Deeply resentful of royal neglect and judicial meddling from the capital, he actively seeks retribution against criminals who endanger the darkened region. While Darkshire struggles under the shadow of the undead and ferocious beast attacks, its local council fights an uphill battle against the bureaucracy of Stormwind City. Councilman Millstipe represents the town's growing bitterness toward the crown. When the notorious grave robber Dextren Ward was caught selling freshly dug corpses to the necromancer Morbent Fel, Darkshire's leaders sentenced him to death. Instead, Stormwind's House of Nobles intervened, commuting Ward's execution and locking him safely away inside the Stormwind Stockade.

Count Remington Ridgewell. In Stormwind Keep, Count Remington Ridgewell tends a collection fit for a noble’s pride. A wealthy human in the House of Nobles, he gathers rare artifacts, heirlooms, and fine art. Count Remington Ridgewell favors antiquities over military campaigns or local uprisings. His family’s personal museum holds jewelry and artifacts, and he spends his wealth gathering relics from fallen civilizations and houses across Azeroth. To fill his gallery, he finances adventurers and sends field agents such as Mayara Brightwing to retrieve rare objects from dangerous ruins, from Alterac’s mountain redoubts to the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes.

Counterattack!. Following the systematic elimination of their local chieftains in the Barrens, the Kolkar centaur mount a desperate retaliation out of Desolace. An invading force marches directly upon Regthar Deathgate's outpost west of the Crossroads, culminating in a fierce confrontation with Warlord Krom'zar. The campaign against the Kolkar centaur in the Barrens struck deep into their tribal leadership. With Barak Kodobane, Verog the Dervish, and Hezrul Bloodmark dead, the remaining centaur found themselves shattered and without direction. In response to this humiliation, word traveled west across the mountains to their ancestral homeland in Desolace. Rather than scattering into the scrubland, a fresh contingent of hardened Kolkar warriors rallied and crossed into the Barrens, burning for blood and retribution against the fledgling Horde encampments.

Courser Eye. Courser Eyes are biological reagents harvested from the antlered coursers roaming the highlands of Stonetalon Mountains. Witch Doctor Jin'Zil in Malaka'jin seeks a large quantity of them to prepare a concoction he mockingly refers to as forest magic.

Covert Ops - Alpha. Covert Ops - Alpha is an Alliance infiltration mission directed by the gnome tinker Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. While operating out of the peaks, operatives are tasked with penetrating the Venture Company's lumber mill in Windshear Crag to recover proprietary engineering schematics. Securing these blueprints allows the Alliance to decipher the mechanical vulnerabilities of goblin machinery while co-opting their logging technology. Operating from Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle conducts a persistent covert campaign to disrupt the aggressive logging operations of the Venture Company. While goblin deforesters fell the primeval timber south of Cragpool Lake, Gaxim recognizes that wanton destruction alone cannot halt the enterprise. Instead of merely detonating industrial hardware, Plan Alpha prioritizes intelligence gathering, requiring agents to slip past goblin loggers and overseers to seize their core technical schematics directly from the lumber mill.

Covert Ops - Beta. Covert Ops - Beta is an Alliance mission organized by the gnome engineer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Building upon previous sabotage against the encroaching Venture Company, this operation sends an agent deep into Windshear Mine to trigger explosive diversions and extract vital operational letters. The retrieved intelligence serves both gnome curiosity and the territorial defense of the regional night elf Sentinels. Following initial strikes against the Venture Company's clear-cutting operations across Windshear Crag, Gaxim Rustfizzle devises a follow-up operation aimed directly at their logistical heart. Plan Beta follows the same fundamental logic as its predecessor: creating an explosive, chaotic diversion to scatter the goblin operators and mercenaries while an operative slips through the confusion to search the mines for written correspondence.

Covert Ops Pack. The Covert Ops Pack is a kit of specialized demolitions gear and operational schematics assembled for Alliance espionage in the Stonetalon Mountains. Designed to dismantle the Venture Company's rapacious presence in Windshear Crag, the satchel equips agents to trigger coordinated sabotage while securing high-value technical intelligence. Issued for clandestine strikes deep within Venture Company territory, the Covert Ops Pack pairs brute destructive power with tactical precision. Inside are color-coded NG-5 explosives matched to remote triggers, alongside thorough instructions designated Plan Alpha and Plan Beta. The strategy relies on triggering high-yield distractions at key infrastructure nodes—namely the Cragpool Lake lumber mill and the eastern mine. While goblins scramble to extinguish blazes and assess mechanical failures, an infiltrator slips past the chaos to pilfer critical documents and schematics.

Coyote Thieves. In the outpost of Kargath, Neeka Bloodscar wants you to hunt the crag coyotes of the Badlands, tough beasts that have dared to sneak into Kargath and steal its food. Thirty jawbones are what Neeka asks for. Neeka Bloodscar asks whether you have spent many days in the Badlands, felt its heat and met the beasts of its dusty plains. Crag coyotes are a tough breed, and they have crept into Kargath to steal from the outpost's food. Neeka wants them hunted and their jawbones brought back. Bring enough, and Neeka may believe you know the Badlands.

Crab Season. Crab Season is an urgent foraging task on Zephras centered on harvesting rare Windsong crawlers during their brief annual window. Because recent cultist activity has made the shores of Windsong Lake perilous, adventurers are called upon to brave both hostile interlopers and aggressive crustaceans. On the shores of Windsong Lake across Zephras, a brief seasonal harvesting window opens for only a few weeks each year. The native Windsong crawlers emerge in numbers along the freshwater banks and tributary rivers, offering a rare harvest of meat to anyone bold enough to gather them before the annual opportunity slips away.

Cracking Maury's Foot. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley has retrieved the foot of his late debtor Maury, only to find that what he is owed is locked inside it. To claim what is owed, he directs travelers to the Mosh'Ogg ogre mound in Stranglethorn Vale to search for the missing key. Following the retrieval of Maury's foot in Voodoo Dues, "Sea Wolf" MacKinley faces an unexpected complication in Booty Bay. The late debtor put a lock on his foot, and the valuables he owes are sealed inside.

Craftsmen's Terrace. The Craftsmen's Terrace is the bustling artisan district situated in the northern reaches of Darnassus. It serves as the primary trade and manufacturing hub for the night elf capital, housing workshops, profession trainers, and a lively inn. The district also hosts external representatives, including an embassy for the neutral Argent Dawn. Spanning the northern edge of the canopy city, the Craftsmen's Terrace gathers the diverse trades that keep Darnassus running. Woodworkers, leathercrafters, alchemists, and other artisans operate their shops here, integrating classic night elven methods with practical craft. The district also provides essential community amenities, including an inn, a guild master, and guild petition vendors. Bridges connect the terrace directly to the Cenarion Enclave to the west and the Warrior's Terrace to the south.

Crag of the Everliving. The Crag of the Everliving is a verdant cavern chamber nestled deep within the Wailing Caverns. Dominated by lush, corrupted flora and predatory plant creatures, it serves as the domain of the Fanglord Lord Pythas. Its towering upper reaches shelter the ancient entity after whom the crag is named. While much of the Wailing Caverns is carved of damp subterranean stone, the Crag of the Everliving bursts with unruly, twisted vegetation fueled by the Nightmare corrupting Naralex's slumber. Towering mossy platforms and winding paths are choked with Deviate Shamblers—living plant hulks prowling the undergrowth. Lord Pythas, one of Naralex's fallen disciples, watches over the crag's central reaches, having traded his noble druidic vows for the venomous rites of the Druids of the Fang.

Cragpool Lake. Cragpool Lake is a body of water tucked inside Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains. Looming above its dark waters sits a massive timber structure erected by the Venture Company. Nestled within Windshear Crag, Cragpool Lake lies directly beneath the towering logging apparatus built by the Venture Company. An enormous wooden structure spans above the water, serving as the vantage point from which Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle oversees operations across the mountain valley. Venture Company workers occupy the platforms overhead.

text.enUS: Crane Operator Bigglefuzz. Crane Operator Bigglefuzz is a goblin dockhand working the heavy machinery at the port of Ratchet. After an overloaded crane mishap scattered cargo across the docks, he finds himself desperate to recover a valuable stolen bottle before his superiors notice. Like many goblin dockworkers, Crane Operator Bigglefuzz prioritized efficiency and haste over basic safety margins. While attempting to hoist an excessively heavy haul from a merchant vessel, his crane buckled, sending crates crashing down across the Ratchet wharves. In the ensuing chaos, opportunistic scoundrels swept in, leaving Bigglefuzz to scramble to clean up the mess and salvage the most precious goods before Gazlowe or the local port masters dock his pay.

Crate With Holes. A portable transport container provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Pierced with air vents, it safely houses a trained Snufflenose Gopher used to track down subterranean culinary delicacies within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul. To acquire rare Blueleaf Tubers from the thorny depths of Razorfen Kraul, goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix relies on trained Snufflenose Gophers rather than blind digging. Because gophers cannot simply follow an adventurer across the dusty trails of the Barrens on foot, Mebok packs each critter into a well-ventilated wooden crate. Once brought into the humid, root-choked corridors of the quilboar lair, the crate is unlatched, allowing the beast within to follow its keen sense of smell toward buried tubers.

Crate of Crash Helmets. A heavy supply shipment of dwarven Siege Engine headgear destined for the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. The sturdy helmets are urgently required by the Brassbolts brothers to protect test drivers from concussions caused by their experimental rocket cars. Out across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineers test the absolute limits of mechanical propulsion. Unfortunately for the test pilots, the experimental rocket cars designed by the Brassbolts brothers move far faster than their steering can reliably handle. With drivers routinely suffering violent crashes and head trauma, ordinary leather caps no longer suffice. To prevent their roster of willing daredevils from vanishing entirely, heavy-duty dwarven Siege Engine helmets are packed and dispatched across the sea to keep drivers conscious—and alive.

Crate of Horseshoes. In Elwynn, fifty iron horseshoes are bound for Lakeshire. Smith Argus forged fifty fresh horseshoes in Goldshire, then packed the crate and hammered it shut. Verner Osgood commissioned them for Lakeshire, where constant pressure from gnolls and orcs leaves local craftsmen reliant on Elwynn for essential metal goods. The delivery answers Verner's desperate need for equipment, and Argus includes a stern bill of sale so the Redridge craftsman knows frontier survival comes at a steep price.

name.ruRU: Ящик с припасами для постоялого двора

text.enUS: Crate of Inn Supplies. The Crate of Inn Supplies is a parcel packed in Coldridge Valley destined for the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. With the mountain pass overrun by troggs, regular supply routes are cut, leaving the inn dependent on passing travelers to carry goods through. Ordinarily, goods flow smoothly between the quiet training grounds of Anvilmar and the bustling towns of Dun Morogh. However, recent trogg incursions have severed Coldridge Pass, cutting off civilian couriers until armed Mountaineer escorts can clear the roads. Packed by Hands Springsprocket, this heavy crate holds essential tavern provisions that Tannok Frosthammer in Kharanos has been waiting on anxiously amid the disruption.

name.ptBR: Caixote de Lingotes de Forja de Luz

text.enUS: Crate of Lightforge Ingots. In Duskwood, the Crate of Lightforge Ingots carries hope against Morbent Fel. The rare consecrated metal is bound for the Dwarven District in Stormwind. Duskwood's hope rests in this crate of lightforge iron. The rare metal can channel holy power against dark entities, while Morbent Fel's protections turn aside ordinary steel. Only an artisan who knows its temper and honors its sacred nature can work it.

Craven Drok. Craven Drok is a wandering orc found skulking in the dimly lit tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow beneath Orgrimmar. True to his moniker, he keeps to the dark corners of the city, occasionally reaching out to travelers willing to help with a delicate matter: how the Alliance sees the Horde. While most orcs of Orgrimmar proudly walk the sunlit avenues of the Valley of Honor or the Valley of Strength, Craven Drok avoids the daylight entirely. He haunts the winding, subterranean paths of the Cleft of Shadow, an enclave typically reserved for warlocks, rogues, and practitioners of less honorable trades. Drok lives up to his cowardly reputation, preferring to stay out of sight while hiring passersby to carry out his discreet errands, including an errand concerning the Horde's standing with the Alliance.

Crawler Leg. A Crawler Leg is a harvested limb taken from the various crabs prowling the mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore. Though worthless to most travelers, these hardy chitinous appendages are surprisingly suited to mechanical improvisation. The crabs of Darkshore—ranging from pygmy tide crawlers to larger reef crawlers—are known for their sturdy, resilient shells. While night elf sentinels pay little mind to the discarded limbs of coastal vermin, the eccentric gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle found an unexpected use for them. Operating out of Auberdine, Wizbang designed his prototype long-distance communication devices, known as buzzboxes, to run on improvised local components. The segmented joints and durable chitin of crawler legs provide the precise mechanical friction and leverage required to repair Buzzbox 827, situated along the shoreline just south of town.

Creature of the Void. Creature of the Void is a pivotal rite of passage for Forsaken warlocks, tasking them with recovering a lost arcane text from the Scarlet Crusade. To learn how to summon and bind a chaotic voidwalker, an initiate must venture west into Tirisfal Glades and retrieve Egalin's Grimoire from hostile zealots. Within the dark alcoves of the Temple of the Damned in the Undercity, Carendin Halgar oversees the development of rising Forsaken summoners. When an acolyte proves competent enough to wield power beyond petty imps, Halgar directs them toward binding a creature forged from pure shadow and chaos: the voidwalker. Rather than relying on simple instinct, Forsaken practitioners base their summons on the meticulous research of Egalin, Halgar's own former master, who first penned the rituals necessary to subjugate these monstrous denizens of the void.

Creature of the Void. Creature of the Void is a pivotal rite of passage for young Horde warlocks training in Orgrimmar. Seeking to expand an initiate's summoning mastery to call forth a voidwalker, Gan'rul Bloodeye tasks the warlock with recovering the stolen Tablet of Verga from the rogue cultists of the Burning Blade hiding in Skull Rock. In the subterranean shadows of Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, Gan'rul Bloodeye watches over the Horde's practicing warlocks. Fel magic is viewed with deep wariness in Thrall's new realm, tainted as it is by the dark history of the orcish clans. Gan'rul acknowledges that few true warlocks remain within the Horde, yet he insists their perilous skills are essential for the Horde's survival. To be useful to the Warchief, an initiate cannot rely solely on the chaotic fire of an imp; they must learn to command beings of pure shadow and endurance.

Creeper Ichor. Creeper Ichor is a rare, virulent fluid harvested from the moss creepers lurking throughout the forests of the Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill as a potent biological agent for formulating novel plagues against the living. In Tarren Mill, Apothecary Lydon conducts experiments to craft deadly new toxins, seeking to eradicate the surrounding human population. Despising the clean air and vibrant life of the foothills, Lydon searches for natural toxins and biological catalysts native to the local wildlife. The venomous fluids of the forest's giant arachnids, particularly the elusive ichor found within mature moss creepers, serve as an ideal base for his Elixir of Suffering. Mixed with other reagents like gray bear tongues, this fluid aids the Forsaken in perfecting their craft of lethal alchemy.

Crest of Lordaeron. The Crest of Lordaeron is a weathered relic bearing the regal mark of the fallen northern kingdom. Found amidst the desolate ruins of Capital City, such relics are scarce since the kingdom's fall, and someone in Stormwind would be very keen to get their hands on this one. When the Scourge tore through the kingdom of Lordaeron, its palaces, archives, and proud insignias were largely obliterated or left to decay under the shadow of the Undercity. Surviving physical artifacts bearing the royal crest are exceedingly rare. Recovering an intact or weathered crest from the northern ruins represents a tangible piece of human history rescued from oblivion.

Crime and Punishment. Crime and Punishment is an Alliance bounty originating in Darkshire that demands the extrajudicial execution of a grave robber imprisoned within the Stormwind Stockade. Councilman Millstipe issues the contract after the House of Nobles overrides Duskwood's death sentence for Dextren Ward. Carrying out the hit satisfies local vengeance while delivering a sharp warning to the capital's negligent aristocracy. Duskwood already suffers beneath a shroud of creeping horrors and official indifference from the capital. When Dextren Ward was caught digging up fresh corpses from the Darkshire cemetery to sell to the necromancer Morbent Fel, the town's ruling council showed no mercy. Lord Ello Ebonlocke sentenced the grave robber to beheadment. However, before the axe could fall, the House of Nobles intervened, claiming Ward as an imperial prisoner and transferring him to the high-security cells of the Stormwind Stockade.

Croaky's Head. Croaky's Head is the severed bounty from a menacing murloc leader who terrorized the roads of eastern Elwynn Forest. Bringing proof of the creature's death to the Stormwind guard at Ridgepoint Tower offers grim relief to a garrison grieving their fallen comrades. It marks an essential victory for local defenders struggling to secure Elwynn's contested waterways. Murlocs along the rivers and streams of Elwynn Forest have grown increasingly bolder, ambushing unwary travelers and threatening vital trade routes. Among these aquatic raiders, Croaky stood out as a particularly aggressive chieftain, rallying other murlocs and leading attacks dangerously close to local roads. For merchants, farmers, and travelers moving between Elwynn and Redridge, the creature's presence turned peaceful roadways into deadly hazard zones. Striking down this aggressive raider halts a relentless series of ambushes, removing a brazen menace that openly challenged Stormwind's hold over the eastern woodland outskirts.

Crocolisk Hunting. Farstrider Lodge in Loch Modan does a steady, if dangerous, trade in the skins and meat of the local crocolisks. Marek Ironheart regularly seeks out hardy trackers willing to brave the lake's shores and islands to harvest these prized beasts. For hunters eager to test their mettle against snapping jaws and tough hides, the Loch offers both sport and profit. While Loch Modan is prized for its serene mountain waters, the lake harbors fierce predators beneath its surface. Crocolisks thrive along the shallows and muddy banks, making crossing or fishing perilous for the unwary. Yet for the outdoorsmen stationed at Farstrider Lodge, these dangerous reptiles are valuable game. Craftsmen and tailors throughout Khaz Modan constantly seek out durable crocolisk hides to fashion into rugged armor and leather goods, while rustic taverns pay good coin for fresh cuts of their flavorful, lean tail meat.

Crocolisk Skin (Classic). Crocolisk skins are harvested from the tough hides of the crocolisks inhabiting the islands and waters of the Loch in Loch Modan. Prized by merchants and leatherworkers for their durability, they fetch a respectable price despite the danger involved in securing them. The cold waters of the Loch teem with aggressive crocolisks that make their dens along the lake's islands and shores. Hunting them is no simple task, as these ferocious beasts possess razor-sharp teeth and thick, resilient scales capable of turning away careless blades. Despite the hazards, hunters operating out of Farstrider Lodge frequently harvest the creatures. Tailors, leatherworkers, and distant merchants continually seek out the skins to craft durable garments and protective armor, making a bundle of undamaged hides a valuable trade commodity in the region.

Crocolisk Tear (Classic). A Crocolisk Tear is a curious alchemical reagent gathered from the crocolisks inhabiting the waters of Loch Modan. It is sought by Chief Engineer Hinderweir to synthesize a neutralizing mixture capable of disarming Dark Iron explosives. Loch crocolisks are hardy reptiles native to the temperate waters of Loch Modan. While hunters often prize their skins and meat, Chief Engineer Hinderweir discovered an unexpected utility in their secretions. Combined with potent spider venom and resonant ogre minerals, the tear of a crocolisk provides the specific chemical properties needed to counteract volatile Dark Iron demolition charges threatening the Stonewrought Dam.

Crossroads. The Crossroads is the beating heart of Horde travel through central Kalimdor, situated where the north-south Gold Road intersects the path from Ratchet to the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a bustling trading outpost, military staging area, and transit hub for travelers journeying between Durotar, Mulgore, and northern frontlines. True to its name, the Crossroads sits squarely at the crossing of the Gold Road and the east-west route cutting from the goblin port of Ratchet into the Stonetalon Mountains. Despite having modest lodgings, the outpost functions as a bustling regional hub. Wind rider masters, merchants, blacksmiths, and trainers maintain permanent setups beneath its watchtowers. For young warriors traveling out from Durotar or Mulgore, the settlement is often the first place they witness the vast, multi-front logistics binding the new Horde together.

Crossroads Conscription. Crossroads Conscription directs newly enlisted Horde recruits from the border outpost into the heart of the Barrens. Carrying a signed letter from Kargal Battlescar, adventurers report directly to Sergra Darkthorn at the vital strategic hub known as the Crossroads. After proving their worth to Kargal Battlescar at the Far Watch Post on the border of Durotar, recruits are handed a signed recruitment letter and sent west. The journey follows the packed dirt road through the arid brush of the Barrens until reaching the central junction. At this sun-baked intersection sits the Crossroads, the Horde's vital logistical hub linking northern Kalimdor to the southern wilderness.
