text.enUS: Crossroads Supply Crate. Crossroads Supply Crates contain vital provisions intended for the settlement of the Crossroads in the Barrens. After a caravan was raided along the arid roads, these stolen goods ended up scattered among local Razormane quilboar camps. The crossroads settlement serves as the beating heart of Horde travel through central Kalimdor, but keeping it provisioned across the arid wastes is a constant trial. Caravan routes running through the Barrens are relentlessly stalked by the native Razormane quilboar. During one such ambush, a vital supply shipment destined for the settlement was ransacked. The crates were dragged into the prickly underbrush and dirt dens of nearby quilboar camps, leaving the settlement's commander, Thork, to enlist travelers to recover them before the outpost runs dangerously low on food, tools, and necessities.

name.frFR: Tour de garde de la couronne

text.enUS: Crown Guard Tower. Crown Guard Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower in the southern Eastern Plaguelands. The Scourge destroyed it during the invasion of Lordaeron in the Third War, and its broken stones have stood amid the blight ever since. Once part of the Kingdom of Lordaeron's defenses, Crown Guard Tower was a scout tower watching over the lands of eastern Lordaeron. When the Scourge overran the kingdom, the tower was destroyed and left in ruins, one of several fallen towers scattered across what are now the Eastern Plaguelands. Its charred stones stand in a land the undead still hold.

Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is an introductory rite given by Tenaron Stormgrip high within Aldrassil. As young night elves prepare to venture beyond the Shadowglen, they are sent to draw sacred water from a nearby moonwell and confront the painful history of Mount Hyjal and their people's lost immortality. Before any fledgling adventurer departs the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen, the elders ensure they understand the steep price the kaldorei recently paid. At the Battle of Mount Hyjal, the World Tree Nordrassil was sacrificed to defeat Archimonde and banish the Burning Legion. With that cataclysmic blast, the night elves lost their ageless immortality and their sacred shield. Tenaron Stormgrip acts as both mentor and historian, assigning novices this ritual to instill humility and purpose before they face a changing world.

Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a transitional journey that takes young night elves out of Shadowglen and into the broader realm of Teldrassil. Carrying sacred moonwell water consecrated atop Aldrassil, travelers are directed south along the forest road to meet Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It marks the graduation from secluded training to the urgent ecological defense of the great World Tree. After proving their dedication by sampling the enchanted waters of Shadowglen's moonwell, initiates are summoned before Tenaron Stormgrip at the crown of Aldrassil. Recognizing their readiness, Tenaron seals the gathered water into a larger vessel and commands them to venture beyond the sheltered grove. The road leading south toward Dolanaar is the primary artery out of Shadowglen, winding through woods that have grown increasingly unpredictable and hostile.

Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a sacred task assigned by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar to draw sanctified waters from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village. In exchange for replenishing the waters of Darnassus, young night elves learn the tragic history that led their people to cultivate the massive boughs of Teldrassil. The great central moonwell of Darnassus demands constant communion with the lesser fonts scattered across the crown of the World Tree. Druids craft refined jade phials specifically to draw and carry these luminescent waters without disturbing their purity. By sending initiates on foot to Starbreeze Village, the elders ensure both that the civic fountains remain brimming with Elune's grace and that the youth understand the labor required to nourish Teldrassil.

Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is an Alliance quest given by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. He directs you to draw water from the moonwell near the Pools of Arlithrien, an area increasingly threatened by crazed Gnarlpine furbolgs. Completing this task uncovers how Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm rallied the night elves to raise Teldrassil in the wake of Malfurion Stormrage's disappearance. Corithras Moonrage tasks you with taking a tourmaline phial to a moonwell resting southeast of Darnassus's entrance, along the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. The journey is far from quiet. The once peaceful Gnarlpine furbolgs have succumbed to sudden, violent fury, ambushing travelers and harrying Sentinel patrols throughout the region. What early reports wrote off as isolated skirmishes has escalated into a pervasive threat haunting the new home of the night elves.

Crown of the Earth. Crown of the Earth is a pivotal step in the Dolanaar quest chain investigating the ailments plaguing Teldrassil. Corithras Moonrage tasks adventurers with gathering water from the sacred moonwell in the Oracle Glade, using the journey to reveal the troubling truth behind the World Tree's creation. Corithras Moonrage directs travelers far to the northwest of Teldrassil, nestled beneath the majestic canopy of the Oracle Glade. Resting directly under the massive boughs of the Oracle Tree lies the first and most potent moonwell raised upon the island. Drawing an Amethyst Phial from its shimmering waters brings seekers face to face with the prime sanctuary from which the druids and the tree itself monitor the health of their new homeland.

Crown of the Earth. "Crown of the Earth" marks the culmination of the moonwell rites across Teldrassil. Handing over the gathered waters to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus underscores the growing anxiety over the World Tree's flawed, unblessed existence. Teldrassil was raised in the wake of the Third War to grant the night elves a new home and restore their lost immortality. However, the Great Aspects Alexstrasza and Nozdormu withheld their blessings, refusing to sanction the tree's creation. Without their divine protection, Teldrassil has fallen victim to creeping sickness, causing bizarre creatures to erupt from the boughs and once-peaceful furbolg tribes to descend into madness.

Crude Flint. Crude Flint pieces are rough fire-starting stones carried by the Mosshide gnolls throughout the Wetlands. The gnolls use them to kindle blazes from freshly hewn marsh timber, an act that deeply enrages the local protector, Rethiel the Greenwarden.

Crusader Outpost. Crusader Outpost is a fortified watchtower perched atop the rugged hills of eastern Tirisfal Glades. Manned by zealous members of the Scarlet Crusade, it guards the approaches leading toward their stronghold at the Scarlet Monastery. From this height, Crusaders observe travel along the road and stand ready to repel any Forsaken incursion. Built into the bluffs overlooking the eastern road, the Crusader Outpost serves as a primary early-warning station for the Scarlet Crusade. From their elevated tower, sentries watch over movement between Brill and the eastern reaches of Lordaeron, ensuring that wandering undead or scouting parties are spotted long before reaching the Monastery gates. The tower also grants the garrison tactical flanking capability against any force seeking to march up the valley toward their holy bastion.

Crusader's Armory. The Crusader's Armory is a fortified interior hall within the Scarlet Monastery Armory wing. Stockpiled with munitions, gunpowder, and cannonballs, it serves as a staging ground for the zealots guarding the path toward the inner sanctum. Beyond its locked iron door lies the Hall of Champions. Situated between the Footman's Armory and the grand Hall of Champions, the Crusader's Armory displays the full military readiness of the Scarlet Crusade. Unlike the training yards outside, these narrow stone corridors are packed to the ceiling with crates of volatile gunpowder, stacked cannonballs, and heavily armed crusaders ready to repel intruders. The Crusade has turned a former monastic compound into a bristling fortress, dedicating every available hall to the tools of total war. At the far end of the armory stands a heavy locked iron door, barring entry to the inner chambers unless one holds the Scarlet Key.

Crusader's Outpost. Crusader's Outpost is a fortified scout tower manned by the Scarlet Crusade in western Tirisfal Glades. Situated adjacent to the Solliden Farmstead, it serves as the Crusade's westernmost position in all of Lordaeron. Its perilous distance from the main Scarlet bastions leaves its garrison isolated in the heart of hostile Forsaken territory. Perched inside the western Tirisfal hills just north of Deathknell, this stone tower represents the farthest reach of the Scarlet Crusade's power in Lordaeron. The garrison stationed here works in tandem with the surviving human laborers of the nearby Solliden Farmstead, attempting to hold back the encroaching undead. From the top of the tower, lookouts keep watch over the surrounding pumpkin fields and forest paths, vigilant against both roaming Scourge fiends and patrols from the Undercity.

Crushridge Bounty. Marshal Redpath in Southshore warns that Crushridge ogres have settled by the ruins of Alterac and claimed them. A bounty is offered to anyone who will go north into the Alterac Mountains and hunt them. Redpath's scouts report that the Crushridge ogres have dug a mound in the Alterac Mountains, close to the ruined city, and have taken over its ruins as well. Redpath will not let them grow cozy: ogres who feel safe will move down into the foothills, right to Southshore's door. So Redpath sends you north to hunt the ogres and bring back the Dirty Knucklebones they carry, for a bounty.

Crushridge Warmongers. Marshal Redpath of Southshore wants the Crushridge ogres hit harder than before. You are sent into the Ruins of Alterac to find the Crushridge Warmongers, so the brutes will stay away from the Alliance. After Crushridge Bounty, Marshal Redpath wants the ogres to feel it in earnest. Redpath sends you into the Ruins of Alterac to seek out the Crushridge Warmongers and cut down plenty of them. Redpath holds that nothing else will teach the brutes to stay clear of Alliance territory.

Cry of the Thunderhawk. Cry of the Thunderhawk is the culmination of Jorn Skyseer's hunting trials in the southern Barrens. Entrusted by the elders at Camp Taurajo, a hunter must seek out a winged serpent soaring through the scrublands and bring back its wings to prove their mastery over the savanna's fiercest beasts. After proving their mettle against prowling plainstriders, prowlers, and agitated thunder lizards, hunters in the Barrens are directed toward their ultimate challenge by Jorn Skyseer. The thunderhawk is considered one of the most fierce aerial predators inhabiting the scrublands surrounding Camp Taurajo. Slaying one requires patience, sharp aim, and an awareness of the sky that few landbound predators possess.

Crypt (Badlands). Tucked away high in the dusty hills of the Badlands lies a secluded underground tomb known simply as the Crypt. Inside rests the silent remnant of an ancient warrior: an armored skeleton seated upon a stone throne, flanked by urns, chests, and a massive relic sword. Perched southeast of Hammertoe's Digsite along an unmarked earthen path rising up the hillside, the Badlands Crypt is easily missed by passersby. Down in its dark stone chambers sits an armored skeleton poised atop a throne. Resting beside the remains is the Sword of the Barbarian King, surrounded by scattered bones, urns, and forgotten chests. While miners and adventurers frequent the surrounding gullies in search of dwarven ruins and riches, the true origin and history of this seated sovereign remain a mystery lost to the arid wastes.

Crypt (Stromgarde Keep). Deep within the ruins of Stromgarde Keep lies the royal crypt, situated past the sanctum chapel in the heart of the district held by the surviving Stromgarde defenders. It holds the tomb of the fallen King Thoras Trollbane and the ancestral treasures of his dynasty. Guarded closely by Prince Galen and faithful caretakers, the vault remains a sanctuary of royal honor amid a shattered kingdom. Hidden beneath the Sanctum of Stromgarde Keep, this subterranean burial vault serves as the final resting place of King Thoras Trollbane, the warrior monarch who led Stromgarde through the Second War. Despite the devastation engulfing the city—split among Syndicate rogues and Boulderfist ogres—the remaining Stromgarde militia fiercely maintains their grip on this quarter. Prince Galen Trollbane personally watches over the crypts alongside dedicated royal caretakers, ensuring his father's body and legacy remain undisturbed by the scavengers and enemies outside.

Crystal Kelp Frond. Murlocs carry Crystal Kelp Fronds from the ocean to Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. William Pestle in Goldshire seeks them for an invisibility liquor. Crystal Kelp Fronds come from saltwater oceans, so their presence in Elwynn Forest’s fresh water is unusual. Murloc tribes along Crystal Lake’s shores gather and keep the fronds for reasons of their own. Alchemists value their strange power to distort sight. William Pestle in Goldshire uses them as the chief ingredient in an invisibility liquor, meant to help sweethearts slip past watchful family eyes.

Crystal Lake. East of Goldshire, Crystal Lake draws travelers toward a shore claimed by murlocs. Their attacks make the water a danger to villagers and passersby. Crystal Lake lies east of Goldshire, within walking distance of the Lion's Pride Inn. Freshwater murlocs now claim its shore and shallow shoals, attacking anyone who comes too close. William Pestle, an alchemist at the inn, hires travelers to drive them back and gather the crystal kelp they carry for his experiments.

Crystal Phial. A pristine Crystal Phial entrusted to young night elf adventurers by the druid Tenaron Stormgrip in Shadowglen. It is used to draw sacred water from a nearby moonwell, beginning a series of rites meant to honor and nourish the growing World Tree, Teldrassil. Given to novice night elves atop Aldrassil, this delicate glass phial serves a vital ceremonial purpose. Tenaron Stormgrip tasks young protectors with carrying it to the moonwell just north of the bough to collect its glowing waters. While simple in construction, the phial holds water infused with the sacred legacy of the Well of Eternity. Bringing back a Filled Crystal Phial marks the first step of the Crown of the Earth pilgrimage, teaching young kaldorei the precarious balance of magic, history, and nature in their new island home.

Crystal Shore. Crystal Shore is a stretch of sandy coastline along the southeastern edge of Stranglethorn Vale, washed by the waves of the South Seas. Tucked beneath steep coastal bluffs, the beach lies just south of the ancient Ruins of Aboraz and across the waters from Jaguero Isle. Running along the southeastern perimeter of Stranglethorn Vale, the Crystal Shore forms a natural boundary between the dense tropical interior and the open waters of the South Seas. The beach itself is walled off from the inland jungles by steep ridges, leaving only a couple of rugged passes for travelers attempting to move between the coast and the deeper wilderness of Mistvale Valley. To the north lie the crumbling troll structures of the Ruins of Aboraz, while the Wild Shore extends along the southern curves of the cape. Its location makes it a quiet, windswept margin far removed from the bustling docks of Booty Bay.

Crystal Vale. Tucked away in the far northwestern corner of Silithus, the Crystal Vale is a remote canyon dominated by jagged mineral spires and swirling elemental forces. Earth and air elementals roam its rocky flats, guarding rich veins of raw ore. It is also a site of potent summoning magic, deeply tied to the ancient elemental lords. The Crystal Vale stands distinct from the barren desert sands of southern Silithus. Framed by steep cliffs, the basin is filled with shimmering crystalloid formations, roaming earthen elementals, and roaring whirlwinds of living air. Rich deposits of thorium draw occasional daring prospectors, but the vale is far from quiet. The elemental beings here are inherently hostile to intruders, guarding a realm that feels steeped in the primal conflicts of primordial Azeroth.

Crystal in the Mountains. The Pendant of Myzrael pulses in your hand and a pleading reaches you, as if someone desperately needs help. A vision shows a gleaming crystal rising out of the ground in the northern mountains of Arathi, and you feel drawn to that place. The pendant pulses as you hold it. From it comes a sense of pleading, as if someone is trying to reach you and badly needs your help. Then a vision opens before you: the mountains in the north of Arathi, and a gleaming crystal thrusting up out of the ground. You feel drawn to that place.

Crystalized Scales. Crystalized Scales are the hardened, mineralized hides harvested from basilisks dwelling in harsh Kalimdor environments such as the Charred Vale and Thousand Needles. When ground into a fine powder, these unusual scales serve as an exotic magical reagent coveted by spellcasters in Stormwind. Basilisks that endure extreme environmental heat and ash—particularly those dwelling within Stonetalon's Charred Vale or the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles—develop rigid, crystal-encrusted hides. These crystalized scales possess latent arcane resonance, making them exceptionally valuable to scholarly wizards across the Great Sea who experiment with rare spellcraft.

Crystalvein Mine. Crystalvein Mine is a cavern in central Stranglethorn Vale, situated near the ancient ruins of Zul'Mamwe. The cavern is rich in valuable 'Singing Crystals', but aggressive native basilisks have completely overrun the site, turning prospective miners to solid stone. Tucked away in the jungle hills near Zul'Mamwe, Crystalvein Mine boasts rare deposits of Singing Crystals, a unique mineral that fetches a high price in southern trade ports. Enticed by the promise of immense profit, the Venture Company set its sights on extracting the veins. However, the mine's natural inhabitants have proved catastrophic for business. Local basilisks consume the strange crystals, hardening their scales and making them unnaturally lethal. Outside the cave mouth, petrified statues of trolls and humans stand as a silent testament to the Venture Company's failed expeditions.

Culling the Threat. Culling the Threat is an Alliance defensive operation issued by Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar. Faced with rapidly multiplying Thistlefur furbolgs directly to the north, the night elves seek to preempt an assault on the settlement by slaying their warlord, Dal Bloodclaw. It reflects the grim reality that former woodland allies must now be culled to safeguard kaldorei homes. Astranaar lies in the heart of Ashenvale, constantly surrounded by danger. Just north of the settlement dwell the Thistlefur furbolgs. Once peaceable dwellers of the ancient forest, they have fallen into madness and aggression like so many of their kin. Sentinel scouts watched their populations swell over recent months, raising fears that a coordinated assault on Astranaar itself was only a matter of time.

Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a secretive cabal of mortal zealots, necromancers, and aristocrats devoted to the Lich King. Formed in northern Lordaeron prior to the Third War, its members poisoned the grain supplies that spawned the Scourge and engineered the downfall of humanity's greatest kingdom. Today, the surviving cultists manage the plague cauldrons and necromantic academies across the Plaguelands while actively infiltrating the cities of the living. The Cult of the Damned was forged by the exiled Archmage Kel'Thuzad after he answered the telepathic whispers of the Lich King emanating from the Frozen Throne. Returning to Lordaeron with vast wealth and forbidden dark arts, Kel'Thuzad offered two false gospels: to the desperate, impoverished lower classes, he promised social equality and liberation from misery; to the wealthy landowners, such as the noble House of Barov, he promised eternal life and an unshakeable grip upon their domains. In truth, both the destitute and the affluent were cattle intended for slaughter, bound into a death cult designed to betray their homeland from the inside.

Curative Animal Salve. Curative Animal Salve is an herbal remedy brewed by druidic herbalists to soothe and heal wildlife afflicted by spreading ecological sickness. Formulated in both Darkshore and the Barrens, it serves as a frontline treatment for sickly creatures suffering from the land's unseen taints. Crafted from locally gathered herbal reagents, Curative Animal Salve is prepared in ten-dose batches to treat wildlife caught in the throes of spreading corruption. In the misty forests of Darkshore, Alanndarian Nightsong directs young druids to apply the ointment to sickly deer wandering between the Cliffspring River and the borders of Ashenvale. Far to the south in the arid expanse of the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem brews an identical remedy to treat sickly gazelles grazing north of the Crossroads. While both herbalists work with local authorities to produce larger supplies, field practitioners administer the salve directly to beasts suffering from environmental malaise.

Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Alliance druids, tasking them with using a prepared salve to heal the poisoned wildlife wandering Darkshore. By directly relieving the afflicted deer, initiates address the encroaching malaise troubling northern Kalimdor before reporting back to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the shadowed forests of Darkshore, from the waters of the Cliffspring River south to the borders of Ashenvale, the local wildlife suffers from a persistent sickness. Sickly deer wander aimlessly through the mist, weakened by unnatural toxins seeped into the soil and streams. Having gathered the necessary reagents, Alanndarian Nightsong entrusts an aspiring druid with a freshly brewed curative animal salve to treat the afflicted creatures in the field.

Curing the Sick. Curing the Sick is an essential trial for young Horde druids, tasking them with healing afflicted wildlife in the northern Barrens. By applying a freshly concocted herbal salve to ailing gazelles, initiates demonstrate both their practical field medicine and their commitment to preserving natural balance. Completing this duty proves their dedication directly to the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Across the northern savanna of the Barrens, grazing gazelles have begun succumbing to an unnatural affliction. After gathering earthroot and kodo horns to assemble a curative remedy, Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads entrusts a young druid with administering the field treatment. The initiate must search north of the main crossroads to find and minister to ten suffering animals, providing immediate relief before the rot takes further root in the ecosystem.

Curse These Fat Fingers. Hansel Heavyhands, in the Searing Gorge, can no longer dish out beatings as before, thanks to swollen fingers. Hansel asks you to go pound the heavy war golems for them. Hansel Heavyhands says the climate in the Gorge, with its thin air, makes Hansel's fingers swell until they resemble huge Thelsamar blood sausages. As a result, Hansel cannot deliver beatings the way Hansel used to, and needs you to see to Hansel's business instead.

Cut-Throat Alley. Behind the canal shops, Cut-Throat Alley lies quiet and empty in Stormwind City. Reach it through the Shady Lady near the Dwarven District, where a paved courtyard ends at an unoccupied residence. Cut-Throat Alley lies in a quiet corner of Stormwind, charted with the Dwarven District but apart from its forge fires and soot. No main avenue leads here; the only footpath passes through the Shady Lady, a small canal-side shop just south of the bridge from Cathedral Square. Beyond its door, a paved dead end holds stacked crates, forgotten barrels, and one empty two-story residence. Passing guards and ordinary citizens cannot see the alley, which stays silent amid the capital.

Cutting Teeth. Cutting Teeth is the initial trial given to fresh recruits arriving in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Overseer Gornek assigns newcomers to thin the mottled boar population roaming the nearby cactus dirt farms, testing their basic combat readiness. Surviving this modest rite of passage proves an aspiring warrior or spellcaster possesses the backbone necessary to serve the Horde. The Valley of Trials does not indulge delusions of grandeur. While young recruits might dream of pursuing massive beasts across the Barrens or winning glory on battlefields, overseer Gornek begins their evaluation with far more grounded matters. Thinning the mottled boars around the valley farms serves as a baseline assessment: it ensures a recruit knows how to wield a weapon or cast a spell, can handle wild aggression, and possesses enough sense to survive their very first skirmish.

Cycle of Rebirth. Cycle of Rebirth is a Horde task assigned by Tammra Windfield at Sun Rock Retreat to gather rare Gaea seeds from the shores of Mirkfallon Lake. Distressed by the toll of industrial greed and ongoing warfare across Stonetalon, Tammra seeks to bless these resilient kernels with shamanic power to revive the mountain's ravaged soil. It forms the essential first step in a restoration effort aimed at healing the scarred wilderness. The peaks of Stonetalon bear deep wounds from both commercial exploitation and relentless regional conflict. Between aggressive logging operations and clashes between rival factions, entire swaths of forest have been scorched, clear-cut, or reduced to ash. For the tauren stationed at Sun Rock Retreat, witnessing this rapid destruction of the natural world is a grievous wound. Rather than merely fighting to hold ground, shamans like Tammra Windfield look toward the ancient natural order, striving to enact the Earthmother's restorative cycle.

Cyclonian. Cyclonian is a mighty wind lord whose defeat has been sought for ages. To challenge him, a champion must gather the components required to summon the elemental and strike him down to claim his whirlwind heart. Defeating the wind lord allows the heart's power to be infused into a formidable weapon. Cyclonian is a raging elemental wind lord whose presence commands reverence and caution. For ages, an attentive watcher has kept vigil over the summoning site, waiting for a combatant possesses enough raw martial prowess to challenge and destroy this tempestuous entity.

Cyrus Therepentous. Cyrus Therepentous is a formidable black dragonspawn residing in the cavernous depths of Slither Rock in the Burning Steppes. Rather than immediately striking down intruders, he tests daring mortals to see if they possess the strength to serve the purposes of the Black dragonflight. Secluded inside a cavern at Slither Rock, Cyrus Therepentous oversees the volcanic crags of the Burning Steppes. Like many of his kind, he views mortal travelers with immense condescension, declaring that only fools would disturb his lair. Yet beneath his ferocious exterior lies a cold calculation: rather than consuming every trespasser on sight, he offers them a lethal challenge against his minions, willing to exploit those resilient enough to survive the trials of flame.

Dabyrie's Farmstead. Dabyrie's Farmstead is an Alliance-aligned rural settlement situated in northern Arathi Highlands. In a realm shattered by the Third War and overrun by Syndicate outlaws and Witherbark trolls, this estate remains a stubborn bastion of Stromgarde citizens led by Kenata Dabyrie. Perched in the northern fields of the Arathi Highlands, Dabyrie's Farmstead is one of the very few functioning human homesteads remaining in the fractured kingdom of Stromgarde. Owned by Kenata Dabyrie and worked alongside her sons, Fardel and Marcel, the grounds are fiercely defended by a local family militia. Surrounded by aggressive wildlife, opportunistic bandits, and the nearby Forsaken presence in the north, the farm stands as a symbol of human endurance in a ruined land.

Daelin's Men. Adjutant Tesoran has found Lieutenant Paval Reethe in the guard's records. They tell of an enlistment in the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, distinguished service with promotions, and a place in the Theramore guard among the recruits who sailed over with Lady Proudmoore. The last entry lists Reethe as missing, and Captain Garran Vimes is to hear of it. Captain Garran Vimes sent you to Adjutant Tesoran, who has now searched the books and found Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Reethe signed up with the Kul Tiras marines at sixteen, and distinguished service brought promotions. Reethe went on to the Theramore guard, like most of the recruits who sailed over with Lady Proudmoore. The record ends with Reethe listed as missing. The news is for Vimes in Theramore.

Daffodil Bouquet. The Daffodil Bouquet is a fresh bundle of bright flowers gathered by the herbalist Martie Jainrose in Lakeshire. Intended as a romantic token of appreciation from Guard Parker to Darcy, the gift inadvertently stokes local gossip and petty rivalry. When Guard Parker wishes to express his gratitude to Darcy at the Lakeshire inn for packing his daily lunch, he arranges a gesture through the town's herbalist, Martie Jainrose. Martie prepares a bouquet of daffodils, noting they are her personal favorite. However, when delivered to Darcy, the bright blooms immediately raise suspicions: Darcy recognizes the selection as Martie's signature flower and suspects petty jealousy from the other woman, half-joking that Martie might have poisoned the stems out of spite.

Dagger Hills. Bandits hold the Dagger Hills, the rocky heights behind Moonbrook in southern Westfall. With royal patrols gone, the ridge threatens travelers and the plains below. The Dagger Hills rise above Moonbrook in southern Westfall, where Defias outlaws watch the rocky ridges. Stormwind's royal patrols are gone, leaving the dry highland as a natural stronghold for the Defias Brotherhood. Knuckledusters, pathstalkers, and highwaymen hide among the crests and scrub. They ambush travelers and watch the approaches to their strongholds below.

Daggerspine Scale. A Daggerspine Scale is a tough reptilian scale harvested from the Daggerspine naga prowling the southern shores of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society, these scales serve as a crucial catalyst to activate virulent brews in the Forsaken's ongoing plague experiments. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks biological reagents to enhance their toxins, plagues, and concoctions. When refining the experimental brew known as the Elixir of Agony, the apothecaries discovered that scales taken from the local Daggerspine naga possessed unique reactive properties. When combined with troll regenerative elixirs and murloc organs, the scales help chemically activate dormant contaminating agents suspended in raw mixtures. Procuring them requires hunting along the rocky coastline east of Southshore, braving both the vicious naga tribe and nearby Alliance forces.

Daily Delivery. Daily Delivery is an errand on behalf of the dwarven hunter Einar Stonegrip, who asks travelers heading toward Menethil Harbor to deliver cured crocolisk hides to the local tanner. Rather than facing domestic friction at home, Einar relies on passing adventurers to keep his supply line moving. Out in the marshlands, Einar Stonegrip makes his living hunting the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive crocolisks that lurk along the waterways. While he gathers plenty of valuable skins, delivering them requires a trip home to Menethil Harbor. Reluctant to confront his wife Sida during a rough patch in their marriage, Einar prefers to stay in the field and hand his parcels off to passing travelers instead.

Dal Bloodclaw's Skull. Dal Bloodclaw's Skull is taken from the chieftain of the Thistlefur furbolg in northern Ashenvale. Brought to Raene Wolfrunner in Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that an imminent attack on the night elf settlement has been averted. The Thistlefur furbolgs residing north of Astranaar have grown rapidly in number and aggression, corrupted alongside much of Ashenvale's ancient forests. Fearing that the growing tribe would soon amass the courage to march directly on Astranaar, the night elf sentinel Raene Wolfrunner ordered the culling of their ranks and the death of their leader, Dal Bloodclaw. Claiming Dal Bloodclaw's Skull serves not as a trophy of petty vengeance, but as grim and undeniable evidence that the tribe's leadership has been shattered, buying the defenders of Astranaar precious time.

Dalar Dawnweaver. Dalar Dawnweaver is a former archmage of Dalaran who now serves the Forsaken at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Slain during the Scourge's destruction of the magi's city and later freed from the Lich King's control, he turns his magical intellect toward dissecting regional threats. From the shadows of the tomb, he directs efforts to understand Dalaran's lingering presence and undo the madness of Archmage Arugal. In life, Dalar Dawnweaver held high rank among the Kirin Tor, walking the halls of the Violet Citadel when Dalaran was a pinnacle of arcane mastery. His mortal life ended when the Scourge sacked the city to pave the way for Archimonde's summoning. Reanimated into the mindless thrall of the Lich King, Dalar broke free alongside Lady Sylvanas Windrunner when the Scourge's grip faltered. Now stationed at the Sepulcher, he retains the piercing intellect of an archmage, turned entirely toward safeguarding the Forsaken realm.

Dalar's Analysis. Dalar's Analysis is a Horde quest in Silverpine Forest linking Shadow Priest Allister's espionage against Ambermill with the arcane research of Dalar Dawnweaver. After uncovering a rune-inscribed pendant from a Dalaran supply crate, adventurers bring the relic to Dalar at the Sepulcher for scrutiny. The artifact reveals that the surviving mages of Dalaran are marshaling significant magical power for a hidden initiative. Following a raid on a Dalaran supply crate at a camp north of Pyrewood Village, Shadow Priest Allister receives a rune-inscribed pendant found beneath a bundle of old maps. Recognizing that its enchantment lies beyond his spiritual purview, Allister directs the relic to Dalar Dawnweaver, an arcane scholar stationed at the Sepulcher who is better suited to decipher Dalaran's magical warding.

Dalaran. Dalaran was once the shining magocratic capital of the Kirin Tor, nestled on the southern shore of Lordamere Lake. Shattered by the Scourge and the demon lord Archimonde during the Third War, its surviving magi are rebuilding the city, having removed its protective violet shield early in the reconstruction. Founded after the ancient Troll Wars by sorcerers of the Arathorian Empire, Dalaran stood for centuries as humanity's premier sanctuary for arcane study. Under the leadership of the Council of Six, the Kirin Tor amassed vast magical archives and guarded powerful artifacts within the Violet Citadel. That age of splendor ended abruptly during the Third War. The traitor prince Arthas led the Scourge through the city gates to seize the Book of Medivh, and soon after, the demon lord Archimonde crushed Dalaran's soaring spires into rubble.

Dalaran Mana Gem. Dalaran Mana Gems are crystallized arcane reserves carried by Kirin Tor personnel operating in Silverpine Forest. Forsaken spellcasters covet these gems as potent raw components for crafting enchanted vestments like spellfire robes. The mages, conjurors, and guards of the Kirin Tor stationed around Ambermill in Silverpine Forest carry specialized mana gems to focus and replenish their arcane energies. For the Forsaken practitioners in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, these crystalline conduits represent an accessible source of concentrated magical essence. Although some undead mages acknowledge a shared academic heritage with Dalaran, pragmatic necessity and a philosophy of survival dictate that unyielding rivals are fair game to be stripped of their magical resources.

Dalaran Patrols. Magus Wordeen Voidglare in Tarren Mill cares nothing for why the wizards of Dalaran raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. What matters is that the ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, while the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. Voidglare wants those patrols thinned. After Prison Break In, Voidglare turns to the wizards of Dalaran, who raised a great dome of magic over their city's heart. Some say it shelters them from the violence of the age; others say they simply wanted solitude to study and plot. Voidglare does not care which. The ruined outskirts beyond the dome may conceal treasures of real magical worth, but the wizards and their elemental slaves patrol the area. You are to hunt six Dalaran Summoners and twelve Elemental Slaves, then return to Voidglare in Tarren Mill.

Dalaran Pendant. Dalaran Pendants are magical talismans carried by the Kirin Tor wizards stationed at the village of Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. The Forsaken seek to collect these pendants to disrupt the magi's arcane workings and trace the source of their power. In the village of Ambermill, Kirin Tor sorcerers, conjurers, and protectors actively weave formidable arcane spells threatening Forsaken control over southern Silverpine Forest. Each operative carries an attuned Dalaran Pendant. At the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister tasks Forsaken operatives with recovering these pendants to slow down the mages' efforts and uncover who is guiding their magical weave.

Dalaran Status Report. The Dalaran Status Report is a cache of sensitive intelligence compiled by the Kirin Tor wizards stationed at Ambermill in Silverpine Forest. It details the current state of the rebuilding city of Dalaran, making it a prized document for the Forsaken and the Deathstalkers of Undercity. The Scourge sacked Dalaran and Archimonde brought down its towering spires during the Third War. Its surviving magi removed its protective shield early in the reconstruction and are rebuilding the city in the open. The Kirin Tor also maintains enclaves such as Ambermill in southeastern Silverpine Forest. The Dalaran Status Report contains intelligence about the state of Dalaran sought by the Deathstalkers.

Dalaran's Intentions. Dalaran's Intentions is a Silverpine Forest quest delivered by Dalar Dawnweaver to Shadow Priest Allister. Having studied a rune-inscribed pendant bound for the Kirin Tor in Ambermill, Dalar realizes the wizards intend to tap a dormant ley energy node beneath the town, prompting the Forsaken leadership at the Sepulcher to plan a counter-offensive. While examining a rune-inscribed pendant recovered from a Dalaran supply crate, Dalar Dawnweaver remembers an old Kirin Tor survey. Ambermill was not chosen by the mages by coincidence; the quiet village rests directly atop a dormant ley energy node. Awaking such a subterranean nexus requires immense magical reserves, and the enchanted pendants worn by the wizards serve as key components in channeling and catalyzing that power.

Dalin's Heart. Dalin's Heart is a macabre ritual component carved from Dalin Forgewright, an honorable man patrolling near the Greymane Wall in Silverpine Forest. Undercity warlocks seek it out as an offering of unblemished purity, intended to lure and bind a succubus to their service. To summon and subjugate a succubus, Undercity warlocks require rare bait: the physical hearts of truly virtuous mortals. Dalin Forgewright earned his dark fate through selfless devotion, spending his days defending desperate Lordaeron refugees barred from safety at the sealed Greymane Wall. His unstinting altruism marks him as an emblem of goodness in a fallen land, making his heart an irresistible prize for demonic seduction rites conducted within the Temple of the Damned.

Dalson's Tears. Dalson's Tears is a blighted farmstead located in the heart of the Western Plaguelands. Once known as Dalson's Orchard, the land was overrun during the Third War and converted into a staging ground for one of the Scourge's noxious plague cauldrons. The undead remains of the former owners still haunt the fields and outbuildings. Before the Third War, this estate flourished as Dalson's Orchard, a productive farm in the breadbasket of Lordaeron. Today, the fields are choked with decay and rechristened Dalson's Tears. At the center of the ruined property stands a massive iron cauldron, constantly billowing virulent green plague vapors across the landscape. The device is overseen by Cauldron Lord Malvinious and defended by a pack of blighted zombies, rotting cadavers, and skeletal horrors serving the Lich King.

Dancing for Marzipan. During the festive season of Hallow's End, adventurers traveling through Darnassus are tasked with collecting festive sweets for a sick orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Saelienne upholds the trick-or-treat tradition in full, requiring an impromptu dance performance before parting with her prized Darnassus Marzipan. Even in the sacred forest city of Darnassus, the revelry of Hallow's End brings a lighter spirit to the long-lived night elves. When travelers arrive looking to gather holiday confections on behalf of Jesper, a sick child recovering in Stormwind, Innkeeper Saelienne insists that the rules of the season remain unbroken. Charity or not, a treat requires a proper trick first.

Dancing for Marzipan. Dancing for Marzipan is a festive Hallow's End quest offered by Innkeeper Pala in Thunder Bluff. To gather a sweet treat for a sick orphan, adventurers must put aside their battle-hardened dignity and perform a joyful dance for the innkeeper. It highlights the playful, community-focused spirit of the holiday even high upon the windswept mesas of Mulgore. During the autumn festival of Hallow's End, spirits run high across Azeroth, even in the serene heights of Thunder Bluff. Innkeeper Pala, overseeing the hospitality of the high mesas, gets into the festive spirit by demanding a trick before handing out any treats. Even when an adventurer arrives on behalf of an ailing child, tradition holds firm: Pala insists on seeing some festive dancing before parting with her prized Thunder Bluff Marzipan.

Dandred's Fold. Dandred's Fold is a secluded farmstead and manor tucked along the misty northwestern shores of Lordamere Lake in the Alterac Mountains. Now overrun by the Syndicate, it serves as a secure hideout for Lord Aliden Perenolde and his co-conspirators. Both the Horde and the Alliance keep a watchful eye on this lakefront retreat for very different reasons. Perched on the western edge of the Uplands with private access to the waters of Lordamere Lake, Dandred's Fold was once a tranquil country estate, likely owned by an Alteraci noble named Dandred. In the aftermath of the kingdom's fall, the estate transformed into a fortified enclave for the Syndicate. Syndicate assassins and enforcers now patrol its fences and docks, shielding the fallen nobility from the eyes of Southshore authorities and the Forsaken across the lake.

Dangerous!. Posted on the wanted board in Tarren Mill, this bounty marks four prominent Hillsbrad humans for execution. High Executor Darthalia has declared them dangerous enemies of the Forsaken due to specific assassinations and supply ambushes. The front lines across the Hillsbrad Foothills are brutal and personal. To High Executor Darthalia and the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, ordinary citizens of Hillsbrad have become lethal combatants. The wanted notice singles out four specific figures whose resistance has cost Forsaken lives and valuable shipments from the Undercity.
