text.enUS: Excavation Progress Report. Excavation Progress Report is an Alliance errand run from the digs in Loch Modan back to town. Prospector Ironband tasks an adventurer with carrying his latest excavation dispatches and a renewal of his explosive supply orders to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar. Prospector Ironband's archaeological efforts in Loch Modan require constant logistical support from nearby settlements. Excavation is strenuous labor, demanding picks, manpower, and generous quantities of blasting powder to cut through stubborn bedrock. Ironband relies on runners to relay his regular status reports and material requisition orders to Jern Hornhelm, the local expedition contact stationed in Thelsamar.

Excelsior. In Booty Bay, Drizzlik has finished the inner part of the Excelsior boots and now needs the skin of an elder saltwater crocolisk for the outside. With the inside done, only the outer layer remains, and for it Drizzlik uses nothing but the finest elder crocolisk skins, which are tougher and make a better surface for the designs and accents of the Excelsior line. The only skin that fits Drizzlik's plan is that of an elder saltwater crocolisk, and finding one is hard, for such elders come out only to guard other saltwater crocolisks. Drizzlik has also read somewhere that the numbers of saltwater crocolisks are dwindling, which would hurt business.

Executor Arren. Executor Arren is a high-ranking Forsaken officer stationed in Deathknell. He oversees the immediate defense and consolidation of the settlement as newly awakened undead emerge from their graves. Arren coordinates the local campaign against mindless Scourge zombies, feral beasts, and the encroaching zealots of the Scarlet Crusade. Standing resolute just outside the chapel in Deathknell, Executor Arren serves as the primary military voice for the nascent Forsaken within their awakening grounds. While the caretakers in the crypts guide newly raised undead through their disorientation, Arren directs their focus outward toward survival. Under Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's banner, he organizes local operations to sweep away mindless zombies that threaten the village borders, establishing secure territory in the shadow of Lordaeron's fall.

Executor Zygand. Executor Zygand is a senior Forsaken commander stationed at the town hall in Brill, overseeing defensive and military operations across central Tirisfal Glades. Reporting directly to the Undercity's high command, he coordinates the purge of Scarlet Crusade forces pressing into Forsaken territory. Positioned at the administrative heart of Brill, Executor Zygand coordinates regional defense for the Forsaken after their initial awakening in Deathknell. Serving as the direct superior to regional officers like Executor Arren and field sentries such as Deathguard Linnea, Zygand synthesizes scout intelligence and dispatches able recruits to safeguard Lordaeron's borders from encroachment.

Expanding Horizons. Thundris Windweaver sends word from Auberdine across the Great Sea to Stormwind. The letter asks City Architect Baros Alexston to recognize Auberdine's work and its home. Auberdine now links Darkshore to Stormwind by sea. Night elves once kept to Kalimdor's forests, apart from the Eastern Kingdoms, but after the Third War they joined the Grand Alliance. The new passage gives the northern port a direct tie to the human kingdom. Local leaders want the shipping route secured and Auberdine connected to the wider Alliance. Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran, ruined cities nearby, have long drawn more notice than the living coastal settlement.

Explorers' League. The Explorers' League is a renowned dwarven archaeological guild headquartered in Ironforge's Hall of Explorers. Founded under King Magni Bronzebeard and led by his wandering brother Brann, the League seeks to uncover the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Their expansive digs span across Azeroth, uncovering ancient titan ruins while frequently igniting regional conflicts. For centuries, the dwarves of Khaz Modan focused their formidable energies on mining, stonework, and engineering. That focus changed drastically when ancient ruins were unearthed, hinting at a forgotten legacy connecting dwarves to mythical titan creators. Eager to solve the mystery of his people's beginnings, King Magni Bronzebeard decreed that dwarven industry pivot heavily toward archaeology. Magni, alongside his brother Brann, established the Explorers' Guild—now widely known as the Explorers' League—to scour the world for relics, forgotten cities, and traces of their ancient ancestry.

Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, toxic industry beneath the Deadmines is poisoning the farmland. You travel to Stormwind's Dwarven District to seek an engineer who can supply heavy explosives. Westfall faces displaced vagrants and banditry under the Defias Brotherhood. Evidence from across the region points to a coordinated, mechanised threat underground. Industrial refuse and caustic toxins foul the soil, and their trail leads into the Deadmines, where an organized operation works below the earth.

Explosive Consultation. In Westfall, Sprite Jumpsprocket sends a volatile charge to Alba Fairmoon. The primed explosives must reach her safely, with the detonator undisturbed. Sprite Jumpsprocket has finished a bundle of Extra-Destructive Explosives for Alba Fairmoon. Carrying a live charge through wartime Westfall adds danger to a road already threatened by Defias bandits and feral beasts.

Explosive Stick of Gann. The Explosive Stick of Gann is a customized blasting charge assembled by Gann Stonespire using stolen dwarven schematics. It was designed specifically to sabotage the dwarven flying machine stationed at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. When the dwarven Prospector Khazgorm led the Ironforge excavation into southern Kalimdor, the dwarves drove the Stonespire tauren from their ancestral village and razed their sacred grounds to build the fortress-dig of Bael Modan. Driven by vengeance and a desire to honor his displaced and fallen kin, Gann Stonespire reclaimed Khazgorm's blueprints to turn dwarven engineering against the invaders. By studying the recovered plans, Gann assembled this specialized charge with enough concussive force to wreck heavy machinery.

Eyes of the Sentinels. Eyes of the Sentinels is a Darnassus quest where players assist Sentinel Dalia Sunblade in stationing magical scout owls at critical posts throughout the night elven capital. Facing growing unease across Teldrassil, this aerial surveillance bolsters the city's defenses while allowing the Sentinels time for prayer to Elune. In the sacred sanctuary of the Temple of the Moon, Sentinel Dalia Sunblade maintains the vigil over Darnassus. Guided by General Shandris Feathermoon's decree that every warrior must balance martial prowess with spiritual devotion, Dalia arranges the deployment of watchful sentinel owls across key city hubs. Taking over these daily duties affords the sentinel valuable moments of prayer and reflection before the Moon Goddess, while ensuring the kaldorei capital remains tightly guarded.

Facing Negolash. Following the trail of Captain Hecklebury Smotts' lost weapon, Sprogger reveals a plan to bait the giant Negolash using the creature's favorite delicacies. By staging a banquet in a wrecked lifeboat on the coast of Stranglethorn Vale, adventurers can confront the brute and reclaim the captain's stolen cutlass. When giants smashed Captain Smotts' vessel, one brute named Negolash headed straight for the galley. Unlike his brethren, he wasn't hungry for the crew. Sprogger saw that Negolash wanted wine and Barbecued Buzzard Wings, Sprogger's own specialty, whose recipe he had to travel to the Badlands to get.

Faded Shadowhide Pendant. A tarnished talisman once worn by the Shadowhide gnolls of Redridge, enchanted to serve as a conduit for dark orders. To the astonishment of whoever holds it, the pendant also carries a delayed magical message cast by the wizard Theocritus. The Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains answer to a sinister master named Morganth, coordinating their movements through enchanted pendants. While investigating these talismans from his sanctuary at Tower Azora, the High Mage Theocritus devised an experimental spell to breach their mystical frequency. Though his magical broadcast took weeks to manifest, this faded pendant proved that the gnolls' communication line can be hijacked, opening a path to disrupt their dark master's reach.

Faerie Dragon Muisek. After the hippogryph spirits, Witch Doctor Uzer'i wants the spirit of a faerie dragon next. You are sent west to hunt sprite darters and sprite dragons and capture what makes them strong. Uzer'i points out that faerie dragons seem delicate, yet their spirit is the real prize. They have been allies to the night elves, and Uzer'i wants the Horde to share in that strength. Uzer'i gives you a Muisek Vessel and sends you west to slay eight sprite darters or sprite dragons, then shrink and capture each fallen faerie dragon with it.

Falaath Village. Falaath Village is a gathering place for penitent shen'dorei seeking to win back the favor of the Windlord, Al'Akir. Marked recruits journey from Shen'dar Village to report to Missionary Jasaan and join their fellow faithful. In Shen'dar Village, Sania Silverstream laments that her people grew prideful, taking the bounty of the air for granted until the spirits of the wind abandoned them into stagnation. To remedy this fall from grace, penitent recruits are marked and sent to Falaath Village, seeking fellowship with fellow shen'dorei who believe that only acts of contrition can restore the wind's favor.

Faldir's Cove. Faldir's Cove is a secluded natural harbor nestled along the southern coastline of the Arathi Highlands. Steeped in human history, it is traditionally remembered as the departure point from which early settlers sailed south to found Stormwind. Today, it serves as an emergency shelter for stranded Blackwater Raiders whose fleet ran afoul of local hazards. Tucked away behind the rugged bluffs south of Stromgarde Keep, Faldir's Cove is linked to the mainland by a concealed cave tunnel. The cove honors the memory of Faldir, the ancient Arathor explorer whose expedition set sail from these very shores to cross the Great Sea and establish the southern kingdom of Stormwind. In the present day, however, its quiet waters house a very different crowd: an expedition of Blackwater Raiders from Booty Bay, led by Captains Steelgut and O'Breen, who sailed north pursuing ancient elven treasures only to end up trapped in the bay.

Falfarren River. The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict. Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

Falfindel Waywarder. Falfindel Waywarder is a night elf druid stationed at Thalanaar, the outpost guarding the border between Feralas and the Thousand Needles. From this frontier watchpost, he works to heal corrupted lands and safeguard the southern wilderness of Kalimdor. Travelers wandering down from Stonetalon or the Barrens often find him seeking aid to restore balance to the wild. Thalanaar marks the gateway where the lush forests of Feralas descend into the towering mesas and dry salt plains of Thousand Needles. Falfindel Waywarder stands watch at this remote outpost, greeting weary travelers who have ventured far across the continent. Surrounded by natural grandeur and lurking dangers, he serves as a point of contact for the night elves seeking to monitor both local threats and broader environmental calamities across Kalimdor.

Fall of Dun Modr. Dun Modr, the northern dwarf fortress overlooking the Thandol Span, has succumbed to a violent assault by the Dark Iron dwarves. A severely wounded survivor in Menethil Harbor seeks an Alliance adventurer to venture north and discover if commander Longbraid the Grim and any remnant of the garrison survived. Dun Modr has long anchored northern Khaz Modan, guarding the vital road and bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands across the Thandol Span. Following an ambush at the bridge itself, the garrison scrambled back to regroup within the fortress walls. Before defensive lines could be reestablished, Dark Iron forces struck in overwhelming numbers, slaughtering the defenders and forcing a desperate evacuation.

Falla Sagewind. Falla Sagewind is a reclusive tauren mystic perched high upon a rocky peak overlooking the central Barrens. Stationed between the Crossroads and the Lushwater Oasis, she studies the natural and mystical anomalies troubling the surrounding land. Adventurers probing the twisted corruption seeping from the nearby Wailing Caverns often seek her guidance. Falla Sagewind makes her camp far above the dust and bustle of the Barrens trails, situated on a secluded summit just southwest of the Crossroads. From this vantage, she keeps a solemn watch over the fragile savannas below, observing the sudden shifts in wildlife behavior and the encroaching corruption rising from the subterranean fissures of the Wailing Caverns. Her solitary vigil separates her from the daily trade of the Crossroads, positioning her as an observant hermit tuned to the spirits and the land's silent wounds.

name.frFR: Héros de la Horde tombé au combat

text.enUS: Fallen Hero of the Horde. The Fallen Hero of the Horde is the lingering spirit of an orc warrior standing watch on the southern road out of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bound by regret and dishonor, he warns passing travelers of the horrors awaiting them in the Blasted Lands and seeks champions willing to deliver his tortured soldiers from demonic bondage. In life, this warrior was a celebrated champion dispatched with a handpicked regiment of soldiers to investigate the Blasted Lands and report back on the presence of the Burning Legion. His dispatch never made it; the courier sent north toward Stonard was ambushed and slain by the Swamp Talker and his murlocs. Stranded without orders or reinforcements, the commander eventually marched his soldiers south into the shattered wastes to confront the growing darkness. It was a fatal misjudgment. Overwhelmed by demonic forces, his army was scattered, captured, and subjected to horrific torment at the hands of the dreadlord Razelikh the Defiler.

Fallen Moonstone. A Fallen Moonstone is a luminous, magically charged stone gathered from the tranquil waters of Fallen Sky Lake in Ashenvale. Imbued with sacred lunar energy, these stones possess potent restorative properties capable of renewing vitality and curing severe frailty. Fallen Moonstones were once gathered in abundance along the shores and shallows of Fallen Sky Lake, southeast of Astranaar. Highly treasured by the night elves for their restorative magic and lunar blessing, they were often sought out to aid in recovery when ordinary remedies proved insufficient. However, harvesting them became treacherous when corrupt Shadethicket bog beasts overran the lake. Their leader, a Shadethicket Oracle, hoarded every stone it could find on a small central island, cutting off the local Kaldorei from a vital source of healing.

Fallen Sky Lake. "Fallen Sky Lake" is the emotional culmination of Pelturas Whitemoon's quest chain to save his dying daughter, Relara, in Astranaar. Although her initial fever has broken, her vitality remains dangerously depleted, requiring a celestial moonstone to restore her life force. Players must journey into the untamed waters of Fallen Sky Lake to wrest one of these hoarded stones from a corrupted Shadethicket Oracle. Pelturas Whitemoon has spent agonizing days watching his young daughter, Relara, slip closer to death. While powerful curatives brewed from Bathran's hair and stardust helped break her raging fever, the ordeal left her body hollowed and frail. Time is no longer on her side; Pelturas fears that without supernatural intervention, she has only breaths remaining before her spirit fades permanently into the night.

Fallen Sky Lake. Fallen Sky Lake is a secluded body of water nestled deep within the forests of eastern Ashenvale. Situated between Silverwing Outpost and the encroaching Warsong Labor Camp, the serene waters hide danger in the form of hostile shadethicket bog beasts that aggressively defend the lake and its central isle. Tucked south of Silverwing Outpost and just west of the Warsong Labor Camp, Fallen Sky Lake offers a fleeting glimpse of Ashenvale's natural splendor before the Orcish axes took root nearby. The shores and the small islet rising from the middle of the lake are inhabited by shadethickets—hulking bog beasts that view any intruder as a threat. The heart of the island serves as the domain of a powerful Shadethicket Oracle, who hoards the fallen moonstones once gathered at the lake and keeps the local shadethickets bound to the waters and relentlessly vigilant against travelers passing through.

Fallen in the Fen. Fallen in the Fen is a somber journey begun by uncovering a fallen dwarf amidst an excavation site. Delivering the tragic news to his brother, Dorin Songblade in Lakeshire, brings closure to a heartbroken craftsman who had been forging gifts for his departed kin. A quiet tragedy unfolds at the excavation sites, where the lifeless body of an adventurous dwarf is discovered. After covering the remains with the dwarf's own cloak, an adventurer carries the grim news back to Lakeshire to find his kin.

Falling With Style. "Falling With Style" is an introductory rite of passage for young Skyborne in Thendal Village. Offered atop the local watchtower by the mischievous Myriaal Mistwake, it challenges novices to test their innate slow-fall ability by leaping from the platform toward Rorian the Dayseeker below. Perched high above Thendal Village on Zephras Isle, Myriaal Mistwake invites young Skyborne to test their heritage through a game of daring. Rather than treating their innate magical gifts as sacred relics kept under strict restraint, Myriaal encourages newcomers to leap into the open air from the watchtower ledge. The purpose is practical as well as playful: mastering the instinctive art of walking upon air before life beyond the grove demands it in perilous situations.

Fallow Sanctuary. The Fallow Sanctuary is a secluded village hidden deep within the bogs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as home to an isolated tribe of mutated draenei known as the Lost Ones, whose severe grief and homesickness have driven them feral. Tucked away among the sunken trees of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Fallow Sanctuary was established by stranded Lost Ones seeking a place of their own. Severed from their ancestral world and deformed by dark energies, these wretched outcasts found no peace in the marshland. Over time, relentless sorrow and isolation shattered their sanity, reducing the tribe to a hostile, feral state where they fiercely attack any outsiders who trespass into their village.

Family Tree. Cliffwatcher Longhorn asks you to carry a report to Nataka Longhorn, Cliffwatcher's brother, who is stationed in Desolace. Word of unusual centaur activity is meant to reach Ghost Walker Post. Nataka, Cliffwatcher's brother, holds a posting at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. A year has passed since Cliffwatcher last wrote, and in that time the centaurs have been behaving unusually. Nataka should hear of it, and you are asked to carry the report.

Fandral Staghelm. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. Stepping into power after Malfurion Stormrage vanished into the Emerald Dream, he championed the planting of the new World Tree, Teldrassil. Proud, abrasive, and relentlessly ambitious, Fandral advocates for an aggressive Kaldorei resurgence that frequently pits him against High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil atop Mount Hyjal, the night elves lost their immortality and their sacred sanctuary. When Malfurion Stormrage vanished, Fandral took up leadership of the druids and convinced the Circle of Ancients that it was time for their people to rebuild and regain their immortality. With the Circle's approval, he led the druids in raising Teldrassil off the coast of Kalimdor. He envisioned the colossal bough as a monument to Kaldorei endurance and a vessel to restore their lost supremacy, even though the Dragon Aspects pointedly withheld their blessings from the unapproved endeavor.

Fandral's Message. Fandral's Message is a missive penned by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus. It is entrusted to an adventurer to carry across the sea to the Ancient of Lore, Onu, in Darkshore. Written by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in the Cenarion Enclave, this sealed dispatch serves as direct correspondence between the acting leader of the night elven druids and Onu, the venerable Ancient of Lore dwelling within the Grove of the Ancients. After receiving reports regarding the state of Teldrassil's Oracle Glade, Staghelm wastes no time pressing couriers into service to send word south of Auberdine. The delivery requires travelers to journey across the waters to Darkshore, bridging the heart of the new World Tree with the older, shadowed mainland.

Fang of Githyiss. The Fang of Githyiss is a rare and formidable specimen taken from a giant arachnid stalking the wilds near Aldrassil. Delivering the fang to a naturalist in the sanctuary allows scholars to study the monstrous creature and monitor the predatory threats nesting within Shadowglen. The Fang of Githyiss is a trophy and biological sample harvested from the overgrown spider Githyiss, who lurks in the wilds of Shadowglen. A beast of such notable bulk poses a clear threat to young travelers venturing out from Aldrassil, making the recovery of its fang both a matter of safety and scientific interest. Rather than letting the creature's remains rot in the underbrush, resourceful scouts take the specimen back to the sanctuary of the great tree.

Fang of Vagash. The Fang of Vagash is a massive predator tooth taken from the notorious beast Vagash in the snowy crags of Dun Morogh. It serves as tangible proof for local breeders that the marauding monster threatening their prized rams has finally been slain. Dun Morogh's high crags are home to bitter cold and ferocious predators, but none have plagued the local ranches quite like Vagash. Looming in the ridges above the Amberstill Ranch, this savage beast frequently stalks downhill under cover of darkness to slaughter prized rams. With Ironforge's troops already stretched thin, the local herdsmen cannot count on the city guard for protection. Slaying the beast and carving away one of its vicious fangs offers indisputable evidence that the pasturelands are safe once more.

Fangore's Paw. Fangore's Paw is the severed hand of Lieutenant Fangore, a commanding officer among the Shadowhide gnolls in the Redridge Mountains. It serves as gruesome proof of the gnoll chieftain's demise for Magistrate Solomon in Lakeshire. The grim bounty was placed to dismantle the warlord's threat against the besieged township. Lieutenant Fangore acts as a primary field commander for the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching across the Redridge Mountains. Operating in direct service to the renegade mage Morganth, Fangore directs violent assaults against trade roads, outlying farms, and the defenses around Lake Everstill. Because gnoll raiders do not leave traditional uniforms, official seals, or banners to confirm their casualties, the township authorities rely on grim physical evidence. Magistrate Solomon specifically demanded Fangore's paw as unmistakable proof of his execution, allowing the town of Lakeshire to breathe slightly easier amid mounting surrounding perils.

Faol's Rest. Faol's Rest is a quiet, neglected gravesite situated in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. It was erected as the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, the revered spiritual patriarch who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Today, untended beneath the blighted canopy, it serves as a release graveyard for those who perish near the monastery. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, this secluded hollow was a place of solemn pilgrimage. It holds the stone tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, who led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and instituted the order of paladins to protect humanity. Faol passed away peacefully prior to the arrival of the Scourge, spared the mortal agony of seeing his kingdom fall. In those brighter years, mourners regularly journeyed up the road from Capital City to leave offerings and pay respects to the beloved patriarch.

Far Watch Post. Far Watch Post is a fortified Horde outpost situated just west of the Southfury River bridge connecting Durotar to the Barrens. Serving as the front line of defense for the orcish homeland, the post guards vital trade caravans against aggressive quilboar packs and hostile Alliance incursions. Located at the western foot of the bridge out of Durotar, Far Watch Post is the first bastion of Horde authority travellers see when entering the vast, arid savannah of the Barrens. The settlement is Spartan but functional, built for tactical readiness rather than comfort. It features a sturdy orcish watchtower, a burrow, and pre-sighted siege catapults trained toward the dusty plains. Directly south of the main road, peons tend a pen of riding wolves ready to bear messengers or reinforcements. Far Watch Post exists primarily to keep the supply road to Crossroads secure, screening incoming traffic and repelling raids from roaming quilboar tribes and stealthy Alliance scouts.

Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds now swarm through Fargodeep Mine, south of Goldshire in central Elwynn Forest. The mine once brought gold to Stormwind, but its tunnels are now a kobold warren. Gold once flowed from Fargodeep Mine into Stormwind's treasury. As the Kingdom's military presence in Elwynn dwindled, outlying resources became vulnerable. Kobolds soon filled the mine's dark tunnels and made a warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and Goldshire's authorities fear the lost ore and the danger to nearby farms, including the Stonefield and Maclure holdings.

Farmer Furlbrow. Near the Jansen Stead, Farmer Furlbrow and his wife are stranded beside their broken wagon. Driven from their northern Westfall farm by the Defias Brotherhood, they hope to reach Elwynn Forest. Theodore Furlbrow left his pumpkin patch in northern Westfall with his wife, Verna, as criminals drove them from their home. They salvaged what they could and set out for Elwynn Forest, urging neighbors such as Farmer Saldean to leave too. Near the Jansen Stead, their wagon broke down, leaving them exposed to bandits and wild beasts. Verna tends to their horse, Old Blanchy, while Theodore keeps watch over the road. He hopes to recover the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day and warn Sentinel Hill about the approaching bandits.

Farmer Saldean. At Saldean's Farm in central Westfall, Farmer Saldean keeps working the troubled fields beside his wife, Salma. While other farmers flee or give up, the veteran homesteader faces rogue harvest golems and growing banditry. Farmer Saldean remembers when Westfall prospered, before those years crumbled away. Overgrown fields, rampaging mechanical harvest watchers, and predatory bandits now surround his farm, but he refuses to yield his land. Other homesteaders have abandoned their acres or turned to thievery. Saldean and his wife, Salma, stay and work to harvest what little grain they can. He asks wandering adventurers to destroy the rogue Harvest Watchers that have taken over his fields and his neighbors' fields, so he can clear the soil for planting.

Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is an Alliance assignment in Southshore given by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Tasked with proving his coastal patrol efforts to his superior, Marshal Redpath, Farren sends recruits out to harvest severed murloc heads along the Western Strand. Following initial sweeps along the coastline in Down the Coast, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle finds himself under scrutiny by Marshal Redpath and town leadership. Claiming credit for clearing out the local murlocs is one thing; presenting undeniable evidence to skeptical superiors is quite another. Unwilling to soil his own hands with gruesome butchery, Farren tasks wandering Alliance adventurers with returning to the shoreline to collect tangible proof of the kill.

Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is a short delivery mission in Southshore where an adventurer carries a grisly bounty of murloc heads from Lieutenant Farren Orinelle to Marshal Redpath. Having let someone else do the bloody work of hunting the coast, the squeamish lieutenant delegates the actual reporting as well. It marks an intermediate step in securing town recognition along the Hillsbrad coast. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is tasked with patrolling and securing the southern coastline of Hillsbrad Foothills, yet he has little stomach for the brutal realities of frontier warfare. After sending an adventurer out to cull the rampant murlocs infesting the beaches, he balks at actually touching the severed heads brought back as proof. Rather than personally marching the dripping trophies to Southshore's town command, Farren gladly dumps the errand right back onto the bearer.

Farren's Proof. Farren's Proof is an Alliance courier mission within the harbor town of Southshore. Acting on behalf of Marshal Redpath, an adventurer delivers orders directing Lieutenant Farren Orinelle to focus his military attention on the naga encroaching upon the Eastern Strand. Southshore's military leadership is hard-pressed by surrounding threats, yet Marshal Redpath remains attentive to maritime dangers along the southern coast. Having received fresh intelligence concerning naga incursions upon the Eastern Strand, Redpath dispatches a runner across town to Lieutenant Farren Orinelle with direct orders: abandon peripheral distractions, eliminate the amphibious menace, and deliver his progress reports directly to the Marshal in person.

Farren's Report. Farren's Report is an official dispatch drafted by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle in Southshore detailing his investigations into the local naga. Farren uses this document to appeal to his former mentor, Major Samuelson in Stormwind Keep, hoping to secure a reassignment back to the capital. Stationed on the embattled coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle grew weary of local leadership and the remote frontier. After tasking adventurers with hunting the Daggerspine naga to gather proof of their threat, Orinelle compiled his findings into a formal report. Rather than submitting it to his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Farren aimed to send it directly to Major Samuelson, the captain of the guard in Stormwind Keep. Having trained under Samuelson, Farren hoped the document would demonstrate his competence and justify an immediate transfer back to the comforts of Stormwind City.

Farsen's Watch. Farsen's Watch is an observational task given by Earthseer Farsen, a visiting Wildhammer shaman stationed high above Gol'Bolar Quarry. Using the earthseer's shamanic far sight, adventurers witness firsthand the growing infiltration of Dark Iron dwarves into the heart of Dun Morogh. This crucial survey marks an early step along the path toward the Hall of Thanes. Perched above the snowblown excavation of Gol'Bolar Quarry, Earthseer Farsen keeps a vigilant watch over the lower reaches of Dun Morogh. Having journeyed south from the crags of Aerie Peak, the Wildhammer visitor brings a keen spiritual awareness to lands usually patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers. Rather than relying on simple scouts, Farsen uses the traditional arts of his clan to monitor subterranean rumblings and unexpected movement along the hillsides.

Farstrider Lodge. Farstrider Lodge is a hunting outpost in southeastern Loch Modan. Its architecture appears to be high elven, while its residents include the high elf Vyrin Swiftwind, dwarves, and humans. Hunters and travelers come here for training, supplies, and work in the surrounding wilds. Farstrider Lodge stands apart from the sturdy stone buildings typical of Khaz Modan. Its architecture suggests high elven craftsmanship. Vyrin Swiftwind is the only known high elf still residing here, alongside dwarves and humans. The lodge's founder and date of construction are not established.

Farthing. Farthing serves the faithful from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. The kind and wise human clergyman guides parishioners and directs aid to settlements across the kingdom. Bishop Farthing tends to the spiritual needs of Stormwind City from the Cathedral of Light. Alongside Archbishop Benedictus and the gathered clergy, he counsels travelers, assists those pursuing the holy arts, and attends to the Church of the Holy Light's civic and pastoral duties.

Fathom Core. The Fathom Core is a specialized relic recovered from a submerged fathom stone in the depths of Blackfathom Deeps. When deciphered, it provides a comprehensive record of elemental activity in the surrounding region. The Earthen Ring seeks this artifact to discern what dark rituals the Twilight's Hammer cult is conducting beneath Ashenvale. Resting within an ancient fathom stone submerged among the Moonshrine Ruins, the Fathom Core serves as a historical record for elemental phenomena. It registers and preserves shifts, disruptions, and surges in the elements over time. For the shaman of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost, acquiring the core is essential for understanding how the Twilight's Hammer cultists are manipulating the regional elements to serve their own ends.

Favor for Krazek. While repairing a crock pot brought down to Booty Bay, the goblin Krazek demands a personal favor in return. He wants rare lesser bloodstone ore retrieved from a distant cave in the northern hills before he will hand back the repaired cookware. After accepting the broken cookware in Booty Bay, Krazek pauses his tinkering to ask for a trade. Rather than repairing the pot for free, he directs you far northward into the Arathi Highlands. Within a cave in Drywhisker Gorge lies lesser bloodstone ore, a low-grade yet prized mineral sought after by those who understand its properties.

Feast at the Blue Recluse. Your work for Morgan Stern in Dustwallow Marsh, ending with ... and Bugs, leads you back to Angus Stern at the Blue Recluse. Angus Stern is the uncle of Morgan Stern, whose recipe research you helped with in Dustwallow Marsh. Your road now leads back to Angus at the Blue Recluse.

Feather Charm. Feather Charms are crude magical trinkets carried by Frostmane troll novices in the snow-swept valleys of Coldridge Valley. Though fashioned from simple materials, they harbor an innate sorcerous resonance that catches the eye of local warlock mentors. The Frostmane trolls inhabiting the snowy caverns southwest of Anvilmar are known mostly for territorial savagery, but their novices dabble in primitive spellcraft. The feather charms carried by these young trolls hold a faint yet unmistakable magical power. In Anvilmar, warlock instructor Alamar Grimm considers them an intriguing subject of study—surprising for crude trollcraft—and uses them as a proving ground for fledgling warlocks seeking to master the binding of their first imp.

Feathermoon Stronghold. Feathermoon Stronghold is the premier night elf military base in southern Kalimdor, situated securely on Sardor Isle off the Forgotten Coast of Feralas. Commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, this fortified outpost projects Sentinel strength across the wild forest and keeps watch over regional threats. Perched on Sardor Isle across the channel from Feralas's mainland, Feathermoon Stronghold serves as the primary strategic base for the Sentinels in southern Kalimdor. Built among ancient elven groves and supplied with a sacred moonwell, the fortress houses archers, huntresses, and support staff under the direct supervision of General Shandris Feathermoon. From this insular sanctuary, the night elves project their influence over the verdant interior of Feralas, guarding against demonic corruption, hostile wildlife, and encroaching Horde expeditions.

Feathermoon Stronghold (Classic). Feathermoon Stronghold is a fortified night elf bastion situated on Sardor Isle off the western shores of Feralas. Established by General Shandris Feathermoon, it serves as the Alliance's primary staging ground and military anchor in southern Kalimdor. Perched on Sardor Isle just off the Forgotten Coast, Feathermoon Stronghold stands as a crucial bulwark for the Night Elves and the broader Alliance. Built under the direction of General Shandris Feathermoon—Tyrande Whisperwind's trusted lieutenant for ten millennia—the fortress projects Sentinel power deep into southern Kalimdor. Its isolated island geography shields it from the beasts, ogres, and Horde interlopers prowling the primeval jungles of mainland Feralas.

Feathers for Binding. Feathers for Binding is a quest in Shadowgale Forest centered on gathering insulating plumage from young shrieklings to craft a protective medicinal poultice. While these normally docile creatures have grown dangerously aggressive, their feathers remain essential for preserving antiseptic salves against the elements. Adventurers must brave the hostile fledglings to secure the materials needed for regional care. In the depths of Shadowgale Forest, preparing field medicine often demands resourcefulness from the land. When treating grave injuries, herbalists and healers turn to a specialized poultice built on moss and antiseptic tree sap. To ensure the sap does not rapidly dry out or lose its potency to harsh weather, durable insulative bindings are required. The juvenile feathers of Shadowgale shrieklings provide an ideal natural barrier, shielding the wound while sealing in the medicinal treatment.

Feegly the Exiled. Feegly the Exiled is an outcast dwarf found lurking near the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Once praised as one of the expedition's finest diggers, his obsession with an uncovered relic led General Twinbraid to drive him off.

Feero Ironhand. Feero Ironhand is a human paladin stationed at Maestra's Post in the western reaches of Ashenvale. Standing guard along the border between Darkshore and the forest, he works closely with Delgren the Purifier to combat the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand. Located along the road leading south from Darkshore into Ashenvale, Maestra's Post serves as a critical watchpoint for travelers and Alliance defenders alike. Feero Ironhand operates out of this outpost, maintaining communications and trade lines with Auberdine while keeping a vigilant watch over the surrounding woods. Together with Delgren the Purifier, Feero focuses his efforts against the malevolent Cult of the Dark Strand, ensuring the cultists and forest predators do not sever the path between Darnassus's supply lines and the front lines of Ashenvale.

Fel Cone. Fel Cones are corrupted seed pods that drop from the boughs of Teldrassil, easily spotted by the noxious green fumes drifting from their hulls. Though foul and tainted by dark energies, local night elf defenders find clever uses for them against nearby tricksters. Teldrassil is young, but corruption has already seeped into its living wood. Fel Cones are the visible evidence of this insidious rot—gnarled, fallen pine cones that billow with foul green smoke. Scattered beneath the boughs just east of Dolanaar, these pods are steeped in tainted magic that warps natural flora and makes them dangerous to touch or consume without caution.

Fel Moss. Fel Moss is a tainted vegetative substance spreading through the forests of Teldrassil. Carrying demonic and corruptive energies, it is carried by hostile grell and grellkin and poses an insidious threat to the wildlife and native furbolg tribes of the World Tree. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' immortality and heal the natural world, but corruption has already crept into its pristine boughs. Fel Moss is one of the most visible signs of this degradation. Found clinging to and carried by the impish grells and grellkin infesting Shadowglen, this malevolent growth radiates an unnatural, wicked magic. Forest protectors like the dryad Tarindrella have begun gathering samples to measure just how deeply this rot has infiltrated the sacred woodland canopy.

Fel Rock. Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells. Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin.

Fel'zerul. Fel'zerul is an orc warlock stationed at Stonard in the murky depths of the Swamp of Sorrows. Acting under direct orders from Warchief Thrall, he investigates the ominous presence lurking within the sunken Temple of Atal'Hakkar. While Thrall's Horde generally views dark arts with suspicion, the Warchief recognizes that understanding sinister powers requires those who study them. Fel'zerul was dispatched to Stonard specifically to unravel the corruption surrounding the Pool of Tears and the submerged Temple of Atal'Hakkar. By directing adventurers to recover artifacts and investigate the exiled Atal'ai trolls, the warlock seeks to determine what evil stirs beneath the murky waters before it threatens the Horde's southern outpost.

Felfire Hill. Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements. During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal.

Felgur Twocuts. Felgur Twocuts is a blunt orc scout stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. He coordinates Horde efforts against the regional centaur clans. Standing watch amid the bleak expanse of Ghost Walker Post in central Desolace, Felgur Twocuts has little patience for pleasantries. As a forward scout for the Horde, he assesses the threats facing travelers and settlers venturing west through the mountains, particularly the local Kolkar centaur.

Felix Whindlebolt. Felix Whindlebolt is a displaced gnome refugee taking shelter at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. In his haste to flee the radiation flooding Gnomeregan, he lost his personal belongings, and hostile Frostmane trolls made off with them. Following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, thousands of gnomes found themselves wandering the freezing reaches of Dun Morogh in search of safety. Felix Whindlebolt fled the irradiated city in such haste that he lost all his personal belongings and tools. To make matters worse, Frostmane ice trolls carried his chest, his box and his bucket of bolts back to their camps southwest of Anvilmar, leaving him stranded, destitute, and relying on sympathetic wanderers to retrieve his stolen gear.

Felix's Box. Felix's Box is a small container of personal belongings belonging to Felix Whindlebolt, a refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. Lost during the frantic evacuation into Dun Morogh, the box was looted by local Frostmane trolls and carried off to their camps southwest of Anvilmar. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan during the failed attempt to purge the trogg menace, Felix Whindlebolt joined the frantic exodus of gnomes into Coldridge Valley. In his desperation to escape the radioactive fumes, Felix dropped his most prized personal possessions and crafting gear along the snowy road. Before he could recover them, indigenous Frostmane trolls plundered the roadside remnants and dragged his box, along with his chest and bucket of bolts, back to their crude settlements southwest of Anvilmar.

Felix's Bucket of Bolts. Felix's Bucket of Bolts is a container of spare hardware and tools owned by Felix Whindlebolt, a gnome refugee who fled the fall of Gnomeregan. During his escape into Dun Morogh, the bucket was snatched by local Frostmane trolls and dragged into their nearby camps. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan following the disaster against the troggs, thousands of gnomes fled into the freezing wilds of Dun Morogh with whatever they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape with his vital equipment, but in the chaos of his flight toward Anvilmar, he was ambushed by the Frostmane trolls who inhabit the crags southwest of town. The trolls plundered his belongings, including this bucket full of bolts and parts, leaving the artisan stranded without the essential materials needed to ply his craft in exile.

Felix's Chest. Felix's Chest is a container of personal belongings lost by the exiled gnome Felix Whindlebolt during the flight from Gnomeregan. Carried away by Frostmane trolls lurking near Coldridge Valley, it sits abandoned within one of their primitive mountain camps. When the subterranean techno-city of Gnomeregan fell to trogg incursions and toxic radioactive fallout, thousands of gnomes fled toward the snowy surface of Dun Morogh with whatever possessions they could carry. Felix Whindlebolt managed to escape the irradiated ruins, but amidst the panic of the evacuation, native Frostmane trolls scavenged the roads and overtook the scattered survivors. Felix lost his primary toolkits and belongings, with his sturdy chest hauled off to the crude camps the trolls maintain in the crags southwest of Anvilmar.

Felpaw Village. Felpaw Village is a corrupted furbolg settlement nestled in the far northern reaches of Felwood, guarding the mountain path leading directly to Timbermaw Hold. Inhabited by the fallen Deadwood tribe, its huts and gathering grounds are tainted by demonic influence and hostile to all outsiders. Situated at the northern edge of Felwood, Felpaw Village serves as the primary northern redoubt for the fallen Deadwood furbolgs. Once gentle forest wardens, the tribe fell victim to the demonic blight unleashed during the Third War, driving them into a state of feral madness. Now, the village stands as a blighted enclave filled with crude huts, ritual totems, and hostile warriors who attack anyone wandering near the tunnel entrance to Timbermaw Hold.

Felstalker Hoof. A Felstalker Hoof is a physical token taken from demonic beasts infesting the Burning Blade Coven in Durotar's Valley of Trials. Young shaman must retrieve these hooves as a trial of readiness before learning to commune with the elemental spirits of the earth. Within the sun-baked Valley of Trials, the trainer Canaga Earthcaller tasks budding shaman with facing the demonic taint threatening Durotar. The Burning Blade Coven to the north harbors vile familiars and demonic felstalkers. Taking the hooves of these fiends is not merely an act of culling pests, but a rigorous test of endurance, resolve, and spirit. Only by subduing these chaotic beasts can an aspiring shaman prove worthy of receiving the secrets of the earth and preparing the ceremonial sapta needed to commune directly with elemental spirits.

Felstone Field. Felstone Field is a blighted farmstead located in the northwestern Western Plaguelands. Once a thriving piece of Lordaeron agricultural land, it has been claimed by the Scourge and anchored by a plague cauldron spewing toxic fumes across the ruined soil. Before the Third War, Felstone Field was a peaceful, productive family farm feeding the citizens of Lordaeron. When the plague swept through the north, the homestead fell swiftly to the Cult of the Damned and the Scourge. Today, the fields sprout dead weeds and creeping rot instead of grain. At the heart of the farmland sits an enormous plague cauldron, continuously churning foul vapors into the sky under the watch of Cauldron Lord Bilemaw and legions of skeletal flayers, sorcerers, and ravenous ghouls.

Fenris Isle. Fenris Isle is a large, mist-shrouded island in Lordamere Lake, bordering the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest. Once home to a bustling Lordaeron military stronghold, the island now lies under the iron grip of undead Rot Hide gnolls and a rogue Scourge necromancer. Before the Third War devastated northern Lordaeron, Fenris Isle served as a vital outpost for the kingdom, anchored by Fenris Keep. When the Scourge tore through the realm, the garrison was slaughtered or fled into exile, leaving the island abandoned to the dead. In the years since, the island became a stronghold for the Rot Hide gnolls—vile, plague-ridden creatures who established a crude empire across the lake's shores. The Forsaken of Silverpine Forest keep a vigilant watch on the island, viewing its entrenched inhabitants as a severe threat to their northern territories.

Fenris Keep. Fenris Keep is an isolated stone fortress situated atop Fenris Isle in the heart of Lordamere Lake. Once a strategic stronghold housing Lordaeron troops, it has fallen into the hands of the Scourge under the rogue mage Thule Ravenclaw.

Fenrus the Devourer. Fenrus the Devourer is an enormous worg that prowls the upper sanctum of Shadowfang Keep. Kept as a personal pet and guardian by Archmage Arugal, the ravenous beast is bloated on unnatural magics. Anyone daring to breach the archmage's personal study must contend with this feral horror and the master who watches over it. Deep within Shadowfang Keep, just outside Archmage Arugal's personal chambers, lurks the monstrous worg known as Fenrus the Devourer. Unlike the lupine worgen roaming the ramparts, Fenrus is an actual worg, swollen to gargantuan proportions. Prowling the shelves, scrolls, and arcane apparatuses of Arugal's private study, the beast serves both as a pet and as a violent perimeter guard against any intruder seeking the mad mage's head.

Fenwick Thatros. Mennet Carkad assigns promising rogues in the Undercity to hunt down Fenwick Thatros on orders directly from Lord Varimathras. Thatros is suspected of organizing independent undead forces along the shores of Silverpine Forest. Eliminating him proves an operative's mettle to the Deathstalkers, opening the way for more sophisticated trade training. Within the dark corridors of the Rogues' Quarter, Mennet Carkad handles internal contracts and training for the Deathstalkers—the Forsaken's secretive intelligence wing. When Lord Varimathras sends down a priority target, it is not an assignment handed to novice recruits lightly. Fenwick Thatros has drawn the dreadlord's attention by establishing a foothold among the rogue undead in Silverpine Forest. Left unchecked, independent undead leadership could jeopardize Forsaken consolidation across Lordaeron's old holdings.

Fenwick's Head. Fenwick's Head is the grisly proof of execution taken from Fenwick Thatros on the shores of Lordamere Lake. It is claimed by Forsaken rogues operating on direct orders passed down through Lord Varimathras. Within the Rogues' Quarter of the Undercity, Mennet Carkad acts on urgent intelligence routed directly from dreadlord Varimathras. A hostile undead leader named Fenwick Thatros has established a foothold near the decaying docks along Lordamere Lake in Silverpine Forest. To prevent this threat from rallying hostile undead against the Forsaken, Carkad dispatches promising Deathstalkers to locate Thatros, eliminate him, and sever his head as undeniable proof of the kill.

Feral Scar Vale. Feral Scar Vale is a rocky gorge tucked within the High Wilderness of western Feralas. Overrun by territorial Feral Scar yetis, its cavernous tunnels are notoriously perilous to travelers who venture off the overgrown forest trails. Situated amid the thick foliage and sheer cliffs of the High Wilderness, Feral Scar Vale serves as the primary den for the savage Feral Scar yetis. While yetis are common in the snowy peaks of Alterac and Dun Morogh, these primal brutes have adapted completely to the wild, humid climate of Feralas. They fiercely defend the vale's cave network, hoarding bone trophies and aggressively driving off any intruders who wander into their hunting grounds.

Feralas: A History. You find a book that looks as if nobody has opened it in ages, and it may be exactly what Troyas needs. It belongs to Daryn Lightwind, so you need to ask whether you may borrow it. The book's covers are badly worn and its pages have yellowed. After looking it over, you suspect it may be what Troyas is searching for. You pick it up, then think better of borrowing it without asking. It is Daryn Lightwind's, so she should be asked first.

Ferocitas the Dream Eater. Ferocitas the Dream Eater is an Alliance quest given by Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar. After recovering his damaged heirloom dreamcatcher, Tallonkai discovers its potent emerald core was pried away by Gnarlpine furbolgs north of Starbreeze Village. Adventurers are sent to slay the corrupted mystics and recover the stolen jewel from their leader, Ferocitas. When Tallonkai Swiftroot examined the dreamcatcher recovered from the corrupted wilds, relief quickly turned to dismay. The sacred artifact had been vandalized, its vibrant emerald centerpiece pried from the woven frame. Word among the night elves held that a band of Gnarlpine mystics north of Starbreeze Village had fallen under the influence of a furbolg leader known as Ferocitas the Dream Eater, who brazenly wore a brilliant green stone around his neck. Knowing the sacred gem was useless and perverse in the creature's clutches, Tallonkai sent defenders to wrest it back.

Fey Dragon Scale. A Fey Dragon Scale is a shimmering woodland relic harvested from the elusive faerie dragons living around Stonetalon Peak. It is sought after by the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses it as an exotic reagent in an alchemical brew mocking night elven nature magic. Faerie dragons are mysterious, elusive creatures tied closely to the wild groves of Kalimdor, particularly the untouched forests around Stonetalon Peak. Their scales carry a natural magical luster reminiscent of the deep woods they guard. While revered by the night elves as harmless woodland spirits and allies, outsiders view them as an untamed source of rare magical ingredients.

Field Marshal Snowfall. Field Marshal Snowfall is a dwarven military officer stationed in Ironforge's Military Ward to coordinate the Alliance war effort against the rising silithid threat. Facing an ancient evil stirring in the southern sands of Silithus, he oversees the massive logistical drive required to equip the allied armies. Snowfall tracks donated raw materials and rewards those who aid the realm's preparation for war. Standing watch in Ironforge's Military Ward, Field Marshal Snowfall serves as the central coordinator for the Alliance's mobilization against Ahn'Qiraj. He views the brewing conflict not merely as a border skirmish, but as a critical fight against an ancient enemy hostile to all creations of the Titans. Snowfall oversees staggering stockpiles of supplies—millions of bandages, tons of metal bars, leathers, herbs, and rations gathered by adventurers—ensuring that Alliance forces will be armed, armored, and fed when the march south to Silithus begins.

Field Marshal Stonebridge. At Stormwind's gates, Field Marshal Stonebridge helps oversee the city's defenses with General Marcus Jonathan. She also receives reports and trophies from major victories. Field Marshal Stonebridge watches the eastern archway at the entrance to the Valley of Heroes, beside Stormwind's main gates. A senior officer in the Grand Alliance, she works closely with General Marcus Jonathan. From the gate, she watches defenders, travelers, and returning champions enter the capital, ready to organize the garrison if danger breaches the outer defenses.

Field of Giants. The Field of Giants is an expansive plain covering the southern Barrens between Camp Taurajo and the marshes of Dustwallow. Named for the towering kodo, thunder lizards, and massive beasts that graze its arid scrub, the region has recently grown far more perilous due to an encroaching silithid infestation. Stretching along the southern span of the Gold Road, the Field of Giants is remote, rugged, and lightly defended compared to the Barrens to the north. While the road's wooden watchtowers stand largely abandoned, the land itself thrums with life. Tremendous herds of Kalimdor's megafauna wander the vast flats, drawing hunters and naturalists alike. However, safety is elusive here: dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a far more sinister menace has begun burrowing beneath the earth.

Fields of Grief. Fields of Grief is an early Forsaken mission assigned by Deathguard Simmer along the road north of Deathknell. It tasks fledglings with raiding a living human farmstead to harvest Tirisfal pumpkins for the Royal Apothecary Society in Brill. For new Forsaken adventurers freshly risen from the crypts of Deathknell, stepping onto the misty roads of Tirisfal Glades is an immediate lesson in hostility. Deathguard Simmer represents the pragmatic malice of Sylvanas Windrunner's forces: survival means seizing what the living possess and turning it toward the Undercity's darker endeavors.

Fields of Grief. Fields of Grief concludes Apothecary Johaan's experiment to weaponize ordinary pumpkins gathered from Solliden Farmstead. Having infused the crop with his latest alchemical concotion, Johaan dispatches you to feed the laced vegetable to a captive Scarlet Crusader languishing in Brill. Apothecary Johaan of the Royal Apothecary Society believes the Forsaken must exploit every tactical advantage to fend off the Scourge from the north and human incursions from the south. Rather than relying solely on raw blade-work or dark sorcery, the Society seeks to harness ordinary staples of the land. By tainting the pumpkins recovered from the mortal farmers of Solliden Farmstead, Johaan intends to prove that even common produce can be transformed into an instrument of death on behalf of the Dark Lady.

Fiery Blaze Enchantments. Sigrun Ironhew, waiting in the Badlands for word from Ironforge, knows a technique for imbuing weapons with fire. It needs blood from the still-beating heart of a rare black drake whelp, and the whelps of Lethlor Ravine are where to find one. Sigrun Ironhew learned a special way of imbuing weapons with fiery enchantments as an apprentice to Feranor Steeltoe, last heard of among a hunting party's smiths in Lordaeron. Sigrun is waiting for word from Ironforge and has little else to do.

Fiery Menace!. Hansel Heavyhands says that every time he wants a moment to relax and reflect on his life, the powers that be hand him another job. Greater lava spiders are causing a ruckus in the Searing Gorge, and he wants you to kill twenty of them. Hansel Heavyhands complains that the powers that be never leave him in peace. Greater lava spiders are causing a ruckus, and he would rather you did the killing than him.

Filled Amethyst Phial. The Filled Amethyst Phial contains sacred water taken from the ancient moonwell beneath the boughs of the Oracle Tree. Gathered on behalf of Corithras Moonrage, this purified water is used by the Cenarion druids to study the troubled, imperfect growth of Teldrassil. Far to the northwest in Teldrassil lies the Oracle Glade, where the oldest and most potent of the island's moonwells rests beneath the great Oracle Tree. While the lesser moonwells across the boughs serve the day-to-day needs of the night elves, this well's waters are saturated with the raw essence of Elune's grace. Druids tasked with monitoring the health of the World Tree use specialized amethyst phials to collect and preserve this powerful liquid for testing and ritual cleansing.

Filled Blue Waterskin. The Filled Blue Waterskin holds pristine water gathered from a fountain at the ancient Ruins of Stardust in Ashenvale. Shaman seeking communion with the water spirits collect this sample as a vital reagent for their trial of passage. Initiates undertaking the Call of Water are directed northward across the border from the Barrens into the dense forests of Ashenvale. Nestled against the mountains dividing Ashenvale from Stonetalon, beyond Lake Mystral, lie the Ruins of Stardust—a secluded elven sanctuary guarded by fierce forest beasts. At the center of this sacred lake stands an untouched fountain. Drawing from its basin into a blue waterskin yields water untainted by corruption or drought, prized by shaman masters for ritual attunement.

Filled Brown Waterskin. The Filled Brown Waterskin contains fresh water drawn from a rare pond near Brine's hut in the Barrens. Collected by aspiring shaman, it forms the first fundamental step in brewing the sapta needed to commune with the spirits of water. In the parched expanse of the Barrens, surface water is both a blessing and a battleground. The pond nestled beneath Brine's hut offers precious hydration that draws the desperate and defensive quilboar who dwell nearby. For an initiate walking the path of the shaman, filling this simple leather waterskin is not merely an errand of gathering supplies; it is an elemental lesson. By approaching the pool and witnessing the fierce territorial struggle surrounding it, the novice observes firsthand how the very substance that sustains life in the desert can drive mortal creatures to violence.

text.enUS: Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler. The Filled Cliffspring Falls Sampler contains murky water drawn from the headwaters near Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore. Gathered on behalf of the Cenarion Circle, it serves as crucial evidence in uncovering what is poisoning the local deer population. Cliffspring Falls provides the principal drinking water for much of Darkshore, cascading down from the eastern highlands toward the sea. Recently, however, the wildlife relying on these waters—specifically the local deer—have fallen prey to a debilitating, unnatural malady. At the behest of Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, druidic initiates retrieve this sample directly from the mouth of a cave infested by hostile naga. The vial holds visibly putrid liquid, confirming that the region's primary fresh water supply is actively corrupted.

Filled Containment Coffer. A Filled Containment Coffer is an enchanted receptacle used by Forsaken spellcasters to trap erratic magical entities. By deploying a Cantation of Manifestation to reveal and weaken rift spawn in the Apothecarium, mages can trap the anomalies inside these reinforced boxes for safe examination. When unexplained magical disturbances manifested within Algernon's shop in the Apothecarium, the Forsaken mage Anastasia Hartwell commissioned practitioners of the arcane to capture the entities responsible. Because the rift creatures exist purely as living magical energy and wander unseen, ordinary cages are useless. Instead, spellcasters reveal the entities with a Cantation of Manifestation, defeat them in combat, and snap these specially prepared containment coffers shut around them. The sealed boxes shield the carrier from volatile magical backlashes while keeping the specimens intact for magical dissection.

Filled Crystal Phial. A Filled Crystal Phial contains sacred waters drawn from the moonwell just north of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Gathered at the instruction of Tenaron Stormgrip, this water serves as a novice's introduction to the sacred and volatile power coursing through Teldrassil. To prepare young night elves before they venture into the wider world, Tenaron Stormgrip sends them to gather water from the moonwell nestled in Shadowglen. The phial holds more than simple spring water; moonwells are infused with residual energies traced back to the ancient Well of Eternity. While the Sentinels honor these sites as blessed shrines of Elune and druids channel their restorative qualities into tending nature, the arcane sorcery of old remains strictly forbidden. Drawing this water is the first step in understanding the sacrifices of Mount Hyjal and the delicate balance required to nurture Teldrassil.

Filled Cursed Ooze Jar. A Filled Cursed Ooze Jar contains the noxious remains of a cursed ooze collected from the corrupted forests of Felwood. It is gathered on behalf of Laris Geardawdle, a gnome scholar in Ironforge seeking to uncover the primordial origins of slimes across Azeroth. While most adventurers avoid the vile puddles and caustic slimes crawling across Kalimdor, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle sees them as a biological mystery. Noticing that slimes appear in diverse environments and observing Forsaken apothecaries diligently harvesting them, Geardawdle developed a controversial theory: oozes might be primordial secretions tied directly to Azeroth's creation. Gathering a sample requires braving Felwood's blighted woods, defeating a cursed ooze, and scooping the acidic matter into an empty jar before it completely dissolves.
