text.enUS: Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler. The Filled Dreadmist Peak Sampler is a vial containing corrupted water drawn from the elevated pools atop Dreadmist Peak in the northern Barrens. Gathered by fledgling druids of the Horde, it provides the physical evidence needed by the Cenarion Circle to study a vile affliction poisoning the region's wildlife. The high crags of Dreadmist Peak house natural pools whose mists historically shape weather and rainfall across the northern Barrens. When the demon-worshipping Burning Blade established their coven atop the summit, the water quickly soured. Suspecting that demonic rituals poisoned the vapors feeding the surrounding savanna, Cenarion druids dispatch initiates to capture a specimen using a specialized sampler. The foul liquid inside confirms their worst fears, reeking of corruption potent enough to sicken the herds wandering below.

Filled Etched Phial. A Filled Etched Phial is an ornate dryad vessel laden with consecrated water drawn directly from a night elf moonwell in Ashenvale. Requested by the tauren of Thunder Bluff, this sanctified water possesses the rare spiritual potency required to quench the eternal flame shielding a sacred centaur relic. Obtaining this phial demands infiltrating night elf territory deep within Ashenvale. The empty vessel must first be claimed from the dryads around Raynewood Retreat, whose delicate containers are crafted to hold pure restorative draughts. Filled subsequently at a sacred moonwell near the western bank of the Falfarren River, the phial captures water brimming with celestial, nature-bound power. To the night elves, taking this water uninvited is an act of blatant desecration, but the tauren see it as a vital necessity for addressing a regional threat further south.

Filled Jade Phial. The Filled Jade Phial holds sacred waters drawn from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village. Carried back to Dolanaar, it serves as part of an ongoing ritual to replenish the capital's central waters while young night elves learn the history of their people. The druids of Darnassus rely on sacred moonwell waters drawn from across the boughs of Teldrassil to replenish their central wells. Specially crafted vessels, such as the jade phial entrusted to young adventurers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, are attuned to contain these pure waters safely. By venturing eastward to the moonwell outside Starbreeze Village, initiates collect the vital water while proving their devotion to the maintenance of the World Tree.

name.deDE: Mit einer reinen Probe gefülltes Glas

text.enUS: Filled Pure Sample Jar. A Filled Pure Sample Jar contains an uncorrupted specimen of primordial ooze gathered from the remote wilds. It serves as crucial baseline data for the gnome scholar Laris Geardawdle in Ironforge, who is studying how environmental corruption alters living matter. In his study of oozes across Azeroth, the gnomish researcher Laris Geardawdle discovered a troubling phenomenon: these amorphous creatures absorb and reflect the magical and environmental corruption of their habitats. After cataloging the tainted slimes of Felwood, Laris determined that deciphering the nature of the rot required a control group. A Filled Pure Sample Jar holds ooze harvested from pristine, untainted wilderness—such as the primordial ecology of Un'Goro Crater—offering scholars an unaltered specimen to compare against diseased and corrupted strains.

Filled Red Waterskin. The Filled Red Waterskin contains pristine spring water drawn from the village well in Tarren Mill. Gathering this pure water amidst the blighted ruins held by the Forsaken serves as a vital trial for young shaman seeking communion with the water spirits. While training shaman in the ways of water, the hermit Brine in the Barrens dispatches initiates on a lengthy journey to Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Amidst the decay and the dead, the town's central well miraculously draws clear, untainted spring water. Brine regards this holy vestige in an unhallowed land as an emblem of enduring spirit—drawing a parallel between the uncorrupted spring and Warchief Thrall's enduring resolve despite profound hardship. Gathering this sample proves an initiate's reverence for water's purity regardless of hostile surroundings.

Filled Tainted Ooze Jar. A Filled Tainted Ooze Jar contains viscous, tainted ooze scooped directly from the remains of oozes wandering the corrupted forests of Felwood. Secured in specialized containment jars, these samples are brought to Ironforge to support radical theories regarding the origin of life on Azeroth. The tainted oozes roaming northern Kalimdor carry the deep, lingering corruption of Felwood. Harvesting them requires careful containment using jars provided by gnomish researchers. While most travelers avoid the noxious creatures entirely, collecting these samples provides rare material for natural philosophy and biological study far from the blighted forests.

Filled Tourmaline Phial. The Filled Tourmaline Phial holds enchanted waters drawn from the moonwell bordering the Pools of Arlithrien in southern Teldrassil. Collected at the request of Corithras Moonrage, the water serves as part of an effort to monitor the health and balance of the growing World Tree. The Tourmaline Phial is prepared specifically to draw water from the moonwell located southeast of the road to Darnassus, on the shores of the Pools of Arlithrien. Gathering water from this shrine has become fraught with peril due to the sudden aggression of the Gnarlpine furbolgs, peaceful neighbors who have rapidly deteriorated into violent madness. Corithras Moonrage tasks travelers with braving the hostile groves to secure this water, aiming to diagnose the deepening corruption unsettling the land.

Filled Vessel. The Filled Vessel contains purified waters drawn from the various sacred moonwells across Teldrassil. Entrusted to couriers by Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar, it is delivered to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm in Darnassus to aid his study of the World Tree's ailments. Teldrassil was planted without the blessings of the Great Aspects, Alexstrasza and Nozdormu, leaving its immense boughs vulnerable to unexpected corruption, strange beasts, and crazed furbolg tribes. In an attempt to monitor and cleanse the burgeoning boughs, night elf acolytes are dispatched to gather water samples from moonwells situated across the boughs. Corithras Moonrage consolidates these gathered phials into a single Filled Vessel, sending it onward to the capital. The mixture serves as a vital sample of Teldrassil's vitality for Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, who works tirelessly in the Cenarion Enclave to uncover a remedy for the Great Tree's pervasive flaws.

Filling the Soul Gem. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, an attempt is made to preserve the young troll Yenniku. With the youth caught in a trance, a prepared soul gem is brought forth to capture his spirit. Following the effort to save Yenniku, you stand face to face with the young troll in Stranglethorn Vale. His mind is lost, caught entirely in another place while he remains motionless before you. The only path forward involves the enchanted gem prepared specifically to hold his essence.

Filthy Paws. Filthy Paws is a task given by Mountaineer Stormpike to salvage valuable equipment from the infested Silver Stream Mine. Though depleted of ore, the mine was repurposed as a depot by the Miners' League before encroaching kobolds overran the tunnels. Dwarven authorities want their sturdy tools recovered before the Mountaineers launch a destructive purge of the site. The Silver Stream Mine, tucked into the hills of northern Loch Modan east of Algaz Station, yielded its last silver veins long ago. Rather than abandon the subterranean complex, the dwarven Miners' League repurposed the dry shafts as a secure storage depot for spare excavation equipment, picks, and staging materials. Sturdy subterranean tunnels make natural storehouses in Khaz Modan, provided they remain garrisoned and locked against the wilderness.

name.esES: Pista final del tesoro de Sander

text.enUS: Final Clue to Sanders' Treasure. Along Westfall's coast, Captain Sanders' last directions point out to sea. A note in an old jug sends scavengers west toward his buried treasure. Captain Sanders left his final directions in an old whiskey jug on the Westfall coast. The pirate had scattered cryptic notes along the shoreline, and this one completes the trail. From the jug, the directions lead due west into the ocean. Follow them through the surf to a lonely offshore rock, where his ironbound sea chest lies.

Final Passage. Parqual Fintallas tells you that you have passed this test and the ones before it. You are sent back to Dorn Plainstalker in Thousand Needles, who will sense the change in you and see whether you have grown strong in mind, body and spirit, enough to be honoured for your efforts. This is the last step of the Test of Faith, the chain of trials that Dorn Plainstalker began. Dorn waits in the Weathered Nook, in a cave reached by a ramp, north of Freewind Post. Parqual Fintallas urges you to stay true to the balance you have shown throughout these trials.

Find Agmond. Prospector Ironband has not heard from Prospector Agmond in weeks. Agmond was in charge of the excavation sites in the Badlands, and Ironband wants Agmond found so the report can be collected. Agmond ran the excavations in the Badlands, to the southwest. Ironband says "ran" on purpose, for there has been no word from Agmond in weeks. Ironband wants Agmond found, and the report with him. Agmond was last heard of at the farthest-south dig of the Badlands, a small outfit beyond Angor Fortress, and that is where the search should begin.

Find Bingles. Find Bingles is an Alliance breadcrumb quest initiated in Ironforge by the gnome Gnoarn. Concerned about an aviator who vanished over a week ago during an aerial reconnaissance flight toward fallen Gnomeregan, Gnoarn directs adventurers to scour the shores of Loch Modan. Tracking down the missing pilot leads right to Bingles Blastenheimer, who is very much alive but in desperate need of mechanical salvage. In the bustling gnome enclave of Tinker Town within Ironforge, anxiety runs high over missing kin and lost machinery. The gnome aviator Bingles Blastenheimer was dispatched on an aerial reconnaissance mission over the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. When more than a week passed without word, Gnoarn feared the worst—suspecting Bingles had succumbed to gnome engineering's occupational hazard and blown himself out of the sky. The last reported sighting placed the eccentric flyer somewhere above the waters of the Loch.

Find OOX-09/HL!. An egg-shaped metal device in the Hinterlands springs open at the turn of a knob, and a gnome named Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks from inside it. A homing robot of Oglethorpe's has crashed near Skulk Rock, and the beacon is to be carried to it. Fiddle with a knob on the strange metal egg and it opens into a gnomish contraption. A crackling voice gives the name Oglethorpe Obnoticus and says the homing robot has crashed. The coordinates have been worked out: the robot came down where the river begins, close to Skulk Rock. The beacon is to be taken to it.

Find OOX-17/TN!. A strange egg-shaped metal device you have uncovered springs to life when you fiddle with its knob, and a voice from inside introduces itself as Oglethorpe. Oglethorpe's homing robot has gone missing, and you are asked to carry the beacon to it. Fiddling with a knob on the strange egg opens it up into a gnomish robotic contraption, and a voice crackles to life from inside. The speaker gives the name Oglethorpe and says a homing robot has gone missing. Oglethorpe has now computed where it went down, near the Gaping Chasm in Tanaris, and asks you to take the beacon to the robot.

Find OOX-22/FE!. You come across a strange egg-shaped device of metal. A voice inside it introduces itself as Oglethorpe Obnoticus, whose homing robot has crashed. You are asked to bring the beacon to the machine, which lies in a cave close to Feral Scar Vale. Fiddling with a knob springs the metal egg open into a gnomish robotic contraption, and a crackling voice speaks from within. Oglethorpe Obnoticus says the homing robot has crashed, and promises payment if you recover it. The beacon is to be taken to the robot, and Oglethorpe has computed where it lies: a cave near Feral Scar Vale.

Find the Lost Guards. Guard Thomas is waiting at Elwynn's eastern bridge for word of two missing guards. Rolf and Malakai were sent north along the river to watch for murlocs, but neither has returned. Guard Thomas watches the eastern crossing of Elwynn Forest, where the King's road approaches Redridge. Murlocs have made the nearby waters more dangerous. Days ago, Thomas sent two Stormwind guards, Rolf and Malakai, north along the riverbanks to scout the threat and clear out nests. Neither has returned, and Thomas fears violence stopped their patrol.

Find the Shattered Hand. Find the Shattered Hand is a journey quest sending promising Forsaken rogues from Tirisfal Glades across the sea to Durotar. Directed by the Deathstalkers, the initiate travels to Orgrimmar's shadowy underbelly to learn specialized arts from the Shattered Hand clan. While the Forsaken cultivate their own covert order in the Deathstalkers, their mutual alliance with the Horde opens avenues of collaboration in darker arts. Mennet Carkad, having seen a rogue prove their worth in Tirisfal Glades, recognizes the need for broader instruction. He directs promising shadows to seek out the Shattered Hand in Orgrimmar, leaning on the quiet partnership between Lordaeron's undead operatives and Kalimdor's orcish guild of assassins.

Finding Warmth. Finding Warmth is a humble errand centered on keeping a welcoming hearth fueled with firewood. With the host occupied by other responsibilities, travelers are asked to gather logs so that any soul seeking warmth can find comfort. Completing the task keeps the fire burning and opens the way to further chores. Finding Warmth is a simple chore undertaken to sustain a welcoming fire. The questgiver keeps an open hearth ready to warm any wandering soul, but mounting obligations have left them unable to gather fuel on their own. By stepping in to collect firewood, travelers ensure the hearth remains alight for anyone seeking shelter and comfort.

Finding the Antidote. Finding the Antidote is an urgent task undertaken for Kor'ghan in Orgrimmar to brew a cure for the poisoned hunter Rhinag. Facing a strict deadline before the venom proves fatal, an adventurer must gather venomtail poison sacs from scorpids outside the city walls. It highlights the unforgiving nature of Durotar's wildlife and the necessity of wilderness preparation. While hunting throughout Durotar, a Darkspear troll named Rhinag made the perilous mistake of engaging native venomtail scorpids without bringing along an antidote. Stung and succumbing rapidly to their potent toxins, he was forced to send for immediate aid. The task falls to Kor'ghan, an experienced hunter residing in Orgrimmar, to mix a restorative draught before the poison finishes its work.

name.esES: Trozos de cangrejo de gran calidad

text.enUS: Fine Crab Chunks. Fine Crab Chunks are prime cuts of meat gathered from the coastal crustaceans roaming the beaches of Darkshore. Highly prized for their culinary versatility, they are sought after by local shore-dwellers and hungry fishermen looking to prepare an endless variety of seafood dishes. The misty, jagged shores of Darkshore are thick with skittering crustaceans, specifically Reef Crawlers and Encrusted Tide Crawlers. While many travelers view these armored shore-prowlers as pests or aggressive hazards along the waterline, enterprising gourmands consider their meat among the finest bounty of the coast. Prized cuts harvested from these creatures yield rich, tender morsels that lend themselves to practically any cooking method imaginable, from boiling and broiling to deep frying and savory stews.

Fine Moonstalker Pelt. A Fine Moonstalker Pelt is the thick, pristine hide taken from the most mature predatory moonstalkers roaming southern Darkshore. Terenthis of Auberdine uses these prized furs to weave an enchanted cloak that allows searchers to slip past the woods' hostile beasts unnoticed. While common moonstalkers prowl throughout the mist-laden forests of Darkshore, only the older moonstalker sires and matriarchs possess coats dense and healthy enough to yield a fine pelt. These powerful wildcats establish territories along the Wildbend River and further south toward the borders of Ashenvale, where they hunt with lethal patience.

Fiora Longears. This errand introduces Alliance adventurers from the Eastern Kingdoms to the untamed continent of Kalimdor. Directed by the enthusiastic recruiter Red Jack Flint in Menethil Harbor, travelers take ship across the Great Sea to report to his high elf contact, Fiora Longears, in the inn of Theramore. For many humans, dwarves, and gnomes, the Eastern Kingdoms feel fraught with old conflicts and scarred earth. In the bustling port of Menethil Harbor, the sailor Red Jack Flint spends his days urging adventurous travelers to board a vessel bound across the Great Sea. Describing Kalimdor as an uncharted realm of fortune and opportunity, Flint directs bold wanderers to Theramore to meet his associate, an elf named Fiora Longears.

name.esES: Armadura de malla endurecida con fuego
name.frFR: Une cotte de mailles en acier trempé

text.enUS: Fire Hardened Mail. In Stormwind, Furen Longbeard has a new armor design for an Alliance warrior. The dwarf armorer offers to forge Fire Hardened Mail if the warrior brings him rare materials from both continents. Furen Longbeard has forged an exceptional buckler for the aspiring warrior and now proposes a greater work: mail made to withstand fierce blows. His craft calls for more than iron or steel. He needs rare materials touched by elemental heat and natural resilience. Furen cannot leave his Stormwind forge, so the warrior seeking the armor must gather these dangerous ingredients.

name.esES: La forja del Penacho en Llamas

text.enUS: Fire Plume Forged. Krinkle Goodsteel points you to Fire Plume Ridge, a simmering volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where the lava lake at the top is hot enough to forge the stem of a skeletal key. Afterward you carry it to Alchemist Arbington at Chillwind Point in the Western Plaguelands. Forging the stem of the key takes two bars of thorium and fierce heat. The thorium is yours to find, but Krinkle Goodsteel can help with the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, and it only needs dipping in the lava lake on top of Fire Plume Ridge. The lava does the rest, fusing thorium and bone together.

name.esES: La forja del Penacho en Llamas

text.enUS: Fire Plume Forged. Krinkle Goodsteel points you to Fire Plume Ridge, a simmering volcano west in Un'Goro Crater, where the lava lake at the top is hot enough to forge the stem of a skeletal key. Afterward you carry it to Apothecary Dithers at the Bulwark in the Western Plaguelands. Forging the stem of the key takes two bars of thorium and fierce heat. The thorium is yours to find, but Krinkle Goodsteel can help with the heat. Your gold has bought a mold, and it only needs dipping in the lava lake on top of Fire Plume Ridge. The lava does the rest, fusing thorium and bone together.

Fire Plume Ridge. Fire Plume Ridge is the active volcano rising directly from the center of Un'Goro Crater. Its searing slopes and subterranean magma channels fuel the crater's geysers and steam pools while playing host to fierce fire elementals. Towering over the primeval basin of Un'Goro, Fire Plume Ridge stands in sharp contrast to the surrounding lush jungle. Lava steadily cascades down its scorched rock faces, carving a landscape of ash and basalt. Subterranean magma arteries spiderweb outward beneath the soil from the ridge, fueling the bubbling geysers and hot springs scattered across the basin. The oppressive heat here is legendary—far exceeding ordinary volcanic temperatures according to goblin measuring devices—making it perilous for ill-prepared explorers to wander without ample water and shade.

Fire Scar Shrine. Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep. Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders.

Fire Taboo. Fire Taboo is a task assigned by Rethiel the Greenwarden along the marshy roads of the Wetlands. Tormented by the suffering of the local forest, the bog beast sends travelers to strip the Mosshide gnolls of the crude flints they use to ignite and burn living wood. By depriving the gnolls of fire, Rethiel hopes to spare the bog's ancient boughs from being consumed. Rethiel the Greenwarden watches over the wilds of the Wetlands, maintaining a profound spiritual kinship with the trees of the marsh. While the natural cycle of rot and renewal belongs in a swamp, the deliberate destruction of the timber cuts deep into Rethiel's spirit. To a living spirit of the marsh, hearing the groans of living boughs chopped down and cast into hearthfires is an agony Rethiel can no longer endure in silence.

Fire Tar. Fire Tar is a volatile substance gathered by Razormane quilboar spellcasters across the eastern Barrens. To Horde shamans, it serves as a crucial ritual component used to brew the Fire Sapta, which grants spiritual communion with the element of fire. Carried almost exclusively by spellcasting Razormane quilboar—including their geomancers, mystics, and thornweavers—fire tar is an alchemical substance tuned closely to flame. While the bristled tribes of the Barrens use it for their own harsh magic and rituals, shamanic instructors recognize it as an essential worldly reagent capable of bridging the gap between mortal senses and raw elemental fury.

Firewatch Ridge. Firewatch Ridge is a high volcanic bluff in the northern reaches of Searing Gorge, serving as a primary encampment for the Dark Iron dwarves. Looming directly above the vast excavation known as the Cauldron, the ridge is heavily fortified by dwarven sentries, mechanical golems, and nesting fire spiders. To the northwest, an ominous cave system reveals an entrenched presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Perched above the industrial devastation of the Cauldron, Firewatch Ridge functions as a critical staging ground for the Dark Iron clan's operations in Searing Gorge. Dwarven guards, engineers, and molten golem creations patrol the crags, fiercely defending their foothold alongside venomous flame spiders native to the smoldering rocks. Its elevation provides the Dark Irons an unobstructed view of the surrounding ash plains, ensuring early warning against rival incursions from Ironforge or the Thorium Brotherhood.

First Mate Fitzsimmons. First Mate Fitzsimmons is a ragged, reeking sailor who spends his days drinking outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Once the first mate aboard the Wave Mistress of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, he is the sole known living survivor of the fleet's destruction during the Second War. Haunted by the tragedy, he seeks willing adventurers to face the restless spirits of his drowned comrades. Lounging outside the Deepwater Tavern amid the damp salt air of Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons is an easy man to overlook—or avoid entirely, given his unwashed stench. To most patrons, he is just another broken old salt drinking his memories away. Yet those willing to sit and listen will hear harrowing tales of a proud fleet brought low by fire and claw.

First War. The First War was the devastating five-year conflict in which the Orcish Horde emerged through the Dark Portal and completely destroyed the human Kingdom of Stormwind. Orchestrated behind the scenes by the demon-possessed Guardian Medivh and the warlock Gul'dan, it concluded with the assassination of King Llane Wrynn I and the flight of human survivors north to Lordaeron. Before the war, the Kingdom of Stormwind enjoyed long years of peace following the Gnoll War, guarded by its Knights and the Clerics of Northshire Abbey. That stability shattered when the Guardian Medivh, secretly possessed by the demon lord Sargeras, contacted the orc warlock Gul'dan on Draenor. Together, they forged the Dark Portal in the swampy Black Morass. Driven by demon blood and the slow death of their homeworld, the Orcish Horde crossed into Azeroth in force. Early rumors dismissed the invaders as vengeful spirits or strange offshoots of trolls, but Sir Anduin Lothar's scouting patrols quickly confirmed the arrival of a disciplined, bloodthirsty army.

Fish in a Bucket. Jinar'Zillen of Shadowprey Village in Desolace likes to do as little as possible. Many shellfish traps sit below the village docks, and anyone who gathers the shellfish from them will be repaid with something worth having. Jinar'Zillen keeps many shellfish traps below the docks of Shadowprey Village, and would far rather someone else did the collecting. Anyone willing to take on that work is promised something they want in return: one fine Bloodbelly fish for every five shellfish brought in.

Fishin' Time. At Stormwind harbor, Gilbert Gray's bait runs low as the fish begin to bite. He asks passersby to fetch supplies from a shop along the city's canals. Gilbert Gray spends quiet days fishing at the edge of Stormwind harbor. He watches his bobber on the water, but a good run of biting fish can empty his bait tin. With his supplies gone and the fish still biting, the elderly angler asks passersby to bring him more.

text.enUS: Five Signets for War Supplies. Field Marshal Snowfall in Ironforge oversees the collection of provisions and equipment for the Grand Alliance's war effort. Champions contributing to the stockpiles can barter their commendation signets directly for field rations, bandages, and critical combat supplies. It ensures that those working tirelessly on the home front remain equipped for the coming conflicts. The massive staging of armies requires more than just raw courage; it demands a relentless logistical pipeline. Field Marshal Snowfall acts as one of the Alliance's primary quartermasters in Ironforge, organizing the flow of materials destined for active fronts. When couriers and heroes bring in commendation signets earned through civic service, Snowfall offers survival rations and tactical materiel in direct exchange.

text.enUS: Five Signets for War Supplies. Five Signets for War Supplies is a logistical exchange coordinated by Warlord Gorchuk in Orgrimmar. By turning in commendation signets earned during the Horde's massive military mobilization, champions receive personal supplies to keep them equipped for the coming conflict. Across Kalimdor, the Horde is marshaling vast quantities of raw goods, munitions, and provisions for a massive campaign. While ordinary gatherers and tradesfolk haul crates of bandages, metals, and herbs into the city centers, military overseers issue commendation signets to honor their service. These tokens signify direct contribution to the grand stockpile accumulating in Orgrimmar's central avenues.

Fizzle Brassbolts. Fizzle Brassbolts is a prominent gnomish engineer stationed out on the baked salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Alongside his rival, the goblin Pozzik, Fizzle co-founded the raceway to pit gnomish precision engineering against reckless goblin ingenuity in high-speed rocket car races. He constantly seeks parts, fuel, and strange desert reagents to keep his racing team running. Out in the shimmering heat of the Shimmering Flats, political alliances and ancient grudges yield to the roar of motorized engines. Fizzle Brassbolts arrived here with one goal in mind: proving once and for all that gnomish craftsmanship is vastly superior to crude goblin tinkering. Together with his goblin counterpart Pozzik, he helped lay out the Mirage Raceway, bringing race cars, pit crews, and spectators to an otherwise desolate basin.

Fizzle's Claw. Fizzle's Claw is the severed hand of the goblin warlock Fizzle Darkstorm. Taken from his encampment in Thunder Ridge, it serves as physical proof to the Horde commanders in Razor Hill that a dangerous Burning Blade conspirator has been slain. Orgnil Soulscar, tasked with uprooting shadow cults threatening the orcish homeland, identified Fizzle Darkstorm as an instigator spreading corruption in Thunder Ridge. Demand for Fizzle's claw was not merely out of savagery, but practical necessity: the Horde requires indisputable evidence when a covert warlock operating under the banner of the Burning Blade is eliminated.

Flagongut's Fossil. Flagongut's Fossil is an ancient specimen recovered from the dig sites of the Wetlands. Entrusted to the dwarven Explorers' League, it holds latent secrets that Archaeologist Flagongut seeks to decipher using a mysterious relic known as the Stone of Relu. Unearthed as part of the dwarven expeditions across Khaz Modan, this ancient fossil represents more than just petrified stone. Archaeologist Flagongut believes it holds forgotten powers tied to the deep antiquity of the world, comparable to artifacts found across the sea in Darkshore. For safekeeping during regional studies, the fossil was held by Prospector Whelgar at his excavation site in the southern hills of the Wetlands.

Flame Crest. Flame Crest is a rugged neutral outpost perched atop a rocky ledge overlooking the volcanic wastes of the Burning Steppes. Accessed only across a crude span, this precarious encampment serves as a forward staging ground against the Dark Horde entrenched in Blackrock Mountain. It provides essential aerial connections and a haven for scouts, beast collectors, and strategists. Situated high on an isolated stone outcropping, Flame Crest commands a watchful view over the scorched ash and lava plains of the Burning Steppes. Reached only by crossing a narrow, rickety wooden bridge, the outpost is naturally defensible against the prowling beasts and roaming orc warbands of the wastes. Wind riders roost along the heights, connecting the camp back across the Redridge range to Kargath, Stonard, Thorium Point, and Rog'mar in the Riverglades.

name.esES: Fémur de puma de las estepas
name.frFR: Fémur de puma des basses plaines

text.enUS: Flatland Cougar Femur. A Flatland Cougar Femur is a dense thigh bone taken from the predatory cougars that prowl the golden grasses of Mulgore. It serves as a vital component in a traditional tauren folk remedy used to counter lethal, venomous infections. The flatland cougar is one of Mulgore's most dangerous native stalkers, blending seamlessly with the dry brush until it springs upon unsuspecting prey. While hunters often harvest cougar pelts and claws for leatherworking and trophies, their heavy marrow-rich bones possess practical value in regional medicine. When Maur Raincaller, a tauren of Bloodhoof Village, suffered a venomous wound from the monstrous pink strider Mazzranache, he urgently requested a cougar femur alongside parts from other local beasts. The bone is crushed or boiled to extract its potent properties, forming an antitoxin poultice capable of drawing fever and necrotic venom out of a festering bite.

name.esES: Garra de merodeador de las estepas
name.frFR: Griffe de Rôdeur des basses plaines

text.enUS: Flatland Prowler Claw. A Flatland Prowler Claw is taken from the dangerous feline predators that stalk the grassy plains of Mulgore. For aspiring hunters, gathering these claws serves as a traditional rite of passage, demonstrating cunning and martial resolve to the elders of Thunder Bluff. Flatland prowlers are among the most cunning and territorial predators roaming the wind-swept plains of Mulgore. Quick on their feet and adept at ambushing prey in the tall grass, they present a genuine threat to travelers and a worthy test for young hunters. Collecting their sharp claws is not merely a task of survival, but a recognized tradition. Skorn Whitecloud advises promising wanderers to harvest these trophies to present to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise, proving they possess the resolve and fieldcraft necessary to pursue the hunter's way.

name.esES: La piedra de energía con imperfecciones

text.enUS: Flawed Power Stone. Deep within the arid expanse of the Barrens, mysterious stones infused with arcane energy rest atop arcane tables. Intentionally fashioned with fatal defects, these volatile relics consume their own power rapidly once separated from their source. The flawed power stones found scattered in the Barrens are curious magical anomalies. While undeniably charged with arcane essence, their structure was intentionally compromised during their creation. Whatever hands shaped them ensured that they would remain deeply unstable, decaying into inert matter mere moments after being handled.

name.ptBR: Mestre de Frota Chifre do Mar

text.enUS: Fleet Master Seahorn. Fleet Master Seahorn is a seasoned tauren mariner who serves as the naval commander of the Blackwater Raiders in Booty Bay. Stationed on the upper balcony of the Salty Sailor Tavern alongside Baron Revilgaz, he oversees the goblin port's maritime defenses. His primary duty is protecting the harbor from the looming threat posed by their sworn enemies, the Bloodsail Buccaneers. While tauren are renowned across Kalimdor as plains-dwellers, Fleet Master Seahorn chose a vastly different life upon the ocean. Clad in pirate regalia, he commands the fleet of the Blackwater Raiders, the private naval arm of the Steamwheedle Cartel's operation in Stranglethorn Vale. Stationed atop the Salty Sailor Tavern, Seahorn works shoulder-to-shoulder with Baron Revilgaz, coordinating shipping routes, crew deployments, and coastal defenses for the lawless yet strictly managed port of Booty Bay.

text.enUS: Flexing for Nougat. During autumn's Hallow's End, you gather festive sweets for an orphan in Stormwind. Innkeeper Allison at the Gilded Rose asks you to flex before she gives you Stormwind Nougat. Hallow's End brings a lighter mood to Stormwind's streets. The holiday marks the turning of the seasons and wards off dark spirits. Common folk celebrate with disguises, revelry, and trick-or-treating. Alliance innkeepers join in, offering traditional sweets to those who perform a harmless trick.
