Initiates are sent into the field to locate and mend the wounds of an injured grunt standing vigil against Kul Tiras survivors. Completing the task earns a priest their first ceremonial vestments and formal recognition among the Horde's spiritual practitioners. In the arid scrub south of Razor Hill, the Horde faces relentless skirmishes against remnants of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's forces. Rather than sending prospective priests into abstract rituals, the troll trainer Tai'jin tests their discipline in real combat triage. Initiates are charged with seeking out Grunt Kor'ja, a warrior critically injured while repelling human infiltrators, to tend her injuries and bolster her constitution before she succumbs.

Garments of the Light. At Goldshire, Garments of the Light mark a novice priest’s first trial under Priestess Josetta. She sends you east to Crystal Lake to tend the wounded Guard Roberts. The work tests your healing and earns you vestments recognized by the Church of the Holy Light. Priestess Josetta teaches acolytes who come to Goldshire from Northshire Abbey. Before the Church of the Holy Light formally recognizes a novice, she tests their skill with divine power. When Guard Roberts is reported wounded by the lake east of Goldshire, Josetta sends you to care for him. His need gives you a chance to prove your healing in practice.

Garments of the Light. Garments of the Light is an early rite of passage for fledgling dwarven priests in Dun Morogh. Directed by Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol in Kharanos, the initiate is tasked with aiding a wounded mountaineer just outside town to earn their vestments. Traditionally, acolytes of the Holy Light undergo formal trials to prove they are worthy of wearing church vestments. In Kharanos, however, priest trainer Maxan Anvol favors practical results over ceremony. With local patrols hard-pressed against troggs and wild beasts, theoretical exams take a back seat when actual defenders lie bleeding in the snow.

Garments of the Moon. Garments of the Moon is an introductory rite of service for young night elf priests in Dolanaar. Assigned by priest trainer Laurna Morninglight, it tasks an initiate with tending to Sentinel Shaya, a wounded defender patrolling the woods south of the settlement. Fulfilling this duty marks an initiate's formal recognition within the Sisterhood of Elune. Within the boughs of Teldrassil, the Sisterhood of Elune tends both to the spiritual life of the kaldorei and the practical defense of their borders. When Sentinel Shaya is wounded while patrolling the dangerous wilderness south of Dolanaar, priest trainer Laurna Morninglight cannot abandon her post to render aid. Instead, she charges a newly trained initiate with proving their devotion by mending Shaya's wounds and bolstering her constitution with protective magic.

Garren's Haunt. Garren's Haunt is an abandoned farmstead nestled in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a prosperous human homestead, the farm fell to ruin when the Scourge wiped out the Garren family, leaving the overgrown grounds overrun by feral Rot Hide gnolls. Before the Third War, this farmstead supported a family and produced bountiful harvests under the Kingdom of Lordaeron. When the Plague of Undeath swept across the countryside, the Scourge descended upon the farm and slaughtered Garren and his kin. Today, the fields lie gray and withered, the farmhouse and barn decaying under the perpetual gloom of Tirisfal.

Garrick's Head. At Northshire's vineyards, Garrick Padfoot's severed head proves the cutthroat is dead. The authorities at Northshire Abbey require it to pay the bounty. Garrick Padfoot and his gang harassed Northshire Valley's farmers and merchants for weeks. With Stormwind's defenses stretched thin, Garrick made his hideout in a shack near the vineyards and raided passing trade. Local guards were occupied by kobolds and Defias bandits, so Deputy Willem offered a bounty for the outlaw's death. He sought someone willing to kill Garrick and bring back proof.

Garrison Armory. The Garrison Armory is an Alliance mining operation carved into the hills southwest of Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands. Miners and engineers work the underground veins to harvest valuable minerals, sustaining the lonely fortress and shipping raw wealth back to Stormwind. It forms a crucial industrial lifeline in an otherwise blasted, barren wilderness. Maintaining a permanent military garrison in the arid wastes of the Blasted Lands requires constant supply, and Nethergarde Keep cannot rely purely on long supply trains from Stormwind. The Garrison Armory serves as the keep's primary industrial excavation. Nethergarde miners, overseen by foremen and assisted by engineers, work these subterranean shafts to pull valuable minerals from the earth. The ore extracted here is utilized directly by Nethergarde's smiths and fortifications or hauled back to the capital in exchange for the foodstuffs, tools, and provisions the fortress needs to maintain its vigil over the Dark Portal.

Gart Mistrunner. Gart Mistrunner is the resident druid trainer stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa. He welcomes novice tauren called by the Earth Mother and guides them through their first rites of nature magic. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Gart Mistrunner represents the ancient druidic path rekindled among the Shu'halo. New tauren druids are directed straight to Gart upon taking their first steps on the Red Cloud Mesa, often carrying a verdant note commending them into his care. Through his patient guidance, young practitioners learn to commune with the natural world, drawing upon the restorative powers of nature and the lunar radiance of Mu'sha to heal their allies and strike down threats to the land.

Gatehouse Goods. Gatehouse Goods is a local Stormwind task involving the transport of a shipment up the stairs within Trias' Cheese. Because the cheese shop shares a floor with the adjacent gatehouse, goods can be quietly dropped outside the stockroom door for guards to collect. The arrangement highlights the tight, interconnected urban design of Stormwind's commercial and defensive quarters. Gatehouse Goods entails a straightforward delivery task nestled within the bustling streets of Stormwind. The job requires carrying a gatehouse shipment up the interior stairs of Trias' Cheese. While the famed cheese shop is an entirely distinct business with its own separate inventory, its physical structure shares a floor with the neighboring gatehouse facilities. This architectural quirk makes the shop's upper landing a practical passage for moving supplies between neighboring quarters without disturbing the front avenues.

Gates of Ironforge. The Gates of Ironforge serve as the monumental main entrance leading travelers from the snowy mountain vales of Dun Morogh into the dwarven capital. Carved directly into the sheer stone face of the mountain, they are guarded inside by a colossal statue of High King Modimus Anvilmar. Approached by climbing the winding, fortified ramp ascending from central Dun Morogh, the Gates of Ironforge present an imposing facade visible across much of the snowy lowlands. Beyond the massive portal, visitors enter the city proper, greeted immediately by an enormous stone statue honoring High King Modimus Anvilmar—the legendary ruler who united the dwarven clans before the War of the Three Hammers. Passing through these gates leads directly into the bustling commercial district of the Commons.

Gates of Orgrimmar. The Gates of Orgrimmar form the imposing southern threshold of the Horde capital, carved directly into the red rock of northern Durotar. Flanked by heavy timber and iron battlements, this grand entryway connects the arid wastes outside to the busy commons of the Valley of Strength. It stands as a physical declaration of orcish endurance and martial strength. Framed by towering wooden palisades, massive iron spikes, and fortified watchtowers, the main gate guards the primary chasm cutting into the mountains sheltering Orgrimmar. For travelers approaching from Razor Hill and the scrublands of Durotar, the entrance serves as both a welcoming monument and a stark deterrent to any who would threaten the new Horde. Heavily armed Orgrimmar Grunts patrol the approach, keeping vigilant watch over all traffic entering the city.

Gath'Ilzogg. Gath'Ilzogg is the fearsome Blackrock orc warlord who commands the invasion force occupying Stonewatch Keep in the Redridge Mountains. Under his brutal leadership, the orcs seized the fortress and launched devastating raids against the town of Lakeshire, earning him an urgent bounty from the town's desperate magistrate. Gath'Ilzogg marched north out of the Burning Steppes under orders to secure Redridge for the Blackrock clan. Aided by the foul sorcery of the renegade human warlock Morganth, Gath'Ilzogg's warband battered the defenders of Stonewatch Keep and seized the high ground overlooking the entire region. From this entrenched redoubt, he oversees aggressive raids into the valleys and down toward the bridge of Lakeshire, steadily suffocating the human settlement. He rarely fights alone, keeping elite Blackrock guards and a vicious black dragon whelp named Singe close at hand.

Gather Rot Blossoms. Tavernkeep Smitts of Darkshire requires rot blossoms to concoct a batch of his infamous 'zombie juice'. These macabre flora sprout directly from the decaying skulls of skeletal horrors and fiends prowling Duskwood's restless graveyards. While most barkeeps pride themselves on aged ales and fine wines, Tavernkeep Smitts of the Scarlet Raven Tavern occasionally brews more unsettling fare. His recipe for 'zombie juice' demands rot blossoms—foul, necrotic vegetation that takes root within the empty skulls of animated skeletons. Smitts himself is sensible enough never to get close to the undead, leaving the gruesome harvest to passing mercenaries.

Gathering Leather. Gathering Leather is a straightforward trade request offered by Veren Tallstrider on the rises of Thunder Bluff. To sustain the capital and test young hunters, Veren exchanges a bundle of cured light leather skins for crafted goods. It highlights the deeply ingrained tauren tradition of turning the fruits of the plains hunt into essential clothing and armor. In the newly settled capital atop the high mesas of Mulgore, craftsmanship and survival walk hand in hand. Veren Tallstrider works skins into clothing and protective armor needed by the growing population of Thunder Bluff. Rather than harvesting everything himself, he encourages young adventurers heading out into the plains to bring back their quarry, turning mundane hunting into honorable civic service.

Gathering Materials. Gathering Materials is a rite of passage for aspiring Horde mages training in the Undercity. Assigned by Anastasia Hartwell, the task sends apprentices into Silverpine Forest to claim arcane gems from the wizards of Dalaran, assembling the components needed to weave their first true mage's robes. Within the arcane cloisters of the Magic Quarter, novice mages must prove their mastery over more than just raw incantations. To earn their first true robes—a formal mantle marking their station and personal worth—initiates are directed by Anastasia Hartwell to harvest the raw components required for enchanted weave: a bolt of simple linen and a set of potent Dalaran mana gems.

Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is an essential trial for young night elf druids learning to master nature's healing powers in Darkshore. Guided by Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine, the druid collects vital natural reagents to brew a restorative salve for the region's ailing wildlife. This task lays the practical foundation for understanding how herbal remedies combat venom and disease. Following the discovery of a contaminated water source plaguing the local wildlife, Alanndarian Nightsong in Auberdine sets out to concoct an effective curative salve. While the sampled Cliffspring water forms the base of the mixture, genuine healing requires potent natural catalysts. The afflicted forest deer cannot recover on their own, making the gathering of wholesome remedies a matter of urgency for the Cenarion Circle.

Gathering the Cure. Gathering the Cure is a sacred rite of passage for young tauren druids stationed at the Crossroads. Tasked by Tonga Runetotem, the druid gathers earthroot and sturdy kodo horns to craft a curative salve for the poisoned gazelles of the Barrens. Having secured a sample of water from Dreadmist Peak, Tonga Runetotem requires raw reagents to brew an effective physical antidote. While natural water provides the salve's base, common earthroot provides foundational medicinal qualities, and ground kodo horn gives the mixture the restorative potency needed to shock venom out of a creature's system. For a young druid, obtaining these ingredients means relying on the gifts of the earth and culling local beasts.

Gaxim Rustfizzle. Gaxim Rustfizzle is an ambitious gnome scholar and tinker stationed at a small Alliance camp along the Webwinder Path in Stonetalon Mountains. A representative of the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he seeks to prove to skeptical night elves that advanced artifice and alchemy can preserve their woodland realm. His scientific curiosity is matched by a fierce vendetta against the destructive operations of the Venture Company. While night elves traditionally rely on ancient druidism and nature magic, Gaxim Rustfizzle arrived in the craggy passes of Stonetalon to demonstrate a radically different perspective. Representing the Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy and Engineering Sciences, he genuinely believes that calculated mechanisms and chemical solutions can defend and restore Kalimdor's wilderness just as effectively as prayers to Elune. Camped alongside the sentinel Kaela Shadowspear on the Webwinder Path, he works tirelessly to convince his tall, reclusive allies of engineering's ecological merits.

Gazin Tenorm. In Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Gazin Tenorm keeps watch near the altar after a dangerous scouting mission in Elwynn Forest. Gazin Tenorm stays in the Cathedral of Light, though his thoughts remain in Elwynn Forest. He and his close friend Henze Faulk went into the woods to gather proof of the Defias Brotherhood's movements for the royal court. Defias forces ambushed them. Gazin escaped to Stormwind, but Henze was left in mortal danger. Now Gazin seeks a hero of the Light to help his companion.

Gazlowe's Ledger. Gazlowe's Ledger is a detailed record of trade goods and inventories kept by the goblin boss of Ratchet. It serves as an accounting book to cross-check cargo shipments arriving from Booty Bay against the harbor manifest. Overseeing a bustling trade port like Ratchet requires meticulous accounting. Gazlowe maintains this personal ledger to track imported crates, outbound cargo, and warehouse stores. When a long-awaited shipment from Booty Bay goes unaccounted for, Gazlowe uses the book to cross-reference his projected inventory against the maritime records kept down at the docks by Wharfmaster Dizzywig.

Gazrog. Gazrog is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the heart of the Barrens. Tasked with maintaining logistics and security along the savannah's perilous roads, he recruits able Horde travelers to deal with regional threats and investigate lost patrols. The Crossroads serves as the vital junction for all Horde transit through Kalimdor, but its isolation leaves supply lines vulnerable to marauders and beasts alike. Gazrog stands watch alongside the settlement's defenders, working to ensure that cargo, coin, and couriers reach their destinations. Maintaining order in a sprawling wilderness requires constant vigilance, and Gazrog relies heavily on passing adventurers to handle crises brewing beyond the outpost's stockades.

Gearing Redridge. Gearing Redridge is an Alliance blacksmithing trade quest offered by Tormus Deepforge in Ironforge. Aspiring smiths forge sturdy copper equipment to relieve Lakeshire's besieged garrison and aid resident smith Verner Osgood in defending the region from hostile orcs and gnolls. While Ironforge’s Great Forge rarely sleeps, dwarven smiths recognize that the Alliance's frontline struggles stretch far beyond Dun Morogh. Down in the Redridge Mountains, the human settlement of Lakeshire finds itself constantly embattled, suffering routine incursions from Blackrock orcs marching out of Stonewatch Keep and roving packs of gnolls infesting the northern ridges. With royal reinforcements from Stormwind slow to arrive, local supplies stay dangerously depleted.

Gelbin Mekkatorque. Gelbin Mekkatorque is the High Tinker of the gnomes, currently residing in exile in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned as a visionary engineer whose inventions include the mechanostrider and the Deeprun Tram, he now carries the heavy burden of Gnomeregan's fall and oversees efforts to reclaim his people's ancestral home. Gnomish leadership is earned through intellect and merit rather than bloodlines, and Gelbin Mekkatorque's rise to High Tinker was propelled by pure inventive genius. Mekkatorque revolutionized personal transportation with the creation of the first functioning mechanostrider. He also assisted the Bronzebeard dwarves in developing their formidable siege engines, and he was instrumental in the creation of the subterranean Deeprun Tram linking Ironforge to Stormwind.

Gelihast. Gelihast is a ferocious, twin-blade wielding murloc chieftain residing in the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps. Surrounded by his Blindlight murlocs, he guards a strange altar in the flooded ruins of the sunken temple. While most murlocs stay near coastal shallows, Gelihast has claimed a lair deep in the sunken temple of Blackfathom Deeps beneath the Zoram Strand. Wielding twin swords with blinding speed, he cuts down intruders before they can react, and casters who stray into his reach rarely survive.

Gelkak Gyromast. Gelkak Gyromast is a gnome who talks like a pirate captain, found stranded along the foggy shoreline of Mist's Edge in northern Darkshore. His ship was sunk offshore by threshadons, and he wants his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, back in working order. Perched on the desolate northern coast of Darkshore just west of the ancient Ruins of Mathystra, Gelkak Gyromast represents a peculiar sight among the gloomy night elven shores. Talking like an old sea dog, the self-styled captain lost his ship to the threshadons just offshore. When he washed up on the misty sands, the key to his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100, broke on the rocks, and its pieces were carried off by the crawlers, foreststriders and murlocs rummaging through the wreckage.

Gelkis Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Gelkis means killing their worst enemy, the Magram, then meeting Uthek the Wise, a shaman of the Gelkis, on the edge of Gelkis Village in the southwest of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Gelkis and you kill the Magram, whom the Gelkis hate most, to win their respect.

Gelkis Village. Gelkis Village is the primary stronghold of the earth-aligned Gelkis centaur clan in southwestern Desolace. Built around a rugged ravine connected by wooden spans and cliffside paths, the settlement guards the southern route toward Feralas. Its vantage directly overlooks the main north-south road, making it a perilous crossing for any traveler who has not earned the clan's favor. Gelkis Village sits in a deep, craggy gorge framed by precarious bluffs and rope bridges. Unlike the nomadic raiders of the Barrens, the Gelkis have fortified their ancestral grounds into a permanent settlement, complete with outposts spreading toward the border of Feralas. The heart of the clan's leadership lies within Bolgan's Hole, a cavern carved into the southern cliff face where Khan Shaka oversees his warriors. Travelers trekking south through Desolace must either cut a bloody path through the gorge or tread carefully, as the Gelkis view uninvited wanderers as fair game in their eternal war against their rival centaur brethren.

Gem of Anacondra. The Gem of Anacondra is one of four dream gems held by the corrupted serpent leaders within the Wailing Caverns. Carried by Lady Anacondra, it serves as tangible proof of her defeat and the curbing of the Nightmare's spread over the Barrens. When Naralex entered his deep slumber to bring water and life back to the arid Barrens, the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts and warped his closest disciples. Lady Anacondra and her fellow conspirators abandoned their traditional ways to become the Druids of the Fang, twisting their noble restorative purpose into a toxic delusion. The Gem of Anacondra is one of the four dream gems carried by these serpentine leaders, focusing their corrupted bond with the Emerald Dream and anchoring the nightmare within the cave system.

Gem of Cobrahn. The Gem of Cobrahn is a dream gem carried by Lord Cobrahn, one of the corrupt leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. It serves as both a focus of his corrupted reverie and physical proof needed by Nara Wildmane to confirm his defeat. When the night elf druid Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the barren plains of Kalimdor, his nightmare twisted both the Wailing Caverns and his disciples. Among them was Cobrahn, who abandoned the peaceful ways of the Cenarion Circle to take the shape of the serpent. Lord Cobrahn carries one of the four dream gems that anchor the leaders' hold over the subterranean waterways, using it to channel the twisted dreams that threaten to transform the Barrens into a venomous marsh.

Gem of Pythas. The Gem of Pythas is one of four corrupted dream gems carried by the leaders of the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Held by Lord Pythas, it fuels the nightmare twisting the subterranean oasis and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex entered the Emerald Dream to restore the arid Barrens, his noble vision was twisted into a living nightmare. His foremost followers fell with him, styling themselves the Druids of the Fang and seeking to remake the surface world into a venomous jungle. Lord Pythas carries this resonant stone, one of four dream gems anchoring the corruption within the caverns. The gem serves as a conduit of their dark design and proof to the druids of Thunder Bluff that Pythas's twisted trance has finally been broken.

Gem of Serpentis. The Gem of Serpentis is a dream gem carried by Lord Serpentis, one of the four leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. It acts as a focal conduit for the twisted nightmare reshaping the cave network and threatening the Barrens. When Naralex's slumber inside the Wailing Caverns succumbed to the Emerald Nightmare, his most devoted followers were warped into the fanatical Druids of the Fang. Lord Serpentis is one of the cabal's four leaders. Like the other three, Serpentis carries an enchanted dream gem that anchors their collective will to the corrupted vision. Recovering this gem breaks Serpentis's hold over the cavern's ecosystem, striking directly at the leadership directing the corruption spreading across the Barrens.

General Marcus Jonathan. General Marcus Jonathan is the High Commander of Stormwind Defense, stationed directly at the gates in the Valley of Heroes. A veteran of the Second War, he oversees the garrison protecting the capital and manages military requests from the kingdom's frontier settlements. Mounted atop his steed in the Valley of Heroes, General Marcus Jonathan stands as the first line of defense and the highest-ranking military officer overseeing the city gates. He fought in the Second War alongside renowned soldiers like Reginald Windsor under the command of General Turalyon. In this era of rising tension, Jonathan must balance the immediate security of the capital with the increasingly desperate calls for aid from frontier towns like Lakeshire.

Gerard Tiller. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works under the warm sun and longs for spring water. He offers a shiny red apple to any traveler who brings him a skin of it. Gerard Tiller works the grounds outside the barn at the Maclure Vineyards, south of Goldshire. The vineyard is known for its grapes, and keeping the harvest going takes hard labor. The chores leave Gerard thirsty, so he welcomes travelers who bring him a skin of fresh spring water. In return, he gives them shiny red apples gathered from local orchards.

Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. This bounty tasks adventurers with eliminating Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, a rogue gnome overseer perched high above Cragpool Lake in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gerenzo has heavily augmented his decaying flesh with gears, clockwork machinery, and artificial limbs. The goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks seeks his mechanical arm as indisputable proof of his demise to earn a coveted promotion from his superiors. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle is infamous even among veteran tinkerers for his gruesome physical transformations. By the account of those who have seen him, his natural flesh appears to be rotting away, patched over by grafted gears, iron plating, and whirring clockwork prosthetics. Perched near the massive water wheel perched high above Cragpool Lake, the gnome watches over operations with mechanical precision and an unsettling disregard for his own mortal biology.

Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm. Gerenzo's Mechanical Arm is the grafted prosthetic limb taken from the rogue engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle in the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as unmistakable proof of his demise for goblin operatives seeking to clear out competition. Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle took self-modification to a grotesque extreme, grafting whirring gears and metal directly onto his failing body. Perched above Cragpool Lake, the renegade gnome replaced natural limbs with intricate machinery. When the goblin tinker Ziz Fizziks seeks Gerenzo's elimination to impress his superiors, this distinctive mechanical arm is the only trophy unique enough to serve as indisputable evidence of the engineer's death.

Gerenzo's Orders. At the Venture Company dig site in Stonetalon Mountains, an ousted goblin named Piznik schemes to expose his new boss, Gerenzo. By defending Piznik from camp patrols while he extracts a strange gold-green ore, adventurers help uncover the lucrative secrets behind the company's aggressive excavation. The Venture Company's massive operations within Stonetalon rely on cutthroat competition, where promotions are won through ruthlessness rather than loyalty. Piznik once enjoyed the status of being second-in-command at the excavation until Gerenzo seized power, ousted supervisor Ziz Fizziks, and demoted Piznik to swinging a pick in the dirt. Rather than walking away, Piznik stayed on as an informant under Ziz's instructions, watching Gerenzo's every move and biding his time to strike back at his treacherous new supervisor.

Gerenzo's Orders. Having fought off the dig site's patrols and secured a sample of the strange ore Gerenzo ordered mined, Piznik dispatches adventurers to take the specimen to his contact, Ziz Fizziks. The delivery wraps up a risky act of corporate espionage deep in the Venture Company operations of Windshear Crag. With his cover blown by the fight at the dig site, Piznik knows his time among the Venture Company crew at Windshear Crag has expired. Corporate management in Undermine does not take kindly to internal sabotage, prompting the nervous goblin to orchestrate his escape. Before slipping away to seek a new employer, he entrusts the Unidentified Ore mined under Gerenzo's orders to an outsider, ensuring the prized specimen gets delivered safely without drawing suspicion to himself.

Gerrig Bonegrip. Gerrig Bonegrip is an unassuming dwarven shopkeeper tucked away in the shadowy corridors of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern. Behind the counter of Bonegrip's Runes and Dooms, he quietly buys and sells esoteric texts concerning dark rituals and forgotten ancient powers.

Gershala Nightwhisper. Gershala Nightwhisper is a night elf researcher residing in the coastal settlement of Auberdine in Darkshore. Driven by grave concern over the path taken by the high elves of Quel'Thalas, he studies specimens of cursed aquatic and demonic creatures to understand how magical corruption warps both mind and body. Stationed peacefully within Auberdine, Gershala Nightwhisper looks beyond the immediate coastal troubles of Darkshore toward a broader, creeping danger. Watching with dismay as the remaining high elves embrace perilous arcane practices and dub themselves blood elves, Gershala seeks to understand the biological and spiritual descent that follows unchecked magic. To unlock these secrets, he directs seasoned Alliance adventurers into the submerged halls of Blackfathom Deeps to harvest corrupted brain stems from the naga and satyr who dwell within.

Get Me Out of Here!. Melizza Brimbuzzle traveled into the Valley of Spears hoping to do business with the Maraudines, but they would not talk, and she fears they mean to eat her. She asks you to get her out of there; her brother Hornizz will pay you handsomely. Melizza walked into the Valley of Spears to speak with the Maraudines, thinking she could strike a deal. They would not talk, and she suspects they would rather eat her. She says she overheard centaurs only minutes ago discussing wood for their cookpot, and she wants out quickly.

Get the Gnomes Drunk. Kravel Koalbeard wants the Fool's Stout tested on a pit crew at the Mirage Raceway. If you choose the gnomes, you take the stout to the Gnome Pit Boss. The stout will go bad eventually, so Kravel says not to wait too long. Kravel Koalbeard needs the Fool's Stout tried out on one of the pit crews. You may try it on the gnomes: he hands you the stout and sends you with it to the Gnome Pit Boss, who is nearby at the Mirage Raceway. Choosing the gnomes tips the races toward the goblins. Kravel warns you not to dawdle, because the stout will go bad eventually.

Get the Goblins Drunk. Kravel Koalbeard wants the Fool's Stout tested on a pit crew at the Mirage Raceway. If you choose the goblins, you take the stout to the Goblin Pit Boss. The stout will go bad eventually, so Kravel says not to wait too long. Kravel Koalbeard needs the Fool's Stout tried out on one of the pit crews. You may try it on the goblins: he hands you the stout and sends you with it to the Goblin Pit Boss, who is nearby at the Mirage Raceway. Choosing the goblins tips the races toward the gnomes. Kravel warns you not to dawdle, because the stout will go bad eventually.

Get the Scoop. Magus Tirth has locked a crucial spellbook inside his magically sealed strongbox, but he cannot recall the activation phrase to open it. To retrieve the tome, you must locate his missing apprentice somewhere around the Shimmering Flats racetrack and pry the forgotten words from him. Magus Tirth is an eccentric spellcaster dwelling on the cracked salt bed of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. While he possesses the esoteric knowledge and tomes that advancing mages desperately seek, dealing with him requires patience. Tirth relies heavily on an assistant to manage mundane details, including the spoken passwords guarding his arcane repositories. When tasked with retrieving a book of power, visiting practitioners quickly learn that Tirth has locked the volume away behind magic words that have slipped his mind entirely.

Ghamoo-ra. Ghamoo-ra is an ancient, giant sea turtle inhabiting the Pool of Ask'ar within Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken temple of Elune now overrun by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Armored in a massive shell, he savagely tramples any intruders who approach his island. Blackfathom Deeps was once a night elven temple dedicated to Elune, now flooded and claimed by naga, satyr and the nihilistic Twilight's Hammer cult. Ghamoo-ra dwells among its drowned ruins, an enormous turtle whose thick shell turns aside all but the most determined blows.

Ghost Hair Comb. The Ghost Hair Comb is an eerie grooming tool entangled with the spectral strands of the spirit Blind Mary. Sent to the ghost by Madame Eva, the comb becomes an instrument of tragic realization before its gathered hair is spun into uncanny thread. Madame Eva of Darkshire sends the comb to the haunted spirit Blind Mary, who resides in a lonely dilapidated dwelling on the outskirts of Duskwood. When presented with the comb, the ghost recoils in sheer horror, suddenly confronted with the harrowing reality that she is no longer the lovely living woman she once was. In her grief and distress, Mary thrusts the comb away, leaving it tangled with strands of her own ghostly hair.

Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is a rare, supernatural material spun by Madame Eva in Darkshire. Infused with potent occult properties, it is said to bind spiritual energies and even sew life into inanimate things. The hermit Abercrombie requests it to ward his dilapidated shack against restless ghosts. Spun by the fortune teller Madame Eva in Darkshire, Ghost Hair Thread is far more than an ordinary tailoring supply. According to Eva, the spectral thread possesses versatile occult properties, ranging from binding malevolent spirits to stitching vitality into inanimate objects. Its ethereal nature makes it a valuable asset for rituals and wards in the cursed realm of Duskwood.

Ghost Hair Thread. Ghost Hair Thread is an errand undertaken for the fortune-teller Madame Eva in Darkshire. In order to gather the ghost hair she needs to spin Ghost Hair Thread, travelers are sent south to seek out Blind Mary, a tormented spirit who dwells in an abandoned farmhouse. By presenting her with an ethereal comb, one can gather the necessary strands from her ghostly tresses. Madame Eva of Darkshire requires specialized, otherworldly materials to spin Ghost Hair Thread for Abercrombie. Standard threads of linen and wool will not suffice for the rituals of Duskwood; instead, she requires ethereal strands harvested directly from a spirit. To secure this macabre component without violence, Eva provides a delicate Spectral Comb capable of passing through the veil of death to gather loose spectral hair.

Ghost Walker Post. Ghost Walker Post is a modest tauren settlement situated in the heart of Desolace right beside the ancient Kodo Graveyard. Far more exposed to regional dangers than Shadowprey Village on the western coast, it serves as a frontline Horde staging ground against centaur clans and the Burning Blade. Perched on the dusty flats of central Desolace, Ghost Walker Post provides the Horde with an austere foothold in a hostile territory. Unlike the sheltered coastal fishing haven of Shadowprey Village, this post directly faces roaming centaur marauders and demon-worshiping cultists of the Burning Blade. Facilities are spartan, offering only the bare essentials for travelers, with no inn or flight master in sight. Despite the harsh conditions, a garrison of tauren and an orcish detachment sent by Warchief Thrall keep vigilant watch over the badlands.

Ghost-o-plasm Round Up. Hornizz Brimbuzzle thinks there is money in the ghosts of the Valley of Bones. He figures the Magram centaurs would pay plenty for ghost energy, and he gives you a crate of ghost magnets to draw the spirits out. Hornizz points you southeast, to the Valley of Bones, where Magram ghosts walk. It sounds frightening, he admits, but surely it is scarier still for the Magram. He is sure that ghost energy captured there would be worth plenty to those centaurs.

Ghoul Fang. Ghoul Fangs are gruesome trophies harvested from the undead prowling the blighted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. In Darkshire, the seer Madame Eva uses them as essential components in crafting defensive talismans for travelers facing the encroaching darkness. The shadowed forest of Duskwood crawls with ravenous undead, from flesh eaters lurking near the graves to rotted corpses roaming the woods. Taking a fang from these monstrous creatures is both grim work and proof of survival against the ravenous dead that threaten Darkshire's borders.

Ghoul Rib. Ghoul Ribs are harvested from the undead prowling the haunted groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. The hermit Abercrombie claims to need them as materials to construct a grotesque effigy to ward off the flesh-eating horrors near his shack. The cursed forest of Duskwood crawls with violent undead, including ravenous ghouls such as Flesh Eaters, Bone Chewers, Brain Eaters, Rotted Ones, and Plague Spreaders. Abercrombie, an eccentric recluse living isolated in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery, requests these sturdy, rotted bones from passing travelers. He claims that living outside the protection of the Night Watch in Darkshire leaves him vulnerable, and that assembling a terrifying effigy from ghoul ribs will serve as a scarecrow to frighten off prowling packs of the dead.

Ghoulish Effigy. Deep in the gloomy wilderness of Duskwood, the eccentric hermit Abercrombie claims his isolated shack is under siege by the walking dead. To protect his home, he tasks passing adventurers with harvesting ghoul ribs to assemble a bizarre protective scarecrow. Abercrombie lives far beyond the guarded boundaries of Darkshire, isolated amidst the shadowed trees of Duskwood. Out here, wandering ghouls like Flesh Eaters and Bone Chewers roam unchecked. Claiming that ravenous corpses recently battered down his walls, the panicked hermit requests the ribs of these horrors to fashion a deterrent, hoping a grisly effigy will keep the hungry dead at bay.

Giant Crocolisk Skin. Giant Crocolisk Skins are thick hides taken from the massive reptiles native to the marshes of the Wetlands. Prized by Menethil Harbor tradesmen for leatherworking, harvesting them is perilous work that has maimed more than one unwary hunter. The bogs and waterways of the Wetlands are home to enormous crocolisks whose hides are dense enough to resist the damp rot of the marshes. In Menethil Harbor, artisans like James Halloran rely on steady shipments of skins to craft rugged leather goods. However, taking a hide from a fully grown giant crocolisk requires braving deep waters and outmatching ferocious swamp predators, making every gathered pelt hard-won.

Gilneas. Gilneas is a secluded human kingdom occupying a rugged, storm-lashed peninsula south of Silverpine Forest. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane severed ties with the outside world and locked his nation behind the colossal Greymane Wall, leaving neighboring territories abandoned and the kingdom shrouded in total isolation. Gilneas was once an assertive maritime powerhouse among the human realms, claiming lineage from the ancient empire of Arathor. King Genn Greymane participated reluctantly in the Second War, believing his kingdom could defend itself without foreign entanglements. Bitter over the loss of Gilnean lives and unwilling to help finance the internment camps for captured orcs, Greymane severed relations with the Alliance of Lordaeron. To permanently shield his realm from outside calamity, he ordered the construction of a massive stone barricade along the kingdom's northern frontier.

Gilnid. Gilnid, known as the Smelter, is the goblin master engineer running the forges in the depths of the Deadmines. He oversees the smelting of raw ore into refined metal and munitions for Edwin VanCleef's hidden ironclad juggernaut. Without his fiery operations, the Defias Brotherhood would lack the heavy cannons needed to assault Stormwind. Deep within the Deadmines, the Defias Brotherhood relies on industrial expertise to forge weapons of war. Gilnid serves as VanCleef's head smelter, commanding a small army of goblin laborers, tinkers, and smiths in the central foundry. Towering over most of his kin, he drives his crew relentlessly through smoke and slag, barking orders and refusing breaks to ensure raw iron ore is processed into heavy plating and lethal ordnance.

Gilshalan Windwalker. Gilshalan Windwalker is a night elf researcher resting at the base of the great tree Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Concerned by the sudden corruption taking root within Teldrassil, he studies the local wildlife to understand the unnatural aggression plaguing the boughs. His investigations into the Webwood spiders provide early clues about the rot afflicting the World Tree. Sitting calmly on the stone steps leading into Aldrassil, Gilshalan Windwalker watches over the tranquil canopy of Shadowglen with growing unease. Teldrassil was planted to restore the night elves' lost sanctuary and harmony with nature, but signs of deep spiritual malaise have emerged almost immediately. Gilshalan dedicates himself to examining how this corruption manifests in the local beasts, beginning with the venomous arachnids that weave their webs nearby.

Gilthares Firebough. Gilthares Firebough is an elven deckhand held captive atop a tower inside Northwatch Hold. Formerly employed by the Thalo'dan Privateers aboard a moonshine transport between Ratchet and Booty Bay, he seeks any opportunity to escape his Theramore captors. While hauling illicit cargo between Ratchet and Booty Bay, Gilthares Firebough saw his ship blasted to splinters by naval forces out of Theramore. As the sole survivor of the assault, the privateer was dragged ashore in chains and locked away in a tower within Northwatch Hold. Though dressed in vivid red and bearing little affection for the Alliance zealots who slaughtered his crew, Gilthares is not picky about who aids his breakout—so long as they can fight their way down from the ramparts.

Give Gerard a Drink. At the Maclure Vineyards, Gerard Tiller works long days in the fields and needs fresh spring water. He trades apples for water brought by passing travelers. Elwynn Forest's farms supply grain, fruit, and vegetables to Stormwind's townsfolk and garrisons. Tending crops under the open sky is hot, demanding work. Gerard Tiller spends long days in the dirt at the Maclure Vineyards, keeping pests away and managing the harvest. With little time to return to town wells, he relies on passing recruits to bring clean spring water so he can keep working.

Gizelton Caravan. Rigger Gizelton and Cork launched their caravan to get rich, and found the trade more dangerous than they expected. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead, and Rigger wants a capable adventurer to guard the caravan past it. Rigger Gizelton and Cork set up the caravan to make a fortune, and had no idea how risky turning a profit could be. Mannoroc Coven lies ahead. The demons usually leave the caravan alone, but this time the kodos are spooked. Rigger offers payment if you protect the caravan past the coven. Once it is safely through, your pay waits with Smeed, a business associate of theirs, at Scrabblescrew's Camp.

Gizmo for Warug. Warug, in the Magram Village, remembers a gnome who once came to Desolace with a cart of strange things. He kept a wooden human from that cart until he broke it, and now he wants a new one: an advanced target dummy. A little gnome once came to Desolace, long ago, with horses and a cart. The cart held curious things: some burned in different colors, others moved though they were not alive. Warug killed the gnome, but first the gnome made him laugh. Warug kept his favorite thing from the cart, a human made of wood that waved at him until he hit it and broke it. Now he wants a new one, an advanced target dummy, and expects it from anyone who is no enemy of the Magram.

Gloom Weed. Gloom Weed is a sickly plant native to the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades, commonly growing in the fields between Deathknell and Brill. It is best known as the wrong plant collected by Gordo, a lumbering Forsaken abomination who confuses it with the alchemy reagent doom weed. Sprouting amid the gloom and decay of Tirisfal Glades, Gloom Weed thrives in the fallow earth west of Brill and east of the Solliden Farmstead. Despite its morbid name, the plant is relatively harmless and lacks the potent alchemical kick prized by the Royal Apothecary Society. Its primary notoriety stems from the abomination Gordo, who wanders the roadway attempting to pull weeds with his massive, clumsy hands. Having misunderstood his master's commands, Gordo constantly gathers Gloom Weed and enlists gullible travelers to carry bunches of it back to Master Holland in the Brill graveyard, much to the apothecary's supreme annoyance.

Glorin Steelbrow. Glorin Steelbrow is a dwarven operative found drinking at the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor. Acting as an associate of Bishop Farthing of Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he helps adventurers investigate the lost Third Fleet and recover sacred relics and materials scattered across the Wetlands coast. His efforts tie the haunted wilderness of Duskwood directly to the sunken shipwrecks of the north. While Bishop Farthing aids the people of Duskwood against its creeping terrors from Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, he maintains ties far to the north in Menethil Harbor. Stationed inside the bustling Deepwater Tavern, Glorin Steelbrow acts as Farthing's eyes and hands on the coast. He offers aid and direction to travelers sent north in search of sacred metals and forgotten relics, providing a crucial bridge between the troubles of the southern forest and the sunken wreckage of the Wetlands.

Glowing Ember. A Glowing Ember is the lingering, elemental core recovered from a defeated Minor Manifestation of Fire atop the crags of Durotar. It serves as a vital ceremonial reagent in a shaman's trials, used to ignite the brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame. When a rising shaman drinks the fire sapta and faces the fiery spirits atop the ridge near Telf Joolam, they confront a Minor Manifestation of Fire. Upon the elemental's defeat, this smoldering remnant is all that remains of its physical form. Still pulsing with raw elemental heat, the ember carries the living spark of fire necessary to awaken the sacred brazier at the Shrine of Eternal Flame.

Glowing Fruit. The Glowing Fruit is an exotic, luminescent specimen found growing amid strange fronds on the boughs of Teldrassil. Its unnatural radiance and bizarre interaction with the World Tree's soil make it an object of urgent botanical study for naturalists. Discovered hanging beneath unusual fronds on Teldrassil, this large, round fruit radiates an unmistakable light. Botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth recognizes it as non-native to the World Tree, speculating its seeds arrived from distant lands across the sea. Whatever its origin, the fruit reacts strangely to the rich, enchanted soil of Teldrassil, demonstrating how vulnerable the nascent world bough is to foreign and unpredictable flora.

Glowing Gem. The Glowing Gem is an enchanted stone recovered from the murloc camps along the waters of Ashenvale. Originally sought by the fallen scout Teronis, the stone is a vital component needed to reconstruct the magical rod crafted by Dartol. Discovered in the possession of the aggressive murlocs dwelling near Lake Falathim, the Glowing Gem is imbued with latent magical energy. The young night elf Teronis ventured out from Astranaar to track it down, aiming to piece together a tool capable of driving back the corruption seeping through Ashenvale's forests. Though Teronis met an untimely end at the lake, the stone itself survived intact among the shoreline scavengers.

Glowing Soul Gem. A Glowing Soul Gem is a dark ritual artifact carried by operatives of the Cult of the Dark Strand in northern Ashenvale. Imbued with shadowy sorcery, the stone traps the spirit of an unwitting victim to fuel the cult's sinister operations. Northeast of Maestra's Post, in the shadowed ruins of Ordil'Aran, members of the Cult of the Dark Strand wield dark sorcery under the watchful eyes of their shadowy masters. Among their ranks, operatives carry Glowing Soul Gems—vessels enchanted to trap and torment the souls of the dead. Rather than mere decorative trinkets, these stones act as conduits of magical energy, anchoring bound spirits to serve the cult's shadowy ends.

Glutton Shackle. Glutton Shackles are enchanted restraints worn by Moonrage Glutton worgen in Silverpine Forest. Crafted by the mad archmage Arugal, these bands channel magic to bolster his otherwise flawed sorcery and sustain his cursed lupine creations. To the trained mages of the Forsaken, the feral worgen infesting Silverpine are not merely savage monstrosities—they are evidence of gross arcane ineptitude. Dalar Dawnweaver, an accomplished arcanist stationed at the Sepulcher, holds nothing but contempt for Archmage Arugal, deeming him an incompetent hack unworthy of the Kirin Tor. Dawnweaver discovered that Arugal relied on enchanted relics to compensate for his fragile spells. The Glutton Shackles, worn by the heavy Moonrage Gluttons wandering northern Silverpine, act as magical anchors that reinforce the curse binding the beasts.

Glyph of Azora. From the Tower of Azora, Theocritus uses Glyphs of Azora to watch distant threats. The inscribed stones extend the Eye of Azora's reach, letting him read enemies' thoughts and plans. Theocritus watches hostile powers from his tower in Elwynn Forest. His crystal relic, the Eye of Azora, lets him see across great distances, but cannot reach into the minds or plans of his adversaries. He places small focuses called Glyphs of Azora on surfaces far away to carry his magic farther. Each glyph anchors his power, letting him read enemy intentions and project his voice across miles to speak with field agents.

Glyphic Letter. At Northshire Abbey, Glyphic Letter calls promising novitiates to arcane study. After early service to the garrison, they are summoned upstairs to Khelden Bremen, the resident mage trainer. Khelden Bremen seals the Glyphic Letter with his personal insignia. Apprentice spellcasters receive it after proving their discipline in Northshire Valley. The summons calls them away from basic field duties and into dedicated magical instruction within the abbey. Bremen tests each student's resolve before they take up the arcane, with its dangerous forces, unyielding scrutiny, and burdens.

Glyphic Letter. A sealed summons reaches novice human mages in Northshire Valley, sent by Marshal McBride. Khelden Bremen calls promising spellcasters to Northshire Abbey to begin their arcane tutelage. Marshal McBride gives the rune-marked letter to an aspiring apprentice who has proved capable by helping him against local vermin. Khelden Bremen, Northshire's resident mage trainer, wrote it. He watches new recruits arriving at the abbey for signs of magical discipline and talent.

Glyphic Memorandum. The Glyphic Memorandum is a written notice delivered to novice mages arriving in Coldridge Valley. Penned on behalf of the mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, it directs fledgling spellcasters indoors to begin their formal arcane instruction. Novice spellcasters setting out into the bitter frost of Coldridge Valley receive this brief missive after completing their initial tasks. Authored by the local mage trainer Marryk Nurribit, the memorandum summons young practitioners into the warmth of Anvilmar. Rather than stern academic dogma, Marryk's guidance is informal and blunt: learn your incantations, set aside coin for training and tavern ale, and steer well clear of the irradiated ruin of Gnomeregan.

Glyphic Memorandum. Glyphic Memorandum is an introductory task directing novice mages in Coldridge Valley to their local trainer inside Anvilmar. Entrusted to mountaineer Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons budding arcane practitioners to seek out the eccentric gnome Marryk Nurribit to begin their formal spellcraft studies. While assisting mountaineer Sten Stoutarm with early duties across Coldridge Valley, newly arrived mages find themselves summoned by local arcane authority. Sten receives a written memorandum addressed to the fledgling spellcaster and passes it along, advising them to take a moment to read its contents and head inside the warmth of Anvilmar to meet its author.

Glyphic Parchment. Glyphic Parchment is an introductory summons directed to aspiring mages in the Valley of Trials. Delivered via Gornek, the written missive guides fledglings toward Mai'ah, a troll mage trainer stationed near the Den, to begin their arcane discipline. While new recruits prove their physical mettle against the local pests of Durotar, those possessing an affinity for the arcane cannot rely purely on brute force. Gornek passes along a written notice scribed with runes, instructing novice spellcasters to seek out Mai'ah, who oversees the early magical instruction of the Horde's newest recruits.

Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is a summons delivered to newly raised Forsaken magi in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of Isabella, the local arcane trainer, it calls fledgling spellcasters to the desecrated church to refine their craft in undeath. When a freshly awakened Forsaken mage returns from culling mindless Scourge in the graveyard of Deathknell, this sealed missive awaits them. Written under the mark of Isabella, the settlement's resident mage trainer, the scroll calls the recipient into the ruined parish sanctuary. For newly risen magi, it serves as an initial orientation into the discipline of the arcane under the Forsaken banner—reminding them that while death may have unburdened them of mortal weakness, the corrupting temptations of magical power remain as persistent as ever.

Glyphic Scroll. The Glyphic Scroll is an official summons delivered to newly awakened Forsaken mages in Deathknell. Bearing the seal of the mage trainer Isabella, the parchment directs promising practitioners of the arcane to seek her out in the desecrated village church to hone their volatile powers. When a freshly raised Forsaken demonstrates an affinity for arcane magic while culling mindless Scourge around Deathknell, they quickly catch the attention of their elders. Delivered by hand, the Glyphic Scroll is marked with the arcane sigil of Isabella, the local mage instructor. It bids the newly risen practitioner to report to her station within the ruined church, recognizing that unregulated magical aptitude poses as much danger to the Forsaken as it does to their enemies.

Glyphic Tablet. The Glyphic Tablet is an inscribed slate handed to novice Darkspear troll mages upon beginning their trials in Durotar. Delivered through the overseer Gornek, it directs fledgling spellcasters to seek tutelage from the troll mage trainer, Mai'ah. In the Valley of Trials, new Darkspear troll initiates exhibiting an affinity for arcane power are presented with the Glyphic Tablet. Passed along by Gornek while young recruits handle early tasks around the red canyons, the tablet contains an invitation from Mai'ah, a seasoned troll mage posted outside the Den. For the Darkspear, whose arcane traditions diverge from the scholarly academies of humans or high elves, the tablet serves as a formal call to discipline. Mai'ah uses the meeting to offer both arcane instruction and a solemn warning: raw magic is corruptive, deceptive, and far more hazardous to a practitioner's mind than any enemy soldier.

Glyphic Tablet. Glyphic Tablet is an introductory class quest in the Valley of Trials directed at novice Horde mages. Dispatched via Gornek after proving one's strength, it directs young spellcasters to Mai'ah, a troll mage trainer stationed outside the Den. After proving their basic mettle against the local wildlife in the Valley of Trials, fledgling mages are presented with an inscribed tablet passed along by Gornek. The missive originates from Mai'ah, the valley's resident mage trainer, bidding the initiate to seek her out by the entrance to the Den when they are ready to pursue their formal arcane studies.

Glyphs of Summoning. The Glyphs of Summoning are ritual inscriptions used by apprentice warlocks in Orgrimmar. Transcribed from the ancient Tablet of Verga, they allow a practitioner to draw a voidwalker from the Nether into a summoning circle and bind it to their service. In the subterranean depths of the Cleft of Shadow, the dark arts are studied far from the prying eyes of the Warchief's guards. For an aspiring warlock under the tutelage of Gan'rul Bloodeye, commanding a voidwalker marks a vital step in their craft. The Glyphs of Summoning, derived from the esoteric knowledge inscribed upon the Tablet of Verga, bridge the boundary between Azeroth and the Nether. Laid down within the summoning circle in Neeru Fireblade's tent, the glyphs tear open a threshold, pulling a creature of the Void into the mortal realm. The ritual demands that the warlock conquer the summoned entity in combat before Gan'rul imparts the final methods of binding.

Gnarlpine Corruption. Gnarlpine Corruption is an urgent courier task in Teldrassil delivered on behalf of the wounded Great Warden Gaerolas Talvethren. It warns the night elf leadership in Dolanaar that the Gnarlpine furbolgs have succumbed to demonic corruption and overran Starbreeze Village. This report sets the stage for military and druidic interventions to prevent the taint from reaching the sleeping druids of Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Gaerolas Talvethren lies grievously wounded near the ruins of Starbreeze Village after being ambushed by his former allies. The Gnarlpine furbolgs, long considered peaceful neighbors and stewards of the wild, have abruptly turned feral. Too injured to carry the news back to civilization himself, Gaerolas entrusts an adventurer to carry word swiftly to Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar before the madness spreads any further across the boughs of Teldrassil.

Gnoam Sprecklesprocket. The Gnoam Sprecklesprocket is a sophisticated power supply salvaged from Sneed's shredder deep within the Deadmines. Gnomish engineers seek this component to supercharge specialized drilling machines in an ambitious bid to reclaim their fallen home of Gnomeregan. Found in a goblin shredder operated within the Defias stronghold, the Gnoam Sprecklesprocket represents an exceptional feat of compact mechanical energy. Operating deep in the lumbering machine piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this specialized core delivers enough sustained energy to drive heavy industrial logging and cutting blades. Its stability and potent output make it an invaluable piece of salvage amidst the subterranean tunnels of Westfall.

Gnoarn. Gnoarn is an exiled gnome residing in Tinker Town within the dwarven mountain city of Ironforge. Displaced following the devastating fall of Gnomeregan, he assists his scattered people by directing adventurers to assist fellow gnomish engineers and survivors. Like the majority of his brethren, Gnoarn was forced to flee the depths of Gnomeregan when troggs invaded and catastrophic radiation rendered the great subterranean metropolis uninhabitable. Taking refuge in Ironforge's Tinker Town under the hospitality of the Bronzebeard dwarves, Gnoarn spends his days keeping track of other survivors. He serves as an informal coordinator among the refugees, pointing capable travelers toward gnomes abroad who urgently require assistance, such as the stranded pilot Bingles Blastenheimer in Loch Modan or the ambitious engineer Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind.

Gnogaine. Gnogaine is an Alliance quest offered by Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos. In an eccentric attempt to synthesize a cure for the leper gnomes—or perhaps concoct an extraordinarily potent beverage—Ozzie tasks adventurers with venturing toward Gnomeregan to gather radioactive fallout from glowing troggs. Ever since the fall of Gnomeregan, refugees like Gnoarn have fixated entirely on exterminating the trogg invaders and reversing the radioactive affliction that mutated their brethren. In contrast, Ozzie Togglevolt and his partner Razzle Sprysprocket take a somewhat less orthodox approach from their workshop in Kharanos. While purporting to pursue a cure for the leper gnomes, Ozzie openly admits their experimental formula might just as easily end up being a recipe for remarkably strong rum.

Gnoll. Gnolls are a savage, hyena-like race of humanoid scavengers and raiders found scattered across both the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Renowned for their vicious infighting, brutal strength, and animal cunning, they survive by pillaging settlements, butchering wildlife, and ambushing unwary travelers. Left unchecked, their sprawling packs and warlords pose a constant threat to frontier hamlets and trade roads alike. Standing slightly shorter than the average human but possessing explosive physical power, gnolls are bipedal hyena-kin known for their spiky teeth, thick pelts, and distinct barking laugh. While fully capable of walking upright, they often drop to all fours to lope swiftly through brush or track prey by scent. Gnoll culture values raw physical dominance above all else. They organize into fractious packs led by the strongest, cruelest alpha, only yielding when battered into submission by a superior force.

Gnoll Paw. Gnoll Paws reach Sentinel Hill as proof of a patrol against Westfall’s Riverpaw packs. The People's Militia offers bounties to help protect local farmsteads. The People's Militia defends Westfall from Sentinel Hill. With the royal army absent and the crown seemingly blind to rural troubles, ordinary citizens and volunteers face outlaws, rogue mechanoids, and Riverpaw gnolls. Captain Danuvin offers bounties for proof that gnolls have been slain. Bringing back their paws shows that patrols have searched the scrublands instead of resting beneath the watchtower.

Gnome. Gnomes are a diminutive, eccentric, and astonishingly intelligent race renowned across Azeroth for their inventive engineering and mastery of the arcane. Despite their cheerful demeanor, they recently suffered a catastrophic tragedy when a subterranean trogg invasion and a disastrous defense plan irradiated their capital of Gnomeregan. Now living as refugees in Ironforge's Tinker Town, the gnomes remain staunch Alliance allies as they fight to reclaim their lost home. Small in stature but towering in intellect, gnomes approach the world with boundless curiosity and scientific ambition. While other races focus on recording histories and preserving traditions, gnomes look relentlessly forward, dedicating their lives to mechanical engineering, arcane studies, and technological innovation. Their inventions—ranging from clockwork devices and flying machines to complex subterranean trains—have shaped the modern world. Even after devastating hardships, gnomefolk maintain an irrepressible cheerfulness and an unshakable drive to rebuild and solve the impossible.

Gnome Improvement. After an adventurer brings him a ring he once crafted, recovered from the irradiated depths of Gnomeregan, Talvash del Kissel offers to upgrade the piece for an adventurer willing to supply the materials. Down on his luck in the dwarven capital of Ironforge, the gnome artisan combines silver, moss agate, and intricate lattice work to craft a far superior trinket. Talvash del Kissel is one of the many gnome refugees who fled Gnomeregan following its disastrous fall to the trogg invasion and radiation. Residing in the Mystic Ward of Ironforge, Talvash finds himself down on his luck, out of stock, and desperate to prove that his talents as a master jeweler and tinkerer remain untarnished despite his exile.

Gnomeregan. Gnomeregan was the magnificent subterranean capital of the gnomish race, renowned across Azeroth for its mechanical brilliance and technological marvels. Today, it stands as a radioactive tomb, overrun by subterranean troggs, haywire defense automatons, and deranged leper gnomes after a desperate defense ended in catastrophe. Carved into the snowy crags of western Dun Morogh, Gnomeregan was built with the aid of the Ironforge dwarves centuries ago. Inside, massive steam-driven gears, intricate copper piping, and cavernous assembly halls formed the intellectual and industrial beating heart of gnomekind. It was from these subterranean halls that gnomish designs, flying machines, and complex armaments supplied the Alliance throughout the Second War, standing firm even when besieged by Orgrim Doomhammer's Horde.

Gnomeregan Gumdrop. During Hallow's End, Gnomeregan Gumdrops reach travelers from the exiled gnomes. One sweet helps sick Jesper celebrate at the Stormwind orphanage. At Ironforge's Mystic Ward, Talvash del Kissel hands out Gnomeregan Gumdrops to travelers who play along with his Hallow's End tricks. Innkeepers across the Alliance offer regional treats, but the exiled gnomes have no capital inn of their own. The radioactive disaster drove them from their underground kingdom, yet they still share their distinct sweets with the Alliance.

Gnomes Win!. In Thousand Needles, a gnome race ticket pays off when the gnomes come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The gnome race ticket is the stub that counts when the gnomes win. Hold on to it, and a gnome prize box is yours once the result is in. The goblin ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

Gnomish Tools. Gnomish Tools are intricate mechanical implements recovered from the sunken warships of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's fleet off the coast of Durotar. The Horde seeks these salvaged devices to study Alliance engineering and turn their enemies' technological advantages to their own benefit. When Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore led Kul Tiras and Alliance forces to the shores of Durotar, his fleet carried vast supplies of modern equipment, including sophisticated gear manufactured by their gnomish allies. Following the destruction of Proudmoore's fleet along the Scuttle Coast, east of Tiragarde Keep, these delicate mechanical kits sank beneath the waves. Today, waterproof toolboxes remain scattered among the rotting timbers and barnacle-encrusted hulls in the shallows.

Go'Shek Farm. Go'Shek Farm is an agricultural outpost in the eastern Arathi Highlands, occupied by the Horde and guarded by orcs from Hammerfall. Behind its mundane rural facade, Forsaken apothecaries conduct secretive alchemical experiments far from prying eyes. Go'Shek Farm is held by the Horde. Positioned south of Hammerfall and just north of the hostile Witherbark troll territory, the farmstead nominally serves as a vital supply and staging hub for the orcish settlement. Hammerfall Grunts patrol the fields and stables, securing food and livestock to sustain the Horde's embattled foothold in the Arathi Highlands.

Goblin. Goblins are diminutive, cunning humanoids originating from the Isle of Kezan, renowned across Azeroth for their relentless pursuit of profit, explosive engineering, and aggressive trade cartels. While most maintain a stance of strict neutrality to maximize commerce between the Alliance and Horde, mercenary and cutthroat outfits like the Venture Company and Steamwheedle Cartel leave an indelible mark on every corner of the world. Goblins hail from the Isle of Kezan in the South Seas, where their society long ago divided into competing economic syndicates known as cartels. Rather than building kingdoms or armies of their own, goblin leaders channeled their ambitions into cutthroat mercantilism, volatile engineering, and industrial ventures that now reach every corner of the world.

Goblin Foundry. The Goblin Foundry is an industrial workshop deep within the Deadmines where goblin tinkerers manufacture heavy metalwork for the Defias Brotherhood. A massive smelting cauldron dominates the chamber, which remains occupied by goblin craftsmen and engineers under Gilnid. Carved into the subterranean depths of Moonbrook, the Goblin Foundry provides the Defias Brotherhood with heavy manufacturing power. Goblin craftsmen and engineers work among the smelters and iron ramps, producing anchors and cannonballs.

Goblin Invaders. Goblin Invaders is a Horde quest tasked by Seereth Stonebreak at the border between the Barrens and the Stonetalon Mountains. It directs warriors of the Horde into Windshear Crag to strike directly at the Venture Company loggers despoiling the region's ancient woodlands. The Venture Company has pushed deep into the Stonetalon Mountains, carving wide swaths of destruction through the crags and valleys. Their logging operations strip the hillsides of timber and set fire to underbrush, leaving behind smoldering scars. To the tauren and their allies, this is not merely an unsightly mining and lumber operation; the primal spirits bound to Stonetalon are howling in torment. Seereth Stonebreak, stationed along the mountain border, observes that these spirits have grown blind with agony and fury under the goblins' relentless assault.

Goblin Sponsorship. Pozzik of the goblin racing team is waiting on a prototype fuel regulator that Gazlowe promised a few weeks ago, and it has not come. Gazlowe is usually very prompt, so Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask what happened, since the gnomes are gaining on the team. Pozzik calls the racing team the pride of goblins, and says many people help it in one way or another. Gazlowe hunts down parts from all over the world for the team, and once even came to work on one of their rigs. A few weeks ago Gazlowe said a new prototype fuel regulator would be sent, but nothing has arrived, which is unlike him. With the gnomes gaining, Pozzik asks you to go to Ratchet and ask Gazlowe about it.

Goblin Sponsorship. Gazlowe is back to the matter you came about: the fuel regulator promised to Pozzik has not reached Ratchet. Revilgaz in Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. Gazlowe sends you to Wharfmaster Lozgil there, who can check the cargo records. Gazlowe admits he promised Pozzik a new fuel regulator and still has not received it. Revilgaz of Booty Bay said he would have it shipped over, but it may have slipped through the cracks. If so, there is not much to be done, but you can at least learn whether it left Booty Bay. Wharfmaster Lozgil, at the far northwestern end of the Booty Bay docks, can look through the cargo records.

Goblin Sponsorship. Wharfmaster Lozgil cannot help any further with the missing fuel regulator, and suggests you ask Baron Revilgaz himself. You will find the Baron at the tavern across the harbor in Booty Bay, on the top floor. Wharfmaster Lozgil tells you he cannot be of much more help in tracing the missing shipment bound for Ratchet. If you want to follow it up, he suggests you go to the Baron himself, since if anyone knows Revilgaz's business, it is Revilgaz. He waits in the tavern across the harbor, on the top floor.

Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz tells you the Venture Company shredders at Lake Nazferiti in northern Stranglethorn have a new model fuel regulator that Pozzik could use. Foreman Cozzle has proven cleverer than the Baron expected, so Revilgaz sends you to find the blueprints. Baron Revilgaz explains that the Venture Company's shredders at Lake Nazferiti, in northern Stranglethorn, carry a new model of fuel regulator. Pozzik could take advantage of it if he had the details, but Cozzle, the foreman there, is cleverer than Revilgaz gave him credit for. You might have better luck. Revilgaz knows the blueprints are kept in Cozzle's house, almost certainly under lock and key. The Venture Company is based around Lake Nazferiti, in the vale's north-eastern corner. The key is with Foreman Cozzle in the cabin atop the oil tower, and the box holding the blueprints is in the small house near the tower's base. Revilgaz admits the gnome team out there is pretty good, and says the team needs every advantage it can find.

Goblin Sponsorship. Baron Revilgaz has the Fuel Regulator Blueprints ready and sends them to Pozzik on the Shimmering Flats. He gives his regards and adds that Pozzik should not hesitate to ask if he ever needs anything. Baron Revilgaz says you are all set. You carry the blueprints to Pozzik, out on the Shimmering Flats, with the Baron's regards and a message: if Pozzik ever needs anything, he should not hesitate to ask. Revilgaz says he will be waiting for news that Pozzik breaks the track record.

Goblins Win!. In Thousand Needles, a goblin race ticket pays off when the goblins come out ahead. A prize box comes back to whoever held the winning stub. The goblin race ticket is the stub that counts when the goblins win. Hold on to it, and a goblin prize box is yours once the result is in. The gnome ticket has a result of its own, for the other side of the race.

Godrick Farsan. Godrick Farsan is an undead warlock assistant located in the Undercity, serving alongside Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter. Despite being entirely blind, he says that he sees in a different way. Situated amidst the summoning circles of the Magic Quarter, Godrick Farsan aids Master Carendin Halgar in guiding aspiring Forsaken warlocks. Though he lacks physical sight, Godrick says he can still see in a different way, without explaining the means. He tests practitioners seeking to bind greater demonic entities, dispatching them to gather pure hearts and essences needed for intricate summoning rituals.

Gol'Bolar Quarry. Gol'Bolar Quarry is a dwarven excavation site carved into the snowy hills of southeastern Dun Morogh. Rich in stone and ore, the bustling mining operation has ground to a halt after being overrun by vicious troggs surging from the depths. Situated southeast of Kharanos, Gol'Bolar Quarry was established by Ironforge dwarves to extract vital stone and mineral wealth from the mountains. However, deep excavation work uncovered underground warrens, unleashing a horde of hostile troggs that quickly drove out the miners. Today, the upper camp serves as an embattled staging ground where overseers, tradesfolk, and Prospector Gehn rally dwarven and gnomish recruits to drive the beasts back and reclaim the pit.

name.frFR: Mine de la carrière de Gol’Bolar

text.enUS: Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine. Gol'Bolar Quarry Mine is an overrun excavation pit deep within the heart of Gol'Bolar Quarry in eastern Dun Morogh. Originally worked by dwarven miners, the tunnels breached subterranean trogg caverns, unleashing a violent infestation that claimed the entire site. Today, the deepest shafts serve as the stronghold for the trogg warband led by the brute Hammerspine. The mine was established by Ironforge dwarves seeking stone and rich ore deposits beneath the craggy peaks of Dun Morogh. Work came to an abrupt, violent halt when pickaxes fractured a wall into an ancient subterranean cavern system inhabited by troggs. Swarming out from the dark, the subterranean beasts overwhelmed the work crews and forced a hasty retreat, ultimately spilling outward to overrun the surrounding quarry pit as well.

Gol'dir. Krusk has gone through the documents you procured and concludes that Gol'dir is kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Gol'dir has languished in captivity far too long and needs to be freed. Krusk, in Tarren Mill, has gone through the documents you brought back after Infiltration. They point to Gol'dir being kept in a big Syndicate base up north, quite possibly in the Alterac Mountains. Krusk says the captivity has dragged on far too long and Gol'dir needs to be freed.

Golakka Hot Springs. Golakka Hot Springs is a geothermal basin in western Un'Goro Crater, nestled just north of Terror Run. Its bubbling pools and erupting geysers are fueled by the intense volcanic activity of nearby Fire Plume Ridge. The mineral-rich waters attract eccentric researchers, alchemists in search of exotic reagents, and wandering water elementals known as Steaming Furies. Situated in the western reaches of Un'Goro Crater, the Golakka Hot Springs are a direct product of the subterranean heat radiating from Fire Plume Ridge. Scalding water bubbles continuously to the surface, shaping tiered mineral terraces and violently erupting geysers. The environment is heavily prowled by Steaming Furies, elemental manifestations born from the convergence of subterranean groundwater and volcanic heat. Despite the danger, the springs frequently draw explorers, herbalists, and researchers fascinated by the crater's unique geology.

name.esES: Mina de la Costa del Oro
name.frFR: Carrière de la côte de l'Or

text.enUS: Gold Coast Quarry. In southwestern Westfall, the Gold Coast Quarry has fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. The mine once supplied Stormwind with stone, minerals, and gold; now the Brotherhood draws on its remaining resources for its insurrection. The Gold Coast Quarry once supplied Stormwind with stone and gold for the kingdom's rebuilding. After royal troops withdrew from Westfall, Defias highwaymen and renegade laborers seized the mine. Brotherhood patrols watch from its terraced ramps, which overlook the coast, and take what minerals remain to fund their rebellion.

Gold Dust. In Elwynn Forest, kobolds gather and hoard flecks of gold in the mines. Local buyers pay for the dust, while miners seek whole veins of ore. Kobolds dig through the Fargodeep and Jasperlode mines beneath Elwynn Forest. They keep the gold dust they find in pockets and pouches instead of refining it. Local peddlers and fences want these scraps, hoping to profit without paying official smelting tariffs.

Gold Dust Exchange. At Goldshire's crossroads, Gold Dust Exchange brings Remy "Two Times" coin for gold dust from kobolds in Elwynn's mines. Travelers gather the dust and trade it to the nervous broker for pay. Goldshire sits where Elwynn Forest's roads meet, and travelers, merchants, and guards pass through town. Remy "Two Times" is a shady broker with a habit of repeating his words and a sharp eye for profit. Instead of paying mining crews to dig for raw minerals, he turns to travelers passing through the Lion's Pride Inn. He offers coin for gold dust taken from the kobolds in the region.

Gold Road. The Gold Road is the primary north-south artery cutting through the arid expanse of the Barrens. Stretching from the Mor'shan Rampart on the border of Ashenvale down past the Crossroads toward the southern reaches, it serves as the vital transit line for the young Horde. The Gold Road is a long, sun-baked dirt highway that carves its way through the center of the Barrens. To the north, it begins near the fortified Mor'shan Rampart and Mor'shan Base Camp, which guard against night elf incursions from Ashenvale. Traveling south, it connects with the eastern roadway leading to Durotar before intersecting the bustling trading settlement of the Crossroads. Continuing southward past the lush waters of the local oases and the foothills near the Wailing Caverns, the northern span of the highway reaches a dried-up riverbed, where travelers cross into the more hazardous southern portion of the savanna.

Golden Plains. The Golden Plains form a vast, sun-drenched basin stretching southeast of Thunder Bluff in central Mulgore. Cherished by the tauren, these sweeping grasslands serve as prime hunting territory and a vital grazing habitat for wandering herds of kodo. Spreading out beneath the towering mesas of Thunder Bluff, the Golden Plains represent the untamed heart of Mulgore. The shifting sea of golden and green grass offers an abundant sanctuary for local wildlife, making it one of the most treasured traditional hunting grounds of the nomadic tauren.
