Broad kodo herds roam across the rolling basin, while hunters share stories of legendary quarry, most notably the great kodo Arra'chea, who wanders quietly through the tall stalks.

Goldshire. Goldshire sits where Elwynn’s roads meet, linking Stormwind City with Westfall, Redridge, and the southern frontier. Rebuilt after the First War, the town now offers travelers the Lion’s Pride Inn, while a hard-pressed Stormwind Guard defends it. Goldshire stands where the king’s highways meet, the civic and commercial heart of rural Elwynn. Threats press closer as Stormwind’s forces stretch thin and King Varian Wrynn remains mysteriously absent. Marshal Dughan relies on passing adventurers instead of regular troops to hold the surrounding borders. Riverpaw gnolls push in from the west, while hostile murlocs claim the shores of Stone Cairn Lake and Crystal Lake. Their attacks have killed royal guards and brought danger close to the town center.

Goldtooth. Near Fargodeep Mine, Auntie Bernice Stonefield's necklace is missing, and the Stonefield and Maclure families blame each other. Billy Maclure admits he lost it while playing nearby, and you follow the trail to the kobold Goldtooth. Auntie Bernice Stonefield's missing necklace has stirred up trouble between the Stonefield and Maclure families. Bernice suspects her rivals, but Billy Maclure lost the trinket while playing near Fargodeep Mine. He tries to hide his guilt, saying he only found the necklace before a creature snatched it away.

Goldwell the Elder. Goldwell the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest offered by Elder Goldwell in Kharanos, Dun Morogh. Honoring him reflects the enduring tradition of seeking out ancestral spirits across the snowbound dwarven lands. In exchange for your respects, he bestows a token of ancestral blessing. Standing in the bitter cold beside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, Elder Goldwell watches over the bustling trade path leading to the gates of Ironforge. During the Lunar Festival, this venerable figure welcomes weary travelers, adventurers, and locals alike, embodying the long memory of ancient days when early mortals walked beneath the stars of Azeroth.

Golm Fragment. The Golm Fragment is one of four missing pieces chipped from the Goaz Stone, an ancient relic uncovered at the Wetlands excavation site. Recovered by adventurers dodging ferocious raptors, it helps dwarven archaeologists piece together mysterious Titan inscriptions. Discovered at the excavation site in the southern Wetlands, the Golm Fragment is part of a monumental slab known as the Goaz Stone. Prospector Whelgar discovered the stone shortly before raptors drove the Explorers' League back, but found its inscription severed in four critical places. The Golm Fragment was abandoned amid the dirt and overturned crates when the dig was overrun, hidden away inside an ancient relic box until brave explorers could retrieve it.

Golnir Bouldertoe. Golnir Bouldertoe is a dwarven mining vendor stationed beside the bustling Great Forge in Ironforge. He provides essential supplies for miners and prospectors while handling dispatches for local couriers and travelers. Standing within the roaring heat of Ironforge's Great Forge, Golnir Bouldertoe outfits prospectors and craftsmen with the necessities of their trade. From sturdy mining picks to fluxes and coal, his wares fuel the tireless smelting fires and smithies that define the dwarven capital. Kin to Geofram Bouldertoe, Golnir is a reliable point of contact for workers arriving in the city, often directing fresh hands or receiving supply missives shuttled in from nearby outposts.

Good Steel. Good Steel is an Alliance quest originating at Eastvale Logging Camp in eastern Elwynn Forest. In the wake of recent conflicts, high-quality metal has become scarce, leaving the camp's woodcutting equipment worn and difficult to replace. Craftsman Hagar Lowe tasks adventurers with delving into Jasperlode Mine to salvage well-crafted pickaxes so their steel can be repurposed. Following the devastating conflicts that have battered the human kingdoms, high-grade steel has become an increasingly scarce luxury in Elwynn Forest. At Eastvale Logging Camp, daily timber harvesting relies heavily on durable axes, saws, and hardware, but the tools currently available have suffered badly from substandard metal and constant wear. Without reliable shipments coming from Stormwind's foundries, camp craftsmen like Hagar Lowe are forced to find inventive solutions to keep the forestry camp functioning.

Gorbold Steelhand. Gorbold Steelhand is a dwarven merchant stationed in Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore. Operating far from the snowy halls of Khaz Modan, he supplies travelers, crafters, and local night elves with general goods and trade supplies. While most of Kalimdor's northern reaches are populated by the secretive night elves, Alliance outposts like Auberdine rely on merchants from across the Great Sea to keep trade moving. Gorbold Steelhand represents the far-reaching presence of Ironforge commerce in the region. Working alongside the kaldorei, he sells trade goods, reagents, crafting sundries, and tools to adventurers preparing to explore the treacherous shores and forests of Darkshore.

Gordo's Task. Gordo's Task is an errand in Tirisfal Glades given by Gordo, a wandering abomination trying to gather flora along the road to Brill. Unsuited for delicate fieldwork, he recruits travelers to pick Gloom Weed and deliver it to his handler, Junior Apothecary Holland. Gordo is an abomination who trudges back and forth along the countryside between Deathknell and Brill. While abominations excel at brute combat and heavy hauling, their massive, sutured hands make fine manipulation almost impossible. Sent into the meadows to gather ingredients for the Royal Apothecary Society, Gordo quickly realizes his blunt fingers crush more stems than they pluck, prompting him to bully or bribe passersby into doing the tedious work for him.

Gordok Commons. The Gordok Commons comprise the fortified northern quarter of the ancient Highborne ruins of Dire Maul. Under the rule of King Gordok, this sprawling stone complex serves as the seat of power for the elite warrior caste of the Gordunni ogres. Occupying what was once an aristocratic wing of Eldre'Thalas, the Gordok Commons have been thoroughly desecrated and refitted for ogre tastes. Grand night elven pillars and arched passageways now house armories, crude barricades, and training grounds for the Gordok—the fiercest, most disciplined fighters among the Gordunni clan. At the deepest end of the wing lies Gordok's Seat, where King Gordok presides over his brutes through sheer force and intimidation.

Gordon Wendham. Gordon Wendham is a Forsaken weaponsmith and merchant operating out of the bustling Trade Quarter in the Undercity. He equips newly arrived champions and local defenders of the Dark Lady with reliable steel, blades, and bludgeons. Beyond hawking basic armaments, he frequently serves as a local point of contact for couriers arriving from the surface. Situated amidst the damp stonework and chemical canals of the Undercity's Trade Quarter, Gordon Wendham provides essential weaponry to those taking up arms for the Forsaken. From basic daggers and hand axes to sturdy broadswords and maces, his stock caters to fledgling fighters who need dependable iron before venturing out into the contested reaches of Lordaeron.

Gordon's Crate. Gordon's Crate is a heavy shipment of weapons packed in the Undercity for the Forsaken forces stationed in Silverpine Forest. It serves as an essential supply consignment meant to be ferried directly to the remote garrison at the Sepulcher. Maintaining the Forsaken grip on Silverpine Forest requires a steady logistical flow from the Undercity. Gordon's Crate holds armaments intended to bolster Deathguard Podrig's defenders at the Sepulcher, ensuring outpost sentries are not caught off guard by the worgen, wild beasts, or human remnants lurking in the woods.

Gordunni Cobalt. Orwin Gizzmick has just arrived in Feralas and heard that the Gordunni ogres keep interesting minerals buried. Orwin offers a shovel and asks you to head for the Gordunni Outpost, north of Camp Mojache, and dig up twelve samples of Gordunni cobalt, following the blue glow. Orwin Gizzmick has only just reached Feralas and has heard the Gordunni ogres possess some interesting minerals. Orwin does not know what the ogres are up to, but they guard it fiercely and do not leave it lying about. They bury it, to keep folks like Orwin from getting hold of it. Orwin gives you a shovel. The Gordunni Outpost lies north of the camp; a blue glow shows where to dig. Twelve samples of Gordunni cobalt are wanted.

Gordunni Outpost. Tucked into the rugged cliffs north of Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost serves as a fortified camp for the brutish Gordunni ogres of Feralas. The clan's corrupting influence has choked the once-vibrant wilderness here, leaving the surrounding earth dry, withered, and brown. Carved into the northern mountains above the Lariss Pavilion, the Gordunni Outpost stands out as a stark scar against the lush canopy of Feralas. Wherever the Gordunni ogres settle, their reckless magical channeling and destructive habits sap the vitality of the wild, leaving the local flora dead and the hillsides barren. The outpost consists of dirt trails, a shallow entrance cave, and a larger ogre mound burrowed deep into the rear cliffs. Patrolled by heavily armed hillguards, cunning channelers, and ogre tamers, the camp also holds dangerous trophies—including a captured sasquatch named Bigfist kept in crude confinement near the deeper den.

name.frFR: La tourte au foie de broche-tripes

text.enUS: Goretusk Liver Pie. At the Saldean Farm in Westfall, Salma Saldean prepares a pie amid hard times. Bandits have ravaged the breadbasket of the kingdom, and local homesteaders hunt aggressive boars to feed their families. Westfall was once Stormwind's fertile breadbasket, but hard times have fallen on the land. Neglected roads, roving outlaws, and overgrown fields make daily life a struggle for the few settlers who remain. At the Saldean Farm, Salma Saldean works to keep a sense of home despite the dangers around her. A traditional meat pie offers one of the few modest comforts for homesteaders trying to preserve their way of life.

Gornek. Gornek is an orc overseer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He serves as the primary point of intake for fresh orc and Darkspear troll recruits preparing to prove their worth to the New Horde. Standing directly at the heart of the Valley of Trials, Gornek represents the initial test of discipline for aspiring Horde warriors, scouts, and spellcasters. Under Warchief Thrall's order, every youth and newcomer must earn their place through grit and perseverance rather than entitlement. Gornek assesses those stepping into the valley, reading their introductory orders and directing them to trainers throughout the compound. Whether an initiate carries an encrypted scrawl, a glyphic parchment, or a simple tablet, it is Gornek who receives their credentials and sets them upon their harsh path of survival.

Grace of An'she and Mu'sha. Grace of An'she and Mu'sha is a sacred tauren pilgrimage undertaken on Red Cloud Mesa to honor the sun and moon as the celestial eyes of the Earthmother. By carrying fragile, smoldering incense to an elevated shrine in the southeastern hills, travelers show respect to the heavenly lights that bring warmth, life, and direction to the plains. In tauren myth, the sun and the moon are known as An'she and Mu'sha, revered as the twin eyes of the Earthmother. While the elemental spirits dwell directly within the stones, winds, and waters of Azeroth, these celestial twins watch over the world from the heights of heaven. Their constant journey across the sky marks the eternal rhythm of day and night, granting warmth, guidance, and hope to all living creatures. Honoring the twins is an essential spiritual duty, teaching that balance requires reverence not only for the land beneath one's feet, but also for the light shining down from the sky.

Gramma Stonefield. At the Stonefield farm in Elwynn, Gramma Stonefield quietly works to ease a family feud. Gramma Stonefield has watched the Stonefields and the Maclures bicker for decades across the road. The oldest living member of the Stonefield clan, she sees their rivalry as senseless and harmful. When her grandson Tommy Joe Stonefield falls in love with Maybell Maclure, Gramma chooses compassion over clan loyalty. She turns to her old friend William Pestle in Goldshire and quietly plans ways for the sweethearts to meet in secret, despite the hostility between their farms.

Grand Mason Marblesten. Grand Mason Marblesten is an esteemed dwarven stonemason stationed in the busy Commons of Ironforge. Deeply devoted to the royal legacy of Khaz Modan, he has been commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to build a memorial to Sully Balloo, a dwarven soldier who died in the Thandol Span tragedy. Adventurers often meet him when assisting with the materials needed to complete this solemn tribute. Dwarven stonemasonry is not merely a trade; it is an enduring art form that shapes the very soul of Ironforge. Grand Mason Marblesten stands among the city's foremost masters of the chisel, representing the centuries-old tradition of carving halls, pillars, and great effigies straight from the living mountain. Based in the Commons, he oversees civic projects and commemorative monuments that immortalize Bronzebeard history.

Grand Vestibule. The Grand Vestibule is the monumental entrance hall of the Scarlet Monastery in Tirisfal Glades. Lined with crimson pillars and stone effigies of fallen crusaders, it serves as the threshold where adventurers prepare to breach the monastery's inner halls. Past the heavy outer gates of the Monastery lies the Grand Vestibule, an expansive marble hall dedicated to the martial pride of the Scarlet Crusade. Statues of armored champions stand vigil beside vaulted stone pillars, and zealous sentries, disciples, and augurs patrol the flagstones to strike down anyone daring to enter without the order's crimson tabard. For trespassers, it is the first taste of the Crusade's unrelenting discipline and fanaticism.

Granis Swiftaxe. Granis Swiftaxe is a dwarf warrior trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Known for his blunt demeanor and hardy training regimen, he mentors fledgling Alliance fighters emerging from Coldridge Pass before directing seasoned warriors to the city of Ironforge. Found warming himself among the casks of the Thunderbrew Distillery, Granis Swiftaxe serves as the primary combat instructor for young warriors traversing Dun Morogh. He possesses the unyielding pride typical of dwarven fighters, showing open amusement and disdain toward non-warriors who try to catch his ear. Once a student demonstrates sufficient prowess in combat, Granis sends them up the mountain path to seek out master trainer Muren Stormpike in the Military Ward of Ironforge.

Grape Manifest. At Northshire Abbey, the Grape Manifest records grapes recovered from Milly Osworth's vineyard after brigands seized the harvest. The fruit is bound for the abbey's cellars. Milly Osworth tends a vineyard in Northshire Valley, where local farms help feed Northshire Abbey. Defias bandits seized the harvest, putting the abbey's supply of fresh fruit and fermentable grapes at risk. The Grape Manifest records the grapes reclaimed from the fields and their quantity, so the abbey's quartermasters can account for their stores and prepare barrels for fermentation.

Grape Manifest. Milly Osworth records her rescued grape harvest for Northshire Abbey. She writes a manifest of the yield recovered from Defias thieves, then sends it to Brother Neals so the brotherhood can replenish its wine stores. Northshire Valley's soil and orchards have long supported local food and the abbey's wine. When thieves and bandits seized the eastern fields, they cut off the abbey's supply of grapes and food. With the harvest recovered from the occupied fields, Milly Osworth records the yield in a manifest.

Graveborn the Elder. Graveborn the Elder is a Lunar Festival encounter situated near the town of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. During the celebration, travelers seek out Elder Graveborn among the blighted groves to honor the ancient forebears of Azeroth. Paying respects to this spirit earns his blessing and a token of the holiday. While the Forsaken dwell among ruined manors and grave sites in Tirisfal Glades, the Lunar Festival brings an unexpected communion with ancient times. Elder Graveborn appears as a spectral elder stationed just outside Brill. Even in a realm shattered by the Scourge and reclaimed by the undead, he welcomes pilgrims who pause to honor the ancient ways.

Graverobbers. Magistrate Sevren of Brill tasks adventurers with purging Rot Hide gnolls from the Mass Grave southwest of Garren's Haunt. These undead beasts were sent by the Scourge to dig up the corpses of early plague victims to swell their ranks. Slaying them and recovering their embalming ichor protects the fallen and aids the Royal Apothecary Society's research. When the Plague of Undeath first tore through Tirisfal Glades, the dead piled up faster than formal burials could accommodate. Immense mass graves were dug across the north to contain the staggering loss. Until recently, those buried remains escaped resurrection. Now, however, the Scourge has unleashed Rot Hide gnolls upon the trenches southwest of Garren's Haunt, sending them to exhumate the decayed remains to reinforce the Lich King's armies.

Gray Bear Tongue. A gray bear tongue is a raw reagent harvested from the wild bears roaming the Hillsbrad Foothills. It is sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill to serve as a biological component in their experimental toxins. The untamed wilderness surrounding Tarren Mill is rich in native fauna, including several varieties of sturdy gray bears. While natural predators pose a constant threat to travelers, the Forsaken see them as a harvestable source of raw alchemy components. Apothecary Lydon studies local wildlife to isolate potent organic agents, using the heavy muscular tissue and fluids of gray bear tongues as a base ingredient for concocting lethal solutions such as the Elixir of Suffering.

Great Forge. The Great Forge is the fiery heart and namesake of the dwarven capital of Ironforge. Situated at the very center of the city, its massive furnaces and famed Great Anvil never rest, producing legendary armaments and serving as the bustling center of civic life. The Great Forge was the very first structure built by the early dwarves beneath Ironforge Mountain, and the grand capital grew in concentric rings around it. Molten stone and slag pour constantly from giant foundries into glowing channels, illuminating the cavern with an amber haze. At its center stands the massive Great Anvil, overseen by Master of the Forge Myolor Sunderfury. Renowned masters of metalwork gather around its rim, hammering out armor, tools, and weapons day and night.

Great Lift. The Great Lift is a massive, tauren-engineered elevator system perched on the southern edge of the Barrens. It serves as the primary route lowering travelers and supplies hundreds of feet into the sheer canyon basin of Thousand Needles. Despite its strategic value, aggressive quilboar encroaching through the southern wastes have made approaching the rim increasingly perilous. Spanning the sheer cliff edge between the southern Barrens and the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, the Great Lift stands as a marvel of practical tauren construction. Built using heavy timber, braided rope, and counterweighted pulleys, its paired platforms carry caravans, couriers, and warriors safely across a vertical precipice that would otherwise break any wagon. At the top and bottom platforms, tauren like Brave Moonhorn and Grish Longrunner maintain watch, keeping travelers informed of the road ahead and ensuring cargo passes smoothly.

Great-father Winter. Great-father Winter is an elderly orc hired by the Smokywood Pastures merchant company to pose as the legendary holiday figure in Orgrimmar. Stationed near Grommash Hold in the Valley of Strength during the Feast of Winter Veil, he listens to children's wishes while visibly growing weary of commercial holiday cheer. In exchange for holiday gifts and seasonal tasks, he routinely asks passersby for gingerbread cookies and ice cold milk. While ancient lore speaks of Greatfather Winter as a majestic, elemental spirit wandering the land bringing snow and seasonal renewal, the figure sitting in the Valley of Strength is rather more mundane. He is an orc performer on the payroll of Smokywood Pastures, hired specifically to drive commerce, promote company wares, and entertain the youth of the Horde. Critics grumble that this commercial mascot cheapens genuine seasonal traditions, but few can deny the festive buzz he brings to the city streets.

Greatfather Winter. Greatfather Winter is the legendary personification of the winter season and the central figure of the Feast of Winter Veil. While ancient legends revere him as a mythical being who blankets Azeroth in snow to allow the land to rest and renew, modern city-dwellers know him primarily through the commercial spectacle managed by the goblins of Smokywood Pastures. According to ancient lore, Greatfather Winter is an ethereal wanderer who walks the world late in the year, casting his billowing snowy cloak across the land so nature may slumber and be reborn. Dwarves view him as an embodiment or herald of the titans, pointing to the frosted crags of Dun Morogh as living proof of his favor. Other traditions, such as those of the tauren, respect his role in the season's turning while attributing the cold and storms to the elemental work of the Sun and Moon, giving the Earth Mother time to rest. Wherever the legend traveled, communities learned to gather and feast together against the cold, celebrating the promise of returning life.

Greatmother Hawkwind. Greatmother Hawkwind is a revered tauren elder resting by the water well on Red Cloud Mesa. As the mother of Camp Narache's leader, Chief Hawkwind, she embodies the enduring spirit and communal responsibility of the tribe despite her advanced age. Greatmother Hawkwind spends her days beside the fresh water well at Camp Narache, serving as the spiritual matriarch for young tauren beginning their rites of passage. Though years have slowed her stride, she refuses to let age sideline her duty to the village. She believes that every member of the tribe, young or old, has an active role to play in sustaining the community, often asking fledgling youths to lend a hand with simple domestic chores like fetching fresh water.

Greatwood Vale. Greatwood Vale is a forested valley nestled in the eastern foothills of the Stonetalon Mountains, reached via the perilous Webwinder Path. Recently, the hostile Grimtotem tribe seized the vale, using it as a staging ground for bloody assaults on neighboring settlements. Tucked away off the Webwinder Path, Greatwood Vale has become a violent frontier. The Grimtotem tribe, under the ruthless leadership of Grundig Darkcloud, has moved into the vale in force, cutting off safe passage and bringing terror to the surrounding foothills.

Green Belt. The Green Belt is a wild stretch of marshland in the eastern Wetlands, sprawling below the ridges of Grim Batol. It is overrun by roaming bog beasts, predatory crocolisks, and toxic oozes, guarded primarily by the solitary night elf Rethiel the Greenwarden. Stretching across the eastern interior of the Wetlands, the Green Belt is one of the sodden region's untamed hollows. The local wildlife—ranging from massive crocolisks to shifting oozes and shambling bog beasts—makes travel through the mossy waters hazardous. Deep within its reaches sits a solitary watch post manned by Rethiel the Greenwarden, a lone night elf dedicated to studying the fen's ecology and keeping its hostile denizens in check.

Greenpaw Village. Greenpaw Village is a furbolg settlement nestled in central Ashenvale, situated between Raynewood Retreat and Silverwind Refuge. It serves as the primary home of the Foulweald tribe, led by Chief Murgut and the shaman Oakpaw. Gripped by demonic corruption and embattled by outside forces, the village is an active conflict point for both Alliance and Horde travelers. Situated south of Raynewood Retreat and northeast of Silverwind Refuge, Greenpaw Village was once a quiet home for the forest's ursine denizens. In the wake of the Third War, its resident furbolgs—the Foulweald tribe—succumbed to the insidious corruption tainting Ashenvale's soil and spirits. Under the dominion of Chief Murgut and their corrupted spiritual guide, Shaman Oakpaw, the Foulweald have become hostile and unstable, attacking any travelers who stray into their forest territory.

Gregor's Remains. Gregor's Remains are the physical bones recovered from the Scourge-enslaved Gregor Agamand. Once part of the wealthiest dynasty in Tirisfal Glades, his remains are sought by a former mill worker eager to settle an old score from beyond the grave. Before the Third War, the Agamand family held immense wealth and vast tracts of land across northern Tirisfal Glades. When the Scourge invaded Lordaeron, the patriarchs chose pride over flight, fortifying their family mills and persuading their loyal laborers to make a desperate stand against the undead. The defense failed entirely. The estate was overrun, and those who stood their ground were butchered and raised into undeath. Gregor Agamand became another mindless thrall in the service of the Lich King, haunting the very mills his family once ruled.

Grelin Whitebeard. Grelin Whitebeard is a dwarven scout stationed in Coldridge Valley by royal decree to assess the Frostmane troll threat. Operating out of an isolated camp, he relies on rising adventurers to keep the trolls contained while Ironforge's attention remains consumed by the trogg crisis. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were dispatched to Coldridge Valley under direct orders from the Senate of Ironforge and King Magni Bronzebeard himself. Their mission was clear: assess and neutralize the threat posed by the native Frostmane trolls. With Ironforge's official military fully bogged down combating trogg outbreaks across Dun Morogh, the brothers were given very few resources to accomplish their task. Grelin had to establish an outpost in the snowy hills and look toward local recruits and passing initiates to carry out the necessary work.

Grelin Whitebeard's Journal. Grelin Whitebeard's Journal is a personal field notebook kept by the dwarf scout Grelin Whitebeard in Coldridge Valley. Containing critical notes on local Frostmane troll activity, the journal was stolen by the Frostmane brute Grik'nir the Cold and dragged into the troll cave in Coldridge Valley. While observing the aggressive movements of the Frostmane trolls near Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard diligently recorded his findings in this leatherbound notebook. The document contains his raw field observations regarding the strength, organization, and threat level posed by the indigenous winter trolls. However, during a confrontation or ambush, the journal was snatched away by Grik'nir the Cold—a heavily marked troll brute—forcing Grelin to recruit passing adventurers to delve into the troll cave and wrest it back before his report could be finalized.

Grelin's Report. Grelin's Report is a dispatch written by Grelin Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll situation in Coldridge Valley. Entrusted to an adventurer rather than a novice apprentice, it serves as the official link between the scouts guarding Anvilmar and Senir Whitebeard stationed in Kharanos. Written after observing the Frostmane trolls in Coldridge Valley, Grelin's Report concludes that they pose no large threat and can be dealt with by the Mountaineers already stationed there and mercenaries paid from Senate funds. Rather than trusting his fumbling apprentice with such vital intelligence, Grelin enlists a capable traveler to carry the document through the trogg-infested Coldridge Pass. The paper acts as an official pass through Mountaineer Thalos's blockade, proving the bearer travels on urgent business to the wider snowy expanse of Dun Morogh.

Grell Earring. Grell Earrings are crude baubles scavenged and worn by the feral creatures infesting the ruins of Bashal'Aran. Though unremarkable at a glance, their proximity to ancient relics allows sensitive spirits to trace the lingering magical seals holding them in torment. The Wild Grells and Vile Sprites lurking around the collapsed marble of Bashal'Aran hoard assorted trinkets, frequently fashioning earrings from scraps they scavenge among the ruins. To most mortals, these items are worthless refuse. However, to Asterion, an ancient night elf bound as a tormented phantom within the ruins, they serve as dowsing implements. By scrutinizing the resonant magical traces absorbed by these earrings, Asterion attempts to locate the ancient seal that imprisons his spectral form.

Grenka's Claw. Grenka's Claw is a physical trophy taken from the formidable harpy Grenka Bloodscreech in the depths of Roguefeather Den. Presented to Dorn Plainstalker at the Weathered Nook, it serves as undeniable proof that an aspiring adventurer has endured a grueling physical trial in the canyon heights. Within the winding caverns of Roguefeather Den, west of Freewind Post, harpies cache food and violently defend their territory against outsiders. To test the physical resilience of young champions, Dorn Plainstalker tasks them with invading the deep roosts and destroying the flock's food reserves. Such brazen provocation inevitably draws the fury of Grenka Bloodscreech. Severing and returning her wicked talon proves that a warrior can withstand wave after wave of enraged harpies and survive the vicious onslaught of their matriarch.

Greta Mosshoof. Greta Mosshoof is a tauren druid allied with the Emerald Circle at the Emerald Sanctuary in southern Felwood. Alongside night elves and fellow guardians of nature, she investigates the foul taint creeping across the ancient forest and directs scouts into the Shadow Council stronghold of Jaedenar. Stationed at the Emerald Sanctuary on the southern boundary of Felwood, Greta Mosshoof works alongside the Emerald Circle to combat the pervasive corruption consuming the ancient woods. Rather than surrendering the blighted lands to the demonic taint left in the wake of the Third War, she coordinates efforts to understand and push back the spreading rot. Her investigations zero in on the poisoned waters of Felwood and the foul cultists burrowed within Jaedenar.

Greymane Wall. The Greymane Wall is a massive stone bulwark spanning the southern frontier of Silverpine Forest. Built by King Genn Greymane after the Second War, it seals the kingdom of Gilneas away from the outside world behind impenetrable, locked gates. Following the Second War, King Genn Greymane grew resentful of the Alliance of Lordaeron, particularly the taxes required to maintain the orc internment camps. Deciding Gilneas had given enough of its coin and blood for foreign troubles, Greymane withdrew from the Alliance and ordered a colossal barrier raised across the head of the peninsula. When the Third War brought the Plague of Undeath and countless desperate refugees to its foot, the gates remained pitilessly barred.

Grif Wildheart. Grif Wildheart is a seasoned dwarven hunter trainer stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Renowned among the local mountaineers for his deep affinity with wildlife, he instructs budding marksmen in tracking, marksmanship, and the rites of beast taming. For young hunters emerging from Coldridge Valley, Grif provides the vital bridge between firing a rifle and walking alongside a loyal animal companion. While many Ironforge dwarves prefer the fiery warmth of a forge or the steady clink of pickaxes, Grif Wildheart has dedicated his life entirely to the frozen wilderness of Dun Morogh. Local mountaineers half-jokingly say he spends a bit too much time with four-legged beasts, but none dispute his mastery of the wild. Having spent years tracking across snowbound ridges alongside seasoned hunting companions, Grif possesses an intimate understanding of the natural predators that roam the crags.

Grim Batol. Grim Batol is an ancient, ruined dwarven mountain fortress looming over the eastern edge of the Wetlands. Built by the Wildhammer clan, abandoned after a dark curse during the War of the Three Hammers, and later occupied by the Dragonmaw orcs as a dragon breeding lair, its sealed gates remain an ominous blight upon the highlands. Following the ancient civil war of the three clans, Thane Khardros Wildhammer carved Grim Batol out of the jagged mountains east of the marsh. During the subsequent War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron sorceress Modgud laid siege to the fortress. Although Khardros struck her down, Modgud cast a foul shadow across the stones before her death. The lingering taint rendered the halls uninhabitable, forcing the surviving Wildhammer dwarves to abandon their magnificent kingdom and migrate north into the Hinterlands.

Grim Message. Nimboya wants the Witherbark trolls punished for betraying Thrall, though they were once allies of the Horde. Nimboya's pike is to carry Witherbark skulls and be planted in a Witherbark village in the Hinterlands. Once the Witherbark trolls stood with the Horde, until they betrayed Thrall. Nimboya hands you a pike and sends you a long way north to the Hinterlands, northeast of Tarren Mill, the village held by the Forsaken. Hunt Witherbark trolls there and collect their skulls, then plant the pike in the ground in Hiri'watha or Zun'watha, two of their smaller villages, so they learn what their deeds cost. Afterwards Nimboya waits in Stranglethorn.

Grimand Elmore. Following the creation of specialized armor, the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard sends a copy of his findings across the district to Grimand Elmore. The brief errand carries technical notes between two headstrong weaponsmiths sharing space in Stormwind City. Having forged the specialized Fire Hardened Mail, Furen Longbeard documents the intricate heat-treating techniques and elemental principles he uncovered during the process. Rather than keeping the knowledge entirely to himself, he commits the notes to parchment and tasks an adventurer with delivering them straight to Grimand Elmore, a seasoned crafter operating out of a nearby weapon shop.

Grimand's Armor. In Stormwind, Grimand's Armor takes shape through a test of Furen Longbeard's methods. Grimand Elmore crafts a helm from rare materials, meant to endure punishing blows in battle. For an Alliance warrior, it marks a step toward mastery. Grimand Elmore tests Furen Longbeard's daring smithing methods at his forge in Stormwind's Dwarven District. Grimand had doubted the dwarven master armorer's theories. To put them to the test, a warrior gathers rare elemental and beast components in hostile territory and brings them to Grimand. He uses the materials to forge a reinforced helm built to endure crushing impacts.

Grimbooze Thunderbrew. In Westfall's Dagger Hills, Grimbooze Thunderbrew brews potent spirits and speaks in verse. The eccentric dwarf belongs to the Thunderbrew clan. Grimbooze Thunderbrew camps in the Dagger Hills, where he tends his private casks. He comes from the Thunderbrew brewing family of Kharanos and left the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh for Westfall's windswept hills. Jovial and devoted to potent spirits, he speaks only in rhymes. A traveler must complete a simple task before he answers any questions, and he is always ready to test a thirsty palate.

Grime-Encrusted Ring. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan, adventurers can recover a jewelry piece heavily caked in toxic filth and hardened muck from a Dark Iron dwarf invader. Discovering its true identity requires using the Sparklematic 5200, an industrial cleaning automaton found inside the Dormitory sector. Once scrubbed clean, the ring reveals personal markings that launch a journey to return or refashion the heirloom. Gnomeregan's corridors are swimming in toxic sludge, oil, and radioactive fallout, so it is no surprise that items dropped in the fighting become coated in impenetrable sludge. Slain Dark Iron dwarves infiltrating the city often carry heavily soiled trinkets, chief among them this grime-encrusted band. The crust is far too tough for mundane hand-washing, completely obscuring whether the metal beneath is copper, gold, or junk.

Grimesilt Dig Site. Grimesilt Dig Site is an archaeological excavation in the Searing Gorge originally broken ground by Ironforge dwarves. Overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves, the pit is now firmly under enemy control while surviving members of the original expedition struggle to endure in hiding. Situated within the soot-choked badlands of the Searing Gorge, the Grimesilt Dig Site began as an expedition sanctioned by Ironforge scholars seeking relics beneath the crags. That venture met a violent end when the native Dark Iron dwarves drove out the excavators and claimed the equipment for themselves. Today, the trench swarms with Dark Iron sentries, leaving the wounded and scattered survivors of the original Ironforge crew trapped in and around the pit.

Grimtotem Compound. The Grimtotem Compound is a fortified tribal settlement nestled in the central wilds of Feralas, just east of the elven ruins of Dire Maul. Occupied by the aggressive and insular Grimtotem clan, the encampment serves as a base for their mysterious and destructive operations in the region. Spanning two encampments east of Dire Maul, the Grimtotem Compound establishes a firm foothold for the Grimtotem clan in Feralas. Unlike the tauren aligned with Cairne Bloodhoof in Thunder Bluff, the Grimtotem here operate independently and with hostility toward outsiders. In the southern half of the settlement, they keep captive sprite darters locked inside a large wooden cage for reasons of their own, while rogue gnolls stalk the fringes of their northern perimeter.

Grimtotem Satchel. The Grimtotem Satchel is a leather pouch clutched by the fallen tauren Maur Grimtotem deep inside Ragefire Chasm. Even as troggs overwhelmed him in the subterranean cavern beneath Orgrimmar, Maur shielded this pack with his dying breath. Recovering it and returning it to Thunder Bluff reveals that Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem had an active interest in whatever her clansman carried. Discovered beneath the broken body of Maur Grimtotem in the depths of Ragefire Chasm, this simple pack was held in a fierce, vice-like embrace. Maur fought desperately to protect whatever it contains while surrounded and slain by savage troggs. The sheer determination required to shield a satchel above one's own life suggests its contents are far more significant than ordinary trail rations or supplies.

Grimtotem Spying. Cliffwatcher Longhorn tasks Horde champions with infiltrating Darkcloud Pinnacle to discover what the elusive Grimtotem clan is plotting. Three unknown couriers were spotted visiting the mesa, leaving guarded correspondence scattered across their mountaintop village. Uncovering these secret notes exposes a brewing scheme that threatens the tauren settlements of Thousand Needles. Freewind Post sits precariously on high spires, but its defenders must constantly look over their shoulders at their hostile cousins. The Grimtotem clan has long maintained a tense, resentful stance toward the Horde, clinging to their isolationist strongholds atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn noticed a shift in their behavior when three mysterious agents arrived over successive weeks, conferring with clan leadership in secret. Longhorn suspects these emissaries carried marching orders or alliances meant to undermine Thunder Bluff's presence in the canyon.

Grimtotem tribe. The Grimtotem tribe is an aggressive, fiercely traditionalist tauren clan that refuses to formally swear allegiance to Thrall's Horde. Distinguishable by their dark hides and fierce warpaint, they seek to purge foreign races from Kalimdor and retake ancestral lands by any means necessary. Even as their matriarch, the Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem, resides atop Thunder Bluff playing regional politics, her kin actively raid settlements across Kalimdor. Unlike their peaceful cousins who honor the Earth Mother through reverence, the Grimtotem believe Kalimdor belongs exclusively to the tauren. From youth, they are trained not in the patient harmony of the Great Hunt, but in ruthlessness, stealth, and lethal combat. They harbor immense disdain for the other races that have settled upon their ancient soils. Though Cairne Bloodhoof has welcomed them into Thunder Bluff in an effort to unite all tauren people, the Grimtotem clan stands alone as the only major tribe that has never formally joined Thrall's Horde, maintaining their own insular and violent agenda.

Grish Longrunner. Grish Longrunner is a tauren scout and messenger stationed near the Great Lift, the vital mechanical crossing connecting the southern Barrens with the canyons of Thousand Needles. Serving the interests of the Horde along this bustling boundary, he keeps watch over travelers and coordinates military movement across the frontier. Positioned right beside the towering machinery of the Great Lift, Grish Longrunner stands watch over one of central Kalimdor's most precarious border crossings. The platform elevator is a lifeline connecting the arid wastes of the southern Barrens to the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles below. Between roving quilboar packs and competing territorial threats, travel along this vertical boundary is dangerous, making scouts like Grish essential for keeping the Horde informed and summoning reinforcements where they are sorely needed.

Grizzled Bear Heart. A Grizzled Bear Heart is a biological reagent harvested from the sturdy bears roaming Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital component in the Royal Apothecary Society's grim research into the New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works ceaselessly to develop an engineered blight capable of exterminating both the Scourge and living humanity. In the woodlands of Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel discovered that a unique toxin derived from the heart of a grizzled bear, when combined with arachnid ichor, yields a remarkably lethal concoction. Couriers and Forsaken loyalists hunt down ferocious grizzled bears, giant grizzled bears, and the infamous beast Old Vicejaw to carve out these organs and deliver them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell deep within the Apothecarium of the Undercity.

Grizzled Den. The Grizzled Den is a cavern nestled in the snowy hills just southwest of Kharanos. It serves as a notorious lair for the ferocious, frost-breathing wendigos indigenous to Dun Morogh. Carved deep into the crags southwest of Kharanos, the Grizzled Den is notorious among local mountaineers as the nesting ground of Dun Morogh's wendigo packs. These aggressive, ape-like beasts wield frosty breath against intruders and band together to protect their hollows. Despite the peril, daring hunters regularly brave the cavern's depths to harvest thick wendigo manes, which fetch a respectable sum among craftsmen looking to line cold chairs and carriage seats with insulated fur.

Grizzled Scalp. A Grizzled Scalp is the thick, furred hide taken from grizzled thistle bears roaming the southern forests of Darkshore. While seemingly an odd trophy, these pelts are sought by the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle to supply his hidden wilderness machinery.

Grizzlepaw Ridge. Grizzlepaw Ridge is a rugged, craggy hillside rising south of Thelsamar in Loch Modan. It is notorious among local mountaineers for its dense population of wild bears, led by the legendary beast Ol' Sooty. Overlooking the road south of Thelsamar and bordering Stonesplinter Valley to the west, Grizzlepaw Ridge is rough country dominated by predatory wildlife. The slopes are claimed by territorial bears that pose a hazard to travelers skirting the mountains. Deep within the ridge dwells Ol' Sooty, a massive and unusually fierce bear feared by local hunters. Travelers moving between the dwarven settlements must keep a wary eye on the tree line and rocky terraces above.

Grol'dom Farm. Grol'dom Farm is a modest orcish homestead situated in the northern Barrens along the road between Durotar and the Crossroads. Inhabited by Kranal Fiss and his family, the farm raises swine in the arid plains despite constant harassment from aggressive local quilboars. Established following the settlement of Durotar, Grol'dom Farm represents the Horde's early efforts to farm the dry expanse of the Barrens. Tended by the orc Kranal Fiss and his children, the small homestead primarily raises pigs while braving the harsh wildlife and aggressive Razormane quilboar raiders that prowl the nearby ridges. It is a lonely, rugged outpost that supplies vital sustenance to the emerging orcish nation.

Grom'gol Base Camp. Grom'gol Base Camp is the Horde's primary fortified outpost in Stranglethorn Vale, situated along the western coast of northern Stranglethorn. Commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh, the settlement secures a critical foothold and supply chain in the southern Eastern Kingdoms. With direct zeppelin towers linking to Orgrimmar and the Undercity, it stands as an armed staging ground against local jungle troll tribes and hostile Alliance forces. Carved into the dense jungle of northwestern Stranglethorn Vale, Grom'gol Base Camp is a fortified military bastion commanded by Commander Aggro'gosh. Ringed by defensive palisades and heavily armed grunts, the base camp endures non-stop harassment from Bloodscalp headhunters, lurking naga, and prowling beasts. Despite these threats, its vital strategic location secures safe supply routes north toward Stonard in the Swamp of Sorrows while keeping a watchful eye on Alliance traffic descending from Duskwood or traveling up from Booty Bay.

Grommash Hellscream. Grommash Hellscream was the legendary chieftain of the Warsong clan, a close brother-in-arms to Warchief Thrall, and the first orc to drink the blood of Mannoroth. Though his thirst for battle once bound his people to the Burning Legion, he redeemed the orcish race by slaying the demon lord in Ashenvale at the cost of his own life. Before the Dark Portal ever bridged worlds, Grom Hellscream led the Warsong clan with unyielding ferocity, distinguished by his pitch-black tattooed jaw and the deadly sweep of his two-handed axe, Gorehowl. When Gul'dan and the Shadow Council offered the chalice of demonic strength on Draenor, Grom was the first chieftain to drink the blood of the pit lord Mannoroth. That fateful draught doomed the orcish race to demonic subservience and a burning bloodlust. Yet unlike many chieftains who perished or succumbed entirely, Grom possessed an iron will that kept his fierce spirit intact, surviving the horrors of the old Horde while harboring an unspoken ache for what his people had surrendered.

Grommash Hold. Grommash Hold is the fortified seat of Warchief Thrall, nestled high in the red cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Named in honor of Grommash Hellscream's sacrifice, the fortress serves as the command center and political heart of the new Horde. Perched within the tranquil Valley of Wisdom, Grommash Hold serves as the royal court and strategic sanctum of the Horde. Built into the towering canyon walls, its thick stone interior remains notably dim and chilly—a deliberate choice by Warchief Thrall to keep emissaries, petitioners, and warlords sharp and sober during audiences. Here, Thrall deliberates on the defense of Kalimdor, guided by veteran counselors like Eitrigg and visited by racial chieftains such as Vol'jin.

Grove of the Ancients. Grove of the Ancients is an Alliance delivery quest that directs adventurers out of Darnassus and across the sea to Darkshore. Tasked by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm, the courier carries correspondence to Onu, a venerable Ancient of Lore residing south of Auberdine. Having assisted with matters concerning the Oracle Glade atop Teldrassil, adventurers find themselves brusquely summoned into further service by Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. Not one to waste idle hands, Staghelm tasks the messenger with carrying an urgent dispatch across the sea to the ancient forests of Darkshore, instructing them to book flight aboard a hippogryph from the city.

Grove of the Ancients. The Grove of the Ancients is a sacred night elven sanctuary set amidst old temple ruins in southeastern Darkshore. Nestled beside the Wildbend River, this serene haven serves as a gathering ground for nature spirits and is watched over by the venerable Ancient of Lore, Onu. Tucked away near the southeastern mountains of Darkshore, the Grove of the Ancients stands as a peaceful haven surrounded by aged temple stones. Through its heart flows the surging Wildbend River, providing a quiet refuge amidst a coastline increasingly plagued by corruption and restless wildlife. The grove serves as a meeting place for the Circle of Ancients, where nature spirits and kaldorei tend to the delicate balance of the forest.

Growless Cave. Growless Cave is a frigid cavern carved into the crags of the Alterac Mountains, overrun by ferocious mountain yetis. It is best known as the resting place of the Flame of Uzel, an unholy ceremonial pyre tied to the dark necromancy of Helcular. Tucked away in the snow-dusted heights overlooking the foothills, Growless Cave serves primarily as a den for the territorial mountain yetis that roam Alterac. Travelers navigating the treacherous slopes often steer clear of its mouth, especially when the notorious yeti Skhowl is sighted prowling outside. Beyond the primal danger of the beasts, the cave harbors a sinister past: inside lies the Flame of Uzel, an arcane brazier left behind by the ambitious human mage Helcular. Before his demise, Helcular intended to use the pyre in a dark ritual to achieve lichdom, and its foul warmth once drew the massive predator Frostmaw out from the frozen wastes.

Grub. Grub is an enterprising orc living in a roadside hut just east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. Operating a modest frontier eatery alongside a cook and a baker, he is famous—or perhaps notorious—for introducing travelers to the culinary uses of local vermin. Tucked against the crags just east of the Crossroads, Grub oversees a rustic dwelling shared with Duhng, his cook, and Tarban Hearthgrain, a baker. While life on the plains demands a hearty stomach, Grub takes frontier self-sufficiency to an extreme. Rather than letting the abundant dig rats of the Barrens go to waste, he has turned them into a staple ingredient, offering to teach passing wanderers how to simmer the subterranean rodents into a savory, if unglamorous, stew.

Grull Hawkwind. Grull Hawkwind is a young tauren brave stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. As the son of Chief Hawkwind, he helps guide novice tauren taking their very first steps into the world. He directs young hunters and warriors through their earliest trials to test their resolve and honor their ancestors. Standing proudly beside the braves and elders of Camp Narache, Grull Hawkwind bears both the proud lineage of Chief Hawkwind and the responsibility of preparing the tribe's youth. He serves as an initial mentor for new arrivals on the Red Cloud Mesa, assessing their readiness to serve the Shu'halo. By assigning trials that test stamina, tracking, and survival against local beasts such as plainstriders and mountain cougars, Grull ensures that young tauren understand that balance and respect for nature are foundational to life in Mulgore.

Grund and Gozwin. Grund and Gozwin recounts an ambush at a campsite in the snowy northwestern hills, where a dwarf and a gnome were attacked by a predatory snow leopard. Although the gnome survived thanks to his partner's shotgun, his prized mechanic's log was left behind in the commotion. Adventurers are sent into the hills to recover the delicate notes and slay the stalking beast. While traveling together in the snowy hills, the dwarf Grund and his gnomish companion Gozwin set up an encampment for the evening. As Grund turned his back to prep a boar over the fire, a snow leopard prowler lunged from the brush and grabbed Gozwin in its jaws. Reacting instantly, Grund grabbed his trusty shotgun and blasted a round over the beast's head, startling the predator into dropping the gnome and fleeing into the cold crags.

Grunt Dogran. Grunt Dogran is an orc soldier of the Horde held prisoner deep within the quilboar territory of the southern Barrens. Originally assigned to the Crossroads and later Camp Taurajo, his patrol met with disaster during a raid on Agama'gor. Following his promotion within the Horde military, Grunt Dogran was dispatched from the Crossroads to reinforce Camp Taurajo. While leading a detachment of grunts into the bristled territory of Agama'gor, his unit clashed fiercely with the Bristleback quilboar. Severely injured and crippled during the fray, Dogran could not be carried away by his retreating comrades and was dragged into captivity.

Grunt Logmar. Grunt Logmar is an orc warrior of the Horde stationed in the southern Barrens at Camp Taurajo. Dutiful and vigilant, he monitors threats surrounding the camp and coordinates efforts to locate and aid missing Horde scouts in the region. Stationed among the tauren at Camp Taurajo, Grunt Logmar serves as a watchful orc guard on the southern Barrens frontier. The settlement sits close to hostile quilboar grounds and the mountain passes leading into Stonetalon and Mulgore, requiring constant vigilance. Logmar coordinates scouting reports and reaches out to capable Horde travelers when his comrades find themselves ambushed or captured by local hostiles.

Grunth. Grunth is an energetic young orc orphan living under the care of the Orgrimmar orphanage in the Drag. During Children's Week, he eagerly accompanies Horde champions on grand journeys across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to learn what it means to be a hero. Residing in the Drag of Orgrimmar under the watchful gaze of Orphan Matron Battlewail, Grunth represents the next generation of the newly established Horde. Like many young greenskins raised in Durotar's harsh red wastes, he looks upon armored adventurers with wide-eyed awe and an inexhaustible stream of questions—wondering whether armored warriors are truly terrifying, why lightning on water doesn't kill every fish, and whether he will ever see someone fight an actual dragon.

Gryan Stoutmantle. At Sentinel Hill in Westfall, Gryan Stoutmantle leads the People's Militia. A paladin of the Silver Hand, he returned from Lordaeron to defend his birthplace after Stormwind's crown left it to banditry. Gryan Stoutmantle first served far from Westfall's fields. As a young man, he traveled north to Lordaeron and took vows as a Knight of the Silver Hand. He endured the horrors of the Third War there. News reached him that his native province was collapsing into lawlessness, overrun by organized brigands and abandoned by the crown. Gryan left the northern fronts to defend honest farmers, determined that his home would not fall as the north had.

Gryphon Master Talonaxe. Falstad Wildhammer will not be drawn on who once flew with an old Explorers' League friend, and sends you off to ask the gryphon master. Gryphon Master Talonaxe waits inside the Aerie Peak Aviary. Falstad Wildhammer has no patience for someone sent on behalf of an old Explorers' League member. Who that friend once flew with is not something Falstad knows, and the flight assignments are for the gryphon master to answer. Gryphon Master Talonaxe is to be found inside the Aerie Peak Aviary, and lingering around Falstad will earn real work.

Gryphon Roost. Gryphons take travelers from Stormwind’s eastern ramparts across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, a human gryphon master, manages the roost beside the Trade District. From the eastern ramparts, gryphons carry travelers from Stormwind to Alliance garrisons and settlements across the Eastern Kingdoms. Dungar Longdrink, the seasoned gryphon master, coordinates flights to Ironforge, Lakeshire, Sentinel Hill, and other destinations.

Gryshka's Letter. Gryshka's Letter is a personal note of thanks written by Innkeeper Gryshka of Orgrimmar and addressed to the butcher Zargh at the Crossroads. Sent after receiving a delivery of fresh meat, the letter serves as both a sign of gratitude and an excuse to teach young Horde couriers how to navigate the wind rider flight network. When Zargh ships a bundle of prepared steaks from the arid expanses of the Barrens to Orgrimmar's central tavern, Innkeeper Gryshka pens this note in return. Beyond expressing her satisfaction with the butcher's cuts, the letter reveals a fond—if rugged—appreciation for Zargh, recalling humorous misadventures such as the time he lost a finger while preparing meat. Gryshka concludes with affectionate amusement, remarking that he looks handsome even when bloodied by his trade.

Gryth Thurden. This errand introduces adventurers to Ironforge's gryphon network by tasking them with carrying a bundle of ceremonial tools to the city's gryphon master. Entrusted with the Honorary Picks by Golnir Bouldertoe, the courier must deliver them to Gryth Thurden so they can be dispatched back to Loch Modan. After traveling from Loch Modan to the Great Forge, couriers receive a bundle of Honorary Picks from Golnir Bouldertoe meant for Brock Stoneseeker's mining apprentices. Rather than making the trek back down the mountain passes on foot, Golnir advises taking advantage of the dwarven gryphon network, sending the messenger across the city to coordinate with Ironforge's master handler.

Guard Berton. Guard Berton is a human town guardsman stationed outside the Lakeshire Inn in Redridge Mountains. Frustrated by the bureaucratic delays of Stormwind's legal system, he seeks swift justice against Targorr the Dread, an imprisoned orc leader. While Redridge Mountains buckles under the threat of the Blackrock orc invasion, Guard Berton remains posted outside the Lakeshire Inn. Despite local defenses being pushed to the brink, Berton's attention is fixed on a captive enemy: Targorr the Dread. Targorr was captured and locked away deep within the Stormwind Stockade, sentenced to death for his crimes against the kingdom. Yet with Stormwind's execution postponed indefinitely, Berton refuses to let the brutal raider linger in a cell while Lakeshire bleeds. Taking matters into his own hands, he hires willing adventurers to bypass royal delays and execute the orc directly.

Guard Howe. Guard Howe is a town guardsman stationed near the southern foot of the Lakeshire bridge in the Redridge Mountains. Driven by a personal vendetta against the Blackrock orcs encroaching on the valley, he offers bounties to any adventurer willing to cut down the invaders. Positioned just south of the large stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill, Guard Howe stands watch over the heart of Lakeshire. Like many in the beleaguered town, he sees the encroaching Blackrock orcs as an existential threat to Redridge. Harbouring a bitter desire for revenge against the clan, Howe actively recruits passing mercenaries to hunt orcs in the eastern hills, offering pay in exchange for tangible proof of their defeat.

Guard Thomas. At the bridge west of Eastvale Logging Camp, Guard Thomas watches Elwynn’s eastern frontier. The Stormwind soldier guards local workers from wild predators and murlocs. At the stone bridge over the river toward Eastvale Logging Camp, Guard Thomas holds a quiet but exposed post. The woods around him shelter aggressive creatures, and the logging workers depend on the Stormwind guard for protection. With the army stretched thin, Thomas must rely on travelers to help keep order and carry messages to central command.

name.frFR: La garde du tonneau de Tonnebière

text.enUS: Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel. The Guarded Thunderbrew Barrel rests in the cellar of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. It represents the prized stock of the famed dwarven brewing family, watched over day and night to keep thieves and rivals from meddling with their craft. In the cold snows of Dun Morogh, few things are guarded more fiercely than good ale. Beneath the floorboards of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos, stout casks of potent brew age in peace. The family takes no chances with their stock, posting watchful sentries like Jarven Thunderbrew right beside the barrels to ensure not a single drop is tampered with or siphoned off.

Gubber Blump. Gubber Blump is a dwarf fisherman and trainer stationed along the shores of Auberdine in Darkshore. Positioned on the sands between the docks and the flight master, he is an enthusiastic lover of the angling craft and seafood, particularly fresh crab meat. While most dwarves find comfort beneath stone or beside a roaring forge, Gubber Blump prefers the misty coastline of Darkshore. Stationed along the beach at Auberdine, between the flight master and the ferry pier, Gubber teaches the art of fishing and sells basic angling gear to passing travelers. He holds a deep culinary appreciation for crab meat, though he frequently relies on adventurers to help secure his catches along the dangerous coast, as well as reclaim sentimental family fishing tackle.

Guile of the Raptor. Guile of the Raptor is a quest in which Tor'gan seeks to awaken the dormant warrior spirit within Gor'mul. By harvesting the hearts of Highland Fleshstalkers, Tor'gan plans to fashion an enchanted item imbued with the cunning and predatory power of the raptor. Tor'gan works to restore a listless compatriot named Gor'mul, whose warrior spirit has fallen dormant. Rather than relying on simple persuasion, Tor'gan turns to primal magic to shock Gor'mul back into action. By crafting a charm imbued with the essence of wild predators, he hopes to reintroduce Gor'mul to martial resolve and demonstrate the strength of their new power.

Guile of the Raptor. After the earlier Guile of the Raptor, Tor'gan hands you an orb and sends you to Gor'mul at Hammerfall. Its energy carries the essence of the raptor, meant to stir Gor'mul's spirit and give him new purpose. Tor'gan gives you an orb whose energy is meant to fill Gor'mul with the raptor's essence. He hopes it will rouse the warrior's spirit and set him on a fresh course in life. Once Gor'mul is himself again, Tor'gan means to explain the current state of the Horde to him and gain a great warrior's help in the unceasing battles.

Guile of the Raptor. After Tor'gan's orb gave Gor'mul the raptor's essence, the power he felt has him wondering about the shamans' magic. He sends you to tell Tor'gan he has been convinced, for the time being, and will listen. Gor'mul wonders aloud whether the power coursing through him is the shamans' power that Tor'gan tried to show him. He finds it interesting. He asks you to tell Tor'gan that he has been convinced, for the time being, and will hear what Tor'gan has to say.

Gunther Arcanus. Gunther Arcanus is an exceptionally powerful necromancer dwelling on an isolated island in Brightwater Lake. Slain during the Third War and raised into undeath, he managed to shatter the Lich King's mental grip entirely on his own. Long believing he was the sole undead possessing free will, he defended his retreat against all outsiders until discovered by the Forsaken. When the Scourge swept across the north during the Third War, Gunther perished to the Plague of Undeath and was raised into servitude. Unlike most who required the Lich King's power to weaken or Lady Sylvanas to break their chains, Gunther's raw arcane mastery and sheer willpower allowed him to shake off the Lich King's mental domination entirely by himself. Convinced that every other walking corpse remained a mindless thrall of the Scourge, he retreated to an island in Tirisfal Glades, surrounding himself with shambling guardians and cutting off all contact with the living and dead alike.

Gunther's Retreat. Gunther's Retreat is an isolated island sanctuary set in Brightwater Lake in central Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the refuge of Gunther Arcanus, a renegade necromancer who broke free from the Scourge through raw willpower. Distrustful of all outsiders, the recluse surrounds his campsite with loyal undead minions to keep intruders away. Situated amid the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, Gunther's Retreat is an unassuming island encampment easily mistaken for another pocket of the Scourge. Its master, Gunther Arcanus, achieved what few mortal sorcerers could: when raised in undeath, his arcane mastery allowed him to tear away his soul from the Lich King's iron grip without any outside help. Mistrusting everyone, Gunther assumed the rest of the undead wandering Lordaeron were still puppets of the Scourge. He retired to this lonely isle to practice his craft in peace, posting zombie sentinels to tear apart anyone who crosses the water.

Gunther's Spellbook. Gunther's Spellbook is a personal arcane tome tied to a mysterious mage dwelling in Tirisfal Glades. Imbued with an enchantment by Bethor Iceshard, the book serves as proof that other practitioners of magic have successfully broken free of the Lich King's control, though the true history between its owner and the Forsaken remains to be unraveled.

Gurda Ragescar. Gurda Ragescar was an orc stationed at a small Horde outpost southwest of Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Alongside Feran Strongwind, she fell defending their camp against local perils in the shadowed forest. Resting just southwest of the fortified walls of Splintertree Post, Gurda Ragescar maintained a modest Horde camp under the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Deep within territory contested by night elven defenders and wild beasts, maintaining such isolated positions is perilous work. Gurda, along with Feran Strongwind and their detachment of guards, was ultimately overrun and killed at their post, leaving only the remnants of their final stand for passing allies to discover.

Gurubashi Arena. Gurubashi Arena is an ancient stone colosseum standing in southern Stranglethorn Vale, originally built by the mighty Gurubashi Empire. In the present day, it serves as a chaotic free-for-all proving ground where pirates and wandering brawlers shed blood over locked chests of treasure. Long before human or orc set foot in Stranglethorn Vale, the Gurubashi Arena—known also as the Great Arena—was built as a monument to martial strength by the sprawling Gurubashi troll empire. In ancient days, champions fought to the death upon its sands until the earth was slick with troll blood.

Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde is a night elf residing in the coastal port of Auberdine. Stationed along the misty Darkshore coast, she watches the tides and directs travelers to investigate the strange remains washing ashore. Her concerns center on the mysterious sea creatures and massive turtles whose carcasses have begun littering the northern beaches. Gwennyth Bly'Leggonde makes her home in Auberdine, the bustling seaside haven of Darkshore. While many in town concern themselves with the forest or shipping across the Veiled Sea, Gwennyth keeps her gaze firmly on the coastline. The tides have recently turned grim, depositing the remains of colossal marine life onto the surf. To understand what is happening in the waters offshore, she relies on willing adventurers to scour the sands, retrieve skeletal samples, and bring back answers.

Gyro... What?. Having brought Lotwil Veriatus the Frost Oil from Coolant Heads Prevail, you find Lotwil still absorbed in a contraption in the Badlands. One small but crucial part is missing: a gyrochronatom. Lotwil Veriatus, distracted by the work, says you have done the job well beyond all standards and tells you to come and apply for work if you ever meet in Kharanos. Then comes a hurried scramble to catch hold of something, and the real request: a gyrochronatom. It is a small part, Lotwil admits, but a crucial one. Bring one and the project should be ready to complete.

Gyrodrillmatic Excavationators. Deep in the Dwarven District of Stormwind, Shoni the Shilent is preparing a fleet of massive tunneling machines intended for transit to Dun Morogh. Stalled by a shortage of mechanical parts, she dispatches adventurers into the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan to harvest intact gears and innards from rogue automatons. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, gnomish engineers work tirelessly to support their displaced kin. Among them is Shoni the Shilent, who oversees an ambitious subterranean venture: a fleet of gyrodrillmatic excavationators destined for Dun Morogh. The project faces a critical bottleneck, as she lacks the necessary components to get the massive digging rigs operational.

Gyromast's Retrieval. Shipwrecked on the misty coast of Darkshore, the eccentric gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast seeks aid to restore his mechanical first mate. His vital winding key was shattered upon the rocks and scavenged by the local wildlife and murlocs. Recovering the three pieces is the first step toward getting his crew back in working order. Gelkak Gyromast is an odd sight along the gloomy sands of Darkshore: a gnome pirate stranded far from the typical sea routes of the South Seas. According to Gelkak, his vessel met an unfortunate end just off the coastline after being attacked and sunk by aggressive threshadons. Washing ashore amid the flotsam, he found himself utterly marooned and separated from his trusty crew.

Gyromast's Revenge. Gelkak Gyromast seeks payback against the local murlocs who plundered his wrecked ship along the Darkshore coastline. To carry out his vendetta, the eccentric captain sends adventurers to reactivate his mechanical first mate, the Threshwackonator 4100. Stranded upon the misty strands of Darkshore, Gelkak Gyromast refuses to accept defeat at the hands of the shore-dwelling murlocs. Having salvaged the pieces needed to fuel his schemes, the eccentric captain sets his sights on complete retaliation against the tribe and their chief. Rather than wading into the surf with cutlass in hand, Gelkak relies on heavy engineering to exact his vengeance, entrusting a winding key to any landlubber brave enough to handle his mechanical subordinate.

Gyromechanic Gear. A Gyromechanic Gear is a salvaged piece of precision engineering recovered from the fallout outside Gnomeregan. Gnomish inventors in Kharanos seek these specific gears to construct an experimental device capable of reversing leper gnome mutations. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan to purge the trogg invasion, it corrupted a vast portion of the surviving gnome population into mad, irradiated leper gnomes. Refusing to abandon their twisted kin, inventors Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket set to work drafting schematics for the Recombobulator—an ambitious contraption designed to undo the radiation's horrific effects. Building the prototype requires precision mechanisms capable of enduring volatile internal pressures, particularly Gyromechanic Gears and complementary Restabilization Cogs. Because local manufacturing collapsed with the fall of their capital, researchers are forced to scavenge these delicate parts directly from the hostile leper gnomes roaming Dun Morogh.

Hagar Lightninghoof. Hagar Lightninghoof is a tauren scout stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Driven by rumors of a strange clutch hidden in the canyon depths, he investigates reports of an alien egg guarded fiercely by local wind serpents. While stationed among the towering bluffs of Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof caught wind of rumors regarding an unnatural egg nestled deep inside a cavern below. The local wind serpents guarded the nest with unusual ferocity, keeping curious scouts at bay. Seeking an adventurer bold enough to brave the serpents' den, Hagar hopes to study the specimen firsthand and discern what manner of beast could warrant such defensive instincts from the canyon's natural predators.

Halaan Hawk-Eye. Halaan Hawk-Eye is a Skyborne lookout stationed atop the watchtower of Thendal Village on Zephras Isle. Lacking both magical sensitivity and the mystic skysight of his peers, he relies instead on keen mundane vision to monitor the surrounding island. From his perch, he tracks the distant anchor pylons and warns visitors of their faltering arcane stability. Perched high above Thendal Village, Halaan Hawk-Eye serves his people without the gifts common to many Skyborne. He cannot draw upon the arcane power flowing through the ley lines beneath Zephras Isle, nor can he gaze between worlds through the mystical skysight. Instead, Halaan relies entirely on his sharp natural senses. From his vantage point on the watchtower, he scans the horizon to observe the island's anchor pylons, calling attention to their increasingly volatile and inconsistent arcane energies.

Haldarr Encampment. The Haldarr Encampment is a corrupted satyr outpost nestled in western Azshara, situated northeast of the Shadowsong Shrine and southwest of Valormok. Densely inhabited by the vicious Haldarr satyrs, it stands as a dangerous blight among the ancient elven ruins. It is also where an injured Night Elf Sentinel, Keldara Sunblade, can be found. Perched among the broken stones of western Azshara, the Haldarr Encampment serves as a gathering ground for the Haldarr clan of satyrs. These twisted creatures, ancient remnants of the Highborne cursed by demonic corruption during the Sundering, actively hunt and harass any who traverse the autumn forests. The dense settlement poses an ongoing threat to both the Horde forces stationed at nearby Valormok and the dwindling Night Elf sentinels trying to monitor the region.

Halgar's Summons. Halgar's Summons is a formal directive given to rising Forsaken warlocks who have reached a critical threshold in their dark craft. Master Carendin Halgar requires their presence in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity to begin rigorous advanced training. Answering his call sets the stage for summoning and binding dangerous entities from the Nether. When a warlock operating around Brill or the Tirisfal wilderness demonstrates adequate control over basic fel energies, word reaches the deeper subterranean halls of the Undercity. Senior practitioners such as Ageron Kargal serve as talent spotters, relaying notices to those who show genuine promise. To be summoned by Carendin Halgar is both a rare privilege and a perilous undertaking, indicating that basic imps and petty curses no longer suffice for the practitioner's education.

Hall of Arms. The Hall of Arms serves as the headquarters of Ironforge's military might and the chief arsenal of the dwarven kingdom. Located within the Military Ward, this fortified compound trains dwarven combatants and orchestrates the deployment of heavy armor and aerial war machines. Situated in the southeastern corner of the Military Ward, the Hall of Arms is the operational command center for the armed forces of Ironforge. Beyond housing veteran trainers for warriors and hunters, the expansive facility serves as a massive depot and staging ground for mechanized warfare. Heavy steam tanks are assembled and maintained on-site to reinforce Alliance battlefields, while gyrocopters and flying machines are brought up via industrial conveyor belts and launched directly through vertical access shafts in the cavern ceiling toward the Ironforge Airfield above.

Hall of Arms (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, recruits train with the Stormwind Army in the Hall of Arms, south of the Main Hall. The Hall of Arms rings with blunted steel and the measured cadence of instruction. South of Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall, the wing trains human fighters and devout aspirants who take up arms for the Stormwind Army. Veteran battle instructors and paladin mentors teach the postures and disciplines needed to defend Elwynn Forest from kobolds, Defias bandits, and gnoll raiders. Across the courtyard, clerics and scholars study ancient tomes in the Library Wing.

Hall of Arms (Tyr's Hand). The Hall of Arms is a heavily guarded wing within Tyr's Hand Abbey in southeastern Eastern Plaguelands. It serves as a staging ground and barracks for the martial vanguard of the Scarlet Crusade garrisoned at the stronghold. Positioned across the abbey from the library, it houses some of the crusade's most zealous and well-armored fighters. Situated to the south of the abbey's main hall, the Hall of Arms functions as an armory and quarters for the militant forces of Tyr's Hand. While the opposing wing holds archives and holy texts, this wing is dedicated purely to the discipline of war. Clad in heavy armor and sworn to eradicate the undead and anyone deemed impure, the Scarlet defenders stationed here maintain a tireless watch over their eastern bastion, keeping weapons sharpened and shields polished against the surrounding horrors of the Plaguelands.

Hall of Champions. The Hall of Champions is the inner sanctum of the Scarlet Monastery's armory wing. It serves as the seat of Herod, the Scarlet Champion, and a proving ground for the Scarlet Crusade's elite. Situated past the Footman's Armory, the Hall of Champions lies at the heart of the monastery's armory wing. Here Herod, the Scarlet Champion, holds sway over the Crusade's fiercest fighters, and Scarlet trainees harden their resolve to purge Lordaeron of all undead and outsiders.

Hall of Explorers. The Hall of Explorers is the sprawling archaeological wing of Ironforge and the bustling headquarters of the dwarven Explorers' League. Part museum, part archive, and part expedition command, it gathers relics, fossils, and ancient tomes from every corner of Azeroth to piece together the forgotten origins of the dwarven race. Occupying the northeastern cavern of Ironforge, the Hall of Explorers—sometimes referred to as the Assembly of Explorers—serves as the nerve center for all Alliance-sanctioned archaeological endeavors. Under the direction of High Explorer Muninn Magellas, scholars and field agents coordinate digs across distant lands, shipping back mysterious relics, ancient titan machinery, and prehistoric bones. The vast Library at its center functions as both a public museum and a restricted storehouse of historical lore.

Hall of Gears. The Hall of Gears is a multi-tiered industrial chamber situated inside the fallen city of Gnomeregan, just past the Clockwerk Run. Once a bustling center of mechanical movement, it has fallen into ruin, flooded with toxic sludge, roaming oozes, and irradiated troggs. Positioned just beyond the Clockwerk Run, the Hall of Gears illustrates the catastrophic collapse of the gnome capital. Divided into two main levels, the chamber's upper catwalks are held by aggressive, irradiated troggs that claw through collapsed access shafts. Below, the floor sits drenched in pools of radioactive fallout, where corrosive slimes and living poison elementals thrive in the toxic runoff.

Hall of Legends. The Hall of Legends is the elite military sanctuary and officer barracks of the Horde, nestled within Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength.
