text.enUS: Hillsbrad Human Skull. A gruesome war trophy harvested from slain human defenders and townsfolk across the Hillsbrad Foothills. These skulls are collected by Forsaken stationed at Tarren Mill as grim mementos of the relentless assault against the local human settlements. As conflict rages between the Forsaken of Tarren Mill and the human inhabitants of Southshore and surrounding settlements, severed skulls serve as physical proof of the slaughter. While Deathstalkers and soldiers carry out the systematic purge ordered by Darthalia during the Battle of Hillsbrad, other guards stuck on watch duty crave a piece of the carnage. Deathguard Samsa eagerly solicits these trophies from frontline fighters, taking twisted pleasure in amassing the remains of the very people the Forsaken once lived among in life.

name.zhCN: 希尔斯布莱德城镇文档

text.enUS: Hillsbrad Town Registry. The Hillsbrad Town Registry is an official municipal ledger kept inside the town hall of the Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as an accounting of the settlement's surviving citizens, landowners, and civic records, making it a key strategic target during the Forsaken offensive against the human stronghold. Resting in the town hall near the podium of Magistrate Burnside, the Hillsbrad Town Registry documents the population, households, and administrative rights of Hillsbrad. As the Forsaken from Tarren Mill push to break human resistance in the foothills, Darthalia commands Horde champions to infiltrate the town hall, eliminate the council, and seize this ledger. Confiscating the registry strips Hillsbrad of its civic order and provides the Undercity with valuable intelligence on the surviving population and their assets.

Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is an urgent journey undertaken by Horde rogues suffering from a debilitating tropical toxin. Contracted during an infiltration mission in the Barrens, the affliction requires the specialized expertise of Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill. Seeking his aid promises both a life-saving cure and instruction in the art of concocting deadly poisons. Following the daring infiltration of the Venture Company's tower north of the Sludge Fen, rogues find themselves afflicted by Zanzil's altered mixture. The poison wreaks havoc on the body, dulling reflexes and threatening life itself. Recognizing the severity of the affliction, rogue trainer Shenthul in Orgrimmar admits that local remedies are inadequate and directs the poisoned operative across the sea to the Eastern Kingdoms.

Hinott's Assistance. Hinott's Assistance is the culmination of a Horde rogue's journey to overcome Zanzil's deadly creeping poison. Waiting upon apothecary Serge Hinott in Tarren Mill, the afflicted operative receives an antidote to the toxin alongside foundational training in alchemical venomcraft. After contracting a virulent, mind-altering toxin during an assignment in the Barrens, Horde rogues are directed north to Tarren Mill to consult Serge Hinott. A Forsaken chemist of singular focus, Hinott displays professional awe toward the poison concocted by the jungle troll exile Zanzil. While unconcerned with the troll's identity or lineage, Hinott openly commends the brew's vicious efficacy, eager to study its mechanism before formulating an antidote.

Hints of a New Plague?. Quae has gone through the folder and learned that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. Quae is in poor shape after clashing with orcs and cannot help Kinelory, who will need your protection when she heads for the farm to steal any of Jorell's research not yet sent to Tarren Mill. Quae reads through the folder and finds that Apothecary Jorell is running deadly experiments at Go'Shek Farm. How that touches Hillsbrad is unclear to Quae, yet Phin would not want it to go on. Some of Jorell's research has already been sent to Tarren Mill.

Hints of a New Plague?. Quae and Kin have been watching Go'Shek Farm for days. Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south, and they suspect the courier carries notes bound for Tarren Mill. Quae wants those documents and asks whether you are a skilled tracker. Quae is not surprised that Phin Odelic sent you to check on them, since Phin worries too much. Quae and Kin have been watching the farm for days. Not long ago Kin saw a courier come out of a small house to the south. Kin talks a lot, but Quae can always trust Kin's senses in dangerous areas.

Hints of a New Plague?. Phin Odelic leads a band of adventurers looking into odd happenings in the area, and believes the undead are involved. Two companions, Quae and Kinelory, headed for Go'Shek Farm, in the Arathi Highlands. No word has come from them for days. Not long ago, a cousin of Phin's in Hillsbrad had to put down his dog, Stanley. The beast had mystically swollen to a huge size and savagely turned on anyone who came near. Phin believes the undead are involved in the odd happenings, and the group is looking for signs to prove it.

Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is ready to head down to the farm and wants you at her side. She fears the undead may be doing harm back in Hillsbrad the longer they wait, and you are asked to see her safely back to Quae. After the earlier steps of the investigation, Kinelory is ready to act. She asks you to come with her down to the farm. You are to see her safely back to Quae, and anyone who cares about the people of Hillsbrad is urged to protect her.

Hints of a New Plague?. Kinelory is back from the farm, none the worse for wear, and Quae has the items she brought. Quae and Kinelory mean to stay in Arathi a while longer, so it falls to you to carry word to Phin Odelic in Southshore. Quae is pleased with how well you looked after Kinelory, who has come back in better shape than after a night at the tavern. The items from the farm should give Phin Odelic some idea of what is happening out in Arathi. Since the farm was attacked, Quae and Kinelory plan to stay put a little longer in case of retaliation, and ask you to go back to Southshore and speak to Phin.

Hippogryph Harassment. Hippogryph Harassment is a local task concerning an aggressive flock of wild hippogryphs nesting southeast of Shen'dar Village. Travelers passing along the nearby road have come under frequent attack from the territorial beasts inhabiting the Shen'dar Highlands. To secure the passage, adventurers are called upon to cull the flock's youths, protectors, and their commanding matriarch. Travelers navigating the roads near Shen'dar Village face a rising danger from the skies. A wild flock of hippogryphs has recently claimed the rugged territory southeast of the settlement, carving out active nesting grounds in the Shen'dar Highlands. While hippogryphs are known across Kalimdor as noble beasts occasionally bonded to elven riders, untamed flocks guard their territory with fierce ferocity. Any wagon or lone traveler traversing the paths below has become a target for aerial ambushes, disrupting vital passage and leaving the village vulnerable to isolation if the creatures are left unchecked.

Hippogryph Muisek. After your trials with the muisek vessel, Witch Doctor Uzer'i asks you to deal with a different creature. Frayfeather hippogryphs in the High Wilderness are to be slain and shrunk into the vessel at once, so that their muisek is kept. Witch Doctor Uzer'i has judged you trustworthy and gifted with the vessel, and now wants the spirit of a different creature. Hippogryphs are old companions of the night elves, and their spirits are loyal and steadfast. Ten Frayfeather hippogryphs of any kind are to be killed, each shrunk and captured quickly with the vessel so that its muisek is preserved. Uzer'i places them in the High Wilderness, southward from the camp.

Hive'Ashi. Hive'Ashi is a sprawling silithid colony dominating the northern sands of Silithus. As one of three major insectoid hives in the region, its creeping tunnels and towering mounds churn with countless hostile workers, defenders, and stingers. Situated in northern Silithus, Hive'Ashi serves as a prime hive-complex for the re-emerging silithid swarms. Its chitinous spires carve out a distinct territory among the dunes, sending foraging workers and venomous defenders south and east toward the Swarming Pillar. Anyone seeking to understand the strange, coordinated intelligence stirring within the desert wastes inevitably finds their path leading directly into the dangerous, buzzing tunnels beneath these mounds.

Hive'Regal. Hive'Regal is a massive silithid hive burrowed into the southern reaches of Silithus. As one of the three primary insectoid colonies dominating the arid wastes, it teems with aggressive silithid castes that threaten to overrun the surrounding desert. Sprawling across southern Silithus, Hive'Regal represents one of the greatest concentrations of silithid activity in Kalimdor. Its towering resin spires and cavernous underground tunnels churn with dangerous insectoid broods, from venomous spitfires and burrowers to predatory slavemakers. The hive acts as a coordinated warren, aggressively defending its perimeter and harvesting organic material from any unfortunate travelers who wander too close to its borders.

Hive'Zora. Hive'Zora is one of the three major silithid colony mounds dominating the arid expanse of Silithus. Located along the western edge of the desert, this teeming subterranean hive crawls with aggressive insectoid castes serving the greater swarm. Rising out of the barren sand dunes of western Silithus, Hive'Zora serves as a bustling hub of insectoid activity. Great, porous stone spires and mounds mark the entrances into deep subterranean tunnels dug out by silithid burrowers. Waywatchers and reavers patrol the perimeter relentlessly, while tunneling castes and hive sisters brood within the depths below. For the Cenarion Circle and other scouts keeping watch over the desert, the hive represents a terrifying sign of the insectoid menace steadily reclaiming the ancient frontier.

Hogger. In southwestern Elwynn Forest, Hogger leads the Riverpaw gnolls in raids on farms and travelers. His violent attacks have earned him a bounty from the Stormwind Marshals. Hogger commands the Riverpaw pack from Hogger Hill in southwestern Elwynn Forest. Since the Third War, the gnolls have grown bolder and more coordinated in their raids on nearby homesteads. The Riverpaw have joined forces with the Defias Brotherhood, exchanging their raw ferocity for arms, tactical direction, and magical support. To protect Elwynn's borders and trade routes from further bloodshed, Marshal Dughan has posted a bounty on Hogger's head.

Hollow Vulture Bone. Hollow Vulture Bones are lightweight, durable skeletal remains harvested from the scavengers of the Shimmering Flats. At the Mirage Raceway, goblin mechanics prize them as specialized building materials to lighten their rocket cars without sacrificing structural integrity. Speed is everything out on the salt, and weight is the enemy of speed. While standard engineering leans heavily on iron and copper, the goblin pit crews at the Mirage Raceway turn to whatever the desert provides to gain an edge. Vulture bones are naturally hollow yet remarkably sturdy, providing the perfect strength-to-weight ratio for internal brackets, steering rigs, and minor structural supports. For chief tinkerers like Pozzik, harvesting bones from local scavengers is a practical and cheap shortcut to shaved seconds on the track.

Holt Thunderhorn. Holt Thunderhorn is a tauren hunter trainer stationed upon Hunter Rise in the elevated city of Thunder Bluff. He instructs novice and seasoned track-masters in their craft, offering basic martial guidance and pointing maturing marksmen toward specialized trials across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on Hunter Rise above the sweeping plains of Mulgore, Holt Thunderhorn serves the Horde as a seasoned instructor in ranged combat, tracking, and survival. Like many elders of his craft, he guides young tauren as they make the transition from roaming hunters into disciplined defenders of their new capital.

Homeward Bound. Homeward Bound is a Horde quest that tasks adventurers with rescuing Pao'ka Swiftmountain, a young tauren naturalist stranded in the wyvern nesting grounds of Highperch. After getting separated and lost while studying the dangerous beasts, Pao'ka must be escorted safely down the cliffs back toward Whitereach Post. Pao'ka Swiftmountain accompanied the elder Motega Firemane to Thousand Needles to study the unique wildlife of the canyon floor and its towering stone pillars. Driven by curiosity and overconfidence, Pao'ka crept alone into the heights of Highperch to observe the local wyverns firsthand. The territorial beasts drove him off, leaving the young scholar stranded, terrified, and hiding among the crags for days.

Honor Students. Mining instructor Brock Stoneseeker rewards promising young apprentices in Thelsamar with honorary mining picks. To arrange delivery of the tools from Ironforge, he directs adventurers to enlist the aid of the local gryphon master, Thorgrum Borrelson. In the dwarf town of Thelsamar, mining is more than an occupation—it is a cornerstone of daily survival and dwarven pride. Brock Stoneseeker watches dozens of fresh recruits pass through his training, drilling them on rock composition and tunnel safety. For the students who distinguish themselves above the rest, tradition demands recognition in the form of a finely crafted honorary pick. Because local supply is limited, obtaining these picks requires reaching across Khaz Modan into the heart of Ironforge.

Honorary Picks. The Honorary Picks are a bundle of ceremonial tools crafted in Ironforge for young dwarven mining apprentices. Entrusted to travelers by way of the gryphon network, they are delivered to Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar to mark his students' readiness to work the rich ore veins of Loch Modan. In dwarven society, mining is far more than a trade; it is a cultural cornerstone that keeps the great forges burning and the kingdom supplied with iron and stone. The Honorary Picks represent formal recognition for novice prospectors learning under Brock Stoneseeker in Thelsamar. Sourced directly from Ironforge, these picks are presented to students who have proven their dedication and are ready to tackle the open ore deposits across Loch Modan.

Horde. The Horde is a coalition of outcast nations united under Warchief Thrall to secure their mutual survival and freedom. Anchored by the shamanic bond of the orcs, Darkspear trolls, and tauren across Kalimdor, the faction also maintains an uneasy alliance of convenience with the Forsaken in Lordaeron. Beset by historical grievances and hostile neighbors, the Horde values strength, action, and honor over political maneuverings. The modern Horde bears little resemblance to the demonic army that marched through the Dark Portal in the First and Second Wars. After shattering the Burning Legion's grasp upon his people, Warchief Thrall led the orcs across the Great Sea to Kalimdor to build a spiritual homeland founded on ancestral traditions and honor. Along the way, Thrall forged lasting ties with Vol'jin's displaced Darkspear trolls and Cairne Bloodhoof's tauren tribes, fighting side by side to drive off centaur and demonic incursions during the Third War.

Horde Presence. Horde Presence is a military strike commissioned by the orc Kadrak at the border of the Barrens and Ashenvale. Prompted by an intercepted missive, the Horde sends a champion high into Stonetalon Peak to eliminate the dryad Rynthariel and plant a Horde banner directly inside the Talon Den. Guarding the northern boundary of the Barrens, Kadrak stands watchful against encroachments from the Alliance and the night elves. When a messenger carrying a runed scroll is cut down, Kadrak decodes the missive and traces its origin to Rynthariel the Keymaster, an influential dryad stationed in Stonetalon Peak. Rather than merely defending the mountain passes, Kadrak chooses an aggressive response to deter any future scouts from probing Horde territory.

name.frFR: Service de traumatologie de la Horde

text.enUS: Horde Trauma. Horde Trauma is a summons directing accomplished Horde medics to report to Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands. Doctor Gregory Victor, the chief physician of the Horde's trauma division, is looking to recruit and evaluate skilled hands capable of saving lives under extreme pressure. Answering the call places a medic directly into the grim, high-stakes reality of front-line field surgery. In Orgrimmar's Valley of Spirits, the orc first aid trainer Arnok delivers word to proficient healers that they have caught the attention of Doctor Gregory Victor himself. Victor oversees Horde Trauma from the fortified outpost of Hammerfall, tucked away in the contested hills of the Arathi Highlands. Arnok views the summons not merely as an order, but as the pinnacle of professional advancement for any battlefield surgeon.

Horizon Scout. The Horizon Scout is a sunken vessel resting on the ocean floor in the Ruined Reaches off the southern coast of Azshara. While its captain remains stranded ashore, several crew members remain trapped in the submerged hull, kept alive beneath the waves by an arcane water-breathing enchantment. Resting beneath the waves among the treacherous shoals of the Ruined Reaches, the Horizon Scout met a violent end off Azshara's jagged coast. While Captain Vanessa Beltis managed to reach land on a nearby peninsula, a portion of the crew went down with the hull. Miraculously, the survivors inside have not drowned; a gnome named Roland Geardabbler maintains a sustained magical bubble of water breathing that preserves them within the wreckage. Surrounded by hostile aquatic predators and predatory naga, the remaining sailors wait in the dark forward compartments, unable to surface on their own.

Horn of Arra'chea. The Horn of Arra'chea is a hunting trophy taken from the legendary kodo Arra'chea, who wanders the plains of Mulgore. Claimed at the behest of High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, the horn serves as definitive proof that an aspiring hunter has the discipline and tracking prowess to provide for the Shu'halo. Though passing the initial Rites of the Earthmother grants a youth their rightful place atop Thunder Bluff, High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof expects his people to continually prove their worth. For the tauren, identity is bound directly to the hunt and their enduring harmony with the land. Cairne tests young hunters by tasking them with tracking down Arra'chea, a massive, lone kodo bull roaming the grasslands below. Taking Arra'chea's horn proves mastery over the fundamental art of tracking prey across vast distances.

Horn of Awakening. The Horn of Awakening is a sounding instrument kept in a chest by Kerlonian Evershade in southern Darkshore. It is used to rouse the drowsy druid whenever he collapses into a slumber on the road to Ashenvale. Kerlonian Evershade, a Druid of the Claw recently awoken from centuries inside the Emerald Dream, finds himself persistently lethargic in the waking realm. Journeying south toward Maestra's Post, he entrusts this horn to travelers willing to escort him. Whenever exhaustion overtakes him along the perilous wilderness trail, a clear blast from the instrument jolts his senses, prodding him back to his feet before wild beasts or cultists can seize upon his slumber.

Horn of Echeyakee. The Horn of Echeyakee is a hunting instrument provided by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. Sounding it among the ancient kodo remains northeast of the settlement calls forth Whitemist, the legendary white predator of the Barrens. Given to initiates testing their prowess in the hunt, the horn's call echoes across the savannah to summon Echeyakee, whose name translates from Taur-ahe as 'Whitemist.' Known as the king of the savannah cats, Echeyakee is revered by tauren hunters as both mercy and death, striking so swiftly that his quarry feels neither terror nor suffering. The horn is meant to be sounded only at the great predator's lair, a sun-bleached nest of giant kodo bones tucked behind the hills northeast of the Crossroads.

Horrors in the Highland. Rethiel the Greenwarden senses a foul corruption seeping through a mountain gully into the unsalted waters above the Wetlands. Adventurers must ascend to the excavation sites to slay a Highland Horror and recover its root core. Rethiel discovers that an ancient energy is stirring, warning that ongoing digging threatens the safety of everyone in the region. Deep in the Wetlands, Rethiel the Greenwarden senses a disturbing shift in the land. A foul taint seeps through a mountain gully, infecting the freshwater creatures inhabiting the highlands above. Unlike the hardy life shaped by the brackish lowland waters, these freshwater beings have never known the sea's protective salt, leaving them entirely defenseless against spreading evil. Rethiel calls upon adventurers to venture up to the excavation sites, slay a Highland Horror, and retrieve its root core.

Hostile Takeover. Gelriz has been muscling out the moguls appointed by the trade princes and now makes a move on the most notorious pirate of all, and Baron Revilgaz will not stand for it. In response, Kebok in Booty Bay directs adventurers to steal strange blue crystals that Venture Company geologists have been finding near Lake Nazferiti. Gelriz has stepped over the line by shoving aside moguls chosen by the trade princes and making a move on the most notorious pirate of all. Baron Revilgaz refuses to permit such insolence, instructing Kebok to handle the intrusion however he sees fit. Kebok's chosen response is outright theft, targeting the strange blue stones that Venture Company mining crews have been unearthing.

Houndmaster Loksey. Houndmaster Loksey is the officer charged with breeding and training the fearsome war dogs of the Scarlet Crusade. Stationed in the Scarlet Monastery's Library wing, he directs packs of hounds to hunt down undead, intruders, and perceived heretics. His merciless discipline has made the Monastery's beasts infamous throughout Tirisfal Glades. Within the heavily fortified walls of the Scarlet Monastery, Houndmaster Loksey commands the training of vicious tracking and attack dogs. The Scarlet Crusade relies on these trained hounds to sniff out plague-tainted corpses, uncover hidden infiltrators, and run down any survivors fleeing the zealots' wrath. Loksey holds absolute authority over the hounds guarding the Library wing, ensuring his charges are primed to tear intruders apart limb by limb.

House of Nobles. The House of Nobles is the hereditary aristocratic council that helps administer the kingdom of Stormwind from Stormwind Keep. Holding immense leverage over regional land, taxation, and trade, their refusal to pay the rebuilt city's laborers ignited the bloody riots that ultimately shook the realm. Composed of Stormwind's most powerful patrician bloodlines, the House of Nobles serves as the primary advisory body to the Crown. Because the aristocracy owns the majority of the arable land throughout Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood, they wield outsized authority over commerce, regional magistrates, and royal decrees. While the boy-king Anduin Wrynn and Highlord Bolvar Fordragon officially rule the kingdom, the council routinely ties the throne's hands in red tape, asserting the power to stall trials, block executions, and meddle in provincial administration.

name.frFR: Quelle est l'ampleur de la menace ?

text.enUS: How Big a Threat?. How Big a Threat? is an Alliance quest given by Terenthis in Auberdine. Having witnessed furbolg madness taking root across Teldrassil, the night elf druid directs scouts to investigate local furbolg settlements in Darkshore to confirm whether the same dark taint has crossed the sea. The night elves of northern Kalimdor have long maintained cordial or peaceful relations with indigenous furbolg tribes. However, following the Third War, strange corruptions began unhinging furbolg minds in Teldrassil, resulting in violent kidnappings and feral attacks against their former allies. Stationed in Auberdine, the druid Terenthis fears that this sinister affliction is not isolated to the World Tree, but is actively spreading among the mainland tribes along the misty coasts of Darkshore.

name.frFR: Quelle est l'ampleur de la menace ?

text.enUS: How Big a Threat?. How Big a Threat? is an Alliance quest offered by the night elf Terenthis in Auberdine. Having already scouted the hostile Blackwood furbolg camp south of town, adventurers are sent to cull the corrupted pathfinders and windtalkers before their frenzy threatens the settlement. Following initial scouting south of Auberdine, the Sentinels have determined that the Blackwood furbolgs pose an immediate danger to Darkshore's refugees and defenders. Terenthis tasks combat-capable travelers with striking directly at their camp, eliminating Blackwood Pathfinders and Windtalkers to break their offensive momentum.

Howling Vale. Tucked away in north-central Ashenvale near the Felwood border, the Howling Vale is a darkened dell overrun by savage, alien wolf-beasts known as the Terrowulf worgen. Hidden deep within its caves lies the ancient Shrine of Mel'Thandris, an Elune-blessed ruin tied intimately to the tragic origins of the worgen curse on Kalimdor. North of the road toward Felwood, the calm majesty of Ashenvale gives way to eerie, predatory howling. The vale shelters ancient trees alongside corrupted Terrowulf packlords and aggressive wildlife. At its heart lies a cave enshrining the memory of Mel'Thandris, an ancient night elf priestess. While the shrine once stood as a place of quiet devotion, its tranquil halls have fallen into ruined disrepair, defiled by feral wolf-men whose origin puzzles the Sentinels stationed nearby.

Howling in the Hills. Howling in the Hills is an Alliance bounty offered by Verner Osgood in Lakeshire to hunt down Yowler, the fearsome alpha leading the Redridge gnolls. With Stormwind's military stretched too thin fighting the Blackrock orcs to defend the local borders, Lakeshire relies on visiting adventurers to break the gnoll pack's command. Even after culling the lesser gnolls raiding the paths around Lakeshire, their ominous calls continue to echo through the Redridge ridges. Verner Osgood, Lakeshire's hardworking farrier, recognizes that killing scouts and scavengers will never stem the tide as long as their pack leader remains alive. Rising above the rabble is Yowler, an exceptionally cunning and massive gnoll whose calls direct the pack across the hills. Verner tasks adventurers with hunting down the beast and severing his paw to ensure the howling is silenced once and for all.

Huge Gnoll Claw. In southwestern Elwynn, Hogger’s huge claw is sought as proof of his death. Stormwind’s authorities in Goldshire require it for the bounty. Hogger has terrorized the southern woodlands of Forest's Edge for months. Patrols have failed to stop the brute, and the local garrison cannot corral or subdue him. The Stormwind Army, stretched thin across Elwynn, posted an open bounty on his head. Marshal Dughan in Goldshire requires clear proof before paying it. Hogger's oversized claw leaves no doubt that the notorious marauder has fallen.

Huldar. Huldar is a dwarven teamster stationed along the southern road of Loch Modan, near the shores of the lake. Tasked with hauling vital blast powder to the dig site in the south, his delivery caravan faces relentless harassment from local threats and Dark Iron saboteurs. Hauling explosives through Loch Modan is no simple trade route. Huldar was tasked with driving wagonloads of mining blast powder down toward the southern excavation site, where dwarven archaeologists and prospectors desperately need supplies. However, the wilderness roads have become increasingly hazardous. With local wildlife, troggs, and Dark Iron infiltrators lurking near the lake's southern bend, Huldar finds himself stranded by his damaged wagon, relying on wandering travelers to safeguard the remaining powder kegs and ensure the shipment reaches the dig.

Human. Humans are an adaptable and resilient mortal race who have shaped much of the Eastern Kingdoms' history. Once unified under the ancient Empire of Arathor, their civilization fractured into the Seven Kingdoms, with Stormwind now standing as humanity's primary surviving bastion within the Alliance. Millennia ago, early humans lived as scattered, nomadic tribes constantly threatened by the Amani forest trolls. Recognizing that disunity would mean extinction, Warlord Thoradin of the Arathi tribe united the disparate clans through diplomacy and conquest, establishing the Empire of Arathor with its fortress capital at Strom. During the Troll Wars, the beleaguered high elves of Quel'Thalas allied with Arathor, teaching one hundred humans the arts of arcane magic. Together, they broke the troll armies, securing humanity's dominion over the central continents and laying the foundation for future mortal alliances.

Humbert's Sword. Humbert's Sword is the personal sidearm belonging to Deathguard Humbert of Tarren Mill. The weapon was looted from his camp by dwarven soldiers while he was scouting their stronghold at Dun Garok. Deathguard Humbert was dispatched by High Executor Darthalia to monitor the dwarven presence at Dun Garok from a concealed position. While he left his post unattended one morning to collect firewood to boil water, dwarven patrols stumbled across his campsite and plundered all of his gear, including his personal blade. With so many dwarves to search, Humbert relies on Horde agents to infiltrate the fortress and retrieve his lost weapon.

Humbert's Sword. While scouting the Ironforge stronghold of Dun Garok under orders from High Executor Darthalia, Deathguard Humbert stepped away from his camp to collect firewood. Dwarven scouts looted his campsite and made off with his personal weapon, leaving the humiliated sentry desperate to recover it before his commanding officer notices. Tasked by High Executor Darthalia with keeping a watchful eye on Dun Garok, Deathguard Humbert took up a concealed vigil near the dwarven fortress. When morning broke, he briefly left his outpost unguarded to gather firewood for boiling water. That lapse was all the opportunistic Ironforge dwarves needed. Upon his return, Humbert found his camp looted and his trusty sword gone, taken deep into the heavily defended bunker.

Humble Beginnings. Baros Alexston seeks help from his home in Stormwind's Cathedral Square. His family's Westfall farm has burned, and thieves hold its ruins; he hopes to recover an heirloom from his youth. Baros Alexston grew up working the fields of Westfall. Now he is an accomplished architect in Stormwind City, advising on stonework and city buildings. His path from farm boy to city planner is rare in the kingdom, yet he remains attached to the modest beginnings that shaped him.

Hungry!. Mudcrush Durtfeet, an ogre in northern Dustwallow Marsh, is hungry. Mud wants you to go bash the fishy Mirefin and bring back their heads, or Mud will eat you instead. Mudcrush Durtfeet is a big ogre and says so plainly. Mud is hungry and has a simple bargain: go bash the fishy Mirefin and bring Mud their heads as food. Feed Mud, or Mud will eat you.

Hunt for Yenniku. Nimboya has returned from Orgrimmar to the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale to search for Yenniku, the youngest son of his chieftain. Suspecting the Bloodscalp tribe holds the youth captive, the scout asks you to hunt their warriors and take their tusks to demonstrate your strength. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Nimboya speaks of a grim fate looming over Yenniku, the youngest son of the Darkspear chieftain. In accordance with an old tribal custom, the boy had been placed among the Gurubashi trolls of Zul'Gurub. When the Darkspear tribe departed their homeland alongside the orc warchief Thrall, Yenniku was left behind and lost. Sent back from distant Orgrimmar, Nimboya has undertaken the responsibility of finding the chieftain's son and bringing him to safety.

Hunt the Savages. Huntsman Markhor, of the village of Revantusk in the Hinterlands, calls the savage owlbeasts some of the region's most ornery creatures and asks you to kill twenty of them. Markhor describes the savage owlbeasts as among the more ornery creatures of the Hinterlands, and says the claws and beaks of the beasts have cost Revantusk many good warriors. Markhor wants every one you see killed, until you can bear no more bloodshed, and then the contribution you made will be weighed and judged. Twenty must fall.

Hunter. Masters of wilderness survival and deadly marksmanship, hunters roam the untamed reaches of Azeroth alongside fierce beast companions. Armed with bows, rifles, or crossbows, they excel at harassing enemies from a distance while relying on clever traps and primal aspects to control the flow of battle. Whether tracking elusive quarry across snowcapped peaks or stalking prey through dense forests, they live by their wits and connection to nature. At the heart of every hunter lies an instinctual empathy for the primal world. Unlike those who exploit nature or isolate themselves within stone bastions, hunters immerse themselves entirely in untamed lands. They study the habits, movements, and strengths of predatory beasts, earning their respect rather than breaking their spirits. Through patient bonding, a hunter tames dangerous creatures—such as fierce prowling cats, stubborn mountain bears, and sharp-eyed raptors—turning wild animals into steadfast allies that defend them to the death.

Hunter Rise. Hunter Rise is one of the elevated mesas making up the city of Thunder Bluff, situated just south of the central bluff. It serves as the primary training and gathering ground for the tauren's warriors, hunters, trackers, and skinners. Across its windswept platforms, young braves hone their martial skills and prepare for combat. Connected to the neighboring bluffs by swaying rope bridges, Hunter Rise is dedicated to the martial traditions of the tauren. It is anchored by the Hunter's Hall, where experienced marksmen, trackers, and warriors pass down their discipline to younger generations. Surrounding the lodge are practice grounds outfitted with training dummies, weapon racks, and skinning posts, making it a bustling center for those who live by spear, bow, and hide.

Hunting for Ectoplasm. Mux Manascrambler in Gadgetzan has his ectoplasmic distiller ready and now needs ectoplasm. You carry it to three distant lands, Silithus, Winterspring and the Eastern Plaguelands, and gather twelve of each kind from the incorporeal dead. This follows The Ectoplasmic Distiller. Mux Manascrambler is proud of the distiller and warns that you have some travelling ahead to find the incorporeal undead. In Mux's view, climate changes what the spectral fabric of the dead is like. Silithus has tortured night elves, Winterspring has spirits of the highborne, and the Eastern Plaguelands have ghosts and banshees. Each place yields a different ectoplasm: twelve scorched, twelve frozen and twelve stable. Mux says to set the distiller down nearby before harvesting, then bring it and the ectoplasm back to Gadgetzan.

Hunting in Stranglethorn. Roon Wildmane, a tauren in Desolace, once hunted beside a dwarf named Hemet. Now Roon sends you off with a kodo horn, bound for Hemet Nesingwary in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long ago a dwarf named Hemet came to Desolace, eager to hunt great beasts. Hemet handled a rifle with uncanny skill, and the two hunters passed many days together, the old enmity between their peoples set aside. When Hemet went off to Stranglethorn, Roon vowed to welcome Hemet back one day for another hunt, and Roon decides that time has arrived. You are to carry Roon's kodo horn to Hemet, who will know whose it is. Look in Stranglethorn, north of Grom'gol Base Camp.

Hushed Bank. The Hushed Bank is the shadowy western shoreline of Duskwood, bordering the river that divides the forest from Westfall. Stretching from the junction near the Three Corners south toward Stranglethorn Vale, it is a quiet yet hazardous woodland stalked by prowling beasts and shadowed by dark mysteries. Running along the river boundary between Duskwood and Westfall, the Hushed Bank marks the transition from open plains and sunlit farms to pervasive, unnatural twilight. The wooden covered bridge crosses the river here, offering passage to travelers heading west out of the grim wood. Thick underbrush and creeping fog dominate the riverbanks, where large spiders and hungry forest wolves stalk unwary wayfarers who stray from the beaten path.

Hyacinth Mushroom. Hyacinth Mushrooms are distinctive fungi found sprouting at the roots of trees throughout Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Prized by local night elf herbalists for their medicinal properties, they also happen to be favored food and forage for the mischievous grell and grellkin. Hyacinth Mushrooms grow abundantly across Shadowglen, flourishing in the damp shadows at the bases of trees, mossy stones, and the sprawling roots of Aldrassil. While useful in woodland remedies, they have also caught the attention of the corrupted grell, who frequently hoard them. When young night elf sentinels or trainees are afflicted by local venomous fauna—such as the spiders of Shadowthread Cave—these mushrooms serve as a core component in soothing draughts and antivenoms concocted by forest healers.

Hypercapacitor Gizmo. The Hypercapacitor Gizmo is an eccentric piece of engineering recovered from the canyon floor of Thousand Needles. Once dangling from the neck of a caged beast in a ruined caravan, its true purpose remains a mystery even to the tinkerer who claims to own it. When centaur marauders ambushed a goblin caravan traveling through Thousand Needles, they plundered nearly everything in sight. The sole survivor, Wizlo Bearingshiner, managed to crawl his way to safety at Whitereach Post, leaving behind his best gizmo: the Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Strangely, the gadget wound up secured around the neck of a ferocious, enraged panther locked inside a transport cage. The raiding centaur feared the beast enough to leave the cage entirely alone amidst the burning wreckage, unwittingly preserving Wizlo's odd machine.

Hypercapacitor Gizmo. Following a deadly centaur ambush on a merchant caravan in Thousand Needles, the goblin tinkerer Wizlo Bearingshiner was left as the sole survivor. Desperate to reclaim his prized invention, he hires adventurers to breach the wreckage, unlock an iron cage, and wrest the gizmo from the neck of a fearsome caged predator. Caravans venturing beneath the towering sandstone spires of Thousand Needles run a perilous gauntlet. Hostile centaur prowl the canyon floor, fiercely guarding their territory and raiding any travelers bold enough to pass through. When one such trade caravan was overrun just north of Whitereach Post, the centaur slaughtered the travelers and plundered the wagons, leaving only the goblin Wizlo Bearingshiner to limp back to safety.

Ice Thistle Hills. The Ice Thistle Hills are a snow-covered highland rise lying just southeast of the goblin outpost of Everlook. Dominated by a rugged cavern system, the area is claimed by ferocious Ice Thistle yetis that threaten any travelers venturing off the main road. Rising sharply out of the central drifts of Winterspring, the Ice Thistle Hills serve as the primary hunting grounds and nesting territory for the valley's aggressive Ice Thistle yetis. Centered around a prominent cave dug deep into the rockface, these hulking beasts roam both the rocky slopes and the winding tunnels within. Because of their proximity to Everlook, the yetis present a constant nuisance and danger to goblin commerce and visiting prospectors, who regularly commission intrepid hunters to cull the beasts for their valuable thick pelts and pristine horns.

Iceflow Lake. Iceflow Lake is a frigid, partially frozen body of water situated in western Dun Morogh, directly north of Brewnall Village. Despite the relentless frost, local dwarves maintain fishing holes through the sheet ice to secure fresh water and fish. The snow-covered islands in the center of the lake are prowled by aggressive winter wolves and their alpha, Timber. Spanning western Dun Morogh just outside Brewnall Village, Iceflow Lake battles the bitter Khaz Modan climate year-round. Thick ice sheets continually creep across the surface, forcing local residents like Paxton Ganter to regularly clear holes for ice fishing and drinking water. While the shore provides sustenance, the islands rising from the middle of the lake are far less welcoming. A fierce pack of wild wolves has made these icy mounds their territory, dominated by the notoriously savage gray worg known as Timber.

Identifying the Brood. In Brackenwall Village, Draz'Zilb calls Mok'Morokk a craven fool who wallows in power, and says Tharg is wrestling with sorrow and vengeance while vying to lead the clan. Draz'Zilb believes nobody else is concerned with finding who attacked the old home, and asks you for fifteen searing tongues and fifteen searing hearts. Draz'Zilb says Mok'Morokk wallows in power while Tharg wrestles with sorrow and a thirst for vengeance, so by Draz'Zilb's account nobody else is concerned with who is behind the aggression against the old home. Draz'Zilb notes that you may have expected an ogre to speak like a brute.

Ignition. Ignition begins when an adventurer stumbles upon an operative trapped inside a Venture Company shredder in the northern Barrens. Having impulsively hijacked the machine without its starter key, the pilot needs someone to fetch the ignition key from the site supervisor before their cover is blown. Deep within the bustling Venture Company drilling grounds of the northern Barrens, an ambitious heist has run into an embarrassing snag. An operative sent on behalf of Sputtervalve managed to slip inside one of the corporation's cutting-edge shredders, intending to commandeer the machine and study its inner workings. However, the thief overlooked a fundamental detail: the steering and movement column is locked tight without a dedicated ignition key.

Ignition Key. The Ignition Key is an essential control key carried by Supervisor Lugwizzle at the Venture Company's drilling operation in Sludge Fen. It is required to unlock the steering column and activate the controls of an advanced Venture Company shredder. When Sputtervalve of Ratchet dispatched an operative to steal a proprietary Venture Company shredder from Sludge Fen, things did not go smoothly. The undercover pilot, Wizzlecrank, managed to slip into the machine's cockpit only to find its movement column completely locked down. To keep suspicious foremen from catching on, he feigned mechanical troubles while awaiting an adventurer to retrieve the necessary Ignition Key. The key remains held under lock and key by Supervisor Lugwizzle high atop the central oil derrick, controlling access to the machine's state-of-the-art arm, speed, and rotation mechanisms.

name.zhCN: 伊克鲁德·玛格苏尔之书

text.enUS: Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome. Ilkrud Magthrull's Tome is a grimoire recovered from a dangerous orc warlock residing within the corrupted depths of Ashenvale. Brought to Delgren the Purifier, its foul contents reveal the broader dark dealings surrounding the cultists operating out of the Tower of Althalaxx. Ilkrud Magthrull is a formidable orc warlock entrenched at the Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, a site poisoned by lingering demonic influence. Surrounded by summoned minions, Magthrull recorded his foul rituals and shadowy communications within this personal tome. While the Argent Dawn paladin Delgren the Purifier had long known of the warlock's presence, the uncovered links between Magthrull and the dark cultists gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx made recovering the book an urgent priority.

Illiyana. Illiyana is an ancient dryad stationed in southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to protecting the woodland from ancient corruption. Wandering near the Shrine of Aessina, she rallies champions of the Alliance to push back against the vicious satyrs that plague the ancient groves. Her vigilance represents the enduring bond between the daughters of Cenarius and the night elven wilderness. Like all dryads, Illiyana is one of the daughters of the demigod Cenarius. Peaceful yet fiercely protective of wild lands, she patrols the woods of southwestern Ashenvale. As dark forces stir and the woodlands suffer under creeping corruption, Illiyana keeps watch over sacred relics and groves, acting as a steward for nature's primal sanctity.

Illiyana Moonblaze. Illiyana Moonblaze is a night elf supply officer stationed at Silverwing Grove in Ashenvale. Operating alongside the Silverwing Sentinels, she supplies Alliance champions waging war against the Warsong Outriders. Illiyana Moonblaze serves as the supply officer for the Silverwing Sentinels nestled in Silverwing Grove. From her post near the path into Warsong Gulch, she outfits the defenders who hold the southern woods of Ashenvale against the Warsong clan.

Ilthalaine. Ilthalaine is a night elf guardian standing watch over the sacred glade of Shadowglen in Teldrassil. He serves as the primary greeter and mentor for young night elves taking their very first steps into the world. Vigilant and attuned to the wilderness, he guides novice adventurers toward maintaining the delicate balance of nature across the boughs of the World Tree. Positioned just outside the heart of Shadowglen, Ilthalaine is often the first face a fledgling night elf sees upon beginning their journey. He observes the woodland paths and notices the subtle shifts within the forest that go unseen by ordinary eyes. His duty is to welcome returning kin and ensure that any newly awakened defenders are grounded in the traditions of their people, ready to face the responsibilities that come with tending to Teldrassil.

Important Heirlooms. Important Heirlooms is a quest where an adventurer aids a nervous gnome named Thom, who was caught lurking in the Hall of Thanes when Dark Iron dwarves breached the vaults in subterranean mole machines. The task involves retrieving scattered dwarven relics under the dubious guise of historic preservation. While exploring the subterranean vaults of the Hall of Thanes, an enterprising gnome named Thom was interrupted by the sudden arrival of Dark Iron dwarves tunneling upward in mole machines. Unable to secure the area himself, Thom recruits passing adventurers to brave the hostile dig site and retrieve valuable dwarven relics scattered across the chambers before the invaders seize or destroy them.

Improved Quality. Pratt McGrubben has heard of hides better still than the last. Up in the north of Feralas, inside Rage Scar Hold, roams another throng of yetis, tougher than those you faced before. Ten of their hides are wanted at Feathermoon Stronghold. After The Mark of Quality, Pratt McGrubben has found a lead on a still finer supply of hides. Up in the north of Feralas, inside Rage Scar Hold, another throng of yetis lives, tougher than the ones you faced earlier. Pratt McGrubben will pay handsomely for ten of their hides, brought back to Feathermoon Stronghold to settle the matter. If they match the quality of the Feral Scar hides, they could prove as resilient as thorium.

Improved Quality. Jangdor Swiftstrider has heard of hides better still than the last. Up in the north of Feralas, inside Rage Scar Hold, roams another throng of yetis, tougher than those you faced before. Ten of their hides are wanted at Camp Mojache. After The Mark of Quality, Jangdor Swiftstrider has found a lead on a still finer supply of hides. Up in the north of Feralas, inside Rage Scar Hold, another throng of yetis lives, tougher than the ones you faced earlier. Jangdor Swiftstrider will pay handsomely for ten of their hides, brought back to Camp Mojache to settle the matter. If they match the quality of the Feral Scar hides, they could prove as resilient as thorium.

text.enUS: In Defense of the King's Lands. In Defense of the King's Lands culminates with a direct strike against the leadership of the trogg incursion in Loch Modan. Dwarven scouts trace the violent infestation to Chieftain Grawmug and his brute bodyguards deep within Stonesplinter Valley. Captain Rugelfuss tasks bold Alliance adventurers with slaying the chieftain to shatter trogg morale and reclaim the realm's southern borders. The persistent trogg menace across southern Loch Modan has proven to be more than random subterranean crawling. Captain Rugelfuss's scouts discovered that the Stonesplinter troggs are operating under the crude direction of a chieftain named Grawmug. Unlike typical scattered marauders, this pack moves with concerted aggression, threatening to overrun the King's Lands if left unchecked. By taking the fight into their lair and executing Grawmug alongside his personal bruisers, the Dwarven defenders hope to break the pack's cohesion and stem the tide.

text.enUS: In Defense of the King's Lands. Mountaineer Cobbleflint guards the southern tower in the Valley of Kings, desperately seeking aid against the encroaching Stonesplinter troggs. With Ironforge's military stretched thin across distant fronts, the defense of Loch Modan's southern passes falls to passing Alliance volunteers. The massive dwarven monuments carved into the mountains of the Valley of Kings loom over a garrison under severe strain. Mountaineer Cobbleflint and his fellow guards stationed at the southern watchtower face an ever-growing invasion of troggs erupting from the rock. With much of King Magni Bronzebeard's regular army dispatched abroad to support Alliance commitments, the home front relies heavily on local patrols and hired blades to prevent the province from being overrun.

text.enUS: In Defense of the King's Lands. This military assignment tasks Alliance adventurers with blunting a trogg offensive in southern Loch Modan on behalf of Mountaineer Gravelgaw. With dwarven regular forces tied up in distant Alliance campaigns, local outposts must rely on volunteers to cull dangerous Stonesplinter Skullthumpers and Seers before the Valley of Kings is overrun. The Mountaineers stationed along the southern pass into Dun Morogh are stretched dangerously thin. With King Magni Bronzebeard committing significant dwarven military strength to the wider Alliance front, outposts like the Valley of Kings guard towers lack regular infantry. Mountaineer Gravelgaw relies on outside volunteers to run aggressive spoiling raids into Stonesplinter Valley, keeping the subterranean invaders at bay while local garrisons wait for reinforcements that may never arrive.

name.enUS: In Defense of the King's Lands
name.frFR: À la défense des terres du roi

text.enUS: In Defense of the King's Lands. This mission represents the escalating fight waged by Ironforge's Mountaineers against the trogg infestation in southern Loch Modan. Operating from the Southern Guard Tower, Mountaineer Wallbang directs seasoned recruits into Stonesplinter Valley to cull dangerous trogg shamans and front-line bonesnappers. Completing this trial earns Wallbang's full trust and opens an audience with the garrison's commanding captain. Loch Modan's defenses are stretched to their limits. With dwarven regular reserves summoned to distant fronts across Azeroth, local outposts like the Southern Guard Tower are left short-handed. Mountaineer Wallbang and his few comrades face relentless pressure from the Stonesplinter clan, forcing them to rely heavily on visiting Alliance travelers to hold the southern pass.

In Eranikus' Own Words. Itharius wants to find a way of speaking with Eranikus through the gem. Eranikus lies somewhere between sleep and death, caught in a weave of nightmares, and the essence you gave is badly tainted, yet a chance remains. Itharius sends you far off, to eastern Winterspring. Itharius explains that Eranikus lies between sleep and death, twisted within a weave of nightmares. The essence you gave is badly tainted, yet there is a chance of reaching him. To open a conversation through the gem, Itharius sends you to eastern Winterspring, a land of ice, to seek one of their mortal allies.

In Favor of Darkness. In Favor of Darkness marks a Forsaken priest's transition beyond the starting crypts of Deathknell toward advanced instruction in Brill. Entrusted by Dark Cleric Duesten, the fledgling disciple travels to study under Dark Cleric Beryl to master the delicate balance between the Holy Light and the Shadow. While priests of other races revere the Holy Light as an unblemished source of moral virtue, the Forsaken approach faith through the harsh lens of their own undeath. As Dark Cleric Duesten teaches, the Forsaken were forged in corruption and discarded like carrion. Their survival demands understanding both Light and Shadow without sentimentality. In Favor of Darkness directs new disciples out of Deathknell's cloistered graveyard to confront the wider reality awaiting them in Tirisfal Glades.

In Favor of Elune. "In Favor of Elune" is a rite of passage for young night elf priests ready to step out of the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen. Directed by Priestess Shanda, novitiates travel down the path to Dolanaar to seek further guidance and training under Laurna Morninglight. For an initiate serving Elune within Aldrassil's secluded shelter, learning begins with simple prayers and defensive invocations under the watchful eye of Priestess Shanda. Yet the cloistered life of Shadowglen cannot prepare a priestess or priest for the turmoil gripping the wider world. Once an initiate demonstrates steady faith and discipline, Shanda sends them down the shadowed forest path toward Dolanaar to continue their education.

In Favor of Spirituality. "In Favor of Spirituality" is a foundational rite of passage for young Darkspear priests departing the Valley of Trials. Directed by Ken'jai to report to the priest trainer Tai'jin in Razor Hill, initiates take their first real steps beyond the secluded training den into the wider challenges of Durotar. The journey highlights the delicate balance the Darkspear strike between honoring their ancestral troll heritage and integrating into the newly forged Horde. After mastering their basic rites under Ken'jai in the secluded Valley of Trials, Darkspear acolytes are ready to leave the training grounds behind. The winding paths out into Durotar lead directly to the crossroads settlement of Razor Hill. For a young priest, this journey represents a major milestone: transitioning from basic survival drills in the dirt to shouldering spiritual and cultural responsibilities for the tribe.

In Favor of the Light. Priestess Anetta sends you south from Northshire Abbey to continue your training in Goldshire. Priestess Josetta is waiting at the Lion's Pride Inn to guide your next steps in the Holy Light. Northshire Abbey gives you shelter and your first lessons in the Holy Light. After you learn prayer and divine healing, Priestess Anetta sends you south along the road to Goldshire. There, you leave the abbey's sheltered study for service among the people of Elwynn.

In Favor of the Light. "In Favor of the Light" marks a young priest's rite of passage from the isolated training grounds of Coldridge Valley into the wider reaches of Dun Morogh. Instructed by Branstock Khalder, novitiates are sent through the mountain tunnel to Kharanos to further their studies under Priest Trainer Maxan Anvol. It signals that an acolyte is ready to shoulder real responsibilities and earn the traditional vestments of their calling. In the secluded cradle of Coldridge Valley, dwarven priests begin their studies under the watchful eye of instructors like Branstock Khalder. Once a novice demonstrates sufficient dedication and grasp of Holy magic, their preliminary instruction comes to an end. Rather than keeping them sheltered in Anvilmar, Khalder directs promising students beyond the mountains to Kharanos, where the demands of ministry and defense intersect with the daily struggles of Dun Morogh's folk.

In Good Taste. Marin Noggenfogger finds the thistleshrub dew terrible to taste, yet decides not to give up on it. You are sent to Sprinkle, a friend of Marin's in Gadgetzan, with the dew in hand. Marin tastes the dew and finds it awful, yet decides not to give up on the idea after all. Instead you are handed the dew and sent to Sprinkle, a friend in Gadgetzan whom Marin calls an excellent chef. You are to tell her what is going on and that the drink needs to go down more easily. Marin also wants it to have some kick.

In Nightmares. In Nightmares is a Horde quest that tasks an adventurer with carrying a disturbing relic, the Nightmare Shard, to Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem atop Elder Rise in Thunder Bluff. Originally recovered as a glowing fragment from the Wailing Caverns, the shard reveals a deeply unsettling corruption seeping into the Emerald Dream. After examining the strange crystal retrieved from the depths of the Wailing Caverns, Falla Sagewind recognizes that it is made from the pure essence of the Emerald Dream. Yet the vision dwelling inside is dark and chaotic, bearing the hallmark not of peaceful slumber, but of a waking nightmare. Reluctant to speak openly about such alarming omens, she entrusts the shard to you with instructions to seek out Thunder Bluff's most venerated elder druid, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem.

In Nightmares. Following the discovery of a strange glowing shard, Falla Sagewind recognizes that the artifact contains the pure essence of the Emerald Dream tainted by dark visions. She dispatches an adventurer to Darnassus to deliver the disturbing relic directly to the elder druids of the Cenarion Circle. The glowing shard recovered from the depths of Wailing Caverns proves far more dangerous than simple crystal. Upon inspecting it, Falla Sagewind identifies it as an embodiment of the Emerald Dream's purest essence. Yet rather than reflecting the verdant harmony of the natural world, the stone twists with unsettling, fearful visions. Shaken by what she sees, Falla refuses to delve deeper herself and insists the shard must be safely transferred to senior leadership within the Cenarion Circle.

In Search of Knowledge. Troyas Moonbreeze found what looks like an ordinary stave in the rubble of the Feralas ruins, but he cannot shake the feeling there is more to it. He sends you to talk to his colleague Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village. Troyas Moonbreeze says the Feralas ruins are dangerous but have much to tell about what has happened there. A few days ago, searching the rubble to the south, he came upon a stave that seems ordinary, yet he cannot shake the feeling there is more to it. He and Angelas have pored over their books without finding a word about it.

name.frFR: À la recherche de Menara Taillevide

text.enUS: In Search of Menara Voidrender. This quest sends promising Alliance warlocks across the sea to the arid Barrens in search of Menara Voidrender. Operating out of Strahad Farsan's tower above Ratchet, Menara offers seasoned practitioners the chance to craft specialized tools and garments to bolster their control over demonic forces. Briarthorn, an associate lurking in Ironforge's darker corners, recognizes when a warlock has advanced beyond basic demonology without succumbing to corruption. Rather than keeping his pupils cloistered under the mountain, he points them outward toward Kalimdor, commending their discipline and urging them to seek instruction from an artisan far more skilled in practical felcraft.

name.deDE: Auf der Suche nach Menara Leerbringer
name.frFR: À la recherche de Menara Taillevide

text.enUS: In Search of Menara Voidrender. Zevrost, a cynical warlock trainer lurking in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, directs seasoned practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender in the Barrens. Despite his harsh warnings about the inevitable price of demonic corruption, he points ambitious warlocks toward an expert mentor capable of fashioning powerful arcane vestments. Deep beneath Orgrimmar in the Cleft of Shadow, warlocks operate under a veil of uneasy tolerance. Zevrost is among the more bitter tutors in the dark arts, quick to sneer at ambitious acolytes striving for mastery. In his eyes, anyone delving deeper into fel magic is merely racing toward their own enslavement. He insists that it is only a matter of time before demonic addiction overtakes the practitioner completely, reducing even the most disciplined scholar into a thrall of the Twisting Nether.

name.deDE: Auf der Suche nach Menara Leerbringer
name.frFR: À la recherche de Menara Taillevide

text.enUS: In Search of Menara Voidrender. An Alliance warlock seeking to craft powerful vestments is directed by the Mage Quarter's covert practitioners to seek out Menara Voidrender across the Great Sea. Stationed high above the neutral port of Ratchet, Menara trains dark spellcasters across faction divides in the dangerous arts of binding and artifact creation. Within the dark crypts beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, warlock trainer Demisette Cloyce is known for her strict, unsparing standards. When an aspiring warlock reaches the threshold of weaving significant items of power, Demisette rarely believes they are truly ready. Nevertheless, higher authorities within the cabal mandate the student's advancement, dispatching them far from the safety of the capital to prove their mettle.

name.deDE: Auf der Suche nach Menara Leerbringer
name.frFR: À la recherche de Menara Taillevide

text.enUS: In Search of Menara Voidrender. This quest sends promising Horde warlocks from the shadowy quarters of the Undercity across the sea to Ratchet. Atop a hill overlooking the port, the mentor Menara Voidrender awaits those prepared to craft powerful arcane garments. In the Forsaken capital of the Undercity, Kaal Soulreaper observes the growing talent of practicing warlocks. Recognizing that a practitioner has grown past rudimentary hexes and impish thralls, he urges them to seek specialized instruction across the Great Sea. The craft of demonic control leaves no room for hesitation, and only skilled mentors can ensure a warlock's survival against the volatile powers of the Nether.

In Search of Thaelrid. In Search of Thaelrid is an Alliance reconnaissance mission dispatched from Darnassus on behalf of the Argent Dawn. Dawnwatcher Shaedlass tasks adventurers with venturing into the sunken ruins of Blackfathom Deeps to locate a missing scout who vanished while investigating a dangerous alliance between naga and cultists. It represents an early encounter with the reach of the Argent Dawn beyond their typical northern vigil. Though the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line against the Scourge in the plague-ridden ruins of Lordaeron, its vigilance extends across Kalimdor. Stationed within Darnassus, Dawnwatcher Shaedlass gathers whispers and intelligence on unnatural threats emerging across the world. When unsettling reports arose that sea-dwelling naga and the doomsday zealots of the Twilight's Hammer had forged a pact within the flooded chambers of Blackfathom Deeps along the Ashenvale shore, the order recognized the potential catastrophe.

text.enUS: In Search of The Excavation Team. In Search of the Excavation Team begins with Tarrel Rockweaver in the Wetlands, who is distraught over a sudden silence from his wife, Merrin. Assigned to the prestigious Whelgar Excavation Site to the east, she has missed two weeks of regular letters, prompting fears that disaster has struck the expedition. Travelers are tasked with venturing into the marsh to locate the dig site and ascertain her safety. While stationed in the soggy expanse of the Wetlands, Tarrel Rockweaver anticipated steady correspondence from his wife Merrin. Operating out of the dwarven dig known as the Whelgar Excavation Site, Merrin had maintained weekly dispatches describing their work. When two full weeks passed without a single word, Tarrel grew convinced that calamity had overtaken the camp. With official dwarf authorities stretched thin, he relies on passing scouts to brave the perils of the marshes to see if the diggers still draw breath.

text.enUS: In Search of The Excavation Team. This errand delivers word of a disastrous dinosaur attack at the Whelgar's Excavation site back to Menethil Harbor. Merrin Rockweaver writes a hasty letter to reassure her anxious husband, Tarrel, while recounting how the expedition was overrun. After locating the remnants of the excavation team cowering near the ridge overlooking the dig site, Merrin Rockweaver provides a hasty report. Unearthing rare artifacts alongside massive prehistoric fossils proved fatal when packs of native mottled raptors swarmed the diggers. The sudden ferocity left most of the crew dead and the survivors cut off from civilization.

Incantations from the Nether. Incantations from the Nether is a grimoire of demonic magic held by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar. Sylvanas Windrunner and her dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras, seek to claim the tome to harness its fel knowledge for the Forsaken. Beneath the red stone streets of Orgrimmar, the Searing Blade—a subterranean sect tied to the Shadow Council—operates in the fiery tunnels of Ragefire Chasm. Among their darkest treasures is the Incantations from the Nether, a spellbook laden with demonic rites bestowed by agents of the Burning Legion. While the cultists use its vile secrets to plot treason within the Orcish capital, word of the text reached far across the sea to the royal quarters of Undercity.

Incendia Agave. Incendia Agave is a rare, spiky aquatic plant native to the Boiling Pool beneath Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. When enchanted by a skilled shaman, its unique properties allow it to kindle the sacred fire of life. Growing beneath and around the waters of the Boiling Pool in Thousand Needles, Incendia Agave thrives directly in the shadow of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Guarded naturally by wandering steam elementals, the plant is difficult to harvest and scarce across Kalimdor. Despite growing submerged in water, it contains potent natural elements that lend themselves directly to rituals of flame.

Incendia Powder. Incendia Powder is an enchanted ritual catalyst refined to ignite sacred flames. Carried by Horde emissaries into Thousand Needles, the powder is specifically treated with shamanic incantations to invoke the slumbering spirit-beast Arikara atop Darkcloud Pinnacle. Incendia Powder is no mundane explosive or mundane flash powder; it is a purified, ritualistic substance carefully infused with shamanic magic. Enchanted and entrusted to travelers by Magatha Grimtotem on Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise, the mixture is designed to react solely with the dormant sacred fire of life atop the isolated spires of Darkcloud Pinnacle. Once scattered across the consecrated brazier where the dead are laid to rest, its alchemical and spiritual warding calls forth the vengeful winged serpent Arikara.

name.enUS: Incendosaurs? Whateverosaur is More Like It
