name.ptBR: Incendosaurs? Whateverosaur is More Like It

text.enUS: Incendosaurs? Whateverosaur is More Like It. Hansel Heavyhands says his bunions have bunions, and he cannot do any killing with his feet in such disarray. Scrange and Burninate told him to clear out the incendosaurs of the Slag Pit, so he sends you instead to slay twenty. Hansel Heavyhands is in no state to fight. Scrange and Burninate told him to kill the incendosaurs so that expeditionary teams can go down into the lava pools of the Slag Pit and explore. Hansel passes the work on to you.

name.ptBR: Café com pão, café com pão

text.enUS: Incoming Gumdrop. Incoming Gumdrop is a seasonal Hallow's End quest found in Ironforge, given by the gnome artisan Talvash del Kissel. In order to obtain a festive treat for a sick child in Stormwind, adventurers must first perform a playful train impression for the delighted gnome. During the autumn celebration of Hallow's End, trick-or-treaters scour the major Alliance strongholds gathering unique regional confections. In Ironforge's Mystic Ward, the gnome Talvash del Kissel holds the coveted Gnomeregan Gumdrop. While sympathetic to the plight of the young orphan who desires it, Talvash insists on upholding the holiday's spirit of mischief before parting with his sweet, demanding a convincing train impression from anyone seeking a handout.

Indurium. Martek the Exiled says the Badlands hold a wealth of metal for anyone with the nerve to get it. Indurium is said to stand up to heat and stress, and Martek wants samples to test whether it could serve Fizzle's racecar. Stonevault troggs out in the Badlands are the ones carrying flakes of it. Martek the Exiled tells you he is not out in the Badlands just to avoid company. The region holds indurium, a metal said to stand up to heat and stress, and it might do for Fizzle's car. Martek wants samples to test, and has the forge hot and waiting.

Indurium Ore. Pozzik plans to work indurium into several parts of the racers, which calls for a great deal of raw ore. The ore is to be had at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. The gnomes are already getting hold of their own, and Pozzik wants to keep up with them. Pozzik asks for four pieces of raw indurium ore. It can be had at the Uldaman dig in the Badlands, across the sea in Khaz Modan. The gnomes are already getting hold of their own, so Pozzik wants a supply too. This follows Rizzle's Schematics.

Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. Seeking an explosive countermeasure against the Venture Company in the Stonetalon Mountains, Alliance adventurers are sent across the sea to Ironforge. There, the eccentric gnome Lomac Gearstrip agrees to brew his volatile invention, Nitromirglyceronium, provided you fetch the necessary alchemical reagents. Gaxim Rustfizzle, stationed high in the craggy passes of the Stonetalon Mountains, needed potent explosives for the most advanced device he had yet devised against the Venture Company. For that, he turned to an eccentric former colleague living in Ironforge: Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac is the creator of Nitromirglyceronium, a substance so inherently unstable and destructive that he finds the prospect of anyone using it hilarious, regardless of who gets blown apart in the process.

Ineptitude + Chemicals = Fun. This errand delivers a canister of volatile NG-5 from the tinker Lomac Gearstrip to Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. Gaxim requires this unstable chemical to create a potent igniter for several wagons packed with dynamite. The resulting blast forms a critical distraction for Alliance operations in the disputed crags. Gnomish engineering often balances brilliance on the razor edge of catastrophe, and Nitromirglyceronium—or NG-5—is no exception. Lomac Gearstrip hands over the unstable compound with a stern warning: handle it with extreme care, or risk blowing yourself to pieces on the road back to Gaxim Rustfizzle.

Infectis Scar. The Infectis Scar is a deep, unnatural chasm carved into the blighted terrain of the Eastern Plaguelands near Corin's Crossing. Unlike natural ravines, this wound in the earth was ripped open by necromantic power when a cursed runeblade shattered against a dwarven shield. The blight festering at the bottom of the fissure remains an enduring testament to the Scourge's dark sorcery. While neighboring gorges like the Pestilent Scar originated as natural terrain features poisoned by the plague, the Infectis Scar is entirely artificial. It was created during the third war's violent clashes near Corin's Crossing. When the notorious death knight Marduk Blackpool clashed with a stalwart dwarf captain, Marduk's cursed runesword shattered against the captain's shield. Discarding the broken weapon, Marduk kept the hilt, but the severed runeblade sank deep into the soil. Its foul enchantment violently tore open the crust of the earth, creating the jagged chasm that sits festering in the Plaguelands today.

Infestation Investigation. Infestation Investigation is an early task given to young adventurers stepping out into Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight orders a cull of pesky cirrusflies that have begun swarming the eastern groves. Left unchecked, the fast-breeding insects threaten to destabilize the peaceful grove and endanger local settlements. Thendal Grove has long maintained a delicate balance, but recent reports by local rangers indicate a sudden population surge of pesky cirrusflies on the eastern edge of the woods. While individual cirrusflies are minor pests, their swarms quickly turn aggressive and destructive when numbers balloon. Ranger Elatrell Featherlight wastes no time dispatching capable youth to cull the flying insects before their presence completely overwhelms the grove.

Infiltrating the Castle. Master cheese monger and intelligence broker Elling Trias directs you into the royal seat of Stormwind Keep. Your objective is to rendezvous with his fellow operative Tyrion, who has spent weeks watching the corrupt nobleman Lord Gregor Lescovar from the keep's gardens. When you bring your findings to Elling Trias in his Trade District cheese shop, he quickly grasps the gravity of the Defias threat nestled deep inside the kingdom's governance. Legal channels will not suffice to expose or punish someone as deeply entrenched and protected as Lord Gregor Lescovar. Trias offers a dangerous route forward: delivering extrajudicial justice within the very walls of Stormwind Keep to permanently sever the conspiracy.

Infiltrating the Cult. Infiltrating the Cult is a quest in Shen'dar Village where an unfamiliar adventurer is tasked with approaching a local missionary named Sania Silverstream. Beneath her benign religious exterior, Sania recruits followers for the Al'Aketh, a cult dedicated to the Windlord Al'Akir. The mission seeks to uncover the cult's true designs for the settlement before an uneasy peace shatters. In Shen'dar Village, an uneasy truce is beginning to unravel. For some time, local authorities have tolerated the presence of Sania Silverstream, a self-proclaimed missionary living among them. She represents the Order of the Al'Aketh, an organization that dresses itself in the vestments of a benign religious movement while deploying gentle recruiters to attract unsuspecting followers. Village leaders permitted her recruitment efforts solely to avoid provoking the cult into outright conflict, but the pretense of mutual coexistence is wearing thin.

Infiltration. In Tarren Mill, Krusk at last hears word and rumor of Gol'dir, an orc held prisoner by the Syndicate. The humans keep moving their captive about, so Krusk has narrowed the search to the Syndicate's large camp, just to the north of town, and wants you to bring back whatever information you can find. Krusk has begun to hear word and rumor of Gol'dir. The Syndicate's humans keep moving the orc about, but the search is narrowing to their large camp, just to the north of Tarren Mill. Krusk sends you there to lay hands on whatever information you can and carry it back. Krusk fears that with each day Gol'dir's prospects darken.

Ink Supplies. In Northshire Abbey, Brother Paxton needs fresh ink for his work as a monastic scribe. He sends you east to Lakeshire for Rethban ore, the mineral his fast-drying ink requires. Brother Paxton takes pride in his craft and uses a special ink for important writings such as The Stresses of Iron. His recipe dries quickly and resists smearing, but the ink can dry in its pot if left too long. To make more, he needs raw Rethban iron ore, mined in the rocky Redridge Mountains.

Innkeeper Allison. In Stormwind's Trade District, Innkeeper Allison keeps the Gilded Rose ready for travelers and merchants. The busy inn stands between the bank and auction house, where she offers hearthstone bindings, drinks, and shelter. Innkeeper Allison welcomes travelers at the Gilded Rose in Stormwind. The inn stands between the Trade District auction house and the city's main vaults, and its ground floor sees a steady flow of peddlers, mercenaries, and visiting diplomats. She keeps order behind the main counter and offers lodging and hearthstone services. Allison also joins local holiday festivities and coordinates small errands for traveling heroes seeking rest in the capital.

Innkeeper Farley. At the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, Innkeeper Farley welcomes travelers with food, beds, and hearthstones. Well-liked and observant, he keeps misplaced mail and hears the troubles of those on the road. Travelers bound for Stormwind, Westfall, and Duskwood find Innkeeper Farley behind the Lion's Pride Inn counter in Goldshire. He offers meals, ale, cheese, and a bed, and sets hearthstones for those who need one. With a welcoming hand and a sharp eye, Farley serves all who pass through this busy waystation and keeps order at the inn.

Innkeeper Firebrew. Innkeeper Firebrew manages the Stonefire Tavern in the bustling Commons of Ironforge. A genial host to weary mountaineers and visiting dignitaries alike, he serves hearty dwarven staples and keeps travelers rested beneath the mountain. Situated in the central ring of the Commons, Innkeeper Firebrew's establishment is often the first sanctuary encountered by travelers entering through the Great Gates of Ironforge. Behind a counter laden with flagons of ale, skins of stout, and roasted joints of meat, Firebrew offers hospitality to adventurers bound for the snowy passes of Dun Morogh or deeper into the mountain kingdom. His tavern remains a lively crossroad where miners, riflemen, and emissaries gather to escape the drafty tunnels and exchange tales around the hearth.

Innkeeper Grosk. Innkeeper Grosk manages the inn at Razor Hill, providing weary travelers with food, drink, and a place to rest in central Durotar. Located on the bustling road between the Valley of Trials and Orgrimmar, his establishment serves as the primary resting point for young Horde adventurers setting out into the wider world. Razor Hill serves as the vital crossroad settlement connecting the southern training grounds of Durotar to the high walls of Orgrimmar. At the center of this waystation stands Innkeeper Grosk, an orc tasked with sheltering warriors, scouts, and peons alike. His inn offers a respite from the harsh desert heat, stocked with basic provisions, hearty meats, and cool water for any traveler passing beneath its sturdy timbers.

Innkeeper Gryshka. Innkeeper Gryshka is an orc host who manages the Broken Tusk inn in Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. Serving as the primary hospitality contact for travelers arriving through the city gates, she provides hearthstone bindings, food, and drink to visiting Horde adventurers. She maintains close ties with hunters and scouts across Durotar and the Barrens to keep her tavern stocked with choice cuts of meat. Standing behind the counter of the Broken Tusk, Gryshka manages one of the most heavily trafficked inns in the Horde. Located just beyond the main gates of Orgrimmar in the Valley of Strength, her establishment serves as the first point of rest for warriors, messengers, and newly arrived champions seeking shelter under Thrall's banner.

Innkeeper Keldamyr. Innkeeper Keldamyr manages the hearth and lodgings of the central inn in Dolanaar, Teldrassil. He offers food, drink, and a resting place for young night elves venturing forth from Shadowglen into the wider boughs of the World Tree. Dolanaar is the primary village newcomers reach after departing the sheltered glade of Aldrassil. Innkeeper Keldamyr maintains the community's central haven, providing bread, spring water, and soft beds beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. Travelers, sentinels, and young novices bound for Darnassus frequently pause at his counter to rest their spirits, secure their hearthstones, and stock rations for the journey through the boughs.

Innkeeper Norman. Innkeeper Norman tends the hearth at the primary tavern in the Trade Quarter of the Undercity. A quiet, diligent Forsaken, he offers travelers of the Horde respite, hearthstone bindings, and food suited to the varied tastes of both the living and the dead. Located in the bustling Trade Quarter beneath the ruined Capital City of Lordaeron, Innkeeper Norman provides lodging for emissaries, mercenaries, and adventurers passing through the Forsaken stronghold. Despite the damp chill and alchemical stenches of the Undercity, Norman's tavern remains a bustling hub for travelers looking to anchor their hearthstones, share news from across Azeroth, or prepare for expeditions into the Plaguelands.

Innkeeper Pala. Innkeeper Pala manages the Cat and the Shaman, the bustling tavern situated on the lower tier of Thunder Bluff. She offers visiting adventurers a hearthstone binding, cold drinks, and a place to rest between journeys across Mulgore and beyond. Perched on the lower rise of Thunder Bluff's sweeping mesas, Innkeeper Pala tends the hearth at the Cat and the Shaman. The establishment serves as one of the primary gathering points for travelers stepping off the central lifts or arriving from the sprawling plains of Mulgore. Holding a steady vigil over her common room, Pala ensures that weary warriors, wandering druids, and visiting allies of the Horde find a dependable shelter, a warm drink, and a familiar home away from home.

Innkeeper Renee. Innkeeper Renee runs the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, offering shelter, food, and drink to the Forsaken and to Horde travelers passing through Tirisfal Glades. Renee keeps the Gallows' End Tavern, the inn at the heart of Brill. Behind her counter she sells food, drink and general goods, and she welcomes weary newcomers to rest their bones, remarking that the Forsaken certainly do have huge appetites. For the undead of Tirisfal, her tavern is a cozy little place where victims of the plague try to make their way in the world.

Inquire at the Inn. Inquire at the Inn is an Alliance quest in Darkshire that continues the investigation into the mysterious stranger connected to Sven Yorgen's ruined farm. Directed by Clerk Daltry, adventurers take a recovered journal to the Scarlet Raven Tavern to question Tavernkeep Smitts about who stayed there. After Clerk Daltry finishes examining the tattered book recovered from Sven Yorgen's farm, he suggests that any stranger visiting Darkshire would almost certainly have passed through the local tavern. The Scarlet Raven Tavern stands across town as Darkshire's only gathering hall and lodging house, making it the most sensible place to track down transient visitors.

Insane Druids. Investigating Forsaken incursions in eastern Ashenvale, Kayneth Stillwind uncovers a tragic massacre deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The resident druids were poisoned and slaughtered in their sleep by undead agents, leaving their maddened spirits trapped in torment. Alliance adventurers are tasked with granting eternal rest to their slain leaders to soothe the agonizing spiritual blight. While battling the effects of virulent Forsaken toxins recovered in eastern Ashenvale, the night elf sentinel Kayneth Stillwind was struck by a terrifying waking vision. Beneath the earthen mounds of the nearby Dor'Danil Barrow Den, he witnessed an atrocity: the druids resting within had been quietly poisoned and slaughtered by undead infiltrators. Rather than passing peacefully into nature's embrace, their souls were severed violently from their flesh, warped by unnatural venom into shrieking, errant specters.

Insane Scribbles. Torn from the baffling Twilight Tome, these Insane Scribbles are a fragment of dark literature carried by cultists in Darkshore. Merely looking at the dancing text and distorted scrollwork induces severe dizziness and mental strain. Ancient protectors of the forest study such fragments to decipher the sinister motives of the Twilight's Hammer. Gazing upon the pages of the Twilight Tome proves profoundly hazardous to mortal sanity. The script writhes across the parchment, while graceful scrollwork warps into grotesque, unsettling imagery before the reader's eyes. Tearing loose even a single sheet—these Insane Scribbles—is an ordeal that leaves the bearer lightheaded and disoriented. Despite the chaotic incoherence of the script, the parchment hums with a primal, deeply ancient magic tied directly to dark powers long buried beneath Azeroth.

Inscribed Bark. Inscribed Bark is a living parchment entrusted by the ancient Oracle Tree to carry word of Teldrassil's state to Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm. It serves as an official report on the boughs of the World Tree and the lingering threats troubling its woods. Carved from the sacred wood of the Oracle Tree, this inscribed bark acts as a direct communique between the ancient guardian and the leadership of the Cenarion Circle in Darnassus. After adventurers suppress the encroaching harpies in the glades, the Oracle Tree entrusts them with this token, reluctant to risk ordinary couriers through the tainted paths of the boughs. The inscribed message informs Arch Druid Fandral Staghelm of both recent victories and the deeper, unsettling blight that continues to grip Teldrassil.

Insect Part Analysis. With Scrimshank lost, Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser sets about going over the surveying gear and putting Scrimshank's personal effects in order, and asks you to call on Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan about the insect parts. Fizzledowser means to spend some time with Scrimshank's surveying gear and personal effects, and has a sneaking feeling that these bugs will claim more losses. You are asked to call on Alchemist Pestlezugg in Gadgetzan and learn whether the insect parts the surveyors sent have been processed yet. If they are ready, Fizzledowser wants them brought back.

Insect Part Analysis. Alchemist Pestlezugg has finished the report on the insect parts and says Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser must see it at once. The threat faces Tanaris and Gadgetzan and, if left unchecked, all of southern Kalimdor. Pestlezugg insists that Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser must see the report right away, and that everyone who can read must see it too. The threat is grave and serious, for Tanaris and Gadgetzan and, if left unchecked, for all of southern Kalimdor. It may even reach the whole of Azeroth, for it has given no sign that it will subside. You are asked to carry the report to Fizzledowser in Gadgetzan and have a duplicate made, to share freely with your allegiance. Everyone must know of this threat.

Intact Raptor Horn. An intact horn harvested from the predatory raptors stalking the savannas of the Barrens. Kept in pristine condition, it is coveted by an entrepreneurial goblin looking to tap into rumors of raptor intelligence. While common hunters value raptor parts for hides, talons, and trophies, unbroken horns are harder to come by in the field. In the port town of Ratchet, an eccentric goblin alchemist named Mebok Mizzyrix has formulated a wild theory regarding local wildlife: because the raptors of the Barrens display cunning beyond their kin elsewhere, he suspects their intellect resides directly within their headgear. By grinding whole horns down and brewing them into tonic concoctions, Mebok aims to bottle this perceived genius into commercial 'smart drinks.'

Interrogator Vishas. Interrogator James Vishas is the Scarlet Crusade's master of torment, stationed deep within the Scarlet Monastery's Graveyard wing. Infamous for his shrill voice and sheer cruelty, he takes twisted pleasure in breaking captives and testing the limits of mortal flesh. Few who enter his torture chambers ever leave with their minds or bodies intact. Within the dark crypts and burial grounds of the Scarlet Monastery, Interrogator Vishas tends to the Crusade's captive enemies. While the zealots outside march in gleaming armor under banners of purity, Vishas represents the grim reality behind their crusade: unbridled sadism cloaked in religious righteous fury. He approaches interrogation not merely as an intelligence duty, but as a prized craft, reveling in the agony of Forsaken captives, captured Scourge, and any living travelers unlucky enough to be branded heretics.

Into the Field. Apothecary Zinge sends you into the Tanaris desert with a field testing kit to test the tissue of basilisks, scorpids and hyenas. The modified kit also needs a power source that the goblins of Gadgetzan have, so Zinge points you to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle there. Apothecary Zinge wants the consistency of the tissue of the desert's basilisks, scorpids and hyenas tested. You gather samples and run them through the testing kit you carry, though a good chunk of the samples will fail. Eight acceptable samples of each kind of creature are needed, and Zinge asks you to return only once you have succeeded.

Intrepid Strongbox Key. The Intrepid Strongbox Key is a rusted iron key once guarded jealously by Captain Halyndor, commander of the doomed Alliance vessel Intrepid. Even in undeath, the captain clutches it, keeping locked away the cursed artifact that brought ruin to his crew off the coast of the Wetlands. During the wreck of the Third Fleet off the stormy shores of the Wetlands, the warship Intrepid was cast into ruin, its crew twisted into restless, cursed spirits. Captain Halyndor obsessively watched over a mysterious item stowed inside the vessel's heavy strongbox. In death, his spectral figure continues to prowl the waterlogged deck, refusing to relinquish the rusted key that unlocks the hold's deepest, darkest cargo.

name.frFR: Enquête sur la crête aux échos

text.enUS: Investigate Echo Ridge. Marshal McBride sends recruits north as kobolds gather at Echo Ridge Mine. The mine supplies ore and raw materials to Northshire Abbey and the Stormwind guard, and the growing threat puts both at risk. After early skirmishes with scattered vermin around Northshire's forested edge, scouts report a more organized threat. Kobolds have gathered in force at Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride sends you north to face the workers at the entrance and learn how deeply they have settled in.

name.frFR: Enquêter dans le magasin de l'Alchimiste

text.enUS: Investigate the Alchemist Shop. Investigate the Alchemist Shop is an Undercity quest for Horde mages tasked with resolving an arcane anomaly in the Apothecarium. Guided by Anastasia Hartwell, practitioners track and capture invisible creatures made of pure magical energy running loose inside Algernon's shop. The Undercity is no stranger to unnatural phenomena, but the Apothecarium recently developed a problem of purely arcane origin. Unseen magical entities were detected wandering Algernon's alchemy shop, passing silently among bubbling cauldrons and toxic reagents. Recognizing an unnatural breach in the flow of magic, the Undercity's mage instructor, Anastasia Hartwell, directs promising arcane initiates to investigate and contain the entities before catastrophic damage occurs.

Investigate the Camp. Investigate the Camp is an expedition task originating in Booty Bay to scout a newly established hunters' campsite in Stranglethorn Vale. Commissioned by Krazek, it tasks travelers with confirming rumors that the legendary dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary has arrived near Lake Nazferiti. Reports circulating through the docks of Booty Bay speak of an expedition of big-game hunters encamped in the northern jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Word has reached Krazek that the camp lies along the river just past the Venture Company's busy mining claim near Lake Nazferiti. In a lawless jungle teeming with dangers and competing interests, unexplained armed encampments always demand a watchful eye.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Darnassus
name.zhCN: 调查达纳苏斯的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus. Investigate the Scourge of Darnassus is an emergency mission issued by Lieutenant Beitha on behalf of the Argent Dawn. With a necropolis looming over the Scourge encampment, Alliance defenders are tasked with destroying encroaching undead and deciphering the dark runic circles appearing outside the city gates. The Scourge invasion has reached the sheltered boughs of Teldrassil. Floating necropolises appear in the sky, vomiting forth ghouls, skeletons, and necromantic horrors right outside Darnassus. Lieutenant Beitha of the Argent Dawn has stepped forward to coordinate the capital's defense, enlisting willing volunteers to blunt the vanguard and gather intelligence before the undead can overwhelm the night elven homeland.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Forgefer
name.zhCN: 调查铁炉堡的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Ironforge. Lieutenant Nevell of the Argent Dawn calls upon brave defenders as the Scourge arrives directly outside the gates of Ironforge. Undead troops and ominous runic circles threaten the snowy passes of Dun Morogh beneath a hovering necropolis. Defenders are tasked with destroying the walking corpses and deciphering the purpose behind these strange glowing sigils. The Scourge invasion does not stop at Lordaeron or the plagued lands of the north. Floating necropolises cast grim shadows across Azeroth, including the frigid heights of Dun Morogh right outside Ironforge's mountain entrance. The Argent Dawn has stationed observers such as Lieutenant Nevell to monitor and counter this creeping blight before it can breach the fortress of the Bronzebeards.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Orgrimmar
name.zhCN: 调查奥格瑞玛的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Orgrimmar. The Scourge has brazenly established an encampment right outside the gates of Orgrimmar under the shadow of a floating necropolis. Lieutenant Dagel tasks defenders with repelling the undead, recovering necrotic stones, and probing the mysterious runic circles humming with necromantic energy. This sudden intrusion brings the Lich King's reach directly to the heart of Durotar. The threat of the Scourge is no longer confined to the ruined kingdoms of Lordaeron or the icy wastes of the north. Floating necropolises have appeared across Azeroth, casting dark shadows even over Durotar. At Orgrimmar's very threshold, undead forces have gathered, carving out encampments and threatening the capital of the Horde. Lieutenant Dagel and the Argent Dawn are coordinating defensive efforts, calling upon local champions to push the invaders back before they can establish an unbreakable siege.

name.frFR: Enquêter au sujet du Fléau à Hurlevent
name.zhCN: 调查暴风城的天灾入侵

text.enUS: Investigate the Scourge of Stormwind. Scourge forces press against Stormwind, with necropolises looming beyond its walls. Lieutenant Orrin calls defenders to strike their camps, gather Necrotic Stones, and study the runes there. Scourge forces have reached the outskirts of Stormwind City. Necropolises float overhead as undead and cultists take hold near the kingdom’s greatest bastion. Lieutenant Orrin gathers defenders outside the city to drive them back before they threaten the capital.

Invisibility Liquor. Invisibility Liquor gives Maybell Maclure a way to slip from her family's sight and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. Their households are locked in a feud. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks a quiet meeting with Maybell Maclure, though their families' feud keeps the households apart. Their kin watch closely, and ordinary secrecy is not enough. Invisibility Liquor lets the drinker pass unseen across the disputed farmland.

Iris Lake. Iris Lake is a blighted body of water resting in north-central Ashenvale, east of Astranaar. Once pristine, its waters have turned a sickly yellowish-green from demonic corruption seeping down from Felwood, and hostile bog beasts now prowl its shores. Nestled between Astranaar and the moonwell tended by Shael'dryn, Iris Lake stands as a grim reminder of the wounds inflicted during the Third War. Fel energies drifting south from the tainted heights of Felwood have poisoned the basin, turning its once-clear waters into a foul, sickly yellow-green mire. The corruption has twisted the native plant life and water spirits, raising aggressive bog beasts that lash out at any traveler who wanders near.

Iron Coral. Iron Coral is an Alliance quest given by the gnome blacksmith Klockmort Spannerspan in Tinker Town, Ironforge. Eager to test newly shared smithing methods on a custom suit of armor, Klockmort sends you to dive for rare searing coral along the coast of the Wetlands. Completing his request allows him to fuse gnomish ingenuity with dwarven craftsmanship. After exchanging insights with the master dwarven smith Furen Longbeard, Klockmort Spannerspan is bursting with inspiration. The eccentric gnome blacksmith wants to combine Furen's metallurgy with his own tinkering ideas to craft an exceptionally resilient suit of armor. To pull off this daring metallurgical experiment, standard mountain ores will not suffice; Klockmort requires an unusual, naturally hardened marine element known as searing coral.

Iron Pike. Iron Pikes are sturdy construction materials originally shipped from Stormwind to aid in repairing the Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire. The shipment was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, leaving the town short on essential rebuilding supplies. When Lakeshire faced recent attacks from the Blackrock orcs, the town's metal reserves were melted down to forge armor, blades, and ammunition for defense. In response to the shortage, local builders requested a resupply shipment of iron from Stormwind City. Before the materials could reach the town, a pack of Redridge gnolls hijacked the transport caravan along the road. The gnolls dragged crates of iron pikes and rivets north into the hills, halting critical repairs on the Everstill Bridge.

Iron Pommel. The Iron Pommel is the final missing fragment of Dartol's Rod, a rod created by the long-dead wizard Dartol and sought by the night elves of Astranaar to slow the furbolg attacks on their people. Entrusted to the druids of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den for safekeeping, it was lost when their sanctuary was slaughtered and overrun by oozes. Dartol's Rod was divided and scattered across Ashenvale to protect its mystic power. The Iron Pommel was placed into the care of the night elf druids dwelling near the road winding south toward the Barrens. Tragedy struck the secluded enclave at the Dor'Danil Barrow Den when the circle was massacred, their tranquil shelter falling into ruined silence. The pommel vanished into the aftermath, swallowed by the grotesque, bubbling oozes that now shamble through the defiled glade.

Iron Rivet. Iron Rivets are sturdy construction fasteners manufactured in Stormwind to help rebuild the ruined Everstill Bridge in Lakeshire. After a supply caravan was ambushed and looted by Redridge gnolls, these heavy metal components ended up scattered across the gnoll camps in the northern hills. When Lakeshire faced repeated assaults from the Blackrock orcs, the town council was forced to melt down their structural iron reserves to forge urgent weapons, armor, and munitions. Once the immediate crisis subsided, Foreman Oslow requested fresh building supplies from Stormwind to mend the fractured Everstill Bridge. However, the supply caravan ferrying the shipment was ambushed by local Redridge gnolls before reaching the town. The pack beasts and wagons were dragged into the hills north of Lake Everstill, scattering essential construction materials like iron rivets and pikes among the gnoll packs.

Iron Shaft. The Iron Shaft is a metallic segment of Dartol's Rod, a relic Raene Wolfrunner's friend Teronis sought in hopes of slowing the furbolg assaults on Ashenvale. Recovered from a locked chest near the border of Felwood, it serves as a crucial component in restoring the relic for the defenders of Ashenvale. Dartol's Rod was the creation of Dartol, and its pieces were scattered across Ashenvale; one was even given to the druids of Dor'Danil for safekeeping. The Iron Shaft represents the sturdy metal core of the instrument, secured away inside a locked chest in a secluded glade near the northern border of Ashenvale, not far from the tainted realm of Felwood.

Ironband's Compound. Ironforge smith Tormus Deepforge seeks vengeance for his mentor, Sturgy Ironband, whose remote teaching outpost in eastern Dun Morogh fell to a sudden and bloody assault. The slaughter followed the arrival of a rare umbral ore shipment, which immediately drew the violent attention of the Dark Iron dwarves. Sturgy Ironband was revered across Ironforge as an unmatched instructor of the smithing craft. From his secluded compound south of Helm's Bed Lake, he instructed promising pupils far from the crowded anvils of the Great Forge. That peaceful enterprise ended abruptly when one of his students acquired an unfamiliar mineral dubbed umbral ore. Intrigued by its properties, Ironband resolved to experiment with the sample, entirely unaware that possessing it had marked his school for ruin.

Ironband's Compound. Ironband's Compound is a fortified outpost tucked into the snowy hills south of Helm's Bed Lake in eastern Dun Morogh. Formerly home to the prospector Sturgy Ironband, the camp has been overrun by hostile Dark Iron dwarves who attack anyone venturing too close. Originally established by Sturgy Ironband, this compound south of Helm's Bed Lake once served as a staging post in the snowy wilderness of Dun Morogh. That changed when Dark Iron infiltrators pushed deep into Bronzebeard territory and seized the site for themselves. Now bristling with hostile dwarves, the compound serves as an enemy forward base threatening travelers and nearby settlements, right under the nose of Ironforge.

Ironband's Excavation. Ironband's Excavation is an Alliance quest connecting Thelsamar to an ongoing archaeological dig east of the loch. Jern Hornhelm grows suspicious over unexplained supply delays, dispatching an adventurer to discover what stalls Prospector Ironband's team. Upon reaching the dig site, the truth quickly emerges: a relentless horde of troggs has overrun the ruins. In the town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm monitors shipments sent across Loch Modan to the Explorers' League. Despite a steady stream of provisions and tools, the dig site led by Prospector Ironband has reported minimal progress. Knowing Ironband as an upright, diligent dwarf, Hornhelm fears that something untoward has disrupted the operation rather than mere laziness.

Ironband's Excavation Site. Ironband's Excavation Site is an expansive dwarven dig located in southeastern Loch Modan, just south of the lake and southwest of Farstrider Lodge. Led by Prospector Ironband, the archaeological operation was abruptly halted when aggressive, volatile troggs overran the trenches. Spurred by the dwarven drive to uncover their ancient Titan origins, Prospector Ironband established this sprawling digsite along the rugged cliffs of southeastern Loch Modan. What began as a promising excavation quickly turned into a disaster when the digging disturbed an unusually fierce and large breed of subterranean troggs. The creatures surged from the earth, driving back the miners and setting up camp amidst the scattered tools, broken carts, and half-excavated relics.

name.zhCN: 铁环挖掘场的进度报告

text.enUS: Ironband's Progress Report. Ironband's Progress Report is a written dispatch detailing the troubles facing Prospector Ironband's excavation site in eastern Loch Modan. It conveys both an account of slow digging hindered by aggressive troggs and an urgent plea for more blastpowder. Prospector Ironband's excavation in Loch Modan faces continuous disruption from local troggs. To keep the project moving forward, Ironband compiled this progress report to restate his desperate need for blastpowder. Carried first to Jern Hornhelm in Thelsamar and then forwarded to the Assembly of Explorers in Ironforge, the report documents the site's stalls while requesting heavy munitions. The dispatch quickly raises eyebrows among league leadership, as an ample supply of blastpowder was dispatched to Ironband weeks prior, leaving superiors wondering where the previous shipments vanished.

Ironbeard's Tomb. Ironbeard's Tomb is a defiled dwarven burial site situated west of the road leading north toward Dun Modr in the Wetlands. Marked by an outdoor graveyard and a stone statue of its namesake, the crypt has fallen into disuse as acidic oozes swarm the grounds. Travelers rarely set foot in the hollow unless searching for lost possessions swallowed by the slime. Overlooking the marshes along the road north to Dun Modr, Ironbeard's Tomb stands as a testament to the dwarven presence in the Wetlands. A monumental stone statue, presumed to depict Ironbeard himself, watches over the surrounding burial plot. Yet solemn peace no longer keeps vigil here. The subterranean crypt has been completely overrun by oozes of various black and crimson strains, leaving the tomb contaminated. Dwarves no longer bring their dead to this ruined sanctuary, and those brave enough to disturb the vaults do so primarily to hunt through the remains digested by the lurking slimes.

Ironclad Cove. Ironclad Cove is a massive subterranean cavern hidden beneath Westfall, housing an underground shipyard and dock. It serves as the secret construction dock for the Defias Brotherhood's war juggernaught and connects directly to the sea. Buried at the deepest point of the Deadmines, Ironclad Cove is a monumental sea cavern converted into a fortified dockyard. Here, Edwin VanCleef and the Defias Brotherhood have constructed an enormous warship known as the juggernaught. The cavern features extensive wooden scaffolding, islets, and loading catwalks manned by Defias pirates, deckhands, and overseers. Its existence reveals the true scale of the Defias threat: VanCleef intends not merely to raid Westfall's farmsteads, but to assemble a private naval force capable of bombarding the shores of Stormwind itself.

Ironforge. Ironforge is the underground capital city of the dwarves, excavated deep into the stone of Ironforge Mountain within Dun Morogh. Centered around the roaring Great Forge, it serves as the political and mercantile anchor of the Kingdom of Khaz Modan and a bulwark of the Alliance. Carved into the subterranean depths of Ironforge Mountain, the city is arranged in concentric stone rings radiating out from the monumental Great Forge. Originally founded millenia ago after the dwarves awakened and migrated from Uldaman, it has weathered ages of history, including the ancient War of the Three Hammers that left the Bronzebeard clan in sole control. Powered by cascading torrents of molten magma and fortified behind massive stone gates, the cavern city is equal parts industrial powerhouse and impenetrable bastion. Beyond dwarven craftsmen and warriors, its halls also host a substantial population of exiled gnomes following the recent fall of Gnomeregan.

Ironforge Airfield. Tucked away high in the snowy peaks northeast of Ironforge, this remote dwarven airstrip serves as a proving ground and staging area for gnome flying machines and dwarven mountaineers. Unmarked by main roads, the plateau overlooks the jagged crags of Dun Morogh and the steep descent toward the Wetlands. Perched far above the beaten trails of Dun Morogh, the high-altitude airfield is a quiet marvel of Alliance cooperation. Sheltered by surrounding mountain peaks, dwarven masonry anchors the blustery ridgelines while gnomish flying machines sit parked along open landing strips. Mountaineers keep watch over the perimeter alongside engineers busy wrenching gears and inspecting steam-belching engines in the biting cold.

Ironstone Camp. Ironstone Camp is an outpost established by the Horde along the western border of the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Originally deployed to expel Alliance dwarven excavators from the nearby digsite, the encampment's forces now face a deadly threat after subterranean silithid overran the excavation. Ironstone Camp sits directly on the threshold between the high pillars of Thousand Needles and the blazing salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats. The Horde detachment stationed here was initially dispatched with a clear and singular objective: dislodge the dwarven excavators digging at the Rustmaul Digsite. However, their military confrontation was cut short when a swarm of voracious silithid burst forth from a nearby cavern, violently engulfing the dig and attacking both sides. Led by Moktar Krin, the surviving camp defenders have diverted their efforts to combating the insectoid infestation before the swarm spreads unchecked across the region.

Irontree Woods. Irontree Woods is a blighted grove situated in northern Felwood, once cherished by the night elves as a peaceful forest sanctuary. Ravaged by the demonic corruption of the Third War, its ancient protectors have been petrified into stone while twisted treants and elementals prowl among the ruins. Irontree Woods was once a tranquil woodland glade tended by the kaldorei, but the demonic taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War choked the life from its soil. The grove's guardian Ancients—Hastat, Stoma, and Vartrus—succumbed to the dark magic, petrifying into lifeless stone monuments that still stand entombed amid the corrupted brush. Now, maddened treants, vile bog beasts, and tainted water elementals wander the twisted forest floor, striking violently at any travelers who dare approach.

Isha Awak. Isha Awak is a sacred rite of the hunt issued by the mystic Mahren Skyseer along the Merchant Coast. Brave Horde wanderers are charged with diving into the Great Sea to track down and slay a fearsome aquatic predator known as the Deep Doom. By claiming the beast's heart, the hunter partakes in an ancient bond of spirit and respect. Off the coast south of Ratchet, lurking beneath the waves, roams Isha Awak. Known as the Deep Doom, this immense sea creature commands the coastal waters with formidable strength and predatory solemnity. The human encroachers encamped along the shoreline have learned to dread the waters, having lost many of their scouts and soldiers to the creature's relentless hunger.

Ishamuhale. Ishamuhale is a rite of the hunt assigned by Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo. To test your prowess and respect for nature's deadliest predators, you are directed to bait and slay the fiercest sunscale raptor in the Barrens. Among the predators of the Barrens, sunscale raptors are feared for their cunning and vicious pack tactics, but none commands more dread than Ishamuhale. Known as Speartooth, he does not stalk the savannah merely for food or territory. As Jorn Skyseer explains, Ishamuhale hunts out of sheer instinct and passion—he kills simply because it is his nature to kill. Facing such a creature tests whether a hunter can withstand pure, unbridled feral malice.

Ishamuhale's Fang. Ishamuhale's Fang is a hunting trophy taken from Ishamuhale, the notorious sunscale raptor known as Speartooth in the Barrens. Brought to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, the tooth serves as proof of besting one of Kalimdor's deadliest natural predators. Ishamuhale is feared across the central savanna as the fiercest sunscale raptor alive, an apex hunter said to kill purely out of predatory passion rather than mere hunger. Lured into the open with fresh zhevra meat beside a withered tree northwest of Ratchet, the beast offers no quarter. Severing its massive fang proves to the hunting instructors of the Horde that a traveler has conquered not just a beast, but the sheer savagery of the plains.

Isle of Dread. The Isle of Dread is a desolate, cliff-bound island situated in the Great Sea off the southwestern coast of Feralas, south of Sardor Isle. It is notorious for sheltering monstrous two-headed chimaeroks and an entrenched coven of hostile naga hidden within its subterranean sea caves. Rising out of the crashing surf of the South Seas, the Isle of Dread lives up to its ominous name. Ringed by sheer cliffs, the island's interior valley is only accessible through a narrow pathway on its southeastern coast. Within this enclosed highland roams a lethal population of chimaeroks—ravenous, two-headed beasts empowered by ambient arcane energies. These beasts are led by the monstrous Lord Lakmaeran, making the island a deadly deathtrap for unwary explorers who cross the channel from Sardor Isle.

Islen Waterseer. Islen Waterseer is a respected tauren shaman who dwells beside a quiet fishing hut on the Tidus Stair, overlooking the eastern sea of the Barrens. Possessing an intimate communion with the spirits of water, she guides initiates on the trials necessary to attune with the element. Novice shamans across the Horde seek her wisdom to earn their Water Totem. Far from the bustling crossroads and encampments of the Barrens, Islen Waterseer lives along the craggy coastline known as the Tidus Stair. Here, where the arid plains break against the Great Sea, the presence of the water spirits is raw and pervasive. Rather than dwelling in thunderous halls or busy cities, Islen prefers this quiet outpost, dedicating her days to listening to the tides and assisting shamans who seek communion with the fluid element.

Items of Some Consequence. Tyrion gathers silk and apples for a spy inside Stormwind Keep. The covert operative needs the materials to disguise Spybot and send it past the royal guards to listen in on Lord Lescovar. Elling Trias has moved the operation against Lord Gregor Lescovar forward. The cheese merchant suspects Lescovar's schemes inside Stormwind Keep threaten the realm. In the keep's gardens, Tyrion agrees to the tighter schedule, but says the disguise needs careful preparation.

Itharius's Cave. Itharius's Cave is a secluded hollow tucked into the far southwestern cliffs of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as the refuge of the enigmatic Itharius, who appears to be a high elf and tends to the brood of green dragonkin inhabiting the surrounding marsh. Tucked away in the treacherous, moss-draped crags of the southwestern Swamp of Sorrows, this damp cavern shelters the recluse Itharius. Outside its mouth, unruly green whelps wander the mire. Though he appears to be a high elf, a folk who rarely wander so far south into wild swamps alone, Itharius keeps a watchful eye on these young dragonkin as they grow, living alongside them in quiet isolation.

Ivar Patch. The Ivar Patch is a blighted pumpkin farm located in northern Silverpine Forest. Once a thriving agricultural homestead of Lordaeron, its residents were wiped out during the Third War and transformed into ravenous, mindlessly hostile ghouls. Before the Third War swept through Lordaeron, this pumpkin patch was a prosperous homestead owned by a farmer named Ivar, who employed a lively crew of farmhands and servants. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the countryside, the farm was consumed completely. Rather than rising with their minds intact like the free-willed Forsaken, Ivar, his family, and his laborers were reduced to rotting, feral ghouls bound to prowl the ruined soil.

Ivar the Foul. Ivar the Foul is a quest in Silverpine Forest that marks the culmination of the reconnaissance mission undertaken by Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick. Trapped at the farmstead known as the Ivar Patch, Rane asks Horde travelers to eliminate the savage ghoul Ivar the Foul so Quinn can recover from his mauling and complete their report to High Executor Hadrec. Siblings Rane and Quinn Yorick were deployed by the Deathstalkers to conduct reconnaissance across Silverpine Forest on behalf of High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Their reconnaissance grinded to a sudden, violent halt when moving through a farmstead in the northern forest, where they were ambushed by the vicious ghoul known as Ivar the Foul.

Ivar's Head. Ivar's Head is the gruesome proof of the destruction of the ravenous ghoul Ivar the Foul in Silverpine Forest. It is sought by the Deathstalker Rane Yorick to ensure safe recovery for her wounded brother Quinn. While scouting northern Silverpine Forest on the orders of High Executor Hadrec, the Forsaken Deathstalkers Rane and Quinn Yorick were ambushed at an abandoned farmstead by a feral ghoul known as Ivar the Foul. Though the siblings managed to fend off the fiend, Quinn was severely mauled in the confrontation. Stranded at the ruined farm while her brother recovered, Rane could not safely leave Quinn unattended to complete their mission. Severing Ivar's head provides definitive proof that the beast will never terrorize the estate again, granting Quinn the necessary time to recuperate under Rane's watchful eye.

Iverron. Iverron is a young night elf found in Shadowglen, the sheltered starting bough of Teldrassil. Stricken by the venom of the woodland's increasingly agitated arachnids, his plight serves as an early warning of the growing corruption within the World Tree. While wandering through the quiet canopies of Shadowglen, Iverron ran afoul of the webwood spiders nesting in the vale. Succumbing quickly to their toxic bite, the young elf was left incapacitated, unable to return to safety on his own. His helpless condition highlights the sudden aggression sweeping through creatures that once shared the glade in peace.

Iverron's Antidote. Iverron's Antidote is an urgent task in Shadowglen to save a poisoned night elf scout. By gathering wild mushrooms, lilies, and spider ichor, adventurers help Dirania Silvershine brew a remedy before the venom takes full hold. While scouting the boughs of Shadowglen, young Iverron fell victim to the poisonous fangs of the local Webwood spiders. Collapsed and dying, his survival depends entirely on the herbal knowledge of Dirania Silvershine at Aldrassil. With the youth fading fast, she must quickly prepare a specialized concoction to neutralize the aggressive venom coursing through his blood.

Iverron's Antidote. This errand tasks an adventurer with racing against time to deliver freshly brewed medicine to a poisoned night elf scout. Stranded outside a spider-infested cave in Shadowglen, Iverron depends entirely on Dirania Silvershine's herbal concoction before the potent mixture loses its efficacy. Dirania Silvershine crafts the curative brew using freshly harvested venom sacs, lily roots, and hyacinth fungi, but its unstable alchemical nature poses a grave risk. The medicine retains its potency for a mere five minutes after distillation. Anyone carrying the vial must sprint directly from the glade toward the northern heights without hesitation.

Iverron's Antidote (item). Iverron's Antidote is a delicate medicinal draught concocted by Dirania Silvershine in Shadowglen. Specially brewed to neutralize the lethal venom of the local Webwood spiders, the mixture is highly unstable and spoils rapidly once prepared. Crafted by Dirania Silvershine in Aldrassil, this antidote is formulated to counteract the potent venom afflicting the young night elf Iverron. Due to the volatile nature of its ingredients and herbal catalysts, the draught possesses an exceptionally short shelf life, remaining viable for only five minutes after brewing. Courier messengers must sprint north toward the Webwood cave without delay to deliver the concoction before it degrades into useless slurry.

text.enUS: JOB OPPORTUNITY: Culling the Competition. A notice announces that Taskmaster Scrange wants some capable hands to cull the competition in the Searing Gorge. The work is slaying Dark Iron Taskmasters and Dark Iron Slavers until your clothes are bloody enough, then returning to Scrange. Scrange wants applicants to head out through the gorge and slaughter the Dark Iron Taskmasters and Dark Iron Slavers they meet: fifteen of each. Come back when your clothes are bloody enough. You will know when that is, and you are not to ask.

Jade Phial. The Jade Phial is a specially crafted vessel provided by the night elf druid Corithras Moonrage in Dolanaar. It is designed to safely draw and transport sacred water from Teldrassil's moonwells to replenish the druids' central well in Darnassus. Teldrassil is dotted with moonwells that channel lunar and natural energies vital to night elf society and druidic worship. As part of maintaining this harmony, the central moonwell used by the druids in Darnassus must periodically be replenished from the outlying wells across the great bough. Corithras Moonrage entrusts young initiates with the Jade Phial, a receptacle carefully prepared to gather pure waters from the moonwell near Starbreeze Village without disturbing its delicate spiritual potency.

Jadefire Run. Jadefire Run is a heavily fortified satyr encampment nestled in northern Felwood. It houses some of the most powerful and cunning satyrs in the region, serving as a bastion of demonic corruption deep within the tainted forest. Situated amid the blighted woods of northern Felwood, Jadefire Run functions as a stronghold for the Jadefire satyrs. Unlike lesser outposts scattered throughout the valley, this camp features substantial demonic construction and shelters formidable spellcasters and tricksters. The satyrs here actively conspire to spread corruption further across Kalimdor, employing dark sorcery and foul trickery against anyone who dares intrude on their territory.

Jaedenar. Jaedenar is a blighted hollow in central Felwood built over ancient night elf ruins and druidic barrow dens. Named in foul homage to the demon lord Kil'jaeden, it serves as the primary base of operations for the Shadow Council in northern Kalimdor. Cultists, warlocks, and summoned demons scour the corrupt hollow, guarding the subterranean descent into the Shadow Hold. Long ago, these hollows sheltered night elf sacred grounds and slumbering druids connected to the Emerald Dream. After the devastation of the Third War, the vile remnant of the Shadow Council laid claim to the valley, christening it Jaedenar to honor the demon lord Kil'jaeden. Warlocks—predominantly renegade orcs and Forsaken—have gathered here alongside satyrs, succubi, and felguards. They occupy both the surface ruins and the deeper barrow dens, twisting what was once holy woodland into a grim center of demonic invocation.

Jagged Reef. The Jagged Reef forms the rugged northern coast of Azshara, where sandy beaches meet jagged stone spurs and churning surf. Treacherous rocks lurk beneath the shallow water, making maritime travel impossible. The desolate shore is primarily populated by prowling hydras, scavenging makrura, and territorial murloc tribes. Stretching across Azshara's northern edge, the Jagged Reef is a harsh littoral expanse where broken cliffs and jutting stone outcroppings divide the sandy shores into secluded inlets. Beneath the breaking waves lie submerged crags and shifting shallows, turning the waters into a graveyard for any vessel foolish enough to venture near. On land, the wild coastline offers little comfort; salt-crusted beasts, predatory hydras, and aggressive makrura wander the surf line alongside entrenched murlocs scouring the tides for scraps and unwary prey.

Jaggedswine Farm. Jaggedswine Farm is a modest livestock steading situated in northern Durotar, just south of the main entrance to Orgrimmar. Comprising a timber storage shed, a sprawling pen, and a muddy watering hole, it serves as a critical food source raising hardy swine for the nearby Horde capital. Carved out of Durotar's unforgiving, sunbaked earth, Jaggedswine Farm represents the harsh reality of sustaining an urban stronghold like Orgrimmar. The red soil of the region yields sparse agriculture, making robust livestock essential to feeding thousands of orcish warriors and laborers. The farm centers on a timber storehouse, a wide wooden pen, and a natural watering pond where swine are herded, bred, and butchered to keep the Horde's granaries stocked.

Jaguero Isle. Jaguero Isle is an isolated, jungle-covered island resting off the eastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale's Wild Shore. Dominated by fierce wild panthers and gorillas, it is infamous as the domain of the colossal silverback gorilla known as King Mukla. Situated off the southeastern coast of Stranglethorn Vale, Jaguero Isle stands well apart from the mainland pirate camps and troll ruins. The island is entirely overrun by untamed fauna, mainly panthers and aggressive gorillas. Looming over them all is the gargantuan ape King Mukla, whose rule over the rocky interior is absolute and territorial. Few sailors willingly approach its reefs, though occasionally washed-up bottles along the mainland beaches carry desperate pleas for rescue from those unfortunate enough to be stranded ashore.

Jahan Hawkwing. Jahan Hawkwing is a tauren armorer stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. He provides essential leather and chainmail gear to travelers braving the harsh, predator-filled plains. Situated at the bustling hub of the Crossroads, Jahan Hawkwing tends to the equipment needs of Horde wanderers and defenders. The Barrens is a brutal expanse where durable protective gear often makes the difference between survival and falling to centaur, quilboar, or wild beasts. Jahan works alongside local leatherworkers, handling deliveries of cured hides to keep his shop stocked with reliable tanned leather and sturdy chainmail.

Jaina Proudmoore. Lady Jaina Proudmoore is the ruler of Theramore Isle and the most powerful human sorceress alive. Formerly a star pupil of Dalaran's Kirin Tor, she led the survivors of Lordaeron across the Great Sea and now strives to maintain a fragile peace between the Alliance and the New Horde. The daughter of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore of Kul Tiras, Jaina showed remarkable aptitude for the arcane at an early age and studied under Archmage Antonidas in Dalaran. During the Third War, she investigated the mysterious Plague of Undeath alongside Prince Arthas Menethil, witnessing firsthand the tragic downfall of Lordaeron. Guided by the warnings of the Prophet Medivh, she rallied an expedition of human survivors and set sail westward to the forgotten continent of Kalimdor. There, her forces forged an unprecedented alliance with Thrall's Horde and the night elves, standing together atop Mount Hyjal to defeat Archimonde and shatter the Burning Legion's invasion.

James Halloran. James Halloran is a human tanner working out of the Wetlands to supply fine hides across the eastern continents. Based in Menethil Harbor, he makes a living harvesting the tough, prized skins of the region's native crocolisks. He relies on passing travelers and nearby trade channels to gather raw materials and transport his finished leathers to market. From his home in Menethil Harbor, James Halloran makes his living from the marshland just outside town. As an enterprising tanner, Halloran recognized that the perilous bogs offer a lucrative commodity: crocolisk skins. Transforming the rugged hide of marsh reptiles into high-quality leather requires rare craftsmanship, and Halloran's finished goods are shipped out through local trade channels to buyers all across Azeroth.

James Hyal. "James Hyal" is an Alliance quest concerning a human settler who sailed to Kalimdor with Lady Jaina Proudmoore's expedition. After setting out to open an inn on the frontier, his family in the Eastern Kingdoms lost touch with him and seeks news of his fate through Theramore's administrative records. During the Third War, countless souls left their ancestral homes in the Eastern Kingdoms to follow Lady Jaina Proudmoore across the Great Sea. Among them was James Hyal, remembered fondly by his kin as a gifted cook. After the fighting subsided and Theramore Isle was founded, James chose to carve out a living on the rugged continent of Kalimdor by opening an inn of his own to serve travellers and fellow settlers.

Janeiro's Point. Janeiro's Point is a small, rocky island situated just outside the harbor of Booty Bay in southern Stranglethorn Vale. It is crowned by a colossal stone statue of an unknown goblin welcoming incoming maritime traffic with outstretched arms. The island's waters and shores are dominated by the menacing sea giant known as Mok'rash the Cleaver. Standing as the monumental gateway to Booty Bay, Janeiro's Point greets every vessel charting a course into the southern seas of Stranglethorn Vale. Atop the crag looms an immense stone effigy of a goblin, arms spread wide in a grand gesture of welcome and unbridled mercantile ambition. Though visible to sailors and corsairs for miles around, landing on the island's shores is a perilous prospect due to Mok'rash the Cleaver, a terrifying sea giant who has claimed the outcrop as his territory.

Jangolode Mine. In Westfall’s rolling hills, the Defias Brotherhood works Jangolode Mine for itself. The mine once supplied Stormwind City with ore and raw materials. Before Westfall declined, Jangolode Mine sent metals to Stormwind City for its reconstruction and supply. As civil order weakened and the kingdom withdrew its garrisons, the Defias Brotherhood seized the mine to support its own operations. The bandits now work its rich veins and defend the shafts fiercely.

Jannok Breezesong. Jannok Breezesong is a night elf rogue trainer stationed in the village of Dolanaar on Teldrassil. He offers instruction in stealth, cunning, and bladecraft to young kaldorei rogues venturing out into the boughs of the World Tree. Found lounging beneath the boughs of Dolanaar, Jannok Breezesong serves as the primary instructor for novice night elf rogues. Unlike the formal sentinels or cloistered druids of Teldrassil, Jannok guides those who operate quietly on the fringes of society, teaching them how to stalk the shadows, strike from behind, and survive unseen amidst the boughs. Once a rogue has advanced beyond initial lessons in Dolanaar, Jannok directs them onward to more experienced masters in the capital city of Darnassus.

Jansen Stead. Jansen Stead lies just west of the Elwynn border, where Defias bandits and mechanical Harvest Watchers now roam its fields. Jansen Stead lies beside the road from Elwynn into Westfall. The farm once fed the kingdom, but unrest has driven its family from the land. Now Harvest Watchers, mechanical constructs associated with the Defias Brotherhood, patrol the fields alongside brigands. Couriers and travelers between Goldshire and Sentinel Hill pass close by.

Jarl Needs Eyes. "Swamp Eye" Jarl at Swamplight Manor wants 40 unpopped Darkmist eyes, because Darkmist eye juice is smooth and salty. The spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor. Following Soothing Spices, Jarl turns to eye juice, which is good for drinking. Most critters carry a mere pair of eyes, whereas spiders carry a great many, and Jarl finds Darkmist eye juice tasty. The Darkmist spiders live in Darkmist Cavern, west of the manor, and Jarl muses over whether the cave gave the spiders their name or the reverse.

Jarl Needs a Blade. "Swamp Eye" Jarl, in Dustwallow Marsh, has cutting to do and will not say what. Jarl wants a certain blade, a moonsteel broadsword, and does not want you to dawdle. "Swamp Eye" Jarl has cutting to do, and cannot say what is to be cut. Jarl needs a particular blade, which some call a moonsteel broadsword and Jarl calls a swing blade. You might find one in town, or a blacksmith might make one special. Jarl warns you not to sleep on it, since what is to be cut will not keep forever.

Jasper Fel. In Stormwind's Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies daggers and vials from SI:7 headquarters. He keeps watch on visitors and warns them to mind their speech. Inside SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, Jasper Fel supplies the agents who work there. He offers simple daggers and empty vials for brewing and applying poisons. Jasper works under Mathias Shaw's intelligence division and warns visitors to mind their speech. In a place built for espionage, careless words can put people in danger.

Jasperlode Mine. In north-central Elwynn, Jasperlode Mine lies lost to kobolds and giant spiders. Its shafts once supplied Stormwind City with vital iron and minerals, but the resource-strapped kingdom cannot reclaim them. Jasperlode Mine once supplied Stormwind with a steady wealth of minerals, alongside nearby Fargodeep. With the kingdom's forces stretched thin by outside threats and unrest, local garrisons cannot protect the shafts. Kobolds seized their chance, drove out the human miners, and hoarded stolen gold and tallow candles.

Je'neu Sancrea. Je'neu Sancrea is a Darkspear troll and a member of the Earthen Ring stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the Ashenvale coast. Sensing dark disturbances deep beneath the shoreline, he directs Horde adventurers to investigate the corruption infesting the ancient submerged temple of Blackfathom Deeps. While most of the Earthen Ring focuses on elemental harmony across Kalimdor, Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over the secluded and dangerous Zoram Strand. Perched at Zoram'gar Outpost, he observes the dark tremors and unnatural tides stirring near the ruined temple of Blackfathom Deeps. Though bound by the shamanic duties of his circle, his strong loyalties to the Darkspear tribe and Thrall's Horde keep him working exclusively alongside Horde champions.

text.enUS: Je'neu of the Earthen Ring. This errand directs Horde adventurers to deliver a corrupted water globe recovered from Ashenvale's elementals to Je'neu Sancrea of the Earthen Ring. As a shaman dedicated to elemental harmony, Je'neu seeks to understand the spreading corruption along the Zoram Strand and within Blackfathom Deeps. Studying the relic offers hope of halting the unnatural blight poisoning the region's waters. When strange, contaminated elementals began surfacing across Ashenvale, scouts took notice of the unnatural power animating them. Among the remains lay a befouled water globe, an intact vessel pulsing with corrupted magic. Knowing standard soldiers and scouts lacked the spiritual insight to diagnose such an anomaly, Mastok Wrilehiss directed Horde travelers to seek out someone with deep knowledge of ancient legends and elemental lore: Je'neu Sancrea.

Jen'shan. Jen'shan is a Darkspear jungle troll and hunter trainer stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She guides fledgling orc and troll marksmen as they take their first steps into the wilds of the Horde. Young hunters are directed to her to learn the basics of tracking, ranged combat, and survival. Perched among the weathered encampments of the Valley of Trials, Jen'shan serves as the primary hunter mentor for new recruits proving their worth to the Horde. Together, young orcs and Darkspear trolls arrive clutching inscribed tablets and parchments directing them straight to her side. With keen eyes sharpened by years in the untamed wilderness, she imparts foundational techniques in archery, marksmanship, and wilderness survival, ensuring no novice falls prey to the scorpids and boars prowling the canyon floor.

Jennea Cannon. In Stormwind, Jennea Cannon guides new mages through their first studies. From the Wizard's Sanctum in the Mage Quarter, she teaches caution and self-control, and investigates disturbances in local arcane energies. At the top of the Wizard's Sanctum's spiral walkway, Jennea Cannon guides those who come to Stormwind to study the arcane. She teaches more than spells, insisting that students learn caution and self-control. Even those who do not study magic hear her warning: without training, magic can burn its wielder.

Jennea's Flask. At the Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind, Jennea Cannon sends apprentices to Mirror Lake for water. They bring the sample back for arcane analysis. After magical struggles across Azeroth, arcane currents have torn loose from their ancient channels. Jennea Cannon seeks to learn how these shifts have affected Elwynn Forest. She gives promising apprentices a glass flask and sends them southwest of Stormwind's gates to the base of Mirror Lake's waterfall. The flask protects the water sample on the journey back to the Wizard's Sanctum, where it can be examined for arcane disturbances.

Jergosh the Invoker. Jergosh the Invoker is a treacherous orc warlock hiding deep within Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar. As a high-ranking leader among the Searing Blade cultists, he practices demonic arts directly under the Warchief's nose and plots against the Horde. While Thrall works tirelessly to lead the orcs along a path of honor and shamanism, Jergosh rejected these ideals in favor of raw demonic power. Concealing himself within the subterranean labyrinth of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar, he gathered followers into the Searing Blade, an insidious sect aligned with the remnants of the Shadow Council. Operating in the shadows directly below the Horde capital, Jergosh works to undo everything the new Horde stands for.

Jern Hornhelm. Jern Hornhelm is a dwarven miner affiliated with the Explorers' League, stationed in the town of Thelsamar. He coordinates vital logistics and communication between the settlement, Ironforge, and the archaeological dig site deeper in Loch Modan. Adventurers frequently assist him with shuttling mining supplies and progress reports across the region. Stationed within the rustic town of Thelsamar, Jern Hornhelm plays a key logistical role for dwarven operations throughout Loch Modan. While dwarven scholars and field teams venture out into the wilderness to unearth their ancestral past, maintaining consistent supply chains remains essential. Jern ensures that vital resources, tools, and communications reach the active dig sites safely.

Jerod's Landing. Defias smugglers hold Jerod's Landing on the Elwynn Forest bank of the Nazferiti River. The dock gives them a hidden route for illicit shipments across the kingdom's waterways. Defias outlaws now control the river dock at Jerod's Landing, where Elwynn Forest meets the waters of the Nazferiti River. Once an ordinary boat dock, it now receives goods plundered from the Redridge Mountains under a Defias dockmaster's watch. The outlaws move the cargo discreetly downstream toward holdings such as Klaven's Tower in Westfall.

name.frFR: Magie de la forêt de Jin'Zil

text.enUS: Jin'Zil's Forest Magic. At the small outpost of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil has captured three night elven scouts in crude iron cages. Rather than executing them outright or holding them for ransom, the eccentric troll tasks Horde adventurers with gathering wilderness reagents from Stonetalon Peak to concoct a gruesome dose of 'forest magic.' In the red-rock defile of Malaka'jin, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil conducts his craft under the watchful gaze of the Horde. When three night elf captives fall into his clutches, Jin'Zil decides against ordinary butchery, concocting instead a mocking ritual tailored specifically for his captive woodland foes. He directs travelers north into the untamed peaks to collect an array of indigenous parts: thick tree sap, feline whiskers from predatory twilight runners, a shimmering fey dragon scale, and scores of eyes plucked from the local forest coursers.

Jitters. Jitters is a terrified, half-starved human hiding among the ruins of Raven Hill in Duskwood. He clings to scraps of food and struggles to speak about the horrors he has witnessed. Found shivering amid the dilapidated houses of Raven Hill, Jitters lives in constant terror of the predators stalking Duskwood's western trails. He relies on passing adventurers for simple sustenance, desperate for food while keeping a frantic eye on the encroaching shadows. His skittish mannerisms and uncanny reflex for leaping clear of sudden danger earned him his moniker long ago, but his frantic paranoia is born from firsthand encounters with horrific horrors.

name.itIT: Diario completo di Jitters il Teso

text.enUS: Jitters' Completed Journal. Jitters' Completed Journal is a handwritten account detailing the grim tragedies of Duskwood, specifically the massacre at Sven Yorgen's farm. Fearing vengeance, the reclusive Jitters surrenders the finished text to clear his name and shed light on the sinister forces haunting the region.

Jitters' Growling Gut. Stranded and terrified in the ruins of Raven Hill, the paranoid vagrant Jitters is desperate for real sustenance after subsisting on weeds and insects. He begs passing adventurers to travel east to Darkshire and convince Chef Grual to prepare a hot batch of his famous Dusky Crab Cakes. Raven Hill has become a den of ravenous undead and lurking beasts, leaving the eccentric hermit Jitters trapped in hiding for weeks. Prowling through dilapidated shanties under perpetual gloom, he has survived solely on dirt-dwelling grubs and wild weeds. Starved of civilized comfort, his nerves and stomach are pushed to their absolute limits.
