Dispatched directly under Warchief Thrall's orders to investigate the Syndicate and recover relics from the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he now coordinates reconnaissance and rescue efforts after his initial infiltration was ambushed. When Warchief Thrall turned his attention back to the ruins of Durnholde Keep, he dispatched Krusk and a small strike team to scout Syndicate activity and retrieve relics tied to the fortress's grim past. However, the human outlaws proved more entrenched and coordinated than anticipated. An ambush inside Durnholde's crumbling walls overwhelmed the orcish scout squad. Krusk managed to fight his way out, but his comrades were taken captive: Drull and Tog'thar were locked away within the ruins, while the expedition's leader, Gol'dir, was moved to another Syndicate hold. Regrouping at Tarren Mill, Krusk now directs Horde adventurers to breach Durnholde, recover the lost items, and liberate his trapped comrades.

Kul Tiras. Kul Tiras is an insular maritime human kingdom situated on an island archipelago in the Great Sea, west of Dun Morogh and Baradin Bay. Renowned for possessing the mightiest navy in Azeroth, it served as a cornerstone of the Alliance of Lordaeron during the Second War under Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. Following the fracturing of the old Alliance and tragic losses in Kalimdor, the island realm has largely receded into isolated waters. Kul Tiras blossomed into an unmatched seafaring power, sustained by an industrious merchant marine, rich fishing grounds, and a naval armada without peer in human history.

Kuray'bin. Kuray'bin is a Darkspear jungle troll scout stationed at a guard post outside Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. He watches the surrounding forest trails for night elf scouts sneaking close to the Horde encampment. Positioned just outside Splintertree Post, Kuray'bin keeps watch against Alliance infiltration in the deep woods of Ashenvale. The Silverwing Sentinels constantly patrol the surrounding canopy, sending agile outrunners across the border to gather intelligence on Horde lumber operations and defenses. Knowing that unmonitored scouts quickly become ambushing forces, Kuray'bin directs capable Horde fighters to hunt down the outrunners before they can report back to Silverwing Outpost.

Kurzen's Compound. Kurzen's Compound is a heavily fortified human settlement tucked into the hills of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Established by an expedition dispatched from Stormwind under Colonel Kurzen, the outpost has devolved into a rogue camp of cutthroats and wild beasts following their commander's descent into madness. What began as an official expedition into the untamed jungles of Stranglethorn turned into a nightmare when Colonel Kurzen lost his mind. Rather than fulfilling Stormwind's mission, the garrison broke away from the kingdom's authority, cutting ties with the crown and descending into tyranny. Today, the compound operates like a mercenary stronghold, complete with a functional lumber mill, stables for training captured Stranglethorn panthers and tigers as weapons of war, and an extensive cave complex known as the Stockpile where the rogue soldiers stash their plundered supplies.

Kurzen's Mystery. Brother Nimetz at the Rebel Camp wants to know what turned Colonel Kurzen to depravity. Suspecting that troll magic holds him, Nimetz sends you to the troll ruins of Stranglethorn to copy the legends written on four tablets. Colonel Kurzen was once a great and noble man, and Brother Nimetz means to learn what caused his fall into depravity. Nimetz suspects troll magic has a hold on the colonel. To test that, the old troll legends must be read, and they are carved on four tablets hidden among the troll ruins of Stranglethorn. You are asked to copy the markings from each tablet and carry the copies back.

Kuz's Skull. Kuz's Skull is the severed head of Kuz, a prominent Razormane quilboar raider in the southern Barrens. Brought forward from Razorfen Kraul, Kuz helped orchestrate violent raids against Horde outposts before being targeted for death by a captive former kin. The plains of the southern Barrens crawl with the Razormane tribe, but their organized aggression stems from specific leaders sent directly out of Razorfen Kraul. Kuz, alongside Nak and their ruthless chieftain Lok Orcbane, coordinated brutal incursions against travelers and settlements like the Crossroads. However, their internal treachery proved their undoing. Having betrayed their fellow quilboar Mangletooth and left him to rot in a cage at Camp Taurajo, they made a vengeful enemy. Mangletooth bartered Kuz's location to Horde champions willing to sever the raider's head and end his raids for good.

Kyle's Gone Missing!. Kyle's Gone Missing! is a local quest in Bloodhoof Village where Ahab Wheathoof asks passing adventurers to find his wayward dog, Kyle the Frenzied. Feeding the hungry pup a cut of tender strider meat soothes his temper and ensures his safe return home. In Bloodhoof Village, elder Ahab Wheathoof worries over his wayward pet, Kyle the Frenzied. While the title might sound alarming to outsiders, Kyle is Ahab's prized puppy who has slipped away onto the grassy plains of Mulgore. Ahab asks travelers passing through the settlement to track down his unruly companion and offer him a hearty meal to calm his wild spirits.

Kzan Thornslash. Kzan Thornslash is an orc weapon merchant stationed in the Valley of Trials in Durotar. He provides essential starter weaponry and supplies to fresh recruits beginning their training under the Horde. Situated within the dusty red canyon of the Valley of Trials, Kzan Thornslash serves as the primary weapon vendor for young orcs and Darkspear trolls taking their first steps as warriors of the Horde. Offering an assortment of basic armaments—ranging from crude hand axes and shortswords to clubs and staves—Kzan ensures that newly awakened aspirants are armed adequately to face the local wildlife and regional hazards.

Laced Pumpkin. A Laced Pumpkin is an ordinary gourd treated with a lethal concoction developed by Apothecary Johaan in Brill. Handed to a starving, imprisoned Scarlet Crusader under the guise of sustenance, it serves as a live field test for the Forsaken's growing arsenal of alchemical weapons. To the untrained eye, the laced pumpkin appears to be ordinary produce salvaged from the blighted soil of Tirisfal Glades. Under the supervision of Apothecary Johaan in Brill, however, the vegetable is treated with experimental toxins designed to realize the full potential of undeath. The Royal Apothecary Society constantly seeks new weapons to repel both the Scourge in the north and living human forces advancing from the south, turning even simple harvest goods into vectors for infection and chemical death.

Lack of Surplus. Dar is gathering supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east, where Tok'Kar has little time to spare between guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers. Dar asks you to bring Tok'Kar a shipment of sawtooth meat. Dar is collecting supplies for the outpost by the beach in the east. Tok'Kar does what is possible there, but guard shifts and cooking for the soldiers leave little time in the day. The soldiers enjoy cooking sawtooth meat when they can get it, and Dar has had no time to send them another shipment.

Lack of Surplus. Tok'Kar and the soldiers on the coast are stationed to guard Stonard against murlocs, or to send warning when the force is too large. Tok'Kar wants six sawtooth snapper claws and offers one of the outpost's weapons in thanks. With murlocs a threat along the coast, Tok'Kar and the soldiers are posted here to protect Stonard, or to warn it if the force is too large. That leaves little time for rest, and Tok'Kar could use more help. The claws of sawtooth snappers make fine weapons when properly prepared. Tok'Kar asks for six, and offers one of the outpost's weapons in return, grateful for the meat and the company.

Lady Anacondra. Lady Anacondra is one of the Fanglords leading the Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once one of the night elf druids who followed Naralex in his ambitious effort to heal the Barrens, she was lost when her master's Emerald Dream communion turned into a nightmare. Her mind broke, twisting her devotion into a drive to remake the land to match that twisted dream. Before adopting her serpentine title, Lady Anacondra was one of Naralex's druids. When the elder druid Naralex conceived of tapping into the subterranean springs of the Barrens through the Emerald Dream, she followed him into the caverns. Her loyalty, however, proved her undoing. As Naralex's mind was seized by dark visions, the nightmare seeped out from the dreaming realm and contaminated his disciples, shattering her sanity and reshaping her reverie into a cold, reptilian obsession.

Lady Sarevess. Lady Sarevess is a twisted naga sorceress dwelling within the flooded ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, where she dabbles in dark sorceries. Within the Pool of Ask'ar, Lady Sarevess conducts her rituals in a flooded grotto of the ruined temple. A very twisted spellcaster, she dabbles in dark magic while the Twilight's Hammer cultists who also haunt the sunken temple pursue their own worship deeper in the cavern.

Laird. Laird is a night elf fish vendor found inside the seaside inn of Auberdine. Working along Darkshore's mist-shrouded coast, he provides trade goods and culinary recipes to travelers and fishermen braving the rugged shoreline. Situated inside the bustling inn of Auberdine, Laird sells fresh fish and supplies to sailors, locals, and journeying adventurers. Darkshore's waters are notoriously turbulent and rife with danger compared to the sheltered shores of Teldrassil, but Laird knows well that risk brings reward. For daring anglers willing to cast their lines along the misty beaches, the local catch yields a handsome profit.

Laird's Response. Laird's Response is a sealed dispatch penned by the fish curer Laird in the coastal port of Auberdine. Written for Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village, the letter details curious ecological differences between mainland marine life and the unusually large fish thriving along Teldrassil's shores. After reviewing catch reports from across the Veiled Sea, Laird of Auberdine noted a striking discrepancy: the fish hauled from Teldrassil's coast are remarkably larger and more plentiful than those taken along the mainland beaches of Darkshore. In this written response addressed to Nessa Shadowsong, Laird shares his working theory—that the unnatural presence and raw vitality of the newly planted World Tree may be warping and stimulating the surrounding marine life. Delivered by travelers returning across the waters, the letter prompts wonder and quiet curiosity among the fisherfolk of Rut'theran Village.

Lake Al'Ameth. Lake Al'Ameth is one of the largest freshwater bodies nestled high in the boughs of Teldrassil, located just south of Dolanaar. Though once a tranquil haven featuring little more than a simple wooden jetty, its shores have grown perilous due to the violent agitation of the local plant life. Resting immediately south of the village of Dolanaar, Lake Al'Ameth serves as a vital natural basin in the heart of Teldrassil. Despite its serene waters and minimal settlement, peace here has evaporated. Swarms of agitated timberlings and timberling sprouts prowl the water's edge, driven mad by an unnatural sickness spreading through the world tree. Druids and researchers from Dolanaar frequently dispatch travelers to these shores to gather seeds and cull the aggressive creatures before the corruption spreads deeper into the surrounding forest.

Lake Creeper Moss. Lake Creeper Moss is an organic compound harvested from the aquatic creepers dwelling among the Dawning Isles in Lake Lordamere. It serves as a vital reagent sought by the Royal Apothecary Society for their efforts to engineer a lethal new plague. Grown along the hides of the vicious freshwater beasts that prowl the southern Dawning Isles of Lake Lordamere, Lake Creeper Moss carries unique properties shaped by Lordaeron's blighted waters. Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, documented it in his journal, noting that the moss resembled trace materials on the fossils of creatures killed by an ancient plague in the lake. When recovered by Forsaken agents, samples are dispatched directly to the Apothecarium in the Undercity to fuel Master Apothecary Faranell's dark research.

Lake Elune'ara. Lake Elune'ara is the shimmering, sacred body of water that occupies the heart of Moonglade. Revering the Moon Goddess Elune, the lake serves as a place of spiritual reflection for the Cenarion Circle, though deep within its murky floor lies the dormant, corrupted demigod Omen. Framed by the moonlit groves of Moonglade, Lake Elune'ara provides serene waters said to be blessed by the White Lady herself. The lake lies at the spiritual center of the druidic haven, bordered by Nighthaven to the north and the shrine grounds of the Cenarion Circle. Initiates have long plumbed its tranquil depths to retrieve long-lost relics, attuning themselves to the currents of nature as they seek harmony with the land.

Lake Everstill. Lake Everstill is the expansive azure body of water dominating the heart of the Redridge Mountains, flanking the town of Lakeshire. Once celebrated for tranquil fishing and clean mountain runoff, its shores and waters have lately turned treacherous due to aggressive murloc tribes and predatory lake beasts. Spanning the central basin of Redridge, Lake Everstill provides the scenic backdrop and vital waterway for the township of Lakeshire. Its crystal-clear waters drain eastward toward the looming heights of Stonewatch. Spanned by the town's central bridge, the lake has long sustained local trade and quiet anglers, though anyone walking the shoreline today will find its peaceful reputation thoroughly shattered by encroaching wilderness threats.

Lake Falathim. Lake Falathim is a tranquil body of water nestled in the forested hills of western Ashenvale, southwest of Maestra's Post. Revered for the constant touch of Elune's moonlight upon its surface day and night, it was once a beloved retreat for night elves. In recent days, however, aggressive murlocs have overrun its shores, turning a sacred haven into a perilous hazard. Tucked away southeast of the Zoram Strand, Lake Falathim was long cherished by the Kaldorei as a peaceful sanctuary for swimming and fishing. According to local lore, the gentle radiance of Elune rests upon these waters at all hours, day or night. Despite this sacred blessing, ferocious murlocs have surged inland to seize the shores, nesting in thick numbers and driving away local travelers and scholars alike.

Lake Kel'Theril. Lake Kel'Theril is a vast, frozen lake nestled in the heart of Winterspring. Along its ice-locked shores stand ancient kaldorei ruins haunted by restless spirits who have lingered since the Great Sundering. Lake Kel'Theril is shrouded in eternal cold, its waters sealed under thick sheets of ice. Scattered across its surface and snowy banks are the shattered pillars and arches of ancient elven architecture. These are the remnants of Kel'Theril, once an outpost of the ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering shattered Kalimdor. Rather than finding rest in death, the spirits of the fallen aristocracy wander the ice as tormented ghosts and specters, forever tethered to the tragic remnants of their former glory.

Lake Mennar. Lake Mennar is a tranquil body of freshwater nestled amidst the shattered ruins of Azshara. It is remarkably renowned as one of the exceedingly rare havens outside of Northrend where members of the blue dragonflight reside. While the perimeter teems with protective blue dragonspawn, the shores of the lake itself remain strangely serene. Situated in the ancient, broken landscape of Azshara, Lake Mennar serves as a secluded gathering ground for the blue dragonflight. Aside from Mazthoril to the north in Winterspring, it is virtually unheard of to encounter blue dragons in such numbers across Kalimdor. Blue dragonspawn tirelessly patrol the ridges and approaches circling the basin, fiercely guarding the waters. Yet for any wanderer daring enough to slip through this vigilant ring of sentries, the calm waters of the lake offer unexpected quietude, shielded from the arcane turmoil and roaming beast packs common to the rest of the peninsula.

Lake Mereldar. Lake Mereldar is a sprawling, contaminated body of water resting south of Corin's Crossing in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once part of the idyllic rural heartland of Lordaeron, its corrupted waters now spawn twisted elementals and rot beneath the lingering taint of the Scourge. Situated just south of the crossroads town of Corin's Crossing, Lake Mereldar was once a peaceful fixture of northern Lordaeron's countryside. Dotting its shores are the decaying ruins of an old homestead, an abandoned shack, and a dilapidated ferry that once carried local farmers and travelers across the gentle waters. With the coming of the Scourge and the plague of undeath, the lake fell into complete ruin. The surrounding soil withered, and the waters turned foul and poisonous.

Lake Nazferiti. Lake Nazferiti is a sprawling freshwater lake nestled in the dense jungle of northern Stranglethorn Vale. Fed by a vast river system stretching far north into the mountains, its waters are infested with ferocious crocolisks and snapping frenzies, while its shores host an industrial encampment operated by the goblin Venture Company. Lake Nazferiti sits along the Nazferiti River, one of the longest continuous waterways across the southern Eastern Kingdoms. The river traces its origins deep into the northern heights, tumbling down waterfalls from the Redridge Mountains and possibly originating as far inland as Deadwind Pass. Within Stranglethorn, the water widens into this murky lake, teeming with vicious predators like snapping river frenzies and ambush-hunting crocolisks that make casual swimming deadly.

Lake Skulker Moss. Lake Skulker Moss is a biological reagent gathered from the bog beasts inhabiting the northern reaches of Lake Lordamere. It was identified by Apothecary Berard, before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, as a key organic component for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into brewing a New Plague. Harvested from the mossy bodies of Lake Skulkers and Elder Lake Skulkers on the Dawning Isles, this damp aquatic moss possesses properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Before Arugal's curse claimed his mind, Apothecary Berard meticulously cataloged the flora and fauna of eastern Silverpine Forest, concluding in his journal that both Lake Skulker and Lake Creeper mosses could serve as stabilizing or reactive agents. After Berard became a mindless servant of Arugal, his journal was recovered from Pyrewood Village for Apothecary Renferrel, who instructed Forsaken champions to gather moss samples alongside a rare tumor from local Vile Fin murlocs, delivering them directly to Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity.

name.frFR: Grand-route de la Crête du lac

text.enUS: Lakeridge Highway. Lakeridge Highway is an old thoroughfare running along the southern shore of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Once a vital and heavily traveled artery prior to the First War, it has fallen into ruin and disuse. Today, roving packs of gnolls and Blackrock orcs make passage along the road perilous for travelers. Before the devastation of the First War, the Lakeridge Highway served as a bustling trade corridor through Redridge, carrying goods and folk along the southern banks of Lake Everstill. In those peaceful days, travelers could journey between the valley settlements and the eastern heights under the protection of the Kingdom of Stormwind. That safety shattered when the Horde marched through the region, leaving eastern Redridge contested and desolate.

Lakeshire. Lakeshire is the primary human settlement in the Redridge Mountains, nestled along the northern shores of Lake Everstill. Led by Magistrate Solomon and guarded by Marshal Marris, the picturesque town is currently on the brink of collapse due to relentless assaults by Blackrock orcs, aggressive gnoll packs, and shoreline murlocs. Once a peaceful haven in the foothills east of Stormwind, Lakeshire has become the kingdom's most embattled frontier. The town's garrison at Stonewatch Keep was brutally overrun by Blackrock clan orcs sweeping down from the north, and dark wizardry has riled local Shadowhide gnoll packs into organized raiding parties. Blackrock saboteurs have even shattered parts of the Everstill Bridge, leaving Foreman Oslow and his crew struggling to repair the span while under constant threat of attack. With murlocs choking the lake's shores and gnolls stalking the high passes, Lakeshire's defenders are stretched to their breaking point.

Lakeshire Inn. The Lakeshire Inn is the social hub and primary refuge in the beleaguered town of Lakeshire. Situated in the heart of the Redridge Mountains, it provides warmth, ale, and safe lodging for local townsfolk and weary travelers contending with the surrounding perils. Perched on the shore of Lake Everstill, the Lakeshire Inn offers a brief respite from the gnoll bands and Blackrock orcs pressing in on the town. Despite Lakeshire's increasingly desperate military situation, the tavern maintains a cozy, bustling atmosphere. Barkeep Daniels and Innkeeper Brianna attend to the locals and travelers, serving up flagons of ale, wine, and warm meals. It is a vital meeting point where townspeople trade news, drown their sorrows, and seek hired blades to help defend the eastern border of the kingdom.

Lakeshire Town Hall. Lakeshire Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the Redridge Mountains, standing at the heart of the lakeside settlement. Inside, Magistrate Solomon oversees local governance while wrestling with relentless threats from Blackrock orcs and gnolls. Lakeshire Town Hall is an aging stone structure that has been diligently refurbished multiple times over the years. Positioned prominently within Lakeshire, it houses Magistrate Solomon, a kind and dedicated civil leader tasked with maintaining order in the eastern reaches of the Kingdom of Stormwind. With Stormwind's military resources stretched thin and royal aid scarce, the hall has transformed from a quiet administrative office into an active command center where desperate appeals for volunteer defenders and mercenaries are processed daily.

Lakkari Tar Pits. The Lakkari Tar Pits are a series of foul-smelling, bubbling pools of thick black sludge in northern Un'Goro Crater. Situated just below the cliffs of Marshal's Refuge, they act as a natural death trap for unwary beasts and an incubator for hostile tar elementals. The Lakkari Tar Pits dominate the low ground of northern Un'Goro Crater, directly south of Marshal's Refuge. Thick, reeking pools of pitch entrap anything careless enough to step into them, quickly bogging down beasts and adventurers alike. The protruding bones of hundreds of prehistoric creatures break the black surface, bearing witness to generations of animals sucked into the mire. Opportunistic scavengers circle the margins waiting for trapped prey to exhaust itself, while living tar beasts, lurkers, and creepers rise directly from the muck to batter interlopers.

Lakota Windsong. Lakota Windsong is a young tauren held captive atop the bluffs of Darkcloud Pinnacle in Thousand Needles. After rejecting an unwanted proposal from Arnak Grimtotem, she was abducted by force and awaits rescue from the Grimtotem tribe's clutches. Not long after the Third War, Lakota Windsong was pursued by Arnak Grimtotem. Unwilling to join his clan or accept his courtship, she turned down his proposal. Arnak refused to take no for an answer; he returned under cover of night, slaughtered Lakota's brother when he tried to intervene, and carried her off into the jagged heights of Thousand Needles. Confined high above the canyon floor at Darkcloud Pinnacle, she remains trapped under heavy guard while Arnak still insists on making her his bride.

Lakota'mani. Lakota'mani is a rite of the hunt initiated by claiming the hoof of Lakota'mani, a massive roaming kodo of the Barrens. Bringing this trophy to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo honors the spirit of the mighty beast and marks the hunter as an equal to its thunderous strength. In the Taur-ahe tongue, Lakota'mani translates to 'Earthshaker.' Among the herds that wander the sun-baked plains of the Barrens, he stands apart—a kodo of tremendous size and endurance whose footsteps echo like gathered thunder. To tauren hunters, tracking and defeating such a creature is not an act of wanton slaughter, but a sacred communion with the raw vigor of Kalimdor's wildlife.

Land Ho!. At Faldir's Cove, the lookout Lolo greets you with news that Captain O'Breen's stop here will last far longer than planned. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, are lost, and Lolo suggests you speak with the captain. Lolo, ever on the lookout, spots you arriving at Faldir's Cove. Captain O'Breen had promised the crew only a few hours here, time enough to collect the treasure and head back to Booty Bay. Lolo doubts it will be so quick. Two ships of the formation, the Spirit of Silverpine and the Maiden's Folly, now rest on the bottom of the sea. Anyone who means to stay is told to talk to the captain.

Land's End Beach. Land's End Beach is a desolate stretch of coastline at the far southern tip of Tanaris, effectively marking the southern edge of Kalimdor. Shielded by towering mountain ridges and vast ocean waters, it remains one of the most secluded and inaccessible shores on the continent. Tucked away behind the southern mountain ranges of Tanaris and the sealed titan gateway to Uldum, Land's End Beach represents the absolute southern edge of Kalimdor's mainland. Cut off from overland routes across the desert dunes, reaching this windswept coast requires swimming along the dangerous, fatigue-inducing open waters of the South Seas. The beach is a barren frontier of crashing surf, shifting sand, and quiet isolation, largely untamed by the cartels or desert explorers who dwell farther north around Gadgetzan.

Lanka Farshot. Lanka Farshot is a tauren hunter trainer stationed at Camp Narache within the Red Cloud Mesa. He guides novice tauren hunters as they take their first steps in tracking, marksmanship, and surviving the plains of Mulgore. Standing watch over Camp Narache, Lanka Farshot greets new tauren called to the path of the hunter. Fresh recruits arrive carrying an etched note directing them to seek his counsel. Under his steady eye, apprentices learn the fundamentals of ranged combat, tracking prey, and respecting the wild beasts that roam the grassy plains of Mulgore. His teachings ensure that every young hunter serves as a capable scout and provider for the tribe.

Lar Prowltusk. Lar Prowltusk is a Darkspear troll sentinel stationed southwest of Sen'jin Village in Durotar. From his post on the frontier, he keeps watch over encroaching threats to the young troll settlement, directing adventurers to blunt the advances of nearby enemies. Situated southwest of Sen'jin Village along the rugged Durotar coastline, Lar Prowltusk stands as one of the Darkspear tribe's forward sentinels. With the trolls still working to secure a permanent home after fleeing their sunken island chain, Sen'jin Village faces constant harassment from hostile neighbors. Lar coordinates scouts and warriors to monitor coastal movements and curb the aggression of hostile forces—particularly the Kolkar centaur—ensuring the fragile settlement has room to breathe.

Lard Lost His Lunch. Lard, of the village of Revantusk in the Hinterlands, is hungry and frightened. A Vilebranch struck Lard during a private picnic, and Lard fled without lunch. You are asked to fetch it from an island to the north. Lard was picnicking at a secret spot when a Vilebranch, ugly and mean in Lard's telling, hit Lard with a big stick. Lard bolted for Revantusk and left the lunch behind. Now Lard is hungry, and afraid to go back.

Large Candle. In Elwynn's mines, kobolds carry Large Candles on their heads for light and wax. Their flames guide them through dark tunnels, and apothecaries value the wax. Kobolds use candle flame to find their way through the dark shafts beneath Elwynn Forest. They fasten the tapers to their heads, and Kobold Miners, Tunnelers, and Geomancers defend them fiercely from intruders. Though crudely made, the Large Candles carried in Fargodeep Mine and Jasperlode Mine hold valuable wax. Surface tradesmen cannot easily produce it in bulk, so the candles are both tools for the kobolds and a commodity for alchemists.

text.enUS: Large Soran'ruk Fragment. The Large Soran'ruk Fragment is a sizable remnant of an ancient artifact bound with demonic energy. Originally housing the spirit of a disgraced Burning Legion demon, this shard found its way into the hands of sinister spellcasters within the haunted walls of Shadowfang Keep. When demons of the Burning Legion fall out of favor with their dark masters, their spirits are sometimes condemned to imprisonment within enchanted orbs. These vessels are subsequently distributed among mages and warlocks aligned with the Legion, who draw upon the potent fel forces trapped within. Even when shattered into fragments, the lingering essence of the bound fiend still radiates power, making each piece a prize for ambitious practitioners of shadow magic.

Laris Geardawdle. Laris Geardawdle is an eccentric gnomish researcher stationed in the Library of the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. He dedicates his academic life to studying the bizarre nature and origins of oozes across Azeroth. Adventurers willing to collect noxious slime samples find him an eager, if slightly unhinged, patron. Tucked away among the towering bookshelves and ancient relics of the Hall of Explorers, Laris Geardawdle pursues a rather unglamorous niche of natural philosophy: the genesis of oozes. While his dwarven colleagues pore over Titan tablets and ancient stone carvings, Laris is convinced that Azeroth's vile, gelatinous horrors hold fascinating alchemical and biological secrets. He tasks roving explorers with gathering caustic samples from remote corners of the world, eager to test his strange hypotheses on how these mindless puddles of malice come to life.

Lariss Pavilion. Lariss Pavilion is an ancient elven structure tucked into the wilderness of Feralas just north of Camp Mojache. While once a peaceful retreat of classical night elf architecture, the surrounding forest has grown dangerous due to corrupted dryads, and an exiled Highborne mage now bides his time within its shade. Standing quietly on the bluffs north of Camp Mojache, Lariss Pavilion showcases the graceful stonework and towering archways of the ancient kaldorei empire. In its prime, it served the great city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Today, it offers a sheltered overlook above the dense canopy of Feralas, but the peace here is frail: the once-gentle dryads wandering the surrounding glades have fallen to madness and corruption, turning fiercely hostile to anyone who draws near.

Lars. Lars is a beleaguered human survivor camping out in the wilderness of Duskwood. Along with his companion Sven Yorgen, he struggles to hold his ground on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank against the terrors that stalk the forest. Perched in a modest camp on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank, Lars ekes out a precarious survival far from the questionable safety of Darkshire. Duskwood is treacherous at the best of times, but the surrounding woods crawl with ferocious beasts, relentless undead, and creeping worgen. Lars stays close by Sven Yorgen, striving simply to stay alive in an increasingly hostile wilderness.

Laughing Sister's Hair. Laughing Sister's Hair consists of soft, magical locks harvested from dryads residing in the enchanted forests of Ashenvale. Highly sought after by skilled weavers, these strands possess innate mystical properties ideal for crafting fine robes. Harvested from the dryads known as laughing sisters near Raynewood Retreat in Ashenvale, this hair holds remarkable natural magic. While dryads are sacred woodland protectors linked to Cenarius and the night elves, craftsmen within the Horde value their hair purely as a potent crafting reagent. The troll tailor Kil'hala at the Crossroads spins these gathered locks into enchanted vestments for burgeoning practitioners of the arcane.

Laughing Sisters. Laughing Sisters is a Horde quest that sends mages into the heart of Ashenvale to gather enchanted locks of hair from wild dryads. The material is destined for Kil'hala, an experienced troll tailor at the Crossroads, to spin into an empowered mage robe. Hunting the daughters of Cenarius underscores the relentless friction between Horde spellcasters and the native defenders of the ancient woodland. Following their efforts to secure water from Xavian, rising mages are directed by Deino in Orgrimmar to assist in crafting their own enchanted vestments. Arcane tailoring of this nature demands materials imbued with raw magical essence. Dryad locks, naturally suffused with the primeval vitality of the forest, hold the necessary qualities to thread intricate magical garments capable of shielding and augmenting a caster's powers.

Launch Bay. The Launch Bay is a subterranean airfield and hangar tucked within the depths of Gnomeregan, located just beyond the Hall of Gears. Once the staging ground for gnomish flying machines and bombers, it has fallen completely under the control of hostile leper gnomes and corrupted mechanical contraptions. Serving as the primary hangar for Gnomeregan's aerial fleet, the Launch Bay is split across two tiers. Its central platform, reached by ramps from the upper walkway, still houses parked gnomish flying machines and heavy bombers that never made it out before the city was evacuated. Instead of skilled pilots, the flight decks are now crawling with crazed leper gnomes who maintain and guard the idling war machines.

Laurna Morninglight. Laurna Morninglight is a night elf priest trainer residing in the tranquil settlement of Dolanaar within Teldrassil. Devoted to the Sisterhood of Elune, she guides budding acolytes emerging from Shadowglen in the spiritual rites and healing graces of the Moon Goddess. Her teachings prepare young night elf priests for the growing threats encroaching on the boughs of the World Tree. Situated amidst the boughs of Dolanaar, Laurna Morninglight serves as one of the primary mentors for young priests who have completed their initial rites in Shadowglen. As new initiates step out into the broader reaches of Teldrassil, she instructs them on expanding their communion with Elune, balancing the light of healing with defensive rites necessary to survive an increasingly hostile wild.

Lazy Peons. Foreman Thazz'ril is fed up with the Valley of Trials' workforce falling asleep on the job. Entrusted with his weighted blackjack, young recruits are tasked with roaming the valley to discipline sleeping peons and ensure vital lumber continues flowing to Durotar's settlements. Building a new home in the arid plains of Durotar demands vast amounts of timber, stone, and sheer physical toil. Much of that burden falls squarely upon the peon caste—orcs who lack martial prowess but form the industrious backbone of the Horde. Unfortunately for Foreman Thazz'ril, the baking heat and grueling labor of the Valley of Trials make it easy for these laborers to slip off to shady trees for unauthorized naps.

Leaders of the Fang. Leaders of the Fang is a pivotal Horde quest tasked by Nara Wildmane from the heights of Thunder Bluff. It directs adventurers into the Wailing Caverns to strike down the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang and retrieve their twisted dream gems. Halting these rogue druids is essential to preventing their serpentine nightmare from permanently overtaking the Barrens. The night elf druid Naralex ventured into the subterranean springs of the Wailing Caverns with a selfless ambition: to use the Emerald Dream to restore lush vitality to the arid Barrens. Tragically, when his slumber took root, his dream turned into a waking nightmare. The acolytes who accompanied him lost their devotion to nature's harmony, succumbing to the nightmare's corruption and adopting the mantle of the Druids of the Fang.

text.enUS: Ledger from Tanaris. After Caught!, the occupant of the wooden outhouse in Searing Gorge offers you a small job taken on in Tanaris. Krinkle Goodsteel in Gadgetzan wants certain things found in the gorge and a few other places, and you are to collect them and bring them to him. Having been helped, the occupant recalls a little job taken on while in Tanaris. Krinkle Goodsteel of Gadgetzan wants a list of things gathered, some from this gorge and some from elsewhere. Goodsteel's ledger will be slid under the door for you, and you are to carry it, along with everything on it, to Goodsteel in Tanaris.

text.enUS: Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle. Legacy Reward: Replica Ironforge Air Rifle marks the collection of a mysterious package held on your behalf. Left behind by an unidentified messenger, the parcel was narrowly saved from being dumped into the sea before reaching your hands. A mysterious parcel addressed specifically to you was dropped off with an unwilling caretaker. The unknown courier insisted you would arrive to collect it, leaving so swiftly that the receiver could not even refuse delivery. Fortunately, you arrived just before the unclaimed box was tossed into the ocean alongside the evening's refuse.

Legacy of the Aspects. Legacy of the Aspects is an ancient tome hidden deep within the Dor'Danil Barrow Den in southern Ashenvale. Retrieved during a Horde trial of the intellect, the volume contains essential lore concerning the Great Aspects that shaped ancient Azeroth. While earlier trials set forth by tauren elders test physical endurance and resolve, the pursuit of Legacy of the Aspects is designed to challenge the mind. Tasked by Braug Dimspirit at the entrance to the Talondeep Path in the Stonetalon Mountains, an aspirant must delve into the haunted barrow dens of Dor'Danil. Guarded by the restless spirits of fallen druids and the vicious creatures that slew them, the ancient text rests upon a stone pedestal. Claiming the volume is only the first step; the seeker must commit its contents to memory before relinquishing the book, as they are tested on its historical lessons.

Legging It. Legging It is a quest focused on clearing a dangerous southern path to protect working peons. Threats along the roadway had frightened the labor force into halting their travels, stalling essential duties. By driving back the dangers, adventurers restore safe passage and enable the workforce to return to their assignments. Legging It addresses a disruption in local labor operations where peons became too frightened to journey southward. Rather than performing their assigned tasks, the workers refused to risk travel along the road due to looming perils. By intervening to push back threats along the path, travelers restore enough security for overseers to send their crews back to work.

Lelanai. Lelanai is a night elf mount handler residing in the Cenarion Enclave of Darnassus. She provides the fierce saber mounts of the night elves to worthy riders, offering both standard nightsabers and swift war beasts to her kin and trusted allies of Darnassus. Stationed beside riding instructor Jartsam among the towering trees of the Cenarion Enclave, Lelanai attends to some of the finest big cats bred in Kalimdor. Night elves have long formed profound bonds with the fierce predators of northern forests, training nightsabers and frostsabers to carry sentinels and scouts across rugged terrain with predator grace. Lelanai serves as the primary provider of these revered mounts in the capital.

Leonid's Letter. Leonid's Letter is a delivery quest directing travelers into the depths of Undercity. Wary of entering the Forsaken capital himself due to a strained past with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid hires an impartial courier to deliver a message to Glix Xizzix, an old goblin acquaintance stationed in the Trade Quarter. Leonid needs a courier to transport a sealed letter to an acquaintance in Undercity. Because of past friction and a fraught relationship with Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, Leonid chooses not to walk the halls of the Forsaken capital himself, entrusting a traveling neutral party to pass past the city's guards without raising alarm.

Leper gnome. Leper gnomes are the tragic, mutated survivors of Gnomeregan's catastrophic irradiation during the Third War. Maddened by toxic fallout and lingering fumes, most have sworn fealty to the usurper Mekgineer Thermaplugg, fiercely defending their ruined city against all outsiders. When trogg invaders breached Gnomeregan during the Third War, Mekgineer Thermaplugg advised High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque to flood the city with radioactive toxins. Thermaplugg claimed the poison would exterminate the troggs while sparing the gnomish population. Instead, the catastrophe wiped out eighty percent of the city's inhabitants. Those who survived within the sealed lower levels were warped in mind and flesh by toxic fallout, mutating into pale, pustulant wretches dubbed leper gnomes.

Lessons Anew. "Lessons Anew" is an initiation quest given to developing Alliance druids by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus. It directs initiates to travel to the sacred haven of Moonglade to meet with Dendrite Starblaze and begin their training in the art of purging venom and toxins. Druids hold a sacred connection to the living world, inherited through the teachings and blessings of the demigod Cenarius. Among these boons is the power to cleanse foul venoms through simple incantation. However, such potent gifts are never bestowed lightly upon initiates. To truly respect the miraculous ease of their magical arts, young druids must first understand the painstaking mundane toil required to fight toxins without nature's direct intervention.

Lessons Anew. Lessons Anew is a rite of passage for young tauren druids, initiated by Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff. It directs apprentices to travel to the sacred haven of Moonglade to begin mastering the art of cleansing natural and unnatural poisons. Guided by the night elf Dendrite Starblaze, this lesson sets aside mock trials in favor of confronting an urgent, real-world poisoning crisis. Druids hold a sacred mandate to protect the wilds, which includes the miraculous ability bestowed by Cenarius to purge virulent toxins with a simple incantation. However, such potent magic is not handed over without grounding. Turak Runetotem insists that before channeling divine energies to effortlessly dispel blights, a druid must understand the physical toll of venom and learn to treat it through grounded, mundane means.

Lethlor Ravine. Lethlor Ravine is a jagged, rocky canyon winding through the eastern reaches of the Badlands. It serves as a perilous roost and breeding ground for the black dragonflight, swarming with aggressive whelps and mature drakes. Carved deep into the scorched plateaus of the eastern Badlands, Lethlor Ravine is one of the most hazardous stretches of the desert. The craggy canyon walls provide a natural aerie for the black dragonflight, housing nests of fierce dragon whelps guarded by larger, fire-breathing drakes. Few travelers dare approach the valley floor, as the shadows overhead constantly betray the flight of winged predators circling among the rocky spires.

Letter to Delgren. The Letter to Delgren is an urgent missive penned by Balthule Shadowstrike near the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore. Addressed to his mentor, the paladin Delgren the Purifier, it details the sinister operations of the demonic Dark Strand cult. Delivering it carries vital intelligence southward to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. As cultists of the Dark Strand gather around the ruins of the Tower of Althalaxx, the night elf Balthule Shadowstrike keeps watch over their escalating malice. Lacking the martial might to eradicate the cult alone, Balthule drafts this dispatch to request aid from his tutor in the Holy Light, Delgren the Purifier. Because the cult's foul rites threaten more than just Darkshore's coastline, the message must be carried the entire length of the region into western Ashenvale, where Delgren works in concert with night elf Sentinels to hunt down demonic and undead threats.

Letter to Jin'Zil. The Letter to Jin'Zil is a piece of correspondence penned by the orc Darsok Swiftdagger at the Crossroads. Entrusted to an adventurer after the defeat of Serena Bloodfeather, it bears word to the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil in the Stonetalon Mountains that the northern Barrens have been purged of the Bloodfeather threat. Following the eradication of the harpy infestation at the Dry Hills and the slaying of Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok Swiftdagger drafts this missive to an old comrade. Recognizing that the harpies of the Barrens originally roosted within the peaks of Stonetalon Mountains, Darsok uses the dispatch to introduce a promising warrior to the wider frontier while notifying the witch doctor Jin'Zil that the harpy matron has fallen.

Letter to Jin'Zil. Letter to Jin'Zil is a Horde delivery quest entrusted to adventurers who have slain Serena Bloodfeather in the northern Barrens. Orc rogue Darsok Swiftdagger sends you across the border into the rugged crags of Stonetalon Mountains to deliver word of the harpy matriarch's demise to his old friend, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil. After the harpy threat around the northern Barrens is systematically dismantled, Darsok Swiftdagger reveals that the winged raiders were never native to the scrublands. The Witchwing and Bloodfeather broods descended from the rugged ridges of the Stonetalon Mountains to the northwest. Impressed by your prowess in dispatching Serena Bloodfeather, Darsok sends you into those dangerous peaks to carry news of her death to an old acquaintance, Witch Doctor Jin'Zil, residing at the troll settlement of Malaka'jin.

Letter to Jorgen. A sealed letter calls on Jorgen in Stormwind City to help with a missing diplomat. A diplomat bound for Theramore failed to arrive for talks with Lady Jaina Proudmoore, and royal investigators moved quickly to keep the matter quiet. While official agents searched the capital, other channels stirred. The letter bypasses military bureaucracy and seeks out Jorgen, a gruff veteran who fishes beneath the great statues in the Valley of Heroes. It invokes old obligations and draws him into a covert inquiry amid rumors of a Defias conspiracy.

Letter to Stormpike. Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore holds a cleverly encrypted letter, and he knows someone in Ironforge who might decrypt it. He sends you with the letter to Prospector Stormpike, in the Library of the Hall of Explorers. Prospector Stormpike is to be found in the Library, in the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge. Dibbs wants you to tell Stormpike that he sent you, and to show the letter. Dibbs reckons that if anyone north of Blackrock Spire can read it, Stormpike is the one.

Lewis' Note. At Sentinel Hill, Quartermaster Lewis sends an urgent supply requisition to a private armorer in Stormwind. A courier carries it by gryphon, asking for protective gear for the Westfall garrison. The People's Militia at Sentinel Hill gets little support from Stormwind's House of Nobles. Skirmishes with the Defias Brotherhood keep draining its meager stocks of gear. To keep the defenders outfitted, Quartermaster Lewis turns to private business instead of crown supplies. His requisition bypasses official military channels entirely. An Alliance courier must fly by gryphon to Old Town and present the order to Osric Strang, proprietor of Limited Immunity.

Library (Ironforge). Tucked inside the eastern wing of the Hall of Explorers, the Library serves as Ironforge's foremost repository of historical knowledge, archeological relics, and ancient lore. Maintained diligently by the Explorers' League, it houses extensive historical tomes alongside rare artifacts recovered from digs across Azeroth. Occupying a massive chamber within the Hall of Explorers, the Library is where dwarven scholars sift through the relics and field reports recovered by adventurers across the world. Administered by the Explorers' League, the shelves are packed with foundational chronicles detailing the War of the Three Hammers, the ancient Troll Wars, and the origins of the dwarven race. Inquiries regarding rare books or archival locations are directed to Librarian Mae Paledust.

Library Wing (Northshire). In Northshire Abbey, the Library Wing gathers scholars and new priests and mages. Its quiet southern rooms offer instruction for those joining Stormwind’s defense. The Library Wing branches south from Northshire Abbey’s Main Hall. Dusty shelves, study lecterns, and quiet alcoves fill its rooms, where aspiring mages and priests learn the Arcane and the Holy Light. Across the abbey, martial recruits drill in the Hall of Arms. Priestess Anetta guides novice priests in faith and healing, while Khelden Bremen teaches budding mages to shape primal elemental energy.

Library Wing (Tyr's Hand). The Library Wing is a secluded hall inside Tyr's Hand Abbey, nestled within the Scarlet Crusade's heavily fortified redoubt in the Eastern Plaguelands. Once dedicated to holy study and contemplation, its shelves are now consumed by the zealous order's rigid dogma and propaganda. Members of the Crusade congregate here to study scripture and guard the sanctum's religious relics. Situated off the central nave of Tyr's Hand Abbey opposite the martial quarters, the Library Wing reflects the ideological core of the Scarlet Crusade. Within these quiet stone alcoves, priests and crusaders immerse themselves in theological tracts, militant doctrines, and writings twisted by years of relentless warfare against the Scourge. Rather than preserving open scholarship, the texts sheltered here fuel the Crusade's paranoia, reinforcing their conviction that all outsiders carry the taint of corruption.

Lich King. The Lich King is the lord and psychic master of the undead Scourge, ruling from the Frozen Throne far to the north in Icecrown. Originally forged by the demon Kil'jaeden from the spirit of the orc shaman Ner'zhul, the entity eventually lured Prince Arthas Menethil into corruption, culminating in their fateful union atop Northrend's icy peaks. When the orc shaman Ner'zhul attempted to flee the dying world of Draenor, he fell directly into the clutches of Kil'jaeden the Deceiver. The demon lord tore Ner'zhul's body to shreds but bound his tormented soul into a block of diamond-hard ice cast out of the Twisting Nether. Flung into Azeroth, the glacial monolith struck the northern wastes of Northrend, forming the Frozen Throne. Kil'jaeden intended the Lich King to forge an unstoppable undead vanguard that would dismantle the mortal kingdoms without succumbing to the infighting that ruined the Orcish Horde. Instead, armed with immense telepathic power, Ner'zhul immediately began plotting his own bid for freedom.

Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is an officer of the Stormwind army currently stationed at the Southshore inn in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Deeply unhappy with his frontier posting, he spends most of his time drinking while outsourcing his duties to passing travelers. His primary military assignment is dealing with the encroaching murlocs along the coast, a chore he eagerly delegates in hopes of securing a transfer back south. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle did not choose Southshore. Dispatched far from Stormwind City, the lieutenant finds the damp, contested shores of Hillsbrad a miserable step down from the civilized comforts of the capital. Instead of patrolling the fields or coordinating defenses with his commanding officer, Marshal Redpath, Orinelle has practically taken up permanent residence inside Southshore's inn. His days are spent sulking, drinking, and dreaming of an official transfer order that will return him to the south.

Lieutenant Haggerdin. Lieutenant Haggerdin is a dwarven officer stationed upon the Headland in the Alterac Mountains. Standing watch outside the fortified gate to Alterac Valley, he acts as the primary recruitment and liaison officer for the Stormpike Guard. He evaluates aspiring Alliance champions and rewards those who prove their valor against the Frostwolf Clan. Perched in the snowy heights of the Headland above the Hillsbrad Foothills, Lieutenant Haggerdin oversees the muster point for the Alliance's ongoing campaign in Alterac Valley. Dwarven banners flutter beside the massive wooden gate as recruits and veterans assemble under his watchful eye, preparing to plunge into the frigid warzone.

Lieutenant Lisande. Lieutenant Lisande is an emissary of the Argent Dawn stationed upon the high mesas of Thunder Bluff. As a human operating openly in tauren lands, she serves as a liaison against the shared existential threat of the Scourge. While human faces are rare across the windblown heights of Thunder Bluff, the Argent Dawn transcends traditional faction enmities. Lieutenant Lisande serves the holy order by watching for signs of the Lich King's taint even in remote Kalimdor. When undead forces stir on the plains below, she rallies brave Horde champions to ride out and investigate the encroaching menace before it can defile the sacred earth.

Lieutenant Nevell. Lieutenant Nevell is an officer of the Argent Dawn stationed outside the gates of Ironforge in Dun Morogh. Serving as a bulwark against the spreading darkness of the Scourge, he coordinates local defenders and alerts arriving adventurers to undead threats probing the dwarf kingdom's borders. While the Argent Dawn is most renowned for holding the line in the shattered Plaguelands of Lordaeron, its vigilance reaches far into the south. Stationed in the freezing winds outside Ironforge, Lieutenant Nevell represents the order's proactive defense against necromantic incursions. When Scourge activity stirs in the mountain passes of Dun Morogh, Nevell directs recruits and capable adventurers toward the front lines to ensure Ironforge's snowy doorstep remains secure.

Lieutenant Orrin. At Stormwind's gates, Lieutenant Orrin watches for Scourge incursions and calls for scouts. The Argent Dawn officer stands in the Valley of Heroes, where he directs recruits to investigate undead threats beyond the capital. Lieutenant Orrin watches the road from the Valley of Heroes. The Argent Dawn is known for holding the front lines in the ruined north, but it also guards strongholds farther south, including Stormwind City. When necromantic magic stirs beyond the capital, Orrin sounds the alarm and rallies adventurers before the undead can threaten the people within.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Something gleams beneath the rubble: a badge bearing Theramore's sign, a golden anchor over white enamel, with the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe embossed under the anchor. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to bring it to. Something gleams beneath the rubble. Brushing off the ash and debris reveals a badge showing the sign of Theramore, with Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name embossed below it. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore should see it, and will ask what turned up in the ruins of the Shady Rest Inn.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Captain Garran Vimes does not recognize the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe, and sends you to Adjutant Tesoran in Theramore, who looks after the records of the Theramore guard. Captain Garran Vimes cannot place the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Adjutant Tesoran keeps the records of the Theramore guard, covering its people as well as its equipment, and Vimes expects a look through those books to show who Reethe is.

Lieutenant Paval Reethe. Beneath the rubble lies a badge bearing Theramore's sign, a golden anchor over white enamel, with the name Lieutenant Paval Reethe embossed under the anchor. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to. Something gleams beneath the rubble. Brushing off the ash and debris reveals a badge showing the sign of Theramore, with Lieutenant Paval Reethe's name embossed below it. Krog at Brackenwall Village awaits it, and will ask if you have a lead on what befell the Shady Rest Inn.

Lifting the Curse. First Mate Fitzsimmons believes that the restless curse binding his fallen crewmates stems from a dark artifact secured aboard their wrecked ship, the Intrepid. To set his brethren free, an adventurer must face the ghost of Captain Halyndor, take the strongbox key, and recover the relic from the submerged hull. First Mate Fitzsimmons survived the tragic fate of the Third Fleet, but the memory of his comrades haunts his waking hours and his dreams. He remains convinced that the undeath gripping his shipmates is tied to a mysterious, malignant object locked away inside the strongbox of his old vessel, the Intrepid. Overseeing the wreck is the spectral remnants of Captain Halyndor, who even in death fiercely guards the key to the vessel's deepest secrets.

Light. The Light is a boundless primal cosmic force whose energy connects and suffuses all living things across creation. Manifested in the mortal realm as Holy magic, it responds to willpower, meditation, and unyielding faith to mend flesh, shield allies, and purge darkness. The Light is an omnipresent force of living energy. When brought into Azeroth, it manifests as Holy magic. Its power flows through living souls as a connective tissue, binding mortal hearts together. While mortals often personify it as a conscious protector, the Light fundamentally answers the absolute conviction of the soul calling upon it.

name.esES: Capilla de la Esperanza de la Luz

text.enUS: Light's Hope Chapel. Light's Hope Chapel is a sacred sanctuary situated in the eastern reaches of the Plaguelands, serving as the primary redoubt and headquarters for the Argent Dawn. Once a secluded shrine of the Church of the Holy Light in the Eastweald, it now stands as an enduring bulwark against the Scourge. Originally a chapel of the Church of the Holy Light within the verdant Eastweald, Light's Hope Chapel endured the fall of Lordaeron to become a vital shelter in a blighted realm. When the zealous extremists among the survivors splintered to form the Scarlet Crusade, more temperate knights and priests banded together to establish the Argent Dawn. Choosing this secluded, hallowed site as their forward base of operations, the Dawn opened its doors to all races and factions—Alliance and Horde alike—united in the common crusade to purge the Scourge and reclaim the northern lands.

Lightforge Iron. Lightforge Iron is an Alliance salvage task given by Glorin Steelbrow in Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are sent to scour the wreckage of the Flying Osprey, an elven destroyer carrying rare sacred metal that was lost alongside the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras during the Second War. While most of the sunken hulls littering the Wetlands coastline belonged to the famed Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, one vessel was distinct: an elven destroyer christened the Flying Osprey. Bound from Lordaeron, the ship sought safety in numbers alongside the naval fleet, carrying a precious cargo of Lightforge iron. Unfortunately, convoying with war galleys did little to spare it when the Dragonmaw clan's enslaved red dragons descended from the sky, setting the fleet ablaze and plunging both soldiers and sanctified metal beneath the tides.

Lightning Gland. Lightning Glands are harvested from stormhide beasts roaming the plains of the Barrens. Imbued with natural elemental charge, they are sought by Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet to brew a fiery, potent trogg ale learned from the wandering pandaren Chen Stormstout. The savannas of the Barrens host a variety of elemental-touched predators, including the stormhides. Within their flesh lies the lightning gland, an organ pulsating with latent electrical energy. While hardly suitable for ordinary fare, these volatile glands are prized by eccentric brewers who appreciate a brew with a genuine sting.

name.frFR: Auberge de la Fierté du Lion

text.enUS: Lion's Pride Inn. Travelers gather at the Lion's Pride Inn, Goldshire's tavern and community center in Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps the inn, a place to rest, meet others, and find work just south of Stormwind City. The Lion's Pride Inn anchors Goldshire at the crossroads of Elwynn Forest. Innkeeper Farley keeps it by the old motto, “Rest and relaxation for the tired and cold.” Inside, warm hearths, strong drinks, and rooms welcome weary travelers from Northshire. Goldshire sits on trade routes between Stormwind, Westfall, Redridge, and Duskwood, making the inn an indispensable gathering place. Town marshals, local crafters, and seasoned trainers meet there to share news and hire passing mercenaries.

Llane Wrynn I. King Llane Wrynn I was the ruler of Stormwind during the catastrophic First War, whose reign ended with the fall of the kingdom and his own tragic murder. A beloved and proud monarch, his steadfast refusal to believe his friend Medivh had betrayed humanity ultimately doomed his defense of the capital. Born to King Barathen Wrynn, young Prince Llane grew up alongside Anduin Lothar and Medivh. In their youth, the three companions ventured into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale and clashed with the Gurubashi trolls there. In time, Llane ascended to the throne as Stormwind's king.

Load Lightening. Pozzik, the head goblin engineer out at the Mirage Raceway, needs materials to shave critical ounces off his rocket-car chassis. Rather than relying purely on heavy metal plating, the goblins salvage hollow bones from local desert vultures to build sturdy, ultralight steering and structural rigs. Across the blinding white expanse of the Shimmering Flats, the rivalry between goblin and gnomish engineers is decided by fractions of a second. Raw engine thrust is useless if a racer is weighed down by excessive bulk. While gnome teams obsess over intricate gears and brass fittings, the goblin crew led by Pozzik seeks ruthless pragmatic efficiency: stripping out dense iron framing and replacing it with lighter, hollow structural components wherever the frame permits.

Loading Room. The Loading Room is an industrial staging chamber inside Gnomeregan's sprawling mechanical complex. In the current era, this subterranean staging area lies deep within the corrupted fallen capital, dangerously close to rogue constructs such as Techbot. Before the fall of Gnomeregan, the Loading Room functioned as a bustling transit point and cargo staging bay linked to the subterranean transit networks of the tinker capital. Today, like the rest of the ruined city, it has succumbed to chaos. Radioactive fallout, invading troggs, and malfunctioning machinery have rendered the area extremely perilous. The rogue mechanized construct Techbot guards the vicinity, posing a severe threat to any gnome survivors or daring Alliance reclaimers attempting to secure the perimeter.

Loganaar. Loganaar is a night elf druidic instructor residing in the haven of Nighthaven in Moonglade. Dedicated to guiding initiates from both the Alliance and the Horde, he instructs young druids as they attune to the wild and prepare for the call of the Emerald Dream. Situated amidst the serene boughs of Nighthaven, Loganaar serves as a primary mentor to newly initiated druids traveling to Moonglade. Regardless of whether an initiate hails from Darnassus or Thunder Bluff, Loganaar provides guidance in balance, shape-shifting, and reverence for nature. He reminds his students that even within cold stone and unfamiliar lands, true tranquility must be found within oneself. He also acts as a welcoming guide for those journeying deeper into the Cenarion Circle's affairs, sending promising students to wanderers like Torwa Pathfinder in Un'Goro Crater or deeper into ancient woodland rites.

Logging Rope. Logging Rope is heavy cordage vital to the Warsong clan's ongoing logging operations within Ashenvale. Shipments of this sturdy line were ambushed and stolen by local furbolg tribes who violently resist the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest. Maintaining the goblin-built machinery and lumber mills of the Warsong Lumber Camp requires massive quantities of durable logging line. Rather than reaching the loggers at their encampment, essential shipments were intercepted by the Foulweald and Thistlefur furbolg tribes. Driven mad by corruption and fiercely defensive of their ancestral woods, these furbolgs hoard the stolen ropes in their encampments across northern and central Ashenvale.

Lok's Skull. Lok's Skull is the severed head of Lok Orcbane, a fierce Razormane warrior who led brutal quilboar raids against Horde supply routes in the southern Barrens. Sought after by the imprisoned quilboar Mangletooth as an act of vengeance, the skull serves as undeniable proof that the raiders' chieftain has fallen. Emerging from Razorfen Kraul into the southern Barrens, Lok Orcbane spearheaded aggressive Razormane quilboar assaults on Horde supply lines alongside his lieutenants Nak and Kuz. After betraying and abandoning Mangletooth to captivity in Camp Taurajo, Lok earned a grim reputation among orcish defenders who struggled to contain his ruthless raids. Claiming Lok's skull not only avenges the wronged captive who directs Horde champions to Lok's camp, but also shatters the core leadership driving the Razormane offensive.

Lomac Gearstrip. Lomac Gearstrip is an ambitious gnome inventor based in Tinker Town within Ironforge. Renowned for formulating the devastating NG-5 explosive, he liaises with fellow gnomish researchers operating across Kalimdor. Amid the clanging gears and hissing pipes of Ironforge's Tinker Town, Lomac Gearstrip pursues the finer points of gnomish ordnance. Like many exiled gnomes who fled the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Lomac has integrated his tinkering operations directly into the dwarven capital. His workshop focuses on volatile chemical mixtures and specialized munitions designed to overcome heavily defended enemy strongholds.

Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is a weathered diary found clutched in the skeletal remains of the dwarven explorer Henrig Lonebrow at the base of the Great Lift. Its pages detail the final grim journey of Lonebrow through the Barrens and point toward dangers lurking within Razorfen Kraul. Henrig Lonebrow met an unfortunate end near the base of the Great Lift connecting the Barrens to Thousand Needles. Lying abandoned on a rocky ledge, his skeletal remains still grip this weathered journal. The diary serves as a testament to his final travels and directs whoever discovers it to bring word to the night elf druid Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, the border outpost leading into Feralas. Lonebrow's notes shed critical light on the quilboar menace brewing in the southern barrens.

Lonebrow's Journal. Lonebrow's Journal is an Alliance quest initiated by finding a weathered book held in the hand of a dead dwarf at the base of the Great Lift in Thousand Needles. The notes detail his final journey and prompt the finder to deliver the volume west to a night elf druid stationed on the Feralas border. Near the base of the Great Lift, the massive mechanical elevator connecting the Barrens to the canyon floor of Thousand Needles, lies the body of Henrig Lonebrow. Clutched in his hand is a personal journal detailing his travels through this rugged territory. Left behind in a hostile desert dominated by centaur and tauren, his corpse serves as a grim warning of how unforgiving the canyon can be to isolated travelers.

Long Wash. The Long Wash is a bleak, windswept stretch of beach in Darkshore running just south of Auberdine toward the ruins of Ameth'Aran. Gloomy and scattered with marine carcasses and flotsam, the shoreline has recently grown dangerous due to an increasing presence of hostile murlocs. Despite its name, the Long Wash is actually the shortest distinct stretch of coastline in Darkshore. It sits under the region's perpetual overcast skies, an expanse of damp sand littered with flotsam, beached driftwood, and the carcasses of sea creatures washed up by the Veiled Sea. While local crabs comb through the surf, travelers southward from Auberdine must tread cautiously: murloc tribes have established camps along the water's edge, aggressively attacking anyone encroaching on their scavenged territory.

Longbraid the Grim. Longbraid the Grim is an Ironforge dwarf commander stationed just outside the fallen fortress of Dun Modr in the northern Wetlands. Mourning the loss of his brother and the overrun of the Thandol Span, he coordinates the surviving dwarf forces against the invading Dark Iron clan. Positioned within sight of the bridge to the Arathi Highlands, Longbraid the Grim rallies what remains of the dwarven garrison after the Dark Iron clan seized Dun Modr. The sudden assault devastated the regional defenders and resulted in the death of Longbraid's own brother during the siege of the Thandol Span. Burdened by grief and hatred, Longbraid refuses to abandon the northern boundary, directing travelers and surviving mountaineers in surgical strikes to curb the Dark Iron advance.

Longshore. Along Westfall’s western edge, Longshore’s broad sands are claimed by hostile murlocs and broken ships. Longshore runs along Westfall’s western coast, a wide stretch of unbroken sand. Travelers find little peace there. Murlocs dominate the surf, with Old Murk-Eye among the feared leaders, and sunken ships, including ruined elven destroyers, lie in the shallows. Near the south, Daphne Stilwell’s isolated farm faces Defias bandits. Across the water, the Westfall Lighthouse stands within sight.

Longwalker Malah. Longwalker Malah is a missing tauren scout dispatched to survey the eastern borderlands of Mulgore on behalf of Bloodhoof Village. As an elite Longwalker answering directly to the High Chieftain, her sudden failure to return after three days prompts an urgent search to ensure both her survival and the safety of the valley. The Longwalkers serve as the eyes and ears of the shu'halo, renowned across the plains for their tireless stride and survival prowess. Pledged directly to High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof, these elite scouts are tasked with traversing vast territories to gather intelligence and deliver vital messages. Though their ultimate loyalty lies with the High Chieftain alone, young Baine Bloodhoof occasionally calls upon their aid to safeguard the settlement of Bloodhoof Village and its surrounding pastures.

Look To The Stars. Look To The Stars begins Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to gaze past the eerie canopy of Duskwood. Believing that a scientific answer beyond arcane superstition explains the forest's dark curse, Viktori recruits you to gather components for a telescope designed by his gnomish associate. Amid the gloom and fear shrouding Darkshire, Viktori Prism'Antras takes a distinctly unconventional view of Duskwood's misfortune. Rather than attributing the land's corruption purely to black magic, curses, or restless dead, Viktori suspects that greater truths await high above the canopy. With the aid of blueprints drawn up by his gnomish partner, Cog, he sets out to build an optical device capable of peering into the heavens.

Look To The Stars. Following the blueprints provided by the tinker Cog, Viktori Prism'Antras seeks a reflective surface to assemble his observatory telescope in Darkshire. He directs travelers to southern Duskwood to locate Mary, a local woman remembered for carrying a looking glass. Having secured a bronze tube for his telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras turns to the next requirement outlined in Cog's blueprints: a reliable mirror to direct and reflect light through the device. Rather than forging fine silvered glass from scratch amidst the shortages plaguing Darkshire, Viktori recalls Mary, a local resident known across the region for always carrying a looking glass.

Look To The Stars. This quest sends adventurers to recover Blind Mary's discarded looking glass for the astronomer Viktori Prism'Antras. The fragile mirror fell into the hands of an Insane Ghoul that wanders the desolate Tranquil Gardens Cemetery in southern Duskwood. Before the creeping gloom overran Duskwood and turned her into a weeping spirit, Blind Mary treasured an ornate looking glass. Following the horrific incident that claimed her sight and sanity, she cast the keepsake into the dirt behind her family barn. The reflective mirror is exactly what Viktori Prism'Antras needs to build his grand telescope in Darkshire, but it was snatched away into the shadows long before the astronomer dreamed of studying the heavens.

Look To The Stars. This quest marks the final chapter in Viktori Prism'Antras's endeavor to assemble a stargazing device in Darkshire. With the telescope structure otherwise built, Viktori sends travelers to the dangerous Vul'Gol Ogre Mound to retrieve a lens large enough for his contraption: a monocle worn by the ogre Zzarc'Vul. Throughout the construction of his stargazing telescope, Viktori Prism'Antras has relied on plans drafted by the gnome engineer Cog Glitzspinner. While brass tubes and sturdy mountings could be scavenged or assembled from local supplies, the apparatus required an exceptionally massive focusing lens. Standard magnifying glasses and optical components from Stormwind traders simply lacked the diameter called for by Cog's ambitious design, leading Viktori to look toward an unlikely and perilous alternative.

text.enUS: Look at the Size of It!. You have come into a gigantic, ornate pillow that once belonged to Chambermaid Pillaclencher. Evonice Sootsmoker, in the Searing Gorge, is bound to want it. The pillow Chambermaid Pillaclencher kept is now yours. Evonice Sootsmoker will surely be eager to get hold of it. Bring it to her in the Searing Gorge and see what she offers you for the trouble.

name.frFR: Le point de vue d'un vieil ami

text.enUS: Look to an Old Friend. Master Mathias Shaw sends you to seek an unusual contact in Stormwind's Trade District. Noble corruption shields traitors from ordinary justice, so Shaw turns to the city's finest cheesemonger and his intelligence network.

Looking Further. Looking Further is an Alliance espionage mission directed by the wizard Theocritus via an enchanted conduit. To investigate tensions between the rogue mage Morganth and the Blackrock orcs, you must infiltrate the watch tower beside Stonewatch Keep and plant an enchanted glyph inside an unnoticed container. From his sanctum in Elwynn Forest, the wizard Theocritus maintains a vigilant watch over eastern Redridge through scrying magic. While monitoring the Tower of Ilgalar, he detects sudden contention between the renegade human warlock Morganth and the Blackrock orcs entrenched in Stonewatch Keep. Rather than working together against the Kingdom of Stormwind, these hostile factions are locked in conflict over an unknown prize, prompting Theocritus to intervene before the balance shifts.

Loramus Thalipedes. Loramus Thalipedes is a reclusive night elf demon hunter secluded on a remote isle off the coast of Azshara. Flanked by loyal felhounds, he dedicates his existence to destroying Razelikh the Defiler, directing seasoned champions through rituals to strike down the dreadlord. Perched on a solitary, storm-tossed island southeast of Hetaera's Clutch, Loramus Thalipedes stands apart from the rest of his kin. He is a demon hunter—an exile who underwent the agonizing ritual of blinding himself to gain spectral sight. Surrounded by three towering felhounds named Raytaf, Shahiar, and Zaman, Loramus watches the unseen currents of demonic corruption across Azeroth while keeping a watchful vigil over the shattered ruins of Azshara.

Lord Aliden Perenolde. Krusk wants Lord Aliden Perenolde, leader of the Syndicate, dead and the Warchief's pendant recovered. His manor stands north, on the shores of Lordamere Lake, and his mistress Elysa is the one to ask about the pendant. After Blackmoore's Legacy, Krusk says Perenolde has to die, and the world be rid of his foulness. The manor sits a way to the north, on the shores of Lordamere Lake, at Dandred's Fold. When the deed is done, you are to put your questions about Taretha's pendant, which the Warchief desires, to his mistress Elysa.

Lord Arkkoroc. Lord Arkkoroc is an ancient, towering sea giant who dwells within the ruined Temple of Arkkoran along the ragged coast of Azshara. Described by the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes as a lesser deity, he holds sway over the surrounding waters and commands lesser sea giants who serve as his sons. Reclining amidst the brine-crusted ruins of the Temple of Arkkoran, Lord Arkkoroc is far more than a typical sea giant. To hermits like Loramus Thalipedes, this colossal being is considered a lesser deity whose divine will shapes the surrounding waters. His sons patrol the crags and shallows around the sanctuary, enforcing his quiet dominion over Azshara's tempestuous shores.

Lord Baurles K. Wishock. In Stormwind Keep, Lord Baurles K. Wishock lives among the petitioners and dignitaries. Barkeeps know him for unpaid tabs and a taste for strong drink, but his nights in the city’s underbelly brought him near darker dealings. Lord Baurles K. Wishock moves among petitioners and dignitaries in Stormwind Keep, where he belongs to the influential House of Nobles. Though his station is high, he often drinks in the Mage Quarter’s dive bars, especially the Slaughtered Lamb, and leaves large bills unpaid. There, he hears of a warlock coven practicing dark arts in cellars beneath the floorboards. Wishock sets out to have the tavern closed and asks fellow nobles for a formal investigation. Uncovering demonic cabals in Stormwind rarely goes unpunished.

Lord Cobrahn. Lord Cobrahn is one of the four leaders of the corrupted Druids of the Fang lurking deep within the Wailing Caverns. Once a night elf druid of Naralex's noble order, which hoped to heal the Barrens, he succumbed to the nightmare infecting the cavern springs. Taking a lethal serpent guise, Cobrahn now commands broods of deviate serpents and defends the twisted labyrinth. Before his fall, Cobrahn was one of the noble druids who followed Naralex. When Naralex ventured into the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens hoping to tap their underground springs and restore lush life to the arid wastes, Cobrahn accompanied him. However, when Naralex's Emerald Dream communion decayed into a twisting nightmare, Cobrahn's mind shattered alongside his brothers.

Lord Ello Ebonlocke. Lord Ello Ebonlocke is the mayor of Darkshire and the leader of its governing council, stationed inside the Darkshire Town Hall. Surrounded by darkness and creeping horrors, he struggles daily to maintain order and protect his besieged citizens despite receiving little aid from Stormwind. Seated in the gloom of the Darkshire Town Hall, Lord Ello Ebonlocke bears the heavy burden of governing a settlement on the brink of ruin. Once part of the prosperous rural haven known as Grand Hamlet, Darkshire is now smothered by perpetual shadow and besieged by ravenous ghouls, skeletal abominations, and feral beasts.
