Ello presides over the Council of Darkshire, striving against impossible odds to keep the remnants of civilization functioning while Stormwind turns a blind eye to their plight.

name.zhCN: 格雷森·沙东布瑞克公爵

text.enUS: Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker is a veteran paladin commander of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. One of the Alliance's foremost paladins, he trains budding champions of the Light and oversees the sacred, arduous trials required for senior paladins to claim their holy chargers. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker stands among the foremost defenders of the Alliance, anchoring the order's presence in Stormwind City. A veteran of the Silver Hand, Grayson does not merely instruct recruits in martial skill; he tests their spiritual conviction. When promising knights demonstrate their readiness, Grayson dispatches them north toward the contested front lines of the Western Plaguelands to aid Commander Ashlam Valorfist at Chillwind Camp.

Lord Jorach Ravenholdt. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt is the master of Ravenholdt, an elite guild of rogues and assassins operating out of a secluded estate in the Alterac Mountains. He directs the league's clandestine operations, training promising operatives while waging a bitter war against the regional bandits of the Syndicate. Lord Jorach Ravenholdt presides over the Assassin's League from his hidden manor nestled in the crags between Alterac and Hillsbrad. A nobleman of mysterious heritage, he opens his halls to outlaws, cutpurses, and assassins regardless of allegiance, provided they exhibit exceptional skill and respect his authority. Under his command, the league acts as both a fraternity for master thieves and an independent syndicate for wetwork and espionage. Ravenholdt harbors a fierce hatred for the Syndicate—the band of disgraced Alterac nobles turned outlaws—and routinely directs his subordinates and visiting freelancers to sabotage their camps and plunder their assets.

name.zhCN: 玛克斯韦尔·泰罗索斯男爵

text.enUS: Lord Maxwell Tyrosus. Lord Maxwell Tyrosus is the supreme commander of the Argent Dawn, stationed at their forward redoubt of Light's Hope Chapel in the Eastern Plaguelands. A veteran paladin of the Silver Hand from the Third War, he guides the coalition's crusade against the Scourge and orchestrates strikes into blighted strongholds like Stratholme. Maxwell Tyrosus rode alongside Uther the Lightbringer during the catastrophic Third War, guarding the exits of Andorhal when the Scourge tore through the kingdom. After the fall of Lordaeron, he cast his lot with the Argent Dawn, an order that welcomes anyone willing to stand against the Scourge, in stark contrast to the human-only zealotry of the Scarlet Crusade.

Lord Pythas. Lord Pythas, once a night elf warrior, is one of the four corrupted leaders of the Druids of the Fang in the Wailing Caverns. Originally one of the personal guards of the druid Naralex, he fell victim to the nightmare tainting the oasis underground. Now he wields both martial might and twisted serpent magic against any who try to reach his slumbering master. Before his corruption, Pythas was a seasoned night elf warrior who served among the druid Naralex's personal guard when the expedition ventured into the dry wastes of the Barrens. Alongside his martial training, he took up the druidic arts in service of Naralex's dream of restoring lush life to the arid realm. However, physical discipline and martial valor offered no shelter against the insidious corruption waiting deep within the subterranean fissures.

Lord Serpentis. Lord Serpentis is a corrupted night elf druid who stands as one of the four leaders of the rogue Druids of the Fang within the Wailing Caverns. Once a druid of great power and prestige in the order of Naralex, he was twisted into madness when Naralex's dream became a nightmare within the subterranean springs. Now, he helps command the serpent-worshipping sect deep in the caverns where the corrupted Naralex lies slumbering. Before darkness overtook the cavern springs, Serpentis was a druid of great power and prestige, one of the noble order led by Naralex that hoped to use the caverns' springs and the Emerald Dream to heal the Barrens. However, when Naralex's vision became a corrupting nightmare, Serpentis was among the druids whose minds fell to the emerging madness.

Lord Shalzaru. Lord Shalzaru is the tyrannical leader of the Hatecrest naga operating out of the Isle of Dread off the coast of Feralas. Ruling his serpentine followers with absolute cruelty, he oversees extensive excavations among the submerged and ruined elven settlements. His recent discovery of a strange, ancient relic has drawn the attention of outside investigators eager to wrest it from his grasp. Lord Shalzaru commands the Hatecrest naga, directing their presence along the southern coast of Feralas. From his subterranean lair within a cavern on the Isle of Dread, he enforces his rule through cruelty and ruthless authority. Under his command, the Hatecrest scour the ancient ruins of ancient Kalimdor, searching for forgotten treasures and powerful relics left behind from the Sundering.

Lordaeron. Lordaeron is the great northern subcontinent of the Eastern Kingdoms, once the glorious heart of human civilization and the Alliance. Following the devastation of the Third War, its former kingdoms lie in ruins, contested by the undead Scourge, Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, and desperate remnants of the living. Lordaeron shares its name with the human city-state of Lordaeron, which rose in the north after the ancient Empire of Arathor and grew into the most powerful of the human kingdoms. Stretching from the rugged Arathi Highlands in the south across scenic forests and waterways up toward Quel'Thalas, the region nurtured thriving kingdoms like Lordaeron, Dalaran, Gilneas, and Alterac. It was historically celebrated for fertile farmlands in Tirisfal and Hillsbrad, mountain strongholds, and the sacred cradle of the Holy Light.

Lordamere Internment Camp. Lordamere Internment Camp is a former Second War detention facility perched on the heights overlooking Dalaran. Once built to confine lethargic orcs, the camp is now occupied by surviving Dalaran magi and guards alongside a treacherous band of Forsaken defectors. Following the Second War, the Alliance constructed internment camps across the northern kingdoms to contain the defeated orcish Horde. Lordamere was unique as the sole camp established within the Alterac Mountains, placed under Dalaran's jurisdiction. With the orcs long since liberated or fled, the camp today functions under Warden Belamoore as an outpost for Dalaran remnants studying dangerous magical relics.

Lordamere Lake. Lordamere Lake is one of the largest bodies of freshwater in the Eastern Kingdoms, bordered by Tirisfal Glades, Silverpine Forest, and the Alterac Mountains. Once the bustling aquatic heart of human civilization in the north, its cold waters and islands are now haunted by Scourge necromancers, feral murlocs, and the spreading shadow of the undead. In the golden age of the Alliance of Lordaeron, Lordamere Lake sat at the crossroads of human power. The Capital City of Lordaeron guarded its northern shores, the sorcerous city-state of Dalaran rose near its southern reach, and the kingdom of Alterac lined its mountainous eastern edge. Merchant vessels and fishing boats once crossed its broad, mist-covered expanse without fear. Following the devastation of the Third War, the lake was transformed from a hub of commerce into a natural barrier dividing the Forsaken-held lands of Tirisfal and Silverpine from the treacherous heights of Alterac.

Lorekeeper Raintotem. Lorekeeper Raintotem is a tauren elder stationed in northern Mulgore just south of Red Rocks. He tends to the sacred burial grounds and asks adventurers to drive off the Bristleback quilboar disturbing them. Positioned near the sacred bluffs of Red Rocks in Mulgore, Lorekeeper Raintotem tends to the spiritual obligations of his people. He asks adventurers to drive Bristleback Interlopers from the burial ground, restoring peace to the ancestors' resting place.

Lorgalis Manuscript. The Lorgalis Manuscript is an ancient text tied to the worship and lore of the Old Gods, preserved from the fallen night elven ruins beneath Ashenvale. Hidden within the sunken temple complex of Blackfathom Deeps, it holds secrets coveted by dark scholars seeking to awaken ancient, slumbering powers. The Lorgalis Manuscript rests at the bottom of Blackfathom Deeps, the sunken ruins where long-dead elves once dwelt before their city fell. Written by one Lorgalis, it speaks of the Old Gods who raged across Azeroth when the world was new and now lie chained and sleeping, and it praises Aku'mai, a servant of the Old Gods who dwells in the Deeps. Its lore is said to open mystical doorways and stir ancient entities that sleep deep beneath the world. Stored away in a pitted iron chest amidst the flooded corridors, it has drawn the attention of cultists and shadow scholars alike.

Lorgus Jett. Lorgus Jett is a human member of the Twilight's Hammer cult operating within the flooded corridors of Blackfathom Deeps. Wandering the Moonshrine Ruins, he serves as a ruthless commander in the cult's service to the Old Gods. Horde leaders have singled him out as a primary target to disrupt the cult's encroaching presence along the Ashenvale coast. While many members of the Twilight's Hammer working under Blackfathom Deeps hail from orcish or tauren lineages, Lorgus Jett stands out as a human in the deep recesses of ancient night elf ruins. Roaming anywhere between the upper Moonshrine Ruins and the cavernous tunnels beyond the murloc defiler Gelihast, Jett coordinates the cult's dark rituals and violent ambitions.

Loslor Rudge. Loslor Rudge is an enterprising dwarven engineering supplier stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. He provides mechanical parts, tools, and munitions to tinkerers across the snowy mountain ridges, keeping critical connections open with gunsmiths like Hegnar Rumbleshot. Operating out of Steelgrill's Depot just down the road from Kharanos, Loslor Rudge keeps a steady inventory of engineering essentials—ranging from copper modulators and bronze tubing to blasting powder and spanners. Dun Morogh's harsh weather and sprawling tinker operations mean practical parts are constantly in demand, and Loslor prides himself on keeping the local gearheads supplied. However, the wilderness between outposts is treacherous; when a courier taking a shortcut near the Grizzled Den was chased away by wendigos, an essential shipment of ammunition meant for his valued client, gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot, was left behind in the snow.

Lost But Not Forgotten. Lost But Not Forgotten is a somber quest given by Misha Tor'kren at her homestead northwest of Razor Hill. Desperate for closure, she asks travelers to search the dangerous banks of the Southfury River for any trace of her headstrong son, Kron. Northwest of Razor Hill, tucked away in the arid red wastes of Durotar, sits the humble Tor'kren farmstead. Here lives Misha Tor'kren, an orc mother paralyzed by sorrow and anxiety. Days earlier, her son Kron declared he was heading west toward the Southfury River on the border of the Barrens to hunt the river's ferocious crocolisks. Despite her warnings about the deadly beasts, Kron's stubborn pride drove him to storm off to prove his mettle. He has not been seen since.

Lost Deathstalkers. Lost Deathstalkers is a reconnaissance mission assigned by High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. Two Forsaken scouts, Rane and Quinn Yorick, went missing weeks ago while surveying the haunted farmsteads of northern Silverpine Forest. Tracking them down reveals not only their fate, but the encroaching perils that threaten the Forsaken hold on the region. The Deathstalkers serve as the eyes, ears, and hidden daggers of Lady Sylvanas and the Forsaken. When operatives go silent, command takes notice. High Executor Hadrec deployed the scouts Rane and Quinn Yorick into northern Silverpine Forest weeks ago to monitor the abandoned farms and watch for enemy movements. Having received no courier or report since their departure, Hadrec fears the duo met a grim end at the hands of the Scourge or worse.

Lost Fleet. The Lost Fleet consists of the shattered wooden hulks of the Kul Tiras Third Fleet, sunken off the northern coast of the Wetlands along Baradin Bay. Decimated during the Second War by Dragonmaw-enslaved red dragons, the wreckage is now haunted by restless, cursed undead sailors bound to the wreckage by a mysterious curse. During the Second War, on its last voyage, the Kul Tiras Third Fleet was ambushed from above by red dragons enslaved by the Dragonmaw clan. Sheets of dragonflame quickly engulfed the fleet, sending proud vessels like the Wave Mistress and the Intrepid crashing onto the shallows and reefs of northern Bluegill Marsh. Almost the entire contingent drowned or burned, with First Mate Fitzsimmons standing as the lone living survivor of the disaster.

Lost Necklace. In southern Elwynn, Bernice Stonefield searches for her missing necklace. She suspects Billy Maclure, the young son of the neighboring family, and asks you to find him across the road. The Stonefield and Maclure families live on adjoining land in southern Elwynn Forest, but they share little goodwill. When "Auntie" Bernice Stonefield discovers her cherished necklace is gone, she blames the youngest Maclure. Certain that Billy Maclure slipped onto her farm and took it, the bitter widow asks you to cross the road to the vineyards, find the boy, and demand its return.

Lost Point. Lost Point is a dilapidated wooden watchtower standing in western Dustwallow Marsh, originally constructed by Theramore's forces as an advance scout post. It has since fallen into disrepair and slipped from the control of Lady Jaina Proudmoore's guard, now serving as a hideout for rogue deserters. Erected by the expeditionary forces of Theramore to monitor traffic and threats emerging from the Barrens, Lost Point has long outlived its intended military function. The outpost has decayed under the relentless moisture of the marsh, its timber rotting and its defenses abandoned by regular troops. Instead of garrison sentries, the tower and its immediate surroundings are occupied by human deserters who broke away from Theramore's service, finding shelter in the isolated wilderness far from the discipline of the city's commanders.

Lost Relic Carry. Lost Relic Carry involves recovering a fractured piece of an ancient rock-mech automaton and delivering it to Prospector Whelgar in the Wetlands. The relic's unknown composite material hints at the sophisticated engineering of the Titans, earning serious reverence from dwarven researchers. Deep within ancient grounds, adventurers can uncover a fractured component of a rock-mech automaton. Far from being simple rubble, its unusual composite material reveals the craftsmanship of an advanced, ancient mechanism tied to the Titans.

Lost Rigger Cove. Tucked away along the eastern cliffs of Tanaris, Lost Rigger Cove serves as the primary base of operations for the Southsea Pirates in the region. Shielded by towering desert mountains on three sides, this hidden port boasts docks, fortified encampments, and an active shipyard constructing new pirate vessels. Naturally fortified by sheer rock walls on almost every side, Lost Rigger Cove provides the Southsea Freebooters an ideal maritime stronghold on Kalimdor's southeastern edge. Here, pirate cutthroats, dockworkers, and brigands haul salvage and assemble fresh hulls right under the noses of Gadgetzan's authorities. The cove allows the Southseas to project power across the Great Sea while raiding trade routes between Ratchet, Booty Bay, and coastal settlements.

Lost in the Shadows. 'Lost in the Shadows' is a quest involving the rescue of Pal'juh, an impetuous hunter who ventured into danger alone. Her rescue highlights the delicate balance between raw aggression and patient stalking required of wilderness trackers. 'Lost in the Shadows' involves locating and rescuing Pal'juh, a talented but hotheaded hunter who ventured out alone into hostile territory. Unwilling to wait for support, she found herself in over her head, requiring outside assistance to ensure her safe return.

Lost in the Thicket Things. A concerned alchemist asks travelers to track down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman, who vanished after pursuing rumors of towering, unknown grasses. Ardin's botanical curiosity led him straight toward a nearby excavation site, where dangerous wildlife and spider attacks have besieged the crew. In 'Lost in the Thicket Things', an alchemist seeks help tracking down her missing husband, Ardin Grassman. Ardin possesses an uncanny, instinctual affinity for nature, routinely braving steep cliffs and distant wilderness to gather rare herbs and botanical specimens to stock her alchemy supplies. When a passing excavation crew brought word of bizarre, towering grasses unlike anything seen before, Ardin's curiosity got the better of him, and he set out to inspect the flora for himself.

Lotwil Veriatus. Lotwil Veriatus is an eccentric gnomish scholar conducting dangerous elemental experiments in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. Stationed east of Kargath with his sarcastic apprentice Lucien Tosselwrench and a mechanical attendant named Servo, he is dedicated to blending arcane theory, alchemy, and engineering into a unified discipline. Originally from Kharanos in Dun Morogh, Lotwil envisions a grand University for his Enlightened Assembly of Arcanology, Alchemy, and Engineering Sciences. He believes these three disciplines should not be practiced in isolation, but harmonized. In pursuit of this dream, he chose the harsh Badlands as his laboratory to study native rock elementals and construct binding shackles capable of mastering elemental forces. While an accomplished researcher—having studied elemental machines and defeated dark iron constructs in the past—his single-minded focus often blinds him to the explosive hazards of his fieldwork.

name.esES: Una canción de amor para Narain

text.enUS: Love Song for Narain. Meridith the Mermaiden has a message for Narain Soothfancy, the gnome she once rescued from the wreckage of a crashed flying machine. She asks you to carry her love letter to him in Tanaris. You can take this up while seeking Narain's book in Draconic for Dummies. Meridith the Mermaiden seldom has visitors. The last was the gnome she rescued from the wreckage of a crashed flying machine, and she gazes into nothing for a moment, lost in the memory. She asks whether you know Narain Soothfancy, because she has to tell him how she feels, and she is sure it is love. She begs you to carry a message to him, and promises to be forever in your debt.

Love's Gift. Love's Gift is the penultimate quest in the Horde warlock chain to summon and bind a succubus. After being tracked down and revived in the Barrens, the dying Grunt Dogran relinquishes a treasured keepsake to provide the bait necessary for the dark ritual. To summon and subjugate a succubus, a warlock requires a talisman of intense, unblemished emotion. Succubi feed on mortal desire and pervert genuine affection into anguish. Dogran's pendant carries the weight of authentic devotion and tragic parting. Returned to Gan'rul Bloodeye in the shadowy clefts of Orgrimmar, the talisman is cleaned and polished so its radiant emotional resonance can lure the devourer of souls across the Twisting Nether.

Lower Wilds. The Lower Wilds form the eastern threshold of Feralas, where the humid forests meet the arid canyons of Thousand Needles. The main road cutting through these woods connects Thalanaar at the border to the settlements further west, flanked by ancient greenery and unpredictable woodland creatures. Spanning the eastern reaches of Feralas, the Lower Wilds serve as the natural transition between the sun-baked ravines of Thousand Needles and the deep, primordial jungle to the west. Travelers entering the zone must traverse this stretch of forest along the main highway, past the elven outpost of Thalanaar guarding the mountain pass. The dense canopies here house ancient treants, alongside indigenous wildlife that makes straying from the beaten path perilous.

Lucius. At the Lakeshire docks, Lucius watches the Redridge waterfront. The dwarf works undercover for Stormwind’s SI:7, helping agents with reconnaissance and trade skills. Lucius watches the Lakeshire docks for SI:7, Stormwind’s intelligence service. He keeps an eye on trade, unusual traffic, and threats moving into the Redridge Mountains. Agents sent east from Stormwind come to him to coordinate covert work and practice field skills such as lockpicking. Through Lucius, Stormwind keeps a hidden reach beyond Elwynn Forest.

Lunar Fungus. Lunar Fungus is a potent medicinal growth harvested from fungal blooms deep within Darkshore's cavern systems. Druid initiates collect these mushrooms alongside common herbs to brew a restorative salve capable of treating diseased wildlife. Harvested from Lunar Fungal Blooms, this distinctive fungus thrives in dark, subterranean caverns across Darkshore. The Cenarion Circle values it for its amplifying effects; when blended with a soothing water base and common Earthroot, the fungus provides the necessary potency to create an effective counteragent against debilitating afflictions. Because it grows primarily in damp underground spaces frequented by territorial moonkin, obtaining it requires careful navigation of the untamed wilderness.

Lurker Venom. Lurker Venom is a potent natural toxin harvested from the predatory spiders that prowl the rocky hills and woods of Loch Modan. Dwarven defenders require this caustic venom as a key ingredient to prepare an alchemical neutralizing compound against Dark Iron sabotage. The hills and crags surrounding Loch Modan crawl with predatory arachnids—ranging from common wood lurkers to the infamous matriarch Shanda the Spinner. While their bites pose a constant hazard to mountaineers and travelers, the explosives expert Ashlan Stonesmirk named their virulent poison as one ingredient of a disarming mixture, which Chief Engineer Hinderweir prepares. Combined with rare minerals and tears harvested from the loch's crocolisks, Lurker Venom forms a reactive solvent capable of disarming complex Dark Iron explosives.

Lushwater Oasis. Lushwater Oasis is one of the three life-giving watering holes nestled in the arid Barrens, located just south of the Crossroads. Despite its verdant appearance, the oasis is fraught with danger, infested by aggressive Kolkar centaur and harboring the entrance to the Wailing Caverns. Its tainted waters are well-known to anglers seeking the peculiar Deviate Fish. Situated a short march south of the Crossroads, Lushwater Oasis offers a deceptive respite amid the sun-bleached expanse of the Barrens. While its palm canopies and fresh springs draw thirsty beasts from across the savanna, Kolkar centaur claim the banks, lying in wait to butcher both game and unwary travelers. The oasis is also the gateway to the Wailing Caverns, whose sprawling underground networks seep corruptive energies into the pools above, breeding unnatural wildlife and bizarre mutations.

Lydon's Toxin. Lydon's Toxin is an alchemical concoction synthesized by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to disrupt the Venture Company's deforestation in the Stonetalon Mountains. Entrusted to Horde adventurers, it is delivered to Apothecary Zamah in Thunder Bluff so she can devise an effective delivery mechanism. Developed by Apothecary Lydon in the Hillsbrad Foothills, this virulent compound is designed to combat the invasive Venture Company loggers despoiling the Stonetalon Mountains. According to Lydon, the concoction produces lethal and potentially contagious results upon contact. However, before the substance can be unleashed against the goblins' operations around the Windshear Crag, it must be ferried across continents to Apothecary Zamah, the Royal Apothecary Society's representative in Thunder Bluff. Zamah requires the raw mixture to engineer a wide-dispersal apparatus—the Toxic Fogger—ensuring the brew wipes out the exploitative deforesters without needlessly endangering Horde assets.

Lyria Du Lac. In Goldshire, Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors behind the village smithy. She teaches them to master their stances and arms. Lyria Du Lac trains young warriors in the yard behind Goldshire's forge. She teaches those fresh from Northshire Abbey, judges their readiness, and introduces specialized combat techniques. Warriors take up shield and blade for Stormwind, facing the threats of Elwynn Forest.

Ma Stonefield. At Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn, Ma Stonefield tends to hardships close to home. Beside Auntie Bernice, she faces farm troubles, neighboring rivalries, and pests. Ma Stonefield watches over the farm beside her family cottage in southwestern Elwynn Forest, with Auntie Bernice Stonefield at her side. The neighboring Maclure homestead and nearby pumpkin patches bring little peace. Wild boars threaten the Stonefield crops, and Princess causes the greatest trouble. The enormous prize sow tramples fields and devours the harvest the family worked hard to grow.

MacGrann's Dried Meats. MacGrann's Dried Meats are a month's worth of salted provisions prepared by the hunter Tundra MacGrann to survive the harsh Dun Morogh winter. Stored in a reinforced thorium meat locker, the entire cache was snatched by the ferocious yeti known as Old Icebeard. Life in the freezing crags of Dun Morogh demands careful planning. To prepare for the blizzards of the cold season, the dwarf hunter Tundra MacGrann spent weeks hunting game, salting the meat, and securing it inside a sturdy chest. Aware that scavenging bears and prowling predators routinely plague his homestead, MacGrann took no chances and locked his food supply away inside a thorium meat locker. Even with those precautions, he did not anticipate an intruder strong enough to carry away the entire chest rather than trying to pry it open on the spot.

MacKreel's Moonshine. MacKreel's Moonshine is a potent dwarven liquor brewed by Foggy MacKreel, stationed on the broken Thandol Span north of the Wetlands. Strong enough to knock out a sentry on duty, it is prized as far north as Southshore, where Brewmeister Bilger accepts it as payment for debts. Brewed by the guard Foggy MacKreel on the Thandol Span, this moonshine carries an infamous reputation for potency. Even hardened dwarven sentries find themselves laid low by a night with the brew, waking with headaches akin to a brigade of siege engines rolling overhead. Despite its punishing kick, it is highly valued for warming up travelers against the damp chills of Lordaeron and Khaz Modan.

MacKreel's Moonshine. MacKreel's Moonshine is a fast-paced errand run on behalf of Foggy MacKreel, a dwarf stranded on the broken part of the Thandol Span. Having overindulged on his own potent brew and slept through his watch, Foggy entrusts an Alliance traveler with rushing a fresh batch to Hillsbrad to settle a lingering debt with Brewmeister Bilger in Southshore. Life on watch atop the shattered Thandol Span is wet, cold, and notoriously dull. Foggy MacKreel manages the damp chill by imbibing his own homemade moonshine, a concoction so fierce he compares its aftermath to an entire brigade of siege engines rolling across his skull. Unfortunately for Foggy, one drink too many caused him to pass out during his shift. With Longbraid the Grim commanding the dwarves defending the Span, Foggy cannot afford any further lapses in discipline.

Maclure Vineyards. In southern Elwynn, Maclure Vineyards sends grapes and wine to Stormwind. The Maclure family's estate is known as much for its bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields as for its harvest. The Maclure Vineyards should be a peaceful haven of farming and winecraft in southern Elwynn Forest. Instead, the feud with the Stonefields down the road overshadows the family's daily labor. Accusations of theft and old resentment keep tempers high between the households. Hungry boars prowl the land, while kobolds press toward both homesteads.

Madame Eva. Madame Eva is a revered fortune-teller and matriarch living in Darkshire in the shadowed forest of Duskwood. Practicing older, mystic arts of divination and cartomancy, she often serves as the first townsperson to sense unnatural disturbances across the woods. Travelers frequently seek her out to unravel grim mysteries or procure occult charms against the creeping dark. Dwelling quietly amidst the gloom of Darkshire, Madame Eva practices cartomancy and ancient folk rituals that many in Stormwind's cathedral would view with suspicion. In a forsaken region plagued by feral beasts, the undead, and darker horrors, her eerie insights are tolerated and sought after by desperate townspeople and visiting adventurers alike.

Maestra's Post. Maestra's Post is a small Alliance settlement in western Ashenvale, perched along the road northwest of Astranaar and south of the Ruins of Ordil'Aran. Guarded by night elven Sentinels and hosting a rare human presence in Kalimdor's ancient forest, it serves as a forward watch against encroaching threats. Positioned under the canopy of western Ashenvale, Maestra's Post consists of a slender night elven tower and an open lodge. It sits as an essential waypoint for travelers marching between the coast of Darkshore and the larger hub of Astranaar. Despite its tranquil elven architecture, the outpost stands perpetually on edge. The local Sentinels keep a wary eye on the surrounding wilderness, where corrupted furbolg stir and nearby Horde movements constantly threaten the Alliance's supply lines.

Magatha Grimtotem. Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch of the Grimtotem tribe and the Elder Crone of Thunder Bluff. A formidable shaman and political schemer, she resides on Elder Rise while continually challenging Cairne Bloodhoof's vision for the tauren nation. Magatha rose to absolute authority over the Grimtotem through an arranged union followed by the sudden, fatal climbing accident of her mate. Operating from Elder Rise with her personal retinue and bodyguards, she stands as the undisputed political and spiritual leader of her reclusive tribe. Unlike Cairne Bloodhoof, Magatha preaches tauren dominance, viewing other mortal races as intruders upon Kalimdor who ought to be eradicated or swept aside.

Mage. Mages are scholarly spellcasters who bend the fabric of reality through arcane study, hurling destructive fire, controlling frost, and raw arcane energy. While physically fragile and cloaked only in cloth, their mastery over teleportation, conjuration, and battlefield crowd control makes them formidable allies and terrifying foes. Their discipline requires immense mental dedication, balancing immense destructive potential against the perilous history of arcane misuse. The path of the mage demands intellect, focus, and years of rigorous study. Rather than communing with spirits or relying on divine faith, magi treat magic as a precise cosmic science. By drawing upon arcane energies, a practitioner can weave raw destructive power, summon searing bursts of flame, or chill the surrounding air into solid ice and howling blizzards. Because heavy armor disrupts the delicate somatic gestures and mental focus required for incantations, mages wear light cloth, relying instead on wards, mana barriers, and evasive spells to protect themselves.

Mage Quarter. The Mage Quarter forms the arcane heart of Stormwind City, resting across the canals in the capital's southwestern corner. Towering over its cobblestone streets and esoteric specialty shops stands the Wizard's Sanctum, where the kingdom's conjurers hone their craft. Beneath the district's scholarly surface also lie shadowy recesses, harboring practitioners of far darker arts. Reachable by bridges crossing the canals from Cathedral Square or the Trade District, the Mage Quarter caters entirely to the mystical needs of the Alliance. Centered around the spire of the Wizard's Sanctum, human and allied spellcasters gather to study the weave of arcane magic and train apprentices. The surrounding streets are crowded with purveyors of tailoring cloth, reagents, alchemical supplies, and enchanted staves, creating an insular district dedicated to research and the defense of the kingdom.

Mage Summoner. Mage Summoner is an Alliance strike mission directed by Sentinel Velene Starstrike from Silverwind Refuge. After investigating corrupted water elementals near Mystral Lake, the Sentinels dispatch adventurers across the border into the Barrens to execute the undead mage Sarilus Foulborne atop Dreadmist Peak. The night elves rarely send scouts southward into the sun-scorched savannas of the Barrens without dire cause. After investigating unnatural disturbances among the water elementals around Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike traces the meddling directly to Sarilus Foulborne, a Forsaken conjurer practicing his arts just across the border. For the Sentinels guarding Silverwind Refuge, letting an enemy sorcerer defile nature right on their doorstep is intolerable.

Magga. Magga is an orc resident living in the Valley of Trials within Durotar. Stationed near the Den, she serves as a welcoming face for newly arrived Horde adventurers beginning their journey in the valley. The Valley of Trials is the first taste of the world for young orcs and darkspear trolls. Positioned near the Den, Magga greets new arrivals to the valley. While she keeps a low profile among the valley's busy trainers and recruits, she helps bind the small camp together.

Maggot Eye's Paw. Maggot Eye's Paw is the gruesome trophy taken from the gnoll chieftain Maggot Eye at Garren's Haunt. Carried back to Brill, it serves as physical proof of the beast's execution for grave-robbing on behalf of the Scourge. Maggot Eye earned the harsh wrath of the Forsaken by raiding graves and pillaging the countryside near Garren's Haunt, providing corpses to bolster the ranks of the Lich King's armies. In response, a formal death sentence and bounty were posted in the town of Brill. Because mere rumors of a death are never enough for military administrators like Executor Zygand, bounty hunters must sever the villain's paw and bring it back to town to collect their reward and close the bounty.

Maggran Earthbinder. Maggran Earthbinder is a grizzled tauren veteran appointed by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to lead the Horde encampment at Sun Rock Retreat. Hardened by a lifetime of brutal conflict, he oversees the defense of the craggy valleys of Stonetalon against ravenous beasts and aggressive harpy covens. Though wearied by countless battles, he remains a steadfast guardian of the settlement. Maggran Earthbinder was sent into the Stonetalon Mountains by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof himself. A veteran of countless skirmishes and bloody campaigns, Maggran admits that age and violence have hardened his heart, stripping away the natural gentleness typical of his people. Sun Rock Retreat was meant to be both an outpost under his steady command and a place of respite, where warm winds and mountain sunshine might soothe his battle-worn spirit.

name.esES: Dorso de la carta de Maggran

text.enUS: Maggran's Reserve Letter. Maggran's Reserve Letter is an official dispatch written by Maggran Earthbinder at Sun Rock Retreat. Carried across Kalimdor to the Great Lift, it grants a stationed sentry long-awaited relief so he may return home to visit his family. Maintaining outposts across the rugged expanse of Kalimdor demands vigilance, but the leaders of the Horde recognize that prolonged watch duty takes a heavy toll on morale. Penned by Maggran Earthbinder in the high crags of Sun Rock Retreat, this simple missive serves as official orders notifying Grish Longrunner that a replacement warrior has been dispatched to take over his post at the Great Lift. For a lonely guard watching over the towering wooden winches far to the south, the letter promises something rare in troubled times: an honorable leave of absence to reunite with family.

Magic Quarter. The Magic Quarter is the northeastern district of the Undercity, serving as the center for Forsaken arcane study and dark spellcraft. Dominated by an ominous Temple of the Damned, the quarter houses practitioners of both the arcane and fel arts. Occupying the northeastern quadrant of the subterranean city, the Magic Quarter is where the Forsaken preserve their arcane heritage and delve into darker methodologies. The centerpiece of the district is a looming Temple of the Damned, an architectural relic of Scourge design that has been repurposed by the free-willed undead. Beneath its vaulted, shadowy ceilings, mages practice subtle manipulations of magical energies alongside warlocks communing with demonic entities, making the quarter the nexus of intellectual power and occult research in Lordaeron.

Magical Analysis. Baron Revilgaz directs you northward from Booty Bay to consult the Kirin Tor in Dalaran. Taking a bag of water elemental bracers, you seek out Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver to decipher the arcane curse tied to the Stone of the Tides. Following your hunt for the water elemental bracers, Baron Revilgaz hands over a bundle of their bracers. The goblin leader knows that unraveling the curse behind the Stone of the Tides requires deeper magical expertise than Booty Bay can provide. He directs you north toward the ruins of Dalaran, where the wizards remain deeply engaged in rebuilding their broken kingdom. Convinced that arcane scholars cannot ignore an intriguing puzzle, Revilgaz recommends seeking Archmage Ansirem Runeweaver directly, having had dealings with the knowledgeable wizard in the past.

Magis Sparkmantle. Magis Sparkmantle is a gnome mage trainer stationed inside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. He offers guidance and training to fledgling spellcasters who venture out from Coldridge Valley into the heart of Dun Morogh. While dwarves gather in the Thunderbrew Distillery for hearty ales, Magis Sparkmantle provides an arcane presence among the casks and kegs of Kharanos. Gnome mages often integrate closely with their dwarven allies across Dun Morogh, and Sparkmantle serves as a key mentor for novice spellcasters ready to expand their theoretical and practical grasp of the arcane arts.

Magistrate Henry Maleb. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees civic administration in the port town of Southshore, the Alliance's primary coastal bastion in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tasked with maintaining order amid constant threats, he focuses much of his authority on hunting down the Syndicate conspirators targeting the town's leadership. Operating from the town hall in Southshore, Magistrate Henry Maleb handles civil governance for one of the last true Alliance settlements in Lordaeron. The town sits under constant siege from the Forsaken to the north and West, while ruthless highwaymen prowl the foothills. Maleb stepped into his current station after the mysterious assassination of the prior magistrate, an act he attributes directly to the Syndicate. Determined not to suffer the same fate, he coordinates active investigations to root out hidden assassins, dismantle Syndicate supply networks, and unmask the rogue nobles pulling the strings from the ruins of Alterac.

Magistrate Sevren. Magistrate Sevren is the chief administrative official presiding over the settlement of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Standing inside the town hall, he organizes early Forsaken defense and directs arriving champions to stabilize the territory around the Undercity. Operating from the town hall in Brill, Magistrate Sevren coordinates civil authority and strategic efforts in the lands just north of the Undercity. As new Forsaken step forth into Tirisfal Glades, Sevren assesses local crises and dispatches adventurers to restore order, secure ruined infrastructure, and suppress persistent threats lingering in the surrounding hills.

Magistrate Solomon. Magistrate Solomon is the chief magistrate of Lakeshire, presiding over local affairs from the town hall. Besieged by Blackrock orcs and relentless gnoll clans, he spends his days frantically pleading for military aid from an indifferent and distracted Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon governs Lakeshire during the darkest hour in its recent history. The tranquil lakeside settlement is surrounded by hostility: Redridge and Shadowhide gnolls prowl the surrounding hills, while Blackrock orcs descend from the north in organized warbands. Solomon works alongside Marshal Marris to maintain civil order and muster a defense, but Lakeshire's local guards and militia are stretched to their absolute breaking point.

Magni Bronzebeard. Magni Bronzebeard is the Lord of Ironforge, Thane of the Bronzebeard clan, and ruler of Khaz Modan. A veteran commander of the Second War, he leads his mountainous kingdom through grief and political tension while championing dwarven archaeology across Azeroth. The eldest of three brothers, Magni grew up keenly aware of the weight awaiting him under the mountain. When the Horde invaded during the Second War, he held Ironforge behind its impenetrable gates, emerging to pledge Khaz Modan to the Alliance of Lordaeron once the siege was broken. In the years of peace that followed, Magni welcomed his gnomish allies into the city after the fall of Gnomeregan, granting High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his refugees sanctuary within the mountain. To unite the fractured southern and northern kingdoms, Magni petitioned Mekkatorque to engineer an unprecedented subterranean marvel: the Deeprun Tram, connecting Ironforge directly to Stormwind.

Magram Alliance. Gurda Wildmane proposes turning the centaur clans' hatred against them: befriend one clan and use it to learn how all of them can be beaten. Siding with the Magram means slaying their enemies the Gelkis, then speaking with the Magram spokesman Warug at the edge of Magram Village, in the southeast of Desolace. Gurda Wildmane's plan is to exploit the centaurs' hatred of each other. A single clan is chosen as ally, and what it teaches shows how to defeat every clan. Choose the Magram and you cut down the Gelkis, their foes, which wins you respect among the Magram.

Magram Village. Magram Village is the settlement of the Magram centaur clan, situated among foul yellow pools in southeastern Desolace. It serves as the primary base for the Magram as they wage relentless war against their hated rivals, the Gelkis. Sprawled across islands and shores around stagnant, sulfurous pools in southeast Desolace, Magram Village is a rugged settlement cobbled together with crude wooden bridges and hide tents. The Magram centaur dwell here in constant vigilance against neighboring clans. Known for their sheer brutality and deep-seated animosity toward the southern Gelkis clan, the Magram are willing to tolerate outsiders only if those travelers prove their worth by slaughtering their Gelkis enemies.

Magus Rimtori. Magus Rimtori is a rogue blood elf sorceress leading an expedition among the ancient ruins of Azshara. Known for her ruthless deception, she manipulated the Horde into securing her passage across Kalimdor before butchering her orcish escort. Magus Rimtori led an expedition of high-borne blood elves across the sea to the ancient shores of Azshara. To ensure her party survived the perils of Kalimdor, she manipulated the orc Belgrom, charming and playing him until he agreed to supply an armed escort. Once the soldiers had delivered her safely to her destination, Rimtori revealed her true colors, turning on her protectors and massacring the entire garrison. Establishing her forces at the Thalassian Base Camp, she ventured out into the coastal wilds accompanied by elite bodyguards to hunt for forgotten magical artifacts.

Magus Tirth. Magus Tirth is an eccentric human wizard dwelling out on the salt flats of the Mirage Raceway in Thousand Needles. Known locally for breeding chickens and tormenting his polymorphed apprentice, he is also a scholar of formidable arcane lore who has squandered valuable tomes on racing bets. While most mages of his caliber study in the libraries of Dalaran or Stormwind, Magus Tirth has taken up residence amid the grease and roar of the Shimmering Flats. Surrounded by speeding rocket cars, Tirth peddles chickens to passersby, drinks, gambles, and has long since cursed his unfortunate apprentice, 'Plucky' Johnson, into poultry form. Despite this eccentric demeanor, Tirth possesses genuine arcane mastery, having authored esoteric texts on magical power before losing them to reckless wagers on the speedway.

Mahren Skyseer. Mahren Skyseer is a Horde journey that directs proven hunters from Camp Taurajo out toward the eastern shores of the Barrens. After mastering the plains' predators, adventurers are sent by Jorn Skyseer to learn coastal tracking from his sister. Finding her requires braving the waters and human encampments dotting the Merchant Coast. Through the trials set by Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, hunters prove their tenacity against the most dangerous beasts stalking the red plains of the southern Barrens. Yet Jorn teaches that a true predator never limits themselves to dry earth and rolling savannas. To truly master the craft, a tracker must be ready to stalk prey through swamps, sheer crags, and the crashing waves of the Great Sea.

Mai'Zoth. Brother Nimetz believes Colonel Kurzen was driven to evil by a hidden power that still lives. An ogre mage known as Mai'Zoth lurks within the eastern mountains, wielding an artifact reputed to twist and control minds. Destroying him and recovering this relic is meant to ensure no other commander suffers the same corruption. Though Kurzen has fallen, Brother Nimetz insists the primary catalyst behind the rebellion remains intact. His research points to Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage dwelling inside an ogre mound deep within the eastern heights of Stranglethorn Vale. Nimetz is certain that Mai'Zoth employed mind-altering sorcery to warp Kurzen's thoughts, warning that leaving the ogre alive invites another commander to succumb to the very same sinister influence.

Mai'ah. Mai'ah is a jungle troll mage trainer stationed within the sun-scorched basin of the Valley of Trials in Durotar. She mentors fledgling spellcasters among the Darkspear trolls who step into the red canyons to hone their command of the arcane. For young trolls beginning the path of wizardry, she offers early guidance and instruction in the foundational arts of magic. While orcs overwhelmingly favor the primal call of the elements or the physical dominance of the warrior, Darkspear trolls possess a rare affinity for arcane study. Standing within the Valley of Trials, Mai'ah serves as an instructor for young troll mages arriving to undertake their rites of adulthood. She receives candidates carrying glyphic inscriptions and begins shaping their chaotic raw power into disciplined incantations, ensuring they learn the control required to survive Durotar's perils.

Main Hall (Northshire). Newcomers report in the Main Hall at Northshire Abbey in western Elwynn. From there, they reach the Hall of Arms, the Library Wing, and the abbey tower, then receive their first assignments defending Stormwind. Trainees and clerics pass through the Main Hall after entering Northshire Abbey. The chamber links the Hall of Arms, where recruits prepare for battle, with the Library Wing and the stairs to the abbey tower. Strife in the valley reaches even this quiet place, and officers rally able newcomers to defend the kingdom's borders.

Major Mattingly. At Stormwind’s main gates, Major Mattingly helps guard the capital and advises crafters on protection from dragons. Major Mattingly is a high-ranking officer responsible for Stormwind City's landward defense. He stands watch in the Valley of Heroes under General Marcus Jonathan, alongside the city's garrison. His duties include overseeing gate patrols and travelers entering the city. Mattingly also knows the lethal nature of dragons and guides skilled crafters who seek to make protective dragonscale gear for facing dangerous lairs.

Major Samuelson. In Stormwind Keep, Major Samuelson commands the city guard and its personnel. The high-ranking veteran officer serves in the throne room and once mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle. Before Stormwind's royal court, Major Samuelson leads the Stormwind City Guard. He oversees officer postings and military orders across the realm. He mentored Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, who serves at Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. When junior commanders struggle or seek transfer from distant frontier garrisons, their requests and official reports travel across the kingdom to Samuelson's desk in the capital.

Makaba Flathoof. Makaba Flathoof is a tauren survivor hailing from Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains. Having witnessed the devastation of his home and people at the hands of the Grimtotem clan, he seeks brave champions of the Horde to bring vengeance upon the attackers and ensure his family's safety. Makaba Flathoof represents the tragic toll of internal strife among the tauren. His home, Camp Aparaje in the Stonetalon Mountains, fell victim to a ruthless surprise attack by the Grimtotem clan. While many tauren strive for peace and unity under the leadership of Cairne Bloodhoof, the treacherous Grimtotem continually sow discord and violence, leaving survivors like Makaba displaced and grieving.

Make Yourself Useful. Make Yourself Useful is an assignment at Windfield Orchard where adventurers help secure the stormapple crop against undisciplined bandits. An extortionist named Ferauu is due to collect his regular share of the harvest, but hungry outlaws have broken ranks to pilfer the trees ahead of time. Dealing with these rogue thieves earns the respect of the watchful orchard keeper. At Windfield Orchard, farming is complicated by extortion. A bandit leader named Ferauu and his crew have established an arrangement to collect their regular cut of the fruit harvest. However, lack of discipline within the bandit ranks means that petty outlaws cannot always wait for their boss's scheduled visit, sneaking in early to pick over the trees.

Maker's Terrace. The Maker's Terrace is a sprawling outdoor excavation site situated in the northern Badlands, directly fronting the entrance to the ancient titan vault of Uldaman. Travelers venturing south from Loch Modan must navigate its rugged perimeter, which is aggressively occupied by Dark Iron dwarves. The dig represents a contested threshold between the surface wastes and the titan mysteries entombed below. Sprawling across the northern bluffs of the Badlands, the Maker's Terrace serves as the exterior staging ground for the subterranean halls of Uldaman. Long before travelers delve into the subterranean ruins, they must contend with the sun-scorched earthworks, scaffolding, and stone trenches of this grand excavation. It sits right along the pass coming down from Loch Modan, making it the first landmark greeting any traveler daring to venture into the arid wastes. The Terrace buzzes with violent industry as rival factions seek a way into the ancient secrets buried beneath the rock.

Malaka'jin. Malaka'jin is a small Horde encampment nestled in the lower hills of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of the Grimtotem Post. Inhabited primarily by Darkspear troll hunters, the settlement serves as a rustic waystation and hunting outpost for travelers ascending into the rugged peaks from the Barrens. Tucked away near the main path into the Stonetalon Mountains, Malaka'jin provides a welcome sanctuary for Horde wanderers venturing into contested heights. The village is home to a band of rugged troll hunters who eke out a living off the crags and scrublands. While living modestly, these hunters offer supplies, trade their fresh game to weary adventurers, and keep a wary eye on the hostile mountain wildlife and the belligerent Grimtotem tauren lurking further up the trails.

Malden's Orchard. Malden's Orchard is a ruined farmstead in northern Silverpine Forest, named after the human owner who fled during the Scourge invasion of Lordaeron. Long abandoned, its dark evergreen trees sit overgrown while vicious black worgs stalk the grounds. The orchard's crumbling cottage served as a temporary refuge for a stranded Forsaken scout cut off from his unit. Before the Third War, this homestead supplied fresh fruit to the towns of Lordaeron, tended by a farmer named Malden. When the Scourge tore through the kingdom, Malden abandoned his land to flee the plague. In the years since, the orchard has choked under the dark, encroaching mists of Silverpine Forest. The evergreen trees remain unpruned and their fruit rots ungathered on blighted boughs, leaving the plot entirely reclaimed by wild predators.

Malfurion Stormrage. Malfurion Stormrage is the first mortal druid and the revered leader of the night elves alongside High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind. Renowned for defeating the Burning Legion in both the War of the Ancients and the Third War, he is venerated as the Shan'do, or honored teacher. Currently, he lies trapped in a comatose slumber within the Emerald Dream, leaving the kaldorei without his waking guidance. Ten thousand years ago, before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, Malfurion studied under the demigod Cenarius. While Queen Azshara and her Highborne caste delved dangerously into the arcane energies of the Well of Eternity, Malfurion turned toward the primal forces of nature, becoming Azeroth's first mortal druid. His suspicions regarding the Highborne proved tragically correct when Azshara's reckless sorcery pierced the veil and summoned Sargeras and the Burning Legion into Azeroth, igniting the catastrophic War of the Ancients.

Malin's Request. In Stormwind, Malin asks for help recovering relics from fallen Stromgarde. Archmage Malin sends seasoned Alliance adventurers north to Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands, where an expedition seeks the magical relics left behind when Stromgarde fell. Archmage Malin serves in Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum and acts for his former mentor, Archmage Trelane. When Stromgarde fell into chaos, Trelane made a desperate stand at the Tower of Arathor. As hostile forces took the city, he had to abandon his post and leave powerful enchanted possessions behind. Malin fears those relics may fall into hostile hands. He sends capable mercenaries north to strengthen his agents in the field and reclaim Trelane's lost belongings.

Malin's Request. Skuerto gives you a sealed letter for Archmage Malin, who is found in Stormwind's Mage Quarter. It tells Malin that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon, and Skuerto is certain Malin will repay you well for helping them in Arathi. After the work in Arathi, Skuerto hands you a letter to take back to Stormwind. Its message for Archmage Malin in the Mage Quarter is that Kryten and Skuerto will be home soon. Skuerto has no doubt that Malin will repay you well for helping them, and sends you off with a wish for a safe journey.

Manaweave Robe. In Stormwind, Wynne Larson presents the Manaweave Robe as a proud showcase for her family’s shop. She has woven the enchanted garment from fine materials for a commission that is now complete. Larson Clothiers serves spellcasters in Stormwind’s Mage Quarter with garments made to channel volatile energies. Fine magical robes call for rare materials, careful needlework, and threadwork that holds through mystic resonance. Wynne Larson takes pride in each piece that leaves her shop, where every robe worn into the field carries the Larson name.

Mangletooth. Mangletooth is an imprisoned Razormane quilboar held captive by the Horde inside Camp Taurajo. Facing execution, he trades strategic information about his rivals and the ancient lore of Agamaggan to adventurers willing to do his bidding. Held in a cage at Camp Taurajo by tauren hunters and orc sentries, Mangletooth is a captured Razormane quilboar awaiting execution. Rather than resigning to death, he attempts to manipulate his captors and visiting Horde adventurers into striking down the enemies of his tribe, hoping his cunning will prove his worth or secure his rescue.

Mangy Claw. The Mangy Claw is a severed claw taken from the great ice claw bear Mangeclaw in Dun Morogh. It serves as grim proof that the deadly beast responsible for killing a stranded dwarven pilot has finally been slain. When Pilot Hildelve's steam tank broke down in the frozen hills of Dun Morogh, he continued his search for ore on foot, only to face the mountain wilderness alone. As recorded in his recovered journal, Hildelve managed to fight off an initial attack by a monstrous ice claw bear named Mangeclaw, though he was savagely mauled in the struggle. The beast later returned to finish off the weakened pilot. Hildelve's final written entry pleaded for vengeance against the predator, a task fulfilled by taking the Mangy Claw from the fallen bear.

Manhunt. Marshal Dughan sends you after a Defias bagman called the Collector in Elwynn Forest. The Collector works from the overrun Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and sends stolen gold from the forest's mines into the Brotherhood's coffers. Marshal Dughan sends you to Brackwell Pumpkin Patch after Elwynn's gnolls are found carrying a schedule for gold pickups. Defias bandits and gnolls have taken over the once quiet homestead. The Collector hides among its overgrown vines, skimming ore from the kingdom's mines and arranging shipments for the growing rebellion.

Mankrik. Mankrik is a grief-stricken orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads in the Barrens. After a vicious quilboar ambush separated him from his wife, Olgra, he has dedicated his life to avenging her and cutting down every bristled beast he can find. While traveling through the scrublands of the Barrens, Mankrik and his wife Olgra were overrun by swarms of quilboar during a skirmish at a small tauren settlement. Separated in the chaos and frantic fighting, Mankrik watched Olgra disappear under a tide of tusks and thorn-woven weapons. Overwhelmed by fury, he fought recklessly until he was struck down unconscious. He survived only because a passing tauren druid discovered him bleeding out along the Gold Road and bound his injuries.

Mannoroc Coven. Mannoroc Coven is a demon-infested ruin in southern Desolace, named after the pit lord Mannoroth. Settled among ancient night elf architecture, it stands as the largest stronghold of the Burning Legion in central Kalimdor. Cultists of the Burning Blade maintain active summoning portals here, filling the ash-choked land with felhounds, succubi, and infernals.

Manor Mistmantle. Manor Mistmantle is a decaying estate nestled in the shadowed hills of northeastern Duskwood, north of Darkshire. Once a proper family homestead, it has fallen into ruin and horror, crawling with undead ghouls bound to its infamous master. Located west of Beggar's Haunt, Manor Mistmantle stands as a grim monument to murder and madness. The grounds are choked with decay and prowled by vicious ghouls who defend the ruined structure. Amidst the rot and withered vegetation, the only sign of living beauty on the entire property is a solitary, sorrowful blossom growing in the untended garden: the flower known as the Tear of Tilloa.

Maps and Runes. Maps and Runes is a Forsaken reconnaissance mission in Silverpine Forest. After discovering a suspicious shipment shipped toward Ambermill, adventurers recover a rune-inscribed pendant to deliver to Shadow Priest Allister at the Sepulcher for further investigation. While intercepting logistics around Ambermill, Horde agents uncover a Dalaran crate concealed along the border routes. Rather than mundane supplies, the container holds detailed regional charts and an enigmatic, rune-inscribed pendant. Recognizing the potential danger of Dalaran's arcane reach so close to their borders, scouts carefully retrieve the artifact to avoid alarming the surrounding human sentries.

Marcus Redpath. Marshal Marcus Redpath is the senior military authority defending the Alliance town of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. He organizes patrols and bounty contracts to hold off surrounding ogres, murlocs, and naga. His leadership is essential to maintaining Lordaeron's last southern bastion on the coast. Marcus Redpath is the marshal of Southshore, the Alliance port on the southern coast of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Southshore endured the fall of Lordaeron's capital and the devastating Scourge invasion, and Redpath now stands at the head of its defense, guarding the port's beleaguered survivors.

Mardant Strongoak. Mardant Strongoak is a night elf druid trainer residing in Aldrassil in the heart of Teldrassil. He guides fledgling druids in communing with the spirits of nature and introduces them to the mysteries of the Emerald Dream. Within the boughs of Aldrassil, young night elves who feel the call of the wild turn to Mardant Strongoak. His primary task is teaching novitiates how to open their senses to nature spirits, interpret their murmurs, and channel rejuvenating magics. For those taking their initial steps as protectors of the wild, he is often the first master to unveil the vast complexities and ancient perils of the Emerald Dream.

Mardenholde Keep. Mardenholde Keep is the imposing stone citadel overlooking Hearthglen in the northern reaches of the Western Plaguelands. Once the ancestral seat of Lord Tirion Fordring, it now serves as the regional command center for the fanatical Scarlet Crusade under the rule of his son, Highlord Taelan Fordring. Built as the administrative heart of the Hearthglen principality, Mardenholde Keep was long celebrated by the people of Lordaeron for having never breached during the Second War. From its council chambers, Lord Tirion Fordring governed the surrounding vales alongside his trusted advisors, maintaining peace until his controversial trial and exile for defending the orc Eitrigg. Following Tirion's fall, governance fell to his ambitious apprentice Barthilas and eventually passed to Tirion's son, Taelan, who inherited his father's domain on the eve of Lordaeron's destruction.

Marek Ironheart. Marek Ironheart is a veteran dwarven hunter stationed at the Farstrider Lodge in south-eastern Loch Modan. Dedicated to the traditions of the wild, he tests wandering travelers and marksmen alike before welcoming them into the ranks of the lodge's honored hunters. Perched on the scenic ridge overlooking the lake, the Farstrider Lodge serves as an outpost for the finest marksmen and trackers in the dwarven lands. Marek Ironheart embodies this frontier spirit. Unimpressed by titles or talk, Marek requires anyone seeking the lodge's respect to demonstrate their practical prowess against the varied beasts roaming Loch Modan, proving they have the patience and nerve demanded of a true stalker of the wild.

Marg Speaks. From beyond death, Marg tells of the muckshell that killed Marg and of a duty still undone. Marg asks you to find that muckshell, recover the jeweled pendant stolen from Alliance soldiers and carry it to Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village. Near Theramore, Marg spotted Alliance soldiers camped on the beach. One of them wore a pendant studded with more gems than a soldier could ever pay for. That night Marg snuck into the camp and stole it, but a muckshell crab-man killed Marg on the way back to base. Now Marg asks you to find that muckshell, recover the pendant and bring it to Nazeer in Brackenwall Village.

Margoz. Margoz is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with seeking out an isolated orc shaman who watches over the northern reaches of Durotar. Following the confrontation with fel corruption in the canyon, Orgnil Soulscar directs champions to consult Margoz before assaulting a nearby cultist stronghold. The wise hermit provides crucial counsel regarding the growing shadow cast by the Burning Blade. After discovering the depths of fel taint at Thunder Ridge, Orgnil Soulscar recognizes that brute strength alone will not suffice to cleanse Durotar. He directs his champions toward Margoz, an experienced orc shaman who keeps a lonely camp in the crags northeast of Razor Hill. Positioned between the jagged heights of Drygulch Ravine and the eastern sea, Margoz keeps watch over dark omens that the bustling warriors of Orgrimmar often overlook.

Marisa du'Paige. In the caves outside the Deadmines, Marisa du'Paige fights beside Moonbrook's outlaws. Rare among their laborers and highwaymen, she uses arcane magic in the tunnels of southwestern Westfall. Deep in the caves leading toward the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, cutpurses, renegade miners, and thugs guard the tunnels. Marisa du'Paige is a skilled human mage among them. Many spellcasters train in Stormwind's Mage Quarter or serve the Kirin Tor, but Marisa has joined the outlaws and brigands in Westfall's underground passages.

Marla's Last Wish. Marla's Last Wish is an early Forsaken task given by Novice Elreth in Deathknell. It asks you to hunt down the Scourge-enslaved remnants of Samuel Fipps so he can be buried beside his murdered wife, Marla. The task reflects the fledgling Forsaken society's yearning to honor human ties and distinguish themselves from the mindless Scourge. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Marla and Samuel Fipps lived together as husband and wife. When the plague swept through their lands, Samuel succumbed to the contagion and was reanimated as a mindless thrall of the Scourge. Though Marla was spared undeath, she could not escape Samuel himself, who brutally slew her in his mindless frenzy. Despite dying at her husband's hands, Marla harbored no hatred in her final moments. Her dying wish, remembered by Novice Elreth, was to rest eternally beside her husband in the Deathknell graveyard.

Marleth Barleybrew. Marleth Barleybrew is an ambitious dwarven brewer stationed out in Brewnall Village. Frustrated by the Thunderbrew clan's dominance over the local beer market, she constantly schemes to prove her family's brew is superior to Kharanos's famous Thunder Ale. In Dun Morogh, alcohol is taken as seriously as steel, and the rivalry between the Barleybrew and Thunderbrew families is legendary. Marleth Barleybrew resents the near-monopoly that Ragnar Thunderbrew and his kin maintain out of the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Convinced her own craft is every bit as robust, she seeks clever ways to slip Barleybrew kegs into the hands of tavern patrons. Rather than engaging in open conflict, she opts for petty subterfuge, recruiting passing travelers to secretly swap out Kharanos's prized ale casks with her own.

Marris Stead. Perched on a ridge in the southwestern Eastern Plaguelands, the Marris Stead was once a peaceful Lordaeron homestead. Following the devastation of the Third War, it now serves as the lonely, heavily defended redoubt of Nathanos Blightcaller, Champion of the Forsaken.

Marryk Nurribit. Marryk Nurribit is the resident gnome mage trainer stationed at Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A bit more fond of local brews than disciplined pedagogy, he introduces fledgling gnomish arcanists to their craft while frequently soliciting spare coins for a drink. Tucked away inside the warm hearth of Anvilmar, Marryk Nurribit offers arcane guidance to young gnomes taking their very first steps into magic. Though knowledgeable in the arcane arts, his demeanor is decidedly casual—often seeming far more interested in nursing a flagon of dwarven ale and bumming spare pocket change off his new pupils than drilling them in complex theorems. Despite his vices, Marryk remains acutely aware of the perils outside Coldridge Valley, regularly warning aspiring spellcasters about the lingering radioactive and trogg-infested horrors of fallen Gnomeregan.

Marshal Dughan. Goldshire's marshal faces threats on every road and mine. Marshal Dughan commands the Stormwind Army detachment there, but kobolds, gnolls, and bandits stretch his small garrison. He depends on independent adventurers to help protect the town and nearby farms. Marshal Dughan directs Elwynn Forest's defense from Goldshire, outside the Lion's Pride Inn. Stormwind's soldiers are tied up elsewhere, while trouble grows in the woods. Kobolds crowd the mines, gnolls gather along the riverbanks, and highwaymen harass travelers on the King's Road. With too few footmen under his command, Dughan sends new recruits to reinforce outposts and scout dangerous ground.

Marshal Haggard. At Eastvale, Marshal Haggard keeps the arms he gathered over a lifetime of service. Harry Burlguard sends novice warriors from Stormwind City to meet the retired marshal and seek better weapons. Stormwind's novice warriors need more than skill to face danger beyond the city. Harry Burlguard sends promising fighters east through Elwynn Forest to find Marshal Haggard, a retired officer who served the realm for years. Haggard gathered a personal armory over a lifetime in the field, and his home near the Eastvale Logging Camp holds weapons for young warriors seeking better arms.

Marshal Haggard's Badge. At his farm in Elwynn, Marshal Haggard has lost the badge he carried in Stormwind's service. Dead-tooth Jack stole it by trickery, and the Defias may use it to impersonate city officials. Marshal Haggard retired to a small farmstead in the hills of Elwynn Forest, but his old Stormwind Marshal's badge still carries official weight. One night, Dead-tooth Jack, a Defias rogue, wore a Stormwind tabard and posed as Marshal Dughan, Goldshire's garrison commander. He tricked Haggard into believing his former peers needed the insignia for official business. The aging marshal handed it over without suspicion. Jack fled into the woods before Haggard saw through the ruse. In Defias hands, the emblem of Stormwind authority could let outlaws pass checkpoints or confuse local patrols.

Marshal Marris. Marshal Marris is the beleaguered military officer commanding the town watch at Lakeshire. Stationed near the town's bridge, he coordinates defense operations against the massive Blackrock orc invasion pressing down from the heights of the Redridge Mountains. With Stormwind's army absent, he relies on visiting adventurers to blunt the horde's advances. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse, caught between the gnolls to the west and the terrifying military might of the Blackrock clan to the east. Marshal Marris oversees the guard line at the town's primary bridge, but his resources are depleted and his soldiers are spread impossibly thin. With the kingdom of Stormwind withholding royal reinforcements, Marris carries the heavy burden of keeping the township from being overwhelmed by brute force.

Marshal Maxwell. Marshal Maxwell is a high-ranking officer of the Stormwind army stationed at Morgan's Vigil in the Burning Steppes. Tasked with holding the Alliance's northernmost fortified ridge above the Redridge Mountains against the Blackrock clan and the Dark Iron dwarves, he directs scouting missions into the hostile crags below. He also plays a crucial role in coordinating efforts to discover the fate of his captured comrade, Marshal Reginald Windsor. Morgan's Vigil stands as a precarious outpost on the southern rim of the Burning Steppes, overlooking a wasteland choked with ash, dragonkin, and Blackrock orcs. Marshal Maxwell commands the Stormwind military detachment stationed here, providing a rare friendly sight for travelers braving the fiery crags. From this rocky bastion, he oversees defensive maneuvers to keep the hostile forces of the mountain contained before they can sweep southward into Redridge and Elwynn.

Marshal McBride. At Northshire Abbey, Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison and defends the valley. Kobolds threaten its farms and mines, so he directs new recruits against them. Marshal McBride commands Stormwind's garrison outside Northshire Abbey. The abbey is a place of faith and learning, while unrest across the kingdom has left military garrisons short of soldiers. With only a handful of sworn guards, McBride must keep the valley peaceful and protect its food and resources. Green recruits arrive seeking training from the abbey's masters, and he must put them to work.

Marshal's Refuge. Marshal's Refuge is a precarious, neutral haven tucked into the northern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Established by Williden Marshal and his expedition party, it serves as an emergency redoubt after the basin's primeval beasts routed their lower camps. When Williden and Hol'anyee Marshal led their expedition into Un'Goro Crater, they drastically underestimated the ferocity of its prehistoric denizens. After their initial base camps were repeatedly overrun by rampaging beasts, the battered survivors scrambled up into the cavernous northern cliffside to escape slaughter. Re-established as Marshal's Refuge, the camp clings high above the jungle floor, offering the only stable resting ground, basic supplies, and flight masters for weary explorers in the northern crater.

Marshlands. The Marshlands is a sprawling, sodden marsh occupying the southeastern reach of Un'Goro Crater. Sitting directly at the base of the winding ramp down from Tanaris, it is often the first wilderness newcomers witness upon entering the primeval basin. Descending the steep trail from the arid expanse of Tanaris brings travelers directly into the humid mire of the Marshlands. Navigating anywhere else along the sheer crater rim invites a lethal fall, making this treacherous swath of wetlands the primary threshold into Un'Goro. Dense canopies, standing water, and mud conceal abundant packs of fierce raptors, including venomous varieties that stalk the reeds. Amid the damp clearings, explorers can find Blue Power Crystals scattered across the earth, unique to this quarter of the crater.

Martek the Exiled. Fizzle Brassbolts is building a new engine for his car, but he cannot make pistons hard enough to take the strain. He sends you with a letter to a great smith named Martek the Exiled, far off in a camp in the Badlands. After Salt Flat Venom, Fizzle at the Mirage Raceway explains that his new engine should make the car so fast it could fly. All his trials have failed because he cannot make pistons hard enough for the heavy stress. He knows one person who might know how: Martek the Exiled, a great smith who knows more about metal than anyone. Martek is a long way off in the Badlands, camped there with a goblin, and you carry Fizzle's letter to him.

Martie Jainrose. Martie Jainrose is Lakeshire's local herbalist, tending to her garden along the edge of Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Beside cultivating remedies and flowers for the beleaguered town, she contends with wild beasts trampling her plots and harbors a quiet affection for Guard Parker. Residing in Lakeshire, Martie Jainrose works diligently as the settlement's resident herbalist. Even as Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and local brigands threaten the region, Martie focuses on keeping the town supplied with fresh herbs and floral arrangements. Her daily labors are often disrupted by local wildlife—most notably the monstrous boar Bellygrub, who frequently ravages her prized garden beds. Beyond her herbal pursuits, Martie seems to hold a fondness for Guard Parker, though Parker is courting Darcy, who calls Martie a jealous rival.

Marukai. Marukai is a Darkspear jungle troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the foggy coast of northwest Ashenvale. Dedicated to holding this remote beachhead for the Horde, she coordinates efforts to cull the encroaching Wrathtail naga who threaten the outpost. Zoram'gar Outpost sits isolated on the northern edge of the Zoram Strand, surrounded by ancient ruins, hostile night elf territory, and the restless sea. As the Wrathtail naga emerge in force from the waters and ancient elven ruins to claim the shoreline, Marukai works to keep the encampment from being overwhelmed. She directs Horde champions to push the serpent-folk back into the tide and collect their heads, ensuring the outpost remains a viable coastal stronghold.

Mary's Looking Glass. Mary's Looking Glass is a discarded hand mirror once treasured by Blind Mary before tragedy claimed her sight and life. Abandoned in the haunted groves of Duskwood, it was scavenged by a roving ghoul before being sought out to complete Viktori Prism'Antras's telescope. Before her terrible fate, Blind Mary treasured this polished looking glass. After her death and the loss of her eyes, looking upon her reflection became an agonizing reminder of what she had lost. She cast the mirror away behind her barn, leaving it to the encroaching gloom of Duskwood. There it fell into the clutching claws of an Insane Ghoul that wandered the ruined outskirts, carrying the trinket south into the crypts of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery.

Mast Room. The Mast Room is a cavernous subterranean lumber mill nestled deep within the Deadmines. Overseen by the goblin taskmaster Sneed and his woodcarvers, this chamber processes timber stripped from Westfall to construct Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut.

Master Apothecary Faranell. Master Apothecary Faranell is the head of the Royal Apothecary Society, stationed within the depths of the Apothecarium in the Undercity. In life a respected Dalaran scholar, in undeath he directs the Forsaken's search for a devastating New Plague to eradicate both the Scourge and the living. Before the Third War, Faranell was an esteemed alchemist who spent decades studying alongside the learned mages of Dalaran. He spent his mortal days seeking cures, remedies, and potions to improve mortal health. When the Scourge plague claimed his life and he arose as a free-willed Forsaken, his former scientific curiosity curdled into cruelty. Retaining his encyclopedic intellect, he traded healing salves for catastrophic reagents, quickly becoming one of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner's most valued researchers in the bowels of Lordaeron's fallen capital.

Master Gadrin. Master Gadrin is an elderly jungle troll and a venerable witch doctor of the Darkspear tribe, currently residing in Sen'jin Village. Having once trained the tribe's priests and mages alongside the renegade witch doctor Zalazane, he now coordinates efforts to aid his displaced people and break the dark curse gripping their stolen home on the Echo Isles. Long before the Darkspear arrived on Kalimdor, Master Gadrin served as a witch doctor of his tribe in their ancestral South Seas islands, where he guided the mystical training of generations of Darkspear trolls.

Master Vornal. Master Vornal is an elderly Darkspear jungle troll who resides in Sen'jin Village along the southern coast of Durotar. Despite his advancing years and extensive knowledge of alchemical concoctions, he stubbornly refuses to take on any apprentices. Master Vornal is a fixture of Sen'jin Village, known for brewing potent draughts and spirits for his fellow Darkspear trolls. Though age is visibly catching up with him, Vornal remains intensely independent and stubbornly refuses to train any apprentices, preferring to mix his remedies and volatile mixtures entirely by his own hand.

Master's Cellar. The Master's Cellar is a sprawling subterranean complex situated beneath the ruined settlement south of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass.
