Once serving Medivh's estate as wine cellars and storage vaults, it has descended into a haunted ruin teeming with the restless spectres of former servants and caretakers. Just south of the imposing tower of Karazhan lie the ruined remnants of a hamlet that once housed the servants, groundskeepers, and attendants who maintained Medivh's estate. Beneath these crumbled homes sits the Master's Cellar. Accessible through two separate entrances in the surface ruins, the complex expands far underground. One doorway opens into an extensive vaulted wine cellar, while the other descends through collapsed stonework into deep natural caverns. Whatever dark demise befell Karazhan and its master swallowed this basement as well, leaving the unliving remnants of caretakers, wailing spectres, and damned souls trapped in endless servitude.

Master's Glaive. The Master's Glaive is an ancient, unsettling landmark tucked into southwestern Darkshore where a colossal adamantine weapon stands impaled in a massive petrified skull. Long revered by local night elves as a sacred mystery, the site now swarms with Twilight's Hammer cultists drawn to the lingering malevolence of an ancient entity. Rising out of the Darkshore earth, the Master's Glaive is a massive adamantine blade buried deep in a colossal petrified skull. No record names the creature that died here or the hand that drove the blade home. Onu, the Ancient of Lore, says only that an old, old lord of the earth fell on this spot, and the night elves long believed that only the titans could have wielded so gigantic a weapon. Today, the impaled monolith stands as a stark, petrified monument to that forgotten struggle.

Mastok Wrilehiss. Mastok Wrilehiss is an orc officer stationed at Splintertree Post in eastern Ashenvale. Serving as a crucial defensive coordinator for the Horde in the contested forest, he directs scouts and warriors to secure nearby borders and handle corrupting elemental threats. His presence is vital for maintaining the precarious foothold the Horde holds amidst constant night elf hostility. Splintertree Post stands deep in the shadow of Ashenvale's towering canopy, completely surrounded by hostile night elven territory. Mastok Wrilehiss serves as one of the post's core defenders, monitoring supply routes and forest activity. The position is perilous; any sign of weakness invites swift strikes from the Sentinels who view the settlement as a despoiling intrusion.

Mathias Shaw. In Old Town, Mathias Shaw directs SI:7, Stormwind's covert intelligence agency. From the shadows, he sends spies and scouts to guard the realm against conspiracies within and horrors beyond. Mathias Shaw leads Stormwind's spies and assassins from SI:7's hidden headquarters behind the barracks in Old Town. His covert network reaches across the Eastern Kingdoms and beyond. Loyal to the House of Wrynn, Shaw weighs every threat with care. He trusts unseen daggers and stolen messages to defend Stormwind as much as armor and palace guards.

Mathiel. This quest sends an adventurer carrying Furen Longbeard's crafting notes across the seas to Darnassus. The recipient is Mathiel, an artisan smith residing on the Warrior's Terrace eager to study dwarven innovations in mail forging. It represents a vital exchange of martial metallurgy between Ironforge and the kaldorei. After mastering the difficult process of forging fire-hardened armor, the veteran dwarven smith Furen Longbeard resolves to share his breakthroughs with fellow Alliance craftsmen. Instead of hoarding his newfound metallurgy, Furen copies down detailed technical diagrams and sends his tested adventurer across continents to find Mathiel, an accomplished smith dwelling high in Teldrassil.

Mathiel's Armor. "Mathiel's Armor" marks the completion of an armorsmithing effort undertaken by Mathiel in the Warrior's Terrace of Darnassus. By combining his own night elven craftsmanship with innovative dwarven metalworking methods devised by Furen Longbeard, Mathiel reforges exotic materials into protective battle gear. The quest represents a fruitful blending of allied traditions in service of Alliance warriors. Night elven armorers traditionally favor methods honed over millennia, relying on harmony with nature, supple leathers, or delicately worked metals. However, the exchange between the night elves and the Eastern Kingdoms has prompted master smiths like Mathiel to experiment. By incorporating newly devised techniques from the dwarven armorer Furen Longbeard, Mathiel manages to meld dwarven metallurgy with elven artistry.

Mathredis Firestar. Mathredis Firestar is an eccentric blood elf mage residing at Flame Crest in the Burning Steppes. He crafts powerful enchantments known as Lesser Arcanums, drawing upon the arcane research of his deceased master. In doing so, he feeds on the residual energies unleashed during the binding process to stave off his magic addiction. Mathredis Firestar learned the craft of making arcanums—concentrated gems of arcane empowerment—from his mentor, Telmius Dreamseeker. Telmius met a grim end within the ancient ruins of Dire Maul while trying to wrest magical secrets from the Shen'dralar. While Telmius invented these magical bindings, Mathredis lacks the mastery to produce the greatest of them. Instead, he specializes in Lesser Arcanums. For Mathredis, this work is far more than an academic exercise: like all blood elves following the fall of the Sunwell, he suffers from a gnawing hunger for arcane power. Binding materials to ancient librams releases violent discharges of magical energy, which Mathredis siphons to sustain himself.

Mathrengyl Bearwalker. Mathrengyl Bearwalker is a master druid trainer and respected elder of the Cenarion Circle residing in Darnassus's Cenarion Enclave. Having once served as Archdruid Fandral Staghelm's direct assistant, he guides young Alliance druids through their spiritual trials, shapeshifting rites, and duties across Kalimdor. Perched within the verdant reaches of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus, Mathrengyl Bearwalker stands as one of the most venerable and balanced druids on Teldrassil. He serves as a primary guide for fledgling Alliance druids, overseeing their communion with Moonglade and testing their readiness to master primal animal forms. Having undergone the intense, bewildering communion with the Great Bear Spirit in his own youth, Mathrengyl understands the weight of these rites, personally charging initiates to prove their spirit against the sacred moonkin Lunaclaw before inducting them into the path of the Druid of the Claw.

Mathystra Relic. Mathystra Relics are ancient night elven artifacts scattered among the overgrown ruins of Mathystra in northern Darkshore. Though remnants of a fallen elven bastion, they retain dormant shards of magic that have drawn the interest of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the Great Sundering, Mathystra stood as a proud city and bastion of elven civilization along the Kalimdor coast. Today, its toppled columns and cracked stones sit half-swallowed by brush and sea mist, haunted by restless spirits and lurking beasts. Scattered across the ruins are ancient relics dating back to that golden age. Though worn by ten thousand years of neglect, these artifacts still hold faint traces of elven arcane craft, making them dangerous prizes if left unattended.

Mathystra Relics. This quest sends Alliance adventurers north along the coast of Darkshore to sift through the overgrown Ruins of Mathystra. Onu, an Ancient of Lore rooted in the Grove of the Ancients, seeks these ancient kaldorei artifacts to understand how the Twilight's Hammer cult is manipulating night elven sorcery for their sinister rites. To counteract this dark endeavor, Onu directs heroes to the Ruins of Mathystra, located along the northeastern shores of Darkshore. Long ago, Mathystra was a shining bastion of highborne civilization before it shattered during the Sundering. Though the city has collapsed into rubble, weeds, and naga infestation, powerful remnants of its original arcane and spiritual enchantments linger in shattered urns and ancient relics scattered across the stone foundations.

Maul (subzone). The Maul is a sunken fighting arena situated in the Broken Commons outside the ruins of Dire Maul in Feralas. Formerly a grand venue of ancient elven Eldre'Thalas, the pit is now an uncontrolled bloodsport ring where wanderers fight for glory or survival against fierce beasts and rival champions. Carved deep into the stone of the Broken Commons, the Maul once served the Highborne of Eldre'Thalas as a theater or ceremonial arena. Following the Sundering and the subsequent occupation by the Gordok ogres, the pit devolved into a raw colosseum. Like the notorious Gurubashi Arena in distant Stranglethorn Vale, entering the sands of the Maul suspends all allegiances, casting combatants into a lawless free-for-all where faction lines dissolve and survival depends purely on martial strength.

Maur Grimtotem. Maur Grimtotem was an emissary sent by Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem into the depths of Ragefire Chasm. Dispatched on an ill-fated diplomatic mission to the troggs infesting the subterranean tunnels beneath Orgrimmar, he met a brutal end at their hands. Today, only his remains and personal satchel linger in the dark as evidence of the foolish errand. While most in the Horde view troggs as mindless, savage brutes beneath negotiation, Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem thought otherwise—or at least claimed to. She dispatched Maur Grimtotem deep into the winding caverns of Ragefire Chasm beneath Orgrimmar to attempt a peaceful overture with the subterranean beasts. Predictably, diplomacy failed. Maur was swiftly slain, his corpse left in the caverns under the watchful eye of the trogg chieftain Oggleflint.

Maur Raincaller. Maur Raincaller is a tauren resident found residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Connected to the natural and spiritual life of the plains, he assists the village elders and watches over local matters affecting the herds and wild beasts. Situated near the heart of Bloodhoof Village on the shores of Lake Stonebull, Maur Raincaller serves his community by attending to regional ecological and beast-related concerns. Like many who bear the mantle of Raincaller, he pays close attention to the balance of the elements and wildlife across the fertile plains of Mulgore. After a bite from the fearsome strider Mazzranache left his wound infected, Maur turns to capable young travelers to gather the animal parts he needs for a remedy.

Maurin Bonesplitter. Maurin Bonesplitter is a Forsaken scholar and spellcaster stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Appointed by Keldran to monitor demonic cult activity, he leverages his deep understanding of ancient lore to dismantle the Burning Blade. Maurin regards the cultists with sheer contempt, viewing them as fools blind to the dark entities pulling their strings. While Ghost Walker Post primarily serves as a tauren and Horde outpost amidst the arid wastes of Desolace, Maurin Bonesplitter stands apart as one of its few undead occupants. Rather than a brutish soldier, Maurin is a learned spellcaster possessing extensive knowledge of forbidden histories and occult forces. His arcane aptitude and sharp intellect caught the eye of Keldran, who dispatched him to the region to observe the growing demonic presence and coordinate targeted strikes against it.

Maxan Anvol. Maxan Anvol is a dwarven priest trainer stationed within the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Dedicated to the Holy Light, he guides fledgling dwarven priests as they learn to channel divine power amid Dun Morogh's frigid climes. He tests young acolytes to ensure they are worthy of wearing the vestments of the church. While it might seem strange to find an ordained minister of the Holy Light stationed inside Thunderbrew Distillery, it suits dwarven culture well. Kharanos serves as the primary hub between Coldridge Valley and Ironforge, and the local inn is where travelers, mountaineers, and acolytes naturally gather. Maxan tends to the spiritual welfare of the hamlet alongside pints of stout, offering prayers and counsel to any who step through the doors.

Maybell Maclure. At the Maclure Vineyards in Elwynn Forest, Maybell Maclure loves a Stonefield in secret. Her family’s bitter feud with the neighboring Stonefields keeps her apart from Tommy Joe Stonefield. Maybell Maclure works the family vineyards under the shadow of a long feud with the Stonefields next door. She has fallen in love with Tommy Joe Stonefield, heir to the rival farm. Their relatives keep them apart, and Maybell searches for a way to speak with him beyond her family’s watchful eyes.

Mazthoril. Mazthoril is a massive, frostbitten cavern in central Winterspring that serves as the primary redoubt for the blue dragonflight in northern Kalimdor. Heavily guarded by dragonkin, spell-wielding wyrms, and arcane sentries, its winding ice tunnels conceal powerful magic and lead to the aerie of the reclusive blue matriarch Haleh. Carved into the frozen mountains just south of Everlook, Mazthoril houses an extensive brood answering to the Spell-Weaver, Malygos. The cavern and its surrounding crags are patrolled by vigilant dragonkin including Spellmaw, Azurous, and General Colbatann, while elite guardians watch the inner caverns. Intruders who wander into Mazthoril face dragonspawn thoroughly attuned to raw arcane energy, making any venture inside perilous without serious preparation.

Mazzranache. Maur Raincaller in Bloodhoof Village has fallen victim to a venomous bite from Mazzranache, a legendary plainstrider that terrorized his grandfather a generation ago. Struck by fever and delirious nightmares, the tauren requires a potent remedy brewed from Mulgore's wildlife before the infection claims his life. For years, Maur Raincaller regarded Mazzranache as little more than a harrowing family tale passed down by his grandfather. The elder tauren spoke of an unusually savage plainstrider armed with glowing red eyes, razor-sharp talons, and a toxic bite that defied the peaceful nature of most Mulgore wildlife. When Maur crossed paths with the beast out on the open grass, the legend proved all too real, leaving him severely wounded and struggling to make it back to safety.

Me Brother, Nipsy. Me Brother, Nipsy is an Alliance delivery quest that takes travelers across the Deeprun Tram between Ironforge and Stormwind. A gnome named Monty tasks commuters with transporting a crate of live rats to his brother Nipsy, who runs a rat kabob stall at the opposite terminal. Beneath the quirky errand lies a touching look at Monty's fractured mind following the tragedy of Gnomeregan. Me Brother, Nipsy is a brief courier errand that introduces commuters to the wonders—and hazards—of the Deeprun Tram. Stationed on the Ironforge side of the tramway, an odd gnome named Monty tasks travelers with ferrying a carton of fresh critters through the subterranean transit corridor to his brother Nipsy at the Stormwind depot. The delivery highlights the bizarre everyday commerce taking place beneath the mountains connecting the dwarven and human capitals.

Meal Appeal. Meal Appeal is an Orgrimmar errand given by Thatog, an orc tied down by his daily duties who worries his young son Migi is skipping meals to play. Travelers are asked to pick up a prepared lunch from Borstan's Firepit and track down Migi playing behind Grommash Hold. It offers a grounded look at domestic family life within the Horde's capital. In the bustling red-rock avenues of Orgrimmar, everyday domestic life continues alongside the drills of grunt warriors and the machinations of the Horde. Thatog, bound to his daily post by duty, finds himself unable to keep a watchful eye over his energetic young son, Migi. Left to his own devices, Migi spends from morning till dusk racing through the city streets with his friends, consistently neglecting his stomach until returning home famished.

Meats to Orgrimmar. Meats to Orgrimmar is a short introductory logistical quest offered by Zargh at the Crossroads. He asks young orc and troll adventurers to take a package of prime Barrens meat to the settlement's wind rider master, Devrak, introducing them to flight transport back to the Horde capital. The vast plains of the Barrens support an abundance of wildlife, from zhevras and plainstriders to kodos and thunder lizards. Zargh has prepared several choice cuts intended as a personal delivery to Gryshka, the bustling innkeeper of Orgrimmar's Valley of Strength. To keep the meat fresh and avoid the long, dust-choked trek across the Southfury River into Durotar, Zargh sends runners across the Crossroads directly to the wind rider perch.

Mebok Mizzyrix. Mebok Mizzyrix is an enterprising goblin entrepreneur residing in the port town of Ratchet. Ever eager to turn bizarre wilderness reagents into profit, he hires passing adventurers to gather unusual flora and fauna from across the Barrens and beyond. His most notorious project involves concocting a commercial intellect-enhancing beverage out of raptor horns. Operating out of the bustling, neutral port of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic Steamwheedle spirit of relentless opportunism. While Ratchet caters to sailors, pirates, and merchants of all stripes, Mebok focuses his keen eye on Kalimdor's wilderness. Rather than mining standard ore or trading mundane cloth, he seeks out rare biological curiosities that he believes can be refined into highly lucrative concoctions and commodities.

Meddlesome Mages. Meddlesome Mages centers on rising friction in the Shen'dar Highlands, where apprentices of the High Order trespass near sacred standing stones. Local guardians must drive them away to protect the delicate mystical forces that hold their island together from reckless arcane tampering. Tensions have flared north of the village in the Shen'dar Highlands, where apprentices of the High Order have gathered around ancient standing stones. Despite repeated warnings to leave these sacred sites undisturbed, the mages have pressed forward with their arcane interests. The local leadership, though hesitant to shed the blood of their shen'dorei kin, has called for outside intervention to disperse the encroaching apprentices before their interference causes permanent harm.

Medivh. Medivh was the last Guardian of Tirisfal, an ancient order tasked with defending Azeroth from demonic corruption. Bound from before his birth by the spirit of the Dark Titan Sargeras, he opened the Dark Portal and brought the orcish Horde into the world, setting off decades of catastrophic warfare. Medivh was born to the powerful Guardian Aegwynn and the court conjurer Nielas Aran. Centuries earlier, Aegwynn had fought the fallen Titan Sargeras in Northrend, unaware that his dark essence slipped into her body to await an heir. When Medivh reached his fourteenth birthday, the vast magical inheritance bestowed by his mother manifested in a terrifying explosion of power, plunging the boy into a decade-long coma under the watch of the clerics at Northshire Abbey.

Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Mekgineer Thermaplugg is the self-proclaimed ruler of ruined Gnomeregan and the greatest traitor in gnomish history. Once the trusted chief advisor of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, he orchestrated the catastrophic irradiation of the underground city in a twisted bid to seize power. Now thoroughly deranged and transformed into a leper gnome, he commands the irradiated halls from within a massive mechanical battle suit. Mekgineer Thermaplugg served for many years as chief advisor to High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque, who trusted him completely. All the while, Thermaplugg secretly coveted the office of High Tinker. What finally drove him to betray that trust, whether power or wealth, not even Mekkatorque can say; the High Tinker can only note that Thermaplugg would have had both in time.

Melenas' Head. Melenas' Head is the severed bounty taken from Lord Melenas, a satyr commander encamped inside Fel Rock. Brought back as absolute proof of his demise, the trophy marks the quiet elimination of a lingering demonic threat on the boughs of Teldrassil. To the night elves guarding Shadowglen and the surrounding reaches of Teldrassil, the mere existence of satyrs upon their new World Tree is a bitter disgrace. Lord Melenas chose to make his lair inside the twisted caverns of Fel Rock, just north of the elven settlements, rallying aggressive grell warriors to his banner. Because the kaldorei prize discretion when handling corruptions so close to their heartlands, this bloody trophy serves as private proof that his scheming has been snuffed out before his influence could spread.

Melithar Staghelm. Melithar Staghelm is a night elf stationed just outside Aldrassil in Shadowglen, Teldrassil's starting glade. He assists young night elf adventurers as they embark on their early training, sending them to learn what has brought the dryad Tarindrella back to the glade. While he shares the prominent Staghelm surname with Archdruid Fandral Staghelm, his exact connection to the ruling druid remains unconfirmed. Standing directly outside the entrance to the great bough of Aldrassil, Melithar serves as an early point of contact for night elves emerging into the world. A druid who listens to the whisperings of the forest spirits, he has learned that the mysterious woodland protector Tarindrella has returned to Shadowglen after years away. Sensing that something is amiss, Melithar sends newcomers to seek out the dryad southwest of Aldrassil and learn what business brings her to the grove.

Melor Sends Word. Melor Sends Word is a summons delivered by Jorn Skyseer in the Barrens on behalf of the renowned hunter Melor Stonehoof. Rising adventurers who have proven their grit across Kalimdor are directed to Hunter's Rise in Thunder Bluff to receive a far more demanding trial. Word travels fast across the plains. As an adventurer cuts their teeth in the Barrens and surrounding lands, notable hunters take notice of those who show true promise. Jorn Skyseer, keeping watch over the crossings and encampments, serves as an emissary for the elders of Hunter's Rise. He intercepts promising hunters and warriors to let them know that Melor Stonehoof, a revered mentor among the tauren, has marked out a specific path for them.

Melor Stonehoof. Melor Stonehoof is a veteran tauren huntsman stationed atop Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. As a mentor in the ways of the hunt, he tests the tracking prowess and mettle of Horde hunters by sending them after the most dangerous predatory beasts across the Barrens and Thousand Needles. Perched upon the breezy expanse of Hunter Rise, Melor Stonehoof observes the plains below with a practiced eye. The art of the hunt is sacred to the tauren, entwined with survival, spiritual balance, and respect for nature's greatest predators. Melor ensures that those who carry bow and blade in the name of the Horde understand this balance, directing promising stalkers to master their craft through trials against legendary beasts.

Menara Voidrender. Menara Voidrender is a human warlock residing in the goblin port of Ratchet. She acts as a mentor to ambitious practitioners of the dark arts from both the Alliance and the Horde, sharing her deep knowledge of demon-binding artifacts and arcane craft. Her secluded position in Kalimdor keeps her far from the watchful eyes of orthodox authorities. While most warlocks in the Eastern Kingdoms practice in damp cellars or secluded slaughterhouses beneath their home cities, Menara Voidrender chose the neutral goblin port of Ratchet in the Barrens. Operating far from the scrutiny of the Kirin Tor, Stormwind's guards, or Orgrimmar's overseers, she is free to pursue her occult studies in plain sight. Her willingness to deal with any capable apprentice, regardless of faction, makes her a rare point of commonality among practitioners of the dark arts.

Menethil Bay. Menethil Bay is the sheltered body of water along the western coast of the Wetlands, nestled between Menethil Harbor and the steep northern cliffs of Dun Morogh. Opening outward into the wider Baradin Bay, these waters are home to aggressive crocolisks and the remains of sunken vessels. It serves as the primary maritime approach for Alliance traffic journeying between the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor. Part of the larger Baradin Bay along the Great Sea, Menethil Bay forms a natural inlet bordered by Menethil Harbor to the north, Black Channel Marsh to the east, and the towering coastal bluffs of Dun Morogh to the south. Its shallow margins and marshy shores crawl with crocolisks of various ages and sizes, making the shallows treacherous for unguided travelers even though the bay serves as the lifeblood of Alliance maritime travel. Near the mouth of the bay lies the ruined wreckage of the Flying Osprey, a silent reminder of the dangers lurking beneath the surface.

Menethil Harbor. Menethil Harbor is a heavily fortified dwarven port town perched on an island off the western shore of the Wetlands. Named after King Terenas Menethil II, it acts as the primary maritime lifeline connecting the Eastern Kingdoms to the distant shores of Kalimdor. Sheltered behind massive stone battlements and the sturdy towers of Menethil Keep, it is a bustling hub for merchants, off-duty soldiers, and salty adventurers. Named in tribute to King Terenas Menethil II of Lordaeron, Menethil Harbor stands as a premier Alliance haven on the Wetlands coast. Despite its remote marshland setting, it remains a heavily defended bastion, reinforced by massive walls, a single bridged causeway, and the four stone watchtowers of Menethil Keep.

Menethil Keep. Menethil Keep is the stone stronghold dominating the skyline of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Marked by four sturdy watchtowers, it serves as the administrative heart and defensive bastion of the Alliance port, housing the local militia commander, Captain Stoutfist. Rising above the wooden docks and soggy marshes of the Wetlands, Menethil Keep is the central military strongpoint of Menethil Harbor. With four stone watchtowers gazing out over the town and the bay, the fortress offers a commanding view against seaward raiders, renegades, and the encroaching swamp beasts. Inside, Captain Stoutfist oversees the defense of the port, directing the town militia and organizing patrols to safeguard Alliance interests throughout the region.

Menethil Statuette. The Menethil Statuette is a rare silvery figurine portraying the late King Terenas Menethil II as a youthful paladin with an upraised warhammer. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of the Wetlands, it is an exceptionally scarce memorial of Lordaeron's fallen sovereign. The statuette depicts King Terenas Menethil II in his early years, portrayed as a long-haired paladin lifting a hammer toward the heavens. Terenas was notoriously humble during his reign and disliked personal monuments, meaning few statues or likenesses were ever commissioned in his honor. Following the collapse of the Kingdom of Lordaeron to the Scourge, almost all such relics were obliterated, making this surviving effigy extraordinarily valuable to the Alliance.

Mennet Carkad. Mennet Carkad is an introductory rogue quest in the Undercity that brings promising operatives into the fold of the Deathstalkers. Directed by Marion Call, aspiring assassins are summoned to report directly to Mennet Carkad deep within the Rogues' Quarter. Within the dark corridors of the Undercity, word travels quietly among the Forsaken's covert operatives. When a scout or assassin catches the eye of the higher leadership, an invitation is issued. Marion Call passes down word that Mennet Carkad, a prominent figure among the rogue handlers, has taken personal notice. Given the lethal reputation of the Forsaken intelligence apparatus, ignoring such a directive is not considered a viable option.

Mercenaries. Mercenaries is a bounty contract issued by Magistrate Bluntnose in Thelsamar to cull the encroaching Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. With military reinforcements from Ironforge bogged down in months of bureaucratic delay, the magistrate is forced to hire passing adventurers to protect the valley's vulnerable settlements, excavations, and the vital Stonewrought Dam. Thelsamar is feeling the sting of dwarven bureaucracy. It took two full months for Ironforge to even promise a handful of soldiers to bolster Loch Modan's local defense, and another two months before those troops are slated to arrive. With town guards stretched to their limits, Magistrate Bluntnose cannot afford to wait four months while hostile forces mass just beyond the valley's borders.

Merchant Coast. The Merchant Coast is the stretch of eastern shoreline in the Barrens bordering the Great Sea. Dominated by the bustling goblin port of Ratchet, the coast derives its name from lucrative sea trade, though it remains constantly contested by pirates. Running along the eastern edge of the Barrens, the Merchant Coast serves as a vital maritime artery connecting central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms and Theramore. Its name honors the industrious goblin traders of the Steamwheedle Cartel, whose neutral port of Ratchet handles cargo for anyone with coin. However, the open sea lanes attract more than merchant vessels: Southsea Freebooters prowl the sands and nearby waters, preying on merchant ships and setting up illicit operations along the beaches.

Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears. Mercy Falls on Deaf Ears is a bounty offered by a grieving enclave seeking violent vengeance against the Al'Aketh cult. After suffering a terrible tragedy at the cultists' hands, the enclave promises coin and access to the Nightclaw's hidden lore in exchange for trophies harvested from their slain enemies. Taking up this task plunges travelers directly into the conflict spreading across Shadowgale Forest and surrounding territories. The feud between the Nightclaw enclave and the Al'Aketh cultists is bitter and merciless. Following an unspecified but devastating tragedy inflicted upon the enclave, the survivors have abandoned any hope of peaceful reconciliation. To avenge their fallen kin, they turn to wandering adventurers and mercenaries, demanding violent retribution. In exchange for cutting down the cultists and taking their ears as grim proof of the deed, the enclave offers cold coin and the prospect of deeper trust.

Merissa Stilwell. At Northshire Abbey, Merissa Stilwell welcomes newcomers to Northshire Valley. The young human townsperson offers a cheerful greeting and a helping hand to those training nearby. Merissa Stilwell greets fresh recruits arriving in Northshire Valley from her place at Northshire Abbey. She offers newcomers simple hospitality and practical advice on resting and finding their way. Her surname is shared by craftsmen and homesteaders across the kingdom, including the blacksmith Jordan Stilwell and the Westfall defender Daphne Stilwell. Merissa remains a peaceful local presence amid the kingdom's rising tensions.

Merrin Rockweaver. Merrin Rockweaver is a dwarven researcher representing the Explorers' League in the Wetlands. Following a violent raptor infestation that overran Whelgar's Excavation Site, she took refuge alongside Prospector Whelgar on a ridge overlooking the site. Merrin Rockweaver traveled to the Wetlands on behalf of the Ironforge Explorers' League to unearth ancient Titan secrets buried beneath the muck. The expedition ended in disaster when the large bones they unearthed drew raptors to the dig. Vicious prehistoric beasts swarmed the trenches, forcing Merrin and the surviving crew to abandon their equipment, notes, and progress. She is now trapped with the few survivors on a bluff overlooking the overrun ruins.

Merrin's Letter. Merrin's Letter is an urgent message written by Merrin Rockweaver, an archaeologist trapped at the dig site in the Wetlands. It recounts the catastrophic overrun of their archaeological expedition by vicious raptors and assures her loved ones of her immediate survival. While excavating enormous prehistoric fossils and relics at the Whelgar's Excavation site in the Wetlands, the dwarven expedition disturbed a nest of ferocious Mottled Raptors. The beasts swarmed the trenches, slaughtering several workers and cutting off the surviving researchers from escape. Penning this note amidst the chaos, Merrin Rockweaver wrote to inform her husband Tarrel back at Menethil Harbor that while the dig lies in ruins, she, Prospector Whelgar, and Ormer Ironbraid managed to survive behind barricaded shelter.

Message in a Bottle. A washed-up bottle found along the shores of Stranglethorn Vale holds an urgent plea for rescue. Its author claims to be held prisoner by a great beast on an isolated island in the South Seas. Inside a glass container half-buried in the sand lies a neatly penned note asking for immediate assistance. The captive reports being trapped on a foreign island beneath thick jungle canopies, held by a great Skymane. Glimpses through the trees offer only faint landmarks: the coast of Wild Shore lies visible to the northwest, while large sailing vessels drift to the southwest.

Message in a Bottle. Having answered an ocean-borne plea, you find Princess Poobah chained as a captive on an isolated island off the Stranglethorn coast. The monstrous ape King Mukla commands the local beasts and keeps her bound, requiring his defeat to secure the key to her shackle. Following the message in the bottle brings you directly to Princess Poobah, who is held against her will by a heavy chain. The great Skymane gorilla known as King Mukla commands the creatures roaming the island and oversees her imprisonment. Poobah places her faith in you to face this formidable ape and retrieve the key needed to sever her bonds.

name.esES: Mensaje para el Poblado Viento Libre
name.frFR: Un message pour le poste de Librevent
name.ptBR: Mensagem para a Aldeia Vento Livre

text.enUS: Message to Freewind Post. Message to Freewind Post is a Horde quest tasking travelers with carrying urgent dispatches from Brave Moonhorn near the border lifts down into Thousand Needles. The missive warns Cliffwatcher Longhorn of intensifying centaur raids against local caravans. It also raises early concerns regarding the suspicious, standoffish behavior of the neighboring Grimtotem clan. Standing watch near the canyon's western approaches, Brave Moonhorn keeps a vigil over the roads leading down into Thousand Needles. With centaur aggression abruptly spiking, communication between border sentries and the regional leadership is vital. Moonhorn entrusts passing Horde adventurers with carrying an urgent dispatch southeast to Cliffwatcher Longhorn, the commander stationed atop the mesa settlement of Freewind Post.

name.esES: Un mensaje para los Martillo Salvaje

text.enUS: Message to the Wildhammer. At Revantusk Village in the Hinterlands, Otho Moji'ko says the Wildhammer are striking deals with the trolls' enemies, and this time the high elves are their partners. Otho wants a message sent to the Wildhammer dwarves in the blood of the Highvale high elves at Quel'Danil Lodge. The Wildhammer are forging new alliances with the trolls' enemies, and this time the high elves are their partners. Otho Moji'ko spits at the thought. A message is owed to the dwarves, written in the blood of their new friends: slaughter every Highvale high elf you come across and leave the bodies as a warning. Highvale Outrunners, Scouts, Marksmen and Rangers gather at Quel'Danil Lodge, in the Hinterlands' northwest.

Messenger to Darkshire. Messenger to Darkshire is an urgent diplomatic mission sent by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire to Lord Ello Ebonlocke in Duskwood. Desperate for military reinforcement against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls threatening Redridge, Solomon turns to his neighboring settlement for aid. The courier must brave the shadowed highways of Duskwood to deliver Solomon's formal plea to the mayor of Darkshire. With Stormwind's royal court ignoring his pleas and neighboring Westfall bogged down in its own insurrection, Magistrate Solomon looks south to Duskwood. Redridge faces a mounting siege from the Blackrock orc clans and aggressive gnoll packs, leaving Lakeshire's local guards stretched to their breaking point. In desperation, Solomon pens a letter directly to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke, hoping to hire or borrow Darkshire's vaunted Night Watch to reinforce the town's perimeter.

Messenger to Darkshire. Messenger to Darkshire concludes the desperate diplomatic correspondence between Lakeshire and Darkshire. Magistrate Solomon's plea for military reinforcement is firmly rejected by Lord Ello Ebonlocke, exposing the bitter truth that both towns have been abandoned to their fates by Stormwind. Facing an onslaught of Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Magistrate Solomon of Redridge hoped his old peer in Duskwood could spare troops. But Lord Ello Ebonlocke's reaction is bordering on outrage. Darkshire is barely holding back the living dead, ravenous beasts, and cursed magic pressing in from every corner of the woods. Ebonlocke bluntly states that the Night Watch exists only because Stormwind abandoned Duskwood first. Stripping Darkshire of its defenders would ensure the settlement falls before the patrol even crosses the forest's edge.

Messenger to Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire is desperate for military aid as gnolls and Blackrock orcs encircle the town. Unable to spare garrison troops, he dispatches an adventurer to carry 'The State of Lakeshire' directly to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind City. Lakeshire stands on the brink of collapse. Gnoll packs contest every road, Blackrock orcs raid from the north, and the local guardsmen are stretched beyond their limits. Magistrate Solomon cannot afford to send fighting men on a days-long ride to the capital, leaving an independent traveler to carry his official plea for regular troops to the city gates.

Messenger to Stormwind. You carry General Marcus Jonathan's reply from Stormwind to Lakeshire, where Blackrock orcs and gnolls threaten the town. The capital offers no troops, leaving the settlement to face danger while Stormwind's leaders delay. You brought Magistrate Solomon's plea for reinforcements to General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind. Now you carry his preliminary reply back to Redridge while he waits for approval from the throne. Without royal authorization, the General cannot commit the army. Lakeshire's citizens remain without city guards, and each day brings the settlement closer to falling under the Blackrock clan.

name.frFR: Un message pour la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Messenger to Westfall. Messenger to Westfall is an Alliance errand carrying an urgent plea from Magistrate Solomon in Redridge across Elwynn to Westfall. Facing total abandonment by the Stormwind military, Lakeshire's leadership seeks mutual aid from Gryan Stoutmantle's newly formed People's Militia. Magistrate Solomon finds Lakeshire in a desperate situation. The Redridge Mountains are besieged by Blackrock orcs and gnolls, yet the Stormwind Army has failed to arrive in force. Recognizing that Lakeshire cannot survive on town guards and irregulars alone, Solomon writes a formal plea for assistance. With regular royal reserves nowhere in sight, he turns his eyes west, having heard word of a citizen defense group forming beyond Elwynn Forest.

name.frFR: Un message pour la marche de l'Ouest

text.enUS: Messenger to Westfall. A letter from Westfall brings Magistrate Solomon a hard answer in Lakeshire. He asked Gryan Stoutmantle for soldiers to defend Redridge, but Westfall has been left to face its own troubles. Magistrate Solomon faces growing troubles in the Redridge Mountains without Stormwind's royal garrison. He looks to the southern frontier for help and writes to Gryan Stoutmantle, commander of the People's Militia in Westfall. Solomon hopes the volunteers at Sentinel Hill can spare fighters to strengthen Lakeshire's defenses. He does not know how hard pressed the western plains are.

Michael Garrett. Michael Garrett is a simple courier task linking trade in the Undercity with the Forsaken's flight network. After collecting supplies packed by Gordon Wendham in the Trade Quarter, you are directed to deliver the crate to the bat handler Michael Garrett to arrange aerial transport out toward the Sepulcher. It highlights how the Forsaken utilize trained vampire bats to connect their capital with outposts across Lordaeron. Running a fledgeling kingdom carved out of the ruins of Lordaeron requires constant logistics. Outposts like the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest rely heavily on goods, munitions, and provisions moving out from the Undercity. Gordon Wendham packs the necessary field supplies into a single crate in the city's Trade Quarter, but carting freight by ground through blighted forests is both slow and vulnerable to ambush by Scourge remnants or wild beasts.

name.esES: Mitad de la llave de Gelkak
name.itIT: Frammento Centrale della Chiave di Gelkak
name.ptBR: Parte do Meio da Chave de Gelkak

text.enUS: Middle of Gelkak's Key. The Middle of Gelkak's Key is a broken metal fragment belonging to the shipwrecked gnome pirate Gelkak Gyromast. After his vessel went down off the coast of Darkshore, this central section was snatched away by scavengers among the local Greymist murlocs. When Gelkak Gyromast's ship was dragged beneath the waves by wild threshadons, the gnome pirate tumbled ashore with his most precious belongings shattered on the rocky shoals. Among the wreckage was a specialized winding key meant for his mechanical first mate. The key snapped into three distinct fragments during the catastrophe, scattering across the strand. While the tops and bottoms ended up carried off by coastal beasts, the middle section caught the eye of the Greymist murlocs prowling the Darkshore surf, who quickly hoarded the shiny metallic piece in their camps and wreckage holdings.

Miles Welsh. Miles Welsh is a Forsaken priest trainer residing deep within the Pools of Vision beneath Thunder Bluff. He offers spiritual instruction and shadow discipline to priests traversing the tauren capital. Miles Welsh stands far from the plague-scarred ruins of Lordaeron, making his home in the humid, spirit-laden grotto beneath Thunder Bluff known as the Pools of Vision. As a Forsaken priest, he instructs travelers who channel divine and shadowy energies. His presence in the heart of Mulgore reflects the tenuous diplomatic ties binding the Forsaken to the Horde, sharing sanctuary with tauren mystics and shamans while guiding acolytes in the arts of shadow and faith.

Military Ward. The Military Ward serves as the martial heart of Ironforge, housing the city's command infrastructure, weapons masters, and barracks. Marked by bold red banners, it is where dwarven soldiers, hunters, and siege engineers train alongside mechanized siege engines and flying machines. Situated within the northern perimeter of the mountain fortress, the Military Ward concentrates Ironforge's defensive forces into a bustling staging ground. The central complex, the Hall of Arms, accommodates warrior and hunter trainers, battlemasters, and hangars housing dwarven flying machines and steam tanks. Surrounding the drill squares and training dummies are supply outlets such as Craghelm's Plate and Chain, Goldfury's Hunting Supplies, and Timberline Arms, making the ward the primary staging point for mountaineers and city defenders.

Milli Featherwhistle. Milli Featherwhistle is a master gnomish mechanostrider engineer stationed at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Following the fall of Gnomeregan, she meticulously handcrafts and maintains the clockwork mounts favored by her kin. She sells her prized mechanical creations to fellow gnomes and trusted allies of the exiled Gnomeregan survivors. Operating outdoors in the biting chill of Steelgrill's Depot just east of Kharanos, Milli Featherwhistle oversees the supply of clockwork steeds for Gnomeregan's displaced populace. Unlike the biological beasts favored by dwarves and night elves, Milli builds her entire inventory herself, personally calibrating gears, pistons, and balancing gyros to ensure each mechanical bird runs at peak efficiency across the snowy crags of Dun Morogh.

Milly Osworth. At Northshire Abbey, Deputy Willem sends you to help Milly Osworth. Her wagon and livelihood are in jeopardy, and she needs help across the abbey grounds. The work takes you from defending the abbey to aiding Elwynn Forest's civilians. After you prove your mettle against the Defias thieves encroaching on Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem recognizes you as capable and willing to help. He sends you to assist his friend Milly Osworth. This favor is personal, outside the abbey's official guard duties, and Milly is a civilian caught in the valley's growing unrest.

Milly's Harvest. In the Northshire Vineyards, Milly's grapes lie abandoned after the Defias arrive. Crates and buckets of fruit remain at risk of theft or being crushed beneath the abbey guards' boots. Milly Osworth gathers grapes in the Northshire Vineyards, where the harvest matters to local vintners and the abbey community. When armed brigands in red masks push into the fields, Milly flees to the abbey grounds. Her fresh-picked grapes remain scattered between the rows.

Milly's Harvest. Defias brigands have driven Milly Osworth from the Northshire vineyards. Her harvest lies scattered in buckets and crates among the occupied rows, where it may be stolen or crushed. Milly Osworth fled the southeastern fields of Northshire Valley when Defias brigands swarmed the vines. She left her gathered grapes behind in buckets and crates among the occupied rows. Northshire's garrison is stretched thin, and Milly fears that boots and fighting will crush any fruit the bandits leave behind.

Milton Sheaf. In Stormwind Keep, Milton Sheaf guards the kingdom's written history. He tends the Royal Library and calls on Alliance travelers to recover lost books and records. Milton Sheaf tends the Royal Library inside Stormwind Keep. While the court handles politics, noble disputes, and military concerns, he preserves the written record. He sees accurate histories of the Alliance and the Eastern Kingdoms as a duty, especially amid war, loss, and instability.

Miner Johnson. Miner Johnson is an elusive, seasoned miner affiliated with the Defias Brotherhood deep inside the Deadmines. Tucked away in a side alcove alongside ordinary laborers, this dangerous prospector oversees excavation efforts ahead of the heavy machinery found deeper underground. Because he wanders the subterranean tunnels erratically, adventurers only occasionally cross his path. While hundreds of laborers pick at the subterranean veins of the Deadmines to supply Edwin VanCleef's hidden fortress, Miner Johnson stands out as an unusually formidable figure among them. Lurking in a shadowed alcove to the left before the lumbering shredders of the Mast Room, he is far tougher and more aggressive than the regular workforce. His unpredictable presence makes him a legendary target for explorers traversing the Defias tunnels.

name.frFR: La bonne fortune d'un mineur pauvre

text.enUS: Miner's Fortune. Wharfmaster Dizzywig of Ratchet catches wind of an extraordinary discovery at the Venture Company's Boulder Lode Mine: an emerald the size of a fist. Rather than letting the ruthless mining syndicate profit from it, Dizzywig hires an adventurer to liberate the Cats Eye Emerald from the mine's supervisors for a split of the profits. As the port official managing the bustling harbor between Ratchet and Booty Bay, Wharfmaster Dizzywig overhears virtually every secret whispered on the merchant routes. When rumors arrived detailing an enormous fist-sized gem struck deep inside the Boulder Lode Mine, Dizzywig immediately recognized a lucrative opportunity. The Venture Company's reckless strip-mining across the northern Barrens makes them few friends, meaning few questions would be asked if their greatest recent find quietly vanished from their custody.

Miners' Gear. Miners' Gear consists of sturdy dwarven picks, shovels, and excavation tools stored within the Silver Stream Mine. Following an infestation of vermin, the Miners' League tasked adventurers with retrieving these valuable implements before local guards launched an assault. When the Silver Stream Mine in northern Loch Modan ran out of ore, the Miners' League repurposed the quiet tunnels into a subterranean storage depot for mining equipment. Unfortunately, tunnel-dwelling kobolds quickly overrun the complex, making off with the stored goods and nesting among the crates. Fearing the valuable dwarven gear would either be wrecked in an all-out assault by the Mountaineers or ruined by the scavengers, the league relies on bold adventurers to venture inside and haul the crates back to safety.

Miners' Union Card. A Miners' Union Card is an identification credential once carried by laborers working the rich subterranean veins beneath Moonbrook. Following a catastrophic cave-in that sealed a wing of the tunnels, these tokens now remain on the restless skeletal corpses wandering the dark drifts. Long before the Defias Brotherhood took absolute control over Moonbrook, laborers toiled underground under the banner of the miners' guild, extracting valuable ore for the kingdom. That ended in disaster when a severe tunnel collapse crushed a major shaft, trapping and killing dozens of workers beneath tons of rock. Rather than finding a quiet grave, those who perished rose again as skeletal miners, excavators, and dynamiters. The union cards clutched in their bony pockets are the sole surviving proof of their identities, sought out by surviving colleagues in Stormwind hoping to bring closure to grieving families.

Mining Consultant. Mining Consultant is a Northshire Valley quest that sends adventurers to confer with Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed outside Echo Ridge Mine. Her observations reveal an unusual development: the local kobolds have begun plundering books from Northshire Abbey's library. The kobold infestation at Echo Ridge Mine has taken an unexpected turn. Rather than merely defending subterranean claims and gathering candles, the creatures have caught the attention of local authorities due to strange, coordinated disturbances. Adventurers are directed to seek out Kelsey Fargo, a mining apprentice stationed near the mine's entrance, to ascertain what she has witnessed from her vantage point outside the tunnels.

Minor Manifestation of Earth. A Minor Manifestation of Earth is a localized elemental spirit bound to sacred stones in Mulgore and Durotar. Invisible to ordinary sight, it reveals itself only to fledgling shamans who drink the sacred Earth Sapta, providing the rough quartz required to carve their very first earth totem. The spirits of the earth dwell everywhere beneath the dirt and stone, but communicating with them requires deliberate ritual. At sacred landmarks like Kodo Rock in Mulgore and Spirit Rock in Durotar, Minor Manifestations of Earth linger in the unseen realm, surrounded by even smaller elemental presences. Only initiates who have drunk the Earth Sapta—a ritual draught brewed by shamanic mentors—can lift the veil between the physical world and the elements. Once acknowledged, the spirit imparts the earth's blessings along with a piece of rough quartz, granting the novice the spiritual focal point needed to fashion an Earth Totem.

Minor Manifestation of Water. The Minor Manifestation of Water is an elemental spirit found along North Tide's Run on the coast of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital trial for Horde shamans seeking to commune with and master the element of water. Before this peaceful spirit can be consulted, initiates must first cleanse its corrupted counterpart. Lurking along the mist-shrouded shores of North Tide's Run, west of the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, the Minor Manifestation of Water represents an essential rite of passage for developing shamans. Water elementals embody life, renewal, and fluidity, but they can easily fall victim to malevolent blight. An initiate must face and defeat a corrupted manifestation of this elemental before the pure Minor Manifestation of Water can reveal itself. Once cleansed, the spirit offers guidance to shamans completing their sacred journey to fashion a Water Totem.

Minshina's Skull. Minshina's Skull contains the bound soul of the Darkspear troll Minshina, brother of Master Gadrin. Trapped by the rogue witch doctor Zalazane on the Echo Isles, the skull serves as a grim vessel used to fuel dark ritual magics. When Zalazane seized control of the Echo Isles and drove out the Darkspear tribe, Minshina was among those captured and slain. Rather than letting his victim pass into death, the traitorous witch doctor bound Minshina's soul to his own severed skull. Placed within a foul circle of power on the southernmost isle, the skull became a tether of magical enslavement. Master Gadrin, guided by tormented visions of his brother calling to him in dreams, seeks out brave travelers to venture into the occupied islands, reclaim the relic, and shatter Zalazane's hold over his brother's spirit.

Minshina's Skull. Master Gadrin of Sen'jin Village is haunted by the desperate cries of his deceased brother, Minshina. Slain and subjected to dark magic by the rogue witch doctor Zalazane on the Echo Isles, Minshina's soul remains bound inside his own severed skull. Freeing the fallen troll requires infiltrating Zalazane's ritual grounds to reclaim the relic and release his spirit from eternal torment. Master Gadrin serves as one of the Darkspear tribe's spiritual anchors in Sen'jin Village, but his mind is tormented by dark visions. His brother Minshina fell victim to Zalazane's betrayal when the mad warlock seized control of the Echo Isles. Minshina perished during the conflict, but in troll tradition and voodoo mysticism, physical death does not always grant peace. Minshina's tormented voice speaks into Gadrin's dreams, pleading for salvation from a fate worse than death.

Mirage Flats. Mirage Flats is a barren, sun-scorched expanse nestled in the central wastes of the Badlands. Lying east of Dustbelch Grotto, this dry plateau is notorious for shimmering heat hazes and hungry predators. Situated east of Dustbelch Grotto, the Mirage Flats present travelers with an unforgiving stretch of cracked red dirt and shimmering heat waves that give the plain its name. Few civilized souls linger here; instead, the open flats are dominated by opportunistic scavengers and lethal beasts. Flocks of giant buzzards circle lazily on hot thermals above, watching for the leavings of ferocious ridge stalkers and pack-hunting crag coyotes that scour the brush for easy prey.

Mirage Raceway. The Mirage Raceway is an impromptu engineering proving ground situated in the shimmering salt flats of Thousand Needles. Founded on the heated rivalry between goblin tinkerer Pozzik and gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts, it pits high-speed rocket cars against one another across the baked earth. The track serves as a neutral gathering place where members of both the Alliance and Horde come to wager, tinker, and cheer on their favored machines. Sprawled across the vast white desert floor of the Shimmering Flats, the Mirage Raceway was born out of an unrelenting grudge match between two master tinkerers: the goblin Pozzik and the gnome Fizzle Brassbolts. Determined to settle once and for all whose race possesses superior technical ingenuity, the two constructed custom rocket-powered drag cars and recruited rival crews to pit them against each other in daily high-velocity showdowns. The relentless competition has turned the barren flats into a bustling hub of invention, sabotage, and testing as each crew desperately looks for any mechanical advantage.

Mirages. Hurrying away from the Uldaman excavation site, Sigrun Ironhew's party left wagons and crates behind. Ogres from Camp Kosh took the cart holding all their weapons, and since then the party has had no food. In their rush to leave the Uldaman excavation site, Sigrun Ironhew and company left many wagons and supply crates behind. Ogres from Camp Kosh have been picking over the leftovers like vultures. They took the cart holding all the party's weapons, and since then the party has had no food. Sigrun admits it is embarrassing and asks you to retrieve the supply crate.

Mirkfallon Lake. Mirkfallon Lake sits in a central highland basin in the Stonetalon Mountains, nestled beneath the sheer cliffs of Windshear Crag. Its waters and surrounding banks teem with native wildlife, including aggressive slimes, roaming thunder lizards, and descending wyverns. Positioned at the geographic center of the Stonetalon range, Mirkfallon Lake rests between the mountain passes leading south toward the Webwinder Path and north toward Stonetalon Peak. Fed by highland runoff, the lake offers a fertile oasis amidst the craggy peaks, drawing thunder lizards down to drink and wyverns from their roosts high above. The waters are also inhabited by strange, bubbling slimes, turning an otherwise serene mountain tarn into a hazardous crossing for lone travelers.

Mirror Lake. Novice Alliance mages in Stormwind's Mage Quarter are sent to sample Mirror Lake's waters for magical contamination. Jennea Cannon sends them southwest of the city gates to test the waterfall spray. Azeroth's arcane currents were shaken by conflicts from the opening of the Dark Portal through the Third War and the battle at Mount Hyjal. Those shocks tore ancient currents from their stable channels. In Stormwind's Wizard's Sanctum, magi like Jennea Cannon watch the changes closely. They fear that displaced arcane power could reach the wilderness and corrupt local ecosystems.

Mirror Lake. Water spills into Mirror Lake beneath Stormwind's cliffs in northwestern Elwynn Forest, near an orchard. Defias bandits prowl the surrounding orchards, while mages watch for trouble in the forest's arcane currents. Mirror Lake lies beneath Stormwind City's walls, where fishermen and weary travelers might seek a quiet rest. Defias Brotherhood brigands stalk the surrounding orchards, making a long stay perilous for locals. Mystical disturbances across Azeroth have also begun to warp the forest's natural channels of arcane energy. Mages from the Wizard's Sanctum watch the lake closely. They send practitioners to sample its currents and guard against chaotic arcane runoff poisoning communities downstream.

Mirror Lake Orchard. Defias bandits now hold Mirror Lake Orchard, on Mirror Lake's southern shore in western Elwynn Forest. The quiet homestead near Thunder Falls has fallen to outlaws while Stormwind's guards are stretched thin. Mirror Lake Orchard once fed a peaceful farmstead with the clean waters of Mirror Lake. Now Defias Brotherhood bandits have seized the cottage and grounds near Thunder Falls. With Stormwind's military stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn missing, rural homes across Elwynn are easy targets for outlaws seeking shelter.

name.esES: Muestra de agua del Lago Espejo
name.ptBR: Amostra de Água do Lago Espelhado

text.enUS: Mirror Lake Water Sample. At Mirror Lake in Elwynn Forest, a flask of water is gathered for Jennea Cannon in Stormwind. The mages will test it for signs of altered arcane currents in local water. Jennea Cannon sends promising apprentices to collect water from Mirror Lake. The lake lies just southwest of the Stormwind Gate, and they fill a specially prepared flask at the base of its waterfall. The Wizard's Sanctum in Stormwind is concerned that the world's mystic channels remain unsettled after catastrophic conflicts. Its mages will examine the sample for stray magical taint in the waterways used by people nearby.

Misha. Misha is the loyal bear companion of Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde. She wanders Kalimdor faithfully at the half-ogre beastmaster's side. Misha is a brown bear who walks at the side of the wandering Rexxar, a solitary spirit who trusts beasts more than people. Together they have forged a fierce, protective partnership that has weathered countless wildernesses and bloody battles.

Misha Tor'kren. Misha Tor'kren is an orc mother dwelling at the Tor'kren Farm in western Durotar, southeast of Thunder Ridge. Plagued by anxiety over her missing son Kron, she appeals to passing travelers for aid in discovering his fate. Tucked away near the edge of Thunder Ridge, Misha Tor'kren works her isolated farmstead while enduring a parent's worst fear. Her son Kron ventured west toward the Southfury River to hunt crocolisks and prove his mettle, but he never returned. With Durotar's frontier dangers stretching orcish watchtowers thin, Misha is left alone to hope for word of his whereabouts, desperate for anyone willing to search the riverbanks for signs of her boy.

Missing In Action. Missing In Action is an Alliance escort mission in the Redridge Mountains to rescue Corporal Keeshan from Blackrock orc captivity. After his regiment was wiped out in the hills, Keeshan was knocked unconscious and dragged into a cave fortress. Guiding the wounded soldier safely back to Lakeshire helps the local garrison confirm the grim fate of their missing men. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as Blackrock orcs descend from the northern peaks. Patrols sent out by the town guard frequently run into ambushes, and Corporal Keeshan's unit suffered the worst of it. Outnumbered and overwhelmed, most of the soldiers in his regiment were cut down on the spot. Keeshan survived only because a crushing blow knocked him cold before he could be executed, allowing the orcs to drag him back to their cave as a prisoner.

name.deDE: Mission: möglich, aber nicht sehr wahrscheinlich

text.enUS: Mission: Possible But Not Probable. This critical assignment tests a Horde rogue's stealth, thievery, and combat skills against a rogue Venture Company outpost in the northern Barrens. Operatives infiltrate an oil tower, assassinate Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix, and seize a potent chemical concoction for the Shattered Hand. North of the Sludge Fen oil rigs, the Venture Company maintains an isolated drilling tower. Under orders from Taskmaster Fizzule, an embedded Shattered Hand operative posing as a Venture Company supervisor, rogues are instructed to use classic underworld methods rather than outright assault. Fizzule asks rogues to pickpocket a key directly off Foreman Silixiz and keep it for him before mounting an ascent through heavily altered workers and sentries.

Mist. Mist is an escort quest in the shaded boughs of Teldrassil. After discovering a wounded gray sabercat abandoned deep in the woods, travelers must shepherd her safely back to Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak at a nearby moon well. Tucked away amid the wild undergrowth of Teldrassil lies Mist, a distinctive gray sabercat marked by severe, slashing lacerations across her back and belly. Rather than acting as a feral beast of the wilds, Mist exhibits remarkable calm and bright intelligence in her blue eyes, immediately looking to friendly travelers for guidance and protection.

Mist Veil's Lockbox. Mist Veil's Lockbox is a sturdy strongbox resting in the submerged wreckage of the night elven vessel Mist Veil off the coast of Darkshore. It holds the captain's log and personal effects, which were lost when the ship was ambushed and sunk by coastal murlocs. The night elven vessel Mist Veil met its end while sailing the treacherous coastal waters toward Auberdine. Ambushed by hostile murlocs alongside its sister ship, the Silver Dawning, the vessel was overwhelmed and sent to the ocean floor. Its captain perished during the attack, leaving behind their logbook and prized personal belongings sealed inside this lockbox. Resting in the flooded hold, the chest remains a grim trophy surrounded by the very creatures responsible for the catastrophe.

Mist's Edge. Mist's Edge is the long, windswept coastline stretching north from Auberdine along western Darkshore. Shrouded in damp ocean fog, these gray beaches are littered with shipwrecks, colossal sea creature remains, and roving packs of crabs and murlocs. Running along the western edge of Darkshore, Mist's Edge is defined by damp sands, rocky tidepools, and perpetual coastal fog. The beach is a graveyard of the sea, littered with decaying sea behemoths, drift timber, and the shattered ribs of wrecked vessels. While seemingly barren, the coastline teems with shoreline scavengers, notably aggressive crabs and territorial murloc tribes that nest in the surf.

Misty Pine Refuge. Misty Pine Refuge is a small outpost building of the Argent Dawn tucked amidst the frigid snows of central Dun Morogh. Situated amid the windswept hills of Dun Morogh, Misty Pine Refuge is an unassuming outpost of the Argent Dawn in the dwarven realm. While the surrounding crags are patrolled by Ironforge mountaineers, the refuge is home to Father Gavin, the order's lone agent here, who offers a quiet hearth amid the bitter elements and the perils that threaten the mountain roads.

Misty Reed Post. Misty Reed Post is a rugged Horde encampment situated between Stagalbog and the Misty Reed Strand in the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Established as a frontline watch under the authority of Stonard, it serves to monitor the dangerous wetlands and the treacherous coastline. Tucked away in the humid gloom between the Stagalbog and the eastern shore, Misty Reed Post is little more than a spartan camp under Stonard's banner. It is manned by a handful of Stonard hunters, a shaman, Katar, and Tok'Kar, who oversees the watch. Conditions are rough, offering no fortified shelter from the marsh's hostile wildlife and lingering damp. Tok'Kar harbors quiet ambitions that the Horde command in Stonard will one day reinforce the position with a sturdy orcish burrow or watchtower, though for now, the scouts must hold the marsh with tents, campfire smoke, and sharpened steel.

Misty Reed Strand. The Misty Reed Strand is the fog-shrouded, desolate eastern coastline of the Swamp of Sorrows. Lined with jagged rocks, washed-up wreckage, and creeping swamp mist, it is home to aggressive crabs, crocolisks, and coastal murloc tribes. Travelers venturing down to the surf often find themselves contending with the local wildlife for whatever resources wash ashore. Stretching along the entire eastern border of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Reed Strand forms a damp barrier between the deep mire and the Great Sea. Heavy mists constantly roll in off the water, obscuring vision and muffling the cries of native wildlife. The beaches are littered with sea debris, driftwood, and decaying vegetation washed out from the bog inland. Because of its remote position and harsh climate, no formal permanent settlements hold the shoreline, leaving the sands to aggressive crustaceans, stalking crocolisks, and territorial murlocs who violently defend their foraging grounds.

Misty Shore. Misty Shore is the quiet lakeshore of the Alterac Mountains, skirting the eastern shore of Lordamere Lake. Stretching between Dandred's Fold and the perimeter of Dalaran, it offers wide, foggy views of the Dawning Isles and the sinister silhouette of Fenris Keep. Running along Lordamere Lake, the Misty Shore stretches between Dandred's Fold and Dalaran. Thick, damp air regularly drifts off the lake, obscuring snapping turtles and the occasional zealous fanatic who wanders down from regional strongholds.

Misty Valley. Tucked away in the northwestern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows, the Misty Valley is a shadowed, fog-drenched hollow north of the pass into Deadwind. The secluded basin is overrun by primordial swamp beasts, wandering swampwalkers, and tangled horrors. Deep in its rearmost cave dwells the colossal and terrifying Mire Lord. Nestled beneath the high cliffs separating the Swamp of Sorrows from Deadwind Pass, the Misty Valley is perpetually choked with thick marsh vapor. Unlike the open wetlands to the east, this isolated pocket is dense with colossal marsh elementals, including looming swampwalkers, ancient swampwalker elders, and creeping tangled horrors. At the far end of the misty gorge lies a cavern that serves as the lair of the Mire Lord, one of the most formidable natural threats haunting the bog.

Mitsuwa. Mitsuwa is a Darkspear troll stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost along the misty coast of Ashenvale. Deeply troubled by the ambush of his traveling kin, he enlists Horde champions to avenge the fallen and reclaim stolen spiritual talismans. Situated at the remote Zoram'gar Outpost on the strand of the Zoram Strand, Mitsuwa serves the Horde alongside his companion Marukai. When a group of traveling trolls bound for the encampment was ambushed and slaughtered by the aggressive Thistlefur furbolgs of northern Ashenvale, Mitsuwa took the loss as a grievous offense. Driven by duty and anger, he directs able-bodied warriors toward the Thistlefur dens to reclaim the stolen troll charms, ensuring the spirits of his kin are honored and their sacred possessions recovered from the beasts.

Mizjah Ruins. The Mizjah Ruins are ancient stone remains nestled in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp. Long abandoned by their original troll architects, the crumbling structures have been seized by the brute-strength Mosh'Ogg ogres. From this vantage, the ogres launch disruptive ambushes against passing supply caravans traveling toward the Swamp of Sorrows. Like many of the ancient stone ruins scattered throughout Stranglethorn Vale, the Mizjah Ruins were built by the Gurubashi Empire long before modern empires rose. Today, the moss-choked arches and cracked flagstones are occupied by the Mosh'Ogg clan, primarily brute warriors and crude witch doctors. Far from keeping to their stolen perimeter, these ogres routinely raid nearby supply convoys bound for the Horde settlement of Stonard, transforming ancient history into a persistent, bloody thorn in the side of Grom'gol's commanders.

Mo'grosh Crystal. Mo'grosh Crystals are rare mineral formations mined and hoarded by the Mo'grosh ogres in northeastern Loch Modan. Prized for their unusual alchemical properties, they serve as a vital component in neutralizing Dark Iron demolition materials. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, the Mo'grosh ogres excavate these distinctive crystals from their stronghold. Though the brute-strength ogres rarely specialize in delicate metallurgy, Mo'grosh Crystals are prized treasures among their clan, carried by common enforcers, mystic shamans, and their towering leaders alike. The crystals are relatively uncommon, making them a heavily guarded possession within the Mo'grosh Stronghold.

Mo'grosh Stronghold. Mo'grosh Stronghold is a fortified den of ogres dug into the northeastern hills of Loch Modan. Nestled among ancient, weathered ruins, these brutal giants pose a constant threat to the dwarven settlements below. Tucked away in the crags of northeastern Loch Modan, Mo'grosh Stronghold serves as the primary base for the Mo'grosh clan of ogres in the region. The brute forces lurking within the caves and outer camps raid traveling dwarven supply caravans and present an enduring danger to the peace of Thelsamar. The rugged stonework scattered around the camp suggests the site once belonged to an older settlement, before the lumbering ogres claimed the territory and raised their distinctive mounds.

Modr Fragment. The Modr Fragment is one of four missing pieces broken off from the ancient Goaz Stone, a relic unearthed in the Wetlands. Discovered amid relics and loose earth within the Whelgar Excavation Site, it bears ancient Titan script vital to assembling a forgotten prophecy. Before vicious raptors drove the Explorers' League from their dig in the Wetlands, Prospector Whelgar uncovered the Goaz Stone—a massive tablet inscribed with ancient Titan markings. Its translated text abruptly broke off across four distinct gaps, obscuring warnings of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy. The Modr Fragment is one of those four lost pieces, left behind among ancient relics and overturned soil when the diggers were forced to flee for their lives.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin seeks to harness the natural magic of Stranglethorn Vale for the benefit of the Horde. Building upon his previous rituals at Grom'gol Base Camp, he asks for sharp claws and a pristine feline fang to weave a powerful enchantment. Within Grom'gol Base Camp, Far Seer Mok'thardin works to understand and bend the feral power of the wild to strengthen the Horde. Having seen success in his initial rites, he promises to craft a specialized enchanted relic for those willing to brave the dense underbrush and stalk the deadly predators prowling the surrounding territory.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin in Grom'gol Base Camp needs a sturdy magical binding to hold together the Stranglethorn trophies collected so far. To bind the feathers, claws, and fang securely, he requires an aged sinew harvested from the elder primates roaming southern Stranglethorn Vale. Having gathered feathers, claws, and a pristine fang, Far Seer Mok'thardin reaches the next stage of his ritual. To fasten these potent relics together, he requires a magical tether of exceptional toughness. Only the aged sinew of an Elder Mistvale Gorilla will suffice to endure the magic he intends to weave.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin continues assembling the components for a potent shamanistic item to aid the Horde. After working with feline trophies, he turns his attention toward the feathers worn by the raptors of Stranglethorn Vale. Following the recovery of materials from the jungle's feline predators, Far Seer Mok'thardin reveals that more components are needed before his shamanistic ritual can begin. To forge a tool fit to assist the Warchief, he requires feathers worn by Jungle Stalkers. These raptors inhabit the dense jungle south of Grom'gol Base Camp, not far from the great arena.

Mok'thardin's Enchantment. Far Seer Mok'thardin requires one final sacred component to complete the enchantment of a ceremonial choker at Grom'gol Base Camp. He directs you to an elevated Holy Spring along the southern bluffs near the western sea, which has drawn the attention of a hostile naga expedition. Following the earlier stages of Mok'thardin's enchantment, the far seer seeks water from a Holy Spring situated high above the bluffs in the southern reaches of Stranglethorn Vale, near the western coast. The site is a point of contention among scholars of the mystic and divine, with every race across Azeroth claiming the holy waters were sanctified specifically for their own people.

Moldy Tome. The Moldy Tome is a water-damaged, salvaged remnant containing half of the original Tome of the Cabal. Lost in a shipwreck off the coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, it holds dark esoteric rituals coveted by warlocks seeking to master demonic summonings. The Tome of the Cabal was a singular, irreplaceable treatise on dark arts once held within the kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point in its murky history, the grimoire was ruthlessly vandalized and split in two. The portion now designated as the Moldy Tome was being transported south by ship toward Menethil Harbor and Ironforge. The vessel never reached its destination, succumbing to the treacherous waters west of Southshore. Swept ashore south of Azurelode Mine, the surviving half lay ruined by damp and surf amidst the scavenging murlocs that stalk the Hillsbrad coast.

Molsen Farm. Molsen Farm is an abandoned homestead located in the breadbasket region of Westfall. Once a fertile piece of farmland feeding Stormwind, it has fallen into ruin following the rise of the Defias Brotherhood and the prowling mechanical harvest golems left in their wake. Like many homesteads across Westfall, Molsen Farm stands as a casualty of the kingdom's neglect and criminal uprising. When the Defias Brotherhood took control of the countryside, the resident farmers were driven out or worse, abandoning their crops and buildings. Now, instead of laborers gathering grain, hostile mechanical Harvest Watchers and wandering outlaws scour the untended fields, making the farm a hazard to anyone traveling through the province.

Monte Gazlowe. Gazlowe is the pragmatic goblin engineer and overseer who established and rules the port town of Ratchet. After serving as the Horde's chief engineer during the founding of Durotar and Orgrimmar, he used his substantial earnings to build a bustling, neutral trading hub for the Steamwheedle Cartel. After securing a handsome payday for his engineering work with the new Horde, Gazlowe invested directly into the barren coastline, founding the port of Ratchet. Operating under the Steamwheedle Cartel, he runs the dockside town as a strictly neutral port where Horde, Alliance, and independent traders can barter freely—provided they keep their weapons sheathed and their purses heavy.

name.esES: Cubil del Horror de la Luna

text.enUS: Moon Horror Den. Moon Horror Den is a secluded, frost-rimed cave located just northeast of the goblin trading post of Everlook in Winterspring. Tucked against the jagged mountainside, the cavern serves as a nesting hollow for ferocious raging owlbeasts. Travelers must take care when venturing near its icy mouth, as these territorial wildkin fiercely defend their shelter. Situated only a short trek northeast from Everlook's guarded gates, the Moon Horror Den cuts deep into the mountain rock. The cave is home to powerful raging owlbeasts—formidable wildkin known for their brute strength and feral disposition in the harsh snows of Winterspring. Although geographically close to the furbolg settlement of Winterfall Village to the south, the sheer mountain face creates an impassable natural barrier, ensuring the den remains an isolated refuge for the wildkin rather than a corridor of travel.

Moon Priestess Amara. Moon Priestess Amara is a night elf priestess stationed along the main road west of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Flanked by loyal huntress guards, she keeps watch over the woodland pathways connecting the heart of the bough to the capital city of Darnassus. Stationed at a quiet wayside post west of Dolanaar, Moon Priestess Amara represents both the spiritual authority of the Sisterhood of Elune and the practical vigilance required to keep Teldrassil's roadways secure. She travels and watches with two huntress companions, Nhemai and Yaeliura. To travelers journeying westward, Amara acts as a guiding hand, directing adventurers along the road toward Darnassus and tasking those with burdened spirits to seek out paths of redemption.

Moonbrook. In southwestern Westfall, Moonbrook lies under Defias control, its streets emptied of peaceful residents. The Brotherhood uses the town as a guarded screen for its hidden headquarters in the Deadmines. Before the First War, Moonbrook stood at the heart of Westfall’s breadbasket, supporting farming families and the gold shafts of the Deadmines. The Old Horde razed the town, but it was rebuilt after the Second War. Its peace did not last. The House of Nobles in Stormwind neglected the settlement, and its military protection was stripped away. Unable to resist the red-masked bandits, Moonbrook’s people were driven from their homes. Citizens and teachers fled toward Sentinel Hill and Elwynn Forest.

name.esES: Espionaje en Arroyo de la Luna
