text.enUS: Moonbrook Espionage. Alba Fairmoon sends you to scout Moonbrook, where signs of industry trouble the Alliance. The poison found across Westfall does not seem to come from the lesser mines, so attention turns to the Deadmines beneath the town. The mines already examined across Westfall offer no answer to the poison spreading through the region. No known surface excavation appears to be its source. One major site remains unexplored: the vast shafts of the Deadmines, directly beneath Moonbrook’s ruined streets.

name.esES: Escuela de Arroyo de la Luna

text.enUS: Moonbrook Schoolhouse. In Moonbrook's northwestern corner, the schoolhouse stands abandoned under Defias occupation. A small graveyard lies behind the hall where Stalvan Mistmantle once taught local children. Moonbrook's schoolhouse once welcomed children before ruin and bandits overtook the town. After Stalvan Mistmantle began tutoring local children, the mayor commissioned him to run a school. Students filled the hall in Moonbrook's brighter days, when the town prospered. Now outlaws occupy the abandoned building, and weathered headstones in its rear cemetery look out over Westfall's decline.

Moonglade. Moonglade is an introductory rite of passage for young night elf druids learning to commune with the sacred lands of Kalimdor. Guided by Mathrengyl Bearwalker in Darnassus, novices learn the spell to magically transport themselves across the world into Moonglade to meet Dendrite Starblaze in Nighthaven. This marks the beginning of their spiritual journey toward mastering the strength of the bear form. Moonglade stands apart from the rest of Azeroth as an ancient sanctuary dedicated to the teachings of Cenarius. Under the watchful stewardship of Keeper Remulos, its tranquil groves provide peace and deep communion with nature. For a young druid, learning to project one's spirit across the land into Moonglade via the teleportation spell is a critical step, granting constant access to the heart of druidic wisdom regardless of mortal distances.

Moonglade. This quest marks a young tauren druid's introduction to Moonglade, the sacred sanctuary of Cenarion druidism. Guided by Turak Runetotem in Thunder Bluff, the initiate learns to traverse the waking world to commune directly with nature's ancient keepers. Moonglade stands apart from the turbulent politics of Kalimdor. Sheltered beneath primeval boughs and watched over by Keeper Remulos, the son of Cenarius, this ancient valley is a neutral refuge for all who walk the path of nature. Whether night elf or tauren, any druid who enters Nighthaven does so as an equal peer under the timeless mantle of the Cenarion Circle.

Moonglow Vest. Moonglow Vest is a trade training task offered by the night elf leatherworker Lotherias in Darnassus. Overwhelmed by the constant needs of young adventurers heading into the wilds of Kalimdor, she trades the knowledge of a specialized night elven tunic pattern in exchange for bulk shipments of embossed leather gear. In the sheltered boughs of Darnassus, tradesmen work tirelessly to outfit the swelling ranks of sentinels and aspiring wilderness scouts. As young night elves and allied wanderers venture forth beyond Teldrassil into a volatile Kalimdor, reliable armor is in fierce demand. Master leatherworkers like Lotherias bear the burden of keeping these frontiers supplied with sturdy hides.

Moonpetal Lily. Moonpetal Lilies are large, luminous flora native to Teldrassil that flourish around freshwater pools. Renowned for their potent restorative qualities, their petals are prized as key ingredients in natural remedies and healing draughts. Moonpetal Lilies grow exclusively along the moist banks of freshwater pools and ponds, particularly favored along the northwestern side of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Like much of the plant life flourishing atop the newly grown World Tree, they absorb the unique essence of Teldrassil's sheltered groves. Their broad petals are gentle and radiant, easily spotted hugging the tranquil water's edge where natural moisture allows them to thrive.

Moonshrine Ruins. The Moonshrine Ruins are a flooded expanse of ancient night elven architecture deep within Blackfathom Deeps. Once dedicated to the worship of Elune, these crumbling halls have been desecrated and seized by the Twilight's Hammer cult. Past the cavernous Pool of Ask'ar lies the Moonshrine Ruins, a somber testament to the night elves' ancient past along the Ashenvale coast. These partially submerged halls once rang with chants honoring the Moon Goddess Elune, but the Great Sundering shattered the temple and drowned its lower levels in sea water. Today, the murky waters churn with feral aquatic beasts, from aggressive crabs to serpentine threshadons, while the Twilight's Hammer cult maintains an active presence throughout the stones, bent on dark rituals that mock the shrine's sacred origin.

Moonshrine Sanctum. Moonshrine Sanctum is an ancient elven shrine deep within Blackfathom Deeps, now serving as the inner redoubt for the Twilight's Hammer cult. Presided over by Twilight Lord Kelris, the chamber houses a pristine monument to Queen Azshara and directly guards the sealed entrance to Aku'mai's lair. Situated just beyond the flooded Moonshrine Ruins, the Moonshrine Sanctum represents the central hub of cultist activity inside Blackfathom Deeps. Though originally built millennia ago by night elves to honor the moon and their rulers, the hall is now defiled by the Twilight's Hammer. Interestingly, the cultists have carefully maintained the towering effigy of Queen Azshara, seemingly untroubled by its subject. Under the watchful gaze of Twilight Lord Kelris, dark rituals are chanted day and night beneath the cavernous stone ceiling.

Moonspray. The Moonspray is an Alliance transport vessel belonging to the Kaldorei Fleet. It provides essential maritime passage across the waters separating mainland Kalimdor from the great World Tree, Teldrassil. The Moonspray serves as an indispensable lifeline between the docks of Auberdine on Darkshore's coast and Rut'theran Village at the root of Teldrassil. Traversing the Veiled Sea, the transport carries adventurers, couriers, and vital provisions between the isolated night elf sanctuary in the crown of the World Tree and the ancient mainland of Kalimdor.

Moonstalker Fang. Moonstalker Fangs are sharp canine teeth taken from the predatory moonstalkers roaming the misty woods of Darkshore. They are gathered by travelers assisting Wizbang Cranktoggle with the maintenance of his automated sampling devices. Moonstalkers are stealthy saber cats that haunt the forest fringes of Darkshore, stalking prey between the shadowed pines. Their elongated fangs serve as formidable hunting weapons, capable of shearing flesh and bone. For the eccentric gnome tinkerer Wizbang Cranktoggle, however, the teeth serve a very different mechanical purpose. Stationed north of Auberdine near the bridge, his automated contraption known as Buzzbox 323 is calibrated specifically to crush these durable fangs to dust as part of his erratic ecological surveys.

Moonwarden the Elder. Elder Moonwarden is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival, standing under a celestial beam of light at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Speaking with him offers travelers ancient wisdom and guidance toward other elders scattered throughout the continent. Standing amidst the dusty thoroughfare of the Crossroads, Elder Moonwarden appears bathed in a radiant column of heavenly light. He represents the ancient spirits revered during the Lunar Festival, a time when mortals pause their conflicts to pay homage to the wisdom of past generations.

Moonwell (Ashenvale). This secluded shrine, known to the night elves as the Moonwell of Purity, rests in central Ashenvale east of Iris Lake and west of Raynewood Retreat. Its blessed waters channel the grace of Elune to nourish the ancient forest and cleanse creeping foulness from the land. Alliance travelers following Raene Wolfrunner's research often seek out Shael'dryn, who keeps watch beside its tranquil basin. Tucked away beneath the canopy of central Ashenvale, this moonwell serves as a spiritual anchor for the kaldorei. Its luminescent waters tap into nature's latent magic and the light of the Moon Goddess. As the surrounding forest suffers from satyr corruption, fel taint, and logging incursions, pure shrines like this one become vital lifelines for those trying to heal the woods.

name.frFR: Tube d'eau du Puits de lune
name.ptBR: Tubo de Água do Poço Lunar

text.enUS: Moonwell Water Tube. A vial filled with consecrated water drawn from the moonwell in Auberdine. Its potent, purifying nature magic is used to test and react with a mysterious red crystal embedded along Darkshore's eastern ridges. Drawn directly from the shimmering moonwell resting in Auberdine, the Moonwell Water Tube contains liquid steeped in the blessed energies of Elune. Moonwells serve night elf settlements as sacred reservoirs of restorative magic and purity, rendering even a small phial remarkably potent against corruption or unknown mystical phenomena.

Mor'Ladim. Mor'Ladim is a dangerous, vengeful skeletal warrior wandering the grounds of Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. Formerly the noble knight Morgan Ladimore, he succumbed to profound grief and madness upon discovering the loss of his family, rising in undeath to slaughter anyone crossing his path. Before he became the terror of Raven Hill, Mor'Ladim lived as Morgan Ladimore, a devoted knight and defender of the helpless from Grand Hamlet—the town now known as Darkshire. Married at eighteen to his wife Lys, he raised three children in peace until war summoned him north. Morgan marched alongside Uther the Lightbringer to Lordaeron during the Third War, witnessing the downfall of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the spread of Kel'Thuzad's plague, and the tragic death of Uther himself.

Mor'rogal. Mor'rogal is a tauren resident of Sun Rock Retreat in the Stonetalon Mountains. He serves as an advisor and guide for travelers seeking glory and peril within the rugged subterranean reaches of the crags. Perched within the refuge of Sun Rock Retreat, Mor'rogal takes a keen interest in the deep crevices and caverns that cut through the Stonetalon Mountains. Recognizing that the region's twisting subterranean passes offer both great riches and lethal danger, he directs brave Horde wanderers to investigate troubled areas like the Boulderslide Ravine. For Mor'rogal, delving into these treacherous depths is not merely a matter of survival, but a test of spirit for those who follow their heart and soul in search of glory.

Mor'shan Rampart. The Mor'shan Rampart is a heavily fortified Horde barricade positioned at the northern border of the Barrens, guarding the entrance to Ashenvale. Constructed primarily by the Warsong clan, it shields Horde territory from night elf counterattacks while serving as a staging ground for incursions deeper into the forest. Standing at the northern terminus of the Gold Road, the Mor'shan Rampart marks the transition between the arid plains of the Barrens and the ancient canopies of Ashenvale. Built from heavy timber, defensive palisades, and fortified watchtowers, this bulwark was raised to stem the retaliatory strikes of night elven forces outraged by the Horde's logging operations. It acts both as a shield securing the northern gate to Kalimdor's interior and as a forward staging post for raiding parties pushing north toward Astranaar.

Morbent Fel. This quest is the final reckoning with Morbent Fel, the necromancer haunting the heights above Raven Hill Cemetery. Armed with the enchanted relic Morbent's Bane, heroes are sent by the grieving Sven Yorgen to shatter the sorcerer's wards and end his reign of terror over western Duskwood. Morbent Fel makes his lair in an abandoned house perched atop a rocky ridge just east of Sven's camp, overlooking the sprawl of Raven Hill Cemetery. From this grim vantage, the necromancer has directed waves of undead to terrorize the surrounding forest and defile the graves of Duskwood. Protected by formidable dark magic and attended by loyal undead thralls, he has remained untouchable to ordinary steel.

More Sparklematic Action. Deep within the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan stands the Sparklematic 5200, an automated cleaning apparatus left behind during the city's evacuation. For a small fee of silver, this machine vigorously scrubs salvageable curiosities from the muck and radioactive sludge coating the fallen capital. The Sparklematic 5200 represents the ingenious automated infrastructure gnomes installed throughout Gnomeregan before the trogg invasion and subsequent fallout. Even with toxic waste and hostile automatons filling the corridors, this contraption still performs its exact programming whenever provided with three silver coins and a grime-encrusted artifact.

More Wastewander Justice. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan now turns to the tougher Wastewander nomads: their rogues, assassins and shadow mages, to be found east and southeast of town. The fewer nomads left, the easier it will be to take back the water wells. You have done a good job so far, in Bilgewhizzle's view, but taking back the wells is best done against as few nomads as possible. Now the targets are the nomads' rogues, assassins and shadow mages, east and southeast of Gadgetzan. Bilgewhizzle admits they are a nasty lot, but says the wells are rightfully the company's.

Morgan Pestle. In Stormwind, Morgan Pestle runs Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. He works with his brother William Pestle in Goldshire, handling supplies and alchemical research for the capital. Morgan Pestle sells alchemical goods, reagents, and practical remedies at Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. His brother William keeps a workshop at the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire, while Morgan tends their family trade in the capital. He receives supplies from the rural heartlands, including candles sent by William.

Morgan Stern. Angus Stern of the Blue Recluse in Stormwind is putting together a new menu of rural dishes with a bayou theme. Angus has a nephew, Morgan, who was sent to Theramore to gather recipes from the locals, and wants word of what Morgan has found so far. Angus Stern believes the customers of the Blue Recluse will love a menu of rural dishes in the bayou style. To build it, Angus sent nephew Morgan off to Theramore, a city beside Dustwallow Marsh, to gather the locals' recipes. The trip is too long for Angus to make, so a young traveler like you is wanted to go and speak with Morgan.

Morgan the Collector. At the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, Morgan the Collector directs Defias extortion and gathering across Elwynn Forest. A high-ranking operative, he coordinates local theft from the farmhouse while Goldshire's guard keeps watch nearby. Morgan the Collector skims gold from Elwynn Forest's mines for the Defias Brotherhood. While common bandits harass travelers on the roads, he directs organized shakedowns and gathers stolen coin and supplies for the Brotherhood's wider network. His headquarters is the farmhouse at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, where loyal enforcers including Surena Caledon and Erlan Drudgemoor surround him.

Morgan's Plot. Morgan's Plot is a desolate burial ground and crumbling chapel tucked away just behind the tower of Karazhan in Deadwind Pass. Dominated by restless undead and brooding silence, it holds the forgotten crypts and final resting places of those once tied to Medivh's domain. Nestled against the sheer rocky slopes directly behind Karazhan, Morgan's Plot is a sorrowful, overgrown cemetery centered on a ruined chapel and underground crypts. Long before the land decayed into Deadwind Pass, the estate served the burial needs of the tower's inhabitants and nearby grounds. Following the downfall of the Last Guardian, Medivh, dark energies seeped into the earth, driving away all normalcy. Today, restless unliving wander the chapel grounds, haunting the headstones of servants and historic figures alike.

Morgan's Vigil. Morgan's Vigil is a ruined Alliance redoubt nestled in the southeastern heights of the Burning Steppes. Once a small village, its charred homes and shattered wizard's tower now serve as an austere forward camp for scouts watching the passes to Blackrock Mountain. It remains the sole Alliance foothold in an ash-choked land dominated by Dark Iron dwarves and Blackrock orcs. Perched upon high stone overlooking the fiery wastes, Morgan's Vigil was once a modest settlement before the horrors of the Burning Steppes overran it. Today, charred timbers and the cracked shell of a ruined mage tower stand as grim reminders of the onslaught. The remaining defenders make do beneath rough canvas tents pitched amid the soot. Despite the ruin, the camp retains a gryphon roost, offering an unbroken aerial link back across the mountains to Stormwind City. It serves as a desperately needed haven where scouts, marshals, and passing adventurers catch their breath away from the marauding warbands below.

Morganth. Morganth is the climactic quest concluding a long investigation by the mage Theocritus into a sinister rival perched in Redridge. Entrusted with stopping a dark warlock seeking an ancient relic of horrific power, adventurers must breach the Tower of Ilgalar and put an end to his machinations. From his sanctum at the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest, the mage Theocritus kept a vigilant scrying eye trained upon the crags of Redridge. What he observed confirmed his deepest anxieties: the warlock Morganth, holed up in the Tower of Ilgalar, was actively seeking the legendary Scythe of Elune. Realizing the warlock stood on the precipice of securing this dark might, Theocritus called upon bold Alliance champions to intervene before Morganth's shadow fell across the entire kingdom of Stormwind.

Morin Cloudstalker. Morin Cloudstalker is a tauren scout keeping watch along the road leading east from Bloodhoof Village toward the Barrens in Mulgore. Standing vigil over the plains, he monitors local trade routes and investigates the encroaching threats endangering tauren travelers. Positioned beside the dirt path winding east toward the Barrens, Morin Cloudstalker acts as both a scout and a guardian for travelers through Mulgore. The grassy plains here are usually peaceful, but the opening of trade routes and shifting territories have drawn opportunists and bandits dangerously close to the heart of the tauren homeland.

Morlos'Aran. Morlos'Aran is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in the southern reaches of Felwood. Once a proud and thriving settlement before the Great Sundering, it now stands as a grim monument to a lost golden age, drowned under the demonic blight that plagues the surrounding forest. Ten thousand years ago, prior to the Sundering, Morlos'Aran was a grand urban center of the ancient kaldorei civilization. Much like sister settlements such as Ameth'Aran, Bashal'Aran, and Ordil'Aran across northern Kalimdor, its marble arches and moonlit plazas bustled with elven life and arcana. When the Well of Eternity collapsed, the city broke, leaving only shattered colonnades behind as monuments to their civilization's zenith.

Morningdew the Elder. Morningdew the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit visited during the Lunar Festival in Thousand Needles. Illuminated by a radiant beam of starlight, she offers ancient wisdom and directs pilgrims toward other elders scattered across Kalimdor. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient ancestors manifest across Azeroth to share their blessings with travelers. Elder Morningdew appears bathed in a shaft of lunar light, standing out starkly against the dusty red stone and noisy industrial hubbub of Thousand Needles. She reminds mortal travelers to look beyond earthly concerns to the starry expanse above.

Mortality Wanes. Deep within the hostile briars of Razorfen Kraul, a dying night elf named Heralath Fallowbrook whispers his final plea to passing Alliance adventurers. Stripped of his strength and life, he asks only that his wife's stolen pendant of bonding be recovered and brought home to Darnassus alongside news of his demise. Razorfen Kraul is a perilous redoubt overrun by savage quilboar and dark magic, far from Alliance territory. Among these treacherous brambles lies Heralath Fallowbrook, mortally wounded and fading fast. With his dying strength, he manages only broken whispers, revealing that a brave dwarf named Lonebrow was sent ahead to deliver a warning to Falfindel. Heralath, however, knows he will never leave the Kraul alive.

Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. The Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound is a fortified cavern complex in northern Stranglethorn Vale, situated just south of the ruins of Zul'Gurub. It serves as the primary stronghold for the brute Mosh'Ogg tribe in the jungle, dominated by their ruthless ogre mage chieftain, Mai'Zoth. Carved into the rugged jungle ridges south of Zul'Gurub, the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound swarms with brutish Mosh'Ogg maulers, shamans, and warmongers. The ogres seized the cavernous network as an ideal redoubt against hostile jungle trolls and prowling beasts.

Mosshide Fen. Mosshide Fen is a swampy, treacherous tract in the eastern Wetlands overrun by the Mosshide gnoll tribe. Dotted with primitive encampments, it is one of the most perilous regions for travelers venturing off the main trade roads. Sprawling across the murky eastern reaches of the Wetlands, Mosshide Fen serves as the primary domain of the aggressive Mosshide gnolls. The swamp here is dense and tangled, dotted with rough lean-tos and bone-strewn camps. Under the vicious command of pack leaders like Gnawbone, the gnolls fiercely guard their muddy claims, readily ambushing and devouring any travelers, scouts, or prospectors foolish enough to wander into their hunting grounds.

Mossy Tumor. A mossy tumor is a foul, poisonous growth carved from the bark and flesh of corrupted timberlings on Teldrassil. Found primarily around Wellspring Lake, these growths serve as outward signs of an unnerving malevolence spreading through the newly grown World Tree. The timberlings of Teldrassil were created to nurture and tend the boughs of the great tree, but many have turned hostile and diseased. These mossy tumors are physical manifestations of this inner sickness. Heavily laden with toxins, the growths sprout across the bodies of Mire Beasts, Tramplers, and Elder Timberlings that prowl Wellspring Lake. Rellian Greenspyre and the keepers in Darnassus have tasked travelers with severing the tumors so they may be thoroughly burned, preventing their poison from taking deeper root in the island's soil.

Motega Firemane. Motega Firemane is a tauren scholar stationed at Whitereach Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to cataloging the dangerous wildlife of the canyon, he finds his studies disrupted by a vengeful wind serpent spirit and the reckless misadventures of his young assistant. Four years following the Third War, Motega Firemane journeyed south into Thousand Needles to observe and record the distinct beasts surviving among the towering mesas. Accompanied by his youthful assistant, Pao'ka Swiftmountain—whose protective father was reluctant to let him leave Mulgore—Motega set up camp alongside Kanati Greycloud at Whitereach Post. While his original calling was quiet natural observation, the harsh perils of the canyon floor continually demand a more martial approach to survival.

Mountain Giant Muisek. Witch Doctor Uzer'i calls this the last job and sends you northwest to find the final enemy: mountain giants, whose size and strength Uzer'i is eager to harness. In Uzer'i's telling, the mountain giants came down out of the mountains to help the night elves once the Burning Legion arrived in the world. They are easy to know by their sheer size and the tremors underfoot on their rocky ground. Uzer'i is eager to harness power on that scale. Uzer'i wants seven Land Walkers or Cliff Giants brought down, each one shrunk and captured with the Muisek Vessel.

Mountain Lion Blood. Mountain Lion Blood is a reagent collected from the prowling predators of the Hillsbrad Foothills and the snowy slopes of Alterac. Apothecary Lydon of Tarren Mill seeks this fresh blood to formulate the Royal Apothecary Society's dreaded Elixir of Pain. The highlands and foothills flanking Hillsbrad and Alterac are prowled by feral and starving mountain lions. While ordinary hunters seek these predators for their pelts and claws, the Forsaken of the Royal Apothecary Society find value in what pumps through their veins. Fresh mountain lion blood possesses specific biological properties that Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill believes will serve as the base for a potent new toxic brew designed to bring misery to the living.

Mountaineer Barleybrew. Mountaineer Barleybrew is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at the South Gate Outpost in Dun Morogh. Guarding the pass leading eastward toward Loch Modan, he relies on hearty dwarven brews to keep sentries alert in the biting cold. Perched at the South Gate Outpost guarding the snowy roadway toward Loch Modan, Mountaineer Wellart Barleybrew stands as part of Ironforge's border watch. Like many mountaineers serving in the bitter winds of Dun Morogh, he appreciates the fortifying qualities of fine dwarven drink. Bearing the name of the renowned Barleybrew clan, he helps see to it that shipments of potent Shimmer Stout make their way to fellow watchmen who need warmth and stamina during long shifts along the mountain passes.

Mountaineer Kadrell. Mountaineer Kadrell is a stalwart dwarven sentry stationed across from the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Serving as a crucial liaison within the Loch Modan Mountaineers, he coordinates reconnaissance, supply deliveries, and border defense across the region. Standing watch in the bustling settlement of Thelsamar, Mountaineer Kadrell acts as an anchor for dwarven defenses throughout Loch Modan. While outposts on the valley's fringes face relentless pressure from troggs, gnolls, and native beasts, Kadrell remains at the center of town to organize reinforcements, relay orders, and assess incoming field reports from wandering scouts.

Mountaineer Stormpike. Mountaineer Stormpike is an Ironforge mountaineer stationed at Algaz Station in northern Loch Modan. Watching over the mountain pass leading toward the Wetlands, he works tirelessly to keep vital supply routes safe from lurking troggs and kobolds. As a proud member of the Stormpike clan, his loyalty lies squarely with Ironforge and the safety of dwarven lands. Perched along the northern border of Loch Modan, Algaz Station serves as a critical checkpoint before the perilous descent into the Wetlands. Mountaineer Stormpike is stationed here amid rocky crags and constant wilderness threats. His primary duty is maintaining the line of communication and keeping the roads open for travelers and supply convoys traversing through Dun Algaz.

text.enUS: Mountaineer Stormpike's Task. Mountaineer Stormpike's Task is a brief Alliance courier dispatch in Loch Modan. Mountaineer Kadrell directs roving adventurers to the northern watchtower, where Mountaineer Stormpike requires a reliable runner for an assignment beyond the valley. It serves as an introduction to a longer errand that reaches into neighboring lands. Patrolling the roads and outposts of Loch Modan leaves the Mountaineers stretched thin against trogg incursions and roving wildlife. Mountaineer Kadrell frequently points capable travelers toward guards who cannot abandon their posts. Mountaineer Stormpike, stationed high in the northern guard tower, finds himself tied down by watch duties just when urgent private business requires a messenger to venture far beyond the region's borders.

Mountaineer Thalos. Mountaineer Thalos is a dwarven sentry stationed at the Coldridge Valley mouth of Coldridge Pass. Tasked with guarding the route, he warns travelers about the sudden trogg infestation choking the tunnel. Adventurers carrying urgent reports from the valley rely on him to point the way safely toward Kharanos. Perched on the snowy border where Coldridge Valley gives way to the deeper crags of Dun Morogh, Mountaineer Thalos serves as the first line of defense for travelers leaving the dwarven training grounds. Coldridge Pass has become a treacherous chokepoint overrun by hostile troggs who have burrowed up from the subterranean depths. Thalos stands vigil in the cold, warning the unready to turn back and assessing whether hardy couriers possess the grit to fight their way through to the wider kingdom.

Mr. Smite. Mr. Smite is the imposing tauren first mate serving aboard the Defias Brotherhood's flagship deep inside the Deadmines. An expert weaponmaster under Captain Greenskin, he commands the dockside approach to the hidden juggernaut with ruthless discipline. Intruders who face him must contend with his shifting arsenal and devastating physical strength. Guarding the docks of Ironclad Cove, Mr. Smite serves as first mate to the goblin Captain Greenskin. While the Defias Brotherhood is predominantly composed of disenfranchised humans and allied goblin tinkerers, Smite stands as a striking anomaly: a massive, battle-hardened tauren far from the plains of Kalimdor. Tasked with maintaining strict order among a rowdy pirate crew, he ensures that the labor fitting out Edwin VanCleef's secret dreadnaught proceeds without disruption.

Mudrock Soup and Bugs. In Theramore, Morgan Stern is working on a dish called Mudrock Soup and Bugs, which could be the next big thing at the inns of Stormwind City. Morgan Stern doubts they would survive a long trek through Dustwallow Marsh, and so asks you to gather tongues from the Mudrock turtles. Morgan Stern is working on a dish called Mudrock Soup and Bugs, and still needs the major ingredients. A long trek through Dustwallow Marsh is more than Morgan Stern expects to survive, so you are asked to do some hunting. First come the tongues of Mudrock turtles.

Mudsnout Blossom. Mudsnout Blossoms are pungent, toxic fungal growths found sprouting in Nethander Stead in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Guarded by local gnolls and harvested by the Royal Apothecary Society, these foul mushrooms are used in Apothecary Lydon's elixir research. Despite their floral name, Mudsnout Blossoms are actually large, foul-smelling mushrooms that flourish primarily in the soiled dirt of Nethander Stead, south of Tarren Mill. They grow amidst the camps of the local Mudsnout gnolls, who defend the territory fiercely. To living organisms, the spores and flesh of the mushroom act as a virulent poison, causing agony and rapid biological deterioration.

Mudsnout Composite. Mudsnout Composite is an alchemical paste prepared by Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill from harvested Mudsnout Blossoms. It serves as an essential base ingredient carried to the Undercity for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a new plague. Crafted in the field by Apothecary Lydon, this fine composite is derived directly from Mudsnout Blossoms gathered in the Hillsbrad Foothills. While noxious on its own, the mash requires a specialized colloid of decay—concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell himself—to activate its more lethal qualities. Once bound, the mixture forms a key chemical component in the development of the Dark Lady's Elixir of Agony.

Mudsnout Mixture. Mudsnout Mixture is a toxic alchemical base concocted by Master Apothecary Faranell in the Undercity. Created by blending a mudsnout composite with an alchemical colloid of decay, it serves as the foundation for the Royal Apothecary Society's deadly Elixir of Agony. When Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill seeks to craft a virulent new biological weapon, he sends a base composite of Mudsnout Blossoms, toxic mushrooms from the gnoll-held Nethander Stead, north to the Undercity. Impressed by the composite's potential, Master Apothecary Faranell introduces his own colloid of decay into the blend, producing the volatile Mudsnout Mixture. The solution stabilizes the mushroom compound while readying its virulent properties for further catalytic refinement back in the foothills.

Mull Thunderhorn. Mull Thunderhorn is a tauren elder residing in Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Deeply devoted to the Earth Mother and the balance of the land, he watches over the sacred water wells scattered across the plains. As outside exploiters threaten the region's lifegiving waters, Mull guides young tauren through the rituals required to cleanse the ancestral springs. Standing watch in Bloodhoof Village, Mull Thunderhorn carries the weight of Mulgore's spiritual well-being. The nomadic tribes have gathered under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof to establish a permanent home, yet their lands are already under siege by greed and reckless expansion. Mull serves as a spiritual anchor for the young braves stepping out of Camp Narache, calling upon them to safeguard the vital resources of their ancestors.

Mupsi Shacklefridd. Mupsi Shacklefridd is a goblin resident stationed just outside the port town of Ratchet in the Barrens. She serves as a local contact for travelers looking to smooth over troubled relations with the Steamwheedle Cartel. Mupsi Shacklefridd operates just outside Ratchet along the dusty coastal roads of the Barrens. Life near the port town is always busy, with Steamwheedle guards patrolling the perimeter and merchants coming and going. For those who find themselves in poor standing with the goblins, Mupsi provides a path to reconciliation—provided travelers are willing to offer the supplies and labor the cartel demands.

Mura Runetotem. This quest entrusts a traveler with a sample of altered snapjaw shell from the Barrens to deliver to Mura Runetotem in Silverpine Forest. It bridges the healing efforts of the tauren across continents, connecting the strange vitality of Kalimdor's plains to the blighted lands of the Forsaken. While investigating the bizarre, magically mutated wildlife surrounding the lush oases in the Barrens, Tonga Runetotem notices something peculiar about the altered snapjaws. Despite their corruption, their shells pulse with vibrant, resilient energy. Believing this strange vitality could serve a greater purpose, Tonga asks an adventurer to carry a shell across the Great Sea to his clanmate, Mura Runetotem, stationed in the Eastern Kingdoms.

Muradin Bronzebeard. Muradin Bronzebeard was the brother of King Magni Bronzebeard and Brann Bronzebeard, as well as a renowned warrior, diplomat, and co-founder of the Explorers' League. Revered across Khaz Modan and Lordaeron alike, he is believed to have died in the frozen wastes of Northrend when Prince Arthas Menethil claimed the cursed runeblade Frostmourne. Muradin fought with distinction during the Second War, acting as the vital liaison between the mountain halls of Khaz Modan and the Alliance of Lordaeron. He helped hold Ironforge during the Horde's siege and marched alongside Alliance forces all the way through Blackrock Spire to the Dark Portal. In the peaceful years that followed, Muradin settled into Capital City as Ironforge’s official ambassador. Jovial yet formidable, he became a fixture in the palace, growing close to King Terenas Menethil and taking it upon himself to tutor young Prince Arthas in the arts of swordplay and combat.

Murdaloc. Agmond's battered remains lie in the Badlands, and a name is scrawled in the sandstone beside the dead hand: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be put down, with word carried back to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan. Agmond's trail comes in from the west, and the blood smeared over stone and sand tells how far the dwarf crawled before dying here. Beside the lifeless hand, scratched into the Badlands sandstone, is a single word: Murdaloc. Agmond's killer is to be slain, along with a number of Stonevault Bonesnappers, and the news taken to Prospector Ironband in Loch Modan.

Muren Stormpike. Muren Stormpike is an introductory quest for developing Alliance warriors, given once a recruit proves their basic mettle in Dun Morogh. Directed by Granis Swiftaxe in Kharanos, the young fighter travels into the mountain city of Ironforge to seek formal instruction in martial discipline. Meeting Muren marks the beginning of deeper training in tactical stances and dwarven military traditions. After cutting their teeth against local threats in the snowy valleys of Dun Morogh, warrior novices catch the eye of Granis Swiftaxe in Kharanos. Recognizing that crude skirmishing can only take a brawler so far, Swiftaxe sends promising fighters to the heart of dwarven martial prowess: the Military Ward of Ironforge. There, within the echoing halls of the forge-city, senior combatants oversee the formal schooling of those bound for battle.

Murloc. Murlocs are amphibious, bipedal humanoids famous for their gurgling battle cries, territorial coastal villages, and sudden swarming tactics. Though historically dwelling in the deep ocean, they have steadily migrated inland along the shores, lakes, and rivers of Azeroth, acting with far greater coordination and cunning than their primitive appearance suggests. Murlocs dwell in densely populated settlements along coastlines, riverbanks, and freshwater lakes. Averaging roughly four feet in height, they possess bulbous, slime-coated bodies, wide mouths filled with sharp fangs, and keen vision capable of piercing pitch-black water. While individuals are rarely seen wandering far from their kin, encountering one murloc invariably means a dozen more lurk just beneath the surface. They rely on overwhelming numbers and sharp crude weaponry.

Murloc Gills. Alba Fairmoon sends Alliance help to Westfall's Longshore to gather murloc gills. She fears the crop blight may reach the Great Sea, and the gills could reveal whether the coastal waters are tainted. Westfall is already near ruin, with crops failing, farmers displaced, and bandits roaming the roads. Alba Fairmoon fears the blight may be draining from inland fields into the Great Sea. If the coast is tainted, the fish that feed Westfall's poor and grace Stormwind City's tables could vanish. That loss could tip an already strained kingdom into outright famine.

Murloc Head. Murloc Heads are grim trophies severed from the amphibious creatures prowling the Western Strand in Hillsbrad Foothills. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle of Southshore requires them as physical proof of culled threats to satisfy his superior, Marshal Redpath. Southshore faces dangers from all directions, but the aggressive murlocs clustering along the Western Strand are an immediate menace to local fishermen and coastal travelers. Although Alliance adventurers frequently sweep the beaches to cull the creatures, Marshal Marcus Redpath demands undeniable verification before signing off on defensive reports. To humor the bureaucracy, Lieutenant Farren Orinelle relies on hired fighters to haul in cold, dripping murloc heads—an unpleasant task Farren himself finds entirely repulsive, especially given how thoroughly the sight has spoiled his appetite for Southshore's local seafood.

Murloc Poachers. Dockmaster Baren of Lakeshire needs adventurers to thin the swelling ranks of murlocs along Lake Everstill before they deplete the town's primary food source. What begins as a practical pest-control bounty raises an unsettling ecological question: why are coastal creatures settling so deep into the inland mountains? Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, keeping the mountain town fed and supplying its market with fresh catches. When large tribes of murlocs began dropping anchor along the shallows, Dockmaster Baren realized the town faced an ecological crisis. The ravenous fish-men were aggressively scouring the waters, threatening to wipe out the local fish populations entirely if left unchecked.

Musquash Root. Beneath the Stonewrought Dam, Musquash Root grows in the Wetlands. The rare root is hard to gather, and a hidden coven beneath Stormwind needs it for a brew. Musquash Root grows in the damp ground beneath the Stonewrought Dam's falls. The mist and secluded setting make it hard to gather. Few herbalists seek it, but practitioners of the darker arts prize its chemical and alchemical properties.

Mutanus the Devourer. Mutanus the Devourer is a monstrous, pale murloc manifested directly from the Emerald Nightmare. Lurking in the darkest recesses of the sleeping druid Naralex's mind, it emerges to devour anyone attempting to break the Nightmare's hold over the Wailing Caverns. Slaying this twisted aberration is the final step in freeing Naralex from his tormented slumber. When the night elf druid Naralex tapped into the underground springs beneath the Barrens, he aimed to restore life to the arid wastes by connecting them to the Emerald Dream. Instead, an ancient corruption known as the Emerald Nightmare invaded his thoughts. Trapped in an agonizing vision, Naralex's subconscious fears took physical form. The corruption gave that nightmare the shape of an immense, albino murloc.

Mux Manascrambler. Mux Manascrambler is an eccentric goblin engineer dwelling in the desert outpost of Gadgetzan. Unlike many of his peers focused strictly on explosives or mining equipment, Mux harbors a peculiar fascination with the supernatural and occult energies. Tucked away inside a building in central Gadgetzan, behind Driz Plunkbow and his clanking Butcherbots, sits Mux Manascrambler. While the Steamwheedle Cartel trades heavily in oil, guns, and salvage, Mux focuses his ingenuity on more esoteric pursuits: the realm of spirits and supernatural anomalies. He uses his technical acumen to design bizarre devices capable of detecting, distilling, and interacting with spectral remnants, bridging crude goblin craftsmanship with the invisible worlds of the dead.

Mydrannul. Mydrannul is a night elf general goods vendor stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. He serves the capital's sentinels, soldiers, and visitors by keeping basic supplies, munitions, and provisions readily available. Located among the military pavilions and training grounds of the Warrior's Terrace, Mydrannul provides essential gear to Darnassus's defenders and traveling adventurers alike. His wares include the practical everyday items needed for life in the field: ammunition for archers and gunners, throwing blades, flint, pouches, and simple rations. By tending his stall in the city's martial district, he ensures that the sentinels and trainees preparing for duty on Teldrassil do not want for basic sundries.

Mysterious Fossil. The Mysterious Fossil is an ancient specimen unearthed along the coast of Darkshore by Prospector Remtravel. Its curious characteristics have drawn the intense curiosity of the dwarven Explorers' League, prompting scholars to shuttle it across the sea to uncover its hidden secrets. While conducting fieldwork among the wild shores of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel uncovered a fossil unlike the common petrified stone scattered across Kalimdor. Deeming it of monumental historical importance, Remtravel arranged for the specimen to be delivered to dwarven scholars rather than let it languish in the wilderness. When brought before Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker in Darnassus, the relic immediately stood out as an extraordinary find.

Mystic Ward. The Mystic Ward is the northwestern district of Ironforge, serving as the dwarven capital's quiet sanctuary for spiritual devotion and arcane study. Distinguishable by its cool, pale blue banners and quiet halls, it stands in stark contrast to the clanging anvils of the nearby Great Forge. Its grandest structure, the Hall of Mysteries, gathers priests, paladins, and mages beneath cavernous stone arches. While dwarves are famed across Azeroth for their prowess at the forge and on the battlefield, the Mystic Ward represents the kingdom's quieter intellectual and spiritual pursuits. Marked by pale blue heraldry, this cavernous quarter connects the bustling Commons to the Forlorn Cavern and the Great Forge. Within its reaches, merchants supply scholars and spellweavers with regalia, scrolls, and alchemical reagents from shops like The Fighting Wizard and Maeva's Mystical Apparel. Dominating the district is the majestic Hall of Mysteries, where the holy disciplines of the Holy Light intersect with the practiced arts of arcane magic, offering guidance to those who wield unseen powers in defense of the Alliance.

Mystral Lake. Mystral Lake is the largest body of water in Ashenvale, resting in the south-central forest just below Silverwind Refuge. Its deep waters draw travelers from both the Alliance and the Horde. Spanning a vast expanse south of Silverwind Refuge and east of Talondeep Vale, Mystral Lake is the largest lake in Ashenvale. The night elves keep watch over it from their outpost at Silverwind Refuge on its northern shore, and travelers from both the Horde and the Alliance frequently find their journeys pulling them to its banks.

Myzrael's Allies. Myzrael cries out that she is free, and that she will gather her strength in hiding from her captors. She calls you a noble ally and sends you to Gerrig Bonegrip in a shop of Ironforge's Forlorn Cavern, who knows how she can be summoned. Myzrael is free, and means to gather strength hidden from her captors, since if they met her now they would surely overpower her and lock her away again. In time she means to face the giants, and she swears they will rue having held her. She calls you a noble ally and says she will need your help again, to summon her to the surface when she is ready.

Myzrael's Allies. Myzrael speaks through the keystone, declaring herself free but in hiding from her captors, and tells you to speak with Zaruk in Hammerfall, who knows how she can be summoned. Myzrael cries out that she is free. For now she must gather her strength out of sight of her captors, because if they faced her today they would overpower and imprison her again. In time, she vows, she will confront the giants who held her, and they will regret keeping her.

NG-5. NG-5 is the shorthand designation for Nitromirglyceronium, a notoriously volatile chemical compound. Procured for the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains, it serves as the essential catalyst for his explosive engineering schemes. Known formally as Nitromirglyceronium, NG-5 is an exceptionally hazardous chemical solution handled only with extreme caution—or reckless gnomish enthusiasm. Gaxim Rustfizzle, an operative stationed in the Stonetalon Mountains, requires the substance as a critical ignition compound. According to Gaxim, NG-5 provides the exact reaction necessary to detonate entire wagons loaded with dynamite, orchestrating a massive explosion meant to serve as a chaotic distraction against his adversaries in the region.

Naga. The naga are a monstrous, serpentine race dwelling beneath the ocean's depths, ruled by their ancient empress, Queen Azshara. Once the Highborne elite of the Kaldorei Empire, they were warped into amphibious horrors during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago. Recently emerging from the dark waters, they have seized shorelines across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms to reclaim their forgotten surface empire. Ten millennia ago, the Highborne nobility of the Kaldorei Empire ruled supreme from their grand capital of Zin-Azshari. Consumed by an obsession with arcane power, Queen Azshara and her inner court tapped the Well of Eternity to draw the gaze of the Dark Titan Sargeras, inviting the catastrophic invasion known as the War of the Ancients. When the Well of Eternity collapsed into ruin, triggering the Great Sundering, the palace slipped into the crushing abyss. Facing utter annihilation, Azshara bargained with the malevolent Old Gods deep below. In exchange for survival, she and her followers were transformed into cold, scaly, serpentine beings bound to the deeps.

name.frFR: Des nagas sur la grève de Zoram

text.enUS: Naga at the Zoram Strand. Naga at the Zoram Strand is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with culling the aggressive serpentine invaders along northwestern Ashenvale's coastline. Stationed at Zoram'gar Outpost, the troll Marukai seeks to secure the contested coast by driving the Wrathtail naga away from the sunken ruins of ancient Zoram. The Horde's presence on the Zoram Strand is tenuous. Surrounded by hostile night elf territory and bitter woodland skirmishes in Ashenvale, the outpost provides a vital coastal connection. However, the unexpected emergence of aggressive naga crawling ashore threatens to cut the Horde off from the sea and overrun the small defensive garrison before their position can be fully fortified.

Nak's Skull. Nak's Skull is a grisly hunting trophy severed from Nak, one of three prominent Razormane quilboar commanders directing warbands in the southern Barrens. Taken as proof of the raider's defeat, it is sought by the captive quilboar Mangletooth to avenge a bitter tribal betrayal. Emerging from Razorfen Kraul, the trio consisting of Nak, Kuz, and Lok Orcbane launched vicious raids targeting Horde settlements and roadways across the Barrens. Unknown to the defenders at the Crossroads, these warlords were orchestrating attacks far more cunning than typical tribal skirmishing. When the Razormane prisoner Mangletooth was abandoned to die in a cage at Camp Taurajo, his thirst for retribution turned against his former brethren. Demanding physical proof of Nak's demise, Mangletooth asks Horde adventurers to deliver the severed skull alongside those of his cohorts to break the back of the southern raiding parties.

Nalpak. Nalpak is a tauren druid disciple who watches over the troubled Wailing Caverns in the Barrens. Stationed in the high cliff-cave overlooking the cavern entrance, he enlists passing adventurers to help contain the nightmare twisting the subterranean ecosystem. Perched inside a hidden cavern directly above the mouth of the Wailing Caverns, Nalpak remains loyal to the vision of Naralex. While his master lies trapped in a corrupted slumber deep below, Nalpak works to keep the spreading corruption at bay. He asks adventurers to gather deviate hides for use as leather.

Nara Meideros. In Stormwind's Park, Nara Meideros guides young seekers in Elune's teachings. As a night elf priestess in the human capital, she offers a familiar spiritual presence to her kin. Nara Meideros serves Elune far from Kalimdor, across the Great Sea in Stormwind City. In the Park, night elf druids and priests have tended a green refuge. Nara guides young seekers in devotion to the Moon Goddess. Human priests serve the Holy Light in nearby Cathedral Square, while Nara gives night elves visiting or living in the Eastern Kingdoms a connection to their own faith.

Nara Wildmane. Nara Wildmane is a young tauren druid in Thunder Bluff seeking to unravel the tragedy unfolding deep within the Wailing Caverns. After Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem peered into the Emerald Dream and withdrew from the corruption festering there, he dispatched adventurers to confer with Nara, whose fierce spirit endured long enough to witness the nightmare taking hold of their kin. She serves as the pivotal Horde contact directing champions to put an end to the Druids of the Fang. When strange, unnatural phenomena began spreading across the Barrens, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem journeyed into the Emerald Dream to discern the cause. There he witnessed a cult of druids who had originally sought to restore life to the arid savannah, only to lose their minds to a vile taint. Being aged and unable to linger long against the nightmare's assault, Hamuul fled back to the waking world. However, his younger disciple, Nara Wildmane, refused to yield so easily. Her fiery resolve kept her anchored in the dreamscape far longer, allowing her to observe the transformed cult firsthand.

Narain Soothfancy. Narain Soothfancy is an eccentric gnome dwelling in a secluded beach hut just north of Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris. While he loudly advertises himself as a master soothsayer capable of divining the future, those who know him consider his psychic talents a complete farce compared to his genuine engineering genius. Perched on the eastern coast of Tanaris just north of the goblin docks, Narain Soothfancy lives as a retired engineer turned self-proclaimed master fortune teller. He routinely greets visitors by pressing unopened envelopes against his forehead or making wildly inaccurate guesses about their business, such as wondering if they have arrived seeking the legendary Ashbringer. Despite his theatrical charade, Narain possesses deep technical knowledge. Even ancient beings like the blue dragon Azuregos note that while Narain is a terrible psychic, his engineering aptitude is undeniably brilliant. A handbook titled 'Soothsaying for Dummies' rests nearby.

Naralex. Naralex is a night elf druid who sought to restore the parched Barrens to a lush forest using the powers of the Emerald Dream. Instead, his slumber was overtaken by a dark nightmare, twisting the Wailing Caverns beneath the earth and turning his followers into venomous fiends. Long before the Great Sundering, the sun-scorched plains of the Barrens were once a vibrant forest. Viewing this loss as a tragedy, Naralex journeyed to the Barrens with a cohort of devoted disciples to reverse the drought. Deep beneath the savannah, he discovered an intricate subterranean network of underground springs and rushing geysers, naming them the Wailing Caverns after the howling wind and steam that moaned through the rock. He believed that by entering a deep trance and channeling the pristine energies of the Emerald Dream into these subterranean waters, the life-giving flow would reach the surface and cause the entire wasteland to bloom.

Nat Pagle. Nat Pagle is widely hailed as the most renowned angler in all of Azeroth, despite claiming he only fishes as an excuse to drink heavily. He makes his home on a secluded inlet in Dustwallow Marsh, where he trains elite anglers from both the Alliance and the Horde who manage to prove their patience. Though his name is synonymous with angling mastery across the known world, Nat Pagle is remarkably casual about his craft. Having cast lines for several decades, he often admits he has no great reverence for the sport itself, famously calling it little more than a convenient excuse to sit back and drink heavily. Despite this gruff nonchalance, Nat understands aquatic life and the art of angling better than anyone alive, even licensing fishing gear sought out by professionals.

Nat's Landing. Nat's Landing is a modest fishing outpost nestled along the shores of Dustwallow Bay in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the personal camp and retreat of Nat Pagle, widely regarded as the most famous angler on Azeroth. Adventurers from across the world seek out this humble dock to hone their mastery of the fishing craft. Tucked away southwest of Theramore Isle along the murky waters of Dustwallow Bay, Nat's Landing is little more than a weathered campsite. It consists of a simple canvas tent, drying racks heavy with the day's catch, extra tackle hung from trees, and a rickety wooden pier jutting into the bay. Despite the mists and hazards of the swamp, this quiet patch of shoreline provides the legendary angler Nat Pagle with a solitary place to cast his line and enjoy a quiet drink away from civilization's clamor.

Natalia Mar'alith. Mistress Natalia Mar'alith is a night elf priestess and Cenarion Circle researcher lost deep within the silithid nests of Hive'Regal. Once part of the expedition investigating Silithus alongside her husband, Commander Mar'alith, she has succumbed completely to the maddening influence of the Old Gods. When the Cenarion Circle established their outpost at Cenarion Hold to monitor the awakening sands, Natalia accompanied her husband, Commander Mar'alith, into the wastes. Eager to unravel the mystery behind the resurgence of the silithid and the ancient Qiraji ruins, she joined an exploratory party led by the famed explorer Brann Bronzebeard, accompanied by the dwarven researchers Rutgar Glyphshaper and Frankal Stonebridge.

Nathanos Blightcaller. Nathanos Blightcaller, once Nathanos Marris, stands at his ruined homestead in the Eastern Plaguelands as the deadly champion of Queen Sylvanas Windrunner. In life he was the first and only human Ranger Lord of Quel'Thalas, and in undeath he trains Forsaken hunters while guarding the eastern frontier with biting contempt for all who approach. Before the Third War, Nathanos Marris was an extraordinary marksman and tactical genius hailing from the rural outskirts of Lordaeron. Trained by the high elves of Quel'Thalas and close to Sylvanas Windrunner, he became the only human to ever attain the prestigious rank of Ranger Lord. His home remained the family estate in Lordaeron, the Marris Stead.

Natural Materials. Witch Doctor Uzer'i in Camp Mojache needs materials to complete an endeavor, to be gathered alongside the other trials: splintered logs, encrusted minerals, resilient sinew and metallic fragments, taken from treants, mountain giants, faerie dragons, owlbeasts and hippogryphs. After you return to Witch Doctor Uzer'i, a further list of materials awaits, to be collected alongside the other trials. Two splintered logs are needed from a Feralas treant. Six pieces of encrusted minerals are found on mountain giants and faerie dragons, westward. Twenty pieces of resilient sinew come from owlbeasts in the Hinterlands or hippogryphs in Feralas. A large amount of metallic fragments, forty in all, can come from any of these creatures.

Nature's Call. Nature's Call is a Shadowglen quest where the dryad Tarindrella seeks to uncover why the local Gnarlpine furbolgs suddenly turned against their long-standing night elf allies. By gathering carved totems from their abandoned camps, adventurers help reveal the distressing spiritual corruption spreading through Teldrassil. Nature's Call is an investigative mission in Shadowglen given by the dryad Tarindrella. Refusing to believe that the Gnarlpine furbolg would abandon centuries of friendship with the night elves without reason, she asks travelers to comb through the furbolgs' hastily abandoned camps along the western border of the glen to recover intact engraved totems.

Need for a Cure. Stranded along the rugged cliffs of northwestern Durotar, the Darkspear troll Rhinag lies poisoned by a venomtail scorpid. With precious little time before the toxin finishes him, he relies on a courier to sprint to Orgrimmar and retrieve a cure from Kor'ghan. The arid canyons of Durotar are crawling with venomtail scorpids, aggressive predators whose sting carries a swift, debilitating neurotoxin. Rhinag made the mistake of dropping his guard while battling the beasts near the borderlands. Knowing that the venom coursing through his veins will kill him in under an hour, he is unable to walk the distance to the city gates himself and must place his survival in the hands of whoever passes his remote camp.

Neeka Bloodscar. Helgrum the Swift sends you from Stonard to the Badlands outpost of Kargath, to speak with its head scout, Neeka Bloodscar. Word between Stonard and Kargath is often cut. The Badlands are harsh country and lie close to Loch Modan, which the Alliance holds. Because of this, word between Stonard and Kargath is often cut. Helgrum asks you to prove yourself by travelling to the Badlands and speaking with Neeka Bloodscar, who is head scout there. Neeka's report is then to be sent back to Helgrum.

Neeru Fireblade. This quest sends Horde adventurers from Margoz in Durotar to Orgrimmar's shadowy underbelly. Entrusted with a demonic Searing Collar recovered from the Burning Blade cult, you are directed to Neeru Fireblade, a prominent warlock residing in the Cleft of Shadow who claims to study dark arts only to protect the Horde. After recovering Searing Collars from the cultists lurking in Skull Rock, the shaman Margoz discovers that unraveling their foul sorcery exceeds his ancestral arts. Shamans commune with elemental spirits and the earth, while these artifacts reek of raw demonic corruption. Recognizing that understanding the Burning Blade's devices requires someone well-versed in the occult, Margoz sends you to seek out a warlock residing in the capital.

Nek'mani Wellspring. Perched high in the cliffs above the Southern Savage Coast, the Nek'mani Wellspring holds a fountain of remarkably pure holy water. It is renowned as the only pristine source of fresh water found south of Duskwood. However, this sacred site has recently been overrun by hostile naga explorers who jealously guard its flow. The Nek'mani Wellspring sits tucked away in the jagged coastal heights of western Stranglethorn Vale. Dispensing the only untainted freshwater south of Duskwood, the spring is hailed by various scholars and pilgrims as holy. Because differing cultures and traditions each claim its divine waters were blessed uniquely for their own kind, it remains a subject of intense theological fascination. Despite its spiritual renown, peaceful contemplation here is impossible: a vicious contingent of naga has recently seized the basin and guards the waters against all intruders.

Nek'rosh's Gambit. Nek'rosh's Gambit is an urgent strike mission commissioned by Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor. Learning that Chieftain Nek'rosh has constructed siege engines to bombard the vulnerable port town while reinforcements remain cut off at Dun Algaz, the Alliance sends brave volunteers deep into the marshes to burn the Dragonmaw catapults before an assault can begin. While Alliance adventurers were clashing with Dragonmaw raiding parties, dwarven scouts uncovered the clan's true ambition. Chieftain Nek'rosh has overseen the construction of full-scale siege catapults in the wetlands encampments. His goal is bold and catastrophic: to march his war engines to Menethil Harbor and batter down the fortress walls, wiping out the Alliance's primary shipping hub on the western coast.

Nek'rosh's Head. Nek'rosh's Head is the gruesome proof of the downfall of Chieftain Nek'rosh, leader of the Dragonmaw clan in the Wetlands. Procured by Alliance adventurers, this trophy is delivered to Captain Stoutfist to confirm that the orcish threat menacing Menethil Harbor has been shattered. The Dragonmaw clan poses a persistent danger across the marshlands, massing forces and siege weapons against the Alliance port of Menethil Harbor. After burning their catapults, the defense of the port hinges on slaying Chieftain Nek'rosh himself. Severing his head provides undeniable proof to Captain Stoutfist and the Ironforge authorities that the warlord's grip over the Wetlands is broken.

Neru Fragment. The Neru Fragment is one of four ancient carved stone pieces belonging to the Goaz Stone, a relic discovered in the Whelgar's Excavation site within the Wetlands. Unearthed from the disturbed earth, it holds a segment of ancient Titan script detailing the primeval history of Azeroth. Discovered by the dwarven archaeological expedition led by Prospector Whelgar, the Goaz Stone broke apart into four distinct remnants: the Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru fragments. When raptors overrun the dig site, work ground to a halt, leaving the Neru Fragment buried beneath loose soil amid the aggressive beasts. Recovering this fragment is crucial for reassembling the tablet, allowing dwarven scholars to decipher a forgotten record whose surviving words mention a divine plan and a doomed prophecy.

Nesingwary's Expedition. Nesingwary's Expedition is a rustic hunting encampment situated in northern Stranglethorn Vale, just north of Lake Nazferiti. Established by the famed dwarven marksman Hemet Nesingwary, the outpost serves as a staging ground for hunters seeking to test their mettle against the jungle's fiercest predators. Tucked alongside the river north of Lake Nazferiti, this remote encampment is a bustling haven for big game hunters, trackers, and marksmen. Hemet Nesingwary established the camp to stalk the legendary beasts of Stranglethorn Vale, surrounded by seasoned peers like Sir S. J. Erlgadin, Ajeck Rouack, and Barnil Stonepot. Guarded by hired marksmen and supplied by neutral vendors, the camp welcomes anyone capable of handling a rifle or bow, regardless of their allegiances, uniting them under the singular pursuit of tracking down the deadliest predators the jungle has to offer.

Nessa Shadowsong. Nessa Shadowsong is an introductory courier quest offered by Mydrannul in Darnassus. It guides fledgling adventurers down from the World Tree to Rut'theran Village to meet the fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong. This task serves as the initial step connecting the canopy capital to the shores and harbors below. Within Darnassus, Mydrannul watches over travelers looking for work and purpose. When fishing merchant Nessa Shadowsong needs a package delivered across the sea to Darkshore, Mydrannul directs able couriers toward the coast. While many young night elves spend their early journeys entirely within the boughs of Teldrassil, this simple request encourages them to look outward to the mainland.

Nessa's Collection. Nessa's Collection is a package of fish bones and scales gathered from the waters surrounding Rut'theran Village. Prepared for study by fish vendor Laird in Auberdine, it illustrates the unusually massive size of aquatic life thriving around the roots of Teldrassil. Nessa Shadowsong, a fisherwoman residing in Rut'theran Village at the base of Teldrassil, gathered this collection of fish bones and scales to compare the island's marine life with that of the Kalimdor mainland. The waters feeding into the Great Tree yield catches of staggering proportions, prompting Nessa to send physical proof across the sea to Laird, a fish merchant operating along the docks of Auberdine. Transferred by way of the village's hippogryph master, Vesprystus, the parcel serves as practical evidence of Teldrassil's burgeoning vitality.

Nethander Stead. Nethander Stead is an abandoned farmstead lying along the road just east of Southshore in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Once a working human farm, it has fallen into ruin and is completely overrun by the Mudsnout gnoll pack. The fields are overgrown with giant white mushrooms known as Mudsnout Blossoms, attracting the interest of Forsaken alchemists. Situated within sight of Southshore's eastern borders, Nethander Stead was once an active piece of the region's agricultural belt. Like much of the eastern foothills, the farm was abandoned as regional security eroded and wild packs moved in. Today, it serves as the sole enclave of the Mudsnout gnolls in the foothills. The brutes dwell among the ruined fences and outbuildings, aggressively driving off any travelers who wander too close to their claimed territory.

Nether Gem. The Nether Gem is an enchanted arcane stone entrusted by an enigmatic figure from Brightwater Lake. Imbued with magical power, it acts as a long-distance conduit allowing its master to manifest an arcane projection and communicate directly with Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, though the full nature of the connection between them remains to be uncovered.

Nether-lace Garment. Nether-lace Garment marks the completion of tailor Kil'hala's specialized crafting work in the Barrens. By weaving the gathered hair of dryads into refined cloth, the tailor crafts an enchanted garment fit for spellcasters. Kil'hala, working out of the Crossroads in the Barrens, undertakes the delicate process of fashioning nether-lace. Requiring rare and magically resonant components—specifically the locks harvested from the dryads known as laughing sisters in Ashenvale—the tailor binds natural woodland enchantment directly into comfortable, durable cloth.

Nethergarde Keep. Nethergarde Keep is a fortified Alliance stronghold perched high upon the bluffs along the road entering the Blasted Lands. Raised by the Alliance after the Second War, it stands as a vigilant sentinel over the dormant Dark Portal and the chaotic energies bleeding across the red wastes. Today, mages and garrisons supported by Stormwind continue their lonely vigil against demons and lingering corruption. Following the destruction of the Dark Portal at the end of the Second War, Archmage Khadgar and the leaders of the Alliance of Lordaeron recognized that Azeroth could never again leave the rift unguarded. Builders labored to raise towering bastions, barracks, and mage spires along the canyon pass into the Blasted Lands. Staffed by Kirin Tor sorcerers, its dual purpose was to keep constant watch on the shattered gateway and weave wards preventing the demonic blight of the scorched landscape from creeping northward into the human kingdoms.
