text.enUS: Raid on the Kolkar. After Strange Alliance, Uthek the Wise sends you against the Kolkar centaurs to the northeast. Kill them, take their charms, and bring ten of those charms back to Uthek. Uthek scoffs at the Kolkar centaurs for thinking their magic strong; in Uthek's view they know nothing of magic. You go northeast to the Kolkar, kill them, and take their charms. Uthek wants ten Crude Charms to throw in the fire, laughing as they burn.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands where Tor'gan seeks to lift the spirits of a despondent orc named Gor'mul. When tales of Orgrimmar and Warchief Thrall fail, Tor'gan turns to newly rediscovered shamanic traditions to craft a revitalizing amulet from highland raptor eyes. At the remote outpost of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, the orcs face enemies from without and quiet battles within. One of their own, Gor'mul, has fallen into a deep, unshakable melancholy. His companions attempted to rally him with proud tales of Kalimdor, the mighty fortress city of Orgrimmar, and the visionary leadership of young Warchief Thrall. Yet none of these grand victories or distant wonders could pierce Gor'mul's gloom or give him reason to hope.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest aimed at rekindling the fighting will of Gor'mul, a broken warrior consumed by despair. An emissary delivers a Raptor Talon Amulet in hopes of awakening the fierce spirit he once possessed. However, Gor'mul remains bitter, questioning whether any simple trinket could ever mend his sorrow or restore glory to the Horde. Raising Spirits involves delivering a Raptor Talon Amulet to an orc named Gor'mul. His allies hope that the wild strength and ferocity of raptors, channeled through the talisman, will reawaken the warrior's flame that once burned fiercely within his veins.

Raising Spirits. Raising Spirits is a Horde quest that addresses the lingering emotional trauma of an old orc veteran. Through the guidance of Tor'gan, a shaman attempts to reach the embittered Gor'mul using ancestral magic to restore his lost pride and will to live. In the wake of past wars, many orcish veterans struggle with the burdens of survival and perceived dishonor. Gor'mul is one such warrior, languishing in bitter despondency because he was denied what he considers an honorable death alongside his fallen Warchief. Tor'gan, an empathetic shaman, seeks to alleviate Gor'mul's suffering by reminding him of his people's spiritual strength. Believing that ancestral energies can heal emotional wounds, Tor'gan prepares an enchanted amulet intended to rekindle the old fighter's pride.

Raleigh Andrean. Raleigh Andrean is a Forsaken resident of the Undercity. His requests reveal a callous attitude toward his former human life and those he once knew. Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, Raleigh Andrean lived an ordinary human life, married to a woman named Deliah and keeping company with his friend Valdred Moray. Like countless others, he fell when the Scourge tore through the kingdom, only to be raised as a mindless thrall in service to the Lich King. He regained his free will following the shattering of the Ner'zhul's grip and Sylvanas Windrunner's uprising, taking his place among the Forsaken in the Undercity.

Raleigh and the Undercity. This quest bridges an investigation from Brill to the Undercity, tasking an adventurer with delivering a recovered heirloom ring to a widower named Raleigh. Found on a woman's stolen corpse bound for Fenris Isle, the jewelry points to a tragedy among Lordaeron's former inhabitants. Delivering it sets into motion a dark pursuit of vengeance. In Brill, Magistrate Sevren pieced together clues surrounding a stolen corpse and an engraved ring that once belonged to a woman named Deliah. Hoping to confirm its origin and see it returned to her family, Sevren directed the finder deep into the subterranean halls of the Undercity to seek Deliah's surviving husband, Raleigh.

Ran Bloodtooth's Skull. Ran Bloodtooth's Skull is a grisly trophy taken from the chieftain of the corrupted furbolgs in Ashenvale. Brought back to the night elves of Astranaar, it serves as tangible proof that a ferocious threat to the woodland realm has been ended. The forests of Ashenvale have suffered immensely from demonic taint and wilderness corruption, driving once-peaceful furbolg tribes into murderous madness. Among the fiercest of these hostile chieftains was Ran Bloodtooth. Recovering his skull provides the night elf Sentinels with definite proof that the brute has fallen, breaking his hold over the local furbolgs and offering a small measure of respite to the beleaguered town of Astranaar.

Randis. In Cathedral Square, Randis waits for a chance to see the world beyond Stormwind. During Children's Week, he eagerly joins willing adventurers across Alliance lands. Randis lives in the orphanage near Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, one of many children left without family by the realm's conflicts. When Children's Week comes each year, Orphan Matron Nightingale gives sympathetic heroes a whistle and entrusts them with his care. Curious and full of questions, Randis dreams of adventure, asks riddles, and declares that he wants to be king of Stormwind when he grows up.

Rane Yorick. Deathstalker Rane Yorick is an operative of the Forsaken intelligence guild stationed deep in Silverpine Forest. Together with her brother Quinn, she was sent to scout the farms of northern Silverpine and report to High Executor Hadrec. The Deathstalkers serve as Lady Sylvanas Windrunner's eyes, ears, and blades across Lordaeron. Operating out of shadows and hidden posts, agents like Rane Yorick monitor the wilderness for threats that could disrupt Forsaken dominion. When sent to scout northern Silverpine Forest, Rane and her brother Quinn found themselves hemmed in by surrounding feral dangers, turning an undercover reconnaissance mission into a battle for survival.

Ranger Glynda Nal'Shea. Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea is a seasoned night elf sentry stationed in the coastal town of Auberdine. From her post near the town watch, she directs local defense efforts across Darkshore, dispatching travelers to eliminate lurking threats and investigate strange coastal phenomena. As Darkshore grapples with rising corruption and hostile incursions, Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea coordinates vital scout work from Auberdine. She keeps a watchful eye over the surrounding wilderness, relying on capable adventurers to maintain the perimeter and safeguard night elf holdings along the fog-shrouded coast.

Raptor Grounds. Tucked into the dusty hills of the southern Barrens, the Raptor Grounds is a secluded valley claimed by the Sunscale raptors. Unlike ordinary wild beasts, the pack here exhibits an eerie, tool-using cunning and a compulsive urge to steal bright trinkets from nearby settlements. Located west of Northwatch Hold, the Raptor Grounds serves as the primary nesting territory for the Sunscale raptors. Travelers quickly discover that these creatures are far from mindless predators: they display an unnatural intelligence, fashioning crude shelters, assembling primitive tools, and coordinating their hunts. Driven by a relentless fascination with shiny and unusual items, the pack regularly raids passing caravans and Horde encampments, dragging coins, trinkets, and supplies back into their canyon dens.

Raptor Head. A severed raptor head serves as bloody proof of a beast slain in the Barrens. Gazrog of the Crossroads demands these macabre trophies to purge the local packs after an improbable theft of guard payroll. Life in the arid plains of the Barrens is harsh enough without local wildlife raiding settlement towers. When a chest containing guard payroll vanished from the Crossroads watchtower, the defenders caught an improbable culprit red-handed: a wild raptor. Perplexed and furious, Gazrog placed an immediate bounty on the cunning reptiles prowling the savannah. Bringing severed raptor heads back to the outpost proves that these predatory pests are being culled before they can pilfer any more Horde supplies.

Raptor Horns. Mebok Mizzyrix, an enterprising goblin in Ratchet, believes the cunning of local raptors is stored entirely in their horns. He hires travelers to hunt Sunscale Scytheclaws across the Barrens to collect intact horns for a bizarre commercial venture. Ratchet is full of goblins seeking their next fortune, and Mebok Mizzyrix is no exception. Observing that the raptors of the Barrens display unusual craftiness and coordination compared to beasts in other regions, Mebok arrived at an eccentric conclusion: their intelligence must be concentrated within their horns. Naturally, rather than conducting formal scientific inquiry, his immediate instinct was to exploit this theoretical resource for profit.

Raptor Mastery. At his expedition camp in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges travelers to prove their prowess in the wilderness. The famed hunter demands ten Stranglethorn Raptors slain to test whether you possess genuine hunting talent. Following your arrival in the jungle after Welcome to the Jungle, Hemet Nesingwary offers to test your tracking and hunting capabilities. Rather than handing out maps or directions, he insists that finding the Stranglethorn Raptors yourself is half the test, challenging you to venture out into the brush and bring down ten of the fierce beasts.

Raptor Mastery. Deep in the jungle of Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges hunters to step up their game against more dangerous quarry. Following an earlier raptor hunt, he directs adventurers to pursue and bring down ten Lashtail Raptors. After proving an initial measure of hunting prowess, Hemet Nesingwary expects more than idly passing time by the camp's fire. To prove true focus and skill, hunters are dispatched into the dense jungle brush just north of Grom'gol Base Camp to track down and slay ten fierce Lashtail Raptors.

Raptor Mastery. Hemet Nesingwary raises the stakes of his hunting expedition by sending you after a elusive breed known as Jungle Stalkers. Tracking down ten of these cunning raptors will prove your mettle as a true stalker of wild beasts in Stranglethorn Vale. Having tested your aim against lesser raptors, Hemet Nesingwary presents a more demanding quarry. Jungle Stalkers are notably cagey and far more difficult to track and slay than the breeds hunted previously. Hemet expects you to venture out into the jungle, fell ten of these wary predators, and return to camp to earn a lead on his finest hunt yet.

name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia al raptor

text.enUS: Raptor Mastery. Deep in Stranglethorn Vale, Hemet Nesingwary challenges seasoned trackers to bring down an elusive predator that has escaped even him. Having proven your mettle against lesser beasts, you are tasked with tracking the cunning raptor known as Tethis and securing its talon. Following your earlier trials in the jungle, Hemet Nesingwary reveals the existence of a particularly vicious raptor named Tethis. While lesser hunters have chased prey across the foliage, Tethis has evaded capture entirely, defying even the expedition leader himself. Ajeck Rouack bestowed the beast with its moniker, marking it as the ultimate prize among Stranglethorn's scaled horrors.

Raptor Ridge. Raptor Ridge is an elevated, rugged expanse in the eastern Wetlands, sitting northwest of the fortified Dragonmaw Gates. It serves as the primary hunting and nesting grounds for packs of ferocious Razormaw raptors, overseen by a particularly vicious matriarch deep within its caverns. Rising above the sodden marshes of the eastern Wetlands, Raptor Ridge is among the most perilous wilderness areas in the region. Vicious Razormaw raptors prowl its crags and rocky trails in large packs, making travel near the foothills of Khaz Modan hazardous for wanderers. At the heart of the ridge lies a brooding cavern dominated by the Razormaw Matriarch, whose aggressive brood aggressively defends their nests against any encroaching predators or foolish travelers wandering too close to the Dragonmaw Gates.

Raptor Thieves. When a vital shipment of guard payroll went missing from the Crossroads guard tower, the defenders caught an impossible culprit: a wild raptor. Perplexed and enraged by the heist, Gazrog orders a retaliatory cull to prevent the cunning beasts from striking again. The Crossroads relies heavily on mercenary and grunt guards to keep vital trade arteries open across the Barrens. Keeping those guards paid is essential for morale and discipline. When the silver payroll vanished directly from the guard tower, leadership expected Centaur raiders or Quilboar scavengers. Instead, one thief caught red-handed in the dead of night was a predatory Barrens raptor, leaving the settlement's leadership stunned and out of pocket.

Rare Books. Rare Books is an Alliance quest in Northshire Valley focused on recovering two stolen magical primers for Brother Paxton. Kobolds have hauled the missing texts into the Jasperlode Mine, where they appear to be studying elementary magic and summoning rituals. Brother Paxton of Northshire Abbey faces a crisis in his library: several volumes have been carried off by vermin infesting the valley. Only two books remain missing from his catalog: 'Geomancy for Curious Young Wizards' and 'Arcane Explainer: Magical Stuff in Simple Words'. These educational primers were carted away into the depths of the Jasperlode Mine by the occupying kobolds.

Rare Earth. Rare Earth is a specialized package of mineral-rich soil procured from Darnassus for botanic experiments on Teldrassil. It is sent via courier from Dolanaar to the herbalist researcher Denalan at his lakeside camp near Lake Al'Ameth. Teldrassil's newly grown ecosystem requires careful observation and nurturing, prompting herbalists across the island to study how various plants respond to foreign or enriched soils. This particular parcel of rare earth was requisitioned directly from Darnassus by Denalan, an eccentric botanist stationed along the eastern shore of Lake Al'Ameth. After languishing in transit and turning up late in Dolanaar, herbalist Syral Bladeleaf entrusts travelers passing south to deliver the perishable soil to Denalan before its potency fades.

Rascally Rodents. Rascally Rodents is a quest in Northshire Valley where Brother Paxton tasks adventurers with recovering stolen books from the local kobolds. Though Paxton initially fears the vermin are devouring his library, retrieving the texts reveals an unsettling mystery behind the creatures' motives. Brother Paxton in Northshire Valley is in distress over the local kobold infestation, which has spilled over from the surrounding hills and mines into the sacred grounds. Convinced that the ravenous creatures have begun devouring the texts from his collection, he enlists the aid of young adventurers to hunt down the vermin and salvage whatever volumes remain before the entire library is lost.

Ratchet. Ratchet is a bustling neutral port town run by the Steamwheedle Cartel on the eastern coast of the Barrens. Founded by chief engineer Gazlowe after he helped construct Orgrimmar, it serves as the primary maritime trade hub linking central Kalimdor to the Eastern Kingdoms. Perched on the arid coastline between Durotar and Dustwallow Marsh, Ratchet offers safe harbor to anyone carrying coin. Founded by the entrepreneurial engineer Gazlowe following the Third War, the port arose from smugglers, exiles, and daring traders looking to exploit Kalimdor's frontier. It operates beneath the banner of the Steamwheedle Cartel, maintaining strict neutrality between the Horde and the Alliance. Ships like The Maiden's Fancy regularly ply the waters across the Great Sea to Booty Bay, transporting goods, mercenaries, and raw materials between continents. Local bruisers keep a watchful eye on the docks, ruthlessly thrashing anyone foolish enough to start a brawl and disrupt commerce.

Rattlecage Skull. Rattlecage Skulls are the shattered remnants of mindless undead roaming the ruined outskirts of Deathknell. Novice Forsaken warlocks must gather these calcified trophies for Venya Marthand to demonstrate their emerging will and qualify for the dark arts of summoning. Within the sunless bounds of Deathknell, newly raised Forsaken with an affinity for dark magic are guided by Venya Marthand. To prove that a fledgling practitioner has the fortitude to bend extraplanar creatures to their command, Venya tasks them with subduing the lingering Rattlecage Skeletons near the ruined smithy. Striking down these lesser undead and retrieving their severed skulls serves as both a practical test of discipline and a ritual foundation before learning to breach the void and enslave a first demonic minion.

Rattling the Rattlecages. Rattling the Rattlecages is an early trial assigned by Shadow Priest Sarvis to newly awakened Forsaken in Deathknell. Tasked with destroying twelve Rattlecage Skeletons, fresh undead prove their resilience against the Scourge and demonstrate that they possess the willpower to defend their newly won freedom. Having culled the mindless zombies stumbling through Deathknell, newly risen Forsaken are immediately pushed into a harsher trial. Shadow Priest Sarvis directs recruits to confront the Rattlecage Skeletons roaming the outskirts of the settlement. These animated bones lack any trace of sapience or self-control, yet they hit harder and fight with greater ferocity than the decaying corpses nearby. Surviving their clattering ambushes demonstrates that a new recruit will not falter when placed under immediate pressure.

Rau Cliffrunner. Rau Cliffrunner is a tauren scout and scholar stationed high atop Freewind Post in Thousand Needles. Dedicated to protecting his people from regional threats, he studies the history and origins of the hostile Galak centaur through their ancient relics. Working closely with allies in Thunder Bluff, Rau coordinates ventures into dangerous enemy strongholds across the canyon. Perched on the perilous bluffs of Freewind Post, Rau Cliffrunner maintains a watchful eye over the sweeping, sun-scorched expanse of Thousand Needles. The tauren outpost serves as a crucial Horde sanctuary in an otherwise hostile territory teeming with ferocious predators, quilboar, and aggressive centaur clans. Rau acts as both an outpost organizer and a dedicated investigator, keen on neutralizing emerging threats before they can overwhelm the vulnerable mesa settlements.

Ravaged Caravan. The Ravaged Caravan is a smoldering wreck located on the northeastern shore of Stonebull Lake in Mulgore. Once a supply convoy bound for Supervisor Fizsprocket's mining operations, it was ambushed and destroyed by local tauren determined to halt goblin exploitation of their homeland. Perched on a rise above Stonebull Lake, the Ravaged Caravan marks an early clash between the tauren of Bloodhoof Village and the encroaching Venture Company. Sent to deliver mining supplies, blueprints, and equipment to Supervisor Fizsprocket's dig site, the caravan was cut off and wrecked by tauren defenders before it could reach its destination. Despite the devastation, stubborn Venture Co. survivors still cling to the ruined wagons and smoldering crates, jealously guarding what little cargo remains.

Ravaged Twilight Camp. Tucked away in the secluded Crystal Vale of northwestern Silithus, the Ravaged Twilight Camp sits ruined among towering mineral formations. It serves as an isolated redoubt for the eccentric hermit Highlord Demitrian, a devotee of the Windseeker. While the Twilight's Hammer maintains numerous active outposts across the sands of Silithus, this broken encampment in the Crystal Vale tells a different story. Nestled far from the primary cult fortresses, the camp lies largely ruined and deserted, save for Highlord Demitrian. A servant of Thunderaan, Demitrian lingers amidst the stones, seemingly abandoned by or detached from the wider Twilight hierarchy while brooding over elemental bindings and the lost power of the Windseeker.

name.frFR: Talisman de la griffe du corbeau

text.enUS: Raven Claw Talisman. The Raven Claw Talisman is a sacred night elf relic tied to the Druids of the Talon. Kept deep within Ban'ethil Barrow Den on Teldrassil, it is one of the four essential Relics of Wakening required to safely guide slumbering druids back from the Emerald Dream. The Raven Claw Talisman is preserved within a designated chest inside Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the subterranean sanctuary where Teldrassil's Druids of the Talon entered their deep meditative slumbers. Druidic hibernation is a delicate spiritual threshold. If a druid's link to the waking world is shattered without the proper ceremonial focus, their spirit risks being stranded within the Emerald Dream indefinitely. Alongside the Black Feather Quill, the Sapphire of Sky, and the Rune of Nesting, the talisman is required by Athridas Bearmantle in Dolanaar to conduct the ritual of awakening and bring the slumberers back safely.

Raven Hill. Reports of shifting shadows and flickering window light in the abandoned settlement of Raven Hill have set the Night Watch on edge. Dispatched by Elaine Carevin in Darkshire, travelers are sent west across the haunted woods to confront whatever sinister presence has taken shelter among the ruins. To the rangers of the Night Watch, the far western edge of Duskwood has long been surrendered to the dead and the wilderness. Yet complete abandonment would be preferable to unexpected activity. Calor, a watcher patrolling the gloomy roads, noticed movement among the silent houses of Raven Hill two nights in a row, punctuated by the unsettling flicker of a lantern in a window. In a land plagued by ghouls, skeletons, and beasts, any unexplained signs of life demand immediate investigation.

Raven Hill. Raven Hill is a desolate, ruined village in western Duskwood sitting in the long shadow of the vast Raven Hill Cemetery. Once a lively human settlement, it lies abandoned by all but a handful of frightened squatters and invisible spirits. Situated along the western thoroughfare of Duskwood just north of Addle's Stead, Raven Hill is a tragic shell of its former self. When dark magic and undead horrors swept through the Grand Hamlet region, the living evacuated eastward toward Darkshire or fled the territory entirely. Today, ruined timber homes rot beneath perpetual gloom, avoided by travelers who fear both the restless dead wandering down from the neighboring cemetery and the invisible Unseen lurking between the crumbling walls.

Raven Hill Cemetery. Raven Hill Cemetery is a vast, cursed graveyard stretching across the western reaches of Duskwood. Once a peaceful burial ground for local hamlets, the cemetery has been overrun by hordes of walking dead, scavenger spiders, and ruthless grave robbers. Before the darkness engulfed the Dawning Wood, Raven Hill Cemetery served as the primary resting place for the surrounding settlements. As dark sorceries fell upon the region, the dead failed to remain in their plots. Skeletons, ghouls, and shambling horrors clawed their way out of the soil, swelling the graveyard's grim boundaries. Today, it stands as one of the most perilous blights in Duskwood. The cemetery is prowled not only by rotting abominations and giant spiders, but also by desperate grave robbers eager to plunder ancestral crypts unhindered by local authorities.

Ravencrest Monument. Perched upon the windswept cliffs of southern Azshara, the Ravencrest Monument marks the shattered remnant of an ancient night elven colossus. Once a towering tribute overlooking the Great Sea, the statue has long since broken apart, leaving only towering legs and scattered stone ruins now stalked by hostile Spitelash naga. Standing high above the ocean southeast of the Ruins of Eldarath, the Ravencrest Monument was once an awe-inspiring marvel of Kaldorei stonework. Today, little remains of the majestic colossus beyond its pair of gigantic broken legs rooted to the stone plinth, with the shattered fragments of its torso and head either buried in the cliffside dirt or lost beneath the waves below. Reaching this remote coastal promontory requires trekking across the mainland bridges of Azshara, as sheer, rocky drops prevent any approach from the sea.

Ravenholdt. Ravenholdt, also known as the Assassin's League, is an elite guild of rogues, thieves, and killers based out of a secluded mountain manor above the Hillsbrad Foothills. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the league maintains strict neutrality from faction politics while waging an unending shadow war against their bitter rivals, the Syndicate. They test and recruit only the most cunning operatives across Azeroth, valuing peerless discipline, stealth, and lethal efficiency above all else. Tucked away in the craggy mountains connecting Hillsbrad to Alterac, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the nerve center for Azeroth's premier brotherhood of assassins. Led by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the organization operates far beyond the jurisdiction of kings and warchiefs. Within its walls, master specialists hone every lethal art: Master Kang instructs disciples in close combat and assassination, the Thunderwood brothers brew rare and deadly poisons, and gnome craftsmen engineer intricate locks to test fledglings. To non-rogues, entering the estate is an overt flirtation with death, where an unwary step easily ends with a poisoned dagger in the ribs.

Ravenholdt Manor. Tucked away high in the mountains above Hillsbrad Foothills, Ravenholdt Manor serves as the secluded headquarters for the guild of thieves and assassins known as Ravenholdt. Overseen by Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, the estate provides a discreet haven where practitioners of stealth hone their craft far from the eyes of authorities. Hidden behind a narrow mountain pass and a winding cave northwest of Durnholde Keep, Ravenholdt Manor sits isolated on the borderlands of the Alterac Mountains. The property belongs to Lord Jorach Ravenholdt, a nobleman who maintains a disciplined enclave of rogues, assassins, and intelligence operatives. The grounds feature a tranquil garden and an outdoor training arena overseen by martial experts like Master Kang, providing a disciplined space to practice lockpicking, poison-crafting, and close-quarters combat. While the manor welcomes those with a talent for skullduggery, clumsy outsiders and unwanted visitors are treated with cold suspicion by the manor's watchful sentries.

Raynewood Retreat. Raynewood Retreat is an ancient night elf outpost perched around a massive great tree in north-central Ashenvale. Guarded by dryads and Cenarion protectors, it serves as a watchful sanctuary monitoring the northern passes toward corrupted Felwood. It is also the sanctuary of Keeper Ordanus, an elder son of Cenarius targeted by sinister outside forces. Nestled between Shael'dryn's moonwell and the satyr-infested ruins of Night Run, the outpost is fiercely guarded by Cenarion Protectors, faerie dragons, and Laughing Sisters. Their collective vigilance keeps a wary eye on the encroaching taint descending from Felwood just to the north.

Razor Hill. Razor Hill is the principal Horde settlement in central Durotar, nestled at the strategic crossroads between the Valley of Trials, the Barrens, and Orgrimmar. Centered around a prominent fortified barracks, it serves as the staging ground and training center for young orc and troll warriors testing their mettle in the harsh wilderness. Built at a vital geographical junction, Razor Hill connects northern Durotar with the coastal settlements to the south and the sprawling plains of the Barrens across the Southfury River. Dominated by its stone-and-timber barracks and classic orcish burrows, the settlement was established early in the founding of Durotar. Shortly after the Third War, human forces from Kul Tiras lured the Horde into an ambush here under the guise of an emissary summit, an assault thwarted when Rexxar went in Thrall's stead. Today, the outpost stands fully fortified against further coastal incursions.

text.enUS: Razor Hill Watchtower. Perched on the red stone bluffs overlooking Razor Hill, this sturdy outpost serves as an early warning post for the heart of Durotar. Furl Scornbrow keeps a vigilant eye across the dusty plains and toward the coast, safeguarding the settlement below from encroaching threats. Constructed from thick timber and iron framing, the Razor Hill Watchtower guards the settlement of Razor Hill and the surrounding canyons. Durotar faces relentless threats from Kul Tiras marines along the eastern shore, quilboar raiders prowling the scrublands, and Burning Blade cultists lurking in nearby crags. From this elevated vantage point atop the ridgeline, the lookout can spot approaching warbands, smoke signals, and incursions long before they reach the settlement gates.

Razorfen. Razorfen is the collective name associated with the predominant quilboar tribe of southern Kalimdor and their sprawling thorn-choked settlements. Carved into massive briars along the southern border of the Barrens and the edge of Thousand Needles, Razorfen encompasses the strongholds of Razorfen Kraul and Razorfen Downs. It serves as both the spiritual heart and the central bastion of quilboar power. According to legend, the colossal thorned brambles that make up the Razorfen sprouted ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients. When the giant boar Ancient, Agamaggan, fell in battle against the Burning Legion, his blood seeped into the earth wherever he bled and died. From that divine sacrifice grew massive vines of petrified bramble and iron-hard thorns, creating a natural fortress where his descendants, the quilboar, have dwelled ever since.

Razorfen Downs. Razorfen Downs is the ancestral capital and sacred burial labyrinth of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal brambles bordering the southern Barrens and Thousand Needles. Once their holiest sanctuary, it has fallen under the sway of the undead Scourge, transforming into a festering bastion of necromancy. Long revered as the ancestral capital city and burial grounds of the quilboar race, Razorfen Downs rests within the colossal petrified briars sprung from the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Legend holds that its arched entryway was carved directly from the Great Boar's very maw. For centuries, the high priests of the Death's Head tribe tended these deep, winding burrows and honored their revered dead. Yet despite its sacred standing among the boar-folk, the maze of bone and bramble has recently suffered a catastrophe far darker than any squabble over Barrens water.

Razorfen Downs (Classic). Razorfen Downs is the ancestral burial ground and traditional capital city of the quilboar, nestled deep within giant thorny brambles in the southern Barrens. Recently, agents of the undead Scourge led by the lich Amnennar the Coldbringer seized control of the labyrinth, reanimating the quilboar dead and threatening to expand their dominion across central Kalimdor. Grown from the same towering, petrified vines as nearby Razorfen Kraul, Razorfen Downs rests where the ancient boar demigod Agamaggan fell during the War of the Ancients. For generations, the labyrinth of thorns served as the sacred necropolis and seat of power for the quilboar, guarded closely by the mystics of the Death's Head tribe. To the quilboar, the dense briars are holy ground, soaked in the blood of their divine progenitor.

Razorfen Kraul (Classic). Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of the quilboar, carved deep into the colossal thorns that sprang from the blood of the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan. Ruled by the ruthless crone Charlga Razorflank, this fortified labyrinth serves as a staging ground for bloody raids across the southern Barrens. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the colossal boar demigod Agamaggan perished battling the Burning Legion to save Azeroth. Wherever his sacred blood seeped into the soil of southern Kalimdor, massive, impenetrable thorn vines erupted from the earth. The quilboar, believing themselves the mortal progeny of the Great Boar, gathered within these dense briars to dwell and venerate his sacrifice. The dense mass known as Razorfen Kraul stands as their most revered redoubt, thick with quilboar warriors, beast trainers, and earth-shaping shamans.

Razorflank's Medallion. Razorflank's Medallion is a personal token carried by Charlga Razorflank, the crone ruling over Razorfen Kraul. Recovered from the heart of the quilboar stronghold, it serves as undeniable proof that the matriarch has been brought down. Carried by Charlga Razorflank herself, this medallion represents the authority of the crone who leads the Razorfen quilboar. When Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar learns of the fates of fallen explorers like Heralath and the dwarf Lonebrow, he tasks Alliance adventurers with striking directly at the quilboar leader. Presenting the crone's medallion confirms her death, reassuring the night elf sentinels guarding the borders of Feralas that the gathered forces within the Kraul have lost their leader.

Razorhide. Razorhide is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By offering him blood shards infused with the life essence of the Ancient boar god Agamaggan, warriors and wanderers can gain a powerful blessing of hardened skin and resilience before heading into combat. The quilboar trace their ancestry and power directly to Agamaggan, the Great Boar who perished battling the Burning Legion thousands of years ago. His blood soaked into the soils of the Barrens, calcifying into crystalline blood shards that still thrum with ancient power. Even though the quilboar remain sworn enemies of the Horde, Mangletooth—held in a cage at Camp Taurajo—is willing to trade their sacred knowledge in exchange for these precious fragments.

Razormane Grounds. The Razormane Grounds form the forward encampment of the Razormane quilboar pushing eastward from the Barrens into central Durotar. Choked with sharp briars and the stripped carcasses of wild game, this bristling outpost serves as the frontline in the quilboars' unending clash with the orcs of Orgrimmar. Sprawling beneath the red cliffs of central Durotar, the Razormane Grounds mark the furthest eastern reach of quilboar expansion out of the Barrens. Entangled within thick brambles and surrounded by bleached bones, the encampment poses a constant danger to travelers along the Southfury River. The camp is led by figures such as Captain Flat Tusk of the Battleguard and Geolord Mottle, who orchestrate raids against neighboring orc settlements and passing supply lines. Despite regular patrols dispatched from Razor Hill and nearby outposts, the Razormane replenish their ranks tirelessly, sprouting from the briars faster than the Horde can clear them.

Razorwind Canyon. Razorwind Canyon is a winding, rocky gulch split across the main road between Razor Hill and Orgrimmar. Infested by the aggressive Dustwind harpies, the canyon poses a persistent danger to travelers moving north toward the Horde's capital. Razorwind Canyon flanks the central artery linking Razor Hill to Orgrimmar, carving paths into both the eastern bluffs and the western scrublands toward Tor'kren Farm. The canyon is the nesting ground of the Dustwind harpies, territorial creatures that strike without hesitation at travelers who stray too close to their roosts. Their presence so near the capital's trade routes makes clearing out these gullies an ongoing necessity for the defenders of Durotar.

Razzeric's Tweaking. On the Shimmering Flats, Razzeric adds personal modifications to racers once Pozzik has finished with them. A seaforium booster ordered from Shreev in Gadgetzan was on a zeppelin that Razzeric hears crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, and Razzeric wants it brought back. Razzeric grants that Pozzik is a great mechanic, but thinks Pozzik too wary of loading on firepower and hanging on for the ride. Once Pozzik is done with a racer, Razzeric spends time making personal changes: loosening the controls, removing frame sections and piling on power. A seaforium booster was ordered from Shreev at the Gizmorium in Gadgetzan, but the zeppelin carrying it crashed in Dustwallow Marsh, by Razzeric's account. The booster is needed back on the Shimmering Flats, since showing up at the track without that extra kick would be a travesty.

Razzle Sprysprocket. Razzle Sprysprocket is a gnomish engineer residing in Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Known for his technical tinkering alongside Ozzie Togglevolt, he enlists travelers to help salvage disrupted gnomish machinery and components around the snowy hills. Following the tragedy at Gnomeregan, Razzle Sprysprocket found refuge among the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh, setting up his workshop in Kharanos. With a knack for delicate mechanical parts, Razzle works alongside fellow engineer Ozzie Togglevolt. Their efforts frequently involve recovering gyro-mechanisms and cog assemblies that were lost or scavenged during the flight from their irradiated homeland.

Reading the Ley Lines. Reading the Ley Lines is a rite of passage for young Skyborne discovering their Highborne magical heritage. Entrusted by Falorne Fallwind on Zephras Isle, novitiates travel to the standing stones in Thendal Grove to sense and draw upon the raw arcane currents surging through the elemental terrain. Even within the windswept confines of the elemental plane, latent arcane conduits run beneath the earth. While strange elementals and the hostile Al'Aketh drift across Zephras Isle, subterranean ley lines have begun pushing toward the surface. To practitioners of magic, these ruptures provide direct access to untamed arcane reservoirs, offering strength to any who possess the bloodline and knowledge necessary to channel them.

Reagent Pouch (shaman). A reagent pouch carried by Burning Blade cultists lurking in the crags of Durotar. Shaman seeking to communing with fire require these gathered spell components to distill their initial fire sapta. To forge a fire sapta and attune a young shaman to the spirits of flame, specific ritual catalysts are vital. Cultists of the Burning Blade carry small satchels stocked with reagents tailored for demonic fire conjurations. The hermit Telf Joolam uses these gathered powders and oils, combined with the fire tar of Razormane quilboar, to craft the draught needed to grant sight into the realm of fire.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor is gathering reagents for the gnome mage Leftwitch, who lives in Kharanos, and the Reclaimers are short-handed. He wants claws and horns from the Hatefury satyrs to the east before the rest of the list can begin. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor has another job on his hands: fetching reagents for Leftwitch, the gnome mage who lives in Kharanos. Roetten reckons it is easy coin, since the Reclaimers are already out in Desolace, and Kreldig says he does not care that the crew is short-handed.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Next on Leftwitch's list for Kreldig Ungor is venom from the scorpashi and hides from aged kodo. Kreldig cannot say where to find either, since he does not know Desolace well. Following the first part of Leftwitch's list, Kreldig Ungor turns to the next items. They look simple enough, but the instructions are exact. The mage wants venom from the scorpashi, any of them will do, and hides from kodo, but only aged kodo. Dying and ancient kodo are no use. Kreldig wants seven vials of venom and three hides. Mages, Kreldig muses, ask for some odd things.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor has the last of the items Leftwitch wants, and he admits it is not pretty and will take longer than the others. All of it comes from demons: brains, wings and vials of blood. Kreldig warns that the final set is a grim business, slower to gather than any before it. Leftwitch wants three kinds of parts, ten of each. The brains come from felhounds: mana eaters, mage hunters or ley hunters. The wings come from the nether maidens, sisters or sorceresses. The blood comes from doomwarder captains or lords. Kreldig says he would understand if you passed on this one.

Reagents for Reclaimers Inc.. Kreldig Ungor gives you Leftwitch's package and sends you back to Ironforge. Roetten Stonehammer is the one to see about your pay, and Kreldig promises a kind word about you once back home. Kreldig says your pay waits in Ironforge with Roetten Stonehammer himself. Roetten will be glad to be rid of Leftwitch's package, and handing it over should be enough to get what you are owed. Kreldig expects to be in Desolace only a little longer, and still means to speak well of you once home.

Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a military scouting mission tasked by Deathguard Linnea to protect the Forsaken defenses along Tirisfal's eastern border. It directs operatives to purge stray Scourge horrors and lingering spirits haunting the Balnir Farmstead before they can compromise the supply lines supporting the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the primary bulwark holding back the pestilence and armies of the Western Plaguelands from spilling into Tirisfal Glades. Deathguard Linnea oversees rear-echelon security along this frontier. Because the line cannot afford to divide its forces against ambushes from behind, any undead that bypass the choke point must be destroyed before they can sever the supply lines feeding the front.

Rear Guard Patrol. Rear Guard Patrol is a critical defense assignment given by Deathguard Linnea in Tirisfal Glades. Rather than fighting off mere wandering ghouls, patrollers are tasked with hunting down Riptear, an abomination roaming near Venomweb Vale that should never have made it past the Bulwark. The Bulwark stands as the sole fortified barrier separating Tirisfal Glades from the horrors of the Western Plaguelands. The strategy of the Forsaken military hinges upon a strictly one-front war. If mindless undead slip behind the lines, the supply routes feeding the front can be strangled in an instant. While stray spirits or ghouls occasionally bypass the barricades, reports of an abomination roaming the glades signal a severe failure of containment.

Reassignment. Reassignment is the culmination of Lieutenant Farren Orinelle's campaign to escape his posting in Southshore. Having compiled an exaggerated report of his deeds against the coastal naga, Farren dispatches an adventurer all the way to Stormwind Keep to deliver the documents to his former mentor, Major Samuelson. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle has made no secret of his disdain for his station in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Tucked away in Southshore, far from the comforts of the capital and under the stern watch of Marshal Redpath, Farren has spent his days scheming for a transfer back south. By taking credit for clearing out the nearby Daggerspine naga, he hopes to present himself as an indispensable, battle-hardened officer ripe for promotion.

Rebel Camp. Tucked just off the road in northern Stranglethorn Vale, the Rebel Camp serves as a fortified refuge for Alliance soldiers who broke away from Colonel Kurzen. Led by Lieutenant Doren, these troops refused to surrender to the madness gripping their commander's expedition and now fight to survive and undo his descent into tyranny. When Colonel Kurzen's expedition pushed deep into the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale on behalf of Stormwind, things rapidly fell apart. Afflicted by the dark jungle magic and the curse of the ogre mage Mai'Zoth, the Colonel and his core loyalists succumbed to madness, turning rogue and terrorizing the wilds. A handful of sound-minded soldiers led by Lieutenant Doren refused to participate in the atrocities. Breaking away from Kurzen's Compound, they established this hidden camp in the north to stage a desperate guerrilla campaign against their former comrades.

Reception from Tyrande. Reception from Tyrande is an Alliance quest that sends adventurers from the embattled slopes of the Stonetalon Mountains directly to the night elf capital of Darnassus. After aiding the Sentinels in securing their precarious foothold in Stonetalon against the Venture Company, you are sent by Sentinel Thenysil in Astranaar to receive formal recognition from High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind herself in the Temple of the Moon. The night elven outposts scattered throughout the Stonetalon Mountains face intense pressure, particularly from the Venture Company ravaging the land. Sentinel Thenysil coordinates efforts from Astranaar, but sustaining these remote bases requires immense resilience. Securing supply lines and intelligence is vital to maintaining an Alliance presence in Kalimdor's interior, making outside aid profoundly impactful to the Sentinels stationed there.

Recipe of the Kaldorei. Recipe of the Kaldorei is a lesson in balance taught by Zarrin, a culinary instructor in Dolanaar. By gathering a precise number of spider legs across Teldrassil, aspiring cooks learn that sustaining oneself from nature requires restraint and respect. Behind the inn in Dolanaar, Zarrin tends a bubbling cauldron and instructs young adventurers on the traditions of his people. Long before the modern age, night elves knew themselves as the kaldorei, meaning 'children of the stars.' For Zarrin, understanding that ancestral heritage begins not on the battlefield, but in the relationship between a hunter, their food, and the surrounding boughs of Teldrassil.

text.enUS: Reclaimers' Business in Desolace. Reclaimers' Business in Desolace is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers from Ironforge out to the harsh badlands of Desolace. Issued by Roetten Stonehammer, it sends recruits across the sea to meet Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point to assist the Reclaimers in recovering lost treasures and relics for a price. While Ironforge bustles with tradesfolk and dwarven affairs, distant Kalimdor remains an untamed frontier. Roetten Stonehammer acts as an urban liaison for the Reclaimers, an enterprising group looking to capitalize on forgotten ruins and barren lands. He recruits eager adventurers passing through the great mountain city, warning them that Desolace is an atrocious expanse overrun by warring centaur clans, yet ripe with profitable opportunity for those brave enough to make the journey.

text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is an Alliance quest offered by Keeper Albagorm atop Stonetalon Peak. It charges adventurers with culling the aggressive Bloodfury harpies who occupy the ruined valley of the Charred Vale, clearing a path so druids and caretakers can begin healing the scorched landscape. To the south of Stonetalon Peak lies the Charred Vale, a once-lush alpine haven reduced to ash and smoldering ruins. The devastation began when a mechanized logging and mining army swept through the sacred crags, stripping trees and fueling uncontrolled blazes. For the guardians stationed around Stonetalon, watching ancient woodland succumb to industrial greed is an intolerable wound upon the wilderness.
