text.enUS: Reclaiming the Charred Vale. Reclaiming the Charred Vale is a messenger quest tasked by Keeper Albagorm in Stonetalon Peak. Having temporarily suppressed the local harpies, Albagorm sends an Alliance traveler far south to Feralas to recruit the aid of the druid Falfindel Waywarder. The Charred Vale in southern Stonetalon Mountains remains an ash-choked reminder of catastrophic devastation. While Alliance forces under Keeper Albagorm have struck back against the rampant Bloodfury harpies nesting in the ruins, driving them off is merely a holding action. Albagorm recognizes that physical force alone cannot mend the ravaged earth before the harpies rally and reclaim their dominance.

Reconstructed Tome. The Reconstructed Tome is a pieced-together grimoire of dark cabal lore, compiled for warlocks seeking to expand their mastery of demonic servants. It contains the arcane knowledge and rituals necessary to summon and bind a predatory felhunter from the Twisting Nether. Recovered in fragments and painstakingly pieced back together, the Reconstructed Tome represents an elusive collection of cabal teachings known formally as the Tome of the Cabal. Warlocks of both the Alliance and the Horde go to great lengths to restore its frayed leaves, consulting occult scholars eager for a mere glimpse of its esoteric contents before surrendering the completed manuscript.

Recover the Key!. Elder Torntusk is held at Jintha'alor in shackles. He says Hitah'ya the Keeper has the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded, and he asks you to kill her and bring it back. After Kidnapped Elder Torntusk!, you find Elder Torntusk bound in shackles at Jintha'alor. Hitah'ya the Keeper holds the key to his bindings and is in the nearby cave, well guarded. Elder Torntusk asks you to kill her and fetch the key so his shackles come loose, for only then can he go home.

Recruitment Letter. The Recruitment Letter is an official dispatch handed to promising adventurers departing Durotar for duty in the Barrens. Issued by scout Takrin Pathseeker, it directs able-bodied volunteers to report to the border outpost overseen by Kargal Battlescar. As young warriors and scouts prove themselves around Razor Hill, the Horde's gaze turns west toward the vast, untamed expanse of the Barrens. Takrin Pathseeker identifies promising recruits who appear strong enough to handle frontline service and provides them with this letter. Crossing the Southfury River bridge marks a rite of passage: leaving the sheltered red dirt of Durotar behind to join the ranks of the Horde standing guard against quilboar, centaur, and Alliance scouts.

Red Burlap Bandana. In Northshire Valley, Deputy Willem gathers red bandanas from slain Defias thieves near the abbey vineyards. The cloth marks low-ranking highwaymen and cutpurses of the Brotherhood. Red burlap masks mark the Defias Brotherhood's rank-and-file. Cheap, rough cloth dyed red hides a thief's features and signals allegiance to the growing rebellion. In Northshire, young recruits and common thugs carry these scarves into the eastern orchards. The local guards recognize the striking red fabric as proof of thieves slain nearby.

Red Jack Flint. Red Jack Flint is a seasoned human mariner stationed within Menethil Keep in Menethil Harbor. A member of the crew of the vessel Maiden's Virtue, he serves as a point of contact for travelers seeking passage or contacts across the sea toward Kalimdor. Found inside the stone walls of Menethil Keep, Red Jack Flint is an experienced seafarer tied to the harbor's maritime trade. As part of the crew of the Maiden's Virtue, he navigates the dangerous sea routes linking the marshlands of Khaz Modan with distant shores. Rather than staying confined to naval routine, Flint directs capable adventurers to allies across the Great Sea, including contacts in Kalimdor like Fiora Longears.
Red Leather Bandana. In Westfall, Red Leather Bandanas mark those who defy Stormwind’s Crown. The Defias Brotherhood wears them as face coverings and a sign of their cause.

Red Leather Bandanas. At Sentinel Hill, Red Leather Bandanas mark the fight against the Defias Brotherhood. Scout Galiaan offers a reward for the red cloth masks worn by the outlaws, as the People's Militia struggles to track them across Westfall. Across Westfall, the red bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. The gang draws cutpurses, looters, and traitors from many walks of life, but its members rally beneath the same crimson sign. Scout Galiaan and the People's Militia at Sentinel Hill collect the bandanas as proof that bandits have fallen. The cloth also helps them follow the Defias as their fronts shift across the countryside.

Red Linen Bandana. Across Elwynn Forest, Red Linen Bandana marks the Defias Brotherhood. Its cloth hides a wearer’s face and can be put to use by local settlers. Across Elwynn Forest, full Defias operatives wear woven red linen bandanas. In Northshire Valley, lower-ranking initiates and common thugs use coarse burlap masks instead. The crimson cloth hides a face and marks allegiance to Edwin VanCleef's rogue fraternity. It also signals their rebellion against Stormwind's crown.

Red Linen Goods. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain needs cloth for her tailoring. She asks passing adventurers to hunt Defias bandits and take their linen bandanas, then uses the cloth to make goods for travelers. Defias bandits across Elwynn wear red linen bandanas. Their less organized kin in Northshire Valley make do with cheap burlap masks. For local craftsmen short on materials, the bandanas offer cloth they can use.

Red Rocks. Red Rocks is a towering sandstone bluff in northeastern Mulgore that serves as a sacred ancestral burial ground for the tauren. Here, the most valiant fallen champions are laid to rest, and young braves travel to its quiet heights to seek the wisdom of their forebears. Rising high above the plains of northeastern Mulgore, the crimson formations of Red Rocks mark a sacred threshold between the living world and the next. Tauren tradition reserves this solemn ground for their most valiant heroes—chieftains, defenders, and champions who gave their lives founding and protecting Thunder Bluff. They are laid to rest here in honor, among the graves of their forebears. It is equally a place of spiritual beginning, where young tauren complete their rites of passage by honoring the ancestral graves and communing with the wind.

Red Silk Bandanas. Red Silk Bandanas is a mission issued by Scout Riell on behalf of the People's Militia. It directs Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines to hunt down high-ranking Defias operatives and bring back their distinctive red silk masks as proof. While common cutpurses and highwaymen throughout Westfall tie coarse red cloth around their faces, the Defias Brotherhood maintains a strict internal hierarchy indicated by fabric. Scout Riell and the People's Militia have discovered that rank-and-file bandits wear rough weave, while senior conspirators and inner-circle operatives are distinguished by fine red silk. Stripping these bandanas directly targets the experienced officers coordinating Edwin VanCleef's uprising.

Red Wool Bandana. Red Wool Bandanas are makeshift symbols fashioned by imprisoned Defias cutthroats inside the Stormwind Stockade. Torn from jailhouse wool blankets, they serve as defiant emblems of brotherhood even behind bars. Even locked deep within the high stone walls of the Stormwind Stockade, members of the Defias Brotherhood refuse to surrender their identity. Using scraps torn from prison wool blankets, inmates secretly craft red bandanas to wear as identifying colors. To the guards, these scarves are contraband that spark fatal mutinies; to the prisoners, they are a statement that their brotherhood and rebellion endure, even in chains.

Rediscovering the Light. Offered by Aramis Hammerhand in Deathknell, this task challenges newly raised Forsaken paladins to embrace the Holy Light once more. Calling upon holy powers inflicts intense agony upon undead flesh, requiring fledgling paladins to channel healing into injured Deathguards despite the burning torment. For former champions of the Silver Hand and fallen knights of Lordaeron, awakening in undeath means confronting a horrifying reality: the Holy Light still answers their call, but it burns their withered bodies from within. Aramis Hammerhand instructs newly risen Forsaken paladins that abilities once practiced as second nature now bring excruciating pain. Because holy energy naturally conflicts with the foul magic sustaining undeath, channeling the Light requires raw willpower and agonizing perseverance.

Redridge Goulash. Redridge Goulash is a local culinary tradition kept alive by Chef Breanna in the lakeside settlement of Lakeshire. After exhausting her pantry to feed the defending Stormwind garrison during the recent Blackrock orc incursions, Breanna turns to traveling adventurers to replenish her supply of hearty mountain ingredients. Lakeshire sits perpetually under siege from Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and ferocious wild beasts. When the recent orc uprising broke out along the ridges, Chef Breanna shouldered the task of feeding the entire brigade of Stormwind troops stationed in town. Sustaining an active military garrison rapidly cleared out her cupboards, leaving the town cook with plenty of appetite to satisfy but empty larders.

Redridge Rendezvous. Promising Alliance rogues are sent east from Stormwind’s intelligence headquarters to train in Lakeshire. SI:7 wants them ready for dangerous field work under seasoned operatives. Renzik 'The Shiv', SI:7’s second-in-command in Stormwind, warns that untrained rogues rarely survive dangerous operations. Sending raw recruits into hostile territory brings casualties instead of intelligence. SI:7 sends promising agents east to the Redridge Mountains, where they train under Lucius, stationed among Lakeshire’s docks.

name.frFR: Encore du carburant pour la zappette

text.enUS: Refuel for the Zapping. Zorbin Fandazzle needs more water elemental cores. Setting up shop on the Forgotten Coast is a struggle, so the pay will be smaller, but Zorbin promises to tell everyone in earshot of your help and says there are friends in the Cartel. Zorbin Fandazzle jokes about the heroic deed of collecting goo from inside elemental beings, wondering whether you will want more of the same. Melodrama aside, Zorbin does need more water elemental cores. Establishing the shop here is a desperate business, so there is little to give in return, but Zorbin promises to tell everyone in earshot how you helped, and says to trust this because Zorbin knows people in the Cartel. Six cores are wanted, taken from Sea Elementals and Sea Sprays on the Forgotten Coast, and brought to Zorbin near the dock.

Refuge Pointe. Refuge Pointe is the primary redoubt for the Alliance and the surviving remnants of Stromgarde within the Arathi Highlands. Perched centrally along the highlands' trade road, it serves as a staging ground to reclaim the shattered capital of Stromgarde Keep and hold back rival forces across the region. Following the devastation of the Third War and the catastrophic fall of Stromgarde Keep, the bulk of Stromgarde's surviving populace fled south toward friendlier lands. Those who remained formed a resolute vanguard, digging in at Refuge Pointe under Captain Nials. Composed of battle-hardened Stromgarde soldiers, League of Arathor forces, and supporting Alliance specialists, the encampment represents the kingdom's last organized stand in its ancestral homeland.

Refugee. Throughout the violent history of Azeroth, constant warfare has repeatedly driven civilian populations from their homes. From the exodus of Stormwind during the First War to the tragic flight from Lordaeron in the Third War, refugees remain living testaments to the devastating costs of invasion, plague, and betrayal. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War, settlements like Goldshire, Moonbrook, and Grand Hamlet burned. Following the assassination of King Llane Wrynn, Sir Anduin Lothar took command of the kingdom's remnants. He gathered surviving soldiers and desperate civilians, escorting them to the harbor as the city burned. Lothar led a massive fleet across the Great Sea to the northern shores of Lordaeron. Arriving near Southshore, the exiled survivors—including the young Prince Varian Wrynn—were granted sanctuary by King Terenas Menethil II.

Regthar Deathgate. This directive dispatches seasoned Horde champions from major capitals to reinforce an outpost in the western Barrens. The veteran warrior Regthar Deathgate is marshaling capable volunteers for an impending campaign across the mountains into the arid wastes of Desolace. He seeks those willing to carry Horde steel against the entrenched centaur clans terrorizing the frontier. Across Kalimdor, influential leaders of the Horde—including Shadow Hunter Vol'jin, Nazgrel, and seasoned commanders like Belgrom Rockmaul—keep a watchful eye on potential threats along the borders. In the Barrens, an experienced warrior named Regthar Deathgate has established a defensive post guarding the western passes. Recognizing that regional skirmishes require hardened fighters rather than raw recruits, Horde officers direct proven adventurers west of the Crossroads to answer Regthar's call.

Rejold Barleybrew. Rejold Barleybrew is a master dwarven brewer stationed in the lakeside settlement of Brewnall Village in western Dun Morogh. Devoted to perfecting hearty mountain spirits, he regularly enlists travelers to gather regional ingredients and test his potent recipes across the snowy valley. In Dun Morogh, brewing is treated not merely as trade, but as a defining art form. Rejold Barleybrew embodies this tradition from Brewnall Village, an outpost nestled near the frozen lake of the Iceflow River. Rather than settling for common tavern swill, Rejold continually refines his blends, seeking rare hops, mountain minerals, and pristine ice water to produce stouts capable of warming the stoutest dwarven warriors.

Rejold's New Brew. Rejold's New Brew is an Alliance errand in Dun Morogh summoning an adventurer back to Brewnall Village. Having perfected a new concoction using gathered Shimmerweed, brewmaster Rejold Barleybrew wants a trusted friend to sample his latest recipe. It serves as the bridge between gathering brewing supplies and distributing his prized Shimmer Stout across the mountain realm. Word spreads quickly through Dun Morogh when a dwarven brewer strikes gold in his cellar. After securing Shimmerweed from the bitter slopes, local contacts like Tharek Blackstone or Pilot Bellowfiz urge passing adventurers to report back to Brewnall Village. Rejold Barleybrew has finished fermenting his experimental batches and is eager to share the spoils with the traveler who made it possible.

Release Them. A dying archaeologist in Searing Gorge urges you to release those whom the power of the Suntara still drives to keep at their labor, though their bodies have given out. Everything hinges on the altar of Suntara, and a relic guarded by Twilight's Hammer must be placed upon it. Before collapsing, the archaeologist begs you to release them. Their bodies have given out, yet the Suntara's power drives them on to keep at their labor. The key, says the archaeologist, is the altar of Suntara.

Rellian Greenspyre. This errand sends you from Denalan's lakeside retreat in Teldrassil into the capital city of Darnassus. Handing over a timberling seed to the druid Rellian Greenspyre reveals disturbing news about the spreading corruption in the boughs of the World Tree. Denalan has spent considerable effort cultivating and understanding the flora and elemental life around Lake Al'Ameth. Having collected seeds from the local timberlings, he dispatches you into Darnassus to present a sample to his colleague, Rellian Greenspyre. Rellian, a fellow druid who walks the tranquil terraces of the Cenarion Enclave, previously voiced curiosity about Denalan's research and hopes to raise a timberling of his own.

Rema Schneider. In Stormwind City, Rema Schneider works from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. She is a human citizen who often helps local shopkeepers and artisans with trade deliveries. Rema Schneider manages daily trade from the Canal Tailor and Fit Shop. The shop stands just west of the stone bridge into Cathedral Square, along Stormwind's canals. Cloth and finished garments move between local craftsmen, and Rema relies on helpful couriers to carry supplies between workshops.

name.esES: Gotas que quedan del agua más pura
name.ptBR: Gotas Restantes da Mais Pura Água

text.enUS: Remaining Drops of Purest Water. The Remaining Drops of Purest Water are the final residue of a specialized draught prepared by the water seer Brine. Shaman carrying these potent drops travel across kingdoms to cleanse a sacred water shrine corrupted by the Scourge's undead plague. Forged through ritual gathering across Kalimdor and Lordaeron, this concentrated elixir retains the purest essence of clean water, prepared by the hermit Brine in the Barrens. While part of the draught is consumed to grant shaman vision of distant elements, the remaining drops are safeguarded for a far more perilous task. Carried to the plague-choked shores of Silverpine Forest near the Sepulcher, the drops serve as the vital purifying catalyst atop the Brazier of Everfount. Consumed in ritual flames alongside the bracers of a fallen, tainted elemental, this pure water cuts through the necrotic corruption, calling forth an untainted spirit of water to commune with the shaman and complete their communion with the element.

Remedy of Arugal. The Remedy of Arugal is an incantation penned by the mage Arugal during his early experiments with worgen magic. Left behind in a dilapidated farmhouse in Silverpine Forest, the spell is sought by Dalar Dawnweaver to unravel the sorcerer's dark work. Before seizing Shadowfang Keep, Archmage Arugal took refuge at an abandoned wheat farm north of the river bridge in Silverpine Forest. There, amidst forgotten farm tools and rotting floorboards, he documented his strange arts in a set of dusty spellbooks. The scroll titled the Remedy of Arugal is among these notes, outlining early methods and magical formulations he devised while dabbling in the dangerous transmutations that cursed the local populace.

name.esES: Recuerda el amor que te tengo
name.ptBR: Lembre-se de que eu te amo

text.enUS: Remember That I Love You. "Remember That I Love You" begins with a torn, stained parchment discovered among the undead-stalked graves in the Ruins of Lordaeron. The letter tells the tragic tale of a lost child belonging to the Heartweaver family. Seeking answers requires carrying this fragile relic south to the orphanage in Stormwind City. Amid the blighted earth and shambling undead haunting the ruins of Capital City, survivors and scavengers occasionally stumble across reminders of the Third War's devastation. This torn, blood-stained bundle of parchment has barely survived the undead-trodden grounds of the graveyard. Mentioning a missing child of the Heartweaver lineage, it is a testament to lives shattered when Prince Arthas and the Scourge tore through the kingdom.

name.esES: Recuerda el amor que te tengo
name.ptBR: Lembre-se de que eu te amo

text.enUS: Remember That I Love You. In Stormwind, a blood-stained letter is bound for Jeremy Heartweaver. He has left the orphanage for a new home with Avette Fellwood in Duskwood. Children at the Stormwind Orphanage have lost their families to war, hardship, and the chaos gripping the kingdom. Jeremy Heartweaver was one of them until Avette Fellwood adopted him. She took him to live in Duskwood, where the woods are gloomy and life brings peril and hard labor. The orphanage caretakers believed a home with a family offered him more than remaining in the city.

Remnants of War. Remnants of War tasks adventurers with recovering shattered shards of the necrotic focusing crystal blown off Naxxramas during its assault on the Undercity. Both the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn suffered heavy losses repelling the citadel, and gathering these dangerous fragments prevents Scourge cultists from reclaiming their dark magic. Not long ago, the dread citadel Naxxramas loomed directly over Tirisfal Glades, seeking to wipe out the Undercity and erase the Forsaken entirely. In a desperate defense, the Forsaken and the Argent Dawn fought back the floating fortress at great cost. During the clash, the immense necrotic focusing crystal mounted atop Naxxramas was destroyed, blasting fragments across the glades below.

Remtravel's Excavation. Remtravel's Excavation is an archaeological dig site located in the southern reaches of Darkshore. Established by the dwarven Prospector Remtravel, the expedition recently struck ancient subterranean ruins, inadvertently unearthing hostile troggs and stone golems that quickly overran the quarry. Prospector Remtravel came to Darkshore in search of relics of the distant past, establishing an ambitious dig far from the safety of Auberdine. While excavating ancient strata, his team unearthed a swarm of subterranean Gravelflint troggs alongside hulking stone golems buried beneath the earth. The site was instantly transformed from a scholarly quarry into a hazard zone, scattering the miners and leaving Remtravel scrambling to retrieve his most promising findings.

Remulos. Keeper Remulos is a demigod son of Cenarius and the venerable protector of Moonglade. Alongside Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and Hamuul Runetotem, he helps guide the Cenarion Circle in the absence of his fallen father and the sleeping Malfurion Stormrage. Unlike Staghelm, Remulos prioritizes the broader balance of nature over night elven isolationism. Keeper Remulos is an immortal keeper of the grove, bearing the lower body of a great stag and the antlered torso of an ancient dryad-father. He watches over Moonglade, the sacred sanctuary of Azeroth's druids nestled north of Mount Hyjal. While Malfurion Stormrage remains trapped in the Emerald Dream, Remulos provides divine authority and counsel to the mortals of the Cenarion Circle. He remains deeply invested in healing Azeroth's scars, offering aid to druids pursuing their sacred rites around Lake Elune'ara.

Remy "Two Times". In Goldshire, Remy "Two Times" trades goods and pays for raw materials. He came from the Redridge Mountains and repeats the ends of his sentences. Remy "Two Times" trades from Goldshire, where he deals with travelers. He came west from the Redridge Mountains. When he speaks, he usually repeats the last words of each sentence twice. The odd habit gives him his nickname, but it does not keep him from seeking a profit in troubled Elwynn Forest.

Renato Gallina. In Stormwind's Trade District, Renato Gallina calls travelers toward his family's winery. Renato Gallina calls to passers-by among the Trade District stalls, proclaiming his family's vintages the finest in Stormwind. The Gallina family runs a winery along the Canals, and Renato promotes it with pamphlets. Travelers can bring one to his sister Suzetta at the shop for a free bottle of wine.

Render's Rock. Render's Rock is a cavern stronghold tucked into the northwestern crags of the Redridge Mountains, sitting near the high pass leading toward the Burning Steppes. Controlled by the fierce Blackrock orcs, it serves as a forward redoubt and an active staging ground for their raids on the valleys below. Carved into the rugged heights north of Lakeshire, Render's Rock serves as a fortified cave system for the invading Blackrock clan. From this defensible redoubt near the mountain pass to the Burning Steppes, veteran Blackrock orcs orchestrate attacks against the local defenders of Redridge. Its shadowed depths are strictly guarded, making any foray inside a perilous undertaking for those seeking to disrupt the orcish supply lines or recover captives lost in the ongoing conflict.

Render's Valley. Render's Valley is a tucked-away encampment held by Blackrock orcs in the southeastern Redridge Mountains. Far less entrenched than the massive fortresses of Stonewatch, it nonetheless poses a persistent threat to nearby travelers and hosts captives taken from surrounding lands. Tucked among the rocky ridges southeast of Lake Everstill, Render's Valley serves as an auxiliary camp for the Blackrock orcs operating in Redridge. Unlike the heavily fortified keeps and stone towers of the northern cliffs, the valley consists of a modest cluster of war tents, banners, and sentry outposts. Despite being smaller and less armed than the clan's core forces, the warriors here raid local roads, harass travelers, and keep captured prisoners in crude cages under guard.

Rendered Spores. Rendered Spores are a volatile emulsion prepared from fungal samples gathered across the Barrens. Created by Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads, the mixture decays rapidly unless swiftly delivered to Apothecary Zamah beneath Thunder Bluff for stabilizing. After acquiring strange fungal spores from mushrooms near the damp oases of the Barrens, Apothecary Helbrim processes them into an active chemical emulsion known as Rendered Spores. The delicate extraction suspends the potent compounds of the fungal growths in a liquid medium, but the solution is chemically unstable. It maintains its vital potency for only forty-five minutes before breaking down and becoming completely useless for scientific study.

Renferrel's Findings. Renferrel's Findings is a collection of research notes compiled by Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine Forest. Entrusted to Horde couriers, these documents carry vital data southward to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill to assist in brewing the Forsaken's New Plague. The Royal Apothecary Society labours tirelessly under direct orders from the Dark Lady, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, to engineer a New Plague. Achieving this breakthrough requires constant collaboration among researchers scattered across Lordaeron. Stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest, Apothecary Renferrel compiles these findings to document his progress and experiments, sending the gathered intelligence south to Tarren Mill so fellow researchers can build upon his results.

Renzik "The Shiv". Renzik "The Shiv" is a goblin operative and the trusted second-in-command of SI:7, stationed inside their headquarters in Stormwind City's Old Town. He serves Spymaster Mathias Shaw faithfully, directing the new rogue recruits sent to him from across the Alliance. Renzik keeps the story of his past to himself. What Stormwind knows is that this goblin found his way into SI:7 and now stands as Spymaster Mathias Shaw's second in command. He is short on patience and pleasantries, greeting new recruits by asking whether they are ready to get to work or need a nap first.

Report Back to Fizzlebub. Kravel Koalbeard says the Fool's Stout worked great. He has put money on the next race, hoping the crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. You carry a note about the successful test to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay. This follows the pit crew you chose to make drunk. Kravel Koalbeard says the Fool's Stout worked great. He has put money on the next race, hoping the pit crew you made drunk wrecked their own car. One more job remains: take a note about the successful test to Crank Fizzlebub in Booty Bay, who will want to hear of it. Kravel also hopes more of the stout can be had for future races.

Report on the Defias Brotherhood. At Stormwind Keep, a report on the Defias Brotherhood carries the findings of a long investigation to the royal court. City Architect Baros Alexston entrusts it to the adventurer who uncovered the conspiracy. City Architect Baros Alexston prepared a report for Stormwind's leaders after a long investigation into unrest in Westfall and nearby lands. He entrusted the document to the adventurer who unraveled the conspiracy. The report is carried to Stormwind Keep, where it is meant to accompany a personal audience about the conspirators' schemes and the danger they pose to the kingdom.

Report to Anastasia. Report to Anastasia is a summons issued to developing Horde mages across Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Anastasia Hartwell, a prominent arcanist in the Undercity's Magic Quarter, has detected an unknown magical disturbance within the city and requires capable spellcasters to investigate. Word travels quickly through the ranks of Horde spellcasters. Whether studying atop the bluffs of Thunder Bluff, in the dusty heat of Durotar, or amid the ruins of Lordaeron, mages of sufficient talent receive a clear directive. The arcane practitioners of the Undercity have sensed an unexplainable disturbance rippling through their domain, and they require assistance on the ground.

Report to Captain Stoutfist. Report to Captain Stoutfist is an Alliance military directive in Menethil Harbor. Following initial skirmishes against the Dragonmaw clan at Dun Algaz, Valstag Ironjaw sends proven combatants inside the harbor's keep to coordinate deeper defense efforts. Captain Stoutfist commands the local garrison and is organizing direct strikes against the entrenched orcs across the Wetlands. While dwarven mountaineers have long monitored the narrow mountain passes of Dun Algaz, the resurgence of the Dragonmaw clan cannot be contained to the borders of Loch Modan alone. Valstag Ironjaw recognizes that these orcs are pressing outward, establishing encampments and threatening the entirety of the marshlands. Securing the pass is merely the opening move in a larger campaign to safeguard the road to Ironforge.

Report to Doren. After obtaining the patrol information, Corporal Sethman directs you back to Lieutenant Doren. Delivering these findings brings crucial military intelligence directly to the rebels' commander in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Corporal Sethman reminds you that Lieutenant Doren wants a direct report on the patrol information. You must bring what you learned back to Doren.

Report to Goldshire. Report to Goldshire marks an adventurer's formal transition from the sheltered grounds of Northshire Valley into the broader jurisdiction of Elwynn Forest. Bearing dispatches from Marshal McBride to Marshal Dughan, recruits are granted Acting Deputy Status amid growing regional neglect from Stormwind's nobility. Having proven their mettle against local troubles within Northshire Valley, recruits are officially released from Northshire's local guard by Marshal McBride. In recognition of their service, McBride prepares transfer papers directing them south past the border gates along the road into Goldshire, transferring their responsibilities to the wider expanse of Elwynn Forest.

Report to Gryan Stoutmantle. Westfall needs fighters, and Report to Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to answer the call. The crown leaves the outer farmlands to fend for themselves, so local defenders gather under Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Westfall calls for skilled fighters from across the river. Brigands, gnolls, and hostile harvest golems are driving the farmlands into chaos. With no royal battalions answering, local volunteers must defend the realm.

Report to Hadrec. Report to Hadrec is a Horde military dispatch directing champions within the Sepulcher to consult Silverpine's field commander. Following Apothecary Renferrel and Bethor Iceshard's investigation into the Scourge presence in Lake Lordamere, High Executor Hadrec coordinates the martial preparations required to storm Fenris Isle. It marks the transition from magical reconnaissance to direct tactical warfare. While Apothecary Renferrel and the mage Bethor Iceshard spent considerable effort divining the threat posed by the renegade necromancer Thule Ravenclaw, scholarly study alone cannot dislodge a rising Scourge stronghold. With Ravenclaw actively binding the restless dead across Fenris Isle, Renferrel recognized that the problem had grown far beyond alchemical or arcane solutions. Halting this burgeoning infection required the hard steel and disciplined forces of the Forsaken military, shifting the matter from the apothecaries' tables straight to the commander's desk.

Report to Helgrum. Neeka Bloodscar has written a fresh report for Helgrum the Swift in Stonard, and asks you to carry it there. This follows your visit to Neeka at Kargath. Neeka Bloodscar has written a new report for Helgrum in Stonard and hands it to you. Neeka adds that anyone who calls themselves an outrunner must not lose the way, or fall to an enemy.

Report to Ironforge. This errand sends an adventurer from Thelsamar in Loch Modan into the heart of Ironforge with critical updates from Ironband's Excavation Site. Delivering the excavation progress report to Prospector Stormpike in the Assembly of Explorers sets off an investigation into missing blastpowder and stalled archaeology in the foothills. Archaeological expeditions throughout Khaz Modan rely heavily on funding, supplies, and oversight from the Explorers' League. When Prospector Ironband's dig site in southern Loch Modan runs short of blasting supplies, his overseers cannot simply requisition more locally. Jern Hornhelm at the Thelsamar inn entrusts an adventurer with carrying Ironband's written report across the mountain passes directly to Prospector Stormpike at League headquarters.

Report to Kadrak. Thork at the Crossroads directs able Horde fighters north to Kadrak's watch tower near the Ashenvale border. Kadrak coordinates the Horde's expansion into the ancient forest and prepares incoming recruits for the ongoing skirmishes ahead. While the Crossroads deals with quilboar, centaur, and local brigands, the Horde's broader territorial interests look north toward the thick forests of Ashenvale. Thork acts as an intermediary, directing seasoned fighters who have proven themselves in the central Barrens toward the northern border tower manned by Kadrak.

Report to Kadrak. This military dispatch directs Horde warriors from Malaka'jin in the Stonetalon Mountains to Kadrak's watch post on the border of the northern Barrens. It marks the transition from defending the crags to reinforcing the Horde's contentious military campaign inside Ashenvale. By reporting to Kadrak, soldiers are marshaled to support forward encampments like Splintertree Post and the Zoram Strand. In the craggy pass of Malaka'jin, the orc Darn Talongrip keeps an eye on the Horde's southern and mountain frontiers. Yet the greatest military pressure lies northward in the ancient forests of Ashenvale, where night elf sentinels clash incessantly with Warsong lumber gatherers. Recognizing blooded fighters passing through Stonetalon, Darn directs capable recruits toward the northern Barrens watch tower to assist with ongoing campaigns.

name.frFR: Un rapport pour le Montagnard Rochegar

text.enUS: Report to Mountaineer Rockgar. Report to Mountaineer Rockgar is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing adventurers north from the guard posts of Loch Modan toward Dun Algaz. Mountaineer Kadrell dispatches capable travelers to join Rockgar, who is organizing a vital expedition into the sodden lowlands of the Wetlands. It serves as the gateway passage connecting the dwarven homeland to northern territories. Dun Algaz represents the crucial artery between Loch Modan and the marshy expanses of the Wetlands. Built into the northern mountain ridge, the fortified pass has long guaranteed safe passage for trade, messengers, and military detachments moving between Ironforge and Alliance settlements further north. With tensions rising along the borders, Mountaineer Kadrell keeps a close watch on travellers passing through, recruiting hardy volunteers to reinforce the northern outposts.

Report to Orgnil. Report to Orgnil is an early Horde quest dispatched by Master Gadrin from Sen'jin Village. It directs fledgling adventurers northward to Razor Hill to warn Orgnil Soulscar about the insidious reach of the Burning Blade cult. This dispatch helps coordinate Durotar's scattered defense against demonic corruption brewing right in the orcs' homeland. While Sen'jin Village grapples with its own local woes—most notably Zalazane's treachery on the Echo Isles—Master Gadrin recognizes that reports of the Burning Blade cult represent a far wider danger. Whispers of demonic corruption were uncovered in the Valley of Trials, and the Darkspear witch doctor knows these threats cannot be handled in isolation. He dispatches traveling heroes north along the dusty road to Razor Hill, where the local orc authorities maintain a broader watch over Durotar.

name.frFR: Faire un rapport au Village de Sen'jin

text.enUS: Report to Sen'jin Village. Report to Sen'jin Village marks the moment young Horde initiates leave the secluded Valley of Trials behind to alert the Darkspear trolls of demonic cult activity. Entrusted by Zureetha Fargaze, messengers carry word of the Burning Blade to Master Gadrin, discovering that shadow magic already threatens the nearby coasts. After proving their combat mettle and recovering dark medallions from the Burning Blade Coven within the Valley of Trials, novices are declared ready for the wider world. Zureetha Fargaze recognizes that the demonic presence within the sacred proving grounds is no isolated nuisance, but a symptom of a creeping blight across Durotar. She directs young adventurers east past the ravine's mouth and south toward the coast to warn the Darkspear tribe.

Report to Zor. Nazeer Bloodpike finds it strange that common soldiers were carrying the jeweled pendant Marg stole. Calling it a noble's piece, Nazeer sends you to Orgrimmar with it, to Zor Lonetree, who is well schooled in Alliance politics. Nazeer Bloodpike finds it strange that common soldiers held a pendant like this. Its owner may have been in disguise, or the soldiers may have stolen it themselves. Either way, Nazeer judges it a noble's pendant, and its true owner must be found if the mystery is to unravel. Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar knows a great deal about Alliance politics, and can say whether the pendant belongs to Stormwind's nobility.

Rescue OOX-09/HL!. After the beacon has stirred the fallen homing robot, Oglethorpe Obnoticus speaks from the robot itself. OOX-09/HL needs an open, safe place to begin its take-off, so it is to be escorted to the shoreline beyond Overlook Cliff, and then Oglethorpe waits in Booty Bay. Oglethorpe's voice crackles from the robot again. The machine needs an open, safe place to begin a lengthy take-off procedure, and the shoreline beyond Overlook Cliff will do nicely. Its built-in cloaking cannot be used yet, and Oglethorpe needs time to make it operational again.

Rescue OOX-17/TN!. The damaged homing robot OOX-17/TN speaks with Oglethorpe's voice. It needs an open, safe place for a lengthy take-off, and you are asked to see it safely to Steamwheedle Port, and then to find Oglethorpe Obnoticus in Booty Bay. Oglethorpe's voice crackles from the robot once more. The robot has built-in cloaking, but Oglethorpe needs time to make it operational again, so it must reach an open, safe place where its lengthy take-off procedure can begin. Steamwheedle Port is the spot Oglethorpe has in mind, and the trip gives the time needed to get things working. Your part is to escort the robot there safely.

Rescue OOX-22/FE!. After finding the homing robot OOX-22/FE in Feral Scar Vale, you hear the gnome's voice crackle from it once more. The robot is to be escorted to the Forgotten Coast dock, and afterwards Oglethorpe Obnoticus wants a word with you in Booty Bay. The gnome's voice says OOX-22/FE needs somewhere open and safe where a lengthy take-off can begin. The robot has built-in cloaking, but Oglethorpe Obnoticus needs time to make it work again. Oglethorpe suggests the Forgotten Coast dock, long enough for getting everything running, so the robot is to be walked there from where it stands.

Researching the Corruption. Gershala Nightwhisper in Auberdine seeks corrupted brain stems from the creatures infesting Blackfathom Deeps. Disturbed by reports of the blood elves dabbling in demonic magic across the sea, he hopes to study the physiological descent of the naga and satyr to foresee—and perhaps avert—another catastrophic elven mutation. To the night elves of Kalimdor, the ruin of their ancient kin is a living memory etched into monsters. Ten thousand years ago, the Highborne succumbed to the allure of demonic energies, warping themselves into horned satyrs or drowning into serpentine naga. Watching the high elves rebrand themselves as blood elves and embrace dark magic strikes Gershala Nightwhisper not as a distant curiosity, but as history doomed to repeat itself.

Resonite Crystal. Resonite Crystals are rare mineral samples mined by kobolds inside Boulderslide Cavern in the Stonetalon Mountains. Their frantic digging has drawn the concern of Mor'rogal at Sun Rock Retreat.

Rest and Relaxation. Rest and Relaxation is an introductory Alliance quest directing newly trained adventurers from Northshire south along the road to the Lion's Pride Inn. Run by Innkeeper Farley, the bustling Goldshire tavern offers food, drink, and a warm hearth for those seeking a reprieve from the road. After cutting their teeth in Northshire, weary travelers are pointed south toward the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. The road south leads directly to the beloved tavern, run by Innkeeper Farley. For new adventurers stepping out into the wider forest, it represents the first major outpost offering hearth, shelter, and hot meals away from the Abbey.

Restabilization Cog. Restabilization Cogs are precision mechanical components salvaged from the leper gnomes wandering outside the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. In Kharanos, gnomish tinkerers require these intact parts to construct the Recombobulator, an ambitious machine intended to reverse leper mutation. When radiation flooded Gnomeregan in a disastrous attempt to wipe out the invading troggs, countless gnomes were twisted into sick, hostile leper gnomes. Despite their madness, these afflicted exiles still carry intricate gnomish machinery and salvageable fittings. Tinkers Ozzie Togglevolt and Razzle Sprysprocket believe the horrific transformation can be systematically undone. To finish their prototype Recombobulation Device, they rely on adventurers to recover vital parts directly from the afflicted outside Gnomeregan's gates, including intact Restabilization Cogs to balance the machine's inner combustion systems.

Resting in Pieces. Resting in Pieces begins when an adventurer recovers the animated, severed head of Alaric, a former servant of the necromancer Thule Ravenclaw on Fenris Isle. Alaric pleads to be carried across Fenris Keep to an unmarked grave near the stables where the rest of his remains lie buried. Before his gruesome fate, Alaric served as the chief servant and personal bodyguard to Thule Ravenclaw, a powerful Scourge-aligned mage operating out of Fenris Keep in Silverpine Forest. When the Plague of Undeath swept the region, Thule claimed he would use his arcane sorcery to protect Alaric from falling victim to it. Instead, the twisted ward trapped Alaric in a permanent, agonizing state of undeath, leaving his consciousness fully intact within his severed parts.

Restocking the Larders. Restocking the Larders is a provisioning quest in the Shen'dar Highlands of Zephras. With escalating wilderness threats keeping villagers from foraging, an adventurer is enlisted to gather eggs and strider meat to sustain the settlement. As unrest and rising dangers spread across the Shen'dar Highlands, normal daily life on Zephras has grown increasingly fraught. Everyday villagers can no longer safely venture into the wilderness to forage or hunt, leaving communal food stores severely diminished. To keep the settlement fed, local cooks must turn to traveling adventurers with the strength and skill to brave the wild trails.

text.enUS: Restoring Fiery Flux Supplies via Heavy Leather. After What the Flux?, Master Smith Burninate turns to replenishing the dwindling supply of fiery flux in the Searing Gorge. Burninate wants incendosaur scales, heavy leather, and coal, and will take all you can offer. Master Smith Burninate has no time for idle talk. Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, heavy leather, and coal: two scales, ten pieces of heavy leather, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.

Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, iron bars, and coal: two scales, four iron bars, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.

text.enUS: Restoring Fiery Flux Supplies via Kingsblood. After What the Flux?, Master Smith Burninate turns to replenishing the dwindling supply of fiery flux in the Searing Gorge. Burninate wants incendosaur scales, Kingsblood, and coal, and will take all you can offer. Master Smith Burninate has no time for idle talk. Fiery flux is running low, and Burninate asks for incendosaur scales, Kingsblood, and coal: two scales, four Kingsblood, and coal. Burninate will take all that you can offer.

Resupplying the Excavation. Resupplying the Excavation is an Alliance quest in Loch Modan where adventurers pursue a powder shipment meant for Ironband's Excavation Site. Dispatched by Jern Hornhelm to catch up with the pack team, the traveler follows their route along the shore of the Loch. Ironband's Excavation Site in southern Loch Modan requires a steady supply of blastpowder to break through the stubborn rock of the dig. After blastpowder was delivered to Thelsamar, local quartermaster Jern Hornhelm arranged for three dwarves—Huldar, Miran, and Saean—to haul the volatile barrels south along the lakeside road. Burdened by the weighty cargo, the supply party moved slowly, giving travelers in Thelsamar an opportunity to catch up and lend support on the road.

Rethban Caverns. Rethban Caverns is an extensive cave system tucked into the northwestern cliffs of the Redridge Mountains. Infested with aggressive Redridge gnolls, it is best known as the sole source of uncommon Rethban ore. Carved deep into the northwestern mountains overlooking Lake Everstill, Rethban Caverns serves as a fortified redoubt for the local gnolls. Under the cunning leadership of Ardo Dirtpaw, the pack fiercely guards the twisting passages and subterranean chambers, attacking any wanderers who stray too close to their hillside entrance.

Rethban Ore. Foreman Oslow sends you into Rethban Caverns in Redridge for a dark mineral the scribes of Northshire Abbey need for ink. It is too soft for strong weapons or armor, but its color makes it useful for their work. Scribes at Northshire Abbey prize Rethban Ore for its dark, flat color. Bart Rethban discovered the mineral, but it has little use at an armorer’s anvil. Smelted metal from the ore lacks the strength needed for sturdy weapons or plate. Its raw color instead makes a valued base for manuscript dyes.

Rethiel the Greenwarden. Rethiel the Greenwarden is an enigmatic presence residing deep within the Green Belt of the Wetlands. He is tied to the marsh's uneasy balance and calls on travelers to deal with the threats that disrupt it. Rethiel seeks to alleviate the suffering of the Wetlands by dispatching sympathetic adventurers against its major agitators. He urges visitors to hunt down destructive Mosshide gnolls who ravage the wildlife, strip them of the crude flints they use to burn the marsh's living trees, and thin out the diseased fen creepers that fester in the marsh waters. Through these cullings, he hopes to restore peace to the wounded soil.

Retrieval for Mauren. Retrieval for Mauren is a quest given by Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind. Hearing tales of travelers venturing deep into Kalimdor, the wizard contracts Alliance adventurers to gather crystallised scales from basilisks dwelling in Stonetalon's Charred Vale. Mauren seeks these rare specimens to grind into dust as reagents for his personal spellcraft. Collin Mauren, a wizard residing in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind City, keeps an ear close to the chatter of wandering adventurers. Word has reached him that the distant Stonetalon Mountains in Kalimdor have become a burgeoning hotspot for travelers seeking wild wyverns, unruly elementals, or lucrative deals and clashes with the Venture Company. Rather than seeking riches or glory, Mauren's interest lies in the rare natural wonders reported from the region's harshest corners.
