text.enUS: Royal Historian Archesonus. Royal Historian Archesonus is a dwarven scholar serving King Magni Bronzebeard within Ironforge's High Seat. Renowned for her scholarly works documenting recent catastrophes in the northern human kingdoms, she also directs research into ancient dwarven tragedies, notably the scorched remains of the Dark Iron kingdom. Stationed steps from King Magni Bronzebeard's throne in the High Seat, Royal Historian Archesonus maintains historical records on behalf of the Ironforge crown. Her academic gaze extends well beyond the Khaz Modan mountains. She authored 'The Fall of Lordaeron and the Scouring of the Eastweald' as well as 'On Plagues, Curses, and Blights,' tracking the horrific collapse of humanity's northern realm under the Scourge. Rather than hiding from dark histories, Archesonus approaches disasters methodically, seeking to record the truth of ruinous magic and political collapse.

Royal Library. Scholars come to the Royal Library in Stormwind Keep for the kingdom’s records and histories. Head Librarian Milton Sheaf watches over its scrolls and treatises, from ancient wars to accounts of realms beyond the sea. The Royal Library offers quiet among Stormwind Keep’s guarded halls and courtly intrigues. Milton Sheaf oversees its shelves of southern human history, from surviving texts written before the First War to recent military chronicles and recovered tomes. Alliance scholars, priests, and travelers may browse its treatises. They cover the founding of the Alliance of Lordaeron and the recent arrival of Thrall’s Horde in Kalimdor.

Royal Quarter. The Royal Quarter is the secluded seat of power within the Undercity, serving as the throne room for Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. Here, the Banshee Queen directs the Forsaken alongside her dreadlord enforcer, Varimathras, guarded by an elite cohort of Royal Dreadguards. Tucked away behind towering archways and shadowed corridors, the Royal Quarter—also known as the Hall of the Dark Lady—is the political and military nerve center of the Forsaken. Sylvanas Windrunner holds court in this cavernous subterranean chamber, plotting the survival of her free-willed undead and the destruction of the Scourge. Heavily armored Royal Dreadguards stand vigil along the dais, ensuring that uninvited guests and would-be assassins never reach their queen.

Rude Awakening. Rude Awakening is the first task given to newly awakened Forsaken within the crypts of Deathknell. After rising from death freed from the Lich King's iron grip, you are directed away from the incinerators and sent down the hill to learn the reality of your new existence from Shadow Priest Sarvis. Opening your eyes in the damp subterranean chill of Deathknell's crypt is an unsettling introduction to undeath. Undertaker Mordo stands watch over the freshly interred, sorting the revived into those who have reclaimed their free will and those destined for the burning pits. For many, rising from the grave means waking to rot, cold stone, and total disorientation, having slipped through the grasp of the Scourge by sheer circumstance.

Ruga Ragetotem. Ruga Ragetotem is a veteran tauren warrior stationed at Camp Taurajo in the southern Barrens. Serving as a mentor to promising Horde fighters, he tests their mettle against the strange silithid infestation emerging nearby before sending them toward custom armor. Standing watch over Camp Taurajo, Ruga Ragetotem helps train emerging warriors looking to prove their strength in Kalimdor. Recognizing the sudden, unsettling emergence of insectoid silithid carving hives into the Field of Giants to the south, Ruga sets a trial for young fighters to hunt the beasts and sever their antennae. Those who endure the ordeal earn his respect and a recommendation to the renowned armorsmith Thun'grim Firegaze.

Ruined Reaches. The Ruined Reaches comprise the treacherous southern coastline of Azshara near the border with Durotar. Marked by crumbling ancient ruins, shattered shipwrecks, and jagged shallows, these beaches are overrun by aggressive shoreline predators. Amid the desolation, a small gnomish outpost perches high on a cliffside above the surf. Stretching along the southern borders of Azshara just north of Durotar, the Ruined Reaches are a maze of rocky inlets, cliff faces, and debris-strewn sand. Like the Jagged Reef further north, hidden shallows make maritime travel extremely hazardous, leaving numerous ruined vessels broken along the shore. The waters and beaches teem with hostile wildlife, including territorial murlocs, vicious hydras, and armored makrura, making overland transit just as dangerous as navigating the surf.

Ruins of Aboraz. The Ruins of Aboraz are ancient Gurubashi stone ruins nestled along the southeastern cliffs of Stranglethorn Vale. Once part of the sprawling jungle troll empire, the crumbling terraces now serve as the secluded redoubt for the renegade witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his mind-addled thralls. Perched on the bluffs southeast of the Ruins of Jubuwal and south of the Crystalvein Mine, the weathered masonry of Aboraz has been transformed into an alchemical testing ground. Zanzil the Outcast was banished by the local tribes and the mainlanders alike, retreating here to brew potent mind-altering concoctions and toxic elixirs. Within the stone courtyards, Zanzil exerts total control over an unsettling menagerie of servitors, including shambling undead ghouls, corrupted troll thralls, and even co-opted coastal naga.

Ruins of Alterac. The snow-covered Ruins of Alterac are all that remain of Alterac City, once the proud mountain capital of the Kingdom of Alterac. Cast out of the Alliance and put under martial law after King Aiden Perenolde's treason during the Second War, the shattered stronghold is now overrun by the brutish Crushridge ogres. Alterac was once an independent human realm carved out of the old Arathor empire, perched high on the trade routes through the mountains. During the Second War, fearing destruction at the hands of the invading Old Horde, King Aiden Perenolde secretly struck a pact with the orcs. When the betrayal was uncovered following the fighting at Caer Darrow, the Alliance of Lordaeron retaliated swiftly. King Terenas Menethil II put the city under martial law and deposed Perenolde. The grand fortifications, church, and palace fell into disrepair as the populace fled or turned to outlawry.

Ruins of Andorhal. Once the agricultural hub and grain distribution center of northern Lordaeron, the Ruins of Andorhal now lie at the heart of the Western Plaguelands as a devastated Necropolis stronghold. Under the dominion of the lich Araj the Summoner, the shattered township crawls with legions of undead abominations, ghouls, and wraiths. Andorhal was the initial staging ground for the plague of undeath in Lordaeron, where grain tainted by the Cult of the Damned was packed and distributed across the human kingdom. Today, the ruined city serves as a sprawling bastion of the Scourge in the Western Plaguelands. Araj the Summoner presides over the center of the ruins, flanked by ghouls, skeletal horrors, and towering flesh golems. Scouting parties of the Scarlet Crusade periodically probe the city's outskirts, but the Scourge maintains iron control over the shattered streets.

Ruins of Constellas. The Ruins of Constellas are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in Felwood, nestled near the roots of Mount Hyjal. Today, the once-sacred grounds are overrun by the Jadefire satyrs, who have violently profaned the settlement's moonwell with demonic fel magic. The classical stone arches and crumbling plazas of Constellas reveal that this was once an idyllic night elven community. During the Third War, the Burning Legion's march through Felwood shattered the haven, leaving it exposed to lingering demonic corruption. Now, the foul Jadefire satyrs hold dominion over the stones. Led by Xavathras, they actively tend to a defiled moonwell, transforming pure waters into a font of noxious fel power on behalf of their master, Lord Xavaric.

Ruins of Eldarath. The Ruins of Eldarath are the shattered remains of a pre-Sundering Highborne city perched along the rocky bluffs of Azshara. Once a bastion of Kaldorei arcane scholarship, its fallen plazas and crumbling temples are now overrun by hostile naga. Scholars and adventurers brave the dangerous coastal ruins searching for inscribed tablets and forgotten relics of the ancient past. Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor ten thousand years ago, Eldarath was a flourishing night elven city. Renowned Highborne mages gathered here, carving their deepest arcane insights and fundamental magical rules into grand stone tablets left in public squares for their peers to study. The Sundering dropped much of Eldarath into the Bay of Storms. The portions that survived along the eastern cliffs have sat shunned by modern night elves for millennia, slowly claimed by creeping salt spray and ivy.

Ruins of Isildien. The Ruins of Isildien are the sprawling remains of an ancient night elven city in southwestern Feralas, destroyed ten millennia ago during the Great Sundering. Today, the overgrown stonework and cracked temple courtyards are occupied by brutish Gordunni ogres. Ten thousand years ago, before the world shattered, Isildien was a grand night elven settlement nestled in the primordial forests of ancient Kalimdor. Its graceful marble arches and grand terraces stood as monuments to kaldorei civilization and devotion. When the Well of Eternity imploded and tore the continents apart, Isildien fell into ruined desolation, smothered under millennia of untamed jungle growth. Dominating the upper terrace is a colossal domed structure remarkably reminiscent of Darnassus's Temple of the Moon, suggesting the city was once a significant sanctuary dedicated to Elune.

Ruins of Jubuwal. The Ruins of Jubuwal are the crumbling remnants of an ancient Gurubashi settlement located just east of the Gurubashi Arena in Stranglethorn Vale. Once a place of empire and ritual, the ruins have fallen under the sway of the rogue witch doctor Zanzil the Outcast and his bizarre retinue of minions. Situated off the primary thoroughfare cutting through Stranglethorn Vale, Jubuwal was once part of the grand Gurubashi civilization. Today, stone carvings and ivy-draped masonry have been overtaken by Zanzil the Outcast, an eccentric witch doctor known for his potent concoctions and foul voodoo. Zanzil has filled the ruins with an unnatural menagerie of followers, including enthralled ghouls, subjugated naga, and renegade trolls. Desperate fugitives also lurk among the stone arches, such as Jon-Jon the Crow and Maury 'Club Foot' Wilkins, both hiding from the ruthless debt collector 'Sea Wolf' MacKinley back in Booty Bay.

Ruins of Kel'Theril. The Ruins of Kel'Theril are the shattered remnants of an ancient night elven city bordering the frozen expanse of Lake Kel'Theril in central Winterspring. Destroyed ten thousand years ago during the Great Sundering, its frostbitten stone pillars and temples remain haunted by the tormented spirits of Highborne who perished in the cataclysm. Long before Winterspring became a frozen highland, Kel'Theril stood as a grand settlement of the ancient night elven empire. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, the city was blasted into ruin and buried beneath ice and snow. The disaster caught the residing Highborne unaware, binding their souls to the snowbound stones. Today, the spirits of these former spellcasters linger among the frostbitten arches, endlessly reliving their final, catastrophic moments.

Ruins of Lordaeron. The Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollowed-out surface remnants of Capital City, the once-glorious heart of humanity's northern empire. Destroyed when Prince Arthas murdered his father and unleashed the Scourge, the blasted courtyards and throne room now serve as the fortified gateway to the Undercity below. Capital City was once the radiant summit of human civilization, uniting the northern realms under King Terenas Menethil II. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend carrying the cursed runeblade Frostmourne, the celebrations turned into a slaughterhouse. Arthas slew his father on the throne, leaving the metropolis to rot under Scourge rule. Following the civil war that tore the Scourge apart, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner claimed the devastated palace, securing the surface while expanding the crypts and dungeons beneath into the Undercity.

Ruins of Mathystra. The Ruins of Mathystra are the crumbled remnants of an ancient night elven city sitting along the northern coast of Darkshore. Shattered during the Great Sundering ten thousand years ago, the coastal ruins are now overrun by hostile Stormscale naga and prowled by elusive Ghost Sabers. Ten millennia ago, Mathystra stood as a bustling night elven settlement, home to high-ranking Highborne nobility. When the Well of Eternity collapsed during the Great Sundering, cataclysmic waves shattered the coastal city, toppling its grand marble arches and washing much of its stonework into the sea. The surviving night elves abandoned the ruined city in favor of smaller woodland villages further south, leaving Mathystra's sunken courtyards and cracked foundations to the relentless coastal elements.

Ruins of Ordil'Aran. The Ruins of Ordil'Aran are the crumbling remnants of an ancient night elf settlement in northwestern Ashenvale, situated between Maestra's Post and Bathran's Haunt. Once a hidden redoubt for shadow cultists, the fallen stones have recently been overrun by the corrupted Thistlefur furbolgs. Little remains of the original Kaldorei architecture at Ordil'Aran save for weathered pillars, cracked arches, and moss-draped stonework. For a time, the isolated ruins served as a lair for the Cult of the Dark Strand, who lurked among the debris to ambush travelers along the northwestern paths of Ashenvale. Recently, however, violent furbolgs of the Thistlefur tribe drove out the cultists in a bloody takeover. The bodies of fallen Dark Strand practitioners still litter the ground while aggressive furbolgs patrol the perimeter, fiercely guarding the site and the ancient Heartswood tree growing within.

Ruins of Ravenwind. The Ruins of Ravenwind are the shattered remnants of an ancient Highborne city nestled in northern Feralas. Today, the crumbling marble structures are heavily infested by the vicious Northspring harpies and guarded by brooding dragonkin. Much like the great city of Dire Maul to the east, the Ruins of Ravenwind stand as a solemn monument to the height and hubris of ancient Highborne civilization before the Great Sundering. Long abandoned by its original kaldorei architects, the site has succumbed to creeping wild foliage, forgotten arcane altars, and the foul roosts of Northspring harpies who prey on anything wandering beneath the shattered arches.

Ruins of Stardust. The Ruins of Stardust are an ancient, fallen night elven holy sanctuary nestled on a lake island in southwestern Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, the island's waters and native bog beasts have suffered corruption from demonic rot washing down from Felwood. Despite this pervasive blight, luminous stardust shrubs still thrive amidst the crumbling stones, retaining potent restorative power. Resting on a solitary island south of Astranaar, the Ruins of Stardust were once a venerated night elf holy site. Today, an eerie, sickly yellowish-green hue hangs over the water—a consequence of foul demonic rot draining south from Felwood, much like at nearby Iris Lake. The local plant life has twisted into hostile bog beasts that prowl the fallen masonry, their temperaments warped by the tainted lake.

Ruins of Thaurissan. The Ruins of Thaurissan are the scorched remnants of the Dark Iron clan's original surface capital in the Burning Steppes. Once a proud city nestled in the lush northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, it was blasted to cinders during the War of the Three Hammers when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan inadvertently summoned the Firelord, Ragnaros. Roughly two centuries ago, following their exile from Ironforge after the death of High King Modimus Anvilmar, the Dark Iron clan journeyed south and established Thaurissan City. At the climax of the War of the Three Hammers, facing total defeat by the combined forces of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan sought an ultimate weapon to turn the tide. He and seven trusted sorcerers channeled ancient magic deep beneath the earth. Instead of an obedient servant, their ritual ripped open a conduit to the Elemental Plane and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The cataclysmic eruption shattered the surrounding mountains, burned the verdant landscape into the ashen Burning Steppes, raised the volcano of Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the city.

Ruins of Uldum. Tucked into the jagged cliffs of the Valley of the Watchers in southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum consist of an ancient stone hall guarding a sealed Titan facility. Massive stone doors protect its secrets from grave robbers and curious explorers alike. Carved deep into the bedrock of southern Tanaris, the Ruins of Uldum appear to be an antechamber or grand threshold to a far larger, sealed subterranean complex. Its colossal stone gates stand shut against the outside world, and no mechanism or key known to modern scholars has managed to open them.

Ruins of Zul'Mamwe. Tucked away in a mountainous pocket south of the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, the Ruins of Zul'Mamwe serve as a heavily fortified stronghold for the Skullsplitter troll tribe. Enclosed by steep cliffs on almost all sides, the ancient stone platforms now teem with fierce jungle trolls under the rule of their ruthless chieftain, Ana'thek the Cruel. The Ruins of Zul'Mamwe represent one of the primary seats of power for the Skullsplitter tribe in central Stranglethorn Vale. Cradled within a natural mountain amphitheater, the site has only a single open approach from the north, making it an exceptional defensive redoubt. From atop its weathered ziggurats and stone terraces, Chief Ana'thek the Cruel directs his warriors and witch doctors, defending their territory fiercely against both intruding adventurers and rival jungle troll tribes.

Rumbleshot's Ammo. Rumbleshot's Ammo is a mislaid crate of munitions bound for the gunsmith Hegnar Rumbleshot in Dun Morogh. Lost when a frightened courier fled from hungry wendigos, the heavy crate sits abandoned in the snow near the Grizzled Den. Hegnar Rumbleshot operates a roadside arms shop along the mountain path leading down from Coldridge Pass toward Anvilmar. With Ironforge riflemen, mountaineers, and dwarven mortar teams constantly drilling in the snowy heights, his supplies burn away almost as fast as powder catches flame. This particular shipment of shot was dispatched by Loslor from Kharanos, but never reached the shelves. The courier tasked with transporting it pitched camp too close to the predatory wendigos of the Grizzled Den, panicked when attacked, and fled for his life, leaving the heavy supply crate sitting deep within the beast's hunting grounds.

Rumors for Kravel. Krazek has found what you came for. After calling in favors, doing plenty of deducing and giving up a rare bottle of elven wine, Krazek wrote a letter about Nazz Steamboil. It is too dangerous for Krazek to use, so you carry it to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats, and you are asked not to say where it came from. Krazek tells you what the search cost: some favors were used up, a rare bottle of elven wine was parted with, and a good deal of deducing was done. The result is a letter holding some very interesting bits about Nazz Steamboil. Krazek finds it too dangerous to use, and leaves it to you to do with as you will, as long as nobody learns where it came from. It goes back to Kravel Koalbeard, out on the Shimmering Flats.

Rune of Nesting. The Rune of Nesting is one of the four sacred Relics of Wakening kept within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den on Teldrassil. It is an essential component in the delicate druidic ritual required to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Night elf druids undergo deep, cyclical hibernations within underground barrow dens to commune with nature through the Emerald Dream. Waking from this profound trance is not simply a matter of stirring; it requires a precise ritual guided by sacred instruments. The Rune of Nesting, kept safely within the Chest of Nesting deep in the winding chambers of the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, anchors this process. Alongside the Raven Claw Talisman, the Black Feather Quill, and the Sapphire of Sky, the rune serves as a conduit to call the Druids of the Talon back to the waking world.

Rune-Inscribed Parchment. A written missive delivered to aspiring orc shamans in the Valley of Trials. Penned by the trainer Shikrik and handed out by Gornek, it calls initiates to embrace their role as spiritual leaders and conduits for the elemental spirits. Within the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, new orc shamans begin their training under the watchful gaze of veteran overseers. While performing initial trials for Gornek, an initiate is handed this rune-covered document. Sent directly by Shikrik, the local shamanic instructor, the parchment serves as a formal summons into the deeper mysteries of elemental communion. Orcish culture regards the shaman not merely as a battlefield spellcaster, but as an essential mediator between the living and the ancestors. This brief writ marks the transition from simple brute strength to the disciplined path of ancestral reverence.

Rune-Inscribed Parchment. Rune-Inscribed Parchment is a missive delivered to fledgling Horde shamans beginning their journey in the Valley of Trials. Written by the trainer Shikrik, the parchment summons promising initiates to begin their formal tutelage in commune with the spirits and elements. After proving their basic survival skills against the local wildlife, new orc shamans are handed a rune-inscribed parchment by Gornek, the overseer of the Valley of Trials. The parchment bears mystical writing from Shikrik, the valley's resident shaman trainer, requesting an audience with the newly arrived initiate.

Rune-Inscribed Pendant. The Rune-Inscribed Pendant is a magical trinket recovered from Dalaran supply shipments destined for Ambermill. Prized by the Kirin Tor, these pendants serve as conduits for channeling potent arcane energies. Discovered among crates of cartographic supplies bound for the Dalaran enclave at Ambermill, this pendant bears intricate arcane inscriptions. High-ranking wizards of the Kirin Tor frequently employ such artifacts to focus and amplify their spellcasting. The presence of numerous channeled pendants moving into the region immediately draws the suspicion of the Forsaken at the Sepulcher, signaling an impending project of immense magical power.

Rune-Inscribed Tablet. A Rune-Inscribed Tablet is a stone message delivered to young Darkspear troll shamans in the Valley of Trials. Handed over by Gornek, it directs promising mystics to begin formal communion with the elements under the tutelage of the orc trainer Shikrik. Carved with elemental runes, this tablet serves as a formal invitation for burgeoning troll shamans taking their first steps in Durotar. When an initiate demonstrates their mettle in the Valley of Trials, the overseer Gornek presents the stone, sent by the troll shaman Ishi-yo to direct the initiate to the shaman trainer Shikrik. For the Darkspear trolls—who hold deep spiritual traditions of their own—the tablet marks the beginning of their shared path with the orcs, bridging ancient troll mysticism with the revitalized shamanic heritage championed by Warchief Thrall.

Rune-Inscribed Tablet. The Rune-Inscribed Tablet is a summoning missive delivered to aspiring shamans training in the Valley of Trials. Sent by Shikrik, it invites promising initiates to begin formal instruction in communing with the spirits and commanding the elemental forces of earth, fire, water, and air. After proving their early discipline in the dusty training grounds of the Valley of Trials, fledgling shamans are handed a carved stone tablet by Gornek. The runes upon it serve as an invitation from Shikrik, the local shaman trainer, signaling that the initiate is ready to look beyond simple physical combat and heed the deeper currents of the natural world.

Runes of Summoning. The Runes of Summoning are a ritual item provided by the warlock trainer Carendin Halgar in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity. They are used to call forth an unbound voidwalker into a summoning circle so that an aspiring warlock may bend it to their will. Within the dark recesses of the Undercity's Magic Quarter, Forsaken practitioners of the dark arts study the manipulation of the Nether. Carendin Halgar entrusts the Runes of Summoning only to warlocks who have prepared themselves to take command of a voidwalker. By casting the runes within the active summoning circle below Halgar's station, the practitioner tears through the fabric of the Void, drawing forth a creature that must be overpowered and bound into servitude.

Runetotem the Elder. Runetotem the Elder is an encounter with an ancestral spirit during the Lunar Festival in Durotar. Found standing within Razor Hill under a pillar of heavenly light, she offers blessings and festival tokens to travelers who come to pay their respects to the past. During the Lunar Festival, the spirits of ancient elders materialize across Azeroth to commune with the living. Elder Runetotem manifests inside Razor Hill, positioned just past the southern entrance. Bathed in a clear beam of starlight from above, she watches over the orcish settlement and welcomes adventurers who step aside from their travels to acknowledge the wisdom of those who came before.

Rustmaul Dig Site. The Rustmaul Dig Site is a ruined excavation in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats. Originally established by the dwarven Explorers' League to unearth ancient ruins, the camp fell into tragedy when a Horde war party slaughtered the miners, after which a subterranean silithid swarm emerged. Now abandoned by mortals, the site crawls with hostile insectoids emerging from the caverns below. Prospectors from the Ironforge Explorers' League set up the Rustmaul Dig Site hoping to uncover forgotten artifacts buried beneath the salt flats. Their efforts were brutally cut short when an aggressive Horde war party, led by Moktar Krin, fell upon the camp and wiped out the dwarven excavators. However, the conquerors enjoyed no triumph. The violent clash apparently disturbed a dormant cave network beneath the site, releasing an endless horde of silithid insects that quickly overwhelmed and drove off the battered survivors.

Rut'theran Village. Rut'theran Village is a coastal haven nestled at the southern base of Teldrassil. Serving as the primary maritime harbor for Darnassus, it connects the secluded World Tree to the mainland of Kalimdor via ferry and hippogryph routes. Perched at the water's edge below the towering heights of Teldrassil, Rut'theran Village acts as the threshold between the night elven capital and the wider world. While Darnassus rests within the boughs high above, Rut'theran provides the logistical foundation required to sustain it. A mystical portal arches beneath the trees, whisking travelers between the shore and Darnassus in an instant. For journeys across the sea, ferry service runs from the village docks directly to Auberdine on the mainland of Darkshore, accompanied by flight masters tending dedicated roosts of trained hippogryphs.

Rutgar Glyphshaper. Rutgar Glyphshaper is a dwarven archaeologist stationed at the Bronzebeard Encampment in the southern reaches of Silithus. As a member of Brann Bronzebeard's expedition, he studies ancient silithid relics and runes, striving to uncover the mystery of the hives even after Brann wanders off into the desert. Rutgar Glyphshaper traveled to Silithus under the leadership of Brann Bronzebeard to investigate the vast silithid hives and unearth lost relics buried beneath the desert wastes. Establishing their base at the Bronzebeard Encampment south of Cenarion Hold, Rutgar and his companions frequently ventured directly into the bug hives to harvest inscribed stones and runic artifacts, often cooperating with Cenarion night elf researchers.

Ruul Eagletalon. Ruul Eagletalon is a tauren resident of Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore. Stationed near the settlement's perimeter, he keeps a watchful eye on the local wildlife, particularly the aggressive Windfury harpies encroaching upon tauren lands. Ruul Eagletalon stands guard in Bloodhoof Village, tending to the security of the settlement as young braves arrive from Camp Narache. While Mulgore is a peaceful homeland compared to the arid wastes of the Barrens, territorial predators and hostile creatures continually press against the pastures. Ruul concerns himself with threats roaming the nearby plains, notably directing capable travelers to confront the savage Windfury harpies who prey on unwary nomads and game.

Ruul Snowhoof. Ruul Snowhoof is a tauren druid held captive inside Thistlefur Hold in northern Ashenvale. Trapped in his bear form within a crude cage, he relies on Horde adventurers to break him out and guide him to safety. Ruul Snowhoof ventured into northern Ashenvale only to fall into the clutches of the corrupt Thistlefur furbolgs. When captured, he assumed the shape of a mighty bear—a guise his captors entirely mistook for an actual wild beast. Instead of slaying him outright, the furbolgs locked him inside a wooden cage deep within Thistlefur Hold, leaving him to slowly starve. Weakened and unable to safely drop his form or fight his way out alone, Ruul waits for allies of the Horde to spring his lock, fight off his jailers, and clear a path through the den so he can return to his sister, Yama Snowhoof, at Splintertree Post.

Ruuzel. Ruuzel is an Alliance quest offered by Talen on the edges of the Zoram Strand in Ashenvale. After recovering an ancient Kaldorei statuette from the coast, adventurers are sent to wrest the Ring of Zoram from the naga leader Ruuzel to unlock its sealed secrets. Before the Great Sundering tore Kalimdor apart and cast its grand coastal cities beneath the sea, the city of Zoram was governed by powerful night elven nobility. Chief among their regalia was the Ring of Zoram, which Talen believes is the key to the ancient statuette's lock. Following the cataclysm, the ring was lost to the tides for millennia, preserving the secrets of sunken relics from curious eyes.

Rwag. Rwag is the orc rogue trainer stationed in the Den, tucked within Durotar's Valley of Trials. He instructs newly arrived orcs and trolls in the arts of stealth, subterfuge, and dirty fighting under the watchful gaze of the Horde. Operating deep within the cave known as the Den, Rwag trains fledgling rogues, cutpurses, and thieves before they step out into the wider world of Durotar. While the new Horde champions martial honor and battlefield valor, Rwag understands that subtlety, poisons, and a well-placed dagger remain invaluable tools for survival in an unforgiving desert. He keeps a sharp eye on Valley business and harbors deep suspicions regarding the dark practitioners also sheltering in the cave, particularly the warlock Nartok.

SI:7. In Goldshire, Keryn Sylvius sends promising young rogues toward Stormwind's hidden ranks. Recruits report to Renzik "The Shiv" in Old Town, where they enter Master Mathias Shaw's service. Keryn Sylvius watches local recruits from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. When a rogue proves cunning and capable against the growing Defias threat, Sylvius passes along a message from headquarters. The order is plain: report to Renzik "The Shiv" without delay. The recruit leaves Elwynn's fields for the covert heart of Stormwind.

SI:7 (Stormwind City). Tucked away in the eastern corner of Old Town, this unassuming stone manor houses the headquarters of SI:7, the kingdom of Stormwind's elite intelligence and espionage service. Behind its heavy doors, spymaster Master Mathias Shaw and his senior operatives quietly monitor threats to the realm, coordinating undercover agents across the kingdom. To the casual passerby in Old Town, this fortified stone structure looks little different from a standard manor or military barracks. In truth, it serves as the nerve center for Stormwind Intelligence, Section 7. Directed by Master Mathias Shaw, SI:7 gathers intelligence, conducts surveillance, and executes covert operations to protect the kingdom from subversion. While the city guard patrols the open cobblestones and the Royal Guard defends Stormwind Keep, SI:7 works in the margins, training handlers and dispatching stealthy operatives against foreign enemies, saboteurs, and domestic unrest alike.

text.enUS: STOLEN: Smithing Tuyere and Lookout's Spyglass. A notice lists two items stolen: a Dark Iron tuyere and a Lookout's Spyglass. The Thorium Brotherhood is certain unscrupulous, jealous Dark Iron dwarves of the Searing Gorge took them, and whoever finds them is to take them to Taskmaster Scrange for payment. The notice calls the spyglass a fine tool for lookouts and the tuyere a smithing tool that cannot be replaced. All that is known is that Dark Iron dwarves definitely took them. Whoever finds them is to return them to Taskmaster Scrange.

Sack of Murloc Heads. The Sack of Murloc Heads is a gruesome bundle collected along the beaches of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Assembled as proof of military action against local shore pests, it is pawned off by Lieutenant Farren Orinelle onto passing adventurers for delivery to Marshal Redpath in Southshore. Southshore stands under constant siege from Syndicate outlaws, Forsaken skirmishers, and wild murlocs crowding the coast. To secure funding and favor from town leadership, local officers must demonstrate that coastal threats are actively being culled. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle gathers proof in the form of severed heads, but the distasteful nature of the cargo—and his own squeamishness—prompts him to hand the dripping sack off to travelers rather than deliver the grisly evidence to Marshal Redpath himself.

Sack of Supplies. These supply sacks belong to a caravan shipment intended for the goblin engineer Rezlak outside Orgrimmar. Transported across Durotar, the goods were intercepted by the Dustwind harpies roosting in the crags of Razorwind Canyon. Rezlak, an engineer contracted out of Ratchet by Gazlowe, relies on regular caravans through Durotar to supply his construction efforts for the Horde. Durotar's wilderness, however, is far from tame. When a promised shipment passed near the canyon road south of Orgrimmar, it was ambushed and pillaged by the local Dustwind harpies. The vicious creatures hauled the cargo deep into their roosts within Razorwind Canyon, scattering the sacks among the dirt and scree alongside harpy nesting sites.

Sacred Fire. Sacred Fire is a Horde rite of passage that bridges the jagged canyons of Thousand Needles with the heights of Thunder Bluff. To summon and banish the vengeful wind serpent Arikara, hunters must gather rare Incendia Agave from the Boiling Pool so that Magatha Grimtotem can enchant it into ritual powder. The monstrous wind serpent Arikara cannot simply be tracked across the canyon floor; she must be called. Motega Firemane instructs hunters to prepare the sacred fire of life, an ancient ritual flame that acts as a beacon to the spirit beast. Feeding this fire requires more than ordinary kindling, calling for the rare Incendia Agave that sprouts only around the scalding waters of Thousand Needles.

Saelienne. Innkeeper Saelienne manages the inn situated on the Craftsmen's Terrace in Darnassus. She provides weary travelers and local artisans with food, drink, and a peaceful hearthstone retreat in the heart of the night elven capital. Situated amidst the bustling workshops and trade stalls of the Craftsmen's Terrace, Innkeeper Saelienne offers a calm respite for both residents and visitors to Darnassus. As a keeper of the hearth, she caters to adventurers arriving from across Kalimdor and beyond, serving staple night elven refreshments alongside goods brought into the city port. Her establishment serves as a primary gathering place for tradesfolk seeking rest after long hours at the forge or loom.

Safety First. Razzeric has found that Shreev left the safety on the seaforium booster. It caps the power Razzeric gets out of the booster, and Razzeric had asked for it to be taken off. You are sent to Shreev in Gadgetzan, in Tanaris. Razzeric looks over the seaforium booster and finds the safety still on. It caps the power the booster can give, and Razzeric had told Shreev it should be off. Razzeric gives you the booster and sends you south of the Shimmering Flats into the Tanaris desert, to the Gadgetzan Gizmorium, to have Shreev remove the safety.

Safety First. Shreev has done what Razzeric wanted with the seaforium booster, and you carry the modified booster back to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Shreev's warning with it: be careful when setting it off, because one slip and Razzeric ends up a scorch mark on the track. This follows the first Safety First. Shreev hands over the modified booster, done as Razzeric asked. Shreev's warning with it: Razzeric needs to be careful when he sets it off. A single slip and he will not be racing ahead; he will be a scorch mark on the track. Shreev adds that it would be a shame, wondering whether the nineteenth driver would have been any good.

Saldean's Farm. At Saldean's Farm, the Saldeans hold Westfall's only homestead not completely overrun and abandoned to the Defias Brotherhood. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma keep the farmhouse as a rare safe haven amid the region's turmoil. The Saldean family stayed on their soil as neighboring lands fell to banditry and mechanical sabotage. Farmer Saldean and his wife Salma still offer hot food and a kind word to travelers. Rogue harvest golems deployed across the plains plague their fields, so the family keeps close to the farmhouse walls.

Salma Saldean. At Saldean's Farm, Salma Saldean keeps a welcome place for travelers. She and her husband, Farmer Saldean, tend the homestead in Westfall, where bandits threaten the farms and Stormwind has left the region. She offers meals in return for help around the farm. Salma Saldean welcomes travelers to a farm that has endured where neighboring homesteads have burned or fallen to the Defias Brotherhood. A hearty pot waits on the stove, and she looks for capable hands to help around the farmstead.

text.enUS: Salt Flat Venom. Out on the blinding salt expanse of the Shimmering Flats, gnome engineer Fizzle Brassbolts searches for unusual ingredients to supercharge his rocket car. Convinced that the intensely saline venom of local scorpids will produce an ultra-hot burning propellant, he tasks passing adventurers with braving the stinging beasts. The Mirage Raceway is an endless battle of high-speed technical supremacy between gnomish precision and goblin audacity. For Fizzle Brassbolts, standard hydrocarbons and clockwork parts simply are not enough to outpace the competition. He envisions a custom fuel mixture tailored to burn far hotter than conventional propellants, driving their rocket cars across the dried salt lake at blistering speeds.

Saltspray Glen. Saltspray Glen is a windswept expanse in the northwestern Wetlands hugging the shores of Baradin Bay. Strong coastal gales regularly fling briny seawater across the mossy lowland, which is overrun by aggressive wild raptors. It forms a treacherous natural corridor between neighboring murloc-infested marshes and ancient dwarven ruins. Tucked away in the far northwestern reach of the Wetlands, Saltspray Glen takes its name from the sea spray driven inland off Baradin Bay whenever coastal gales kick up. Bordered by the murloc-haunted waters of Bluegill Marsh to the south and the quiet bluffs of Ironbeard's Tomb to the east, the glen offers little comfort to passing travelers. Packs of cunning wild raptors nest throughout the marshy grass, hunting along the brackish flats alongside their kin from nearby Raptor Ridge and Black Channel Marsh.

Salty Sailor Tavern. The Salty Sailor Tavern is the beating heart of Booty Bay's social life, serving as the port's primary inn and watering hole. Run by the goblin Innkeeper Skindle, it welcomes scoundrels, mercenaries, and travelers from both factions seeking respite from the perils of the jungle. Perched amidst the wooden tiers of Booty Bay, the Salty Sailor Tavern offers warm beds and strong drinks under the watchful eye of the Blackwater Raiders. Behind the bar stands Innkeeper Skindle, keeping glasses filled while a menagerie of buccaneers, traders, and adventurers mingle on neutral ground. Outside the establishment hangs a massive, curious curio—a Zul'Gurub Protector Stone—serving as a strange trophy in this bustling den of commerce.

Salty Scorpid Venom. Salty Scorpid Venom is a caustic fluid harvested from the scorpids stalking the Shimmering Flats in Thousand Needles. Packed with natural salts from the desert floor, it is prized by gnomish rocket racers attempting to engineer volatile, ultra-hot fuel. The scorpids crawling the arid expanse of the Shimmering Flats have adapted to an intensely mineral-rich environment. Over generations, the venom of beasts like the Scorpid Reavers and Scorpid Terrors has absorbed enormous quantities of local salt. Rather than brewing antidotes or standard poisons, gnomish tinkers like Fizzle Brassbolts prize this caustic compound as a prospective additive for high-combustion engine fuel.

Samophlange. Commissioned by the goblin engineer Sputtervalve in Ratchet, this task sends adventurers north into a Venture Company research outpost southwest of the Sludge Fen. Their goal is to locate a mysterious contraption known only as a samophlange. Equipped with a pilfered operating manual, the curious investigator must navigate an erratic control console to extract the device. Goblins are notoriously driven by innovation, curiosity, and profit, but even the Tinker Sputtervalve finds himself perplexed by the latest development coming out of the Venture Company's digs in the northern Barrens. Operating southwest of the Sludge Fen, the rival outfit has been tinkering with a device designated as a samophlange. Without knowing its precise mechanical function or lucrative potential, Sputtervalve is eager to lay his hands on the equipment to reverse-engineer its design before his commercial rivals capitalize on it.

Samophlange. This task requires shutting down the intricate machinery powering the Venture Company's digging operations in the northern Barrens. By cutting off three separate control valves, adventurers can safely power down the central apparatus. Turning off these valves halts the volatile flow of fuel and pressure keeping the machine active. The Venture Company's machinery at the Sludge Fen is as dangerous as it is complex. When confronting the central control console, the dials and indicators make it clear that the core mechanism cannot simply be shut down at the flip of a switch. To prevent an explosion or mechanical failure, the feed lines must be handled manually first.

Samophlange. This quest is the critical step in shutting down the Venture Company machinery at the Sludge Fen in the northern Barrens. Having already shut down the surrounding valves, an operative must secure the console key from Tinkerer Sniggles to open the main control unit and extract the mysterious samophlange. Before the core component can be physically extracted, the machinery must be completely unpowered and unlocked. With the auxiliary valves turned and the pressure relieved, the terminal's dials and gauges settle into an idle state. However, the housing itself remains locked tight to prevent sabotage, requiring a physical key held by the lead goblin engineer overseeing the drilling site.

Samophlange. This quest marks the culmination of the investigation into the Venture Company machinery in the northern Barrens. Having dismantled the system's defenses and shut down the control console, you extract the elusive samophlange itself and bring it back to Ratchet for evaluation. It proves to be far more finicky and fragile than anyone could have predicted. Behind the faceplate of the Venture Company console lies a baffling nest of wiring, purposeless tubing, and idiosyncratic engineering. Deep within this mechanized labyrinth rests the core component that baffled engineers across the region: the samophlange. With a firm tug, the device breaks free from its housing, ready to be presented to the goblin who set the entire recovery effort in motion.

Samophlange (item). The samophlange is an enigmatic mechanical component recovered from the deep interior of an automated control console in the Barrens. Despite its complex appearance, its precise function remains an engineering mystery even to the goblin mechanics who sought it. Tucked away behind a labyrinth of superfluous wiring and hollow tubing within a Barrens control console lies the samophlange. It takes some rooting through deliberately confounding machinery just to unseat it from its housing. To the untrained eye, it appears to be an essential nexus of clockwork and steam-driven technology. To goblin tinkerers, it is an irresistible mechanical puzzle intended for shipment to the Tinkers' Union in Undermine—though its fragile build means it rarely survives casual handling long enough to be understood.

text.enUS: Samophlange Manual. The Samophlange Manual is a technical operating guide detailing the inner workings of the elusive samophlange. Kept under tight lock and key by the Venture Company, its scattered pages hold the instructions needed by goblin engineers to repair and operate the bizarre contraption. Engineering schematics and operating handbooks are guarded like gold among goblin enterprises, and the Samophlange Manual is no exception. While working within the Venture Company, an ambitious overseer named Boss Copperplug jealously hoarded knowledge regarding the device, distributing only scattered pages to his most loyal subordinates to retain control over the machinery. When the device fell out of Venture Company clutches, repairing it proved impossible without assembling the torn, distributed documentation from the overseer and his crew at the Boulder Lode Mine.

text.enUS: Samophlange Manual. Samophlange Manual is a quest given by goblin engineer Rilli Greasygob in Orgrimmar. Determined to repair a broken samophlange, Rilli sends adventurers back into the Barrens to wrest the device's proprietary operating instructions from his former Venture Company rival. Within the mercenary ranks of the Venture Company, technical knowledge is currency. Rilli Greasygob previously worked alongside Boss Copperplug, an overseer who guarded the internal mechanics of the mysterious samophlange with paranoid secrecy. Rather than sharing the manual, Copperplug parceled out individual pages only to trusted underlings, leaving peers like Rilli completely in the dark regarding its inner workings.

Sample Ichor. This vial contains a refined extract of the foul fluid that sustains the rot hide gnolls of Silverpine Forest. Distilled down to its base components by Apothecary Renferrel, the substance carries lingering traces of both necromancy and warlock sorcery. The Rot Hide gnolls that prowl Silverpine Forest are no ordinary beasts. After recovering samples from the creatures and their lingering remnants, Apothecary Renferrel of the Royal Apothecary Society reduced the vile liquid into its constituent elements. His chemical breakdown revealed that the ichor was artificially manufactured through a convergence of dark schools: necromantic rites woven together with warlock magics. Because the craft behind it borders on arcane disciplines outside simple alchemy, Renferrel packaged this sample and dispatched it to the Undercity for Bethor Iceshard to examine with divination.

text.enUS: Sample Snapjaw Shell. A Sample Snapjaw Shell is a durable tortoise carapace harvested from the freshwater oases of the Barrens. Remarkable for its lingering vitality, it is sent across the Great Sea to aid druidic research into rejuvenating the blighted woodlands of Silverpine Forest. The snapping turtles that dwell in the lush, anomaly-tinged oases of the Barrens possess shells of surprising vigor. Unlike common shell matter, a fresh Sample Snapjaw Shell retains a faint inner radiance and an energetic pulse long after being separated from the creature. To the tauren druids observing the land's rapid ecological shifts, these carapaces embody the resilient, adaptive spark of Kalimdor's wilderness, suggesting that nature can flourish even amidst harsh arid surroundings.

Sample for Helbrim. Sample for Helbrim is a Horde courier task bridging Undercity alchemical experiments with Forsaken outposts in central Kalimdor. Handed down by Apothecary Zinge, it sends couriers across the sea to deliver a blighted wolf heart to Apothecary Helbrim at the Crossroads. The Royal Apothecary Society rarely keeps its gruesome experiments confined to the ruins of Lordaeron. After receiving tainted organs from Apothecary Renferrel in Silverpine, Apothecary Zinge in the Undercity sought to expand their research globally. She entrusted an adventurer with a Wolf Heart Sample to be carried overseas to Apothecary Helbrim, an alchemist stationed in the arid savanna of the Barrens.

text.enUS: Sample of Zanzil's Altered Mixture. This vial contains a potent specimen of a concoction brewed by the witch doctor Zanzil, recovered during a covert infiltration in the Barrens. Carried by an operative suffering from its debilitating effects, the sample is sent across the sea to Tarren Mill in hopes of unlocking both an antidote and the lethal secrets of poisoncraft. After infiltrating the Venture Company's tower near the Sludge Fen and looting the cache of Zanzil's mixture from Gallywix's lockbox, an operative ends up afflicted by Zanzil's foul touch. Shenthul orders the stricken agent across the Great Sea with a sample of the brew in hand. Finding a cure means locating Serge Hinott, an apothecary stationed at Tarren Mill in Hillsbrad Foothills, who possesses the rare expertise required to isolate the toxin and decipher its components.

Samuel's Remains. Samuel's Remains are the recovered earthly remnants of Samuel Fipps, a former resident of Tirisfal Glades who fell to the Scourge. Gathered by adventurers near Deathknell, they are laid to rest beside his wife Marla to fulfill her dying wish. Before the plague of undeath swept across Lordaeron, Samuel Fipps lived peacefully with his wife, Marla. When the contagion struck, Samuel succumbed and was bound into mindless service to the Scourge. Marla escaped undeath only to be struck down by the very husband she loved. Despite this brutal end, her final wish was not vengeance, but eternity together: she pleaded to be interred beside Samuel once his cursed form was put to rest. Novice Elreth in Deathknell enlists newly awoken Forsaken to track down Samuel's wandering form northeast of the settlement, recover his bones, and bury them in the front row of the local cemetery.

Sanctum (Stromgarde Keep). The Sanctum is a sacred redoubt tucked behind the chapel within Stromgarde Keep. Sheltered within the crumbling fortress, it guards the entrance to the ancestral Trollbane family crypt and stands as one of the few remaining bastions of the Holy Light amidst Arathi's ruin. While much of Stromgarde Keep has fallen to Syndicate infiltrators and the Boulderfist ogres, the Sanctum and its adjacent chapel have remained under the fierce protection of the surviving Stromgarde defenders. Located behind the house of worship, the Sanctum borders the citadel's graveyard and marks the threshold to the royal crypt where the kings of Stromgarde rest. For the battered loyalists rallying around Prince Galen Trollbane, holding this hallowed ground represents more than a tactical foothold; it is a desperate fight to keep their kingdom's ancestral heritage and faith from being trampled by invaders.

Sandsorrow Watch. Sandsorrow Watch is a sprawling desert outpost located just west of Gadgetzan in Tanaris. The surrounding dunes and ruins are overrun by hostile Sandfury trolls and their reanimated dead, who also hold the eastern watch tower overlooking the waste. Situated directly west of the bustling goblin trading hub of Gadgetzan, Sandsorrow Watch is a grim borderland in the Tanaris desert. The broad expanse is dominated by the Sandfury tribe, who aggressively defend the arid territory alongside legions of shambling troll zombies. An elevated watch tower at the eastern edge anchors the position, providing a fortified vantage point amidst the encroaching desert wilderness and the hostile indigenous tribes.

Sapphire of Aku'Mai. Sapphires of Aku'Mai are glowing, water-infused mineral clusters growing along the subterranean tunnels of Blackfathom Deeps. The encroaching naga have begun harvesting these gems, prompting the Earthen Ring to seek them out before their potent arcane power can be exploited. Discovered within the watery cavern entrances of Blackfathom Deeps along Ashenvale's Zoram Strand, Sapphires of Aku'Mai are crystalline formations rich in elemental energy. The spirits of water cling tightly to them, making them exceptional catalysts for magical workings. When scouts reported that the subterranean naga had begun actively quarrying these clusters from the cavern walls, the Shaman Je'neu Sancrea sought adventuring assistance to confiscate them. Left in the serpent peoples' clutches, the stones could easily fuel devastating arcane rites.

Sapphire of Sky. The Sapphire of Sky is one of four sacred Relics of Wakening kept by the night elves within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. It is an essential focus used to safely summon sleeping Druids of the Talon back from the Emerald Dream. Deep within the roots of Teldrassil, Druids of the Talon commune with the wilds while resting in hibernation within Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Awakening from such deep trance-states into the waking world is a fragile, perilous process. To safeguard the transition, the druids rely on four consecrated artifacts known as the Relics of Wakening: the Black Feather Quill, the Raven Claw Talisman, the Rune of Nesting, and the Sapphire of Sky. Without this resonant gem, the harmony required to call sleeping spirits back from the Emerald Dream remains incomplete, leaving them vulnerable to eternal entrapment.

Sar'theris Strand. Sar'theris Strand forms the western coastline of Desolace, fronting the Veiled Sea. In stark contrast to the barren, grey inland wastes, the shore is sunny and grassy, though it remains perilous due to prowling naga, sea giants, and makrura. Running the length of western Desolace, Sar'theris Strand offers a bizarre respite from the ash and dust of the inland plains. Here, the clifftops and beaches are bright and green. Yet the strand is far from welcoming: serpentine naga patrol the surf alongside towering sea giants and territorial makrura. Shipwrecks litter the shoals, including the ruined Karnitol vessel to the north and small shattered skiffs beneath the towers of Ethel Rethor, proving the sea is as treacherous as the shore.

Sara Balloo. Sara Balloo is a grieving dwarven widow residing in the Military Ward of Ironforge. She spends her days mourning her late husband, Sully Balloo, clinging to any remnant or message left behind from his final days in service. Standing within the bustling Military Ward of Ironforge, Sara Balloo presents a somber contrast to the clatter of weaponry and martial drills. Her husband, Sully Balloo, fell in battle far from home, leaving her alone with memories and lingering grief. For Sara, closure arrives only through recovered words—a final letter carrying Sully's devotion across the mountains from the scene of his demise.

Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a handwritten missive penned by a grieving widow in Ironforge. Unable to face the monarch directly in her sorrow, she entrusts this letter to a trusted champion of the Alliance to carry before King Magni Bronzebeard. Written in the shadow of deep personal tragedy, Sara Balloo's Plea represents a humble appeal directly to Ironforge's throne. Rather than braving the High Seat herself in her grief-stricken condition, Sara seeks an adventurer who has demonstrated loyalty and valor to the Alliance to deliver her words. The message asks for the attention of King Magni Bronzebeard, drawing the sovereign's gaze toward the private mourning and sacrifices made by ordinary dwarven families serving the kingdom.

Sara Balloo's Plea. Sara Balloo's Plea is a somber errand undertaken on behalf of a grieving dwarven widow in Ironforge. Unable to face her monarch directly in her state of sorrow, Sara entrusts a personal appeal to King Magni Bronzebeard regarding her fallen husband, Sully Balloo. After receiving the tragic final letter recovered from the watery depths of the Thandol Span, Sara Balloo finds herself paralyzed by mourning. Rather than let her husband Sully's sacrifice fade into obscurity, she writes a plea addressed directly to the throne of Ironforge. Too overwhelmed by heartbreak to appear before court etiquette herself, she entrusts the sealed parchment to a trusted champion of the Alliance to petition King Magni Bronzebeard on her behalf.

Sara Timberlain. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Sara Timberlain stitches gear for the Stormwind Army. She makes useful armaments from salvaged cloth and leather. Sara Timberlain works with needle and thread outside a small cottage on the western edge of Eastvale Logging Camp. Axes sound through the camp as workers fell trees. Though Eastvale lies far from settled lands, wolves and murlocs prowl nearby, and Sara still offers travelers hospitality. She turns scraps of linen and salvaged bandanas into sturdy gear. Her skill has earned official recognition and commissions to supply cloth and leather armaments to Stormwind's military forces.

Sardor Isle. Sardor Isle is a lush island situated off the western coast of Feralas, north of the perilous Isle of Dread. It serves as the home to Feathermoon Stronghold, the primary night elven military bastion in southern Kalimdor. Despite the heavy sentinel presence, parts of the island remain prowled by wild beasts and hostile naga creeping up from the shallows. Resting across the water from mainland Feralas, Sardor Isle is anchored by Feathermoon Stronghold, an impressive elven garrison commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon. While the fortress itself is heavily fortified and linked to the mainland via regular ferry crossings, the broader island is far from tame. Roaming wolf packs claim the timbered slopes, while encroaching naga lurk along the rocky western and northern beaches, constantly testing the resolve of the night elven sentinels.

Sargeras. Sargeras is the fallen titan and supreme creator of the Burning Legion, bent on scouring all life from the cosmos. Once the noble champion and defender of the Pantheon, his descent into madness led to the Sundering of ancient Azeroth and nearly every demonic catastrophe since. Before his fall, Sargeras was the greatest and noblest warrior among the titans. Entrusted by the Pantheon of Order to safeguard their grand creations across the Great Dark Beyond, he waged war against the chaotic demons spawned from the Twisting Nether. Incapable of conceiving pure evil, Sargeras trapped countless fiends away within a great prison. Yet eons of relentless warfare against cosmic horrors gradually wore down his altruistic spirit.

Sargeron. Sargeron is the crumbled ruin of an ancient night elf city located in northern Desolace. Shattered during the Great Sundering, its former temples of Elune have been defiled and claimed by the Hatefury satyrs, who renamed the grounds in tribute to their master, Sargeras. Before the War of the Ancients broke the continent, this settlement was a flourishing center of worship dedicated to Elune, housing sacred grounds such as Elune's Temple, Sanctuary, and Cathedral. Its true name is lost to antiquity. When the world shattered, the city collapsed into rubble, leaving behind sanctified relics like the Cup of Elune, Elune's Brazier, and Elune's Handmaiden. In the millennia since, corrupted Hatefury satyrs overran the stones, repurposing the sacred Kaldorei architecture into a stronghold honoring the titan Sargeras.

text.enUS: Sarilus Foulborne's Head. Sarilus Foulborne's Head is a gruesome trophy claimed from an undead sorcerer who defiled the waters of northern Kalimdor. Carried back across the border from the Barrens into Ashenvale, it serves as undeniable proof that the meddling mage has met his end at the hands of the Sentinels.

Sarkoth. Having avenged the wounded troll Hana'zua by slaying the monstrous scorpid Sarkoth, an adventurer must carry word of his plight back to the Den. Gornek must be alerted so that rescue can reach the stricken scout before his venomous wounds claim his life. Stranded upon the high bluffs of the Valley of Trials, the Darkspear scout Hana'zua found himself venom-struck and unable to return down the treacherous paths unassisted. Though vengeance was delivered upon Sarkoth—the dread scorpid that felled him—pride alone cannot carry an envenomed warrior across the arid stones. Bound to his rock, he relies on a passing initiate to bring word back down to the training encampment.

Sarkoth. High on a southern plateau in the Valley of Trials lurks Sarkoth, an unusually vicious scorpid whose venomous sting has brought a young Darkspear hunter to death's door. Lying wounded beneath a tree, the dying troll Hana'zua pleads for a passing warrior to slay the beast and retrieve its mangled claw to salvage his honor. The trials in the Valley are meant to temper aspiring warriors of the Horde, but the harsh desert rarely offers second chances. While stalking the valley's venomous native fauna, the young troll scout Hana'zua encountered a scorpid far larger and deadlier than the rest. Though he managed to strike a heavy blow that mangled one of its pincers, Sarkoth's tail plunged into Hana'zua's chest, leaving him bleeding out in the dry red dirt. Facing what seems to be the end of his life, his only remaining wish is that the beast does not outlive him.

Sarkoth's Mangled Claw. Sarkoth's Mangled Claw is the severed pincer of Sarkoth, a monstrous scorpid stalking the southern bluffs of the Valley of Trials. Heavily scarred by the badly wounded troll Hana'zua, the trophy serves as both proof of the beast's death and a final consolation for a wounded hunter's pride. While hunting in the Valley of Trials, a young Darkspear troll named Hana'zua engaged a massive scorpid known as Sarkoth. Before Sarkoth's venomous stinger pierced his chest and left him bleeding under a nearby tree, Hana'zua landed a crushing blow against the creature's massive pincer. Severing this battered limb offers undeniable proof that the monstrous scorpid has been slain. For Hana'zua, holding the mangled claw confirms that his desperate strike left a lasting mark, providing a fleeting spark of warrior's honor as venom courses through his veins.

Sarltooth's Talon. Sarltooth's Talon is a severed claw taken from the alpha raptor lurking above Whelgar's Excavation Site in the Wetlands. It serves as tangible proof for the dwarf Ormer Ironbraid that the vicious beast responsible for overrunning the archaeological dig has been slain. When raptors overran Whelgar's Excavation Site and butchered the dwarven expedition, Ormer Ironbraid watched from the ridge above, unable to prevent the slaughter. He singled out one massive, menacing raptor—Sarltooth—as the likely pack leader behind the assault. Seeking retribution for his fallen kin, Ormer demanded the beast's death and requested one of its vicious talons as proof of the deed. Severing this claw marks the end of Sarltooth's reign of terror over the ancient dwarven ruins.

Sathrah's Sacrifice. Sathrah's Sacrifice consists of the silvery spinnerets taken from Lady Sathrah, a mighty spider dwelling in Teldrassil. Entrusted to adventurers by Priestess A'moora, this offering is presented at the fountain of the Temple of the Moon to cleanse the creature's corruption and lay her spirit to rest. Lady Sathrah was once a venerable creature of Teldrassil who fell prey to the creeping madness and corruption afflicting the boughs of the great tree. Tasked by the Sisterhood of Elune, adventurers retrieve her silvery spinnerets not as mere trophies, but as a consecrated offering. By bathing these remains within the sacred fountain of the Temple of the Moon, the foul taint that poisoned Sathrah's mind is washed away. The rite frees her troubled soul, allowing her spirit to manifest peacefully within the sanctuary and granting her the promise of rebirth under Elune's grace.

Sathrah's Sacrifice. Sathrah's Sacrifice is the conclusion to a somber ritual performed within the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus. Entrusted with the remains of Lady Sathrah, players offer the fallen creature's spinnerets to Elune's sacred waters to cleanse her soul of corruption and lay her spirit to rest. Following the tragic slaying of Lady Sathrah, Priestess A'moora charges initiates with a final spiritual duty. The great spider had fallen prey to the dark madness spreading across Teldrassil, warping her once-peaceful nature into mindless aggression. Rather than treating her death as a simple culling, the Priesthood of Elune seeks to redeem her fallen essence. By placing her silvery spinnerets into the central fountain of the Temple of the Moon, the consecrated waters wash away the tainting corruption, granting her release.

Satyr. Satyrs are twisted, caprine demons born from the curse of the Highborne sorcerer Xavius during the ancient War of the Ancients. Once night elves, they were warped by Sargeras into horned, hooved beasts dedicated to spreading fel corruption, tormenting their former kin, and furthering the Burning Legion's will. Across the wilds of Kalimdor, scattered satyr sects corrupt pristine woodlands, desecrate moonwells, and subvert vulnerable mortal cults. Ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, the Highborne councilor Xavius failed to keep the Burning Legion's initial gateway stable against Malfurion Stormrage. Enraged by this blunder, Sargeras dismantled Xavius's spirit and rebuilt him as a punishment and tool: his torso retained elven features, but he gained wicked horns, taloned claws, a leonine tail, and the cloven lower body of a goat. Sent back into Zin-Azshari, Xavius gleefully passed his fel affliction to other power-hungry Highborne. Though Xavius was struck down, his demonic progeny survived, continually seeking to reproduce their kind by corrupting others.

Satyr Hooves. Satyr Hooves is a quest given by the troll craftsman Ula'elek in Sen'jin Village. In pursuit of forging a pair of empowered brutal gauntlets, warriors must journey north into Ashenvale to hunt satyrs and harvest their magically bloated, uncloven hooves. To forge armor capable of rivaling the most brutal forces on Kalimdor, the Darkspear craftsman Ula'elek looks beyond mundane iron and leather. He directs aspiring warriors north to the ancient woods of Ashenvale, where lingering demonic corruption festers within the local satyr covens.

Satyr Horns. Satyr Horns are grim trophies harvested from the corrupted satyrs that plague the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Coveted both by grieving forest dwellers seeking retribution and opportunistic merchants trading out of Ratchet, they serve as undeniable proof that another servant of the Burning Legion has fallen. The curled horns of Ashenvale's satyrs are stark symbols of demonic corruption taken root in the sacred forest. For the dryad Illiyana at the Shrine of Aessina, gathering these severed horns is a matter of grief and vengeance for her lost sister Anilia. To outside traders like the traveling goblin Pixel resting at Splintertree Post, however, the horns represent raw opportunity. Demand for satyr horns has surged in the neutral port of Ratchet, transforming these macabre remnants of slain demons into lucrative trade goods for anyone daring enough to hunt their bearers.

Satyr Horns. Satyr Horns is a mercenary contract offered by the traveling goblin Pixel at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Recognizing a lucrative trade opportunity back in the port town of Ratchet, Pixel hires capable Horde adventurers to cull local satyr enclaves and harvest their prized horns. While resting at the Horde forward encampment of Splintertree Post, an opportunistic goblin traveler named Pixel noticed an opening in the frontier market. Horns taken from the demonic satyrs of Ashenvale are in high demand across the Barrens in Ratchet. Unwilling to risk life and limb facing the corrupted creatures directly, Pixel enlists passing adventurers to gather sixteen intact horns before the return journey south.

Satyr Slaying!. Grieving the loss of her sister Anilia, the dryad Illiyana at the Shrine of Aessina seeks vengeance against the satyrs lurking in Ashenvale. She asks Alliance champions to cull the corrupted creatures and return with their horns as proof of their downfall. Dryads are typically playful and serene forest spirits, deeply bonded to nature and elusive to mortals. The brutal slaying of Anilia shatters this tranquility for Illiyana, who dwells at the Shrine of Aessina. Pushed past her carefree nature into unfamiliar sorrow, she turns to travelers of the Alliance to strike down the demonic beasts responsible.

Satyrnaar. Satyrnaar is an ancient, ruined night elf settlement in northeastern Ashenvale that has fallen entirely into the hands of the Bleakheart satyrs. Perched just off the main road between Splintertree Post and Azshara, it is the most intact and easily accessible of the satyr strongholds in the forest. Located northeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of Forest Song, Satyrnaar stands as one of Ashenvale's three primary satyr settlements alongside Xavian and Night Run. Unlike the deeper wilderness ruins, Satyrnaar is relatively well-preserved, featuring pitched tents nestled among crumbled elven architecture. It serves as a bustling camp for the Bleakheart satyrs, making the nearby trade route fraught with peril for travelers moving east toward Azshara. Furthermore, dark ties fester here: the satyrs have forged an alliance with the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand, harboring one of their insidious soulgems amidst the corrupted stones.

Savage Coast. The Savage Coast is the rugged western shoreline of northern Stranglethorn Vale, stretching from the southern border of Westfall down toward Grom'gol Base Camp. Prowled by river crocolisks, shore basilisks, and hostile troll tribes, the strand earns its brutal name with every tide. Running from the cliffs bordering Westfall south toward Grom'gol Base Camp, the Savage Coast marks the perilous western edge of northern Stranglethorn Vale. The sandy banks offer little hospitality: snapjaws, crocolisks, and stonestalkers roam freely among the tide pools and drift logs. Just inland lie territorial jungle troll encampments, making any casual walk along the beach a fight for survival. Offshore, the waters dip toward the submerged dangers of the Vile Reef, ensuring that danger lurks both on the sand and under the waves.

Savannah Lion Tusk. Savannah Lion Tusks are hefty fangs taken from the predatory big cats roaming the arid plains of the Barrens. While common hunting trophies for travelers, they serve an exotic purpose as a brewing ingredient for Chen Stormstout's legendary potent ale. The great cats of the Barrens—from prowlers and huntresses to majestic prides ruled by patriarchs and beasts like Humar the Pridelord—are armed with sharp, heavy tusks. While most who fell these predators take their teeth as simple proof of prowess, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks them out for a far more spirited craft. Drohn uses the tusks alongside plainstrider kidneys and thunder lizard horns to recreate Chen Stormstout's famous namesake brew, imparting a legendary kick that few mortal gullets can easily withstand.

Save Techbot's Brain!. Tinkmaster Overspark tasks Alliance adventurers with retrieving the memory core of Techbot from the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. The once-helpful mechanical assistant suffered severe brain polarization during the city's fall, causing it to run amok. Overspark hopes recovering its core will allow him to reverse the damage and restore his beloved creation. Before the disaster that claimed Gnomeregan, Techbot served as a marvel of gnomish ingenuity. Designed by Tinkmaster Overspark, the automaton aided researchers with countless integrated gizmos and an encyclopedic repository of technical knowledge. However, the chaos of the trogg invasion and the venting of toxic radiation did not spare the machine. A stray electrical surge jolted Techbot's delicate internal architecture, completely polarizing its positronic brain into a volatile negatronic state.

Saving Sharpbeak. Gryphon Master Talonaxe sends you to the summit of Jintha'Alor, which stands in the heart of Vilebranch territory. Vile Priestess Hexx has the key to Sharpbeak's cage, and you are to take it from her and free the gryphon. Following Thadius Grimshade's divination and your report to Talonaxe, the way to rescue Sharpbeak is clear. Jintha'Alor stands in the heart of Vilebranch territory, and you are to fight your way to its summit. Vile Priestess Hexx holds the key to Sharpbeak's cage. Take it from her, then find the cage and save the gryphon.

Saving Yenniku. After obtaining the Mind's Eye, Kin'weelay crafts it into a specialized soul gem to rescue the young troll Yenniku from Zanzil the Outcast. The enchanted vessel is designed to stun Yenniku and capture his spirit, allowing him to be freed and carried back to Nimboya. Following the recovery of the Mind's Eye, Kin'weelay reshapes the potent relic into a magical soul gem. Its dual enchantment allows an adventurer to first stun Yenniku and then place the stone upon his head to capture his wayward spirit within. Once the boy's essence is contained inside the gem, it can safely be returned to his kin at Grom'gol Base Camp.

Scaber Stalk. Scaber Stalks are rare mushrooms that flourish in the damp, secluded cavern hidden behind Cliffspring Falls in Darkshore. Prized by herbalists and alchemists for their unusual properties, they are sought by Barithras Moonshade for his concoctions. Scaber Stalks are obscure mushrooms found deep within the cavern nestled behind Cliffspring Falls, situated along the northeastern mountains of Darkshore. Unlike ordinary forest flora, these pale stalks thrive strictly in the secluded dampness of the subterranean cave network. Their remote and hazardous habitat makes gathering them exceedingly rare, leading alchemists like Barithras Moonshade in Auberdine to commission daring scouts willing to brave the dark.
