name.frFR: À la recherche de la gemme de Kor

text.enUS: Seeking the Kor Gem. "Seeking the Kor Gem" is an Alliance paladin quest that sends an initiate deep into the ancient ruins of northern Kalimdor. Directed by the night elf Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine, paladins venture into Blackfathom Deeps to wrest a potent Kor gem from the naga who corrupt it. The retrieved stone serves as a key material in Jordan Stilwell's craft. When paladins in training seek the materials needed by the human smith Jordan Stilwell, their journey crosses continental borders to Darkshore. There, at Auberdine, Thundris Windweaver remembers the blacksmith with respect. Despite the natural aloofness of the night elves and the transgressions of certain fallen human figures, Thundris holds faith in paladins pursuing a righteous path and willingly reveals where such ancient gems are found.

Seer Graytongue. Seer Graytongue is a venerable tauren elder and spiritual guide residing on Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. Stationed near Camp Narache, he tests young braves undertaking their earliest tribal trials. Through rituals such as the Rite of Strength, he ensures that the youth honor the Earthmother before stepping into the wider world. Seer Graytongue makes his home atop Red Cloud Mesa, serving as an early instructor for aspiring tauren braves and spellweavers. As young adventurers set forth from Camp Narache, Graytongue oversees critical steps of their sacred passage, including the Rites of the Earthmother. By testing their resolve against the harsh plains and dangerous beasts of Mulgore, he instills the virtues of honor, patience, and reverence that every true tauren must carry into adulthood.

Seer Ravenfeather. Seer Ravenfeather is a tauren shaman instructor stationed at Camp Narache on the Red Cloud Mesa. She guides fledging spiritualists through their early trials, helping them attune to the voices of the spirits and the land of Mulgore. Standing within the quiet shelters of Camp Narache, Seer Ravenfeather serves as a patient teacher for young tauren called to walk the shamanic path. The Red Cloud Mesa is a sacred proving ground, and Ravenfeather ensures that novice practitioners understand their duties before venturing into the wider expanses of Mulgore. She instructs them in the foundational rites needed to commune with elemental forces and honor the Earth Mother.

Seer Wiserunner. This respected tauren elder is known as Seer Wiserunner, serving his people faithfully in the rolling hills of Mulgore. From a cave in the hills northwest of Bloodhoof Village, he aids young tauren braves as they undertake the traditional rites of passage that lead toward spiritual adulthood. Seer Wiserunner stands among the gentle bluffs of Mulgore as an elder and mystic of the shu'halo. When young tauren complete their initial trials of strength and vision, they are sent to seek his counsel during their ancestral rites. He interprets visions of the Earth Mother and guides the youth on how to honor their forebears, offering the steady wisdom that binds the scattered nomadic tribes into a unified community.

Seereth Stonebreak. Seereth Stonebreak is an orc shaman who serves the Horde by monitoring the disturbances unsettling the land. Camped near the Greatwood Vale on the border of the Stonetalon Mountains and the Barrens, she directs travelers to address environmental ruin, rogue machines, and rising tensions in Kalimdor. Seereth Stonebreak is an orc dedicated to the harmony of the elements and the protection of Horde territories. Sent to Stonetalon after the land's spirits cried out against the goblins' plunder, she keeps her camp near the Greatwood Vale and maintains a vigilant eye over the landscape. Rather than retreat into despair, she uses her spiritual insight and knowledge of the wild frontier to guide adventurers against looming dangers.

Selling Fish. Dockmaster Baren manages the bustling pier at Lakeshire, but finding fresh stock for his trade has grown difficult. He pays travelers to haul in spotted sunfish, a prized local staple of Lake Everstill that has become dangerous to gather due to the encroaching murlocs. Lake Everstill is known throughout the surrounding lands for its spotted sunfish, a delicate catch that remains in perpetual demand among the townspeople and passing merchants. Yet despite the abundance beneath the lake's surface, the town's supplies regularly run thin. With Lakeshire stretched to its limits under various local threats, even basic commerce requires the help of freelance adventurers.

Senani Thunderheart. Senani Thunderheart is a tauren huntress stationed at Splintertree Post in Ashenvale, just north of the Barrens. Serving the Horde, she tests the mettle of passing travelers by challenging them to pursue the fierce wild predators that roam the ancient forest. Through her trials, hunters prove their skill while thinning the deadly beasts prowling near Horde territory. Found keeping camp at Splintertree Post, Senani Thunderheart represents the hunting traditions of the tauren amid the shadowed groves of Ashenvale. Far from the open plains of Mulgore, she directs Horde adventurers to test their tracking and combat prowess against the forest's apex beasts. She views the hunt as both an honorable challenge and a necessary ritual to survive in an untamed, contested land.

Senator Mehr Stonehallow. Senator Mehr Stonehallow is an Ironforge politician and member of the Explorers' League stationed at the Gol'Bolar Quarry in Dun Morogh. Rather than debating policy in the capital, he has traveled to the front lines to personally oversee the containment of the local trogg infestation. He enlists eager adventurers to cull the beasts before they overrun the quarry completely. While most members of the Ironforge Senate spend their days safely sequestered within the great stone halls of the capital, Senator Mehr Stonehallow prefers direct action. As a dwarf dedicated both to governance and the historical pursuits of the Explorers' League, he understands the practical dangers facing the realm. When vicious Rockjaw troggs began clawing out of the deep rock in Gol'Bolar Quarry, Stonehallow made the journey to the mining pit himself. Convinced that bureaucratic posturing will not save the workers, he offers bounties to capable travelers to eradicate the aggressive troggs and reclaim the quarry.

Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser. Senior Surveyor Fizzledowser is a goblin researcher working from Gadgetzan in Tanaris. He investigates disruptions around the local water supply and sends adventurers to look into the disappearance of Scrimshank.

Senir Whitebeard. Senir Whitebeard is a dwarven dignitary and field agent stationed outside the Thunderbrew Distillery in Kharanos. Serving as a special envoy from the Senate of Ironforge, he is tasked with monitoring the growing threats encircling Dun Morogh. His mission centers on evaluating the Frostmane troll offensive and reporting their movements directly back to the dwarven leadership. While most travelers visit Kharanos for its bustling inn and famous stout, Senir Whitebeard is here on official business. As a representative sent directly by the Senate of Ironforge, his presence highlights how seriously the high halls take the destabilization of Dun Morogh. He serves as an essential bridge between local scouts facing danger on the snowy frontier and the legislators arguing policy behind the city's stone gates.

Senir's Observations. Having gathered vital intelligence on local threats in Coldridge Valley, Grelin Whitebeard entrusts you with carrying his findings to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, out in Kharanos. However, leaving the sheltered valley requires passing through a tunnel recently overrun by hostile troggs, guarded by Mountaineer Thalos. Grelin Whitebeard spent considerable effort documenting the troll activity stirring around Coldridge Valley. When his journal was pilfered and subsequently recovered, it became clear that the collected intelligence was far too critical to trust to an inexperienced apprentice. Looking to bypass intermediate hands, Grelin selects a seasoned adventurer to convey his report directly to his brother, Senir Whitebeard, who conducts operations outside the valley in Kharanos.

Senir's Observations. This errand completes a scouting line out of Coldridge Valley, carrying Grelin Whitebeard's completed report through the trogg-infested pass to his brother Senir in Kharanos. It bridges the secluded training grounds of Anvilmar with the broader troubles facing Dun Morogh. Through Senir's candid reception, travelers catch their first glimpse of political friction simmering between field scouts and the Ironforge Senate. After Grelin Whitebeard recovers his stolen journal from the Frostmane trolls, he prepares a detailed report of the valley's threats for his brother Senir. Mountaineer Thalos, stationed guarding the gate out of Coldridge Valley, entrusts passing adventurers with carrying this dispatch. Leaving the relative seclusion of the introductory vale means braving the tunnel cut through the mountain, which has recently been overrun by violent troggs ambushing all traffic. Travelers who punch through emerge onto the snowblown highways of central Dun Morogh, following the main road straight into the cozy hub of Kharanos.

Senir's Report. Senir's Report is a dispatched document penned by Mountaineer Senir Whitebeard detailing the Frostmane troll threat in Dun Morogh. It carries findings commissioned under royal directive and is destined for Senator Barin Redstone in Ironforge. Drafted after scouting missions against the Frostmane trolls nestled in the crags of Dun Morogh, this field report contains mountaineer observations intended for the dwarf Senate. Senir Whitebeard, stationed out in the cold foothills, penned the document and enclosed his brother Grelin's report on Coldridge Valley, which states that Grelin acted under a sanction from King Magni Bronzebeard. Senir tasks adventurers with hauling the findings straight to Senator Barin Redstone in the High Seat of Ironforge—cautiously advising couriers to omit just how much outside help he required to compile it.

Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak is a night elf guardian stationed within the serene groves of the Oracle Glade on Teldrassil. Charged with monitoring the sacred balance of the northern boughs, she keeps a wary watch over the glade's enchanted waters and woodland wildlife. Arynia Cloudsbreak serves the Sentinel army in one of the most secluded and mystical reaches of Teldrassil: the Oracle Glade. Amid ancient trees and ethereal springs, she carries out her watch far from the bustling avenues of Darnassus, ensuring the sanctity of the wilderness remains undisturbed.

Sentinel Aynasha. Sentinel Aynasha is an operative of the night elven Sentinels serving in the wild borders of Darkshore. Tasked with scouting enemy movements and carrying critical intelligence, she regularly faces peril against hostile forces threatening northern Kalimdor. As a scout and archer for the Sentinels, Aynasha is deployed to the dangerous frontiers where night elven lands clash with hostile incursions. Carrying out stealth missions and bearing urgent dispatches across rugged terrain, she relies on her marksmanship and survival instincts to evade enemy patrols and survive deep within contested territory.

Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze is a night elf guardian stationed in Auberdine along the misty coast of Darkshore. Operating from the upper floor of a lodge across the bridge, she monitors growing regional threats and directs travelers toward pressing concerns in the wilderness. While many Sentinels patrol the foggy coastline and woodlands directly, Elissa Starbreeze coordinates defensive efforts from Auberdine. Stationed on the upper level of the building just northeast across the bridge from the town inn, she stays alert to unusual disturbances in Darkshore. Her tasks frequently point adventurers toward remote points of interest, including the mysterious Tower of Althalaxx looming far to the north, ensuring that shadowy incursions do not take the coastal settlement unawares.

Sentinel Farsong. Sentinel Farsong is a night elf sentinel stationed at Silverwing Grove in Ashenvale. Serving as a crucial liaison for the Silverwing Sentinels, she coordinates intelligence and combat efforts against the encroaching Warsong Outriders in Warsong Gulch. Standing vigil within Silverwing Grove, Sentinel Farsong is deeply involved in the defense of Ashenvale's southern border. With the Warsong clan continuously harvesting lumber and pushing deeper into ancestral night elf territories, she mobilizes Alliance champions to strike at Warsong Outriders and ensures field reports reach Silverwing command. Her duties center on rallying volunteers to check the Horde's territorial expansion and preserve the sacred woods.

Sentinel Hill. In Westfall, Sentinel Hill remains the Alliance's main stronghold and the People's Militia's command post. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and hostile outlaws surround the rise, the only secure foothold for lawful citizens in the region. Sentinel Hill rises above central Westfall, with a barracks-style inn, a gryphon roost linking travelers to Stormwind and beyond, a forge, and a lumber mill around Sentinel Tower. Overgrown fields, scavenging gnolls, and outlaws crowd the surrounding land. The encampment keeps a fragile perimeter where travelers, beleaguered farmers, and recruits can regroup under the watchful eyes of veteran defenders.

Sentinel Onaeya. Sentinel Onaeya is a night elf guardian stationed at Maestra's Post in northwestern Ashenvale, near the border with Darkshore. Tasked with holding the line against encroaching perils, she rallies capable Alliance adventurers to safeguard the forest and aid fellow sentinels. Maestra's Post serves as a critical wayside outpost along the road from Darkshore into the dense, contested canopy of Ashenvale. Sentinel Onaeya stands guard outside the settlement's main lodge, keeping a vigilant watch over travelers and coordinating defensive actions. Between hostile wildlife, corrupting forces, and border tensions, sentinels like Onaeya represent the first line of defense for night elf settlements in the region.

Sentinel Selarin. Sentinel Selarin is a night elf scout dispatched to the coastal settlement of Auberdine. Acting as an emissary for the defenders of Ashenvale, she seeks reinforcements to help stem the rising perils threatening the ancient forest. As tensions and dark threats mount across Ashenvale, the garrison there has found its resources stretched to the breaking point. Under the direction of Raene Wolfrunner, Sentinel Selarin traveled north along the forest road into Darkshore. Her mission was straightforward: seek out Terenthis in Auberdine and request assistance from the sentinels and scouts stationed on the coast.

Sentinel Thenysil. Sentinel Tara Thenysil is a night elf sentinel stationed in Astranaar within the ancient forest of Ashenvale. Vigilant over the surrounding wilderness, she keeps close tabs on military operations in the region and coordinates scouts watching neighboring territories. Her attention is particularly focused on allied movements pushing south into the contested Stonetalon Mountains. From her post in the fortified settlement of Astranaar, Sentinel Thenysil helps secure Ashenvale against growing hostility. Night elf holdings throughout the region face relentless encroachment, making communications between distant outposts vital. While much of the local garrison focuses directly on defending the forest road, Thenysil directs Alliance volunteers beyond Ashenvale's borders to ensure distant allies remain supported.

Sentinel Tower. Defenders watch Westfall from Sentinel Tower atop Sentinel Hill. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia organize resistance against bandits, gnolls, and the Defias Brotherhood. Sentinel Tower rises above the unsettled plains of Westfall. With Stormwind's official army largely absent and aid withheld, local volunteers and veterans joined together around this central stronghold. From its stone heights, lookouts can see across the dusty plains, from abandoned pumpkin patches to the misty shores. They watch for highwaymen and gnoll raiding parties moving through the region.

Sentinel Tysha Moonblade. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade is a night elf scout stationed along the main road of Darkshore, just west of the ancient ruins of Ameth'Aran. Tasked with patrolling the troubled coastal wilderness, she directs travelers and recruits aid to investigate the restless spirits haunting the shattered elven settlements nearby. Standing sentinel along the overgrown highway of Darkshore, Tysha Moonblade keeps a vigilant eye over an increasingly unstable land. Directly to her east lie the haunted remnants of Ameth'Aran, where cursed Highborne ghosts and malevolent banshees linger among ancient stone pillars. Recognizing that Auberdine's limited defenses are stretched thin by threats across the coast, Tysha enlists capable adventurers passing by to uncover the history behind Ameth'Aran's tragic fall and put down the restless dead.

Sentinel Velene Starstrike. Sentinel Velene Starstrike is a night elf guardian stationed at Silverwind Refuge in central Ashenvale. Tasked with protecting the sanctuary and the surrounding waters, she confronts encroaching unnatural threats such as rogue elementals and foul sorcerers. Her vigilance helps safeguard the ancient woodland from corrupting magical interference. Stationed beside the clear waters of Mystral Lake, Sentinel Velene Starstrike maintains a watchful vigil from Silverwind Refuge. Like many night elf sentinels scattered throughout Ashenvale, her primary duty is preserving the balance of the forest and repelling threats to elven sanctuaries. The serene grove serves as a vital rest stop for travelers traversing the central woods, making her presence essential to the area's ongoing safety.

Sentinels. The Sentinels are the elite, predominantly female military force of the night elves, formed ten thousand years ago after the War of the Ancients. Guided by the Sisterhood of Elune and commanded by General Shandris Feathermoon, they guard kaldorei settlements and defend sacred lands from Ashenvale to Feralas. Today, they wage a bitter war against Horde deforestation while watching over their new home on Teldrassil. Before the Great Sundering, the military of the ancient Kaldorei Empire had devolved into a decadent hierarchy where rank was decided by noble lineage rather than martial skill. The devastation of the War of the Ancients proved that this aristocratic structure was utterly unfit to defend Azeroth. In the aftermath, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind spearheaded radical reforms across night elf society. She turned to the Sisterhood of Elune, an order that had survived intact and possessed extensive experience in tactics, combat, and healing. From its devout ranks, Tyrande forged the Sentinels: a standing martial army dedicated to selflessly protecting their emerging society without regard to noble heritage.

Sentry Point. Sentry Point is a human watchtower stationed on the mainland edge of Dustwallow Marsh, guarding the causeway bridge that leads directly to Theramore Isle. Maintained by Theramore's forces, it monitors traffic entering and exiting Lady Jaina Proudmoore's island citadel. Positioned at the western end of the long bridge linking Theramore Isle to the treacherous wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Sentry Point serves as the stronghold's first line of defense on the mainland. The stone scout tower keeps watch over the swamp road, ensuring that hostile marsh beasts or Horde raiders cannot approach the island city unnoticed.

Separation Anxiety. Huntsman Markhor in Revantusk Village has lost his twin brother Malkhor, taken by the Vilebranch in the same raid that took Torntusk's mate. Malkhor met a swift, brutal end, and his remains were fed to the Vilebranch's oozes and wolves. Markhor says his brother's life is beyond saving, yet his soul can still be rescued, and he asks you to recover the remains. Markhor says that many in the village have lost loved ones to the wilds, and his own loss is Malkhor, his twin. The Vilebranch took Malkhor during the raid that took Torntusk's mate. Malkhor was not fated to live, and his captors put him to a swift, brutal death.

Sepulcher. The Sepulcher is the primary Forsaken settlement and stronghold in Silverpine Forest. Once an ordinary Lordaeron graveyard and burial crypt overlooking the western coast, it now serves as a fortified sanctuary for the Horde against surrounding regional threats. Perched in the hills above the Lordaeron coastline, the Sepulcher was originally a quiet cemetery and crypt alongside the western road. In the wake of the Third War, the newly emancipated Forsaken repurposed the ancient stone vault and its grounds into an essential outpost. Surrounded by hostile forces on all sides—the feral worgen to the south, wandering Scourge remnants to the east, and Kirin Tor wizards watching from Ambermill—the Sepulcher provides a rare haven of safety, supplies, and command for travelers marching through Silverpine.

Serena Bloodfeather. This bounty task charges Horde adventurers with slaying Serena Bloodfeather, the matriarch driving harpy raids against Crossroads supply lines. Her campaign is a personal blood feud stemming from the Champion of the Horde Rexxar slaying her sister. Putting an end to Serena aims to shatter the coordination behind the harpy flock in the northern Barrens. The Witchwing harpies infesting the crags northwest of the Crossroads do not strike solely out of animalistic hunger. Their leader, Serena Bloodfeather, wages an explicit blood feud against the Horde. Years ago during the founding of Durotar, the wandering beastmaster Rexxar struck down Serena's sister, a notorious matriarch named Bloodfeather. Consumed by hatred for the nascent Horde, Serena has rallied her flock into an organized scourge intent on butchering supply trains, scouts, and merchants traveling the arid trails.

Serena's Head. Serena's Head is the grisly trophy taken from the matriarch of the Dry Hills harpies in the northern Barrens. Darsok Swiftdagger of the Crossroads demanded it as proof of her demise, intending to display it upon Horde supply wagons as a harsh deterrent against further aerial raids.

Serge Hinott. Serge Hinott is a Forsaken alchemist stationed in Tarren Mill in the Hillsbrad Foothills. Working closely alongside Apothecary Lydon, he assists the Royal Apothecary Society with brewing concoctions, antidotes, and reagents essential to the Forsaken war effort. Positioned beside Apothecary Lydon in the fortified settlement of Tarren Mill, Serge Hinott plays a crucial supporting role for Forsaken operations in Hillsbrad Foothills. While Lydon focuses on broader chemical development and aggressive plague research against neighboring human settlements like Southshore, Hinott manages specialized brewing tasks. His expertise includes preparing restorative salves and critical antidotes required when field agents and scouts encounter dangerous poisons and toxic mishaps.

Sergra Darkthorn. Having proven their basic tracking and stalking skills in the rolling hills of Mulgore, young tauren are directed outward into the arid wilderness of the Barrens. Melor Stonehoof sends aspiring hunters north of the border to report to Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. This journey marks the hunter's formal transition from local trials to the demanding predatory hierarchy of Kalimdor's broader plains. For a novice tauren hunter, completing initial rites in Mulgore is only the beginning. The lush valleys of their ancestral homeland are protected and familiar, nurturing beasts that test patience rather than sheer survival. Melor Stonehoof recognizes when a hunter's spirit has grown enough to require harsher trials. He instructs his pupils to pack their gear, leave the safety of Bloodhoof Village, and venture east across the mountain pass into the baked scrublands of the Barrens.

Serpent Wild. Serpent Wild is a Horde quest in Thousand Needles that connects the discovery of strange alien eggs to ancient tauren legends. Following an unsettling revelation at Freewind Post, Hagar Lightninghoof dispatches adventurers northwest to Motega Firemane at Whitereach Post to confront the awakening of Arikara. When strange, unnatural eggs began appearing in Thousand Needles, local tauren feared an ecological disaster. However, inspecting the artifacts reveals something far older and more ominous than ordinary predators: signs pointing to the vengeance spirit Arikara. Stunned by the horrifying confirmation, Hagar Lightninghoof realizes the canyon faces a mythical threat long thought relegated to fireside lore.

Serpent's Coil. Serpent's Coil is a winding network of caves and burnt-out encampments nestled in the eastern ridges of the Blasted Lands. Littered with scorched orcish architecture left behind from the older wars, it serves as a secluded redoubt for dark cultists. Carved into the jagged eastern cliffs of the Blasted Lands, the winding path and caverns of Serpent's Coil wind past ruined orcish huts that date back to the First and Second Wars. Rather than simple beasts, the tunnels harbor cabals of Shadowsworn cultists and practitioners of dark arts drawn to the residual demonic energies permeating the red wastes. Deep within its twisting hollows, they work far from the watchful eyes of Nethergarde Keep.

Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a rare, subterranean herb found growing only in the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Its potent natural properties have drawn the keen interest of the Forsaken's Royal Apothecary Society. Serpentbloom grows exclusively within the damp, shadowy tunnels of the Wailing Caverns beneath the Barrens. Rooted in an ecosystem warped by unrestrained Emerald Dream energies, the plant thrives far from sunlight and often harbors venomous serpents nesting among its stems. Because the cave system is overrun with hostile beasts and corrupted druids, few who venture inside ever return with viable specimens.

Serpentbloom. Serpentbloom is a gathering task issued by Apothecary Zamah, an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society residing in Thunder Bluff. Zamah seeks specimens of a rare herb native to the subterranean depths of the Wailing Caverns to aid the research of the Forsaken. Stationed in the Pools of Vision beneath the Spirit Rise in Thunder Bluff, Apothecary Zamah serves as an envoy of the Royal Apothecary Society from the Undercity. While the tauren hosts focus on spiritual balance and healing the wounded land, Zamah's attention is fixed on rare and virulent materials. Having isolated a sample of an unusual plant known as Serpentbloom, she seeks bulk quantities to advance the research directives of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken.

Service to the Horde. The jeweled pendant now sits with Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar, delivered after Report to Zor, and Zor has one more word for you. You carried the jeweled pendant to Zor Lonetree in Orgrimmar, and the pendant now sits with Zor. Return to Zor Lonetree and there is more to hear about what you have done for the Horde.

Set Them Ablaze!. Squire Maltrake tells you the four towers of Searing Gorge can never be destroyed, but the Torch of Retribution can set them burning for a very long time. While they burn, no guard or sentry can hold the watch posts, and the Dark Irons lose their first line of defense. The flames the torch lights cannot be put out by any element or force. Maltrake sends you inside each of the four sentry towers, North, South, East and West, to use the torch within their walls. The Dark Irons have posted lookouts at the towers, and Maltrake warns you to beware of them.

Sethir's Journal. Sethir's Journal is a personal record carried by the elusive satyr Sethir the Ancient in Teldrassil. Recovered through stealth, its contents confirm the alarming spread of corruption from mainland Kalimdor onto the World Tree.

Sevren's Orders. Sevren's Orders are written dispatches penned by Magistrate Sevren of Brill. They direct a proven Forsaken agent to report to Bethor Iceshard, a formidable mage stationed in the Undercity's Magic Quarter. As the Forsaken solidify their grip on the ruins of Lordaeron, skilled agents who have proven their worth against the Scourge in Tirisfal Glades are summoned south to the capital. Issued by Magistrate Sevren, these written orders serve as official introduction and credentials to Bethor Iceshard, one of the Dark Lady's foremost practitioners of the arcane in the Magic Quarter. While Sevren knows little beyond the fact that the assignment involves reaching out to an errant lich, the summons carries the absolute authority of the Undercity's high mages.

Sewers. The Sewers are a sprawling subterranean drainage network that provides a secondary entrance directly into the Undercity. Cutting beneath the hills west of the ruined palace of Lordaeron, this conduit allows bat handlers and stealthy travelers to bypass the precarious elevators leading down from the throne room. Before the plague wiped out Lordaeron, these stone culverts served as the mundane sewer lines draining the royal capital. In the hands of Sylvanas Windrunner's Forsaken, however, the runoff tunnels have been integrated into the Undercity's outer defenses. Emerging west of the surface ruins near a contested Scarlet Watchtower in Tirisfal Glades, the passage provides a level, direct slope inside. Forsaken bat handlers use this cavernous conduit to fly riders swiftly into the subterranean rings, avoiding the sluggish cage lifts entirely. Because it circumvents the heavily fortified surface courtyards, it remains a dangerous vulnerability that hostile infiltrators constantly seek to exploit.

Shadow Council. The Shadow Council was the secret cabal of warlocks and necrolytes that orchestrated the corruption of the Old Horde on Draenor and guided its invasion of Azeroth. Founded by Gul'dan under the direction of the Burning Legion, the cult manipulated clan chieftains from behind the scenes until Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer purged their stronghold in Blackrock Mountain. Before the crossing into Azeroth, Gul'dan brought together a clandestine assembly of warlocks, necrolytes, and opportunistic chieftains to manipulate the orcish clans. By elevating Blackhand the Destroyer as a malleable figurehead, the Shadow Council ruled the Old Horde from the dark. They disseminated fel magic across Draenor and fed the blood of the demon Mannoroth to the clans, binding the orcs to the will of the Burning Legion.

Shadow Grave. Shadow Grave is a stone crypt perched atop the sloping burial grounds above Deathknell in Tirisfal Glades. It serves as the physical awakening point where newly liberated Forsaken shake off the stupor of death and the Lich King's faded control. Tucked into the rocky foothills at the top of the graveyard slope above Deathknell, the Shadow Grave is a simple stone mausoleum with an extraordinary purpose. Inside its damp vaults, corpses raised into the mindless servitude of the Scourge gradually awaken to free will. Under the watchful eye of caretakers like Undertaker Mordo, these freshly liberated undead stand up from their stone slabs and take their first shuddering steps into a world that despises them, setting out down the footpath toward Deathknell to pledge themselves to the Banshee Queen.

Shadow Hold. Shadow Hold is a sprawling subterranean complex hidden within the blighted canyon of Jaedenar in western Felwood. Once a sacred night elf barrow den, it has been seized and desecrated by the Shadow Council to serve as their primary bastion on Kalimdor. Beneath the corrupted red earth of Jaedenar lies Shadow Hold, a vast underground labyrinth carved out of what was once an ancient night elf barrow den. Where sleeping druids once rested to tend the Emerald Dream, dark warlocks and demonic servitors now stalk twisted corridors illuminated by fel fire. At its deepest tiers, the cult commands a formidable force under the dreadlord Lord Banehollow, Prince Xavalis, and Shadow Lord Fel'dan, making it the supreme seat of demonic influence in the region.

Shadow Magic. Shadow Magic is a desperate task given by Marshal Marris to disrupt the dark arts bolstering the Blackrock invasion of Redridge. Blackrock shadowcasters have brought demon-tainted midnight orbs to the battlefield, weaponizing dark energies against the beleaguered defenders of Lakeshire. Securing and destroying these cursed relics is vital to holding the town's defensive line. While brute force has always been the hallmark of the Blackrock clan, their recent incursions into the Redridge Mountains display a far more insidious threat. The invaders have bolstered their ranks with shadowcasters wielding dark powers. These casters do not rely on sorcery alone; they channel their fel and shadow energies through demon-tainted artifacts known as midnight orbs. The artifacts have inflicted terrible losses upon the local town militia, tilting an already desperate war further in favor of the invaders.

Shadow Priest Allister. Shadow Priest Allister is a Forsaken priest stationed at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. Overseeing intelligence and tactical efforts in the region, he coordinates operations to monitor Dalaran's wizards and secure the borders of Lordaeron for the Dark Lady. Operating out of the Sepulcher, Shadow Priest Allister directs Forsaken reconnaissance throughout Silverpine Forest. From this central crypt settlement, he tracks nearby threats ranging from renegade humans and beastly incursions to the arcane machinations unfolding around Dalaran.

Shadow Priest Sarvis. Shadow Priest Sarvis stands inside the ruined chapel of Deathknell, serving as one of the primary guides for newly awakened Forsaken. He introduces fresh corpses to their grim reality, directing them to purge mindless undead and gather intelligence on local threats. Under Lady Sylvanas's banner, Sarvis works tirelessly to shape bewildered undead into disciplined servants of the Forsaken. Within the shadowy chapel of Deathknell, Shadow Priest Sarvis waits for those who have just clawed their way out of the grave. The awakening of a Forsaken soul is jarring and horrific, with many immediately losing their minds to mindless frenzy or despondency. Sarvis acts as an anchor, giving purpose to the newly risen. He assigns new recruits to put down the shambling, mindless corpses roaming the cemetery and directs them to secure Deathknell's borders against the encroaching Scourge.

Shadow of the Past. In Stormwind, the trail from a Stockade prisoner leads into the city’s hidden dealings. Baros Alexston sends you to Mathias Shaw after a mysterious visitor spoke with Bazil Thredd. Baros Alexston cannot identify the visitor who spoke with Bazil Thredd, the Stockade’s chief prisoner. Warden Thelwater’s account has brought investigators to the city architect, but he has no name to offer. Instead, Baros points you toward Master Mathias Shaw, who leads SI:7 and makes it his business to know Stormwind’s secrets.

Shadowbreak Ravine. Shadowbreak Ravine is a secluded mountain hollow tucked away in southeastern Desolace. Cloaked among jagged crags near Magram Village, this eerie ravine serves as a hidden redoubt for the demonic forces and mortal zealots of the Burning Blade. Tucked deep into the barren mountain ridges southeast of Magram Village, Shadowbreak Ravine provides the Burning Blade with a secluded staging ground away from the eyes of wandering centaur tribes. Amid strange, oversized mushrooms and grim ritual encampments, cultists labor alongside summoned demons. Here, dark practitioners invoke fel energies and tend heavy ritual chains, using the natural isolation of the ravine to marshal reinforcements and maintain a firm demonic foothold within the badlands of Desolace.

Shadowfang Keep. Perched on a rugged bluff overlooking Pyrewood Village in southern Silverpine Forest, Shadowfang Keep is the dark lair of the mad Archmage Arugal and his feral worgen. Formerly known as Silverlaine Keep, the fortress fell to ravenous wolf-beasts summoned during the Third War, leaving its ancient halls haunted by the slain nobility and crawling with lupine horrors. Before the Third War, this towering fortress was called Silverlaine Keep, the ancestral seat of Baron Silverlaine and the center of authority for nearby Pyrewood Village. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron, desperate wizards sought forbidden means to stem the undead tide. Relying on the dimensional research of the Dalaran mage Ur, the Archmage Arugal summoned the extra-dimensional worgen into Azeroth. The savage beasts tore through the Scourge, but quickly spiraled out of control. Rampaging across southern Silverpine, the pack besieged the stronghold, slaughtering Baron Silverlaine, his family, and Commander Springvale's defenders. Guilt and grief shattered Arugal's sanity; rather than flee, he claimed the fortress, renaming it Shadowfang Keep and adopting the monstrous predators as his 'children.'

Shadowguard. Shadowguard is a priestly calling issued to Darkspear troll priests who find themselves far from home in the Forsaken capital of Undercity. Aelthalyste recognizes that the young troll has matured enough for their tribe's sacred rites and sends them back to Orgrimmar. In the Valley of Spirits, the priest trainer Ur'kyo awaits to guide them into a vital tier of spiritual protection. Even in the gloom of the Undercity, the bonds of faith and tribal tradition remain strong. Forsaken priest trainer Aelthalyste observes visiting troll priests closely, noting when an initiate has grown potent enough to face their culture's trials. Rather than imposing the bleak philosophy of the Forsaken priesthood upon them, she directs the troll back across the Great Sea to the ancestral ways of their own elders.

Shadowhide Pendant. Shadowhide Pendants are crude ornamental charms carried by the Shadowhide gnolls roaming the Redridge Mountains. Collected as legal proof of bounty enforcement, they signify that local defenders have enacted Lakeshire's law against gnolls collaborating with the rogue mage Morganth. Carried by warriors, brutes, and spellcasters of the Shadowhide clan, these pendants serve as crude personal totems or rank insignias. Deep in the hills of Redridge, the clan has rallied under Lieutenant Fangore and fallen under the sway of Morganth, a rogue wielder of the Arcane. To the townspeople of Lakeshire, these charms are not mere primitive jewelry; they are identifying marks of an organized menace harassing settlements across the region on behalf of an enemy of the Crown.

Shadowprey Village. Shadowprey Village is a remote Horde fishing settlement built along the rocky southern coast of Sar'theris Strand in Desolace. Populated largely by Darkspear troll fishermen and supported by tauren service keepers, it acts as a critical coastal outpost and trade lifeline amidst a barren wasteland. Tucked against the cliffs of southern Desolace, Shadowprey Village offers safe harbor in a region notorious for centaur clans and desolate wastes. The settlement is primarily an encampment of troll fishermen whose hauls sustain not only their own village but also inland outposts like Ghost Walker Post. Despite the rough shoreline, towering wooden piers reach out into the ocean, allowing local anglers to brave deep waters and dive for shellfish among the submerged wreckage dotting Sar'theris Strand.

Shadowsong Shrine. Shadowsong Shrine is a ruined hillside sanctuary situated in western Azshara, not far from the Ashenvale border. Haunted by the restless spirits of ancient Highborne, the site bears the illustrious name of the Shadowsong bloodline, though its true historical connection to them remains shrouded in mystery. Perched upon a high hill overlooking the shattered lands of Azshara, the Shadowsong Shrine lies in ancient, overgrown ruin. Like much of the surrounding coast, it is plagued by the lingering apparitions of Highborne ghosts who wander among the fallen stonework, seeking to extinguish any mortal life that trespasses upon their domain. The shrine shares its name with Maiev Shadowsong, the unrelenting warden of Illidan Stormrage. Whether this sanctuary honors her family or dates back to before the Sundering is a secret lost to the ages.

Shadowthread Cave. Shadowthread Cave is a damp cavern carved into the northwest cliffs of Shadowglen on Teldrassil. Traditionally inhabited by indigenous Webwood spiders, the cave has recently turned dangerously aggressive under the dominion of their broodmother, Githyiss the Vile. Tucked away in the shaded perimeter of Shadowglen, Shadowthread Cave has long served as a natural lair for Teldrassil's giant spiders. In earlier years, these arachnids coexisted quietly alongside the nascent boughs of the World Tree. Recently, however, their temperament has turned fiercely territorial. Thick layers of webwood silk now choke the stone corridors, and the aggressive nature of the brood poses an immediate hazard to young kaldorei taking their first steps beyond Aldrassil.

Shadumbra's Head. This quest represents the proof of victory over Shadumbra, a notoriously ferocious nightsaber stalking the western paths of Ashenvale. Taking the beast's severed head back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post fulfills a key trial of the Ashenvale Hunt and secures travel routes toward the Zoram Strand. Shadumbra is no ordinary predator among the towering trees of Ashenvale. The great nightsaber stalked the wilderness west of Splintertree Post, preying upon Horde scouts and couriers attempting to journey toward the Zoram Strand. Her speed, stealth, and sheer savagery made travel on foot perilous, leaving Splintertree's defenders on edge whenever patrols moved west.

Shady Rest Inn. The Shady Rest Inn was once a welcoming human-built waystation sitting just off the road between the Barrens and Theramore Isle. Today, only charred timbers and smoldering ashes remain following a sudden and violent arson attack. The tragedy left the innkeeper shattered and sparked tension across the marsh as investigators sift through the wreckage for clues. Built to serve travelers navigating the treacherous crossing between Dustwallow Marsh and the Barrens, the Shady Rest Inn stood as an outpost of civilized comfort in a harsh wilderness. That ended when the inn was abruptly razed to the ground in a devastating fire. Innkeeper James Hyal managed to survive the inferno, but the blaze claimed the lives of his wife and child. Traumatized and grief-stricken, Hyal was left with nothing as the ruins became an active crime scene, drawing scrutiny from Theramore authorities desperate to identify who ignited the flames.

Shael'dryn. Shael'dryn is an inquisitive dryad residing beside the Moonwell of Purity, east of Iris Lake in Ashenvale. She serves as a vital contact for night elf scouts investigating forest corruption. She plays a pivotal role in aiding Astranaar's sentinels with cleansing relics to combat demonic and foul influences spreading across the wilderness. Stationed beside the Moonwell of Purity, Shael'dryn keeps watch alongside the night elf sentinels guarding the eastern approaches of the forest. When corruption surfaces among the local wildlife or tainted relics threaten the land's harmony, her deep natural understanding allows her to guide adventurers through the steps required to restore spiritual balance.

Shalzaru's Lair. Shalzaru's Lair is a sprawling, submerged cavern located at the northern tip of the Isle of Dread in Feralas. It serves as a major stronghold for the Hatecrest naga and shelters their formidable master, Shalzaru. From within these damp tunnels, the serpentine invaders coordinate their aggressive presence just south of Feathermoon Stronghold. Carved into the rugged bluffs at the northern end of the Isle of Dread, Shalzaru's Lair is divided into a massive main cavern and a smaller auxiliary chamber, linked together by submerged subterranean waterways. The interior teems with Hatecrest serpent guards and spell-weaving sorceresses on high alert. Deep within the recesses dwells Lord Shalzaru, the serpentine overlord directing the Hatecrest brood across the island. Its proximity to Sardor Isle poses a direct, constant threat to the night elf Sentinels garrisoned at Feathermoon Stronghold just across the channel.

Shaman. Shaman are spiritual mediators who commune with the primordial forces of earth, air, fire and water. Balancing raw nature through totems, lightning and ancestral healing, they are the spiritual core of orc, tauren and troll culture under Warchief Thrall. Dwarves walk the path too, as the Wildhammer long have, and the Skyborne Windshapers seek to restore their people's bond with the winds. Unlike priests who revere the divine or mages who bend the arcane, shaman interact directly with the primal forces of nature. The elements of earth, air, fire, and water are inherently chaotic and locked in perpetual conflict. A shaman does not enslave these forces, but petitions and negotiates with them, serving as a balance keeper between primal fury and the mortal world. Through wooden and stone totems planted into the soil, shaman channel these elemental bargains to protect allies, hinder foes, or mend the wounded with cleansing water.

Shaman Voodoo Charm. The Shaman Voodoo Charm is a dark ritual trinket carried by Gnarlpine furbolg shamans deep within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Emanating a vile aura, this charm channels an unnatural magic capable of severing a slumbering druid's spirit from their physical flesh. The Gnarlpine tribe of Teldrassil has fallen into madness and corruption, but within the Ban'ethil Barrow Den, their shamans wield powers far beyond ordinary wilderness sorcery. Utilizing these strange voodoo charms, the shamans discovered a way to rip a sleeping druid's consciousness away from the mortal realm and trap it helplessly within the Emerald Dream. By severing the soul from the vessel, the furbolgs are able to animate the empty physical form, turning venerable night elf protectors into mindless guardians that slaughter anyone venturing into the barrows.

Shan'do. Shan'do is a revered Darnassian honorific meaning "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." Traditionally used within night elven society and druidic circles, it denotes deep reverence toward a mentor who guides another along the path of wisdom and natural magic. Its direct counterpart is thero'shan, meaning "honored student." In the Darnassian language, shan'do translates directly to "honored teacher" or "honored instructor." It is far more than an occupational label: addressing an elder or mentor as shan'do expresses solemn humility, filial devotion, and enduring respect for their guidance.

Shanda. Shanda is a night elf priestess and mentor located within the hollow trunk of Aldrassil in Shadowglen. Serving the Sisterhood of Elune, she instructs novice night elf priests in the fundamental prayers, wards, and rites of the Moon Goddess. Her guidance helps fledgling acolytes balance the light of Elune with their duties in defending Teldrassil. Standing within the tranquil sanctuary of Aldrassil, Shanda serves as one of the first spiritual guides for young night elves dedicated to Elune. While the druids tend to the waking roots and boughs of Teldrassil, priestesses like Shanda ensure that the spiritual heart of the Kaldorei remains tethered to the White Lady. She instructs new initiates on channeling lunar grace for healing and protective wards, preparing them to face the corruption creeping into the boughs of the World Tree.

Shandris Feathermoon. Shandris Feathermoon is the General of the Sentinel Army and, for ten thousand years, Tyrande Whisperwind's right hand. She now commands night elf military forces throughout Kalimdor from Feathermoon Stronghold on Sardor Isle off the coast of Feralas. Shandris Feathermoon is one of the oldest defenders of the night elves. For ten thousand years she has served at Tyrande Whisperwind's side as the high priestess's right hand among the Sentinels, through the long vigil that followed the Sundering.

Shaper's Terrace. Perched high on the northern bluffs above Marshal's Refuge, the Shaper's Terrace is a mysterious overlook marked by ancient titan architecture. It is named in honor of Khaz'goroth the Shaper and bears quiet witness to the primordial experiments that shaped Un'Goro Crater. Overlooking the lush, prehistoric basin of Un'Goro Crater, the Shaper's Terrace holds monumental stone edifices left behind by the titans. Believed to be dedicated to Khaz'goroth the Shaper, this high plateau stands as a testament to the celestial architects who cultivated the crater as a living laboratory for early life on Azeroth. From these elevated stones, ancient entities once observed and directed the flora and fauna below. Its cold stone arches and massive metallic plinths stand in stark, enigmatic contrast to the untamed wilderness thriving directly beneath them.

Shard of Water. The Shard of Water is an elemental remnant gathered during a shaman's communion with the spirits of water. Delivered to Islen Waterseer along the Barrens coast, it serves as tangible proof that an initiate has understood water's life-giving nature and conquered its corruption. For shamans seeking mastery over the elements, communing with water demands a deep understanding of balance, life, and preservation. In the trials of the Call of Water, shamans are directed to confront corruption seeped into natural springs—even journeying across the sea to blighted lands like Silverpine Forest. The Shard of Water is granted upon purifying these corrupted waters. Returning this crystal token to Islen Waterseer on the rocky shores of the Barrens proves the initiate's worth, providing the final key needed to forge their Water Totem.

Shari Stilwell. Shari Stilwell is a Forsaken paladin trainer stationed in the settlement of Brill within Tirisfal Glades. Bearing a surname shared with notable figures in the Eastern Kingdoms, she instructs Forsaken who take up the mantle of holy warriors. Her presence marks a rare and unconventional discipline among the undead under the Banshee Queen. Found among the blight-touched buildings of Brill, Shari Stilwell stands out as a mentor to Forsaken holy warriors. While the holy Light is excruciating to the undead, Shari guides fledgling Forsaken who endure that agonizing path. She aids newcomers seeking their footing in Tirisfal Glades through their early training and adjustments, offering guidance to those looking to secure a place within the Forsaken kingdom.

Sharing the Land. Assigned by Baine Bloodhoof in Bloodhoof Village, this task sends young Horde adventurers to curb the destructive poaching of the local Palemane gnolls. By culling their tanners, skinners, and poachers, you protect Mulgore's wildlife and learn the tauren philosophy of living in balance with the Earth Mother. The tauren hold deep reverence for the natural world, taking from it only what is necessary to survive and honoring the Earth Mother in all things. The Palemane gnolls, having settled south of Bloodhoof Village and in a cavern to the west, harbor no such respect. Rather than hunting in moderation, they aggressively butcher wildlife across the plains, leaving stripped carcasses and upset ecosystems in their wake. For a people striving to build a peaceful homeland in Mulgore, this reckless slaughter cannot be tolerated.

Sharptalon's Claw. Sharptalon's Claw is a trophy quest representing the defeat of the ferocious hippogryph Sharptalon in Ashenvale. Taking the creature's severed talon back to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post proves your skill and protects Horde supply lines through the ancient forest. As the Horde attempts to carve out resources in Ashenvale, the native fauna proves just as perilous as the night elven sentinels. Sharptalon, a notoriously aggressive hippogryph, haunted the canopies and paths winding toward Splintertree Post. The beast preyed upon vulnerable peons and couriers traveling between the forward logging camps and the outpost, severely hampering Horde operations in the region.

Shatter Scar Vale. Shatter Scar Vale is a scorched basin in central Felwood, located just north of Bloodvenom Falls. It marks the ground zero where demonic infernals crashed into northern Kalimdor during the Third War. Today, the craters still burn with fel fire and host lingering remnants of the Burning Legion. During the Third War, the Burning Legion rained living siege engines down upon northern Kalimdor. Shatter Scar Vale bore the brunt of this celestial assault. Demonic infernals plummeted from the skies, tearing through the ancient canopy and smashing deep craters into the earth. The violent impact shattered the terrain, leaving blackened hollows that smolder with unholy fire to this day. Though the Legion was shattered at Mount Hyjal, the infernals and lingering lesser demons never truly dispersed, maintaining an entrenched foothold in the scarred earth.

Shattered Strand. The Shattered Strand is a wild, rugged coastline flanking the northern rim of the Bay of Storms in Azshara. Dominated by crashing surf and crumbling ancient ruins, the beach crawls with hazardous marine beasts and tribal aquatic creatures. Stretching along the northern edge of the Bay of Storms, the Shattered Strand is far from a peaceful shoreline. The rocky beaches and tidal shallows are heavily inhabited by aggressive wildlife, including towering sea giants, multi-headed hydras, and snapping makrura, alongside encampments of coastal murlocs. Crumbling elven architecture overlooks the waves, anchored by landmarks such as the ancient Temple of Arkkoran and the solitary Tower of Eldara. For travelers navigating Azshara's treacherous cliffs, descending to this isolated strip of coast means confronting some of the region's deadliest amphibious threats.

Shaw's Report. In Westfall, Shaw's Report carries confidential intelligence from SI:7 to Gryan Stoutmantle. Written by Master Mathias Shaw, it describes the Stonemasons Guild, Edwin VanCleef, and their grievance with the crown after Stormwind was rebuilt.

Shelene Rhobart. Shelene Rhobart is a Forsaken leatherworking trainer stationed along the road in Tirisfal Glades. Operating out of a Deathguard waystation, she supplies cured hides and leathercraft training to support the Forsaken's military and logistical efforts across the blighted lands. Shelene Rhobart plies her trade at a Deathguard waystation, an outpost situated southeast of Brill along the main road toward the ruins of Lordaeron. Even in undeath, practical crafts remain essential for survival and war. Shelene works with animal pelts collected from the prowling beasts of Tirisfal, refining tough hides into armor, straps, and field gear to supply local Forsaken patrols contending with both the Scourge and Scarlet crusaders.

Shenthul. Shenthul is a jungle troll rogue trainer based in the shadowy subterranean reaches of the Cleft of Shadow in Orgrimmar. As an operative of the Shattered Hand, he orchestrates espionage operations across Kalimdor and initiates rising rogues into the guild's covert ranks. Tucked away inside the murky depths of the Cleft of Shadow, Shenthul serves as one of the Horde's foremost rogue mentors. While the warriors and shamans above march openly across the red dust of Durotar, Shenthul trains those who prefer stealth, ambush, and subterfuge. Under his tutelage, initiates master essential fieldcraft and lethal arts, learning to operate within the unforgiving politics and harsh wilderness of Kalimdor.

Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds. 'Shhh! We're Hunting Kobolds' is a quest that leads adventurers out of Northshire Valley to track wandering kobolds into Elwynn Forest. Using a tracking kit, players discover the trail leads toward the infested Fargodeep Mine and report the findings to Marshal Dughan in Goldshire. As the kobold infestation in Northshire Valley escalates, signs indicate that the vermin are organizing beyond the isolated abbey grounds. Equipped with a tracking kit, scouts are dispatched to follow the trail of the creatures to determine where they are concentrating their efforts. This reconnaissance serves as a crucial bridge between Northshire's local troubles and the broader defense of Elwynn Forest.

Shifting Mire. The Shifting Mire forms the vast, muddy heart of the Swamp of Sorrows, lying just west of the Pool of Tears. Its name comes from the strange, restless silt beneath the murky water, which seems to drift and gather under the influence of an unseen force. Spanning the central reaches of the marshland, the Shifting Mire is an unsettling expanse where solid footing is hard to come by. The silt along the swamp floor shifts and collects as though moved by a living will, driven by a strange, ambient energy permeating the peat. Amidst the drifting mud prowl predatory swamp jaguars, massive sorrow spinners, and hungry sawtooth crocolisks, while bands of broken draenei known as the Lost Ones stalk the sunken paths.

Shimmer Ridge. Shimmer Ridge is a rugged highland nestled in northern Dun Morogh, directly west of the Gates of Ironforge. Occupied by hostile Frostmane trolls, the rocky heights consist of two camps joined by a rickety bridge and are renowned as the sole harvesting ground for potent shimmerweed. Perched along the craggy slopes just west of Ironforge's mighty entryway, Shimmer Ridge serves as an active redoubt for the Frostmane troll tribe. Divided into twin camps straddling a chasm and linked by a wooden span, the enclave is heavily guarded by troll scavengers and their tamed mountain boars. Their proximity to the main roadway and the dwarven capital poses a continuous nuisance to travelers and mountain patrols, who must constantly remain on guard against opportunistic raids from the high ground.

Shimmer Stout. Following the creation of his experimental Shimmer Stout in Brewnall Village, Rejold Barleybrew asks travelers to carry a fresh barrel out to his brother Wellart. Wellart serves as a dwarf Mountaineer stationed at the southern guard tower guarding the pass toward Loch Modan, where a cold post makes a strong drink all the more welcome. Rejold Barleybrew has perfected his new creation, Shimmer Stout, using shimmering fronds gathered from the icy crags of Dun Morogh. While the rest of the Barleybrew family dedicates their craft to the vats and kegs of Brewnall Village, Rejold's brother Wellart chose the life of a Mountaineer. Knowing the lonely conditions of guard duty on the frontier, Rejold sends a fresh barrel along with passing travelers as both a brotherly favor and a true taste test.

Shimmering Flats. The Shimmering Flats is an expansive salt flat lying at the southeastern tip of Thousand Needles, bordering the desert of Tanaris. Once the bed of an ancient lake, this sun-baked expanse is now famous for the high-speed mechanical rivalries of the Mirage Raceway and a harsh population of desert beasts. Stretching out under the blinding southern sun, the Shimmering Flats is a vast dried lakebed devoid of vegetation, dotted with the sun-bleached bones of turtles and even the wooden wreck of an ancient sailing vessel. Its sheer, unbroken level surface makes it the premier testing ground on Kalimdor for experimental vehicles. At the center of the flats lies the Mirage Raceway, where gnome and goblin tinkerers constantly clash to see whose rocket cars, gyrocopters, and engines can achieve the highest speeds—often resulting in fiery crashes and smoking craters across the white crust.

Shimmering Frond. A Shimmering Frond is a specimen harvested from a strange, glowing plant growing within the Oracle Glade of Teldrassil. Its unusual luminescence and twisting aura reveal it to be an exotic species entirely alien to the boughs of the World Tree. While wandering the verdant canopies around the Oracle Glade, travelers may come across strange vegetation boasting a pulsing, radiant aura. The fronds plucked from this plant catch the filtered woodland light in unnatural ways, shimmering with vibrant vitality. Denalan, a botanist tending to his planters by Lake Al'Ameth, recognizes the foliage immediately as a species native to the distant Swamp of Sorrows in the Eastern Kingdoms. How seeds from a marsh so far across the Great Sea managed to take root and flourish upon the newly raised Teldrassil remains an intriguing mystery, prompting Denalan to sprout and study specimens in his own soil.

Shimmerweed. Shimmerweed is a distinct herb cultivated by the Frostmane trolls on Shimmer Ridge in the snowy heights of Dun Morogh. While the trolls harvest it for their own tribal rituals, local dwarven brewers covet its sharp, unique flavor for experimental ales. High above the lowlands of Dun Morogh, the Frostmane trolls tend patches of shimmerweed along the icy crags of Shimmer Ridge. The trolls harvest and store the plant in woven baskets scattered throughout their camps, relying on it to fuel their sacred and enigmatic rituals. Outside of troll society, few mountaineers pay the weed much mind, though its potent properties have drawn the gaze of inventive outsiders.

Shindrell Swiftfire. Shindrell Swiftfire is a night elf sentinel and scout stationed in Astranaar, the heart of night elf operations in Ashenvale. Keenly aware of shifting perils along Kalimdor's western reaches, she directs capable Alliance adventurers toward gathering threats on the coastline and nearby mountain passes. Her duties make her an essential hub for coordinating local defense against emerging oceanic and wild menaces. From Astranaar's winding walkways, Shindrell Swiftfire serves as an alert observer of Ashenvale's broader frontiers. While the forest's Sentinels are constantly pressured by the Horde's logging incursions from the east and south, Shindrell keeps her eyes fixed on dangers that lie beyond the immediate woodland front. She acts as a vital liaison for travelers arriving from Darkshore or heading out toward the jagged ridges of Stonetalon, ensuring no sudden menace strikes Astranaar undefended from the flank.

Shindrell's Note. Shindrell's Note is a written missive detailing recent observations of corruption around Astranaar and the Ashenvale coastline. Penned by the night elf Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire, it serves as an intelligence report dispatched east across the forest to the druid Kayneth Stillwind. As unrest spreads throughout Ashenvale, night elf sentinels and druids coordinate to monitor the woodland's borders. Penned by Sentinel Shindrell Swiftfire in Astranaar, this report details troubling disturbances spotted along the western coast and through the central canopies. It is addressed to Kayneth Stillwind, a druid stationed at the shrine of Forest Song within the Nightsong Woods to the east. By dispatching couriers with her firsthand observations, Shindrell aids Kayneth's investigation into the subtle corruption creeping through the sacred groves.

Shining Strand. The Shining Strand is the strip of shoreline hugging Lordamere Lake along eastern Silverpine Forest, stretching south from the Ruins of Lordaeron toward the rugged foothills of Alterac. Its shallows are home to settlements of aggressive Vile Fin murlocs, making the lakeshore dangerous ground for unseasoned travelers. Running along the eastern edge of Silverpine Forest, the Shining Strand borders the misty waters of Lordamere Lake. The Vile Fin tribe of murlocs has established several aggressive settlements along these shallows, posing a deadly hazard to anyone attempting to travel the lake road, while feral worgen roam the deep woods of Silverpine behind the shore.

Ship Schedules. A scroll records ships sailing between Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, with marks beside some voyages. It belongs in the hands of an authority at Steamwheedle Port. The scroll lists the shipments that sail between Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, those already made and those to come, along with the ships' names. Some journeys are marked with a large X, and others carry notes about plunder to be had or a hard fight. It is meant for someone in authority at Steamwheedle Port.

Shipment of Boots. A crate of footwear dispatched from Booty Bay by the merchant Drizzlik, intended for Gazlowe's trade network in Ratchet. It was intercepted off the coast by Southsea Freebooters and stashed away in their encampment south of the port. Running a goblin trade port requires endless supplies, and Gazlowe arranged for a fresh delivery of boots from Drizzlik, a purveyor of apparel based out of Booty Bay. The consignment never reached Ratchet's docks. Southsea Freebooters prowling the Merchant Coast ambushed the transport vessel, carrying the crates off to their beach encampments south of the harbor. The pirates scattered the stolen freight throughout their tents and shanties, leaving Gazlowe without his expected wares until adventurous mercenaries could be hired to scour the shoreline.

Shipment of Iron. A crate of raw metal stored at the human smithy in Hillsbrad Fields. It serves as vital stock for local armament production, making it a priority target for Forsaken forces seeking to cut off the supply lines arming the Hillsbrad townsfolk. In the ongoing struggle across the Hillsbrad Foothills, the human peasantry has mounted surprisingly stiff resistance against Tarren Mill. Much of this fighting capability stems directly from the smithy at the southwestern edge of the Hillsbrad Fields, where Blacksmith Verringtan and his apprentices work round the clock churning out weapons and armor from heavy shipments of iron. To break the farmers' resolve, Forsaken commanders ordered the forge extinguished, its smiths eliminated, and its stockpiled metal seized for the Horde war effort.

Shipment to Stormwind. William Pestle sends a parcel from Goldshire to his brother Morgan in Stormwind. Its candles carry wax supplies from Elwynn Forest to Pestle's Apothecary in the Trade District. William gathers herbs, reagents, and raw goods in Goldshire, while his brother Morgan runs Pestle's Apothecary in Stormwind's Trade District. William cannot easily leave his post at the Lion's Pride Inn, so he depends on travelers heading into the city to carry goods for him.

Shipping Label. The Shipping Label is a recovered freight marker attached to a supply crate owned by the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Directing couriers to their trade hub at the Three Corners crossroads in Redridge Mountains, it introduces travelers to the organization's network of independent haulers. Found pasted to a stocked supply crate, this damaged shipping label marks cargo belonging to the Azeroth Commerce Authority. Although the intended destination and recipient have been torn away, clear instructions direct anyone who discovers the freight to return it or report to the authority's trade outpost in the Redridge Mountains. Beside the formal text, a rudimentary map sketches out the roads leading toward the Three Corners intersection.

Shipping Schedule. At Jerod's Landing, the Defias Brotherhood moves contraband along Elwynn's waterways. Its dockmaster guards a schedule that maps shipments between Redridge and Westfall, and SI:7 wants it. South of Goldshire, Jerod's Landing sits on the Elwynn bank of the Nazferiti River. The Defias Brotherhood seized the landing as a hub for river traffic. From there, they move contraband between Redridge and Westfall along waterways beyond the Stormwind Guard's notice. Their dockmaster keeps the Shipping Schedule close, recording these shipments.

Shoni the Shilent. Shoni the Shilent is an industrious gnome engineer stationed in Stormwind City's bustling Dwarven District. As commander of the Gnomeregan underground assault crew, she directs Alliance adventurers into the Deadmines to salvage the power supply of a goblin shredder, fuel for the machines she hopes will break a path back into Gnomeregan. Operating out of the smoky workshops of the Dwarven District, Shoni represents gnomish strategic ingenuity far from the lost halls of Gnomeregan. Her engineering plans are ambitious. With Gnomeregan in the hands of the troggs, Shoni is organizing an underground assault to retake it, and she sends operatives into the subterranean tunnels beneath Westfall for the parts her crew needs.

Show of Force. Show of Force is an Alliance defensive task in the Redridge Mountains issued by Deputy Feldon. Tasked with halting encroaching gnoll packs near Lakeshire, adventurers are sent to hunt gnoll thrashers and collect their spiked collars to deter further incursions into human settlements. The Redridge Mountains have long sheltered wild tribes of gnolls, but they have grown increasingly audacious. Rather than remaining isolated high in the craggy hills, gnoll raiding packs have set up camps disturbingly close to Lakeshire and the outlying human homesteads. With Stormwind's military stretched thin and unable to spare reinforcements for rural borderlands, local authorities must rely on passing adventurers to secure the perimeter before these encroaching bands gather the nerve to strike the town itself.

Shredding Machines. Shredding Machines is a Horde quest tasking adventurers with hunting down two specialized Venture Company logging mechs in Windshear Crag. Directed by the shaman Seereth Stonebreak, players strike against the mechanical deforestation that torments Stonetalon's native spirits. Stationed along the dusty border between the Barrens and the Stonetalon Mountains, the orc shaman Seereth Stonebreak listens closely to the unseen realm. While much of Stonetalon's spiritual voice is drowned out by chaos, one vision came to her with harrowing clarity: man-shaped contraptions tearing through ancient woods with unnatural haste. Marked with the mechanical designations XT:4 and XT:9, these goblin-engineered shredders butcher the timberlands of Windshear Crag, sending waves of distress through the surrounding nature spirits.

Shrewd Negotiations. Magus Wordeen Voidglare praises your infiltration of the mages' city, and says the time has come to be more negotiatory. You are to carry the arcane mote you acquired to Archmage Celindra in Dalaran. Magus Wordeen Voidglare admits that no place on Azeroth rivals the Kirin Tor for knowledge of the arcane, and that even Wordeen's own brilliant work pales beside their ancient wisdom. He thinks it high time the Horde was granted access to their exclusive order. You are to carry the mote you acquired to Archmage Celindra in Dalaran, for Wordeen is sure the Kirin Tor will give anything to get it back.

Shrine of Aessina. The Shrine of Aessina is a sacred elven landmark nestled in the forests of southwestern Ashenvale, dedicated to the ancient forest spirit of nature and wild creatures. Located between Maestra's Post and Astranaar, it stands as a serene sanctuary amidst the growing border friction in the region. Tucked away west of Astranaar, the Shrine of Aessina honors the mysterious Wild God who embodies the heart and spirit of the deep forests. For generations, night elves and their woodland kin have revered this quiet place, communing with nature away from the bustling main roads. However, with the Horde pushing into Ashenvale to gather timber and establish footholds, sacred grounds throughout the territory face an uncertain peace.

Shrine of the Dormant Flame. Perched atop the highest peak northwest of the Valley of Trials, the Shrine of the Dormant Flame is a secluded sanctuary revered by Horde shaman. Guided by its solitary keeper, Telf Joolam, initiates make the treacherous climb to commune with the element of fire and prove their spiritual mastery. Reaching the Shrine of the Dormant Flame requires braving a narrow, winding trail that begins along the Southfury River at the southwestern edge of the Southfury Watershed. High above the red cliffs of Durotar, the mountain summit offers a commanding view of the surrounding lands, though a single misstep along the precipice means certain death. In this quiet refuge wanders Telf Joolam, a solitary hermit tasked with overseeing sacred rites. For aspiring orc and troll shaman undertaking the ritual Call of Fire, the shrine's brazier serves as the crucible where they must ignite slumbering coals using the ember of a vanquished elemental, proving their power to commune with and respect the destructive spirits of flame.

Shrine of the Fallen Warrior. Perched upon a secluded ridge west of the Crossroads lies the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior, a quiet memorial overlooking the sweeping red savannahs of the Barrens. Marked by a stone plinth bearing the initials 'MK' and the body of a fallen orc warrior, it is watched over by the gentle presence of a Spirit Healer named Koiter. Tucked away high upon the hills northwest of the Crossroads, the Shrine of the Fallen Warrior stands as an unusually solemn haven amidst the dust and peril of the Barrens. To find it, travelers must scale a winding ridge pathway southwest of the summit until they reach a gentle mound. Upon the summit rests a carved stone monument, its plinth carved with the initials 'MK'. Before it lies the armored form of an orc warrior at rest, watched over day and night by a named Spirit Healer known as Koiter. There are no battle horns here, only quiet contemplation honoring a champion who walked Kalimdor's lands.

Sida. Sida is a dwarven resident of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Known for her estranged marriage to Einar Stonegrip, she spends her days in the port town while dealing with personal misadventures out in the surrounding marshes. Sida resides in the bustling Alliance port of Menethil Harbor, living apart from her husband, Einar Stonegrip. Their relationship is strained enough that Einar flatly refuses to travel to Menethil so long as Sida remains in town. Despite keeping to the coastal settlement, Sida occasionally ventures out into the dangers of the Wetlands, having recently suffered the misfortune of losing her personal bag during an expedition out toward Ironbeard's Tomb.

Sida's Bag. Sida's Bag is the personal satchel of Sida, a resident of Menethil Harbor. Swallowed whole by a creeping ooze during her excursion to Ironbeard's Tomb, the bag and its mysterious contents require a thorough hunt through the acidic slimes of the Wetlands to recover. While paying her regular weekly visit to Ironbeard's Tomb near Dun Modr, Sida found herself ambushed by the dreadful, dripping oozes that infest the area. Panicking in the face of the encroaching sludge, she flung her personal satchel directly at one of the creatures. Rather than driving the beast off, the ooze simply absorbed the bag into its gelatinous body. The distraction bought Sida enough precious moments to flee with her life back to the safety of Menethil Harbor, leaving her possessions trapped inside an unknown slime.

Sigil of Arathor. Following the Sigil of Thoradin, Zengu tells you the human prince entrusted another sigil to Lieutenant Valorcall, who commands the cavalry. Find him, and bring the sigil back to Zengu in Hammerfall. Zengu scoffs that the humans can scarcely call Stromgarde their own, never mind the whole of the Arathi Highlands, yet their prince keeps the last of his horsemen riding about the countryside. Zengu cannot understand why. More important is that one of the sigils rests with Lieutenant Valorcall, who leads those riders. Zengu wants him found and the sigil brought back to Hammerfall.

Sigil of Strom. Zengu in Hammerfall wants the sigils that guard Trol'kalar, the sword of Lord Ignaeus Trollbane. The first, the Sigil of Strom, was taken by the Syndicate, and a Syndicate agent in Stromgarde is likely to hold it. In ancient times the trolls fought the Arathorian Empire, and their ablest foe was Lord Ignaeus of Strom, called Trollbane. He went into battle wielding Trol'kalar, a name that means troll slayer in the trolls' old tongue. Now Trollbane's sons are weakened and their stronghold lies in ruins.

Sigil of Thoradin. Tor'gan's reconstruction of the broken sigil worked flawlessly. The restored Sigil of Thoradin can now open the seal on Trollbane's tomb, and he tells you to return it to Zengu in Hammerfall. Tor'gan says the reconstruction worked flawlessly, and the Sigil of Thoradin is now able to open the seal on Trollbane's tomb. Take it back to Zengu in Hammerfall, who no doubt has more for you to do.

Sigil of Trollbane. Following the Sigil of Arathor, Zengu sends you to slay Prince Galen Trollbane and take the last sigil, the one that unlocks his father Thoras Trollbane's tomb. The prince keeps it on his own person, far inside Stromgarde. The last sigil that can open the tomb of Thoras Trollbane is kept by Thoras's son, Prince Galen, in person. He is to be found far inside Stromgarde, in a chapel within the districts the militia holds. Zengu warns that Galen is well guarded and a fine fighter, so this could prove very hard. You are to kill him and carry the sigil to Zengu in Hammerfall.

Signed Recruitment Letter. The Signed Recruitment Letter is an official dispatch issued by Kargal Battlescar at the Far Watch Post. Bearing Kargal's mark, it transfers new recruits deeper into the arid interior of the Barrens to report for duty at the Crossroads. Standing as the eastern threshold of the Barrens, the Far Watch Post evaluates newcomers crossing over the Southfury River from Durotar. Once a conscript proves their readiness to Kargal Battlescar, he stamps and signs this letter of introduction. It serves as military orders directing recruits west down the road to the Crossroads, where Sergra Darkthorn coordinates logistical operations and territorial defense across the dry plains.

Silithid Egg (The Barrens). Silithid Eggs are the developing brood of the insectoid creatures nesting in the southern Barrens. Found buried within earth mounds around the Field of Giants, these clutches are gathered by Horde researchers seeking to uncover the origins and intelligence of the encroaching swarm. In the arid basin of the Field of Giants, bizarre insect-like beings have begun churning the earth into towering mounds. Deep within these nests lie their eggs, buried beneath hardened soil and watched over by territorial broods. The Horde knows remarkably little about the silithid, but scouts stationed at the Crossroads have noted signs of coordinated behavior and uncanny intellect far exceeding ordinary wild beasts. Gathering unhatched eggs offers scholars in Orgrimmar their best chance to study the lifecycle and nature of this emerging menace.

name.frFR: Clé de la tour de Silixiz

text.enUS: Silixiz's Tower Key. Silixiz's Tower Key is a small key carried by Foreman Silixiz outside the Venture Company tower near the Sludge Fen. Horde operatives belonging to the Shattered Hand are tasked with lifting it directly from the foreman's pockets as part of an undercover sabotage assignment. The Venture Company operation north of the Sludge Fen runs under tight security, centered on an isolated lookout tower supervised by Grand Foreman Puzik Gallywix. Outside the compound patrolled by goblin mercenaries, Foreman Silixiz carries the tower key that the Shattered Hand operative is instructed to steal and keep. For the rogue network of the Shattered Hand operating out of Orgrimmar, obtaining this key is not a matter of blunt force; field operatives must slip into the compound undetected and pick the foreman's pockets cleanly, proving their mastery of stealth before climbing into the toxic upper levels.
