Silky Sutures. Silky Sutures is a Horde quest in the Arathi Highlands offered by Doctor Gregory Victor in the outpost of Hammerfall. Frustrated by unrepaired siege damage and dwindling medical supplies, the camp's resident physician recruits adventurers to gather venomous highland spider silk for use as emergency field sutures. The task highlights the desperate, resource-starved conditions facing the defenders of Hammerfall as they struggle to keep their guards and laborers on their feet. Hammerfall endures in the rugged Arathi Highlands, but the encampment shows visible signs of prolonged strain. Unrepaired siege damage marks the perimeter, leading the local physician, Doctor Gregory Victor, to bitterly observe that neglect seems to be official policy. Despite the crumbling fortifications and lack of broader support, Victor refuses to let the decay claim his infirmary. Maintaining a working clinic is essential for keeping the laborers and sentinel guards upright and ready for conflict.

Silver Dawning's Lockbox. The Silver Dawning's Lockbox is a sturdy chest resting within the sunken wreckage of the vessel Silver Dawning off the coast of Darkshore. It holds the personal effects and ship log of the vessel's fallen captain, lost during an ambush by coastal murlocs. The ship Silver Dawning was en route across the sea toward the port of Auberdine when disaster struck. Coastal murlocs swarmed the vessel, driving it down into the dark surf north of the harbor. The captain perished in the assault, leaving the wreckage submerged beneath the waves as a grim monument claimed by the creatures. Inside the flooded hull remains the captain's personal lockbox, holding the ship's log and private belongings. Recovering these effects offers a final measure of peace to the surviving crew members ashore.

Silver Stream Mine. Silver Stream Mine is a depleted dwarf mine located in northern Loch Modan, nestled between Algaz Station and the Stonewrought Dam. Once a rich silver vein for the kingdom of Ironforge, the excavated hollow was repurposed as a Miners' League supply depot before being overrun by vermin. Today, Tunnel Rat kobolds squat inside the tunnels, hoarding stolen equipment and rare mineral curiosities. Silver Stream Mine once flowed with precious ore, contributing heavily to the silver reserves of Ironforge. In time, the dwarf pickaxes dug deep enough to exhaust the primary veins, turning the sprawling chambers into an empty subterranean complex. Rather than abandon the hard-won earthworks, the Miners' League transformed the shafts into a secure storage depot for tools, mining crates, and regional equipment. It also serves as the only known source of rare Charged Rift Gems, which draw inquisitive arcanists searching for delicate tailoring reagents.

Silvervein the Elder. Silvervein the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit who appears during the Lunar Festival atop the hills overlooking Thelsamar in Loch Modan. Travelers pay their respects to him to honor the ancient ties among Azeroth's elder peoples. In return for acknowledging his presence and heritage, he bestows his ancestral blessing. Perched on the rolling ridges above Thelsamar, Elder Silvervein stands as a quiet guardian and reminder of antiquity. As a figure honored during the Lunar Festival, he represents the enduring memories of bygone eras. Even as the surrounding lands of Loch Modan grapple with trogg invasions and local disputes, Silvervein watches peacefully from his overlook.

Silverwind Refuge. Silverwind Refuge is a serene night elven settlement nestled in south-central Ashenvale, situated just north of Mystral Lake. Protected by Sentinels, it offers a welcoming haven for travelers along the forest's wooded trails. Resting between the placid waters of Mystral Lake and Iris Lake to the north, Silverwind Refuge stands as one of the major night elven waystations in central Ashenvale alongside Astranaar. It boasts craftsmen and wilderness trainers who instruct travelers in herbalism, alchemy, skinning, and hunting. Guarded by stalwart Sentinels, the retreat serves as a peaceful rest stop for allies moving through the shaded ancient woods.

Silverwing Grove. Tucked away in south-central Ashenvale near Fallen Sky Lake, Silverwing Grove serves as the staging grounds for the Silverwing Sentinels. From this fortified hollow, night elf warriors muster Alliance forces to push back the Warsong Clan loggers tearing through the forest. Hidden beneath the emerald canopy southwest of Silverwing Outpost, Silverwing Grove is a crucial military staging post for the Silverwing Sentinels. Rather than a tranquil woodland retreat, it functions as the operational heartbeat for the night elves' bitter territorial contest against the Horde's lumber operations in Warsong Gulch. High-ranking Alliance officers, provisions, and scouts gather here, organizing skirmishes and marshaling champions to defend ancient Ashenvale against orcish expansion.

Silverwing Outpost. Silverwing Outpost is a fortified night elf garrison positioned in south-central Ashenvale, east of the Falfarren River. Commanded by Duriel Moonfire, it stands as the easternmost bastion of the Alliance against the Horde in the contested woodland. Situated southwest of Splintertree Post and just north of the border with the Barrens, Silverwing Outpost holds an inherently perilous strategic position. By sitting on the eastern side of the Falfarren River—territory heavily contested and patrolled by the Horde—the outpost serves as a direct shield for night elf holdings deeper in the forest. Duriel Moonfire and her Silverwing Sentinels remain under constant siege from nearby orcs determined to purge night elf forces from the area entirely.

Silvery Spinnerets. Silvery Spinnerets are harvested from the great spider Lady Sathrah in northern Teldrassil. Once used to weave webs that captured healing evening dew for the Temple of the Moon, they are sought by the Priestesses of Elune to honor the fallen creature's soul through a sacred ritual of rebirth. Lady Sathrah was once counted among the favored creatures of Elune, renowned for spinning shimmering webs through the moonlight near Wellspring Lake. Her silver silk gathered the evening mist, forming healing dews prized by the Sisterhood of Elune in Darnassus. Unfortunately, the corruption creeping through the boughs of Teldrassil did not spare her. Falling into violent madness, Sathrah became a danger to her own brood and the surrounding forest. Priestess A'moora asks travelers to end the spider's suffering and recover her spinnerets as an act of mercy, bringing closure to a revered resident of the great boughs.

Simple Letter. The Simple Letter is an introductory directive that guides novice warriors to trainer Llane Beshere at Northshire Abbey. It marks the beginning of their formal martial instruction and urges them to assist the troubled citizens of the valley. The Simple Letter serves as an initial introduction for aspiring warriors arriving in Northshire Valley. Directed to Llane Beshere, the resident warrior trainer at Northshire Abbey, the letter prompts newly arrived fighters to make contact with their instructor, familiarize themselves with their surroundings, and prepare for the demands of martial life.

Simple Memorandum. The Simple Memorandum is an official notice delivered to novice gnome warriors training in Coldridge Valley. A terse gnomish directive, it instructs fledglings to report to the warrior trainer Thran Khorman in Anvilmar to prepare for the war to take back Gnomeregan. Novice adventurers in Coldridge Valley frequently find themselves entrusted with letters of introduction as they demonstrate their mettle against the local wildlife and trogg threats. For young gnome fighters, this memorandum serves as a formal order to report to Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer within Anvilmar. Dwarven veterans recognize that while gnomes may rely on intellect and contraptions, retaking Gnomeregan will demand pure physical resolve and martial discipline. The memorandum directs the bearer to put aside preliminary tasks and seek personalized instruction in the art of war.

Simple Memorandum. The Simple Memorandum is a missive delivered to aspiring gnome warriors starting out in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm outside, it directs newly trained fighters into Anvilmar to meet Thran Khorman, who has pledged to prepare them for reclaiming Gnomeregan. While clearing out the troggs and boars troubling Coldridge Valley for mountaineer Sten Stoutarm, a young gnome warrior receives a brief message slipped into the dwarf's hands. Recognizing the potential in the refugee recruit, veteran trainer Thran Khorman uses the memorandum to call the newcomer into Anvilmar's central hall to begin proper martial instruction.

Simple Rune. A Simple Rune is an inscribed stone token passed to fledgling dwarven warriors training in Coldridge Valley. It serves as a summons from the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, directing recruits to seek instruction inside Anvilmar. Carved with basic martial marks, the Simple Rune is handed to promising recruits who have begun clearing out the threats around Coldridge Valley. Rather than a magical charm, it acts as a formal calling stone from Thran Khorman, the resident warrior trainer at Anvilmar. Upon reading its inscribed guidance, a young fighter is expected to report directly to Thran to learn basic combat techniques and hear practical advice on surviving Dun Morogh's hostile wilds.

Simple Rune. Simple Rune is an introductory task given to novice dwarven warriors in Coldridge Valley. Passed along by Sten Stoutarm on behalf of the warrior trainer Thran Khorman, it directs fresh recruits inside Anvilmar to begin their martial training. As young recruits clear pests and prove their grit around Coldridge Valley, veteran scouts keep a watchful eye out for promising fighters. Sten Stoutarm delivers an inscribed stone—a simple rune—handed off to him by Thran Khorman. This summons calls martial hopefuls from the snowy valley paths into the warm forge-hall of Anvilmar to formally pledge themselves to the warrior's trade.

Simple Sigil. A Simple Sigil is a modest training token presented to novice night elf warriors in Shadowglen. Carried as a summons from the warrior trainer Alyissia, it marks a young fighter's formal introduction into the martial defense of Teldrassil. Within the sheltered boughs of Shadowglen, young night elves are guided by Conservator Ilthalaine to find their calling. For fledgling warriors, Ilthalaine delivers a Simple Sigil sent by a runner from the warrior trainer Alyissia. Bearing an inscription that directs the recruit to report for instruction, this token represents the start of disciplined martial training amidst troubling times for the World Tree.

Simple Sigil. The Simple Sigil is an introductory summons directed to aspiring night elf warriors in Shadowglen. Delivered by Conservator Ilthalaine on behalf of the trainer Alyissia, it formally marks the recruit's transition into combat training to protect the fledgling boughs of Teldrassil. After proving their basic survival skills against the restless wildlife of Shadowglen, young night elf warriors receive an inscribed sigil passed through Conservator Ilthalaine. The token is a formal request from Alyissia, the local warrior trainer stationed at Aldrassil, bidding the novice to step forward and dedicate their martial strength to defending their people.

Simple Tablet. The Simple Tablet is a written missive handed to novice troll warriors arriving in the Valley of Trials. Delivered by Gornek, it directs the fledgling combatant to present themselves to Frang, the local warrior trainer. Within the harsh red bounds of the Valley of Trials, new recruits are quickly set to work. For young trolls seeking the path of the warrior, Gornek passes along this simple slate or parchment. Written by the troll Tar'sere and addressed to Frang, the master-at-arms resting near the Den, it serves as an official introduction to martial training in Durotar. It urges the recruit to step forward, present themselves, and prove their willingness to swing weapons under the banner of the Horde.

Simple Tablet. Simple Tablet is an introductory rite of passage for fledgling warriors entering the Valley of Trials. Delivered into your hands after proving your mettle against local beasts, it directs you toward Frang, the local veteran tasked with honing raw brawn into martial discipline. After proving you can hold your own against the Mottled Boars of the valley, Gornek hands over a parchment specifically marked for you. In the harsh environment of Durotar, the Horde does not leave its fighters without guidance for long. The tablet serves as an invitation to seek out Frang, the warrior trainer stationed outside the Den.

Singed Scale. Singed Scales are the charred, shock-hardened plates harvested from the electrified thunder lizards of Durotar. Procuring them serves as a rite of passage for young Horde warriors striving to master defensive battle arts. To the veterans of the Horde, a true warrior is not measured solely by the blood drawn by their axe, but by the blows they can absorb to shield their allies. In the arid canyon of Thunder Ridge in western Durotar, lightning hides and thunder lizards crackle with volatile storm energies. Hunting these beasts requires a warrior to endure relentless electrical shocks and crushing physical strikes. The blackened, scorched scales torn from their hides offer undeniable proof of a fighter's ability to weather punishing assaults and stand firm where lesser soldiers would fall.

Singing Blue Shards. Crank Fizzlebub seeks an enterprising adventurer to gather Singing Crystal Shards from the basilisks of Stranglethorn Vale. Competition with the Venture Company prevents him from harvesting the mineral deposits directly, leaving basilisk hides as the next best option. He promises a cut of the profits to anyone willing to bring him ten decent specimens. Crank Fizzlebub has identified an eager market for the Singing Crystals unique to Stranglethorn Vale. Unfortunately for his business ambitions, the aggressive presence of the Venture Company makes it hard for him to gather raw crystal in the field. To circumvent his rivals, Fizzlebub turns to an alternative method: basilisks consume the crystals, incorporating the mineral into their hardened hides, which allows usable shards to be retrieved from them instead.

Sirra Von'Indi. Sirra Von'Indi is the resident historian of Darkshire, stationed within the town hall amid stacks of forgotten records. Versed in ancient languages and local history, he assists the township in deciphering mysterious documents and uncovering the dark past of Duskwood. Sirra Von'Indi serves as Darkshire's foremost scholar, keeping watch over the settlement's archives from inside the Darkshire Town Hall. While the town guard focuses on the immediate threats lurking in the woods, Sirra turns his attention to the written word, translating cryptic texts and preserving the fading history of Grand Hamlet before the shadow fell across the region.

Sishir Canyon. Sishir Canyon is a rugged gorge in the Stonetalon Mountains, carving an eastward path through the craggy heights. Thickly swarmed by monstrous Deepmoss spiders and choked in webbing, it serves as the dangerous approach to the Ruins of Eldre'thar. Travelers who brave its tangled depths must contend with venomous arachnids and their brooding matriarch. Branching off the mountain roads of the Stonetalon range, Sishir Canyon is a treacherous natural corridor cutting toward the ancient Ruins of Eldre'thar. Rather than a quiet mountain trail, the gorge has been thoroughly overrun by Deepmoss spiders. Their sticky silken sheets and clusters of egg sacs smother the stony ground and rock walls, transforming the ravine into a living nest. Travelers and sentinels seeking the night elven ruins beyond must cut their way through swarms of aggressive webspinners.

Sister Aquinne. Sister Aquinne is an acolyte of Elune residing within the serene Temple Gardens of Darnassus. A novice priestess, she is studying under the Priesthood of Elune at the Temple of the Moon. Sister Aquinne has dedicated herself to the Priesthood of Elune in the night elf capital. Stationed in the tranquil Temple Gardens beneath the shadow of the Temple of the Moon, she continues her studies under the guidance of the High Priestess and elder sisters. When a once-great creature of the forest was in need of help, it was Aquinne who sent willing travelers to Priestess A'moora inside the temple to learn what had to be done.

Skeleton Finger. A severed, bony digit scavenged from the walking dead prowling the cursed groves and cemeteries of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire collects these macabre remnants alongside ghoul fangs and spider venom to craft protective talismans. The cursed woods of Duskwood are overrun by the restless remains of the dead, ranging from skeletal raiders and warriors to necrotic mages and fiends. While ordinary travelers avoid touching the foul remains of the risen dead, fortune tellers and mystics value their cold essence. Madame Eva, the resident seer of Darkshire, gathers these bony fingers to bind their lingering necrotic energies into a ward of retaliatory magic known as the Totem of Infliction.

Skin of Sweet Rum. A Skin of Sweet Rum is a specialized liquor sourced from the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. It is sought after by Barkeep Daniels in Lakeshire, who is desperate to keep his tavern stocked while Blackrock orcs cut off Redridge from regular trade routes. In the war-weary town of Lakeshire, tavern supplies are running dangerously low. The Blackrock orc invasion has choked the supply roads leading into the Redridge Mountains, leaving Barkeep Daniels scrambling to quench the thirst of beleaguered town guards and refugees. To restock his depleted shelves, Daniels sends travelers across the kingdom to gather regional specialties, including a waterskin filled with the distinctive sweet rum brewed and served in Goldshire's Lion's Pride Inn.

name.esES: Escaramuza en la Mina del Eco

text.enUS: Skirmish at Echo Ridge. In Northshire Valley, recruits strike at kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Marshal McBride ordered the attack after scouts found the mine overrun. Marshal McBride sends recruits against the kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine. Scouts found the mine overrun, and the garrison fears the creatures will strengthen their hold if left alone. The kobolds dig through the tunnels, gather stolen resources, and multiply. Recruits must thin their numbers to protect Northshire Valley, with its farms and spiritual retreat.

Skittering Blood. Skittering Blood is an alchemical reagent harvested from the arachnids dwelling within the Skittering Dark of Silverpine Forest. It serves as a vital toxic ingredient for the Royal Apothecary Society's research into a New Plague designed to eradicate both Scourge and humanity. Harvested from Skitterweb lurkers, strikers, and their broodmother Krethis the Shadowspinner, this venomous hemolymph possesses virulent properties prized by Forsaken alchemists. Apothecary Renferrel discovered that when refined alongside toxins extracted from grizzled bear hearts, the blood forms the base of an exceptionally lethal elixir. The compounds within the fluid demonstrate severe contaminating agents, making it an ideal biological catalyst for the Apothecarium's chemical experiments.

Skittering Dark. The Skittering Dark is an abandoned mine and shadowy woodland hollow in western Silverpine Forest. Infested by aggressive giant spiders, the cavern and its surrounding woods are thick with webbing and danger for unwary beasts and travelers. Tucked into the hills just east of the western coast of North Tide's Run, the Skittering Dark was once a working mine. Today, the shafts are completely choked with cobwebs, serving as the sprawling nest of giant spiders. With the shadowy weaver Krethis haunting the exterior, the spiders hunt anything that strays too close.

Skorn Whitecloud. Skorn Whitecloud is an aging tauren hunter residing at Bloodhoof Village in the rolling plains of Mulgore. He guides young hunters in understanding their relationship with the land's predators and aids travelers who cross paths with Mulgore's lurking dangers. Living at Bloodhoof Village in Mulgore, Skorn Whitecloud is an old hunter who now serves as an instructor in the ways of the hunt. His primary role is instilling respect for the wild creatures of the plains. He tests aspiring hunters by sending them after the claws of Mulgore's cunning flatland prowlers, to be shown to Melor Stonehoof in Thunder Bluff, ensuring that those who take up the bow or spear understand the balance between predator and prey.

Skuerto. Skuerto is a dwarven scout stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Sent there by Archmage Malin alongside Apprentice Kryten, he aids the Alliance in the field, helping secure magical relics on Malin's behalf. Skuerto, a dwarf of Ironforge, works as a scout in the dangerous Arathi Highlands. Stationed alongside Apprentice Kryten at Refuge Pointe, he works under the direction of Archmage Malin to recover arcane reagents and potent magical artifacts that once belonged to Malin's old master, Archmage Trelane.

Skulk Rock Clean-up. Fraggar Thundermantle of Aerie Peak wants a clean-up crew for the area around Skulk Rock, which the Horde abandoned and which is now overrun with sludges and oozes. The Wildhammers have plans for the area once it is clear. The Wildhammers remember the past, more than their brothers in Ironforge do, and Fraggar Thundermantle says friends are made here by getting your hands dirty. The Horde abandoned their positions around Skulk Rock in the Hinterlands, and nasty sludges and oozes have since overrun them. The Wildhammers have plans for that ground, but first it needs a hole made in the infestation.

Skull Rock. Assigned by the hermit Margoz, this task directs Horde adventurers into the cavern of Skull Rock just east of Orgrimmar. The cave has been overrun by the Burning Blade cult, who use painful demonic devices to bind themselves to dark magic. Securing these cursed artifacts allows Margoz to study the cult's presence right on the capital's doorstep. Skull Rock is a forbidding cave nestled in the craggy hills of northeastern Durotar. While seemingly isolated, it sits distressingly close to the mighty gates of Orgrimmar. Rather than housing wild beasts or mere outlaws, the caverns harbor a cell of the Burning Blade—the shadowy demonic cult that has long plagued orcish society. Within these dim tunnels, cultists conduct unholy rituals under the nose of the Warchief's scouts.

Skull Rock. Skull Rock is a cavern tucked into the eastern coastal cliffs of Durotar, just east of Orgrimmar. It serves as a fortified coven for the demonic Burning Blade cult right under the capital's nose. Hidden beneath the crags of northeastern Durotar, Skull Rock is one of the most perilous strongholds of the Burning Blade cult in the region. Dark cultists, fel-worshipping orcs, and summoners gather deep within the winding tunnels to practice demonic arts and weave conspiracies against the nascent Horde. The cell is led by the dangerous warlock Gazz'uz, whose operations pose an imminent threat to the nearby gates of Orgrimmar and travelers traversing the eastern shoreline.

Skullsplitter Tusks. Kebok in Booty Bay needs materials to meet export demands for tiger fangs destined for the South Seas. Because hunting genuine jungle predators proves too costly, he has devised an undetectable forging process using tusks harvested from the Skullsplitter trolls. Supplying tiger fangs to distant island buyers across the South Seas has grown too expensive and difficult through ordinary hunting. Rather than abandon the trade, Kebok devised an undetectable forging method that turns mundane horn-like objects into convincing replicas. The closest physical match for these fangs comes directly from the jaws of the local Skullsplitter trolls, leading Kebok to hire adventurers willing to strip eighteen tusks from the jungle tribe to fill his upcoming export shipment.

Skychaser the Elder. During the Lunar Festival, Skychaser the Elder appears atop Sentinel Tower in Westfall. Travelers climb to honor her and receive her blessing in return. Sentinel Hill holds against Defias raiders and roving scavengers in Westfall's troubled scrublands. During the Lunar Festival, an ancestral spirit named Elder Skychaser appears on the open platform atop Sentinel Tower. From above the dust and wind, she watches over the weary soldiers and beleaguered settlers below. Anyone may climb the tower and pay her respect.

Skyseer the Elder. Skyseer the Elder is an honored ancestral spirit residing atop Freewind Post during the Lunar Festival. Travelers seek out his presence high above Thousand Needles to pay their respects to the ancestors and receive his ancient blessing. Perched upon the lofty wooden bluffs of Freewind Post, Elder Skyseer appears bathed in a radiant pillar of celestial light. Positioned near the bridges leading toward the massive mechanical lifts, his ghostly presence offers a quiet sanctuary amid the windswept mesas of Thousand Needles.

Skywall. Skywall is the vast, storm-swept domain of the air elementals within the Elemental Plane. Banished here by the titans in ancient days, the creatures of wind, cloud, and lightning dwell under the reign of Al'Akir the Windlord. When the titans overthrew the Old Gods eons ago, they crafted the Elemental Plane as a secure dimensional prison to contain Azeroth's unruly elemental spirits. The lords of the elements fought fiercely amongst themselves, ultimately carving out distinct dominions. The realm of wind and storm became known as Skywall, ruled by Al'Akir the Windlord. While sealed away from the surface world, its tempests continue to swirl in eternal isolation.

Slag Pit. The Slag Pit is an extensive subterranean mining excavation nestled inside the Cauldron of Searing Gorge. Overseen by ruthless Dark Iron taskmasters and slavers, these fiery tunnels are driven by forced labor under the shadow of Blackrock Mountain. Trespassers must contend not only with hostile dwarf overseers, but also ravenous incendosaurs prowling the lower levels. Carved into the depths of the Cauldron, the Slag Pit represents the grinding industrial engine of the Dark Iron dwarves in Searing Gorge. Day and night, enslaved workers are driven to extract rich ores and minerals under the lash of brutal overseers and taskmasters. The environment is harsh and suffocating, dominated by scorching heat, choking dust, and the clatter of iron picks. The Dark Irons maintain ruthless discipline over their excavation, violently repelling any outside interference with their supply lines to Blackrock Depths.

Slake That Thirst. Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan can supply the 4711-FTZ power source for your kit, but first wants something to drink: five Wastewander Water Pouches, to be had from the Wastewander nomads east of town. After Into the Field, you know the kit needs a power source, and Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan can help. The price is a drink: five Wastewander Water Pouches. Bilgewhizzle points you to the Wastewander nomads east of Gadgetzan, suggests you simply walk up to one and ask, and wants to hear how that works out.

Slaughter Hollow. Slaughter Hollow is a secluded ogre mound tucked away in the snowy heights of the Alterac Mountains. Controlled by the brutish Crushridge clan, it stands as a rough camp rather than a bustling settlement. Travelers rarely have reason to trespass unless hunting ogres or exploring the frozen mountain passes. Hidden high in the peaks bordering Hillsbrad and Alterac, Slaughter Hollow serves as an encampment for the local Crushridge ogres. Like many ogre mounds scattered across the highlands, it is littered with makeshift bonfires, discarded bones, and crude shelters. While other ogre dens in the mountains see frequent conflicts over territory or stolen supplies, Slaughter Hollow remains largely quiet and bypassed by major military campaigns.

Slaughtered Lamb. Tucked away in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, the Slaughtered Lamb appears to be nothing more than a quiet, seedy tavern. Beneath its floorboards, however, sprawling catacombs hide the sanctum and training grounds of the Alliance's illicit warlocks. On the surface, the Slaughtered Lamb offers little more than dark corners and sparse patronage, attended by barkeep Jarel Moor, who warns casual visitors to stay away from the shadows. That warning is literal. Descending through the back passages reveals a subterranean complex of crypts and summoning circles, where human warlocks and transfer practitioners from Khaz Modan openly study fel arcana sheltered from the disapproving eyes of the Church of the Holy Light and the Kirin Tor.

Slaying the Beast. Neeru Fireblade, an orc warlock residing in Orgrimmar's Cleft of Shadow, directs Horde adventurers deep into Ragefire Chasm to hunt Taragaman the Hungerer. Claiming to act on orders from Warchief Thrall, Neeru demands the towering felguard's heart as proof of the demonic cult's downfall. Beneath the red earthen streets of Orgrimmar sits Ragefire Chasm, a fiery subterranean fissure infested with troggs, beasts, and the covert agents of the Searing Blade. In the Cleft of Shadow above, Neeru Fireblade presents himself as a loyal servant tasked by Thrall with cleansing this demonic rot. He points directly toward Taragaman the Hungerer, a massive felguard stationed in the heart of the cavern, naming the demon as the mastermind behind the underground cult.

Sleepers' Key. The Sleepers' Key is one of three enchanted keys crafted by night elf druids to seal their sacred vault within the Talon Den atop Stonetalon Peak. Kept safe inside a hidden cache opened with the Gatekeeper's Key, it is one of the three keys needed to open the druids' hoard. Carved into the heights of Stonetalon Peak, the Talon Den serves as a redoubt and sanctum for the druids of Kalimdor. Aware that their sacred relics and potent treasures might draw unwanted attention, the night elf keepers devised an intricate system of locks and hidden caches to protect their hoard. The Sleepers' Key is one third of that protective ward. Placed within a secluded cache in the den's depths, it can only be retrieved using the Gatekeeper's Key hidden near the threshold. Alongside the Claw Key and the Barrow Key, the Sleepers' Key must be set into the stone locks of the Talon Den Hoard to disperse the ward and reveal the ancient items held within.

Slimy Menace. Slimy Menace addresses a growing murloc infestation along the shores of Crystal Lake in Elwynn Forest. These aggressive creatures threaten to deplete the lake's fish supply and endanger nearby locals, requiring swift action to keep their numbers in check. Along the eastern shore of Crystal Lake, an aggressive enclave of murlocs has established a foothold. These savage, semi-aquatic creatures possess sharp teeth and fierce tempers, turning a once-peaceful body of water into a dangerous feeding ground. Local residents rely heavily on the lake for their daily livelihoods, but the murloc presence now threatens anyone daring to fish or approach the water's edge.

Slither Rock. Slither Rock is a secluded cave tucked into the far northeastern cliffs of the Burning Steppes, past the perilous Terror Wing Path. It serves as the solitary refuge of Cyrus Therepentous, a sharp-tongued black dragonspawn with his own hidden agenda. Tucked away in the scorched crags beyond the Terror Wing Path, Slither Rock is easy to overlook amid the fiery wastes of the Burning Steppes. Far from the roaring forges and marching orc warbands of Blackrock Spire, this remote hollow houses the solitary black dragonspawn Cyrus Therepentous. While dragonspawn are typically fiercely loyal soldiers of the Black Dragonflight, Cyrus maintains a strange, cantankerous independence here, willing to converse with mortal travelers rather than slaughtering them on sight—though never without a steady stream of insults.

Slithering Scar. The Slithering Scar is a sprawling silithid hive dominating the southern cliffs of Un'Goro Crater. Home to the aggressive Gorishi swarm, its excavated tunnels and organic spires represent a dangerous insectoid encroachment into the primeval basin. Gouged into the red earth and rock of southern Un'Goro, the Slithering Scar stands as an alien intrusion against the lush prehistoric landscape. The hive is controlled by the Gorishi silithid, an organized strain of insectoids that have honeycombed the cliffs with damp burrows and egg chambers. Within these subterranean warrens, workers and tunnelers nurture vast clutches of eggs and grubs alongside towering wasp broods. More alarmingly, the colony cultivates fledgling silithid colossi, monstrous behemoths intended to carve an uncontested path through the crater's ecology. Strange crystalline formations nestled within the hive pulse with unnatural resonance, acting as focal points for the colony's dark, coordinated will.

Sludge Fen. Sludge Fen is a toxic industrial oil field operated by the Venture Company in the northeastern Barrens. Once a pristine, crystal-blue pool, the wetland was transformed into an oily quagmire after the goblins erected drilling platforms and machinery. The operation is overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle and attracts constant industrial espionage and sabotage from rivals in Ratchet. Before the arrival of the Venture Company, Sludge Fen was an untainted pool of crystal-clear water fed by natural springs in the arid Barrens. Driven by the relentless pursuit of profit, the Venture Company constructed an extensive oil-drilling operation over the basin, despoiling the wetland into a sludge-filled reservoir coated in heavy industrial waste. Overseen by Supervisor Lugwizzle, goblin drillers, engineers, and overseers pump crude oil around the clock, heedless of the environmental ruin. The waters are now thick with runoff and toxic byproducts, leaving the native aquatic life choked beneath the grease.

Smart Drinks. Smart Drinks is an entrepreneurial scheme cooked up by the goblin merchant Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. Having failed to brew an intellect-enhancing tonic out of Sunscale raptor horns, Mebok now tasks adventurers with delving into the Wailing Caverns to harvest ectoplasmic residue for his latest beverage formula. Operating out of the bustling port town of Ratchet, Mebok Mizzyrix embodies the classic goblin philosophy of turning any bizarre regional phenomenon into cold, hard coin. Convinced that an intellect-boosting draught will make him an overnight tycoon, he originally believed powdered raptor horns held the secret. When that batch proved thoroughly underwhelming, he simply set his sights on an even more dubious ingredient: the corrupting essence seeping out of the nearby Wailing Caverns.

Smith Argus. Smith Argus is the resident blacksmith and trainer stationed in the heart of Goldshire in Elwynn Forest. From his open-air forge near the Lion's Pride Inn, he repairs traveler gear, teaches novice smiths their fundamentals, and coordinates with craftsmen across southern Azeroth. His network ties Goldshire's local trade directly to logistical hubs like Stormwind and distant frontiers like Redridge. Situated just outside the Lion's Pride Inn, Smith Argus maintains one of the busiest anvils in Elwynn Forest. While Goldshire faces growing perils from nearby gnolls, kobolds, and Defias bandits, Argus keeps local militia and passing adventurers properly equipped. In addition to mending dented armor and forging sturdy implements, he serves as a blacksmithing trainer, initiating fledgling craftsmen into the fundamentals of working copper and bronze.

Smith Mathiel. Smith Mathiel is a pivotal warrior quest in Darnassus marking the transition from raw materials to forged arms. Having secured sacred elunite ore from a shipwreck off Auberdine, an aspiring warrior delivers the ore to the master blacksmith Mathiel. He agrees to work the blessed metal into a weapon fit for defending the Kaldorei. After recovering elunite ore from the haunted shipwreck off Auberdine and securing it with the aid of the warrior trainer Elanaria, young night elf warriors are sent across the Warrior's Terrace of Darnassus. Elanaria carefully packs the ore into a sturdy case, instructing the novice to seek out Mathiel, one of the premier smiths in the capital, to fashion a weapon worthy of their martial calling.

Smoky Iron Ingot. Smoky Iron Ingots are roughly processed metal bars smelted by the kobolds of the Windshear dig sites in the Stonetalon Mountains. Orcish armorers prize these ingots as raw material for forging sturdy mail gear fit for Horde warriors. Within the soot-stained tunnels of the Windshear Crag in the Stonetalon Mountains, kobolds excavate deep into the rocky earth, pulling unrefined ore from the slopes and smelting it over crude, smoking fires. The resulting Smoky Iron Ingots are far from pristine—thick with residue and charcoal—yet dense enough to retain substantial tensile strength.

Smoldering Embers. Smoldering Embers are the glowing, heat-baked remnants retrieved from the raging fire elementals of the Charred Vale. Night elf Sentinels track these cinders as physical proof that the fiery terrors overrunning the devastated woodland are being subdued. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting and industrial devastation tore through the Charred Vale, setting the forest ablaze and unleashing destructive fury from deep within the earth. In their wake, elementals of living fire—Burning Ravagers, Burning Destroyers, and wandering Rogue Flame Spirits—surged across the scorched basin. These Smoldering Embers are the lingering, ash-covered cores left behind when an elemental is extinguished, serving as proof that the rampant fires of the vale are being systematically suppressed.

Snapjaws, Mon!. In the Hinterlands, Katoom the Angler of Revantusk Village can barely keep a line in the water because saltwater snapjaws keep wrecking it and stealing his bait. He wants fifteen of the turtles dead. Katoom urges you not to be taken in by the snapjaws' large eyes and calls the turtles a menace. By his account, he cannot fish for even five minutes before one of them tears his line and makes off with his bait. He asks you, as a favor to himself and to his neighbours in the village, to wipe out the whole lot; the count is fifteen.

Snatch and Grab. Master Mathias Shaw sends agents to Jerod's Landing for shipping intelligence. The Defias Brotherhood uses the river dock to move supplies in secret. Master Mathias Shaw tests aspiring operatives who seek a place in Stormwind's covert intelligence wing. He asks for finesse and stealth, not brute force. SI:7 agents take down key figures quietly and recover important papers without drawing the realm into open scandal. Each new operative must prove they can work unseen.

Sneed. Sneed is the Defias Brotherhood's goblin lumbermaster stationed deep within the Deadmines. Operating from the lumber chamber known as the Mast Room, he pilots a heavy shredder of his own design to process timber for Edwin VanCleef's secret juggernaut. While the Defias Brotherhood draws its core membership from disenfranchised human stonemasons and common laborers, building an ironclad warship requires specialist trades. Edwin VanCleef recruited Sneed specifically for his engineering know-how and ruthless goblin efficiency. Stationed in the Mast Room along the subterranean rail network, Sneed oversees the rapid felling, cutting, and shaping of timber needed to frame VanCleef's colossal dreadnaught.

Sneed's Shredder. Sneed's Shredder is an imposing mechanised lumber harvester stationed deep within the Deadmines. Piloted by the goblin taskmaster Sneed, this deadly machine acts as both heavy industrial machinery for Edwin VanCleef's shipwrights and a terrifying perimeter defender. Within the goblin-dominated foundry of the Deadmines, mechanical shredders serve a dual purpose: processing vast amounts of timber and lumber required for Edwin VanCleef's hidden juggernaut, and serving as armored shock engines against intruders. Sneed, the overseer of the lumber works, operates this modified mechanical beast directly, turning an oversized buzzsaw into an instrument of defense.

Snellig's Snuffbox. Snellig's Snuffbox is a personal keepsake recovered from the restless undead First Mate Snellig among the wreckage of the Lost Fleet. Bringing this trinket back to First Mate Fitzsimmons in Menethil Harbor serves as proof that his cursed former crewmate has finally been put to rest. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras ran aground along the northern shores of the Wetlands, its sailors and officers did not find peaceful deaths. Bound by a mysterious and dark power tied to a hidden treasure aboard the ships, the drowned crew rose again as tortured spirits and skeletal undead. Among them was First Mate Snellig, who still haunts the rotting hold of the wreck closest to the coastline. Even in death, he clung to his snuffbox—a small, mundane reminder of his mortal life at sea. For the sole living survivor of the disaster, First Mate Fitzsimmons, recovering this small possession provides tangible proof that at least one of his lost shipmates has been released from an eternity of torment.

Snufflenose Command Stick. The Snufflenose Command Stick is a training rod provided by the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It is used to direct trained snufflenose gophers to locate and unearth valuable blueleaf tubers buried deep within Razorfen Kraul. Blueleaf tubers are coveted delicacies across Azeroth, but finding them is nearly impossible without specialized help. Buried in the thorny underground depths of Razorfen Kraul, the roots are entirely hidden from sight. To exploit this lucrative market without braving the quilboar dens himself, the Ratchet merchant Mebok Mizzyrix conditioned keen-scented snufflenose gophers to dig up the tubers. The Snufflenose Command Stick is the tool adventurers use to direct these trained critters, prodding them to sniff out and expose root nodes from up to fifty paces away.

Snufflenose Owner's Manual. The Snufflenose Owner's Manual is an instructional booklet from Marwig Rustbolt of Snuff Inc., kept beside the goblin entrepreneur Mebok Mizzyrix in Ratchet. It outlines how to deploy and direct a trained Snufflenose Gopher to locate rare Blueleaf Tubers buried in Razorfen Kraul. Written by Marwig Rustbolt, owner of Snuff Inc., this short guide details how to work with the company's trained snufflenose gophers. These beasts possess a keen sense of smell capable of detecting subterranean Blueleaf Tubers from fifty paces away. The manual instructs prospectors to release a gopher using a ventilated crate and guide its rooting instincts with a command stick, directing the creature through the hostile thorns and quilboar tunnels of Razorfen Kraul to secure the prized culinary delicacies.

Sodium Nitrate. Sodium Nitrate is a volatile chemical reagent carried by the dwarven excavators and garrison stationed at Bael Modan in the southern Barrens. Though imported by the Ironforge expedition to blast through ancient stone, the exiled tauren Gann Stonespire seeks to reclaim it to assemble an explosive charge against the invaders. The Bael'dun expedition tore into the ancestral lands of the Stonespire tribe armed with heavy earthmovers and blasting reagents. To crack open the stubborn rockbeds of the southern Barrens, the dwarves relied on volatile chemical compounds. Sodium Nitrate forms a crucial stabilizing and oxidizing agent in high-grade explosives, carried routinely by Bael'dun riflemen, soldiers, and officers inside the excavation works and nearby fortress.

Soft Saber Pelts. Soft Saber Pelts represents a trade agreement aimed at keeping wilderness roads secure from predatory cats. Hunters bring in the thick furs of local sabers so they can be crafted into warm, protective blankets and shawls. Traversing the untamed paths of Azeroth requires constant vigilance against prowling predators. Large sabers frequently roam near well-traveled thoroughfares, presenting a persistent hazard to couriers, merchants, and lone adventurers. While local inhabitants admire the grace and majesty of these great cats, allowing their numbers to swell unchecked along trade routes invites deadly ambushes. Gathering hunters to keep the local roads safe serves as a necessary measure for communal survival.

Solliden Farmstead. Solliden Farmstead is an active human pumpkin farm nestled in western Tirisfal Glades, just north of Deathknell. It represents a rare anomaly in northern Lordaeron: living native farmers who survived the Plague of Undeath and cling fiercely to their soil under the shadow of the Scarlet Crusade. While most of Lordaeron fell to ruin and rot, the fields of Solliden Farmstead still produce healthy crops. Today, these surviving human farmers live under the watchful shield of the Scarlet Crusade patrolling from a nearby tower. Traumatized and insular, they defend their homestead with unyielding hostility, striking at any outsiders who draw near—Horde and Alliance alike.

Solm Hargrin. Solm Hargrin is the rogue trainer stationed within Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A pragmatic dwarf who values honor amongst thieves, he instructs novice dwarven and gnomish scoundrels in the art of subterfuge. He firmly believes that covert operatives will prove vital as geopolitical tensions simmer across Azeroth. Tucked away in the dwarven stronghold of Anvilmar, Solm Hargrin watches the snowy passes of Coldridge Valley with a keen, calculating eye. While Ironforge relies heavily on the brute strength of its mountaineers and warriors, Hargrin understands that some threats require a quieter, sharper touch. He welcomes budding rogues of both dwarven and gnomish heritage, deciphering coded missives for them and drilling them in essential techniques like Eviscerate. Above all, Hargrin champions a creed of professional loyalty and honor among thieves, preparing his pupils for an increasingly volatile world where subtle knives often shape the fate of nations.

Solomon's Law. Solomon's Law is a local decree issued through Bailiff Conacher in the Lakeshire Town Hall. It condemns the Shadowhide gnolls of Redridge to death for colluding with Morganth, an enemy of Stormwind. Adventurers are tasked with enforcing the town's harsh frontier justice by bringing back pendants taken from the gnolls. Lakeshire stands largely isolated from Stormwind's immediate military support, forcing Magistrate Solomon and his town officials to govern Redridge with strict frontier authority. Operating out of the town hall, Bailiff Conacher serves as the arm of the local magistrate court. When external threats menace the township, the court has little recourse other than putting bounties on offenders' heads, relying on freelance mercenaries and traveling defenders to uphold the kingdom's statutes.

name.esES: Petición a Villa Oscura de Solomon
name.frFR: Demande d'aide de Salomon à Sombre-comté
name.ptBR: Apelo de Salomão a Vila Sombria
name.zhCN: 所罗门写给夜色镇的求救信

text.enUS: Solomon's Plea to Darkshire. Solomon's Plea to Darkshire is an urgent missive penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire addressed to Lord Ello Ebonlocke. In the face of mounting Blackrock orc and gnoll threats, the letter begs the leadership of Darkshire to send their elite militia, the Night Watch, to bolster Lakeshire's strained defenses. Lakeshire stands on the brink of being overwhelmed by invading Blackrock orcs, gnolls, and murlocs, with virtually no official reinforcements arriving from Stormwind. In desperation, Magistrate Solomon drafted this formal plea to Mayor Ello Ebonlocke of Darkshire, petitioning him to dispatch members of the Night Watch northward into Redridge. The document reflects the severe breakdown of central military support across southern Azeroth, forcing individual human settlements to look to one another for mutual survival.

name.frFR: Demande d'aide de Salomon à la marche de l'Ouest
name.itIT: Appello di Solomon alle Marche Occidentali
name.ptBR: Apelo de Salomão a Cerro Oeste
name.zhCN: 所罗门写给西部荒野的求救信

text.enUS: Solomon's Plea to Westfall. Solomon's Plea to Westfall is an urgent written appeal penned by Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire. Desperate for reinforcements against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Solomon sends this dispatch to Gryan Stoutmantle in Westfall hoping the newly formed People's Militia can lend aid while Stormwind's royal army fails to respond. As the threat of the Blackrock clan and hostile gnolls looms large over Redridge, Magistrate Solomon finds himself dangerously isolated in Lakeshire. The royal army from Stormwind has inexplicably failed to arrive in force to defend the region's borders. Unable to wait for official support from the kingdom's capital, Solomon pens this plea in a desperate bid to recruit assistance from outside the regular military structure. Having caught word of a volunteer defense force coalescing across Elwynn to the west, he turns directly to the People's Militia.

Some Assembly Required. In Booty Bay, Drizzlik reports that the boots are taking shape, but the skins you supplied will not cover the inner layers. Drizzlik proposes filling them out with cheaper, thicker hides from crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti. Drizzlik has settled the rough form of the boots and says they are coming along nicely, yet the skins from Supply and Demand do not go far enough for the insides. Nobody will ever see those layers, so Drizzlik will make do with thicker, cheaper hides from the crocolisks near Lake Nazferiti.

Songblade Search. Songblade Search is a dwarven errand in which Dorin Songblade asks travelers to check on his brother Daewyn in the Wetlands. Daewyn set off with an archaeological crew from Loch Modan to dig in unexplored hills, but his uncharacteristic silence left his brother fearing the worst. Dorin Songblade remained behind at his workshop, inundated with orders to refit girdles, while his brother Daewyn joined a dwarven excavation crew setting out from Loch Modan. Daewyn ventured north into the rugged hills of the Wetlands, eager to explore virgin ground untouched by dwarven pickaxes. However, Daewyn customarily sends letters immediately after arriving, and his silence left Dorin deeply unsettled.

Soothing Spices. "Swamp Eye" Jarl loves cooking, swamp style, and needs soothing spice for a stew. Jarl in Dustwallow Marsh asks you to bring three Soothing Spices. "Swamp Eye" Jarl is fond of cooking in the swamp manner, with fried green frog legs among the dishes. A stew is planned, and for it Jarl needs soothing spice. Whoever brings it will be given a share. Jarl wants three Soothing Spices, and wonders whether you like stew.

Soothing Turtle Bisque. Chef Jessen of Southshore prides himself on preparing the finest cuisine north of Stormwind, but recent unrest has cut off his supply of fresh snapjaw turtle meat. To restore his famous Soothing Turtle Bisque to the tavern menu, he asks culinary-minded travelers to brave the dangerous northern waters near Dalaran and Lake Lordamere. Southshore remains one of the Alliance's last intact coastal towns in Lordaeron, clinging proudly to civilian life amidst mounting regional strife. Chef Jessen claims that his cooking rivals any tavern north of Stormwind, with patrons supposedly trekking from as far as Darkshire in Duskwood just for a taste of his specialty: Soothing Turtle Bisque. The rich, restorative soup depends entirely on fresh meat from the snapjaw turtles indigenous to the rivers and lakes of the northern mountains.

Soothing Turtle Bisque. Soothing Turtle Bisque is a culinary task offered by Christoph Jeffcoat in Tarren Mill. The Forsaken cook aims to disprove the notion that the undead lack culinary talent by preparing a hearty broth from local snapjaw meat. Players must hunt freshwater turtles around the waterways of Hillsbrad Foothills and the shores of Lordamere Lake to master his prized recipe. It is widely assumed that the Forsaken have entirely abandoned the comforts of life, including the art of fine dining. Christoph Jeffcoat, stationed in Tarren Mill, vigorously rejects that assumption. Boasting that his rich, soothing turtle bisque is good enough to tempt souls back from beyond the grave, Jeffcoat seeks to prove that undead hands are capable of delicate, heartwarming craft even in a land tainted by plague and war.

Soran'ruk Fragment. A Soran'ruk Fragment is a shattered shard of a demonic prison orb once bound to the spirit of a disgraced servant of the Burning Legion. Though split and dispersed among cultists deep beneath Ashenvale, each shard still radiates residual fel energy. When demons of the Burning Legion fall out of favor with their masters, their spirits are sometimes condemned to imprisonment inside specialized orbs and distributed to fel spellcasters as conduits of raw power. The orb of Soran'ruk met this fate, yet somewhere in its history, it was cracked apart. One half was broken into smaller shards and fell into the hands of the Twilight's Hammer cultists lurking within the submerged ruins of Blackfathom Deeps, who draw upon the lingering demonic essence for their own dark workings.

Sorrow Hill. Sorrow Hill is an expansive graveyard resting south of Andorhal in the Western Plaguelands. Once the final resting place for commoners, soldiers, and nobility alike, it has been corrupted by nearby plague cauldrons into a sprawling haven of restless undead. Before the Third War, Sorrow Hill served as the primary burial ground for the city of Andorhal and its surrounding townships. When the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath, the gravediggers could not keep pace with the dead. Neatly kept crypts were soon surrounded by shallow, poorly marked earthen pits. Eventually, terrified survivors ceased traditional burials entirely, instead resorting to burning the corpses of their loved ones in a mass pyre to the south out of fear they would rise. Before the town fell completely, the remnants of the populace entombed Lord Uther the Lightbringer atop the cemetery's high ground, bestowing upon the hill its tragic name.

Sorrowmurk. The Sorrowmurk is the treacherous wetland expanse lying directly east of the Pool of Tears in the Swamp of Sorrows. Long dominated by patrolling green dragonkin guarding the approach to the Sunken Temple, it remains one of the most perilous regions in the eastern marshes. Stretching out along the eastern edge of the Pool of Tears, the Sorrowmurk is a dense and murky mire that borders the Forbidding Sea. For years, the waters and tangled boughs have crawled with ferocious green dragonspawn and towering drakes, remnants of the brood sent to watch over the submerged temple of Atal'Hakkar. Their presence ensures that only seasoned travelers dare wander through its sodden reaches.

name.ptBR: Posto de Guarda do Portão Sul

text.enUS: South Gate Outpost. South Gate Outpost is a fortified dwarven mountain post situated along the South Gate Pass between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Manning the snowy southern road, its mountaineers guard the steady flow of travelers walking between Ironforge's frigid heights and the temperate valley of the Loch. Perched midway through the high mountain cut of South Gate Pass, South Gate Outpost marks the frontier between the snowy slopes of Dun Morogh and the verdant basin of Loch Modan. Stationed here are Ironforge mountaineers tasked with patrolling the rocky switchbacks and keeping dangerous wildlife off the main highway. Compared to their hard-pressed kin up at North Gate Outpost, the defenders here have largely secured their stretch of road, allowing travelers, pilgrims, and trade wagons headed toward Thelsamar to journey in relative safety.

South Gate Pass. South Gate Pass is the primary mountain thoroughfare linking the snowy heights of Dun Morogh with the valley basin of Loch Modan. Flanked by dwarven tunnels and watch posts, it serves as the most direct route between Ironforge and the settlement of Thelsamar. Carved straight through the Khaz Modan range, South Gate Pass connects Dun Morogh's high mountains to the rolling valley of Loch Modan to the east. Travelers leaving the cold slopes behind emerge through stone archways into the warmer dwarven heartlands. Because the path leads straight toward Thelsamar, it carries a steady flow of mountaineers, couriers, and newly trained adventurers setting out from the capital.

South Seas. The South Seas encompass the vast, sun-drenched waters separating the southern regions of Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Lapping at the shores of Tanaris and Stranglethorn Vale, these tropical expanses are famed for lucrative trade routes, perilous reefs, and brazen pirate crews. Spanning southward beneath the Great Sea and the Maelstrom, the South Seas wash against the deserts of Tanaris and the lush jungles of Stranglethorn Vale. Since the Great Sundering shattered the primeval continent ten thousand years ago, this ocean has nurtured remote tropical islands, unique oceanic beasts, and independent merchant networks. Goblin shipping cartels, operating out of havens like Steamwheedle Port and Booty Bay, maintain tenuous shipping lanes across the waves. However, the waters remain notoriously lawless, crawling with corsairs, Bloodsail buccaneers, and predatory sea life that prey on any vessel daring to venture far from shore.

South Tide's Run. South Tide's Run is the lonely southwestern coastline of Silverpine Forest, stretching along the cold waters of the Great Sea. Flanking the forested interior, these damp sands and surf serve as the southern complement to North Tide's Run. Stretching along the southwestern edge of Silverpine Forest, South Tide's Run forms a desolate boundary between the woods and the Great Sea. Unlike the protected eastern roads that lead down toward the Greymane Wall, this open shore takes the brunt of the western tides, serving as a bleak coastal wilderness largely untouched by the settlements inland.

Southern Gold Road. The Southern Gold Road is the vital desert thoroughfare stretching through the southern half of the Barrens, linking the central plains to the Great Lift. It serves as an indispensable artery for regional trade, carrying caravans, supplies, and wayfarers traveling between distant reaches of Kalimdor. Officially beginning at the stone bridge dividing the northern and southern halves of the Barrens, the Southern Gold Road runs directly south until it meets the Great Lift leading down into the Thousand Needles. Like the northern portion simply named the Gold Road, this dusty highway derives its moniker from the endless stream of lucrative merchant caravans that trek along its length. Despite constant harassment from local quilboar tribes and predators prowling the savannah, it remains one of the busiest long-distance paths on the continent, ferrying goods between remote outposts and bustling ports.

Southern Savage Coast. The Southern Savage Coast encompasses the long strand of beaches and tidal waters hugging southwestern Stranglethorn Vale. Flanked by the treacherous depths of the South Seas, these shores are home to prowling wildlife, hostile naga, and the ever-present threat of coastal raiders. Stretching down the western edge of the southern jungle, the Southern Savage Coast marks where the mainland gives way to the warm currents of the South Seas. Divided from the northern Savage Coast by the submerged ruins and perils of the Vile Reef, this coastline skirts inlets near the Gurubashi Arena and Nek'mani Wellspring before tapering off past Booty Bay and Janeiro's Point. While the beaches offer open ground compared to the suffocating interior jungle, travelers must contend with aggressive reptilian predators, predatory naga hunting the shallows, and passing corsairs scanning the strand for easy prey.

Southfury River. The Southfury River is one of the most prominent waterways on central Kalimdor, carving a swift and wide path southward from the heights of Mount Hyjal. It forms the natural border separating Azshara from Ashenvale, as well as Durotar from the Barrens, before plunging into the Great Sea near Ratchet. Beginning high in Mount Hyjal, the Southfury drops over dramatic cascades before coursing through central Kalimdor. Its roaring waters serve as a clear geographic divide, separating the sacred forests of Ashenvale from ancient Azshara, and dividing the arid hills of Durotar from the savanna of the Barrens. Only a few strategic bridges dare cross its swift currents—most notably the heavy span guarding the rear gates of Orgrimmar and the crossing connecting Durotar to the Barrens. The river eventually empties into the Great Sea via a cascading waterfall just northeast of the neutral port of Ratchet.

Southmoon Ruins. The Southmoon Ruins are ancient stone remains situated in southern Tanaris, just north of the Valley of the Watchers. Long claimed by the brutish Dunemaul ogres, the crumbling stonework preserves remnants of the ancient troll civilization that dominated the desert before the sands swallowed it. Rising out of the blistering wastes of southern Tanaris, the Southmoon Ruins stand as a weathered testament to the ancient troll empires that once ruled Kalimdor's southern reaches. Like nearby Eastmoon and Noonshade, its stone pillars and altars have weathered thousands of years of wind and abrasive grit. The site has often served as a squalid camp for the Dunemaul ogres, who show little reverence for the craftsmanship of the past, using the ancient structures purely for shelter and territory.

name.frFR: Tour de la Pointe du Midi

text.enUS: Southpoint Tower. Southpoint Tower is a ruined Lordaeron scout tower situated at the western border of Hillsbrad Foothills, overlooking the road to Silverpine Forest. Once a human sentry post, the shattered structure is now utilized by Forsaken scouts keeping watch over Alliance movements in the region. Standing just south of the highway linking Silverpine Forest and Hillsbrad Foothills, Southpoint Tower was originally built by the Kingdom of Lordaeron to guard traffic moving between the eastern farmlands and the western woods. Following the Third War and the Scourge's destruction of the kingdom, the stonework fell into ruin. Today, it stands roofless and crumbling, an isolated relic of human dominion in a fractured territory.

Southridge Beach. Southridge Beach stretches along the southern shores of the Bay of Storms in central Azshara. Once a grand district of the ancient kaldorei city of Eldarath, its shattered ruins are now overrun by hostile naga, murlocs, and towering sea giants. Southridge Beach forms the southern boundary of the turbulent Bay of Storms. Thousands of years ago, this coast was part of the magnificent Highborne city of Eldarath, but the Great Sundering broke the land and plunged most of its palaces beneath the tides. Today, crumbling marble pillars and weathered stone pavilions dot the sand. Rather than scholars and noble courtiers, the strand is contested by aggressive Spitelash naga, prowling makrura, vicious hydras, and scavenging murloc tribes. Even massive sea giants occasionally wander ashore from the deeps.

name.esES: Los filibusteros de los Mares del Sur
name.frFR: Les flibustiers des mers du Sud
name.ptBR: Os Flibusteiros dos Mares do Sul

text.enUS: Southsea Freebooters. Southsea Freebooters is an introductory bounty task commissioned by Gazlowe in Ratchet to curtail local piracy. Infuriated by pirate raids on goblin trading vessels, the chief engineer hires adventurers to assault a Southsea pirate encampment along the Merchant Coast just south of town. Ratchet operates as the premier neutral trading port in central Kalimdor, built on the steady traffic of merchant vessels traveling between the eastern continents and Kalimdor. However, the Southsea Freebooters have established a fortified beach camp directly south along the Merchant Coast. From this staging ground, the buccaneers target incoming and outgoing goblin cargo ships, bleeding profits and destabilizing the local shipping lanes.

name.esES: Tesoro de los Mares del Sur

text.enUS: Southsea Treasure. The Southsea Treasure is a valuable hoard kept deep within the hold of the Southsea Freebooter vessel, the Tide Razor. Sought by Wrenix the Wretched in Ratchet, retrieving it tests the lockpicking and infiltration skills of fledgling thieves. Anchored along the Merchant Coast south of Ratchet, the pirate vessel Tide Razor serves as a forward base and training ground for the Southsea Freebooters. Stashed deep in its lowest hold lies a coveted stash of plunder known as the Southsea Treasure. Wrenix the Wretched, a goblin scoundrel operating out of Ratchet, considers it the ultimate test for aspiring pickpockets. According to Wrenix, the last five operatives sent to filch the chest returned in pieces, owing to the alert pirates aboard and a surprisingly ferocious guardian guarding the hold.

Southshore. Southshore is a coastal human port in the Hillsbrad Foothills and one of the Alliance's few surviving strongholds in fallen Lordaeron. Once a sleepy fishing village, it now stands as an embattled bastion facing constant hostility from the Forsaken garrison at Tarren Mill, rogue Syndicate bandits, and shoreline monsters. Southshore first rose to prominence during the First War when refugee boats carrying survivors from the fallen kingdom of Stormwind landed upon its beaches. Though contested and overrun during the Second War, it was rebuilt and later endured the horrors of the Third War. Today, while the rest of Lordaeron lies in ruins or under the rule of the Forsaken, Southshore remains fiercely loyal to the Grand Alliance. It offers shelter to displaced human survivors, veteran paladins of the Silver Hand, and scholars of the Kirin Tor.

Southshore Town Hall. Southshore Town Hall serves as the administrative seat of the southern coast of Hillsbrad Foothills, standing as one of the last functioning centers of Lordaeron's civil authority. From inside, Magistrate Henry Maleb coordinates local defenses and governs the town's surviving populace. The hall is a vital hub for the Alliance as they struggle to maintain a foothold in the plagued north. While much of Lordaeron lies shattered under Scourge corruption and Forsaken expansion, Southshore's town hall maintains the semblance of an intact human government. Magistrate Henry Maleb oversees daily governance from his office here, working alongside officials like Kundric Zanden to secure resources and preserve civic order. In a region surrounded by aggressive undead, Syndicate rogues, and Hillsbrad's fierce border skirmishes, the hall is the nerve center directing the town's survival against constant threats.

Southwind Village. Southwind Village is the haunted ruin of a night elf outpost located in the sands of Silithus. Wiped out by the qiraji during the War of the Shifting Sands, its streets are now bound by the restless spirits of fallen defenders and prowling silithid. Southwind Village once served as a primary night elf stronghold during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands a thousand years ago. When the qiraji legions breached the defensive perimeter, Valstann Staghelm—son of Archdruid Fandral Staghelm—led a detachment to hold the village. The defense ended in utter disaster: the night elven defenders were overwhelmed and slaughtered, and Valstann himself was dragged away into captivity by General Rajaxx. The village was completely ruined, leaving its former buildings fractured under the sun.

Souvenirs of Death. Souvenirs of Death is a quest given by Deathguard Samsa in Tarren Mill to Horde champions campaigning against the human settlements of the Hillsbrad Foothills. Envious of those sent to the front lines, Samsa asks for thirty human skulls taken in battle to add to his morbid collection. While High Executor Darthalia directs the full military might of the Forsaken against the Hillsbrad human settlements, Deathguard Samsa finds himself stranded on sentry duty in Tarren Mill. Harboring a bitter jealousy toward those dispatched to raid, burn, and pillage, Samsa views the open slaughter of the living as an enviable privilege denied to stationary town guards.

Sparring Match. Sparring Match is an introductory trial overseen by the martial instructor Tang Stonehoof. Designed to test newcomers regardless of their class or background, the trial challenges adventurers to defeat three arena novices or fellow duelists to prove their mettle in direct combat. Overseen by the veteran instructor Tang Stonehoof, the sparring match invites adventurers of all backgrounds into the ring to test their mettle. Though Tang specifically acknowledges those who walk paths outside the warrior tradition, he maintains that martial discipline and direct battle offer universal wisdom to any traveler in a dangerous world.

Speak with Anastasia. Speak with Anastasia is an introductory summons directing promising Forsaken mages to Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity. Dispatched by mage trainer Cain Firesong, the young caster is called to the Magic Quarter to undertake critical work for the magi of the Forsaken. This brief summons sets the stage for investigations out into the blighted lands of Tirisfal Glades. As nascent spellcasters hone their early talents under the guidance of Cain Firesong in Brill, they are soon directed into the capital. The mages of the Forsaken maintain a dedicated enclave within the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, organizing both arcane scholarship and strategic defensive efforts across Lordaeron. Cain Firesong acts as an evaluator, filtering out mere novices and sending those who demonstrate genuine talent directly to senior practitioners who require capable field hands.

Speak with Bink. "Speak with Bink" is an Alliance summons directing novice mages from Dun Morogh to the capital city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Magis Sparkmantle, the call sends promising spellcasters to assist Bink, an arcane researcher working out of the Hall of Mysteries. Novice mages training in the cold crags of Dun Morogh eventually catch the eye of Magis Sparkmantle. Recognizing when an apprentice has outgrown the rudimentary exercises around Kharanos, Sparkmantle passes along word from his colleague, Bink. The request is specific and uncompromising: Bink requires an arcane specialist and refuses to trust the matter to anyone who cannot wield magic.

Speak with Coleman. Speak with Coleman is a transitional task in Tirisfal Glades offered to champions who have proven their worth against the Scourge. Deathguard Dillinger directs capable warriors from the town square to the local tavern to assist Coleman Farthing with personal and factional vendettas. After assisting in the containment of severe local threats—such as laying to rest dangerous Scourge remnants like Ulag the Cleaver—adventurers earn the personal trust of Deathguard Dillinger. As one of the sentinels watching the roads into Brill, Dillinger judges who is capable of handling more than routine perimeter patrols and points capable fighters toward citizens in need of specialized service.

Speak with Deino. "Speak with Deino" is a summons directing promising Horde mages to seek out a skilled practitioner in Orgrimmar. Deino, a troll mage operating out of the Valley of Spirits, requires an adept to undertake critical work on behalf of their craft. Answering her call opens the path to deeper magical study and vital tasks across Kalimdor. As practitioners of the arcane hone their abilities within the Horde, instructors recognize when a student is prepared for more demanding ventures. Mentors like Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity point developing mages toward Orgrimmar. There, tucked away in the troll-dominated quarter, more specialized knowledge and perilous errands await.

Speak with Dillinger. Speak with Dillinger is a Horde military directive issued in Brill. Austil de Mon, the warrior trainer at the Gallows' End Tavern, dispatches able-bodied fighters to Deathguard Dillinger at the west end of the village to take on a hazardous combat mission in service of Lady Sylvanas. Within the Gallows' End Tavern in Brill, the warrior trainer Austil de Mon keeps a watchful eye out for promising combatants willing to serve the Dark Lady. When the Deathguards require capable hands, de Mon directs unproven adventurers out of the tavern and into the field. Deathguard Dillinger, who oversees security on the western edges of Brill, has requested someone with martial competence for an urgent task.

Speak with Gramma. Tommy Joe Stonefield seeks Gramma Stonefield's help to meet Maybell Maclure. Their families' bitter feud keeps the young lovers apart, and Tommy Joe hopes his grandmother can find a way for them to see each other. Tommy Joe Stonefield and Maybell Maclure keep their romance secret from their feuding families. The Stonefields and Maclures have fought over their farms for years, making their neighboring homesteads hostile ground. Tommy Joe wants to meet Maybell without provoking violence between their kin, so he turns to his grandmother for help.

Speak with Jennea. In Goldshire, Zaldimar Wefhellt sends novice mages to Stormwind for further instruction. He directs apprentices who have advanced beyond basic training in Elwynn Forest to Jennea Cannon in the Wizard's Sanctum. Zaldimar Wefhellt sends you from Goldshire to Stormwind City as your training advances. Your time learning elementary spells from local tutors in Elwynn's hamlets has run its course. In the Mage Quarter, the Wizard's Sanctum is where the kingdom's senior mages pursue arcane study and instruction. They coordinate magical matters across the realm.

Speak with Renferrel. Speak with Renferrel is a brief errand within the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. High Executor Hadrec directs you back to the Royal Apothecary Society's local researcher to discuss findings regarding tainted wolf hearts. After assisting the Deathstalkers across Silverpine Forest, High Executor Hadrec passes along an urgent message from Apothecary Renferrel. Renferrel has spent time analyzing the discolored wolf hearts gathered from the local wildlife and requires your presence immediately.

Speak with Sevren. Following the settling of Coleman Farthing's personal score at Agamand Mills, Magistrate Sevren summons the adventurer to Brill. The mills house far more than bitter family ghosts; they represent an active Scourge peril on the settlement's northern border. Coleman Farthing sought personal retribution against his former neighbors, the Agamands, sending travelers north to tear through the undead lurking about the flour mills. Once those remains were delivered, Coleman recognized that his private grudge intersected with a wider tactical problem: the entire Agamand estate remains swarming with mindlessly aggressive Scourge minions right on Brill's doorstep.

Speak with Shoni. This breadcrumb summons Alliance adventurers from the halls of Ironforge to find Shoni the Shilent in Stormwind City. Shoni heads an underground assault unit intended to support the ongoing reclamation of Gnomeregan. Following the radioactive downfall of Gnomeregan, the surviving gnomes established an exile quarter in Ironforge. Their engineers, tinkers, and strategists are constantly scheming to breach their lost home. While central planning remains rooted in Tinkertown, frontline preparations stretch far beyond Khaz Modan. Enterprising adventurers in the mountain city are redirected south to Stormwind, where specialized military hardware is being prepared for subterranean warfare.

Speak with Thun'grim. This errand directs rising Horde warriors to Thun'grim Firegaze, an acclaimed orc blacksmith camping in the Barrens. Having proved themselves through demanding physical trials, warriors are invited to have custom armor forged in recognition of their valor. The quest serves as the crucial bridge connecting general warrior testing with the crafting of Brutal Armor. After proving their mettle against the silithid hives during the Trial at the Field of Giants, Horde warriors earn more than simple praise from Ruga Ragetotem. Word of their endurance and martial prowess quickly reaches Thun'grim Firegaze, a renowned orc smith who maintains a camp perched on a ridge east of the Crossroads. Recognizing a warrior worthy of his craft, Thun'grim sends word that he wishes to fashion them an exceptional suit of battle mail.

Speaking of Fortitude. Brother Kristoff prepares a sermon in Stormwind City's Cathedral of Light. For his message on the Fortitude of the Spirit, he seeks a book in Stormwind Keep's Royal Library. Brother Kristoff, a priest in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, is preparing a sermon on the Fortitude of the Spirit. He wants to draw on the craft of metalworking alongside scripture. To make his point, he needs a treatise called "The Stresses of Iron." Its lessons on bearing pressure may help his congregation understand the strength of faith.

Speaking with Gan'zulah. Even after losing his head to the boiling brew at Grom'gol Base Camp, the Bloodscalp chieftain Gan'zulah seethes with fury. To appease his lingering rage, the severed spirit demands the death of his bitter Skullsplitter rivals and the ruin of their ruler, Ana'thek the Cruel. Following the collection of the Bloodscalp Clan Heads, Gan'zulah's severed head continues to curse anyone standing over the bubbling pot. Consumed by hatred for both his captors and his ancestral enemies, the dead chieftain offers an avenue to quiet his boiling temper: an assault into the eastern stronghold of the Skullsplitter tribe. He demands a slaughter of their hunters, headhunters, and berserkers, daring travelers to perish against their ferocious warband.

Speaking with Nezzliok. After defeating the Bloodscalp witch doctor, his severed head speaks from the bubbling cauldron at Grom'gol Base Camp. He claims to know where the lost Darkspear child was taken, but he refuses to give up the secret without a grim tribute. Though bound within the bubbling cauldron following the hunt for Bloodscalp Clan Heads, Nezzliok is far from cooperative. He admits knowing where Yenniku was taken, yet he demands appeasement before parting with the information. He commands that three trophy skulls be taken from the rival Skullsplitter tribe and brought to his resting place, ensuring his departed spirit will command thralls in the Nether.

name.zhCN: 给加克希姆的特快专递

text.enUS: Special Delivery for Gaxim. Special Delivery for Gaxim represents the return leg of an Alliance courier mission between Stormwind City and the wilds of Kalimdor. Collin Mauren provides a specialized Scroll of Messaging to take back to the gnome tinkerer Gaxim Rustfizzle in the Stonetalon Mountains. The scroll contains the arcane component needed to construct a remote explosive against local deforestation efforts. Gaxim Rustfizzle's efforts to sabotage the destructive operations of the Venture Company require unconventional solutions. Having concocted an explosive compound called NG-5, the tinkerer found himself lacking a reliable means of remote detonation. Rather than turning to crude fuses, Gaxim enlisted help across the Great Sea, reaching out to Collin Mauren in the Mage Quarter of Stormwind to acquire an enchanted Scroll of Messaging.

Special Forces. Following the reduction of the rogue colonel's rank-and-file soldiers, Sergeant Yohwa asks you to target the elite core of the compound.
