You are sent into the Stockpile cave to eliminate the commandos and headshrinkers before reporting to Lieutenant Doren. With the regular soldiers of the Kurzen Compound diminished through the work of the Second Rebellion, Sergeant Yohwa sets her sights on the colonel's elite specialists. She knows many of Kurzen's troops personally and calls them skilled, loyal and cruel. When they are not out in the wilderness slaughtering rebel soldiers, they are found in a cave at the back of the compound called the Stockpile. To break their strength, you are sent into the cavern to dispatch ten Kurzen Commandos and six Kurzen Headshrinkers.

Spectral Comb. The Spectral Comb is an ethereal grooming tool used to interact with the restless dead of Duskwood. Fashioned to pass through intangible forms, it is brought to the sorrowful spirit Blind Mary to harvest strands of ghost hair. Normal implements cannot touch or groom a spirit, making gathering ethereal materials nearly impossible for mortal craftsmen. The Spectral Comb is specially suited to interact with ghostly forms, gliding through otherwise intangible tresses. It is carried south of Darkshire to the ruined farmstead where the weeping ghost Blind Mary wails in isolation. Finding solace in the familiar act of grooming her ruined hair, Mary willingly uses the comb, leaving behind the spectral fibers needed to weave Ghost Hair Thread.

Spellfire Robes. Spellfire Robes is the culminating rite in the training of young Horde mages in the Undercity, completed by the tailor Josef Gregorian. After gathering rare components from across the realm, the apprentice is rewarded with custom enchanted vestments that signify their growing mastery over the arcane. For apprentices mastering the arcane arts in Lordaeron, standard cloaks and common garments do little to channel or insulate against raw eldritch forces. Josef Gregorian, a tailor working in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, weaves genuine magical garb from the specialized materials promising Horde spellcasters gather. The final stitching of the Spellfire Robes represents an apprentice's transition beyond basic incantations into an established practitioner of arcane and fire arts.

Spells of Shadow. Spells of Shadow is a dark grimoire carried by the Searing Blade cultists lurking beneath Orgrimmar in Ragefire Chasm. Filled with fel magic granted by the Burning Legion, it is targeted for recovery by the Forsaken leadership in the Undercity. Hidden deep in the molten caverns of Ragefire Chasm, members of the Searing Blade—a splinter cult tied to the Shadow Council—wield dark rites granted by demon masters of the Burning Legion. Among their most guarded treasures is the Spells of Shadow, a text containing insidious shadow and fel sorcery. Cultists and warlocks of the sect keep this book close at hand as they plot beneath the very feet of the Horde in Durotar.

Spirit Rise. Spirit Rise is the northwest mesa of Thunder Bluff, serving as the tauren capital's premier sanctum for spiritual and shamanic study. Overseen by spiritual guides such as the Skychaser tribe, it features sacred training halls above and descends into the cavernous Pools of Vision below. Perched high upon the bluffs overlooking the plains of Mulgore, Spirit Rise is devoted to communion with the elements and ancestor spirits. Connected to the central mesa by rope bridges, it houses the Hall of Spirits and the Spiritual Healing pavilion, where young and veteran shaman gather to deepen their connection with the earth, air, fire, and water. The Skychaser tribe maintains a strong presence across the rise, guiding seekers through ancient traditions.

Spirit Rock. Spirit Rock is a sacred crag perched in the rugged bluffs above the Valley of Trials in Durotar. Reached by a winding trail known as the Hidden Path, it serves as a secluded holy site where initiates commune directly with the elemental forces of the land. Overlooking the red canyon where young Horde warriors and scouts begin their training, Spirit Rock stands as an altar of communion. Isolated from the clatter of the Valley of Trials, it is approached only via the Hidden Path winding up the rocky ridgeline. Aspiring shaman make pilgrimages to this desolate outcrop to drink the traditional sapta, piercing the veil of the physical world to hear the rumblings and whisperings of the earth itself.

Spirit of the Wind. Spirit of the Wind is a repeatable ritual offered by the captive quilboar Mangletooth in Camp Taurajo. By channeling the residual power within Agamaggan's blood shards, Mangletooth infuses travelers with swiftness to outpace the vast savannas of the Barrens. In the arid sprawl of the Barrens, crossing open territory quickly can mean the difference between survival and falling to predatory beasts or wandering centaur warbands. The captive quilboar Mangletooth, imprisoned within Camp Taurajo, understands the latent power sleeping within the red crystalline blood shards scattered across the region. When handed ten of these relics, he draws upon their primeval resonance to bestow the Spirit of the Wind, granting travelers a burst of fleet-footed momentum to outrun the howling drafts of the plains.

Splinterspear Junction. Splinterspear Junction is a strategic fork in the main road winding through the heart of the Swamp of Sorrows. Dominated by a rugged orc watchtower and regularly patrolled by Horde sentries, it divides the path between northern retreats and southern outposts. Standing near the center of the Swamp of Sorrows, Splinterspear Junction divides travelers between two paths: the northern trail leading toward the Lost One refuge of the Harborage and the Fallow Sanctuary, and the southern road running directly past the fortress of Stonard toward the Blasted Lands. An ancient orcish watchtower oversees the split, garrisoned and patrolled by active Horde troops. For members of the Horde, it serves as a secure landmark in a treacherous marsh; for Alliance travelers, it represents a deadly ambush point along an already unforgiving trail.

Splintertree Post. Splintertree Post is the primary Horde fortress in eastern Ashenvale, situated northwest of Felfire Hill. Established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan during the Third War, it serves as a heavily fortified bulwark against the night elves and a staging ground for territorial expansion. Carved straight out of the ancient woodlands, Splintertree Post serves as the Horde's main military and logistical hub across eastern Ashenvale. Originally established by Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan when orcs first pressed into the forest during the Third War, it remains a heavily armed enclave defended primarily by orcish and tauren scouts and warriors. Armed with a flight master, an inn, and steady supply lines to Orgrimmar, it anchors the Horde's contested presence beneath the canopy.

Split Bone Necklace. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp calls upon Horde allies to hunt the Skullsplitter tribe living to the southeast. Although the Darkspears left Stranglethorn Vale behind, their ancient conflict with these jungle rivals remains unresolved. Returning with twenty-five split bone trophies aids the Darkspears in their war and earns their friendship. Following the collection of Bloodscalp trophies, Kin'weelay turns his attention toward another longstanding enemy. The Skullsplitter tribe dwells to the southeast of Grom'gol Base Camp, where they have clashed with the Darkspears across many years. Even though the Darkspears no longer reside within the jungles of Stranglethorn Vale, they remain bound to this enduring war.

Splithoof Crag. Splithoof Crag is a fortified settlement of the Galak centaur, tucked along the northern cliffs of Thousand Needles. It serves as one of the tribe's major enclaves alongside the high mesas, guarding the entrance to Splithoof Hold. Travelers traversing the canyon floor must contend with aggressive Galak patrols roaming near the bluffs. Nestled against the sheer northern rock face of Thousand Needles, Splithoof Crag sits just east of the towering Darkcloud Pinnacle. It is an established enclave of the Galak centaur, complete with crude tent encampments and dirt pathways cutting through the crags. At the heart of the village against the cliffside lies Splithoof Hold, a subterranean cavern holding the Cloven Hoof, an ancient relic of the centaur safeguarded by a sacred brazier.

Splithoof Hold. Splithoof Hold is a deep cavern stronghold carved into the stone of Splithoof Crag in Thousand Needles. Held by the Galak centaur tribe, the cavern serves as a fortified den and houses the Ancient Brazier, a site holding an eternally burning sacred flame. Tucked away inside Splithoof Crag, Splithoof Hold serves as a fortified redoubt for the Galak centaur. Unlike the windswept canyon floor, this enclosed cave offers them shelter, defensible chokepoints, and a secure sanctuary from rival tribes and travelers passing through the Needles.

Spotted Sunfish. Spotted Sunfish are freshwater fish native to Lake Everstill in the Redridge Mountains. Renowned locally for their flavor, they are a staple commodity for Lakeshire's docks, though the growing murloc infestation makes procuring them hazardous. Lake Everstill has long been celebrated for its spotted sunfish, which fetch a dependable price among local merchants and visitors alike. Dockmaster Baren keeps a steady trade in them at the Lakeshire piers, supplying food and commerce to a town under strain. However, the aggressive murloc tribes prowling the shallows have disrupted routine fishing, often stockpiling catches of their own that adventurers must recover by force.

Sprinkle's Secret Ingredient. After Marin Noggenfogger's brew turns out foul, Sprinkle in Gadgetzan offers to make it edible with her secret ingredient, a mushroom called the Violet Tragan. It grows underwater in a small lake in the Hinterlands. Sprinkle tells of her childhood, when her sister did all the cooking and the results were hard to stomach. Then she found a mushroom, the Violet Tragan, her "secret" ingredient, and it made every dish taste wonderful. She will use it to help turn Marin's horrid brew into something drinkable.

Sprite Darter. Sprite Darters are small, iridescent faerie dragons native to the lush canopy of Feralas. Revered for their innate spiritual and magical qualities, they flit gracefully among the ancient trees. Recently, these rare creatures have become targets for local Grimtotem tauren who seek to capture and exploit them. Sprite Darters are elusive, winged woodland beasts native to the ancient forests of Feralas. Characterized by their gleaming, iridescent wings and mysterious spiritual essence, they embody the whimsical yet fierce magical ecology of Kalimdor's deep forests. Though generally peaceful and shy, their innate resistance to magical forces and natural power make them significant to those attuned to the wilderness.

Sprite Jumpsprocket. In Stormwind's Dwarven District, Sprite Jumpsprocket works among gnomish and dwarven artisans. Like many gnomes who sought refuge after Gnomeregan fell, she pursues engineering alongside fellow tinkers. Sprite Jumpsprocket works as an apprentice engineer in Stormwind's Dwarven District, where gnomes and dwarves forge metal and design intricate devices side by side. She has made her place in the kingdom's capital, where apprentice tinkers hone their craft under experienced masters. Their inventive minds help maintain the Alliance's everyday mechanisms and marvels.

Sputtervalve. Sputtervalve is a stressed goblin engineer stationed in the port town of Ratchet. Serving the Tinkers' Union under Director Riddlevox, he oversees regional shredder research and development under crushing corporate deadlines. To keep his standing, he frequently hires adventurers to engage in industrial espionage against the rival Venture Company. Operating out of Ratchet, Sputtervalve answers to Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union. Put in charge of shredder development, he quickly discovered that keeping pace with modern mechanization is brutal work. Facing fierce competition and an unforgiving deadline, Sputtervalve found himself with few working prototypes of his own. Rather than admit failure to the Union, he turned toward the classic goblin solution: stealing better designs from whoever built them first.

Squire Maltrake. After The Torch of Retribution, Kalaran Windblade sends you on to Squire Maltrake, an envoy of theirs. Maltrake will tell you how the torch is to be used. Kalaran Windblade points you toward Squire Maltrake, an envoy. Maltrake is the one who will explain how the Torch of Retribution is to be used.

Stagalbog. The Stagalbog is a dense, waterlogged marsh stretch across the southern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. Bordering the southern mountain range just below the Pool of Tears, it remains an untamed wilderness. Stretching beneath the shadow of the southern crags, the Stagalbog is typical of the Swamp of Sorrows: stagnant water, drooping reeds, and tangled vegetation. It sits immediately south of the sunken ruins of the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, caught between the tainted lake and the rocky boundary of the region. Apart from rough wildlife, civilization has established no foothold here.

Stagalbog Cave. Stagalbog Cave is a damp subterranean cavern situated in the Stagalbog within the eastern reaches of the Swamp of Sorrows. It serves as a fortified den for the Marsh murlocs and their sinister spiritual leader, the Swamp Talker. Tucked away in the murky eastern wetlands of the Swamp of Sorrows, Stagalbog Cave provides shelter from the relentless swamp rains for the local murlocs. Known as the Marsh tribe, these amphibious creatures aggressively guard the winding cavern chambers alongside their chief mystic, the Swamp Talker. Travelers venturing near the sunken mire of the Stagalbog often hear their gurgling calls echoing out across the mossy banks, warning trespassers away from their nesting grounds.

Staghelm Point. Staghelm Point is an ancient night elven watchtower perched atop a craggy peak in northeastern Silithus. Overlooking the encroaching dunes and the nearby caverns of Twilight's Run, the tower stands as a vigil against the ancient threats haunting the desert. Rising high above the arid flats of northeastern Silithus, Staghelm Point is crowned by a solitary night elf tower. The outpost serves as a lonely sentinel, keeping watch over the wasteland and the shadowed cultists lurking in nearby caves like Twilight's Run. Watched over by Ralo'shan the Eternal Watcher and accompanied by a bronze drake circling overhead, the tower bears the proud and tragic name of the Staghelm lineage—a reminder of the immense sacrifices made by the Kaldorei during the ancient War of the Shifting Sands.

Stagnant Oasis. The Stagnant Oasis is one of the precious bodies of water nestled in the arid heart of the Barrens, positioned between the Gold Road and the Merchant Coast. Ringed by lush palms and contested by Kolkar centaur, its murky waters and surrounding shores sustain unique local wildlife, including snapping turtles and wandering kodos. Tucked away east of the Gold Road and inland from the Merchant Coast, the Stagnant Oasis provides a vital pocket of greenery amid the dusty scrubland of the Barrens. Like its neighboring waters, the pool supports dense foliage and aggressive snapjaw turtles, while weakened Barrens kodos often stray here away from the massive herds of the Field of Giants. However, travelers must tread carefully: Kolkar centaur maintain encampments along its banks, fiercely guarding the water rights against any who wander into their territory.

Stalker Claws. Stalker Claws are the talons harvested from the prairie stalkers roaming the rolling plains of Mulgore. Tauren shamans use them as vital components in carving traditional cleansing totems to purify tainted water wells. The grassy steppes of Mulgore are home to deadly natural predators, among them the stealthy prairie stalkers. These beasts survive through raw instinct and lethal precision, an essential balance within the Earth Mother's design. Mull Thunderhorn, seeking to heal the blighted land, requires these claws not out of malice toward the animals, but because the pure, natural ferocity with which they hunt holds the spiritual resonance necessary to counteract artificial corruption.

Stalking the Stalkers. Huntsman Markhor, of the village of Revantusk in the Hinterlands, names the Silvermane wolves as one of the worst dangers to the village's hunters. You are asked to turn the tables and hunt the hunters. Markhor points to the many trolls the Hinterlands wilds have already claimed, and ranks the Silvermane wolves among the greatest dangers to Revantusk's hunters. The wolves wait hidden among the bushes and the lay of the land, then pounce when the moment is right. Markhor will not let that go unanswered, and urges you to think as a Silvermane does and turn the hunt on the hunters, putting every one of them down.

Standing Our Ground. Standing Our Ground is a decisive quest where an adventurer stands alongside Aamelia Windfield in a desperate confrontation against a menacing bandit leader. Having prepared the defenders for battle, you face what seemed like a lost cause to secure safety from the brigands. Standing Our Ground marks the climax of a desperate struggle against a gang of bandits. Having helped prepare the local defenders for an inevitable clash, you are given one final opportunity to walk away and return safely to Valanaar rather than throw yourself into what appears to be a doomed last stand.

Starbreeze Village. Starbreeze Village is an abandoned night elf settlement situated east of Dolanaar in Teldrassil. Once a tranquil woodland hamlet, it has recently fallen to the maddened furbolgs of the Gnarlpine tribe. The ruined settlement now stands as a glaring symbol of the growing corruption seeping into the roots of the World Tree. Located southeast of Shadowglen and just down the road from Dolanaar, Starbreeze Village was once home to peaceful night elf families living beneath the boughs of Teldrassil. Today, the village lies in shambles, its wooden structures overrun by aggressive Gnarlpine furbolgs. Driven wild by a sinister corruption afflicting the boughs of the World Tree, the beast-men drove the elven residents out and now defend the ruined grounds ferociously.

Starfall Village. Starfall Village is a tranquil night elven sanctuary nestled along the snowy road of Winterspring. As the sole Alliance outpost in the frozen valley, it offers shelter and supplies to travelers braving the bitter northern chill. It also stands watch over the nearby barrow den. Situated northwest of the goblin trading post of Everlook and south of Frostsaber Rock, Starfall Village represents the lone bastion of Alliance civilization in Winterspring. Composed of traditional night elven timber lodges, the settlement serves as a haven for wayfarers, providing critical supplies and a warm hearth amid the harsh mountain elements. Despite its peaceful appearance, the village remains ever vigilant, positioned adjacent to a quiet, unoccupied barrow den.

Stars of Elune. Stars of Elune marks a major milestone in a young night elf priest's communion with the Moon Goddess. Upon proving their dedication to their people, acolytes are invited to the Temple of the Moon in Darnassus to learn sacred arts unique to the Sisterhood of Elune. Night elf priests do not draw their holy power from the broad philosophical tenets of the Light, as humans and dwarves do, but directly from their goddess, Elune. When an acolyte shows steadfast dedication while serving the realm, the Sisterhood in Darnassus recognizes that devotion. Summoned to the Temple of the Moon, the priest is deemed worthy of deeper communion and offered insight into sacred spells passed down through thousands of years of worship.

Starweave the Elder. Starweave the Elder is a Lunar Festival quest encountered in Darkshore. Adventurers seek out Elder Starweave in the settlement of Auberdine to pay their respects to the ancestral spirits of Kalimdor. In exchange for honoring ancient traditions, she offers celestial wisdom and her blessing. During the Lunar Festival, spirits of venerated ancestors manifest across the continents of Azeroth, battened in pillars of radiant celestial radiance. Elder Starweave takes her place among the night elves of Auberdine, a critical harbor town situated along the mist-shrouded coast of Darkshore. Travelers honoring the festival make pilgrimage to her side, seeking the timeless guidance of ages past.

Stealing Supplies. Uthek the Wise says meat gives the Gelkis their strength, and that the Magram keep extra stores so they can fight longer between hunts. You are sent to raid the Magram village to the east and bring back six bags of dried meat. Between wars the Gelkis hunt, because meat means strength and a full belly fights harder than an empty one. Uthek the Wise says the Magram keep spare stock to last them between hunts. Raid their village to the east, take those stores, and their strength will fail. Six bags of crudely dried meat are wanted, to be brought to Uthek at the Gelkis Village.

Steamwheedle Cartel. The Steamwheedle Cartel is the largest and most influential goblin enterprise operating across modern Azeroth. Fiercely neutral, the cartel governs bustling commercial hubs like Booty Bay, Ratchet, and Gadgetzan, serving Alliance and Horde patrons alike so long as their coin is genuine. Their sprawling operations encompass cross-continental shipping, alchemy, salvaging, and cutthroat mercenary contracting. Originating from the subterranean goblin capital of Undermine, the Steamwheedle Cartel initially allied with the Old Horde during the Second War, supplying war machines, sappers, and naval engineering. After the dust settled, the cartel's leaders realized that picking sides cost more than it earned. Embracing absolute neutrality, they expanded across both continents, opening trade networks that welcome Alliance and Horde alike. Today, as open tensions simmer, Steamwheedle ports provide vital common ground where anyone with gold can purchase passage, bank resources, and hire local specialists.

Steamwheedle Port. Steamwheedle Port is a bustling coastal outpost on the eastern shore of Tanaris, directly connected to Gadgetzan. Operated by the neutral Steamwheedle Cartel, it serves as an essential sea link across the South Seas while constantly warding off encroaching Southsea Pirates. Tucked against the dunes along the South Seas, Steamwheedle Port offers the inland desert city of Gadgetzan a direct lifeline to maritime trade. Run by the Steamwheedle Cartel, the settlement bustles with dockhands, traders, and sea captains braving the treacherous waters. Supply vessels regularly ply the routes between here and distant goblin trading posts, bringing valuable mechanical components, luxuries, and raw materials into southern Kalimdor.

Steelgrill's Depot. Steelgrill's Depot is a bustling engineering workshop and repair station situated directly east of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Overseen by Beldin Steelgrill and a crew of craftsmen, it serves as a frontline hub for vehicle maintenance, tinker supply runs, and salvage efforts. Nestled just off the snowy road east of Kharanos, Steelgrill's Depot buzzes with the clamor of clanking metal, hissing steam vents, and the hum of experimental engines. Dwarven miners and eccentric gnome engineers gather here amid heavy machinery, mechanized walking frames, and stockpiles of raw ores hauled out from nearby quarries. With Dun Morogh facing relentless trogg disruptions and mechanical supply shortages, Beldin Steelgrill and his crew keep Alliance machinery in working order, serving as an indispensable stop for travelers seeking spare parts or technical guidance in the bitter cold.

Steelgrill's Tools. Steelgrill's Tools are a specialized set of mechanic implements requisitioned for Beldin Steelgrill, the master technician of Steelgrill's Depot. Renowned for pushing siege engines—and his own equipment—to their limits, Beldin frequently breaks gear and relies on shipments from nearby Kharanos to keep his workshop running. Beldin Steelgrill is widely regarded as one of the finest siege engine technicians in Dun Morogh, but his aggressive repair style is infamous among local merchants. Working tirelessly on armored tanks and mechanical contraptions, Beldin tends to destroy delicate equipment almost as fast as it can be forged. Between snapping arclight spanners and stripping fang-ratchets, the mechanic is constantly placing fresh orders in Kharanos to keep his repair benches stocked.

Steelsnap. Steelsnap is a hunting task issued by Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise in Thunder Bluff. The hunt departs from traditional tauren reasons for killing, seeking the destruction of a vicious hyena whose pack terrorizes the wildlife of Thousand Needles. Tauren tradition dictates that taking a life must serve a sacred or practical purpose: hunting for sustenance, hunting to uphold honor, or hunting to glean wisdom from the Earthmother. Melor Stonehoof offers this quarry as an exception to the rule. Steelsnap is viewed as an abomination against natural balance—a brutal tyrant that sows senseless violence and fear rather than maintaining the cycle of life.

Steelsnap's Rib. Steelsnap's Rib is a grim trophy taken from the carcass of the ferocious hyena Steelsnap in Thousand Needles. Brought back to Thunder Bluff, it serves as physical proof that a creature deemed outside the Earthmother's blessing has been put down. Most tauren hunts are undertaken for sustenance, for honor, or to seek harmony with nature. Steelsnap, however, represents a different kind of quarry. Roaming the canyon floor of Thousand Needles south of Camp E'thok, this vicious alpha hyena terrorizes peaceful wildlife and rallies packs of lesser predators to senseless bloodshed. When the hunt master Melor Stonehoof on Hunter Rise marks Steelsnap for death, he demands a heavy bone—Steelsnap's rib—as undeniable confirmation that the tyrant has been slain and the canyon cleansed of its blight.

Sten Stoutarm. Sten Stoutarm is a practical dwarven outfitter and courier stationed outside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. Responsible for keeping new recruits equipped and managing local dispatches, he helps ensure that novice mountaineers stay warm, fed, and informed despite the harsh mountain conditions. Positioned near the heart of Coldridge Valley, Sten Stoutarm is one of the first friendly faces new dwarven and gnomish recruits encounter outside Anvilmar's tavern. With the valley isolated by winter blizzards and encroaching dangers, Sten takes it upon himself to outfit green apprentices with sturdy gear before they freeze or wander unprepared into the drifts.

Stendel's Pond. Gnolls prowl Stendel's Pond southwest of Sentinel Hill, where anglers still seek fresh fish. Southwest of Sentinel Hill, Stendel's Pond draws anglers despite the danger along its muddy banks. Gnolls roam nearby, and scattered skeletons with two lone graves show that the shore is perilous. The water may be foul, or the beasts may be to blame, but the cause is unknown. Schools of sagefish still bring anglers to the pond.

Stepping Stones. Stepping Stones is an investigation launched from a weathered note posted in the rugged wilds of the Barrens. The scrawled parchment says two couriers had been making deliveries for the New Plague, and calls what befell them simple apothecary accidents. The mysterious writer urges whoever finds it to seek out a secluded mountain refuge tucked along the border of Desolace. Pinned haphazardly to a wooden plank in a backcountry camp, the message stands out against the harsh elements of the Barrens. Campgrounds here often see a quiet rotation of mercenaries, cutthroats, and drifters seeking temporary shelter far away from the prying eyes of the Crossroads or Ratchet. The torn note immediately cuts through mundane wilderness chatter, offering an invitation laced with intrigue and dark undertones.

Stewvul, Ex-B.F.F.. After Translating the Ledger, Narain Soothfancy says nothing can be translated without the scrying goggles. Narain's ex-best friend forever, Stewvul, stole them, and you are to find Stewvul and take them back. Narain Soothfancy needs the scrying goggles before translating anything. They were stolen a while back by Stewvul, Narain's ex-best friend forever, who broke Narain's heart in five places and then abandoned Narain in this place.

Sticks and Bones. Sticks and Bones is a local task offered by Deathguard Bartholomew in Tirisfal Glades. He sends travelers to gather dry branches across the blighted woodland to deliver to Eleanor Shackleton, an experienced survivalist camped in the western hills. While Deathguards in Tirisfal Glades are usually consumed by military patrol duty and guarding against the Scourge or Scarlet crusaders, Deathguard Bartholomew takes a moment to look out for an acquaintance. Knowing that Eleanor Shackleton spends her unlife out in the harsh elements, he encourages passing adventurers to collect dry branches for her camp fire.

Stillwater Pond. Stillwater Pond is a quiet, stagnant body of water resting just west of Brill in Tirisfal Glades. Once a beloved picnic and swimming spot for the living children of Lordaeron, it has decayed into a murky pool inhabited by skeletal fish and prowled by dangerous scavengers. Before the Third War and the ravages of the Plague of Undeath, Stillwater Pond served as a tranquil retreat for the folk of Tirisfal Glades. Families from nearby hamlets gathered on its grassy banks for afternoon picnics, and children too young to brave the treacherous depths of Brightwater Lake learned to swim in its shallows. Today, the idyllic waters have turned lifeless and gray. The living have long vanished, leaving only skeletal fish darting beneath the surface and wandering undead drifting through the surrounding woods.

Sting of the Scorpid. Sting of the Scorpid is an early trial assigned by Gornek to Horde recruits at the Den in the Valley of Trials. Novices are challenged to hunt venomous scorpid workers northwest of camp and return ten tails to prove their combat readiness. The task serves as a vital lesson in surviving battlefield hazards and respecting even the smallest adversaries. In the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, Gornek tests novice Horde recruits by sending them against the local wildlife. The venomous scorpids roaming the arid dirt northwest of the Den have humbled seasoned warriors and clumsy initiates alike. To prove their battlefield competence, young champions must venture into the rocks, slay scorpid workers, and return with ten of their severed tails as proof of prowess.

Stinglasher. While surveying the Writhing Deep, one of Hadoken Swiftstrider's scouts spotted a giant insect, far larger than the others, wandering the twisted terrain. It has been named Stinglasher, and Hadoken wants it brought down and its secretion glands brought back to Camp Mojache. One scout in the Writhing Deep saw an insect much bigger than the others, wandering about the twisted terrain. It also seems to give off an aura that sets it apart from the rest. It has been given the name Stinglasher. Its innards would be invaluable to study while Hadoken works out how to deal with this new threat, so Hadoken wants its secretion glands cut out and brought straight to Camp Mojache.

Stinky's Escape. "Stinky" Ignatz is out in the swamp, where Morgan Stern, a cook in Theramore, sent him to gather bogbean leaves. Critters have surrounded him, and he asks you to help him out and watch his back while he looks for a bogbean plant. Afterward, Morgan Stern in Theramore is the one to see. Ignatz is relieved to meet someone who does not see him as a meal. He says Morgan Stern, a cook, is working on a new recipe and sent him out to collect bogbean leaves, which Ignatz guesses Stern finds tasty. While looking for a plant, Ignatz was surrounded, and he asks you to help him out and guard his back as he searches.

Stinky's Escape. "Stinky" Ignatz is hemmed in by swamp critters and has not found the bogbean he came for. Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin of Ratchet, wants bogbean leaves to brew a potion, and Ignatz asks you to get him out of this and watch over him while he searches. Afterward, Mebok Mizzyrix is to be found in Ratchet. Ignatz is relieved to meet someone who is not out to eat him. He says Mebok Mizzyrix, a goblin from Ratchet, needs bogbean leaves to brew some potion or other. Ignatz claims not to care why, since the money was good and he knows this swamp. He got surrounded before finding the plant, and asks you to help him out of the spot and guard him while he looks for it.

Stitches. Stitches is a colossal, stitched-together undead abomination stalking Duskwood's main thoroughfare. His march threatens travelers, the Night Watch, and the town of Darkshire. Stitches is an undead abomination assembled from harvested corpses and unholy sorcery. Appearing near Abercrombie's shack northeast of Raven Hill Cemetery, the lumbering monstrosity immediately sets out eastward along the road toward Darkshire. Imbued with immense physical strength and relentless malice, Stitches tears through any Night Watch checkpoints stationed along the thoroughfare—including the defense camp across from Vul'Gol Ogre Mound and the outpost outside the Rotting Orchard—bringing outright slaughter to unwary travelers and town defenders alike.

text.enUS: Stocking Jetsteam. Stocking Jetsteam is an Alliance quest offered by Pilot Bellowfiz at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. Preparing his siege engine for an extended deployment with the Ironforge Siege Brigade, the pilot enlists local hunters to gather boar meat and bear pelts to provision his crew. Stationed just outside Kharanos at Steelgrill's Depot, Pilot Bellowfiz oversees preparations for an upcoming long-haul operation on behalf of the Siege Brigade. His siege tank, dubbed Jetsteam, requires both mechanical tuning from master engineer Beldin Steelgrill and a month's worth of field provisions to keep its crew functional in the harsh sub-zero temperatures of Dun Morogh.

Stolen Booty. Stolen Booty concludes Gazlowe's effort to reclaim valuable cargo hijacked by the Southsea Freebooters off the coast of Ratchet. Rather than trying to recover every lost crate, the goblin chief focuses on two essential items: a shipment of cobbler's boots and a delicate telescopic lens needed to complete his observatory. The Southsea Freebooters have long plagued the merchant lanes of the Great Sea, but establishing a fortified encampment just south of Ratchet brought them into direct conflict with Gazlowe. When merchant vessels heading for the port were intercepted and looted, the Steamwheedle Cartel lost considerable supplies. While low-priority goods could be written off as routine shipping hazards, high-value specialized merchandise warranted hiring mercenary muscle to break into the pirate stronghold.

Stolen Enchanting Supplies. Stolen Enchanting Supplies is an errand undertaken near the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn Forest. An apprentice named Blixie Fitzwink lost a shipment of magical reagents during a gnoll ambush, and adventurers must retrieve the stolen goods from camps around Stone Cairn Lake. Recovering the materials spares the apprentice severe chore duty and keeps Master Theocritus's arcane studies supplied. A routine supply run turns perilous when Blixie Fitzwink, an apprentice assisting Master Theocritus, is ambushed by hostile gnolls between the trading post and the Tower of Azora. Fleeing for her life, she drops her cargo, leaving valuable enchanting reagents scattered among the gnoll camps dotting the shores of Stone Cairn Lake. Desperate to avoid weeks of disciplinary cleanup duty following arcane polymorph experiments, she appeals to passing adventurers to recover the missing goods.

Stolen Silver. The Stolen Silver is a recovered strongbox of Horde coin meant for the Crossroads guard garrison. It was bizarrely carried off into the wilderness by the ferocious raptors of the Barrens, leading to disbelief among the outpost's overseers. The vast wilds of the Barrens present constant threats to supply lines, but few expected the local Sunscale raptors to target strongboxes of metal currency. When a shipment of silver meant as payroll for the Crossroads garrison was stolen from the guard tower, the raptors dragged the lockbox back to their communal nests at the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. To overseers like Gazrog, the theft reveals an unsettling degree of cunning in the predators, who apparently value shiny trinkets or possess intelligence far beyond that of ordinary wild beasts.

Stolen Silver. Stolen Silver is a Horde assignment from Gazrog at the Crossroads to recover a cache of payroll coin pilfered by raptors. Following rumors of their uncanny cunning, travelers track the missing currency deep into the Raptor Grounds south of Ratchet. Recovering the lockbox ensures the Crossroads garrison actually gets paid. The Crossroads serves as the vital hub of the Barrens, connecting Orgrimmar, Mulgore, and Ratchet. Maintaining order across this vast savanna requires vigilant guards, and guards require steady pay. When raptors ambushed the payroll shipment, Gazrog initially sought vengeance against the beasts. Yet killing the pack does not balance the settlement's ledgers, forcing the Horde to investigate how and why simple animals hauled off heavy crates of coin.

Stolen Supplies. Stolen Supplies tasks adventurers with recovering plundered highland goods from the Al'Aketh in Falaath Village. Caravan ambushes have cut off vital shipments of food and windstones between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands, leaving local skyborne communities on the brink of starvation. For months, caravans traveling between the lowlands and the Shen'dar Highlands have faced persistent attacks along their trade routes. These shipments transport vital necessities, including food and windstones, to sustain the highland settlements. Without steady deliveries, local townsfolk have been pushed to the brink of starvation, struggling to squeak by as supplies dwindle across the region.

Stoley's Debt. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley has a bet with his old friend Stoley, who tends the bar at Steamwheedle Port, over whose rum is stronger. Stoley seems to be dodging it, so MacKinley asks you to go and talk to him. Stoley owes "Sea Wolf" MacKinley a very special bottle of rum. Stoley boasted that the rum at Steamwheedle Port is stronger than anything in Booty Bay, and said the money owed would be doubled if MacKinley tried it and disagreed. Now MacKinley thinks Stoley has lost his nerve about handing it over, but MacKinley never backs away from a wager. You are asked to go and speak to Stoley at the Steamwheedle Port bar.

Stoley's Shipment. Stoley is out of rum and in debt to a friend over a wager. Captain Cuergo stole the last shipment and keeps it in the walled pirate town to the south, so Stoley asks you to bring it back. Stoley has none left of the rum promised to "Sea Wolf" MacKinley of Booty Bay to settle their wager. Captain Cuergo stole the last shipment, and has it stowed in the walled pirate town to the south, which is Lost Rigger Cove. Stoley asks you to find the rum and return it, so that he can show Kalimdor's drink is far better than anything Booty Bay pours.

Stonard. Stonard is a fortified Horde outpost situated in the southern marshes of the Swamp of Sorrows. Originally built during the First War, it serves the modern Horde as an essential foothold in the southern Eastern Kingdoms and an observation post watching the Blasted Lands. Stonard stands as one of the oldest orcish settlements on Azeroth. First established when the Old Horde spilled through the Dark Portal into what was once the Black Morass, Stonard and its sister post, Rockard, anchored the invaders' lines. Though abandoned and damaged during the fallout of the Second War, Thrall's New Horde moved to reconstruct and garrison Stonard. Anchored by a traditional orcish Great Hall and fortified burrows, the outpost is now a vital island of Horde authority in an untamed, perilous mire.

Stone Cairn Lake. At Stone Cairn Lake in northeastern Elwynn, hostile murlocs hold the southern shore and renegade wizards camp on the island. Heroes' Vigil honors those lost in the First War. Families and pilgrims once crossed the calm waters to honor the dead at Heroes' Vigil. The stone memorial was raised on the lake's central island to mark the heavy loss of human life in the First War against the Orcish Horde. Now renegade wizards have made camp beside the monument, and the island has become a hostile place.

text.enUS: Stone Is Better than Cloth. Lucien Tosselwrench knows how cheap Lotwil can be, and offers to make something for your trouble: enchanted bracers built from the extra stones you collected. What Lucien lacks is a blacksmith's patterned bronze bracers. After the Study of the Elements: Rock trials, Lucien Tosselwrench admits how cheap Lotwil can be and wants to make it up to you. Lucien has been busy with the extra stones you gathered and can make fine enchanted bracers. They may even help guard you against what Lucien calls the coming atrocity of Lotwil's newest invention.

Stone Tokens. Stone Tokens is a Horde assignment issued by Keeper Bel'varil in Tarren Mill to retrieve magical binding artifacts from Dalaran agents in the Alterac region. The Forsaken seek to study the arcane methods Dalaran's mages use to enslave and command powerful elementals. Gathering these inert tokens serves as the foundation for the Magus's research into elemental subjugation. The magi of Dalaran have long possessed a formidable command over elemental entities, using specialized conduits and enchanted foci to bind creatures from other dimensions into servitude. While the city itself is still rebuilding, its agents and remnant forces patrol the surrounding territory, relying on elementals as laborers and defensive shock troops. Magus Voidglare, an arcane researcher working on behalf of the Forsaken in Tarren Mill, seeks to dissect the precise sorcery Dalaran uses to compel these entities into obedience.

Stone of Relu. The Stone of Relu is an ancient archaeological relic recovered from the Wetlands. Believed by Archaeologist Flagongut to be the key to unlocking latent powers within primordial fossils, it was briefly lost when local raptors ambushed the scholar on the road. Discovered during Explorers' League operations, the Stone of Relu is believed to hold the deciphering power needed to unlock prehistoric fossils gathered from Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. Archaeologist Flagongut identified the artifact as the catalyst required to unleash secrets within both his own Wetlands specimens and the fossil unearthed by Prospector Remtravel in Darkshore.

Stonebull Lake. Stonebull Lake is a serene, horseshoe-shaped body of water wrapping around Bloodhoof Village in central Mulgore. Fed by the pristine natural runoff of the plains, it provides vital fresh water, abundant fish, and peaceful shores for the young tauren coming of age under Cairne Bloodhoof's guidance. Curving around Bloodhoof Village on three sides, Stonebull Lake defines the geography of central Mulgore. A wooden bridge crosses the lake's narrowest stretch, carrying the main dirt road between the settlement and the great mesa of Thunder Bluff to the north. Its calm waters are filled with native fish, making its banks a favored spot for resting hunters, weary travelers, and apprentice fishers learning their trade under the sweeping open sky.

Stonefield Farm. The Stonefield family works the fields in southern Elwynn Forest. Their long feud with the neighboring Maclures keeps the two households at odds. Stonefield Farm lies south of Goldshire, where the family grows crops for the realm. For decades, the Stonefields have quarreled with the nearby Maclure Vineyards. The households trade accusations of theft and trespassing, and even small disputes keep tensions high. Gramma Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield make their home here.

Stonefield family. The Stonefield family is a lineage of human farmers residing at the Stonefield Farm in western Elwynn Forest. Known for their long-standing rural roots, they tend their homestead while caught up in an ongoing rivalry with their neighboring peers, the Maclures. Despite the hostility between the two households, younger generations find themselves entangled across the family divide. The Stonefields are quintessential Elwynn agrarian stock, working the soil south of the road leading to Westfall. The homestead revolves around Gramma Mildred Stonefield, Ma Stonefield, and young Tommy Joe Stonefield. Daily life on the farm involves tending crops and managing livestock while fending off local pests and dealing with nearby kobold incursions that plague the region's mines and borders.

Stonefire Tavern. The Stonefire Tavern is the primary inn serving travelers inside the mountain city of Ironforge. Situated in the bustling Commons district just north of the city gates, it provides a warm hearth, strong dwarven ale, and a resting place for adventurers arriving from across Khaz Modan. Located immediately north of the fortress gates in the Commons, the Stonefire Tavern serves as the premier public house in Ironforge. Run by Innkeeper Firebrew alongside his daughter Gwenna, the inn offers weary wayfarers hearty meals, local brews, and lodging beneath the mountain. Whether seeking respite from the harsh mountain snows of Dun Morogh or looking to trade tales and supplies before venturing deep into the city, travelers from all corners of the Alliance routinely gather around its roaring hearth.

Stonegear's Search. Stonegear's Search is an Alliance directive directing adventurous travelers to Pilot Stonegear at Steelgrill's Depot in Dun Morogh. The enthusiastic siege engine operator has caught wind of an exotic mineral and seeks a daring explorer to track down fresh fuel for his tank's ordnance. Dwarven siege engines are legendary feats of engineering, but their operators are rarely content leaving well enough alone. Word around Ironforge and Loch Modan quickly spreads that Pilot Stonegear, stationed just outside the capital, is scheming to boost his war machine's punch. Whether pointed his way by Pilot Longbeard or Mountaineer Kadrell, travelers are recruited simply to meet the ambitious pilot and hear his proposal.

Stonemasons Guild. The Stonemasons Guild was the collective of master builders and artisans responsible for reconstructing Stormwind City after the Second War. Following a bitter dispute over payment with the House of Nobles that ended in deadly riots, the guild was forcibly dissolved, driving its disenfranchised members into exile while leaving the true fate of its scattered artisans an enduring mystery. Led by elected Guildmaster Edwin VanCleef, the artisans of the Stonemasons Guild demonstrated a mastery of masonry that rivaled the Royal Stonecutters Union of the dwarves. Following the devastation of the First and Second Wars, the House of Nobles hired the guild to embark upon the monumental task of rebuilding Stormwind City from ruins, trusting them to restore the capital to its ancient grandeur.

Stonemaul Ruins. The Stonemaul Ruins are the shattered remnants of Stonemaul Village, once the proud Kalimdor settlement of the Stonemaul ogres. After being driven out by the black dragonflight, the clan fled north, leaving their former home overrun by Firemane dragonspawn. Following their migration to Kalimdor, the Stonemaul ogres founded their settlement amid the murky swamps of Dustwallow Marsh. The village became famous when the beastmaster Rexxar braved the clan's lethal trials, slew their brutal chieftain Kor'gall, and rallied the ogres to defend the nascent Horde against Admiral Proudmoore's forces. After the war, Rexxar left the ogre Mok'Morokk in command. Under Mok'Morokk's selfish rule, the village fell into decline and was ultimately ambushed and shattered by the black dragonflight. The surviving ogres fled north to establish Brackenwall Village, while Onyxia's brood took complete possession of the ruins.

Stones of Binding. After The Princess Trapped, a voice from the iridescent shards tells of four Stones of Binding spread across Arathi that hold it down under the ground. The strongest, the Stone of Inner Binding, can be unlocked only with keys taken from the other three. The voice tells of four Stones of Binding spread across Arathi, holding it down under the ground. To loosen them, the strongest must be unlocked first: the Stone of Inner Binding, which needs keys gathered from the other three, the Stones of West, East and Outer Binding. The keys are the Burning Key, the Cresting Key and the Thundering Key. Guardians watch over the stones, but someone clever or lucky may find a way to banish them. Once gathered, the keys are carried to the Stone of Inner Binding.

Stonesplinter Valley. Stonesplinter Valley is a rugged mountain vale in southwestern Loch Modan overrun by hostile troggs. Once a pristine alpine hollow, it has transformed into a fortified encampment under the brute command of the trogg chieftain Grawmug. Tucked away among the craggy slopes of southwestern Loch Modan, Stonesplinter Valley was once a quiet alpine hollow. That serenity ended when waves of subterranean troggs clawed their way to the surface across Khaz Modan. Claiming the valley for their own, the Stonesplinter tribe rapidly turned the rocky defiles into crude fortifications, digging dens, erecting barricades, and hunting anything that strays too close. Their numbers make the valley an open wound on roads through southern Loch Modan, forcing Mountaineers out of Thelsamar to hire adventurous mercenaries willing to cull their ranks and eliminate their towering warlord, Grawmug.

Stonetalon Peak. Stonetalon Peak is an ancient night elven sanctuary tucked into a verdant alpine valley at the northwestern edge of the Stonetalon Mountains. Sacred to the kaldorei and cared for by local druids, it serves as the primary bastion of the Alliance in these craggy heights. Perched high above the arid dust of the lower ranges, Stonetalon Peak opens into a lush, mist-shrouded sanctuary. Long considered sacred and steeped in ancient magic, the valley holds ruins dating back millennia to when the region housed temples honoring Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering. In the modern era, kaldorei Sentinels and druids have restored a measure of peaceful stewardship here, maintaining a tranquil refuge complete with a barrow den and a vital Alliance flight roost.

Stonetalon Sap. Stonetalon Sap is a sticky, potent substance harvested directly from the lumbering sap beasts that roam the craggy heights of the Stonetalon Mountains. It serves as a key reagent for the Darkspear witch doctor Jin'Zil, who uses its raw woodland properties to concoct a spiteful brew.

text.enUS: Stonetalon Standstill. Stonetalon Standstill is a Horde assignment given by Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post to secure the vital passage toward the Stonetalon Mountains. Befouled water elementals in Mystral Lake have brought supply transports to a halt, prompting the Horde to cull the hostile spirits and scout an elven gazebo overlooking nearby Alliance movements. Maintaining the Horde's foothold in Ashenvale requires a constant flow of lumber, supplies, and messengers moving between the forest and the peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains. The Talondeep Path serves as this critical artery, skirting past the western shore of Mystral Lake. When the waters violently churned to life with hostile elementals, travel stopped dead in its tracks. Transport caravans found themselves battered by enraged water spirits, prompting Mastok Wrilehiss to demand swift action before logistical lines collapse entirely.

Stonewatch. Stonewatch is a fortified stronghold in central Redridge Mountains, built to defend the surrounding human lands from northern invasions. Formerly manned by Stormwind soldiers, the fortress has fallen under the brutal control of the Blackrock orcs, posing an immediate threat to nearby Lakeshire. Positioned over the cliffs near Stonewatch Falls, Stonewatch comprises a heavily built tower and keep designed to guard the approaches from the Burning Steppes. Originally held by Lakeshire's defenders, the fortification fell when the rogue warlock Morganth forged an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Infused with dark magic, the invading orcs overwhelmed the local human garrison—the 12th Sabre Regiment—and claimed the fortress. Although Morganth eventually turned on his allies and withdrew to the nearby Tower of Ilgalar with an army of Shadowhide gnolls, the Blackrock orcs retained a stranglehold over the keep under the command of Warlord Gath'Ilzogg and Lieutenant Tharil'zun.

Stonewatch Falls. Stonewatch Falls is a scenic waterfall and deep mountain pool situated in the eastern reaches of the Redridge Mountains, fed by the outflow of Lake Everstill. Cascading down the hillside beneath the looming heights of Stonewatch, its isolated waters are claimed by a hostile tribe of murlocs. Pouring from the eastern river of Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Falls cascades down the rugged terrain beneath the Blackrock orc stronghold of Stonewatch. The plunging water carves out a deep pool tucked against the mountainside. Despite its natural beauty, travelers rarely linger to admire the view; a vicious band of murlocs infests the pool, building crude reed hovels and preying upon any foolish enough to trespass along the water's edge.

Stonewatch Keep. Stonewatch Keep is a fortified stone stronghold looming in eastern Redridge Mountains, once built and manned by the Kingdom of Stormwind. It has fallen to an invading host of Blackrock orcs, serving as the forward operational base from which their warlords terrorize Lakeshire. Stonewatch Keep originally defended the eastern ridges and guarded the settlers of Lakeshire against hostile incursions. That peace shattered when the renegade warlock Morganth struck an alliance with the Blackrock clan. Bolstered by dark magic, the orcs stormed the fortress with vicious ferocity, overwhelming the human defenders and taking the keep for themselves. Although Morganth later abandoned his allies to raise the nearby Tower of Ilgalar and subjugate local gnolls, the Blackrock invaders successfully consolidated their grip over Stonewatch, transforming a former bastion of the Alliance into a fortified staging ground for their assault on the valley.

Stonewatch Tower. Stonewatch Tower is a stone guard tower standing within the overrun stronghold of Stonewatch in northeastern Redridge. Once maintained by the defenders of Lakeshire, the outpost was captured by the Blackrock clan to monitor the surrounding ridges and secure their mountain bastion. Built by the Kingdom of Stormwind to guard the high mountain passes above Lake Everstill, Stonewatch Tower served as the forward scouting sibling to Stonewatch Keep. From its elevated vantage point, sentries could easily watch the eastern ridges and alert Lakeshire to any threats advancing from the Burning Steppes. That early warning network collapsed when Warlord Gath'Ilzogg's Blackrock orcs swept down from the heights, overrunning the human defenders and claiming the stronghold for their own war effort. Today, the tower bristles with Blackrock sentinels, ensuring no Alliance scouts approach the fortress undetected.

Stonewrought Dam. The Stonewrought Dam is a colossal dwarven engineering marvel standing along the northern rim of Loch Modan. It holds back the waters of the Loch, creating the massive highland lake while draining the Wetlands below into habitable marshes. Stretching across the canyon east of Dun Algaz, the Stonewrought Dam is widely regarded as one of the great structural triumphs of dwarven civilization. Designed by the master Dark Iron architect Franclorn Forgewright, the barrier was built using his pioneering stonewrought technique. By trapping the waters of the mountain basin, the dam doubled the surface area of the Loch while steadily lowering water levels to the north, allowing the marshy basin of the Wetlands to emerge from a once completely flooded valley.

Stonewrought Pass. Stonewrought Pass is an underground tunnel cut directly through the southern mountains of Loch Modan into the blighted expanse of the Searing Gorge. Masterfully engineered by the famed architect Franclorn Forgewright, this passage connects the Valley of Kings directly to Dustfire Valley. Heavy iron gates secure both ends to protect peaceful dwarven lands from the volcanic terrors to the south. Carved out of the bedrock by the legendary master architect Franclorn Forgewright—famed also for the massive Stonewrought Dam—the Stonewrought Pass serves as a direct corridor between the pastoral beauty of Loch Modan and the scorched wastes of Searing Gorge. Emerging in Loch Modan near the colossal Valley of Kings, it cuts straight through the mountain ridge down into Dustfire Valley. Because Searing Gorge is infested with Dark Iron dwarves and fiery beasts, the Ironforge mountaineers keep the passage locked tight behind heavy gates to prevent danger from spilling into the north.

Stop the Spread. Stop the Spread is a Silverpine Forest quest concerning the containment of the worgen curse linked to Archmage Arugal. While researchers seek a way to halt the affliction, preemptive measures are ordered against living human refugees at the Greymane Wall to prevent them from turning into Arugal's servants. In Silverpine Forest, the scourge of the worgen spreads at the hands of the renegade Archmage Arugal. While the exact methods and mechanics behind the spread of this feral condition remain largely unknown, the danger it presents to the territory is undeniable. Researchers are actively working to understand the nature of the magic, but their immediate focus is preventing Arugal from amassing an unstoppable host of savage followers.

Stormbrow the Elder. Near Goldshire, Stormbrow the Elder waits beside the water during the Lunar Festival. Travelers honor ancient traditions and the olden races of Azeroth, and receive a token of remembrance in return. A quiet pond lies just behind the smithy in Goldshire, where Stormbrow the Elder appears. Guards, tradesfolk, and weary travelers pass through town on their way into the forest. Beneath Elwynn Forest's canopy, the honored spirit welcomes anyone who comes to honor the realm's long history.

Stormpike Banner. The Stormpike Banner is a military standard hidden deep within the treacherous Icewing Cavern in Alterac Valley. Alliance recruits must brave wild harpies to recover it as an initiation trial, proving they are worthy to wear the Stormpike insignia. To officially join the ranks of the Stormpike expedition in Alterac Valley, prospective recruits must prove their mettle before they ever clash with the Frostwolf orcs. Lieutenant Haggerdin sends newly arrived Alliance soldiers into the Icewing Caverns, situated southwest of Dun Baldar. Planted deep inside this frozen subterranean den, the Stormpike Banner serves as a testing ground: anyone brave enough to brave the native harpies, seize the standard, and bring it back alive earns the rank and insignia of an initiate in the Stormpike Guard.

Stormpike's Deciphering. Loremaster Dibbs sends you to Ironforge with the ensorcelled parchment, hoping Prospector Stormpike, a master of decryption and deciphering, can make sense of it. After The Ensorcelled Parchment, Dibbs tells you to take it to Prospector Stormpike, who is at his studies in Ironforge's Prospector headquarters. Dibbs says to mention that he sent you, since he has been sending Stormpike quite a lot of business lately.

Stormpike's Delivery. Grimand Elmore sends travelers north with an axe for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The road leads from Stormwind's Dwarven District to an Ironforge outpost in Loch Modan. Grimand Elmore has been asked to make a weapon for Mountaineer Gringer Stormpike. The Stormpike clan is respected in Ironforge for its discerning taste and martial pride. Elmore turns to trustworthy travelers to carry the axe north, across the distance between Stormwind and the dwarven borderlands.

Stormpike's Order. In Loch Modan, Mountaineer Stormpike is arranging a shield from Furen Longbeard. The armorsmith works far south in Stormwind City, so Stormpike asks a traveler to carry his order there. Mountaineer Stormpike wants a new shield, and he trusts only Furen Longbeard to forge it. The mountaineer is willing to pay well to place the commission in the smith’s hands, though Loch Modan and Stormwind City lie far apart.

Stormpike's Request. Mountaineer Stormpike sends a written commission from Loch Modan to Stormwind City. He asks Furen Longbeard to craft him a shield of exceptional dwarven quality. Mountaineer Stormpike needs a sturdy shield while stationed in Loch Modan. He trusts no ordinary smith with the work and asks Furen Longbeard, whose craft he greatly admires. Furen now lives among the humans in Stormwind's Dwarven District, having left Ironforge. Stormpike assumes a king's ransom drew him south, so traveling adventurers carry the commission across the kingdoms.

Stormrage Barrow Dens. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are an ancient subterranean sanctuary carved beneath the sacred valley of Moonglade. Named for Malfurion Stormrage, these quiet earth-hewn chambers serve as a dedicated resting place where druids enter long, restorative slumbers to wander the Emerald Dream. Barrow dens serve as sacred havens throughout night elven lands, providing druids a safe subterranean refuge where their physical bodies can lie undisturbed during lengthy immersions in the Emerald Dream. The Stormrage Barrow Dens are particularly esteemed within the sacred realm of Moonglade. Named in honor of Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage, these winding earthen halls hold both ancient reverence and quiet vigil. While some druids like Clintar Dreamwalker still slumber safely within its alcoves, the absence of the great Archdruid himself casts a somber shadow over the hollowed roots and peaceful glowing lanterns.

Stormwind (kingdom). The Kingdom of Stormwind is the southernmost and currently foremost human realm on Azeroth, holding dominion over Elwynn Forest, Westfall, Duskwood, and the Redridge Mountains. Sacked and shattered during the First War, it was rebuilt through blood and labor after the Second, rising to become the military and cultural center of the Alliance following the tragic collapse of Lordaeron in the north. Today, the kingdom stands beset from within and without, ruled by the ten-year-old King Anduin Wrynn under the watchful guidance of Highlord Bolvar Fordragon while its crowned monarch remains missing. Stormwind was established over a thousand years ago by descendants of the ancient Arathi empire who ventured south beyond the crags of Khaz Modan into fertile, forested valleys. Far from the northern kingdoms, the realm grew into a culture fiercely proud of its self-reliance and the Light.
