text.enUS: Stormwind Armor Marker. Stormwind Armor Marker lets those who aid the realm claim crafted gear from sanctioned artisans. Sara Timberlain accepts one at the Eastvale Logging Camp. Stormwind's commanders issue armor markers to those who serve the realm. Keeping law and order across Elwynn Forest stretches Stormwind's resources thin, so commanders sometimes use these official requisition slips instead of handing out standard gear at military outposts. A marker confirms the bearer's service and authorizes local craftsmen under contract to provide tailored armor.

Stormwind Army. The Stormwind Army is the standing military force charged with defending the Kingdom of Stormwind and preserving the security of the Grand Alliance in the south. Though legendary for its resilient knights and marshals, the army is currently crippled by royal absence, political infighting, and crippling troop shortages across the provinces. The army traces its martial lineage through centuries of brutal conflict, from early frontier clashes against gnolls to the desperate defense against the Gurubashi trolls. In the First War, under King Llane Wrynn I and Sir Anduin Lothar, the Knights of Stormwind mounted legendary ambushes against the Orcish Horde, yet fell when the capital burned. Surviving remnants evacuated to Lordaeron, spearheading the formation of the Alliance of Lordaeron and fighting through the Second War. After the Dark Portal's fall, Stormwind's military was rebuilt alongside the restored kingdom.

Stormwind City. Stormwind City leads the Kingdom of Stormwind and the Alliance as their capital and seat of power. Rebuilt after the First War, it is the greatest remaining human stronghold in Azeroth since the northern kingdoms fell. Stormwind City rose over a thousand years ago, founded by Arathi descendants who migrated south. The coastal capital flourished behind stone ramparts, with swift rivermills powering the city. In the First War, the Orcish Horde laid siege, broke through its defenses, and burned Stormwind to the ground. Sir Anduin Lothar led the surviving refugees across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. After the Alliance won the Second War, the Stonemasons' Guild rebuilt the capital with white stone, canals, and towering spires. The fortress now stands north of Elwynn Forest.

Stormwind Gate. At Stormwind Gate, sentries watch the road between Elwynn Forest and Stormwind City. The passage opens onto the Valley of Heroes, where the city’s stone monuments rise beyond the arch. Stormwind Gate guards the southern road from Elwynn Forest into the capital. The Stormwind City Guard watches from the stone portal, while patrols move between the outer arch and the Valley of Heroes. Unrest lingers in Elwynn, yet the massive iron and stone gates stay open. Travelers, merchants, and returning defenders pass through into the heart of the Alliance.

Stormwind Guard. The Stormwind Guard comprises the regional garrisons and sentries tasked with enforcing the kingdom's laws and defending its surrounding territories. Stretched perilously thin by political gridlock and distant military campaigns, its scattered marshals struggle to hold back gnolls, orcs, and bandits across Elwynn and Redridge. Operating as a vital branch of the Stormwind Army, the Stormwind Guard patrols the highways, crossroads, and stone watchtowers that bind the kingdom together. In outlying settlements, governance and defense fall to appointed marshals—such as Marshal McBride in Northshire Valley, Marshal Dughan in Goldshire, and Marshal Marris in Lakeshire. These officers muster recruits and maintain order, relying on trusty brown horses known for stamina to cover ground between fortified outposts like Westbrook Garrison.

Stormwind Ho!. Lieutenant Farren Orinelle is desperate to escape his posting in Southshore and return south to Stormwind City. Sensing a career opportunity after hearing Alliance High Command fears the rising threat of the naga, he hires an adventurer to exterminate the serpent-folk so he can claim the credit and secure a reassignment. Southshore sits on the knife-edge of Lordaeron, hemmed in by Forsaken forces, syndicate brigands, and relentless sea fiends. For Lieutenant Farren Orinelle, an ordinary guardsman accustomed to city drunks and petty brawls in Stormwind, the posting is nothing short of miserable. When word arrives from his former mentor that Alliance High Command is increasingly anxious about the naga encroaching on the coasts, Farren spots his golden opportunity to leave the north behind.

Stormwind Keep. Stormwind Keep stands high above the capital as the stone fortress and seat of power for the Kingdom of Stormwind. Rebuilt after its ruin in the First War, it currently houses the royal court of the young boy-king Anduin Wrynn and his regent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon. Perched upon a plateau overlooking the entire city, Stormwind Keep serves as both a palace and a military bastion. The original stronghold was burned to the ground by the Old Horde when King Llane was assassinated near the end of the First War. Raised anew upon the old foundations after the Alliance reclaimed the kingdom, the reconstructed keep houses not only the grand throne room and the War Room, but peaceful garden courtyards and the expansive Royal Library.

Stormwind Library. In Stormwind Keep, Donyal Tovald copies the kingdom’s histories for those with library scrips. Young King Anduin Wrynn has set aside royal funds for the work, opening these accounts of Azeroth to citizens and scholars. While Highlord Bolvar Fordragon and Lady Katrana Prestor guide Stormwind’s defenses and court in King Varian’s absence, young King Anduin turns royal support toward learning. He funds copies of ancient manuscripts and historical journals, so the kingdom’s past can be preserved and studied. Within Stormwind Keep, the Royal Library keeps these written accounts and copies them for those in royal service.

Stormwind Stockade. Stormwind Stockade holds the city’s most dangerous prisoners beneath the canals near the Mage Quarter. A coordinated revolt has driven the guards from the lower cells, leaving the prison in chaos. Warden Thelwater oversees the Stockade, where Stormwind keeps cutthroats, Defias operatives, captured Blackrock orcs, and Dark Iron dwarves. Now a violent uprising led by the Defias conspirator Bazil Thredd has forced the guards from the lower cells. The prisoners roam freely through the corridors. Thelwater has managed to secure the entrance, but the revolt still threatens to reach the canals. He depends on adventurers to enter the prison and put down the uprising.

Stormwind Stockade (Classic). Prisoners now control the Stormwind Stockade beneath Stormwind City's canal district. A revolt has driven the guards from its halls. The Stockade lies off the canals between Old Town and the Mage Quarter, holding Stormwind's most dangerous prisoners. Warden Thelwater oversees the underground prison. Its inmates include Defias Brotherhood cutthroats, a Blackrock orc, an ogre, and a Dark Iron dwarf. Bazil Thredd recently led a coordinated riot that overwhelmed the garrison. The surviving guards fled, leaving the prisoners in control of the halls.

Stormy Potential. Stormy Potential is a quest in Durotar given by the goblin Rezlak near Drygulch Ravine. Hoping to protect his trade caravan against marauding harpies, Rezlak seeks to supercharge a depleted orb using the potent electrical organs of native thunder lizards. Near the shadow of Drygulch Ravine in Durotar, the goblin Rezlak found himself facing two problems: a caravan under constant threat from local harpies, and an intact magical orb completely depleted of power. Remembering the pragmatic advice of Ratchet's chief engineer Gazlowe—to seize opportunity whenever it knocks—Rezlak hatched an ambitious plan to solve both problems at once by supercharging the dormant device.

Stout to Kadrell. Stout to Kadrell is an Alliance delivery quest that leads travelers out of the frozen heights of Dun Morogh and into the temperate valley of Loch Modan. Entrusted with a cask of Rejold Barleybrew's newly perfected Shimmer Stout, you carry the potent brew across the territorial border to share with Mountaineer Kadrell on patrol in Thelsamar. After tasting the newly finished Shimmer Stout created by his brother Rejold, Mountaineer Barleybrew is convinced it is too good to keep entirely within Dun Morogh. Stationed at the eastern border post guarding the mountain passes, Barleybrew looks out toward his kin guarding neighboring lands. Dwarven mountaineering can be a cold, grueling assignment, and a stout heart calls for stout drink. Wanting an honest appraisal from a fellow patrolman on the line, Barleybrew sends a cask eastward with passing travelers bound for Loch Modan.

Stoutlager Inn. The Stoutlager Inn is the lively heart of Thelsamar and a primary haven for travelers in Loch Modan. Tucked beneath the rolling hills of the loch, it offers warm hearths, strong dwarven ale, and a bustling gathering place for adventurers and locals alike. Situated squarely in the settlement of Thelsamar, the Stoutlager Inn serves as the center of community life for western Loch Modan. Miners, mountaineers, and wayfarers passing between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands stop here to trade rumors, secure lodging, and share hearty drafts of dwarven brew. While the wilderness beyond Thelsamar grows increasingly hostile with trogg and kobold activity, the thick stone walls and roaring fires of the Stoutlager provide a dependable sanctuary.

Stoutmantle's Response to Solomon. Gryan Stoutmantle sends a hard answer from Sentinel Hill to Lakeshire. His dispatch tells Magistrate Solomon that the People's Militia cannot spare a single soldier for Redridge Mountains. Magistrate Solomon of Lakeshire asks Sentinel Hill for reinforcements as Blackrock orcs and gnolls press his town. Gryan Stoutmantle replies in writing with sorrow for Lakeshire's losses, but Westfall faces a war of its own. The People's Militia formed from desperation after the Crown withdrew its garrison. Farmers and volunteers now fight the Defias Brotherhood alone. Stoutmantle's forces are already bleeding and stretched thin, with no men to spare for another abandoned frontier.

Strahad Farsan. Strahad Farsan is a master human warlock who dwells in a secluded stone tower overlooking Ratchet in the Barrens. Renowned across faction lines, he operates outside conventional Alliance and Horde politics, training aspiring summoners in the dangerous arts of binding higher demons. Practitioners of fel magic from Stormwind, Orgrimmar, and the Undercity alike seek his severe guidance. Perched on the bluffs above the goblin port of Ratchet, Strahad Farsan's tower stands apart from the bustling trade docks below. Ratchet's neutrality offers Strahad the freedom to conduct perilous demonic summonings away from the prying eyes of Alliance magistrates or Horde shamans. Surrounded by his acolytes, he studies the deeper mysteries of the Twisting Nether in relative seclusion, unbothered by petty territorial squabbles.

Strahnbrad. Strahnbrad is a ruined human settlement nestled in the northeastern heights of the Alterac Mountains, near the border of the Western Plaguelands. Once famous as the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's early defense against Blackrock orc raiders, the town has since fallen into decay and serves as a fortified stronghold for the criminal Syndicate. Originally a holding of the Kingdom of Alterac before being absorbed into Lordaeron following the Second War, Strahnbrad's misfortune began on the eve of the Third War. Blackrock clan orcs raided the settlement to take human sacrifices for the Burning Legion, leading Prince Arthas Menethil and the Knights of the Silver Hand to ride to its defense. Though Arthas drove the raiders away and slew their slave master, the town was heavily bloodied. When Lordaeron crumbled beneath the Scourge shortly thereafter, Strahnbrad was abandoned to the elements.

Strange Alliance. Captain Pentigast sees luck in the way the centaur clans of Desolace fight each other, since as one force they could not be stopped. The Gelkis are locked in brutal war with the Magram, so Pentigast sends you to Uthek the Wise in southwestern Desolace to seek an alliance. Captain Pentigast counts it good fortune that the centaur clans war on one another, for joined together they could not be stopped. Pentigast wants to push that edge. The Gelkis and Magram are locked in brutal war, so striking at the Magram might win the Gelkis over.

Strange Smelling Powder. Strange Smelling Powder is an enigmatic residue uncovered during investigations into suspicious sabotage around Loch Modan. Feared to be an unstable demolition agent, it prompts Chief Engineer Hinderweir to send an urgent courier north to seek out a demolition expert. Discovered amid signs of sabotage threatening Loch Modan's infrastructure, this peculiar powder immediately raised alarm for Chief Engineer Hinderweir. Its pungent odor and fine consistency suggest an engineered demolition compound rather than standard mining blast powder. Unsure of the mixture's chemical nature or origin, Hinderweir refuses to tamper with it himself, knowing that even a slight spark could trigger disaster.

Strangely Marked Box. A Strangely Marked Box is a piece of cargo discovered inside the harnesses strapped to dead sea turtles along the Darkshore coastline. Its mysterious exterior bears the runic script of the serpentine naga, offering night elf scholars proof that these sea creatures did not strand themselves by accident. While several giant sea turtles and sea creatures simply wash ashore along Darkshore's mist-veiled beaches, others tell a far more ominous tale. Scattered carcasses bear the splintered remnants of riding harnesses and abandoned carriages bound straight to their shells. Within the ruins of these buckled contraptions lie sealed containers covered in foreign, sinuous runes. Scavenging Greymist murlocs frequently take up residence in the hollow ribcages and broken wagons, picking at the carrion and guarding whatever remnants were left behind.

Stranglethorn Fever. In Booty Bay, Fin Fizracket lies sick with Stranglethorn Fever, a deadly virus. He says the only cure is the heart of Mokk the Savage, an elusive white beast, and that he is dying. Fin Fizracket is stammering and fading, sure that he has caught Stranglethorn Fever. He says the only cure is to eat the heart of Mokk the Savage, an elusive white beast. Witch Doctor Unbagwa is the only one who can summon the creature, and Fin sends you to find Unbagwa in a hidden cave on the southern cape, the Spirit Den.

Stranglethorn Fever. Deep within Stranglethorn Vale, Witch Doctor Unbagwa claims to know how to draw out the beast known as Mokk the Savage. Before communion with the spirits can begin, the witch doctor requires ten Gorilla Fangs as an offering. Once the ritual commences, defending the troll from agitated jungle beasts is necessary to lure the creature forth. Witch Doctor Unbagwa possesses the ritual knowledge needed to summon Mokk the Savage out of the surrounding jungle. To begin the incantation, the witch doctor demands ten Gorilla Fangs. Communing with the spirits carries a heavy risk, as the ritual chant draws the attention of other gorilla beasts in the vicinity, demanding protection while the magic does its work.

Stratholme. Stratholme was once the jewel of the Eastweald and the second greatest city in the Kingdom of Lordaeron. During the Third War, it became the site of Prince Arthas Menethil's infamous culling after its citizens consumed grain tainted by the Plague of Undeath. Today, the ruined metropolis still burns, serving as the Scourge's primary stronghold in northern Lordaeron. Long before its downfall, Stratholme stood as a cornerstone of northern civilization. Emerging centuries ago from the Arathi expansion into the Eastweald, it flourished into Lordaeron's second-largest settlement, renowned for holy shrines and sacred water capable of resisting dark sorcery. Prior to the Second War, Archbishop Alonsus Faol gathered at the city's chapel to establish the Order of the Knights of the Silver Hand, ordaining legends like Uther the Lightbringer. Throughout that war, Stratholme served as a vital port, supply hub, and northern oil refinery for the Alliance of Lordaeron, enduring an assault by the Old Horde before rebuilding in victory.

Stratholme (Classic). Stratholme, once northern Lordaeron's proudest jewel and the birthplace of the Silver Hand, is now a burning ruin serving as the Scourge's regional capital. Divided between the fanatical Scarlet Crusade and Baron Rivendare's undead legions, the cursed city remains locked in endless, violent war. Before the Third War, Stratholme was the northern powerhouse of Lordaeron and the sacred birthplace of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Its fate was sealed when Prince Arthas purged the city, slaughtering his own subjects after infected grain brought the plague within its walls. Left smoldering and ruined, Stratholme was claimed by the Scourge. Today, under the overarching authority of the lich Kel'Thuzad and the field command of Baron Rivendare, the city serves as the primary base for undead power in the Plaguelands.

Stratholme Main Gate. The Stratholme Main Gate stands as the grand, burning entrance to Lordaeron's northern metropolis in the northwestern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct access through the city's ruined avenues toward King's Square and the crusader fortifications within. Stratholme was once the pride of northern Lordaeron, famed as the birthplace of the Order of the Silver Hand. Today, its colossal arched main gates mark the threshold of an ongoing nightmare. It was here during the Third War that Prince Arthas turned on his mentor, Uther the Lightbringer, and purged his own citizens before the Plague of Undeath could claim them. The city has burned relentlessly ever since, transformed into the primary Scourge stronghold in the region.

Stratholme Service Entrance. The Stratholme Service Entrance is a fortified rear gateway located at Eastwall Gate in the northern Eastern Plaguelands. It provides direct, covert access into the Scourge-controlled eastern quarter of the burning city, bypassing the grand front gates. While the monumental Main Gate of Stratholme opens into King's Square and provides a route toward the Scarlet Bastion, the Service Entrance breaches the city's eastern fortification at Eastwall Gate. Today, it leads directly into the corrupted heart of the metropolis: Elders' Square and the blighted pathways leading toward Baron Rivendare's slaughterhouses.

Strigid Owl Feather. Strigid Owl Feathers are gathered from the wild strigid owls nesting within the boughs of Teldrassil. While natural forest plumage, they are sought after by questionable figures seeking raw materials for their covert dealings.

Stromgarde Badges. In Stromgarde, the Syndicate is fighting a contingent of militia, and its leaders pay gold for every badge taken from a fallen militiaman. At Refuge Pointe, Captain Nials wants those badges recovered. In Stromgarde the Syndicate is at war with a contingent of militia. To push their followers into fighting the better-trained soldiers, Syndicate leaders pay gold for each badge taken from a slain militiaman. Captain Nials calls them cutthroats and will not let them keep trophies of the brave fallen, so you are sent into the Syndicate-held part of Stromgarde to hunt for the badges and bring them back to Refuge Pointe. Nials wants the Syndicate to learn it cannot profit from the dead.

Stromgarde Keep. Stromgarde Keep is the battered, divided capital of the fallen human kingdom of Stromgarde in the Arathi Highlands. Once the proud cradle of human civilization known as Strom, the fortress is now partitioned between hostile Syndicate rogues, invading Boulderfist ogres, and a desperate remnant of royal defenders under Prince Galen Trollbane. Long before it bore its current name, this fortress was founded nearly three millennia ago as Strom, the first capital of the unified human empire of Arathor under King Thoradin. It served as the staging ground for humanity's victory against the forest trolls and was the birthplace of human wizardry, where high elven magi tutored the first hundred human spellcasters. Over centuries, as younger sister kingdoms like Dalaran, Lordaeron, and Stormwind rose and prospered, Strom's influence waned. Renamed Stromgarde by the stubborn Trollbane dynasty who stayed behind, it remained a proud warrior bastion throughout the Second War, anchoring the Alliance of Lordaeron against the Orcish Horde.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus has stopped in the Badlands to work on shackles of elemental binding. To test some offensive spells and a few pieced-together gizmos, Lotwil needs small stone shards from the lesser rock elementals nearby. Here in the Badlands, Lotwil Veriatus is working on a project: shackles of elemental binding. Once finished, they would let mages summon still stronger elementals for even greater uses. To get started, Lotwil wants ten small stone shards, easily taken from the lesser rock elementals in the hills immediately west.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus praises you as abler than all of Lotwil's apprentices combined, and wants the next step of the tests. This time the need is three large stone slabs, pieces best found on rock elementals. The next parts of Lotwil Veriatus's work need more strength. Rock elementals have larger, sturdier bodies, so they are likelier to carry pieces big enough for the tests. Lotwil points you further west, or southeast along the edges of the mountains, and has you gather three large stone slabs. Lotwil needs a while to test the smaller pieces you brought before.

Study of the Elements: Rock. Lotwil Veriatus needs one more part from the elementals of the Badlands: bracers of rock binding, taken from greater rock elementals. By Lotwil's reckoning they are enough to gauge the strength of Lotwil's own shackles. After the stone slabs, Lotwil Veriatus asks for one last part from the Badlands' elementals. Bracers of rock binding, taken from greater rock elementals, should let Lotwil judge the strength of the shackles under construction. Lotwil's scrying showed a group of the elementals southwest, near some ogres, if memory serves. Five bracers are wanted, so there are spares, since Servo is notorious for misplacing reagents and research.

text.enUS: Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbone. Sturdy Dragonmaw Shinbones are durable skeletal trophies gathered from the renegade Dragonmaw orcs in the Wetlands. Required by armor crafter Velora Nitely in the Undercity, they serve as reinforcement struts for bespoke warrior armor. When forging brutal leg guards for frontline warriors, smiths require raw components that can endure severe punishment. In the Undercity, Velora Nitely prizes the skeletal density of the renegade Dragonmaw orcs entrenched at the Angerfang Encampment in the central Wetlands. Dragonmaw orcs are known for their thick, sturdy frames, making their shins well suited to serve as structural bracers. However, not every collected bone can withstand the strain; warriors must test each piece with their bare hands, discarding those that snap under pressure.

Sully Balloo's Letter. Sully Balloo's Letter is a waterlogged, tender missive recovered from the sunken remains of a dwarven soldier beneath the Thandol Span. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it represents the quiet personal tragedies lingering beneath the grand conflicts of Khaz Modan. Beneath the massive stone pillars of the Thandol Span, connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands, lies the skeletal remains of a dwarf pinned deep under the rushing water. Clutched in his grasp is a fragile, waterlogged envelope containing this letter. Written with painstaking care in his final days or hours, it begins with the poignant words, 'My dear Sara....' Though the parchment has suffered from prolonged submersion, the ink still holds the enduring love of a dwarven defender who never made it back home to the city of Ironforge.

Sully Balloo's Letter. Recovered from a drowned skeleton beneath the shattered arches of the Thandol Span, this waterlogged letter contains the dying words of a dwarven soldier named Sully Balloo. Addressed to his wife Sara in Ironforge, it carries the final thoughts of a defender lost beneath the icy river waters during the battles for the bridge. Beneath the massive stone pilings supporting the Thandol Span—the crucial land bridge linking the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands—rests the drowned skeleton of a fallen dwarf. Still clutched in his skeletal grasp is a water-damaged envelope that barely survives handling. Written with painstaking care amid the fires of battle, the pages open with the tender phrase, 'My dear Sara...', preserving the soldier's voice long after the tides claimed him.

Summoning Shadra. Master Gadrin gives you a parchment to read at the altar of Shadra'Alor, deep in the Witherbark realm of the Hinterlands, to summon Shadra the spider god. Her venom is then to be carried to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Gadrin's parchment is meant to be read at Shadra'Alor's altar, deep within the Witherbark realm of the Hinterlands. Doing so calls up Shadra the spider god. She must be defeated there, and her venom taken to Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill.

Summoning the Princess. Theldurin the Lost says Myzrael must be beaten while she is still growing, before her strength is enough to challenge those who hold her captive. At the Shards of Myzrael you call her forth, defeat her, and bind her Eldritch Shackles to the Shards. Theldurin wants Myzrael stopped before her power swells enough to set her against her captors. Some claim she can be controlled; Theldurin asks why, then, the giants bothered to chain her at all.

Sun Rock Retreat. Sun Rock Retreat is a hidden Horde sanctuary nestled high within the central peaks of the Stonetalon Mountains, just south of Mirkfallon Lake. Dominated by tauren and orcish forces, it serves as the Horde's primary staging ground and supply post in the region. Beyond its strategic utility, the settlement rests upon sacred ground long revered by the tauren for its deep spiritual resonance. Tucked away in a mountain basin south of Mirkfallon Lake, Sun Rock Retreat has long held spiritual importance for the tauren. According to ancient tradition, An'she, the Sun, kissed the very mountain peak where the village stands. For generations before the Horde's arrival, tauren shamans and pilgrims journeyed here to perform rituals bridging the mortal veil, drawing strength from the land's strong bond to the spirit world.

Sundown Marsh. Sundown Marsh marks the deepest, westernmost reaches of the Wetlands where stagnant waters meet treacherous wildlife. Despite the prowling raptors, oozes, and gnolls, an eccentric pair maintains a solitary homestead along its muddy borders. Sundown Marsh sits tucked into the northwest of the Wetlands, characterized by deep water, thick mud, and a dense population of predators. Giant crocolisks, shifting oozes, roaming raptors, and territorial Mosshide gnolls roam freely through the mist. The hazardous terrain keeps most passing travelers strictly to the main cobblestone road connecting Menethil Harbor to Ironforge, leaving this deep corner largely untamed.

Sunken Treasure. Now that they are full-fledged Blackwater Raiders, Professor Phizzlethorpe and Doctor Draxlegauge are to help Mr. O'Breen find the lost elven treasure. To search the dark sea for the gems, the professor needs your protection while he charges a pair of goggles at an enchanted stone in a cave. The gems are next to impossible to find in the dark sea without help, so Doctor Draxlegauge has built goggles for the search. They need charging with power from the enchanted stone, in a cave a short way uphill. The cave is cursed, though: those who draw near are ambushed. Professor Phizzlethorpe asks you to defend him while he draws the stone's energy into the goggles.

Sunken Treasure. After the first part of Sunken Treasure, Doctor Draxlegauge lends you his Goggles of Gem Hunting and asks you to collect ten elven gems from the sea floor for Captain O'Breen, then bring the goggles back. Down on the sea floor, the gems have lain so many years that they have hardened into thick stone. The power built into the goggles lets you find them regardless, and Doctor Draxlegauge is proud of the gnomish ingenuity behind them. He lends you the goggles so you can gather the lost gems for Captain O'Breen.

Sunken Treasure. Doctor Draxlegauge hands you the elven gems and sends you to carry them to Captain O'Breen. After a few weeks among pirates, he and the professor know that holding on to their treasure is unhealthy. Doctor Draxlegauge does not want Captain O'Breen kept waiting, since the captain will want to see the elven gems for himself. After weeks among these pirates, the doctor and the professor have learned that being caught holding on to pirate treasure is bad for their health. He hands you the gems to carry to O'Breen, who waits at the bridge.

Sunken Treasure. After the previous step in the Sunken Treasure chain, Shakes O'Breen is stuck where he is and needs word taken to Fleet Master Seahorn at Booty Bay. He asks you to carry a sample gem as proof of the find. Shakes O'Breen wants Fleet Master Seahorn to hear of the find right away, yet he cannot easily get away. The tide is too low, and the creatures they disturbed are watching every move. He asks you to help the Blackwater Raiders by telling Seahorn in Booty Bay that the treasure is found and more is being brought up. A sample elven gem goes with you as proof.

Sunken Treasure. Fleet Master Seahorn, whose ships cannot sail from Booty Bay until they restock, asks you to carry a secret letter to Shakes O'Breen, busy off the Arathi coast. Fleet Master Seahorn sizes you up as the adventurous sort. His ships cannot leave Booty Bay until they have restocked, and he says heavy things are brewing both here and abroad. He needs top secret correspondence carried to Shakes O'Breen off the Arathi coast, and he asks whether he can trust you to deliver the message safely and in confidence.

Sunnyglade. Sunnyglade was once a wealthy, prosperous human settlement belonging to the kingdom of Stormwind during the First War. Devastated and eventually abandoned as the front lines collapsed, the ruined settlement now languishes under the dark influence of the Twilight's Hammer cult. Before the First War tore southern Azeroth apart, Sunnyglade was celebrated for its wealth and comfortable prosperity. That peace was violently shattered when the Old Horde invaded. Orc raiding parties attacked the town and enslaved its surviving residents, leaving only a lone wizard's tower intact to study the arcane arts of human conjurers. Though Stormwind forces mounted an effort to rescue the captive peasants and rebuild the settlement, the surrounding Riverglades were steadily swallowed by the advancing Horde. Deeming the outer province lost, Stormwind's commanders eventually withdrew their resources to defend the homeland, leaving Sunnyglade to ruin.

Sunscorched Shell. Sunscorched Shells are the sturdy remnants of wyvern eggs gathered beneath the roosts of Highperch in Thousand Needles. Hardened by the harsh desert heat, they are prized by skilled armorcrafters who can render them into a protective lacquer for mail links. Perched high upon the mesa needles of southern Kalimdor, Highperch wyverns lay eggs that endure relentless desert sun and searing winds. The discarded shell fragments accumulate beneath their roosts, baked to remarkable hardness by the arid climate. While seemingly little more than brittle refuse to a casual wanderer, these sunscorched remains possess natural structural resilience that makes them an intriguing reagent for specialized artisans.

Sunscorched Shells. In Darnassus, the armorer Mathiel collaborates with the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard to refine a new mailcrafting technique. He tasks warriors with traveling to Thousand Needles to gather durable wyvern eggshells from the heights of Highperch. Mathiel works out of the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus, but his trade takes him far beyond traditional night elven techniques. He maintains correspondence with Furen Longbeard, an accomplished dwarven armorer in Stormwind. Inspired by Furen's metallurgy and armor-smithing discoveries, Mathiel seeks to forge a suit of mail reinforced by natural components capable of withstanding extreme strain. To test this hybrid theory, he requires exotic materials that cannot be found anywhere near Teldrassil.

Suntara Stones. Dorius Stonetender is badly hurt in Searing Gorge, light-headed, with the world spinning and bleeding inside. He says he must get back to Ironforge and begs for your help to get him there. Dorius groans that he is badly injured. He feels light-headed, the world is spinning, and he is bleeding internally. His one wish is to get back to Ironforge, and he asks you to help him make the journey.

Suntara Stones. A singed letter that Dorius let fall is written to his brother. It tells of the Suntara stones, which are real and in the hands of the Dark Irons, whose leader Lathoric the Black uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. It is meant for Thorius at the Hall of Explorers in Ironforge, and you are the one to carry it there. In the letter, Dorius writes to his brother that if it is being read, he is gone. The stones exist, and the Dark Irons hold them. Their leader, Lathoric the Black, uses their power to enslave Dorius's excavation team. The team was taken to the cauldron, and their minds are twisted as they toil by day and by night to finish something called Obsidion. Dorius begs his brother to help them, his final wish, and asks that those who bring the letter be thanked.

Super Reaper 6000. Super Reaper 6000 is a quest offered by the disgruntled goblin tinkerer Ziz Fizziks in the Windshear Crag of the Stonetalon Mountains. Looking to curry favor with his new boss Sputtervalve, Ziz hires adventurers to infiltrate the local Venture Company logging operation and steal the schematic blueprints for a colossal woodcutting machine designed by his rival, the gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle. The Venture Trading Company has carved an industrial scar straight into the heart of the Stonetalon Mountains, ruthlessly deforesting Windshear Crag. Yet beneath the smog and spinning blades lies petty corporate rivalry. Ziz Fizziks, a goblin engineer recently cast out of the Venture Company's ranks, has found employment with Sputtervalve. Eager to cement his position and show off his value, Ziz seeks to procure the Venture Company's most prized mechanical asset: the blueprints for their massive automated lumber engine, the Super Reaper 6000.

text.enUS: Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints. The Super Reaper 6000 Blueprints are the technical schematics for an enormous mechanized woodcutter deployed by the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains. Designed under the supervision of the gnome engineer Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle, the plans are heavily coveted by his disgruntled goblin rivals. The Venture Company's relentless clear-cutting operation in Windshear Crag relies on massive mechanized lumber harvesters known as Super Reapers. To the utter dismay of traditional goblin engineers, the company placed a gnome named Gerenzo in charge of designing the Super Reaper 6000 model. These blueprints contain the schematics for the contraption, carried by Venture Co. operators working the machinery across the crag. When the goblin engineer Ziz Fizziks was ousted from the operation, he was quickly hired by Sputtervalve to steal the designs. However, deciphering Gerenzo's dense, eccentric gnomish technical notations proves to be almost as difficult as taking the blueprints by force.

Super Sticky. Tran'rek in Gadgetzan wants a fast profit and has a new idea: a super sticky glue. The tar for it must come from beasts in northern Un'Goro Crater, near the tar pits, and Tran'rek will share a little of the profit. Tran'rek hopes this newest idea will bring quick gold, and offers you a little of the profit. Ordinary tar is not sticky enough. Twelve samples are wanted, taken from creatures dwelling near the tar pits of northern Un'Goro Crater.

Supervisor Fizsprocket. Supervisor Fizsprocket is a high-ranking Venture Company overseer stationed within the mining tunnels of Mulgore. Charged by Morin Cloudstalker with putting an end to the goblin enterprise's calculated pillaging, Horde adventurers enter the mine to eliminate him and recover his detailed clipboard. Documents recovered from a destroyed Venture Company caravan revealed that the Venture Company was not merely digging for ore—they were deliberately formulating schemes to drive the tauren from Mulgore entirely. By uprooting the locals, the rapacious corporation sought unchecked freedom to strip the rolling hills and deep subterranean veins of every natural resource.

Supervisor Raelen. At Eastvale Logging Camp, Supervisor Raelen keeps timber moving toward Stormwind. She manages the laborers, tracks daily quotas, and oversees the lumber supply. Supervisor Raelen directs the woodcutters at Eastvale Logging Camp, near Marshal Patterson and the camp’s wagons. The camp stands on the edge of eastern Elwynn, near the Redridge Mountains, where the work brings its share of trouble. Raelen coordinates the crews and keeps them focused on their quotas despite hazards in the surrounding woods. She sees that gathered timber is processed, bundled, and sent on toward Stormwind.

Supplies for Sven. Supplies for Sven is a bundle of vital provisions packaged in Darkshire and destined for Sven Yorgen's secluded camp. Surrounded by the horrors of Duskwood, Sven and his small band rely on sympathetic townspeople like the Carevin family to sustain their vigil against the shadows. Carrying survival gear and basic necessities through Duskwood is no simple chore. Sven Yorgen and his handful of followers camp in the northwestern wilderness of the woods, far from the safety of Darkshire. Their numbers are so depleted and their watch so demanding that they cannot spare a single fighter to make the trek into town. This parcel represents a lifeline sent by the Carevin family, ensuring that the isolated camp has the food, bandages, and materials needed to hold their ground.

Supplies for the Crossroads. Supplies for the Crossroads is a Horde task issued by Thork to recover essential provisions taken during Razormane quilboar raids. By reclaiming these lost supply crates from thorny encampments, adventurers help sustain the Crossroads amidst constant regional conflict. The Crossroads serves as the central junction for Horde travel, trade, and defense throughout the Barrens. Keeping such a hub operational requires a steady stream of cargo flowing from Durotar and Mulgore. When a supply caravan is ambushed, the outpost faces immediate shortages of provisions, tools, and arms vital for enduring the harsh wilderness.

Supplies from Darkshire. Supplies from Darkshire is an Alliance quest in Duskwood where the hermit Abercrombie asks passing travelers to run an errand to Darkshire on his behalf. Claiming to be too frail to make the dangerous trek through the haunted forest, he seeks a rare material known as Ghost Hair Thread from Madame Eva. Isolated in a shack north of Raven Hill Cemetery in western Duskwood, the hermit Abercrombie cuts a pitiful figure. When approached by travelers, he laments his old age and frail body, claiming he cannot survive the journey through the woods to purchase goods from Darkshire. His requested errand appears simple: travel back to the township's town square and speak with Madame Eva to procure a spool of Ghost Hair Thread.

Supplies to Auberdine. Supplies to Auberdine is an escort mission where Alliance adventurers protect Feero Ironhand as he carries critical provisions and messages from Maestra's Post northward toward Darkshore. Given the growing menace radiating from the Tower of Althalaxx and the presence of hostile infiltrators in Ashenvale, safe passage cannot be taken for granted. Maestra's Post sits on the western frontier of Ashenvale, a quiet outpost caught between the wild tensions of the forest and the troubled lands of Darkshore. Following investigations into the sinister activity surrounding the Tower of Althalaxx, Delgren the Purifier gathers vital supplies and intelligence bound for Sentinel Starbreeze in Auberdine. Rather than risking solitary couriers, the outpost relies on armed escorts to accompany Feero Ironhand as he treks along the forest road.

text.enUS: Supplies to Private Thorsen. Krazek in Booty Bay hires a courier to haul miscellaneous goblin supplies north to Lieutenant Doren's camp. Local troll aggression has halted routine shipments, requiring an outside hand to ensure the goods reach Private Thorsen near the northern border. Lieutenant Doren and his outfit stationed near the border between Stranglethorn Vale and Duskwood rely on regular shipments arranged through Krazek. Persistent attacks from local trolls have made standard delivery hazardous, prompting the goblin merchant to contract an independent courier. The package must travel all the way up the jungle road, with Private Thorsen designated to receive it either in their camp northwest of the road or along his patrol route to the south.

Supplies to Tannok. Supplies to Tannok is an errand entrusted to fledgling adventurers departing Coldridge Valley through the dangerous mountain pass into greater Dun Morogh. The gnome tinkerer Hands Springsprocket sends a crate of needed provisions to Tannok Frosthammer at the Thunderbrew Distillery inn in Kharanos, bypassing the trogg-infested trails that have severed routine trade. Coldridge Valley is traditionally the proving ground and sanctuary for young Ironforge dwarves and exiled Gnomeregan survivors, but recent events have strained its connection to the rest of Dun Morogh. Trogg incursions have overrun Coldridge Pass, leaving the mountain defile perilous to cross. Mountaineers are spread thin guarding settlements and defensive perimeters, delaying scheduled supply escorts for days on end.

Supply and Demand. Drizzlik, a leathercrafter in Booty Bay, claims to be the finest in the South Seas. Director Riddlevox of the Tinkers' Union has placed an order for twelve Excelsior-line boots, and Drizzlik needs skins from crocolisks by the northern Stranglethorn river to start shaping them. Drizzlik brags that this leatherwork is famed everywhere as exquisite, a connoisseur's choice. The latest order comes from Director Riddlevox, the Tinkers' Union's chief inventor, who wants a dozen of the Excelsior-line boots he favors, among Drizzlik's best sellers. To begin shaping them, Drizzlik needs skins from the crocolisks by the northern Stranglethorn river. The equipment stands ready, and leaving so important a customer unsatisfied would be a poor idea.

Supplying the Front. Supplying the Front is an early task for developing dwarven blacksmiths, commissioned by Tormus Deepforge in Ironforge. It tasks smiths with forging weapons and armor to support the Mountaineers stationed in Loch Modan against the relentless trogg incursions. In the great forges of Ironforge, master smith Tormus Deepforge keeps a keen eye on the Kingdom of Khaz Modan's borders. The Mountaineers defending the valleys of Loch Modan are hard-pressed by sudden trogg attacks spilling out from unearthed ruins and caverns. Keeping their defensive lines supplied requires a non-stop rotation of fresh blades, belts, and fittings, prompting local artisans to pitch in.

Supplying the Sepulcher. Supplying the Sepulcher is a logistical task issued by Deathguard Podrig at the Sepulcher in Silverpine Forest. To keep the local Deathguard detachment equipped against feral horrors and Scourge prowling the woods, an urgent weapon requisition must be routed via bat handler Karos Razok toward weapon suppliers in the Undercity. While Deathguard Podrig reports that the Sepulcher is relatively well-stocked, continuous attrition in Silverpine Forest consumes equipment at an alarming rate. Between feral beasts, prowling Scourge remnants, and aggressive local threats, frontline gear wears down or gets abandoned in skirmishes. Under orders from Executor Hadrec, Podrig drafts a direct requisition order addressed to Gordon Wendham, a weapon dealer operating out of the capital. Securing a steady flow of replacement blades and armor is essential if the Forsaken hope to retain their fragile footholds outside Tirisfal Glades.

Surena Caledon. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, Gakin seeks his former pupil and a bloodstone choker. He sends an aspiring warlock after Surena Caledon, who betrayed him to join the Defias Brotherhood. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novices the forbidden arts of fel summoning. He once took a young woman named Surena Caledon as his pupil. He admired her natural magical talent and her beauty. Surena left her studies and Gakin's favor, then fled Stormwind with her lover, Erlan Drudgemoor, to join the Defias Brotherhood.

Surena's Choker. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder seeks the choker he gave his former apprentice, Surena Caledon. After Surena fled to join the Defias Brotherhood, Gakin sent aspiring acolytes to take it back by force. Gakin the Darkbinder works quietly beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind, where he took Surena Caledon on as a promising student of the dark arts. Drawn to her youthful charm and magical aptitude, he gave her a valuable bloodstone choker to aid her studies. Surena abandoned her training and fled with Erlan Drudgemoor, a rogue aligned with the Defias Brotherhood. Gakin will not leave a potent artifact in a traitor’s hands. He sends initiates seeking mastery over the void to find Surena at the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch and reclaim the necklace by force. Their deed will show where true loyalty lies.

Suspicious Hoofprints. Tracks of hooves stretch off from the Shady Rest Inn, whose bare frame still smokes. A few can be seen clearly, while more rows are nearly lost in the marsh's soft ground. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to report them to. The Shady Rest Inn is a bare frame now, still smoking, and trails of hoofprints stretch off from it. Some impressions are easy to see; others can hardly be made out in the soft ground. Krog at Brackenwall Village should hear about them.

Suspicious Hoofprints. Hoofprints trail away from the smoking remains of the Shady Rest Inn. A few are easy to see, while others are nearly lost in the soft marsh mud. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to report them to. Rows of prints run off from the Shady Rest Inn, whose ruin is still smoking. A handful of the impressions are plain to see, while further rows are all but invisible in the marsh's soft mud. Captain Garran Vimes, in Theramore, should hear of them.

Suzetta Gallina. At the Gallina Winery in Stormwind City, Suzetta Gallina tends the family wine business. Suzetta Gallina helps run the Gallina Winery along Stormwind's Canals. The shop offers wines imported from across the kingdom or crafted there. Her family supplies taverns, nobles, and common folk. Suzetta is no figure in high politics, but her work keeps the capital's trade moving through troubled times.

Sven Yorgen. Sven Yorgen is a grieving farmer camped on the northern edge of the Hushed Bank in western Duskwood, accompanied by his companion Lars. Having survived the brutal slaughter of his family at the Yorgen Farmstead, Sven is consumed by a relentless drive to uncover who brought ruin upon his home and exact vengeance. Sven was born before the First War, old enough to recall the days before the region became shrouded in gloom following Medivh's fall. For years he worked the soil at the Yorgen Farmstead in southern Duskwood alongside his wife and children. That quiet existence ended in sudden violence when mysterious Dark Riders raided his homestead while he was away, butchering his family and turning the farm into a graveyard.

Sven's Camp. Sven's Camp is an Alliance quest in Duskwood that uncovers a crucial clue regarding the tragedy at the Yorgen homestead. By unearthing a buried, untitled journal from a mound of loose dirt on the abandoned farm, adventurers piece together who witnessed the slaughter of Sven Yorgen's family. Sven Yorgen was away when dark riders struck his farm, returning only to find his family murdered and his farm in ruins. Consumed by grief and vengeance, he sent allies to search the wreckage of the homestead. Hidden beneath a mound of freshly turned earth, a small, dirt-stained book lay buried where a shadowy figure had hastily hidden it.

Sven's Revenge. Driven by grief and vengeance, the hermit Sven Yorgen asks travelers to return to his ruined farmstead in southern Duskwood. While he spent years pursuing the shadowy horsemen who slaughtered his family, a suspicious figure once buried something near his barn that may hold answers. Sven Yorgen was once a simple farmer working the fields in southeastern Duskwood. His life shattered when hooded Dark Riders riding down from Deadwind Pass attacked his homestead, massacring his family while he was away. Returning to the slaughter, Sven caught sight of an unknown figure skulking near the barn, frantically burying something in the earth. Sven chose vengeance, setting off immediately to hunt down the killers, leaving whatever had been concealed behind.

Swamplight Manor. Swamplight Manor is an ironically named, ramshackle wooden shack nestled deep within Witch Hill in Dustwallow Marsh. It serves as the eccentric home and kitchen of 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, an isolated recluse known across the mire for his strange culinary appetites. Despite its humble, eerie isolation, the surrounding garden conceals intrigue that catches the attention of both Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Despite what its grandiose title suggests, Swamplight Manor is far from a lordly estate. It is merely a crooked, weather-beaten shack tucked into the haunted wetlands of Witch Hill. Its lone resident, the odd recluse known as 'Swamp Eye' Jarl, lives a solitary existence surrounded by fog, muck, and restless marsh ghosts. Jarl spends his days concocting unusual regional delicacies out of local wildlife, frequently recruiting wandering adventurers to hunt down bizarre ingredients like marsh frog legs and creature eyes to satisfy his strange craft.

Swarming Pillar. The Swarming Pillar is a towering rock formation in the heart of Silithus, thoroughly infested and reshaped by the silithid. Situated just south of Cenarion Hold, the spire takes its name from the relentless clouds of winged insectoids buzzing around its peaks and subterranean entrances. Rising abruptly from the shifting dunes of central Silithus, the Swarming Pillar serves as a grim monument to the unchecked expansion of the silithid. What began as a natural rock formation has been carved and encrusted with the resinous secretions and burrows of the insectoid swarm. Just south of Cenarion Hold, it constantly churns out broods of winged workers and soldiers, whose dark clouds fill the dry desert air and warn travelers to keep their distance.

Swoop Gizzard. A swoop gizzard is an organ harvested from the predatory birds soaring over Mulgore. Highly sought after for traditional folk remedies, it serves as a crucial ingredient for cleansing deadly toxins. Swoops are predatory avian hunters native to the plains and mesas of Mulgore, known for their keen eyesight and scavenging nature. While their feathers and meat serve everyday uses for the tauren, their internal organs—particularly the gizzard—are prized by herbalists and healers. When combined with other potent animal remnants like cougar bones and wolf hearts, the dense muscular organ aids in neutralizing venomous animal bites and halting festering systemic infections.

Swoop Hunting. Swoop Hunting is a rite of tracking and marksmanship offered by Harken Windtotem in Bloodhoof Village. To prove their cleverness and patience, hunters and travelers are challenged to stalk the elusive birds across the rolling plains of Mulgore. Returning with their pristine trophy quills demonstrates both dedication to the hunt and respect for the natural trials of the Earth Mother. The grassy steppes of Mulgore are teeming with beasts, but few test a pursuer's instincts like the native swoop. These large predatory birds blend seamlessly into the skyline and plains, wheeling overhead or skimming low across the tall grass. Unlike lumbering plainstriders or grazing kodo, swoops demand acute focus and swift feet to run down, making their pursuit a traditional proving exercise for younger hunters seeking to earn their standing among the tribes.

Sylvanas Windrunner. Lady Sylvanas Windrunner is the Banshee Queen and supreme ruler of the Forsaken, holding court in the Undercity beneath the ruins of Lordaeron. Once the brave Ranger-General of Silvermoon, she was slain and raised into undeath by Arthas Menethil before breaking free from the Lich King's grip. Now allied with Thrall's Horde out of mutual survival, she is fiercely dedicated to securing a future for her free-willed undead and exacting vengeance upon the Scourge. In life, Lady Sylvanas was the celebrated Ranger-General of Silvermoon, commanding the defense of Quel'Thalas during the Third War. When Prince Arthas Menethil marched the Scourge into the high elven kingdom to reach the Sunwell, Sylvanas fought fiercely to delay his advance. Frustrated by her resistance, Arthas murdered her, but denied her a clean death. He ripped her soul from her corpse and twisted it into a vengeful banshee, forcing her to serve the Scourge and assist in the slaughter of her own people.

Syndicate. The Syndicate is a widespread human criminal organization founded and led by dispossessed nobles of the fallen kingdom of Alterac. Operating out of fortified strongholds across the Alterac Mountains, Hillsbrad Foothills, and the ruins of Stromgarde Keep, they wage an uncompromising war against both the Alliance and the Horde to restore their lost aristocracy. When the kingdom of Alterac collapsed in dishonor following King Aiden Perenolde's treachery during the Second War, its aristocracy was stripped of land and title. Refusing to accept their exile, the remaining Alteraci nobility banded together under the late king's son, Prince Aliden Perenolde. Adopting distinctive orange bandanas and standardizing their ranks with hired thugs, highwaymen, and hedge wizards, they forged the Syndicate. To the outside world, they behave like common brigands, raiding caravans, ambushing travelers, and running extortion rings. In truth, their criminal enterprises exist solely to fund an organized effort to reconquer their ancestral domains and subjugate surrounding lands.

Syndicate Assassins. Magistrate Henry Maleb, newly assigned to Southshore after the previous magistrate was assassinated, believes the Syndicate hired the killers. The trail led to a Syndicate camp north of Tarren Mill, and Maleb wants the members there slain. Magistrate Henry Maleb is the new magistrate of Southshore, assigned after the previous magistrate was assassinated. The assassins were never found, yet Maleb is almost certain the Syndicate hired them. The Syndicate is a gang of thieves, run by villainous nobles from Alterac, a kingdom that has since fallen. Maleb's last clues pointed to a Syndicate camp north of Tarren Mill, which the Horde occupies, and Maleb asks you to slay the Syndicate members found there.

Syral Bladeleaf. Syral Bladeleaf is a night elf resident of Dolanaar in Teldrassil who serves as a liaison for the Council of the Forest. She guides young adventurers who arrive from Shadowglen, directing them toward local caretakers, herbalists, and elders who watch over the crown's delicate boughs. Found standing near the heart of Dolanaar, Syral Bladeleaf helps organize local affairs in the shadow of Teldrassil's canopy. Acting on behalf of the Council of the Forest, she directs newly arrived night elves to community leaders and herbalists across the village and the nearby wilderness. Through her guidance, travelers connect with the botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth and replenish supplies for the village elders.

Syurna. Syurna is a night elf rogue trainer found nestled among the foliage of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus. She mentors aspiring scouts, spies, and covert operatives of the Kaldorei, guiding newly trained rogues on missions that test their stealth and cunning. While Darnassus celebrates the overt martial might of the Sentinels and the spiritual wisdom of the Sisterhood of Elune, the Kaldorei have always relied on shadows and stealth. Located in the Cenarion Enclave, Syurna acts as a trainer and mentor for those who walk an unseen path. She instructs rogues in the fine arts of evasion, lockpicking, and lethal strikes, ensuring that Darnassus possesses sharp eyes and silent blades to defend Teldrassil.

Tabetha. Tabetha is a reclusive, powerful human mage dwelling deep within Dustwallow Marsh at an isolated farmstead in the Quagmire. Far from the politics of Dalaran or Theramore, she instructs aspiring spellcasters and aids those seeking mastery over potent arcane and occult relics. Hidden away in the sodden expanse of Dustwallow Marsh north of the Stonemaul Ruins, Tabetha lives in a secluded shack alongside her apprentices. Surrounding herself with alchemical vials and ancient tomes, she has deliberately chosen solitude over the academic hierarchies of the Eastern Kingdoms. Despite her remote location, her mastery of the arcane is renowned enough that spellcasters across Kalimdor brave beasts and mire alike to seek her guidance.

Tabetha's Farm. Deep in the murkiest reaches of the Quagmire lies Tabetha's Farm, an isolated homestead centered around a small wooden hut, a modest garden, and a private dock. Despite the treacherous marsh surroundings, this sanctuary serves as a hidden redoubt for the hermit mage Tabetha. Tucked away in the western wetlands of Dustwallow Marsh, Tabetha's Farm defies its unforgiving environment. Consisting of a weather-worn hut, small vegetable plots, and a dock for navigating the swamp's murky waterways, the homestead offers a quiet refuge far from the political rivalries of Theramore and Brackenwall Village. Here, the reclusive human sorceress Tabetha lives in near-total seclusion, pursuing esoteric studies of arcane and fel power without interference from Dalaran or local authorities.

Tablet of Verga. The Tablet of Verga is an arcane stone inscribed with demonic runes essential for binding dark entities. Stolen by the sinister Burning Blade cult, it was taken deep into their lair within Skull Rock. Recovering the artifact allows dark practitioners in Orgrimmar to decipher the rituals needed to bind a voidwalker. The Tablet of Verga holds specific ritual runes required to summon and bend creatures of the Nether to a master's will. When the Burning Blade cult managed to steal the tablet, they concealed it within a hidden chest inside Skull Rock, just east of Orgrimmar. For the warlocks working discreetly in the shadows of the Cleft of Shadow, regaining the relic is crucial—not only to study its ancient markings for summoning a voidwalker, but also to deny the fanatical cultists their own dark advantage.

Tahonda Ruins. The Tahonda Ruins are the sun-bleached remnants of an ancient tauren settlement swallowed by the salt and sand of the Shimmering Flats. Little is remembered of the villagers who once lived here, and dangerous Saltstone basilisks now stalk among the decaying tent poles and shredded leather. Situated in the southern reaches of the Shimmering Flats near the pass into Tanaris, the Tahonda Ruins stand as a somber monument to an abandoned tauren past. The village fell long ago, its weathered structures gradually engulfed by shifting white salt crusts. While some suspect the local Saltstone basilisks drove the inhabitants away, odd clues linger on the surviving structures. Two distinct sets of three parallel tears cut through the leather of a ruined lodge, suggesting the village met a violent end at the claws of powerful predators or hostile invaders before the desert claimed what remained.

Tai'jin. Tai'jin is a Darkspear troll priest trainer stationed within the barracks of Razor Hill in Durotar. She guides fledgling priests of the Horde, introducing Darkspear initiates to traditional troll rites such as the Hex of Weakness. Stationed inside the sturdy barracks of Razor Hill, Tai'jin serves as a spiritual mentor for young priests stepping out into Durotar. While orcs predominantly turn to shamanism or dark warlock arts, the Darkspear trolls bring their own distinct communion with the spirits and loas to the Horde. Tai'jin offers foundational teachings in the priesthood, ensuring that new acolytes understand both the balance of light and shadow and the spiritual heritage unique to troll culture.

Taiga Wisemane. Taiga Wisemane is a tauren elder residing in Shadowprey Village along the rugged western coast of Desolace. Watchful of demonic meddling across the barren wastes, he works to thwart the Burning Blade cult entrenched in the region. He directs Horde champions to disrupt demonic rituals and seal open gateways before the Burning Legion gains ground. Though Shadowprey Village is predominantly a Darkspear troll fishing settlement tucked away against the ocean, Taiga Wisemane has taken up station there to monitor the dark sorceries stirring across Desolace. He remains acutely aware of the spiritual corruption bleeding into the soil, keeping his focus fixed eastward where shadow cults and demonic remnants fester among ancient ruins.

Tainted Heart. The Tainted Heart is a blighted floral core extracted from the corrupt flora of Teldrassil. Given to adventurers by the botanist Denalan, it requires magical and nutritive cleansing to rid it of lingering foul energies. Teldrassil's natural balance suffers from an unnatural malady, warping its native plants and beasts. After stripping away foul moss that clung to a blighted growth, Denalan presents this lingering core: the Tainted Heart. Though freed of its outer rot, darkness still permeates the tissue. Denalan seeks to discover whether specially prepared, nutrient-rich earth can counteract the lingering taint and restore life to what was corrupted.

Tainted Keg. The Tainted Keg is a barrel of stolen dwarven stout laced with a lethal Forsaken brew concocted by Apothecary Lydon. Delivered under the guise of refreshments to imprisoned human farmers in Tarren Mill, it serves as a gruesome field test for the Royal Apothecary Society's developing poisons. The keg began its existence as a barrel of Shindigger Stout, plundered from the dwarven riflemen entrenched at Dun Garok. Rather than drinking it, Apothecary Lydon contaminated the hearty ale with his newly refined Elixir of Agony. By lacing an ordinary beverage, the Forsaken crafted an insidious vector designed to slip past suspicion, turning a familiar comforts of the living into a swift death sentence.

Tainted Letter. Drusilla La Salle sends the Tainted Letter to human warlock initiates near Northshire Abbey. It bears her seal and directs them to seek her tutelage discreetly. The Tainted Letter bears Drusilla La Salle’s insignia and reaches initiates returning from nearby kobold camps. While priests, paladins, and soldiers train openly across Northshire Abbey’s lawns, fel practitioners must keep their path quiet. The letter directs novice warlocks to find their mentor near the abbey grounds without drawing the notice of town guards or clerics.

Tainted Letter. At Northshire, Tainted Letter calls novice human warlocks away from the Abbey guards for instruction in the fel arts. Drusilla La Salle entrusts it to Marshal McBride, who delivers it to her recruits. Novice warlocks receive a letter from Marshal McBride after proving themselves against the kobold menace. While priests and paladins study openly in Northshire Abbey, warlocks must tread carefully. Drusilla La Salle's insignia marks the letter, which directs each fledgling spellcaster to her secluded post outside the abbey's main walls before taking on other duties.

Tainted Memorandum. The Tainted Memorandum is a discreet note handed to novice gnome warlocks starting out in Coldridge Valley. Penned by the warlock trainer Alamar Grimm, it urges the reader to cast aside traditional paths and seek out the true power offered by the dark arts. In the chilly dwarven outpost of Anvilmar, practitioners of fel magic are neither celebrated nor widely trusted. For young gnomes dabbling in forbidden arts, the Tainted Memorandum serves as an invitation from Alamar Grimm. The message rejects reliance on the Holy Light or mundane martial steel, pointing instead to the fall of Gnomeregan as proof that conventional methods and tinkering have failed their people. To Grimm, relying on dwarven charity is a dead end; gnomes must seize undeniable power and summon unquestioning minions if they ever hope to secure their own future.

Tainted Memorandum. Tainted Memorandum is an introductory quest for fledgling gnome warlocks taking their first steps in Coldridge Valley. Passed quietly through Sten Stoutarm, the missive summons the neophyte to the shadows of Anvilmar to meet Alamar Grimm, who preaches self-reliance through dark power rather than trust in their dwarven hosts. Even in the frozen outpost of Coldridge Valley, the practice of the dark arts is met with deep suspicion. While helping Sten Stoutarm deal with local threats, young gnome warlocks receive a slipped note. Sten delivers it reluctantly, giving voice to the uneasy truce that allows warlocks in Alliance lands: 'watch yerself... your kind ain't too trusted 'round these parts.'

Tainted Scar. The Tainted Scar is a demon-infested canyon carved into the southwestern Blasted Lands, saturated with foul fel magic from the nearby Dark Portal. It currently serves as the primary redoubt for the remnants of the Burning Legion on Azeroth, commanded by the doomguard Lord Kazzak. Once lush wetlands belonging to the ancient Black Morass, this desolate trench was utterly drained of life and turned the color of dried blood by chaotic fel energies leaking from the Dark Portal. Following Archimonde's defeat at Mount Hyjal during the Third War, surviving forces of the Burning Legion rallied in the south. The colossal ered'ruin Lord Kazzak claimed the Tainted Scar as his stronghold, stationing elite demons across its blackened rises and dispatching dreadful lieutenants like Razelikh the Defiler to hold dominion over the wasted red soils.

Tainted Scroll. The Tainted Scroll is an early quest in Deathknell that directs newly awakened Forsaken warlocks to their trainer, Maximillion. Through this missive, Maximillion invites the initiate to embrace power and dark servitude as a means of securing genuine freedom. Shortly after newly risen Forsaken begin clearing out mindless Scourge remnants around Deathknell, an ominous missive arrives bearing the seal of Maximillion, the local warlock trainer. The scroll beckons the recipient to contemplate the nature of servitude and autonomy before returning to the ruined settlement to speak with him directly.

Takar the Seer. Takar the Seer is an elusive human hermit encamped deep within the Barrens, east of Camp Taurajo. Despite sitting entirely within Horde-dominated territory, he maintains allegiance to the Alliance and assists certain travelers with esoteric occult knowledge. Dwelling alone beneath a simple tent east of Camp Taurajo, Takar the Seer seems out of place amid the dry plains of the Barrens. Surrounding lands are watched constantly by tauren braves and orc patrols, yet Takar remains undisturbed in his remote clearing. Hostile to curious Horde interlopers but rarely eager to initiate violence, he keeps a sharp eye on the horizon and prefers solitude. His isolated existence suggests deliberate seclusion, far from the bustling politics of Stormwind.

Takata Steelblade. Takata Steelblade is an orc warrior stationed at Ghost Walker Post in Desolace. Dispatched from Orgrimmar by Keldran alongside Maurin Bonesplitter, he spearheads the Horde's local campaign against demonic corruption. His primary focus is eradicating the regional satyr population affiliated with the sinister Burning Blade. Takata Steelblade was sent from the capital to Desolace under direct orders from Keldran, an influential figure in Orgrimmar committed to uncovering and purging demonic subversion. Operating out of the isolated Tauren encampment of Ghost Walker Post, Takata coordinates military efforts against the Legion-aligned forces plaguing the barren wastes.

Tal. Tal is the primary wind rider master of Thunder Bluff, tending the city's aerial roost high above the plains of Mulgore. He provides seasoned wyverns to Horde travelers looking to traverse the vast reaches of Kalimdor. Perched upon the central mesa of Thunder Bluff, Tal manages the vital aerial thoroughfare connecting the tauren capital to the rest of the Horde. From his perch, he tends to the loyal wind riders, or wyverns, ensuring they are healthy, well-fed, and prepared for long-distance journeys across Kalimdor's rugged landscapes. Whether sending messengers down to Camp Taurajo or dispatching scouts across the Barrens to Orgrimmar, Tal maintains an indispensable lifeline that keeps the towering mesa city in constant touch with its allies.
