text.enUS: That Shadowvale Green Elixir. Carolai Anise in Brill seeks salvage from the abandoned settlement of Shadowvale, tucked deep within the secluded Whispering Forest. Before the kingdom fell, the village was infamous for distilling Whispering Elixir from strange local herbs—a potent draught that remained prized on the black market even after being outlawed in Lordaeron. Long before the Third War and the arrival of the Scourge, the reclusive inhabitants of Shadowvale brewed a distinct concoction known as Whispering Elixir. Distilled from rare herbs unique to Tirisfal Glades, the draught gained notoriety across northern Lordaeron. Despite being officially outlawed within the Capital City, its unusual properties made it eagerly sought after by mystics, poisoners, and practicing apothecaries willing to skirt royal decrees.

Thazz'ril's Pick. Foreman Thazz'ril accidentally left his favorite enchanted mining pick deep inside the northern cavern during a mineral survey. Now overrun by dangerous beasts, the cave known as the Burning Blade Coven holds the glowing tool awaiting recovery. Foreman Thazz'ril, the supervisor overseeing work details in the Valley of Trials, previously ventured into the northern cavern to prospect for mineral veins. While surveying the rocky interior, he accidentally left behind his prized mining pick. By the time he realized his mistake and returned to fetch it, vicious beasts and hostile inhabitants had overtaken the cavern, forcing the foreman to seek assistance from capable recruits to recover his lost tool.

The Absent Minded Prospector. Archaeologist Hollee has fled to Auberdine after an excavation site in southern Darkshore was overrun by hostile stone golems. Terrified for her senior colleague, she asks travelers to rush south and rescue Prospector Remtravel, an esteemed dwarven scholar who is notoriously blind to mortal danger when engrossed in his research. Dispatched across the sea by the Explorers' League under orders from Master Greywhisker, Archaeologist Hollee was thrilled to apprentice under Prospector Remtravel. Renowned among Ironforge's academic circles for his groundbreaking discoveries, Remtravel was sent to investigate ancient ruins along the untamed coast of Darkshore. However, during an excavation into what appeared to be the remnants of an ancient, great civilization, violent stone golems burst forth from the earth, rapidly overrunning the dig site.

The Absent Minded Prospector. Deep in the southern ruins of Darkshore, Prospector Remtravel refuses to abandon his dig site without a prize to show the Explorers' League. Despite his severe forgetfulness and an infestation of hostile troggs, he insists on uncovering a mysterious fossil before retreating. Ensuring the dwarven researcher survives his erratic search allows word of his safety to reach his assistant back in Auberdine. Remtravel's Dig lies far to the south of Darkshore, nestled among ancient ruins that were supposed to hold forgotten secrets. Instead, the dwarven excavators struck into pockets of savage troggs, driving out the workers and leaving the camp under siege. While most would flee for Auberdine immediately, Prospector Remtravel became fixated on salvaging his findings. Refusing to leave empty-handed, he wanders right into the teeth of danger to recover an elusive fossil to justify the expedition's costs to the Explorers' League.

The Absent Minded Prospector. This errand delivers a strange petrified specimen recovered from the wild beaches of Darkshore to the Explorers' League outpost in Darnassus. Archaeologist Hollee refuses to abandon her distracted colleague in the field, entrusting the specimen's transport to a passing adventurer instead. The fossil's arrival in the night elven capital immediately captures the keen interest of Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker. Prospector Remtravel's excavations along the misty coast of Darkshore have unearthed a curious fossil, but digging deeper matters more to him than protocol. Archaeologist Hollee, unwilling to leave the wandering prospector alone amidst the shore's dangerous beasts and hostile cultists, remains behind to watch over him. In order to get the discovery documented, she requires an Alliance traveler to ferry the specimen up to Darnassus, where the dwarven guild maintains a scholarly delegation.

The Absent Minded Prospector. This quest bridges an excavation mystery from Darkshore across the Great Sea to the Wetlands. Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker entrusts you with a strange Kalimdor fossil, directing you to Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor to unlock its secrets. While examining the strange fossil uncovered in Darkshore, Chief Archaeologist Greywhisker notices a striking resemblance to a relic shown at an Explorers' League conference back in Ironforge. That earlier piece was presented by Archaeologist Flagongut, who was convinced that such fossils held latent powers waiting to be unlocked. Greywhisker believes Flagongut is the only dwarf capable of discerning what makes this Kalimdor find so extraordinary.

The Absent Minded Prospector. This quest marks the final chapter in the search sparked by Prospector Remtravel's excavations in Darkshore. Archaeologist Flagongut in Menethil Harbor seeks to combine Remtravel's finds with his own fossil and the lost Stone of Relu to unlock the ancient relics' hidden powers. What began as an escort mission aiding the distracted Prospector Remtravel in the northern reaches of Darkshore leads across the Great Sea to the marshlands of the Wetlands. Flagongut's own original fossil is held by Prospector Whelgar at his excavation site in the Wetlands. Archaeologist Flagongut, reviewing the collected finds, realizes that unlocking the mysterious powers within the fossils requires a key artifact: the Stone of Relu.

The Admiral's Orders. Recovered from a locked strongbox atop Tiragarde Keep, these weathered papers bear the personal seal of the late Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore. The recovered orders reveal that the Kul Tiran human garrison along Durotar's coast is far more entrenched and organized than simple shipwreck survivors. Delivering them to Gar'Thok in Razor Hill exposes lingering military plans threatening the fledgling Orc nation. Hidden inside a heavy chest on the upper floors of Tiragarde Keep, an aged envelope survives under the watch of Lieutenant Benedict. Sealed with the crest of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore, the parchment outlines direct naval commands issued during Kul Tiras's bloody invasion of Durotar. Even after the Grand Admiral fell at Theramore, his officers maintained their fortifications, clinging tightly to their mission to eradicate the Horde settlement.

The Adventurer. In Northshire Valley, Marshal McBride sends The Adventurer toward Goldshire to find Sam Sarsaparilla. You have shown your skill defending the abbey, and McBride wants you to look into the newcomer. As threats from the local Defias and vermin ease, Marshal McBride turns his attention to the road beyond Northshire Valley. Stormwind's regular forces are stretched thin across the kingdom, so the local garrison relies on promising fighters to watch travelers and wanderers in the surrounding woods.

The Adventurer. The Adventurer is a local errand given by Mountaineer Thalos at the southern gate of Dun Morogh. Before sending travelers through the mountain tunnel toward Kharanos, Thalos asks them to carry a bundle of supplies to Eric Brighthammer, a newcomer camped just outside the village. Guarding the high passes and tunnels between Coldridge Valley and the broader snowy expanses of Dun Morogh is demanding work for the Ironforge Mountaineers. Stationed at the border gate, Mountaineer Thalos keeps an eye out for both local dangers and travelers passing along the beaten trail. When word reaches the post about a lone adventurer arriving near Kharanos, Thalos uses trusted passersby to haul necessary supplies onward to support newcomers venturing into the frozen crags.

The Adventurer. The Adventurer is a brief quest set in Teldrassil involving the discovery of a discarded journal in the wilds. The plain notebook recounts the humble travels and camping outings of an unknown traveler, intended for delivery to Lyreena Duskblade near Dolanaar. Amid the dense boughs and tangled roots of Teldrassil, travelers occasionally stumble across abandoned personal items. This simple journal recounts the unremarkable yet earnest wanderings of a nameless adventurer. Instead of grand heroics or perilous monster hunts, the bulk of its pages enthusiastically document the simple joys of making camp beneath the twilight canopy.

The Adventurer. "The Adventurer" is an introductory journey quest on Zephras Isle. Given by Aetheen of the Gales in Thendal Grove, it directs newly seasoned wanderers southwest toward Shen'dar Village to meet Raan Wildwind, a veteran camper who knows the wilds. While Thendal Grove provides shelter and quiet refuge, the wider expanses of Zephras Isle remain wild and perilous. Aetheen of the Gales watches over the initiates and sees when an aspiring traveler is ready to step beyond familiar borders. For those seeking fame, fortune, or purpose, remaining behind the grove's sheltered perimeter is no longer enough.

The Adventurer. While exploring the rugged wastes of Durotar, travelers stumble across a plain, discarded journal chronicling the quiet travels of an unfamiliar figure. Its pages speak warmly of outdoor life and camping out under the stars, awaiting delivery to Brakk near Razor Hill. Durotar is a harsh land where survival usually takes precedence over leisurely travel, making the discovery of a wandering chronicler's book an unusual sight. Found lying unattended in the red dirt, the modest journal contains the musings and exploits of someone completely unknown to the common heroes of the Horde. Rather than detailing bloody battles or grand campaigns, its pages dwell on the humble joys of sleeping under the open sky and making camp in the wild.

The Adventurer. The Adventurer is an introductory task given by Executor Arren to seasoned young Forsaken champions outside Deathknell. Having proven reliable in strikes against the Scarlet Crusade, you are dispatched up the road toward Brill to investigate a stranger lingering near the settlement. Rather than uncovering another zealot spy, the task introduces you to Eleanor Shackleton, an independent traveler eager to teach the practical survival skills of the wild. Executor Arren maintains a vigilant watch over Deathknell and the surrounding approaches. With Scarlet Crusaders actively spying on the region and infiltrating northern Lordaeron, any newcomer spotted wandering near Brill warrants immediate scrutiny. Having demonstrated your dedication by eliminating crusader threats along the border, Arren turns to you to investigate the unknown figure quietly, determining whether she poses a hidden danger to the Forsaken.

The Adventurer. As young tauren prepare to depart their ancestral training grounds on Red Cloud Mesa, Chief Hawkwind asks them to perform a final favor. He entrusts them with a bundle of essential supplies meant for Kaga Wildhoof, a seasoned wanderer camped near Bloodhoof Village who once aided the chief in his own past. Before travelers descend the mesa path toward the broader plains of Mulgore, Chief Hawkwind pauses to address unfinished personal debts. Long before guiding new generations of hunters and shamans on Camp Narache, Hawkwind crossed paths with Kaga Wildhoof. Described by the chief as an accomplished adventurer, Wildhoof provided vital aid when he needed it most. Hearing that she has pitched camp just outside Bloodhoof Village, Hawkwind uses the departure of newly proven novices to send provisions to his old benefactor.

The Affray. The Affray is a brutal martial trial conducted on Fray Island off the coast of the Barrens. Administered by Klannoc Macleod, this arena brawl pits ambitious warriors against waves of island challengers and their champion to prove they possess the mettle required for advanced training. Fray Island stands apart from the struggles of the mainland, serving as a sanctuary for hardy brawlers, outcasts, and combat instructors. Klannoc Macleod does not simply teach any wanderer who steps off a boat. To earn his tutelage, aspiring warriors must participate in the Affray, an open trial of martial stamina and battlefield awareness designed to separate true fighters from boastful pretenders.

The Algaz Gauntlet. The Algaz Gauntlet is an urgent military mission to fight through Dun Algaz, a critical mountain pass linking Loch Modan to the Wetlands. Orcs of the Dragonmaw clan have entrenched themselves in the tunnels, threatening to sever Ironforge's vital lifeline to Menethil Harbor. Adventurers are tasked with cutting down the orcish vanguard and delivering word of the invasion to Valstag Ironjaw. Dun Algaz serves as the solitary overland mountain pass carving through the crags between Loch Modan and the marshy basin of the Wetlands. For the dwarves of Ironforge, this stone corridor is essential for trade, troop movements, and supplies heading to Menethil Harbor, the Alliance's primary coastal port in the region. Should the pass fall, Ironforge's connection to the western seas is effectively strangled, leaving isolated outposts cut off from dwarven reinforcements.

The Altar of Zul. The Witherbark trolls do not have Sharpbeak, so Gryphon Master Talonaxe wonders whether the Vilebranch trolls took the young gryphon instead. You are sent to the Altar of Zul, at the western edge of Vilebranch lands, to search for him. The cages of the Witherbark trolls held no sign of Sharpbeak. Talonaxe now suspects the Vilebranch trolls and sends you up to the Altar of Zul, at the western edge of their lands, to look on its top for the gryphon child. Talonaxe fears to think what the Vilebranch may be doing to the captive, if they hold him.

The Anchors of Zephras. The Anchors of Zephras is an introductory quest offered by Halaan Hawk-Eye on Zephras Isle. Halaan invites travelers to borrow his far-reaching vision to observe the ancient anchor pylons that tether and preserve the floating island. Though the soaring monoliths appear untouched from a distance, Halaan warns that the wind spirits' stabilizing magic has begun to waver. The anchor pylons of Zephras are ancient, towering monoliths gifted by the spirits of the winds. Deeply woven into the isle's mystical foundation, they serve to bind, steady, and sustain the landmass amidst the churning skies. To look upon one is to witness the fragile balance keeping Zephras aloft, relying continuously on the benevolence of the wind spirits.

The Ancient Egg. Yeh'kinya in Tanaris tells of an ancient egg named in the Prophecy of Mosh'aru, left from the age when trolls held vast empires. It can contain Hakkar's essence, and Yeh'kinya wants it fetched from Jintha'Alor in the Hinterlands. An ancient egg is spoken of in the Prophecy of Mosh'aru, a relic of the age when trolls held vast empires. Its power can contain Hakkar's essence, and Yeh'kinya believes it could be the sole means of guarding the world from his evil.

The Ancient Statuette. Talen, an elf camped near the dangerous Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale, seeks recovery of a lost relic. After being ambushed and run aground by vicious naga, he dropped his prized ancient statuette along the surf and needs an adventurer to retrieve it from the ruins. The sunken ruins of Zoram along Ashenvale's northwestern shoreline have long attracted those curious about the ancient night elven past. Talen was navigating the shallows in a small vessel when hostile naga surfaced and tore into him with claw and trident. He managed to scramble ashore with bare provisions to make a hasty camp, but in his desperate sprint for survival, his most precious find was dropped into the sands.

The Angry Scytheclaws. Sergra Darkthorn sends ambitious hunters south of the Crossroads to confront the savage scytheclaws stalking the Barrens. By claiming feathers from sunscale raptors and planting them directly within the beasts' breeding nests, hunters prove their courage and earn respect in a hostile wilderness. For Sergra Darkthorn, hunting in the Barrens is never purely about slaughter; it is an enduring rite of passage. Having already tested travelers against lesser beasts, she tasks hunters with seeking out the vicious sunscale raptors south of the Crossroads. Taking their feathers is only the initial trial. To truly prove their mettle, hunters must carry these trophies directly into the heart of raptor territory southwest of the Stagnant Oasis, desecrating their nests to broadcast utter fearlessness.

The Argent Emissary. The Argent Emissary marks the arrival of two Forsaken representatives of the Argent Dawn tracking Scourge cultists near the Undercity. Their presence underscores both the shared fight against the Scourge and the simmering tension between the neutral order and the Forsaken authorities. Two Forsaken emissaries from the Argent Dawn have recently arrived in Tirisfal Glades, setting local authorities on edge. Although the Argent Dawn opposes the Scourge, the local Forsaken remain suspicious of any armed, neutral order operating unmonitored within their sovereign territory. Even the shared heritage of the emissaries does little to soothe their vigilance.

The Ashenvale Hunt. Issued by Warcaller Gorlach in Orgrimmar, this directive summons budding Horde adventurers northward beyond the Barrens into the ancient forests of Ashenvale. Players are directed to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to participate in the ongoing hunt and reinforce the Horde's expanding frontier. Orgrimmar buzzes with martial fervor, but the young city requires vast amounts of timber, meat, and secure trade routes to sustain its growth. Warcaller Gorlach serves as the voice of the Horde's high command, directing seasoned wanderers and new blood alike toward active campaigns. For warriors coming of age in Durotar and the Barrens, the ancient woodlands of Ashenvale represent the next testing ground for both glory and survival.

The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a directive guiding proven Horde adventurers out of the arid Barrens and northward into the dense forests of Ashenvale. Entrusted by Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, travelers are sent to Splintertree Post to assist Senani Thunderheart and test their tracking skills against a wild, contested land. After proving their hunting prowess in the sun-bleached plains of the Barrens, Horde hunters and warriors are directed toward an entirely different proving ground. Jorn Skyseer recognizes when a traveler has outgrown the local game and points them north to Ashenvale. For the young Horde, these ancient woodlands represent both a bounty of resources and a profound political and spiritual frontier that they must learn to understand and claim.

The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a traditional rite overseen by Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post. Horde hunters are challenged to track and overcome three legendary woodland predators prowling the ancient forest: the bear Ursangous, the nightsaber Shadumbra, and the fierce hippogryph Sharptalon. It is conceived not merely as a test of arms, but as a journey to learn cunning, respect, and self-knowledge. As the Horde establishes footholds deep within Ashenvale, the spiritual teachings of the Earth Mother find expression through Senani Thunderheart. Unlike the Orcs' aggressive lumber gathering, Senani's hunt treats the shadowed woodlands as a sacred testing ground. By matching wits with the forest's apex predators, a hunter is expected to commune with the untamed wilderness and develop the quiet humility that survival in Ashenvale demands.

The Ashenvale Hunt. The Ashenvale Hunt is a summons dispatched to young Horde champions visiting Thunder Bluff, urging them north into the dense canopy of Ashenvale. Delivered by the city's heralds, the call directs travelers to report to Senani Thunderheart at Splintertree Post to take part in a proving hunt. Within the serene heights of Thunder Bluff, runners keep the burgeoning Horde informed of opportunities beyond the borders of Mulgore. Bluff Runner Windstrider carries an open invitation aimed at proven adventurers looking for greater challenges. With the Horde establishing footholds deep in the ancient forest north of the Barrens, young warriors are called upon to bolster those outposts and test their survival skills in a far harsher environment.

The Atal'ai Exile. While you were at the Pool of Tears, one of Fel'zerul's scouts brought back a scroll inked in blood on dried flesh. Fel'zerul now bundles the artifacts you gathered and sends you far north to the Hinterlands, to find an exiled Atal'ai priest. The scroll reads as a judicial ruling against a priest of the Atal'ai, a fate worse than death among his own people. He was exiled to live among the Witherbark trolls, far to the north in the Hinterlands. Fel'zerul will bundle the artifacts and sends you to find the exile, discover their true use, and return.

The Balance of Nature. "The Balance of Nature" is the introductory quest offered to newly awakened night elves in Shadowglen. Bestowed by Conservator Ilthalaine, it charges young adventurers with culling overgrown populations of young nightsabers and thistle boars. The task introduces new heroes to the ancient kaldorei duty of stewarding and preserving the natural harmony of Teldrassil. Teldrassil may appear wild and ancient, but its ecosystems are young and fragile. In Shadowglen, sheltered beneath the Great Tree's sprawling boughs, heavy spring rains have disrupted the forest's delicate cycle. Certain wildlife populations flourished beyond the land's capacity to sustain them, threatening to strip the glen of resources and plunge the entire ecosystem into famine. Preserving the forest requires proactive stewardship.

The Balance of Nature. This task continues Conservator Ilthalaine's effort to preserve Shadowglen's fragile ecology by culling mature thistle boars and mangy nightsabers. As Teldrassil's wildlife multiplies unchecked, night elf guardians must step in to prevent the overpopulation of predators and foragers from stripping the boughs bare. While culling young animals stabilizes future growth, the adult populations of Shadowglen also pose an immediate threat to the World Tree's ecosystem. Conservator Ilthalaine directs young defenders deeper into the forest to hunt mature thistle boars and older, mangy nightsabers before their ravenous appetites exhaust the land's finite flora and game.

The Balnir Farmstead. "The Balnir Farmstead" is an early rite of passage for young Forsaken mages, directed by Anastasia Hartwell in the Undercity's Mage Quarter. Initiates are sent to eastern Tirisfal Glades to gather snapdragons from an abandoned farmstead sitting dangerously close to the border of the Plaguelands. The floral samples serve as barometers for the encroaching magical corruption spreading from the Scourge-blighted east. While the Royal Apothecary Society frequently studies the effects of necromancy and decay, the mages of the Forsaken maintain their own watchful eye on the borderlands. Anastasia Hartwell tasks novice spellcasters with travelling to the Balnir Farmstead in eastern Tirisfal Glades. Snapdragons native to the farm's gardens are naturally sensitive to shifting magical currents, absorbing ambient energies from the soil and atmosphere. By examining these blooms, arcane scholars in the Undercity can measure whether the corruptive contagion of the Lich King's domain has seeped past the bulwark into Tirisfal proper.

The Barrens Oases. High on the Elder Rise of Thunder Bluff, Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem senses an unsettling surge of power flowing into the arid soils of the Barrens. To uncover the truth, he dispatches promising travelers eastward past Mulgore's gates to rendezvous with his kinsman, Tonga Runetotem, at the Crossroads. This mission marks the beginning of an investigation into the unnatural waters springing up across the sun-baked plains. While the plains of Mulgore flourish under the watchful gaze of the Earth Mother, the vast savannas of the Barrens to the east have remained harsh, scorched, and dry for generations. Recently, however, the tauren druids meditating atop Thunder Bluff's Elder Rise have detected strange currents of energy waking deep beneath the parched plains. Life is stirring where it ought not to be, and the Cenarion Circle fears that whatever force is causing this surge may harbor hidden peril for the land and its creatures.

The Barrens Port. The Barrens Port is an Alliance quest given by Thyn'tel Bladeweaver in Darnassus as part of the investigation into the disappearance of Velinde Starsong. Believing Velinde took a ship across the Great Sea to the Eastern Kingdoms, the Sentinels direct you across dangerous Horde territory to the goblin-run harbor of Ratchet to consult Wharfmaster Dizzywig's ledgers. Following the inspection of Velinde Starsong's personal effects, the Sentinels discovered clues suggesting she sought passage across the sea toward the Eastern Kingdoms. Ratchet serves as the only operational maritime harbor in the Barrens, making it the solitary conduit through which a traveler from northern Kalimdor could arrange transport south or east without sailing directly out of night elf territory. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver sends you southward to search the harbor master's shipping ledgers for any sign of Velinde's name.

text.enUS: The Battle Plans. You have the gnolls' battle plans. What is left is to carry them back to Hadoken Swiftstrider at Camp Mojache, where he or someone there may puzzle out what the gnolls are after. After Woodpaw Investigation, you hold the Woodpaw battle plans, and the only step left is returning them to Hadoken Swiftstrider at the camp. Hadoken is looking for solid evidence of the gnolls' intentions.

The Battleboars. The Battleboars is a rite-of-passage hunting quest given by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. Young tauren are tasked with culling the vicious war-trained boars of Brambleblade Ravine to defend tribal lands and feed the settlement's youth. To the east of Red Cloud Mesa lies Brambleblade Ravine, a thorn-choked scar held by the Bristleback quilboar. As tensions between the Shu'halo and the quilboar escalate into open war, the Bristlebacks have trained vicious battleboars to probe tauren boundaries and terrorize their traditional hunting grounds. Left unchecked, these aggressive beasts threaten not only game trails but the safety of Camp Narache itself.

The Befouled Element. Upon slaying the agitated water elementals around Mystral Lake, adventurers discover a foul, glowing globe of tainted water. Seeking to understand what has poisoned the lake and its elemental spirits, they carry the specimen back to Mastok Wrilehiss at Splintertree Post. Mystral Lake, nestled in south-central Ashenvale, has fallen into severe distress. The water elementals inhabiting its shallows have grown violently aggressive and visibly corrupted. When struck down, their remains yield strange, intensely glowing spheres of putrid fluid rather than pure elemental essence. Whatever corruption has settled over the lake is concentrated inside these globes, signaling that the disturbance is far more than natural territorial aggression.

The Big Picture. The Big Picture is a Northshire Valley task concerning a thieving kobold named Shinyfinder Narf, who has been hoarding stolen books deep within the local mine. Adventurers are dispatched by local authorities to recover the illustrated volumes and return them to Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey. A peculiar incident has disrupted the peace of Northshire Valley: kobolds lurking around the region have been seen scurrying away with books, crying out 'Picture for Narf!' While kobolds are typically infamous for scavenging candles and shiny trinkets, one particular cave-dweller known as Shinyfinder Narf has developed an appetite for illustrated tomes, accumulating a whole sack of them in his subterranean hideout.

The Binding. The Binding is the culminating rite for Forsaken warlocks seeking to command a voidwalker. In the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, Carendin Halgar requires initiates to summon, conquer, and permanently subjugate a creature of the Void. Unlike minor imps, which are easily coerced into pacts with dark magic, creatures of the Void despise reality and possess formidable physical might. To earn the right to summon a voidwalker, an aspiring warlock in the Undercity must prove total mastery over it. In the shadowed enclave of the Magic Quarter, the Forsaken mentor Carendin Halgar provides the mystic runes required to tear a voidwalker from the Nether into the physical realm.

The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation in an Undercity warlock's journey to summon and command a succubus. Directed by Carendin Halgar, the practitioner uses pure hearts to draw a demon from the Twisting Nether into a ritual circle, subjugating its will through combat. Within the dark alcoves of the Magic Quarter, Forsaken warlocks refine their command over demonic entities. Summoning a succubus is considered a critical rite of passage. Unlike the brute force of a voidwalker or the minor malice of an imp, a succubus wields seductive and mental enchantments capable of ensnaring the caster. Carendin Halgar requires initiates to prove their mind and magic are ironclad before trusting them with permanent dominion over such an entity.

The Binding. The Binding is the final initiation ritual in Orgrimmar for young Horde warlocks seeking command over a voidwalker. Under the direction of Gan'rul Bloodeye, the petitioner inscribes glyphs from the Tablet of Verga within Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle to call forth, subdue, and perpetually enslave a creature of the Void. For an initiate warlock lurking in the dark tunnels of the Cleft of Shadow, summoning an imp is merely child's play. Subduing a voidwalker is the first true test of willpower and arcane dominance. Warlocks do not form polite pacts or commune with these otherworldly horrors; they wrest them across dimensions through raw force and bind them in eternal servitude. Gan'rul Bloodeye demands that the initiate draw upon the glyphs transcribed from the Tablet of Verga, calling the monstrosity directly into Neeru Fireblade's ritual circle to break it in single combat.

The Binding. The Binding is the final trial in an aspiring Horde warlock's quest to enslave a succubus in Orgrimmar. By using the devotion bound up in Dogran's Pendant at Neeru Fireblade's summoning circle, the warlock wrenches a demon from the Twisting Nether and breaks its will through force of arms and spellcraft. Beneath the clefts of Orgrimmar, deep within the tent of Neeru Fireblade, lies a summoning circle prepared for such hazardous work. Under the tutelage of Gan'rul Bloodeye, the warlock activates the rune-scribed circle and battles the summoned seductress. A warlock cannot simply call a demon into service; they must overpower it in single combat, bending its malevolent spirit to their sovereign will.

The Binding. In Stormwind, Gakin the Darkbinder puts a novice warlock through a final trial. With his recovered Bloodstone Choker, you draw a voidwalker into a hidden circle and force it to submit. Beneath the Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter, forgotten catacombs run beyond the watchful gaze of the Silver Hand and Kirin Tor magistrates. Gakin the Darkbinder teaches novice warlocks that dark magic demands more than channeling power; they must also dominate otherworldly beings. You have recovered Gakin's stolen Bloodstone Choker from Surena Caledon. Now he asks you to call a voidwalker into the summoning circle beneath the tavern.

The Binding. Stormwind warlocks seek to bind a succubus to their will. Beneath The Slaughtered Lamb, an initiate uses the enchanted core from the Heartswood to summon the demon and defeat it in combat. A crypt beneath The Slaughtered Lamb in Stormwind's Mage Quarter shelters the city's warlocks. There, away from the city watch and the Cathedral of Light, they practice forbidden arts. Stone summoning circles channel the Nether's power and let initiates reach across the veil between worlds.

The Binding. The Binding is the culminating rite for warlocks seeking to command a felhunter. Overseen by the enigmatic summoner Strahad Farsan above Ratchet, the ritual uses the restored Tome of the Cabal to rip an aggressive demonic predator from the Nether and force it into subjugation through trial of combat. Perched on the bluffs overlooking the goblin port of Ratchet, Strahad Farsan conducts some of the most dangerous demonological trials on Kalimdor. After a warlock gathers the disparate fragments and reagents needed to piece together the ancient Tome of the Cabal, Strahad prepares the binding grounds. He lays down an inner glyph of containment while his loyal acolytes channel through enchanted rods to complete the outer circle, ensuring whatever horrors emerge remain isolated from the settlement below.

The Black Box. A metallic black box has turned up in a giant condor's stomach in the Badlands, its surface heavily pitted as if left in acid. Stamped on its underside, beneath a symbol, is a mark reading Engine #19 - Ironforge Siege Brigade. The pitting suggests the box sat inside the condor for ages while acid ate at the metal. Turn it over and a symbol is stamped on the bottom, with Engine #19 - Ironforge Siege Brigade written below. You are to carry it to the Hall of Arms in Ironforge, to Pilot Longbeard.

The Black Shield. The Shady Rest Inn lies burned out, and one of the few parts still standing is a crumbling chimney. A shield blackened by the flames is fixed to its brick. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to show it to. Fire tore through the Shady Rest Inn, and little of it remains. Fixed to the crumbling chimney is an iron shield charred black, and it can be worked free of the brick. Krog at Brackenwall Village is the one to bring it to, and will ask whether it counts as evidence from the inn's remains.

The Black Shield. An iron shield, blackened by fire, is fixed to the crumbling chimney of the burned Shady Rest Inn. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is waiting on evidence from the inn's site. The Shady Rest Inn burned, and one of the few parts left standing is a crumbling chimney. A fire-blackened iron shield is fixed to its brick, and it can be removed. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore wants evidence from the inn's site.

The Black Shield. Krog now recalls where the name Mosarn comes from: a highly regarded blacksmith in Thunder Bluff, whose armor set was once given to Krog by the Earthen Ring. Krog hopes Mosarn can say more about the blackened iron shield, since nothing useful came from Reethe. Mosarn is to be found in Thunder Bluff. Krog remembers where the name Mosarn was heard before: a blacksmith in Thunder Bluff, highly regarded. The Earthen Ring once thanked Krog with armor that Mosarn crafted, and Krog speaks well of the work. Krog says Mosarn made the shield too and may be able to tell more about it. It is a slim lead, Krog admits, but Reethe yielded nothing useful, so it is all there is. The blackened iron shield goes to Mosarn, who is in Thunder Bluff.

The Black Shield. Captain Garran Vimes is sorry to be of little help with the Blackened Iron Shield, but knows who can do better: Caz Twosprocket, one of the best blacksmiths around, who tends the forge in Theramore's smithy. Vimes apologizes for being unable to help much with the shield, but names someone who can. You are sent with it to Caz Twosprocket, one of the best blacksmiths, who tends the forge in Theramore's smithy. Perhaps Caz can tell you something about it.

The Black Shield. Caz Twosprocket looks over the black shield for the Shady Rest Inn mystery and almost misses one last detail. Caz sends you to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with what was found. Looking over the black shield, Caz Twosprocket almost misses one last detail: the leather strap on its back has burned away, but the strap seems to have been made to fit a large person. Caz guesses a tauren. That is all Caz can tell, and you are sent to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore with the word, and with Caz's apology for not being more help.

The Black Shield. Krog looks over the Blackened Iron Shield and sees nothing unusual about it. Krog suggests that the blacksmith Do'gol inspect it, though without much hope, and sends you to Brackenwall Village. Krog sees nothing unusual about the shield. Do'gol, the blacksmith, might be able to tell more about it, Krog says, but warns against expecting much. Do'gol is in Brackenwall Village.

The Black Shield. At Brackenwall Village, Do'gol has noticed lettering along the shield's edge, but burned residue hides it. Clearing it needs acid, and Do'gol asks you for six venom sacs from the Darkfang spiders of the marsh. Do'gol can see lettering around the shield's rim, though the burnt-on grime makes it hard to read. Acid would clear it, and the marsh's Darkfang spiders carry venom that works well. Do'gol wants six of their acidic venom sacs to clean the shield up.

The Black Shield. Do'gol has rubbed the shield clear enough to see what appears to spell Mosarn, a name that means nothing to Do'gol. Krog in Brackenwall Village knows many people, so Do'gol sends you to ask there. Do'gol poured on a bit too much acid, but a little rubbing brings out writing that is still hard to read and seems to say Mosarn. The name means nothing to Do'gol. Krog in Brackenwall Village knows many people, so Do'gol sends you to talk with Krog.

name.esES: La corrupción de los Bosque Negro

text.enUS: The Blackwood Corrupted. Following evidence found in the tainted waters of Cliffspring River, Thundris Windweaver sends adventurers to sever the dark influence strangling the Blackwood tribe. By purifying their food supply with moonwell water, you provoke their demonic handler into the open to shatter his hold on the northern camp. The night elves of Auberdine have long struggled to understand why the once-peaceful Blackwood furbolgs turned so viciously against their neighbors. Investigations along the Cliffspring River traced the rot to satyr meddling. These ancient servants of the Burning Legion have been actively manipulating the tribe, channeling fel magic through insidious talismans to twist the minds of the furbolgs and drive them into feral aggression.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. First Mate Crazz of the Blackwater Raiders needs an adventurer to investigate rumors of rival pirates. With his crew busy drinking and chasing company in Booty Bay, he asks you to scout a nearby cove along the Savage Coast for signs of the Bloodsail Buccaneers. The Blackwater Raiders have newly docked in Booty Bay, only to hear word that their rivals, the Bloodsail Buccaneers, have been sighted across southern Stranglethorn Vale. With the rest of the crew distracted by grog and shoreline pursuits, First Mate Crazz turns to an outsider for help. He asks you to head north along the Savage Coast and scout a cove to see what the Bloodsail Buccaneers are up to.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. Recovered correspondence from the Bloodsail Buccaneers carries a map of Booty Bay and written orders to secure a quiet camp at the marked spot and wait for a signal from their southern command post before attacking. Following your earlier investigation into the Bloodsail Buccaneers, an intercepted map and written orders uncover the pirates' immediate plans. A red X on a map of Booty Bay marks the exact spot where the pirates are to make camp. The orders command the crew to hold their ground quietly, eliminate anyone who approaches, and await an attack signal sent from the southern command post.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. First Mate Crazz has learned that the Bloodsail Buccaneers intend to launch an assault against Booty Bay. The scale of the threat demands the attention of the Blackwater Raiders' commander, Fleet Master Seahorn, who needs to hear the warning immediately. Upon discovering that the Bloodsail Buccaneers scheme to strike Booty Bay directly, First Mate Crazz decides it is bigger than he thought. He directs you to seek out Fleet Master Seahorn, who is somewhere in the port town, and inform him of the brewing assault before the rival pirates can make their move.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. Fleet Master Seahorn trusts a loyal ally of the Blackwater Raiders with striking the Bloodsail Buccaneers' so-called southern command post on the Wild Shore. Recovering their charts and written orders will show exactly what those pirates are up to. Following earlier efforts for Crazz, Fleet Master Seahorn takes notice of your loyalty to the Blackwater Raiders. The Bloodsail Buccaneers have set up what they call a southern command post on the Wild Shore. Seahorn directs you to raid this encampment, cut down their swashbucklers, and seize their naval charts and written orders so the fleet can learn their intentions.

name.frFR: Les boucaniers de la Voile sanglante

text.enUS: The Bloodsail Buccaneers. With the Bloodsail Buccaneers preparing an attack, Fleet Master Seahorn decides against deploying his entire fleet for a counterstrike. Instead, he directs an adventuring crew to slip into the landing site and eliminate the buccaneers' top leadership before their attack can begin. Having learned the buccaneers' invasion plans, Fleet Master Seahorn refuses to wait for the enemy to muster an assault. Mocking Fleet Master Firallon's nautical skill, Seahorn aims to neutralize the threat swiftly by taking out its commanders. Rather than risking a full naval engagement, he sends a strike party directly to Firallon's landing camp to cut down Firallon alongside Captain Stillwater and Captain Keelhaul, ensuring the buccaneer force crumbles without leadership.

The Boar Hunter. The Boar Hunter is an early errand given by the dwarf hunter Talin Keeneye in Coldridge Valley. A surge in the local crag boar population has made the woods overly dangerous, and young recruits are tasked with culling the aggressive beasts so seasoned hunters can track in peace. Coldridge Valley is typically a quiet, protected training ground for young mountaineers and scholars of Ironforge. However, the wildlife often grows restless and overabundant in the harsh winter climate. Talin Keeneye, a veteran hunter stationed outside Anvilmar, notices that the aggressive small crag boars have multiplied so rapidly that they pose a genuine threat to anyone wandering the snow-covered trails.

The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a scholarly magical treatise penned by the late Dalaran wizard Ur, detailing his research into strange extradimensional entities. Left behind in Shadowfang Keep, it fell into the hands of Archmage Arugal before drawing the keen interest of Forsaken researchers in the Undercity. Before Dalaran fell to the Scourge, Ur was renowned among the Kirin Tor for his esoteric investigations into other planes of existence and otherworldly creatures. Despite his fascination with extraplanar magic, Ur was guided by caution and ethical restraint, choosing to record his discoveries rather than recklessly breach the veil between worlds. Tragically, when the Scourge assaulted the violet city, his magical prowess and moral hesitations were not enough to save him.

The Book of Ur. The Book of Ur is a mission assigned by Keeper Bel'dugur in the Undercity's Apothecarium. Bel'dugur charges Horde champions with infiltrating Shadowfang Keep to recover the arcane treatise of Ur, a deceased mage of Dalaran. The Forsaken seek Ur's extraplanar research, intending to weaponize magical insights he was too scrupulous to exploit. Before the Third War wiped out Dalaran, a brilliant human wizard named Ur dedicated his scholarship to realms beyond Azeroth. Unlike standard Kirin Tor doctrine, which strictly regulated conjuration and outer planar contacts, Ur cataloged entities from other dimensions, including the savage worgen. Despite his curiosity, Ur ultimately hesitated to manipulate these alien powers, deeming them dangerously uncontrollable. That restraint, however, made his written legacy a coveted prize for those who possess no such moral qualms.

The Borrower. Daryn Lightwind is fascinated by the snapjaws on the beach in the Hinterlands, and above all by a giant one named Gammerita. Her research keeps her where she is, so she gives you a letter to carry to Curgle Cranklehop in Tanaris. Daryn Lightwind says she has studied many subjects, and her latest fascination is the snapjaws that live along the beach in the Hinterlands. One she especially wants to see is a giant snapjaw called Gammerita. She would go herself, but her research keeps her here, so a picture of Gammerita would be the next best thing.

The Bounty of Teldrassil. The Bounty of Teldrassil is an introductory errand given by Nessa Shadowsong in Rut'theran Village. Seeking to compare the unusual size and abundance of island fish with those caught along the mainland, she prepares a collection of bones and scales to be shipped across the strait to Darkshore. Delivering this package to the local hippogryph handler marks the first step in crossing the sea to Auberdine. Beneath the massive boughs of the World Tree, the sheltered waters surrounding Rut'theran Village teem with remarkably large and plentiful marine life. Nessa Shadowsong, observing the remarkable yields hauled in by local fishermen, seeks to discover whether this vitality extends to the ancient mainland coast or remains unique to the waters nourished by Teldrassil. To test her theory, she prepares a collection of scales and bones to be examined by Laird, a fellow fishmonger based across the water in Auberdine.

The Branch of Cenarius. Following a desperate plea from the dying dryad Anilia, an adventurer is tasked with recovering a sacred relic stolen by the vile satyr Geltharis. Reclaiming the Branch of Cenarius means confronting the demon-sworn corrupters lurking in eastern Ashenvale and returning the treasured bough to the dryad Illiyana. Sent into the corrupted folds of eastern Ashenvale to search for missing dryads, Alliance travelers stumble upon Anilia clinging to the very edge of life. With her final breaths, the wounded daughter of Cenarius gestures toward the satyr ruins to the north. Gasping out the name of the satyr who has taken it—Geltharis—she begs with her fading strength for the recovery of the Branch of Cenarius before succumbing to her wounds.

The Brassbolts Brothers. Pilot Longbeard in Ironforge needs a courier to deliver a crate of reinforced siege engine helmets across the sea to Kalimdor. His friends, the Brassbolts brothers, are testing high-speed rocket cars in the Shimmering Flats and urgently need head protection for their accident-prone test drivers. While stationed among his aerial machinery in Ironforge, the dwarven aviator Pilot Longbeard received an urgent request from the Shimmering Flats in southern Kalimdor. His friends, a pair of inventive gnomes known as the Brassbolts brothers, had taken up residence on the vast salt pans to race experimental machinery. Longbeard is tied down by military and piloting duties, leaving him unable to deliver the supplies himself.

The Broken Construct. The Broken Construct involves aiding an artisan in Valanaar who is struggling to repair a rare, damaged automaton. These machines were originally gifted by the departed spirits of the wind and preserved by the Windshapers, making every remaining functional construct an invaluable relic of the island's past. Long ago, the spirits of the wind bestowed magical instruments, devices, and animated constructs upon the people of the island. The Windshapers were tasked with their upkeep, preserving these elemental gifts across generations. However, after the spirits left, the flow of their ancient patronage ceased, causing most of the wondrous creations to fall into disrepair until only a handful remained operational.

The Broken Construct. The Broken Construct involves lending aid to Riaani Nightwind, who is shoulder-deep inside the innards of an inoperable machine. Sent as an assistant by Ayessa, travelers must listen to Riaani's plans to discover how they can help restore the device. The Broken Construct begins when an adventurer is dispatched by Ayessa to aid Riaani Nightwind. Riaani is hard at work attempting to diagnose a damaged construct, his attention completely absorbed by the device's inner components. Though he is surprised to receive outside help and doubts whether an untrained traveler can handle delicate mechanical work, he agrees to outline a few necessary tasks once he pulls himself out of the machinery.

The Broken Sigil. After you took the first sigil from the Syndicate, Zengu sends you after the remaining two, which the dug-in Stromgarde militia guards. Galen, son of Thoras Trollbane, broke the Sigil of Thoradin into pieces, and you are to carry them to the troll shaman Tor'gan in Hammerfall. Three sigils guard the tomb of Thoras Trollbane, and you have already recovered the first from the Syndicate. The other two are harder to get, since the firmly entrenched Stromgarde militia holds them. Thoras' son, Galen, divided the Sigil of Thoradin into eleven pieces and dispersed them among the Stromgarde defenders.

The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb tells of the brood of Onyxia invading Stonemaul Village, and wonders why Deathwing's daughter would come to these lands. You are sent to bring word to Overlord Mok'Morokk in Brackenwall Village. Stonemaul Village was invaded by Onyxia's brood, and Draz'Zilb finds it troubling that the daughter of Deathwing would descend upon these lands. Draz'Zilb feels certain Onyxia came for more than a siege on a few ogres, and wants Overlord Mok'Morokk told at once in Brackenwall Village so action can be taken.

The Brood of Onyxia. Overlord Mok'Morokk has no wish to hear about dragons. He says there are no black dragons here and sends you back to Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village with the news that the ogres are staying. After Draz'Zilb sent word of the brood of Onyxia, Overlord Mok'Morokk wants only to be left alone. Mok'Morokk says the ogres stay where they are, that there is no black dragon here, and tells you to go and say so to Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village.

The Brood of Onyxia. Draz'Zilb in Brackenwall Village does not want a single more whelp of Onyxia to hatch. You are sent to find and destroy the black dragon's eggs near the Wyrmbog, down in the marsh's south. Onyxia's brood has been scattered through the Dragonmurk. Draz'Zilb urges haste: the Wyrmbog lies in the south of the marsh, and Draz'Zilb is sure the dragon has made her lair there, with her eggs riddled around it. As long as the land around Stonemaul Village is a nesting place for dragons, the ogres will never take it back, so you are sent to track the eggs down and destroy them.

The Captain's Chest. Captain Hecklebury Smotts used to sail between Booty Bay and Ratchet in Kalimdor, until sea giants wrecked the ship, killed the crew and sent Smotts off in a lifeboat toward Booty Bay. The giant Gorlash took Smotts' Captain's Chest, and Smotts wants it back. Smotts says the voyages to Ratchet in Kalimdor built a successful career and a fine reputation. The sea giants ended all that: they smashed the ship, killed the crew and sent Smotts off in a lifeboat toward Booty Bay.

The Captain's Cutlass. Captain Hecklebury Smotts bought a second vessel named Smotts' Revenge to hunt down the sea giants who took his first ship, only to suffer another defeat. The giants smashed the vessel and killed the crew, and one of them, Negolash, stole the captain's cutlass. Smotts directs you to consult his former ship cook, Sprogger, to track down the behemoth. Following the loss of his initial ship, Captain Hecklebury Smotts procured a second craft called Smotts' Revenge, gathering a fresh crew and provisions to take vengeance on the sea giants. The venture ended in disaster when the giants shattered the ship and slew the crew, leaving Smotts adrift once more in a lifeboat. During the onslaught, the giant Negolash took the captain's cutlass.

The Caravan Road. The Caravan Road is an Alliance quest that traces the footsteps of the missing night elf priestess Velinde Starsong. Following information uncovered in Booty Bay, the trail leads north from the perilous jungles of Stranglethorn Vale into the shadowed town of Darkshire. Tracking Velinde Starsong across the world brings adventurers from the forests of Ashenvale all the way to the southern port of Booty Bay. There, Caravaneer Ruzzgot recalls an unusual passenger: a night elf priestess traveling alongside his dusty shipping caravan. Such solitary journeys are rare for her kind, making her journey through the lawless jungle of Stranglethorn Vale stand out in the minds of merchants.

The Carevin Family. The Carevin Family is a short Alliance investigation quest that connects the mystery of Velinde Starsong to the monster hunters of Duskwood. Guided by town records clerk Daltry, adventurers seeking the lost priestess turn to Jonathan Carevin, patriarch of a family dedicated to culling beasts and fiends. Searching for Velinde Starsong leads away from the ancient forests of Kalimdor and deep into the haunted gloom of Duskwood. Upon arriving in Darkshire, municipal clerk Daltry finds no official log of an elven priestess ever boarding in town. However, mentioning the savage wolf-men seen in Ashenvale immediately catches his ear, as beasts fitting that description have recently begun terrorizing the surrounding woods.

The Charge of the Dragonflights. Anachronos, of the bronze dragonflight, meets you in Tanaris to wrap up the first part of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands. That chain is the road toward opening the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj. This meeting wraps up the opening stretch of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, the chain that leads toward opening the Gates of Ahn'Qiraj. Anachronos is the one who closes this first part with you.

The Chill of Death. In the town of Brill, a Forsaken tailor named Gretchen Dedmar struggles against the creeping cold of mortality and decay. Fearing that the encroaching mindless state will rob her of the ability to serve Lady Sylvanas, she asks for simple materials to sew herself a warm blanket. For the Forsaken, undeath is not a static condition of eternal preservation. As Gretchen Dedmar describes, the lingering Plague of Undeath runs through her body like an icy serpent, draining the warmth from her limbs and threatening to pull her into the mindless state that afflicts so many wandering corpses in Tirisfal Glades. Her shivering hands make ordinary work nearly impossible.

The Cirrusfly Queen. The Cirrusfly Queen is a hunt targeting the matriarch of the aggressive insect hive dwelling in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. Following early reconnaissance of the infestation, Elatrell Featherlight directs recruits into the heart of the grove to eliminate the queen and cull the swarm at its source. Ending her reign provides immediate relief to the local rangers working to keep the wilderness manageable. Initial efforts against the cirrusflies revealed that simply swatting away stray worker drones would never curb the infestation spreading across Thendal Grove. Elatrell Featherlight tasks capable wanderers with penetrating deeper into the southeastern reaches of the grove where the main hive lies. There, the queen directs the colony under the vigilant protection of heavier soldier drones.

The Cliffspring River. The Cliffspring River is a major waterway in northern Darkshore that is rapidly turning foul and threatening the settlement of Auberdine. Thundris Windweaver tasks Alliance investigators with gathering a water sample from beneath a river bridge waterfall to confirm the creeping blight. Thundris suspects a deeper source of corruption beyond the riverbanks. Running down from the eastern highlands, the Cliffspring River empties into the coastal shoals along Mist's Edge, just north of Auberdine. Recently, its waters have begun to turn foul, carrying an unnatural rot toward the night elf settlement. Fearing that the wash will poison the surrounding shores and the town's supplies, Thundris Windweaver sends scouts upriver to draw samples from the waterfall pool beneath the road bridge.

The Coast Isn't Clear. Along Westfall's western shore, shipwrecked sailors face murloc tribes on the beaches. Captain Grayson at the Westfall Lighthouse calls for help clearing the coast so survivors can reach land safely. Westfall's western coast has claimed countless ships. Reefs, sudden squalls, and jagged rocks break vessels against the shoals. Survivors may cling to wreckage and crawl ashore, hoping for rescue. But murloc tribes control the beaches and show no mercy to castaways.

name.ptBR: O mar não está para peixe

text.enUS: The Coastal Menace. Captain Grayson's ghost watches Westfall's rocky coast, where his ship broke on the rocks. He blames Old Murk-Eye for driving the lighthouse keeper's family from their post, then killing them in a later attack. Now he calls on travelers to hunt the murloc chieftain and bring justice to the shore. The Westfall Lighthouse once guided ships through the southern coast's jagged shallows. Captain Grayson's vessel struck the rocks in the dark after murlocs frightened the lighthouse keeper's family into leaving their post. The family returned and lit the flame again, but safety did not last. A cunning, ruthless predator still stalked the shore.

The Collector. An intercepted dispatch from gnoll raiders in Elwynn Forest lays out when gold shipments leave the abandoned mines. It is addressed to a figure called 'The Collector' and points to an organized operation near Stormwind's garrison. Riverpaw gnoll packs in western Elwynn Forest carry more than furs and crude weapons. Among them, a parchment called the Gold Pickup Schedule lays out dates and times for gold taken from local mines. The intercepted note directs each shipment to an overseer identified only as 'The Collector.'

The Collector's Schedule. Near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch, The Collector's Schedule marks when illicit gold shipments move through Elwynn Forest. Gnolls carry the handwritten itinerary, and Marshal Dughan recognizes the name it records. The Collector's Schedule marks dates and times for gold shipments from Elwynn's mines. Stormwind has not officially worked the mines for months, driven off by banditry and creature incursions, yet ore still leaves in an orderly flow. The itinerary names the days and hours when a figure called The Collector receives each shipment. The trail points to a camp near the Brackwell Pumpkin Patch in eastern Elwynn Forest. When Marshal Dughan sees the schedule, he recognizes the Collector's name. Who pays for the stolen gold remains unknown.

The Color of Blood. The Color of Blood is a personal task given by Nikova Raskol, a grieving grandmother living in Stormwind City. Consumed by anger over the murder of her young grandson inside the city's prison, she hires adventurers to venture into The Stockade and claim the Defias gang's trademark red bandanas as retribution. When Stormwind's regular military forces were deployed away to distant fronts, local defense fell upon volunteer recruits and the city's youth. Nikova Raskol's grandson, Mac, was only fourteen years old when he took up arms as a guard within The Stockade. Tasked with watching hardened criminals and mutinous members of the Defias Brotherhood, the young guard was thrust into an intensely dangerous environment far beyond his experience.

The Corrupter. A piece of flayed demon skin, taken from the Burning Blade at Thunder Axe Fortress, smells rotten yet is surprisingly pliable. Red markings of some language cover one side, and at the bottom is a clear symbol that looks like a signature. Maurin Bonesplitter at Ghost Walker Post may be able to tell you more. The torn skin stinks of rot, yet it bends easily, though it seems dry and fragile. Unrolled, it carries red markings on one side, a written language of some sort. At the bottom is a plain symbol, which you take to be a signature.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, but first any wards the creature holds against scrying must be broken. For that, Maurin wants the scalp of a Hatefury shadowstalker, hunted in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast. Maurin Bonesplitter believes the demon lord can be found, given the proper reagents. If the lord is as powerful as Maurin suspects, those must come from deadly creatures, and Maurin is sure you, acting in the Warchief's name, will take up the challenge. The first need is to break any wards the demon has against scrying. For that Maurin wants a scalp from a satyr, though only a Hatefury shadowstalker's will serve. They are to be sought in the old ruins of Desolace's northeast, near Sargeron.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter wants an oracle crystal, which the naga craft for their oracles, in order to find the demon lord Azrethoc. A vast coral reef lies northwest along the coast, home to the Slitherblade naga, and they will not welcome you. Maurin Bonesplitter says an oracle crystal will do the job of finding the demon lord Azrethoc, whose signature was on the skin you brought. Naga craft such crystals, and their oracles use them. Up the coast to the northwest lies a vast coral reef which the naga have made their home while near the shore, and the oracles can be found in that place. The Slitherblade there are deadly and will take your intrusion badly, so Maurin urges you to go carefully and quickly.

The Corrupter. Maurin Bonesplitter has found the demon lord far more dangerous than expected. He is certain Takata Steelblade doubts his abilities, and leaving the swordsman uninformed of what happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin sends you to speak with Takata, who is nearby. Maurin Bonesplitter finds the creature much more dangerous than he had anticipated. No doubt Takata Steelblade questions whether Maurin can handle it, and not being told of what just happened would insult Takata's honor. Maurin asks you to speak to the swordsman and offer to slay the demon, should Takata allow it. Maurin cautions you not to press Takata too hard, since it is better if Takata believes the idea is his own.

The Corrupter. Takata Steelblade knows nothing of Lord Azrethoc, yet sides with Maurin that the demon lord must be stopped, all the more if Azrethoc is trying to win influence over the Burning Blade. Takata trusts you to gather a party against Azrethoc and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Takata has never heard of Lord Azrethoc, yet agrees with Maurin that the demon lord must be stopped, above all if Azrethoc is reaching out to sway the Burning Blade. You have already shown you want to aid the Warchief, so Takata trusts you to gather a party and slay Azrethoc and his warlock servant, Jugkar Grim'rod. Takata tells you to head directly south, to Mannoroc Coven, where both are found.

The Corruption Abroad. Argos Nightwhisper, a night elf envoy visiting Stormwind, seeks capable adventurers to cross the Great Sea and aid his brother in northern Kalimdor. His brother Gershala studies spreading ecological decay in Darkshore, where fresh hands are desperately needed. While Stormwind contends with internal turmoil and regional unrest, representatives from the distant kaldorei lands can be found wandering its stone streets. Argos Nightwhisper came seeking seasoned champions willing to look beyond human borders. The kaldorei are relatively new allies to the Eastern Kingdoms, and formal military aid is scarce, leaving family members and researchers to recruit whatever independent champions answer the call.

The Criminal Element. The Criminal Element involves striking against the Highlands Bandits and their leader, "Badwind" Bennic, who operate out of a concealed cave behind a waterfall in the Shen'dar Highlands. With local forces overwhelmed by the recent arrival of a menacing cult, outside help is required to eliminate Bennic and disrupt the outlaw gang. In the Shen'dar Highlands, a den of outlaws known as the Highlands Bandits has entrenched itself inside a hidden cave concealed behind a northern waterfall. Led by the notorious "Badwind" Bennic, the cutthroats were already a persistent nuisance to locals before an enigmatic cult arrived in the highlands, after which their lawlessness escalated into an outright terror. With local defenders stretched thin and unable to spare forces, adventurers are tasked with infiltrating the waterfall redoubt, breaking the gang's ranks, and eliminating Bennic.

The Crone of the Kraul. The Crone of the Kraul is an Alliance quest offered by Falfindel Waywarder at Thalanaar, on the border of Feralas and the Thousand Needles. After reading the recovered journal of the fallen dwarf Henrig Lonebrow, Falfindel tasks adventurers with infiltrating Razorfen Kraul and slaying the quilboar crone, Charlga Razorflank. At the secluded night elf outpost of Thalanaar, Falfindel Waywarder grieves for the druid Heralath and the dwarf Henrig Lonebrow. Lonebrow, an Explorers' League traveler captured by the quilboar, escaped Razorfen Kraul only to die on the road, leaving behind a tattered journal detailing the growing menace within Razorfen Kraul. Realizing there is no time to send a runner to Darnassus for military reinforcements, Falfindel turns to passing adventurers to strike directly at the heart of the thorned dens.

The Crown of Will. In Tarren Mill, Melisara wants the Crushridge ogres thinned out before any real blow is struck against Mug'Thol, whose ogres now hold the Ruins of Alterac. You are sent to cut down Crushridge maulers. Mug'Thol and the Crushridge ogres have taken the Ruins of Alterac. Melisara says it will be hard to punish Mug'Thol while so many ogres stand around. First their numbers must be reduced, and only after that will the next move be made. Your part is to hunt the Crushridge maulers.

The Crown of Will. With the ogres' defenses weakened, Melisara in Tarren Mill wants the heads of Mug'Thol's three lieutenants, Targ, Muckrake and Glommus, before Mug'Thol himself is dealt with. Mug'Thol's lieutenants are Targ, Muckrake and Glommus, all loyal to him, though Melisara wonders what could make an ogre loyal. You are to kill all three and bring their heads back to Tarren Mill. After that, only Mug'Thol's own head remains to be taken, crown and all.

The Crown of Will. With Mug'Thol's lieutenants dead, Melisara in Tarren Mill sends you after Mug'Thol himself. You are to bring back his head and the Crown of Will, and the Crushridge resistance will be over. Only Mug'Thol is left now. Melisara expects him to be reluctant to give up the Crown of Will, and thinks he is probably expecting you, given what befell his lieutenants. Find him, kill him, and carry his head and the Crown back to Tarren Mill.

The Crown of Will. Only one thing remains. The Crown is to go to Sharlindra in the Undercity, who will make sure it reaches Lady Sylvanas. Melisara says all that remains is to take the Crown to Sharlindra in the Undercity, and she will pass it on to Lady Sylvanas. Melisara also warns you against thinking of using it for your own purposes. Mug'Thol's fate, Melisara says, is illustration enough.

The Cult of the Damned. The Cult of the Damned is a task confronting mortal servants of the Scourge active within Tirisfal Glades. By culling Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers, defenders prevent the Lich King's insidious living agents from repeating the betrayals that originally shattered Lordaeron. The Cult of the Damned represents the mortal face of the Scourge. Composed of living men and women who swore fealty to the Lich King, these cultists act where mindless dead cannot. In Tirisfal Glades, where inhabitants already contend with roaming undead and relentless zealots of the Scarlet Crusade, newly discovered cells of Dark Neophytes and Dark Enforcers signal an insidious attempt by the Scourge to re-establish a foothold.

The Curious Visitor. After the Stockade uprising, Warden Thelwater has a troubling discovery about Bazil Thredd. For months before the riot, a man named Maelik visited Thredd with legitimate papers. Warden Thelwater learned that Bazil Thredd had not been abandoned by his former comrades, as the guards believed. Months before the riot, a quiet visitor began meeting with Thredd once or twice a week. He passed every inspection, carried authorized paperwork, and gave his name as Maelik. Thelwater suspects the visits helped coordinate the bloody uprising. He gathers a physical description and sends you to City Architect Baros Alexston to learn who the visitor was.

The Curse of the Tides. With her knife recovered from Pretty Boy Duncan, Catelyn the Blade loans the troll artifact so it can be used against a sunken altar off the coast. Baron Revilgaz in Booty Bay wants the Stone of the Tides for his collection of ancient troll artifacts. Catelyn the Blade lends her recovered troll dagger to break an altar submerged deep beneath the waves. Though no expert on troll ruins like her father, she has heard of a sunken troll city, and she points toward it, out near the reef northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp. Within the underwater ruins of the Vile Reef, the Altar of the Tides rests, surrounded by a distinct blue glow amid sea life and murlocs.

The Cursed Crew. First Mate Fitzsimmons, the sole living survivor of the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras, asks for mercy on behalf of his lost brethren. Trapped by a dark relic hidden aboard their sunken ships off the Wetlands coast, the drowned sailors and marines wander the wrecks as restless undead. When the Third Fleet of Kul Tiras foundered along the jagged shores north of Menethil Harbor, its tragedy did not end beneath the waves. While First Mate Fitzsimmons managed to wash ashore alive, his fellow crewmen met a fate far worse than death. A mysterious and terrible treasure hidden deep within one of the hulls unleashed an eerie sorcery upon the dying sailors, binding their souls to the sea-battered timbers and denying them the peace of the grave.

The Damned. The Damned is an early task given to newly awakened Forsaken by Novice Elreth in the chapel of Deathknell. In exchange for the materials needed to fashion crude clothing and battlefield wraps, Elreth provides salvageable armor to protect fledgling undead from the perils surrounding the cemetery. Awakening into undeath leaves little room for vanity or sentimentality. Novice Elreth attends to the steady stream of fresh Forsaken pulled from the dirt of Deathknell, serving as an assistant to Shadow Priest Sarvis. Between tending to battered soldiers and mending garments, supplies run perilously thin. To ensure new arrivals do not fall apart during their initial trials, Elreth sends them into the surrounding glades to hunt native duskbats and scavenger wolves, trading salvaged armor for the raw pelts, wings, and sinew required to keep the camp functioning.
