text.enUS: The Dark Iron War. At the northern edge of the Wetlands, Motley Garmason mounts a desperate defense to reclaim Dun Modr from the Dark Iron clan. After enemy saboteurs shattered the Thandol Span and seized the town, the Ironforge Mountaineers are left holding a tenuous line while waiting for reinforcements that may never arrive. Dun Modr once stood as Ironforge's proud bastion guarding the southern end of the Thandol Span, the colossal bridge connecting Khaz Modan to Lordaeron. When Dark Iron saboteurs and demolitionists detonated the bridge's archway, they severed Alliance transit and swiftly overwhelmed the stronghold. Motley Garmason and a handful of surviving defenders managed to pull back just far enough to establish an observation camp, but without immediate counterattacks, the entire northern gateway risks permanent Dark Iron dominion.

The Day After. The Day After is an Alliance quest that bridges the survivors in Ironforge with researchers stationed in Dun Morogh. Gnoarn, lamenting the catastrophic radiation leak that cost him his legendary hair and his homeland, sends adventurers to assist Ozzie Togglevolt in Kharanos as he searches for a solution. Gnomeregan's downfall took a deeply personal toll on every survivor, and Gnoarn is no exception. A refugee in Ironforge's Tinker Town, Gnoarn mourns not only the mechanical wonderland stolen by trogg invaders, but also his prized gnomefro—a glorious mane lost in an instant when a bolt of toxic fallout blasted him. Driven by lingering fury toward the troggs and a desperate hope to recover the city, he directs sympathetic travelers to colleagues who might still possess the scientific prowess to salvage what remains.

The Dead Fields. The Dead Fields is an assault mission issued by High Executor Hadrec from the Sepulcher. Forsaken scouts discovered that the Rot Hide gnolls infesting an abandoned northern farmstead are led and shielded by the Scourge banshee Nightlash, whose destruction is critical to securing Silverpine Forest. North of the Sepulcher lies an abandoned farmstead known as the Dead Fields. Once ordinary farmland, the grounds are now choked by Rot Hide gnolls—pestilent, plagued scavengers that infest the Silverpine countryside. High Executor Hadrec previously sent small raiding parties to dislodge them, but every offensive stalled under unnatural magical resistance.

The Deathstalkers. This task marks the trial for initiates seeking entry into the Deathstalkers, the covert and lethal arm answering to Lord Varimathras in the Undercity. Assigned by Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter, the mission demands ruthless initiative to intercept a traveling messenger. Completing it opens the door to deeper clandestine schemes within the Forsaken realm. The Deathstalkers do not admit just anyone into their ranks. Operating directly under dreadlord Varimathras, this secretive order acts as both the secret police and elite assassination corps of the Forsaken. To earn their notice, a hopeful agent must demonstrate cunning, discretion, and an unhesitating willingness to eliminate targets. In the shadowy corners of the Rogues' Quarter, handler Mennet Carkad sets an initiation trial designed to weed out the weak or overscrupulous.

The Deathstalkers. This covert assignment sends an undercover operative into the Undercity's shadowy underbelly to interrogate an unwitting conspirator. Acting under orders handed down from Lord Varimathras, you pose as an expected messenger to uncover treason within the Forsaken's own capital. The Deathstalkers do not merely eliminate external threats to the Forsaken; they maintain a ruthless vigil over their own citizens. Acting on suspicions harbored by Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker Mennet Carkad sets an infiltration plan in motion. Armed with a forged or acquired letter of introduction belonging to Astor Hadren, you are tasked with slipping past the suspicions of a local merchant named Andron Gant.

The Deathstalkers. This errand continues the Deathstalkers' deception of the informant Andron Gant in the Undercity. Still believing you are the messenger he was expecting, Gant hands over a ledger meant for his secret contacts, and the operative delivers it instead to Mennet Carkad in the Rogues' Quarter. The exchange marks the transition from simple inquiries to deeper, more covert operations on behalf of the Forsaken state. The Deathstalkers do not rely solely on brute force or shadow magic; their operations depend heavily on mundane ledgers, recorded names, and meticulous surveillance. Andron Gant, operating out of the Undercity, hands over a personal ledger crammed with intelligence, believing it bound for the mysterious employers he secretly serves. Taken in by the operative's disguise, Gant even asks that the same courier be sent in the future, never suspecting that his ledger is headed straight to the Deathstalkers.

The Deathstalkers. This errand marks the formal induction of a capable operative into the ranks of the Deathstalkers, the Forsaken order of assassins and spies. Tasked with delivering Andron's Ledger directly to the dreadlord Varimathras, the courier brings proof of the Syndicate's covert activities to the highest tier of Undercity leadership. After unearthing incriminating records from Andron Gant, Mennet Carkad officially welcomes the operative into the Deathstalkers. The organization serves as Lady Sylvanas's eyes, ears, and daggers throughout Lordaeron, relying on intelligence networks, ruthless efficiency, and stealth to eliminate threats before they surface. Gaining formal recognition within the order is a major milestone for any aspiring rogue or scout in the Undercity.

The Deathstalkers' Report. The Deathstalkers' Report is a crucial military courier assignment delivered to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher. After securing injured Deathstalkers in the northern wilds, you carry their gathered intelligence concerning unexpected Scourge activity back to Forsaken high command. This dispatch alters the Forsaken's assessment of their hold on Silverpine Forest. The Deathstalkers act as the eyes, ears, and daggers of the Dark Lady, pushing into the untamed wilderness ahead of standard military units. Near the border of Tirisfal and Silverpine, an advance patrol ran into catastrophic resistance while charting enemy movements. Though Deathstalker Quinn barely survived his injuries and Erland fought his way to safety, their scouting mission yielded intelligence essential to the Forsaken occupation of Silverpine Forest.

The Decrepit Ferry. High Executor Hadrec directs Forsaken champions east of The Sepulcher to investigate the Decrepit Ferry. The lakeside dock has been swarmed by Scourge and rot hides, raising alarms about the enemy's expanding footprint along the shores of Lordamere Lake. Following the suppression of Scourge presence in the Dead Fields, High Executor Hadrec turned his strategic gaze toward the eastern waterways of Silverpine Forest. The Decrepit Ferry, once a mundane transit crossing linking mainland Lordaeron to the island estates of Lordamere Lake, had quietly evolved into an active hive of undead activity. Hadrec dispatched scouts to discern what drew the Lich King's servants to these rotted piers.

The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard the Horde's foothold in Stranglethorn Vale and protect their supply chain to Stonard. To keep that supply chain safe, he directs Horde champions to thin out the Lashtail Raptors outside Grom'gol Base Camp. At Grom'gol Base Camp, Commander Aggro'gosh carries the duty of protecting every member of the Horde within the jungle. The camp exists to keep supplies flowing safely to Stonard, but some of the local inhabitants are standing in the way.

The Defense of Grom'gol. Commander Aggro'gosh seeks to safeguard Grom'gol's supply lines through Stranglethorn Vale. After the earlier hunt thinning the raptors outside the camp, a band of ogres encamped at the nearby Mizjah Ruins continues to harass supply caravans heading toward Stonard. The Horde's presence in northern Stranglethorn Vale is centered on supplying Stonard, an outpost of vital strategic interest. While Commander Aggro'gosh did not arrive with the intention of fighting every native group, a band of local Mosh'Ogg ogres has claimed the Mizjah Ruins southeast of the camp. Warnings have failed to stop their continuous raids against Horde supply shipments, prompting the commander to order a strike against the ogre brutes and witch doctors holding the ruins.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, The Defias Brotherhood is building a network beyond banditry. Wiley the Black sends word of its ties to gnolls, kobolds, and goblins. Gryan Stoutmantle needs this intelligence to measure the full reach of the conspiracy choking Westfall. Wiley the Black says telling what he knows about the Defias could cost him his life. Along the edges of Redridge and Westfall, he has caught wind of an operation far greater than highway robbery. His sealed note describes how the Brotherhood has coordinated groups that are usually hostile to one another across the countryside.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's troubles reach Stormwind. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you to deliver Wiley's Note to Master Mathias Shaw, suspecting a link between the Defias and the old Stonemasons Guild. A mention of the Stonemasons in Wiley's communications catches Gryan Stoutmantle's attention. The builders rebuilt Stormwind City after the First War, but the guild has long been thought scattered or dissolved. If the Defias Brotherhood shares ties with them, Westfall's rural insurgency is more than a disorganized band of outlaws.

The Defias Brotherhood. Mathias Shaw sends a confidential report from Stormwind to Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Shaw has investigated the former Stonemasons Guild to help Stoutmantle uncover the origins of the Defias Brotherhood.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the People's Militia seeks the Defias Brotherhood's hidden base. A turncoat agrees to guide Alliance champions there in exchange for protection. The road passes through Moonbrook, where Edwin VanCleef's inner sanctum lies hidden. Gryan Stoutmantle's fight against the Defias Brotherhood reaches a turning point when a captured brigand agrees to talk. His former brothers may execute or assassinate him, so the Defias Traitor bargains with the People's Militia. Escort him safely through hostile territory, and he will reveal where Edwin VanCleef and his ringleaders hide. The thieves' network silences those who speak out, and the turncoat needs armed protection along the road.

The Defias Brotherhood. This mission represents the culmination of Gryan Stoutmantle's long campaign to reclaim Westfall from outlaw rule. Tasked with entering the Deadmines, Alliance champions must breach the criminal hideout and strike down the mastermind Edwin VanCleef himself. For months, Gryan Stoutmantle and the beleaguered People's Militia have fought a desperate holding action against the Defias Brotherhood across Westfall. With the true location of the thieves' stronghold uncovered beneath Moonbrook, Stoutmantle issues his final, grim decree: Edwin VanCleef must be assassinated to break the back of the rebellion once and for all.

The Defias Brotherhood. In Westfall, the Defias Brotherhood's thieves threaten the farms and roads. Gryan Stoutmantle sends you from Sentinel Hill east into Redridge to seek a contact who may know where they hide. Westfall's harvests are gone, and bandits in red bandanas roam the land. Gryan Stoutmantle and the People's Militia hold Sentinel Hill under near-constant attack, but they do not know who directs their enemies. Stoutmantle knows that fighting stray looters will not save the region. He needs to find the cartel's inner circle and learn who commands it.

The Defias Traitor. At Sentinel Hill, The Defias Traitor has given up the Brotherhood's hidden base to save his life. The captured outlaw is held beneath the watchtower after the People's Militia caught him stealing Farmer Saldean's wagon.

The Demon Scarred Cloak. The Demon Scarred Cloak is a ragged pelt recovered from the legendary white wolf Ghost Howl, who roams the grassy plains of Mulgore. Marked by an enduring wound inflicted during past clashes with the Burning Legion, the pelt serves as proof of the beast's release from torment. Bringing it to the elders of Bloodhoof Village brings closure to the story of a tragic local legend. Ghost Howl is an elusive white wolf known across Mulgore for both his ferocity and his sorrowful howl. When slain, the beast leaves behind a pelt that is visibly scarred by foul demonic corruption. These lingering marks date back to the wolf's desperate battles against the invading demons of the Burning Legion, a confrontation that left Ghost Howl wounded in both flesh and spirit long after the Third War came to a close.

The Demon Seed. Acting on orders funneled through Neeru Fireblade, Ak'Zeloth charges Horde travelers with neutralizing the Demon Seed atop Dreadmist Peak. By deploying an unstable Flawed Power Stone upon an altar of fire, adventurers shatter a potent conduit tied to the Burning Legion before its dark influence spreads further across the Barrens. Perched within a jagged cave high on Dreadmist Peak sits the Demon Seed, suspended over a demonic altar of fire. The artifact acts as a powerful apparatus for the Burning Legion, anchoring demonic frequencies into the dusty heart of the Barrens. To combat this threat, the orc Ak'Zeloth prepares specialized power stones capable of disrupting the artifact's link to the Nether, provided an operative can carry one to the peak before its volatile energy collapses.

The Den. The Den is the culmination of a Horde infiltration campaign against night elf druids entrenched on Stonetalon Peak. Directed by the blood elf operative Braelyn Firehand, champions delve into the Talon Den's subterranean barrow chambers to crack a layered security system and plunder the druids' hidden relics. Perched upon the highest reaches of the Stonetalon Mountains, the Talon Den serves as an underground redoubt for night elf druids. Carved deep into living stone, these barrow halls are designed to shield meditating guardians and shelter sacred treasures away from prying eyes. Knowing the strategic and arcane value of what rests within, Braelyn Firehand interrogates a captured druid to pry loose the secrets of their defenses.

The Den. The Den is the sheltered cave at the heart of the Valley of Trials in southwestern Durotar. Serving as the primary base of operations for young orc and troll adventurers, it provides martial and magical training before they set out into the wider world. Tucked into the red canyon walls of the Valley of Trials, the Den serves as an austere proving ground. Within its carved, shadowy interior, novice fighters, spellcasters, and hunters report to veterans like Gornek and Zureetha Fargaze. It is here that fledglings receive their foundational combat instruction, supplies, and initial rites of passage, hardening them for the harsh realities of Durotar and the greater struggles facing the new Horde.

The Deserters. Captain Garran Vimes says deserters have settled into a tower that Theramore had abandoned. The tower stands at Lost Point, which lies southeast of the inn. A man called Jacken leads the deserters, and Vimes wants information about Reethe from him. Vimes admits that holding on in the marsh has been a struggle, though the resolve of Vimes's people has kept several defensive watchtowers standing. Scouting reports say deserters have moved into an abandoned one at Lost Point, which lies southeast of the inn. A man named Jacken leads them. Vimes asks you to see what information Jacken will give up about Reethe, and warns that Jacken may not part with it easily.

The Deserters. Asked about Reethe, Balos Jacken, leader of the Lost Point deserters, calls him a coward and says the deserters drove him from their camp. Jacken then asks you to forget you ever ran into them. Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore is the one to tell about Reethe. Jacken says the deserters drove Reethe out for repeatedly plundering the ogres' stores at Brackenwall Village. By Jacken's account the deserters are too few to stand against those ogres, and Reethe crossed the line once too often, so the band left him to manage alone. In return for the answer, Jacken asks that you forget the meeting.

The Disruption Ends. Following evidence of targeted raids on Horde supply lines, Thork commands the execution of Kreenig Snarlsnout, the Razormane quilboar warband leader orchestrating caravan attacks from Durotar. By breaking their defensive line and claiming Kreenig's tusk, the Horde aims to throw the aggressive tribe into disarray. The vital trade route running between Durotar and the Crossroads has suffered continuous ambushes, threatening the flow of provisions and reinforcements across the northern Barrens. Scout reports pinpointed the culprit: an aggressive Razormane quilboar raiding party organized and directed by a chieftain named Kreenig Snarlsnout. Recognizing that scattered skirmishes would never permanently secure the road, Thork ordered a direct decapitation strike against the leader to break the tribe's tactical cohesion.

The Divination. Thadius Grimshade asks you to give him room while he performs a ritual of divination. He means to follow the link between the feather you brought and its owner until it leads him to Sharpbeak. Thadius follows the link between Sharpbeak's feather and the gryphon who owns it, hoping to reach Sharpbeak himself. He asks for silence and room to work. He admits it may not go to plan, and warns that in that case you had better close your eyes.

The Doomed Fleet. The Doomed Fleet is a journey northward dispatched by Bishop Farthing in Stormwind's Cathedral of Light. Seeking a way to defeat the powerful necromancer Morbent Fel, heroes are sent across Khaz Modan to the drowned wreckage off the coast of the Wetlands. Conventional steel has proven ineffective against the dark wards shielding Morbent Fel at his retreat on the Forlorn Rowe. To pierce such necromantic defenses, Bishop Farthing instructs adventurers that they must forge a weapon bound to the Holy Light. The key component is Lightforge Iron, a rare and consecrated metal whose strikes carry holy truth, cutting through sorcerous protections that turn aside ordinary blades.

The Dormant Shade. The Dormant Shade is a dark ritual performed at Gunther's Retreat on Brightwater Lake in Tirisfal Glades. By placing a mystic candle upon an old, blood-soaked table, a traveler summons forth the Scourge agent Lillith Nefara, whose defeat proves to Gunther Arcanus that the visitor is the Lich King's foe. On the island of Gunther's Retreat in Brightwater Lake rests a battered, bloody dinner table. Far from an ordinary piece of neglected domestic furniture, it serves as the physical focus for a sinister conjuration. Stained with dried gore and abandoned to the shadows, the table acts as a makeshift ritual slab where death and dark magic linger.

The Dunemaul Compound. Andi Lynn in Gadgetzan warns of a large band of nomadic ogres that has lately arrived in Tanaris. South of town they have formed a compound, and Andi Lynn wants it destroyed before they can build up a force. A large band of nomadic ogres has arrived in Tanaris of late. South of Gadgetzan they have seized a broad stretch of desert and formed the Dunemaul Compound. Several smaller bands wander the desert as well, and some have invaded the old troll ruins. Andi Lynn says the ogres cannot be allowed to build up a force.

The Ectoplasmic Distiller. Mux Manascrambler in Gadgetzan is working on his extra-dimensional ghost revealer but has run out of funds and manpower. The first piece he needs is an ectoplasmic distiller, and he asks you for a list of costly materials and forty gold to build it. After A Supernatural Device, Mux Manascrambler welcomes your help with his ghost revealer, a machine meant to reach across dimensions. The first piece is a distiller, meant to gather the fabric of death itself, and he warns that building it will not be easy. He wants a delicate arcanite converter, four greater eternal essences, ten stonescale oil and twenty-five volcanic ash, plus forty gold. The ash is for a filter, and it must come from the lava pools of the Burning Steppes. Mux admits the materials are pricey, but swears every one will be needed.

The Eighteenth Pilot. Pozzik will be busy fitting the new fuel regulator into the racer designs, but suggests that you help the team further by speaking with Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth, and likes to add modifications to the racers. Pozzik says the fuel regulator is keeping him busy, but you can help the team some more by talking to Razzeric on the Shimmering Flats. Razzeric is the team's pilot, its eighteenth in fact, and likes to add little modifications of his own to the racers. Pozzik adds that Razzeric is a little off his rocker, so you should try not to seem too surprised.

The Elder Crone. The Elder Crone is a Horde summons directing adventurers from the scarred crags of Stonetalon Mountains to the towering mesa of Thunder Bluff. Seeking spiritual guidance to mend Stonetalon's enraged elements, Seereth Stonebreak sends emissaries to consult the influential tauren elder Magatha Grimtotem on Elder Rise. In the crags of Stonetalon Mountains, goblin deforestation and mining ventures have enraged the local elemental spirits. Seereth Stonebreak, recognizing that raw force alone cannot quell the land's spiritual anguish, concludes that the wisdom of elder shamans is needed. Aware of few tribal leaders by name, Seereth knows of Magatha Grimtotem, an elder reputed for her deep knowledge and commanding presence.

The Embalmer's Heart. The Embalmer's Heart is an unholy relic beating within the undead corpse of Eliza, buried deep in Duskwood. Once belonging to a grief-stricken alchemist known as the Embalmer, it was transplanted through dark magic to revive his deceased wife, becoming the primary anchor of his twisted power. According to the folklore of Darkshire, the Embalmer was once a gentle alchemist whose mind shattered upon the passing of his beloved wife, Eliza. Desperate to reclaim her from the grave, he turned to foul sorceries and cut out his own heart, placing it inside Eliza's lifeless chest. While the unholy transfusion successfully stirred her corpse back to unlife, the resurrection twisted her into a ravenous creature consumed by an insatiable hunger for living human flesh, forcing the horror-stricken alchemist to inter her once more within the earth.

text.enUS: The Emerald Dreamcatcher. Tallonkai Swiftroot in Dolanaar asks adventurers to recover a cherished heirloom from his abandoned home in Starbreeze Village. The Emerald Dreamcatcher, gifted to him by the druid warden Gaerolas Talvethren, was left behind when corrupted Gnarlpine furbolgs overran the tranquil settlement. Reclaiming this amulet prevents its gentle nature-magic from falling into foul hands. The emerald dreamcatcher is far more than a decorative trinket. A gift from Gaerolas Talvethren, the honored warden of the sleeping druids within Ban'ethil Barrow Den, the amulet was crafted to channel the serene currents of the Emerald Dream. By siphoning this pure spiritual energy, the dreamcatcher bestows peace and fortune upon its bearer. Such tokens are exceedingly rare, bestowed upon only a trusted few whose lives are intertwined with the forest's stewardship.

The Enchanted Glade. In the Oracle Glade on northwestern Teldrassil, Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak struggles to protect the ancient Oracle Tree from aggressive Bloodfeather harpies. After a dispatched runner bound for Darnassus is slain, defenders are called upon to strike back at the harpies' nests and recover their belts as proof. The Oracle Glade is one of Teldrassil's sacred retreats, centered upon a colossal, ancient specimen known as the Oracle Tree. Sentinel Arynia Cloudsbreak was dispatched with an escort of warriors to keep watch over this venerable bough. Unfortunately, savage Bloodfeather harpies have encroached on the hollows, nesting aggressively throughout the surrounding canopy and threatening anyone who draws near.

The Ensorcelled Parchment. A spell on a parchment makes its writing unreadable, apart from one word at the top: Nagaz. You are to take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore. A spell lies on the parchment and keeps its writing from being deciphered. Only a single word at the top can be made out, the name Nagaz. You are to take it to Loremaster Dibbs in Southshore.

The Escape. Maybell Maclure waits for a way to slip away from her family and meet Tommy Joe Stonefield. You bring her William Pestle's Invisibility Liquor, brewed from crystal kelp gathered across the region. The Maclures and Stonefields have feuded for generations, leaving no room for courtship. Gramma Stonefield turns to William Pestle, an alchemist in the Lion's Pride Inn in Goldshire. With crystal kelp from nearby lakes, Pestle brews Invisibility Liquor strong enough to hide Maybell's escape from the Maclure homestead.

The Escape. The Escape is an escort quest in the northern Barrens where adventurers help the goblin pilot Wizzlecrank flee the Venture Company's drill site at the Sludge Fen. Trapped inside a stolen prototype shredder, Wizzlecrank requires protection against waves of company mercenaries until he clears the industrial pit. The mission concludes by reporting back to his contact, Sputtervalve, in the port town of Ratchet. Having ignited the stolen prototype deep within the Sludge Fen drill site, Wizzlecrank quickly discovers that commandeering Venture Company engineering is easier said than done. With only a rudimentary grasp of the control levers and switches, the goblin lurches the heavy machine across the muddy quarry floor. His erratic driving and roaring mechanical joints inevitably alert nearby laborers and armed guards, turning what should have been a stealthy extraction into a chaotic running battle up the western ramp of the excavation pit.

The Essence of Aku'Mai. Je'neu Sancrea at Zoram'gar Outpost has noticed the naga of Blackfathom Deeps harvesting potent sapphire clusters from the caverns. Concerned by their magical properties and elemental water energies, the shaman tasks Horde adventurers with recovering the gems before they can be misused. On the mist-shrouded shores of the Zoram Strand, the Darkspear shaman Je'neu Sancrea keeps watch over ancient Kaldorei ruins now overrun by sinister forces. Deep within the submerged chambers of Blackfathom Deeps, naga have begun mining vibrant sapphire formations that sprout along the damp cavern walls. Sensing that the serpentine invaders seek to harness this volatile power, Sancrea seeks to intercept the harvest before their designs can come to fruition.

The Essence of Eranikus. You engage the Oathstone of Ysera's Dragonflight, and Itharius speaks straight into your mind. Taking up the charge means helping Ysera's Dragonflight redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus, and the first sacrifice is to give Itharius the gem that chains the part of Eranikus' mind that is still free. Itharius waits in the Swamp of Sorrows. Through the Oathstone, Itharius tells you that accepting this charge means aiding Ysera's Dragonflight to redeem the corrupted soul of Eranikus. Itharius expects many sacrifices from the two of you, and the first is to hand over the gem that has bound whatever free-willed part of Eranikus' mind remains. The Oathstone and the Chained Essence of Eranikus must go to Itharius in the Swamp of Sorrows, and there you choose whether to aid the dragonflight.

The Everstill Bridge. The Everstill Bridge is a rebuilding effort led by Foreman Oslow in Lakeshire to repair the town's damaged stone bridge. Progress has ground to a halt because iron meant for the project was redirected into weapons during the last orc invasion, and the replacement caravan from Stormwind was ambushed by Redridge gnolls. The stone bridge spanning Lake Everstill is the lifeblood of Lakeshire, connecting the western roads back toward Elwynn Forest with the far bank and the northern passes. During the recent orc incursions, the town was pushed to the brink. With survival hanging in the balance, Lakeshire melted down its structural iron supplies to forge munitions, blades, and plate armor to repel the Blackrock invaders, leaving the bridge incomplete and vulnerable.

The Eye of Paleth. This quest sees an adventurer recover a blackened, pulsating gem known as the Cursed Eye of Paleth from the flooded wreckage of the Intrepid. Recovered at the behest of the haunted sailor Fitzsimmons, the malevolent artifact must be brought to Menethil Harbor so the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow can divine how to purge its blight. Beneath the treacherous waters of the Baradin Bay, resting inside the locked strongbox of the sunken vessel Intrepid, lies no ordinary treasure. The chest yields a blackened orb pulsing with an unsettling radiance: an Eye of Paleth. Rather than gleaning sacred light, this particular stone has been warped into an engine of suffering, heavily tied to the restless spirits and doom that claimed the sailors of the Third Fleet.

The Fall of Ameth'Aran. Sentinel Tysha Moonblade tasks adventurers with exploring the haunting ruins of Ameth'Aran in Darkshore to decipher ancient stone tablets. These inscriptions record the tragedy and ruin that struck the Highborne city during the Sundering. The gathered knowledge is intended for the Circle of Ancients in Auberdine, recovering history largely lost during the War of the Ancients. Long before the coast fractured into the misty expanse of Darkshore, Ameth'Aran stood as a flourishing settlement where Queen Azshara's elite sorcerers practiced powerful arcane magic. Following the cataclysmic destruction of the Well of Eternity ten thousand years ago, the city was reduced to broken marble and cracked pillars. Today, it remains haunted by the restless, anguished spirits of the Highborne who died when their golden age tore apart.

The Family Crypt. The Family Crypt is a Horde quest tasking players with confronting the Scourge inside the Agamand Family Crypt. Commanded by Magistrate Sevren in Brill, adventurers must destroy the raised Agamand ancestors and slay the skeletal Scourge commander, Captain Dargol. While the Forsaken have carved out a fragile dominion in Tirisfal Glades, remnants of the Lich King's Scourge remain deeply entrenched in the countryside. The Agamand Mills, once a prosperous flour-producing heartland of Lordaeron, have become a dangerous Scourge stronghold. Magistrate Sevren in Brill watches this military buildup with grave concern, knowing that every inch yielded to mindless undead undermines the Forsaken's independence.

name.enUS: The Family and the Fishing Pole
name.esES: La familia y la caña de pescar
name.frFR: La famille à la canne à pêche
name.itIT: The Family and the Fishing Pole

text.enUS: The Family and the Fishing Pole. Gubber Blump, a dwarf dwelling on the docks of Auberdine, seeks assistance catching native Darkshore grouper. Hostile murlocs prowling the coast have disrupted the town's small fishing boats, leaving Gubber stranded on shore and offering an heirloom rod to anyone willing to cast their line. Gubber Blump takes great pride in his lineage, declaring that the Blump name has long been synonymous with the art of angling. While night elves occupy most of Auberdine, dwarves and gnomes have settled into its docks and bustling port facilities. Rather than digging into stone, Gubber spends his days gazing out over the misty waters of the Veiled Sea, eager to haul in the local bounty.

The Fargodeep Mine. Kobolds have overrun The Fargodeep Mine south of Goldshire, between the Stonefield and Maclure farms. The mine's fall points to a growing pest problem across Elwynn Forest. While Northshire Valley faces its own vermin, reports reach Goldshire that kobolds have claimed another vital site. Between the feuding Stonefield and Maclure homesteads south of town, the Fargodeep Mine once supplied stone and ore for the realm. Now shrill chattering and tallow candles fill its damp tunnels. Marshal Dughan sends you to scout the depths and learn how bad the trouble is.

The Fate of Yenniku. At Grom'gol Base Camp, the head of Nezzliok speaks from the bubbling cauldron, ready to tell what became of the young Darkspear troll Yenniku. Kin'weelay stands beside the pot, waiting to hear the spirit's words. Having placated the spirits of Gan'zulah and Nezzliok, you listen as the head within the bubbling cauldron finally imparts its secret. Kin'weelay stands right beside the cauldron, waiting to hear it.

text.enUS: The Fate of a Loved One. The Fate of a Loved One is a quest concerning Resaan, who ventured into the dangerous Ruins of Ban'aethal to scavenge supplies and never returned. Over a week later, his grieving partner asks travelers bound for the ruins to discover his fate and bring him home or recover his cherished heirloom. The Fate of a Loved One centers on a desperate plea from someone whose partner, Resaan, ventured back into the Ruins of Ban'aethal. Despite earnest pleas for him to stay, Resaan felt compelled to brave the ruins in search of supplies, leaving behind someone who now waits in agonizing uncertainty.

The Fate of the Den. The Fate of the Den recounts the grim aftermath of a cultist assault upon a secluded druid den. An adventurer is dispatched to carry a recovered missive to Lotheluum in Valanaar, delivering news of severe casualties. The dispatch uncovers a deeply troubling reality: someone within Valanaar has been feeding vital information to the enemy. Following a violent incursion by cultists at the druid den, the surviving defenders find themselves battered and mourning the loss of their comrades. While the immediate crisis was stabilized with outside aid, the physical and emotional devastation is immense. Those who fell cannot be restored, and the wounded survivors remain in no condition to undertake a long trek while lingering cultists still roam nearby.

text.enUS: The Final Message to the Wildhammer. Otho Moji'ko gives you a spear soaked in blood and bound with gryphon feathers. You are to take it to Aerie Peak, in the west of the Hinterlands, and drive it into the earth beside the well at the heart of the town. Following Another Message to the Wildhammer, Otho Moji'ko gives you the final message: a spear soaked in blood and bound with gryphon feathers. Carry it to Aerie Peak and plant it, dead center of town beside the well, to show the dwarves that trolls mean business. Otho hopes you come back alive, and warns of furious Wildhammer dwarves and rowdy Alliance folk.

The Flame's Casing. After Forging the Shaft, Kalaran Windblade says one final piece is needed for the torch. A large Twilight's Hammer encampment lies to the northwest, rumored to hold symbols and idols honoring its god, and Kalaran wants a single Symbol of Ragnaros. Kalaran calls this the last piece the torch needs. Northwest, among the mountains, a large Twilight's Hammer encampment is rumored to hold symbols and idols honoring their god, and these could carry enough enchantment for a magical casing. Kalaran asks for one Symbol of Ragnaros and will try to draw the magic out of it. The torch of retribution lacks one thing, a suitable source of arcane energy.

The Flawless Flame. Kalaran Windblade says you made the right choice, and that the blow must fall where it does most harm: the four sentry towers. With all four aflame, an offensive can begin before anyone has time to react. To set them alight, Kalaran needs to craft the torch of flawless flame. After Divine Retribution, Kalaran tells you the plan: burn the four sentry towers, so that an offensive can begin before anyone has time to react. Setting them ablaze takes the proper tool, and the tool takes materials. Kalaran will craft the torch of flawless flame if you bring four hearts of flame and four globes of golem oil, and points you first to the golems and elementals of these lands.

The Flying Machine Airport. Tasked by Apothecary Zamah from Thunder Bluff, Horde adventurers hunt down a hidden Venture Company landing pad nestled above Stonetalon Mountains. Carrying an alchemical Toxic Fogger, operatives must slip into the heart of the goblin logging operations to gas their air transit hub. The mission strikes directly at the cartel's communications while underscoring the ruthless methods of the Royal Apothecary Society. While the tauren seek to protect Stonetalon from deforestation and ravaging machinery, the Forsaken bring an entirely different philosophy to the front. Apothecary Zamah readies Apothecary Lydon's toxin to disrupt the Venture Company's logistics. Rather than attacking foot soldiers or loggers directly, she targets the cartel's link to the outside world: a rumored copter pad used to ferry light cargo and messages between Stonetalon and distant corporate offices.

The Forest's Bounty. The Forest's Bounty is a local quest in Shadowgale Forest where a timid forager asks for help collecting fallen acorns. Fierce predatory raptor-birds prowl the deeper woods, making harvesting too perilous without an adventurer's protection. The gathered acorns are then roasted into a tasty forest meal. A cautious forager seeking food in Shadowgale Forest finds themselves in a bind. While acorns lie scattered across the woodland floor, the surrounding trees are prowled by fierce, raptor-like creatures. Having gathered whatever fell near safety, the forager depends on passing travelers to venture into the wilder groves so that neither goes hungry.

The Forgotten Heirloom. In Westfall, the Furlbrows have fled their farm, leaving a cherished heirloom behind. Recovering the pocket watch offers them a chance to salvage something personal from the chaos spreading through the region. Farmer Furlbrow and his wife Verna were driven from their Westfall farm by violence. Shouts rose from the pumpkin patches in the night, waking them with little time to gather what they could carry. In the rush to flee, Furlbrow left behind the pocket watch Verna's father gave him on their wedding day. It remains in the wardrobe of their occupied farmhouse.

The Forgotten Pools. Tonga Runetotem at the Crossroads sends Horde adventurers to inspect the Forgotten Pools, an oasis northwest of the settlement. The Cenarion Circle suspects that unseen subterranean energies are causing verdant life to surge through the arid savannah. Long ago, the Barrens flourished as a fertile, vibrant land before ages of war and Sundering shattered the continent, reducing the region to sun-baked scrubland. Yet recently, lush oases have miraculously begun to take root in the dry basin. To the druids of the Cenarion Circle, this sudden bloom is unnatural. Rather than ordinary springs, they sense subterranean powers pressing upward through the earth, coaxing vegetation and wildlife to life in anomalous pockets across the wastes.

name.esES: La furia mora en las profundidades

text.enUS: The Fury Runs Deep. This quest represents Motley Garmason's bitter quest for vengeance against the Dark Iron dwarf Kam Deepfury. Deepfury masterminded the assault on the Thandol Span, which claimed the lives of Bronzebeard defenders, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Dissatisfied with Stormwind's political detention of the culprit, Motley enlists an adventurer to enact dwarven justice inside the Stockade. The northern reaches of the Wetlands bleed from perpetual clashes between the Bronzebeard defenders at Dun Modr and the insurgent Dark Iron dwarves. When the Thandol Span came under attack, the sabotage cost vital dwarven lives, including the brother of Longbraid the Grim. Intelligence gathered by Roggo revealed that Kam Deepfury planned the deceitful strike. Instead of facing execution on the front lines, however, Deepfury ended up secured inside the Stormwind Stockade—held as a political prisoner rather than executed for murder.

The General's Response. General Marcus Jonathan sends word to Lakeshire while Redridge waits for aid. His dispatch acknowledges Magistrate Solomon's plea against the Blackrock orcs and gnolls, but offers no immediate reinforcements from Stormwind. Magistrate Solomon sends an urgent plea to Stormwind City for troops to defend Redridge from the gathering Blackrock orc clans and Gnoll warbands. General Marcus Jonathan replies that the plea has been forwarded to the throne, but no soldiers are being sent now. He orders the letter returned to Lakeshire. Solomon is left troubled by Stormwind's delay and suspicious that something is wrong with its leaders.

The Giant Guardian. Rockbiter, a giant, was supposed to be watching over his little friend Shay, a night elf girl, but somehow she got away. Worried and unsure what to do, he asks you to go and look for her. Rockbiter was supposed to look after Shay. The last time he saw her, the two of them were walking through the ruins just north of where he stands. All was well until he turned around and found her gone. He cannot work out what to do, but he knows your legs travel much faster than his, so he asks you to search for her.

name.ptBR: O dom da visão do céu

text.enUS: The Gift of Skysight. The Gift of Skysight is an early rite of passage for young Windshapers learning to harness their innate connection to the spiritual realm. Under the direction of Ventaari Brightwish, initiates travel to an Elemental Convergence to awaken their perception and listen directly to the whispers of the spirits. Windshapers possess an inherent bond with the elemental forces that shape their world, embodied by the sacred faculty known as Skysight. This gift allows mortal senses to attune to spiritual wavelengths, bridging the physical gap between the living and the unseen. While a Windshaper can invoke this inner vision across the wilds, doing so near points of concentrated power deepens the connection, unlocking resonant boons and hidden wisdom whispered on the wind.

The Glowing Fruit. The Glowing Fruit is a quest in Teldrassil initiated by discovering a strange fruited plant growing wild in the forest. Suspecting something unnatural, young adventurers deliver the luminescent specimen to the herbalist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth for study. While traversing the misty boughs of Teldrassil, explorers occasionally stumble across curious, luminous flora bearing large, round fruit. Given the delicate balance of the World Tree and the recent strange behaviors among the island's wildlife, unusual botanical specimens demand careful investigation. Convinced that the strange growth should not be ignored, adventurers pluck the radiant harvest to bring to someone versed in the flora of the wild.

The Glowing Shard. The Glowing Shard is a mysterious emerald-hued gem plucked from the dark depths of the Wailing Caverns. Swirling with smoky essence beneath its polished surface, this disturbing relic drives adventurers to seek answers in Ratchet and beyond. Drawn from deep within the Wailing Caverns, the glowing shard immediately unnerves those who hold it. Brilliant green and seemingly solid, it holds churning, mist-like shadows beneath its crystalline face. The crystal exerts a subtle pull, demanding attention while exuding a deeply unsettling aura that hints at the corrupted nature of the slumbering druids and their nightmare-infested sanctuary.

The Goddess Provides. The Goddess Provides is an introductory kaldorei quest centered on recognizing Elune's divine gifts. Set in the boughs of Teldrassil following the end of the Long Vigil, it teaches young night elves to embrace the lunar guidance and cloaking shadows bestowed by Mother Moon. For millennia following the Sundering, the kaldorei maintained their solitary Long Vigil, watching over Kalimdor and guarding the sacred peaks of Mount Hyjal. The devastation of the Third War and the climactic defense of the World Tree forced an end to that ancient seclusion. Now relocated to the sheltering boughs of Teldrassil, the night elves face an unfamiliar world, stepping onto the broader stage of Azeroth by aligning themselves with distant allies across the ocean.

name.enUS: The Good News and The Bad News
name.deDE: Die gute und die schlechte Nachricht
name.frFR: La bonne nouvelle et la mauvaise nouvelle
name.itIT: The Good News and The Bad News
name.ptBR: The Good News and The Bad News

text.enUS: The Good News and The Bad News. Narain Soothfancy has read through the ledger and has both good news and bad. He is nearly certain he can build an arcanite buoy to your specifications, but he needs a great deal of arcanite, elementium ore and fine gems. This comes once the chicken, the goggles and the second Draconic For Dummies book are all done. Narain Soothfancy reads the ledger in silence, mumbling under his breath. He is ninety-nine percent sure he can make an arcanite buoy that will work as you specified, but says all of that depends on the bad news. For the buoy he wants twenty arcanite bars, ten elementium ore, ten Azerothian diamonds and ten blue sapphires. Bring them, and he will craft it.

The Gordunni Orb. Rok Orhan knows the enemy well, but is a warrior and cannot say what the Gordunni orb is capable of. Rok knows of a mage in Orgrimmar who can tell more. The orb is yours to carry to Uthel'nay, at Orgrimmar's Darkbriar Lodge. This follows Dark Ceremony. After Dark Ceremony, Rok Orhan holds the orb, but admits to being a warrior who cannot begin to say what it can do. Rok knows a mage in Orgrimmar who will be able to say more, and sends you off with the orb to find Uthel'nay at the Darkbriar Lodge.

The Gordunni Scroll. A soiled scroll lies in the Gordunni Outpost, and picking it up shows what seems to be a meeting or ceremony. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache would be interested in it, and in what it might mean for the Gordunni. Taking up the soiled scroll, you see that it appears to depict a gathering or ceremony of some kind. Rok Orhan in Camp Mojache, you judge, would want to see it, and to learn what it might mean for the Gordunni.

The Grand Skyseer. The Grand Skyseer is an introductory journey into the heart of Valanaar, directing travelers to seek an audience with Ayessa Dawnsinger at the Windshaper lodge. As tensions simmer between local factions and a shadowy cult threatens the region, the Windshapers urgently seek individuals gifted with spiritual sight. Upon arriving in the town of Valanaar, travelers are directed toward the central lodge where the Windshapers convene under the leadership of Grand Skyseer Ayessa Dawnsinger. Having caught the attention of Elder Amberwind through notable deeds in Shen'dar Village, new arrivals are welcomed into the fold of those attuned to the spirits. Yet Valanaar remains fraught with external and internal dangers, requiring newcomers to navigate fragile local politics carefully.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest where the traveler Sam teaches fledgling adventurers the art of roughing it in the wild. By pausing to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers learn how to sustain themselves on the road before pursuing specialized tradeskills. The wide lands of Azeroth call to countless restless souls seeking fortune, danger, and renown. Yet raw ambition alone cannot shield a fledgling adventurer from the biting cold or exhaustion of the open road. Mastering basic wilderness craft—knowing when to stop, build a fire, and gather one's strength—is the quiet foundation upon which every legendary journey is built. Sam's invitation offers newcomers a chance to pause and learn these essential outdoor survival habits.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest offered by the outdoorsman Raan, who teaches novice adventurers the fundamentals of wilderness survival. By resting beside a basic campfire to gain Boosted Rest, wanderers learn essential campcraft before venturing toward nearby trade trainers to learn practical professions. The Great Outdoors serves as an introductory lesson in surviving beyond the safety of settlement walls. Offered by an experienced wilderness traveler named Raan, the task reminds wandering adventurers that raw ambition and steel are useless without the practical campcraft needed to endure harsh elements. Raan welcomes aspiring wanderers into the ranks of restless souls seeking fortune and glory, offering practical guidance to those willing to learn.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival quest offered by Brakk to aspiring adventurers. By learning to rest beside a basic campfire, travelers discover the fundamentals of sustaining themselves in the wild before pursuing practical tradeskills. Venturing into the untamed reaches of Azeroth requires more than martial grit; it demands the basic knowledge to endure the elements. Brakk greets aspiring adventurers with a hearty 'Lok-tar', recognizing the restless spirit of those seeking fortune and glory. To survive the long road ahead, every traveler must first master the art of making camp and recovering their strength amidst the wilderness.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory quest that instructs aspiring adventurers in the fundamental arts of wilderness survival. Guided by the traveler Kaga, newcomers learn how to recuperate beside a basic campfire before advancing to learn tradeskills and craft specialized camp fixtures. Every adventurer setting foot beyond the safety of civilization quickly discovers that raw courage is not enough to survive the frontier. The Great Outdoors introduces newcomers to the vital necessity of wilderness acclimation. Taught by the experienced traveler Kaga, this brief lesson reminds fledgling heroes that thriving in unexplored territories begins with knowing how to establish a camp and endure the open elements.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors is an introductory wilderness survival lesson offered to hunters by an experienced scout named Lyreena. It emphasizes the importance of resting beside a campfire to recover and gain the Boosted Rest buff while journeying through the untamed wilds. Venturing beyond civilization's borders demands more than sharp aim and keen senses; it requires respect for the raw untamed elements. An experienced scout named Lyreena offers guidance to wandering hunters, welcoming them to pause their trek and take comfort by her campfire. In the perilous wilds of Azeroth, knowing how to establish a hearth and replenish one's strength between hunts is just as critical as knowing how to track quarry.

The Great Outdoors. You learn how rest and preparation help you survive beyond city walls. Travelers across Azeroth teach new wanderers to rest by a campfire and prepare for the wilds. Even a sharp blade or potent magic cannot protect you from the wilds if you neglect the basics of survival. Seasoned wanderers near roadside clearings share this lesson with travelers leaving their home valleys. Resting by a campfire eases sore boots, settles the mind, and readies you for the road ahead. Regular rest and preparation give you a better chance of surviving long enough to find fortune and glory.

The Great Outdoors. The Great Outdoors introduces wandering adventurers to the essentials of wilderness survival and campcraft. By taking a seat at Eric's campfire, travelers learn how to recuperate properly in the wild before taking up tradeskills to support their journeys. Stepping out into the wider world requires more than ambition and a weapon or holy symbol. For fledgling travelers, survival depends on knowing how to rest properly amidst the elements. At his basic campfire, the seasoned traveler Eric welcomes wandering adventurers to take a seat, warm themselves by the embers, and discover how vital proper rest is before tackling the untamed wilderness.

The Green Hills of Stranglethorn. Barnil Stonepot was trusted to proofread the manuscript for Hemet Nesingwary's novel, but a fierce gust of wind scattered the loose pages across the jungle. To spare him his master's anger, you are asked to scour the wilds, assemble the missing pages into four complete chapters, and return the finished work. Following your arrival in the expedition camp after Welcome to the Jungle, Barnil Stonepot finds himself facing a disaster. While reviewing the draft of Hemet Nesingwary's novel, The Green Hills of Stranglethorn, a sudden gale caught the loose leaves and flung them into the wild. Though he managed to recover a fair portion of the work, many sheets remain lost in the brush. To keep his master from discovering the mishap, he needs every misplaced page tracked down and compiled into Chapter I, Chapter II, Chapter III, and Chapter IV.

The Greenwarden. "The Greenwarden" is an Alliance breadcrumb quest directing travelers deeper into the marshes of the Wetlands. Sent by First Mate Fitzsimmons from Menethil Harbor, adventurers venture northeast into the swamp to seek out a mysterious entity rumored to dwell among the beasts. Around the docks of Menethil Harbor, sailors and wanderers trade breathless stories of a beast lurking out in the swamp. First Mate Fitzsimmons paints the Greenwarden as an appetite with legs, warning gullible seekers that stepping off the dry road means being bitten in two by 'ol' Greenie.' To the dockside folk, anything massive lurking out in the murky waters is just another man-eating hazard of the marsh.

The Grizzled Den. Pilot Stonegear of Kharanos is looking for someone with true dwarven grit to spruce up his beloved siege engine, Trollplow. To test an aspiring adventurer's mettle, he sends them west into the perilous cavern known as the Grizzled Den to hunt savage wendigos for their thick pelts. Operating a massive dwarven siege tank requires nerves of iron and the constitution to handle teeth-rattling machinery in freezing mountain air. Pilot Stonegear, stationed at Steelgrill's Depot near Kharanos, claims to have both in spades. Rather than simply giving up work or respect easily, he challenges newcomers to prove they possess the same stalwart temperament by trekking into the frozen hills to face native beasts.

name.esES: Las armas del Fuerte del Norte

text.enUS: The Guns of Northwatch. Captain Thalo'thas Brightsun in Ratchet has had enough of his merchant vessels being blasted to splinters by the Alliance gunners at Northwatch Hold. He hires Horde champions to march down the Merchant Coast, silence the hold's artillery officers, and take the badges of their fallen infantry. Northwatch Hold looms over the southern coast of the Barrens, established as a fortified bastion for the humans of Theramore. While intended to guard Alliance interests and monitor Horde activity in Kalimdor, the soldiers within have succumbed to severe paranoia. Viewing any unfamiliar sail as hostile, their rampart batteries open fire indiscriminately, threatening peaceful merchant traffic and the privateering vessels of Ratchet.

The Hammer May Fall. Dispatched by Tallow from Tarren Mill, Horde champions are directed across the mountains into the Arathi Highlands to relieve the embattled settlement of Hammerfall. Before reporting to Drum Fel, adventurers must prove their battle readiness against the brutish Boulderfist ogres lurking near the ruins of Stromgarde. In Tarren Mill, Tallow harbors little patience for untested adventurers wandering through the Foothills. Seeing undisciplined recruits standing idle while distant allies bleed, he directs capable fighters east through Thoradin's Wall into the Arathi Highlands. The Horde outpost of Hammerfall stands besieged on multiple fronts, but Tallow refuses to send warm bodies unless they have proven their worth against substantial opposition first.

The Harvester. The Harvester is a quest initiated by discovering the severed head of a strange, alien insectoid predator in the southern Barrens. Bringing this unsettling specimen to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo reveals disturbing implications for the land's spiritual and ecological balance. Amid the savannahs of the southern Barrens, travelers occasionally come across an unsettling sight: the severed head of a silithid known as the Harvester. Unlike the native lions, raptors, and kodo that roam the grasslands, this chitinous insectoid seems completely outside the natural order of Kalimdor. Its presence suggests an encroaching alien ecology that does not belong in the open plains.

The Haunted Isle. Krazek keeps his ears open for unusual rumors throughout Booty Bay on behalf of Baron Revilgaz. A tale shared by tavern sailors speaks of a haunted island off the coast, inhabited by water elementals and the ghost of a raving goblin. Delivering this rumor to Revilgaz piques the baron's interest in an ancient troll legend. In the bustling port of Booty Bay, Krazek gathers word of anything unusual happening throughout Stranglethorn Vale at the request of Baron Revilgaz. While Krazek normally pays little heed to spectral gossip, stories told by sailors drinking in the local tavern caught his attention. They speak of an offshore isle occupied by water elementals and haunted by a raving goblin ghost, so he asks you to relay the story to the baron.

The Haunted Mills. Coleman Farthing of Brill seeks vengeance against his former landowners, the Agamands, by having their restless undead remains collected and destroyed. This task sends you north to Agamand Mills to put down Devlin Agamand, the sharp-tongued younger son of the estate. It begins a bitter vendetta against the family who failed to protect Tirisfal's common folk from the Plague. Before the Third War, Agamand Mills stood as the breadbasket of northern Tirisfal, owned by a wealthy landed family. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, the common folk looked to the noble landowners for safety, only to find neither sanctuary nor salvation. Coleman Farthing survived in undeath, but his heart remains consumed by hatred for the family he served. Rather than letting them roam in eternal torment, Farthing desires the morbid satisfaction of collecting their bones to desecrate them under his own heel.

The Head of the Beast. In Stormwind, The Head of the Beast carries you from Elling Trias to Master Mathias Shaw in Old Town. Reporting Lord Gregor Lescovar’s death confirms your place in Stormwind’s covert intelligence network. Master Mathias Shaw directs Stormwind’s covert apparatus through SI:7 from hidden chambers in Old Town. When you report Lescovar’s death, Shaw recognizes your skill and ruthlessness, praises your efficiency, and thanks you for serving the people of Stormwind.

The Hermit. Concerned by the prolonged absence of an elderly recluse, Elaine Carevin in Darkshire asks travelers to check on him. The lonely old man, Abercrombie, lives in a rickety shack perched right on the edge of Raven Hill Cemetery. In a beleaguered settlement like Darkshire, it is easy to lose track of eccentric loners until their absence becomes alarming. Elaine Carevin recalls an old man who once regularly trekked into town for provisions before abruptly vanishing from sight. Given the relentless dangers haunting the roads of Duskwood, she directs wandering adventurers to inspect his shack overlooking the haunted expanse of Raven Hill Cemetery to make sure he hasn't met a grim fate.

The Hidden Key. Tucked away in the binding of Bookie Herod's ledgers is a small brass key alongside notes referencing a secure strongbox. Locating this container deep within the cavern complex behind Kurzen's Compound may reveal how Private Thorsen was betrayed. Searching through Bookie Herod's ledgers yields no direct mention of Private Thorsen, but it reveals something else: a small brass key concealed inside a book's binding. Scraps among the paperwork make passing mention of a secure strongbox tucked away inside the Stockpile, the cavern complex at the rear of Kurzen's Compound. Opening that container might reveal how Thorsen's cover was blown.

The Hidden Niche. After uncovering the talkative remains of Alaric from a shallow grave outside Fenris Keep, adventurers are directed back inside the stronghold. Guided by the deceased human's memories, travelers seek out a forgotten alcove concealed behind a dusty shelf to grant him final repose and claim an old relic. Even after death, Alaric retains vivid memories of Fenris Keep during its better days. Relieved to be exhumed from a shallow, unceremonious dirt grave by Horde scouts, his skeletal remains refuse to simply be carried off to the Sepulcher. Instead, he bargains with vital information: a hidden niche inside the keep's southwestern tower containing an item deeply treasured by Thule Ravenclaw and his fellow mages.

The High Wilderness. Angelas Moonbreeze and Troyas look into old ruins in the forests of Feralas, yet lately Troyas goes alone to the High Wilderness, which worries Angelas. Gordunni ogres hold that ground. Angelas hopes you will make the ruins to the southeast a little safer by culling the ogres. Angelas Moonbreeze admits the work is dangerous, but Angelas and Troyas keep exploring the ruins scattered through the forests of Feralas. Lately Troyas goes to the High Wilderness alone, and Angelas worries. The Gordunni ogres have taken over there and do not take kindly to anyone who enters their territory. Angelas hopes you will go to the ruins southeast of here and cull some of them, to make it safer for Troyas: eight Gordunni Warlocks, eight Gordunni Shamans and eight Gordunni Brutes.

The Hills Have Eyes. "The Hills Have Eyes" is a quest in the Gustberry Lowlands where the beleaguered farmer Aamelia takes a stand against highwayman bandits. Adventurers launch a preemptive strike on an encampment in the northern hills to diminish the bandit forces before their leader, Ferauu, launches a raid. In the Gustberry Lowlands, a farmer named Aamelia faces an impending assault from a ring of outlaws led by Ferauu. Rather than waiting passively for doom to arrive at her doorstep, she urges travelers to launch a preemptive strike against a bandit encampment in the hills to the north. By taking out the highwaymen before they muster their attack, she aims to thin their ranks and buy precious time.

The Horn of the Beast. A gigantic horn that came from Margol the Rager in Searing Gorge is scratched and cracked, with a broken axe head lodged in its rough surface. The axe head is etched as the property of Mountaineer Pebblebitty, and it shatters into a million pieces when you try to dislodge it. The horn is to be taken to Pebblebitty. The horn from Margol the Rager is covered in scratches and cracks. Lodged in it is an unusual metal object, a broken axe head etched to show that it belonged to Mountaineer Pebblebitty. When you try to work it free, it shatters into a million pieces.

The Howling Vale. Assigned by Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow at the Shrine of Aessina, this quest sends Alliance adventurers into the Howling Vale near the Felwood border. The ruined shrine of Mel'Thandris has been overrun by feral wolf-men known as worgen. By consulting the sacred Tome of Mel'Thandris, investigators hope to uncover why these bizarre creatures have emerged in Ashenvale. While night elf sentinels expend heavy resources holding the line against the demonic corruption spilling out of Felwood, a new threat has quietly nested in the northern hills of Ashenvale. The ruined shrine of Mel'Thandris, hidden beyond a cavern path near the Felwood border, has fallen to ferocious wolf-men whose haunting cries echo across the canopy. The area is now known as the Howling Vale, and Sentinel Melyria Frostshadow fears this beastly infestation may herald another disaster for the woodland realm.

The Hunt Begins. The Hunt Begins is a foundational rite of passage for young adventurers in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa. Tasked by Grull Hawkwind, initiates are sent to hunt local plainstriders to provide meat and feathers for the village. Fulfilling this task marks the first step toward earning the respect of Chief Hawkwind and eventually gaining entry into Thunder Bluff. On the heights of Red Cloud Mesa, survival and tradition intertwine. The tauren hunt out of necessity to feed and clothe their people, while also viewing the stalk and chase as a vital test of discipline and sport. When the stores of Camp Narache run lean, the community looks to its rising youth to gather fresh plainstrider meat for cooking and sturdy feathers for tribal garments.

The Hunt Completed. The Hunt Completed is the culminating moment of Senani Thunderheart's great beast trials in Ashenvale. By felling Ursangous, Shadumbra, and Sharptalon, a Horde champion proves their strength, tenacity, and primal prowess in a contested forest. Senani Thunderheart, stationed among the Horde forces in Ashenvale, tests travelers not merely by their loyalty to the warchief, but by their understanding of wild survival. The Ashenvale Hunt targets three legendary predators stalked beneath the ancient boughs: the bear Ursangous, the cat Shadumbra, and the fierce hippogryph Sharptalon. Felling all three and securing their trophies proves a hunter's blood flows true in the challenger's veins.

The Hunt Continues. The Hunt Continues is an early rite of passage assigned by Grull Hawkwind in Camp Narache. It tasks aspiring hunters with gathering mountain cougar pelts from the southern hills to clothe the tribe's children and mend their tents. In Camp Narache, young hunters are taught that taking a beast is never an idle pursuit or a search for trophies. Grull Hawkwind charges fledgling adventurers with venturing into the southern hills of Red Cloud Mesa to track down mountain cougars. Rather than proving martial prowess alone, the task emphasizes responsibility to the community, showing that true hunters must provide essential provisions for their people.

The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a vital milestone for young tauren hunters in Mulgore, directing them toward advanced training in beast companionship. Dispatched by their local mentors once their basic marksmanship and tracking are proven, novices are sent to Bloodhoof Village to seek the counsel of hunter trainer Yaw Sharpmane. This journey initiates the spiritual and practical trials required to tame and bond with wild beasts. To the nomadic Shu'halo, hunting is sacred rather than mere sport. A hunter must understand the balance of nature, honor the spirits of the plains, and show respect for the animals that sustain the tribes. When a young hunter demonstrates sufficient prowess in surviving the wild and wielding a bow or gun, their elders recognize that they are ready to step beyond solitary tracking. The directive to seek out seasoned mentors marks the threshold of true adulthood in tauren culture.

The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a rite of passage directing young orc and troll hunters to Razor Hill. Under the guidance of master hunter Thotar, fledgling trackers learn the vital discipline of binding wild predators to their will. Up to this point, an apprentice hunter in Durotar relies solely on their own bow and cunning. Tracking prey through red clay canyons and harsh scrubland teaches patience, but true mastery in the Horde requires bonding with the untamed fauna of the land. Class trainers recognize when a student has grown capable enough to walk this road, directing them straight to Razor Hill.

The Hunter's Path. The Hunter's Path is a rite of passage offered to novice dwarven hunters across Dun Morogh once they reach basic competence in tracking and marksmanship. Local trainers direct their apprentices to Grif Wildheart in Kharanos to begin learning the art of taming wild beasts as permanent companions. Until a hunter masters the art of beast bonding, they walk the snowy crags of Dun Morogh alone, relying solely on axe, rifle, or bow. Trainers like Olmin Burningbeard and Tristane Shadowstone watch their pupils closely until they demonstrate the poise required to face a savage creature without killing it. Once a novice shows sufficient discipline, they are sent down the mountain roads toward Kharanos.

The Hunter's Way. The Hunter's Way is a rite of passage offered to aspiring trackers in Mulgore by the elder Skorn Whitecloud. To prove their emerging skill and respect for the wild, wanderers must fell the cunning flatland prowlers and present their claws to Melor Stonehoof atop Thunder Bluff's Hunter Rise. For the tauren, hunting is neither mere sport nor simple subsistence; it is considered one of their people's highest honors. It demands patience, awareness of the Earth Mother's balance, and reverence for the beasts that roam the rolling plains. Elder Skorn Whitecloud, resting in Mulgore after decades of tracking across Kalimdor, recognizes this restlessness in young adventurers. Rather than allowing them to wander aimlessly, he channels their ambition into a traditional trial of maturity and discipline.

The Islander. The Islander is an invitation extended by veteran warrior trainers across Azeroth to those who have proven their basic mettle in battle. It directs rising fighters to Fray Island off the Merchant Coast, where an insular brotherhood of warriors tests their peers in raw martial combat. Meeting the chief warrior Klannoc Macleod marks a pivotal step toward mastering advanced combat disciplines. Warrior trainers in capital cities across both the Alliance and the Horde recognize when a student has outgrown basic drills. Rather than formal rank or political loyalty, martial progression demands that combatants measure themselves against true peers. The journey sends warriors away from civilized sparring yards toward a rugged isle isolated in the Great Sea.

The Jasperlode Mine. Kobolds have overrun the Jasperlode Mine in eastern Elwynn. Marshal Dughan sends scouts to learn how far the infestation has spread. After kobolds swarmed the Fargodeep tunnels south of Goldshire, Marshal Dughan feared they had reached other mines. Jasperlode lies in the rocky foothills northeast of the Tower of Azora and supplies raw stone and metal to the kingdom. Dughan cannot spare Stormwind guards from their town patrols, so he sends independent adventurers east to see whether kobolds have taken this mine too.

The Journey Has Just Begun. "The Journey Has Just Begun" is a Horde quest offered in Orgrimmar to skilled leatherworkers following the defeat of Onyxia. Overlord Runthak recognizes the hero's craft and imparts the rare technique required to fashion protective cloaks from the broodmother's scales. This vital craft prepares the Horde for the deadly flames of Blackrock Spire. The fall of Onyxia represents a triumph for the Horde, but it does not mark the end of the threat posed by the black dragonflight. The broodmother's scaled hide possesses remarkable resilience against draconic flame. Rather than letting such materials go to waste, Horde leadership seeks craftsmen capable of turning the dragon's remains into defensive armor.

The Journey Has Just Begun. In Stormwind, Major Mattingly recognizes the artisan who brought down Onyxia. He teaches the craft needed to make a cloak from her scales. Few who helped bring down Onyxia can also work her hide. When an artisan with master leatherworking reports to Major Mattingly in Stormwind, the officer recognizes how much those skills matter in the battles ahead.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor tells you of Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck his ship in the northwest waters of Desolace, and he left a valuable chest behind and teleported away. The chest and what is inside are to be found. After Reclaimers' Business in Desolace, Kreldig Ungor tells you of a first order of business. It concerns Karnitol, a mage who is some kind of noble in Stormwind. Sea giants struck Karnitol's ship in the northwest waters of Desolace. Karnitol and his servants tried to carry one of his costlier chests to shore, but the giants swarmed in, and he gave up the chest and teleported himself and his servants out. The chest and its contents are to be found, then returned to Karnitol in Stormwind. It lies along the northern coastline, in the Ethel Rethor stretch.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. The chest of the mage Karnitol has been pried open, and it is completely empty. Long, deep scratches on its sides and top suggest neither man nor giant was responsible, and you return to Kreldig Ungor at Nijel's Point. You study what forced the chest open. Long, deep scratches run along its sides and top. They point to something that was neither man nor giant, and they do not look like the work of a dagger or sword. The chest is completely empty. With nothing else to be done, you close it and prepare to leave, knowing Kreldig Ungor will be disappointed.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor still thinks Karnitol's belongings can be found. Up the same coast, by Ranazjar Isle, the Slitherblade naga hold a place among night elf ruins that lie at the bottom of the sea, and Kreldig reckons the satchel is most likely there. Following the second part of the Karnitol shipwreck search, Kreldig Ungor tells you hope is not lost. Along the same coast but farther north, close to Ranazjar Isle, sunken night elf ruins lie on the ocean floor, and the Slitherblade naga call them home. Kreldig judges it the likeliest place for Karnitol's satchel. A Recovery Diver's Potion is provided.

The Karnitol Shipwreck. Kreldig Ungor sends you to Ironforge with Karnitol's satchel, to put it in the hands of Roetten Stonehammer, who will pay you for the work. Kreldig Ungor tells you to carry Karnitol's things back to Roetten Stonehammer in Ironforge, who will pay you for the work. With a laugh, Kreldig adds that Roetten may be so pleased that you get asked to join the Reclaimers full time. The way back should be made carefully and without dawdling, since Karnitol has little patience, though he is a generous man.

The Key to Freedom. A small brass key has found its way to you in Searing Gorge. A few words are scratched into its head, marking it as a Dark Iron outhouse key that is not to be copied. Where it leads, you cannot yet say. The brass key looks simple, but for the words scratched into its head, which read Dark Iron Outhouse and warn against duplicating it. Where it leads is unknown, and the way to learn is to search Searing Gorge for a use for it.

The Killing Fields. The Killing Fields is an Alliance quest offered by Farmer Saldean in Westfall. Saldean tasks adventurers with destroying the rogue Harvest Watchers that overrun his crops and the neighboring farmlands. It illustrates the collapse of local agriculture in the wake of the Defias Brotherhood's disruption. While many farmers across Westfall abandoned their acreage when bandits and outlaws swept through the region, Farmer Saldean and his family resolved to hold their ground. Unfortunately, squatting thieves are not the only threat choking the Saldean farm. The mechanical Harvest Watchers intended to tend and safeguard the grain have gone rampant, pacing the furrows and attacking anyone who approaches.

The Knife Revealed. Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the Stronghold's resident druid, who can learn an object's past by touching it. Ginro says Quintis owes a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt that this will clear. After Boat Wreckage, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you with the knife to Quintis Jonespyre, the resident druid of Feathermoon Stronghold, who has unusual skills. One is psychometry, learning an object's past just by touching it. Ginro will not say how it works, calling it magic Ginro does not and chooses not to understand, only that Ginro has seen it work. Quintis owes Ginro a Kalimdor Hold 'Em debt, which will be paid if Quintis works some magic on the knife. Quintis lives in a little tree-house in the Stronghold.
