text.enUS: The Kolkar of Desolace. This quest bridges Horde military operations between the Barrens and the bleak expanse of Desolace. Directed by the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate, Horde champions journey westward across the mountains to reinforce scout Felgur Twocuts at Ghost Walker Post. While the Horde contends with marauding centaur packs across the Barrens, commanders like Regthar Deathgate recognize that trimming branches will never kill a tree. The Kolkar clan traces its root strength directly to the desolate crags of Kalimdor's western coast. As long as their ancestral stronghold remains untamed, endless waves of raiders will bleed through the passes into Horde territory. Neutralizing the Kolkar requires striking at the source.

The Legend of Stalvan. The Legend of Stalvan begins in Darkshire with a foreboding vision from the town diviner, Madame Eva. Disturbed by an omen portending death for her granddaughter Alyssa, Eva draws upon her cards and trance visions to divine a single lingering name: Stalvan. To untangle this thread of dread, she sends travelers to consult town records in the Darkshire Town Hall. In the perpetual gloom of Duskwood, Madame Eva serves as Darkshire's resident seer, interpreting portents and reading cards for troubled locals. After being jolted awake by a terrible disturbance, Eva consulted her divination deck, only to draw the Death card in connection to her young granddaughter, Alyssa. Falling into a deep, shadowy trance to pierce the gloom, she pulled forth only a single clue: the name Stalvan. Terrified of what this omen means for her family and the town, she turns to capable adventurers to follow the thread before tragedy strikes.

The Legend of Stalvan. This errand begins the paper trail into the fate of Stalvan Mistmantle, sent by Clerk Daltry from the town hall of Darkshire. His oldest records point west to the abandoned Moonbrook Schoolhouse in Westfall, setting off a classic investigation into an ordinary man's unraveling. After the initial inquiries in Darkshire, Clerk Daltry pulls the town registry to locate Stalvan Mistmantle. To his surprise, the ledger hasn't been updated in years and lists Stalvan's last known residence far to the west, at the schoolhouse in Moonbrook. Unaware of the sinister nature of the investigation, Daltry treats it as routine bureaucratic upkeep, asking travelers to look into the address and gather whatever records might bring Darkshire's dusty archives up to date.

The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation unearths a forgotten chapter in the dark tale of Stalvan Mistmantle. A dusty, unsent letter pulled from a neglected footlocker in Moonbrook provides tangible proof of where he stayed before his vanished trail turned cold, leading back to Darkshire's records. While tracking down the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, an old footlocker tucked away in Moonbrook yields a vital piece of the puzzle: a dusty, unsent letter. Moonbrook, once a thriving agricultural settlement, fell into ruin and now teems with outlaws and restless specters. Stalvan's presence here was brief enough to escape common memory, but this neglected missive definitively places him in the hamlet.

The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a pivotal turn in the search for the elusive Stalvan Mistmantle, leading investigators out of the gloom of Duskwood and back toward the heart of the kingdom. A hasty, scratched-out entry discovered in Darkshire's town registry points across the river to Goldshire. Following the paper trail to the bustling Lion's Pride Inn is the next step in uncovering where the mysterious tutor went. While reviewing Darkshire's records, Clerk Daltry catches an oversight in the town registry. Tucked beneath an earlier entry for Stalvan Mistmantle lies a second destination, hastily written and partially scratched out as if someone had second thoughts or meant to obscure their movements. The note indicates that Stalvan intended to travel northwest toward Elwynn Forest, specifically to the Lion's Pride Inn.

The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to an abandoned letter left behind at Goldshire's inn years ago. Following the trail of Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Elwynn Forest and into Stormwind's Canal District. When Innkeeper Farley of the Lion's Pride Inn is asked about Stalvan Mistmantle, he recalls a stormy night years ago. A traveling courier had sought shelter from the pouring rain, only to rush downstairs around midnight in sheer panic. Dressed in only his sleepwear, the courier bolted straight out into the dark storm and was never seen again.

The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation directs searchers to the Canals of Stormwind City, where Caretaker Folsom watches over the remaining possessions of the ruined Flintridge family. Looking for answers regarding the mysterious Stalvan Mistmantle, adventurers must dig through crated estate goods while confronting restless spirits tied to a past massacre. Tracking Stalvan's movements leads out of the shadowed groves of Duskwood and into the heart of Stormwind. Beside the city canals, Caretaker Folsom looks after what little remains of the Flintridge household. According to Folsom, his father served the estate before him and had the grisly task of mopping up blood in the wake of a horrific household slaughter—a tragedy somehow tied to the name Stalvan.

The Legend of Stalvan. This step in the investigation leads deep into an old crate of Flintridge heirlooms left beside the canals of Stormwind City. Sifting through the dusty relics uncovers a torn journal page, offering a vital handwritten clue to the past life of Stalvan Mistmantle that leads to Marshal Haggard in Elwynn Forest. While digging through a sealed crate filled with musty heirlooms, old hunting trophies, and family portraits, investigators uncover a lone torn journal page hidden beneath a ceramic vase. Written in Stalvan Mistmantle's own hand, this remnant provides an intimate glimpse into the mind of a reclusive scholar before tragedy struck.

The Legend of Stalvan. This investigation into Stalvan Mistmantle leads out of Duskwood to an isolated home in southeastern Elwynn Forest. Marshal Haggard, an aging veteran whose eyesight has deteriorated, directs you to an upstairs chest containing an old bundle of papers left behind when he moved in. Marshal Haggard lives far from town on the southeastern fringes of Elwynn Forest, near the borders of Duskwood and Redridge. When he moved into his secluded home, he found a chest tucked away upstairs packed with old parchments. With his failing eyesight clouding over, he abandoned any effort to read them, leaving the documents undisturbed until an investigator comes asking about Stalvan.

The Legend of Stalvan. This errand marks a turning point in uncovering the history of Stalvan Mistmantle, sending investigators from Elwynn Forest back into the shadowed town of Darkshire. Guided by Marshal Haggard's memory of his service days, you bring a recovered journal page to Tavernkeep Smitts at the Scarlet Raven Tavern to identify the chilling handwriting. After recovering a weathered, torn journal page from Marshal Haggard's chest in Elwynn Forest, the retired commander cannot read the faded script due to his failing eyesight. Recognizing that the trail leads back across the river, Haggard recalls his past commanding the Stormwind Guard and remembers spending evenings at the Scarlet Raven Tavern in Darkshire. He directs you to Tavernkeep Smitts, a barkeep whose long tenure has made him an unofficial custodian of local history and rumors.

The Legend of Stalvan. This quest marks the moment where scattered rumors about Stalvan Mistmantle solidify into undeniable proof of a brutal crime. Tavernkeep Smitts hands over long-hidden muddy journal pages, directing the investigator straight to Night Watch Commander Althea Ebonlocke. For years, the grim fate of a visiting noble family remained an unresolved tragedy in Duskwood. Tavernkeep Smitts and Marshal Haggard, then a leader of the Stormwind Guard, originally investigated the massacre site and discovered a handful of torn, muddy journal pages. Without handwriting samples or corroborating papers, the notes sat cold, unable to officially implicate the recluse rumored to dwell in the wilderness. The evidence gathered across Elwynn, Westfall, and Duskwood finally connects the handwriting to Stalvan Mistmantle, turning town gossip into an open-and-shut case of murder.

The Legend of Stalvan. This crucial step in the investigation of Stalvan Mistmantle brings the gathered evidence before Darkshire's authorities. With a bloodstained journal page in hand, Commander Althea Ebonlocke directs the investigator to Clerk Daltry to authenticate the handwriting once and for all. Following the trail of journal pages recovered across Duskwood and the surrounding human territories, the Night Watch finally holds what appears to be damning evidence against the elusive tutor, Stalvan Mistmantle. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has harbored suspicions about the man for some time, but bringing formal judgment requires absolute certainty. A single bloodstained page is not enough to pass sentence until it can be proven beyond doubt that the macabre scribblings originated from Stalvan's own hand.

The Legend of Stalvan. This leg of the investigation finally confirms the sinister truth connecting the elusive tutor to Darkshire's records. Clerk Daltry successfully matches the handwriting found on the recovered documents to Stalvan Mistmantle, prompting an immediate report to Commander Althea Ebonlocke. It marks the moment the Night Watch's suspicions harden into undeniable fact. After combing through distant manors, inns, and municipal archives across the human kingdoms, the fragmented trail returns to Darkshire's town hall. Clerk Daltry compares the bloodstained journal page against the signatures in the Town Registry. The result is unequivocal: the penmanship belongs to Stalvan Mistmantle, giving the Night Watch the hard evidence needed to treat the matter as an urgent local threat.

The Lich's Identity. The Lich's Identity is an Undercity quest given by Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter. Seeking to uncover the identity of a reclusive lich living on Brightwater Lake, Bethor sends an emissary to steal the figure's spellbook to gauge his power and allegiance. North of the Undercity, in the misty waters of Brightwater Lake, a lone lich dwells in self-imposed exile on a small island. Unlike the mindless pawns of the Lich King, this necromancer possesses his own free will, yet he lives in deep paranoia. Convinced that any undead who approach him are Scourge thralls sent to drag him back into servitude, he unleashes his summoned minions on anyone setting foot on his shores.

The Lich's Spellbook. The Lich's Spellbook is a volume of necromantic lore kept within a chest on the island in Brightwater Lake. Recovered for Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity, the tome reveals the true identity and immense magical power of a reclusive undead lich dwelling just north of the Forsaken capital. On an isolated island in Brightwater Lake stands an enigmatic lich surrounded by skeletal guardians. Though free-willed, this sorcerer distrusts the outside world, mistaking all other undead for thralls of the Scourge and ordering his minions to destroy any who approach. Bethor Iceshard, seeking gifted necromancers to bolster the Forsaken ranks beneath Queen Sylvanas Windrunner, tasked an emissary with infiltrating the island camp to retrieve the lich's spellbook. Through its study, Bethor hoped to discern the master's magical aptitude and uncover who he was before death took Lordaeron.

The Loch. The Loch is the vast freshwater lake that dominates the valley of Loch Modan. Held back by the monumental Stonewrought Dam, it is the largest body of water on Khaz Modan and the lifeblood of the surrounding dwarven settlements. Spanning the center of Loch Modan, The Loch is among the largest inland lakes in the known world, rivaled only by Lordamere Lake and Darrowmere Lake in the north. Its waters support local fishermen and provide a peaceful backdrop for the town of Thelsamar and nearby hunting lodges. Beneath its calm surface, however, prowl aggressive threshadons and freshwater beasts that make swimming across a perilous venture.

The Lord of Blackrock. Nefarian's severed head is bound for Stormwind Keep after his defeat in Blackwing Lair. Highlord Bolvar Fordragon receives the trophy, a sign that the master of Blackrock Mountain has fallen. The victory is among the Alliance's greatest military triumphs in recent history. Nefarian, brood-master of the Black Dragonflight and ruler of Upper Blackrock Spire, has long threatened the surrounding human kingdoms. His defeat ends his twisted experiments and schemes. Carrying his battle-scarred head back to Stormwind gives proof that the Lord of Blackrock has fallen to the Alliance's greatest heroes.

The Lord of Blackrock. This quest marks the culmination of the assault against Blackwing Lair, tasking champions with returning the severed head of Nefarian to Orgrimmar. Bringing the monstrous trophy to Warchief Thrall secures proof that the brood of the Black Dragonflight has been broken. It is a moment of monumental triumph for the Horde against one of their most insidious enemies. Nefarian, the mastermind of Blackwing Lair and brood leader of the black dragons in the Eastern Kingdoms, has finally fallen. His colossal, battle-scarred head serves as undeniable proof of his demise. For the warriors of the Horde, hauling such a monumental prize out of the burning heights of Blackrock Mountain and across the Great Sea to Durotar is an act of undeniable glory.

The Lord of Blackrock. This quest marks the final delivery of Nefarian's severed head to the leaders of Orgrimmar. Having proven the black dragon's demise to Thrall, champions are directed to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength to display the trophy before the entire Horde. After the black dragon Nefarian is slain atop Blackwing Lair, his head is brought to Orgrimmar as proof of his defeat. Warchief Thrall confirms the fall of the son of Deathwing before sending the victor to High Overlord Saurfang in the Valley of Strength. There, the gruesome remains are prepared to be displayed publicly, serving as a warning to enemies and a rallying cry for the true Horde.

The Lost Caravan. After Encroaching Wildlife, Watcher Biggs has a further matter for you. Stunned in the Lost Ones' attack on the caravan, Biggs still saw a wagon hauled off to the Fallow Sanctuary, the Lost Ones' village in the north. A chest of valuable reagents rode in it, and Biggs wants those reagents brought back. Biggs was knocked senseless in the attack, yet glimpsed one of the caravan's wagons being dragged away to the Fallow Sanctuary, the Lost Ones' village to the north. In that wagon was a chest of reagents prized by the wizards of Nethergarde Keep for their studies. Biggs wants the chest found and its contents carried back.

The Lost Fragments. Theldurin the Lost is in a panic over the Scroll of Myzrael. Its magic could drag Myzrael up to the surface, yet if she is already free, the scroll may be the only way to bind her again. Elementals in a rage have shredded it and fight over the scraps, and you are sent to gather them. Theldurin the Lost is alarmed at the mention of the Scroll of Myzrael, fearing its magic could draw Myzrael to the surface. Then comes a change of heart: if she has already slipped free, or is gathering strength to strike, the scroll is just what you will need to trap her again.

The Lost Ingots. The Lost Ingots is an Alliance task in the Wetlands to recover consecrated metal from a shipwreck. After finding only a single bar in a sunken chest, travelers must hunt down the local Bluegill murlocs who looted the remaining shipment. Off the misty shores of the Wetlands lies the shattered wreckage of the Flying Osprey. Sent to retrieve precious Lightforge iron for the dwarven priest Glorin Steelbrow, seekers discovered that the cargo hold's waterlogged chest was nearly empty. The ravenous local Bluegill murlocs had already scavenged the rest of the vessel, taking the gleaming ingots for themselves.

The Lost Pages. While transporting a newly acquired goblin shredder from Ratchet to the Warsong Lumber Camp, the orc Gurda Ragescar lost the machine's operating manual to a sudden gust of wind. Stranded near Splintertree Post, she cannot run the complex engineering marvel without recovering the scattered pages. The Warsong Clan relies heavily on steam-powered shredders bought from the goblins of the port of Ratchet to clear lumber across Ashenvale. Operating these delicate, noisy contraptions is far from intuitive for an ordinary orc warrior. When Gurda Ragescar made the journey north with a freshly purchased shredder, a sudden blast of wind tore the instruction booklet from her hands, scattering twelve fragile parchment leaves across the forest floor.

The Lost Pilot. Pilot Hammerfoot fears the worst for his comrade, Mori Hildelve, who ventured into the craggy hills of Dun Morogh on foot after wrecking his siege engine. Hildelve was searching for a rare ore vital for potent blastpowder, but days have passed amidst unsettling roars echoing through the peaks. Dwarven siege engines are formidable war machines, but even iron treads struggle against the treacherous, jagged ridges of Dun Morogh. While scouring the slopes for a rare mineral deposit required to produce high-grade blastpowder, Pilot Mori Hildelve pushed his engine too far up a steep hill and busted the machine. Undeterred by the breakdown, Hildelve ordered his companion, Pilot Hammerfoot, to stay behind and guard the broken machinery while he pressed higher into the frozen wilderness on foot.

The Lost Report. Sifting through loose dirt in Dustwallow Marsh, you find an orc's severed hand clutching a tube carved from bone, with a dirt-stained parchment inside. It is a report written by an orc who watched Theramore as a spy for weeks, and it is meant for Nazeer Bloodpike, the orcs' spymaster at Brackenwall Village. In the loose dirt lies an orc's severed hand, gripping a tube carved from bone. The parchment inside is a report from an orc who watched Theramore as a spy for weeks. After scanning it, you see that it should go to Nazeer Bloodpike, the orcs' spymaster at Brackenwall Village.

The Lost Runner. The Lost Runner is a task to locate Sentinel Eralya Leafshadow, an initiate courier overdue from the Oracle Tree. It matters because communications between the sacred tree and the elders in Darnassus are vital to the night elf leadership. The Council of the Forest maintains a contingent of Sentinels stationed at the revered Oracle Tree within Teldrassil. The tree conveys sacred messages to the night elf elders, relying on dedicated runners to carry these dispatches back to Darnassus along the winding forest roads. Ensuring these missives arrive safely is essential for the guidance and governance of the kaldorei.

The Lost Supplies. A small, sturdy barrel has its seams sealed with pungent yellow wax. A stamp on its base names Quartermaster Lungertz and Nethergarde Keep, and that is where it belongs. Pungent yellow wax seals the seams of this compact, stout barrel. Underneath, a stamp reads Quartermaster Lungertz, Nethergarde Keep, so the barrel is meant for the quartermaster there.

The Lost Tools. With Lakeshire under pressure from hostile forces, town maintenance and defense rely entirely on local labor. Foreman Oslow's essential tools, shipped from Goldshire, were lost when Blackrock catapult fire sank his transport boat into Lake Everstill. Retrieving the sunken chest from the lakebed is critical to rebuilding the town's shattered bridge. Lakeshire's lifeline to Elwynn Forest has been severed by the destruction of the Great Bridge. When a replacement shipment of stonemasonry and carpentry tools was dispatched overland from Goldshire, it could not cross directly into town. The crew transferred the supplies into a rowboat to cross Lake Everstill, only for the vessel to be struck directly by a Blackrock orc catapult. The boat was obliterated, and Oslow's heavy ironbound toolbox plunged directly to the deep lake floor.

The Mark of Quality. At Feathermoon Stronghold, the leatherworker Pratt McGrubben will not compromise on quality. Pratt has come across thick yeti hides and wants a stack of ten. Pratt McGrubben will not compromise on leatherwork: only the finest will do. While hunting for fine materials, Pratt came across thick yeti hides. The yetis are native to Feralas, with many around Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast.

The Mark of Quality. In Camp Mojache, the leatherworker Jangdor Swiftstrider holds that quality should never be compromised. Jangdor has found thick yeti hides and wants a stack of ten. Jangdor Swiftstrider takes pride in leatherwork and says quality should never be compromised. Lately Jangdor has discovered thick yeti hides. Feralas is home to the yetis, and they are often found west of Camp Mojache in Feral Scar Vale, just inland of the Forgotten Coast.

The Master's Glaive. This quest sends Alliance adventurers south across Darkshore to scout the eerie Master's Glaive on behalf of the ancient of lore, Onu. The goal is to investigate whether the sinister Twilight's Hammer cult has infiltrated the remains of the fallen ancient horror. While investigating the lingering corruption and displaced wildlife along Darkshore, the ancient of lore Onu notices alarming clues. The naga along the coast are troubled enough, but the presence of the Twilight's Hammer cult is far more ominous. This fanatic sect does not worship ordinary dark powers; they venerate the ancient, primal lords of the world who were overthrown in ages past.

The Might of Kalimdor. Anachronos greets you as the one fate has been waiting a thousand years to bring forward, a champion to lead their people into a new age. This opens the end of the Scepter of the Shifting Sands, and comes only after the Blue, Green and Red Scepter Shard forks are done. Anachronos speaks of a fate a thousand years in the making. The Old God is shaken by your coming and fears your faith, and Anachronos urges you to break the prophecy of C'Thun. You bring Kalimdor's strength with you. Whenever you are prepared, you need only tell Anachronos, who will place the Scepter of the Shifting Sands in your hands.

The Mills Overrun. Tasked by Deathguard Dillinger in Brill, this mission sends Forsaken soldiers to break the Scourge's foothold at the nearby Agamand Mills. Mindless undead gather among the ruined windmills, threatening to establish a forward base dangerously close to Tirisfal Glades' settlements. To halt this staging ground, recruits must shatter the ranks of skeletal soldiers and bonecasters. The Agamand Mills once anchored the agricultural heart of Tirisfal Glades, but in the wake of the Third War, their windmills overlook a far grimmer harvest. Scourge forces under the Lich King's thrall have begun massing on the grounds. If these mindless thralls successfully secure the mills, they will have an entrenched base of operations from which to push deeper into Tirisfal and strike directly at the fledgling Forsaken holdings.

The Mind's Eye. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a powerful gem known as the Mind's Eye, an artifact essential for rescuing young Yenniku. The stone rests in the hands of the formidable ogre spellcaster Mai'Zoth, who dwells deep within the Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound. Following the recovery of the singing crystals, Kin'weelay turns his attention toward securing the Mind's Eye. This potent artifact is the solitary instrument capable of aiding the rescue of Yenniku, the son of the Darkspear chieftain. However, the stone is currently held by Mai'Zoth, a ruthless ogre mage whose presence Kin'weelay remembers from the tribe's earlier days in the jungle.

The Mindless Ones. Shadow Priest Sarvis tasks newly awakened Forsaken with culling the Mindless Zombies and Wretched Zombies that wander the northern edges of Deathknell. These shambling corpses are Scourge thralls, devoid of free will and utterly bound to the Lich King's command. Not all who rise from the dirt of Lordaeron regain their minds. While the Forsaken threw off the mental domination of Ner'zhul when his power waned, countless corpses remain hollow husks chained to his will. In northern Deathknell, these Mindless and Wretched Zombies wander without purpose other than raw violence. For a newly risen undead, putting them down is the first bitter trial of existence—proving one's autonomy by severing the chains of those who never broke free.

The Missing Courier. Latronicus Moonspear in Feathermoon Stronghold says a courier and the parcels he carried went missing about a week ago. The stronghold's own searches found nothing, so the courier is declared missing in action, and you are sent to Ginro Hearthkindle, who is seeking help. Latronicus Moonspear has reached an impasse. A courier has been missing for about a week along with the parcels he was carrying, and the stronghold's own searches have been fruitless, so Latronicus has declared him missing in action. An associate, Ginro Hearthkindle, is looking for help with the matter and should be in Feathermoon Stronghold, perhaps in his quarters. Latronicus asks that you speak with Ginro, if you have time and means to spare.

The Missing Courier. Ginro Hearthkindle tells you the courier, Raschal, set out for Thalanaar about a week ago, planning to row down the coast. Ginro could not find the boat and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, in case it holds a clue to where Raschal is. About a week ago Raschal set out for Thalanaar. Raschal knows Feralas well and has been with the expeditionary forces since General Feathermoon led them here. Ginro's understanding is that Raschal meant to go by row boat down the coast and cross southern Feralas, avoiding the Horde camp. Ginro could not find the boat, which may be hidden or sunk, and asks you to look for it along the coast of Feralas, since it might hold a clue to where Raschal is. On the mainland, the Forgotten Coast stretches south from the jetty.

The Missing Diplomat. In Stormwind, an urgent inquiry begins after a diplomat fails to reach Theramore Isle. Bishop DeLavey suspects Defias foul play and sends trusted operatives to Jorgen, a discreet contact in the Valley of Heroes. A high-ranking diplomat sailed from the Eastern Kingdoms to meet Lady Jaina Proudmoore in Theramore Isle for sensitive talks, but never arrived. Royal investigators search Stormwind for clues. The disappearance remains secret to prevent panic and keep conspirators from learning that the crown is watching.

The Missing Diplomat. Jorgen sends trusted operatives across Stormwind with a sealed note for Elling Trias. The delivery carries the search for the missing diplomat from the Valley of Heroes to Trias' Cheese in the Trade District. After the first inquiries into the diplomat's disappearance, Jorgen asks trusted operatives to keep silent and carry a sealed note across the city. It is meant for Trias' Cheese in Stormwind's Trade District, not a barracks or magistrate's office. The handoff avoids ordinary guard channels as concern over the missing diplomat reaches beyond the palace.

The Missing Diplomat. Elling Trias sends you south to seek news of the missing diplomat. Leads in Stormwind point toward Duskwood and Watcher Backus, a contact near Darkshire who may know of Defias activity. After a frustrating exchange with Jorgen, cheesemonger Elling Trias turns to his wider circle of informants. To save his own coin, he sends you to do the fieldwork instead of hiring agents. You carry a sealed missive across the border into Duskwood, where beasts and the undead make travel dangerous.

The Missing Diplomat. In Duskwood, the search for Stormwind's missing diplomat follows a lead from Watcher Backus to Defias papers at Addle's Stead. Watcher Backus of the Night Watch brings the search to Duskwood. He says an unusually large gathering of Defias bandits came to Addle's Stead several weeks ago. The bandits usually keep to themselves across the border in Westfall, so their gathering in the dark woods marks an unusual move. Now you search the abandoned farmstead for the papers they left behind.

The Missing Diplomat. You carry the recovered Defias Docket back to Stormwind as the search for a missing diplomat grows more dangerous. In Duskwood, Watcher Backus wants no part of the Defias Docket you recovered. Its papers describe plans too intricate to be simple banditry or a diversion. Afraid of royal punishment and wary of his Night Watch superiors, Backus asks you to keep his involvement quiet. The papers point to schemes dangerous enough to end careers or cost lives, so you carry them to Stormwind.

The Missing Diplomat. In Old Town, a lead in the missing diplomat's case points to a street fighter. Elling Trias sends you to find Dashel Stonefist and get answers about the suspicious papers. The investigation reaches Stormwind's rough streets. Elling Trias recalls a name tied to the coded notes and leads: Dashel Stonefist, known as Fist. He is a rough street fighter, far from the nobility around Cathedral Square. Stonefist keeps to Old Town's cramped alleys. Finding him draws the search out of Stormwind Keep's grand halls and into the city's criminal circles.

The Missing Diplomat. Dashel Stonefist has confessed in Old Town, and you carry his warning to Elling Trias. The thug names a backup abduction plot and a contact in Menethil Harbor. Dashel Stonefist gives up when he fears for his health. In an Old Town alley, he admits the conspirators' first kidnapping plan fell apart, leaving his part in the plot in ruins. To shift blame, he tells you of a secret meeting weeks ago at Addle's Stead in Duskwood. He also names one lead in their backup plan: an insider in Menethil Harbor known only as Slim.

The Missing Diplomat. A quiet request in Stormwind draws you to Bishop DeLavey in Stormwind Keep. The Church and crown need help with a matter too perilous for public channels. As you travel through Stormwind, Thomas, an altar boy, approaches with a quiet request. Bishop DeLavey, a respected cleric of the Church of the Holy Light, needs an outsider's help at Stormwind Keep. He calls the matter delicate and urgent. You must keep it discreet, lest the people panic.

The Missing Orders. Dispatch Commander Ruag bristles when asked about the missing orders, insisting they were relayed. Ruag says the soldiers carrying them were ambushed by murlocs and only one lived, and sends you to speak with Bengor. Ruag takes offence at the question and insists the orders were relayed. The soldiers sent with them were, Ruag says, ambushed and brutally beaten by murlocs, and only one lived, if that can be called living. The survivor can barely speak, cannot walk and is fed through a tube. To learn what became of the orders, Ruag says, speak with Bengor, who is around here somewhere, and adds a warning to mind what you poke your nose into, lest it get bitten off.

The Missing Shipment. Gazlowe is expecting a delayed shipment of goods sent across the Great Sea from Booty Bay. Suspecting either dockside administrative blunders or the Southsea Freebooters, he dispatches couriers down to the Ratchet piers to cross-examine Wharfmaster Dizzywig's logs. Ratchet thrives as the Steamwheedle Cartel's commercial beachhead on Kalimdor. Ships regularly cross the Great Sea from Booty Bay, carrying manufactured commodities, exotic supplies, and heavy freight needed to fuel the port's rapid construction and trade ventures. When inbound inventory goes missing, it disrupts business for Chief Engineer Gazlowe, who meticulously tracks every crate entering the port.

The Missing Shipment. Following an inquiry at the docks, Wharfmaster Dizzywig returns Gazlowe's ledger with clear records, pointing the finger away from harbor graft and toward the local pirates. Delivering the paperwork back to Gazlowe prompts the goblin boss to plan retaliation against the Southsea Freebooters to recover his lost cargo. Ratchet thrives on trade, but running a bustling port alongside the Barrens brings constant logistical headaches. When an expected cargo shipment goes missing, Gazlowe assumes an error in harbor accounting or foul play on the piers. Upon examining the manifest, Wharfmaster Dizzywig insists his books are clean and the intake records fully accounted for, meaning the missing merchandise never even made it onto the dock.

The Monogrammed Sash. A fine sash bearing embroidered initials hints at a rightful owner somewhere in Stranglethorn Vale. Finding the seafarer who lost it leads on to The Captain's Cutlass. This fine sash bears the letters 'HS' embroidered along its hem. Whoever lost it can only be traced by those two letters.

The Morrow Stone. The moment you take the artifact from the Equinex Monolith, the power in the Stave of Equinex starts to fade. You are to bring the Sparkling Stone and the stave back to Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold. As the artifact leaves the monolith, the stave's energy starts to fade. Troyas Moonbreeze at Feathermoon Stronghold is eager to hear what you found, so bring both the Sparkling Stone and the stave to him.

The Moss-twined Heart. The Moss-twined Heart is a strange, corrupted core harvested from the monstrous timberling Blackmoss the Fetid. Smothered in oily, dark moss, the heart unnervingly continues to beat on its own, prompting an investigation by the botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth. Carved from the remains of Blackmoss the Fetid, this Timberling heart is almost unrecognizable beneath a layer of dark, oily moss. The only betrayal of its true nature is a slow, rhythmic pulse that persists even after being severed from the creature. Such unnatural resilience hints that the corruption spreading through Teldrassil's wild plant life is far more pervasive than ordinary rot.

The New Horde. The New Horde is an introductory task in the Valley of Trials given by the veteran warrior Eitrigg. It directs fresh recruits to report to Gornek within the Den to begin their training. Through this brief summons, Eitrigg shares his personal journey and Thrall's guiding vision for a redeemed Horde. Eitrigg stands in the Valley of Trials under orders from Warchief Thrall to evaluate and mentor the newest hopefuls of the Horde. Having abandoned the Old Horde after the Second War, disillusioned by its corruption by the Burning Legion, Eitrigg lived in quiet exile until captured by humans. Rescued by Thrall, he chose to return after learning of the young Warchief's dream: an honorable Horde rooted in ancestral shamanism, entirely severed from demonic masters.

text.enUS: The Newest Member of the Family. After A Short Incubation, Quentin calls the egg a magnificent specimen and sends you to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands, to a dwarf named Agnar Beastamer. The egg is fragile and only an hour remains to find Agnar before the hatchling inside dies. Quentin judges the sprite darter egg a magnificent specimen; if it survives, it will make a healthy pet. One last thing is advised: go to Aerie Peak in the Hinterlands and speak to the dwarf Agnar Beastamer, a master animal handler who can guide the final steps of incubation. The egg is fragile and cannot manage long without proper care: the hatchling inside dies if an hour goes by before you find Agnar. Agnar lives in Wildhammer Keep.

The Next Step. Following the resolution of the immediate beast threats near Thendal Village, Elder Aetheen of the Gales directs travelers southward toward Shen'dar Village. The journey marks a shift from clearing wild fauna to confronting the organized zealotry of the Al'Aketh Cult, who revere the Windlord Al'Akir. After proving capable against the local predators and the matriarchs plaguing the northern wilderness of Zephras Isle, adventurers are called to broader duties. Elder Aetheen of the Gales recognizes that simple pest control is secondary to the true peril taking root across the island. To protect the isle's inhabitants, capable defenders must be dispatched to support the outlying settlements.

The Night Watch. Tasked by Commander Althea Ebonlocke in Darkshire, this mission enlists adventurers to thin the ranks of undead rising in the nearby Tranquil Gardens Cemetery. Abandoned by Stormwind's official garrison, Darkshire's local militia relies on traveling mercenaries to stem the encroaching horrors. Duskwood once stood under the shield of Stormwind, but as royal resources stretched thin and political discord gripped the capital, the crown withdrew its commissioned soldiers. Darkshire was left largely defenseless against the encroaching shadows. In response, the people of the forest formed the Night Watch, a homegrown militia now led by Commander Althea Ebonlocke, standing between the cursed forest and the town's remaining residents.

The Night Watch. Tasked directly by Commander Althea Ebonlocke, adventurers are sent into Duskwood's haunted barrows to cull the rising tide of restless dead. This ongoing campaign targets the skeletal horrors clawing their way out of Tranquil Gardens Cemetery and Raven Hill. Driving back the skeletal scourge is essential to keeping the fragile haven of Darkshire from falling completely to the darkness. Duskwood's tragic descent from a verdant forest into a fog-drenched twilight has left its graveyards unnaturally restless. Commander Althea Ebonlocke, leading Darkshire's volunteer militia known as The Night Watch, faces an endless siege. Without aid from Stormwind, her forces are stretched dangerously thin. Reports of animated skeletal fiends and horrors rising from the dirt threaten to overrun the eastern settlements, forcing the militia to recruit any able-bodied travelers willing to enter the deadlands.

The Night Watch. This final mission from Commander Althea Ebonlocke directs Alliance adventurers into the crypts of eastern Raven Hill Cemetery. With the Night Watch spread thin defending Darkshire, outsiders must enter the tombs to exterminate the teeming plague spreaders. It marks the culmination of the town guard's direct military campaign to contain the undead overrun. Darkshire stands almost entirely isolated, abandoned by the Stormwind military and reliant entirely on its own civilian militia, the Night Watch. Commander Althea Ebonlocke has exhausted her limited manpower simply guarding the crossroads, town perimeter, and supply lines. As the restless dead multiply throughout Duskwood, the commander has no choice but to deputize wandering champions to carry the fight directly into the shadowed recesses of Raven Hill.

The Ogres of Feralas. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache wants the Gordunni ogres pushed back before they spread further into Feralas. Following the river north leads to their outpost, where ogres, ogre-magi and brutes are to be thinned out. Rok Orhan points out that the Gordunni ogre tribe is hard to miss around here, since their very presence scars the land. They must be driven back before they reach deeper into Feralas. Their outpost lies up the river to the north. There you cut down ten Gordunni Ogres, ten Gordunni Ogre-Magi and five Gordunni Brutes, to show the tribe they are unwelcome.

The Ogres of Feralas. Rok Orhan at Camp Mojache, satisfied that you are a true fighter, sends you on to the High Wilderness, southwest of the camp. Among ruined structures once held by the night elves, Gordunni ogres far tougher than before are to be pushed back. This follows The Ogres of Feralas. Rok Orhan judges that you have proven yourself a true fighter, and trusts you with the next part of the work. The High Wilderness lies southwest of the camp, where abandoned, wrecked structures stand on ground the night elves once owned. Withered trees and desecrated ground show where the Gordunni are. Rok warns that these ogres are far tougher than the earlier ones. Ten Gordunni Shamans, ten Gordunni Warlocks and five Gordunni Maulers are to fall.
