text.enUS: The Star, the Hand and the Heart. The Star, the Hand and the Heart is an Undercity quest wherein Keeper Bel'dugur tests an aspiring leader seeking to establish a new chapter of their order. To earn the essential Yagyin's Digest, the petitioner must track down three items of power whose names Bel'dugur dares not speak aloud. Within the shadowed corridors of the Undercity, ambitious practitioners seeking to lead their own circle turn to Keeper Bel'dugur. To establish a new flock and open a chapter of their order, an aspiring leader requires Yagyin's Digest, an authoritative text of ritual lore guarded by the keeper. Bel'dugur stands ready to support his fellow brother, but demands proof of worthiness before yielding such authority.

name.esES: El estado de Villa del Lago

text.enUS: The State of Lakeshire. The State of Lakeshire is an urgent written report penned by Magistrate Solomon detailing the desperate military crisis gripping the town of Lakeshire. Intended directly for General Marcus Jonathan in Stormwind, the document pleads for the capital to deploy royal army reinforcements before the Redridge settlement falls. Penned by Magistrate Solomon amid relentless attacks on Redridge, 'The State of Lakeshire' outlines the dire circumstances threatening the township. Besieged by hostile Blackrock orcs and gnolls, Lakeshire lacks the local manpower to hold its borders indefinitely. Entrusted to trusted couriers traveling the road west to Elwynn Forest, this dispatch carries Solomon's formal request for the Stormwind Army to intervene and preserve the eastern reach of the kingdom.

The State of the Mines. Alba Fairmoon finds toxic metals in Westfall's wells and fears for its farmland. She suspects the mines seized by the Defias and warns the soil could fail for decades. You head to Jangolode Mine and Gold Coast Quarry to disrupt the mining. Alba Fairmoon finds dangerous levels of toxic metals in Westfall's wells. Once Stormwind's main breadbasket, the region now faces a threat to its crops. Alba suspects the mines seized by the Defias Brotherhood are poisoning the water. If the contamination continues, the surrounding earth could lie barren for decades.

The Stave of Equinex. Troyas Moonbreeze thinks his stave may be the Stave of Equinex, a key to a monument in the Ruins of Ravenwind. To find out, you are to gather the essence of four flames that still burn among those ruins. After your return to Troyas Moonbreeze, he says his stave could be the Stave of Equinex, which is in fact a key to the Equinex Monolith. The monolith stands in the Ruins of Ravenwind. Among those ruins, four flames are still alight, named Samha, Imbel, Byltan and Lahassa. Each yields an essence, and standing by the monolith you are to use all four to energize the stave. If it truly is the Stave of Equinex, the monolith will open and give up a sacred artifact.

The Stockade Riots. The Stockade Riots is an Alliance quest issued by Warden Thelwater at the gates of Stormwind's prison. To quell the ongoing uprising and prove your loyalty to the city guards, you are ordered to descend into the chaos and execute the riot's ringleader, Bazil Thredd. Deep beneath the cobblestones of the Mage Quarter, the Stockade has descended into utter lawlessness. Criminals, Defias insurgents, and violent cutthroats have broken containment and seized the cell blocks, turning the facility into an impenetrable war zone. Warden Thelwater and his guards are clinging desperately to the entrance, entirely unable to push inward and restore order through ordinary means.

The Stolen Journal. The Stolen Journal is an early Alliance quest in Dun Morogh where Grelin Whitebeard tasks adventurers with entering the troll cave in Coldridge Valley to reclaim his stolen notebook. To recover it, you must defeat the formidable troll leader Grik'nir the Cold. Reclaiming the journal allows Grelin to finalize his appraisal of the troll threat within Coldridge Valley. Grelin Whitebeard has been observing the Frostmane trolls encroaching on Coldridge Valley, keeping detailed notes on their habits and sudden aggression. During the unrest, an unusually imposing troll made off with his personal journal and retreated into the depths of their den. For Grelin, the loss is not merely sentimental; the notebook contains the bulk of his reconnaissance, leaving his official assessment stalled until it is recovered from the cavern.

The Stolen Tome. In Northshire Valley, a novice human warlock is sent to recover a forbidden tome and prove their skill. Drusilla La Salle hopes to claim Powers of the Void from the Defias, whose camp lies in the vineyards. Warlocks in Stormwind's lands hide their craft and keep prying eyes from their research. Northshire Abbey guards forbidden grimoires in its archives. Drusilla La Salle, the warlock mentor on the abbey grounds, covets Powers of the Void but cannot risk suspicion from the clerics and paladins by entering the library's protected wing herself.

The Stone Circle. Marvon Rivetseeker once went into the Sunken Temple and only just got out. A round stone with a serpent symbol, now sitting in Marvon's workshop in Ratchet, might let Marvon tell you more, and you are asked to fetch it. Marvon Rivetseeker speaks of the evil in the Sunken Temple that seeps into everyone who walks its chambers. Escape was a struggle through the ooze now spread across the floors, and what remains is a memory of a big round room crowded with statues of serpents.

The Stone Watcher. You carried the platinum discs out to the Tanaris desert, and the Stone Watcher of Norgannon has appeared at the Uldum Pedestal. It guards entry to the Uldum compound and admits only those whose disc set includes the Plates of Uldum. You are to learn its story before going on. The Watcher's arrival is just the reaction that was hoped for when you were sent out to the desert of Tanaris carrying the platinum discs. It names itself a guardian of entry, and it will not let you into the Uldum compound unless the Plates of Uldum are already integrated with your disc set. Before going further you are to find out the story behind the Stone Watcher, and then use the Uldum Pedestal.

The Stone of the Tides. Following rumours of a haunted isle off the jungle coast, Baron Revilgaz suspects an ancient troll relic has resurfaced. He directs explorers to scout the mysterious landmass and delivers a pass to research the artifact within the archives of Stormwind. Having learned of strange apparitions and water elementals haunting an offshore island in Stranglethorn Vale, Baron Revilgaz sees an opportunity. Suspecting that the goblin mage Gazban may have uncovered the fabled Stone of the Tides, the ruler of Booty Bay sends you to locate the island and confirm whether the rumors are true. To satisfy any curiosity about the relic, he provides a library scrip redeemable among the scholars in Stormwind.

The Strange Hermit. The Strange Hermit is an introductory quest in Shadowgale Forest focusing on a shy, hooded recluse living away from civilization. Seeking conversation after long isolation, the hermit shares glimpses of his simple handcrafted life and his bond with the local singing forest spirits. Deep within the secluded canopy of Shadowgale Forest lives an enigmatic, hooded recluse known simply as the Strange Hermit. Far removed from settled towns and standard trade routes, he spends his days in quiet isolation among the trees. When approached, his awkward speech and nervous demeanor show how long he has lived without ordinary companionship, making even a basic greeting an unfamiliar challenge.

The Strength of Corruption. Talo Thornhoof, a hunter at Camp Mojache in Feralas, believes knowing an enemy well can turn a battle. Talo sends you to Felwood, north of Ashenvale, to face the fel-tainted bears and wolves and learn whether they have truly grown stronger. Talo Thornhoof is a hunter who strives to copy the strengths seen in opponents, and believes simply knowing an enemy well can turn a battle your way. Felwood lies north of Ashenvale, where a substance called fel has tainted the creatures. Talo thinks the bears and wolves there, driven mad by it, have also grown even stronger. Angerclaw grizzlies and Felpaw ravagers are the ones to face, twelve of each. Fel-touched things give off a strange green glow, which Talo senses is evil yet very powerful.

The Sunken Temple. Angelas Moonbreeze tells of the Sunken Temple, a place buried far underground, put there by powers greater than any Angelas has seen. To learn more, you are pointed to a goblin named Marvon Rivetseeker, last known to be in Tanaris. Angelas Moonbreeze speaks of a place sunk deep below the earth's surface, put there by forces mightier than any Angelas has seen: the Sunken Temple. For more, look for the goblin Marvon Rivetseeker, who, like Angelas and Troyas, has made a study of ancient sites across the world. Marvon left home in Ratchet to look into the troll ruins of Tanaris, and word of him has been missing for some time.

The Super Egg-O-Matic. Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention is an impressive piece of machinery, and it sputters wildly when you reach its control panel. Hippogryph eggs go into it. Curgle Cranklehop's newest invention makes an impressive sight. When you walk up to its control panel it sputters wildly. It is built to take a hippogryph egg, and the eggs are to be found in the mountains of southern Feralas, around the Ruins of Isildien.

The Super Snapper FX. Curgle Cranklehop has a new picture-taking device ready, the Super Snapper FX, and hands it to you to try out. The subject is Gammerita, a creature from the Hinterlands. With her snapshot in hand, you bring it and the device to Daryn Lightwind in Rut'theran Village. This follows The Borrower. After The Borrower, Curgle Cranklehop presents you with the Super Snapper FX, a new invention of theirs. Using it is simple: aim at whatever you want pictured and press the button. Curgle gives it to you to try out.

The Swamp Talker. Bengor can barely speak, but he manages to tell what became of the orders. The dispatch commander gave them, and on the way to the Blasted Lands the group was ambushed by many murlocs. One of them, named Swamp Talker, took the orders from his hands. They must be recovered and brought to the Fallen Hero of the Horde. Bengor says the dispatch commander gave out the orders and that his group was on its way to the Blasted Lands when many murlocs ambushed them. One of the murlocs, named Swamp Talker, took the orders from his hands as a spear was thrust into his skull. Bengor manages a word about a cave to the east before passing out. The orders must be recovered and brought to the Fallen Hero of the Horde.

The Swarm Grows. Moktar Krin at Ironstone Camp says Belgrom wants the silithid pushed back into the depths they crawled out of. Moktar's own half-dead war party cannot do it, so Moktar asks you to take on the silithid at the dig site to the south. After The Swarm Grows (2), Moktar Krin says Belgrom considers the silithid a threat and wants them driven back into whatever depths they came from. Having already killed the dwarves the Explorers' League sent, Moktar now has a war party in no state to fight again, and cannot do it without help. The dig site lies to the south, and Moktar expects no more dwarves there. Searchers, hive drones and invaders are the silithid to be killed, and Moktar's party cannot leave until it is done.

The Tear of the Moons. High above the southern Barrens, a crazed dwarf named Feegly the Exiled demands the return of a mysterious relic unearthed at Bael Modan. Known as the Tear of the Moons, the artifact drove Feegly into madness and obsession before General Twinbraid had it locked away as an ill-omened curse. When the dwarves began cutting into the hills of southern Kalimdor to build Bael Modan, the Tear of the Moons was their first major discovery. The strange artifact immediately exerted a powerful and unsettling influence over Feegly, one of the expedition's workers.

The Temple of the Moon. The Temple of the Moon is an introductory quest in Darnassus where Sister Aquinne directs adventurers to seek out Priestess A'moora. The Sisterhood of Elune requires aid for a suffering ancient creature dwelling within the boughs of Teldrassil. It serves as the opening call to a solemn ritual of mercy. While walking among the waters and shaded groves of the Temple Gardens, travelers meet Sister Aquinne, a devoted servant of Elune. Sensing capable hands, she reaches out on behalf of her order. A venerable forest creature is suffering, and the Sisters cannot attend to the matter alone.

The Test of Righteousness. In Ironforge, glad tidings bring Jordan Stilwell news of his wife. Duthorian Rall sends you from Westfall to tell the devout smith that Daphne survived the Defias attack. Duthorian Rall sends you from Cathedral Square with news for Jordan Stilwell. You have guarded Daphne Stilwell through a Defias ambush at her Westfall homestead, and she survived. Her husband left for Ironforge believing his family was in danger. Rall asks you to carry the news in person, so Jordan can know his wife is safe.

The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness represents a defining trial for rising paladins seeking a sanctified weapon of the Light. The master weaponsmith Jordan Stilwell offers to craft an extraordinary holy armament, tasking the champion with scouring distant lands for rare smithing components, including his lost family hammer. Outside the grand gates of Ironforge, Jordan Stilwell seeks a worthy companion of the Light. Recognising the deeds of a rising paladin, the smith proposes a sacred pact: he will forge a legendary weapon that stands as an enduring symbol of devotion, provided the paladin undertakes the perilous legwork required to secure the master-grade materials.

The Test of Righteousness. The Test of Righteousness culminates at Jordan Stilwell's forge outside Ironforge in Dun Morogh. After gathering perilous components from across the Eastern Kingdoms and Kalimdor, a paladin waits while the smith crafts a mighty warhammer. It marks the transition of an apprentice into a recognized champion of the Light. Master smith Jordan Stilwell plies his craft outside the gates of Ironforge. While he admits to a touch of envy toward wandering paladins, he takes profound pride in supporting the cause through his hammer and anvil. Once presented with rare materials gathered from shadowy crypts, sunken ruins, and dangerous mines, Stilwell fulfills his promise to forge a weapon worthy of a true defender.

The Testament of Rexxar. Rexxar says that slipping past the Black Flight's defenses calls for an illusion. He knows a master illusionist, Myranda the Hag, who lives in the Western Plaguelands, and sends you to her with a message. Rexxar asks what you know of illusions, since an illusion is how you will get around the Black Flight's defenses. He names someone who may assist you in such deception: Myranda the Hag, a master illusionist driven out by the Lordaeron alliance, living in the Western Plaguelands. Rexxar says she has lent his kind a hand before, whenever she found a cause worthy. You carry his message to her.

The Thandol Span. Following a devastating explosion that rocked northern Wetlands, Rhag Garmason asks travelers to search the ruined bridges of the Thandol Span for a missing dwarf scout. The Dark Iron clan has launched a brutal assault against Dun Modr, cutting off communication and leaving local defenders stranded without reinforcements. Finding Ol' Rustlocke is the first step toward uncovering the full scale of the sabotage. A catastrophic blast recently tore through the Thandol Span, shattering the massive stone bridge connecting the Wetlands to the Arathi Highlands. Bronzebeard soldiers stationed at the border were caught in the devastation as Dark Iron dwarves ambushed Dun Modr. With their ranks thinned and their strongholds besieged, the survivors under Longbraid the Grim have been forced into a desperate defensive holdout against the attackers.

The Thandol Span. This critical Alliance mission tasks champions with defending the sole surviving bridge across the Thandol Span. Following the tragic murder of Ebenezer Rustlocke, Rhag Garmason discovers a plot by the traitorous Kam Deepfury to detonate hidden explosives and sever Ironforge's vital connection to the north. After discovering the grim fate of Ebenezer Rustlocke within the Thandol Span's substructure, a recovered document brings darker intentions to light. The Dark Iron agitator Kam Deepfury, architect of the bridge's initial destruction, was not finished. Having already collapsed one of the grand stone crossings, his sabotage network planted a second cache of heavy munitions just across the northern border in the Arathi Highlands, poised to finish the job.

The Theramore Docks. Two spies were sent to steal papers from a ship at Theramore, but were found out and had to cast the papers into the sea. Now Nazeer Bloodpike charges you with finding them. After you dealt with the Theramore spies, Nazeer Bloodpike has another matter for you. Two spies were sent to take papers from a ship by the Theramore docks. They got them, were discovered, and had to throw their haul into the sea. One of them got away but could not retrieve it, and came back to report the failure.

The Third Fleet. Sitting outside the Deepwater Tavern in Menethil Harbor, First Mate Fitzsimmons drowns his memories in dwarven mead. He is the lone survivor of Kul Tiras's Third Fleet, a proud naval force incinerated off the coast of the Wetlands by orc-enslaved red dragons during the Second War. First Mate Fitzsimmons spends his days slumped outside Menethil Harbor's Deepwater Tavern, nursing an unending hangover and memories he cannot shake. Once an officer aboard the Wave Mistress—a ship-of-the-line sailing under the maritime banner of Kul Tiras—he now trades his grim memories for flagons of dwarven mead. Anyone willing to buy him another drink receives an eyewitness account of one of the Second War's most devastating naval slaughters.

The Thirsty Goblin. Marin Noggenfogger in Gadgetzan is tormented by thirst. Rumor says the dew collectors of the cactus garden to the southwest store water in special glands, and Marin hopes one of those glands can become a drink that finally quenches it. Marin has heard of strange creatures called dew collectors, living southwest of Gadgetzan, that keep water in special glands. A laden gland, Marin reckons, could be the start of a drink to end the thirst for good. You are asked to find the cactus garden where they live and bring one back.

The Ties That Bind. The Ties That Bind is a quest in the Shadowgale Forest centering on a bitter betrayal within the druidic circle. Elegael Thornpaw discovers that a missing circle druid, Haalien, has joined the attacking cultists as a commander and orders his execution. The task reveals the painful personal cost of duty when family turns against their own kind. In the depths of Shadowgale Forest, druids encounter a vicious cultist presence sowing terror and bloodshed. For Elegael Thornpaw, the attack is compounded by a bitter discovery: the scent of a former circle druid named Haalien hangs over the slaughter. Having vanished months earlier, Haalien did not perish in the wilds, but instead threw his lot in with the invading cultists, taking command of their violent campaign against his former kin.

The Tome of Divinity. In Stormwind, The Tome of Divinity guides young paladins through a solemn rite. Under Duthorian Rall's care in the Cathedral of Light, you face teachings on virtue, devotion, and the duties that come with the Holy Light. Duthorian Rall guides those who answer the paladin's calling in the Cathedral of Light. Early training teaches martial discipline and the order's rites, but advancement asks for a deeper commitment to the spirit. The trials ask you to look beyond battle and weigh the moral duties of a paladin. Stormwind faces dangers within its borders and beyond, and its people need defenders who understand that duty.

The Tome of Divinity. The Tome of Divinity marks an essential milestone in a dwarven paladin's training within Ironforge. Bestowed by Tiza Battleforge in the Hall of Mysteries, this holy text begins a trials-based journey meant to test an initiate's devotion to the Light and their readiness to defend Azeroth against dark forces like the Scourge. Paladin mentors across the eastern kingdoms direct promising initiates to Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries once they demonstrate mastery of martial and spiritual fundamentals. Under the watchful eye of Tiza Battleforge, young dwarven paladins are introduced to the solemn principles that separate a simple warrior from an ordained champion of the Holy Light. Taking up this task represents a conscious pledge toward lifelong self-sacrifice, duty, and spiritual discipline.

The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall awaits paladins seeking trials of faith and courage in Stormwind. The Tome of Valor guides their first steps toward proving their devotion to the Church. The Tome of Valor teaches that valor must be forged through hardship. Its sacred text compares virtues to precious ores, valuable when found but needing refinement to endure. Through hard trials and true commitment, a paladin binds faith, compassion, and courage into a strength that can resist the evils threatening Azeroth.

The Tome of Valor. Duthorian Rall sends a paladin to protect Daphne Stilwell on Westfall's distant shore. With her husband away, Defias bandits threaten her homestead. At Stormwind's Cathedral of Light, Duthorian Rall tests aspiring paladins by asking them to defend the realm's people. After accepting the mantle of valor, you put those ideals to work where law and authority have failed.

The Tome of Valor. At Daphne Stilwell's farm in Westfall, a paladin faces a trial of valor. The Defias Brotherhood is pressing the homestead, and Daphne needs a defender at her side. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall lies in land contested by the Defias Brotherhood. While seeking the virtues recorded in the Tome of Valor, you are sent to defend her farm. The Defias have tried repeatedly to overrun the property and kill Daphne. After earlier clashes, another attack is expected. You must stand beside her house instead of retreating to safer ground.

The Tome of Valor. At the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, word returns that Daphne Stilwell is safe. After defending her Westfall homestead from bandits, an aspiring paladin reports to Duthorian Rall, completing the Church of the Holy Light's trials of valor. The Church's charge is to shield the innocent without thought for oneself. Daphne Stilwell's homestead in Westfall is safe after an initiate of the Church of the Holy Light defended it from bandits. Back at the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, the aspiring paladin reports her safety to Duthorian Rall. The defense shows the courage and conviction expected of one who stands between danger and the defenseless.

The Tome of Valor. The Tome of Valor is a foundational trial for Alliance paladins coming into their own. Directed by paladin mentors in Stormwind and Ironforge, initiates are challenged to prove that their courage and devotion to protecting the innocent match their martial prowess. To wield the Holy Light in battle requires more than heavy armor and martial discipline. As young paladins reach greater heights in their training, instructors in the Cathedral of Light and the Hall of Mysteries demand proof of their inner resolve. The lessons of the Tome of Valor test an initiate's readiness to confront terrifying evils—from dragons to demons—without faltering or abandoning those who cannot defend themselves.

The Torch of Retribution. After The Flame's Casing, Kalaran Windblade asks you to wait while the pieces are joined and the torch is enchanted. The work is a channeling that must not be disturbed. With the pieces gathered, Kalaran needs a moment to join them and lay the needed enchantments on the torch. The work is a channeling that must not be interrupted, so you wait while Kalaran casts.

The Torch of Retribution. With the torch made, Kalaran Windblade says it now needs an owner to be bound to, and tells you to pick it up. Kalaran says the torch needs to be bound to its owner. To do that, you are told to take it up yourself.

The Totem of Infliction. Madame Eva of Darkshire offers to craft a protective ward known as the Totem of Infliction for travelers passing through the shadowed woods. By harvesting remains from the ghouls, skeletons, and venomous spiders haunting the region, she enchants a charm that retaliates against attackers. The task serves as both a grim test of survival and a superstitious safeguard against the pervasive darkness of Duskwood. Within her candle-lit abode in Darkshire, Madame Eva peers past the veil into the fortunes of those who cross her threshold. Sensing impending danger and violence waiting patiently on the horizon, she offers more than mere divination: practical sorcery. By gathering ten ghoul fangs, ten skeleton fingers, and five vials of spider venom from the haunted thickets, an adventurer supplies the raw materials needed to construct a protective ward against Duskwood's ravenous predators.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest represents the sixth chapter in the crusade against the cultists of the Tower of Althalaxx, directed by Delgren the Purifier from Maestra's Post. Delgren deciphers orcish writings recovered from the cult's emissaries to reveal that the warlock Athrikus Narassin has hidden two trapped Highborne soulgems inside demonic satyr strongholds deep in Ashenvale. Champions are dispatched to Night Run and Satyrnaar to shatter these vessels, freeing the tormented ancient spirits and shattering Athrikus's dark source of power. After cutting down the orcish courier Ilkrud Magthrull, Delgren the Purifier puts his controversial studies of the Orcish tongue to good use. While his peers in the Holy Light often scoffed at learning the language of their adversaries, Delgren's pragmatic insight unravels the cult's clandestine trade. The notes reveal that Athrikus Narassin secured two potent soulgems containing the essences of ancient Highborne, hiding them far to the northeast within the defiled groves of Night Run and Satyrnaar.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks the direct assault on Athrikus Narassin, the ancient dark sorcerer holding the pinnacle of the Tower of Althalaxx. Under the direction of Balthule Shadowstrike, an Alliance operative must breach the ruined keep and execute the cabal's master. Eliminating Athrikus strikes a devastating blow to the demonic worship corrupting northern Darkshore. Perched upon the ruined heights of northern Darkshore, the Tower of Althalaxx has become a foul center of demonic summoning. Balthule Shadowstrike, monitoring the ruin from nearby, determines that the time to act is immediate. At the tower's peak dwells Athrikus Narassin, an ancient and formidable night elven warlock who orchestrates the dark rituals taking place beneath its shattered stone roof.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks the tense pause before confronting Athrikus Narassin at the Tower of Althalaxx. Sent northward by Delgren the Purifier, adventurers reconvene with the scout Balthule Shadowstrike to gather intelligence on erratic, dark occurrences rocking the spire. After purifying corrupted relics and unraveling the cult's grip along Darkshore's border, Delgren the Purifier dispatches you back north to consult his sentinel partner, Balthule Shadowstrike. Before assaulting the sorcerer Athrikus directly, Delgren recognizes the necessity of fresh battlefield reconnaissance, trusting Balthule's tireless watch from the ruins overlooking the tower.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Charged with the defense of Auberdine, Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze suspects foul dealings at the ancient ruins to the north. She tasks adventurers with finding Balthule Shadowstrike, a scout dispatched to watch the enigmatic Tower of Althalaxx who has failed to report back on schedule. Auberdine's sentinels must remain ever watchful over Darkshore's creeping perils. Sentinel Elissa Starbreeze noticed suspicious activity stirring around the Tower of Althalaxx in the northern reaches of the forest. She sent Balthule Shadowstrike to survey the ancient ruin. Days have passed without word from the scout, prompting Elissa to seek a willing traveler to journey north, locate Balthule, and ensure he has not met an untimely end.

The Tower of Althalaxx. Investigating suspicious activity around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, the scout Balthule Shadowstrike enlists aid to gather intelligence from the gathering warlocks. By recovering discarded parchment scraps from the fanatics encamped outside the ruins, he attempts to uncover the cultists' identity and sinister purpose. Balthule Shadowstrike stands watch along the misty shoreline of northern Darkshore, keeping a vigilant eye on the ancient ruin known as the Tower of Althalaxx. Sent to monitor the site for Auberdine and warn Delgren the Purifier of any rising danger, Balthule hesitated to leave his post to report. Fearing he would miss crucial movements by the dark spellcasters occupying the stones, he instead relies on passing travelers to scout the perimeter camps.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest bridges the investigation of the Dark Strand cult in northern Darkshore with the broader defense of northern Kalimdor. Balthule Shadowstrike dispatches an Alliance courier south to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale to alert his mentor, Delgren the Purifier, of the cult's sinister gathering at the Tower of Althalaxx. Following initial clashes with the Dark Strand cultists around the Tower of Althalaxx, the night elf scout Balthule Shadowstrike recognizes that the threat surpasses his solitary vigil. To mount a decisive response, he writes a detailed report and entrusts it to an Alliance messenger bound for his master, Delgren the Purifier. Because the cult's summoners are growing bolder by the hour, word must reach seasoned leadership capable of directing an eradication effort.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest marks a critical turn in the investigation of the sinister Cult of the Dark Strand, shifting the pursuit from the ruined Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore across the border to Maestra's Post in Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier dispatches adventurers into nearby cultist camps to secure a potent Glowing Soul Gem. Unlocking this artifact reveals the grim sorcery that fuels the cult's influence over the northern forests. After uncovering the ominous activities around the Tower of Althalaxx in northern Darkshore, reports led directly south into Ashenvale to Delgren the Purifier. Stationed at Maestra's Post, Delgren has long contended with the Cult of the Dark Strand encroaching on the ancient elven woods. Recognizing that the cult's threat spans across both territories, Delgren resolves to strike at the heart of their vile sorcery.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This quest is the fifth chapter in the investigation of the Tower of Althalaxx, leading Alliance adventurers south from Darkshore into Ashenvale. Delgren the Purifier dispatches you to strike down Ilkrud Magthrull, an orc warlock residing at the corrupted Fire Scar Shrine, and retrieve his esoteric tome. Following the trail of dark cultist activity uncovered at the Tower of Althalaxx in Darkshore, the holy warrior Delgren the Purifier recognizes the signature of a dangerous practitioner: the orc warlock Ilkrud Magthrull. Operating out of the demonic blight known as Fire Scar Shrine in southwestern Ashenvale, Ilkrud's shadowy dealings threaten to spread foul magic across the pristine elven woodlands. Delgren tasks you with slaying the warlock and seizing his grimoire to expose his master's designs.

The Tower of Althalaxx. This errand marks the triumphant conclusion of the campaign against the Cult of the Dark Strand at the Tower of Althalaxx. Having eliminated the cult's leadership within the sinister ruins of Darkshore, an adventurer carries word south into Ashenvale to Delgren the Purifier. It represents a vital victory for the Alliance in purging demonic corruption from the ancient night elven borders. The Tower of Althalaxx stood for weeks as a festering wound in northern Darkshore, occupied by the fanatical Cult of the Dark Strand and their shadowy masters. Through relentless tracking, intelligence gathering, and violent skirmishes, the cult's operations were systematically dismantled. With their sorcerers slain and their dark rituals broken, the immediate danger of demonic infiltration in Darkshore has finally been stayed.

The Treaty of Understanding. The Treaty of Understanding is an ancient dwarven tablet detailing the historic peace agreement between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans following the War of the Three Hammers. Recovered from subterranean depths and brought before King Magni Bronzebeard, the artifact preserves a pivotal moment in dwarven history while highlighting the bitter rift that left the Dark Iron clan excluded from the peace. Recovered from deep within an ancient vault, the Treaty of Understanding is a historic stone tablet documenting the formal cessation of hostilities between dwarven clans. Dating to the turbulent aftermath of the War of the Three Hammers, it represents the moment peace was forged between the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans after the Bronzebeards secured control of Ironforge mountain.

The Trogg Threat. The Trogg Threat is an Alliance quest issued by Captain Rugelfuss at the Southern Gate of Loch Modan. With the local Ironforge Reserve called away to support Alliance battlefronts, the remaining defenders are stretched thin against the hostile trogg tribes in the hills. Adventurers are tasked with culling the troggs and returning with their stone teeth to relieve pressure on the mountain pass. The defensive line guarding the southern approach into Loch Modan is in a precarious state. The regular dwarven mountaineers and Ironforge Reserve regiments have been dispatched to reinforce broader Alliance war fronts, leaving Captain Rugelfuss and a skeleton garrison stationed at the southern guard tower. Constrained by strict orders not to abandon the gate, Rugelfuss cannot mount an active offensive into the highlands, leaving nearby settlers and travelers vulnerable to ambushes.

The Troll Cave. Assigned by the mountaineer Grelin Whitebeard, this mission dispatches adventurers to cull young Frostmane trolls gathering in the southern caves of Coldridge Valley. With the Ironforge Senate preoccupied by an escalating trogg crisis, lone scouts and willing recruits must handle border skirmishes before the trolls establish a permanent foothold. While Ironforge's regular forces are consumed with repelling rock-jawed trogg incursions across the snowfields, the southern approaches cannot be left unguarded. Grelin Whitebeard and his brother Senir were deployed by the mountain authorities to assess whether the native ice trolls posed an immediate danger to the heartland. Perched on a bluff overlooking the frozen valley, Grelin maintains a solitary watch on their movements.

The Troll Witchdoctor. Nazeer Bloodpike means to learn what happened around Marg Nighteye's death, and says only the witch-magic of trolls can tell. You carry Marg's head to Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale. After the severed head turned up, Nazeer Bloodpike insists the events around Marg's death must be known, and that only troll witch-magic can reveal them. Marg's head is to go to Kin'weelay in Stranglethorn Vale, at Grom'gol Base Camp. Among the Darkspear trolls no witchdoctor is mightier than Kin'weelay, and Nazeer reckons that Kin'weelay, if anyone, can reach Marg's spirit.

name.frFR: Le camp du Marteau du crépuscule

text.enUS: The Twilight Camp. The Twilight Camp is an Alliance reconnaissance mission directed at the secretive cultists encamped around the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Having caught a glimpse of their ritual site through a scrying bowl, investigators must infiltrate the excavation to uncover what the Twilight's Hammer seeks to unearth. The Master's Glaive has long stood as an ominous, petrified mystery along the craggy hills of southern Darkshore, but the sudden arrival of the Twilight's Hammer cult transformed an ancient curiosity into an active threat. After using a scrying bowl to peer into their fortifications, scouts are sent into the thick of their camp to determine their true designs before defensive measures can be enacted.

The Unsent Letter. In the Deadmines, The Unsent Letter waits to be carried to Stormwind. Its delivery reveals the grievances and shared history binding Edwin VanCleef to the city's master builders. Edwin VanCleef falls aboard his juggernaut beneath Moonbrook, leaving behind more than a broken rebellion. A newly penned, sealed letter is tucked into his clothing. He addressed it not to a criminal lieutenant or financier, but to Baros Alexston, Stormwind's City Architect.

The Venture Co.. Investigating a ravaged Venture Company caravan in Mulgore uncovers an aggressive buildup of Venture Company goblins digging into the eastern hills. Having had their formal requests for mining permits flatly rejected, the company chose to quarry the Earth Mother's soil anyway, prompting Morin Cloudstalker to commission a lethal response. The tauren of Mulgore revere the land as an extension of the Earth Mother, cherishing its pristine plains and balanced wildlife. When the Venture Company approached the tribes seeking rights to blast and excavate the rolling hills for raw ore, their petitions were categorically denied. Undeterred by tribal decrees or territorial sovereignty, the relentless cartel sneaked heavy machinery, laborers, and overseers directly into Mulgore's eastern ridges to mine illicitly.

The Videre Elixir. Gregan Brewspewer will make you a Videre Elixir, but only once an Evoroot is brought. Gregan also claims a great many things are known to him about herbs and alchemy. Gregan Brewspewer can make you a Videre Elixir as soon as an Evoroot is put in hand. Meanwhile Gregan boasts of knowing a great many things about herbs and alchemy, and begins a story about turning the cheese meant for lunch into gold, only to ask where you are going when you walk off. Gregan is the one to ask about where an Evoroot can be found.

The Vile Reef. Kin'weelay at Grom'gol Base Camp seeks a piece of an ancient stone tablet resting deep beneath the Savage Coast. The sunken city, known as the Vile Reef, is infested with aggressive murlocs and holds the legendary history of Gri'lek, which the Darkspear tribe wishes to preserve in Orgrimmar. Northwest of Grom'gol Base Camp, an ancient troll city slipped beneath the waters along the Savage Coast when a violent earthquake shattered the land long ago. Now referred to as the Vile Reef, its flooded ruins crawl with hostile murlocs that assault anyone venturing near. Resting on the sea floor among the ruins is a massive stone tablet carved with the story of Gri'lek, a legendary troll hero whose memory remains sacred to the Darkspear.

The Warrior's Path. The Warrior's Path is an introductory martial quest offered to budding fighters on Zephras Isle. Following instructions delivered through Rorian the Dayseeker, young warriors are directed to Blademaster Ren in the Thendal Village watchtower. Ren stands ready to offer combat instruction and discipline to those prepared to shield their people. Upon returning to Rorian the Dayseeker in Thendal Village after restoring balance nearby, aspiring fighters receive word that the settlement's blademaster has taken notice of them. Rorian delivers a crumpled note penned by Ren herself, asking the novice to seek her out directly. Elevated above the settlement within the village watchtower, Ren keeps an observant eye over both the island's borders and the recruits who may one day defend them.

The Warsong Reports. Assigned by Kadrak at the border watchtower between the northern Barrens and Ashenvale, this mission tasks couriers with coordinating field intel across the contested forest. Adventurers must deliver standing orders and collect front-line reconnaissance from outriders stationed near Azshara, Splintertree Post, and the Zoram Strand. Standing atop the fortified watchtower on the northern edge of the Barrens, Kadrak oversees movement through the narrow mountain canyon leading into Ashenvale. For the Horde, securing access through this pass is crucial: the arid steppes cannot provide the vast timber supplies required by Orgrimmar, forcing the Warsong clan to push deep into ancient elven woodlands. Keeping scattered forward patrols supplied and synchronized requires reliable couriers capable of dodging night elf ambushes along Ashenvale's treacherous wilderness trails.

The Way of the Hunter. The Way of the Hunter is an introductory training quest for fledgling hunters in Thendal Grove on Zephras Isle. After proving their mettle against the local vuldren threat, young trackers are directed by Rorian the Dayseeker to present themselves to Tai'ree Farsight to begin their formal tutelage. Upon returning from thinning the disruptive vuldren prowling the outskirts of Thendal Grove, young hunters find that their practical skills have caught local attention. Rorian the Dayseeker passes along a scribbled summons from Tai'ree Farsight, the grove's resident hunter trainer. For novice rangers setting out into the wider wilds of Zephras Isle, this marked the shift from simple island defense to true martial and survival instruction.

The Weaver. The Weaver is a strike mission assigned by Shadow Priest Allister in the Sepulcher to halt Dalaran's magical operations in Silverpine Forest. A Dalaran archmage, Ataeric, is directing efforts to reactivate a powerful ley energy node in the region. By slaying the archmage and claiming his staff, the Forsaken disrupt Dalaran's occult ambitions and secure their grip on the surrounding lands. Following preliminary investigations into Ambermill and Dalaran's movements in Silverpine Forest, the Forsaken learned of a hazardous development: the wizards are attempting to harness and reactivate a dormant ley energy node. Left unchecked, access to such concentrated arcane power would allow Dalaran to fortify their position and threaten the Undercity's dominion over the southern reaches of Lordaeron.

The Western Watch. The Western Watch is an urgent mission to recall Peacekeeper Vaaniel and the garrison from an isolated southwest outpost under siege by cultists. Recognizing that holding the fortification is not worth the lives it demands, local leadership seeks to pull defenders back to safeguard the main settlement. The western watchtower stands southwest of the settlement as an outpost guarding the frontier. Facing renewed pressure from hostile cultists, local leaders judged the isolated structure too costly to defend. Rather than sacrifice more lives trying to maintain an exposed position, orders were drafted to recall the peacekeepers and concentrate all available military forces on shielding the village and its citizens.

The Windshapers. "The Windshapers" is a quest in which Illaya Amberwind introduces the player to the Windshapers and their spiritual mission. Tasked with reconnecting with the wind spirits, the order strives to protect Zephras and ensure the survival of the Shen'dorei amidst threats within Skywall. The Windshapers are an order dedicated to communing with the wind spirits and protecting the Shen'dorei. Welcoming those with innate spiritual perception, they seek to bridge the growing rift between their people and the elemental forces that sustain their aerial realm. Illaya Amberwind guides new recruits into understanding the heavy burdens the order carries.

The Windwatcher. The Windwatcher is an instructional summons directing seasoned warriors to seek out a reclusive troll shaman far to the north. Having proven their mettle in the trial of the Affray and mastered the berserker stance, warriors are directed to seek a weapon equal to their growing fury. Upon surviving the brutal endurance trial of the Affray on Fray Island, warriors earn the fierce discipline of the berserker stance from Klannoc Macleod. Yet raw martial discipline demands an arm of equal renown. Recognizing this, Klannoc sends promising fighters away from the coast of the Barrens, pointing them across continents to seek out a solitary craftsman capable of forging an extraordinary armament.

The Woodland Protector. The Woodland Protector is an introductory task in Shadowglen given by the druid Melithar Staghelm. Alerted by the whisperings of forest spirits, Melithar asks you to seek out Tarindrella, an elusive dryad who has unexpectedly returned to the grove. Her presence hints that something troubling stirs beneath the canopy of Teldrassil. While training novices beneath the boughs of Aldrassil, Melithar Staghelm receives troubling omens from the woodland spirits. The dryad Tarindrella, regarded as a protector of the wild, has reappeared in Shadowglen after an absence from Kalimdor's woodlands spanning many years. Because dryads rarely emerge without cause, Melithar fears an imbalance in the natural order.

The Woodland Protector. Tarindrella, a dryad tending to Shadowglen, seeks to uncover the source behind the sudden aggression of local creatures and the disappearance of the nearby furbolgs. By investigating the wild grells and gathering samples of corrupt Fel Moss, adventurers confirm that dark magic has begun to fester in the roots of the World Tree. Even within the secluded heights of Shadowglen, the tranquil nature of Teldrassil has begun to fracture. Dryads like Tarindrella have noticed a dark shift sweeping through the woods. The once-placid furbolgs abandoned their ancestral dens, reorganizing into the aggressive Gnarlpine tribe, while feral grells and grellkin began overrunning the woodland paths.

The Woodpaw Gnolls. After Quintis's vision, Ginro Hearthkindle sends you to search the camps of the Woodpaw gnolls in southern Feralas for evidence of the courier or the courier's belongings. Ginro doubts the gnolls were Raschal's undoing, but they are the best place to start. Ginro Hearthkindle allows that the Woodpaw, whom Ginro puts in quotation marks as friends, may have done for Raschal in the end, though something tells Ginro otherwise. Still, they are the best place to start. Ginro has no clearer plan than searching their camps, and knows gnolls keep what they scavenge and fight over it, so they may have come across the backpacks Quintis mentioned. In past searches Ginro steered clear of open fighting, but with the vision to go on now says to rip into them. The camps lie in southern Feralas.

The Wounds of Betrayal. The Wounds of Betrayal is a quest in Shadowgale Forest centering on the aftermath of a tragic assault against the rare shen'dorei druids. Players are sent by Elegael to deliver urgent poultices to her wounded brethren in Nightfang Den and search for her missing mate, Jorel Windsinger. The mission quickly exposes the bitter costs of betrayal and fuels a vengeful conflict against the Al'Aketh. The Wounds of Betrayal begins with Elegael, a shen'dorei druid tending to the aftermath of a catastrophic assault in Shadowgale Forest. Having hastily prepared medicinal poultices, she urgently seeks an adventurer to deliver aid to her brethren taking shelter in the nearby Nightfang Den, just north across the clearing. The shen'dorei druids are exceedingly few in number, making the survival of every single member vital to their fragile enclave.

The Writhing Deep. Among the backpacks lies a hurried note signed by Raschal of Feathermoon. He writes of bug-like creatures he came across, and of his decision to look into them himself. Your search for him now leads there. The backpacks hold a parcel meant for Thalanaar, and a note scribbled in a hurry to no one in particular. Its author, Raschal of Feathermoon, describes insidious bug-like creatures he discovered in the Writhing Deep, south of the gnoll camps. He felt he had to see them with his own eyes, for they seemed a grave danger to all of Feralas. The note shows where he went.

The Zhevra. The Zhevra is an early hunting trial issued by Sergra Darkthorn at the Crossroads. As part of a progressing test of martial prowess across the savannas of the Barrens, young hunters are charged with tracking down swift zhevra runners and taking their powerful hooves. Following an initial cull of the Barrens' overgrown plainstriders, Sergra Darkthorn directs fledgling Horde warriors toward slightly more formidable game. The striped zhevras roam in herds across the northern and southern plains. While not the apex predators of the savanna, they are fleet-footed herd beasts known for their stubborn endurance and powerful, bone-cracking kicks.

The Zoram Strand. Shindrell Swiftfire of Astranaar charges Alliance champions with scouring the northwestern coast of Ashenvale, where an ancient ruined city lies. Naga have surfaced in force along the Zoram Strand, threatening to push inward from the sea. Halting their foothold protects the forest from a haunting echo of the night elves' distant past. Northwest of Astranaar, where the dense canopy of Ashenvale meets the Veiled Sea, lies the windswept shore known as the Zoram Strand. Long quiet and littered with the bleached stones of a civilization torn apart ten millennia ago, the beach has suddenly teemed with serpentine horrors. The Wrathtail naga have slithered out from the dark tides, establishing a hostile beachhead right on the borders of night elven territory.

Theldurin the Lost. Theldurin the Lost is a reclusive, half-mad dwarf wandering the scorched expanses of the Badlands. Formerly aligned with the insidious Twilight's Hammer cult, he fled their ranks with stolen sacred relics after realizing the horror of their designs. Perched in the barren hills of the Badlands, clutching bags of explosives in wild paranoia, Theldurin is far more than a simple mad hermit. He was once an initiate of the Twilight's Hammer cult. When the sinister cabal sought to awaken a primordial elemental power trapped beneath the earth, Theldurin recoiled in terror, rejected their mad teachings, and fled into the desert. He carried with him the Scroll of Myzrael, desperate to prevent his former masters from unleashing an ancient horror upon the world. Though the escape cost him his sanity, his defiance dealt a serious blow to the cult's plans.

Theldurin the Lost. A member of the Twilight's Hammer asks you to find Theldurin the Lost, who was once of their order, lost his mind, and fled with the scroll of Myzrael. Rumor places him in the Badlands. Theldurin once belonged to the Twilight's Hammer, until his mind slipped and he turned his back on the order's teachings. As he fled, he took the scroll of Myzrael with him. Those he left behind could not catch him.

Thelgen Rock. Thelgen Rock is an extensive cavern system cut into the southern mountain wall of the Wetlands. Infested with venomous spiders, it is notorious for harboring rare veins of volatile Incendicite Ore. Nestled against the southern mountains separating the Wetlands from Loch Modan, Thelgen Rock is a deep subterranean cave network overrun by aggressive arachnids. The passages are thick with webs and crawling with poisonous spiders that make entering the caverns extremely hazardous for travelers. Despite the infestation, miners and adventurers brave its depths for the valuable deposits of Incendicite Ore found embedded in the rocky tunnels.

Thelsamar. Thelsamar is the primary dwarven settlement in Loch Modan, nestled on the western bluffs overlooking the great lake. Positioned along the main road between Dun Morogh and the Wetlands, it serves as a bustling hub of commerce, hospitality, and civic defense against surrounding trogg and ogre incursions. Thelsamar serves as the central bastion of dwarven civilian life in the valley. Built with traditional Khaz Modan stone and timber architecture, it features the lively Stoutlager Inn, a dedicated gryphon roost, crafting stations, and various supply merchants. Sitting directly on the thoroughfare connecting the South Gate Pass into Dun Morogh with the Algaz Pass toward the Wetlands, almost all travelers through the region pass beneath its warm hearths and stout roofs.

Thelsamar Blood Sausages. In the bustling town of Thelsamar, cook Vidra Hearthstove keeps the local laborers and miners fed with a famous highland staple: blood sausages. Preparing this hearty dwarven fare requires freshly gathered ingredients from the surrounding valley of Loch Modan. Thelsamar is never short on hungry appetites. Between energetic children and weary miners returning from the Ironband Excavation, Vidra Hearthstove works tirelessly over the tavern stove. To keep the populace fed and satisfied, she relies on a local culinary tradition known across Loch Modan: savory blood sausages made from the wildlife wandering the rugged mountain pass.

Theocritus. At the Tower of Azora in eastern Elwynn, Theocritus watches over the kingdom and opposes Morganth. The eccentric human archmage lives apart from others, surrounded by servants and magical scrying devices. Archmage Theocritus keeps his own stronghold in the kingdom of Stormwind. He lives in the Tower of Azora, near the eastern road to Redridge. Eccentric in his habits, he enjoys a comfortable life with a large household staff, including gnomish attendants and his clothier, Morley Eberlein. He keeps apart from the everyday concerns of local villagers, yet his magic guards eastern Elwynn.

Theocritus' Retrieval. Theocritus' Retrieval begins when an adventurer in Redridge finds a magical trinket carried by the local gnolls, only to hear a distant voice echoing through it. The speaker is Theocritus, High Mage of Tower of Azora, who has successfully intercepted the gnolls' mystical network and urgently requests the pendant be brought to him for study. While fighting off the savage Shadowhide gnolls across the Redridge Mountains, travelers sometimes stumble across an enchanted trinket known as a Shadowhide Pendant. Instead of guttural barking or curses, touching the object triggers a calm, disembodied voice belonging to Theocritus, a human mage residing in Tower of Azora across the border in Elwynn Forest. The transmission is the result of long, painstaking research aimed at breaking into the dark sorceries directing the gnoll packs.

Theramore Isle. Theramore Isle is a heavily fortified human port citadel off the eastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh. Founded by Lady Jaina Proudmoore for refugees escaping the fall of Lordaeron, it stands as the Alliance's primary bastion in southern Kalimdor. Following the devastation of Dalaran and Lordaeron by the Scourge during the Third War, Lady Jaina Proudmoore guided a fleet of survivors across the Great Sea to the shores of Kalimdor. After fighting alongside orcs and night elves to defeat the Burning Legion atop Mount Hyjal, her coalition of humans, dwarves, and high elves retreated to the misty fringes of Dustwallow Marsh. On a jagged island just off the coast, they built Theramore Isle—a thriving harbor city anchored by towering stone ramparts and Jaina's personal citadel, created to safeguard what remained of the northern kingdoms.

Theramore Medal. A Theramore Medal is a military insignia carried by the Alliance garrison stationed at Northwatch Hold. Emblazoned with the mark of Theramore, these tokens serve as identifying proof of service among the marines and officers defending the outpost along the Merchant Coast. Carried by marines, marksmen, commandos, and officers serving out of Northwatch Hold, these stamped medals signify military allegiance to Lady Jaina Proudmoore's realm of Theramore. To the human soldiers perched on the cliffs overlooking the Barrens, they represent legitimate service and sovereign authority in a hostile frontier. To outsiders, however, the medals are trophies of an overzealous foreign garrison that treats every approaching vessel along the coast as a mortal threat.

Theramore Spies. The truce between Horde and Alliance is an uneasy one, with skirmishes and covert deeds on both sides. Nazeer Bloodpike in Brackenwall Village wants the Alliance infiltrators east of the village hunted down and slain. Alliance infiltrators have settled in east of Brackenwall Village, watching it and sending word of Horde movements to Theramore. Nazeer Bloodpike, the local spymaster, will not stand for it. You are sent to find the infiltrators and kill them, so that their superiors know such spies are unwelcome.

Therylune. Therylune is a dryad found held captive at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore. Entrapped by the insidious Twilight's Hammer cultists who have occupied the ancient site, she relies on bold travelers to help her break free and escape their clutches. Dryads are guardians of nature and daughters of Cenarius, normally roaming the tranquil woodlands of northern Kalimdor. However, Therylune ventured too close to the ominous excavation at the Master's Glaive in southern Darkshore, where Twilight's Hammer cultists have gathered. Ambushed and trapped by the dark cult, she is unable to fight her way out alone through the swarms of cultists and requires an escort to flee to safety.

Therylune's Escape. In southern Darkshore, a young night elf named Therylune has wandered into the ominous dig sites of the Master's Glaive and found herself cornered by hostile cultists. An Alliance escort is needed to guide her to safety and deliver word of her survival to her worried sister, Therysil, resting at the Shrine of Aessina. The Master's Glaive is one of the most unsettling landmarks in Darkshore, dominated by the titanic skull of an ancient monstrosity impaled by an immense stone blade. Despite the dread that lingers over the valley, Therylune wandered right into the heart of the ravine. She soon found herself pinned down by cultists of the Twilight's Hammer, surviving only thanks to quick reflexes and an aptitude for hiding in the rough terrain.

Therysil. Therysil is a dryad dwelling at the Shrine of Aessina in central Ashenvale. Deeply devoted to the preservation of nature, she waits anxiously for word of her sister, Therylune, who fell into the hands of sinister cultists. Therysil makes her home near the tranquil waters of the Shrine of Aessina, a sacred glade within the ancient woods of Ashenvale. Like all dryads, the daughters of Cenarius, she is bound to the defense of the wild and the spirits dwelling within it. Yet her focus has been torn from quiet stewardship to gnawing worry. Her sister, Therylune, was captured nearby by the deranged Twilight's Hammer cult, leaving Therysil desperate for any wandering ally willing to aid in her sister's rescue.

Therzok. Therzok is a summons delivered to promising Horde rogues operating near the Valley of Trials and Sen'jin Village. The rogue trainer Kaplak spots your knack for violence and stealth, quietly directing you into the cavernous Cleft of Shadow to meet an operative of the Shattered Hand. Not all servants of the new Horde fight in plain daylight under the banner of Thrall's honor. When young rogues begin making a name for themselves in Durotar, Kaplak pulls them aside with hushed words. Word of an agent who combines physical lethality with a willingness to skirt the rules of open warfare travels fast to the ears of the underground guild in Orgrimmar.

name.deDE: Sie nennen ihn den lächelnden Jim

text.enUS: They Call Him Smiling Jim. Guard Byron feels sorry for a man called Smiling Jim and hints that he was not always the way he is now. Byron would rather not talk about it, and sends you to Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore. Byron pities Jim and says it was not always like this for him: Jim once kept an inn in the marsh, and a wonderful one. Byron prefers not to go into it. Anyone who truly wants the story is told to take it up with Captain Garran Vimes in Theramore.

Thick Bear Fur. Thick Bear Fur is a prized pelt gathered from the cold-hardened bears roaming the snowdrifts of Dun Morogh. Coveted for its heat retention, it is commonly used by traveling scouts and soldiers to craft insulation and warm bedding against the bitter alpine freeze. The bears prowling the ridges of Dun Morogh endure some of the harshest snowfields in the Eastern Kingdoms. Their thick, resilient coats provide vital protection from blizzards, making the pelt an invaluable resource for locals and travelers alike. Rather than being discarded as scrap, these heavy pelts are regularly harvested by hunters and used to line clothes, insulate drafty outposts, and pad cold sleeping rolls.

Third War. The Third War was the apocalyptic conflict that shattered the old world order just a few years ago. Orchestrated by the Burning Legion and unleashed through the Lich King's Plague of Undeath, the war saw the fall of the Kingdom of Lordaeron and the near-total destruction of Quel'Thalas before culminating in a desperate, unified stand at Mount Hyjal. The war began subtly in northern Lordaeron, disguised as a virulent sickness carried in infected grain distributed from Andorhal. The tainted harvest did not merely slaughter its victims; it raised them as ravenous ghouls bound to the Lich King's will. Prince Arthas Menethil raced to stem the contagion alongside the Kirin Tor sorceress Jaina Proudmoore. Blinded by grief, fury, and dreadlord manipulations, Arthas purged the infected population of Stratholme before pursuing his foe to the frozen waste of Northrend. There, he took up the cursed runeblade Frostmourne, casting aside his soul. He returned south only to murder his father, King Terenas, delivering Lordaeron into the hands of the Scourge.

This Fruit Could Bite Back. This Fruit Could Bite Back is a foraging quest focused on collecting wild prickly pears in the arid lands near Orgrimmar. The fruits are prepared into food while their seeds are saved for future planting, with the aim of cultivating a resilient desert crop to nourish the Horde capital. Durotar is a rugged, sun-baked landscape where traditional farming is nearly impossible. To support the burgeoning capital of Orgrimmar, resourceful inhabitants turn to native desert flora. The prickly pear, a hardy cactus fruit equipped with protective spines, thrives in the arid soil and provides much-needed nourishment when gathered with care.
