text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lotwil Veriatus, busy with a set of shackles, sends you to speak with Lucien Tosselwrench in the Badlands. Lotwil needs a cog #5 and wants it brought back. Lotwil glances up at you briefly, then bends over the shackles again. You are to go and speak to Lucien Tosselwrench, because Lotwil needs a cog #5 and asks you to bring it.

name.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard
name.itIT: This Is Going to Be Hard
name.ptBR: This Is Going to Be Hard

text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lucien Tosselwrench hands you cog #5 for Lotwil Veriatus, and heads for cover, inviting you to come along. Lucien hands over the cog and says to take it to Lotwil Veriatus. Lucien will be waiting behind cover, and you are welcome to join. When you reach Lotwil, who is still bent over the shackles, a hand is held out and fingers waggle impatiently for the cog.

name.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard
name.itIT: This Is Going to Be Hard
name.ptBR: This Is Going to Be Hard

text.enUS: This Is Going to Be Hard. Lotwil Veriatus declares the shackles finished and calls on Lucien, Servo and you to bear witness as a powerful elemental is summoned. Lotwil cries out that the shackles are done and the time has come, calling Lucien and Servo to bear witness along with you. Lotwil presents the shackles as alchemy, engineering and the arcane in perfect combination, and means to summon a powerful elemental on what is declared a groundbreaking day for everyone there.

Thistlefur Hold. Thistlefur Hold is a cavernous den carved into northern Thistlefur Village in west-central Ashenvale. Once peaceful bears of the forest, the Thistlefur furbolgs residing here have succumbed to corruption and turn violent toward any outsider who draws near. Tucked into the northern reaches of Thistlefur Village, Thistlefur Hold serves as the heart of the Thistlefur tribe's territory. The furbolgs here have been driven mad by corruption, falling into a state of feral hostility that makes them dangerous to travelers and neighbors alike. Deep within the winding caverns, the tribe hordes scavenged relics—including troll charms of interest to the Darkspear—and keeps captives bound in wooden cages, such as the imprisoned tauren brave Ruul Snowhoof.

Thistlefur Village. Thistlefur Village is a sprawling settlement tucked into the forest north of Astranaar in west-central Ashenvale. It serves as the primary home of the Thistlefur furbolg tribe, who have fallen prey to dark corruption and violently assault any outsiders venturing near their dens. Situated just north of the night elf haven of Astranaar, Thistlefur Village was once part of the peaceful woodland communities native to Ashenvale. However, the malignant corruption that has seeped into the ancient forests has entirely claimed the Thistlefur tribe. Now thoroughly maddened and intensely hostile, the furbolgs fiercely guard the paths winding through their settlement. The clan answers to two exceptionally ferocious chieftains, Dal Bloodclaw and Rorgish Jowl, whose unyielding aggression poses a constant threat to travelers and nearby settlements.

Thistlefuzz Arcanery. Thistlefuzz Arcanery is a prominent workshop and academy of the magical arts located east of the Great Forge in Ironforge. Run primarily by gnome practitioners, it serves as the capital's premier haven for enchanters and scholars seeking to weave magic into metal and parchment. Its busy chambers hum with arcane energy right alongside the roaring fires of dwarven industry. Tucked directly east of the thundering Great Forge, Thistlefuzz Arcanery offers a stark contrast to the clanging anvils of dwarven smiths. Within its two levels, scholars, practitioners, and apprentices gather to master the subtle disciplines of enchanting and magical study. While the Ironforge dwarves prefer to reshape steel through muscle and fire, the gnomes of the Arcanery demonstrate how raw arcane energy can be bound directly into weaponry, armor, and curious tools. It stands as an essential sanctuary for spellcasters navigating the mountain stronghold.

Thistlenettle's Badge. Thistlenettle's Badge is an official insignia of the dwarven Explorers' League, once carried proudly by Foreman Thistlenettle into the depths of the Deadmines. Following a catastrophic cave-in and an invasion of thieves, the token is all that remains to confirm the foreman's tragic fate to his surviving brother in Stormwind. Before the Defias Brotherhood locked down Moonbrook and the cavernous tunnels beneath it, dwarven prospectors affiliated with Ironforge's Explorers' League delved into the old gold mines of Westfall. Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew worked deep underground until a sudden tunnel collapse separated the team. While his brother Wilder managed to escape to Stormwind City, the foreman and several laborers remained trapped in the subterranean dark.

Thistleshrub Valley. Tran'rek in Gadgetzan wants to get into Thistleshrub Valley, but the strange beasts there keep them away. Clear some of the thistleshrubs out, and Tran'rek might think about going back. Thistleshrub Valley lies south-west of Gadgetzan, and Tran'rek calls it a mighty dangerous place. They do not trust the strange beasts there, gnarled thistleshrubs and thistleshrub rootshapers, and with so many around they will not go back.

Thistleshrub Valley. Tucked away in the southwestern reaches of Tanaris, Thistleshrub Valley is a bizarre oasis of prickly plant life amidst endless dunes. The canyon is known for its strange grove of giant cacti and hostile animated thistleshrubs that attack anything stepping through their thorn-choked territory. While most of Tanaris is an arid wasteland stripped bare of vegetation, Thistleshrub Valley is curiously choked with life. Giant blooming cacti tower over the canyon floor, providing a sharp contrast to the surrounding sea of sand. However, this is no peaceful sanctuary. The valley takes its name from the hostile, living plant creatures that lurk among the brush. These thistleshrubs lash out with razor-sharp spines at any traveler who wanders near, making navigation hazardous for those trying to push past the cliffs toward the mysterious southern gates.

Thondroril River. The Thondroril River is a vital natural boundary separating the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. Originating in the mountains of Northern Lordaeron near the Terrorweb Tunnel, its blighted waters flow southward into Darrowmere Lake. Once a vibrant trade and travel waterway of the fallen kingdom, it is now flanked by monstrous Scourge beasts and the humble refuge of a legendary hermit. Before the fall of Lordaeron, the Thondroril served as an important waterway connecting northern holdings toward Stratholme and south to Darrowmere Lake. Today, the river marks the hazardous divide between the Western and Eastern Plaguelands. The waters carry the taint of the plague, and its banks are infested with giant maggots, plaguebats, diseased bears, and predatory snapjaws, turning what was once a scenic riverbed into a deadly crossing for travelers.

Thor. At Sentinel Hill, Thor keeps Westfall linked to Stormwind by gryphon flight. His trained mounts carry travelers and urgent messages above the dangerous roads. Thor tends the gryphon roost at Sentinel Hill, linking Westfall's defenders with the rest of the kingdom. The People's Militia faces bandits, gnolls, and malfunctioning harvest golems on the ground. Thor's gryphons carry travelers and military dispatches above the perilous roads. Reports from Gryan Stoutmantle and urgent requests for aid can reach the court in Stormwind far faster than a ground messenger.

Thoradin's Wall. Thoradin's Wall is a monumental, crumbling stone rampart dividing the Arathi Highlands from the Hillsbrad Foothills. Commissioned millennia ago by King Thoradin during the dawn of the Empire of Arathor, it was built to shield early humanity from the fierce incursions of the Amani trolls. Erected nearly three thousand years ago, Thoradin's Wall marks the western frontier of ancient Strom, the heart of the first unified human empire. King Thoradin recognized that humanity's fledgeling settlements were acutely vulnerable to the predatory raids of the Amani forest trolls. By raising this vast stone barrier across the valley corridor, Arathor secured its heartland and forged a defensible bastion from which humanity could survive and eventually contest troll supremacy in the north.

Thorgas Grimson. Thorgas Grimson is the resident dwarf hunter trainer stationed inside Anvilmar in Coldridge Valley. A seasoned outdoorsman of Dun Morogh, he firmly believes that hands-on survival in the freezing wilds is the finest teacher any fledgling marksman can have. Perched inside the stone halls of Anvilmar, Thorgas Grimson welcomes novice mountaineers and scouts taking their very first steps into the harsh snowdrifts of Coldridge Valley. Rather than bogging young hunters down with dry lectures, Grimson espouses a practical philosophy: real skill is forged out in the freezing winds, bow or gun in hand, tracking Dun Morogh's rugged beasts firsthand.

Thorgrum Borrelson. Thorgrum Borrelson is the dwarven gryphon master stationed above Thelsamar in Loch Modan. From his roost overlooking the settlement, he tends the aerial mounts that connect the valley to Ironforge and the surrounding mountain passes. Perched on the bluff rising immediately above Thelsamar, Thorgrum Borrelson handles aerial transport for the Alliance across Loch Modan. With trogg incursions and gnoll packs threatening overland paths, his trained gryphons provide vital transit over the jagged ridges. He maintains frequent connections back through the South Gate Pass to the Great Forge in Dun Morogh, as well as routes onward toward the Wetlands and beyond.

Thorium Point. Perched upon the northern bluffs of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point serves as the primary staging camp for the Thorium Brotherhood. From this neutral outpost, these rogue Dark Iron dwarves recruit passing adventurers and strike back against their tyrannical kin deeper within the volcanic wastes. Overlooking the scorched slag heaps of the Searing Gorge, Thorium Point is a modest mountain encampment built out of necessity. It is held by the Thorium Brotherhood, a renegade faction of Dark Iron dwarves who have severed ties with their enslaved brethren in Shadowforge City. Unwilling to bow to the Firelord or Emperor Dagran Thaurissan, these outcasts maintain an open-air forge, a busy flight master, and a well-guarded perimeter northeast of Firewatch Ridge. Because of their desperate struggle for survival and master-level smithing aspirations, the Brotherhood keeps the camp open to both the Alliance and the Horde, welcoming anyone willing to dig ores out of the ash or bash Dark Iron skulls.

Thork. Thork is an orc warrior stationed at the Crossroads who oversees the settlement's local defenses. Charged with securing the bustling crossroads of the Barrens, he directs Horde adventurers to push back raiders and secure vital supply lines. The Crossroads serves as the beating heart of Horde transit in Kalimdor, connecting Durotar, Mulgore, and the wilds beyond. Holding it is no easy feat. Thork shoulders the responsibility of defending the town from constant external pressures. Between quilboar raids, centaur aggression, and marauding harpies, his forces are stretched thin, forcing him to rely on capable travelers and emerging champions to handle critical security tasks.

Thorn Hill. Thorn Hill is a fortified Razormane quilboar enclave nestled on the high ridges east of the Crossroads in the Barrens. The settlement serves as a forward base for quilboar warbands raiding Horde supply lines traveling between Durotar and the interior savanna. Perched on the north face of the rugged hills between Durotar and the Crossroads, Thorn Hill commands a watchful vantage over the primary trade corridors of the Barrens. The settlement is home to a dangerous gathering of the Razormane tribe, including hunters, trained wolves, and earth-shaping geomancers. Guided by mystics like Elder Mystic Razorsnout, the quilboar here have escalated their attacks against passing Horde supply caravans. Because this mountain camp sits so close to vital transit routes, the guards at the Crossroads consider Thorn Hill one of the most immediate military hazards in the central savanna.

Thorvald Deepforge. Thorvald Deepforge is a dwarven weapon merchant stationed near the border pass in the Valley of Kings. He helps arm travelers and defenders securing the critical pathway between Dun Morogh and Loch Modan. Positioned within the towering monument of the Valley of Kings, Thorvald Deepforge serves the Alliance as a reliable arms dealer. The mountain passes connecting Khaz Modan's interior to the outlying territories are plagued by trogg incursions and roving wildlife, making well-forged steel essential for any Mountaineer or recruit on the road. Thorvald ensures that those arriving from Dun Morogh or heading deeper into Loch Modan carry the blades and axes needed to defend dwarven lands.

Those Blasted Troggs!. Foreman Stonebrow is at his wit's end after troggs completely overran his operations at Gol'Bolar Quarry. Destructive and aggressive, the beasts have trashed his mining equipment and powder barrels, leaving him furious and demanding retaliation. Unable to fight them himself due to failing aim, he pays brave adventurers to head down into the pit and cull the brute Skullthumpers. Gol'Bolar Quarry was once a proud, productive dwarf excavation site nestled in the snowy hills of eastern Dun Morogh. That prosperity ended abruptly when subterranean troggs broke through the bedrock and swarmed the lower terraces. Instead of merely occupying the tunnels, the savages have wreaked wanton havoc, smashing scaffolding and blowing through precious barrels of blasting powder.

Thotar. Thotar is a seasoned orc hunter trainer stationed in the settlement of Razor Hill in Durotar. He guides aspiring Horde scouts and marksmen in the ancient traditions of tracking, archery, and bonding with wild beasts. For young orcs and trolls taking their first steps outside the Valley of Trials, he provides the foundational rites needed to master Kalimdor's rugged fauna. Perched within the fortified hub of Razor Hill, Thotar serves as a veteran instructor for marksmen of the Horde. While new recruits learn the very basics in the Valley of Trials, it falls to Thotar to guide hunters as they face the harsher predatory wilderness of Durotar. Drawing upon traditions passed down through countless generations of orcs, he teaches not only marksmanship, but the deeper respect required to live alongside and direct Kalimdor's deadliest creatures.

Thrall. Thrall is the Warchief of the Horde and the ruler of Durotar, holding court from the Valley of Wisdom in Orgrimmar. Once a human slave raised to be an arena gladiator, he broke the chains of his people, rediscovered their ancient shamanic traditions, and led them across the Great Sea to build a new homeland. Born Go'el, the son of Frostwolf chieftain Durotan and Draka, Thrall was orphaned as an infant when his parents were murdered by Gul'dan's assassins. He was discovered by human commander Aedelas Blackmoore, who named him 'Thrall'—meaning slave—and raised him at Durnholde Keep as an arena fighter with an education in human tactics. Aided by his foster sister Taretha Foxton, Thrall eventually escaped his captors. Guided by the Frostwolf exile Drek'Thar, he cast aside demonic corruption to master the elemental spirits, becoming the first of a new generation of orcish shaman.

Thran Khorman. Thran Khorman is the resident dwarven warrior trainer stationed in Anvilmar, nestled within the snowy Coldridge Valley. He oversees the basic combat drilling for newly minted warriors stepping out into Dun Morogh. Standing near the training grounds of Anvilmar, Thran Khorman is tasked with turning raw dwarven recruits and visiting gnomes into disciplined combatants. He maintains a gruff, uncompromising demeanor toward anyone who lacks the grit for front-line fighting. In his eyes, even though the Third War has concluded, peace is merely an illusion: troggs encroach upon Coldridge Pass, and the mountains remain fraught with peril. He demands relentless practice with axe, mace, and shield so that Ironforge's defenders never grow dull.

Threat From the Sea. After Lack of Surplus, Tok'Kar begins work on your weapon and tells you to speak with Katar in the Swamp of Sorrows. Katar has said patrols along the beach could use some help. While working on your weapon, Tok'Kar suggests you talk to Katar, who has said patrols along the beach could use some help. Tok'Kar shares the camp with some louses who drink, and would rather see you keep your wits sharp and your weapons ready than join them.

Threat From the Sea. After Tok'Kar sends you to speak with Katar, Katar makes plain a hatred of the sea. Watching the fish men die at the hands of anyone who does the Horde's will gives Katar some pleasure, and Katar asks how many you can slay and whether you would test yourself against their strongest kind. Katar bears no affection for the sea or for any creature that comes out of it, and calls it a mistress strong but blind, callous and brutal. Killing the fish men by the hundreds would delight Katar, were it possible, and watching them fall to those who serve the Horde gives a little satisfaction. Katar, in the Swamp of Sorrows, asks you to slay marsh murlocs, marsh inkspewers and marsh flesheaters.

Threat From the Sea. After your work for Katar, you are told to see Tok'Kar once more before you rest. Katar believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away, and that one will be offered to you for your help. Katar believes Tok'Kar finished a few weapons while you were away, and that Tok'Kar will offer you one for your help. Katar adds that you would do well to try its strength on the fish men when ready, though only to please Katar further.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde quest centered on investigating a violent ambush along the eastern shores of Durotar. After scout Heglan Shadeeye is ambushed at her post in a fierce skirmish, adventurers must inspect the devastated area for clues regarding the attackers. Uncovering physical evidence reveals an encroaching threat that directly endangers Razor Hill's defensive lines. A violent skirmish along the Durotar coast leaves behind shattered earth and immediate cause for alarm among the Horde's defenders. Heglan Shadeeye, a Shattered Hand scout keeping watch from her post, was ambushed by an unseen adversary. The skirmish site clearly demonstrates that Heglan fought back fiercely and injured her attackers. With hostile forces moving unchecked along the eastern shoreline, Horde adventurers are called upon to survey the devastated campsite, comb the surrounding ground for clues, and determine what manner of enemy struck the scout.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a defensive mission to purge aggressive naga scouts who are setting up camp nearby. By striking the scout forces and taking their spinefins, adventurers aim to drive the serpentine invaders back north and safeguard the area. Threat from Below addresses a mounting border disturbance caused by encroaching naga scouts. The serpentine raiders have begun setting up advance camps nearby, prompting local defenders to strike before the intruders can secure a permanent foothold. Adventurers are dispatched to cull the scout forces and return with naga spinefins as proof that the encampment has been crushed.

Threat from Below. Threat from Below is a Horde bounty tasking adventurers with hunting down a dangerous sea giant prowling Durotar's north coast. Overcoming such an enormous coastal titan protects the nearby shores and earns the respect of the warriors of Durotar. Along the northern coastline of Durotar, the waters of the Great Sea wash against jagged sands and rocky shores. While typically frequented by simple scavengers and crabs, the northern coast harbors a far deadlier menace: a hulking sea giant roaming the shallows, threatening anyone attempting to travel or secure the waters bordering the Horde's arid new homeland.

Three Corners. Three Corners is a vital crossroads nestled just inside the western border of the Redridge Mountains. Branching toward the three neighboring towns of Goldshire, Lakeshire, and Darkshire, it marks the boundary between the heart of the kingdom and Redridge's perilous wilderness. A Stormwind Guard watchtower stands over the intersection, holding the line against encroaching gnoll packs. Situated at the western edge of the Redridge Mountains, Three Corners connects three key Alliance settlements: Goldshire in Elwynn Forest to the west, Lakeshire to the northeast, and Darkshire in Duskwood to the south. Because of this strategic junction, Stormwind erected Tower Watch at the center of the crossroads. Manning the post, local guards and scouts attempt to keep the thoroughfares clear of Redridge's aggressive gnolls, who constantly threaten travelers and supply wagons passing between the regions.

Thresher Eye. Thresher Eyes are organic harvesting samples taken from the threshers prowling the coastal waters of Darkshore. They are sought by the eccentric gnome engineer Wizbang Cranktoggle to service his automated field devices known as Buzzboxes. Off the misty shores of Darkshore, aquatic predators known as Darkshore Threshers hunt along the surf and outer shallows. While dangerous to local fishermen and travelers, these beasts possess large ocular organs that have drawn the peculiar interest of Wizbang Cranktoggle. Stationed nearby and deeply fond of crawler wine, the gnomish engineer demands these eyes as essential components to repair Buzzbox 411, one of his far-speaking communication machines, positioned on the beach north of Auberdine.

Thule Ravenclaw. Following the discovery of strange Rot Hide ichor in Silverpine Forest, Bethor Iceshard identifies the foul substance as the handiwork of his traitorous former colleague, Thule Ravenclaw. To aid the Forsaken in repelling the Rot Hide gnolls, Bethor prepares a specialized scroll containing counter-incantations for Apothecary Renferrel. When a courier delivers the sampled Rot Hide ichor to Bethor Iceshard in the Magic Quarter of the Undercity, the veteran sorcerer immediately recognizes its signature arcane resonance. The distillation belongs to Thule Ravenclaw, once a bright and promising young mage alongside Bethor before the Third War. When the Lich King rose to power, Thule betrayed his peers to swear allegiance to the Scourge, abandoning his humanity as Lordaeron fell.

Thule's Head. Thule's Head is the grisly proof demanded by the Forsaken to confirm the demise of Thule Ravenclaw, commander of the Scourge forces on Fenris Isle. Bringing this macabre trophy back to High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher solidifies the Forsaken's hold on Silverpine Forest.

Thun'grim Firegaze. Following their initial training in defensive tactics, Horde warriors are directed across the Barrens to seek out Thun'grim Firegaze. This reclusive master weaponsmith makes his camp atop the rugged ridges of Thorn Hill east of the Crossroads. Finding him is a rite of passage for combatants seeking a weapon worthy of their burgeoning prowess. Once an aspiring warrior demonstrates proficiency in the defensive arts under veteran trainers like Uzzek, they are instructed to hone their martial edge with suitable steel. Conventional armories will only carry a frontline fighter so far; true mastery demands a personalized weapon forged by a craftsperson of exceptional renown. In the harsh savanna of the Barrens, that smith is Thun'grim Firegaze, an aging orc hermit who has withdrawn from settlement life to maintain an isolated forge high above the plains.

Thunder Axe Fortress. Thunder Axe Fortress is a fortified compound in northwestern Desolace serving as a stronghold for the demonic Burning Blade cult. Within its stone barracks, watchtowers, and darkened caves, cultists perform dark rituals to summon demonic entities and store stolen artifacts of power. The cult remains an active threat to anyone traversing the desolate wastes. Perched in northwestern Desolace, Thunder Axe Fortress serves as a heavily guarded redoubt for the Burning Blade. Composed of stone barracks, defensive watchtowers, and deep caverns, it allows the cult to maintain a fortified foothold far from the gaze of Kalimdor's major cities. Here, the cultists gather fel energies, summon lesser demons, and concoct schemes to bring far more dangerous entities into the world.

Thunder Bluff. Thunder Bluff is the high-perched capital city of the tauren, rising hundreds of feet above the rolling plains of Mulgore. Founded by Cairne Bloodhoof following the Third War, it serves as the united sanctuary and cultural heart for a people who roamed as nomads for generations. For countless generations, the tauren lived as nomadic wanderers across central Kalimdor, constantly beset by brutal centaur raiding parties. That era of flight ended during the Third War, when Cairne Bloodhoof forged a bond of honor with Warchief Thrall and the New Horde. Together, they drove back the centaur menace and claimed the fertile grasslands of Mulgore. Cairne gathered the scattered tribes and established Thunder Bluff atop a series of sweeping, natural stone mesas. Today, the city is connected by dizzying rope bridges and accessed by ingenious wooden elevators, offering both absolute defense and a bustling center of trade and spiritual assembly.

Thunder Falls. Thunder Falls lies in Elwynn Forest’s northwestern heights, where bandits have taken a riverside cottage. Thunder Falls cuts through the ridges above Mirror Lake, where a mountain stream rushes between steep cliffs. It enters over an unreachable cascade in the north, then spills away in waterfalls on both sides. One fall empties into Mirror Lake; the stream’s downstream course runs west toward Westfall’s rugged border. A cottage, dock, and outdoor forge sit beside the water. Bandits now claim the clearing.

Thunder Lizard Blood. Thunder Lizard Blood is a vital fluid taken from the massive thunder lizards wandering the southern Barrens. It serves as martial proof of survival against some of Kalimdor's most crushing terrestrial beasts. Thunder lizards, known across the plains as Stormsnouts, Stormhides, and Thunderheads, are colossal beasts whose heavy strides shake the earth. Hunting them is an exercise in perilous footing, as their crushing weight easily flattens unwary stalkers. Bringing back their blood demonstrates not just hunting prowess, but the sheer endurance needed to survive a bout beneath their thundering feet.

Thunder Lizard Horn. A thunder lizard horn is a hardy trophy harvested from the massive, lightning-attuned thunder lizards wandering the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet seeks this unusual reagent to recreate a legendary beverage originally concocted by Chen Stormstout. Thunder lizards roam the arid flats of the Barrens, crackling with raw, localized lightning that arcs from their crested bodies. While hunters occasionally seek their thick hides, Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet values their horns for a very different purpose. Handed down from a mentor who learned it from the wandering pandaren Brewmaster Chen Stormstout, the recipe for Stormstout ale calls for unusual, potent local ingredients. The horn of a thunder lizard provides the electrifying kick that gives the legendary draught its fiery, unforgettable bite.

Thunder Ridge. Thunder Ridge is a rugged canyon in western Durotar, situated just southwest of Orgrimmar along the banks of the Southfury River. Once a lush grove of ancient trees inhabited by herds of thunder lizards, the canyon has suffered severe deforestation from human lumber operations and dark sorcery. Today, the agitated beasts and lingering cultists pose an ongoing threat to nearby settlements. Not long ago, Thunder Ridge was a rare green haven in arid Durotar, sustained by ancient trees. Its tranquil balance shattered shortly after the Third War when human interlopers from Kul Tiras began felling its timber, driving the native thunder lizards into a frenzy. Later, fel sorcery wielded by the Burning Blade finished the destruction, stripping the canopy and leaving behind a barren, exposed gorge where angry lightning-spewing beasts now roam unrestrained.

Thunderaan. Prince Thunderaan is the ancient Prince of Air, a colossal elemental struck down and betrayed during the ancient wars between fire and wind. Consumed in part by Ragnaros the Firelord, his remnant essence was sealed into shattered bindings entrusted to the Firelord's lieutenants. Adventurers who recover these relics can seek out Highlord Demitrian in Silithus to unleash him once more. Long ago, during the Elemental Sundering—a five-thousand-year clash fought between the forces of fire and air deep within Azeroth—Ragnaros sought to destroy and consume Thunderaan. The Prince was ambushed and betrayed by Ragnaros's powerful lieutenants, Baron Geddon and Garr, before being struck down by the Firelord's hammer, Sulfuras. Although defeated, Thunderaan's essence proved too mighty for Ragnaros to fully absorb.

Thunderbrew. In Westfall, Grimbooze Thunderbrew is gathering what he needs for his next batch. Fresh hops keep his ale from turning thick as stew, and he shares kegs with those who help. Grimbooze Thunderbrew keeps his family's brewing tradition alive far from Dun Morogh. Even across Westfall's turbulent plains, he insists on the right ingredients: without proper hops, his current brew may turn into thick stew instead of refreshing ale.

Thunderbrew Distillery. Thunderbrew Distillery serves as the bustling tavern and central gathering place of Kharanos in Dun Morogh. Renowned far and wide for its potent ales, it functions as both an active brewhouse and an essential rest stop for travelers passing through the snowy mountain passes. Inside, patrons find warm hearths, cold pints, and a wide array of class mentors and local tradesfolk. Perched in the center of Kharanos, the Thunderbrew Distillery is the heart of civic life in southern Dun Morogh. Founded by the Thunderbrew clan—established by Arkilus Thunderbrew and maintained by his kin—the brewhouse is famous across Khaz Modan for producing robust, warming ales built to ward off the biting mountain chill. It operates as the local inn, managed on the floor by Innkeeper Belm, offering weary mountaineers a roaring fire, hearty fare, and beds to escape the blizzards outside.

text.enUS: Thunderhawk Saliva Gland. A Thunderhawk Saliva Gland is a potent biological reagent harvested from the greater thunderhawks that soar over the Barrens. Brewmaster Drohn in Ratchet prizes it as an essential ingredient for recreating Chen Stormstout's fiery Trogg Ale. The arid savannas of the Barrens are home to thunderhawks—winged serpents renowned for harnessing the storm itself. Among their population, the older and more dangerous greater thunderhawks produce a saliva gland charged with raw, natural potency. While ordinary travelers steer clear of these deadly beasts, skilled brewmasters recognize the organ's rare properties as an extraordinary base for exotic concoctions.

Thunderhawk Wings. Thunderhawk Wings are feathered trophies taken from the fierce wind serpents soaring above the central and southern Barrens. Presented to Jorn Skyseer at Camp Taurajo, they serve as definitive proof of a hunter's strength, cunning, and endurance in tracking down one of the savanna's most majestic predators. Wind serpents, known to local hunters as thunderhawks, are formidable winged reptiles capable of striking swiftly from above. For the hunters stationed at Camp Taurajo, harvesting a pair of intact Thunderhawk Wings is far more than collecting biological scraps; it represents the culmination of grueling hunting trials in the Barrens. By tracking the aerial predators across the open plains and claiming their wings in combat, an initiate proves their readiness to walk the lifelong path of an accomplished hunter.

Thunderhorn Cleansing. Thunderhorn Cleansing is an essential spiritual rite in Mulgore, charging travelers with purifying the corrupted Thunderhorn Water Well. Armed with a ritual totem prepared by Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers restore the contaminated spring vital to the local tribe. Successful purification earns the heartfelt approval of the Thunderhorn ancestors. Water wells across the sweeping plains of Mulgore are vital lifelines for the tauren nomadic tribes who recently settled the grasslands. When foul poisons taint these underground springs, both wildlife and nearby settlements face devastating consequences. The Thunderhorn Water Well, situated north of Bloodhoof Village, fallen victim to contamination, requires deliberate spiritual intervention to heal the troubled land.

Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem. The Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem is a consecrated ritual implement crafted by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village. It is imbued with ancestral magic to purify the corrupted waters of the Thunderhorn Water Well. Across the rolling plains of Mulgore, the lifeblood of the earth is being fouled by unseen corruption. The ancestral wells dug by the tauren tribes provide vital nourishment to the herds and hunting grounds, but foul agents have tainted the water. Entrusted by the elder Mull Thunderhorn, adventurers carry this prepared totem north of Bloodhoof Village to drive out the pollution settling over the Thunderhorn clan's sacred spring. Through ritual invocation, the totem calms the disturbed spirits of the water and cleanses the ancestral site.

Thunderhorn Totem. Thunderhorn Totem is a task given by Mull Thunderhorn in Bloodhoof Village to craft a sacred cleansing totem. To combat goblin-borne pollution spreading through Mulgore's water wells, young Horde champions must gather natural talons from plains predators to bind the land's primal strength into ritual wood. As the Venture Company's industrial exploitation poisons Mulgore's precious water sources, Mull Thunderhorn works urgently to craft remedies. Creating the Thunderhorn Cleansing Totem requires the natural essences of the plains' most focused hunters: prairie stalkers and flatland cougars. By taking the claws of these predators roaming east and west of Bloodhoof Village, the ritual channels the raw, uncorrupted predatory vigor of the wildlife directly into the totem.

Thunderhorn Water Well. Thunderhorn Water Well is a vital water source situated in the rolling plains of central Mulgore along the path between Bloodhoof Village and Thunder Bluff. Like all the wells across the valley, it provides essential nourishment to the tribes and the herds roaming the grasslands. Keeping this water clean and defended is crucial to maintaining life in the tauren homeland. Situated amid the sprawling grasslands of central Mulgore, the Thunderhorn Water Well taps directly into the pure aquifers feeding the valley. For the nomadic tauren and their newly settled villages, these communal wells represent life, sustenance, and the Earth Mother's bounty. Because water is precious across the sun-drenched plains, controlling the wells means controlling the land itself. Intruders such as the Venture Company have repeatedly eyed these sources, attempting to harness them for industrial exploitation and disrupt the fragile balance the tribes fight to preserve.

Thundris Windweaver. Thundris Windweaver is an Alliance quest connecting the druid Terenthis's reconnaissance of the local furbolgs to the civic leadership of Auberdine. Having confirmed the growing aggression of the nearby Blackwood tribe, adventurers are directed to report directly to Elder Windweaver. The elder seeks to understand the root causes of the encroaching taint warping Darkshore's wilderness. Following your scouting mission into the corrupted furbolg camps of Darkshore, the druid Terenthis directs you to Auberdine's village elder, Thundris Windweaver. While Terenthis investigates the spreading corruption in the wilds, Thundris oversees the daily welfare of the settlement and weighs the broader spiritual and environmental perils facing the kaldorei. The report provides leadership with clear evidence that the furbolgs are not simply territorial, but actively deteriorating under an unnatural malice.

Thurman's Remains. Thurman's Remains are the corporeal remnants of Thurman Agamand, recovered from the family's ruined mills in northern Tirisfal Glades. Once a wealthy mill owner who persuaded his workers to stand against the Scourge, Thurman succumbed to the Plague and wanders his former estate as an undead thrall. Before the Third War, the Agamand family stood as the most prosperous landowners in Tirisfal Glades, operating extensive mills and employing dozens of local workers. When the Scourge swept across Lordaeron, Thurman Agamand and his kin fortified their estate rather than fleeing. Convinced that their wealth and fortified mills could weather the onslaught, they persuaded their loyal laborers to take up arms beside them. The defense failed utterly. The Agamands and their workers were slaughtered and transformed into mindless servants of the Lich King. Today, Coleman Farthing—a former employee risen as Forsaken—demands the destruction of his former masters, seeking Thurman's remains as proof that the foolish patriarch has paid for dooming his household.

Thurman's Sewing Kit. At Larson Clothiers, Thurman's Sewing Kit is needed for his tailoring work. The tools belong to young apprentice Thurman Schneider, who left them behind at his family's canal home to avoid a long day of stitching. Thurman's Sewing Kit holds the everyday tools of an apprentice tailor: needles, shears, and thread. Young Thurman Schneider studies tailoring at Larson Clothiers, deep in Stormwind's Mage Quarter near the Mage Tower. His mother, Rema Schneider, knows he cannot do his work without the kit, so she asks passersby along the Canals to carry it to the shop. When Thurman gets the tools, his reaction shows he left them behind on purpose, hoping to trade a day of stitching garments for leisure.

Thwarting Kolkar Aggression. Thwarting Kolkar Aggression is a vital Horde defense mission handed out by the scout Lar Prowltusk near Sen'jin Village. Players are tasked with infiltrating Kolkar Crag to destroy three sets of coordinated invasion plans before the centaur clan can strike the fledgling settlements of Durotar. While scouting western Durotar, the troll tracker Lar Prowltusk slipped into Kolkar Crag under cover of night. What he discovered was alarming: the Kolkar centaurs were not merely mounting disorganized coastal raids, but coordinating an ambitious, three-pronged invasion aimed squarely at the orc and Darkspear homelands. The centaur warlords divided their battle strategies among three distinct leaders, intending to strike the Valley of Trials, Sen'jin Village, and the gates of Orgrimmar itself.

Thyn'tel Bladeweaver. Thyn'tel Bladeweaver is a night elf sentinel stationed at the Warrior's Terrace in Darnassus. She is deeply troubled by the disappearance of Priestess Velinde Starsong and dispatches trusted Alliance adventurers to track down clues regarding her whereabouts. Through her inquiries, she seeks to piece together the unraveling mystery behind the Scythe of Elune. Standing watch over Darnassus from the Warrior's Terrace, Thyn'tel Bladeweaver represents the vigilant military arm of the kaldorei. When Priestess Velinde Starsong mysteriously vanished without leaving word, Thyn'tel refused to let the trail go cold. Sensing that grave forces were involved, she takes it upon herself to commission adventurers willing to dig into the priestess's personal belongings and uncover where her journey led.

Tidefury Cove. Tidefury Cove is a treacherous stretch of water and rocky shallows along the southeastern coast of Dustwallow Marsh, south of Theramore Isle. Renowned for its hazardous reefs and wrecked vessels, it serves as a secluded haven for roaming makrura and solitary anglers. Tucked away at the far end of Dustwallow Bay between Theramore Isle and the Wyrmbog, Tidefury Cove presents a notorious navigational hazard to passing sailors. Jagged reefs and shifting shoals have claimed multiple vessels over the years, leaving rotting wooden hulks half-submerged in the tideline. Today, the ruined ships are crawled over by opportunistic makrura, turning the cove into a dangerous, isolated stretch of coastline visited mostly by hardy scavengers or quiet hermits seeking distance from Theramore's busy docks.

Tidus Stair. Tidus Stair is a natural rock formation of broad, stepped stone terraces perched over the Merchant Coast southeast of Ratchet. Sheltered beside the Great Sea, it serves as a quiet retreat for two tauren shamans communing with the tides and water spirits. Descending toward the surf southeast of Ratchet, the Tidus Stair resembles a monumental set of weathered stone steps cut directly into the coastal bluffs. While the surrounding Barrens are arid, dusty, and prone to skirmishes, this quiet stretch overlooking the Merchant Coast is dominated by the sound of crashing waves. Perched on the terraces is a modest hut where the tauren Islen Waterseer and Mahren Skyseer reside. Far from the bustling trade docks of the goblins, the two spend their days fishing, watching the horizon, and seeking insight from the coastal water spirits.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. At the northern safari camp in Stranglethorn Vale, the hunter Ajeck Rouack offers to train adventurers in the discipline of big cat stalking. She starts newcomers against the younger tigers prowling near the camp to test basic hunting and tracking prowess. Having learned the art of hunting tigers from her father when she was a girl, Ajeck Rouack shares his craft with travelers who reach Nesingwary's Expedition following Welcome to the Jungle. She insists that tracking and slaying the youngest felines is the essential foundation before any hunter can advance to greater quarry.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. At Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale, Ajeck Rouack escalates his hunting trials. Having seen your early promise with young stalkers, he now sends you into the jungle to fell mature Stranglethorn Tigers. Following your initial success against younger predators, Ajeck Rouack seeks to test your growing skills against more seasoned beasts. She directs you back out into the wilds of Stranglethorn Vale to hunt down ten mature Stranglethorn Tigers before you can pursue even greater challenges.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. Deep in the jungle at Nesingwary's Expedition, Ajeck Rouack raises the stakes of his hunting trials. He demands the death of ten elder Stranglethorn tigers to prove your prowess before the final test. Following the earlier hunts, Ajeck Rouack asks you to pursue ten elder Stranglethorn tigers across the wilds. He considers these beasts both the most elusive to track and the fiercest to overcome. Felling ten of them serves as the prelude to a concluding trial, after which he promises to proclaim you a master tiger hunter before Master Nesingwary.

name.frFR: Maîtrise de la chasse au tigre
name.itIT: La maestria nella caccia alla tigre

text.enUS: Tiger Mastery. Ajeck Rouack offers the ultimate challenge in his series of hunts within northern Stranglethorn Vale. After weeks of tracking an elusive beast, he challenges you to seek out the tiger Sin'Dall and bring back her paw. Having completed the earlier trials against Stranglethorn's tigers, you are offered one last challenge by Ajeck Rouack at Nesingwary's Expedition. The hunting camp has tracked an extraordinarily elusive tiger known as Sin'Dall across the jungle for weeks. Ajeck challenges you to track her down, fell the beast, and claim her paw as indisputable proof.

Timberling Seed. Timberling Seeds are botanical kernels harvested from the agitated plant elementals inhabiting Teldrassil. Naturalists and druids study these seeds to understand why the forest's plant life has grown unusually aggressive. The timberlings of Teldrassil are nature elementals whose temperament reflects the balance of the World Tree. Recently, these creatures have turned hostile and angry, troubling the night elves who tend the boughs. Herbalists like Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth believe the issue lies rooted in the soil, collecting seeds from wild timberlings in hopes that nurturing them under controlled, purified conditions might sprout docile offspring.

Timberling Seeds. Timberling Seeds is an early task given by the botanist Denalan at Lake Al'Ameth in Teldrassil. Concerned by the growing hostility of the local nature elementals, Denalan seeks to harvest their seeds to test whether enriched soil can cultivate calmer, more harmonious growth. The task offers a glimpse into the quiet efforts of night elf herbalists working to understand the subtle afflictions plaguing the World Tree. Timberlings are nature elementals native to the boughs of Teldrassil, intricately linked to the health and vitality of the flora around them. Ordinarily peaceful reflections of the forest's balance, their recent and inexplicable hostility has alarmed the local night elves. Rather than merely culling them, the botanist Denalan hopes to understand the source of their agitation.

Timberling Sprout. Timberling Sprouts are young, nascent plant elementals taking root near the shores of Lake Al'Ameth in Teldrassil. Even in their earliest growth, these sprouts show signs of corruption, prompting night elf wardens to pull them before they mature into aggressive timberlings. Timberlings are plant spirits closely tied to the natural vitality of Teldrassil, but the seedlings sprouting along Lake Al'Ameth have worried the local night elves. Rather than emerging healthy and in harmony with the wild, they sprout already tainted and aggressive. Because these infant sprouts appear beyond cleansing or natural healing, caretakers at Lake Al'Ameth must gather and destroy them to prevent an uncontrolled spread of hostile timberlings across the fragile boughs of the newly planted World Tree.

Timberling Sprouts. Timberling Sprouts is a quest given by the nature-watcher Denalan near Lake Al'Ameth in central Teldrassil. Concerned by the sudden and unnatural proliferation of woodland sprouts around the lake shores, Denalan asks travelers to uproot them before they mature into hostile timberlings. The task highlights early signs that a creeping corruption is disturbing the balance of the newly grown World Tree. Around the serene banks of Lake Al'Ameth, strange plant-like creatures known as timberlings have begun multiplying at an alarming rate. Rather than thriving in harmony with the woodland, the emerging timberling sprouts display signs of corruption from the moment they take root. Denalan, a dedicated student of nature residing beside the lake, recognizes that these sprouts are beyond healing. Left unchecked, they rapidly mature into aggressive bark-covered creatures that menace local wildlife and unwary travelers. Gathering and destroying the sprouts serves as an immediate line of defense to keep the grove clean.

Timbermaw Hold. Timbermaw Hold is a fortified subterranean network of tunnels that links Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring. It serves as the stronghold for the Timbermaw furbolgs, one of the last tribes to resist the demonic corruption plaguing northern Kalimdor. Carved deep into the mountain roots between Felwood, Moonglade, and Winterspring, Timbermaw Hold stands as a desperately guarded bastion. While neighboring furbolg tribes fell to the foul taint of the Burning Legion during the Third War, the Timbermaw clan weathered the nightmare within these stone corridors. Though safe beneath the earth, they were forced to watch their beloved forests warp into corrupted mockeries. Extremely protective and deeply suspicious of outsiders, the furbolgs guard every tunnel entrance fiercely, expecting violence from anyone wandering in from the infected woods.

name.esES: Puesto de los Fauces de Madera

text.enUS: Timbermaw Post. Timbermaw Post is a small furbolg camp situated in the snowy expanse of Winterspring, nestled between Frostfire Hot Springs and Lake Kel'Theril. Despite bearing the name of the uncorrupted Timbermaw tribe, the encampment has fallen under the aggressive grip of the corrupted Winterfall furbolgs. Positioned just southeast across the road from Frostfire Hot Springs and west of the frozen Lake Kel'Theril, Timbermaw Post stands as a bitter reminder of the furbolgs' internal strife in Winterspring. Despite its Timbermaw name, travelers approaching the camp will find no friendly welcomes. The outpost is controlled by the hostile Winterfall tribe, driven mad and violent by demonic corruption. Now crowded with savage Winterfall furbolgs, the camp serves as an aggressive staging ground encroaching upon the central road.

Time to Strike. "Time to Strike" is a Horde reconnaissance mission that transitions scouts across the Hillsbrad Foothills border to the military hub of Tarren Mill. Delivering Deathstalker Lesh's coded signal to High Executor Darthalia marks the transition from quiet surveillance to coordinated offensive operations against the local human populace. Perched along the high ground near the border between Silverpine Forest and the Hillsbrad Foothills, Deathstalker Lesh monitors the movements of human settlers and militia in the valley below. The Deathstalkers operate as the eyes and ears of the Undercity, surveying enemy settlements before any military deployment. Rather than risk abandoning her watchpost, Lesh entrusts passing Horde travelers to relay her gathered intelligence down the road to Tarren Mill.

Tinker Town. Tinker Town is the bustling gnomish quarter nestled within the subterranean dwarven city of Ironforge. Established to shelter refugees following the tragic fall of Gnomeregan, the district serves as the seat of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque's government-in-exile and the primary terminus for the Deeprun Tram. When subterranean troggs overran the high-tech city of Gnomeregan, the dwarven hosts of Ironforge opened their gates to the survivors. To accommodate the sudden influx of refugees, a cavernous district—previously home to dwarven residents and the entrance to the Deeprun Tram—was set aside for them. Under the watchful eye of High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his council, Tinker Town quickly became an energetic hub of whirring gears, experimental alchemy, and gadgetry. Despite being cramped guests in a stone city, the gnomes have rebuilt a semblance of their civilization around a massive spherical contraption, determined to reclaim their subterranean homeland.

Tinkers' Court. Tinkers' Court is the grand council chamber at the heart of Gnomeregan. Once the bustling seat of the High Tinker and his ruling council, it is now the grim stronghold of the traitor Mekgineer Thermaplugg. Before the disaster that ruined Gnomeregan, the Tinkers' Court served as the civic and political heart of the nation. It was here that High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque gathered with advisors and master inventors, including Tinkmaster Overspark, to debate technological advancements, govern civic matters, and guide gnomish society. The court represented the pinnacle of gnomish ingenuity and governance, situated just beyond the industrial works of the Engineering Labs and the Launch Bay.

Tinkmaster Overspark. This errand directs Alliance adventurers in Stormwind to Tinker Town in Ironforge, where Tinkmaster Overspark is mourning a tragic malfunction. Brother Sarno sends word that Overspark's mechanical creation, Techbot, has gone rogue amidst the irradiated ruins of Gnomeregan. Reaching the Tinkmaster is the first step toward recovering the wayward construct's memory core. Brother Sarno, tending to travelers in Stormwind City, shares word of an unfortunate dilemma brewing among the gnomish refugees. Tinkmaster Overspark—one of the brilliant minds behind Gnomeregan's wonders—is distraught over the corruption of Techbot, a once-helpful mechanical servant that served the tinkerers faithfully before the city fell into ruin.

Tiragarde Keep. Tiragarde Keep is a fortified human stronghold situated along Durotar's Scuttle Coast, south of Razor Hill. Originally built during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's invasion, the ruined citadel remains garrisoned by hostile Kul Tiran marines under Lieutenant Benedict. It serves as a defiant, permanent thorn in the Horde's side right on their home territory. Erected during Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore's campaign to eradicate Thrall's newly founded realm, Tiragarde Keep provided the Kul Tiran fleet an entrenched beachhead on the red shores of Durotar. Although the Horde eventually broke the siege and killed Proudmoore at Theramore Isle, the keep was never fully abandoned. Resupply forces under Lieutenant Benedict reclaimed the shattered stone walls, following the late Admiral's standing orders to wage an unyielding war against the orcs, entirely refusing the peace forged by Lady Jaina Proudmoore.

Tirion Fordring. Tirion Fordring is a legendary paladin and former lord of Mardenholde Keep, now living in quiet exile in the Eastern Plaguelands. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, he was stripped of his title and lands for honoring a debt of honor to an enemy orc. From his modest cabin along the Thondroril River, he watches over the tragedy unfolding across Lordaeron and worries for his son. Before the ruin of Lordaeron, Tirion Fordring was renowned as one of the kingdom's finest knights. A paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand, the order Archbishop Alonsus Faol founded during the Second War, Tirion fought the Old Horde with plate, hammer, and holy devotion. He was revered as an unyielding paragon of the Holy Light.

Tirisfal Pumpkin. Tirisfal Pumpkins grow in the tilled plots of the Solliden Farmstead, tended by surviving living humans struggling to survive in the blighted glades. The Forsaken routinely raid these fields to supply the Royal Apothecary Society with organic matter for their ongoing chemical concoctions. Despite the corruption settling over Lordaeron, crops still somehow sprout in the fields west of Brill. At the Solliden Farmstead, living human farmers cling to their soil, cultivating massive orange squash under the watchful guard of the nearby Scarlet Crusade. For these mortals, the harvest is vital sustenance. For the nearby Forsaken of Brill, however, the pumpkins represent both a spiteful target of sabotage and a bounty of raw organic reagents needed by Apothecary Johaan.

Titan. The titans are a primordial race of colossal, godlike beings who wander the cosmos bringing order and shaping worlds. In ancient antiquity, they came to Azeroth to vanquish the chaotic Old Gods, establish massive terrestrial facilities, and foster life before departing into the Great Dark Beyond. The titans are cosmic giants forged from primordial matter and arcane magic, embodying the forces of order and creation. In their journeys across the Great Dark Beyond, they sought out slumbering worlds to cultivate, raising up continents, calming chaotic elemental forces, and designing life. To enforce balance, they established powerful constructs made of stone, iron, and sea to watch over their works.

Tiza Battleforge. Tiza Battleforge is a veteran dwarven paladin of the Knights of the Silver Hand stationed within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries. Renowned for her steadfast devotion and insight, she guides young dwarven paladins along the path of virtue, charity, and self-sacrifice. Through study of the sacred texts and trials in the field, she tests whether initiates are truly ready to wield the Light's gift of resurrection. Within the serene chambers of the Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge, Tiza Battleforge stands as one of the most respected dwarven paladins of the Knights of the Silver Hand. Initiates across the Alliance—directed by tutors such as Brandur Ironhammer in Ironforge, Azar Stronghammer in Dun Morogh, and Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind—are sent to her to advance their spiritual education. Tiza believes that the Holy Light demands more than martial skill; it requires humble service, compassion, and unwavering fortitude against the encroaching darkness of the Scourge and other threats.

Tkashi Ruins. The Tkashi Ruins are ancient stone remnants situated southwest of Nesingwary's Expedition in northern Stranglethorn Vale. Overrun by hostile Bloodscalp trolls, the site remains a stronghold of the tribe. Perched southwest of Hemet Nesingwary's hunting camp, the crumbling stone masonry of the Tkashi Ruins marks the ancient domain of Stranglethorn's jungle trolls. Today, the encampment is heavily occupied by the Bloodscalp tribe, who aggressively defend the territory and practice their shamanistic rituals among the vines and decayed stone. While Hemet Nesingwary noted passing through the ruins without trouble in his hunting memoirs, modern travelers find the trolls far less accommodating, guarding valuable tribal relics buried among the rubble.

To Darnassus. To Darnassus is the culmination of a night elf druid's journey to commune with the Great Cat Spirit. After proving yourself to Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, you are sent back to the Cenarion Enclave to master the art of shifting into cat form. Having commune with the Great Cat Spirit through the guidance of Dendrite Starblaze in Moonglade, an aspiring night elf druid must return to Teldrassil. Starblaze acknowledges that you have proven yourself a worthy student and directs you back to your primary instructor, Mathrengyl Bearwalker, waiting beneath the boughs of the Cenarion Enclave in Darnassus.

To Gadgetzan You Go!. To Gadgetzan You Go! is a journey undertaken by Horde cooks seeking to advance beyond the limits of their capital city instructors. Directed by Zamja in Orgrimmar, aspiring chefs travel south across Kalimdor to Tanaris to seek out the eccentric goblin butcher Dirge Quikcleave. This breadcrumb marks the transition into true mastery over the culinary arts. In the Drag, the troll cook Zamja feeds countless warriors and travelers passing through the red canyons of Durotar. Yet when a dedicated cook absorbs every recipe and technique Zamja has to offer, the master admits defeat. Having imparted all her culinary mojo, she sends her seasoned pupil south to the sands of Tanaris, admitting that only a true master of strange and exotic meats can push a talented cook any further.

name.esES: Ir a Forjaz a buscar el "Compendio" de Yagyin
name.frFR: Aller à Ironforge chercher le « Sommaire de Yagyin »

text.enUS: To Ironforge for Yagyin's Digest. Theldurin the Lost sends you to Ironforge with a sigil. In a shop in the Forlorn Cavern, Gerrig Bonegrip is to take you for one of the people Theldurin fled, and you are to ask Gerrig for Yagyin's Digest. The Tablet tells Theldurin much, but not nearly enough. Yagyin wrote a digest in ages past, and the people Theldurin fled keep copies in many places, with their most learned studying it. Theldurin believes it holds vast knowledge that can offer protection, and wants it brought back.

To Orgrimmar!. To Orgrimmar! is an introductory summons dispatching a developing Horde rogue from Razor Hill to the capital city. Acting on orders from Kaplak, the initiate is sent beneath the surface into the Cleft of Shadow to present themselves before Shenthul and deeper within the network of the Shattered Hand. After cutting their teeth across Durotar, novice rogues eventually catch the attention of more prominent handlers. In Razor Hill, Kaplak bluntly acknowledges that an operative's budding talents—while unpolished—have earned notice. Rather than remaining out among the red crags, the operative is directed north into the cavernous alleys of Orgrimmar.

To Thunder Bluff. To Thunder Bluff marks the triumphant return of a young tauren druid from their communion with the Cenarion Circle in Moonglade. Having earned the favor of the Great Cat Spirit, the initiate returns to Turak Runetotem on the Elder Rise to master the art of feline shapeshifting. After proving their insight and worth before Dendrite Starblaze and the Great Cat Spirit in the sacred groves of Moonglade, a young druid must carry the spirit's blessings back to Mulgore. The communion with such primal powers represents a pivotal milestone in a druid's training, bridging ancient night elven teachings with the tauren's own earthen heritage.

To Valanaar. "To Valanaar" is an island quest in which adventurers carry an urgent military report from Aonda in Shen'dar to Peacekeeper leader Valennia Stormfist. The message alerts the settlement at the southeastern edge of the island that an aggressive cult is expanding rapidly and that direct conflict can no longer be avoided. Following the defense of Shen'dar and its pylon, the highlander Aonda dispatches a trusted traveler to carry urgent word across the island to Valanaar. Situated at the southeastern edge of the land, Valanaar houses the headquarters of the island's peacekeepers under the command of Valennia Stormfist. The mission carries a vital warning: the peaceful days on the island are ending, and Valennia must prepare her people for an inevitable clash with an aggressive, expanding cult.

To the Top. Marli Wishrunner can send you up to see the sights from one of the twin colossals of Feralas, with a warning attached: the trip goes only one way. Marli Wishrunner asks whether you would like to see the view from the top of one of the twin colossals, and can send you there. Marli adds a word of caution: think about how you will get down, because this is a one-way trip.

name.enUS: To the Undercity for Yagyin's Digest
name.esES: Ir a Entrañas a buscar el "Compendio" de Yagyin
name.itIT: To the Undercity for Yagyin's Digest
name.ptBR: To the Undercity for Yagyin's Digest

text.enUS: To the Undercity for Yagyin's Digest. Theldurin the Lost sends you to the Undercity of Lordaeron with a sigil. Keeper Bel'dugur is to take you for one of the people Theldurin fled, and you are to ask the keeper for Yagyin's Digest. The tablet tells Theldurin much, but not nearly enough. Yagyin wrote a digest in ages past, and the people Theldurin fled keep copies in many places, with their most learned studying it. Theldurin believes it holds vast knowledge that can protect them, and wants it brought back.

Token of Thievery. The Token of Thievery is a proof of skill recovered by novice rogues during their training in the Redridge Mountains. Placed inside a locked footlocker at the orc-threatened Alther's Mill, it serves as the final test set by the seasoned thief Lucius to demonstrate mastery over lockpicking. Not every scoundrel possesses an innate knack for working tumblers and slipping catches unnoticed. In Lakeshire, the roguish instructor Lucius puts promising operatives through their paces by testing their wits and tools in the field. Rather than keeping his trials confined to quiet alleys, Lucius stashes the Token of Thievery inside a sturdy lockbox hidden among the ruins of Alther's Mill, directly in the path of encroaching Blackrock orcs. Retrieving the token proves that an initiate can pick a secure mechanism under the pressure of mortal danger, earning them their formal Certificate of Thievery.

Tomb Weed. Tomb Weed is an alchemical quest assigned by Junior Apothecary Holland in Tirisfal Glades. Holland has been modifying wild doom weed and replanting it at the haunted Balnir Farmstead, cultivating a potent new specimen that unexpectedly attracts the local Scourge. Junior Apothecary Holland is not content simply harvesting native herbs for the Royal Apothecary Society; he harbors grand ambitions of his own. By gathering doom weed and subjecting it to minor alchemical alterations, he replanted the strains across the soil of the Balnir Farmstead to cultivate an evolved specimen he christened tomb weed. Holland views this hybrid flora as the centerpiece of his work and a herald of his personal destiny.

Tome of Divinity. The Tome of Divinity is an introductory summons calling young dwarven paladins from their field duties in Dun Morogh to the mountain city of Ironforge. Dispatched by Azar Stronghammer, the initiate is directed to seek guidance from Tiza Battleforge high in the Hall of Mysteries. It marks the formal beginning of a paladin's deeper trials in service to the Holy Light. While dwarven initiates begin their training protecting the snowbound villages and roads of Dun Morogh, martial prowess alone does not make a paladin. Azar Stronghammer recognizes when a defender has grown ready for deeper spiritual instruction. Rather than continuing standard martial drills, he sends promising candidates into the heart of Ironforge to begin their true initiation under the city's revered holy elders.

Tome of Divinity. A summons bearing the Tome of Divinity calls promising paladins from Elwynn to Stormwind. Answering Brother Wilhelm's call begins the sacred trials needed to master resurrection through the Holy Light. Novice paladins in Elwynn Forest spend their early days helping locals and testing their strength against wolves, Defias bandits, and kobolds. When an initiate shows martial discipline and devotion to the Holy Light, mentors such as Brother Wilhelm send a personal summons. Leaders of the paladins take note of promising students and direct them to leave the local chapels behind and report straight to the kingdom's spiritual heart.

Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity is a rite of passage quest offered to young dwarven paladins serving in Dun Morogh. Directed by Brandur Ironhammer, the paladin trainer in Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, an initiate is sent upstairs to speak with the respected paladin trainer Tiza Battleforge. It marks the transition from basic martial training into the deeper spiritual duties and sacred vows of the Holy Light. While novice paladins spend their early days defending Anvilmar and Kharanos from troggs and frost trolls, their duties eventually call for deeper devotion. Brandur Ironhammer, recognizing that an initiate has proven their martial discipline, advises them to take a break from their work in the snowy passes and seek guidance upstairs in his own Hall of Mysteries in Ironforge. There, senior paladins oversee the spiritual maturation of the order.

Tome of Divinity. This errand directs dwarven paladins wandering abroad to return home to Ironforge to further their sacred calling. Offered by Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker in Stormwind, it points fledgling champions toward Tiza Battleforge, one of the most respected instructors in the Hall of Mysteries. Returning home marks the beginning of their formal trials with the Tome of Divinity. While dwarven paladins frequently aid the kingdom of Stormwind and venture throughout human territories, their spiritual and martial roots remain anchored in Khaz Modan. Lord Grayson Shadowbreaker, recognizing when a dwarf's training in the field has progressed enough, advises them to return to the heart of Ironforge. There, their own people oversee the profound spiritual obligations expected of a full Knight of the Silver Hand.

Tome of Divinity. Tome of Divinity is a summons directed at developing human paladins visiting Ironforge. Master Brandur Ironhammer bids initiates make the journey south to the Cathedral of Light in Stormwind, where Master Duthorian Rall oversees advanced training in the sacred Tomes of Divinity. While dwarven paladins train vigorously within Ironforge's Hall of Mysteries, the broader traditions of the Silver Hand remain deeply entwined with the Church of the Holy Light in human lands. Word sent north from Stormwind calls on promising holy warriors to present themselves directly before the senior priesthood and paladin mentors of the Cathedral of Light.

Tome of the Cabal. Tome of the Cabal sends an aspiring Alliance warlock from the heights above Ratchet back to the Library of Ironforge. To summon and dominate a ravenous felhunter, the summoner must locate a legendary manual written by the first warlocks who ever conquered the beast. Subjugating an imp, a voidwalker, or a succubus requires ritual, but a felhunter poses an entirely different hazard. Felhunters do not merely serve the Burning Legion; they actively hunt and devour arcane energy. A standard summoning circle will crumble before one, draining the summoner's magic before a binding can even take hold. Strahad Farsan, watching over Ratchet from his redoubt in the Barrens, knows better than to let an amateur try such a binding unprepared.

Tome of the Cabal. This quest sends Horde warlocks on a journey from Strahad Farsan's encampment in the Barrens to the Undercity in search of ancient demonological lore. To summon and bind a felhunter, an initiate must track down the lost Tome of the Cabal, starting with a cartographer named Jorah Annison. It marks a critical step in mastering higher demonic summoning. Summoning a felhunter is no minor trick of fel magic; the predatory beasts devour magical energies and resist standard summoning circles. Strahad Farsan explains that to draw one forth, an initiate requires the aid of specialized circles and an ancient grimoire known as the Tome of the Cabal. Authored by the first order of warlocks ever to bind a felhunter without outside aid, the book contains the exact rites and seals required to enslave such a dangerous demon.

Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks an Alliance warlock with tracking down the scattered, ruined halves of a singular grimoire known as the Tome of the Cabal. Recovering the missing pages from distant lands is essential for deciphering the dark rites necessary to bind a felhunter. Only a single copy of the Tome of the Cabal was ever scribed, and its violent history ensured it did not stay intact. Torn apart and vandalized, its remnants were scattered to entirely different corners of the world. One portion, a tattered manuscript ripped straight from the binding, somehow found its way across the sea into the rugged canyons of Kalimdor, falling into the hands of the centaur clans. The remaining section was intended for transport by sea from the shores of Lordaeron down to Khaz Modan, but the vessel foundered before reaching its port.

Tome of the Cabal. This quest tasks Horde warlocks with reuniting the severed halves of the ancient Tome of the Cabal for Jorah Annison in the Undercity. Once kept within the kingdom of Lordaeron, the grimoire was torn apart and scattered across the world before being lost entirely. Tracking down its damp and tattered remnants requires braving hostile waters in the Eastern Kingdoms and deep centaur territory in Kalimdor. The Tome of the Cabal was once preserved within the library walls of the old kingdom of Lordaeron. At some point, the sinister grimoire was deliberately vandalized, stripped of nearly half its pages, and sundered into two pieces. The remaining formal text was slated for transit south to the dwarven halls of Ironforge, but fate intervened: the transport wrecked along the rocky coastline west of Southshore, leaving the pages to rot in the shallows under the watchful eyes of scavenging murlocs.

Tome of the Cabal. This quest marks the final preparation for Alliance warlocks seeking to command a felhunter. After piecing together the fragmented Tome of the Cabal, the warlock must gather rods of channeling from Dragonmaw orcs in the Wetlands and return to Strahad Farsan overlooking Ratchet. In Ironforge's Hall of Explorers, Krom Stoutarm meticulously bound the tattered and mouldering remnants of the Tome of the Cabal back together. Reluctant to surrender such a rare piece of dark scholarship, the dwarf scholar extracts a promise of a future copy before passing along a fresh missive from Strahad Farsan. The tome contains the rites required to breach the Nether, but raw parchment alone cannot conduct the necessary ritual.

Tome of the Cabal. This quest marks the final preparatory leg in a Horde warlock's journey to summon and command a felhunter. Having helped Jorah Annison restore the ancient Tome of the Cabal, the practitioner must travel into hostile territory to seize three Rods of Channeling before bringing the components to Strahad Farsan in Ratchet. In the Undercity, the Forsaken scholar Jorah Annison examines the fragments of the recovered Tome of the Cabal, piecing together its eldritch passages. While pleased with the rare intellectual bounty, Jorah delivers an urgent directive sent by Strahad Farsan. To bind a demonic predator like a felhunter, raw knowledge is not enough: a warlock must possess precise instruments of power capable of focusing violent demonic energies into a binding circle.

Tome of the Cabal (quest item). The Tome of the Cabal is a grimoire entrusted to warlocks by Strahad Farsan on the bluffs overlooking Ratchet. It holds the perilous incantations necessary to pull a ravenous felhunter across the Twisting Nether and bind it to the summoner's will. Felhunters are vicious, mana-devouring beasts native to the chaotic expanse of the Twisting Nether. Subduing one is a rite of passage for seasoned warlocks, and the rituals required to tear open a pathway for such a beast are contained within the pages of the Tome of the Cabal. Strahad Farsan, an experienced conjurer operating out of Ratchet, provides the tome only after an aspirant has proven capable of gathering the rare and hazardous components needed to fuel its magics.

Tommy Joe Stonefield. At the river west of Stonefield Farm, Tommy Joe Stonefield longs for Maybell Maclure. Their families have feuded for years, so he relies on secret notes and quiet banks to keep their love hidden. Tommy Joe Stonefield waits by the river west of Stonefield Farm, looking toward the Maclure homestead across the water. The Stonefields and Maclures have clashed for years over land, pride, and farmyard squabbles. Their elders keep the feud alive, but Tommy Joe has fallen in love with Maybell Maclure. The two cannot meet openly without angering both households. Gramma Stonefield, Tommy Joe’s sympathetic grandmother, helps them exchange secret notes and tokens of affection.

Tonga Runetotem. Tonga Runetotem is a knowledgeable tauren druid stationed outside the inn at the Crossroads in the Barrens. Dispatched from Thunder Bluff, he investigates an unnatural corruption seeping into the region's sparse oases and sickening the native wildlife. His research aims to trace the spiritual disturbance back to its origin before the delicate ecosystem collapses entirely. Amid the dust and bustling commerce of the Crossroads, Tonga Runetotem keeps a quiet vigil. Sent down from the high mesas of Mulgore by his elders in Thunder Bluff, Tonga possesses an intimate understanding of the arid savannah. Where others see only barren scrub and predatory beasts, he reads the subtle currents of the land's health. In recent times, those currents have soured dramatically, compelling him to recruit capable travelers to investigate the heart of the savannah's life: its isolated oases.

Tooga's Quest. Tooga, a lost turtle, was sent out to fetch dinner by his wife Torta and took a wrong turn somewhere. Tooga asks you to lead him back to Torta, who waits just south of Steamwheedle Port. Tooga wanders near a crashed goblin zeppelin close to Thistleshrub Valley. Torta sent Tooga out to fetch dinner, and a wrong turn somewhere has left the turtle hopelessly lost. Tooga asks you to lead the way back.

Tools for Steelgrill. Tools for Steelgrill is an early Alliance delivery errand that introduces travelers leaving Kharanos to the nearby mechanic workshop at Steelgrill's Depot. Tharek Blackstone sends you up the road with a fresh crate of heavy equipment for Beldin Steelgrill, the master siege engine tech who works through spanners and ratchets faster than town suppliers can keep up. Beldin Steelgrill carries an undisputed reputation across Dun Morogh as the sharpest siege engine mechanic in the mountains, but his violent work ethic takes a heavy toll on his workshop. According to Tharek Blackstone in Kharanos, Steelgrill cracks arclight spanners and snaps tools almost as fast as local supply crates can arrive. When a fresh batch of durable gear is assembled in Kharanos, anyone heading northeast is quickly recruited to lug the heavy parcel out to the depot.

Tools of the Highborne. Tools of the Highborne is an Alliance quest offered by Thundris Windweaver in Auberdine. Travelers are dispatched south into the shattered ruins of Ameth'Aran to pry lingering magical relics from the hands of restless Highborne apparitions. The goal is simple: recover these ancient artifacts before their latent sorcery can unleash further harm upon Kalimdor. South of Auberdine, east of the coastal highway, lie the overgrown stone foundations of Ameth'Aran. Ten thousand years ago, this settlement served as a bastion for the Highborne—the privileged aristocracy of the ancient night elven empire. When their unchecked arcane dabbling culminated in the Sundering of the world, Ameth'Aran was shattered. Yet its inhabitants never truly departed. Sentinels patrolling Darkshore report that the ghosts of these aristocrats still haunt the sunken plazas, clutching the enchanted tools and trinkets they possessed in life.

Tools of the Trade. Tools of the Trade is an initiation mission for Horde rogues given by Mennet Carkad in the Undercity. Ordered by Lord Varimathras, agents must obtain lockpicking gear and infiltrate Ambermill to recover sensitive Kirin Tor reports detailing Dalaran's current state. Following the interrogation of one of their prisoners, the Deathstalkers learned that vital intelligence concerning the ruins of Dalaran lies hidden in Ambermill. Silverpine Forest remains a precarious front line, and the human mages guarding the village guard their communications fiercely. Under the orders of Lord Varimathras, Deathstalker handler Mennet Carkad directs promising operatives to bypass Kirin Tor sentries and secure the Dalaran Status Report.
