text.enUS: Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe. Verna's Westfall Stew Recipe travels to Salma Saldean as the Furlbrows prepare to leave their farm. Her handwritten formula carries a familiar comfort for those who remain. Verna and Farmer Furlbrow have homesteaded in Westfall for years, but the Defias Brotherhood and rogue harvest golems now run rampant across the countryside. They wait for their wagon to be repaired so they can escape toward Stormwind. While they wait, Verna writes down her beloved formula for Westfall Stew. She entrusts the recipe to travelers bound for her neighboring friend, Salma Saldean, so the familiar comfort of the stew can endure for those left behind.

Verner Osgood. Verner Osgood is the resident blacksmith of Lakeshire, stationed just outside the town smithy. Balancing local civilian trade with the crushing demands of the Stormwind military, he works tirelessly to keep horses shod and defenders armed amid relentless gnoll raids. Standing by the forge in central Lakeshire, Verner Osgood represents the strained industrial backbone of the Redridge Mountains. Tasked with crafting basic supplies like horseshoes for local mounts, Verner finds his stock constantly co-opted to manufacture weapons and armor for the Stormwind Guard. With the kingdom stretching its borders thin and local garrisons lacking supplies, independent smiths like Verner must carry the logistical burden of the realm's defense.

Verner's Note. Verner's Note is a written requisition penned by Lakeshire's blacksmith, Verner Osgood, and carried to Smith Argus in Goldshire. It details a critical shortage of iron in Redridge, asking the Elwynn smith for emergency horseshoes. Maintaining the defense of Lakeshire demands a heavy toll in worked metal. With the Stormwind Guard stationed in town stretched thin against invading gnolls and local perils, Verner Osgood has consumed nearly all his iron reserves keeping soldiers armed and armored. As a result, Lakeshire's stables have fallen into neglect, lacking even basic horseshoes for their mounts. This letter represents Verner swallowing his pride to ask Smith Argus in Goldshire for an external shipment of prepared shoes to keep the town's horses mobile.

Verog the Dervish. Verog the Dervish is an elusive Kolkar centaur leader who roams the southern plains of the Barrens. To put an end to his raids, Regthar Deathgate directs Horde champions to raid the centaur command tent at the Stagnant Oasis, forcing the nomadic commander into the open. Following the downfall of Barak Kodobane, the orc warrior Regthar Deathgate sets his sights on the remaining warlords of the Kolkar tribe. Unlike Barak, who lingered openly near the northern waters of the Forgotten Pools, Verog the Dervish wanders far and wide across the sun-baked plains, rarely staying in one encampment for long. Tracking him across the vast territory would be an exercise in futility, leaving Horde scouts with only one viable strategy: force the commander to come to them.

Verog's Head. Verog's Head is the grisly trophy claimed from Verog the Dervish, a prominent Kolkar centaur leader who oversees forces around the Stagnant Oasis. It is sought by the orc Regthar Deathgate as proof of the chieftain's demise and to demoralize the aggressive Kolkar tribes threatening the Barrens. The Kolkar centaur pose a relentless threat to Horde travelers and supply routes across the northern Barrens. Verog the Dervish, known for his nomadic habits, leaves his command tent at the Stagnant Oasis vulnerable while roaming the arid scrubland. To bring him out into the open, Horde operatives attack his forces around his pavilion until an alarm is raised. Once Verog rushes back to defend his camp, he is slain and decapitated. Delivering his severed head to Regthar Deathgate serves as vital evidence that another dangerous Kolkar chieftain has been dismantled, joining the head of Barak Kodobane on display.

Veron Amberstill. Veron Amberstill is a dwarven ram breeder residing at Amberstill Ranch in eastern Dun Morogh. He tends to the rugged mountain rams that serve as the traditional mounts of Ironforge and offers them to skilled riders who have earned his trust. Tucked away in the snow-dusted hills of eastern Dun Morogh, Veron Amberstill oversees the celebrated stock of Amberstill Ranch. Mountain rams are perfectly suited for Khaz Modan's treacherous slopes, sure-footed and thick-coated against the bite of mountain blizzards. Veron breeds and trains these beasts to carry dwarven scouts, mountaineers, and traveling adventurers. While he gladly provides standard and swift mounts to fellow dwarves, outsiders must prove their unwavering loyalty to the throne of Ironforge before he will part with any of his prized herd.

Veronica Nials. Captain Veronica Nials is an officer of the Stromgarde military stationed at Refuge Pointe in the Arathi Highlands. Amid the kingdom's collapse, she coordinates defensive operations against the Syndicate and ogres that overrun the fallen capital. Following the Third War, the human kingdom of Stromgarde shattered, leaving its remnants struggling to survive against invading Boulderfist ogres and the treachery of the Syndicate. Captain Veronica Nials stands as one of the central commanders of the surviving Stromgarde defenders at Refuge Pointe. Tasked with holding the line, she directs Alliance champions against key Syndicate leadership, such as Lord Falconcrest and the warlock Marez Cowl, while striving to recover fallen soldiers' badges so their grieving families can find closure.

Vesprystus. Vesprystus is the night elf flight master stationed at the docks of Rut'theran Village at the base of Teldrassil. He oversees the roost of trained hippogryphs that carry travelers between the great World Tree and mainland Kalimdor. Perched at the southern base of Teldrassil in Rut'theran Village, Vesprystus tends the hippogryphs that bridge the isolated elven boughs to the rest of the world. While a magical portal connects Rut'theran directly to the canopy city of Darnassus above, hippogryph flights provide a swift crossing toward Darkshore and the mainland. Vesprystus works in coordination with the flight master at Auberdine across the strait, ensuring safe passage for sentinels, emissaries, and adventurers journeying into Kalimdor.

Veteran Uzzek. Veteran Uzzek is a Horde quest that sends promising young warriors to seek out a seasoned combat instructor. Stationed just south of Far Watch Post between Durotar and the Barrens, Uzzek teaches new recruits that true martial greatness requires disciplined study as well as strength. In the culture of the Horde, martial strength is unquestioned and revered above all else. Yet brute force alone does not make a champion. Seasoned commanders know that the greatest warriors are also humble students of the craft, willing to hone their instincts through discipline and study. Aspiring fighters ready to advance beyond basic training are directed to seek out those who have survived the crucible of war.

Vial of Innocent Blood. A Vial of Innocent Blood is a grim alchemical reagent gathered by Syndicate shadow mages lurking in the ruins of Durnholde Keep. Sought after by the Royal Apothecary Society in Tarren Mill, it serves as a key catalyst in brewing experimental toxins. Within the crumbled walls of Durnholde Keep, the fallen human nobles of the Syndicate practice dark and unsavory arts. Among them are shadow mages who systematically harvest the blood of innocents for their own occult rituals. This macabre practice has drawn the keen attention of Apothecary Lydon in Tarren Mill. Needing untainted blood to brew an experimental pacifying agent meant to neutralize the Venture Company in Stonetalon Mountains, the Forsaken apothecary sees the Syndicate's grim stores as a convenient shortcut for his work.

Vial of Phlogiston. A Vial of Phlogiston is an alchemical substance used by master armorers to temper extraordinarily resilient mail. Guarded within the quilboar stronghold of Razorfen Kraul, it is coveted by both Alliance and Horde smiths forging specialized battle armor for promising warriors. Phlogiston is an intensely volatile, fire-bearing substance prized in esoteric metallurgy. Both the dwarven smith Furen Longbeard in Stormwind and the near-blind orc armorer Thun'grim Firegaze in the Barrens consider it an indispensable component for hardening warrior armor beyond ordinary physical limits. Without this alchemical agent, the specialized forging techniques required for Fire Hardened Mail or the Horde's Brutal Armor cannot be completed.

Vial of Purest Water. The Vial of Purest Water is a sacred vessel blessed by the hermit Brine deep in the southern Barrens. Entrusted to an initiate shaman, its purified contents are essential for concocting the draught required to perceive elusive elemental spirits. Forged through trials of patience and cleansing under the guidance of Brine, the water sealed in this vial represents liquid in its uncorrupted elemental essence. Transported across the arid wastes of the Barrens back to the solitary shore where Islen Waterseer keeps watch, the vial serves as the vital component in brewing a water sapta. Without its pristine purity, a shaman cannot commune with the spiritual guardians that dwell in places far removed from the sunbaked flats.

Vial of Spider Venom. A Vial of Spider Venom contains the potent, necrotic poison harvested from the arachnids that infest the darkened woods of Duskwood. Madame Eva of Darkshire uses this dangerous extract alongside undead remains to craft protective wards against incoming harm. The shadowed thickets of Duskwood harbor monstrous arachnids—from skittering pygmy venom webs and green recluses to black widows and the notorious Naraxis. These creatures pump a foul, potent poison through their fangs, potent enough to paralyze travelers and decay flesh. Adventurers brave enough to slay these horrors can extract intact vials of the viscous fluid.

Vice. The Vice is a rugged, desolate expanse of Deadwind Pass situated along the road leading toward Karazhan. It serves as the territory of the Deadwind ogres, who maintain rough mounds and scattered camps in defiance of the land's grim isolation. Travelers passing through must navigate both their crude brutality and their surprisingly adept wielders of dark magic. Stretching across the southern stretches of Deadwind Pass, the Vice is defined by barren earth, jagged rock faces, and crude mounds erected by the Deadwind ogre clan. While the surrounding canyon is largely abandoned to vengeful ghosts and scavenger vultures, these ogres have carved out a stubborn foothold directly beside the main path approaching Karazhan. Why they chose such a bleak and magically scarred waste remains an enduring mystery, but any traveler passing between Duskwood and the Swamp of Sorrows quickly learns they defend their camps with fierce territorial violence.

Vicious Night Web Spider Venom. Vicious Night Web Spider Venom is a potent natural toxin gathered from the arachnids haunting eastern Tirisfal Glades. The Royal Apothecary Society prizes it for its peculiar ability to carry and preserve historical disease strains, making it a critical reagent in the development of the Forsaken's New Plague. According to research conducted by Apothecary Johaan in Brill, ancient texts chronicle a devastating historical plague that wiped out thousands of innocent victims. Curiously, the contagious agent behind that forgotten outbreak managed to endure over centuries by embedding itself within the venom of the local Night Web spiders. By hunting down the vicious breed lurking in Venomweb Vale south of the Scarlet Monastery, the apothecaries extract this preserved virulence to serve as a vital catalyst in their ongoing alchemical experiments.

Vidra Hearthstove. Vidra Hearthstove is a dwarven cook residing in the Stoutlager Inn in Thelsamar. Known for preparing local specialties, she frequently relies on traveling adventurers to gather regional ingredients for her famous blood sausages. Within the bustling warmth of the Stoutlager Inn, Vidra Hearthstove tends the kitchen and helps feed the locals and travelers passing through Loch Modan. Sharing a surname with the innkeeper, she keeps Thelsamar well-provisioned. Her signature dish, Thelsamar blood sausages, is a hearty dwarven staple that requires fresh game meats gathered from the surrounding wilderness, including boar entrails, spider ichor, and bear meat.

Viktori Prism'Antras. Viktori Prism'Antras is an eccentric stargazer residing in a small hillside hut overlooking Darkshire. While the town around him succumbs to dread and looming horrors, Viktori focuses intently on building a telescope to view the heavens clearly. To realize his vision, he relies on adventurous travelers to acquire intricate parts based on gnomish schematics. Perched up the slope just beyond the gryphon roost, Viktori Prism'Antras spends his days peering outward from the gloom of Duskwood. Amid undead incursions, ravenous spiders, and creeping shadows, his obsession lies far beyond the suffocating canopy. He dreams of building a magnificent optical telescope capable of bringing the stars into brilliant focus, offering a quiet escape from the dread that engulfs the hamlet.

Vile Familiar Head. A Vile Familiar Head is a gruesome trophy collected from the feral impish creatures dwelling near the Burning Blade Coven in the Valley of Trials. Young Horde warlocks gather them under the guidance of Ruzan as proof of their combat readiness before learning to bind their first demonic minions. The heads serve as a grim test of discipline, showing that an apprentice understands the lethality of the beings they intend to summon. Within the sun-baked canyon of the Valley of Trials, the warlock trainer Ruzan demands six Vile Familiar Heads from novices seeking to learn the art of summoning. The vile familiars that loiter outside the Burning Blade Coven are vicious, fiery imps whose diminutive stature conceals dangerous elemental cunning. Ruzan requires prospective summoners to face these fiends in battle and sever their heads to prove they can subdue and command demonic life rather than be overpowered by it. Because warlocks are barely tolerated within Thrall's Horde, training requires extreme caution; reckless novices who perish to their own conjurations only deepen the dishonor and suspicion cast upon practitioners of the dark arts.

Vile Familiars. In the arid valley of the Valley of Trials, the warlock trainer Ruzan tasks aspiring practitioners of the dark arts with proving their mettle against vile familiars. To earn the knowledge of demon summoning, initiates must face these impish creatures in combat and claim their severed heads. It marks the humble, dangerous first step toward mastering fel power under the watchful eyes of the Horde. Warlocks hold an uneasy place within Thrall's newly forged Horde. The legacy of demonic corruption and blood pacts that once brought ruin to the orcish race left deep scars and lingering distrust. Though practitioners of fel magic are tolerated in Durotar, they are neither loved nor widely embraced. Many choose reclusive lives in shadowy corners like the Den, practicing their art away from prying eyes while teaching those rare initiates daring enough to walk the path.

Vile Familiars. This task marks the completion of a young warlock's first foray against the demonic minions hiding in the Valley of Trials. After slaying vile familiars under Ruzan's guidance, the neophyte reports their deed to Zureetha Fargaze, who oversees the culling of the encroaching Burning Blade. While other young warriors and scouts in the Valley of Trials are dispatched directly by Zureetha Fargaze to curb the infestation in the Burning Blade Coven, warlock initiates answer first to their shadowy mentors. Ruzan demands proof of strength and control over lesser demons before directing his pupils back into the fold of the Horde's general defense, ensuring their efforts serve both the coven of warlocks and the safety of the Den.

Vile Familiars. Vile Familiars is an early task given by Zureetha Fargaze to newly arrived champions in the Valley of Trials. While monitoring the valley's trials, Zureetha discovered an insidious coven of the Burning Blade hiding in a nearby cavern. To check their sudden spread, recruits are sent to hunt down the demonic familiars creeping out into the red dirt of Durotar. The Valley of Trials is meant to be a proving ground where young orcs and Darkspear trolls demonstrate their strength, discipline, and loyalty to Thrall's Horde. It was intended to test recruits against native predators like scorpids and boars, not demonic corruption. Yet, hidden in a cave to the northeast, agents calling themselves the Burning Blade have established a secret coven right under the watchful gaze of the valley's overseers.

name.ruRU: Чешуя мурлока из племени Злобного Плавника

text.enUS: Vile Fin Scale. Vile Fin Scales are harvested from the murloc tribes prowling the waterways and northern coasts of Tirisfal Glades. In Brill, the Royal Apothecary Society utilizes these resilient biological samples in their ongoing research to engineer a devastating new plague. The Royal Apothecary Society works relentlessly to craft a virulent blight capable of decimating both the living and the Scourge. Simple toxins are easy enough to brew, but creating an infectious disease that spreads effortlessly across populations requires specialized alchemical properties. Apothecary Johaan in Brill studies Vile Fin scales specifically to understand how their natural resilience and mucous coatings can aid in stabilizing and transmitting his experimental contagions.

Vile Reef. The Vile Reef is a submerged, vibrant coral shelf lying off the western coast of Stranglethorn Vale near Grom'gol Base Camp. Beneath its waters, aggressive murlocs make their home among ancient sunken troll ruins, giant clams, and coastal shipwrecks. Stretching beneath the waves of the Great Sea just offshore from Grom'gol Base Camp, the Vile Reef is known for its vivid marine growth and perilous inhabitants. The seabed is dotted with the weathered stonework of submerged troll ruins alongside the enigmatic Altar of the Tides. Flocks of territorial murlocs lurk among the coral shelves and shattered timbers of passing vessels, fiercely defending the shallow waters and preying upon any diver who braves the deep in search of giant clams and rare blue pearls.

name.deDE: Elende Satyrn! Die Dryaden sind in Gefahr!

text.enUS: Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger!. Vile Satyr! Dryads in Danger! is an urgent Alliance quest begun in Ashenvale by the dryad Illiyana. Desperate for aid, she recruits travelers to search for her missing sisters who ventured into the corrupted ruins of Xavian to recover a stolen sacred relic. While resting in Ashenvale, the dryad Illiyana finds herself overwhelmed with worry. A band of her dryad sisters departed into the corrupted northern reaches of the forest on a perilous mission to recover the Branch of Cenarius, a holy relic stolen by the vile satyrs. Though they promised to return swiftly, two days have passed in silence, prompting Illiyana to plead with passing Alliance travelers to track them down before it is too late.

Vilebranch Hooligans. Smith Slagtree of Revantusk Village says Vilebranch trolls invaded the village and stole his tools. He keeps spare tools, but the stolen set was a gift from a kind-hearted gnome who saved his life when he was a young orc, and he wants it back. Vilebranch trolls invaded Revantusk Village and stole Smith Slagtree's tools. He has backup tools, but the stolen set was a gift from a kind-hearted gnome who saved his life when he was a young orc. He tells you the tools mean the world to him and asks you to recover them.

Vimes's Report. Captain Garran Vimes rates your work as the best Vimes has seen from an amateur. Lady Jaina Proudmoore asked Vimes to keep her apprised of a delicate situation, and Vimes gives you the report to bring to her in Theramore. Lady Proudmoore asked Captain Vimes to keep her apprised of a delicate situation, and Vimes has not spoken with her for some time. Vimes meant to deliver the report later, but now judges it more fitting for you to speak with her about it, since you may well have better answers for her questions than Vimes would.

Vimes's Report. Lady Jaina Proudmoore has read Captain Garran Vimes's report and thanks you for your help with the investigation. She asks you to return to Vimes and help get to the bottom of the mystery. Going by Captain Vimes's report, Lady Proudmoore sees that you have been a great help to his investigation, and she thanks you for it. She is easier in her mind knowing the matter rests in such capable hands. She asks you to return to Captain Vimes in Theramore and help him get to the bottom of this mystery.

Viscous Fallout. Viscous Fallout is a toxic water elemental wandering the irradiated corridors of Gnomeregan, a living mass of the poison that fouled the city after Mekgineer Thermaplugg's devastating radiation release. When Gnomeregan was flooded with radiation on Mekgineer Thermaplugg's treacherous advice to wipe out the invading troggs, the fallout left the city's lower levels awash in toxic slime and contamination. Viscous Fallout is a water elemental of that poisoned depth, its very substance thick with the city's toxic waste. Where it came from before the fall is not known.

Visit the Herbalist. Following a meal delivery to his remote post, Guard Parker asks a favor before you return to the Lakeshire inn. Hoping to express his feelings for Darcy, he sends you to the local herbalist to purchase flowers. Parker insists that the herbalist not be told who ordered them or who they are intended for. Stationed along the lonely southern approach to Lakeshire, Guard Parker spends his watch keeping an eye out for blackrock orcs and gnolls. When you bring him a warm meal from Darcy at the Lakeshire Inn, he seizes the opportunity to reciprocate her kindness. Instead of letting you simply walk back, he asks you to stop by the local herbalist shop on the west end of town and purchase a bouquet of flowers for her.

Vital Intelligence. Vital Intelligence marks the end of a freshly risen Forsaken's training in Deathknell. Entrusted with intercepted Scarlet Crusade documents, the courier is sent out into Tirisfal Glades to report to Executor Zygand in Brill. Having neutralized local threats and intercepted a courier of the Scarlet Crusade, newly recruited Forsaken are deemed ready for broader service. Executor Arren entrusts the recovered intelligence to the player, directing them out through the sheltered canyon of Deathknell and east along the road toward Brill, past Cold Hearth Manor.

Vol'jin. Vol'jin is the chieftain of the Darkspear trolls and a master shadow hunter. Residing in Grommash Hold alongside Warchief Thrall, he acts as a trusted advisor to the Horde while working to secure his displaced people a permanent home in Durotar. Vol'jin took up leadership of the Darkspear tribe following the tragic death of his father, Sen'jin, on their ancestral island home. When sea witch-worshipping murlocs and human forces nearly destroyed the isolated tribe, Thrall's orcs intervened, forging a deep bond between the two peoples. After evacuating the ruins of their islands, Vol'jin pledged his trolls to the New Horde and brought them across the Great Sea to Kalimdor.

Volcor. Volcor is an injured night elf scout stranded deep within Blackwood Den in southern Darkshore. Trapped by hostile Blackwood furbolgs, he relies on his faithful companion Grimclaw and the aid of Auberdine's defenders to escape. While tracking the corrupted Blackwood tribe in their subterranean lair, Volcor was ambushed and severely wounded. Unable to fight his way past the hostile furbolgs on his own, he sent his loyal bear companion, Grimclaw, out into the wilds of Darkshore to seek help from the settlement of Auberdine.

Voodoo Charm. The Voodoo Charm is a mystical talisman used within the barrows of Teldrassil to sever a sinister enchantment. Handed to adventurers by the spirit of Oben Rageclaw, it allows his corrupted, puppeted physical form to be permanently released so his soul may rest in the Emerald Dream.

Voodoo Dues. "Sea Wolf" MacKinley in Booty Bay needs to balance his books by collecting outstanding debts from three old associates. Though rumors claim the men were cursed and bewitched into wandering ancient jungle ruins, MacKinley expects their prized possessions retrieved regardless of their grim fate. Following your earlier collection efforts for "Sea Wolf" MacKinley, the pirate still holds an active ledger of unsettled debts. Three particular debtors—Maury "Club Foot" Wilkins, Jon-Jon the Crow, and Chucky "Ten Thumbs"—have let their accounts sit delinquent for months. MacKinley initially assumed the trio merely skipped out of Booty Bay to avoid paying, but he later heard they met a stranger and darker fate deep in the jungle.

Vorlus Vilehoof. Vorlus Vilehoof is a rite of passage for young night elf warriors training in Darnassus. Under instruction from the warrior trainer Elanaria, candidates must hunt down a vile satyr who has defiled a hidden moonwell near the Ban'ethil Barrow Den. Before Elanaria will impart advanced martial techniques to young night elf warriors, she demands proof of their dedication and discipline. Words alone mean nothing in the defense of Kalimdor; a true guardian must be willing to confront corruption face-to-face and cleanse the sacred boughs of Teldrassil from taint.

Vorn Skyseer. Vorn Skyseer is a peaceful tauren resident of Camp Narache atop Red Cloud Mesa in Mulgore. Resting among the camp's tents, he greets young adventurers beginning their journeys and introduces them to local life. Situated in Camp Narache on Red Cloud Mesa, Vorn Skyseer serves as an informal welcoming presence for young tauren. As they undertake their rites of passage before venturing into the wider valleys of Mulgore, Vorn offers kind words and hospitality, helping new arrivals settle into the camp.

Vorsha the Lasher. Vorsha the Lasher is a violent hydra terrorizing the Horde's foothold at Zoram'gar Outpost along the coast of Ashenvale. Revering the creature's ferocity, the local naga maintain an offering brazier on an offshore island to honor her. By extinguishing this sacred flame, Horde champions provoke Vorsha and draw her ashore to end her predatory assaults. Zoram'gar Outpost sits on a tenuous strip of coast in northwestern Ashenvale, constantly besieged by hostile wildlife, night elves, and serpentine invaders. Among the most destructive threats prowling the Zoram Strand is Vorsha the Lasher, a gargantuan hydra known for brutal, unprovoked strikes against the outpost. The beast emerges from the surf to crush fortifications and butcher warriors before vanishing back into the deep tides.

Vul'Gol Ogre Mound. Vul'Gol Ogre Mound is a sunken basin in southern Duskwood overrun by the Splinter Fist ogres under the brute Zzarc'Vul. Once a cluster of human homesteads, its ruined farmhouses and subterranean cavern are now littered with the carcasses and scavenged plunder of the clan. Tucked away in the shadows southwest of the fork heading toward Stranglethorn Vale, the Vul'Gol Ogre Mound serves as the seat of the Splinter Fist clan in Duskwood. The basin was once peaceful farmland, but its human inhabitants have long since fled or perished, leaving behind hollowed-out cabins now claimed by lumbering ogres and used as crude shelters. Inside the cavern beneath the rise, piles of slaughtered black bears attest to the clan's voracious appetite. Their chieftain, Zzarc'Vul, rules over the encampment, hoarding odd trinkets alongside mundane scavenged goods.

WANTED: Andre Firebeard. A wanted notice in Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port names the pirate Andre Firebeard, who stands accused of crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The notice declares that his head, delivered to Security Chief Bilgewhizzle at Steamwheedle Port, counts as a binding contract. The notice calls Andre Firebeard a vile pirate, accused of crimes against Steamwheedle and Gadgetzan. The governing counsel has decreed that anyone who reads it may use lethal force in capturing Andre and those who aid him. He is to be found at the pirate enclave a way south along the coast from Steamwheedle Port, where he stands by a campfire inside the walls.

WANTED: Baron Longshore. WANTED: Baron Longshore is a bounty contract posted on the docks of Ratchet by Chief Engineer Gazlowe. It targets Baron Longshore, a notorious pirate captain originally from Gilneas who commands vessels of the Southsea Freebooters. Longshore's presence along the Merchant Coast poses a direct threat to goblin merchant shipping throughout the region. The waters off the Barrens are vital sea lanes for the Steamwheedle Cartel, connecting Ratchet to Booty Bay and beyond. Unfortunately, the Southsea Freebooters have fortified encampments along the coast south of town. Operating under the command of figures like Baron Longshore, these cutthroats harass merchant vessels, disrupt trade, and bleed the local goblin administration dry.

WANTED: Baron Vardus. A notice carrying High Executor Darthalia's order names Baron Vardus, a human and a high-ranking member of the Syndicate, wanted dead for crimes against the Forsaken. Proof of his death is to be brought to Darthalia in Tarren Mill. Darthalia has put a price on Baron Vardus, a human charged with crimes against the Forsaken and counted among the Syndicate's high-ranking members. Last word placed him in the Uplands of the Alterac Mountains, to the north of Tarren Mill. The order is plain: he is to die, and whoever brings Darthalia proof of his death will be paid for it.

WANTED: Bruuz. WANTED: Bruuz is a bounty posted by Gazlowe in the goblin port of Ratchet. A massive predatory shark has taken up residence near the harbor docks, threatening maritime traffic and coastal trade until someone puts an end to it. Ratchet thrives on merchant shipping, serving as the primary neutral gateway between Kalimdor and the Eastern Kingdoms. That steady stream of commerce makes the waters around the docks bustling and chaotic, but recently it has drawn a far more dangerous visitor. A gargantuan shark, dubbed 'Bruuz' by the frightened dockworkers, has begun prowling the bay. Rather than remaining in deep water, the beast aggressively targets small skiffs, local sailors, and offloading cargo, disrupting port operations.

text.enUS: WANTED: Caliph Scorpidsting. The Gadgetzan Water Company posts a bounty on Caliph Scorpidsting, who heads the Wastewander outlaws. Proof of his death goes to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan. Notices at Gadgetzan and Steamwheedle Port announce a high bounty from the Gadgetzan Water Company for Caliph Scorpidsting, who leads the Wastewander outlaws. The charges against him are the murder of company employees, the theft of company resources and the seizure of company property. Proof of his death is to go to Chief Engineer Bilgewhizzle in Gadgetzan.

WANTED: Chok'sul. A bounty posted in Thelsamar by Magistrate Bluntnose calls for the death of Chok'sul, an ogre warlord menacing northeastern Loch Modan. Believed to be organizing the assaults against local settlements and critical infrastructure, bringing his head secures a handsome reward from the town's leadership. While troggs and wildlife constantly test the borders of Loch Modan, the arrival of organized ogres represents an escalation that the local dwarven mountaineers cannot ignore. Settling into encampments along the rugged northeastern reaches of the valley, these brutes have moved beyond simple scavenging. According to local scouts and town authorities, their raids are focused, persistent, and dangerous.

WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im. WANTED: Incinerator Gar'im is a bounty posted by the authorities in Lakeshire against a hostile orc commander entrenched in Render's Valley. Gar'im commands a dangerous contingent of shadowcasters and is purported to be working with the Blackrock clan holding Stonewatch Keep. Magistrate Solomon offers a handsome bounty for proof of his demise. The Redridge Mountains have grown increasingly perilous as the Blackrock orcs push out from their mountain bastions. In Render's Valley, Incinerator Gar'im leads an active incursion, spearheading dark sorcery alongside loyal shadowcasters. With the local town guard stretched thin and the crown's armies largely absent, Magistrate Solomon has turned to independent mercenaries to eliminate Gar'im, who is purported to be working with the Blackrock of Stonewatch Keep.

WANTED: Jai'vhanel. WANTED: Jai'vhanel is an Alliance bounty posted by the Auberdine Village Council in Darkshore. The notice calls for the elimination of Jai'vhanel, a maddened black owl known as 'Swordfeather' that has begun ambushing travelers along the road near Auberdine. Adventurers must hunt the creature near the ruins of Ameth'Aran and bring proof of her death to Sentinel Glynda Nal'Shea. A posted notice from the Auberdine Village Council alerts travelers along the coastal roads of Darkshore to a dangerous menace. A prominent local owl known as Jai'vhanel, nicknamed 'Swordfeather', has succumbed to a sudden madness. Rather than keeping to the dense wilderness, she has begun ambushing travelers and couriers journeying near Auberdine, transforming an ordinary woodland predator into a critical hazard for the settlement.

WANTED: Marez Cowl. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty quest issued against a high-ranking Syndicate operative entrenched within the ruins of Stromgarde. As both an influential advisor and a dark warlock trafficking with demons, Cowl represents a severe threat to the Alliance forces attempting to secure the Arathi Highlands. WANTED: Marez Cowl is an Alliance bounty decree posted to eliminate one of the Syndicate's key leadership figures in the Arathi Highlands. Marez Cowl serves as a high-ranking advisor and field operative within the organization, orchestrating their activities in the ruined capital of Stromgarde. By placing a price on her head, Alliance commanders at Refuge Pointe aim to decapitate the Syndicate's local command structure.

WANTED: Murkdeep!. WANTED: Murkdeep! is an Alliance bounty posted on the notice board outside the inn in Auberdine. The village council seeks the death of Murkdeep, a dangerous murloc chieftain blamed for slaying a night elf Sentinel and sinking merchant vessels off Darkshore. Adventurers must march south along the mist-shrouded coast to draw out the raider and deliver justice. The Greymist murlocs along the Darkshore coastline are usually considered a nuisance, but Murkdeep escalated matters into open warfare against Auberdine. According to the wanted poster pinned outside the town inn, the ferocious beast is directly responsible for killing at least one night elf Sentinel and is suspected of sabotaging or wrecking two cargo vessels in the waters offshore. Facing mounting maritime losses and coastal raids, the Auberdine Village Council authorized a public bounty to put an end to the rampaging murloc leader.

text.enUS: WANTED: Otto and Falconcrest. A bounty posted by the Stromgarde Militia marks Lord Falconcrest, leader of the local Syndicate forces, and his deadly bodyguard Otto for death. Eliminating them strikes a crucial blow against the criminal organization's foothold in the Arathi Highlands. Proof of their demise must be delivered to Captain Nials at Refuge Pointe. The Stromgarde Militia has issued an official bounty targeting two key figures in the Arathi Highlands: Lord Falconcrest and his ferocious bodyguard, Otto. Stationed out of Refuge Pointe, the beleaguered defenders of Stromgarde seek to break the Syndicate's hold over their ancestral lands. Hunters must bring the heads of both targets to Captain Nials to claim the reward.

WANTED: Overseer Maltorius. A bounty notice declares that Overseer Maltorius, a rogue Thorium Brotherhood agent and newly hired commander of the Dark Iron Slag Pit crew of the Cauldron, is to die. By order of Overseer Oilfist, his head must be brought back as proof to Lookout Captain Lolo Longstriker. Overseer Maltorius, a traitorous Dark Iron dwarf, is to be found in the depths of the Cauldron's Slag Pit. The order is to slay him, take his head, and carry it back to Lookout Captain Lolo Longstriker for the bounty.

name.esES: SE BUSCA: Personal de la Hermandad

text.enUS: WANTED: Syndicate Personnel. Posted on the Tarren Mill bounty board under the authority of Lady Sylvanas, this decree condemns all members of the Syndicate to death. The Forsaken seek to purge the brigands gathering in the ruins of Durnholde Keep before they threaten Horde operations in the foothills. The Syndicate's sudden presence southeast of Tarren Mill has not gone unnoticed by the Forsaken. Rather than offering parley or treating them as mere displaced nobles, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and her commanders view the Syndicate as an active pestilence. The bounty dictates immediate death, specifying that any prisoners brought in will be executed without trial.

WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable. WANTED: Vulgara the Insatiable is a Peacekeeper bounty targeting a monstrous winged beast terrorizing the Shen'dar Highlands. Issued by Constable Aonda, the contract calls for adventurers to slay the ravenous vuldren and present her head to Danarii Bellowveil. A formal bounty posted by Constable Aonda of the Peacekeepers marks Vulgara the Insatiable as an immediate danger to the highlands. The massive winged vuldren has terrorized travelers and local settlements from her roost southwest of Shen'dar Village, prompting local authorities to call on adventurous bounty hunters to bring her reign to an end.

WRIGGLE.. WRIGGLE. is an encounter with an excitable young slime that loves to dance until it runs out of energy. To revive and befriend the creature, an adventurer must fetch a special batch of nutritious sludge from the canals of the Undercity. WRIGGLE. involves interacting with a lively, excitable little slime that delights in mirroring the dance movements of friendly travelers. Despite its enthusiasm, dancing quickly exhausts the small ooze, leaving it weary and in need of sustenance to restore its strength.

Wailing Caverns. Tucked into the bluffs above Lushwater Oasis in the Barrens, the Wailing Caverns are a sprawling network of subterranean springs and caverns. Originally explored by the night elf druid Naralex to restore lush vitality to the arid plains, the subterranean complex has instead become a twisted haven of bizarre mutations, agitated wildlife, and unnatural perils whose true source remains an unsettling mystery.

Wailing Essence. Wailing Essence is a strange, concentrated substance found within the ectoplasms roaming deep inside the Wailing Caverns. Suspected of fueling the bizarre mutations spreading through the flora and fauna of the Barrens, it has drawn the attention of opportunistic alchemists eager to bottle its potent properties. The subterranean caverns beneath the central Barrens have grown thick with unnatural energy, warping beasts and giving rise to gelatinous ectoplasms. These oozing creatures concentrate a viscous substance known as Wailing Essence. While local druids observe these waters with growing dread, goblin entrepreneurs see only raw commercial opportunity. In the port town of Ratchet, an eccentric alchemist named Mebok Mizzyrix believes this essence is the missing active ingredient for a line of lucrative 'smart drinks' meant to enhance consumer intellect, utterly unconcerned with the nightmarish corruption it might actually harbor.

name.frFR: Attendre la fin des travaux de Sirra

text.enUS: Wait for Sirra to Finish. This brief pause marks the moment Sirra Von'Indi deciphers the cryptic note delivered from the reclusive hermit Abercrombie. As he puts quill to paper in Darkshire's Town Hall, an ominous dread settles over the room, hinting that the hermit's words are far darker than expected. After receiving the mysterious note penned by the hermit Abercrombie, Sirra Von'Indi requires only a short spell to decipher its text. As a resident scholar aiding the Night Watch and town leadership, he undertakes the task without realizing immediately what horrors the message conceals.

Wand over Fist. Skuerto at Refuge Pointe has worked out where the first of Trelane's items ended up. Kor'gresh has Trelane's Wand of Invocation in Boulderfist Hall, and Skuerto wants it brought back. After your work for Apprentice Kryten, Skuerto has found where Trelane's first item went. Kor'gresh holds it in Boulderfist Hall, and has been throwing blasts of ice at his own kin to keep them in line. Skuerto reckons the ogre must be close to figuring out all of the wand's powers. Boulderfist Hall lies south of Refuge Pointe and then east of Thandol Span.

Wand to Bethor. This quest concludes the Fenris Keep confrontation by delivering a long-lost relic, the Woven Wand, back to Bethor Iceshard in the Undercity. Crafted years ago by three apprentice mages as a symbol of fellowship, the wand was hidden away when Thule Ravenclaw chose the Scourge. Returning it closes a bitter chapter in Bethor's past. Long before Lordaeron fell into ruin, three young mages bound their training wands together into a single instrument known as the Woven Wand. It was meant to symbolize their shared bond and ambition within the magical arts. However, when Thule Ravenclaw turned his loyalty toward the Lich King and embraced the Scourge, that fellowship broke irrevocably. Though Thule came to despise the friendship they once shared, he could not bear to destroy the wand, nor could he stomach leaving it in his former comrades' hands.

Wandering Shay. Shay Leafrunner, once found, asks you to help her get back to her friend Rockbiter. She admits she wanders off whenever there is something to see, but she has a bell whose sound brings her running back. Shay wants to find her way back to Rockbiter, who was supposed to be watching her. She admits she tends to wander off now and then, since there are so many things to see and she gets distracted.

Wanted - Arnak Grimtotem. Wanted: Arnak Grimtotem is a Horde bounty posted at Freewind Post demanding the execution of a violent Grimtotem exile. Arnak is targeted by the local authorities for murder and kidnapping on the mesas above the canyon. While tensions between the mainstream tauren of the Horde and the reclusive Grimtotem tribe are perpetually strained, Arnak took matters far beyond political friction. Branded an outcast, Arnak murdered a tauren and abducted the victim's sister, Lakota Windsong. In response to these heinous acts, Cliffwatcher Longhorn of Freewind Post sanctioned an open bounty calling for the rogue tauren's death.

Wanted: "Hogger". Wanted: "Hogger" is an Alliance bounty posted outside Goldshire for the head of a massive, savage gnoll chieftain. Hogger prowls the southwestern woods of Elwynn Forest and has violently thwarted every attempt by the local authorities to bring him down. While Elwynn Forest struggles with banditry and kobold infestations, the gnoll tribes in the south have grown bolder and more organized under the brute leadership of Hogger. Towering over typical Riverpaw gnolls, Hogger has established camp near the Forest's Edge, ambushing travelers and overpowering the local militia patrols sent to subdue him.

Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg. Wanted: Gath'Ilzogg is an Alliance bounty posted in Redridge Mountains targeting the warlord behind the Blackrock invasion of Stonewatch. Magistrate Solomon offers a generous reward for anyone daring enough to assault the conquered keep and bring back the commander's severed head. Gath'Ilzogg is the brutal commander directing Blackrock clan raids across the Redridge Mountains. Under his direction, the orcs stormed and conquered Stonewatch Keep, turning a former human bastion into a fortified staging ground for assaults on the surrounding settlements. From the keep's highest ramparts, he plots further incursions into Lakeshire, threatening to cut Redridge off from the rest of the kingdom.

Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore. Wanted: Lieutenant Fangore is a local bounty posted in Lakeshire by Magistrate Solomon. It calls on adventurers to hunt down Lieutenant Fangore, the vicious chieftain of the Shadowhide gnolls encroaching upon the Redridge Mountains. Eliminating him strikes a direct blow against the renegade sorcerer Morganth, whom the gnolls serve. Lakeshire sits in a desperate position. With Stormwind's army stretched thin and King Varian Wrynn mysteriously absent, Highlord Bolvar Fordragon has left frontier settlements like Redridge to look after themselves. The Shadowhide clan has grown increasingly bold, raiding trade routes, burning farmsteads, and pressing right up against the town's perimeter. Magistrate Solomon relies on posted bounties to draw mercenary blades where royal soldiers will not march.

Wanted: Maggot Eye. Wanted: Maggot Eye is an official death bounty posted on the Brill notice board by the town's Forsaken leadership. A notorious gnoll has been looting nearby graveyards and farms to supply dead bodies directly to the Lich King's Scourge. Executor Zygand requires proof of the creature's execution to secure the lands around Garren's Haunt. In Tirisfal Glades, the dead are far from resting peacefully. The gnoll known as Maggot Eye earned a severe death sentence not merely for scavenging, but for active collaboration with the Lich King. While gnolls are generally viewed as savage brutes driven by simple hunger, Maggot Eye has been systematically digging up corpses and collecting remains to fuel the ranks of the Scourge army.

text.enUS: Wanted: Vile Priestess Hexx and Her Minions. Primal Torntusk has ordered Vile Priestess Hexx and her minions brought to justice, and a grand prize awaits anyone who slays the priestess and her elite Aman'zasi guard. You will find them atop Jintha'alor in the Hinterlands. Primal Torntusk has ordered that Vile Priestess Hexx and her minions be brought to justice. The targets are the priestess herself and the Aman'zasi guards, her elite. Atop Jintha'alor, in the Hinterlands, is where they are found. Once they are slain, you report back to Torntusk at Revantusk Village.

War Banners. Captain Stoutfist in Menethil Harbor tasks Alliance champions with striking an encampment of Dragonmaw orcs northeast of the town and claiming their war banners. The remnant orcs, broken and scattered after the Second War, have begun gathering strength once again in the bogs of the Wetlands. During the Second War, the Dragonmaw clan subjugated the red dragonflight from the mountain fortress of Grim Batol. When their foul control broke, the liberated dragons turned upon their captors with ferocious vengeance, hunting the orcs nearly to extinction. What few survived fled Grim Batol into the high mountains east of Whelgar's Excavation, hidden away from the red flight's wrath.

War Quarter. The War Quarter is the northwestern district of the Undercity, serving as the command post and martial training ground for the Forsaken. Within its echoing stone chambers, the soldiers, priests, and crafters of Lordaeron hone their weapons and shadow magic in defense of their fledgling kingdom. It houses training halls for warriors and priests alongside weapon masters and heavy industry. Occupying the northwest sector of the subterranean metropolis, the War Quarter stands as the bastion of martial strength for the Forsaken. Beneath its gloomy stone arches, rank-and-file guards and elite champions assemble to drill in armed combat. Unlike traditional barracks of living kingdoms, this military center combines ruthless iron warfare with the chilling rites of shadow, housing an ominous Altar of Darkness where spiritual discipline merges with military ambition.

War Room. Deep inside Stormwind Keep, the War Room gathers the arms, records, and charts used to plan the Alliance’s defense. Beyond Stormwind Keep’s grand chambers, commanders turn to military logistics and high-level campaign planning. Swords, blunderbusses, and heavy artillery cannons line the stone walls. Military treatises and chronicles of past wars fill nearby tables. At the center, a large map lets commanders assess Alliance deployments across Azeroth, while the royal court handles affairs of state just steps away.

War of the Ancients. Ten thousand years ago, the reckless sorcery of Queen Azshara and her Highborne tore a portal through the Well of Eternity, unleashing the demonic Burning Legion onto Azeroth. Led by the young druid Malfurion Stormrage, his brother Illidan, and Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind, a desperate coalition of night elves, dragons, and ancient forest demigods repelled the invaders. The resulting destruction of the Well triggered the Great Sundering, violently shattering the ancient continent of Kalimdor and permanently altering the face of the world. At the height of the ancient Kaldorei Empire, Queen Azshara and her elite caste of sorcerers, the Highborne, relentlessly drew upon the vast arcane depths of the Well of Eternity. Their reckless manipulation sent massive ripples into the Great Dark Beyond, attracting Sargeras, the master of the Burning Legion. Entranced by promises of ultimate power and perfection, Azshara and her advisor Xavius opened a trans-dimensional rift within the Well. Legions of felhounds, felguard, doomguard, and monstrous commanders poured into the capital city of Zin-Azshari, slaughtering all non-Highborne and beginning their crusade to purge the world of life.

War on the Woodpaw. At Camp Mojache, Hadoken Swiftstrider calls the gnolls a lasting danger to the camp itself, with attacks growing more fevered of late. Hadoken asks you for ten Woodpaw Gnoll Manes to thin their numbers. To Hadoken, it makes no difference whether the gnolls belong in Feralas. If the camp does not harden its resolve, he warns, it will be pushed out of the whole region. With the attacks on the camp growing more fevered, he wants their numbers thinned and offers generous pay for ten Woodpaw gnoll manes.

Warcaller Gorlach. Warcaller Gorlach is an orc herald roaming the dusty streets of Orgrimmar, calling champions of the Horde to distant battlefronts. True to his title, he rallies travelers and seasoned warriors to answer commands in perilous outposts across Kalimdor and beyond. Patrolling the thoroughfares of Orgrimmar, Warcaller Gorlach serves as a primary herald for the Horde's expansion and strategic defenses. Rather than staying confined to a garrison desk, he marches among the citizenry, issuing orders directly to volunteers ready to test their mettle. Whether dispatching hunters into the contested canopy of Ashenvale, directing scouts toward the wilderness of Camp Mojache in Feralas, or issuing desperate calls to arms for distant campaigns like the Plaguelands, Gorlach ensures that no warrior lingering in the capital remains idle while the Horde faces threats abroad.

Ward Restocking. Ward Restocking is a task in the Arathi Highlands where travelers assist Doctor Gregory Victor in Hammerfall. With the outpost's infirmary running short on vital elixirs, couriers are dispatched to retrieve neglected supplies from Apothecary Jorell's lab at Go'Shek Farm. At the Horde settlement of Hammerfall in the Arathi Highlands, Doctor Gregory Victor tends to the wounded and ailing in the outpost's medical ward. Keeping the infirmary functional demands a regular supply of remedies, antidotes, and elixirs, which are usually provided by the Forsaken apothecary stationed nearby. When these deliveries stall, Victor must enlist capable travelers to step in and keep the clinic stocked.

Warden Thelwater. Warden Thelwater is the besieged overseer of the Stockade, Stormwind City's underground maximum-security prison. Caught unprepared when a violent riot erupted among the Defias prisoners, he now desperately recruits capable adventurers to quell the rebellion before word spreads to the city above. Hidden beneath the canals of Stormwind, the Stockade holds the kingdom's most dangerous miscreants, petty thieves, and political conspirators. Warden Thelwater was charged with keeping them securely locked away, but an organized revolt took the guards completely off guard. With the prisoners overwhelming security and taking control of the cells, Thelwater found himself barricaded at the threshold, struggling to contain an armed insurrection right beneath the streets of the capital.

Warlord Goretooth. Warlord Goretooth is the commanding orc officer stationed at Kargath in the dusty wastes of the Badlands. From his watchtower, he coordinates the Horde's frontier campaigns against the neighboring Dark Iron dwarves and monitors the volcanic menace of Blackrock Mountain. Though strict in military matters, he can occasionally be found relaxing around the camp's bonfire. Perched atop the watchtower of Kargath, Warlord Lunk Goretooth directs Horde operations on the hostile eastern frontier. Kargath serves as Orgrimmar's primary staging ground against the threats lurking within Blackrock Mountain and the surrounding ravines. Goretooth oversees patrols, coordinates scout forces like the Kargath Expeditionary Force, and issues direct kill orders targeting the Dark Iron clan's ranks and leadership. When he descends from his lookout, the stern commander shows a lighter side, frequently warming himself by the camp bonfire and trading quips with the camp's Forsaken casters before returning to duty.

Warmaster Laggrond. Warmaster Laggrond is a seasoned orc commander stationed outside the Horde entrance to Alterac Valley in the Alterac Mountains. He oversees recruitment and frontline recognition for warriors answering the call to aid the Frostwolf clan. Through his trials, fighters prove their mettle and earn the respect of the Horde vanguard. Standing watch in the bitter cold at the threshold of Alterac Valley, Warmaster Laggrond organizes the Horde's war effort against the Stormpike Expedition. He ensures that only capable fighters enter the valley to represent the Frostwolf clan and the wider Horde.

Warpwood Quarter. The Warpwood Quarter encompasses the eastern district of the ruined Highborne city of Eldre'Thalas, now known as Dire Maul. Once a center of elven nature cultivation and lush gardens, it has devolved into a warped, demon-tainted ruin overrun by frenzied flora and corrupted satyrs. Formerly known for its grand botanical marvels, the Warpwood Quarter has become a choking forest of twisted ancients and lethal lashers. The district fell under the sway of Alzzin the Wildshaper, a satyr who bent his dark magic toward defiling the ancient Fruit of Fertility. Under his malign influence, the plant life grew grotesque and predatory, saturating the halls with vile Felvine shards and drawing demons, rebellious imps, and demonic thralls into the ruined halls.

Warrior. Warriors are the quintessential frontline combatants of Azeroth, mastering heavy plate armor, shields, and nearly every form of martial weaponry. Fueling their most devastating strikes with pure combat rage, they charge into the thick of battle to defend weaker allies or carve through enemy ranks. They are found across every race and civilization, serving as everything from stalwart city guards and royal champions to wandering mercenaries. Warriors rely neither on divine prayers nor arcane incantations. Their power stems entirely from physical endurance, battlefield discipline, and an exhaustive mastery of weaponry. Clad in the heaviest plate mail, they dictate the frontline. Some fight behind towering shields to withstand punishing assaults and draw peril away from spellcasters and archers. Others step forward with two-handed polearms, axes, and greatswords, or wade into melee wielding a blade in each hand to cleave through whole formations.

Warrior's Terrace. The Warrior's Terrace is the eastern district of Darnassus, acting as both a martial training hub and the capital's fortified gateway. Overlooking the road into greater Teldrassil, it houses the city's battlemasters, warrior trainers, and Sentinel patrols. Positioned at the eastern threshold of Darnassus, the Warrior's Terrace—sometimes referred to as the Hall of Justice—stands as the primary defensive bulwark against incursions from the Teldrassil wilds. Heavily armed Sentinels mounted on nightsabers guard its high arched gates, maintaining a vigilant watch over incoming travelers. Within its open-air plazas, aspiring combatants drill alongside seasoned veterans on extensive dueling grounds and target ranges. The district also serves practical military needs, hosting weapon smiths, armorers, and the battlemasters coordinating night elf forces across the wider world.

text.enUS: Warsong Axe Shipment. The Warsong Axe Shipment is a heavy crate of newly forged axes waiting on the docks of Booty Bay in Stranglethorn Vale. Ordered by the Warsong Outriders to sustain their harvesting operations in Ashenvale, it serves as a crucial link in the Horde's overseas supply chain. Maintaining the logging operations at the Warsong Lumber Camp requires a continuous flow of durable tools that cannot always be forged on the front lines. To keep woodcutters supplied, orders are sent across the Great Sea to the neutral goblin port of Booty Bay. Stored near Wharfmaster Lozgil, this crate contains sharpened axes intended for shipment back to Splintertree Post, highlighting the logistical hurdles the Horde faces in keeping its distant frontier camps armed and functional.

name.esES: Campo de trabajos forzados Grito de Guerra

text.enUS: Warsong Labor Camp. The Warsong Labor Camp is an isolated Horde timber-harvesting outpost tucked away in southeastern Ashenvale. Operated by Warsong loggers and defended by orcish sentries, the work site cuts lumber to fuel the growth of Durotar while braving the hostility of the surrounding forest. Situated east of Fallen Sky Lake and southwest of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den, the Warsong Labor Camp exists for one vital purpose: harvesting the dense timber of Ashenvale. The dry plains of Durotar offer little usable lumber to build cities like Orgrimmar, forcing the Warsong clan to push deep into the contested woods. Staffed by hardy loggers and orcish guards, the site operates in relative isolation, grinding through ancient trees despite the ever-present threat of night elf scouts and passing Alliance warbands.

Warsong Lumber Camp. The Warsong Lumber Camp is a fortified orc logging operation deep in Ashenvale, run by the Warsong clan to harvest timber for the Horde. Anchored by the fortified Kargathia Keep, it stands as both an economic lifeline for nearby Horde settlements and an unrelenting provocation to the night elves. The constant sound of goblin-built shredders chewing through ancient boughs makes this clearing a primary flashpoint of the forest war. Carved straight out of the dense canopy of eastern Ashenvale, the Warsong Lumber Camp is the industrial engine fueling the Horde's expansion across Kalimdor. Orc peons and hired goblin engineers strip the forest with whirring shredders, processing towering trunks into lumber to reinforce outpost walls like nearby Splintertree Post and build up the fledgling nation of Durotar. The camp is heavily fortified against constant night elf counterattacks, centering on the stockades of Kargathia Keep and an active kennel for the clan's fierce war wolves. For the Warsong, every felled tree is survival and strength; for the native Sentinels, every saw blade is an act of sacrilege.

Warsong Oil. Warsong Oil is a crucial industrial lubricant intended for the machinery at the Warsong Lumber Camp in Ashenvale. A vital supply shipment was intercepted en route by local satyrs, who took the oil to their corrupted woodland sanctuaries for foul rituals. The Warsong Clan's logging efforts in Ashenvale rely heavily on heavy machinery, goblin-engineered shredders, and massive sawmills. Keeping this industrial equipment running requires a steady supply of specialized oil. Without it, the clan's timber harvest risks grinding to an abrupt halt, stalling the flow of lumber desperately needed to build Orgrimmar and fortify Horde settlements across Durotar and the Barrens.

Warsong Outrider. Stationed along the contested road leading east from Ashenvale into Azshara, the Warsong Outrider keeps watch over the Horde's frontier. She serves as an advanced scout for the Warsong clan, monitoring travelers and relaying crucial intelligence back to their forward encampments. Although armed and vigilant against night elf incursions, she maintains a passive watch unless directly provoked. The borderlands between Ashenvale and the shattered ruins of Azshara are fraught with danger. Operating far from the fortified safety of Splintertree Post or the lumber camps, the Warsong Outrider observes troop movements and patrols the transit corridor. Armed with a bow and toxic stingers, she stands ready to defend the Horde's claim over the region, though she conserves her strength by only firing upon Alliance trespassers who actively attack her.

text.enUS: Warsong Outrider Update. The Warsong Outrider Update is a military intelligence dispatch penned by a Warsong outrider stationed along the eastern borderlands of Ashenvale. Entrusted to couriers serving the Horde, it provides frontline observations vital for securing the crossing toward Azshara and strengthening the orcish foothold against night elf resistance. Stretching along the eastern road past Splintertree Post toward the ancient ruins of Azshara, the border of Ashenvale remains a volatile frontier. The Warsong Outrider Update compiles tactical sightings, patrol movements, and resource evaluations from the mounted orcish vanguards riding this perimeter. Sent back to Kadrak at the northern watchtower guarding the Barrens border, these field notes grant Horde commanders a clear assessment of enemy troop concentrations and territorial threats lurking beneath the forest canopy.

text.enUS: Warsong Outrider Update. Warsong Outrider Update is a Horde delivery quest originating along the perilous paths of eastern Ashenvale. A lone Warsong scout entrusts an adventurer with vital intelligence detailing threats from the nearby Alliance, entrenched satyr, and encroaching naga in neighboring Azshara. Eastern Ashenvale is a contested border zone where Horde supply lines face constant harassment. The Warsong Outriders maintain a vigilant screen across the woods, scouting enemy movements long before raiding parties can strike outposts like the Mor'shan Rampart or Splintertree Post. Encountering an outrider on patrol means stepping directly into an active theater of reconnaissance, where information can mean the difference between holding a fortification or losing it to ambush.

text.enUS: Warsong Runner Update. The Warsong Runner Update is a military dispatch carrying situational observations from the Zoram'gar Outpost along the western coast of Ashenvale. Delivered to the Horde commander Kadrak at the Barrens border, it helps coordinate the Warsong clan's ongoing campaign against the night elves. Positioned at the edge of the Zoram Strand, the Warsong runner at Zoram'gar Outpost keeps watch over coastal waters and nearby threats in western Ashenvale. This update contains critical intelligence gathered from the outpost's frontline scouts, documenting regional activity and securing supply lines. Carried back to Kadrak's watchtower on the Barrens border, the dispatch provides the Horde leadership with the clarity needed to fortify their position and plan subsequent movements deep in ancestral elven woods.

text.enUS: Warsong Runner Update. Warsong Runner Update is a Horde communication task connecting the forward defenses of Ashenvale with commanders along the border. Entrusted to couriers and fresh recruits, the missive details the rising military pressure facing Warsong scouts, notably the aggression of encroaching naga. The Warsong Clan maintains a string of scouts and runners throughout Ashenvale to monitor surrounding hostilities and keep lines of supply intact. Between territorial skirmishes with night elf sentinels and the harsh environment, swift intelligence is vital. Couriers carrying frontline dispatches are essential in ensuring remote garrisons remain coordinated with commanders like Kadrak posted on the Mor'shan Rampart.

Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades are specialized industrial cutting tools ordered to supply the Horde's clear-cutting operations in Ashenvale. Delivered through goblin logistical networks, they are vital for keeping the Warsong Lumber Camp's timber machinery running. The Warsong Clan's logging efforts in Ashenvale rely heavily on heavy-duty machinery provided and maintained with goblin engineering. Standard axes alone cannot feed the Horde's massive appetite for Kalimdor lumber, requiring steam engines and circular saws that continually chew through raw timber. Because Ashenvale's ancient hardwood rapidly dulls and snaps ordinary blades, constant shipments of replacement saw blades are vital to keep the mills running at the Warsong Lumber Camp.

Warsong Saw Blades. Warsong Saw Blades is a Horde errand undertaken at Splintertree Post on behalf of the Warsong Clan's logging campaign. To acquire heavy saw blades imported from Ratchet, adventurers must strike an under-the-table bargain with the courier Pixel, who demands personal protection before surrendering the shipment. Fulfilling her trade secures essential machinery needed to keep the Horde's lumber mills humming in Ashenvale. The Warsong loggers in Ashenvale rely entirely on imported heavy machinery to cut through the ancient timber of the deep forest. While Pixel has successfully brought a shipment of specialized saw blades straight from the goblin port of Ratchet to Splintertree Post, she has no intention of simply handing them over for free. Out in the perilous wilds of Ashenvale, coin is only worth so much; personal safety is worth far more. Rather than demanding gold, Pixel insists on bartering the heavy saw blades for a reliable Deadly Blunderbuss to keep herself safe during her dangerous travels through hostile territory.

text.enUS: Warsong Scout Update. The Warsong Scout Update is a written dispatch containing battlefield reconnaissance from Splintertree Post in Ashenvale. Gathered by a forward scout of the Warsong clan, it provides commander Kadrak with critical intelligence needed to secure the Horde's foothold against night elf resistance. As the Horde attempts to claim timber and establish supply routes through Ashenvale, scouts from the Warsong clan patrol deep behind enemy lines. The Warsong Scout Update compiles local observations from the fortified encampment of Splintertree Post, tracking night elf sentinels and territorial movements. Handed over to messengers trading routine orders, the document allows Kadrak at the Barrens-Ashenvale border to assess troop readiness and coordinate logistics in the contested woods.
